**Newest research update — FIELD format flag `0x02` remains unqualified (2026-10-22; normative/peer-source review):** ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.99 documents only `Flags & 0x01 => type is kGeneral`; it does not define `0x02` as an empty-value flag. Autodesk's public FIELD DXF table defines serialized value kinds but not this DWG flag. LibreDWG's shared decoder suppresses payload when either low bit is set, but its source/NEWS does not establish the undocumented bit's semantics. Keep `0x02`'s semantic meaning unproven; do not promote it to format support based on local writer-generated vectors or peer behavior. [Research note](#research-update-field-format-flag-0x02-semantics-remain-unqualified-2026-10-22).

**Previous implementation progress — PAR-14 R2004 decompressor extended-length overflow (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted):** source arithmetic showed that an AC1018 long-copy token with 16,843,008 zero continuations can exceed `UINT32_MAX` after its fixed bias and wrap to 31 bytes; an extended literal length with the same continuation count wraps to 16. Generated 64-byte-window controls now verify both the long-copy pattern and long-literal bytes fill exactly the bounded window. Focused selector/CTest, DWG reader-matrix CTest, `lc3_compat_check`, and scoped diff check pass. No external drawing/PoC, fixture, support claim, or external status changed. **Previous implementation progress — PAR-14 32-bit DWG decompressor-size admission (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted):** `decompress18` and `decompress21` accepted 64-bit lengths but stored them in 32-bit cursor fields, so a declared size of `2^32 + N` could wrap to a valid `N`-byte stream and be reported as successful. Both paths now reject unrepresentable compressed or decompressed sizes before retaining pointers or decoding, and cast only after the guard. Generated valid AC1018/AC1021 controls verify oversize input/output refusal and unchanged sentinels. **Newest deeper/broader research — DWG EED unsigned-size and continuation boundary (2026-10-19; ODA + LibreDWG + ACadSharp source/report + local audit):** ACadSharp issue [#1282](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1282) reports a 32,768-byte EED block written through a signed `short`, then dropped on read. That is a peer writer defect, not evidence that DWG EED is capped at 32,767: ODA §28 defines the block length as a 16-bit `BS`, LibreDWG defines `BITCODE_BS` as `uint16_t`, and local `getBitShort()` / `putBitShort()` use the unsigned 0..65,535 profile. Existing 7K generated controls already cover 32,767/32,768 and 65,535/65,536, including an item-boundary split and following-entity alignment. The open question is narrower: ODA's repeated-block grammar does not explicitly document whether multiple consecutive blocks may reuse one APPID handle; LibreDWG's public example uses multiple blocks but distinct APPIDs. Therefore keep >65,535 same-APPID continuation `LOCAL_WIRE_ONLY / EXTERNAL_ACCEPTANCE_PENDING`; do not adopt a 32,767 ceiling or promote the local self-read. No code/test/fixture/dependency, peer/native run, new finding/subplan, support promotion, or validation-cadence change; counts remain 139/77 and J256/J260/J268/J284/J293/J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. **Previous deeper/broader peer-source audit — gradient color wire semantics, Swift-port attribution, and a narrow DXF writer (2026-10-18; normative PDF + primary-source + local source review):** checked the ambiguous group-63 claim against the ODA DWG specification (§2.11 and §20.4.75), Autodesk's HATCH DXF table and `AcCmColor` color contract, ezdxf's gradient parser/writer, ACadSharp's R2004+ DWG reader, and LibreDWG's published history. ODA specifies each DWG HATCH gradient stop as 463 BD, an unknown short, color BL, and an RC color byte; the R2004+ `CmColor` definition says its short is always zero and the long is the packed color. Autodesk specifies the high byte of the packed color as the color method, with the lower three bytes carrying color components. The local bounded reader stores the whole BL as `GradientStop.rgb` and leaves `colorMethod` at its default; DXF preflight rejects any `rgb` outside 24 bits. This is a source-confirmed format/model incompatibility for method-tagged CMC values and becomes a concrete write failure for the values shown by the ACadSharp-derived encoder; exact method mapping still needs a focused vector. This is now PAR-134 under existing 7Q ownership, not a new top-level subplan. On the DXF side, ezdxf associates 63/421 with each gradient stop, while Autodesk's HATCH table documents top-level code 63 only for MPOLYGON and does not define a separate HATCH background field. Thus the group code is context-sensitive; the Swift-port README's “background fill” wording does not establish a new DXF field. The plan adds fast DXF group-63 assertions plus a small in-memory DWG CMC vector covering raw fields, semantic normalization, DXF emission and next-record alignment; do not rely on writer/reader self-round-trip alone. Zephyr remains derivative and its retrieved README snapshots disagree about its DWG converter lineage. LibreDWG's changelog records a past HATCH gradient-color fix but gives no sufficient detail to infer another defect. A newly surfaced Go R2010 writer covers only five simple 2D entities and offers test-methodology leads, not feature-parity evidence. No production code or tests changed; current roll-up is 134 findings / 76 top-level subplans. J256/J260/J268/J284/J293/J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. This pass audited the exact downstream conversion wrapper and compared the
current GDAL/OGR and ezdxf documentation at their 3D boundaries. It adds
qualification precision to existing PAR-07/S8 work; no peer executable,
kernel, or native CAD application was run, and no external drawing was
downloaded.

| Route/source | Source-backed observation | Evidence ceiling and plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| FreeCAD current [importDWG.py](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py) | The DWG-to-DXF wrapper starts a selected converter and waits for it, then labels conversion successful when the expected DXF path exists. The inspected path does not test the converter process return code before that success message. | Native-qualification harnesses must record the exact converter executable/build, arguments, return code, stdout/stderr, fresh output hash and actual DXF version; strict-parse the intermediate before invoking the selected FreeCAD importer. An output file or GUI success message alone is not converter success. This is a harness requirement, not a newly reproduced libdxfrw or FreeCAD defect. |
| [GDAL DXF 3D extensibility](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html#3d-extensibility) | Current docs say 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY/SURFACE modeler content is skipped by default because GDAL cannot turn it into OGR geometry. Optional DXF_3D_EXTENSIBLE_MODE exposes an ASMData binary field and a 12-real ASMTransform for AC1027 and later. The DXF driver also documents Binary DXF input beginning with GDAL 3.12. | This can be a narrowly useful raw-carrier/projection observation when the exact GDAL version and option are pinned. It does not establish source owner graph closure, ACIS interpretation, B-rep validity, or DWG parsing; omitted-by-default rows must not be counted as negative semantic results. |
| [ezdxf 1.4.5 ACIS API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) and [FAQ](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/faq.html) | The API documents load of SAT/SAB, export_sab, and body_from_mesh output to SAT for R2000-R2010 or SAB for R2013+. It also says mesh_from_body extracts only flat polygonal faces and loses faces bounded by curved edges. The older FAQ broadly describes ezdxf as reading SAT/SAB but only writing SAT. | Keep two claims separate: exact release/API support for SAB generated from the documented mesh-origin Body subset, versus general arbitrary ACIS/SAB editing and round-trip. Do not promote the latter from the existence of export_sab. At the composed optional-peer checkpoint, pin the package/wheel and verify generated output by strict reopen, carrier placement, identity and digest; curved or unsupported structures are explicit negative controls, not silently simplified semantic passes. |
| [LibreDWG NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) and local SAT/group-310 tests | The release notes continue to expose specific SAT-final-block and binary DXF group-310 history; local fast selectors already cover related carrier framing and SAT-v1 cases. | Reuse existing selectors and add a cross-implementation row only at the planned composed checkpoint. Add a local control only if a specific uncovered boundary remains after comparing exact versioned behavior; do not add an external fixture or run peer tools per implementation slice. |

### Readiness changes to existing PAR-07/S8 route ledger

1. Preserve separate stages for DWG converter execution, intermediate DXF
   existence/hash/version, strict intermediate parse and per-source-object
   disposition, then the selected native importer. A nonzero converter status
   fails the converter stage even if a partial output exists.
2. Keep the ordinary FreeCAD Linux and Windows qualification scoped to the
   intended converter/importer route and supported explicit geometry/2D
   contract. Record importer backend and preferences. The stock importer
   route is not an ACIS B-rep semantic oracle.
3. If GDAL is already available at the composed checkpoint, use its optional
   AC1027+ raw-ASM route only to check a named carrier/transform projection;
   record option state and distinguish default skip from malformed/lost data.
4. If ezdxf is already available at that checkpoint, test exact release-specific
   SAT/SAB read/write operations separately. A mesh-origin SAB export is not
   evidence for arbitrary SAB round-trip; use analytic flat-mesh expectations
   and explicit curved-face/unsupported-node negative cases.
5. Preserve current implementation cadence: no peer dependency, no peer run in
   each fast slice, no new committed peer/sample drawings, and no full-suite or
   native run outside the existing composed gates. Continue preserving the
   LibreCAD and LibreCAD_3 2D consumer path independently from optional 3D
   semantic evidence.

### Implementation-ready refinement to existing owners

At the existing composed PAR-07/S8 modeler checkpoint, record a conservation
tuple per source solid: source entity handle and owner/block path; modeler

when the semantic route is absent or cannot represent it. If an edit dirties

the composed result. Keep routine work to generated, focused local tests; no
new peer runtime belongs in the per-slice loop. Continue 2D LibreCAD and
LibreCAD_3 compatibility work independently of optional 3D consumer evidence.

### Implementation-ready route gate

At the existing composed PAR-07/S8 consumer checkpoint, capture one
source-identity/owner/disposition manifest and preserve it across each stage:

1. Pin the source producer/profile and input hash; enumerate entity handle,
   concrete type, owner/block/layout, geometry/carrier presence, and expected
   disposition before conversion.
2. Run the named DWG converter as a separate stage. Record executable/build,
   arguments, exit code, diagnostics, fresh output hash, and actual DXF version.
3. Strictly parse and inspect the intermediate DXF before FreeCAD. Reconcile
   each source identity against emitted typed/raw records and explicitly label
   omitted, approximated, refused, or unsupported records. For `3DSOLID`/
   `REGION`/`BODY`, score entity shell, inline SAT/SAB, AcDs key/owner/payload,
   and semantic result independently.
4. Exercise the selected FreeCAD backend on each requested OS/build and record
   its importer/add-on identity, preferences, warnings, and imported-object
   inventory. A source object present in the DXF but absent from FreeCAD is a
   consumer disposition, not converter loss. The stock route's inability to
   parse ACIS/SAT is `NOT_CONSUMED_BY_STOCK_DXF_IMPORTER`; it neither proves nor
   disproves carrier preservation or B-rep semantics.
5. Keep strict parser acceptance, repair/recovery, native open/audit, and
   independently authored geometric expectations as separate fields. A
   same-codec round trip or a successful conversion process cannot substitute
   for any of them.

This is a clarification/refinement of the existing PAR-07/S8 route ledger,
not a new implementation finding or blocker. Findings/top-level subplans

`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; no evidence in this pass promotes support claims. No code,
test, fixture, dependency, CTest registration, peer execution, native
qualification, or implementation-order/cadence change was made. The
repository-local ODA PDF was not present at the documented path, so this pass
makes no new DWG byte-layout claim.

   `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests` owner. Parse a complete DXF with an APPID,

   that the XDATA remains attached to the same BLOCK_RECORD, between its
   ordinary fields and the next group-0 record; it must not migrate to BLOCK,
   ENDBLK, or the following record. Include one typed numeric tuple as well as
   text so a string-only assertion cannot pass vacuously.

   BLOCK_RECORD precollection/pending-emission boundary. Use an additive
   `dxfRW` writer overload or equivalent non-pure adapter path; do not add a
   pure `DRW_Interface` virtual. Do not keep borrowed `DRW_Variant*` values

   preservation, and corrected same-writer retry. Keep the test local-generated

## Implementation progress — PAR-05/7AR generated DWG TV/TU → modern DXF characterization (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Added two selectors to the existing `libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests` executable.
`--dwg-tv-tu-target-matrix` generates in-memory string fields for AC1018 TV and
AC1021 TU paths; no drawing fixture is written. An independent test-local bit
writer assembles expected bit-short lengths, version-specific payloads,
terminators, and a trailing `0xA7` byte. The production reader must decode the
typed value and leave the sentinel untouched.

The three observations are intentionally field-scoped:

- A BMP omega scalar has equivalent typed values on both source paths despite
distinct TV/TU wire layouts.
- A literal `\\U+0041` spelling decodes to `A` through TV but remains literal
through TU. The test records this current behavior; it does not choose which
interpretation is normative for every consumer/string field.
- A lone-surrogate escape spelling remains literal on both routes. Strict
modern-DXF output quotes its backslash, remains valid text, and preserves the
following group.

`--dwg-tv-tu-entity-integration` writes complete AC1018 and AC1021 DWGs at test
runtime, each with ordinary TEXT, MTEXT, and a geometrically distinct following
LINE. `dx_iface` imports each DWG and strictly exports a complete AC1027 ASCII
DXF. A physical group-pair scan checks exact TEXT/MTEXT value bytes, ordering,
`$ACADVER=AC1027`, terminal group-0 EOF, and following LINE coordinates. DXF
re-import checks the version-specific typed text values, LINE geometry, and
exactly three modelspace entities. All generated DWG/DXF files are removed by
test cleanup.

Focused verification passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests -j2`
- `./build-gcc/libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests --dwg-tv-tu-target-matrix`
- `./build-gcc/libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests --dwg-tv-tu-entity-integration`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_gbk_codepage$' --output-on-failure` (1/1)
- Receipt JSON validation and scoped `git diff --check`

## Deeper/broader direction-specific support claims and downstream adoption policy (2026-10-18; research only)

This pass cross-checked the current standalone support boundary and package
integration guidance against LibreCAD 3's explicit DWG read/write position,
then verified the policy against this checkout's machine-readable claim
ledger. It adds no codec, parser rule, or format-support evidence. The value is
to make the plan's final adoption and claim-promotion gates directional and
operational rather than allowing a successful read, package build, or opaque
carrier round-trip to imply writer or 3D support.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not establish | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standalone [libdxfrw README support boundary](https://github.com/LibreCAD/libdxfrw/blob/master/README.md) | The project distinguishes baseline ASCII/Binary DXF, raw sections/opaque/ACIS carriers, DWG reading, DWG writing, 2D compatibility, and 3D typed-data routes. The README labels these scopes implemented or experimental according to evidence; even the baseline DXF lane is explicitly marked experimental for broad independent qualification. A capability table is the project's declared scope, not a file-by-file conformance result. | Preserve one claim per `(format, AC code, direction, operation, feature family, exact route)`. Keep implemented-but-experimental baseline-DXF claims separately scoped from experimental DWG, raw-carrier, writer, and semantic-solid claims; do not roll counts or version badges into one parity percentage. |
| Local [`qualified-format-claims-v1.json`](metadata/qualified-format-claims-v1.json), [`qualified-format-status-v1.json`](metadata/qualified-format-status-v1.json), and their plan-defined transition rules | The current snapshot is `FROZEN`; it has 15 read-direction value claims only, of which 11 are `EXPERIMENTAL` and 4 are `PENDING_NATIVE`. It contains no writer-direction claim. This is an exact ledger observation for the current implementation digest—not a timeless statement about future revisions or a writer result. | A reader claim cannot promote a writer claim. Before changing source or native support language, update the digest-bound ledger through its declared transition rules and add direction-specific evidence; do not silently reinterpret `PENDING_NATIVE` or `FROZEN` as a pass. Keep local implementation, independent decode, external/native acceptance, and product release decisions distinguishable. |
| LibreCAD 3 [DWG support policy](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/blob/master/docs/dwg-support.md) | The project documents `WITH_DWG_IMPORT` as opt-in/read-only and says DWG writing is not exposed. Its rationale is the asymmetric consequence of a bad read versus silently misleading output. For write support it calls for promoted write claims, a file reopened by an independent implementation, and an explicit project decision; the native acceptance step is human-gated rather than a CI dependency. This is a downstream consumer policy, not a second DWG implementation. | Keep the LibreCAD 3 compatibility check on its actual read/import contract; never use it as writer validation. A future DWG-save claim needs its own exact-version/feature ledger entry, independent readback, and release-owner decision. If proprietary/native tooling is unavailable in CI, record the native result as pending and continue other implementation work. |
| Standalone [`LIBRECAD_SYNC.md`](https://github.com/LibreCAD/libdxfrw/blob/master/LIBRECAD_SYNC.md) | The documented package adoption gate stages the standalone install, checks CMake and pkg-config consumers, builds the pinned LibreCAD filter in system-package mode with no bundled-fork include path, and separates fast local tests from the six-version writer matrix, fuzz, and sanitizer lanes. This validates integration method and cadence, not every downstream UI behavior. | Retain the staged-package/system-consumer check as a composed integration gate, not a per-slice full suite. Capture package prefix, exact consumer revision/configuration, compile/link command and selected include/library paths so a bundled checkout cannot accidentally mask an uninstalled or incompatible standalone library. |
| Autodesk [DXF 3DSOLID fields](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm) and ezdxf [renderer limitations](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/addons/drawing.rst) | The DXF entity contract exposes proprietary modeler data as group 1/3 carrier strings; ezdxf says its renderer does not render ACIS and projects 3D entities into the XY plane. Thus syntactically retained `3DSOLID` tags, entity recognition, and 2D display do not prove a valid B-rep or 3D consumer result. | At the existing PAR-07/S8 composed gate, preserve separate outcomes for entity shell, exact inline/section carrier, owner/key association, parsed model, shape validity/metrics, and named native-consumer result. Successful DXF parse or visible placeholder is not a semantic-solid pass. |

### Implementation-ready release-gate delta

1. On each future support update, first regenerate and validate the exact
   claim ledger against the implementation digest; key the claim by format,
   version, direction, operation, feature family, and route. Do not infer
   writer support from reader claims or 3D semantics from carrier retention.
2. Keep the existing per-slice fast path unchanged. At the composed package
   checkpoint, install into a fresh prefix, compile the exact consumer/filter
   against that prefix, and verify the compile/link inputs do not resolve to a
   bundled fork. Run the full writer matrix, fuzz/sanitizer, and native
   application checks only at their existing scheduled checkpoints.
3. For optional LibreCAD 3 validation, pin its source revision and
   `WITH_DWG_IMPORT` setting; classify this strictly as reader/consumer
   compatibility. Do not create a DWG-write check that the application does
   not expose.
4. For a DWG writer claim, require a generated-from-scratch source manifest,
   exact requested and actual target version, strict independent readback,
   owner/reference closure, per-record disposition, and (where the claim
   requires native acceptance) an explicit human receipt and release decision.
5. Keep carrier-byte identity and geometry semantics separate. The exact ACIS
   bytes can be preserved while a named parser/kernel rejects or cannot
   interpret them; conversely, a consumer's projected display does not prove
   all source records or metadata survived.
6. No new source finding, implementation subplan, dependency, fixture, test,
   or CTest registration follows from this policy research. The six external
   items remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; unsupported native routes remain
   `NOT_RUN`/`PENDING_NATIVE` rather than blocking locally ready slices.

This refines the existing release, consumer, and PAR-07 evidence gates only.
It does not change implementation order, fast/full-test frequency, the 130
finding / 73 top-level-subplan counts, or any support/J disposition.

## Deeper/broader peer root-cause and strict-versus-recovery evidence review (2026-10-18; research only)

This pass compared how independent DWG/DXF projects describe and verify
specific failures, then checked whether their issue-level conclusions are
supported by a reproducer, a root-cause change, or only a symptom report. It
does not treat any peer issue as evidence of a libdxfrw defect. No peer was
built or run, no external drawing was downloaded, and no implementation,
test, fixture, or dependency was changed.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not establish | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ACadSharp [#1074](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1074) and merged [#1077](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1077) | The issue title and initial diagnosis blame absent VisualStyle/Material objects. The linked fix records the same AC1027 TrueView crash reproduced on a minimal LINE-only file, identifies active VPORT `AmbientColor` defaulting to ByBlock as the cause, and changes the default to black; the PR reports that the same native repro then opens and allows Realistic/Conceptual mode. Thus a peer symptom was reproduced and fixed, but the title-level object-omission theory was not the demonstrated root cause. | Treat issue titles, reporter hypotheses, and root causes as separate evidence fields. Do not open a VisualStyle/Material local fix from #1074 alone. A peer issue can guide a local generated scenario, but a local owner/fix requires a source-backed local mismatch or a reproducible local minimal case with a discriminating expected result. |
| ACadSharp [#1172](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1172), including its discussion of [#1001](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1001) | The report counts `OfType<Insert>()` before/after an AC1032 round-trip. A later commenter notes `TableEntity : Insert`, and that a separate TABLE loss can change this count; the commenter also notes its diagnostic differs from the original no-notification report, so the alternate cause is not proven for #1172. This demonstrates a confound, not resolution of the reported loss. | At any peer or local cross-format census, partition by exact runtime/entity type, handle/source identity, owner/layout/block, and disposition. Do not use base-class counts such as INSERT as a substitute for exact source-to-output identity; separately record diagnostics and attribute-child/SEQEND structure. |
| ACadSharp [#1161](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1161) | The report identifies a single inverted R13/R14 LTYPE-presence condition in AC1014 DWG writing, contrasts the AC1015+ path, and supplies an in-memory explicit-linetype repro plus readback/native-audit results claimed by its author. It is a strong version-branch test-design example, but remains a peer report and not a libdxfrw defect or DWG rule. | When touching a versioned optional-field branch, use the smallest locally generated positive/negative pair on each side of the version boundary, assert both semantic reference and exact cursor/handle alignment, and keep the generated case in the current owning fast-test target. Do not import the peer's thresholds or files. |
| ACadSharp [#1297](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1297) | The reporter says a native AC1032 rejection persisted after the serialized MTEXT object matched the AutoCAD object byte-for-byte; the missing VisualStyle hypothesis is explicitly unproved. This leaves the whole-file cause unresolved. | Record per-object byte equality as a diagnostic only. Native rejection triage still needs the complete versioned file context (classes, tables, dictionaries, references, owners, and other objects); keep the native result pending until the whole-file cause and exact route are established. Do not change local MTEXT or object serialization based on the unresolved report. |
| ezdxf [strict/recovery guidance](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/usage_for_beginners.rst), [launcher/audit and raw-browser documentation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/launcher.rst) | ezdxf distinguishes ordinary `readfile` for structurally sound documents from `recover.readfile` for flawed files. Its CLI describes `audit` as audit/recovery, and its `info` command warns the loaded view may not represent original contents; the raw structure browser is provided for diagnosis. These capabilities describe ezdxf's route, not conformance or semantic correctness of another codec. | In composed comparisons, record strict parse and recovered parse as distinct results. A file that opens only after recovery is not a strict-parse pass; record repairs, dropped/changed records, and warnings. Use raw-tag inspection only to locate structural loss, not as a semantic or native-acceptance result. Keep such peer checks optional and outside each implementation slice. |

### Implementation-ready evidence triage

1. For each new peer report, record exact repository/release or commit,
   format-version, direction, operation, reported symptom, reproducer
   availability, root-cause status, linked fix status, and the validation
   route. Use `UNREPRODUCED`, `SYMPTOM_REPRODUCED`, `ROOT_CAUSE_CONFIRMED`,
   `FIX_MERGED`, and `NOT_COMPARABLE` as evidence states; do not collapse them
   into one “peer supports/fails” label.
2. Before mapping a peer symptom to a local PAR item, check type inheritance,
   owner/layout membership, exact handle/source identity, callbacks or
   notifications, and whether the named writer/reader is the path that lost the
   record. Keep plausible alternative explanations visible until a minimal
   case discriminates them.
3. For versioned writer branches, add only a local from-scratch fast vector
   where needed: one case with the optional field/reference present, one absent,
   adjacent target versions where the grammar changes, and a following-record
   or handle sentinel. Verify both readback semantics and emitted bytes/handles
   before the owning CTest; no peer fixture is admitted.
4. For strict-vs-recovery consumers, store separate statuses and reports for
   strict decode, recovery/audit, structural inspection, and native open/audit.
   Recovery cannot upgrade strict parsing; raw inspection cannot upgrade
   semantic interpretation; a successful in-library round-trip cannot upgrade
   independent writer acceptance.
5. Leave the current implementation order, fast per-slice target/focused
   selector/owning-CTest cadence, and scheduled full/fuzz/native gates
   unchanged. No new finding, top-level subplan, test registration, dependency,
   or fixture follows from this evidence-method refinement. Findings/subplans
   remain 130/73, and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

### Composed-checkpoint procedure

1. Select the needed peer question before installing anything. Use v0.6.4
   only for a tag-pinned release result; for a registry result, resolve and
   hash the exact crate archive; use a full immutable main commit only for
   branch behavior. Never combine outcomes across these channels.

   Cargo.lock entry, Rust toolchain, feature flags, OS/architecture, command,
   input/output hashes, and read/write direction. Record PASS, FAIL, IGNORED,
   and NOT_RUN separately, including missing-sample tests.
3. For any peer output, compare a locally authored expected manifest and
   source-to-output identity/owner disposition. A successful parse, same-codec
   reopen, drawing render, or Unknown fallback is not a preservation pass.
4. Keep private/customer samples out of this repository. Continue to use only
   existing eligible fixtures or controls created locally from scratch; do
   not import the peer’s private corpus or its release-specific thresholds.
5. Keep all peer work at the existing composed checkpoint. Fast implementation
   slices remain focused generated tests, strict touched-target builds,
   compatibility checks when applicable, and the owning CTest; no full-suite,
   peer, or native-app frequency change follows from this review.

## Deeper/broader ACadRust AcDs writer-control route and artifact freshness recheck (2026-10-18; research only)

The current [ACadRust `roundtrip.rs`](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/blob/main/tests/roundtrip.rs)
has a named `dwg_r2018_planar_body_solid_survives_roundtrip` test. It builds a
closed planar cube from eight literal vertices and six quad faces, converts it
to a SAT document, places it in an AC1032 `3DSOLID`, writes a DWG, then reads
the produced bytes through ACadRust's own `DwgReader`. The shared helper makes
the same-codec direction explicit: `DwgWriter::write_to_vec` feeds
`DwgReader::from_stream`. The test asserts the entity remains a `3DSOLID` and
that ACIS data remains present; it does not provide a second-parser result,
native CAD acceptance, or independent mass/topology comparison. The adjacent
`fake_sab_blob` helper fabricates ASM magic, repeated tag bytes, and a terminal
marker for association tests; those bytes are a synthetic transport control,
not a valid solid or SAB semantic witness. The generic [docs.rs DWG entity
writer source](https://docs.rs/acadrust/latest/src/acadrust/io/dwg/dwg_stream_writers/object_writer/entities.rs.html)
also shows the intended R2013+ branch: it gates `pending_has_ds_data` on an
AcDs section plus SAB-contributing data, writes the modeler entity's inline
empty form, then queues the SAB entry with that entity handle (and converts
SAT text when needed). This is a useful output-inspection checklist, not a
verified emitted-file result or normative wire rule; because the docs.rs
artifact identity is inconsistent, the code must be rechecked at an exact
source pin before any runtime comparison. The single-cube self-roundtrip also
cannot detect cross-body misassociation; the synthetic tag test is not a
substitute for two semantically distinct bodies.

The package identity remains unresolved: the [GitHub release list](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/releases)
shows v0.6.4, mutable `main`'s [Cargo manifest](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/blob/main/Cargo.toml)
declares 0.6.5, the [docs.rs crate index](https://docs.rs/crate/acadrust/latest)
labels latest as 0.6.4, and the [docs.rs primitive API](https://docs.rs/acadrust/latest/acadrust/entities/acis/primitives/index.html)
banner says 0.6.5; cached source pages also still surface 0.5.5. These generic
views do not prove the exact registry archive or immutable source snapshot.
Earlier 0.5.5 and 0.6.4 observations are preserved as time/page-specific
evidence, not used as a package pin. The exact immutable `main` commit
containing the test was not resolved, so do not attribute it to any release
or registry artifact solely from a version string.

### Implementation-ready use: conditional scratch producer, not a gate

1. Keep this route optional and at the existing composed checkpoint. First
   resolve the exact ACadRust commit and test-source hash; inspect the chosen
   writer path and confirm its actual output is AC1032 with the expected
   AcDs/Prototype1b association and SAB bytes. A test name/comment or own
   readback alone does not establish the outer carrier.
2. Check consumer readiness before spending time authoring: libdxfrw's current
   AC1032 reader is a pass-through stub. Prefer an AC1027 producer output only
   if the pinned ACadRust writer demonstrably emits that profile and the local
   reader can parse it; otherwise defer this probe until the AC1032 reader is
   qualified. Treat writer success plus local read failure as `NOT_APPLICABLE`
   to the SAB parser question, not as an ACIS defect.
3. If the route is usable, generate only in scratch from source literals, not
   by importing peer fixtures: use box A from (11,-7,3) to (14,-2,10), with
   expected volume 105, and box B from (-8,13,-4) to (-6,17,5), with expected
   volume 72, plus an ordinary following entity. The off-origin asymmetric
   bounds distinguish axis swaps, translation errors, unit changes, and
   association swaps. Record expected WCS bounds, volume, entity identities,
   and units in a separate source-authored manifest. Keep every DWG/SAB output
   outside Git and hash it before any reader sees it.
4. Capture the raw modeler entity handles, `has_ds_data`, section/schema/key
   and owner linkage, record offsets/lengths, payload signatures and hashes,
   exact associated SAB bytes, and the following-entity sentinel. Verify
   cursor/owner closure and each body association independently of ACadRust's
   reader. Then, if the admitted SAB profile permits, send the exact payload
   hash to an independent parser and compare analytic metrics; run native
   platform acceptance separately. Stop at the first unqualified stage and
   report each later stage `NOT_RUN` rather than inferring a pass.
5. Do not add ACadRust as a dependency, copy its code, import its synthetic
   marker vectors, make this an every-slice test, or promote a support claim.
   The candidate is a source-authored carrier probe only; it does not resolve
   DWG reader correctness, independent solid semantics, native acceptance, or
   J256/J260/J268/J284/J293/J295.

This correction adds no finding or top-level subplan, changes no queue or
validation frequency, and changes no local support claim. Counts remain 130
findings / 73 top-level subplans; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

## Deeper/broader R2000 DWG/DXF peer availability and false-independence screen (2026-10-17; research only)

### Scope and evidence boundary

This source-only pass screened a newly surfaced historical DWG implementation,
its named successor, and a JavaScript DXF parser against the already planned
peer routes. Repository descriptions establish candidate scope, not measured
runtime behavior. No source was cloned or built; no peer test, native CAD
application, or kernel was run; no drawing was downloaded; and no fixture or
dependency was added. The ODA v5.4.1 specification remains authoritative for
DWG byte layout.

### Findings and plan refinements

| Route | Source-backed scope and limits | Implementation-ready disposition |
|---|---|---|
| [`nextgis-borsch/lib_opencad`](https://github.com/nextgis-borsch/lib_opencad) | Its README describes an under-development OpenCAD library and says that only DWG R2000 is currently supported. This is a potentially independent C++ reader route for AC1015, but the README does not establish entity/object coverage, record diagnostics, owner closure, output support, runtime compatibility, or a release artifact. | Keep as an optional AC1015-only structural comparator candidate. Do not add it to the required peer quorum or install/build it during implementation slices. Admit it only when an active AC1015 issue cannot be answered by existing spec/local controls and an immutable source revision, license, reproducible build, and exact exercised path can be recorded. Compare only fields the API actually exposes; missing geometry, objects, or references must be counted as omissions, not normalized away. |
| [Original `sandyre/libopencad`](https://github.com/sandyre/libopencad) | The repository explicitly labels itself abandoned and directs users to `nextgis-borsch/lib_opencad`. Its README's old matrix describes only R15 basic geometry reading and lists omissions; those historical limitations do not automatically describe the successor. | Do not build or score the abandoned repository as a current comparator. Treat its old status/issues as historical leads only; verify any suspected inherited behavior against the successor's exact source before creating a local test. |
| [`codelibs/libdxfrw`](https://github.com/codelibs/libdxfrw) | Its project documentation identifies the code as libdxfrw and describes a 0.6.3 lineage with the same broad ASCII/binary DXF and R14–V2015 DWG-reader architecture. A separately maintained repository is not an independently developed parser merely by repository identity. | Use only for downstream-fork/source-delta discovery if a concrete porting question arises. Exclude it from independent-parser counts and from semantic qualification; compare changed code and revision explicitly rather than counting it as another DWG vote. |
| [`gdsestimating/dxf-parser`](https://github.com/gdsestimating/dxf-parser) | Its README accepts DXF file text and describes parsing into a JavaScript object model; it lists most 2D entities and explicitly excludes 3DSolids and less-common records. The package metadata identifies version 1.1.2, but no runtime or package/source binding was tested here. | At most an optional ASCII-DXF 2D model/projection diagnostic at the existing composed checkpoint. It cannot qualify binary DXF, DWG, object/owner graph closure, or ACIS/3D semantics. Since existing DXF comparators already cover more suitable paths, do not add a new gate, dependency, or routine execution. |

### Readiness and speed impact

The practical opportunity is narrow: an exact-pinned `lib_opencad` build could
add implementation diversity for one legacy AC1015 reader cell, while the
other newly screened routes either share libdxfrw lineage or are bounded to
ASCII 2D projection. To keep the work cheap and evidence useful:

1. Continue the current implementation queue without waiting for a peer build.
2. Reconsider `lib_opencad` only when a specific AC1015 decoding or writer
   interoperability question remains after the existing generated fast test
   and ODA-spec check.
3. For that one question, select a locally generated-from-scratch AC1015
   control or a fixture already tracked in LibreCAD/libdxfrw; keep generated
   outputs and logs scratch-only. Bind the source revision, build flags, file
   hash, version, operation, decoded/skipped/error counts, and field manifest.
4. Interpret a peer disagreement against the normative spec and an independent
   expected manifest. A parser's geometry projection is not evidence of raw
   record retention, object ownership, or complete DWG support.

No new finding or implementation subplan is warranted: these observations
change only the optional comparator inventory and admission threshold. The
existing fast-local / composed-peer / scheduled-broad-validation cadence stays
unchanged. No support claim is promoted; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

Sources: [`lib_opencad`](https://github.com/nextgis-borsch/lib_opencad),
[abandoned predecessor](https://github.com/sandyre/libopencad),
[`codelibs/libdxfrw`](https://github.com/codelibs/libdxfrw),
[`dxf-parser` README](https://github.com/gdsestimating/dxf-parser), and
[`dxf-parser` package metadata](https://github.com/gdsestimating/dxf-parser/blob/master/package.json).

## Deeper/broader current peer lineage and release-versus-source ACIS route review (2026-10-17; research only)

### Scope and method

This pass broadened the existing peer audit by checking primary repository
source, tagged release notes, and issue provenance for the ACIS/AcDs route.
It is a source/release review only: no peer binaries or packages were installed,
no native CAD application was run, and no external DWG/DXF was downloaded or
used. Mutable `master` source is treated as a discovery lead, not as a released
behavior claim. The ODA v5.4.1 document remains the normative authority for DWG
byte layout; peer implementations can inform differential tests but cannot
override it.

### Findings and plan refinements

| Evidence lane | What primary sources establish | What they do not establish | Readiness consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG report vs source vs release | Open [issue #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411) reports silent R2013+ AcDs/SAB loss for a stated LibreDWG build (`0.14.8593`, commit `8a1ae764`) on a described round trip and a confidential R2018 drawing. Current mutable [`decode_r2007.c`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode_r2007.c) contains an `AcDsPrototype_1b` section-reader path. The historical v0.11 section of LibreDWG's [`NEWS`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) describes incomplete AcDs handling and brute-force SAB extraction; 0.14.1 (2026-07-25) separately records a fix for dropping the last SAT block in 3DSOLID/REGION DXF export. | The issue is scoped to one reported build/input, and the mutable source path proves section discovery/read code exists—not complete object ownership, SAB association, valid SAT conversion, or successful modern DWG writing. A release note for the last-SAT-block fix is a distinct DXF behavior, not proof the AcDs route is closed. | At the existing composed peer checkpoint, record exact binary/release and source commit separately. Trace source entity → owner/section → payload association → converted/output entity. Test input/output direction and target AC version explicitly; report carrier preservation and semantic geometry separately. Do not let issue status, a function name, or a downstream DXF fix stand in for a successful route. |
| ACadSharp release chronology and old report | [v3.6.51](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/releases/tag/v3.6.51) lists ACIS payload reading for 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY, AcDs payload-area offset reading, and full Prototype1b section parsing. [v3.8.0](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/releases/tag/v3.8.0) lists only an `InternalsVisibleTo` change. Open [issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) describes omitted solids on DWG→DXF against v3.4.9, including block-contained solids. | The v3.4.9 issue is not a measured result for current source or current packages. The v3.6.51 notes establish implementation work, not complete write support, all-version correctness, nested ownership closure, or valid B-rep output. The v3.8.0 release note alone cannot be read as either a regression or a fix. | Any planned comparison must bind the exact package/tag/commit to each result and cover reader and writer directions independently. Retain separate cases for model-space and nested/block-owned solids; verify payload bytes and ownership, then geometry validity. Label older issue reports as historical until reproduced on a pinned current artifact. |
| Newly surfaced `cadcodec` lineage | [`compscientific/cadcodec`](https://github.com/compscientific/cadcodec) describes itself as forked from [`HakanSeven12/opencadcodec`](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/opencadcodec) and republishes broad ACadRust-family coverage claims. | It is not an independent codec implementation or a second independent parser vote merely because it has a separate repository, package name, or feature list. Its claims do not independently validate AcDs ownership or ACIS semantic output. | Do not add it as a separate peer lane, dependency, or evidence vote. If it is ever useful operationally, trace and pin its inherited code and dependency lineage first, then score only genuinely changed code. |

### Implementation-ready impact

These findings refine the already planned S8/PAR-07 peer evidence intake; they do
not add a new implementation item. For each future result, capture (1) exact
release/package and source commit, (2) reader/writer/converter and direction,
(3) source entity and owner/carrier path, (4) target DWG/DXF version, (5) raw
payload/handle comparisons, and (6) independent semantic result. Keep these
outcomes distinct: section is discoverable; payload is associated with the
correct entity; payload survives conversion; output is accepted by a consumer;
and a valid B-rep/expected geometry is independently established. A peer's own
round trip is useful structural evidence but not independent semantic evidence.

No source implementation, test, fixture, peer dependency, build, or runtime was
added or run in this review. No external drawing is proposed for the committed
test corpus. The plan's existing fast local tests and composed external/native
checkpoint remain the validation owners; this research does not add a per-slice
validation step. No finding/subplan count, implementation order, support claim,
or external disposition changes: the ledger remains 128 findings / 71 top-level
subplans, and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

## Deeper and broader INSERT scale-default and consumer-boundary review (2026-10-17; research only)

This pass traced one real 2D interoperability failure from its reported input
through LibreCAD's merged application fix, compared current peer INSERT scale
policies, and checked the local codec boundary. It identifies a test/readiness
gap, not a standards violation: the public DXF reference specifies defaults
for omitted scale groups but does not state that an explicit zero is invalid.
No peer revision was pinned or executable run; no drawing was fetched or added.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autodesk [INSERT DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-28FA4CFB-9D5E-4880-9F11-36C97578252F.htm) | Groups 41, 42, and 43 are each optional with default 1. This is authoritative for the omitted-value contract; it does not prescribe how a consumer must handle an explicitly serialized zero. | A missing group 43 is a valid unit-Z case and must not become zero in any `DRW_Insert`, adapter model, or emitted DXF. Do not cite this page as a nonzero-scale prohibition. |

### Implementation-ready refinement — existing INSERT and consumer owners only

1. **Fast codec control:** extend the existing DXF fixture/round-trip test owner
   with source-generated ASCII and Binary DXF INSERT records that omit 43 while
   retaining 41/42, plus a following LINE sentinel. Assert exact decoded
   X/Y/Z values, record alignment, and a second parse after export; with the
   current writer, require emitted group 43 to equal 1. Do not add a new
   fixture file, CTest, or peer runtime. Cover omitted 41/42 in the same
   helper only if that adds no new setup; Autodesk documents the same default
   for all three.
2. **Explicit-zero disposition:** test parser retention independently from
   ordinary valid-input compatibility. Keep the core codec's explicit value
   visible; do not silently rewrite it to 1 based on a peer policy. Before
   changing strict converter/writer admission, choose and document one
   operation-specific disposition: preserve raw zero for a low-level codec,
   but either repair with a diagnostic at a named consumer adapter (the
   current LibreCAD policy) or refuse strict conversion atomically. A zero
   scale is a singular transform and is not a positive consumer-acceptance
   control. Never turn this test into an unsupported normative validity rule.
3. **LibreCAD compatibility:** at its already-planned composed gate, start
   from a scratch-generated 2D DXF with omitted 43; verify import yields
   `zscale == 1`, save/reopen does not emit zero, and an asymmetric XY block
   retains expected placement. Separately exercise explicit zero only to
   record the adapter's chosen repair/refusal behavior. Pin the app commit,
   bundled libdxfrw revision, platform, output hash, and final model values.
4. **LibreCAD_3 and FreeCAD remain independent:** keep `lc3_compat_check` as a
   source/API compile check, not runtime or file-semantic proof. Its composed
   consumer gate must observe the actual callback/model scale and emitted DXF.
   For FreeCAD, pin Linux/Windows build, C++ versus legacy Python importer,
   parametric versus flattened mode, and manual scale preference; test the
   omitted-43 DXF directly and assert block geometry/coordinates, not merely
   that a document opened. If both importer routes are claimed, qualify them
   independently. Do not promote the old issue report to current platform
   qualification or ACIS/3D support.
5. **Speed and ordering:** implement the omission/default vector in the
   existing focused DXF test executable, build only its owning target, run its
   focused selector/CTest and `lc3_compat_check` if public or adapter-facing
   APIs change. Defer LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/FreeCAD runtime work to the already
   scheduled composed consumer gate; no per-slice full suite or native-app
   install is justified. Generate all controls in memory or under scratch and
   keep repository fixtures unchanged.

Correct 7BG accordingly: do not call scalar 79 an orthographic type or use it to infer option types; keep nonzero-79 and UCS-record 346 behavior unresolved pending a producer-authored witness, and fail closed on serialization rather than silently normalizing it. Treat each supported option as one ordered 71+complete XYZ tuple, with only documented type values 1–6; add malformed partial/duplicate-coordinate controls. Before the legacy/modern TABLE payload, the entity has insertion point, versioned scale, rotation in radians, extrusion and an ATTRIB-presence bit. R2000+ scale uses a two-bit selector with four valid encodings; R24 adds a different TABLECONTENT route and extra prefix fields. This review widens the S3.7c transform comparison beyond the previously
pinned ezdxf profile and screens a new ACIS-producing DXF route. The sources
expose an unresolved payload-shape conflict; they do not establish which
interpretation is correct for SAB 21800. ODA v5.4.1 remains authoritative for
DWG AcDs/container linkage and does not define SAB internals. No peer binary,
kernel, native CAD application, or downloaded drawing was run; no fixture,
dependency, test registration, support claim, or external-J disposition
changed.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ACadRust v0.6.4 [SatTransform](https://docs.rs/acadrust/0.6.4/acadrust/entities/acis/types/struct.SatTransform.html), [SatDocument placement](https://docs.rs/acadrust/0.6.4/acadrust/entities/acis/types/struct.SatDocument.html), and [release notes](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/releases/tag/v0.6.4) | Its API documents nine 3×3 values, three translations, a separate scale, then rotation/reflection/shear hints. It describes SAB Position triplets plus scale or a long-string carrying 13 numeric values. The release reports BricsCAD V20 validation of 18/20 generated files, but the reviewed summary has no independent expected-transform manifest. This is a peer profile, not ACIS authority. | Treat this as a conflicting implementation profile. Add raw characterization for 12-value literals, 13-value literals plus scale, triplets plus scalar, hints, malformed/truncated, and unknown token shapes. A bounded 13-value/triplet form is not automatically malformed just because current code accepts exactly 12. |
| Pinned ezdxf 1.4.4 profile and current [ACIS API docs](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) | The previously reviewed profile reads a 12-value literal and reconstructs a Matrix44 column. Public docs also limit supported ACIS entities and warn against arbitrary load/re-export. They do not resolve whether scale is folded into the 3×3, omitted, or tied to a different producer profile. | Keep the source observations version-/producer-scoped. Preserve exact tokens and build a raw field map before choosing one internal matrix model. |

These are useful transport/order controls, not proof of valid topology or correct placement. | Score AcDs linkage, payload survival, transform decoding, B-rep semantics and application acceptance separately. |

It explicitly marks DWG and curved surfaces beta pending AutoCAD acceptance. At one composed checkpoint only, pin the build, generate asymmetric analytic input from scratch, cross-read with exact ezdxf/ACadRust versions and compare independent expected geometry. Do not fetch/commit its corpus or count its ACadRust-based DWG writer as independent. |

A fallback mesh does not qualify completeness or exact solid semantics. |

### Implementation-ready S3.7c transform sequence

1. **Completed local fast slice: raw grammar census, no math.** Generated
   controls cover the 12-value candidate, bounded 13-value literal,
   triplet-plus-scalar tokens with a trailing literal hint, bounded
   non-literal tokens, empty/malformed/non-finite/14-value records, and
   absent/unresolved/wrong-type pointers. Exact raw tag/order, literal
   presence, candidate presence, and status are asserted independently;
   token budgets remain enforced. No external drawing fixture was added.
2. Keep the 12-number parse profile-specific and `ParsedUnapplied` only. The
   bounded 13-value, structured-triplet and bounded non-literal forms now use
   `UnsupportedVariant`, not `Invalid`; empty, truncated, malformed,
   non-finite and beyond-census values remain invalid. Numeric classification
   scans at most thirteen values in one bounded pass; no tokens are normalized
   and no hints are interpreted.
3. **Next local step:** Resolve the 12-versus-13 discrepancy with exact peer
   pins and, if available, one provenance-approved producer-authored
   asymmetric body. Record whether scale is separate, folded into matrix terms
   or absent. If unresolved, leave transforms uninterpreted and continue
   other locally actionable plan items; do not pause implementation for
   external access.
4. Only after that evidence, test translation, rotation, uniform/non-uniform scale,
   reflection, shear, composition, point/direction behavior, handedness,
   multiplication order and bounds against independent expected coordinates.
   A peer's own writer/reader roundtrip is not the expected answer.
5. Keep placement separate from $INSUNITS, model units, body-local coordinates
   and consumer scaling. Keep WCS false until the full convention and origin
   have independent expected-coordinate evidence.
6. If obj2cad proves useful, use it once at the composed checkpoint with a
   hash-pinned build and a from-scratch asymmetric model in a temporary
   directory. Separate DXF syntax, carrier bytes, each reader disposition and
   shape metrics. No fetched corpus, dependency, CI registration or per-slice
   run. If unavailable, record NOT_RUN and continue.
7. Keep fast validation to touched strict target, focused generated test,
   LibreCAD compatibility check, focused CTest and git diff --check. Update
   plan/receipt after each slice; full suites, fuzz/sanitizers and native or
   peer consumers remain scheduled phase gates.

## Deeper/broader Dime DXF route review (2026-10-16; research only)

This pass screened Coin3D's Dime to close a gap in the C++ DXF comparator
inventory: a distinct model-oriented parser with a small explicit 3D geometry
projection route. This is a public-source review only. Dime was not cloned,
built, or run; no external drawing was downloaded; and no test, fixture,
dependency, code, finding, or support claim changed.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Coin3D [Dime project](https://github.com/coin3d/dime), its [official documentation](https://www.coin3d.org/dime/), and the [Dime input API](https://www.coin3d.org/dime/classdimeInput.html) | Dime is a distinct C++ library under BSD-3-Clause for reading, constructing, manipulating, and writing a DXF model. Its official docs call the current documented library 0.9.1; they say internal testing covered DXF versions 10–14 and report customer use with AutoCAD 2000, not a tested modern-version matrix. The input API exposes `DXB` as its binary mode and reports version values 10/12/13/14. DXB is not the Binary DXF encoding supported by libdxfrw, so Dime is not a binary-DXF comparator. Its own tested-version statement takes precedence over its aspirational “past and future versions” wording. | Add Dime only as an optional legacy ASCII-DXF parser/model comparator when an exact source pin and a local generated AC1006/AC1009/AC1012/AC1014 control are available. Do not use it to infer modern DXF behavior or as a substitute for an independently generated producer file. Record source commit, compiler/build, parsed version, diagnostics, and the exact route. |
| Dime's [public class inventory](https://www.coin3d.org/dime/annotated.html), [`dimeEntity` geometry API](https://www.coin3d.org/dime/classdimeEntity.html), and [input details](https://www.coin3d.org/dime/classdimeInput.html) | The API includes classic explicit entities such as `3DFACE`, `SOLID`, `TRACE`, `POLYLINE`, and `INSERT`, plus generic unknown entity/object/section/table classes. `extractGeometry()` is documented as a convenience for viewers, returns indexed vertices/extrusion information for implementing subclasses, and relies on traversal state/UCS transforms being applied by the caller. The listed API does not expose a DWG reader or a typed ACIS `3DSOLID`/`REGION` shape kernel; generic unknown-record classes do not alone prove safe reference remapping or lossless document-graph round trips. | If Dime is used, compare only overlapping explicit geometry that its exact build actually extracts. Use source-authored controls for 3DFACE/legacy SOLID/TRACE, non-default extrusion/UCS, and a block/INSERT transform with an independently authored expected-coordinate manifest. Compare parsed records and transformed projection separately; do not treat a rendered mesh, unknown-record retention, or a successful Dime self-round-trip as graph or semantic parity. |
| Dime [`dimeOutput`](https://www.coin3d.org/dime/classdimeOutput.html) documentation | The class-level summary mentions DXF and DXB output, but the same API page says `setBinary()` currently supports only ASCII and that the DXF header writer is a no-op pending binary support. This is an API-doc ambiguity, not evidence of a usable binary-DXF writer. | Exclude Dime from binary-DXF writer/readback evidence and from DWG input/output claims. Do not build a writer comparator until a pinned source and a minimal generated output demonstrate the exact emitted encoding/version; no implementation or validation dependency is warranted now. |

### Implementation-ready comparator disposition

1. Keep Dime outside the implementation queue and fast test loop. Do not add
   it to CMake, CI, test registration, or the dependency graph. If the exact
   comparator is not already available at a later composed checkpoint, record
   `NOT_RUN` and continue local work.
2. If admitted, use only locally authored old-version ASCII DXF controls and
   compare literal source tags, parsed entity values, and the Dime geometry
   projection as three separate outputs. Test OCS/extrusion/INSERT transforms
   against a hand-computed manifest; omit any entity that the pinned Dime
   route does not decode/project rather than imputing success.
3. Label the route `LEGACY_DXF_PROJECTION_ONLY`: no DWG, modern-DXF, binary-DXF,
   opaque graph/reference, arbitrary 3D, or ACIS/B-rep claim. Do not add a
   finding or implementation subplan based solely on a comparator capability
   boundary.
4. This review refines existing DXF peer admission and explicit-geometry
   projection gates only. Totals remain125 findings / 71 top-level subplans;
   no support claim changes, and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. Receipt:
   [`deeper-broader-dime-dxf-route-review-2026-10-16.json`](docs/research/deeper-broader-dime-dxf-route-review-2026-10-16.json).

## Implementation progress — PAR-122 paper-space VIEWPORT projection (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

The DXF contract identifies group 68 as an on/off/active-stacking field and
group 69 as the viewport ID; it does not require those fields to be equal.
The current output adapter uses the peer-reported `68 == 69` convention only
for resolved DWG-origin paper-space layout viewports, with counters scoped to
the unique `BLOCK_RECORD.layoutHandle`. This is a candidate projection policy,
not a normative claim about every DWG producer. It never derives layout from
`entmode` or a name alone, leaves DXF-origin/model-space/ordinary-block values
unchanged, and does not mutate retained entities. A missing or ambiguous
paper-space owner fails preflight before destination publication.

The existing fixture target now creates ASCII and binary controls with two
layout owners and repeated viewport positions, explicit entity ownership plus
the implied current-space fallback, model space, an ordinary block, exact
68/69 readback, following LINE owner/coordinate checks, and unresolved-owner
sentinel/retry behavior. It also sets LAYOUT 331 to an ownerless viewport in
the current ENTITIES container and verifies that only DWG-origin data may infer
the unique `*PAPER_SPACE` owner; DXF-origin export rejects the same graph
without replacing a sentinel destination. Readback verifies that LAYOUT 331
still resolves to the emitted viewport. The source values are checked
unchanged after export.

A pre-existing local AC1021 sample now confirms the reader-side input that the
generated adapter control could not: two layouts are delivered, the active
`ISO A1` LAYOUT backlinks to `*Paper_Space`, its 331 handle resolves to an
ENTITIES VIEWPORT, and all three ENTITIES VIEWPORTs have `space=PaperSpace`
with `parentHandle=0`. ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.1–20.4.2 defines common entity and
handle framing, while §20.4.84 records the LAYOUT's associated paper-space
BLOCK_RECORD (330) and last-active VIEWPORT (331); this role chain—not
`entmode` or a name alone—is the safe adapter inference. The sample's reader
outcome remains partial-observed with 10 object parse failures and recorded
CRC/integrity observations. Its normal CLI conversion still fails at
unqualified FIELD/FIELDLIST serialization. A diagnostic in-memory probe that
omitted those plus adjacent unqualified TABLE/SORTENTSTABLE families advanced
past layout validation but stopped at the next dynamic-block serializer gate;
it did not produce a qualified DXF. Thus real parser layout delivery is
observed, but composed DWG→DXF correctness is not established.

Validation completed: `dwg2dxf` builds from the existing build tree;
`libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests` builds under strict warnings and its executable
passes; `ctest --test-dir /tmp/libdxfrw-viewport.tjymg5 -R
'^libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures$' --output-on-failure` passes 1/1; and
`lc3_compat_check` builds in that focused tree. The real AC1021 reader/adapter
trace was run as described above; it is diagnostic input, not a fixture. The
full suite, external converter and native CAD applications were not run for
this slice. No drawing fixture, new CTest registration, dependency or support
claim was added. No commit was made because the touched files also contain
pre-existing uncommitted work; staging those files wholesale would mix this
slice with unrelated changes.

Remaining PAR-122 work is real-file CLI composition after FIELD/FIELDLIST and
dynamic-block serializer gates, separate DWG viewport-count and handle-list
semantics, external reader comparison, and native/platform acceptance. The
peer's `68 == 69` remains a tested convention, not a DXF requirement. J256,
J260, J268, J284, J293 and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and cannot be promoted by these local controls.

**Latest deeper/broader format and runtime review (2026-10-15; baseline
`873eb76`):** the local ODA v5.4.1 text explicitly summarizes R2018 as
structurally identical to R2013, but its AcDs chapter still caveats its
historical knowledge and does not define ACIS/SAB semantics. It specifies the
`0x40000` direct-record/blob transition, bounded `blob01` page chains, and an
asymmetric search-index rule: a reader may ignore search data, but AutoCAD
ignores emitted objects without the required mapping. The committed S8.3
controls now cover direct sizes `0x3ffff` and `0x40000`, the first blob size
`0x40001`, one page at the exact `0xfffb0` cap, a two-page chain at cap+1, and
a two-page maximum-size chain in reverse physical order. Existing generated
cases also cover record-span bounds, a following-record sentinel, aliased page
references and unequal assembled totals; the latest focused slices add
missing-segment, duplicate-ordinal, wrong-start and wrong-reference-length
rejection plus atomic section-capture assertions. A one-byte-short Blob01
segment extent, an aligned segment too short for its page header, a descriptor
cut off at the next-record boundary, and a `UINT64_MAX` declared total all fail
without losing the suffix record. Under the current `HARD_MAX_ENTRIES` and
per-page cap, the maximum accumulated page bytes are far below `UINT64_MAX`,
so the checked aggregate addition cannot overflow for an admitted page count;
the source audit records this as a range invariant rather than fabricating an
unreachable arithmetic-overflow state.
Autodesk also documents inaccurate polyface header counts and noncanonical
child order as cases tolerant readers must accept. A source/test audit found
these controls already present: `runDxfPolyfaceCompletedPool` exercises zero
and stale-99 counts, interleaved and faces-first sequences, and forward face
references in ASCII/binary; `testClassicVertexPresenceBoundaries` checks
optional/partial face locations and canonical rewrite. No duplicate PFACE test
is needed; retain native application acceptance as a separate gate. The plan
tightens kernel/reader lineage qualification; no support,
finding count, fixture, dependency or J state changes. Receipt:
[`broader-acds-polyface-and-kernel-boundary-review-2026-10-15.json`](docs/research/broader-acds-polyface-and-kernel-boundary-review-2026-10-15.json).

## Deeper AcDs, polyface-reader, and geometry-kernel boundary review (2026-10-15; research only)

This pass re-read the local Open Design Specification v5.4.1 pages for R2018,
ACIS modeler objects and AcDs DataStorage, then compared its exact byte/count
requirements with the current parser tests and current Autodesk DXF, ezdxf,
Open Cascade, Ansys and CAD Exchanger documentation. It is static primary-source
and implementation-coverage research: no parser code/test was changed or run,
no external product was installed, and no support/qualification gate moved.

| Evidence | Finding and confidence boundary | Readiness refinement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ODA v5.4.1 [R2018 organization and DataStorage specification](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf), §§8, 20.4.41, 24; the local reference copy is Version 5.4.1, created 2018-02-15 | Chapter 8 says R2018 is structurally identical to R2013 and summarizes the known deltas (including three zero shorts at the end of AuxHeader and selected entity/object changes). That does **not** close the semantics of every 2018 AcDs/ACIS payload: §24 retains a December-2012 knowledge caveat, §20.4.41 says the modeler stream is not completely decrypted, and §24 explicitly puts detailed ACIS/SAB bytes outside its scope. | Keep the R2018 section/header deltas, AcDs container structure, entity linkage, and ACIS grammar as distinct evidence rows. Use ODA's explicit R2018 changes where stated; continue to pin actual AC1032 segment revision, page/index metadata and payload marker from real samples. Do not infer profile completeness from “structurally identical.” |
| ODA §24.2.2.2–24.2.2.4 and current `src/drw_datastorage.cpp`; `tests/graph_preservation_tests.cpp::testDataStorageBounds` | ODA says byte arrays up to `0x40000` are direct records; larger values use a blob reference to one or more `blob01` segments, each capped at `0xfffb0` bytes. Data-index rows identify the segment, local offset and schema index; the record supplies a handle; page metadata redundantly describes total length, page ordinal/count, start offset and byte size. The code has validation, page concatenation and a bounded-retention path, but current tests have no generated blob-reference/page-chain case. | Before ACDS writer expansion, generate direct records at `0x3ffff` and `0x40000`, a `0x40001` blob and a multi-page vector. Assert total/page lengths, page indexes and starts, segment/schema/record-handle joins, exact concatenated bytes, and the non-retained large-payload path. Add malformed missing/wrong/out-of-order page, length, offset, overflow and truncation cases; require no partial payload publication and preserve the following record. Keep buffers synthetic/in-memory; do not add DWG/DXF/SAB fixture files. |
| ODA §24.2.2.7–24.2.2.7.1 | The specification says schema-search data can be ignored while reading, but says AutoCAD ignores the entity if the required search-index object/handle mapping is not created. Read-acceptance and writer-acceptance therefore have different requirements. | Keep extraction allowed to consume the data index directly where proven, but do not declare a DWG AcDs writer interoperable until it emits and verifies the complete sorted/search-index-to-object-handle mapping. Mutate physical data-record order independently from sorted handle rank. |
| Autodesk [Polyface Meshes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-96B6288E-F413-46C0-968A-A314171C0AAE.htm) and [VERTEX](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-0741E831-599E-4CBF-91E1-8ADBCFD6556D.htm) references; current classic POLYLINE tests | Group 71/72 polyface header counts are not required to be accurate; readers should tolerate unusual coordinate/face child ordering. Writers should output coordinates first. Face group 71–74 values are signed 1-based indexes, negative values mark the edge starting at that corner invisible, zero terminates the face, and face records are limited to four corners. This plan records a comparative review of the current standalone libdxfrw
implementation against open-source DWG and DXF implementations, then turns
verified differences into bounded implementation slices. It is not a promise to
match every peer's feature list, and a peer's version matrix is not evidence
that libdxfrw supports that version or feature.

The existing [DWG/DXF 3D support plan](DWG_DXF_3D_SUPPORT_PLAN.md) remains the
source of truth for its detailed ACIS, DataStorage, and 3D-consumer work. This
plan adds cross-project semantic comparison, independent interoperability
validation, and the findings below; it must not fork or duplicate that plan's
implementation sequencing.

The broader round also inspects headers, symbol-table ownership, nested attribute
grammar, HATCH/MPOLYGON weights/colors/associations, handle width, token-byte
budgets, unknown tables, and comparator blind spots. Findings distinguish
executed reproductions, source-confirmed discrepancies, policy questions, and
qualification gaps. Only cases explicitly recorded as executed are test
evidence. Small local fixes can proceed alongside independent evidence; the
entire comparator matrix is not a prerequisite for a bounded fix.

The previous research added assigned binary-width inventory, typed graph identity
planning, MPOLYGON-specific grammar, locale/precision contracts, completed
NURBS validity, annotation index/enum meaning, fixture-admission readiness and
Windows/CLI consumer boundaries. These were not eleven newly implemented fixes:
the finding table distinguishes source-confirmed issues, executed bounded
reproductions, policy choices and platform evidence still needed.

## Upstream reconciliation and research controls

The [master revision](https://github.com/LibreCAD/libdxfrw/commit/d68fb1ed937ad2a74a54f6208277ec10a1b031b0)
was two commits beyond the old local remote-tracking ref and is now merged. [Merged #103](https://github.com/LibreCAD/libdxfrw/commit/8bdaf90b0b184d118d67ebae6699d1561abd8f37)
already fixes ATTRIB/ATTDEF continuation routing under the existing legacy
group-100 marker and changes filesystem opens/temporary basenames to the UTF-8
native-path contract. #104 clarifies standalone upstream ownership. Do not
reimplement those changes or mistake the old local failure for an upstream
omission. Canonical group 101, embedded writer chunking and downgrade policy
remain separate findings. Upstream's mutable status binding also changed;
the original baseline digest below is historical, not live-master qualification.

The reviewed merge and focused integration checks are recorded above. Retain
them; do not repeat that integration or revert upstream fixes. At the current
`8306162` research boundary, 7X.3/4/5, 7G.0/1, 7AB/7AF, 7P.2 and 7AD are
already committed. Pending isolated work is not silently integrated by this
documentation pass. A read-only live-master check again resolves `d68fb1e`;
a stale local remote-tracking ref must not decide whether a fix is absent.

### Broader peer and consumer refresh (2026-10-14; plan-only)

This read-only refresh expands the peer comparison across current DWG readers/
writers, DXF document libraries, and the actual FreeCAD DWG handoff. It updates
existing owners 7AQ, Slice8 and Slice9; it does not add a local defect finding
or treat another project's issue report as a libdxfrw reproduction.

| Source snapshot | New evidence from the source review | Limit / plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [LibreDWG `34f02f54b9aacb5708c1d3d2070efb3e4b2d8c43`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/commit/34f02f54b9aacb5708c1d3d2070efb3e4b2d8c43) | The repository's `NEWS` records a new R2004 DWG encoder in 0.14 and later security work around R2004/R2007 decompression bounds, SAT block-size arithmetic and non-finite writer inputs. The [README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) says DWG write reaches “until r2004”, while the [package description](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/libredwg.spec#L705-L714) still says the writer is good through R2000. | These are peer hardening leads and out-of-sync capability statements, not libdxfrw defects or a reliable version matrix. Keep checked-length/cumulative-work owners 7S.2/7S.3; add no parallel framework. For each executed peer route capture exact release/build flags, return code, output magic and `$ACADVER`, ordinary reopen, and field/graph result. ### Implementation-ready refinement

1. **Keep carrier work split by container and target.** The existing four
   lanes remain distinct: pre-2013 DXF inline SAT; R2013+ DXF ACDSDATA/SAB;
   pre-AC1027 DWG modeler stream; and AC1027+ DWG AcDs. Keep `group 70`, inner
   SAT/SAB version, target drawing version, history handle, and data-record
   owner handle as separate fields. The unmerged peer does not authorize
   normalization or carrier conversion between these lanes.
2. **Resolve the DXF R2004/R2007 boundary with a small matrix.** Using the
   existing generated DXF writer test target, emit equivalent 3DSOLID carrier
   controls at AC1018 and AC1021. Check exact subclass-marker and group-350
   presence, owner/history closure, ordered payload, ASCII and binary output,
   ordinary parser reopen, and unchanged following entity. Use the peer's
   TrueView report to select the candidate boundary only; final rule must be
   pinned to ODA/source evidence and a named consumer reopen. No new CTest or
   committed drawing is needed.
3. **Make SAT chunking an exact wire property.** In the same existing fast
   test, use a locally authored payload whose split candidates fall before
   and after a token boundary, exactly at the group-value limit, and adjacent
   to an escape. Assert byte-exact reconstruction of all groups 1/3 in order,
   legal chunk sizes, token-safe split policy if validated for the target,
   and no consumption of the next record. Keep chunk correctness separate
   from ACIS parse success and native solid semantics.
4. **Keep AcDs record association adversarial.** Retain the existing two-body
   vector with different handles/payloads and independently permute entity
   traversal, segment order, directory order, and sorted-handle rank. A
   round trip where all orders happen to match is insufficient; the PR's
   reported bug is precisely a directory-index/rank aliasing case.
5. **Freeze one FreeCAD consumer profile at the composed gate.** Record only
   the importer preferences that can affect the chosen manifest, but include
   backend, converter, entity filters, object-creation mode and unit scale.
   Assert imported objects by expected source/owner identity and coordinates;
   do not let automatic converter fallback, filtered layouts/anonymous blocks,
   or display joining silently shrink the denominator. Run platform variants
   as scheduled native qualifications, not per-slice tests.

No new PAR finding or top-level implementation subplan is justified: this
review sharpens the already-owned S8.4/S8.5 and FreeCAD gates. Totals remain
123 findings / 71 top-level subplans. No support claim was promoted; J256,
J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and
non-promoting. Full source notes and status limits:
