### 7BR — Implement the DXF GEODATA objectVersion-1 projection

**Scope:** PAR-121; `DRW_GeoData::parseCode`, the DXF `processGeoData` typed
callback, `dxfRW::writeGeoData`, and the public `DRW_GeoData` model. This is a
separate tagged-code grammar from the DWG CIVIL tail in 7BP. The local raw
companion is a same-DXF preservation path, not a typed semantic projection or
a substitute for DXF↔DWG conversion.

1. **Freeze both version axes and the full collision map.** Use the object's
   group90 `m_version` to select its v1/v2+ field meanings; track `$ACADVER`
   separately and only call a target/objectVersion combination producer-valid
   when an authoritative source says so. Autodesk's [2009 DXF reference,
   GEODATA pp.187–189](https://damassets.autodesk.net/content/dam/autodesk/www/developer-network/platform-technologies/autocad-dxf-archive/acad_dxf_2009.pdf)
   documents v1 group70 as a bits-control flag, not the modern coordinate-type
   enum. Keep its exact numeric value in a v1-specific field; do not infer or
   publish `m_coordinatesType` from it without stronger primary evidence. The
   same table documents v1: groups40–42 are latitude/longitude/elevation; 52
   is north angle; 43–46 hold legacy drawing scales/map units; 91 is drawing
   units; 92 is mesh point count; 96 and97–99 are face count/indices;
   source/target mesh pairs
   are12/22 and13/23. Group10 is the first DWG WCS point and group11 is a
   second WCS point reserved for future use; do not map v1 group11 to the v2
   coordinate-system reference point. CIVIC3D_DATA uses marker3/4 and fields292,14/24,15/25,
   93/94,293,16/26,17/27,54,140,95,141,294,142 and143. The 2009 table calls
   140 Grid azimuth, 95 Scale estimation method, and 141 Scale estimation
   method; later [2016](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2016/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-104FE0E2-4801-4AC8-B92C-1DDF5AC7AB64.htm)
   and [2020](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-104FE0E2-4801-4AC8-B92C-1DDF5AC7AB64.htm)
   tables call 141 User specified scale factor. Store v1 code141 separately
   without inferring its meaning. Also include v1 definition/datum/observation
   tags301–307. The searchable text of the 2009
   PDF prints `210, 20, 330` for up direction, while later official [2013 DXF
   reference](https://images.autodesk.com/adsk/files/autocad_2013_pdf_dxf_reference_enu.pdf)
   and [2016 GEODATA table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2016/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-104FE0E2-4801-4AC8-B92C-1DDF5AC7AB64.htm)
   use `210, 220, 230` and preserve330 as the host BLOCK_RECORD reference.
   Treat the searchable `20/330` tuple as an archival transcription anomaly,
   not an alternate data map. If a legacy producer witness later conflicts,
   preserve the raw sequence and resolve against the visual archived page or
   producer profile before adding another grammar. Keep common owner and
   coordinate-component occurrences disambiguated by ordered context. The
   [2020 Autodesk reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-104FE0E2-4801-4AC8-B92C-1DDF5AC7AB64.htm)
   documents the modern v2+ map: 40/41 are unit scales, 12/22 north vector,
   13/23 source mesh, 14/24 destination mesh, 93 mesh count, and 92 vertical
   units. The later Autodesk tables label object versions1/2 only; LibreDWG's
   current `src/dwg2.spec` says R2013 emits version3 with the version2 body.
   Treat v3's modern map as a peer-derived profile pending an eligible producer
   witness, not as independently producer-qualified by the official table.
   Add an ordered crosswalk to the subplan for all remaining legacy
   definition/datum/observation groups; do not treat repeated or
   context-sensitive codes as one global map.
2. **Use peer implementations as bounded evidence only.** ezdxf
   [1.4.4 `geodata.py`](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/1.4.4/src/ezdxf/entities/geodata.py)
   explicitly switches the legacy mesh group pairs but says v1 is not really
   supported, discards `north_direction` for v1, and warns its v1 exporter may
   corrupt DXF. LibreDWG's current [`src/dwg2.spec`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dwg2.spec)
   labels class_version1 as R2009, comments that v3 is the R2013 v2-body
   layout, and maps DXF code70 to `coord_type` in its v1 path. That conflicts
   with Autodesk's 2009 table describing code70 as a bits-control flag; retain
   an uninterpreted v1 flags field until an Autodesk/API source or eligible
   producer resolves the meaning. LibreDWG is peer evidence, not authority,
   and its DWG grammar/CIVIL tail must not be transplanted into DXF. No peer
   self-roundtrip closes the semantic gap.
3. **Add generated regression vectors before changing public semantics.** In
   the existing `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests`, generate ASCII and binary
   GEODATA objects with literal ordered tags, distinctive sentinels for every
   colliding group family, one mesh point/face, a populated CIVIC3D_DATA block,
   and a following LINE/object. Include copy/assignment/reset controls for
   the legacy model, plus deliberately out-of-marker Civil-only group sentinels
   after CIVIC3D_DATA_END. Use AC1021/group90=1 as the R2009-reference
   field-map vector, AC1024/group90=2 and AC1027/group90=3 as modern positive
   controls. ezdxf's R2010/AC1024 export minimum is its own writer policy, not
   authority to erase Autodesk's 2009 v1 table. Keep `$ACADVER` and group90
   separate in every assertion; exercise same-objectVersion/different-target
   cases only as diagnostic synthetic vectors unless an applicable Autodesk
   reference or eligible producer establishes validity. Assert typed values
   and independent raw tag order, no code bleed between coordinates/units/
   north/mesh/CIVIL fields, exact point/face association, suffix alignment,
   and unchanged raw companion bytes on the DXF-to-DXF path. Do not add
   downloaded or checked-in DWG/DXF fixtures, CTest registrations, or new
   dependencies.
4. **Model and parse v1 without aliasing v2 fields.** Add explicitly named
   legacy properties in a separate profile (`DRW_GeoDataLegacy` and nested
   CIVIC values), and include them in constructor/assignment/reset behavior.
   Preserve code70 as uninterpreted legacy flags and code141 as an uninterpreted
   scalar until the archival/later-reference conflict is resolved. Parse using
   `m_version` plus narrowly scoped sequence state where code meaning depends
   on CIVIL3D_DATA markers. Keep current v2/v3 values and behavior byte-for-byte
   stable. If a documented value cannot be represented, retain it in the raw
   companion and expose a truthful typed-loss disposition; do not put it into
   an unrelated modern field. No new pure virtual is allowed. Public layout
   changes require downstream rebuild and do not imply ABI compatibility.
5. **Make writing symmetric or fail closed.** `writeGeoData` must not emit the
   modern group map while writing group90=1. Either serialize the complete
   documented v1 grammar from represented values, preserving marker and field
   order, or reject the typed-v1 write before bytes/identity state are
   published until all required fields can be represented. Preserve current
   v2/v3 output. Test a corrected retry on the same writer and an unchanged
   destination after rejection. The generic raw-object re-emitter remains a
   separate path and must not silently duplicate a typed GEODATA object.
6. **Fast slices and self-unblocking.** Commit 7BR.1 generated map/collision
   tests, 7BR.2 model+reader, and 7BR.3 writer/rejection+retry separately; after
   each implementation commit update this plan's ledger and progress. For each
   slice run changed `-Werror` TUs plus `lc3_compat_check` and only the focused
   DXF fixture target. Run one composed ASCII/binary v1/v2/v3 check when the
   reader/writer pair settles; no full suite per field. Lack of native AutoCAD
   or a shareable Civil3D drawing is not a blocker for deterministic tagged
   vectors or source-local correction. Keep external interoperability claims
   pending and continue to the next ready slice.

### 7BQ — Declare dynamic DXF symbol-table capacities

**Scope:** PAR-120; group70 capacities for VPORT, LTYPE, LAYER, STYLE, VIEW,
UCS, APPID and DIMSTYLE. BLOCK_RECORD is an already-computed control. Preserve
the `DRW_Interface` callback contract, one-pass behavior, handle-allocation
order, table order and destination transactionality.

1. **Freeze the rule and table inventory.** Autodesk's [symbol-table group
   rules](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-5AB9300F-F0AC-4ADE-89EA-A9D1D152D8B8.htm)
   define group70 as the maximum capacity, not a row terminator: actual rows
   may be fewer, but readers must not use it as an iteration count. Autodesk's
   [group-code value types](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2019/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-2553CF98-44F6-4828-82DD-FE3BC7448113.htm)
   make group70 a 16-bit integer. Freeze source-derived row accounting:
   VPORT = callback rows plus implicit `*ACTIVE` when empty; LTYPE = three
   manually emitted mandatory rows plus callback-emitted noncanonical rows;
   LAYER = callback rows plus implicit `0` when absent; STYLE = callback rows
   plus implicit `Standard` when absent; VIEW/UCS = callback rows; APPID = one
   manually emitted `ACAD` plus callback-emitted non-ACAD rows; DIMSTYLE =
   callback rows plus implicit `Standard` when absent. The already-computed
   BLOCK_RECORD count (`2 + m_pendingBlockRecords.size()`) stays unchanged and
   is a regression control. Keep DIMSTYLE `AcDbDimStyleTable` group71 and
   table-level group340 handling out of the group70 fix until their exact
   ordered meaning is resolved. LibreDWG's object model calls the related
   control fields `num_morehandles` (DXF 71) and `morehandles` (repeated DXF
   340), a useful schema clue but not an ordered DXF table-header witness.
   Autodesk's published common-table contract establishes group70; its
   DIMSTYLE record contract assigns entry-level group71 to `DIMTOL` and
   entry-level group340 to the `DIMTXSTY` STYLE reference. Do not conflate
   these scopes or call table-level group71 an entry count without evidence.
2. **Count one emission pass, then backpatch.** The `DRW_Interface` table
   callbacks are void callback streams, not enumerable containers; never call
   them twice to count. Use one active-table counter incremented only when an
   entry record successfully commits, plus explicit increments for manual
   mandatory rows. Reset/scope it per table and include all implicit rows.
   The enclosing `writeTables()` already buffers through `DxfWriterRecordScope`
   (an `ostringstream`) under `RecordStateScope` and the whole-file output
   transaction. Prefer a small format-aware helper that backpatches the
   recorded group70 value in this private buffer after each table's one-pass
   callback completes; this avoids a second callback and a duplicate
   table-sized staging copy. Verify stream-position/restore behavior for ASCII,
   binary R12 and modern binary encodings. If backpatching cannot be made
   reliable without changing public API, use bounded per-table staging once,
   with identical version/encoding and allocation order. Fail transactionally
   if the exact emitted count exceeds the signed 16-bit representable range;
   do not write a guessed oversized capacity. Do not add a pure virtual,
   consumer count API, dependency or unchecked direct-stream writes.
3. **Add tiny generated ordered-tag vectors to the existing
   `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests` target.** Exercise each dynamic table with zero,
   one and multiple caller rows where applicable, implicit/explicit defaults,
   mandatory LTYPE/ACAD entries, canonical LTYPE suppression, and a late
   invalid row. Assert exact emitted row inventory independently from the
   header, `group70 == rows` under the selected exact-count writer policy,
   duplicate-default behavior, one callback pass,
   preserved handles/order, `ENDTAB` and next-table sentinels, and unchanged
   destination/allocator on failure. Keep BLOCK_RECORD count as a positive
   control. Cover R12 and R2000+ plus ASCII and binary formats (all four
   profile combinations across the generated set); assert binary short width
   and reject 32768 through the tiny count-helper boundary test rather than
   constructing tens of thousands of drawing records. Avoid writer→reader
   agreement as the only oracle. Do not add fixture drawings or CTest entries.
4. **Fast, staged implementation and self-update.** Split into three commits:
   `7BQ.1` adds the internal count/backpatch helper and exercises VIEW/UCS plus
   one implicit-row table; `7BQ.2` wires successful-row and mandatory/fallback
   accounting for the full dynamic table matrix; `7BQ.3` adds the composed
   ASCII/binary, R12/modern matrix, late-failure transaction check and
   BLOCK_RECORD control. For each commit, build only the changed library/test
   TUs with warnings-as-errors, run the corresponding writer vectors and
   `lc3_compat_check`, update the ledger and show progress. After `7BQ.3`, run
   one composed `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests` and relevant hardening checkpoint;
   do not run full suites after each field/table. After every committed slice,
   refresh this plan's status, evidence, remaining blockers and next ready
   slice. If strict AutoCAD output is unavailable, record it as an external
   qualification limit and continue the local correction; do not block other
   implementation or promote strict-application compatibility. Add no
   external/peer drawing payload, generated fixture file, dependency or CTest.
5. **7BQ.4 / Large-count qualification (composed, not per-slice).** The exact
   group70 policy is locally verified only through 32767; 32768 currently
   fails transactionally. Keep that behavior as the safe default. Before
   changing it, add one generated temporary/scratch BLOCK_RECORD case above
   the signed-16-bit boundary and compare a candidate group70=0 header while
   retaining every actual row. Verify output row count independently, strict
   readback, next-table/EOF alignment, and rollback on candidate failure. If a
   pinned AutoCAD/ODA/independent-reader run is available, record exact build,
   actual AC code, audit/repair output, and handle-joined rows; otherwise leave
   the overflow policy `EXTERNAL_ACCEPTANCE_PENDING`. Do not add the peer's
   large production drawing or run this scale case after each implementation
   slice.
6. **Large-document performance discipline.** For a source-confirmed hot path,
   classify the loop/index complexity before editing. Prefer a stable key
   index constructed once per phase and reused over repeated full-document
   scans, while preserving output order and duplicate/error semantics. Add a
   bounded synthetic scale smoke or benchmark only after the relevant path
   composes; no wall-clock threshold or performance sweep belongs in the
   default per-slice gate. Keep the touched strict build, owning CTest,
   compatibility compile where needed, and diff check as the fast loop.
7. **7BQ.5 / DIMSTYLE table-control subclass (reported-producer evidence
   recorded; bounded AC1024 candidate locally implemented, external acceptance
   pending).** Resolve the `AcDbDimStyleTable` subclass
   fields independently from PAR-120's completed group70 capacity work.
   The AC1024 candidate now stages only its DIMSTYLE rows once, captures each
   successfully committed group105 handle in order, then emits table-subclass
   group71 as the row count and a group340 for each captured handle before
   publishing those staged rows. AC1015/AC1018/AC1021/AC1027+ retain their
   previous table-subclass output. `writeDimstyle()` still separately emits
   per-record fields, where group71 is `DIMTOL` and group340 is `DIMTXSTY`.

   - Freeze a three-scope tag table before implementation: common
     `AcDbSymbolTable` header group70 (maximum entries); `AcDbDimStyleTable`
     subclass group71 / possible repeated group340 control handles; and
     `AcDbDimStyleTableRecord` group71 / group340 values. LibreDWG's
     `DIMSTYLE_CONTROL` model names group71 `num_morehandles` and group340
     `morehandles`, but that reverse-engineered object model alone does not
     prove the exact DXF ordering, requiredness, or target-handle inventory.
     ACadSharp #1253 calls the table-header 71 an entry count and reports one
     340 per style; retain that as a competing peer observation, not the
     expected value.
   - Inspect the local parse/write scopes and emit generated ASCII/binary
     AC1018/AC1021 controls with zero, one and multiple DIMSTYLE records.
     Assert literal ordered tag scopes and each record's allocated 105 handle,
     71 `DIMTOL`, and 340 style reference separately from the table subclass.
     Do not use self-readback alone. Prefer an existing repository sample with
     documented provenance if one contains the relevant sequence; do not
     download or commit a peer drawing.
   - **Evidence update (2026-10-17):** Autodesk's 2012 DXF reference documents
     the common header and DIMSTYLE *record* fields but has no
     `AcDbDimStyleTable` serialization entry; ObjectARX's class page only says
     this class derives from `AcDbSymbolTable`. The ACadSharp #1253 author
     reports a direct AutoCAD DXFOUT 2010/AC1024 sequence of subclass marker,
     group71=`4`, and four group340 handles, plus AutoCAD 2027 acceptance of
     three post-fix files. This is an actual-producer observation as reported,
     but the DXF artifact/hash is absent and the comparison was conducted in a
     third-party issue. Treat it as an implementation hypothesis with stronger
     provenance than a peer schema—not as a published normative rule or a
     local pass.
   - **Implementation status (2026-10-17):** the local AC1024 candidate is
     implemented in `writeTables()` / `writeDimstyle()` without adding a public
     API, virtual, class data member, or CTest. The generated census covers
     AC1018/AC1021 controls and AC1024 ASCII/binary with zero/one/multiple
     caller rows, implicit and explicit `Standard`, exact record order,
     subclass group71 cardinality, group340-to-group105 identity, unchanged
     record-level 71/340 scopes, following `BLOCK_RECORD` framing, and a late
     invalid row followed by same-writer retry. The local low-level tag scan is
     not an independent producer/consumer oracle.
   - **Remaining qualification:** keep AC1015/AC1018/AC1021 and AC1027/1032 on
     their prior table-subclass behavior absent matching producer evidence or a
     primary versioned contract. The reported AutoCAD observation still lacks
     its raw artifact/hash; run one pinned AC1024 AutoCAD/ODA strict open/save
     at the composed checkpoint and retain output/hash. Until then label
     strict/native acceptance `EXTERNAL_ACCEPTANCE_PENDING`, not failed or
     passed. Continue other implementation-ready slices without waiting for
     this optional external qualification.

### 7BS — Preserve pre-R13 repeated-entity and external-resource semantics

**Scope:** this section coordinates two different legacy reader routes without
merging their formats or findings. PAR-123 / 7BS.1 and 7BS.2 are limited to
`AC1.40` / AutoCAD Release 1.4; PAR-143 / 7BS.3 is limited to the local
`AC1006`/`AC1009` pre-R13 reader. Both are distinct from `AC1014` / Release 14
and from R13+ object streams. ODA v5.4.1 does not define the pre-R13 record
grammar; do not transfer semantics between these magic/version routes based
only on similar record names, a peer issue, or inferred field names.

1. **Close false-success immediately; freeze semantics in parallel.** The
   current independent evidence is structural only: LibreDWG's mutable
   `dwg2.spec` defines an empty REPEAT marker and ENDREP's row/column counts
   and spacings; the separate BSD-2 Kaitai schema models the same fields and
   LOAD string but leaves its REPEAT-begin decoder case commented out. The
   official Autodesk INSERT reference documents modern block-array fields,
   not a mapping from old REPEAT. No authoritative R1.40 behavior source was
   found in this pass. Therefore the first code slice must not wait for a
   specification: when a repeat group is encountered, return an explicit
   incomplete/unsupported-conversion outcome and use the existing atomic
   publication gate so output is not presented as complete. Preserve the
   supported non-repeat path. Also reject an independently encountered
   `T_ENDREP` after its existing fixed-width body-bound check; do not consume
   and discard the unresolved row/column metadata as success. This is a
   conservative unsupported outcome, not a claim that a particular historical
   producer's standalone sequence is malformed. In parallel, continue a bounded search for an
   old-format manual or native producer witness that resolves repeat scope,
   seed inclusion, row/column order, spacing axes, accepted counts/nesting,
   and malformed/missing ENDREP handling. LibreDWG #1354 remains a concrete
   selection lead, not normative authority. Keep LOAD→SHAPE external
   file/glyph identity separate.
2. **Add source-authored, in-memory reader vectors** to the existing
   `libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix` target. Start with a minimal `AC1.40` stream
   containing one repeatable primitive, `REPEAT`, a one-record seed body,
   `ENDREP` with distinguishable rows/columns/spacings, and a following
   unrelated entity. Assert expected instance coordinates/order and that the
   sentinel survives. Add adjacent arrays, counts at the agreed boundary,
   missing/early terminators, unsupported nested/compound members, arithmetic
   overflow, and budget-exhaustion cases only after step 1 freezes their
   expected dispositions. The immediate generated guards also cover a
   standalone ENDREP with distinct counts/spacings and a following POINT.
   Assert no partially published repeat group on a
   malformed unit and same-reader reuse after failure.
3. **Choose an explicit output representation only after the contract passes.**
   Prefer the simplest exact supported 2D representation admitted by the
   legacy contract: transformed typed instances, or one anonymous block plus
   an arrayed INSERT only if existing identity/ownership callbacks can
   represent it without changing LibreCAD or LibreCAD_3 contracts. The
   presence of DXF INSERT codes 70/71/44/45 is not evidence that legacy REPEAT
   maps to that entity. If semantics remain unavailable, retain the explicit
   unsupported outcome from step 1; do not stall unrelated implementation or
   silently emit only the seed. Do not add a pure virtual. Test actual
   `dwg2dxf` output in an existing generated adapter/CLI owner only after the
   reader semantics pass.
4. **Bound expansion and publication.** Compute `rows × columns` with checked
   wide arithmetic, reserve work/retention from the existing resource-budget
   path before expanding, and enforce the existing documented per-operation
   ceiling. Parse/stage the repeated unit before any child callback so a
   truncated or malformed group cannot leak a partial array. The sentinel and
   destination-preservation controls must prove framing and failure behavior;
   do not add a bespoke global budget framework.
5. **Keep the fast loop local.** Build changed `-Werror` targets, run only the
   owning reader-matrix test and any touched adapter test, then run
   `lc3_compat_check` only if public interface/adapter code changed and
   `git diff --check`. Do not run native CAD, a full suite, or a corpus sweep
   for each slice. After one composed implementation slice, run one CLI output
   check with exact source/output version and per-instance identity/coordinate
   inventory; defer old-native producer acceptance to a single explicit
   qualification checkpoint. Use no downloaded/committed DWG/DXF fixture,
   dependency, or new CTest registration. Update the ledger and show the
   committed slice and next ready task before continuing.

**Self-unblocking rule:** if the bounded old-format source search does not
produce a semantic witness, complete and report the fail-closed conversion
slice as a useful interim result, then continue with other ready work. Keep
array expansion explicitly deferred; revisit only when a producer/manual
witness or independently consumed control resolves the contract. The
fail-closed result does not count as successful REPEAT support.

<a id="par-143-ac1006-ac1009-repeat-endrep-load"></a>

### 7BS.3 — Fail closed on AC1006/AC1009 REPEAT, ENDREP, and LOAD

**Scope:** PAR-143, only the current `dwgReaderR11` path for AC1006/R10 and
AC1009/R11-R12. Do not use the AC1.40 implementation or controls as a
substitute: shared type names are not proof of a shared record grammar.

The local source audit found that `dwgReaderR11::readEntityR11()` decodes the
bounded record envelope and then treats `R11_REPEAT`, `R11_ENDREP`, and
`R11_LOAD` as successful no-ops. The source comment itself says REPEAT/ENDREP
bracket a repeated group and that multiplicity is not expanded; the read can
therefore succeed after delivering only the seed once. LOAD's body is likewise
consumed without retaining its file/resource directive. This is a
source-confirmed false-success/loss route, but the expected legacy semantics
and version applicability remain unqualified.

The current [LibreDWG #1354 report](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1354)
shows an R1.4/R2.10 `REPEAT` + entity + `ENDREP` shape whose conversion drops
array instances and emits unknown names as DXF entities. It explicitly does
not settle seed inclusion, order/axes, or a correct lowering. LibreDWG
[#1386](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1386) separately reports
pre-R13 writer structure/offset gaps, illustrating that legacy route success
is layered and direction-specific; it is not evidence about this reader.
ODA v5.4.1 §§20.4.9–20.4.10 (pp.112–114) documents INSERT/MINSERT fields in
R13+ formats, not a mapping from R10/R11 REPEAT. Autodesk's current DXF
group-code guidance likewise cannot fill that historical gap. Treat these
sources as bounded discovery evidence, not a normative AC1006/AC1009 contract.

**Implementation progress (2026-10-21; local and uncommitted):** the reader
now fails after restoring the bounded record cursor and records a marker-specific
`unsupported-r11-*` validation diagnostic. The DWG adapter prints that reason
for all three AC1006/AC1009 markers. Generated in-memory controls cover each
marker on both versions, prove a following block/end-block sentinel is not
delivered, and retry a marker-free sentinel on the same reader. The focused
selector, owning CTest, and six scratch-only CLI refusal controls pass; the CLI
controls verify missing outputs remain missing and an existing destination is
unchanged. No repository DWG/DXF fixture was added. This closes the immediate
false-success guard, not the unresolved semantic contract.

1. **Close false success before attempting semantic lowering.** After the
   existing fixed-size/section bounds checks, encountering any of these
   marker/resource record types must produce a specific unsupported/incomplete
   diagnostic and a failing read result. Do not skip the marker and continue as
   if the drawing were complete; do not emit literal REPEAT/ENDREP/LOAD DXF
   entity names; do not guess an MINSERT or resource-resolution mapping. Keep
   the ordinary non-marker reader path unchanged. Preserve earlier callbacks
   only under the existing failed-read contract, and verify the converter
   does not publish a DXF after the failed read.
2. **Generated fast controls — implemented locally.** The existing
   `libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix` owner covers AC1006 and AC1009 separately and
   exercises every marker with the current bounded envelope/common header, a
   following supported block/end-block sentinel, exact diagnostic code/offset,
   failed complete-read status, and marker-free sentinel retry on the same
   reader. The existing adapter reports the diagnostic; the existing CLI
   contract test now generates six scratch-only inputs and checks nonzero
   refusal, no output creation, preservation of an existing destination, and
   source immutability. No DWG/DXF sample or CTest registration was added. The
   controls validate fail-closed behavior, not normative marker legality or
   complete REPEAT/LOAD semantics.
3. **Research semantics only in parallel and keep the gate bounded.** Seek an
   R10/R11 producer/manual or independently consumed, version-identified
   control that settles whether each marker is legal in each version; REPEAT
   scope and nesting; seed inclusion; row/column order and axes; count limits;
   malformed/missing ENDREP behavior; and LOAD string/resource identity and
   lookup rules. A peer's issue, schema, or parser implementation alone is not
   enough to implement array expansion or open external resources. If no
   stronger source is available, retain the fail-closed behavior and continue
   other local work.
4. **Only after the contract is established**, model repeated instances or a
   resource-backed shape through an existing representable consumer contract.
   Use checked arithmetic, bounded expansion/retention, and complete-group
   staging before callbacks. Assert source identity, intended instances,
   transforms, order, and the following sentinel; then validate the composed
   CLI output with strict reparse and destination-preservation controls. Never
   infer legacy equivalence from ODA's modern MINSERT fields.
5. **Fast validation cadence:** build the touched `-Werror` targets; run the
   focused reader-matrix selector and its existing CTest; run
   `lc3_compat_check` only if a public interface/adapter changes; run the
   focused generated CLI publication control; and run scoped `git diff --check`.
   These checks pass for the guard slice. Do not run the full suite or
   peer/native matrix for each slice. Refresh the finding and show the committed
   slice plus the next ready task after each commit; if this working tree cannot
   be committed, report that state and continue without broadening the git
   operation.

**Self-unblocking rule:** no semantic witness is a reason to keep waiting or
to guess. Finish the local fail-closed guard and its fast generated controls,
then resume the next locally actionable implementation item. Keep this
AC1006/AC1009 result separate from AC1.40 PAR-123 and from all R13+ support
claims. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

### 7BS.2 — Fail closed on unresolved pre-R2.0b LOAD/SHAPE resources

**Scope:** PAR-123, limited to AC1.40 / Release 1.4 `T_LOAD` and `T_SHAPE`
records. The local reader previously consumed and discarded the LOAD filename
and emitted SHAPE using only its numeric glyph index. The available structural
schemas do not establish SHX search paths, string encoding/normalization,
shape-index-to-glyph mapping, resource-version rules, geometry, or transforms.
Do not infer that `T_SHAPE`'s numeric index is a glyph identity, and do not
auto-open arbitrary external files as part of a drawing read.

1. **Prevent false success now:** at `T_LOAD` and `T_SHAPE`, return the
   existing entity-read failure with distinct `unsupported-legacy-load` and
   `unsupported-legacy-shape` diagnostics and source offsets. For SHAPE, first
   retain the existing fixed-body bounds check. Keep streams without these
   records unchanged. These refusals do not promise rollback of callbacks
   made before the marker; the operation must remain visibly incomplete and
   must not be described as a complete DXF conversion.
2. **Use generated fast controls only:** extend the existing
   `libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix` target with source-authored in-memory LOAD and
   SHAPE records followed by geometry sentinels. Assert the distinct failure
   codes/offsets, no post-marker callback, and same-reader retry on a stream
   without either record. Do not add an external drawing, fixture, dependency,
   or CTest registration. Both fail-closed slices are implemented and
   recorded below.
3. **Resolve semantics before adding resource loading:** require an old-format
   producer/manual witness for string framing and encoding, base/search-path
   policy, resource identity, missing-resource behavior, glyph index mapping,
   shape coordinate basis, scale/rotation, and supported primitive/profile
   subset. Any future resolver must be opt-in or constrained to an explicit
   caller-supplied resource root, reject path traversal, and report missing or
   ambiguous identities rather than silently drawing a substitute.
4. **Choose a loss-explicit 2D representation only after the contract is
   frozen.** Stage the complete supported SHAPE before callbacks, apply the
   proven insertion transform, and preserve layer/style semantics; otherwise
   retain the explicit unsupported outcome. Test source identity, resolved
   resource identity, glyph index, expanded geometry, following record, and
   destination-preservation behavior in the existing fast owners.
5. Keep this route separate from REPEAT's 7BS semantics and from modern DXF
   SHAPE/SHX support. Run only the strict touched target, owning CTest,
   compatibility compile when public/adapter code changes, and `git diff
   --check`; defer native application qualification to a composed checkpoint.
   No support claim or external-J disposition follows from refusal tests.

### 7BT — Make DXF top-level framing explicit (PAR-129)

**Scope:** the outer DXF stream only: comments, `SECTION`, section name,
`ENDSEC`, and `EOF`. Do not change record parsing inside an admitted section.
Autodesk documents `TABLE`/`ENDTAB` as table records within the `TABLES`
section. ACadSharp issue #1128 reports older NC/CAM/plotting files that omit
that wrapper, but no producer artifact was available here; do not silently
reinterpret that report as a new normative grammar.

1. **7BT.1 — Reject silent top-level loss (implemented, focused pass):**
   `processDxf()` now returns `BAD_READ_SECTION` for an unexpected top-level
   record, including a bare `TABLE`, an unexpected group-2 section name, or an
   `ENDSEC` before a section name. Preserve the established pre-section 999
   comment behavior, ordinary `SECTION`/section-name dispatch, unknown-section
   raw preservation, and `EOF` handling. This is an explicit malformed-input
   refusal, not a compatibility-recovery implementation.
2. Generated controls in the existing `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests` target
   cover (a) a minimal R12 `ENTITIES` file with no `TABLES` section, (b) the
   standard `TABLES`/`LAYER`/`ENDTAB` path, and (c) an out-of-section `TABLE`,
   detached group-2 section name, and unmatched `ENDSEC`, in both ASCII and
   Binary DXF. Assert the minimal LINE callback, table and later LINE callbacks
   on the standard path, and `BAD_READ_SECTION` with no later entity callback
   on each malformed path. Absence of a `TABLES` section alone is not an
   error; the malformed condition is a table/control record outside section
   framing. Reuse the existing target and CTest; no persistent or externally
   sourced drawing fixture is needed.
3. **Future recovery is separately gated:** only add it for a named consumer
   workflow after obtaining and hashing a provenance-bound producer file,
   confirming its record boundaries and table grammar, and choosing an
   explicit opt-in compatibility policy. Recovery must remain bounded, report
   a warning/loss observation, and preserve later-section alignment. Do not
   auto-wrap all orphan records or let successful recovery promote general DXF
   conformance.
4. Fast validation: strict-build `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests`, run
   `--top-level-section-framing`, run only the owning
   `libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures` CTest, build `lc3_compat_check` when public adapter
   surfaces change, and run scoped `git diff --check`. Leave broader format
   suites and external/native CAD checks at the existing composed checkpoint.

**7BT.1 implementation status (2026-10-17):** source-generated ASCII/Binary
minimal R12-without-TABLES, standard, and malformed controls pass. The strict
fixture target and `lc3_compat_check` build, and the existing DXF-fixtures
CTest passes (1/1). The generated regression first reproduced the old
behavior: the orphan table was ignored, the later LINE callback ran, and the
reader returned success. No real legacy sample, external parser, native CAD
application, or recovery mode was exercised. Header/table callbacks before a
later parse error are not rolled back by this parser API; whole-file
publication remains the CLI transaction's responsibility. No DWG behavior,
support claim, or external-J status changes.

## Validation and implementation operating rules

- **Fast-first tests:** run the smallest relevant unit/CTest targets after each
  implementation slice. Run broad DWG/DXF suites at integration gates and
  release qualification, not after every small edit.
- **Composed repeat check:** changed conversion routes get two successful
  conversions and a third read, with raw and before-audit semantic projections.
  Compare intended geometry/metadata/presence/graph roles, not reminted handles
  or whole-file byte identity. Use a few generated sentinels; do not multiply
  the whole corpus. Raw malformed-tag rejection and valid full-graph source
  qualification are different gates.
- **Operation-state scope:** destination publication, one-record/compound
  rollback and whole-operation caller-memory rollback are separate contracts.
  Failure/retry tests must check successful prefixes as well as unwritten
  suffixes; clearing maps or stopping later callbacks alone cannot qualify
  full retry of a mutated caller model. Never retain borrowed stack-local
  consumer records after individual methods return without an explicit
  lifetime-constrained contract. Global debug synchronization is separately
  scoped; it does not qualify general concurrent parse/write behavior.
- **Thin oracle first:** install/build each pinned comparator once and cache
  generated seed inputs/projections by generator, input, implementation,
  comparator, and config digest. Recompute only affected scopes. Never cache
  an audit-repaired result under the original file's identity or reuse an
  output after a relevant digest change.
- **Cache versus qualification:** impact-scoped reuse can accelerate diagnostic
  tests, but a receipt bound to the whole implementation digest is invalidated
  by any selected-input change. Rerun/refreeze all required gates for that new
  binding at the qualification checkpoint; do not relabel cached old results
  as current. Scoped reuse is permitted only where the existing validator
  explicitly binds and accepts that exact scope.
- **Use existing lanes:** extend the receipt-bound target/standalone adapters,
  `tests/hardening_tests.cpp`, and `LIBDXFRW_BUILD_LONG_FUZZ`; do not add a
  duplicate generic differential or fuzz framework. Preserve the current
  focused/final-broad/scheduled-fuzz cadence in `.github/workflows/build.yml`.
- **Report coverage honestly:** for every independent DWG corpus run, capture
  counts of decoded, opaque-preserved, skipped, errored, and callback-published
  records by file/version/family where available. Keep denominators explicit;
  a high aggregate decode percentage can hide one critical family that always
  fails. Coverage counts are diagnostic and never alone promote support.
- **Preserve recovery semantics:** a bad record can remain a reported skip when
  a validated boundary permits safe continuation. Structural corruption that
  prevents safe resynchronization remains a stage failure. Qualification must
  account for both outcomes and warn-only integrity observations; preserve
  first-failure diagnostics and bounded secondary evidence.
- **Research for speed:** before coding, inspect existing parser/writer paths,
  test helpers, peer fixtures/generators, and specification sections. Reuse a
  peer as a comparator/tool where appropriate; do not port its architecture or
  feature list wholesale.
- **Self-update/self-unblock:** after each implemented item, update this plan
  with completion evidence and the next actionable item. When one oracle,
  platform, sample, or license is unavailable, record the limitation and move
  to independent work that can proceed (spec vectors, generated local vectors,
  another reader, focused code/tests). External-only qualification can remain
  deferred, but must never stop unrelated implementation work or promote a
  support claim.
- **Progress after commits:** after each implementation slice is committed,
  report the commit, concise test result, support/evidence impact, and the next
  unblocked slice. Do not imply an entire version is supported from a narrow
  feature fix.
- **Fixture provenance:** do not commit downloaded/customer DWG or DXF testing
  files unless the exact fixture is already tracked in LibreCAD or libdxfrw
  and its reuse is permitted. New binary fixtures must be generated locally
  from scratch with a committed reproducible generator and provenance. Keep
  untracked local samples, derived drawings, logs, and proprietary examples out
  of commits; preserve their existing state.
- **2D compatibility:** maintain LibreCAD and LibreCAD_3 source callback
  compatibility, keep added callbacks non-pure, and test legacy 2D projection
  behavior whenever public callback semantics change. Rebuild affected
  consumers; compile-only mirror checks do not establish binary ABI stability.
- **FreeCAD handoff:** retain the upstream `[dwg2dxf, input, "-o", output]`
  invocation, exact source `$ACADVER`, atomic publication/failure cleanup,
  paths with spaces, Unicode/native Windows argv, installed executable
  discovery and shared-library installation behavior. Reuse existing
  `dwg2dxf_freecad_cli_compat`, installed-CLI and 3D CLI/native probes; keep
  Linux/Windows native application qualification in the existing 3D plan.
  The [pinned importer](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/ca1bae1c7384c1a63a50a1d817f013060a852191/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py#L292)
  judges converter success by output existence; it does not supply a 2D/3D
  projection switch. Keep converter `ext=false` distinct from LibreCAD's
  `ext=true`. Existing macOS/FreeCAD 1.1.3 evidence does not qualify this newer
  source pin, another import backend/mode or another platform.
- **No premature support promotion:** source route presence, unit tests,
  self-round-trip, opaque byte preservation, and another project's README are
  not by themselves qualification. Promotion requires evidence bound to the
  current implementation and meeting the repository's existing status policy.

### Implementation batches and test cost controls

Keep commits small even when builds/tests are batched. Reuse one configured
build and pinned oracle runtime; rebuild only changed targets with the existing
parallel build option. The current local-roundtrip check measured 3.12 seconds,
so adding a new family-filter framework is not presently justified. Optional
GDAL/netDxf/new Rust comparators stay nonblocking discovery lanes, not setup
work on the critical path.

Main probe14-child controls/reconfigure/CLI1/1 pass without production/full rebuild.84/45/exact7 unchanged; enumerate only actual registration changes; no user-sample glob/native/full suite per edit |

Refresh sanitizer once after later unsafe-boundary changes settle, not per documentation/admission edit. Historical b4/d49/bc8 results retain their actual bindings; no repeated native/full suite. |

Optional-peer phase calibration only when that projection is enabled. Exact nonvirtual and callback consumer gates on public changes; sparse order/subtype1/oracle limits separate |

Use pairwise feature compositions for additional discovery after mandatory
positive/negative and version-boundary cases: e.g. text+codepage+attribute,
HATCH+forward reference+layout, table+extension+resource, or mesh+version+override.
Do not take a full feature × version × encoding × platform Cartesian product
after every edit. Conversely, pairwise sampling cannot omit a required binary
width, downgrade boundary, consumer mode or promotion criterion. Record test
duration and cache misses so later speed decisions use measurements.

The new research does not make every optional comparator a prerequisite. Use
the existing ezdxf runtime for represented fields; unsupported profiles stop
that oracle cell immediately with a named exclusion. Do not install another
version merely because its README is newer. Reuse source-only recipes and
small dependency-free self-tests; reserve package variants for package changes
and native CAD/kernel runs for their exact evidence gates. Parallelize disjoint
research/tests, but integrate `src/libdxfrw.cpp`, `dx_iface.*` and low-level
writer edits serially to avoid patch/review churn. Record actual inventory
changes rather than predicting a new count from optional/unintegrated tests.

For the new findings, use a two-checkpoint implementation path: first the
dependency-free literal/wire or configure control, then one composed current-
revision checkpoint after integration. Reuse the existing DXF/local targets
for7BC/7BD and reader-matrix/hardening targets for7BE; add cases to those
executables rather than one new CTest per scalar mutation. Package7AK.6 needs
only configure-level accept/reject controls against one existing install;
thread metadata needs no format rebuild. Do not rerun independent/native
consumers for a plan-only change. At a changed shared writer/reader boundary,
rebuild its affected targets and rerun their fast cases; run the fixed final
broad/receipt gate only when the candidate is stable. This preserves mandatory
version, binary-width and consumer-mode coverage while avoiding a repeated
full matrix during development.

Apply the same cost rule to7BF/7BG/7BI: one table-driven test inside existing
executables covers many string/tuple/range mutations.7BH uses one bounded
subprocess harness and scratch inputs, with source/destination hashes instead
of drawing comparison for option errors. Do not run independent CAD/native
oracles on invalid-API or malformed-option cases. Reuse the exact pinned runtime
for represented raw fields; mark LTYPE orientation and UCS option semantics
unsupported in that comparator rather than normalizing them away. Keep the
producer-witness task off the critical path for text storage and CLI safety.

For the current handoffs, reuse the existing built target and inspect the small
integration delta rather than replaying every isolated observer.7A.2's original
and cf3 observers remain historical; invalid stale-carrier checks need literal
agreement/atomic retry, not a fresh native draw-order run.7AE.1 uses the existing
DXF executable's isolated locale mode, with unavailable locales reported rather
than silently passing.7F.1a uses six small real CLI routes plus import-reset and
bounded-report controls; migrate1b schemas with dependency-free mutation tests.
7M.1 and7AV.5 first need tiny literal/callback negatives, then one affected
main fast gate and the exact consumer source surface. Do not rebuild FreeCAD,
install a newer comparator or run all84 CTests for these documentation changes.
Refresh the shared unsafe-boundary sanitizer gate after related implementation
changes settle; do not reuse d49's green result as a later-source checkpoint.

For7AK.7, assert configure diagnostics rather than compiling absent targets.
For7BM, place the active/inactive and encoding boundaries in one existing
fixture executable; skip native plotting and whole-graph reconstruction for
invalid-API admission. Reuse7BJ's existing tiny header table for survey units
instead of rerunning all84 exploratory routes after every edit. Header hygiene
uses one compiler harness with at most two scheduled compile/build jobs,
bounded process cleanup/logs and an aggregate CTest timeout, not a fresh full
library build per entry point. Keep native MSVC,
casefold-enabled filesystems and FreeCAD qualification at their named gates.

Before adding further findings, check the ordered table and progress ledger
for an existing owner. Extend that subplan when the issue is a missing boundary
or policy case (survey units, conditional oracle fields, clipping projections),
and add a new ID only for a distinct reproduced/source-confirmed discrepancy.
Research should shrink implementation uncertainty, not indefinitely enlarge
the prerequisite set. Reconcile each ready handoff's base, affected files,
test registrations and evidence binding once; retain recorded isolated results
as historical evidence and run only the affected current-main gate on integration.

Apply this rule afterbf1113c: preserve the committed portable probe and HEADER
reader/writer/generated-profile slices; use bounded existing real-file traces
for remaining HEADER witnesses before broader reader claims. The corrected
7AG.1c facade inventory is complete; the invalid test premise is corrected

Keep acceptance sequential per shared source owner, but parallelize disjoint
source review/control design. A failed local test premise is ready repair work,
not an external blocker or evidence that tolerant input should be tightened.
No research-only row closes a parent, native support criterion or historical J
item. Update the ledger after each real slice commit with its own current-source
gate and next unblocked step; do not relabel these research controls as that gate.

For the current research refinements, run the real adapter-inventory preflight
before invoking either expensive adapter build. Preserve frozen-v2 controls,
then prototype only the typed successor-schema validator and capability shim
before changing receipt-bound output. Coincident-grid and IMAGE load-repair

executable, not a native FreeCAD rebuild. Share one current-source sanitizer
checkpoint after finalizer/token state changes settle; retain d49's result
under d49. These local checks do not change the six external J dispositions.

### Focused commands and completion record

Build only the changed library/tool and relevant test executables. CTest names
are anchored to the current source registration; check availability in the
chosen build before invoking them. For example:

```sh
cmake --build <build> --target libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests libdxfrw_wave1_tests
ctest --test-dir <build> -R '^libdxfrw_(dxf_fixtures|wave1)$' --output-on-failure
cmake --build <build> --target lc3_compat_check libdxfrw_3d_consumer_probe
ctest --test-dir <build> -R '^libdxfrw_3d_consumer_probe$' --output-on-failure
```

The compile-only `lc3_compat_check` is intentionally absent from the CTest
selector. Use the existing focused/final-broad runner when required by the
phase gate; the sample commands do not replace required qualification checks.

For a documentation-only research update, run the plan/reference/whitespace
checks and scoped read-only probes, not the full CTest suite. Do not silently
finish or commit previously staged implementation work in a research-only pass.
The persistent implementation objective remains incomplete and can resume
from the recorded ready work when implementation is requested again.

Research observations and implementation results have separate bindings. The
ledger, not the historical reproduction table, determines remaining work:
7BL/7BM/7BD, ARC flags, classic
VERTEX identifiers/presence and ordered XDATA points are now committed, while
their separately named follow-ups remain open. PAR-90 is a source/spec namespace
defect with an API carrier control; PAR-91 is an acceptance negative against a
copied isolated package; PAR-92 is component work/capacity evidence; PAR-93 is
literal versioned-variable conversion. None is authentic producer/native/ACIS
qualification. Comparator metadata-window and omitted-LW-ID observations are
oracle limitations, not additional local parser defects. Source-only67/70/71,
actual Conan, platform evidence and independent semantic witnesses retain
their precise gates. External setup never blocks independent local fixes or
substitutes for promotion criteria.

`libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip` currently runs its ordinary cases together;
there is no general family selector. A reference to a local-roundtrip case
means adding that regression to the existing executable and running its named
CTest. Add a small explicit case/family selector only if measured duration
justifies it; do not document a nonexistent filter or duplicate the whole suite.

After each committed slice, record: ID/status, commit, reproduced trigger,
smallest test result, independent projection/audit outcome, support-claim
impact, unresolved condition, and next ready item. Failed or unavailable
external evidence remains visible; it is never counted as a passing test.

## Research sources

- [LibreDWG repository and README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) and
  [LibreDWG manual](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi)
  for its documented DWG/DXF version, object, reader, writer, and codepage
  boundaries. Also compare its [pinned NEWS snapshot at
  `34f02f54`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/34f02f54b9aacb5708c1d3d2070efb3e4b2d8c43/NEWS)
  with the current README/package wording; these document peer maturity and
  security work, not a capability guarantee for an unexecuted build. The
  similarly pinned [`src/acds.spec`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/34f02f54b9aacb5708c1d3d2070efb3e4b2d8c43/src/acds.spec)
  is the basis for the partial-index/marker-scan distinction in Slice8; current
  [0.14.1 milestone issues](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/milestone/23)
  are peer-reported calibration leads, not libdxfrw findings.
- [ACadSharp repository](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) for its stated
  version matrix and reader/writer architecture; [dynamic-block writer issue
  #1133](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1133) and [writer maturity
  issue #558](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/558) for concrete
  limitations behind the matrix; [merged PR #1151](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1151)
  for the resulting dynamic-block IO changes and residual modified-instance
  caveat. [PR #1154](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1154) is the full
  Prototype1b parser change; [issue #1152](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1152)
  records the source-review concern that prompted it. [Issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195)
  and its still-open [writer PR #1240](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1240)
  show separate DXF ACIS write maturity. The separate, still-open contributor
  [PR #1150](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1150) proposes pre-2013
  SAT carrier output and 2013+ AcDs/ACDSDATA storage; its source audit exposed
  that the index value must be a rank in sorted-handle order, not a directory
  position. Neither #1150 nor #1240 is a released/current-master result; never
  bind a branch's behavior to a release binary without checking ancestry.
- [acadrust repository](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust) and its
  [pinned 2026-09-10 round-trip tests](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/blob/e1f6c0b8816aeaed81a877e6b5209dd386224fd6/tests/roundtrip.rs)
  for project-stated DWG/DXF/ACIS reach and the difference between fabricated
  carrier tests and independent producer evidence. Peer test-selection leads
  include [malformed object-data #123](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/123),
  [malformed header #124](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/124),

  The latter reports are from 0.6.4-era behavior and are not locally reproduced;

research conclusions.

## Broader comparator and DXF-semantics research (2026-10-14; plan-only)

This follow-up broadens the source review from DWG writer status and peer issue
reports to normative DXF group typing, loss-preserving DXF model designs, staged
reference binding and an intentionally narrower GIS projection. The local
source boundary is `fd3c2e2` (typed-XDATA retained-string accounting); the
ledger is `9859f88`. This is source/document research only: no peer executable,
binary drawing, issue reproduction or interoperability result was run. Peer
branch URLs below are mutable discovery references; pin repository commit SHAs
before any executable comparison.

| Primary source | New comparison or correction | Plan integration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Autodesk group-code value types](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-2553CF98-44F6-4828-82DD-FE3BC7448113.htm), [XDATA format](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A2A628B0-3699-4740-A215-C560E7242F63.htm), and [group codes in numerical order](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3F0380A5-1C15-464D-BC66-2C5F094BCFB9.htm) | Confirms the just-completed `7S.2c.d.4` category is intentionally only retained-string accounting: XDATA codes 1000–1003/1005 are strings, code 1004 is a hex spelling of chunked binary, while 1010–1071 include numeric point/scalar/integer values. Code 1005 is a database handle, not ordinary opaque text, and Autodesk says INSERT/XREF-style import translates it with the referenced entity handle. The repository has separate existing code-1005 reference-remap/write paths; retained-byte success cannot substitute for their semantic remap vectors. The normative page says ASCII binary chunks are pairs of hex digits and at most 127 binary bytes per chunk. | Keep `7S.2c.d.4` bounded to string destinations and keep handle/reference transformation under existing `7AL` / PAR-63–64 and writer-remap owners. Add one paired control to that existing owner only if it lacks a source handle that collides/remaps during output: verify code1005 still points to the emitted referenced identity, while non-handle strings, 1002 braces and 1004 bytes remain unchanged. Exercise 1010–1071 as typed numeric variants separately; do not silently broaden the retention claim. No additional format defect or support promotion is inferred. |
| [ezdxf entity load implementation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dxfentity.py) and [package design](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/develop/pkg-design.rst) | The peer deliberately has a tolerant first tag-loading stage, then a post-load stage for resolving resource handles after document objects exist; invalid XDATA can be sanitized through a safe initializer. This is an architectural comparator, not proof that all dropped malformed tags are safe to discard or that its normalization matches libdxfrw's callback contract. | Use this as a sequencing cross-check for existing `7G` reference/graph work: raw handles and typed records are captured before resolution; defer only relationships whose owner maps are not yet complete; test missing/ambiguous targets and deterministic diagnostics. Do not import ezdxf's repair policy or treat peer audit success as a normative parse oracle. |
| [IxMilia `DxfEntity`](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf/blob/main/src/IxMilia.Dxf/Entities/DxfEntity.cs) and [changelog](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) | The current entity model exposes extension-data groups and XDATA and keeps unconsumed code pairs in an excess-pair collection; the changelog documents incremental XDATA, handle and MTEXT fixes. This is a useful preservation design contrast, but it is neither a source-byte archive nor proof that arbitrary unknown groups round-trip with identical placement or semantics. | Add only a differential unknown-pair/XDATA-order probe to the existing DXF generated fast cohort when raw typed-carrier work is touched. Compare ordered code/value pairs and placement through read/write/read; keep lexical fidelity, unknown-class replay, and semantic equivalence as separate outcomes. Do not promote general preservation based on this API shape or release notes. |
| [GDAL DXF driver known issues](https://github.com/OSGeo/gdal/blob/master/ogr/ogrsf_frmts/dxf/KNOWN_ISSUES.md) and [DXF driver documentation](https://gdal.org/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | GDAL documents explicit projection limits: unsupported entity families (including MESH, MPOLYGON, RAY, TABLE, TOLERANCE and XLINE in its current issue list), absent 3D/OCS behavior for some annotation entities, and a writer gap for block ATTRIB round-trip. Its OGR layer/geometry model is therefore useful for selected geometry checks, not as a comprehensive CAD object or 3D-semantic oracle. | Narrow GDAL comparator use to concrete common geometric invariants and only where the entity/attribute falls inside its documented projection. Mark unsupported/lossy rows `COMPARATOR_NOT_APPLICABLE`; do not interpret absent output as a libdxfrw omission or include those rows in the parity denominator. Preserve independent CAD-level checks for attributes, resources, ordered XDATA, OCS and 3D fields. |
| [LibreDWG decoder source](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode.c) and [project README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/README) | Confirms a broad native decoder and DXF/JSON conversion tooling exist, but project-level maturity prose is not per-version/per-object proof. The README itself names advanced R2010+ objects that may be skipped; mutable `master` source without a captured SHA is not an executable pin. | Keep LibreDWG as an optional, version-pinned differential reader. ## Broader DXF symbol-table capacity audit (2026-10-14; plan-only)

This source/spec pass rechecks the dynamic `TABLES` writer at local HEAD
`6d76a34`, broadening PAR-120 from DIMSTYLE to the complete callback-backed
symbol-table family. Autodesk defines table-header group70 as the maximum
number of entries that may follow and explains that readers use it as an
allocation hint, not as an iteration terminator. Thus values larger than the
emitted row count are permitted; the defect is a header capacity below the
rows actually emitted. Group70 is a 16-bit integer, so output counts must also
remain representable. This is a source/spec finding, not evidence that AutoCAD
or any other named reader rejects a specific libdxfrw file.

| Table | Current local header and row path | Required accounting |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VPORT | Header writes `70=1`; callback may emit rows; if it emits none, writer emits one implicit `*ACTIVE`. `writeVport()` names the first emitted callback row `*ACTIVE`. | Count each successfully committed row, including the empty-callback fallback. |
| LTYPE | Header writes `70=4`; writer directly emits BYBLOCK, BYLAYER and CONTINUOUS, then invokes `writeLTypes()`; canonical callback duplicates are suppressed. | Count the three manual rows plus each successfully emitted noncanonical callback row. |
| LAYER | Header writes `70=1`; `writeLayers()` may emit multiple rows; implicit layer `0` is written only if none did. | Count callback rows and the fallback if needed. |
| STYLE | Header writes `70=3`; `writeTextstyles()` may emit multiple rows; implicit `Standard` is written if absent. | Count callback rows and the fallback exactly once. |
| VIEW / UCS | Each header writes `70=0`, then the respective callbacks can emit records. | Count each successfully committed callback row. |
| APPID | Header writes `70=1`; writer manually emits mandatory `ACAD`, then `writeAppId()` may emit non-ACAD rows (an ACAD callback is a no-op). | Count manual ACAD plus successful non-ACAD rows. |
| DIMSTYLE | Header writes `70=1`; callback rows are followed by implicit `Standard` when absent. | Count callback rows plus fallback exactly once; keep subclass group71/table-header group340 investigation separate. |
| BLOCK_RECORD | Header uses `2 + m_pendingBlockRecords.size()` and writes the two fixed space records plus pre-collected records. | Preserve the exact computed count as a positive control; do not duplicate its counting path. |

The authoritative Autodesk [symbol-table rules](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-5AB9300F-F0AC-4ADE-89EA-A9D1D152D8B8.htm)
list these table kinds, define group70's maximum-capacity semantics and warn
that it is not a row count. The [group-code value-type reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2019/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-2553CF98-44F6-4828-82DD-FE3BC7448113.htm)
defines codes60–79, including70, as 16-bit integers. The independent open
source [ezdxf table exporter](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/sections/table.py)
sets its table-head count from `len(table)` immediately before serializing
entries. That corroborates exact emitted-count output as a practical writer
policy, but ezdxf's in-memory enumerable model does not solve libdxfrw's
callback-only counting problem and its mutable `master` source is not a
normative format authority.

There is a de-facto-practice counterpoint: the netDxf [2.4.0 changelog](https://github.com/haplokuon/netDxf/blob/master/doc/Changelog.txt)
calls group70 obsolete when explaining removal of its in-memory table limits,
based on its reading of AutoCAD ActiveX documentation. That changelog is a
library-maintainer interpretation, not a DXF writer/reader failure measurement;
AutoCAD's published DXF references continue to describe group70 as maximum
capacity. This disagreement lowers the expected impact until a strict reader
reproduces a consequence. Keep PAR-120 at P2 as a writer metadata/conformance
correction, not a proven file-rejection defect or support blocker; do not add
native AutoCAD qualification as a prerequisite to the deterministic fix.

**Implementation-readiness refinement:** `writeTables()` already runs inside
an outer `DxfWriterRecordScope` backed by `std::ostringstream`, a
`RecordStateScope`, and the whole-file output transaction; each row writer
also stages its own record. This permits a one-pass design without calling
consumer callbacks twice: increment a scoped counter only after each row
commit, count manual mandatory rows explicitly, then format-aware backpatch
the group70 placeholder in the unpublished TABLES buffer. The helper must
prove tell/seek/restore for ASCII, binary R12 and modern binary, preserve
writer error state, and reject an unrepresentable count before output
publication. If a safe patch cannot be demonstrated, use bounded per-table
staging once; account for its peak-copy cost and preserve row/handle order. Do
not inflate every header to32767: that is legal as a maximum but defeats the
allocation-hint purpose and conceals counting errors.

The implementation vector set belongs in existing
`libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests`: generated records only, with zero/one/multiple
rows, explicit and implicit defaults, mandatory entries, canonical LTYPE
suppression, late invalid-row rollback, callback-once and unchanged
destination/allocator controls. Parse ordered tags independently and check
each header against the actual row inventory plus `ENDTAB`/next-table
sentinels. Cover R12 and R2000+ as well as ASCII and binary across the compact
generated set; assert binary short width and reject32768 through the tiny
count-helper boundary test rather than constructing tens of thousands of
records. Keep BLOCK_RECORD as the computed-count control. Run changed strict
targets and `lc3_compat_check` per committed slice, then one composed
writer/hardening checkpoint; do not add a full-suite run per table, CTest,
dependency, or checked-in DWG/DXF fixture.

This broadens PAR-120/7BQ without creating another finding or top-level
subplan: totals remain120/69. This plan-only update changes no implementation,
tests, fixtures, registrations, dependencies or support claims. The six
external J items remain `J256`, `J260`, `J268`, `J284`, `J293` and `J295` in
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; no evidence here promotes them or any DWG/DXF feature.

tail selection by target file version (PAR-119), and DXF tagged-field meaning

payload was downloaded/admitted, and no support claim is promoted.

**NOD policy resolution and implementation result:** the first row's earlier
“strict rejection versus recovery” question is resolved for the reported case:
an owned first DICTIONARY is malformed under the positional root contract and
is rejected with `BAD_READ_OBJECTS` before dictionary callbacks. Autodesk's
[common-object table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-6939D69E-04CB-4F4C-87B2-67BC540FCF58.htm)
marks owner group330 optional; the [DICTIONARY table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2017/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-40B92C63-26F0-485B-A9C2-B349099B26D0.htm)
describes its owner-pointer role. Missing versus explicit zero cannot select
the root; a nonzero owner on a physically first dictionary is inconsistent
evidence. The attempted broader rule rejecting every
non-DICTIONARY first record failed 35 existing synthetic fixture assertions
(primarily intentionally minimal OBJECTS snippets). The implemented scope
therefore tracks whether the actual first OBJECTS record is a DICTIONARY,
rejects only the owned-first case, and never uses a later non-reserved,
ownerless dictionary as the root when that position has passed. Fixed C/D
handles remain reserved writer records, not evidence of source root identity.
Legacy/minimal streams without an initial NOD remain readable but are not
proof of a complete named-object graph.

Commit `5a86b1a` adds generated positive matrices for ASCII/binary DXF,
non-monotonic NOD/extension handles, omitted/explicit-zero root owners, and
present/omitted extension owners; it checks exact dictionary entries, raw
identity, and the `ACAD_LAYOUT` callback handle. Owned-first malformed controls
prove rejection before callbacks. The existing block-owner CLI CTest now also
checks that ASCII/binary CLI rejection creates no destination and preserves
pre-existing destination bytes under overwrite mode. `libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures`
and the four-test block-owner cohort pass (five unique CTests); `-Werror` target
build and `git diff --check` pass. No full suite, peer runtime, external
qualification, new fixture payload, or support metadata changed.

The follow-up `db9d234` extends the same generated test with empty-drawing
ASCII/binary writer output and public readback, asserting reserved NOD handle C
is the first dictionary and precedes reserved `ACAD_GROUP` handle D. This
verifies output order only; it does not retain or prove arbitrary source NOD
entries through the `dx_iface` conversion graph.

case (`0cc564f`), distinct unresolved-owner/orphan-suffix negative
(`0de4495`), and NOD identity/order slice (`5a86b1a`) are committed; these do

roles of mature DXF libraries, multi-format DWG/DXF libraries, and downstream

calibration signals—not format oracles. No peer-reported gap is promoted to a
libdxfrw defect without a local route-specific reproduction, and no product
support matrix is used as semantic conformance evidence.

This pass cross-checked the current layout implementation boundary against
ezdxf's documented DXF data model, LibreDWG's DWG/DXF space model, Autodesk's
group-code/coordinate references, ACadSharp's published version matrix, and
GDAL's explicitly projected DXF reader/writer. These projects have different
data models and support boundaries; the findings below refine the existing
7A/7G/7H/7O/7AG slices rather than introducing new defects. No peer runtime,
native CAD application, or downloaded drawing was used.

| Evidence | Broader result and confidence boundary | Concrete plan refinement |

INSERT adds OCS insertion, independent XYZ scale, rotation, extrusion, MINSERT row/column count and spacing, plus an optional ATTRIB/SEQEND chain. GDAL explicitly lacks OCS/elevation geometry for DIMENSION, LEADER, and MULTILEADER, so its projection cannot validate those families. The exact finite-vector arbitrary-axis algorithm also matters when projecting tilted normals. | Keep 2D API values/raw fields separate from optional 3D WCS delivery. Expand the existing local coordinate matrix—not a general rewrite—to identify at least one analytic control per applicable family: planar tilted-OCS+elevation, nonplanar WCS face/mesh, INSERT with nonzero base point plus rotation/nonuniform scale and extrusion, nested/MINSERT spacing, and mixed-frame DIMENSION. Add a reflected-scale case only under a producer-valid profile. Assert native fields before any transformed bounds; test read→write→read and callback projection independently. Use GDAL only for entities/options it documents, and use source-authored expected values for its unsupported OCS families. Reuse 7H/7O/7AG tests and the 3D consumer probe only where public delivery changes. A peer's single generic transform/bounds result is not an oracle. |

Its implementation binds records and resolves layout links in a later stage. It also states that an object can have only one owner but can have multiple pointers; 320–329 are arbitrary non-relocated handles, 330–369 are pointer/owner categories, 390–399 and 480–481 have additional reference roles, and XDATA 1005 behaves as a soft pointer. This is a pinned-release DXF implementation reference, not a normative repair policy. | In 7G.3e, include both an active-paper entity serialized through ENTITIES and an inactive-paper entity serialized in BLOCKS. Assert logical owner BLOCK_RECORD, paper-space flag, and exactly-once callback/readback—not physical section alone. Extend whole-graph admission to reject conflicting multiple owners while preserving valid non-owning pointer cycles. Keep handle remap role-aware: 320–329 arbitrary values stay literal; 330–369 remain soft/hard pointer/owner classes; 390–399, 480–481, contextual fields, and XDATA 1005 use their specific contracts. Never blanket-remap hex strings. Use a second-stage identity/link pass before emission and fail atomically on ambiguous ownership. Do not copy ezdxf's recovery/audit behavior as default input repair. |

ACadSharp's matrix separately lists DXF read/write and DWG read/write, with version gaps, but gives no per-entity completeness guarantee. Autodesk distinguishes owning relations from pointers and arbitrary handles; XDATA 1005 is a translated soft pointer. The LibreDWG `master` manual and ACadSharp site are mutable and advertised capability is not conformance evidence. | Keep a directional route matrix: DWG decode→adapter handoff→DXF serialization, DXF parse→adapter handoff, and DXF→legacy-DWG viewport synthesis are separate cells. Pin exact peer commit/release and options before any differential run. For each cell record `typed`, `opaque-preserved`, `projected`, `not-applicable`, `dropped`, or `rejected`, with a comparable-field denominator; never convert missing peer projection into a libdxfrw failure or turn a version checkmark into support. Require typed owner closure and semantic field comparisons, not counts/open-success alone. |
| GDAL [DXF driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html), [known issues](https://github.com/OSGeo/gdal/blob/master/ogr/ogrsf_frmts/dxf/KNOWN_ISSUES.md), and ezdxf's [entity/layout data model](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/develop/pkg-design.rst) | GDAL is an OGR geometry projection: it tessellates curves, has documented OCS/elevation exceptions and entity omissions, may inline INSERTs under a default per-block limit, and exposes AC1027+ ASM payload/transform only when configured; it does not decode B-rep semantics. ezdxf's internal entity database/layout spaces are a richer CAD graph than a flattened GIS layer. Therefore no single cross-project output count can serve as a whole-drawing parity measure. | Extend existing comparator receipts with per-field oracle disposition and options: use GDAL only for common geometry/raw-tag checks with block expansion explicitly disabled or its feature cap explicitly bound; use a CAD-graph library for handles/layout/object closure; use the independent kernel/native route for shape semantics. Exclude unsupported projection cells from denominators. Do not install a comparator, add CI dependencies, add CTests, or run a full suite for each individual field. |

and verifies rejection with destination preservation for missing, wrong-type,

control is retained. The repeated version outputs re-import their generated
source because successful entity serialization assigns emitted handles into

decoding, not polyline grammar; and the reporter of LibreDWG #1355 retracted
the initial short-handle-map-section/third-page theory, not the issue itself.

three drawings initially grouped with #1355 were reassigned to #1294's distinct
R2004+ section-reader failure; its proposed fix is also still an open PR.

DWG was obtained or run, and no production code, finding ID, registration,
dependency, support claim, or fixture payload is added here.

The latter is a peer-observed compatibility case, not an ODA rule established by this pass. Local `dwgReader21::parseDataPage` RS-decodes the non-AC1018 path before its copy/decompress branch; `dwgReader18` does likewise on its AC1024+ RS fallback. Both use compression-size comparisons only after decode. Source review found no corresponding defect in entity `parseDwg` grammar, but the fast test search found no explicit generated AC1021 data-page profile matrix. | Keep the entity parsers untouched unless a page-valid input still reproduces bad coordinates after page decoding is proven. Under the existing reader-matrix owner, add compact from-scratch page controls for RS-compressed and RS-uncompressed data, both AC1021 interleaving modes where constructible, plus legacy AC1018-format compatibility on the mixed-page route. Make the expected logical bytes and a following-page/object sentinel explicit. Investigate the peer's apparent verbatim page class against ODA and a shareable producer trace before accepting it: page-size discrimination may be recorded as a candidate classifier, not copied as an unconditional heuristic. Malformed size/encoding combinations must fail with the existing integrity diagnostic and leave the reader reusable. Use only existing fast reader targets; do not import the issue's DWG corpus or expand the per-commit version suite. |

ODA's rule is “not compressed if compression is not shorter,” but the exact validity meaning of `cSize > uSize` in every relevant section/page profile was not established here. This is a narrow asymmetry worth resolving, not yet a confirmed valid-file defect. | Add a page-profile discriminator decision to the reader-matrix subplan: positively cover `cSize < uSize` (compressed) and the authoritative uncompressed representation; add a `cSize > uSize` negative that either rejects or follows a separately documented page rule. Do not let that case fall into arbitrary decompression by default. Confirm the page-map field interpretation and decoded-size bounds from ODA plus a producer witness before changing behavior. Assert checksum/page bounds, exact logical output, next-page alignment, and no section publication after failure. This is a fast, local gate—not a request for a downloaded sample or full reader corpus. |

   direct and nested reachability and source→output correspondence are separate.

   expansion. Use non-monotonic IDs and independently permuted callback/payload
   order; equal totals with swapped bodies or an empty reachable block fail.
2. **B2 — carrier and actual CLI handoff.** Start at one established legacy-SAT
   target in ASCII/binary. Compare reconstructed SAT under a declared rule,

   pass part of the transport gate. Run the actual CLI on the calibrated input.

3. **B3 — discriminating failures and bounded reuse.** Mutate the census oracle

   work policy and cannot count a truncated expansion as complete. Small exact/
   over bounds and corrected reuse replace deep-stack/huge-corpus experiments.
