### Executed calibration: bytes, meaning and escape transport are different

The authored probe compiled the current codec directly with C++17 and
`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`; it did not link a stale library or touch the main
build.35 literal vectors × DWG-style/legacy-DXF-style unit configurations ×
C/tr_TR.ISO8859-9 child locales yielded140 cells. The independent Python3.9.6
strict standard-codec anchors match48 cells;92 differ, of which72 still
round-trip to identical original bytes.16 cells decode to empty. These are
selected discriminating probes, not a failure rate, exhaustive mapping audit,
DWG-file test or family-level support score. Every profile's outputs are
identical on this macOS arm64 runtime; lowercase`ansi_949` passes in both
locales, so no local Turkish-locale failure is asserted.

Examples with different standard meanings include KOI8-R E1, ISO8859-5 B0,
IBM86680, AppleRoman80, EUC-JP A4A2 and GB18030 81308130. Compact and canonical
spellings must be tested independently: accepted`IBM 866` selects CP1251,
while`CP866` falls through to CP1252. Coinciding anchors do not establish
codec equivalence: ISO8859-8 E0 and ISO8859-9 D0 initially agreed with the
substituted Windows tables; additional DF/80 controls discriminate them.

All four Big5-HKSCS two-scalar sequences decode correctly. Their output uses
a representable character plus a CIF escape, so raw byte identity changes
while the local DXF-aware reread retains both scalars. This is not loss and
does not justify a speculative reverse-index rewrite. Separately qualify
raw carrier identity, scalar preservation and target-valid escape transport;
do not interpret a standard-codec-only reread of literal escape bytes as DXF
text loss. Keep combining sequences exact; no Unicode normalization to make
the oracle agree.

### Slice3.1–3.5: bounded implementation-ready sequence

1. **3.1 — freeze the discriminators (`READY_LOCAL`).** Reuse
   `tests/gbk_codepage_tests.cpp` and its existing executable. Add a focused
   alias-policy mode, literal independently expected scalar rows and controls
   proving that equal source/output bytes can still mean the wrong text.
   Separate canonical labels, accepted extra aliases, unsupported labels,
   undefined bytes and escape-preserving output. The embedded scratch recipe
   and35-vector receipt make regeneration possible without Python/Unicode
   downloads in normal C++ tests. Keep matching ANSI/Chinese/Korean/Japanese,
   two-scalar, MIF and current input-only recovery controls. Record the actual
   red baseline before changing a decoder; do not encode today's mojibake as
   the future expected success. Keep intentionally red probes opt-in until
   their corresponding fix; existing mandatory CTests must remain green.
2. **3.2 — classify before changing behavior (`POLICY_GATE`, local).** Make a
   small internal table of canonical IDs, exact aliases, historical inexact
   aliases, recognized-but-unavailable encodings and unknown names. Preserve
   original declaration, selected codec and fallback reason independently;
   distinguish “not declared” from “declared but unavailable.” Use ASCII-only
   byte-safe normalization, without global locale changes. Existing2D facade
   defaults remain compatible; do not silently reinterpret historical aliases
   or turn every unsupported declaration into a new fatal read. Record bounded
   fallback diagnostics through the existing operation mechanism. A strict
   complete-conversion policy must refuse unrepresented required text rather
   than publish corrupted text as complete. Resolve the exact policy boundary
   against current consumer calls before changing it; if that decision is
   pending, complete classification/diagnostic work and continue an independent
   ready slice instead of broadening defaults.
3. **3.3 — repair one evidenced mapping family per commit (`AFTER3.2`).** Start
   with ISO8859-4's local codec mapping, not a DWG numeric-ID change, using
   Unicode's exact mapping and its redistribution terms. Prefer generated fixed tables
   with source/hash provenance; no iconv/ICU runtime dependency. Test decode,
   encode, undefined-byte behavior, actual declared/emitted codec and all
   relevant distinguishing bytes, not one overlap anchor. Keep ISO8859-4/10/13,
   KOI/DOS/Mac and multibyte grammars as separate closures. EUC-JP is not CP932,
   and four-byte GB18030 is not implemented by accepting the GBK subset. Until
   a grammar is implemented, classify it unavailable/compatibility-only under
   the chosen policy, not supported because its name normalizes successfully.
   The latest exhaustive review below supplies3.3a policy/identity,3.3b offline
   table, and3.3c HEADER/CLI handoff substeps. Do not silently replace the
   historical default alias selection or treat a correct Windows/CIF encoding
   of supplied Unicode as proof that ISO source bytes were decoded correctly.
4. **3.4 — join real metadata paths (`VERSION_EVIDENCE_GATE`).** After the
   codec is correct, separately review numeric DWG ID→name, DXF name→codec,
   canonical writer ID and per-field EED codepage. Do not conflate file TV,
   primary TU and EED-local encoding. Reuse committed source-codepage snapshot,
   HEADER-finalization and input-only recovery tests; do not restart7L.5/7AL.
   Before any DWG map/parser change, read the relevant local ODA chapter and
   trace a real eligible version/field. Unsupported ID provenance and retry
   reset must remain truthful, not become a fabricated recognized CP1252.
5. **3.5 — compose once (`INTEGRATION_GATE`).** Generate one small TEXT/MTEXT
   drawing with a distinct following LINE, one selected legacy target and
   ASCII/binary modes. Check independently expected Unicode, physical emitted
   bytes/declaration, repeated handoff and strict-failure destination preservation
   where the policy requires it. Exercise modern DXF UTF-8 and modern DWG TU
   as unchanged controls only where touched; do not multiply every page by the
   entire format/version matrix. Run the existing codec CTest plus the affected
   fixture/HEADER tests and LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3 source checks once. A policy or
   mapping change invalidates only evidence bound to those inputs; it does not
   require native platform/ACIS runs or the whole suite per commit.

### Executed evidence: completion, successful reopening and meaning differ

Sixteen locally authored ASCII DXFs contain a TEXT and a distinct following
LINE. Each is converted to AC1018 and AC1021 ASCII output, then converted
again:32 routes/64 processes in the final calibrated run. All64 return0,
all32 preserve TEXT bytes on the second pass, and CLI stderr is empty in
all32 first conversions. Ordinary ezdxf1.4.4 pure-Python
`readfile(errors="strict")`, without audit/recover, reopens27 outputs; every
successful reopen retains the exact LINE endpoints`(34,35,36)..(37,38,39)`.
This is not binary DXF, DWG, native/platform or broad charset qualification.

| Discriminating source | Observed actual output | Interpretation / existing owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy`ISO8859-4`, payload`left A1 right` | Both targets publish`leftright`, exit0. | The selected compatibility table deletes the distinct U+0104 anchor. PAR-05/Slice3 needs source-loss status, not just a later valid UTF8 string. |
| Legacy`CP866 80` and`ISO8859-5 B0` | Both targets publish U+20AC and U+00B0 instead of independently expected U+0410. | Four more named-codec mismatches; stable output/reopen cannot prove the interpretation. Extra labels/raw high-byte inputs are policy probes, not certified normative DXF declarations. |
| Modern UTF8 U+1F600 | AC1021 preserves the scalar; AC1018 publishes`?`, exit0. | Target downgrade loss is distinct from input decoder selection. Extend Slice6/3.2b.2d; do not invent a surrogate-pair wire convention. |
| Modern overlong, surrogate, out-of-range, isolated-continuation and truncated UTF8 | All five AC1021 outputs are published unchanged and fail strict UTF8 reopening. Their AC1018 counterparts contain replacements and reopen. | Ten malformed-source policy routes, not valid-source parity failures. Strict conversion needs source-validity observations; valid output after substitution does not prove preservation. PAR-05/7AR/7F. |
| Legacy undefined CP1252 byte81 and truncated CP932 lead82 | Both targets publish after deletion or replacement. | Four additional undefined/malformed-source routes. The source event must remain visible even if the semantic string is nonempty and well-formed. |
| Unknown legacy label with plain ASCII or genuine authored BMP CIF; unknown modern metadata with valid UTF8 | ASCII and all scoped scalar transports survive. In two legacy-target outputs ezdxf exposes literal`\U+0410` rather than a decoded scalar. | Warning or literal peer projection is not automatic loss. Separate carrier text from scalar interpretation; do not decode arbitrary escape-looking semantic strings twice. |

There are18 routes with independently specified scalar expectations:
11 preserve authored scalar transport and seven have named-mapping or target
loss. The remaining14 use deliberately malformed/undefined source sequences,
with no successful semantic-decoding expectation. These are discriminators,
not a failure percentage. Initially literal peer projection matched only9;
the two genuine CIF transports are explicitly adjudicated, retaining original
peer strings in the report. The restricted authored BMP escape check is not
a new generic oracle decoder.

The source boundary explains the missing enforcement: ordinary DXF
`dx_iface::fileImport` retains bool/version but deletes its facade without
snapshotting bounded read diagnostics; DWG import already has a separate
owned observation envelope. `dxfWriter::writeUtf8String` converts then writes
without a general source-to-target scalar-loss result. Typed XDATA has its own
UTF8/round-trip preflight, but ordinary TEXT cannot be assumed to inherit it.
Do not duplicate XDATA checks or assume same-codec verification can detect
a character already discarded during input.

### Executed geometry-oracle calibration

These controls reuse installed ezdxf1.4.4 pure-Python; no new dependency
or mandatory CTest.

| Authored operation | Actual result, no exception | Required comparator assertion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nonuniform`(2,1,1)` scale of virtual CIRCLE,`inplace` | CIRCLE survives; log`VIRTUAL_ENTITY_NOT_SUPPORTED`. | Count survival is not transformation. Check unresolved logs and analytic geometry. |
| Same virtual CIRCLE,`copies` | One ELLIPSE, empty log. | Intentional type change; compare meaning, not class counts. |
| Sheared INSERT,`copies` | Zero outputs,`INSERT_TRANSFORMATION_ERROR`. | Account for every source identity; an empty intersection is not agreement. |
|`scale_uniform(...,0.0)` | Empty log; center/radius unchanged. | Check effective transform/domain, not only logs. Its minimum scale is not a format limit. |

For later nested-block/3D projections, record stored definitions, reference
instances, projected primitives and skipped identities separately. Calibrate
with one asymmetric analytic control before a corpus. Preserve base points,
normal/rotation/nonuniform scale and entity-specific WCS/OCS roles. Do not

### Exhaustive evidence, not another overlap anchor

The authored probe executes256 input bytes for five declared profiles through
both AC1015 DXF and non-DXF byte-codec selection:2,560 observations. It checks
decode against Unicode's table, then separately encodes the independently
expected Unicode scalar. Unicode tables and strict CPython codecs agree on
all tested byte definitions. The recorded probe run takes0.031s excluding
compilation; this is a bounded diagnostic measurement, not a benchmark.

| Declared profile | Actual local selection | Decode mismatches per256-byte route | Defined bytes deleted | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ISO8859-4 | ANSI_1257 / CompatibilityAlias |104 |12 | A1 should be U+0104 but disappears; the mapping is not Windows Baltic. |
| ISO-8859-4 | ANSI_1252 / Unavailable |82 |5 | Hyphen spelling selects a different historical fallback; naming normalization alone cannot repair it. |
| ISO8859-10 | ANSI_1257 / CompatibilityAlias |106 |12 | Separate table/profile, not another spelling of ISO8859-4. |
| ISO8859-13 | ANSI_1257 / CompatibilityAlias |36 |12 | A1 should be U+201D; agreement on other Baltic letters is insufficient. |
| ANSI_1257 | ANSI_1257 / Canonical |0 of244 defined |0 defined |12 source bytes are undefined, correctly observed separately; do not invent valid scalars for them. |

The mapping authority is Unicode's
[8859-4](https://www.unicode.org/Public/MAPPINGS/ISO8859/8859-4.TXT),
[8859-10](https://www.unicode.org/Public/MAPPINGS/ISO8859/8859-10.TXT),
[8859-13](https://www.unicode.org/Public/MAPPINGS/ISO8859/8859-13.TXT) and
[CP1257](https://www.unicode.org/Public/MAPPINGS/VENDORS/MICSFT/WINDOWS/CP1257.TXT)
data, not a peer's alias table. All256 bytes are defined and uniquely mapped
in each tested ISO family. C1 controls80–9F are real table entries, not
undefined Windows bytes; byte-codec validity does not admit raw controls in
every DXF field/framing.

**Important non-finding:** encoding supplied expected Unicode through the
selected Windows table/BMP CIF preserves its scalars in all defined rows.
Different encoded bytes are not automatically target loss: U+0104 legitimately
encodes as Windows1257 C0 or CP1252 CIF. The demonstrated failure is wrong ISO
source interpretation. A same-codec inverse check, or changing output metadata
to ISO while still emitting Windows bytes, cannot fix that failure. No whole
DWG, numeric codepage ID, TU/EED or native producer was exercised.

### Executed command-stream calibration

The existing isolated ezdxf1.4.4 pure-Python environment ordinarily reopens28
authored current-CLI outputs: TEXT/MTEXT caret-command, caret-space and raw-BEL
cases, plus MTEXT stacked-fraction/paragraph text, across AC1018/AC1021 and
ASCII/binary output. All28 preserve exact raw carrier values and the following
LINE `(34,35,36)`–`(37,38,39)`; all source hashes remain unchanged. Each child
uses the existing bounded-process helper with5s/65,536-byte limits. There is
no recovery/audit/native renderer, binary input or DWG in this probe.

For `literal^Jend`, raw text remains exact; caret decoding produces LF, while
TEXT's plain-text projection removes that line break and MTEXT's retains it.
`literal^ end` projects to a literal caret. MTEXT `\S1^ 2;\Ptail` retains its
command stream, not a plain-text promise. Raw BEL survives unchanged, which
does not establish SAVEAS-style producer conformance. These observations
calibrate representation/consumer boundaries, not caller intent or a newly
reproduced local defect. First harness invocation used incorrect helper keyword
names and stopped before launching a child; the corrected28-route run passed
without weakening an assertion.

  [pinned DXF writer](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/f860b0fb76d5f8effb5a70769a3389cb1e0308c8/src/out_dxf.c#L4161-L4183)

  Exclude that route as a root-order oracle for non-monotonic graphs.

  distinguish C0–C8; [closest-ACI lookup](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_Colors_EntityColor_LookUpAci_byte_byte_byte.html)

  do not copy a source palette helper or hardcode drawing-specific colors.
- [Pinned ezdxf drawing limits](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/7c64bce52c9d60b9db2dad4d2793c1168c8d3f64/docs/source/addons/drawing.rst)

all nine callback families listed in f.4a, and `dx_iface` copies each callback
into the matching collection (including a null-safe pointer callback for
MLEADERSTYLE). No pure virtual was added and interface default behavior for
LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3 is unchanged. `DRW_DictionaryWithDefault` copy construction
and assignment now preserve the parsed code-340 presence bit, so
`hasCompleteDxfPayload()` stays meaningful across the adapter-owned copy.

The runtime-generated `dwg2dxf_named_object_callback_storage` fast regression
parses a minimal NOD plus DICTIONARYWDFLT from an in-memory DXF, verifies the
stored payload remains complete through copy construction/assignment, invokes
each remaining callback, checks owned handle identities and null MLEADERSTYLE
handling, and leaves no drawing fixture. Target build and that single CTest
passed; no full suite was run. This closes only the storage/copy portion of
f.4a. The initially-open reset, malformed-pointer and following-record checks
are closed by f.4a.2 below. No writer, graph closure, target interoperability
or support claim is promoted; the f.4b/f.4c gates and all six
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` items are unchanged.
Implementation commit: `ed8d925` (parent `05240cf`). The source hashes,
command results and bounded interpretation are recorded in
[`docs/research/named-object-callback-storage-2026-10-15.json`](docs/research/named-object-callback-storage-2026-10-15.json).

## Deeper named-resource emitter and cross-implementation readiness review (2026-10-15)

This pass compared current Autodesk DXF object tables, the ODA DWG
specification, LibreDWG's current `dwg2.spec`, LibreCAD's current bundled
adapter/writer integration, ezdxf's data-model guidance, and this checkout's
parser/model/writer/CLI graph. It is static source/spec research; the only
runtime check intentionally deferred is the next focused implementation gate.
Source URLs, local source hashes, exact route observations, and the review
boundary are recorded in
[`docs/research/named-resource-emitter-readiness-2026-10-15.json`](docs/research/named-resource-emitter-readiness-2026-10-15.json).

### Field-level output contract for the first four families

Common object identity must be handled once across all rows: preserve/remap the
record's group5 handle; emit the exact source owner in group330; preserve
reactors under the 102/330 group and extension-dictionary link under 102/360;
then preserve typed XDATA. Resolve owner/child links from the rooted dictionary
graph, not by callback order. `writeTableEntryAppData`/`writeObjectOwner` are
the existing common writer helpers; typed writers may be selected only when
the origin/profile permits them.

| Record | Exact typed payload groups → modeled member | Reference/output constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SCALE | 70→`flag`; 300→`name`; 140→`paperUnits`; 141→`drawingUnits`; 290→`isUnitScale`. | Custom class `SCALE` requires its matching CLASS metadata for typed DWG-origin output. Resolve only as a leaf owned by the exact parent dictionary; no additional style-resource pointer is present. |
| DICTIONARYVAR | 100 `DictionaryVariables`; 280→`m_schema`; 1→`m_value`. | Custom class `DICTIONARYVAR` requires CLASS metadata for typed DWG-origin output. Required owner is the dictionary reached through the NOD key `AcDbVariableDictionary` (ObjectARX identifies the owner dictionary as `ACDBVARIABLEDICTIONARY`); never manufacture the owner edge from the variable's name. |
| MLINESTYLE | 2→`name`; 70→`flags`; 3→`description`; 62 before first element→`fillColor`; 51/52→start/end angle; 71→`elements.size()`; for each element in order: 49→`offset`, 62→`color`, 6→`linetype` name. | Fixed built-in object, no CLASS. Reject count mismatch and incomplete tuples rather than silently using defaults. Autodesk documents MLINESTYLE fill/element color as DXF ACI code 62; ODA §20.4.73 defines both corresponding DWG values as CMC, which can carry RGB and color-name/book data. The current model/parser/encoder does not retain every such CMC component, and DXF MLINESTYLE has no documented 420/430 equivalent in that table. Before typed DWG-origin emission, either model and prove a target-compatible preservation route for every present CMC component or fail closed before publication; never approximate RGB to ACI or silently drop names/books. DXF-origin raw replay remains eligible only with exact source/profile/identity admission. For R2018+ resolve each linetype handle to one output LTYPE name; for pre-R2018 resolve the signed inline index through the source LTYPE order/name map, treating LibreDWG's special sentinel mapping as a differential lead to verify for the admitted source profile, and reject unresolved or ambiguous values. Never write a DWG handle as DXF group 6. |
| MLEADERSTYLE (base) | 2→`name`; 70→`flags`; 170/171/172→content/draw-MLeader/draw-leader order; 90→`maxLeaderPoints`; 40/41→segment-angle constraints; 173→`leaderType`; 91/92→leader line color/weight; 290/291→landing/dogleg booleans; 42/43→landing gap/distance; 3→description; 341→arrowhead block handle; 44→arrowhead size; 300→default MText; 342→text-style handle; 174/178/175/176→attachment/angle/alignment; 93/45/292/297/46→text color/height/frame/left-align/spacing; 343→content block; 94/47/49/140/293/141/294/177/142/295/296/143→block color/XYZ scale/scale-enabled/rotation/rotation-enabled/connection/scale factor/changed/annotative/break gap; 271/272/273→MText attachment directions. | 340→leader-line LTYPE; 341→arrowhead BLOCK; 342→STYLE; 343→content BLOCK. For each nonzero target require one matching target of the correct kind, remap through the output identity map, and fail before publication for dangling, ambiguous or wrong-kind targets. 179→`styleVersion` only for AC1024+; 298→`textExtended` only for AC1027+; retain base writer floor AC1021. The 179/298 gates follow LibreDWG's versioned schema cross-check; test both boundaries. Register exactly one MLEADERSTYLE CLASS entry with the emitted typed object count. |

For DXF-origin records, pair the raw carrier with the typed value by exact
record name, handle, parent and version; raw is emitted once when its replay
profile is admitted, preserving unknown tags. For DWG-origin records there is
no DXF raw carrier, so typed field coverage and version/reference preflight
are mandatory. A raw carrier that fails source/profile or identity matching
cannot be silently dropped in favor of an incomplete typed projection.

Two architectural findings apply to all four families:

1. `dxfRW::processScale`, `processDictionaryVar`, `processMLineStyle` and
   `processMLeaderStyle` publish typed values **and** a raw `DRW_RawDxfObject`.
   `dx_iface::addRawDxfObject` currently stores only ACAD_PROXY_OBJECT and
   VISUALSTYLE. Thus, the branch has no raw-object preservation lane for these
   four DXF families; it is incorrect to assume DXF-origin raw-net replay
   masks incomplete typed emission. Add source-origin-aware raw retention and
   one-record identity pairing before claiming exact DXF pass-through. For
   DWG-origin records (which have no raw DXF carrier), typed emission remains
   mandatory. If a raw carrier and typed record coexist, require exact unique
   handle/type/owner agreement and emit exactly once.
2. The writer methods' existence is not integration. No `dx_iface` call site
   currently reaches `writeScale`, `writeDictionaryVar`, `writeMLineStyle` or
   `writeMLeaderStyle`; `writeObjects()` emits the existing dictionary,
   XRECORD, LAYOUT, VISUALSTYLE and selected MATERIAL routes only. The bounded
   extension DFS and root-entry resolver must admit a typed leaf only after
   proving unique source identity, exact owner dictionary, root-key/child
   agreement, handle reservation/remapping, and every non-null property edge.
   Use one existing graph service; do not create a second graph or copy
   LibreCAD's owner fallback.

LibreCAD's [current filter integration](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD/blob/master/librecad/src/lib/filters/rs_filterdxfrw.cpp)
is a valuable implementation reference: it emits typed-only DWG resources,
deduplicates matching raw/typed records by source handle, remaps own handles,
and generates custom-class metadata for typed classes. Its permissive fallback
that reparents an unreachable object to the NOD is not a safe strict policy
for this adapter because it changes ownership semantics. Its DWG writer also
shows the necessary name/handle joins for MLEADERSTYLE's line type, text style
and block references. ezdxf's [data-model guide](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/develop/pkg-design.rst)
reinforces the distinct OBJECTS ownership graph and handle-indexed identity
model. These peers inform structure and test design; neither is treated as a
semantic oracle for the local output.

## Implementation progress — f.4b.1c MLEADERSTYLE rooted record output (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

The MLEADERSTYLE low-level writer was already version-gated and handle-aware;
this slice connects its record into the existing bounded extension-object
graph. The DFS now indexes typed/raw MLEADERSTYLE records, rejects duplicate or
invalid handles and identity/owner mismatches, and stages a style only when
reachable from the validated `ACAD_MLEADERSTYLE` child dictionary. DXF-origin
output selects its one-to-one raw carrier; the typed DWG-origin branch invokes
`writeMLeaderStyle`. The output path reserves style handles before allocation,
includes them in fixed-handle collision remapping, resolves the NOD root entry
to the queued style, and injects exactly one canonical `AcDbMLeaderStyle`
CLASS row with the rooted admitted output count. An invalid graph frame now
fails closed rather than dereferencing an absent record variant.

The runtime-generated `libdxfrw_named_resource_import_evidence` control covers
ASCII and binary AC1027 sources with the exact NOD→dictionary→style ownership
chain. It verifies raw opaque group302 replay, readback ownership and CLASS
instance count, then exercises the typed-origin branch using a synthesized
in-memory receipt derived from a DXF import and confirms an edited text height
survives output. Wrong-owner/raw mismatch and a non-null unresolved LTYPE
reference each refuse without replacing sentinel destination bytes. This
synthetic typed-origin exercise is not a real DWG import witness. No MLEADER
entity or non-null property reference is admitted: target-kind/uniqueness,
content-type/field-presence and entity-to-style closure are intentionally the
next f.4b.1c child, and remain transactionally fail-closed. Same-facade
corrected retry and real DWG-origin semantic evidence also remain open.

`cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests -j4` passes;
`ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R named_resource_import_evidence
--output-on-failure` passes 1/1 in 0.36s; scoped `git diff --check` passes.
All DXF controls are generated under the test build directory; no drawing
fixture or CTest registration was added. Full suites and external/native

### CLASS metadata reconciliation and concrete implementation-order refinement

The comparator pass exposed a documentation conflict worth resolving before
changing class admission. Autodesk's [CLASSES group-code table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-DBD5351C-E408-4CED-9336-3BD489179EF5.htm)
describes both code1 (DXF record name) and code2 (C++ class name) as always
unique. ezdxf's current documentation retains an older empirical note that
some Architectural Desktop 2007 files reused code1 with different code2.
The local `dxfRW::preflightDxfClasses()` currently enforces uniqueness for
both fields; the official table supports retaining that fail-closed contract.
Do not loosen it based only on the peer note. If a producer-authored
counterexample is obtained later, preserve the exact product/version/file and
resolve the conflict before changing policy.

A second, directly actionable ordering constraint comes from the local writer:
`dxfRW::write()` validates/freezes the class list and emits CLASSES before
`writeObjects()`. Group91 is the custom-class instance count for AC1018+.
The adapter currently composes counts for selected ACDS/evaluation-graph
routes, but the upcoming named-resource routes need the same explicit
pre-emission planning. Therefore f.4b must compute each custom class's count
from the final admitted output set (after raw-versus-typed dedup and all
refusal checks), then freeze class metadata before writer entry. Never copy a
source count when records have been filtered/remapped; never count fixed
classes such as MLINESTYLE; never attempt to repair counts after CLASSES has
already been written. The fast contract should assert separate code1/code2
uniqueness, exact one-row registration per emitted custom record class, and
group91 equal to the emitted count for AC1018+ in ASCII and binary readback.

The implementation order is sharpened without new PAR IDs or changed ledger
counts: f.3c still owns profile-complete VISUALSTYLE admission; f.4b.0 must
finish the source/target field and handle map plus an immutable output-class
manifest; f.4b.1a / .1c consume that manifest for exact counts before the one
writer invocation. Its fast class-count controls now include a filtered same-
class record and assert counts over the final cross-section emission plan,
not source object inventory. At f.4c, pin the FreeCAD build and importer
profile, distinguish explicit converter mode from Automatic fallback, and
record child status plus output validation before checking consumer semantics.
Peer output is useful for locating a discrepancy, but only the ODA/Autodesk
contract, trace-backed source profiles, and the existing consumer-specific
gates can promote claims. No code, fixture, dependency, CTest registration,
finding/subplan/ledger count, support claim, or J status changed in this
research pass; J256/J260/J268/J284/J293/J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.
The peer-source line mapping, SHA-256 values, and static-only evidence limits
are recorded in
[`class-emission-contract-readiness-2026-10-15.json`](docs/research/class-emission-contract-readiness-2026-10-15.json).

## Deeper VisualStyle slot-map and peer-asymmetry audit (2026-10-15; research-only)

The next f.3c readiness pass pinned a second, more complete implementation
crosswalk: LibreDWG snapshot `6d6a33987a1a97095b069c799c3d8a793320f812`
defines the R2013b VisualStyle 58-value body/DXF candidate map in `dwg2.spec`,
has a separate DXF group consumer in `in_dxf.c`, lists the 58 wire value kinds
in `common.c`, and has typed API checks in `test/unit-testing/visualstyle.c`.
Exact source hashes and a 58-slot crosswalk are in
[`visualstyle-slot-map-readiness-2026-10-15.json`](docs/research/visualstyle-slot-map-readiness-2026-10-15.json).
LibreDWG's checked-out tree was dirty, so the receipt binds the exact inspected
file blobs; no LibreDWG runtime was run. Autodesk's published
[VISUALSTYLE DXF table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-8A8BF2C4-FC56-44EC-A8C4-A60CE33A530C.htm)
defines the conventional face/edge/display groups, but not the complete
R2013b 58-slot extension, group176 companions, or group177 lighting profile.
Therefore LibreDWG gives us a concrete candidate descriptor, not a normative
contract.

The source comparison reveals implementation asymmetries requiring explicit
tests before using that candidate as a writer map. For slots31 (`bProp1f`)
and33 (`bProp21`), LibreDWG's `dwg2.spec` declares value group290 and companion
group0, while its DXF importer consumes value group90 plus group176. Its
`gen-dynapi.pl` separately forces all VisualStyle `*_int` companion metadata to
group176, and the generated API reference also records176. The active writer
output was not executed here, so the three source paths document a mismatch;
they do not yet establish the emitted file behavior. For slot45 (`bProp2d`),
the spec and generated metadata assign group290 plus group176, but the DXF
import path comments out the primary Boolean read. The base R2010b serializer
and R2013b extension also use distinct group layouts; group70 represents the
style type before the code291 property-tail boundary and the 58-slot count
after that boundary. The importer supplies default `extLightingModel` values
when that field is absent, which is not preservation of the source value.
These findings are source-derived risks, not a reproduced failure in a peer
file.

One additional bounded artifact is available: the tracked LibreDWG
`test/test-data/example_2013.dxf` has a same-named DWG pair and contains a
VISUALSTYLE with groups70/177/291, a later group70 count58, repeated group176,
and group290 Boolean values. Its introducing commit says the example was
converted across releases; its original producer and independent application
acceptance are not established. Use it to characterize a real repository
sample and exercise candidate parser paths, but not as an independent writer
or semantic oracle. The path, hash, and provenance limit are recorded in the
slot-map receipt.

### Ready sub-plan: freeze candidates, then resolve conflicts without broadening claims

1. Treat the JSON crosswalk as a candidate manifest with explicit source
   confidence: Autodesk-documented conventional groups versus
   LibreDWG-derived R2013b extension groups. Preserve source primitive kind,
   slot index, group candidates, companion slot/value and source version
   separately; do not fold them into a single “DXF schema” enum.
2. **Completed locally:** the fast generated vector and manifest checks now
   cover all58 decoder/model field names and primitive families, 8 CMC
   positions, the28-versus58 version boundary, and58 candidate group176
   companions; the DWG vector separately asserts the captured companion
   count. The manifest check is deliberately pinned to candidate metadata and
   not a DXF wire oracle. It cannot validate emitted group codes or values.
3. Before typed serialization, first characterize the already-tracked peer
   AC1027 pair read-only. Then execute a pinned LibreDWG writer on a generated
   uniquely-valued 58-slot control to determine actual output tags, and
   resolve 31/33/45 and group70/177/291 semantics against producer-authored
   ASCII/binary R2013b DXF plus an independent parser/readback. Record the
   writer version, argv, warnings, and output hash; do not treat its own
   self-roundtrip as an oracle. Add unique non-default scalar, explicit RGB
   black, unknown CMC method and color name/book controls.
4. If no independent witness is available, the affected field/profile stays
   non-emittable and the converter must refuse before destination replacement;
   do not silently omit a companion, invent a default, clamp, or infer
   semantics from property names. Keep raw DXF-origin replay intact.
5. Only after the conflicts are resolved should f.3c add a per-slot typed
   serializer and parse-back tests. Whole-root f.4b graph/class admission,
   target 177 policy, native FreeCAD qualification and external J gates remain
   subsequent, distinct checkpoints.

This refines f.3c from “implement a candidate table” to “pin the candidate,
test source/model alignment, resolve wire conflicts, then enable only the
evidenced serializer profile.” It adds no PAR IDs or counts; no fixture,
dependency, CTest registration, support claim or external status changes.
All six J items remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. This review used
static primary-documentation and pinned open-source source only; no peer
runtime, native application, full suite or semantic CAD qualification ran.

## Broader 3D representation and consumer-boundary review (2026-10-15; research only)

This pass widens the comparison beyond “does the library know this entity
name?” to five non-interchangeable outcomes: byte/opaque retention, typed
structure and reference closure, explicit-coordinate geometry, kernel-level
solid/surface semantics, and acceptance by a named consumer configuration.
A pass at one level must not be reported as a pass at the next. In particular,
an entity count that survives conversion does not show that its geometry
payload survived, and a valid SAT/SAB byte stream does not establish a valid
body, unit scale, topology, placement, or history graph.

| Representation / peer evidence | What it establishes | Implementation-plan refinement |
| --- | --- | --- |

### Revised 3D implementation-ready slice order

This is a sequencing refinement within existing 3D and f.4 plan IDs; it adds
no finding, top-level subplan, ledger entry or status count.

1. **Preserve the 2D adapter boundary and make losses observable.** Keep new
   callbacks non-pure and typed 3D state orthogonal to existing 2D fields.
   Before adding a family writer, produce a fast disposition census by handle,
   entity/object kind, modelspace/block owner, payload presence, raw/typed
   route, and emitted/refused reason. A successful converter exit/entity count
   cannot mask empty or omitted geometry.
2. **Separate existing explicit 3D from modeler bodies.** Characterize current
   `3DFACE`, 3D `POLYLINE`/polyface, `MESH`, and `SURFACE` parser/writer state
   by format version and coordinates; add generated tests for WCS/OCS,
   topology/index winding, visibility/crease, units, nested INSERT transforms,
   and malformed boundaries. Preserve unsupported schemas opaquely where
   exact safe replay exists; otherwise fail closed with a precise loss report.
3. **Split ACIS by container and version.** For pre-AC1027 DXF/DWG, gate
   inline SAT/SAB body/chunk/profile preservation, version conversion and
   history references. For AC1027+, first decode and close the AcDs data
   storage owner/prototype/history graph and attach SAB to the right entity;
   then version-gate DXF inline serialization. Missing AcDs link, inconsistent
   `has_ds_data`/empty flags, unresolved owner or lossy version conversion
   must prevent publishing the target.
4. **Only then claim semantic solids/surfaces.** Require a source-native
   known-dimension manifest (bounds, units, volume/area, body count and needed
   topology/history properties) and exact input hashes checked by at least two
   independent kernel/parser lineages. A converter/parser's successful read,
   its own self-roundtrip, a mesh proxy, or a visualization is structural or
   display evidence, not independent semantics.
5. **Qualify named consumers last and narrowly.** Run FreeCAD Linux/Windows
   on the tracked eligible cohorts with the actual configured importer and
   converter. Keep stock FreeCAD's standard route distinct from its optional
   CAD Exchanger route; require mass/topology assertions only from a capable
   kernel. Never let external platform receipts promote unrelated J items.

This makes container-loss diagnosis and block-nested silent omission first
priority, moves exact AcDs linkage ahead of “ACIS writer” work, and reserves
long native/kernel validation for composed checkpoints. The faster per-slice
gates remain generated in-memory cases, structural output parsing, targeted
receipts and existing tracked samples; no new external DWG/DXF fixture or
dependency is introduced. The evidence manifest is
[`broad-3d-consumer-capability-review-2026-10-15.json`](docs/research/broad-3d-consumer-capability-review-2026-10-15.json).
The update is research-only: no code, tests, support matrix/count, or platform
receipt changed; J256/J260/J268/J284/J293/J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

### Revised qualification sequence and speed controls

1. **Keep the immediate step local and fast.** Finish the in-memory
   `blob01` page-chain control in `tests/graph_preservation_tests.cpp` before
   writer work: two logical pages, physically reordered segments, exact
   payload/handle join, unequal final page, suffix record, and bounded malformed
   page metadata. Use the existing CTest target and `lc3_compat_check`; do not
   run the full suite for this slice or add a drawing file.
2. **Use GDAL only at a composed carrier checkpoint.** If GDAL3.12+ is already
   installed, read a scratch modern DXF once with raw 3D extensibility enabled
   and blocks left unexpanded. Compare carrier bytes/hash and transform only;
   mark unavailable if the exact build/profile is absent. Do not make its
   geometric projection a pass criterion.
3. **Preflight the official Mac reader before requesting expensive semantics.**
   Verify CAD Assistant's app version, arm64 binary, ACIS component availability,
   accepted SAT/SAB inner revision, exact import source/hash, unit behavior,
   and whether its per-body property dialog can expose stable numeric results.
   If any is unavailable, record the precise blocker and continue local code;
   do not substitute a different platform or silently promote a same-kernel
   read.
4. **Run one bounded geometry control at a milestone, not every commit.** Use
   an independently authored, asymmetric, known-dimension body with explicit
   units and expected body inventory. Independently extract the exact payload
   from the tested DWG/DXF route, then compare body count, area, volume,
   centroid, extents and required topology properties. Feed direct SAT/SAB to
   the kernel reader to isolate model semantics; test the full DXF route
   separately to cover carrier parsing and the transform/history links.
5. **Preserve the two-kernel requirement.** CAD Assistant, `cq-acis`, and
   FreeCAD share OCCT geometry lineage; multiple tools on that kernel count as
   parser-path corroboration, not independent kernels. Ansys stays a candidate
   until kernel lineage and exact entitlement/platform are evidenced. The
   kernel gate remains open until two eligible semantic paths agree on a
   producer-authored expected result; native FreeCAD Linux/Windows remains a
   separate consumer gate.

This research corrects the earlier phrase “no selected macOS reader found” to
“an official macOS ARM64 reader candidate is documented but not yet qualified.”
It does not solve second-kernel independence or native platform qualification.

`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. Finding/subplan totals remain122/70;

## Implementation progress — generated AC1027 DataStorage page-chain regression (2026-10-15)

The local page-chain gap identified above is now covered in the existing
`libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests` executable. The control creates a bounded
AC1027 DataStorage section entirely in memory: a two-page `blob01` payload
whose logical page order is opposite physical segment order, with a 16-byte
first page and shorter final page; two data records; exact handle-based lookup;
payload bytes containing the ACIS marker; and a normal suffix record after the
blob descriptor. Positive assertions cover retained bytes, both page refs and
lengths, page-size fields, marker metadata, owner handle, and suffix payload.
Three malformed controls reject a noncontiguous page start, inconsistent
page-count header, and a descriptor reference to a non-blob segment; each
keeps the independent suffix record readable while disabling structural
replay. This is container assembly coverage, not a valid SAB or solid-semantic
fixture.

The strict test target and `lc3_compat_check` build; the single
`libdxfrw_graph_preservation` CTest passes. `git diff --check` passes. No
production parser change, new CTest, filesystem DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB fixture,
external binary, or full test suite was used. The next local ACIS work remains
direct-vs-blob boundary and multi-page malformed-boundary expansion, then
association through real producer records; external geometry semantics and
native FreeCAD qualification remain composed phase gates, not per-slice tests.
All six external-only J items remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; support counts and
claims are unchanged. Exact commands and assertion scope are recorded in

### Validation layers and implementation-ready comparator contract

The peer research shows that “supports 3D” is not one interoperable capability.
Every future test case must record five independent layers: (1) file/version
and entity/object shell inventory, (2) exact SAT/SAB carrier and transform
bytes, (3) AcDs schema/index/page/body/owner closure, (4) parser or kernel
geometry result, and (5) target-application open/save/render result. Each stage
must report `present`, `valid`, `unsupported`, `lost`, or `not-tested`; absence
must not be inferred from another stage. Kernel results additionally record
validity, solid/body count, volume, area, bounding box, units, transform,
healing/tolerance settings and any approximate/incomplete fallback. Raw-byte
identity is a preservation result, not semantic equivalence.

For speedy implementation, use a source-generated in-memory vector for every
container rule; use one scratch DXF generated locally from scratch for external
tag/carrier comparisons, with its generator and expected handle/body manifest
in source. Keep such generated files in a temporary directory and never add
peer/proprietary DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB files to the repository. The quick gate for a
slice remains the focused parser/test target plus compatibility compile; run
the full suite only at composed gates. Pin peer revisions/builds once before a
composed differential batch, not on every local slice.

This role matrix changes no support count or consumer claim. ACadSharp, IxMilia
and ezdxf are structural/carrier candidates only; ACadRust/OpenCADStudio share
one codec lineage; `ezdxf` has no 3D renderer; and no new exact-kernel semantic
oracle has been established. All six J items remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and
non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — ODA AcDs direct-record boundaries (2026-10-15)

Implementation commit: `3792076` (`Enforce DataStorage record boundaries`).

The S8.3 direct-record pass now uses each segment's ordered payload-local
offsets to compute a record's maximum readable span. Inline byte arrays above
the ODA `0x40000` limit are rejected; valid inline records must fit their
length prefix and payload before the next indexed record; the final record is
bounded by its segment end. Blob-reference fixed headers and full descriptors
are also bounded by the current record span, preventing descriptor reads from
crossing into a following record.

The in-memory graph-preservation test covers exact `0x40000` acceptance,
`0x40001` direct rejection, an inline payload crossing into its successor, a
blob descriptor crossing into its successor, valid suffix preservation, and
the prior reversed-physical-order two-page blob case. The library/test target
and `lc3_compat_check` build; the single `libdxfrw_graph_preservation` CTest
passes, and `git diff --check` is clean. No on-disk DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB fixture,
new CTest, dependency, full suite, or external program was used. This closes
only the local DataStorage record-boundary slice, not producer-profile coverage,
ACIS shape semantics, or native consumer support. Next ready work is
multi-page size/limit hardening, then real-record owner/body association and
same-version untouched-section passthrough. All six J items remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; support claims and 122/70 counts are unchanged. Receipt:
[`acds-record-boundary-fast-test-2026-10-15.json`](docs/research/acds-record-boundary-fast-test-2026-10-15.json).

## Implementation progress — ODA AcDs Blob01 page limits (2026-10-15)

Implementation commit: `630f66c` (`Enforce DataStorage blob page limits`).

ODA v5.4.1 §24.2.2.3–24.2.2.3.1 defines the storage boundary: arrays through
`0x40000` bytes use direct records; larger arrays use Blob01 pages, each capped
at `0xFFFB0` bytes. The parser now rejects blob descriptors at/below the direct
threshold, zero page counts, invalid nominal/final page sizes, zero-length
pages and referenced page lengths above `0xFFFB0`, preserving the following
independent record after malformed input. The generated in-memory positive
fixture uses two full `0xFFFB0` pages in reverse physical order, proving exact
page-limit acceptance and byte-identical logical reconstruction. Negative
vectors cover a page over the maximum, a blob at the direct-size boundary, and
zero pages; the existing page-order/start/count, wrong-segment, descriptor
overlap and suffix controls remain.

The focused graph-preservation test and `lc3_compat_check` build pass;
`libdxfrw_graph_preservation` passes 1/1 in 0.36 seconds and `git diff --check`
is clean. This is container assembly coverage only: payload bytes are
synthetic, not valid SAB and not evidence for a producer profile. No disk
fixture, dependency, new test registration, external executable, or full suite
was used. Remaining local work is hostile/overflow page-chain accounting and
same-page alias rejection, followed by real producer handle/body association.
Receipt: [`acds-blob-page-limits-fast-test-2026-10-15.json`](docs/research/acds-blob-page-limits-fast-test-2026-10-15.json).

## Deep ACadSharp / LibreDWG AcDs readiness research (2026-10-15; plan-only)

This follow-up re-resolved the ACadSharp Prototype1b reader/writer state and
read the linked design discussion instead of relying on feature labels or PR
titles. Sources: [ACadSharp #1152](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1152),
merged [#1154](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1154), the
[v3.6.51 release](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/releases/tag/v3.6.51),
the [#1156 Blob01 follow-up](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1156),
open writer candidates [#1150](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1150)
and [#1240](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1240), and LibreDWG's
open [#1411 AcDs-loss report](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411).
No peer was installed, built, or run; no customer corpus or external drawing
was used.

The key status correction is that ACadSharp #1154 is released, not merely a
candidate: v3.6.51 (`219e5fc`) includes the full DWG Prototype1b reader, with
v3.7.1 (`d7dc111`) as a later pin. The #1152 discussion challenged earlier
signature-scanning and fixed-schema assumptions. The maintainers/contributors
describe a direct segment payload-area anchor (#1146), subsequent full section
parsing, and comparisons over 423/hundreds of private DWGs. These are strong
implementation leads but remain report-only here; ACadSharp and libdxfrw both
use ODA as the format authority, and those private inputs are unavailable for
reproduction.

The #1156 Blob01 follow-up exposed an important API boundary: parsing the
section into document-level DataStorage is not sufficient unless
`ResolveDataEntry` reassembles page payloads and connects each one back to its
own `ModelerGeometry`. #1156 was closed after its author reported this whole
path working over their corpus. Preserve this as a reported peer result, not a
local pass. The just-completed source-generated raw-section path verifies
inline record capture and exact attachment to separate `3DSOLID` and `REGION`
callbacks; multi-page Blob01 parsing remains unimplemented in this local test
path and stays a distinct S8.2/S8.3 gate.

The writer evidence remains different: ACadSharp #1150 and #1240 are separate,
unmerged candidates. One author reports TrueView/ODA checks for #1150, while

### Readiness changes from the comparison

1. **Keep four observable layers separate:** (a) physical DWG section/page
   decode; (b) Prototype1b segment/index/schema parsing; (c) record payload
   assembly and exact modeler-owner association; (d) valid ACIS/SAB and
   consumer/kernel geometry. A pass at one layer never implies the next.
2. **Use identity, not order, as the primary link:** commit `8f5d927` now
   generates four records whose physical record stream, DataIndex row order,
   numeric handle order, and entity callback order are all distinct, then
   verifies exact per-handle payload attachment through the real block walk.
   Continue with multi-segment/page permutations and assert exact handle,
   length, offset, page index/count/start, and bytes; separately assert
   unresolved, duplicate, orphan, and wrong-owner dispositions. A fallback
   may be diagnostic-only and must not publish a guessed payload.
3. **Make Blob01 tests discriminating and bounded:** cover direct-record sizes
   `0x3ffff` and `0x40000`, the first blob-reference size `0x40001`, one-page
   and two-page payloads around the ODA `0xfffb0` page cap, reverse physical
   page order, one missing page, duplicate page index, wrong start/length,
   overflow, and a sentinel next record. The 80-byte ACadRust frame is a
   hypothesis to characterize, not a constant to hard-code into production
   without ODA or traced producer confirmation. Assert no partial publish and
   linear bounded work; avoid one CTest per scalar.
4. **Close passthrough/edit disposition:** the DXF path retains modern
   ACDSDATA raw groups separately from modeler entity fields. Its imported
   entity does not acquire per-entity `dataStorageData` merely because raw
   ACDSDATA was captured. Test edits against the typed DWG-source link (where
   it exists), and test raw DXF section replay as a separate opaque-preserve
   case. Missing typed link must not be described as a linked-payload edit.
5. **Protect 2D consumers:** keep all new `DRW_Interface` callbacks non-pure;
   preserve entity shell, handle, layer/owner, transform and raw carrier for
   LibreCAD and LibreCAD_3. FreeCAD stays a separately recorded converter
   route. Do not invoke an ACIS parser/kernel on the ordinary 2D consumer path.
6. **Keep the fast loop cheap:** each implementation slice uses the existing
   focused test executable and one focused CTest, plus strict `-Werror` build,
   `git diff --check`, and the LC3 compatibility check when interfaces change.
   Run broader/full CTest only at the planned composed checkpoint; native
   consumer and optional peer runs remain opt-in, exact-version gates. Generate
   all new sample bytes in memory or from source in temporary output locations;
   commit no external DWG/DXF fixtures.

## Implementation progress — AcDs hostile page-bound controls (2026-10-15)

Implementation commit: `c82b487` (`Test malformed AcDs page bounds`). The
existing source-authored two-page Blob01 fixture now has two additional
fail-closed checks: a page segment declared one byte shorter than its final
referenced payload byte, and a descriptor/page-header total set to
`UINT64_MAX` while actual page lengths remain bounded. Both reject the blob
record and preserve the later sentinel record. The maximum-total case verifies
bounded handling rather than triggering arithmetic overflow: with at most
1,000,000 pages and each page bounded by `0xFFFB0`, their sum is below the
64-bit limit.

### Implementation-ready selection and gates

1. Finish the local fail-closed DWG/AcDs work first: bind each fixed modeler
   raw frame to its typed peer and owner, reject body edit/deletion/handle or
   history remapping unless the complete reference/section closure is rewritten,
   and keep `REGION`, `3DSOLID`, and `BODY` profiles distinct. The raw-carrier
   reader must receive bytes selected by the validated entity-handle join, not
   a positional or guessed SAB record.

   feed the exact extracted SAT/SAB bytes to a pinned `cq-acis` build only after
   a cheap profile probe confirms its documented parser accepts the actual

   required topology records, a complete body inventory, conversion success,
   valid closed shapes, and independently authored analytic properties. If the
   profile is outside its admission table, record `NOT_APPLICABLE` rather than
   falling back or broadening the claim.
3. If independent-kernel evidence remains a goal, compare that OCCT-derived
   result only with the existing provisional OpenCAD analytic-kernel route, on
   the same exact carrier and a profile both fully admit. Pin both parser and
   kernel sources; require full-face conversion with no tessellation fallback,
   healing, omitted bodies, or incomplete flags. Treat any unsupported profile
   as `NOT_QUALIFIED`; do not count two OCCT frontends as two kernels.
4. Keep InventorLoader and commercial OCCT/CAD Assistant paths optional. First
   verify installability/entitlement, architecture, library/profile and exact
   build; separate native import, STEP translation, and direct SAT/SAB shape
   conversion in the evidence record. Their absence does not block local

   and the relevant open issue state at a pinned revision. Use one small
   known-good, source-generated profile plus a malformed-input control; record
   warnings, raw/typed/skipped outcomes, owner graph and output reopen. Do not
   make that peer a per-slice dependency or add its full suite to each change.
6. Per-slice implementation validation remains the affected strict build target,
   its focused fast CTest, `lc3_compat_check`, and `git diff --check`. Keep full
   peer/native/kernel comparisons for the already-planned composed checkpoint.
   Preserve the current explicit 2D callback and file-compatibility checks in
   every affected slice.

## Implementation progress — paired fixed-modeler raw replay (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

The fixed `REGION`/`3DSOLID`/`BODY` raw-frame writer now requires an explicit
typed `DRW_ModelerGeometry` peer. Before replay, it reparses the baseline raw
frame and rejects a changed typed common/modeler/body state, handle, owner,
layer/reference state, history link, DataStorage marker/record, unsupported
version, or mismatched raw bytes/bit-size. The one-argument raw replay API
continues to handle eligible non-modeler raw objects; it no longer authorizes
fixed modeler-frame replay. Generated in-memory controls cover unpaired
refusal, unchanged paired replay, edited body/layer/history/owner, remapped
handle and AcDs/DataStorage-backed state. This is a fail-closed opaque frame
replay boundary only; it neither rebuilds a modified ACIS body nor binds/rebuilds
an AcDs section, and it makes no semantic geometry claim.

Validation: strict `libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip` build and focused CTest
pass; `lc3_compat_check` is current; `git diff --check` passes. No DWG/DXF
fixture, full suite, peer, native CAD application, or dependency was added or
run. These source/test changes are local and uncommitted because Git metadata
is read-only; therefore this is not a committed progress checkpoint. Counts
remain 122/70, with all six external J items still `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. Next
bounded implementation work should resume the same-version raw-section
provenance/replay closure only after specifying how opaque AcDs records bind
to unchanged modeler entities; until then keep AcDs-backed modeler raw replay
refused and avoid treating section pass-through alone as geometry preservation.

## Implementation progress — validate raw AcDs section admission (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

`dwgWriter18::addRawDwgSection` now applies the existing `MaxBufferSize` cap
to the raw section bytes and, for nonempty `AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b` data,
requires `DRW_parseDataStorage` to finish without parse failure, structural
diagnostics, or a disabled replay disposition before retaining the section.
Empty AcDs remains valid per the existing reader contract. This prevents a
caller from asking the writer to emit a malformed one-byte AcDs payload as if
it were a pass-through section. It validates section structure only: it does
not yet prove every `ASM_Data` row is joined to the emitted modeler entity, or
that a copied SAB body represents valid geometry.

Generated local tests check malformed AcDs refusal, retain the zero-length
AcDs write/read and `readBuffer` case, and round-trip a compact nonempty
source-generated DataStorage container with one `segidx` segment and zero data
records. The nonempty case is reparsed after writing and its raw bytes must be
identical. It validates structural section admission/transport only; it has no
modeler payload and does not replace the still-needed entity-handle/payload/
owner closure test. No DWG/DXF fixture or dependency was added. That closure
is implemented in the following slice; generated record-order, decoy-marker,
and additional-schema adversarial vectors remain queued before broadening the
replay profile.

Validation: strict `libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip` build passes; focused CTest
passes 1/1 in 2.78 seconds; `lc3_compat_check` is up to date; `git diff
--check` and research JSON validation pass. No full suite, peer, native CAD,
or semantic kernel ran. Code/test/plan remain local and uncommitted because

J293, J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. Next: bind the raw AcDs section to
the emitted modeler entity, owner and payload; until that binding is complete,
keep storage-backed modeler replay refused.

## Implementation progress — close raw AcDs/modeler replay binding (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

The raw AC1027+ REGION/3DSOLID replay path now stages a bounded copy of the
typed modeler's DataStorage record identity and requires the unchanged raw
`AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b` section at finalization. Before section packing, the
writer reparses that exact raw section and requires a unique matching numeric
handle and canonical handle key, segment/schema index, retained payload bytes,
SAB marker metadata, and exactly one emitted modeler object. It also verifies
the object is present under its recorded model-space, paper-space, or user
block owner. Every marker-bearing record must be closed by one modeler peer;
missing sections, edited payloads, mismatched handle/schema, duplicate or
orphan marker records fail the write. The AcDs section is not reconstructed or
normalized, and this permits unchanged raw transport only, not modeler
geometry edits or support for unknown schema semantics.

The focused regression builds the nonempty AcDs record bytes in memory,
round-trips one linked modeler and section with exact payload/raw-section
equality, checks a post-parse attempted binding mutation is rejected, and
places an unrelated non-ACIS record before the modeler's DataIndex row to
prove the join is handle-based rather than encounter-order based. It verifies
that unrelated record remains byte-identical and unbound, while missing
section, wrong-payload, wrong-handle, wrong-schema, duplicate-handle,
decoy-marker, and orphan-marker cases fail closed. The SAB-looking token is
deliberately not geometric evidence. No drawing fixture was added or changed.

3. Check stages independently: source DXF parse; output DXF/DWG version and
   body inventory; exact payload and DataStorage-handle association; block

   surviving `REGION` or `3DSOLID` record with an empty body is a loss, not a

   geometry manifest to a pinned, eligible ACIS-capable reader from an
   independent parser/kernel lineage. Require successful complete body

   application's visual result or the same writer/reader pair. If only ezdxf
   or stock FreeCAD is available, mark semantic qualification `NOT QUALIFIED`.
5. Keep native FreeCAD qualification on the existing composed/manual gate,
   with Linux and Windows rows separated by exact converter and importer
   backend. Native FreeCAD may establish downstream acceptance for the
   specific translated entities it actually constructs; it cannot clear the
   ACIS semantic gate through the documented stock DXF importer. Preserve the

6. Retain the speedy validation cadence: affected strict target and focused

   the planned composed checkpoint; full suite, long fuzz/sanitizer, and

## Implementation progress — generated block-owned AcDs replay (2026-10-16)

The paired generated AC1027 modeler replay test now covers both modelspace and
user-block ownership. Modeler `0x708` remains in modelspace; modeler `0x704`
is emitted while writing the generated `LOCAL_ACDS_MODEL_OWNER` block. Both
records refer to schema index 7, while their AcDs section records are
permuted and checked against the same unchanged raw-section bytes. The
round-trip verifies exact record handle/key, schema index and payload, and
checks that the block entity and its `parentHandle` agree with the generated
block-record owner.

The test reserves source modeler handles `0x708` and `0x704` before
`dwgRW::write()`: block definitions allocate handles during `writeBlocks()`,
before fixed modeler frames are replayed, so omitting these reservations made
the generated block metadata collide with the source modeler handles. This
case exercises the existing pending-modeler owner validation and AcDs closure;
it changes no production behavior, adds no downloaded or committed drawing
fixture, and establishes no geometric or ACIS semantic support claim.

## Implementation progress — reject non-finite ACIS projections (2026-10-16)

The S3.7b local decoder slice now validates every numeric value it publishes
from the ACIS wireframe projection: resolved vertex/end-point coordinates,
analytic curve parameters, intcurve control points, surface parameters and

clears the output rather than returning a nominally successful partial graph
or poisoned bounding box. This deliberately leaves SAB count/terminal policy,

result, so stale geometry cannot survive a rejected decode. The test data is
synthetic and demonstrates defensive projection behavior only; it is not a
valid-body witness or an ACIS semantic test.

count (when usable), configured record ceiling, and a conservative lower bound
on records that can fit in the remaining bytes. This avoids geometric
top-level record-vector growth without trusting a corrupt header count as an

against an aggregate `maxTokenCapacityItems` ceiling. The outcome reports the
retained token-vector capacity items; generated exact-cap and one-under
controls cover this reserve budget. This bounds logical vector capacity, not
allocator overhead or process RSS.

uses the same explicit growth policy under `maxTypePartCapacityItems`, with a
reported peak and exact/one-under generated controls over a locally split
entity name. This closes the logical token/type-part vector-capacity items in
the current parser contract; implementation-specific allocator overhead and
RSS remain explicitly outside those counters.

the original carrier; decode no longer materializes a second candidate-sized
aligned vector. A locally generated 3-bit-shifted SAB control verifies exact
header, coordinate, consumed-span, and EOF behavior.

### Readiness changes and faster execution order

1. **Resolve the unit/frame contract before adding geometry normalization.**
   Trace the local producer/spec basis for the ACIS header unit factor and
   document whether `DRW_AcisBrep` coordinates remain modeler-native. Preserve
   the raw factor and source frame. Add source-authored in-memory SAB controls
   for supported unit values (including unitless only if the admitted profile
   permits it), with identical point coordinates but distinct metadata. Add
   separate DXF controls for absent/0/1/4 `$INSUNITS`, block units, and nested
   INSERT affine transforms. Assert round-trip tag/metadata preservation and
   composed transform order; do not assert a physical scale absent independent
   producer/spec evidence.
2. **Keep route identity in the test ledger.** For every composed DWG→DXF or
   DWG→FreeCAD case, capture input AC code, converter executable/version/hash,
   argv and exit code, output DXF AC code/hash, carrier family (inline SAT vs
   DXF ACDSDATA/SAB), FreeCAD importer backend/settings, and per-source-handle
   outcome (`typed`, `opaque-preserved`, `projected`, `rejected`, `omitted`).
   Require a newly created output file and inspect it; never use file existence

   separate from the FreeCAD/ODA ACAD2000 DXF route. Use ASCII and binary DXF

4. **Maintain a feature-direction matrix.** Keep explicit polygonal `3DFACE`,

   write, same-version opaque replay, cross-version conversion, projection,
   and native import as independent columns. An entity shell surviving with an

5. **Schedule slower qualification once per composed boundary.** Leaf slices

### Revised 7G.3d execution slices

These ordered slices remain under the existing 7G.3d owner; they do not add top-level subplans.

1. **7G.3d.1 — DXF parse.** Extend the existing in-memory AC1027 3×2 control with an independently authored literal tag stream: 2×2 merged range, text and block cells, non-default per-cell and virtual-edge flags, row/column sizes, a FIELD reference, empty text, legacy and 2007+ text encodings, a 251-character chunk boundary, and a following LINE sentinel. Run ASCII and binary reads. Assert each field at the TABLE callback, not only the final matrix. Reorder only fields documented as order-insensitive; retain sequence inside repeated cell/value records.
2. **7G.3d.2 — DXF write and reference graph.** Emit only the TABLE representation selected for the route. Stage the *T block/owning BLOCK_RECORD 343, TABLESTYLE 342 and any block-cell, attribute or FIELD handles; remap references once before publication. Before admitting group 344, close the FIELD object graph (360 child ownership, 331 object references, any object-valued cache data, owner/reactor/extension-dictionary edges) and resolve the local FIELD serializer's group-code mismatch against Autodesk's documented FIELD schema using literal controls plus a producer sample. In particular, the current typed writer emits group 4 for `m_formatString` and group 301 for `m_valueString`, while Autodesk documents 301/9 as format-string/overflow and 98 as format-string length; do not treat this as a supported profile until resolved. The 344 target does not encode the separate NOD→`ACAD_FIELDLIST`→FIELD membership or the FIELD's entity extension-dictionary owner: Autodesk's AutoCAD developer guidance says a drawing with fields has this NOD entry and fields are typically accessed from an entity extension dictionary. Preserve and validate those edges for the admitted AutoCAD profile; do not infer their omission or synthesize them without producer-backed rules. Add a TABLESTYLE writer for the explicitly supported field subset and fail closed on unmodeled fields. Verify literal emitted tags and ASCII/binary readback. Keep the INSERT fallback for legacy consumers, but do not serialize both paths as duplicate visible geometry.
3. **7G.3d.3 — Versioned DWG and TABLECONTENT object closure.** Treat AC1021 legacy TABLE plus linked TABLECONTENT/extension-dictionary data separately from AC1024+ embedded content. Read ODA §§20.4.96–20.4.101 and trace a valid sample’s type, handles and layout before undocumented `parseDwg` changes. Source-authored bytes may test bounded branches but cannot establish producer compatibility. The current code audit identified a false-completeness path: `parseTableCell()` drops linked-data and ATTDEF attribute tuples while its caller can still mark TABLECONTENT complete. Implement the following under this existing subplan; keep the valid TABLE entity prefix and *T/INSERT fallback available throughout:

A record-level semantic refusal must not become a file-wide read failure when the outer record boundary is sound.

The DXF parser records the active content slot when it reads that content's attribute count, retaining attributes from multiple contents instead of clearing earlier tuples. ## Implementation progress — ACAD_TABLE DXF parser field retention (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

The first ordered `7G.3d.1` parser slice is implemented. The DXF parser now
distinguishes row/column counts from the repeated cell-level group 91/92
values, treats 171 as the cell type, and retains the documented cell flag,
merge/autofit/span, override, virtual-edge, rotation, dimensions, FIELD and
block references, block attributes, text chunks, common cell text/color/border
overrides, table version/owner/style references, flow, margins, and title/header
suppression fields. Merged ranges are reconstructed from the origin cell and
bounded spans; malformed bounds/overlaps lower semantic completeness. Cell
text is accumulated in source order with a 16 MiB limit. Unmodeled table-level
style-role data (including 97/98/4 and role-specific override sets) is consumed
but marks the semantic snapshot incomplete instead of being attributed to the
last cell.

The existing named-object callback test now authors a 3×2 control in memory
and verifies ASCII parsing plus a binary DXF generated at runtime from the
same source-authored tag stream. It checks a 2×2 merge, a block cell with an
attribute, FIELD linkage, empty text, legacy and 2007+ text chunking at 250+1
characters, overrides, table dimensions/properties, a following LINE, and
deep-copy independence. An entity-boundary finalizer checks grid/cell/attribute
completeness; a negative control confirms unsupported row-role style data marks
the snapshot incomplete without corrupting the last cell. It adds no checked-in
drawing payload or CTest entry.
Autodesk's official [TABLE DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D8CCD2F0-18A3-42BB-A64D-539114A07DA0.htm)
is the source for the DXF tags; it does not qualify the separate DWG layouts.

ACAD_TABLE profile for AC1018+ DXF. It validates rectangular dimensions,
merged-range consistency, payload sizes and representable cell/table fields;
uses the legacy text groups before AC1021, extended cell flags/style fields
from AC1021, and data-version output from AC1024. Incomplete snapshots and
tables with unresolved TABLESTYLE, block-cell, FIELD, or unmodeled content do
not get serialized as an incomplete typed record. The adapter associates each
complete typed table with exactly one matching synthetic INSERT fallback by
source handle and insertion/owner identity, and writes the typed record in
place of that fallback, avoiding two visible copies. Incomplete snapshots keep
the existing 2D INSERT projection path.

range, a 251-character text chunk boundary, an empty cell, row/column sizes,
the following LINE sentinel, one typed TABLE callback plus exactly one 2D
fallback, and closed rejection of a TABLESTYLE reference that this slice
cannot yet emit. No checked-in drawing or CTest registration was added.

## Implementation progress — closed raw TABLESTYLE carrier route (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

The planned follow-up to the bounded ACAD_TABLE writer now closes a narrow
same-version TABLESTYLE carrier path. Before writing a styled table, the
adapter requires one rooted `ACAD_TABLESTYLE` dictionary, complete NOD/dictionary
ownership, unique one-to-one typed/raw TABLESTYLE identities, and matching
typed/raw group-3 descriptions. The dictionary key is treated as the
style identity and is deliberately not equated with group 3, which Autodesk
documents as a description. Each explicit group-7 text-style name must resolve
to exactly one retained `DRW_Textstyle`; unmodeled pointer-valued handle fields
fail closed. The extension-graph walk now
includes TABLESTYLE nodes and the named-object root is emitted whenever the
table's style graph is needed. TABLESTYLE identities are preallocated before
OBJECTS output; the in-memory ASCII/binary AC1027 round-trip confirms the
table's group 342, dictionary child, typed style, raw carrier, and owner links
agree after the handle changes. AC1027 ASCII/binary output also checks modern
cell style/override, text, RGB/fill/background and border fields; explicit
TABLE cell group-7 names must resolve in the emitted STYLE table. Missing
TABLESTYLE graphs, unresolved style names and a mismatched raw owner are
refused before output publication. A no-attribute block-cell subset now writes
group 171=2, remaps group-340 through the preplanned BLOCK_RECORD map, and
preserves group-144 scale; ASCII/binary readback verifies the cell target is
the emitted block record, while a missing target is refused before
publication. FIELD cells and block cells with attributes remain refused.
Generated ASCII/binary version controls
exercise AC1018 legacy text chunks, AC1021 modern cell overrides, and AC1024
data-version plus independently represented title/header suppression.

Fast checks passed: adapter, `dwg2dxf`, and `lc3_compat_check` strict builds;
`dwg2dxf_named_object_callback_storage`, `libdxfrw_extension_graph_limits`,
and `libdxfrw_sortents_adapter` CTests (3/3); `git diff --check`. Test drawings
are generated in the system temp directory and removed; no checked-in fixture,
CTest registration, full suite, peer runtime, sanitizer, or native CAD run was
added. The change remains local/uncommitted because Git metadata is read-only.

This is raw same-version publication, not a typed nested-row/cell TABLESTYLE
serializer or cross-version translator. It does not complete TABLESTYLE's

qualification remain separate. This supersedes the preceding `7G.3d.2`

### Implementation-readiness refinements

1. **Keep the layers explicit.** The 3D evidence row should separately record
   DWG section framing, AcDs index/segment interpretation, entity/owner join,
   exact SAB bytes, ACIS decode/topology, units and analytic measures, and
   native display/import behavior. A result at one layer cannot fill another.
2. **Use only an independent, exact-payload kernel route for geometry.** Before
   an optional `cadmpeg` run, lock its commit/release, toolchain, features,
   artifact hash and tested ACIS profile; pass only the bounded extracted SAB
   bytes. Include independently authored analytic dimensions and at least one
   curved case. If no eligible executable is available, record `NOT RUN` and
   keep local implementation moving; do not substitute OCCT core or a
   same-lineage reader.
3. **Make AcDs tests discriminate association strategies.** The local fast
   controls should assert the specification-defined index-to-payload and
   handle relationship, including non-positional order, and reject truncated,
   duplicate, overlapping, out-of-range or unresolved entries at the narrowest
   safe boundary. A marker-only scan may remain an explicitly labeled
   recovery diagnostic, never an exact join or success condition.
4. **Exercise a rendering-state sentinel at the composed native gate.** Along
   with shape count/validity and import diagnostics, inspect active viewport
   defaults and attempt one supported shaded/realistic transition. Use this
   to catch null/default graph state that does not appear in entity counts;
   do not infer that any particular peer's missing `VisualStyle`/`Material`
   objects caused its crash.
5. These are refinements to existing 3D, peer, and native-consumer owners; no
   finding or subplan is added. Totals remain 122 findings / 70 subplans.

## Implementation progress — bounded ACAD_TABLE block-cell ATTDEF closure (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

The active `7G.3d.2` slice now closes the DXF reference loop for a bounded
attribute-bearing block-cell profile. Adapter preflight admits only uniquely
resolved block definitions and ordered, unique ATTDEF handles owned by that
block, with bounded counts/text and safe failure on unresolved or foreign
references. TABLE writing remaps each ATTDEF handle and emits ordered group
331/group 300 pairs; group 179 is emitted as DXF's 16-bit integer in both
ASCII and binary output. The block writer now emits ATTDEF records, and the
in-tree DXF adapter retains ATTDEF callbacks inside their owning blocks so
typed readback can prove that each emitted reference targets the matching
definition.

The existing named-object callback fast test now builds its block/table graph
in memory, round-trips both ASCII and binary AC1027 DXF, and checks two remapped
attribute references, order/value preservation, and target ATTDEF ownership.
Negative controls verify that unresolved and wrong-owner references refuse
publication. No new drawing fixture or CTest registration was added.

Fast validation passed: strict build of `libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests`,
`dwg2dxf`, and `lc3_compat_check`; focused tests
`dwg2dxf_named_object_callback_storage`, `libdxfrw_extension_graph_limits`,
and `libdxfrw_block_owners` passed (3/3); `jq empty` accepts the adjacent
research receipt and `git diff --check` is clean. No full suite, sanitizer,
peer runtime, or native CAD application was run. This is a local, uncommitted
slice and not full ACAD_TABLE support: FIELD cells, unmodeled table content,
broader consumer semantics, and versioned DWG TABLE paths remain separate
work. No support claim or finding/subplan count is promoted; the six external
J items remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3 compatibility gates
remain unchanged.
