(`300="%lu2"`, `302="598880.00"`) and root cached text/length
(`301="598880.00"`, `98=9`). An earlier AutoCAD object-property dump shows
legacy root `4="%lu2"`, `301="1303.11"`, `98=7`. Both match ODA's
versioned interpretation and the local parser's split, including non-empty
format and cached text. Neither transcript contains group 9, so its overflow
semantics remain unresolved. The 2010 page says the test was performed in
AutoCAD 2010; these are user-posted `entget` transcripts, not downloadable source
drawings, and they omit exact product build, save target, and repeatable
producer artifacts. The Autodesk DXF reference continues to label 301/9/98 as
format/overflow/length. This is strong scoped corroboration, not grounds to
delete the Autodesk schema conflict or claim universal AutoCAD compatibility.

Implementation refinement: stop describing the prerequisite as “no producer
evidence.” Use the two observed profiles for literal parser/writer test
vectors; separate legacy group 4 from modern nested CadValue 300/302; preserve
root 301/98 as cached text only for the observed profile; test absent and
duplicated cache and section/record boundaries. For strings over 255 bytes,
test both group-9 interpretations as literal profiles, and leave the accepted
meaning unresolved until a producer witness includes overflow. The
next evidence gate is a reproducible producer-saved DXF or repeatable native
`entget` plus DXF save/reopen run with exact AutoCAD build/version, not another
local round-trip. Keep the Autodesk-published interpretation as a distinct
unqualified profile until that discrepancy is explained. The serializer must
gate group 4 against output version and must not emit modern FIELD output just
because the low-level writer test passes.

## Implementation progress — bounded TABLE/FIELD graph precheck (2026-10-16; historical snapshot, superseded locally)

### Implementation-ready refinements

1. **Reuse existing fast targets and isolate coverage gaps.** The current local
   suite has generated ASCII/binary controls for block ownership, HATCH zero
   coordinates, embedded ATTRIB/ATTDEF data, and sequence-following records.
   Before adding tests, map each proposed invariant to those controls. Add only
   the missing assertion to an existing test executable; add no fixture from
   the internet, new CTest registration, dependency, or per-slice full suite.
2. **Prioritize output validity and omission visibility.** On a touched route,
   first protect physical DXF framing and the INSERT/ATTRIB/SEQEND grammar;
   next protect per-block/per-layout child completeness and exact owner
   association; then harden damaged-reference continuation and record-local
   recovery. Report skipped/unsupported source identities explicitly, and
   refuse publication when output is structurally invalid or silently
   incomplete under the selected strict profile.

## Deeper GDAL DXF reader, direct-transcode, and 3D-consumer boundary review (2026-10-16; research only)

This pass widens the external comparison from “GDAL supports binary DXF and
can expose raw ASM” to the exact execution path used as evidence. It is based
on current primary project documentation, Autodesk's entity contracts, and a
cross-check against FreeCAD's current importer documentation and maintainer
report. No GDAL executable, native CAD application, peer library, or drawing
fixture was run or added by this research pass.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not establish | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GDAL [DXF driver documentation](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) and [current release page](https://gdal.org/en/stable/download.html) | The DXF feature reader supports Binary DXF beginning with GDAL 3.12. Its `3D_EXTENSIBLE_MODE` exposes raw `ASMData` and a 12-value affine `ASMTransform` for AC1027+ 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY/SURFACE; it does not construct OGR solid geometry. `INLINE_BLOCKS=NO` preserves block definitions/references as separate block features and fields. Separately, the docs state that plain `ogr2ogr out_ascii.dxf in_binary.dxf` with no extra parameter takes a direct-conversion path. The current release page lists GDAL 3.13.3 (2026-08-18). The documentation does not explicitly prove that the binary-reader, 3D-extensible-mode, and non-inlined-block settings compose on every build. | Never count the no-option binary→ASCII direct-transcode path as a GDAL read/semantic pass. Use read-only `ogrinfo` to check open/diagnostics and a small optional GDAL API probe when exact binary `ASMData` extraction is needed. Set `3D_EXTENSIBLE_MODE=YES`; set `INLINE_BLOCKS=NO` for block/owner cases and capture block-reference name, scale, angle and OCS placement separately from per-entity `ASMTransform`. Pin the exact GDAL version/build and record process result, warnings, entity handle/class, raw ASM byte length/hash, and transform. Probe model-space, block-owned, ASCII and binary AC1027+ cases independently; if a build cannot combine the documented capabilities, report that cell as comparator-not-applicable, not as a libdxfrw failure. Treat `ogr2ogr` direct conversion as a separate syntax/transcode check only. |
| Autodesk [3DSOLID DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm), [BODY reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-7FB91514-56FF-4487-850E-CF1047999E77.htm), [REGION reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-644BF0F0-FD79-4C5E-AD5A-0053FCC5A5A4.htm), and [SURFACE reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-BB62483A-89C3-47C4-80E5-EA3F08979863.htm) | These DXF entity contracts locate modeler data in repeated proprietary string groups 1/3 under `AcDbModelerGeometry` with group 70; 3DSOLID also defines a history-object reference. They do not define the internal ACIS/ASM shape grammar or prove the 3D kernel meaning of its bytes. | At the producer/writer gate, keep entity shell, modeler payload, group-350 history link (where applicable), outer entity identity/owner, and geometry interpretation as separately asserted data. Compare exact group-1/3 concatenation/order against an extracted raw carrier; do not substitute proxy-graphics group 310 or a generic raw-code dump for modeler payload. Keep history and AcDs linkage checks distinct. |
| FreeCAD [DXF importer documentation](https://github.com/Reqrefusion/FreeCAD-Documentation-Project/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.wikitext) and maintainer response in [FreeCAD issue #18454](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/18454) | The stock DXF importer is documented not to read ACIS/SAT blobs; the DWG route converts through DXF before importing. The maintainer explains that these proprietary modeler blobs are not a supported stock FreeCAD geometry path. This evidence is a consumer boundary, not proof that a produced DXF is malformed. | Preserve FreeCAD as a separately configured 2D DWG→DXF→consumer compatibility gate (including its selected converter and DXF importer). For 3D, classify stock-FreeCAD ACIS cells as `CONSUMER_NOT_APPLICABLE` unless the exact run uses a separately identified ACIS-capable plugin/converter; never lower the DXF/ACIS output result because the stock importer ignores that representation. Keep an independent shape reader/kernel gate for 3D semantics. |

### Faster implementation-ready validation sequence

1. **Finish the local fast carrier slice first.** Use an in-memory or
   temporary-directory control generated locally from a known SAT/SAB byte
   vector. For ASCII and binary DXF, assert record class/handle/owner,
   group-1/3 reassembly and order, optional 3DSOLID history reference, and the
   following-record sentinel. Do not download or commit a test drawing.
2. **Keep per-change validation cheap.** Each carrier change gets only the
   touched strict build, its existing focused fast test, the relevant
   compatibility compile/check, and `git diff --check`. Do not install GDAL or
   invoke an external reader on every implementation slice.
3. **At one composed DXF checkpoint, use an actual GDAL reader.** Optional,
   pinned GDAL 3.13.3 (or a later exact release recorded in the receipt) reads
   the original ASCII and binary AC1027+ outputs with `3D_EXTENSIBLE_MODE=YES`.
   Use `INLINE_BLOCKS=NO` for separate block-definition/INSERT accounting.
   Capture the exact per-handle/class ASM payload hash/length and 12-value
   transform, plus the INSERT block name/scale/angle/OCS placement when
   applicable. Run explicit model-space, block-owned, ASCII and binary probes
   first because the docs do not promise these option combinations. A same
   payload with a changed/missing handle, changed transform, missing `ASMData`,
   warning, or skipped entity is a carrier/association discrepancy; it is not
   a B-rep verdict.
4. **Label alternate paths correctly.** If testing the documented
   binary-to-ASCII shortcut, record it only as direct-transcode/syntax
   evidence. A byte-stable shortcut cannot replace the reader/API probe. Run a
   pinned strict parser/audit and the independent SAT/SAB reader/kernel only
   once after the related carrier and binding slices compose.
5. **Keep consumer and semantic gates separate.** Retain LibreCAD and
   LibreCAD_3 compatibility checks for the established 2D paths. Keep the
   FreeCAD stock importer in the 2D route; ACIS-aware plug-ins require a
   distinct version/profile/platform record. Neither GDAL raw-carrier output
   nor FreeCAD 2D acceptance can promote 3D semantic support.

This refines the existing DXF carrier, external comparator, and FreeCAD
consumer subplans; it adds no finding/subplan, fixture, dependency, CTest,
production behavior, or support claim. Totals remain 122 findings / 70
top-level subplans. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. Receipt:
[`deeper-gdal-dxf-reader-and-3d-consumer-boundary-review-2026-10-16.json`](docs/research/deeper-gdal-dxf-reader-and-3d-consumer-boundary-review-2026-10-16.json).

## Deeper/broader opaque DXF entity and handle-role review (2026-10-16; research only)

This pass extends the open-source comparison from generic unknown-record
retention to the exact safety boundary for replaying opaque graphical DXF
entities. It uses Autodesk's published DXF contracts, ezdxf's documented
storage/copy boundary, and ACadSharp's current unknown-object proposal as
implementation evidence. Peer issue status is not a local defect report. No
peer was built or executed, no native CAD application or external drawing was
used, and no code or fixture was changed by the research itself.

| Evidence | Establishes—and does not establish | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autodesk [ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-89A690F9-E859-4D57-89EA-750F3FB76C6B.htm) and archived [common object group-code reference](https://damassets.autodesk.net/content/dam/autodesk/www/developer-network/platform-technologies/autocad-dxf-archive/acad_dxf_2007.pdf) | Proxy entities carry an application-class ID, separate graphics/entity-data byte counts, ordered 310 chunks, and an optional sequence of object IDs using 330/340/350/360 terminated by 94=0. Common entity data also has an owner 330. The same numeric group code is therefore context-sensitive; a raw-record writer cannot classify every 330 as the logical owner or blindly translate all hex-looking values. The reference describes DXF structure, not arbitrary custom-entity semantics or whether a target CAD application has the required object enabler. | Keep common owner resolution separate from proxy object-ID sequences. Preserve each raw group occurrence/order and exact binary chunk bytes; validate 92/93 length/count relationships and the 94 terminator only for the recognized proxy grammar. Resolve each proxy object-ID edge by its context and role, and fail closed on a missing/ambiguous target. Never infer editable/visible custom-object semantics from preserved proxy graphics. |
| Autodesk [Extended Data (XDATA) reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A2A628B0-3699-4740-A215-C560E7242F63.htm) | XDATA is sequence-sensitive and allows repeated group codes; code 1005 denotes database handles that are translated with their corresponding entities during INSERT, XREF bind, and partial open. That behavior is distinct from arbitrary application values and from opaque ACIS/proxy payload bytes. | In raw entity replay, retain XDATA occurrence order and delimiters. Treat 1005 as a typed handle edge only in XDATA context, map it through the source→emitted identity table, and reject unresolved/colliding references before publication. Keep arbitrary 320–329 values literal and avoid a blanket hexadecimal-string remapper. |
| ezdxf [entity/TagStorage documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/concepts/entities.html) and [xref/copy limitations](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/xref.html) | ezdxf documents unsupported DXF entity retention as tag storage for export, while its xref module explicitly excludes unknown stored entities and ACAD_TABLE from copy/import. This shows a real implementation distinction between same-document preservation and graph-aware transfer. It does not establish libdxfrw behavior or guarantee that every opaque record remains valid after identity/owner changes. | Maintain separate outcomes for callback capture, same-document raw replay, owner/handle remap, cross-document copy, and typed semantics. The current fast lane should prove only the first admitted local replay profile; do not call it general unknown-entity support. Use ezdxf only as a pinned composed strict-reader comparison for the eligible generated subset, not as a semantic oracle for custom classes. |
| ACadSharp [open issue #1134](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1134), including the maintainer discussion | The proposal states that its unknown wrappers retain class references but not replayable raw object payloads; its maintainer identifies stale references after referenced records are removed/reassigned as a correctness risk. The issue proposes opt-in preservation and is not shipped implementation evidence. It concerns DWG opaque object frames, not DXF raw group records. | Use it as a failure-mode warning only. Keep DWG opaque-frame replay and DXF group-record replay as different format routes. Require identity/reference closure for either; a same-version condition alone does not make handle relocation safe. If a role cannot be enumerated or preserved safely, refuse the touched rewrite before replacing the destination. |

### Implementation-ready refinement to existing PAR-20/PAR-36, 7F, and 7G work

1. Extend the existing generated writer-ledger test (no new CTest) with one
   unknown raw entity in model space and one inside a named block, each
   interleaved with typed sentinels. Run ASCII and binary. Assert exact entity
   order, source identity→emitted identity, unique ownership, expected section,
   and complete output-ledger/readback parity.
2. Add one minimal `ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY` control only if the current capture

3. Add ordered XDATA with at least two 1005 references targeting existing
   emitted records and ordinary 1000/1002/1004 values as anti-alias controls.
   Assert 1005 remapping, literal preservation of non-handle values, and
   repeated-code order. Add missing-target and duplicate-source-handle

4. Preserve the typed sequence and logical owner boundary independently:
   an unknown record must not terminate iteration, consume the following
   entity, move between modelspace/named-block owners, or bypass the existing

5. Keep the implementation bounded: reuse `tests/wave1_tests.cpp` and

The route stays fail-closed if proxy-reference context, XDATA 1005 relocation,

## Implementation progress — PAR-126 direct DWG TABLE encoder refusal (2026-10-21; generated six-version fast slice, uncommitted)

The high-level `dwgRW::writeTable()` already refused TABLE output atomically,
but `DRW_Table` inherited `DRW_Insert::encodeDwg()`. A direct low-level caller
could therefore receive an INSERT/MINSERT-shaped frame with TABLE payload
silently omitted. ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.96 distinguishes the TABLE object layout
from its anonymous-block graphical representation and notes the R24
TABLECONTENT transition; there is not yet a complete local TABLE frame plus
linked-object writer to safely replace that path.

## Implementation progress — narrow raw DXF entity owner replay (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

Completed the first generated adapter round-trip slice prompted by the opaque
entity research. The existing block-owner control now imports one unknown
entity in modelspace and one in a named BLOCK body, each between typed
sentinels, then exports and parses the result in ASCII and binary. It checks
callback placement, source handles, logical owners, record order, and exactly
one retained instance. Raw handles are reserved before writer allocation so
typed records cannot take them. Owner resolution treats a unique source
BLOCK_RECORD as authoritative; a user record whose source handle happens to
equal a canonical target-space handle therefore retains its source name and
maps to that name's emitted record. When BLOCK_RECORD metadata is absent, the
DWG adapter's `BLOCK.parentHandle` remains a fallback; the BLOCK entity's own
handle is not an owner alias.

The serializer remains deliberately narrow: it requires a consistent self
handle and one resolvable owner for modern DXF, and rejects other translated
handle roles or handle-like data inside unqualified 102 application groups.
Thus this closes generated ordering/owner coverage and one allocator/mapping
edge case only. The research-plan follow-ups for exact writer-ledger/readback
set parity, recognized ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY 92/93/94 structure, XDATA 1005
remapping and atomic missing-target rejection, plus an independent strict
reader remain open. It does not establish proxy-entity semantics, general
unknown-entity support, DWG opaque-frame replay, or downstream CAD acceptance.

Validation: `cmake --build build --target libdxfrw_block_owner_tests -j4`,
`ctest --test-dir build -R '^libdxfrw_block_owners$' --output-on-failure`
(1/1), and `git diff --check` passed. Full test suites and third-party/native
comparisons were not run. No external fixture, new test registration,
dependency, support claim, finding, or subplan was added; totals remain 122/70.
LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3 compatibility is unchanged. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293,
and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The source/test changes remain
uncommitted because those paths already contain unrelated workspace changes.

## Implementation progress — context-aware raw DXF entity XDATA 1005 remapping (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

Implemented the ordered-XDATA reference step from the opaque-entity review.
Raw entity replay now treats group 1005 as a translated reference only after
an XDATA group 1001 and outside 102 application data. For nonzero references,
the configured resolver or current source/structural identity map selects the
final handle; the writer requires that target to be present exactly once in the
current emitted-record inventory before accepting the raw entity. Zero-valued
lexemes remain literal. The generic public `writeRawDxfGroups` signature is
unchanged; the raw-entity-specific owner/XDATA logic uses a private helper.

Generated ASCII and binary controls now put two mapped 1005 references in each
raw entity (one to its BLOCK_RECORD and one to a preceding typed LINE), retain
repeated group order and the 1000/1002/1004 XDATA values, preserve the
untranslated arbitrary code-320 value, and retain a `0000` handle spelling.
Negative cases cover an unresolved target, a duplicate raw source identity,
and a 1005 moved outside XDATA. Each rejection leaves a pre-existing
destination byte-for-byte unchanged. Because target closure is currently
checked at raw-record emission, forward references to records not yet emitted
fail closed; broad source-to-emitted planning or delayed resolution remains
necessary before claiming complete raw reference-graph replay.

Validation: strict builds of `libdxfrw_block_owner_tests`,
`libdxfrw_wave1_tests`, and `lc3_compat_check` passed. Focused CTests
`libdxfrw_wave1` and `libdxfrw_block_owners` passed (2/2), as did
`git diff --check`. Full suites, independent readers, native CAD, and fuzz
were not run. No external fixture, new test registration, dependency, support
claim, finding, or subplan was added; totals remain 122/70. LibreCAD and
LibreCAD_3 compatibility remains required, and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293,
and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. Changes remain uncommitted because the

## Implementation progress — validate recognized DXF proxy object-ID terminator (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

`DxfProxyCapture` now tracks whether the proxy object-ID section has ended.
Within the recognized proxy subclass, group 94 must parse as integer zero and
may occur only once. A later 330/340/350/360 handle group is rejected before
typed/raw callback publication. IDs before the terminator retain their code,
mapped handle role, value, and occurrence order. Group 94 remains subclass-
scoped: a nonzero 94 in a foreign subclass and proxy-looking tags inside 102
application groups remain opaque. A missing 94 is still accepted to avoid
turning this refinement into an unverified compatibility restriction.

The existing hardening executable now generates ASCII and binary
ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY and ACAD_PROXY_OBJECT records. Positive controls verify two
ordered ID references and valid 94=0; compatibility controls omit 94; negative
controls cover a nonzero terminator, a duplicate terminator, and an ID after
termination, all requiring refusal before either callback. A foreign-subclass
nonzero-94 control ensures the group code is not interpreted outside its
grammar. No fixture or test registration was added.

`libdxfrw_hardening` CTest ran, and all new proxy assertions passed, but the

publishing either callback. Autodesk's object-specific DXF table says group
92 is unused and proxy objects have no graphics; group 93 supplies the object
data bit size. The entity route remains unchanged: it uses group 92 for
graphics bytes and group 93 for entity-data bits.

## Implementation progress — separate DICTIONARYWDFLT parser state from completeness evidence (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

`DRW_DictionaryWithDefault` now represents two different facts separately:
`m_dxfDefaultEntrySeen` is the duplicate-code-340 guard for one parser walk,
while `m_hasDxfDefaultEntry` records persistent evidence that a nonzero default
edge was supplied. Copy construction/assignment reset the parser-walk guard
but preserve completeness evidence; explicit reset clears both. Consequently,
a copied partial model can begin a fresh parse without accepting a duplicate
340 in the same source record, and a complete adapter-owned copy still passes
`hasCompleteDxfPayload()`.

The existing hardening controls verify copy/assignment parser-state reset.
The named-object adapter regression verifies the valid callback copy remains
complete, reset clears only that object's evidence, malformed missing/duplicate
340 records are rejected, and the following DICTIONARYVAR sentinel survives.
The AcDs hardening control was also corrected to match its intended scope:
BODY still receives exact handle-keyed carrier association, but its seeded
modeler version/empty state remains unchanged because the reviewed ODA mapping
does not qualify BODY for the REGION/3DSOLID normalization. This test-only
correction removes an invalid expectation rather than broadening production
semantics.

## Implementation progress — exact proxy-DXF bit-count span (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

The recognized proxy-payload validator now requires each bit-sized payload to
occupy exactly `ceil(declared bits / 8)` bytes. This removes acceptance of a
whole extra byte when the declared size is already byte-aligned. Generated
ASCII and binary cases cover both `ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY` and `ACAD_PROXY_OBJECT`:
the 16-bit/three-byte surplus is rejected before either typed or raw callback
publication, while existing 9-bit/two-byte and 16-bit/two-byte controls still
pass. No downloaded or committed drawing fixture, new CTest, or dependency was
added.

## Implementation progress — versioned FIELD value wire slice (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

Implemented the first profile-specific FIELD writer changes supported by the
producer observations. For AC1018 and earlier supported FIELD output, the
writer emits root group 4 plus the typed evaluated value and root 301/98 cache,
without the R2007+ `ACVALUE_END` marker. For AC1021+ output, it omits legacy
group 4 and places a compatible root format string in the nested CadValue
format (group 300); conflicting root/CadValue formats refuse before bytes are
published. A modern CadValue string in an older target is also refused rather
than silently dropped. Legacy scalar CadValue emission is now enabled where
the typed payload is supported.

Generated ASCII/binary writer literals assert both profiles, including the
AutoCAD 2010 nested 300/302 value, duplicate root cached text/length, modern
delimiter, legacy delimiter omission, root-format promotion, and transactional
negative cases. The named-object parser test now verifies nested modern
format/value fields and also parses a locally authored legacy AC1018 FIELD
with group 4 format, a typed double cache, root 301/98, and a following
DICTIONARYVAR sentinel through ASCII and binary paths.

Validation passed: strict builds of `libdxfrw_wave1_tests` and
`libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests`; direct Wave 1 test executable; focused CTest
`libdxfrw_wave1` plus `dwg2dxf_named_object_callback_storage` (2/2);
`lc3_compat_check` (no work required); and `git diff --check` on touched
source/test/plan paths. No full suite, peer/native CAD, sanitizer/fuzzer,
external fixture, dependency, test registration, or adapter export enablement
was added. Group-9 overflow and >255-byte string handling remain unresolved;
the independent producer-file/native reopen gate is still outstanding.
`dx_iface::fileExport()` remains fail-closed for FIELD/FIELDLIST and TABLE
group-344. No support claim or external-J disposition changes; totals remain
123 findings / 71 top-level subplans and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The shared worktree stays uncommitted because

digest of the selected compiler-relevant environment and the resolved compiler
path and binary. Configure, build, CMake metadata queries, and hidden file-API

and binary are checked against that identity, and the compiler binary is

The project's provenance note says it did not use LibreDWG source, but this is a project-level statement rather than an independently audited clean-room determination. | Keep `dwg-rs` as a surfaced *separate implementation* candidate for a narrow, optional DWG container/object/record-boundary differential—not as a production alternative, semantic oracle, or coverage score. Do not cite its README aggregate as current parity evidence. If used, pin source commit, crate/toolchain/dependency identity, execute the coverage tool, preserve its emitted raw report and input manifest, and compare only exact overlapping, already-admitted local inputs. If its bundled report cannot accept those paths, use a minimal pinned harness to query the same reader API. Record per-version and per-family decoded/skipped/errored counts plus how many records were actually boundary-checked; compare matching denominators, not cross-corpus percentages. Treat writer assembly as an optional discovery-only output route requiring independent strict/native reopen, not as support evidence. Treat its strict endpoint rule as a test-design lead, not an instruction to change libdxfrw's established record-level soft-error policy. |
| [`Open CAD Studio` README](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/README.md) and [`ACadRust` README](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust) | Open CAD Studio currently advertises native DWG/DXF read/write through R14–2018, 3D modeling, kernel-backed operations, and ACIS-entity tessellation. Its own page says the project is under active development; ACadRust lists Open CAD Studio among its users and advertises the shared file engine. These are current application/project claims, not an independent parser run, AutoCAD acceptance record, or exact-solid witness. | Retain Open CAD Studio in the existing ACadRust lineage. At the existing one-time consumer checkpoint, pin the app release/build and exact codec/kernel dependency revisions, requested and actual file version, raw input/output hashes, notifications, repair/synthesis/loss disposition, and fallback/incomplete tessellation status. App open/render is consumer evidence only; it cannot independently vote for DWG parse correctness or promote ACIS/B-rep support. No per-slice run or mandatory application dependency. |
| [`uncad` README](https://github.com/iyulab/uncad) and its [`undxf` route](https://github.com/iyulab/undxf) | The current project is explicitly read-only: DWG parsing uses LibreDWG through FFI, while DXF parsing uses the separate `undxf` crate; its output is a model/JSON/SVG/PNG projection. The model exposes header unit presence, but the wrapper does not write or convert CAD files. | Preserve the route-specific lineage already recorded: `uncad` is not a second DWG parser vote; `undxf` is at most the optional DXF parser/projection candidate. A visible model/render result does not qualify source ownership, writer fidelity, or ACIS semantics. No added gate is needed. |

## Deeper effective compiler and CMake input-surface review (2026-10-16; research plus local builder slice)

The remaining 7AG.4 gap was re-audited against primary compiler/build-system
documentation. The source review establishes concrete hidden-input classes;
the local implementation closes only the safe ambient-override subset. It
does not claim a complete effective-toolchain closure.

| Source | Confirmed behavior | Local policy consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GCC [environment variables](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Environment-Variables.html) and [directory options](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Directory-Options.html) | `GCC_EXEC_PREFIX` affects compiler subprogram, header, and library lookup; `COMPILER_PATH` changes subprogram lookup; `LIBRARY_PATH` changes linker search; `CPATH` and language-specific include variables inject header search paths. | The controlled build rejects these variables instead of merely hashing their strings. The direct-option include-root allowlist alone could not observe their effective directories. |
| Clang [environment variables](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/CommandGuide/clang.html) and [configuration-file docs](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/UsersManual.html#configuration-files) | `CPATH`, `C_INCLUDE_PATH`, `CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH`, Objective-C variants, `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET`, config files, and `CCC_OVERRIDE_OPTIONS` affect compilation/search. `--no-default-config` disables the default config-file search. | Existing `CCC_OVERRIDE_OPTIONS` and default-config controls remain; ambient include search overrides now fail closed. `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` and SDK/sysroot/toolchain contents remain identified but not fully bound, so the contract stays partial. |
| Microsoft [CL environment variables](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/reference/cl-environment-variables) and [command-line build environment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/building-on-the-command-line) | `CL` prepends and `_CL_` appends compiler arguments; `INCLUDE` adds header search roots; `LIB` and `LIBPATH` affect library lookup; a developer prompt sets a larger platform/tool environment. | `CL`/`_CL_` and `INCLUDE`/`LIB`/`LIBPATH` are rejected in controlled builds until a reviewed Windows profile can content-bind the selected SDK/toolchain roots. This intentionally withholds qualification from an unreviewed developer-prompt environment; it does not change ordinary project builds. |
| CMake [project initialization](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/command/project.html) and [build-variable guide](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/guide/user-interaction/index.html) | `CMAKE_PROJECT_INCLUDE*` hooks and `CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` can execute external CMake input during `project()`; `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` and `CMAKE_MODULE_PATH` alter package/module resolution; a toolchain file can set target/system/sysroot behavior. | Controlled source-environment project-include, prefix/module, and toolchain channels are rejected. Parent cache `CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` and `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_EXTERNAL_TOOLCHAIN` are also rejected instead of forwarding arbitrary setup into the fresh qualification build. |

### Implementation progress — implicit search/toolchain override rejection

Extended `tools/build_semantic_adapter.py`'s closed controlled-environment
policy. It now rejects known ambient include/subprogram/library search paths,
MSVC's environment-supplied include/library roots, CMake prefix/module and
project-include environment inputs, and toolchain-file/external-toolchain
environment settings. Parent-cache admission additionally rejects an active
`CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` or `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_EXTERNAL_TOOLCHAIN`. Diagnostics
name the rejected variable only; secret values and private paths are not
printed. All such names already have test coverage through the environment
rejection loop, and parent-cache self-tests cover both newly rejected
toolchain channels.

Validation passed: `python3 -B tools/build_semantic_adapter.py --self-test`,
`python3 -B tools/run_qualified_differential_v2.py --self-test`, and Python
syntax compilation of both tools. No full suite, qualification pair, external
peer, fixture, or support claim was produced. `implicitConfiguration` remains
`partial`; only the named override channels are screened. Default compiler
resource files and subprocesses, system SDK/sysroot/header/library content,
and native Windows/macOS route behavior still need an explicit content-binding
or supported-profile design. Receipt:
[`deeper-effective-compiler-and-cmake-input-surface-review-2026-10-16.json`](docs/research/deeper-effective-compiler-and-cmake-input-surface-review-2026-10-16.json).

### Implementation progress — bind transitive external compiler header inputs

Primary-source review confirms that CMake's compile database records exact
compiler invocations for project translation units, but is implemented only
for Makefile and Ninja generators and does not work well with unity builds.
The GCC dependency option `-M` emits direct and transitive included-file
dependencies, including system headers and forced includes; `-MM` would omit
system headers, so it is not used. See CMake's
[`CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS`](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/variable/CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS.html)
documentation and GCC's
[`-M`/`-MM` dependency options](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Preprocessor-Options.html).

The controlled target and standalone builders now request the compile
database and, for single-config POSIX GNU/Clang-family builds, select adapter
and library translation units from the CMake codemodel and scan the matching
recorded compiler invocations. The receipt binds reached files outside the
package snapshot and fresh build tree by absolute path, byte size, and SHA-256;
it rechecks them after the build to detect changes between dependency
discovery and compilation. The v2 receipt validator verifies the typed closure
and its digest. Pair admission compares build-profile cores and requires equal
content for shared external dependency paths; it permits different source
versions to include different sets of system headers. The isolated builder
self-test includes a known external header, Makefile depfile escaping,
post-build header-change rejection, and target/standalone profile comparison.
Windows, multi-config generators, and unrecognized compiler families carry
an explicit unavailable status instead of inferred completeness.

Validation passed: `python3 -B tools/build_semantic_adapter.py --self-test`,
`python3 -B tools/run_qualified_differential_v2.py --self-test`, Python syntax
compilation, and `git diff --check`. This is an input-binding improvement,
not a completed compiler contract: GCC subprocesses/specs are bound only when
the driver reports an absolute resolvable path, specs `%include` dependencies
are not traversed, and native GNU execution has not been run here. Compiler
built-in/resource/config files beyond captured headers, SDK/sysroot metadata
and contents, dynamic/static linker inputs,
MSVC developer-environment closure, and native Linux/Windows consumer
qualification remain unresolved. `implicitConfiguration` stays `partial`,
paired receipts remain ineligible, and no DWG/DXF fixture, support claim, or
external J disposition changed. See
[`compiler-dependency-closure-slice-2026-10-16.json`](docs/research/compiler-dependency-closure-slice-2026-10-16.json).

### Implementation progress — bind GCC-reported subprocesses and specs

GCC's official developer-option documentation states that `-print-prog-name`
reports the selected program path; the official specs documentation explains
that the driver uses specs to choose compiler subprocesses and their options,
and that specs can override those decisions. See
[`-print-prog-name` / `-print-file-name`](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Developer-Options.html)
and [GCC spec files](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-12.4.0/gcc/Spec-Files.html).

For CMake's `GNU` compiler ID, the builder now asks the selected driver for
`cc1plus`, `as`, `collect2`, and `lto-wrapper`, and for an external `specs`
file. It hashes only paths the driver reports as absolute files; it does not
guess by resolving a bare name against the builder's `PATH`, since that could
identify a different binary than GCC's private search selected. The content
identities are part of `toolBinaries`, so the existing before/after-build
binary rechecks apply. Non-GNU profiles record these roles as unavailable
(Clang/MSVC frontends remain represented by their already-bound driver).
Receipt validation accepts both the previous six-role map and the expanded
shape; malformed path/digest pairs are rejected.

Validation passed: the builder's dependency-free mocked path-resolution
controls and two actual controlled target/standalone builds, the v2 runner
self-test for current and legacy nested tool-binary shapes, Python syntax
compilation, and `git diff --check`. The host selected AppleClang, so the GCC
path was contract-tested but not executed with native GCC. This improves
content binding but does not close compiler/runtime libraries, default specs
that GCC does not report as an external file, full SDK/sysroot or linker
closure, or native GNU/MSVC routes. `implicitConfiguration` remains `partial`
and receipts are still ineligible. Full receipt:
[`compiler-dependency-closure-slice-2026-10-16.json`](docs/research/compiler-dependency-closure-slice-2026-10-16.json).

### Implementation progress — bind selected build executable identities

Expanded the controlled driver context with the selected CMake executable's
invoked path and binary digest; the builder rechecks CMake alongside the C++
compiler around configure, hidden File API reconfigure, and build operations.
The generated CMake identity now records and validates tool path/digest pairs
for CMake, the generator build program, compiler, compiler linker, archiver,
and ranlib where available. The build program and configured tool identities
are rechecked immediately before and after each actual generator build. New
receipts carry this typed identity; the v2 validator accepts both that shape
and the prior frozen shape without weakening pair eligibility.

Validation passed: the builder self-test (including two controlled fresh
builds and target/standalone parity), the v2 runner self-test (new, malformed,
and legacy tool/context shapes), and Python syntax compilation. The profile
remains `direct-options-only` / advisory: this does not hash compiler-internal
subprograms or resources, SDK/sysroot trees, system headers/libraries, or
prove native Windows/macOS routes. No pair, test fixture, support claim, or J
disposition changed. Full receipt:
[`deeper-effective-compiler-and-cmake-input-surface-review-2026-10-16.json`](docs/research/deeper-effective-compiler-and-cmake-input-surface-review-2026-10-16.json).

## Apple dyld runtime image-UUID closure implementation slice (2026-10-16)

Advanced the remaining system runtime-input work with a host-supported
read-only inspection route. On controlled Darwin Clang/AppleClang builds, the
builder hashes and invokes the fixed `/usr/bin/dyld_info` tool for the adapter's Mach-O load commands, recursively
walks direct/transitive load and re-export edges without dropping batch
remainders, records image UUIDs by architecture (including dyld shared-cache
images), and hashes candidate SDK text-stub (`.tbd`) files only for direct
adapter-linked install names. Transitive images retain UUID/edge evidence but
do not inflate the direct-link stub inventory. It binds the resulting graph to each side's
executable digest, rechecks the tool and captured stub bytes, and records the
`dyld_info` binary identity. The validator
requires exact graph/tool/stub parity across target and standalone while
normalizing only the intentionally side-specific executable digest. Older
receipt shapes remain accepted for historical replay.

Validation on 2026-10-16:

- Python syntax compilation, builder self-test, and v2-runner self-test passed.
- Synthetic runtime-profile controls reject stale graph digests, reject a
  target/standalone image-UUID mismatch, and allow the target and standalone
  executable digests to differ while requiring their runtime graph to match.
- Fresh target and standalone Release builds and artifact-checked receipt
  validation passed. Both observed 617 runtime image nodes, 8,357 load/re-export
  edges, maximum depth 16, and matching node/edge digests. Three private or
  platform-internal image names could not be resolved from the active dyld
  cache, and seven images lacked a matching SDK `.tbd` candidate.
- Pair qualification still refuses at `direct-options-only` /
  `implicitConfiguration: partial`. The profile remains explicitly `partial`
  with reason `link-stub-selection-not-proven`: UUID identity is not a byte
  digest of the runtime image, a candidate `.tbd` match is not proof that the
  linker consumed that exact stub, and this is not a native GNU/MSVC check.

This advances but does not close full effective link/runtime closure. The
unresolved platform-private images, unmatched stub candidates, runtime image
bytes/shared-cache identity, linker-consumed stub proof, SDK/sysroot closure,
and native GNU/MSVC profiles remain open. No parser change, fixture,
dependency, CTest registration, support claim, or external-J transition was
added. Totals remain 123 findings / 71 top-level subplans; J256, J260, J268,
J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. Receipt:
[`apple-runtime-uuid-closure-2026-10-16.json`](docs/research/apple-runtime-uuid-closure-2026-10-16.json).

## Deeper/broader CMC color-route and peer-release review (2026-10-16; research/source audit)

This review checks a current DWG peer report, current peer release notes, the
local CMC decoder-to-DXF LAYER route, and the DXF LAYER color contract. It
found one actionable cross-route validation gap that belongs in existing
PAR-66 / 7AN, not a new finding. The peer report is evidence of a credible
failure mode, not an independently reproduced result: its 43-file / 5,833-
layer measurements were not rerun here. Local statements below are source
audits only; no binary was converted and no CAD application's native accept or
render behavior was checked. The test-vector field sequence below is checked
against ODA §2.11; it remains a generated field-level control, not a complete
DWG-object integration or independent producer sample. ODA specifies the
R2004+ CMC BS color index as “always 0,” so nonzero BS must not be varied as
though it were a valid method/index discriminator. No external drawing or
fixture was added.

| Evidence | What it establishes (and what it does not) | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| [LibreDWG issue #1415](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1415), still open at review time | Reports R2004+ CMC read conversion conflating the stored CMC method/index, including palette-collision damage for `0xC3` and low-byte-as-ACI output for `0xC2`. The reporter says a first index guard was ineffective because that value was vestigial at the later conversion point. Its example, measurements, and comparison against ODA are peer-reported, not reproduced by this task. | Do not copy a guard by name alone, reverse-map truecolor through an ACI palette, or infer correctness from group 420 alone. Test method and serialized DXF groups end to end. |
| Local `getCmColor`, `DRW_Layer::parseDwg`, and `writeLayer` (`src/intern/dwgbuffer.cpp:1063-1107`, `src/drw_objects.cpp:3924-3933,4005-4007`, `src/libdxfrw.cpp:3948-3951`) | Source audit confirms the local decoder distinguishes `0xC2` RGB (retains RGB and returns sentinel 256) from `0xC3` indexed color (returns low-byte ACI), and the LAYER object retains both color and signed on/off state. The writer emits LAYER group 62 directly from `ent->color`; an RGB-only color can therefore reach the DXF writer with 256, while truecolor group 420 is separately emitted. This is a source-confirmed route, not proof of runtime output. | Extend PAR-66 / 7AN to test a real generated R2004+ CMC-to-LAYER-to-DXF route. Resolve the group-62 fallback policy: serialize a valid conventional layer ACI alongside group 420, or reject atomically with an explicit diagnostic. Never emit layer group 62 as 0 or 256 for a truecolor-only LAYER. Preserve sign/off semantics. |
| [Autodesk LAYER DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D94802B0-8BE8-4AC9-8054-17197688AFDB.htm), [AutoLISP truecolor dialog](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2017/PTB/AutoCAD-AutoLISP/files/GUID-E6FF435F-9E66-4F37-8770-2E3FB87B8E0B.htm), and [ezdxf layer-table API](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/dd7f6cc34983fdbf0b2b910f2497e0720d06dd16/src/ezdxf/entities/layer.py) | Autodesk defines group 62 as the layer color number and negative as layer-off. Its truecolor dialog returns group 420 exact RGB plus group 62 as the closest matching ACI; a companion Autodesk API note says truecolor wins if 62 and 420 conflict. The reference does not prescribe a universal nearest-color metric. ezdxf's layer-creation API independently validates ACI inputs, but is not normative or native acceptance evidence. | For C2 truecolor-only data, emit exact group 420 (when target version supports it) and compute only a compatibility/fallback ACI for group 62 from the existing palette; never present that fallback as the source ACI. Preserve explicit C3 ACI verbatim. Keep native app qualification distinct. |
| [LibreDWG 0.14.1 release notes](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | Current notes list R2004 DWG writing and DXB support, but state direct R2007 DWG encoding is not supported and falls back to R2010; release notes also include security fixes and broad CMC changes. | Refresh the existing route/direction/version comparison matrix: do not compress “DWG write support” into one Boolean or mistake DXB/DXF coverage for DWG parity. Do not port unrelated writer behavior without local compatibility evidence. |
| [ACadSharp v3.7.16](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/releases/tag/v3.7.16) and [v3.8.0](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/releases/tag/v3.8.0) | v3.7.16 (Sep 18, 2026) lists DXF decimal precision support, tables over 32,767 entries, WIPEOUTVARIABLES, context-data writer work, and several entity/object fixes. v3.8.0 (Sep 21, 2026) lists InternalsVisibleTo assembly visibility only. These release notes identify useful field-specific probes, not semantic equivalence, broad parity, or ACIS/SAB writer capability. | Pin the version and field before using ACadSharp as a differential oracle; prioritize precision serialization and large-table boundary cases already owned by local plan slices. Keep comparison narrow and reuse current fast test owners. Do not infer unrelated entity or solid support from release activity. |

### Implementation-ready delta for PAR-66 / 7AN

1. Extend the existing fast generated-object/adapter test owner; do not add a
   CTest target or commit external DWG/DXF fixtures. Build complete R2004+
   CMC bit vectors using the ODA §2.11 field order: BS color index fixed at 0,
   the 32-bit CMC word, and raw flags byte. Exercise `0xC3000068`
   (indexed ACI 104, chosen to exercise a palette collision), `0xC30000FF`
   (indexed ACI 255), and `0xC200A600` (RGB `00A600`, blue/low byte zero).
   If a nonzero BS control is useful, label it malformed-input coverage only;
   do not use it to support valid-file behavior or method selection.
2. Assert CMC method semantics before writing: for C3, derive the ACI directly
   from the low byte of the 32-bit CMC word (104 and 255 in these vectors),
   never from the separately read vestigial index or an RGB-palette reverse
   lookup; for C2, preserve exact `00A600` RGB and do not interpret its low
   byte as ACI.
3. For a C2 truecolor-only LAYER (`color=±256`, exact `color24` present),
   compute a deterministic closest ACI from `DRW::dxfColors[1..255]` for the
   group-62 compatibility fallback; match LibreCAD mainline's
   `LC_ColorNumbers::colorToNumber` (`../LibreCAD/librecad/src/lib/engine/lc_colornumbers.cpp`)
   Manhattan-distance selection and lower-index tie behavior. Preserve the
   exact group 420 value for targets that support it and preserve signed
   layer-off state. On pre-AC1018 targets, group 62 is a deliberately lossy
   fallback because truecolor group 420 is unavailable. Never reinterpret
   this generated fallback as source ACI, remap explicit ACI/C3 values, or
   emit group 62 values 0 or 256 on LAYER. Reject malformed zero or invalid
   color/lineweight values before publication.
4. Inspect exact ASCII and binary DXF group-code/value output before ordinary
   readback, then read the result back to assert group 62 and 420 semantics.
   Include destination-preservation and next-record framing checks for the
   refusal path. Keep this a focused test; schedule full suites only at the
   already-defined integration checkpoints.
5. Record evidence as source-confirmed / test-confirmed / native-qualified
   separately. No support-matrix claim is promoted by peer issue text or an
   ezdxf validator alone. Finding totals stay 123 / 71; J256, J260, J268,
   J284, J293, and J295 stay `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

When group 350 exists, validate/remap its target and report unresolved history independently; do not make optional history presence a proxy for body validity or reject geometry-only import solely because no history object exists. |

Record unsupported records and byte disposition. Do not treat successful load/export or its flat-face mesh as arbitrary ACIS preservation, curved-solid semantics, or an independent kernel result. Keep stock FreeCAD/LibreCAD consumer results and an external semantic-kernel gate distinct. |

This pass cross-checks Autodesk's current header/system-variable contracts,
ezdxf's documented interpretation, and FreeCAD's importer controls against
7BJ.4 and the 3D transform/readiness owners. It sharpens the distinction
between preserving drawing metadata and applying a scale in a consumer; no
generated local route was run during this research pass. (The later local
serializer regression is recorded separately below.) No native CAD or peer
runtime was run, no drawing was downloaded, and no fixture, dependency, or
test registration was added.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|

When the source or target value is zero, separate registry-held source/target defaults can participate in insertion scaling. Those installation defaults are not serialized file-header values, and this documentation does not define a universal global rescale when opening a file. | Keep file metadata serialization separate from host insertion behavior. In native insertion/attach qualification with explicit `INSUNITS=0`, bind the effective source/target defaults and operation. Do not encode those profile defaults into libdxfrw's file read/write or geometry coordinates. Preserve omission separately from explicit0. |
| Autodesk [`MEASUREMENT`](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2027/ENG/AutoCAD-Core/files/GUID-1D074C55-0B63-482E-8A37-A52AC0C7C8FE.htm) and the official [DXF HEADER group-code table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A85E8E67-27CD-4C59-BE61-4DC9FADBE74A.htm) | `$MEASUREMENT` chooses imperial/metric hatch and linetype resource families; Autodesk does not define it as a substitute for `$INSUNITS` geometry scaling. The header table labels INSUNITS as default units for DesignCenter blocks. | Continue the crossed-value controls: retain both header values and their independent presence/value, allow them to disagree, and assert coordinates are unchanged in libdxfrw parse/write. Do not derive one variable from the other or infer unit factors from formatting variables. |
| ezdxf [DXF Units documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/concepts/units.html) | The independent implementation documents coordinate values as unitless in isolation, drawing/modelspace units as header context, separate units per block, and explicit INSERT scale attributes for differing unit contexts; it states `$MEASUREMENT` is independent of `$INSUNITS`. Its document explicitly says some behavior is based on BricsCAD experiments and may differ, so this is implementation guidance, not a normative Autodesk ruling. | Make local generated tests distinguish header metadata from INSERT transform data: block units alone must not silently rewrite stored coordinates; an explicit INSERT scale/placement is a separate, expected geometric transform. Use ezdxf only as an optional syntax/behavior comparator, not the only authority. |
| FreeCAD current [C++ DXF importer source](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Import/App/dxf/ImpExpDxf.cpp), its [import/export preferences](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Import_Export_Preferences.md), and [legacy scaling issue #10253](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/10253) | The inspected mutable C++ source reads a separate `dxfScaling` preference (default1.0), applies it through `SetAdditionalScaling`, and records it in import stats; the documentation describes the preference as conversion from DXF units to millimeters. The issue discussion proposes precedence rules for manual scale, INSUNITS, and MEASUREMENT, but is not a released contract or independent runtime result. The source's lack of a literal `INSUNITS` token in this file alone does not establish behavior of the full importer stack. | For FreeCAD native checks, pin the exact release/backend and capture the effective `dxfScaling` preference. Run only the chosen composed consumer batch with identity scale and an explicit nonidentity control; compare final document coordinates/bounds against expected transforms. Keep file-open/import separate from an INSERT/attach operation. Do not claim native auto-detection from source inspection or the issue discussion. |
| Autodesk [AutoCAD release mapping](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A85E8E67-27CD-4C59-BE61-4DC9FADBE74A.htm) and [FreeCAD historical tracker #3494](https://tracker.freecad.org/view.php?id=3494) | The header reference maps AC1014 to R14 and AC1015 to AutoCAD 2000; the historical FreeCAD discussion says INSUNITS was introduced with the AutoCAD 2000 DXF contract. The historical note is not a full normative older-version table. | Correct the proposed controls for version validity: use a legacy profile as omitted-only; exercise absent/0/1/4 in AC1015+ unless a specific older producer/version contract is established. Any deliberately injected pre-AC1015 `$INSUNITS` robustness case must be labeled out-of-profile, not conformance evidence. |

modern DXF INSERT contract. It was source/documentation research only: no peer
was cloned or run, no drawing was downloaded, and no local test or production
change was made. The additional sources corroborate record structure, but
still do not establish historical REPEAT behavior.

It is a maintained open-source implementation schema, not an AutoCAD normative manual; its correspondence with the issue's examples is not an independent semantic oracle. | Use it to check local record-width/field-order test construction only. Do not infer whether counts include the seed, the repeat transform origin/axes, nesting, or what records are in scope. |
| Separate BSD-2 [`CAD-Format-DWG-AC1_40` Kaitai schema](https://github.com/michal-josef-spacek/CAD-Format-DWG-AC1_40/blob/main/dwg_ac1_40.ksy#L1157-L1215) and its [`repeat_end` fields](https://github.com/michal-josef-spacek/CAD-Format-DWG-AC1_40/blob/main/dwg_ac1_40.ksy#L1393-L1410) | The parser model reads a fixed entity count; it names type 5 `repeat_begin` but comments out that case in the entity dispatch, while type 6 carries columns, rows, and column/row distances. It also models LOAD's string. This is useful structural triangulation from a separate codebase, but the repository is a small read-only parser and the schema does not implement or verify geometry expansion. | Record the result as structural corroboration only, not a second semantic vote. Do not use this schema as the expected geometry oracle or as a runtime dependency. |
| Autodesk official [INSERT DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2017/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-28FA4CFB-9D5E-4880-9F11-36C97578252F.htm) | Modern DXF INSERT supports optional columns/rows (70/71) and column/row spacing (44/45), along with a referenced block. It establishes that a modern representation can carry a block array, not that old REPEAT is equivalent to an arrayed INSERT or that arbitrary legacy members can be lowered without changing semantics. | Keep block-array lowering as a candidate only after a historical semantic witness; test anonymous block ownership, base point, identity, and row/column transforms separately. Do not choose it merely because fields exist. |
| LibreDWG open [issue #1354](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1354) | The report gives an R1.4 sample sequence and a 3×2 example where its DXF conversion preserves one point while emitting legacy markers as entities; it reports a broad real-world corpus sweep. The source sample and corpus were not acquired or independently re-run in this review, and the reporter explicitly leaves the intended representation open. | Treat the concrete sequence as a high-value generated-vector shape, not as an authoritative expected-value oracle. Keep external test payloads out of this repository. |
| Local [`dwgReaderR1_40::readEntity`](src/intern/dwgreaderR1_40.cpp) and existing PAR-49 atomic-publication lane | Current code ignores `T_REPEAT`, consumes then discards ENDREP's 20-byte payload, and reads then discards LOAD's text. The source confirms a possible silent-loss route; this review did not execute it. A separate publication gate already exists in the plan for refusing incomplete output. | Make the next implementation slice fail closed on a detected repeat group and route it through the existing incomplete-result/atomic-publication handling. This does not require guessing repeat geometry, and it prevents a successful-conversion claim for a seed-only result. Keep non-repeat AC1.40 behavior unchanged. |

   fail-closed profiles; add only supported fields with a precomputed identity
   map for the `*T` block, owner, TABLESTYLE, field targets, cell BLOCK_RECORDs,
   and attribute definitions. Keep TABLESTYLE raw-carrier replay separate
   from typed DWG-origin writing. Existing global FIELD/FIELDLIST preflight
   remains a distinct earlier gate and must not be mislabeled as a TABLE parse
   failure.
3. **Fail closed on unknown AC1021 cell types, then isolate supported types.**
   Keep the R2007 text/block layout limited to known cell types 1 and 2; for
   other AC1021+ types, mark semantic parsing incomplete and retain the
   anonymous-block fallback rather than guessing field order. The existing
   AC1021 sample observes types 16 and 92, but ODA §20.4.96.1 leaves the
   R2008 change unresolved, so those values are not assigned invented

   reaches the inline TABLECONTENT route and checks one typed cell, style

## ACAD_TABLE unknown cell type fail-closed implementation slice (2026-10-16)

`parseR2007TableCell` now refuses to apply the known text/block body layout to
an AC1021+ cell type other than 1 or 2. It records the observed type as an
incomplete subrecord, stops semantic TABLE parsing, and leaves the separate
anonymous `*T` block projection available. This guard is grounded in the local
AC1021 observations of types 16 and 92 and ODA §20.4.96.1's unresolved note
that R2008 changed cell data. It intentionally does not infer what either
type means or claim that the supported cell types now parse correctly.

Validation and regression status:

- `cmake --build build --target dwg2dxf --parallel 2` (strict project build)
- `cmake --build build --target libdxfrw_dwg_object_vectors_tests --parallel 2`
  and `ctest --test-dir build -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_object_vectors$'
  --output-on-failure` (generated AC1021 unknown/text/block vectors; 1/1 pass)
- Existing local AC1021 smoke input reports types 16 and 92 as unsupported and
  logs the incomplete TABLE / anonymous-block fallback for both records.
- The same whole-file conversion remains independently blocked by
  `FIELD/FIELDLIST` DXF export preflight; no DXF was qualified or published.
- `git diff --check` on the edited source and plan.

The broad `ctest --test-dir build -R dwg_read --output-on-failure` matcher
selected 53 cases, not just the small sample set described in the repository
overview: 2 passed and 51 failed. A sampled AC1024 failure stops at the
existing `LAYOUT last-active viewport is missing or has the wrong owner`
export preflight; AC1021 failures also report reader-integrity mismatches.
Those outcomes do not prove a regression from this guard, but neither do they
qualify it across the matrix. Keep this aggregate run out of the fast-slice
pass column; first reproduce representative failures on the pre-slice build or
separate parser-only controls, then use targeted AC1021/AC1024 checks.

declared data-start marker. The existing last-record-span calculation was left
unchanged pending a separate coordinate derivation.

against the existing route/semantic evidence gates. It adds no new parser
finding: current peers offer complementary evidence layers, not an
end-to-end 3D oracle. LibreDWG's manual assigns `stable`, `unstable`,
`debugging`, and `unhandled` dispositions and distinguishes same-version
unknown-bit replay from general cross-version support. ACadSharp's versioned

AC1027+-only raw ASM+transform exposure that does not create solid geometry.

are distinct compound modes, with signed one-based face indices and edge
visibility semantics.

document values. If the known issue reproduces, do not count that text-height

implementation gates and the speed of their validation, not to infer a
libdxfrw defect from another project's issue. The review used public primary
project issue pages and read-only local plan/source inspection. No peer was
built or run, no native CAD/kernel was launched, no external drawing was
downloaded, and no fixture, dependency, code, test, or CTest registration was
added.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not establish | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LibreDWG [issue #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411) | The open report supplies a from-scratch AC1032 DXF recipe using ezdxf to create one REGION with a cube-derived SAB body (reported length 5,489 bytes), then claims a `dxf2dwg`→`dwg2dxf` route preserves the REGION record but returns no SAB/ACDSDATA. It also reports an unavailable customer R2018 DWG with 88 such empty-body REGIONs. These are reporter-provided observations, not a run reproduced here or normative AcDs layout evidence. | This is a low-cost, source-authored *carrier transport* test candidate at a composed optional peer checkpoint: generate in a disposable directory, hash the SAB immediately, and compare exact input/output bytes and body-presence state through pinned tools. The maintainer confirms those entity writer types were unsupported in the referenced route; the linked PRs are proposals, not released or independently qualified behavior. The customer drawings are not attached. | The composed writer inventory must identify source handle, `3DSOLID`/`REGION`/`BODY` type, owning block path, source carrier path (inline versus AcDs), output entity and payload disposition, and diagnostic. Include one block containing only a modeler entity plus an INSERT of that block; document-level totals can otherwise hide an empty definition. Do not count an open PR or a current version matrix as evidence that the writer is fixed. |

Keep this separate from entity-record state (`emitted`, `unsupported-with-diagnostic`, `refused`) and from kernel interpretation. |

1. Extend the existing feature-direction matrix with distinct result classes:

## Deeper/broader compiler specs, linker-consumption, and runtime-closure review (2026-10-16; research only)

This review expands the last GCC built-in-specs slice to the next 7AG.4
boundary: configuration files that the driver reads indirectly, files selected
by the actual link, and images loaded only when the resulting adapter runs.
It uses current compiler/linker documentation and GCC driver source for the
lookup contract. No native GNU/MSVC toolchain, peer, or application was run;
no local test, build, fixture, or parser behavior changed.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GCC [spec-file documentation](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-15.1.0/gcc/Spec-Files.html) and current [`gcc.cc` source](https://codebrowser.dev/gcc/gcc/gcc.cc.html) | GCC's `%include`/`%include_noerr` directives are parsed as specs-file directives and resolved with `find_a_file(&startfile_prefixes, ..., do_multi=true)`. `%include_noerr` intentionally permits a missing file. The conditional `%:include(filename)` builtin uses that startfile-prefix list too and can be nested in spec text. Prefixes are assembled from compiler install, target/system-root, and multilib configuration. `-dumpspecs` captures a specs representation; the current receipt independently binds the main reported external specs file, but does not enumerate/hash included targets. | Do not resolve includes relative to the containing file, use `PATH`, or assume `-print-file-name=<include>` is equivalent. A profile may become `complete` only when every effective include has an exact resolved path and before/after content identity, including optional-missing disposition and multilib selection. If a directive is dynamic, conditional, ambiguous, or not observed, keep that compiler profile unavailable/partial and paired receipts ineligible. |
| GCC [developer options](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-15.1.0/gcc/Developer-Options.html) | `-print-search-dirs` reports configured installation, program, and library search directories; `-print-sysroot` reports the target sysroot. These are useful context, not a trace of which specs/configuration files the invocation actually opened or which branches of conditional specs executed. | Record these values as search-context metadata if useful, but never treat directory names as content binding or a complete include closure. Prefer exact observed-open paths or a source-verified resolver with native controls. |
| Clang [configuration-file rules](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/UsersManual.html#configuration-files) and [driver/toolchain behavior](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/Toolchain.html), plus GCC [overall options](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Overall-Options.html) | Clang can load default and explicit `.cfg` files; a config may include another via `@file`, resolved relative to the including config, and inject compile, target, sysroot, and linker options. `--no-default-config` can disable default config loading. GCC and Clang `-###` report commands the drivers would run without executing them; actual `-v` reports commands as they run. Clang's frontend command interface is explicitly an implementation detail. | Keep the existing default-config rejection/controlled profile. If a future Clang profile allows config files, recursively bind `@file` contents and selected config roots; capture actual child executable/argv identity. Driver command output alone is not content closure for implicit files. |
| GNU [`ld` script](https://sourceware.org/binutils/docs/ld/Scripts.html), [file commands](https://sourceware.org/binutils/docs/ld/File-Commands.html), and [map/verbose options](https://sourceware.org/binutils/docs/ld/Options.html) | Every link uses a linker script (possibly the script compiled into `ld`). External scripts may use `INCLUDE`, `INPUT`, `GROUP`, and `SEARCH_DIR`, which recursively affect script and object/archive selection. A link map lists included archive members and why they were extracted; verbose output identifies the script and file-open outcomes. Neither a configured `-L` list nor an unexecuted driver preview proves what the actual link consumed. | At the composed build boundary, capture the actual link argv, response/config files, linker binary, map, verbose script/file trace, and exact selected file/archive identities; bind archive bytes plus selected member names. For any script reference not resolved and bound, preserve `partial` status. Do not turn the one-off instrumentation into per-slice full test-suite work. |
| Microsoft [`/showIncludes`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/reference/showincludes-list-include-files?view=msvc-170), [`/VERBOSE:LIB`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/reference/verbose-print-progress-messages?view=msvc-170), and [`LINK` input contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/reference/link-input-files?view=msvc-170) | MSVC can report nested headers and library/object selection, including full paths and symbol reasons. LINK can also consume response files, default-library directives embedded in objects, import libraries, resources, and module-definition files. These diagnostics do not bind bytes, all Windows SDK/runtime components, or DLL resolution on another machine. | These are the corresponding Windows profile's low-cost observation points, not a cross-platform substitute. Hash the reported selected files and response inputs; preserve toolset/SDK/runtime identities. Until a native Windows capture path is implemented and exercised, MSVC remains unavailable for paired qualification. |
| Existing Darwin [runtime UUID/stub-closure receipt](docs/research/apple-runtime-uuid-closure-2026-10-16.json) and current 7AG.4 state | The current profile records dyld image edges/architectures and image UUIDs, and candidate SDK stubs; it explicitly does not prove that a candidate stub was the one selected by the linker or content-bind all protected/shared-cache runtime images. A linked-input inventory and a post-link runtime dependency graph answer different questions. | Preserve separate `linkInputs` and `runtimeImages` subprofiles. UUID/architecture, deployment target, or SDK manifest alone cannot be promoted to byte identity. Keep Darwin partial until linker-selected stubs and a defensible immutable runtime identity/content policy are established. |

kernel instead of treating an application-level “supports DWG/3D” label as one
implementation. This was a public-source audit only: no peer was installed,
built, or run; no external drawing was downloaded; and no code, fixture,
dependency, or test registration changed.

CAD Assistant's page likewise attributes ACIS/DXF import to commercial XDE components and restricts export/conversion for those imported models. This does not negate OCCT's open-source B-rep kernel; it means the vendor's own DXF/ACIS translators are not an eligible open-source parser/writer comparator. | Add an explicit peer-matrix exclusion: label these routes `OCCT_COMMERCIAL_EXCHANGE`, not `OPEN_SOURCE_PEER`. `cq-acis` remains a separately assessed SAT/SAB parser feeding an OCCT-family kernel; do not conflate it with OCCT's commercial SAT/DXF translators or count the shared kernel as an independent kernel result from FreeCAD. Use OCCT only as a kernel backend when the parser, version, and shape-construction path are separately pinned and named. |
| mlightcad [RealDWG-Web README](https://github.com/mlightcad/realdwg-web/blob/main/README.md), [`data-model` converter documentation](https://github.com/mlightcad/realdwg-web/blob/main/packages/data-model/README.md), and [CAD Viewer documentation](https://github.com/mlightcad/cad-viewer/blob/main/README.md) | Current project docs distinguish the default MIT-licensed `AcDbNativeDxfConverter` from optional converters. ## Deeper/broader cross-format DIMENSION flag review (2026-10-16; research only)

This pass checked a new downstream report about dimension text placement across
DWG/DXF against Autodesk's DXF contract, the repository's authoritative local
ODA v5.4.1 DWG specification, and the current local parser/writer/tests. It
found a useful regression-test gap but no source-confirmed implementation
defect. No peer or native application was run; no external drawing was fetched.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CADCraft open [issue #1094](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/issues/1094) | The reporter says CADCraft 0.6.2-generated dimensions produced different AutoCAD 2026 editing behavior: DXF group 70 contained 32 (not user-positioned) and text recentered after moving a definition point, while DWG group 70 appeared as 128 and text remained fixed. The report includes locally generated commands and black-box observations, but no drawing artifact; it is an open report, not a libdxfrw reproduction. A contributor says the bridge fix must invert DWG Flags 1 bit 0 relative to DXF bit 128 and map DWG Flags 1 bit 1 to DXF bit 32; that proposed fix is not release-qualified evidence. | Treat the report as a high-value cross-format test lead only. CADCraft/OpenCADStudio/ACadRust are one codec lineage under the existing peer ledger; the AutoCAD behavior described is a report, not a native acceptance run performed for this plan. Do not change local field meanings from the peer patch proposal. |
| Autodesk [Common DIMENSION group codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2017/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-EDD54EAC-A339-4EBA-AEA6-EC8066505E2B.htm) | DXF group 70 bit 128 marks a user-positioned text location; bit 32 indicates that the dimension's picture block is referenced only by that dimension and is set in R13 and later. This is the DXF semantic contract, not the DWG byte mapping. | Keep the two DXF bits independently observable: subtype (low bits), bit 32, and user-positioned bit 128 must not be collapsed into one Boolean or inferred from group 11 alone. |
| Local authoritative ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.22 (local PDF, pp. 125–126) | The DWG common-dimension “Flags 1” field is an ordinary RC at group-70 position, not bit-pair-coded: bit 0 is the opposite of DXF group-70 bit 128; bit 1 matches DXF bit 32. ODA also identifies adjacent version-scoped dimension fields, so the flag's byte must be read at the proper DWG version/layout boundary. | This confirms the current conversion formula: DWG `Flags1 & 1` clear means DXF bit 128 set; `Flags1 & 2` set means DXF bit 32 set. It does not establish CADCraft's reported source/output behavior or AutoCAD edit result. |
| Local source `src/drw_entities.cpp` (`DRW_Dimension::parseDwg`, `encodeDwgDimBase`) and `src/libdxfrw.cpp` (`writeDimension`) | The DWG parser maps Flags 1 bit 0 inversely to `type & 0x80` and bit 1 to `type & 0x20`; the DWG encoder reverses that mapping. The DXF writer derives subtype from the concrete class, preserves higher caller flags, and forces the documented post-R12 bit 32. Source review therefore finds no mismatch against the ODA/DXF contracts. | Do not add a production fix or retune flags based on peer code. Add raw-wire assertions to the existing generated dimension test owner before parseback so symmetric reader/writer mistakes cannot cancel each other. |
| Existing `dimensionFrameMatches()` in `tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp` and ARC_DIMENSION flag controls | The current generated common-dimension frame matrix checks subtype, points, text, extrusion, and anonymous picture blocks but does not assert bit 32/128 or DWG Flags 1. The separate ARC_DIMENSION vectors check subclass-local flags 70/71, which are different fields and do not cover the common DIMENSION flag byte. | Close the focused coverage gap inside the existing test target, not with a new CTest, fixture, dependency, or full-suite run. |

   Binary DXF records for at least linear, aligned, and ordinate dimensions,
   covering user-positioned off/on while keeping subtype and bit 32 explicit.
   Inspect emitted group-70 wire values before local parseback; then assert
   parsed `eType`, low subtype, bit 32, bit 128, group-11 midpoint, and the
   following entity. Retain all existing geometry/frame checks.
2. Add a source-generated DWG common-dimension vector for the same two
   placement states. Check the raw Flags 1 byte against ODA before reader
   round-trip: bit 0 must invert bit 128 and bit 1 must map to bit 32. Exercise

   needed to pin the field location; do not add external DWG fixtures.
3. Make the first slice fast and local: build the touched test target and run

## Implementation progress — PAR-66 tolerant DXF LAYER read and explicit repair (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

`DRW_Layer::parseCode` now retains an out-of-range group 370 integer alongside
the existing compatibility enum mapping. The new read-only accessors expose
that preserved raw value, and `repairDxfLineweight` accepts only legal LAYER
lineweights; the malformed marker survives ordinary field edits/copies until

still-marked raw-invalid value instead of emitting its lossy mapped default.

handles, but now publishes semantically invalid-yet-representable LAYER rows
with one bounded, non-fatal `dxf-layer-value-preserved` secondary diagnostic.

and binary DXFs for color 0/256 without truecolor, layer lineweight -1/-2, and
out-of-range lineweights -4/500. It verifies typed-value preservation, exact
raw lineweight retention, one structured warning per input, successful parsing
of two following LINEs, atomic refusal to replace a pre-existing valid DXF, and
successful output after an explicit legal repair. No fixture, dependency, or
CTest registration was added. Validation passed:
