## Implementation progress — bounded ACIS transform candidate parser (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

Extended the rooted SAB transform observation with a fail-closed candidate
parser for a transform literal containing exactly twelve finite numeric values.
The source literal, token index, and complete decoded token sequence remain
preserved; unknown trailing hints are not interpreted. A valid tuple is stored
as `ParsedUnapplied`, while absent, truncated, malformed, extra-value, and
non-finite candidates are marked `Invalid`. No matrix ordering, omitted
column, composition, point/vector convention, transform application, unit
scaling, or WCS placement is inferred.

Generated graph controls verify all twelve candidate values in serialized
order, accept trailing whitespace without altering the raw literal, reject
truncated/malformed/extra/non-finite candidates, and retain the existing
missing-literal and resource-limit behavior. No external fixture, dependency,
test registration, or support claim was added.

Validation passed: `cmake --build build-gcc --target
libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests lc3_compat_check -j 2`, focused
`libdxfrw_graph_preservation` CTest (1/1), and `git diff --check`. Full suites,
native CAD/kernel readers, and transform application were not run. Worktree
remains uncommitted and broadly user-dirty. Receipt:
[`acis-transform-candidate-matrix-fast-slice-2026-10-16.json`](docs/research/acis-transform-candidate-matrix-fast-slice-2026-10-16.json).

## Deeper/broader cross-engine evidence-lane and comparator-order review (2026-10-16; research only)

This review revisited the current primary documentation for GDAL's DXF/DWG
drivers, ezdxf 1.4.5's ACIS and recovery paths, and LibreCAD_3's DWG consumer
policy, then reconciled those routes against the existing feature/support
ledger. The useful new result is not another peer capability list: it is a
strict separation of which observations can be collected cheaply, which peer
is independent for which format direction, and what each lane cannot prove.
No peer or native application was installed or run; no external drawing was
downloaded; no production code, test, fixture, dependency, support claim,
finding, top-level subplan, or external-J disposition changed.

| Primary evidence | Verified boundary | Implementation consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GDAL [DXF driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) and [driver matrix](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/) | GDAL documents a built-in DXF reader/writer, Binary DXF reading starting in 3.12, and writing compatible with AutoCAD 2004+. With `DXF_INLINE_BLOCKS=FALSE`, it exposes block definitions and INSERT references separately. It does not convert 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY/SURFACE into OGR geometry; `DXF_3D_EXTENSIBLE_MODE=TRUE` exposes raw `ASMData` and a 12-real column-major `ASMTransform` for AC1027+ DXF. The driver matrix shows DWG uses the external ODA Teigha library, unlike the built-in DXF driver. | Keep GDAL as one optional independent **DXF** feature-projection/raw-carrier comparator, not an open-source DWG parser or solid kernel. At the one composed check, probe ASCII and Binary DXF separately, explicitly set `DXF_INLINE_BLOCKS=FALSE` and `DXF_3D_EXTENSIBLE_MODE=TRUE`, and record build/driver identity, source handle, entity type, block path, `ASMData` length/digest, and transform values. First verify the selected GDAL build supports each option/input combination. Do not treat a successful GDAL open, OGR feature count, bounds, or direct binary-to-ASCII conversion as a 3D semantic result. |
| ezdxf [ACIS API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html), [ACIS browser](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/launcher.html#browse-acis), and [recovery documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/recover.html) | Current docs expose raw SAT/SAB inspection and bounded parsing. The documented `mesh_from_body` projection emits flat polygonal faces and explicitly loses curved faces; `vertices_from_body` bounds are exact only for polyhedra with flat faces/straight edges. `body_from_mesh` can create a locally generated polyhedral test body, not recover arbitrary source solid semantics. Recovery is a repair/audit lane for structurally flawed DXF and can report unrecoverable decode errors; it is not equivalent to a clean strict parse or lossless writeback. | Use ezdxf as a complementary DXF structure/raw-ACIS comparator and as an optional from-scratch polyhedral carrier generator. Keep strict read, audit/recovery diagnostics, raw payload equality, faceted projection, and analytic B-rep validity as distinct results. Never promote a solid claim from a mesh projection, recovered file, or same-tool read/write cycle. Keep all generated controls ephemeral unless they satisfy the existing local-from-scratch admission rule. |
| LibreCAD_3 [DWG support policy](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/blob/master/docs/dwg-support.md) | The current project documentation says `WITH_DWG_IMPORT` is off by default and the reader path through `dwgRW` is experimental; it explicitly does not expose or plan DWG writing. | Maintain a consumer compatibility gate for LibreCAD_3's **reader** integration where relevant. Do not make DWG writer parity a LibreCAD_3 compatibility condition, and do not confuse a library read callback with successful application model construction. |

### Ready-to-run comparator order (refines existing gates only)

1. **Per-slice implementation gate:** use the existing generated fast test,
   touched strict build, and source-to-emitted per-entity/owner inventory.
   External applications are not prerequisites for local reader/writer fixes.
2. **Composed DXF structural check:** when several carrier/owner slices are
   ready, run one pinned GDAL DXF reader/API check over locally generated
   ASCII and Binary DXF controls. Preserve blocks as references and compare
   handle/type/owner/coordinates and raw-code/carrier data where available.
   Record unsupported or missing rows explicitly; if the exact build or option
   composition is unavailable, record `NOT_RUN` and continue.
3. **Complementary parser diagnostics:** use a pinned ezdxf strict read as a
   separate parser observation; run recovery/audit only on a separate damaged
   local control and record repairs/errors. Do not add a second external run
   for each individual group-code or entity fix.
4. **3D evidence gate:** compare raw ASM/SAT/SAB bytes and carrier links first;
   only after those close, use an eligible independent ACIS reader/kernel for
   B-rep validity and analytic invariants. GDAL raw ASM and ezdxf's faceted
   projection cannot substitute for this gate. Keep native consumer acceptance
   separate from parser and kernel evidence.
5. **DWG and consumer lane:** select a DWG reader by exact lineage and release;
   GDAL's ODA-backed DWG driver is not an independent open-source vote. Keep
   LibreCAD_3 read qualification independent of DWG write or ACIS claims.

This ordering avoids network/runtime setup on every implementation slice,
keeps full suites at composed milestones, and makes absent optional tools
non-blocking. It refines existing PAR-07/PAR-14/PAR-49/PAR-65/7AG and
S2.3.9.4/S3.7/S8.9.5 comparator and acceptance owners; it adds no finding or
top-level subplan. Totals remain 125 findings / 71 top-level subplans. J256,
J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and
non-promoting. Receipt:
[`cross-engine-evidence-lane-and-comparator-order-review-2026-10-16.json`](docs/research/cross-engine-evidence-lane-and-comparator-order-review-2026-10-16.json).

It does not prove the exact v2026.41 route or a complete imported solid. | Capture exact source revision and per-face lift/fallback/incomplete status. A fallback mesh is display-only and disqualifies the shape result; do not infer B-rep validity from render success. |
| `opencadkernel` [README](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/opencadkernel) and the app's [v2026.41 lockfile](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/v2026.41/Cargo.lock) | The current README calls the kernel early and describes an `acis` feature lifting `SatDocument` into B-rep, while the application release documents more advanced operations. The visible release lockfile is the right pin to audit; mutable `main` manifests or a short hash mentioned somewhere in cumulative release notes are not a substitute for resolving the exact tag's dependency tree. Neither project page establishes parser independence: OpenCADStudio's outer DWG/DXF and ACIS document path is in the ACadRust-related codec lineage. | Record the exact tag/commit, resolved codec and kernel Git revisions, lockfile hash, enabled features, target/toolchain, and importer command/API. Keep the app, codec/parser, geometry kernel, and consumer result as separate identities; this is at most a cross-kernel geometry comparison, never a second parser vote. |

### Composed-checkpoint procedure

1. **Do not add a per-slice gate.** Continue the existing local fast-test
   cadence and implementation sequence. Schedule this only at the already
   planned composed external/consumer checkpoint; do not add a dependency,
   test registration, committed peer sample, or full-suite run for it.
2. Before opening any payload, perform a no-input preflight on the exact
   OpenCADStudio v2026.41 tag (or a later explicitly pinned release): verify
   the packaged build/source commit, `Cargo.lock` and resolved codec/kernel
   revisions, required `acis`/B-rep features, available command/API, and
   whether `MASSPROP` accepts imported ACIS solids. If any point cannot be
   established cheaply, report `NOT_RUN`/`NOT_AVAILABLE` and continue.
3. If admitted, create one asymmetric analytic body locally from scratch in a
   temporary workspace; do not fetch or commit a third-party DWG/DXF fixture.
   Record producer dimensions, units, transform, entity handle/type, owner and
   block path, exact SAT/SAB or AcDs/ACDSDATA payload hash, and expected
   topology/metrics in a separately authored manifest. Reuse identical input
   bytes for the candidate routes.
4. Capture import disposition and diagnostics before measurement: source
   entity count; body/lump/shell/face counts; unresolved and omitted records;
   kernel-lift success; unsupported surfaces; per-surface fallback count;
   incomplete flags; healing/repair; and source-to-result identity/placement.
   A missing face, fallback, repair, or ambiguous owner/transform link means
   the cell is incomplete, not a pass.
5. Run `MASSPROP` only if the exact pinned importer produces the candidate
   solid and the operation is available non-interactively. Capture raw output,
   units, bounds, surface area, volume, centroid, and tolerance-normalized
   deltas against the independent analytic manifest. Also capture kernel
   validity and closed-solid/topology status through an inspectable API; if
   the app exposes metrics but not validity/closure, call the result scoped
   metric corroboration only, not B-rep semantic qualification.
6. Score four lanes independently: codec/parser delivery and owner graph;
   exact carrier survival; kernel B-rep and metric result; application render
   or UI acceptance. The app's same-lineage parser cannot independently
   confirm DWG/DXF correctness, and a `MASSPROP` value alone cannot establish
   arbitrary ACIS support. Cross-kernel agreement with an eligible independent
   kernel may strengthen only the exact tested profile.
7. Write the receipt with source pins/hashes, commands/settings, stdout and
   diagnostics, expected manifest, tolerances, per-entity disposition, and
   each lane's result. Missing platform/runtime or unsupported geometry is
   `NOT_RUN`/`NOT_AVAILABLE`, never implicit success, and never blocks local
   work.

preserves arbitrary ACIS.

this Apple Silicon host. It is a separate ACIS parser implementation from the
OpenCADStudio/ACadRust route, but uses CadQuery/OpenCascade for shape creation;
count parser agreement separately from kernel agreement. Prefer it only as a
same-payload parser-plus-shape candidate. The digest and source commit make a
later run reproducible; they do not make it mandatory or constitute a pass.

## Implementation progress — versioned MESH DXF record and CLASS profiles (2026-10-16; local fast slice)

Implemented the bounded writer/reader/class-metadata slice from the research
above. `dxfRW::dxfMeshRecordNameForVersion()` centralizes the target policy:
AC1024 writes `SUBDIVISION`; AC1027 and AC1032 write `MESH`; pre-AC1024
supported targets retain the prior `MESH` spelling as an unqualified,
compatibility-preserving behavior; AC1009 remains rejected. The reader accepts
both native record spellings into `DRW_Mesh`. The `dwg2dxf` adapter registers
one matching `AcDbSubDMesh` CLASS row when typed meshes are present and sets
its instance count from modelspace plus block contents. A conflicting alias
row is replaced instead of emitting duplicate class identities.

The fast test now generates temporary ASCII and binary DXFs for AC1014, AC1015,
AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027 and AC1032. It checks the target `$ACADVER`, exact native entity name,
`AcDbSubDMesh` subclass and the selected CLASS identity/tuple, preserved mesh
topology and crease/property fields, typed readback, and a following LINE
sentinel. It checks the class instance-count group only where this writer
serializes it (AC1018+); AC1012 is omitted because the current DXF writer does
not enable that target. The tested class tuple is a local serialization regression
expectation, not a normative Autodesk tuple or application-acceptance proof;
the additional source review below records that distinction. AC1021 is a
compatibility characterization only—not a format-validity claim. No fixture
files were added, and the test remains under the existing fast DXF fixture
target.

- Full suite and independent CAD applications — NOT RUN (not needed for this fast slice).

The older-version witness audit remains an explicit self-unblocking follow-up:
inspect the exact LibreDWG `2004/Surface.dxf` if it can be retrieved, verify

the profile marked `UNQUALIFIED` if those facts cannot be established. Do not

ephemeral. The slice establishes neither complete MESH interoperability nor

## Deeper/broader MESH CLASS metadata and version-evidence review (2026-10-16; research only)

This follow-up checks the *meaning and provenance* of the class tuple in
addition to the entity name and field profile. It finds stronger primary
support for the two documented version profiles, but no source that makes the
current `AcDbSubDMesh` CLASS tuple normative or resolves the earlier-version
conflict. It therefore narrows claims and adds a bounded validation task to
the existing MESH owner; it does not add another top-level subplan.

| Evidence | Finding | Plan update |
| --- | --- | --- |

## Implementation progress — schema-3 CRC warnings block evidence promotion (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

Closed a differential-evidence eligibility gap for DWG integrity warnings.
Schema-3 observations now add explicit eligibility blockers when any available
read phase reports a nonzero `classesCrcMismatch`, `reader21CrcMismatch`, or
`reader18HeaderCrcMismatch` counter. These reader diagnostics are warn-only for
compatibility, so this change does not turn a successful parse into a parser
failure; it prevents a warning-bearing comparison from being used as
claim-eligible evidence.

both target and standalone observations, and verifies the result is
`reviewedNonPromoting`, `claimEligible=false`, retains operation success, and
contains the side-specific blocker for each reader. The clean schema-3 case
remains eligible.

## Implementation progress — HATCH/MPOLYGON gradient target floor (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

Autodesk's AutoCAD 2004 API history marks `AcGradientObject`, gradient hatch
properties, and the `AddHatch` object-type change as new in 2004. The official
AutoCAD 2005 DXF Reference (February 2004) documents HATCH's gradient control
block and required companions. Combined with the repository's AC1018 = R2004
version map, this establishes a conservative minimum qualified target of
AC1018 for group 450+ gradient output; it does not prove that every R2004+
consumer renders every gradient mode identically.

`validateHatchPayload()` now refuses an active gradient when the configured DXF
target is older than AC1018. Because both HATCH and MPOLYGON writers share this
validation, the refusal occurs before either entity publishes bytes. The
focused generated ASCII/binary tests verify transactional rejection at AC1015
for both entity types and successful HATCH serialization at the AC1018 floor.
The existing group-431 string-type, later-field parsing, and modern active
unmapped-method rejection checks remain in place. The strict Wave 1 target and
CTest pass (1/1); the existing `libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip` target and CTest
also pass (1/1). No full suite, native CAD run, downloaded drawing, committed
fixture, dependency, or support-claim promotion was involved.

This closes only the older-target emission half of 7Q. Exact 431/432/433
semantics and cross-application gradient rendering remain open. All six
external J items remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

This pass cross-checks the current public DXF, ezdxf, Open CASCADE, and FreeCAD
surfaces to make the optional ACIS/B-rep qualification path cheaper to decide
and harder to overstate. It separates (1) DXF/DWG container handling, (2) ACIS
payload parsing/serialization, (3) geometric-kernel construction and
measurement, and (4) native-application acceptance. Public documentation and
source pages were reviewed; no peer was installed, built, or run, no drawing
was downloaded, and no license, trial, or network service was activated.

A parser that sees a 3DSOLID record has established only entity recognition. |

Its entity documentation describes a deliberately bounded flat-polyhedron model; `vertices_from_body()` is exact only for straight-edged polyhedra, and mesh projection loses curved faces. It is useful as a pinned structural/control-author route, not a general ACIS kernel or arbitrary B-rep oracle. | For any optional ezdxf probe, record container version, SAT/SAB dialect, supported topology subset, unsupported records, and whether the result is raw carrier, parsed topology, or mesh projection. Never count a vertex/mesh result as curved-surface or solid-semantic support. |

The component catalog identifies ACIS SAT/SAB and DXF exchange as commercial extensions. A FreeCAD/OCCT installation therefore cannot be assumed to provide a usable ACIS reader merely because it contains the OCCT kernel. | Add an early availability/entitlement check before the composed external semantic gate. Its DWG wrapper converts to DXF and calls the normal DXF import route. Neither route description establishes ACIS/B-rep consumption; release, importer mode, converter, and final document remain the actual acceptance tuple. | Keep stock FreeCAD in the 2D/explicit-entity consumer lane already qualified by S8. For an ACIS result, require a separately named modeler component and inspect final shape/topology/metrics. Do not treat successful converter handoff or file opening as an ACIS pass. |
| Current ezdxf/OCCT and FreeCAD source cross-check | These sources distinguish format adapters from kernels and make clear why a single successful route can otherwise be misclassified: a carrier-preserving DXF library, an ACIS subset parser, an OCCT-derived shape path, and a native CAD importer answer different questions. This review did not establish a second-kernel, source-native known-size ACIS witness. | On the composed checkpoint, first screen route role, exact profile, license, platform, and result capability; then run only eligible routes. Semantic evidence still requires independently authored expected geometry, complete body/reference disposition, valid closed topology, declared units/transforms, and numeric bounds/area/volume with tolerances. Track a mesh/wireframe/bounds fallback as projection only. |

## Deeper/broader explicit-mesh topology and geometry-evidence review (2026-10-16; research only)

This pass widens the 3D comparison beyond modeler/ACIS carriers to the
semantic boundary between subdivision `MESH`, legacy `POLYLINE` mesh and
polyface, and a kernel-accepted closed solid. Autodesk's DXF references define
these as different wire representations: `MESH` stores a subdivision cage,
face/edge lists, creases and override metadata; classic mesh/polyface uses
mode flags and child `VERTEX` records, with polyface faces limited to four
indices and signed edge-visibility markers. ezdxf's public tutorial confirms
that MESH n-gons do not translate transparently to polyface/3DFACE: conversion
triangulates them and warns that concave n-gons may not work correctly.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk [MESH](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-4B9ADA67-87C8-4673-A579-6E4C76FF7025.htm), [POLYLINE](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-ABF6B778-BE20-4B49-9B58-A94E64CEFFF3.htm), and [polyface mesh](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-96B6288E-F413-46C0-968A-A314171C0AAE.htm) references; ezdxf [polyface tutorial](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorials/polyface.html) | The standards distinguish the `AcDbSubDMesh` cage and its crease/override fields from classic POLYLINE modes and PFACE child records. ezdxf documents MESH n-gons but only three-/four-corner polyface faces, and warns its MESH-to-polyface/3DFACE conversion may fail for concave n-gons. This does not specify DWG MESH layout or evaluated subdivision semantics. | Preserve native entity identity and exact control topology; never silently substitute a PFACE/3DFACE approximation for MESH. Any explicit tessellation is a separately labeled derived projection, not a wire/semantic-preservation pass. Keep DWG property-override encoding fail-closed until its DWG layout has authoritative evidence. |
| [CGAL Polygon Mesh Processing](https://doc.cgal.org/6.2/Polygon_mesh_processing/index.html) and [Manifold](https://github.com/elalish/manifold) project documentation | CGAL describes polygon-mesh operations on 2-manifold topology while allowing boundaries; it exposes separate checks for orientation, self-intersection, area/volume and components. Manifold is narrower: its solid representation expects manifold triangle meshes and rejects invalid imported meshes, while repair/merge is a separate operation. These are geometry-kernel contracts, not DXF reader requirements or independent DWG/DXF parsers. | Keep wire/topology preservation separate from optional geometry acceptance. Do not make manifoldness or closedness a reader precondition for open surfaces; do not run repair/orientation/triangulation before the source-topology comparison. Use volume checks only on an independently specified closed-solid control, and report any repair or rejection. No kernel install or dependency is needed for per-slice work. |
| Local `DRW_Mesh` source and `testMeshRawFieldTags()` test owner | The model stores base-cage vertices/faces/edges, crease values and DXF overrides; DXF output has documented versioned record spelling, while the DWG encoder emits only base-cage fields and rejects nonempty overrides. At the time of this research review the generated ASCII/binary test was a small triangle wire/readback control, not an independent subdivision or closed-volume result. | Keep raw wire and typed topology as the fast gate. The first generated open/n-gon/closed controls are implemented below; broader format-version, DWG, subdivision, and consumer gaps remain separate. An optional pinned CGAL/Manifold check stays at the existing composed checkpoint and may not turn repaired, triangulated or projection-only output into a preservation pass. |

### Implementation-ready refinement

1. Keep the implementation loop dependency-free: touched-target strict build,
   existing generated ASCII/binary checks, and the owning focused CTest. Add no
   new test registration or checked-in external drawing; generate any expanded
   mesh controls at runtime.
2. Implemented in the existing fixture owner: runtime-generated open quad,
   concave pentagon, and closed box controls exercise ASCII and binary AC1027
   output; checks cover native MESH identity/subclass, following-record
   framing, typed vertex/face/edge/crease/override preservation, and the
   closed box's authored area/volume. Continue asserting wire identity and
   typed topology before any optional projection; do not equate a nonempty
   draw result with topology retention.
3. Keep three separate result rows: (a) DXF/DWG wire and typed-topology
   fidelity, (b) evaluated subdivision/mesh projection, and (c) closed-solid
   kernel validity/metrics. A case may pass one and fail or remain unqualified
   on the others.
4. Only at the composed checkpoint, and only if a pinned geometry runtime is
   already available, test a locally authored closed triangle control through
   its no-repair import path. Capture rejection, repair, orientation change,
   connected components, bounds, area and volume. Open surfaces and n-gons
   remain codec cases, not required solid-kernel inputs.
5. This refines existing S2/S3/S5/S8 and PAR-07 owners. It adds zero findings,
   top-level implementation subplans, fixtures, dependencies, test
   registrations, support claims, or implementation-order changes. Totals
   remain 125 findings / 71 top-level implementation subplans. `J256`,
   `J260`, `J268`, `J284`, `J293`, and `J295` remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and
   non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — linear SAB signature scan (2026-10-16; local, uncommitted)

Replaced repeated candidate-offset comparisons in the ACIS convenience decoder
with a Knuth–Morris–Pratt scan per signature and bit alignment. The scan is
linear in input length for each of the at most 16 signature/alignment pairs;
prefix storage is bounded by the short signature. Candidate-selection order
is unchanged: ACIS before ASM, lower bit shift before higher shift, and earliest
offset within a signature/shift. Existing bit-aligned byte access and parser
limits remain in force.

Generated controls in `libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests` verify byte-aligned
ASM, 5-bit-shifted ASM, and selection of a later ACIS stream over an earlier
ASM marker. Existing ACIS bit-shifted vertex projection also continues to pass.
Validation: strict touched-target build and focused graph-preservation CTest
pass (1/1); `lc3_compat_check` builds; `git diff --check` passes. No full
suite, external reader/kernel, native CAD runtime, fixture file, dependency,
or test registration was added.
No support claim or J status changes; the six external-only J items remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. This slice remains local and uncommitted in the broadly
dirty shared worktree.

## Deeper/broader cross-layer loss accounting and ACIS-kernel admission review (2026-10-16; plan refinement)

### Evidence screened

This pass followed the full route from a source entity through its modeler-data
carrier, writer, and downstream shape consumer. It used current project
documentation/releases and open issue reports as leads; no peer repository was
built, no issue report was independently reproduced, and no external drawing
was downloaded.

* LibreDWG issue [#1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411)
  reports a concrete R2018/AC1032 failure mode: a generated DXF REGION with a
  reported 5,489-byte SAB payload survives DXF→DWG→DXF as a REGION, while the
  AcDs/ACDSDATA payload is absent. The report is pinned to LibreDWG 0.14.8593;
  its confidential production-file observations are not independently
  verifiable here. This is a peer report, not a confirmed defect in libdxfrw,
  but it shows why entity counts alone cannot qualify the route.
* ACadSharp's release notes now list reading the 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY ACIS
  payload from DWG and DXF and reading the AcDs payload offset / Prototype1b
  section ([release history](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/releases)).
  Separately, open issue [#1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195)
  reports its DWG reader finding solids while its DXF writer omits them (the
  report cites 252 solids in one source); linked writer work remains open in
  the inspected state. These are version- and direction-specific reports, not
  a verified ACadSharp result or a libdxfrw finding. They reinforce that
  read-side entity support and write-side carrier closure are separate rows.
* ezdxf's own entity-creation docs state that ACIS data creation requires an
  external library ([ACIS entity API](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/tasks/add_dxf_entities.rst));
  its ACIS browser exposes data for inspection, not an independent solid
  kernel. Treat ezdxf as an optional DXF carrier/control author only. A mesh
  authored into ACIS, then parsed/projected by a related tool, cannot serve as
  independent exact B-rep proof.
* Open CASCADE's official components index lists ACIS SAT/SAB import-export as
  a commercial extension rather than part of the open-source base
  ([components preview](https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT-Components/blob/main/ReadMe.md)).
  Therefore the plan must not assume a default OCCT/FreeCAD installation can
  semantically read ACIS, nor add that extension as an implicit dependency.
  Any licensed kernel route is an optional, separately approved qualification
  lane. FreeCAD documentation also distinguishes its C++ and legacy DXF
  importers and states a current ACIS-solid limitation
  ([Draft DXF documentation](https://wiki.freecad.org/Draft_DXF)); because
  documentation and importer backends can change independently, qualify an
  exact release/backend/runtime rather than treating this page as a timeless
  claim.
* The ODA File Converter is documented as loading and saving matched files to
  a requested output version/type, with an optional audit/repair pass
  ([official description](https://www.opendesign.com/guestfiles/oda_file_converter?language=en)).
  It is useful as a controlled translator in a composed comparison, but a
  converter's successful exit or output entity count is not independent
  semantic acceptance.

### Plan delta: close the carrier-loss gap before semantic promotion

Refine the existing S2.3 modeler-carrier, S5 comparator, and S8 publication /
read-modify-write gates; do not create another broad subplan or reorder the
local fast-test queue.

1. **Track four separate observations per source solid handle:** (a) entity
   parsed, (b) modeler bytes extracted and attached (inline SAT/SAB versus
   AcDs/ACDSDATA is recorded explicitly), (c) bytes and owner/history/block
   links emitted to the exact destination route, and (d) a named consumer
   produced a shape. Record version, direction, payload length/hash, owner
   path, INSERT depth, and disposition. A count at (a) must never imply (b),
   (c), or (d).
2. **Make loss visible and atomic.** If a requested writer route cannot emit
   an input modeler payload and its required associations, reject publication
   and preserve the pre-existing destination; do not silently write an empty
   3DSOLID/REGION/BODY shell or report full success. Reader behavior may retain
   a recognized shell for compatibility, but must record it as
   `ENTITY_ONLY / MODEL_DATA_MISSING` rather than semantic support. Preserve
   the repository's record-level recovery policy for unrelated malformed
   records.
3. **Extend the composed comparator, not every slice test.** At the existing
   optional milestone checkpoint, compare source→destination per-handle
   payload presence/hash and graph closure before invoking a consumer. For
   geometry promotion, require a named ACIS-capable reader and a separately
   recorded kernel/consumer result on a pinned build; verify known analytic
   controls with volume/bounds and valid-shape checks, and record tolerances,
   transformations, and importer backend. Mesh/tessellation output is a
   derived projection and must not be compared or labeled as exact B-rep
   preservation.
4. **Admit peers by route, not product name.** ACadSharp remains optional,
   direction-specific structural evidence until a pinned build proves both
   attached payload output and graph closure; LibreDWG #1411 remains a
   diagnostic lead until reproduced against a pinned binary; ezdxf is a
   bounded carrier/control-author route; OCCT ACIS extensions are excluded
   from required dependencies; ODA File Converter is a translator, not a
   geometry oracle. Do not make any of these a per-slice test dependency.
5. **Keep the implementation loop fast.** Continue generated ASCII/Binary
   DXF and existing no-fixture unit tests for each change. Run the exact-peer
   and native/kernel composition only after a local milestone reaches its
   carrier and graph-closure gates, and report each external lane as
   `NOT_RUN`, `STRUCTURAL_ONLY`, or `SEMANTICALLY_QUALIFIED` with its exact
   build identity. Failure to obtain an optional tool does not stop local
   work; it only leaves that evidence lane open.
6. **Do not duplicate the S2.2.5b local cut-policy tests.** The existing
   focused modeler-DXF matrix already exercises 254/255/256 and 509/510/511
   character boundaries, whitespace and indivisible-token cuts, explicit and
   implicit chunk metadata, and preserved-destination/corrected-retry
   negatives across the scoped versions/encodings. This characterizes the
   current local writer policy; it does not qualify legacy Binary-DXF SAT,
   because both the libdxfrw binary subjects and the ezdxf binary baseline
   remain rejected by the recorded ODA screen. Keep that positive calibration
   as an external acceptance gate, and continue unrelated ready local work
   instead of repeating the unchanged oracle or adding duplicate synthetic
   cases.

## Implementation progress — typed modeler carrier-status observation (2026-10-16; local fast slice)

stable string name for five carrier-evidence states: unknown, explicitly
empty, carrier bytes present, expected but unavailable, and contradictory.

CADKernel's detailed format table marks ACIS SAT/SAB unsupported, while its headline/summary claims broad commercial CAD compatibility and its FAQ says commercial-format import is planned. These are repository claims, not executed behavior. | Do not admit either project as an ACIS/DWG/DXF peer on kernel or headline claims alone. Aetheris is outside the current file-route scope unless a pinned relevant reader appears. For CADKernel, use only a later exact, source-visible route with demonstrated input/output artifact and controls; do not use it to promote semantic or support claims. This is `NO_NEW_EVIDENCE` for all current gates. |
| Current DXF authoring tools, including [`@tarikjabiri/dxf`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tarikjabiri/dxf) | The package's current 2.9.0 release and maintained writer source establish an available DXF generator, not a general 3D reader, a modeler-geometry writer, or an independent semantic oracle. | Keep locally authored controls as the default. Do not add this package as a dependency or replace generated C++ controls; reconsider only if a specific independent DXF tag-generation test is missing and a pinned API demonstrably covers it. |

### Research admission and stop rule

To prevent repeated candidate discovery from delaying implementation, each
future peer pass must answer, in this order:

1. **Which named gate is missing evidence?** Identify the exact layer—outer
   container/parser, entity/owner graph, payload bytes, ACIS topology/geometry,
   kernel validity, or native consumer. A general feature claim is not a gap.
2. **What independent evidence does this candidate add?** Pin source/release,
   dependencies, license/use constraints, platform, test/control lineage, and
   parser/kernel/consumer lineage. Mark shared-code and shared-kernel routes
   explicitly; do not count project or application names as independent votes.
3. **Is there an implementation-ready action?** Require a concrete control,
   expected result, diagnostic/loss accounting, and route-specific stop/pass
   criterion. If the candidate adds no layer beyond existing gates, record
   `NO_NEW_EVIDENCE` and stop without installing, cloning, or running it.
4. **Return immediately to local work** when no candidate passes those checks.
   Reopen this screen only for a new pinned release/source change, a
   reproducible peer failure relevant to a local boundary, or an already
   authorized external candidate that can fill an explicit deferred gate.
   External availability never blocks fast generated implementation slices.

This refines only existing PAR-07/S5/S8 research operations. Findings remain
125 and top-level implementation subplans remain 71. No production change,
local test, peer/native runtime, fixture, dependency, support promotion, or
external-J disposition changed. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; evidence from this scan is advisory and non-promoting.
The follow-up source sweep also surfaced Aetheris and refreshed CADKernel's
format claims; neither provides a newly qualified SAT/SAB + DWG/DXF route, so
the existing research stop rule still applies.

## Implementation progress — MLINESTYLE CMC and DXF schema refusal (2026-10-16; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Started the planned `7G.3f.4b.1b` MLINESTYLE slice without enabling the
adapter's named-resource emission path. `dwgBuffer::getCmColor` now exposes the
packed method, raw flag byte, and BS index. ODA v5.4.1 §2.11 specifies that the
R2004+ CMC index is always zero; the MLINESTYLE parser rejects a nonzero value
instead of silently discarding it. `DRW_MLineStyle` retains fill and per-element
RGB, method, flags, color name, and color-book name. The current DWG encoder and
typed DXF writer reject RGB, named/book, unknown-method, and nonzero raw-flag
forms rather than silently reducing them to ACI. The shared DWG CMC encoder now
emits the required zero R2004+ leading BS for ACI and RGB forms. The typed DXF writer also
uses scoped record state, handle remapping/reservation, validates finite values
and count bounds, and refuses an unresolved DWG linetype index/handle instead
of substituting `BYLAYER`.

DXF `MLINESTYLE` parsing now rejects a missing, duplicate, negative, or
out-of-range group-71 count; duplicate per-element color/linetype fields; and
count or tuple completeness mismatches at the record boundary. Generated
controls exercise legal top-level/tuple field reorder, complete ACI output and
handle remapping, RGB/named-book/unknown-flag refusal in ASCII and binary, and
malformed tuple/count cases. CMC buffer controls verify that method, name,
book, and unknown flag bits remain observable. They are generated in memory;
encoder controls verify its R2004+ zero-index output for ACI and RGB. They are
generated in memory; no testing drawing or fixture was added.

Validation: `cmake --build build-gcc -j4` passes under the repository's
warnings-as-errors configuration; `libdxfrw_wave1_tests
--mline-style-validation` passes; `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests

This pass widened the cross-project comparison while resolving the exact
field-loss boundary in the next planned MLINESTYLE writer slice. It compared

translation code, current DXF carrier/consumer documentation, and local

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |

ODA defines the DWG fill and each segment color as CMC; pre-R2018 stores a signed linetype index, while R2018+ stores a hard-pointer linetype handle. Thus a DWG CMC is not automatically representable by the documented DXF MLINESTYLE fields. Neither source says that a writer may silently reduce true color or color-book identity to ACI. | Keep the field/origin matrix explicit. A DWG-origin typed writer must either retain every observed CMC component and prove an output mapping for the exact target, or reject before publication. Do not use nearest-ACI approximation as preservation. DXF-origin exact raw replay remains a separate, provenance- and identity-gated route. |
| Local `DRW_MLineStyle`, `DRW_MLineElement`, `DRW_MLineStyle::parseDwg`, `encodeDwg`, and `dxfRW::writeMLineStyle` | Source inspection shows the top-level fill parser receives but discards RGB/name/book outputs; each element stores ACI and optional RGB but discards color name/book; the DWG encoder writes fill as ACI-only and writes element RGB without name/book. The DXF writer emits only documented group-62 colors. The local typed value therefore cannot currently distinguish or preserve every DWG CMC form. This is a source-confirmed representational gap, not evidence that a particular sample contains such values. | Amend `f.4b.1b`: add CMC admission/retention before connecting the typed DWG route. Until modeled and output-mapped, reject generated RGB-only, named/book, and other unrepresentable CMC values transactionally. Preserve exact raw DXF records only when the existing source-profile and graph checks admit them. Add locally generated controls for ACI, RGB, named/book, tuple completeness, and refusal-with-destination-preservation. |
| LibreDWG [MLINESTYLE upgrade/downgrade code](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dwg.c) and [current NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | The code explicitly maps pre-R2018 `lt_index` sentinels 0, 32767 and 32766 to CONTINUOUS, BYLAYER and BYBLOCK, and resolves positive indices through the LTYPE table when upgrading to R2018 handles. ## Deeper/broader peer-contract and ACIS operation review (2026-10-16; research only)

This pass checked whether additional open-source DXF implementations can
provide comparable evidence for the current mesh/carrier work, and whether a
successful ACIS import/output should count as end-to-end interoperability. It
used current project documentation/source, Autodesk's DXF references, and one
public peer discussion. This was static research only: no peer was installed
or run, no external drawing was fetched, and no code or test was changed.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ezdxf's [entity export contract](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dxfentity.py), [polyline documentation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/dxfentities/polyline.rst), and [factory API](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/tasks/add_dxf_entities.rst) | ezdxf explicitly describes itself as a DXF interface rather than a CAD application or version converter; its entity layer warns that features unavailable in the selected DXF version may be ignored on export. Its API has distinct POLYLINE modes (2D/3D polyline, polygon mesh, polyface) and a separate MESH factory. This establishes useful typed authoring/read paths, not general downgrade conversion, complete graph preservation, or semantic equivalence across versions. | Admit ezdxf only for the exact version/entity/operation it supports. Do not use export-to-older-version as a converter oracle. If the comparison intentionally downgrades, declare the exact projection (for example MESH to faces), inventory each source handle's emitted/omitted result, and score it as a lossy projection rather than native-entity parity. |
| Autodesk [MESH DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-4B9ADA67-87C8-4673-A579-6E4C76FF7025.htm), [POLYLINE reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-ABF6B778-BE20-4B49-9B58-A94E64CEFFF3.htm), [VERTEX reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-0741E831-599E-4CBF-91E1-8ADBCFD6556D.htm), and GDAL's [DXF known-issues list](https://github.com/OSGeo/gdal/blob/master/ogr/ogrsf_frmts/dxf/KNOWN_ISSUES.md) | Autodesk defines `MESH`/`AcDbSubDMesh` as a cage/subdivision record with versioned topology, crease, and property-override fields; classic POLYLINE mesh and PFACE use different mode flags and child VERTEX records. GDAL documents MESH as unsupported and represents 3DFACE as OGR polygons with an outline-oriented style. The GDAL list is a project limitation note, not a current binary run. None of these is a B-rep or evaluated subdivision specification. | Keep MESH, POLYMESH, POLYFACE, 3DFACE, and 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY as separate matrix rows. Do not accept a GDAL zero-count as MESH loss by libdxfrw, or a face projection as native MESH identity. Keep the existing version-profiled MESH tests and distinguish authored cage topology/creases from evaluated surfaces and modeler geometry. |
| ezdxf maintainer response in [discussion #1295](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/discussions/1295) | A user reports an ezdxf-authored mesh-derived `3DSOLID` that AutoCAD could inspect with `MASSPROP` but that failed in a Dynamo Boolean-intersection workflow; the maintainer characterizes ezdxf ACIS support as very basic and cautions against assuming full feature support. This is a single, uncontrolled report: the payload, exact software versions, and failure cause are not independently reproducible from the discussion. | Refine the existing native-consumer gate to record operation-level outcomes: file open/record recognition, display, mass-property query, editability, and Boolean operations are separate observations. A pass for one operation cannot imply the others. Require exact producer payload, target version, application/backend/build, operation, and independent expected result before any positive semantic claim. Treat this discussion only as a failure-mode lead. |
| Current [LibreDWG issue #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411) and existing peer receipts in this plan | It reports a modern R2013+ ACIS/AcDs payload disappearing while its REGION/3DSOLID record survives in a particular LibreDWG build. It is consistent with the documented separation between entity shell, external carrier association, and downstream operation, but does not reproduce a libdxfrw or current-LibreDWG defect. | Preserve the per-handle chain already required by PAR-07/S8: source entity → inline/AcDs carrier and owner path → emitted target entity/carrier → consumer result. Keep record count, carrier bytes, valid shape, and operation success as independent evidence fields. |

### Implementation-ready peer admission checklist

At the existing composed peer checkpoint (not per fast slice):

1. Freeze the input and output versions, peer source/build, ASCII/binary
   route, strict/recovery mode, options, and exact operation. Verify the peer
   actually supports the source entity identity before comparing counts.
2. Build a per-source-handle ledger with literal DXF type/subclass, block and
   INSERT path, output type, raw-carrier disposition, diagnostics, and any
   conversion/projection. Do not infer a family pass from a document-open
   result or aggregate count.
3. For explicit geometry, compare raw fields/topology first: native `MESH`
   against `MESH`/versioned `SUBDIVISION`, PFACE signed edge visibility and

   rendering, convex hull, and evaluated subdivision as derived projections.
4. For ACIS, retain separate columns for exact bytes/association, parsed
   topology, complete shape construction, kernel validity/expected metrics,
   and each tested native operation. A same-project parser+writer cycle, a
   rendered tessellation, or `MASSPROP` alone is not a complete semantic pass.
5. If the route is unavailable or lacks the needed entity/operation, mark the
   cell `NOT_AVAILABLE` / `NOT_RUN` and continue local implementation. Do not
   add a dependency or block a fast slice to resolve a peer limitation.

### Implementation-ready MLEADER sequence under existing annotation and graph gates

This is a readiness refinement under the existing MLeader finding/annotation and
object-reference owners (PAR-20/7F/7AA and the existing Slice 8 comparison
gates). It is not a new top-level finding or support-promotion path.

1. **Retain before attempting support — COMPLETE.** Override `addMLeader` in `dx_iface`;
   own a copy in the correct model/paper-space or block entity list, matching
   existing entity callback ownership. Test both direct callback and generated
   DXF import. Until a qualified writer exists, strict export must reach the
   existing MLEADER fail-closed diagnostic rather than omit the entity. Verify
   that the check sees entities nested in block definitions as well as the
   current model block.
2. **Close the parser's fidelity boundary — FAIL-CLOSED POLICY COMPLETE.** Make nested-context parsing
   preserve unknown tag sequences as bounded raw tags, or reject unknown
   codes/markers with a structured unsupported-context diagnostic; do not
   silently swallow them. Validate marker nesting, repeated-value ordering,
   vector cardinality, transform length, numeric ranges, and count/byte budgets.
   If policy chooses lossless carrier replay, bind it to source identity,
   exact record name/version, and complete context state; do not mix it with a
   partially edited typed entity.
3. **Correct the low-level writer boundary — COMPLETE.** Require target `>= AC1021` until
   evidence resolves the ezdxf R2000 statement. Keep the DXF record token
   `MULTILEADER`; verify exact entity/class metadata from a valid producer
   output rather than copying third-party `CLASS`/`DwgVersion`/item-class
   guesses. Gate the AC1021 legacy arrowhead/block-label arrays separately
   from AC1024 class-version/context deltas.
4. **Close typed edges before publication — COMPLETE (2026-10-17).** The low-
   level writer remaps modeled non-null entity, context, line, and AC1021 legacy-
   array references through the source-to-emitted map and refuses a remap to
   zero before writing bytes. The adapter preflight then requires a unique,
   correctly typed MLEADERSTYLE rooted under `ACAD_MLEADERSTYLE`; validates
   entity groups 341–344, text/block context handles, leader-line linetype and
   arrowhead handles, and AC1021 legacy references against their target kinds;
   and checks entity group-330 against the actual containing named block or
   model/paper-space BLOCK_RECORD. It distinguishes absent optional edges from
   invalid nonzero edges and preserves the final serializer refusal and
   destination-before-publication behavior. Receipt:
   [`mleader-typed-reference-containing-owner-closure-fast-slice-2026-10-17.json`](docs/research/mleader-typed-reference-containing-owner-closure-fast-slice-2026-10-17.json).
5. **Preserve semantics, not only tags — PARTIAL (2026-10-17).** The low-level
   writer now refuses unmodeled TOLERANCE/unknown content types before
   publication; generated controls cover no-content, MTEXT/BLOCK type-versus-
   context tag distinctions, WCS coordinate passthrough, and the complete
   block transform array. Producer-backed legal-combination and consumer
   qualification remain open. Continue to test MTEXT, BLOCK, no-content, and
   TOLERANCE content states; support TOLERANCE only if its representation is
   complete, otherwise reject it explicitly. Treat the entity-level content
   type (group 172) separately from context-level `hasMText` (290) and
   `HasBlock` (296): Autodesk documents these in different group-code tables
   and does not specify the full legal-combination matrix. Do not infer a
   one-to-one relation from the field names or emit an unsupported combination
   as qualified output; establish accepted tuples from ODA plus producer-authored
   controls. Cover multiple roots/lines, straight/spline/invisible leaders,
   vertex and break pairs, block transforms, attributes, columns,
   text/background fields, per-line overrides, annotative state, R2007 array
   fields, and R2010/R2013 additions. Compare override flags and directly stored
   values independently: ezdxf documents that flags can disagree with field
   values, so neither is an automatic normalization oracle. Its documentation
   describes leader vertices as WCS, including BLOCK-content cases; preserve
   raw coordinates and verify that frame against producer-authored controls
   before introducing any coordinate conversion. Keep context transforms as a
   separate matrix/position/scale/rotation axis.
6. **Use fast local tests first.** Extend the current generated adapter/writer
   owners; exercise ASCII and binary DXF, AC1021/AC1024/AC1027, each context
   family, each producer-confirmed content-type/context-flag tuple, and
   forward/reverse/dangling/wrong-kind/duplicate references, malformed nesting,
   an unknown nested tag, and a following sentinel entity. Assert literal
   context-sensitive tag order/values as well as typed readback; a flat group
   code projection can confuse entity 172 (content type) with context 172 (text
   flow direction). Seed the destination before negative cases and verify byte
   identity after refusal; correct the control and retry to establish
   transactional recovery. Use a pinned ezdxf 1.4.5 parse only at the existing
   optional composed checkpoint, reporting parser acceptance separately from
   field semantics and native acceptance. Run only touched strict targets,
   their focused CTest(s), the narrow adapter mode, and `git diff --check` per
   slice. Do not add or commit test drawings.
7. **Promote only with independent semantics.** Generate controls from scratch
   or use already admitted repository fixtures; pin each producer's exact
   release/commit and output version. Compare normalized entity/context graphs
   and reference kinds with a genuinely independent reader. Add exact-version
   native CAD open/save/render or explode checks for MTEXT and BLOCK cases,
   including block-contained and paper-space entities. A DXF parseback,
   record count, same-library roundtrip, or rendering from a generated
   projection alone is not native acceptance.

wire representation, semantic text, source DWG storage path, and downstream
rendering instead of treating “string round trip” as one result. Peer reports

| Autodesk [Group Code Value Types / Storage of String Values](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-2553CF98-44F6-4828-82DD-FE3BC7448113.htm) | The documented emitted representation follows the selected DXF version: pre-R2007 uses plain ASCII and CIF, while R2007+ supports UTF-8. The examples show `\U+XXXX` as a Unicode control sequence, but do not by themselves settle how every arbitrary application/object string containing those characters should be interpreted. | Keep target-version serialization separate from source-DWG string decoding. For PAR-05/7AR, assert both the physical emitted bytes and the decoded Unicode scalar; do not let a semantic equality check hide a wrong target encoding or invalid UTF-8. Keep MTEXT inline-control semantics distinct from generic/XRECORD payload treatment until the field contract establishes whether a backslash sequence is semantic or literal. |

It gives an author-run 43-file patch comparison, but is framed as a question about intended behavior; neither its patch nor its output is an independent result or a normative rule. Added an explicit lowercase `\U+abcd` CIF positive to the existing GBK/codepage
test owner. The assertion checks the U+ABCD UTF-8 scalar and confirms the

allows this small control to run independently without another CTest entry.

CP936-encoded MLINESTYLE and matching MLINE reference, then applies the
existing round-trip assertions. This keeps the adapter's fail-closed graph
invariant intact and lets the existing codepage CTest remain a valid positive
control.

## Implementation progress — Turkish-locale CP1254 end-to-end control (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

Added a focused `--turkish-codepage` mode to the existing GBK/codepage
executable. When an installed Turkish C locale is available, it generates an
AC1018 ASCII DXF with lowercase `$DWGCODEPAGE=ansi_1254` and a CP1254 `0xD0`
TEXT value, imports it as U+011E, exports legacy DXF, checks that the emitted
TEXT group contains the exact `0xD0` byte and canonical `ANSI_1254` header,
then re-imports and verifies U+011E again. The test restores the prior locale
and removes its generated temporary files. On hosts without a Turkish locale,
the focused mode reports SKIP rather than pretending locale execution passed.

The filename suffix audit found no remaining locale-dependent case operation
in `dx_iface::fileImport`: ASCII extension folding is explicit and the
existing generated adapter control accepts uppercase `.DXF` while refusing a
non-ASCII suffix before either reader starts. This slice does not generalize
that result to unrelated symbol/path strings or other `tolower` call sites.

## Implementation progress — MLEADER context group-172 scope correction (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

The nested MLEADER context parser now treats group 172 as context-level flow
direction, independent of the `hasTextContents` flag. Previously it was
incorrectly included in the text-payload admission gate, so a context carrying
flow direction without an MTEXT branch was rejected even though group 172 is
not part of that branch. Entity-level group 172 remains the distinct
content-type field. Both fields reject negative narrowing; the context field
is stored only when it fits the model's 16-bit range, while the DXF reader
rejects values outside its own 16-bit wire carrier before parser dispatch.

The existing hardening tests exercise entity/context group-172 scope
separately, accept a context with flow direction and no text-content flag,
reject negative parser values, and verify that a 65536 group-172 value is
refused by the ASCII reader. No new CTest, fixture, dependency, or support
claim was added.

## Implementation progress — MLEADER independent context flow direction and content-axis retention (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

The context parser already retained group 172 as text flow direction even when
`hasTextContents` was false, but the low-level DXF writer emitted it only inside
the MTEXT payload branch. That created a local read→write loss path for a
non-default modeled context value. The writer now emits context group 172
outside that conditional when MTEXT is absent, while keeping the established
ordering for MTEXT-bearing contexts. Entity-level group 172 remains the
separate content-type field.

The focused hardening control now crosses content types 0/1/2 with context
flag pairs 00/10/01/11, rooted/rootless contexts, and ASCII/binary DXF (48
generated cases). Each case round-trips context flags, the independent
flow-direction field, relevant branch payloads, nontrivial context/root/leader
coordinates, and a following record sentinel. A non-default flow direction
alone is sufficient to retain an otherwise rootless context wrapper.
Branch-owned payload is expected only when its corresponding flag is set.
This is a representational preservation matrix, not an assertion that every
content-type/flag tuple is valid in a producer-authored file.

Research also screened the local AC1021 candidate named
`architectural_-_annotation_scaling_and_multileaders.dwg`: the debug trace
reaches repeated type-521 MLEADER parses, but the strict CLI reports 13 reader
CRC mismatches and 36 object parse failures and publishes no DXF. The sample
therefore cannot currently establish a producer-valid tuple. Autodesk's

labels group 172 as text flow direction among context-data codes; its table
does not define the full content-type/flag legality matrix. Continue to require
clean producer provenance and independent semantic readback before any
adapter serializer admission.

### Evidence-independence and readiness refinement

Comparator admission must record six different provenance dimensions rather
than one generic “independent peer” flag:

1. **Implementation lineage:** source repository, exact revision/artifact,
   forks/wrappers and reused parser components.
2. **Format-reference lineage:** ODA/spec revision, Autodesk tables, reverse-
   engineering evidence, or producer traces used to derive the behavior. Two
   separately written readers against the same ambiguous specification are
   code-diverse, not independent format witnesses.
3. **Producer lineage:** origin of the test drawing/bytes and exact writer or
   generator; mark same-library round trips as internal consistency only.
4. **Expected-value lineage:** who authored the semantic manifest and how its
   coordinates, handles, topology, units, and version were established.
5. **Consumer/kernel route:** parser, graph resolver, renderer/tessellator,
   B-rep kernel, and native application must be named separately; pixels or a
   preview SceneGraph cannot stand in for field-level preservation.
6. **Artifact/runtime:** immutable source SHA or package hash, build options,
   runtime/toolchain, platform, selected import/export route, input hash, and
   complete diagnostics/loss inventory.

Implementation order stays unchanged: keep the local fast path and proceed
with already-ready generated-vector and parser hardening slices; use peers
only at the scheduled composed checkpoint. For any peer control, use a
locally generated scratch input or a fixture already present in LibreCAD or

### Implementation-ready sequence and stop boundaries

1. **Loss guard first (smallest, fastest slice).** Extend the existing in-memory
   AC1024 frame builder with `hasLinkedData=1` and a nonzero cell-attribute
   count. Mark the semantic cell/table incomplete until the relevant fields are
   captured; assert no partial typed cell publication, valid entity-prefix
   retention, TABLECONTENT cursor rollback, anonymous-block/INSERT fallback,
   and a following-record sentinel. The unsupported route must diagnose at
   the semantic subrecord, not fail the whole DWG read. Run only the touched
   `-Werror` target, `^libdxfrw_dwg_object_vectors$`, and the strict adapter
   CTest if the fallback path changes.
2. **Typed capture next.** Add linked state/handle/range/unknown fields and fill
   the existing `DRW_TableCellAttribute` tuples. Check count/remaining-bits
   admission before allocation, invalid BL92 values, null versus failed handle
   reads, deep copy/reset, and exact source-cursor behavior. Exercise both the
   AC1021 standalone parser and AC1024 inline parser with generated bytes; call
   these parser vectors, not DWG producer qualification.
3. **Graph route as a separate implementation item.** Trace how a real
   existing TABLECONTENT/DATALINK pair is rooted and owned before adding
   adapter output. Then close the edge through reader dispatch → callback →
   `dx_data` retention → object owner/reference census → DXF TABLECONTENT and
   DATALINK emitters → one-time handle remap → ordinary ASCII/binary readback.
   If the object’s root or DATALINK payload cannot be safely represented,
   reject the affected conversion before publication and expose the omission
   rather than writing a table with a severed link.

## Implementation progress — PAR-126 cell-content index retention (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

`DRW_TableCellAttribute` now stores `m_contentIndex` separately from
`m_index`: the former identifies the owning content in the cell's ordered
`m_contents`, while the latter retains the ATTDEF tuple ordinal. The AC1021
TABLECONTENT parser assigns the enclosing content-loop index. The ACAD_TABLE
DXF parser captures the active content slot at group 179, applies it to group
331 tuples, and accumulates attributes across content slots rather than
discarding earlier tuples. If a tuple arrives without a current content, the
parser marks the table incomplete and stores `UINT32_MAX` rather than silently
assigning the default slot zero.

Generated controls cover a scalar value in content slot 0 followed by a block
with an ATTDEF override in slot 1. The AC1021 standalone object vector directly
asserts `m_contentIndex == 1`, `m_index == 0`, value order, block handle and
attribute text. Generated ASCII and binary DXF controls assert the same
association through normal import. The AC1024 inline TABLE vector exercises
the equivalent two-content shape but verifies only the deliberate atomic
fallback: any attribute-bearing inline grid remains unpublished, with the
validated TABLE prefix and cursor intact. The existing DXF writer and adapter
remain one-content-only and now reject a nonzero content index before output.
An additional malformed DXF control confirms an unassociated ATTDEF tuple
remains explicitly unassociated and cannot be mistaken for slot zero.

## Autodesk TABLE multi-content DXF writer evidence boundary (2026-10-17; research only)

The next tempting local TABLE slice was to remove the writer's one-content-per-
cell restriction. A source check does not yet make that implementation-ready.
Autodesk's [TABLE (DXF) group-code contract](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D8CCD2F0-18A3-42BB-A64D-539114A07DA0.htm)
describes group 171 as one cell type per cell, group 301 as a cell-value-block
begin marker, text groups 302/303 as repeated text for a cell, group 340 as a
block pointer for a block-type cell, and group 179/331/300 as its ATTDEF tuple.
It does not define ordering/boundaries for arbitrary ordered `Cell.Contents`
entries or multiple block/text/field contents in one cell. Autodesk's
[managed Table API](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_Table_GetBlockAttributeValue_int_int_int_ObjectId.html)
and [`GetContentTypes`](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_Table_GetContentTypes_int_int_int.html)
confirm a zero-based content ordinal in the in-memory API; they do not specify
its DXF serialization. The generated ASCII/binary multi-content parser control
in this repository uses a hand-authored sequence and therefore tests our
parser's behavior only, not a producer-authored wire contract.

**Implementation decision:** leave `dxfRW::writeTable()` and the adapter
single-content-only, failing before publication for multiple contents or an
attribute tuple whose `m_contentIndex` is nonzero. Do not infer a group-code
sequence from the C++ API or the local generated vector. Reopen this writer
extension only when either (a) authoritative Autodesk/ODA serialization
documentation specifies the complete repeated-content framing, or (b) a
target-authored multi-content DXF can be traced and read back with ordered
content types and attribute-to-content identity. If neither arrives, continue
other ready implementation slices; this evidence gap must not pause the goal.

No code/test was changed and no test was run in this research-only decision.
It adds no finding/subplan or support claim; counts remain 126/71 and J256,
J260, J268, J284, J293 and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

### Implementation-ready refinement under PAR-12/S13

1. **No per-slice expansion.** The smallest source-generated boundary and
   parser-owner tests remain the default. The existing deterministic extended
   lane remains scheduled/manual; do not run it, a full suite, a peer parser,
   or a native CAD matrix for each leaf implementation slice.
2. **Coverage-gap decision gate.** Consider a separate coverage-guided target
   only when a named parser-hardening task has a concrete valid locally-built
   seed but the current focused/deterministic tests cannot explore a relevant
   branch or state transition. If no such gap is demonstrated, record the
   target as unnecessary and continue the ready implementation queue.
3. **Route split and bounds.** If justified, make independent targets for
   ASCII DXF, binary DXF, DWG buffer input, and any decode→encode→decode route;
   do not silently detect-and-mix them. Bound input bytes, work/time, memory,
   and output; create a fresh reader/interface per input unless a specific
   state-reuse bug is under test. Fuzzing a writer route must verify
   failure-atomic output and direct readback, not just non-crash.
4. **Harness qualification before campaign results.** Add a fast self-check
   using each generated seed to verify target invocation, cleanup, state reset,
   and deterministic completion. Unexpected exceptions, sanitizer failures,
   timeouts, OOM, parser rejections, and harness setup errors must remain
   distinct outcomes; never catch-and-discard the crash signal.
5. **Crash-to-regression path.** Reproduce a finding through the direct
   affected API, minimize it, inspect the relevant cursor/owner invariant,
   and express the regression as a compact source-generated byte/string
   builder test. Keep external or corpus-derived bytes outside commits unless
   independently admitted under the established fixture policy. Do not use a
   fuzzer's corpus growth or a non-crashing parse as semantic support evidence.
6. **Cost containment.** Any new target is opt-in and isolated from default
   CMake builds; use a fixed bounded schedule and no uploaded corpus/crash
   artifacts. A future Clang lane must not replace the current GCC fast
   checks. Continue only if its coverage report shows it reaches a named
   source path that existing generated vectors miss.

## Implementation progress — PAR-126 DATALINK callback capture and fail-closed export (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The concrete `dx_iface` previously inherited the base no-op `addDataLink`
callback, so a parsed DATALINK object had no owned adapter representation.
This slice adds `dx_data::dataLinks` and a null-safe callback override that
copies the complete `DRW_DataLink`, including its custom-data vector. It does
not introduce a DATALINK writer or claim that the cell→DATALINK→owner/range
graph is closed.

`dx_iface::fileExport()` now checks the retained object list at the earliest
feature preflight and returns false when it is nonempty. That refusal occurs
before the output destination is opened/replaced because the supported
TABLECONTENT/DATALINK object graph and serializer are not established. The
existing incomplete TABLE INSERT fallback remains unchanged for authored
controls without a typed DATALINK object; importing a real linked object
therefore cannot silently publish a drawing that omits it.

The existing `libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests` target gained a fast focused
mode. Its source-authored ASCII OBJECTS sequence runs through
`dxfRW::processDataLink()` and verifies the adapter owns the parsed object and
nested custom data. For both ASCII and binary targets, it then places a
sentinel at the destination, confirms export refusal preserves it, removes
the unqualified object, and retries on the same adapter/output successfully.
No DWG/DXF payload fixture was created or committed; the test input is built
from a string at runtime. No new CTest registration or dependency was added.

## Implementation progress — TABLECONTENT field-reference role and stream bounds (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.97 identifies the ACDbTableContent field-reference count as
the number of cell contents containing a field reference and specifies each
following `H` as a hard-owner handle to an `AcDbField`. ODA §2.13 defines `H`
with a 4-bit reference code and 4-bit byte counter before the optional handle
or offset payload. Thus each repeated `H` requires at least its 8-bit header;
the bound does not assume any payload width.

`parseTableContent` now verifies, before reserving `m_fieldHandles`, that the
declared count fits the remaining bounded handle stream at that minimum size.
Each entry is then read with a required hard-owner role instead of accepting
any handle code. A zero count preserves the existing optional-handle-buffer
behavior. AC1021 standalone TABLECONTENT generated vectors and AC1024 inline
TABLE vectors cover valid hard-owned references with trailing style framing,
wrong-role rejection, and a count larger than minimum remaining handle
capacity. The AC1024 refusal keeps the validated TABLE prefix and publishes no
partial semantic grid; the standalone AC1021 parser fails and resets the
object as before.

Validation:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_object_vectors_tests dwg2dxf -j2` — pass.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_object_vectors$' --output-on-failure` — pass, 1/1 (0.15 s).
- `cmake --build build-gcc --target lc3_compat_check -j2` — pass.

This pass expands the earlier MLEADER group-code review across the normative DWG layout, Autodesk's public DXF/API descriptions, an independent DXF parser/writer implementation, LibreDWG's current class-maturity registry, and the local parser/writer/test/sample paths. Entity group 172 is the 0=None / 1=Block / 2=MTEXT / 3=TOLERANCE content enum. Inside nested context, group 172 instead means text flow direction; group 290 means root content-valid inside LEADER and context has-text at context level; group 296 means has-block. The DWG body uses a conditional text-or-block branch, and the spec describes the content object as either block or multiline text. It gives no TOLERANCE payload grammar in this context table. | Keep parser state/nesting and carrier-specific grammar explicit. Retain TOLERANCE and unknown content types as output refusals until represented. Do not reuse a group-code number without its current entity/context/root scope. The DWG branch layout is authoritative for DWG bytes, not automatically a complete DXF validity matrix. |
| Autodesk [common MLeader group codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-69B9139A-48B4-48A5-B3CF-A3233ABFBE49.htm), [context group codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-EC56D0DE-026D-46AB-87B1-9692393B0C22.htm), and ObjectARX [ContentType enum](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2019/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OREFNET-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_ContentType.html) | Public DXF tables separately name entity-level content type 172 and context hasMText 290 / HasBlock 296; context-level 172 is text flow direction. The API enum names all four content values. None publishes a full legal cross-product of content type, both flags, payload presence, and version, or specifies how contradictory/stale branch fields must be handled. | Do not invent an equality or exclusivity check from names alone. Build evidence by grammar scope and authored payload; preserve or refuse ambiguous states instead of normalizing them. API enum membership does not prove the library can serialize a type's payload. |

Its block transform stores the 16-value matrix in transposed order. The source comments also distinguish WCS leader vertices and warn that its transform path does not support non-uniform scaling. This is useful peer implementation behavior, not a normative DXF contract, pinned release run, or native CAD result. | A dual-enabled DXF context is not safe to reject solely by importing the DWG spec's conditional encoding into DXF. Preserve the existing dual-branch generated case as an ambiguity/structure control, not as a validity witness. ### Implementation readiness and fastest safe path

1. **Inactive branch payload guard — COMPLETE (local fast slice).** The DXF parser rejects text payload fields when 290 is false and block payload fields when 296 is false. 3. **Separate DXF and DWG admission.** The local DXF writer currently refuses content type 3 and unknown values. Keep that guard. The DWG block-content encoder currently refuses the block branch; any future implementation needs independent ODA-backed body/handle order, block-record reference closure, matrix preservation, same-version round-trip, and independent consumer evidence. Keep per-carrier outcomes distinct. If a tuple has no producer witness, leave it ambiguous and unsupported rather than filling the matrix by assumption.
5. **Keep validation fast.** Run only the touched strict MLEADER target and its existing focused selectors per local slice. Use full suites and native/peer runs once at the composed checkpoint after the local matrix and graph gates close, not in each leaf loop. No new external dependency is required for the local loss guard.

## Implementation progress — MLEADER inactive-branch payload refusal (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

The cross-carrier audit found that DXF context parsing stored branch payload values even when their context flags said those branches were absent, while the writer emitted those fields only for active branches. That could silently narrow an imported entity on re-export. The nested parser now refuses the text-specific field set unless group 290 is true and refuses block-specific handles, placement, scale, rotation, color, and matrix fields unless group 296 is true. The rejection occurs before reading/assigning the offending value and before the entity callback. The LEADER-root group 290, entity-level content type 172, and context text-flow group 172 remain scoped separately.

The existing hardening round-trip deliberately has content type BLOCK with both context flags true. It still round-trips both branches locally; this remains an ambiguity/structure control, not a producer-validity witness. Type 3 TOLERANCE and unknown entity content types continue to fail closed on DXF output. DWG block-context output remains unsupported and rejected by the separate DWG encoder.

Generated hardening controls emit an unflagged MTEXT label and an unflagged BLOCK handle through both ASCII and binary DXF tag readers. Both reject before setting the typed label/handle. The existing writer-version test now also emits a context with no content branches (00) and a following-record sentinel in both encodings; its existing MTEXT and BLOCK controls cover 10 and 01, while the hardening round-trip covers 11. This completes the local four-pair structural grid without calling any pair producer-valid. No downloaded or committed drawing fixture, new CTest registration, dependency, or native/peer run was added.

Validation:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_hardening_tests -j2` — pass.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --mleader-context-roundtrip` — pass; includes both malformed ASCII/binary controls and the existing dual-flag preservation case.
- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_wave1_tests -j2` — pass.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_mleader_writer_version$' --output-on-failure` — pass, 1/1 (0.27 s), including the new ASCII/binary 00 context profile.
- Scoped `git diff --check` and receipt JSON validation — pass.

This closes one local DXF read→write narrowing path only. It does not determine the full content-type × flag legality matrix, validate dual-flag semantics, serialize DWG block content, or establish native/peer support. No support claim or external-J disposition changed. Findings/subplans remain 126/71; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The shared checkout remains broadly modified and uncommitted; continue with the next implementation-ready plan item.
