output volume both source names map to one filesystem output name, but the CLI
admitted the list and began conversion. This is a concrete 7BH.3 collision
gap. An exploratory ASCII-fold plus case-probe implementation was removed
because it contradicted the existing plan requirement to use filesystem-native
equivalence rather than ASCII folding or a small number of Unicode probes.
The reproduction is diagnostic evidence only; it is not a passing regression
control and no support/collision-safety claim is promoted.

### Primary platform evidence and capability boundary

| Platform | Primary-source fact | Implementation consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | Microsoft documents `FILE_CASE_SENSITIVE_INFORMATION` as per-directory state and exposes `FILE_CS_FLAG_CASE_SENSITIVE_DIR`; `GetFileInformationByName` documents querying it. Windows/WSL documents per-directory settings and an inheritance exception in WSL 1. ([structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntifs/ns-ntifs-_file_case_sensitive_information), [query API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-getfileinformationbyname), [WSL behavior](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/case-sensitivity)) | Query the actual output directory; do not infer from `_WIN32`, volume type alone, or a child-directory probe. Query failure/filesystem support gaps must be explicit. Separately model Win32/NT path aliases such as trailing-dot/space normalization and 8.3 aliases; case flag alone does not close collision identity. Test normal NTFS and a case-sensitive directory, and treat WSL/remote-provider behavior as a distinct qualification route. |
| Linux | The kernel documents ext4 case-insensitive lookup as a per-directory feature, requiring the filesystem-wide casefold feature and encoding model. It describes canonical-decomposition comparison, a Unicode-version dependency, and fallback behavior for invalid strings when strict mode is not required. The directory flag is `EXT4_CASEFOLD_FL`. ([ext4 documentation](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/ext4.html), [inode flags](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/filesystems/ext4/inodes.html)) | Do not assume all Linux directories are bytewise case-sensitive or that every filesystem uses ext4 rules. For ext4, query the actual directory flag and supported encoding/version, and define invalid UTF-8 handling. For unsupported filesystems, mounts, or unreadable capability state, fail closed/actionably rather than silently use lexical or ASCII comparison. Keep native Linux validation separate from the Darwin repro. |
| macOS / Apple filesystems | Apple documents APFS case-sensitive and case-insensitive variants; its archived APFS FAQ describes normalization-insensitive behavior in both variants and Unicode 9.0 rules for the documented APFS generation. Foundation exposes `volumeSupportsCaseSensitiveNames`; Apple cautions that non-APFS volumes exist. ([APFS filename FAQ](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/FileManagement/Conceptual/APFS_Guide/FAQ/FAQ.html), [volume capability](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/urlresourcevalues/volumesupportscasesensitivenames), [file access guidance](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technologyoverviews/files-and-directories)) | Case sensitivity alone is not a complete name comparator: canonical Unicode-equivalent names may collide even on case-sensitive APFS. Verify the archived Unicode/normalization details against the target macOS and actual volume before encoding them. Query actual volume/filesystem behavior; do not infer from host OS or copy APFS semantics to HFS+, network mounts, or other providers. |

These sources confirm why the failed preflight cannot be fixed by the current
portable lexical `std::filesystem::path` set alone. They do **not** provide one
portable C++ comparator for all filesystem providers. A temporary child
namespace is acceptable only after the implementation verifies that parent
and child use equivalent collation (Windows per-directory settings make this
nontrivial); every created marker must be exclusively owned, identity-checked,
and cleaned before conversion. Prefer a native capability-derived comparator
or full-name index with expected `O(n log n)` behavior at the 10,000-item batch
limit; avoid pairwise `O(n²)` comparisons and repeated broad test suites.

### Implementation-ready next slice

1. Add a small internal capability result for the actual existing output
   directory: filesystem/provider identity, case sensitivity, normalization
   or casefold profile, and whether the profile is known and supported.
   Windows, ext4, and Apple implementations must remain isolated behind
   platform guards; unknown or unavailable capabilities return a clear
   preflight error without creating outputs.
2. Implement exact future-name equivalence using that profile (not ASCII
   folding). Include Windows trailing-dot/space and short-name concerns where
   the API/provider permits proof; keep dangling symlinks and missing inputs
   distinct from future-name collisions. Recheck protected identities at
   publication as already required by 7BH.3.
3. Extend the current Python batch contract harness with from-scratch local
   name pairs: ASCII case, canonically equivalent Unicode, case-sensitive
   positives, and provider-specific aliases only where safely constructible.
   Assert rejection before any output, unchanged existing entries, and no
   leftover probe. Do not add or download DWG/DXF fixtures; reuse the current
   repository AC1015 DWG plus locally generated minimal DXF.
4. Keep the validation fast: strict `dwg2dxf` build plus the focused batch
   selector on each code change. Add no separate CTest registration and defer
   full CLI/CAD suites to the composed checkpoint. Require native macOS,
   Linux, and Windows runs before marking platform gates qualified; report
   filesystem/provider identities with each receipt.
5. Add a bounded synthetic-name benchmark/control at the 10,000-item limit
   only after the comparator exists. Require `O(n log n)` or similarly
   bounded indexed work; do not time full converters or run a full test suite
   to tune this preflight.

This research adds no finding or top-level subplan and changes no support
claim. It sharpened the existing 7BH.3 implementation sequence only. The
subsequent local APFS implementation slice is recorded below; native Linux and
Windows qualification remains open. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting; totals remain 127 findings / 71
top-level subplans.

## Implementation progress — 7BH.3 native batch-output collation preflight (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

- Batch preflight now sends every planned output basename through native
  filesystem creation in an exclusively created child namespace, so the
  provider itself resolves case and Unicode normalization equivalence. It
  queries and compares the actual parent/child profile before using the
  namespace: Windows per-directory case flag and volume ID; Linux ext4 volume
  ID plus `FS_CASEFOLD_FL`; and macOS APFS volume ID plus Foundation's
  case-sensitivity property. Unknown providers, missing APIs, profile
  mismatch, invalid names, and create/cleanup failures fail closed. POSIX
  entries are created/removed relative to held directory handles with
  `mkdirat`/`unlinkat`; owned marker and namespace identities are checked
  before deletion. Windows markers also use file identity checks.
- The helper is wired only into batch preflight. Existing exact-path, list,
  input, symlink/hard-link, overwrite, and per-file transaction checks remain
  separate. Output basename collisions are rejected before conversion; no
  output file is opened or overwritten by the name-collision probe itself.
- The existing `dwg2dxf_cli_contract_tests.py` batch owner now covers ASCII
  case-equivalent and canonically equivalent Unicode output names, a relative
  output-directory path, case-sensitive positives where the actual test
  filesystem permits them, output-directory cleanliness, and the existing
  suffix/identity cases. Collision inputs are copied from the tracked AC1015
  fixture or generated locally; no DWG/DXF fixture was added or downloaded.
- Strict `cmake --build build-gcc --target dwg2dxf -j2` passed on Darwin 27
  arm64. The focused `--batch-only` harness passed 27 controls. The isolated
  10,000-planned-name limit control passed in 2.316 seconds and left the output
  directory empty. This is an APFS-local result; the case-sensitive branch
  did not run on this case-insensitive host. No full CLI suite, CTest, native
  Linux/Windows build, or CAD application was run.
- The locally reproduced APFS case/normalization collision is now rejected.
  The Windows and Linux/ext4 adapters are source-implemented but not
  compile/runtime validated here; other Apple/Linux filesystems fail closed.
  Keep native macOS case-sensitive, Linux/ext4 (casefold and non-casefold),
  and Windows NTFS (case-sensitive and default) profiles as open acceptance
  gates. The output transaction now snapshots destination state and rejects
  observed create/replace/in-place-modify conflicts before publication; this
  optimistic recheck is not a lock and a narrow check-to-rename race remains.
  Do not claim broad cross-platform name safety until those gates pass.
- Findings/subplans remain 127/71; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
  remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. No support claim changed. The mixed worktree
  remains unstaged/uncommitted.

## Implementation progress — AC1027/AC1032 MTEXT frame-flag vectors (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

The existing `libdxfrw_dwg_object_vectors_tests` target now creates MTEXT
records for AC1027 and AC1032 with background flag values `0`, `16`, and `17`.
Each generated record is decoded, checked for its exact flag value and
distinctive core fields, and followed by a hard-pointer sentinel. When the
current versioned codec includes background scalars for that flag tuple, the
vector also checks scale, color, and transparency. The decoded record is then
re-encoded and reopened to verify that the flag and text remain intact. This
tests the local versioned record path only; it does not determine which flag
tuples AutoCAD accepts or resolve the reported whole-AC1032-file failure.

## Deeper/broader MTEXT column-scope and overloaded-group reconciliation (2026-10-17; research only)

This follow-up corrects a group-code ambiguity in the previous 7E research
note and broadens the check across an authoritative DXF reference and two
independent open-source implementations. The marker `101 / Embedded Object`
is not a universal nested grammar: its payload is selected by the owning
entity/context. No peer program, native CAD application, or renderer was run;
no external drawing was downloaded and no code or tests were changed.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autodesk [MTEXT DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-5E5DB93B-F8D3-4433-ADF7-E92E250D2BAB.htm) and [ATTRIB DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-7DD8B495-C3F8-48CD-A766-14F9D7D0DD9B.htm) | MTEXT assigns group 50 to rotation and 42/43 to read-only extents ignored if supplied. Its column table names 75/76/78/79/48/49 and also says group 50 carries column heights, but does not fully scope that statement against main-entity rotation, legacy XDATA, or an R2018 group-101 payload. ATTRIB’s embedded-MTEXT table explicitly includes group 46 as defined annotation height and group 50 as rotation. | Treat the official table as necessary but not sufficient for the nested R2018 mapping. Keep 50 as ordinary entity rotation unless a particular version/container definition authorizes another meaning. Model 46 per owner/scope, and keep main 42/43 read-only semantics distinct from embedded-column totals. |
| ezdxf 1.4.5 [MTEXT internals](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfinternals/entities/mtext.html), [DXF tags](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfinternals/dxftags.html), and [R2018 exporter](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/mtext.py) | The documented static, dynamic-auto, and dynamic-manual R2018 examples place standalone-MTEXT column data under `101 / Embedded Object`. Its exporter writes group 70 attachment, 10 direction, 11 repeated insertion, 40/41 repeated reference width/defined height, 42/43 total extents, 71 type, 72 count, 44/45 width/gutter, 73/74 flags, and repeated group 46 manual heights. Dynamic-auto uses count 0; dynamic-manual writes the counted heights, including a final zero in the example. The pre-R2018 `ACAD_MTEXT_COLUMN_INFO` XDATA is a separate encoded profile: 1070 sub-key values identify 75/79/76/78/48/49/50; 47 belongs to the linked-columns XDATA profile. The peer docs/source are implementation evidence, not an Autodesk specification or text-layout oracle. | Replace the earlier proposed “repeated column-height group 50” assertion with scoped group-46 tests. Do not parse pre-R2018 XDATA as direct entity pairs. Test top-level 46 defined column height, nested R2018 46 per-column heights, and ordinary attribute embedded-MTEXT 46 defined annotation height as distinct cases. |
| ACadSharp [MText model](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/Entities/MText.cs) and [DWG object reader](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/IO/DWG/DwgStreamReaders/DwgObjectReader.cs) | The peer model distinguishes no/static/dynamic columns; its DWG reader gates column fields on nonzero type and separately handles count, width/gutter, auto/reversed flags, and dynamic-manual size values. This supports testing the separate no-column, static, auto, and manual modes. Its mutable `master` branch and DWG implementation do not prove DXF syntax or downstream acceptance. | Add only mode-specific controls to existing 7E. Use ACadSharp as a cross-check for profile/model completeness, not as the authority for group-code mapping or as a support-promoting comparator. |
| LibreDWG open [issue #1410](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1410) and local source/test/plan audit | The reporter’s failing embedded-attribute code range is a useful robustness scenario but is not a complete scoped grammar or independent AutoCAD reproduction. Local existing controls cover basic ATTRIB/ATTDEF embedding; the plan had overgeneralized group-101 handling and had a stale test instruction treating group 50 as a repeated column height. | Keep the peer report non-promoting. Fix the 7E contract and controls only; retain outer `AcDbAttribute`/`AcDbAttributeDefinition` boundary, tag/prompt/fallback, INSERT ATTRIB/SEQEND, and following-entity assertions. |

### Corrected 7E test matrix

1. **Standalone MTEXT / AC1032.** In ASCII and binary generated DXF, cover type 0
   with no embedded column object, static columns, dynamic-auto, and
   dynamic-manual. Assert: static has positive count but no repeated manual
   heights; dynamic-auto has count 0 and no repeated heights; dynamic-manual
   count equals bounded repeated group-46 values, preserving a legal final
   zero. Exercise finite complete XYZ points, repeated attachment 70, direction
   10, repeated insertion 11, width/height/extents, type/count/flags, main
   group-50 rotation, and a following LINE. Malformed/truncated count or point
   data must fail at the record boundary without callback or partial output.
2. **ATTRIB and ATTDEF.** Keep the same marker but use the ordinary embedded-
   MTEXT body grammar, not the standalone column schema. Give outer fallback
   text/tag/prompt/flags and embedded text/background distinct sentinels; assert

3. **Legacy columns.** Leave pre-R2018 linked-MTEXT/XDATA interpretation under

   sub-key/value sequence; do not treat 1070 sub-key 50 or linked-profile 47 as
   repeated direct MTEXT entity group codes.
4. **Read/write policy.** Keep main MTEXT 42/43 read-only behavior separate
   from group-101 embedded-column total extents. Resolve any preserve-versus-
   ignore choice before claiming parity. Refuse unsupported nested state
   before output publication; test copy/reset and same-writer retry.
5. **Fast validation only.** Extend the existing `tests/dxf_fixture_tests.cpp`
   owner; no new target, committed fixture, dependency, full suite, peer runtime,

## Implementation progress — R2018 MTEXT column object and host-scoped embedded grammars (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

This slice implements the existing PAR-19/7E readiness item using generated
DXF only. The same `101 / Embedded Object` marker now selects different parser
context by host: standalone MTEXT uses the bounded R2018 column-object
profile, while ATTRIB/ATTDEF keep the ordinary embedded-MTEXT body grammar.
The implementation retains standalone attachment, direction and insertion
points, repeated rectangle/extents values, column type/count/width/gutter,
auto-height/reversed-flow flags, and repeated manual heights in distinct model
fields. Main MTEXT orientation is not overwritten by nested direction data;
group 50 is never reinterpreted as a column height. ATTRIB/ATTDEF group 46
remains annotation height and group 50 retains the established rotation/vector
precedence.

The standalone profile is bounded to 4096 column heights. Complete finite
XYZ point tuples, required profile fields, count/mode consistency, and exact
manual-height counts are checked before entity callback publication. Unknown
nested group codes fail closed rather than falling through into main MTEXT
fields. Outer XDATA remains outside the embedded grammar, and finalization is
keyed to marker presence so a trailing XDATA section cannot bypass validation.
AC1032 DXF output writes the modeled standalone profile; older DXF output and
ordinary ATTRIB/ATTDEF embedded output refuse unrepresentable column state
before replacing an existing destination.

Generated ASCII and binary tests in the existing DXF fixture executable
cover no-column, static, dynamic-auto, and dynamic-manual profiles (including
the legal final zero-height entry), exact duplicated-field separation,
round-trip retention, and a following LINE sentinel. Negative controls cover
an incomplete point and a short manual-height list, both rejected without a
partial MTEXT callback. Embedded ATTRIB/ATTDEF controls cover annotation
height, rotation precedence, background ACI/true-colour/name/transparency,
outer tag/prompt/fallback data, sequence termination, and the following LINE.
Separate writer negatives verify that standalone column state cannot be
silently dropped from ATTRIB/ATTDEF output and that an existing destination
sentinel is preserved; pre-R2018 standalone export also fails atomically when
column state is present.

  fixture, dependency, peer runtime, or native CAD application was used.

## Implementation progress — structured XDATA writer APPID preflight (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

This slice implements the generic writer-admission boundary from PAR-19/7K;
it does not decode any application-specific XDATA profile. The writer now
checks that each XDATA list begins with a non-empty 1001 APPID, has no duplicate
case-folded APPID group on that record, and closes all 1002 list controls within
the configured nesting bound. XDATA APPIDs must correspond to an emitted APPID
table row, with the implicit mandatory `ACAD` row included. Duplicate
case-insensitive APPID rows are refused. Since `DRW_Interface::writeAppId()` is
a streaming callback, required application names are collected during data
emission and checked against rows emitted before the output transaction can
publish.

Generated ASCII and binary controls cover valid nested groups, two ordered
APPID groups, a missing initial marker, unclosed and unexpected close controls,
duplicate case-insensitive group names, excessive nesting, an absent
registration, and duplicate table registration. Every invalid profile checks
that an existing destination remains byte-for-byte unchanged. A same-codec
retry verifies that adding the missing APPID clears the failed attempt's
registration state and succeeds. Existing resolver coverage now registers its
local XDATA APPID explicitly; its malformed opaque 1005 preservation control
remains separate. The raw tag scanner has an opt-in switch to retain 1002/1003
only for this focused assertion, leaving unrelated wire-census expectations
unchanged.

Validation:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests -j2` — pass
  with strict warning settings.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --xdata-writer-validation` — pass;
  this selector runs the new ASCII/binary admission vectors plus existing
  XDATA reference-remap and ordered point-XDATA controls.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --classic-vertex-xdata` — pass.
- Scoped `git diff --check` — pass.
- No full suite/CTest, new CTest registration, committed drawing fixture,
  peer runtime, external file, or dependency was used.

This is generic authored-writer structure and APPID registration only. It does
not tighten tolerant reading or opaque replay, interpret legacy MTEXT
application keys, infer arbitrary 1005 targets, or establish native/peer
acceptance. It creates no new finding or top-level subplan and does not change
the wider implementation order. Findings/subplans remain 127/71; J256, J260,

shared checkout is broadly modified and this slice remains uncommitted.

## Implementation progress — 7BH.3 publication-time destination snapshot check (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

- `DwgDxfOutputTransaction` now captures the destination state when its
  exclusive temporary is opened. POSIX records the no-follow destination
  identity, type/mode, size, and nanosecond mtime/ctime relative to the held
  directory descriptor; Windows records volume/file identity, size, creation
  and write times, and attributes through a read-attributes handle.
- Commit rechecks the snapshot after the stream is flushed and immediately
  before rename/replace. A target that was absent but appears, an existing
  path replaced by a different file, or same-inode content changed in place
  rejects publication. The transaction aborts its owned temporary and leaves
  the concurrent writer's destination intact.
- The existing `libdxfrw_writer_primitives_tests` owner now creates all
  conflict inputs in the system temporary directory; no DWG/DXF sample,
  fixture, or test registration was added. The three tests cover concurrent
  creation, path replacement, and in-place content modification.
- Strict `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_writer_primitives_tests
  -j2` and
  `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_writer_primitives$'
  --output-on-failure` passed on Darwin 27 arm64 (1/1 CTest, 0.28 s).
  `git diff --check` passed for the scoped implementation and test files.
  No full suite, sanitizer run, Windows/Linux build, or external/native CAD
  application was run.
- This is an optimistic conflict check, not mutual exclusion. A narrow race
  remains between the final snapshot check and atomic rename/replace; closing
  it portably would require platform-specific no-replace/conditional-publish
  primitives or an explicit locking contract. Windows and Linux branches are
  source-implemented but unvalidated in this turn, so retain those native
  acceptance gates. No support claim or external J disposition changed; J256,
  J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The shared
  worktree remains broadly modified and uncommitted.

   `DXFPolygon.transform()` implementation. If a runtime check is warranted,
   run only translation plus combined rotation/translation with separate

## Implementation progress — 7G.3d ACAD_TABLE inherited placement prefix (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

Extended the existing source-generated TABLE object-vector builders rather
than adding drawing fixtures or registrations. A shared literal prefix writer
now authors all four R2000+ scale selectors for both the AC1021 legacy TABLE
cell route and the AC1024 inline TABLECONTENT route. Each mode uses its valid
scale shape: independent XYZ deltas, default X with independent Y/Z, uniform
raw scale, or unit XYZ defaults. Both version routes use a non-default 3D
insertion point, a nonzero rotation in radians, and a non-default extrusion.

Every generated parse asserts insertion XYZ, scale XYZ, radians, extrusion,
TABLE handle, owning BLOCK_RECORD, TABLESTYLE handle, absence of attributes,
semantic completeness, and the exact post-content body cursor. This is parser
regression coverage for documented inherited fields, not independent producer
evidence or native placement/rendering qualification. Existing table callback
coverage continues to keep typed ACAD_TABLE identity distinct from the 2D
`*T`/ordinary INSERT fallback and the following LINE.

Validation: strict `libdxfrw_dwg_object_vectors_tests` build; direct
`--table-placement` selector; `libdxfrw_dwg_object_vectors` CTest (1/1); and
the existing `libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests --retain-table-callback` control
all pass. No production change, fixture, dependency, or CTest registration was
added. The worktree is broadly modified and this slice remains uncommitted.
Next within 7G.3d is the existing bounded versioned-content/reference-closure
work; AC1024+ string conventions, linked DATALINK graph semantics, complete
FIELD serialization, and native editable/rendered TABLE behavior remain
separate open gates. No TABLE or overall DWG/DXF support claim is promoted.

## Implementation progress — 7BA late-parent/orphan identity conflict (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

Added `m_polylineOrphanClaims`, an ordered inverse index from staged orphan
child handle to its observed parent owner. It complements, rather than
replaces, the existing pending-parent reverse-claim index. Parent staging
checks its deduplicated declaration index against this inverse index before
inserting pending state or acquiring frame ownership. If a declared child is
already staged under another owner, the late parent is rejected and reported
as an owner mismatch; the orphan remains staged for its named owner to adopt.
When an orphan arrives after a conflicting pending-parent claim, the existing
child-first conflict path still terminalizes that parent and refuses the
orphan, preserving arrival-order-independent rejection semantics.

Orphan claim nodes are charged to the shared staging ledger in addition to the
orphan vector and per-owner membership set. The orphan append preflights both
the incoming membership node and the inverse-index node charge. Adoption,
pending-owner terminalization, standalone orphan terminalization, and final
state abandonment remove the corresponding claims and charges. The staged
state validator now checks index-to-orphan and orphan-to-index consistency,
requires one observed owner per child handle, verifies both indexes' modeled
node accounting, and includes both in the exact aggregate ledger comparison.

Extended the existing `--polyline-staging-growth` generated control with
matching-owner admission, late foreign-parent refusal, logarithmic map lookup
work over 512 declared handles, duplicate owner refusal without mutation,
exact byte release, and one-byte budget refusal without partial state. This is
a deterministic component control plus production-path integration; it does
not yet exercise a full source-frame lease/adoption transcript.

Validation:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests -j2` — pass

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target lc3_compat_check -j2` — pass
- Scoped `git diff --check` — pass

No drawing fixture, registration, dependency, or public API was added. The
top-level pending/orphan unordered-map buckets/nodes and allocator metadata
remain outside the current modeled 256 MiB allowance; complete callback,
lease, rollback, and retry transcripts remain open. No full suite, sanitizer,
external runtime, or support claim is inferred. Findings/subplans remain

`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The shared mixed worktree remains uncommitted.

## Implementation progress — 7BA pending/orphan owner-node estimates (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The shared POLYLINE staging ledger now includes a conservative owner-map
value/node estimate for each pending parent and child-first orphan:
`sizeof(pair<const handle, state>) + 3 * sizeof(void*)`. Parent admission
preflights this estimate before allocating its declared-child index; the
charge is retained with the pending state and released through the existing
adoption/terminalization paths. Orphan admission preflights and charges its
owner entry before staging child storage; geometric vector growth now
preserves that charge when recomputing the retained total. The whole-ledger
validator independently reconstructs both estimates, so the orphan-first,
foreign-parent, matching-adoption, terminalization, injected rollback, and
same-reader retry transcript fails if either map-node charge leaks or is
omitted.

transcript in addition to its prior source-less memory/rollback controls. It
seeds four coverage-ledger frames with distinct decoded-buffer offsets and

also receives exactly one frame publication per parent, child, and SEQEND,
with exact source location, ordinal, offset-space, version, and type. The final
coverage report must be complete, with each source frame published exactly

## Implementation progress — 7BA baseline owner-map bucket-array estimate (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The 256 MiB POLYLINE staging ledger previously charged owner-map bucket growth
only above the two maps' construction-time bucket counts. The budget now uses
the full current `bucket_count() × sizeof(void*)` estimate for both the pending
and child-first orphan maps. The reader seeds this charge at construction, and
post-clear/same-reader retry validation retains the estimate for any bucket
arrays the standard-library implementation keeps. Checked multiplication and
addition reject overflow; an initial estimate that exceeds the staging policy
also fails closed. Existing insertion preflight still charges retained and
conservative old-plus-replacement bucket-array growth before reserve/insert.

The focused selector now independently sums the test reader's two bucket
counts to verify the initial baseline charge, then exercises pending and
orphan staging, terminalization/abandonment, retained bucket charges, and
same-reader reuse. Cleanup releases per-state/index charges back to the
retained-map-array estimate rather than claiming a zero-byte or RSS bound.

## Implementation progress — 7BA mapped-POLYLINE ownership-preflight scratch (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Refactored the AC1018+ `preflightMappedPolylineOwnership` path. It previously
retained one copied child vector per mapped POLYLINE, built a per-parent hash
set for duplicate detection, then built a second child-to-first-owner map.
It now uses a single ordered first-owner map and an ordered invalid-owner set;
each later competing owner is marked as encountered. A single local vector
copied from the parsed child list is sorted to identify duplicates without
keeping all parents' child lists resident. After finding invalid parents, a
second pass reparses only those parents and discards their source frames and
declared children, preserving the existing quarantine behavior.

The global preflight in `readDwgBlocks()` already sees all BLOCK_RECORD
entries before any block callback or source-frame consumption. Removed the
redundant per-block invocation from `walkBlockRecordEntities()`, so valid
parents are not decoded again and cross-block claims remain evaluated in the
single pre-walk census.

The helper's byte allowance charges each non-null ownership reference,
including repeated claims, and conservative ordered-map/set node estimates.
While processing a parent it also accounts the existing staged-state estimate,
the frame body's current capacity, the parser's list nodes, and the temporary
sorted-vector capacity against the same 256 MiB policy. Body/list storage is
already allocated when these capacities become observable, so this is a
post-parse admission check before the retained ownership index grows—not a
strict instantaneous RSS ceiling or allocator-failure proof. The generated
selector tests competing owners, repeated references, exact budget refusal,
and retry at the required budget. Existing six-version scratch DWGs exercise
valid production traversal, but the malformed cross-parent quarantine branch
still lacks an end-to-end generated source-frame vector.

### Implementation-ready refinement to existing HATCH and 2D consumer gates

1. **Fast local file contract first (only when the HATCH path is changed).**
   Reuse `7AH.pattern-retention` and the existing ASCII/Binary selectors. Add
   only any missing in-memory/generated cases needed to distinguish: a known
   pattern name with file-authored lines that differ from the library entry; a
   custom name with authored lines; and no authored lines requiring consumer
   fallback. Assert exact stored pattern name, line count/order, angles,
   bases, offsets and dash lists across read/write/read, plus unchanged
   boundary and following-record alignment. Cross `$MEASUREMENT=0/1` with the
   embedded-line cases and assert the embedded numbers are unchanged. Generate
   control files locally in temporary storage; do not add third-party or new
   committed DWG/DXF samples.
2. **Resolve the LibreCAD handoff before claiming 2D semantic parity.** Pin the
   precise LibreCAD commit/submodule source used by the gate and inspect the
   effective `RS_FilterDXFRW` → `RS_Hatch` → pattern resource/render path. A
   scratch control should use a standard name whose embedded definition is
   intentionally distinguishable from the installed resource, plus a custom
   name. Record whether import, edit/save and re-open preserve or project the
   authored definition. If it is dropped, classify that as a consumer-model
   limitation; only a separate scoped LibreCAD change can close it. Keep the
   libdxfrw reader/writer exact-value contract unchanged either way.
3. **Keep rendering scalability separate from serialization and semantic
   support.** At the existing composed native consumer checkpoint, use a
   from-scratch dense patterned drawing and record the exact build/platform,
   input hash, viewport/extents/zoom sequence, generated/run counts, peak
   memory method, and elapsed times. Verify the canvas remains bounded and
   usable, and independently verify that plot/export/pick retain full-detail
   geometry when those routes promise it. Choose any runtime/resource limit
   from the consumer's documented policy and measured target environment; do
   not import CADCraft's 16× or 1M values. No wall-clock threshold belongs in
   the per-slice parser tests.
4. **Fallback and units:** qualify pattern-library fallback separately for
   absent embedded definitions and crossed `$MEASUREMENT`/`$INSUNITS` values.
   Embedded definitions win as file data; fallback resource choice is
   consumer-specific. Do not multiply embedded bases, offsets, or dashes by
   25.4 in the codec. Preserve present/absent header metadata exactly and
   compare displayed geometry against an independently authored expected
   pattern only at the native consumer gate.
5. **Fast implementation cadence:** per code slice, run the touched strict
   target and the nearest focused test only; update the plan/receipt as soon as
   that slice completes and show concise progress after each slice is
   committed. If a gate blocks, record its owner, unblock condition and next
   independent action, then continue the ready queue rather than stopping.
   Run no full suite or performance benchmark until the composed HATCH/consumer
   milestone. Any generated large stress drawing stays scratch-only. Keep the
   active implementation queue moving if the pinned consumer is unavailable,
   recording `NOT_RUN`/`CONSUMER_LIMITATION` rather than blocking unrelated
   file-format work.

This adds no local defect finding or top-level implementation subplan. It
sharpens the existing HATCH codec and primary 2D consumer gates, does not
reorder implementation, and introduces no renderer dependency, fixture,
registration, or support claim. File-level HATCH preservation, native visible
pattern fidelity, export fidelity, and rendering performance remain separate
claims. Findings/subplans remain 127/71; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — rooted SAB cumulative transform-string budget boundary (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Added a generated S3.7c control where the transform literal is 17 bytes,
`maxStringBytes` is 17, and `maxCumulativeStringBytes` is also 17. Thus the
individual string is allowed, but the rooted projection must refuse when it
accounts for retaining the literal in both the full raw-token snapshot and the
separate raw-literal observation. The caller's pre-populated output must be
cleared with `ResourceLimit`; the matrix remains parsed/unapplied only in the
other positive controls.

### Implementation-readiness and speed refinement

Apply the existing research stop rule using three quick admission checks before
spending time on another peer:

1. Confirm a real implementation of the needed operation and exact format
   profile (read versus write, DWG versus DXF versus bare SAT/SAB, and version).
2. Confirm an immutable source/release artifact and a compatible, auditable
   license route.
3. Confirm that the candidate independently measures an uncovered stage with
   observable records/diagnostics and expected results; a project claim,
   renderer, or same-codec round trip is insufficient.

If any check fails, record the route as discovery-only and return to the
existing implementation queue. Do not add a build dependency, per-slice peer
run, CTest, or repository drawing. Keep the one composed checkpoint for
source-handle/AcDs/SAB association and independent geometry metrics; this
screen changes neither the checkpoint nor its evidence gates. Findings and
top-level subplans remain 127/71. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and cannot be promoted by this research.

## Deeper/broader route composition and minimum-cost ACIS/FreeCAD evidence sequence (2026-10-17; research only)

This pass synthesizes the current primary-source route evidence into one
implementation-ready qualification sequence. The goal is to prevent a
successful result at one layer (conversion, payload framing, rendering, or
shape creation) from being mistaken for a result at a later layer. It is a
source/documentation review only: no peer was installed, built, or run; no
DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB was downloaded; and no fixture, dependency, test, or code was
added.

| Route | Supported evidence role | Independence and limit | Plan disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stock FreeCAD DWG import | The current FreeCAD documentation describes an external DWG converter followed by the standard DXF importer. The selected converter and importer/backend are therefore part of the tested route, not incidental setup. The FreeCAD maintainer states that stock FreeCAD cannot read ACIS blobs; the current documentation identifies CADExchanger as the separate 3D DWG workflow. | A successful converter exit or opened document is not ACIS acceptance. The C++ and legacy DXF importers have different entity coverage; a test qualifies only the exact backend, effective preferences, converter build, platform, and entity family exercised. | Retain native Linux and Windows checks for the explicitly supported 2D/3D-entity subsets and converter handoff. Mark stock-FreeCAD ACIS/B-rep ingestion `CONSUMER_NOT_APPLICABLE`, not failed and not passed. A plugin is a separate route. |
| `cadmpeg-codec-sat` v0.6.1 | Separate bare SAT/SAB stream parser with profile admission and decode/loss reporting; useful for an independent record/reference and typed-versus-raw census on the exact extracted payload. | The project declares L1/profile-level support for this codec. It does not parse DWG/DXF/AcDs containers and does not build a kernel solid. It cannot establish entity→AcDs owner/key→payload association or B-rep validity. | Optional once-only structural cross-check at the composed checkpoint. Pin release, platform asset/hash and detected inner dialect; treat unknown/raw or incomplete transfer as non-passing for semantic claims. |
| `cq-acis` v0.3.12 | Separate SAT/SAB/ASM parser plus conversion of supported analytic geometry to CadQuery/OpenCASCADE shapes. Its docs distinguish container/save profiles and record parsing from complete shape conversion. | Shape construction uses OCCT, the same kernel family as FreeCAD. It is an independent parser implementation but not an independent kernel vote. Unsupported records, geometry, placements or trims can remain raw or cause conversion errors. | Optional shape/metrics route for admitted exact payload profiles. Require full body/reference disposition, valid closed result where expected, and analytic values from an independently authored source manifest. Keep the shared-kernel label. |
| InventorLoader FreeCAD add-on | Optional DXF route that extracts SAT/SAB bytes and feeds its own ACIS reader into FreeCAD `Part` construction; can answer a specifically selected add-on import question. | Not stock FreeCAD, does not read DWG containers, has documented unsupported geometry and no export, and shares OCCT lineage through FreeCAD `Part`. Mutable add-on source/version and partial face/shell output require explicit auditing. | Discovery/optional add-on route only. Pin add-on commit, FreeCAD build, dependencies, parser diagnostics, and per-body solid/shell/face/wire outcome before any result is counted. |
| HOOPS Exchange / Ansys ACIS import | Commercial reader routes that document SAT/SAB geometry access; HOOPS also documents DWG/DXF reading, while Ansys documents SAT/SAB and selected DWG/DXF import profiles. | Licensed SDK/application boundaries, supported platforms, exact versions, hidden/suppressed behavior, and import options must be captured. They are not open-source peers or substitutes for local expected geometry. Do not install, purchase, or activate them for this plan without an already-authorized environment. | Use only when the exact runtime/license is already available or expressly selected. A direct DWG reader can test the outer route; a bare-payload reader cannot by itself validate AcDs association. |
| ACadRust/OpenCADStudio; ProGPU/ProCad | ACadRust/OpenCADStudio can provide an optional application or writer route; ProGPU/ProCad describe renderer/tessellation routes. | OpenCADStudio shares its codec family with ACadRust. ProGPU's public SAB path is renderer-oriented; ProCad's DWG/DXF reader uses the ACadSharp family. Tessellated lines/pixels do not establish closed B-rep semantics. | Keep each at its existing optional role; do not count correlated codec wrappers or renderer output as another independent semantic vote. |

### Fastest safe composed sequence

1. Continue local implementation without external setup: use the touched strict
   target, existing focused generated-input selector/CTest, relevant LibreCAD
   compatibility check, and scoped `git diff --check`. Do not add an external
   reader or native FreeCAD to per-slice validation.
2. At the existing composed checkpoint, perform a read-only availability and
   provenance preflight. Record exact app/package version, artifact or commit
   hash, OS/architecture, converter/importer settings, and license status. If
   a required tool is unavailable, record `NOT_AVAILABLE` and continue local
   implementation.
3. Use only a source-authored scratch control with an independently written
   analytic manifest. Admit its inner payload by observed magic and save
   version—not by outer `$ACADVER` alone. A 21800 ACIS BinaryFile control and
   an ASM BinaryFile4/8 control are separate profiles; do not substitute the
   existing 23200 authoring control for an older payload profile without
   direct profile evidence. Keep every drawing ephemeral; commit no new DWG or
   DXF fixture.
4. First bind source entity handle/type and block owner to the exact carrier:
   inline group-1/3 SAT/SAB bytes for inline profiles, or the complete
   DWG/AcDs entity→key/index/owner→record→payload path for handle-linked
   profiles. Compare exact length/hash and all joins before invoking a bare
   payload parser. If the independent outer reader cannot validate the join,
   report payload-only evidence and leave the AcDs gate open.
5. Feed the same byte-identical payload once to the independent bare-stream
   parser (`cadmpeg`) for profile, record, reference, typed/raw and loss
   accounting. Only then run one shape route: the already-selected licensed
   reader if available, or the bounded `cq-acis`/OCCT route as supplementary
   evidence. Compare all bodies, topology/closure, placement, units, bounds,
   surface area, volume, and centroid against the source manifest. Unknowns,
   skipped bodies, warnings, partial faces/shells, or fallback geometry are
   explicit non-passes, not zero values.
6. Run native FreeCAD separately on Linux and Windows with the exact `dwg2dxf`
   executable, arguments/status, output magic/version, DXF importer backend,
   import-as mode, scale, and feature filters captured. Compare only the named
   entity families the selected importer is documented and observed to
   consume. Do not require or claim stock-FreeCAD ACIS acceptance; use the
   add-on only as a separately named optional consumer route.
7. Preserve one compact composed receipt containing per-stage source/output
   hashes, entity/owner disposition, carrier digest, parser dialect and
   losses, shape metrics/kernel lineage, consumer build/settings, and
   `PASS`/`FAIL`/`NOT_RUN`/`NOT_APPLICABLE`/`NOT_QUALIFIED` states. No full test
   suite or repeated peer run follows unless a specific local regression
   requires it.

This route composition refines existing S3/S5/S8, FreeCAD platform, and
external-evidence gates only. It introduces no new finding or top-level
implementation subplan, dependency, fixture, test registration, validation
cadence, queue reorder, or support claim. Findings/subplans remain 127/71;
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and
non-promoting. Native Linux/Windows FreeCAD qualification and independent
external ACIS/AcDs semantic evidence remain outstanding.

validation error. Existing valid enum, role, phase, source-version, and

This pass reconciles Autodesk's published DXF wording, a current independent
DXF library's parser/writer behavior, a recent LibreDWG report, and the local
standalone/embedded writer routes. It refines existing PAR-05/PAR-28/29 and 7M;
it does not add a new finding or claim. No peer checkout/build/runtime, native
CAD app, or local test was run. No external drawing was downloaded.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Existing owner and plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autodesk [MTEXT DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-5E5DB93B-F8D3-4433-ADF7-E92E250D2BAB.htm) and [general DXF group-code limits](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2027/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OARX-RefGuide-DXF_Group_Codes.html) | Autodesk describes content shorter than 250 characters as wholly in group 1; content longer than 250 as 250-character chunks in one or more group-3 records; if group 3 is used, the final record is group 1 with fewer than 250 characters. The cited MTEXT sentences do not explicitly assign the exactly-250 case. Separately, string groups 1–4, 7, 9, and 300–309 have a 255-character maximum, less for Unicode. The pages do not define one universal byte-count rule for UTF-8, legacy code pages, or escape-expanded text. | For PAR-28/7M, model the MTEXT character chunk rule and encoded DXF transport limit as separate constraints. Do not describe a 250-byte cap as the specification. Keep exactly 250 as one group 1 when the target transport permits it unless a matched native witness identifies a profile-specific exception; for content requiring continuations, default to a final group-1 tail shorter than 250. Resolve encoding-specific measurement before claiming cross-profile behavior. |
| Current [ezdxf MTEXT writer/parser](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/mtext.py) and [text splitter](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/tools/text.py) | The writer splits Python strings at size 250, emits all but the last chunk as group 3 and the last as group 1, and emits one empty group 1 for empty text. Its splitter backs up only when a chunk would end in `^`; its loader collects group-3 values in order, appends group 1, then reconstructs text. Consequently, an exact multiple such as 500 characters can produce group 3 length 250 plus group 1 length 250, which differs from Autodesk's published “final group 1 … fewer than 250” wording when continuation records are present. Python character indexing is not evidence of byte-safe output for every DXF encoding. The reviewed `master` URL is mutable and this peer was not run. | Treat this as one peer implementation profile and an exact-multiple compatibility lead, not as a reason to override Autodesk wording. Keep the discrepancy visible until an immutable peer revision and a native-produced/accepted exact-multiple control are available. Add exact multiples to the existing generated test owner; do not use ezdxf self-round-trip as expected truth. |
| LibreDWG [#1408](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1408) | The reporter describes a raw CR inside TEXT/MTEXT-like DXF content causing an empty physical line at a group-code boundary and a dropped adjacent character in LibreDWG 0.14 on Windows. The failing drawing was not public in the report and no reproducer or fix was examined. This is an external report, not a libdxfrw defect or a rule that every control character must be encoded with caret notation. | PAR-05 already owns physical framing and has generated CR/LF refusal/rollback and binary-boundary coverage. Extend that existing gate only as needed to prove standalone and embedded MTEXT propagation, semantic newline policy, and the next-record sentinel; do not duplicate generic framing tests or import the peer's private drawing. |
| Local source and test audit: [`dxfWriter::writeUtf8Chunks`](src/intern/dxfwriter.cpp), [`writeMText`](src/libdxfrw.cpp), [`writeEmbeddedMText`](src/libdxfrw.cpp), and [generated DXF fixture tests](tests/dxf_fixture_tests.cpp) | The low-level helper's `maxBytes` is a target-encoded byte budget and it preserves complete UTF-8 scalar input during strict encoding. Standalone MTEXT still has separate strict and compatibility chunk loops; embedded MTEXT currently emits its full text through one group 1. The existing control-character regression proves generic writer refusal/binary framing and destination preservation, but a CR in an MTEXT background-color name is not an MTEXT-content newline test. This is source/coverage evidence, not a new runtime reproduction. | Keep 7M's code-sharing objective, but implement one profile-aware routine that encodes once and returns ordered output chunks for both standalone and embedded text. Extend existing generated ASCII/Binary MTEXT, ATTRIB, and ATTDEF cases; preserve the generic PAR-05 regression owner. Keep older-target downgrade/loss policy separate from chunk framing. |

### Implementation-ready and speedy sub-plan refinement

1. **Resolve the wire contract before changing the helper.** Use Autodesk's
   stated character chunking and separate target-encoded string transport
   bound. Retain a single group 1 for exactly 250 characters when its target
   transport permits it; the cited prose leaves that edge unstated. For
   chunked output, use a final group-1 remainder in the range
   1–249 characters; the conservative 500-character shape is group 3 of 250,
   group 3 of 249, then group 1 of 1. Keep this as the default pending a
   matched native exact-multiple witness; if AutoCAD's own output or acceptance
   demonstrates a compatibility exception, name and scope it by version/profile
   rather than silently inheriting ezdxf's behavior.
2. **Unify emission and avoid double encoding.** Reuse one target-version-aware
   encoder/chunker for standalone MTEXT and the group-101 embedded-MTEXT body.
   Validate UTF-8 scalar boundaries and target encoded value limits while
   producing chunks; do not split a multibyte encoded scalar. Preserve the
   exact concatenated source text. Keep the helper's character accounting
   distinct from `maxBytes`; decide whether escape sequences are atomic only
   where a target/native observation requires it. Emit all group-3 chunks first,
   one final group 1, and one empty group 1 for empty content.
3. **Exercise boundaries cheaply in the owning target.** Add generated in-memory
   vectors for ASCII lengths 249/250/251 and 499/500/501, non-ASCII UTF-8 where
   byte and character thresholds differ, a supported DBCS or escape case,
   caret-pair-at-boundary, and empty content. Run them through standalone
   MTEXT and both ATTRIB and ATTDEF embedded scopes in ASCII and Binary DXF.
   Assert exact code sequence, character/transport limits, reconstructed text,
   outer tag/prompt/fallback and sequence preservation, plus a following LINE.
   No committed DWG/DXF fixture or new CTest registration is needed.
4. **Keep control-character semantics explicit.** In the same generated owner,
   distinguish logical `\P`, LF, CRLF, bare CR, and literal caret-escaped
   controls. Choose documented route-specific behavior: canonicalize only
   where the text contract is established, otherwise refuse with an explicit
   loss outcome before publication. ASCII physical records must never gain an
   embedded delimiter or lose the next character; Binary DXF must retain
   framing and report any semantic transformation. Reuse PAR-05's transaction
   and destination-preservation assertions.
5. **Use the short validation loop.** For the implementation slice, build only
   the strict DXF-fixture target, run its focused selector/CTest and the existing
   `lc3_compat_check`, plus scoped diff checks. Do not add a full-suite, peer,
   renderer, or native-app run to each slice. A single exact-multiple native
   save/read observation belongs at the already-composed text/consumer gate,

`writeUtf8MTextChunks` maps LF and CRLF to the MTEXT paragraph token `\\P`;
mixed LF/CRLF input retains order and becomes one canonical logical sequence.

entity-field preflight now uses MTEXT-specific safety rules for standalone

normalizer rather than being rejected as generic record delimiters. Ordinary
TEXT remains subject to the stricter generic text policy. A refused standalone
write is checked to preserve the existing output destination.

## Implementation progress — 7M downlevel embedded-attribute MTEXT refusal (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Pre-AC1032 DXF targets cannot represent the R2018 embedded-MTEXT profile on
ATTRIB/ATTDEF. The writer previously could emit only the entity's fallback
single-line value, silently losing the attached multiline body. The shared
`writeAttributeR2018Features` path now refuses these records before their
wire output and records one `multiline attribute (not in this DXF version)`
entry in the existing `leftOut()` diagnostics. This is a safe boundary, not a
claim that a downlevel flattening policy is implemented.

Generated controls exercise ATTRIB and ATTDEF separately in ASCII and Binary
DXF at AC1027. Each verifies the write fails, the matching diagnostic count is
one, and a pre-existing destination remains byte-for-byte unchanged. The same
writer is then retried after removing the unsupported embedded MTEXT; the
diagnostic clears and the ordinary ATTRIB/ATTDEF record is emitted. The split
attempts are intentional because a writer error is sticky within one write
transaction.

## Implementation progress — 7M embedded-MTEXT XDATA scope refusal (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The existing writer emits the outer `AcDbAttribute` subclass before its
R2018 embedded-MTEXT body, while trailing ATTRIB/ATTDEF XDATA follows that
body without a separately qualified scope marker. A generated carrier test
initially showed that treating the nested application's groups as MTEXT data
caused the host's own groups to be read into that same nested list. That
would merge two scopes and break existing host-XDATA round trips; the parser
change was reverted.

The chosen policy is therefore a narrow fail-closed boundary: when an
ATTRIB/ATTDEF has R2018 embedded MTEXT with nonempty `mtext.extData`, the
writer rejects it before publication and records
`embedded MTEXT XDATA (scope not qualified)`. This wording distinguishes an
unqualified writer route from the separate pre-AC1032 “not in this DXF
version” refusal. Clearing only the nested payload permits retry; ordinary
host ATTRIB/ATTDEF XDATA remains supported and separately round-tripped.

Generated controls cover ATTRIB and ATTDEF, ASCII and Binary DXF, exact
diagnostic count, preservation of an existing destination, and same-writer
retry after removing nested XDATA. The pre-existing canonical/legacy embedded
marker tests continue to verify host XDATA does not migrate into MTEXT.

## Deeper/broader LTYPE DXF text-field profile and retained-owner review (2026-10-17; research only)

The research portion of this pass followed the open LTYPE safety signal
through the current peer issue index, a separate upstream LTYPE fix,
Autodesk's DXF field documentation, and the exact local parse/write/retention
paths. It found one actionable local resource-accounting gap and one
unresolved DXF string-profile question. At the time, that research did not
change or run code; the subsequent 7K boundary controls and 7S.2c.d.17.6
implementation are recorded in the progress entries. No peer package or native
CAD application was executed, and no drawing was downloaded or added.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and what remains open | Existing plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG's [live issue index](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues), entries [#1450](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1450), [#1451](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1451), and [#1452](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1452) | At this review the repository index reports 95 open issues and lists all three as open, opened Oct. 14, 2026. Their current titles identify (respectively) a group-9 LTYPE dash-text heap-buffer-overflow, a `FIELD` use-after-free at zero child values, and an unaligned `BITCODE_RS` read in the EED encoder. Direct issue-page fetches were unavailable. Earlier plan text records more specific bodies, including a malformed AC1024 group-9 record without `74=2`; this pass could not independently refresh those bodies or artifacts. | Preserve the old #1450 reduced-input description only as a prior recorded scenario. Do not label it a valid-file interoperability defect or claim the new report's root cause/fix state. Keep #1451/FIELD and #1452/packed-C alignment on their already named local owners; title-only peer reports do not add a libdxfrw finding or mandate per-slice sanitizers. |
| LibreDWG upstream [development `ChangeLog`](https://gitlab.com/LibreDWG/LibreDWG/-/blob/master/ChangeLog) | Its June 1, 2026 entry describes a separate earlier `add_LTYPE_dashes` overflow fix (`GH #1209`): a static dash index could persist across LTYPE calls, and strings up to 4096 bytes could overflow the 256/512-byte `strings_area`. That is useful same-subsystem history and corroborates the need to separate per-record state, cumulative byte areas, and text lengths. It is not evidence that the newer GitHub #1450 is fixed, nor that libdxfrw has the same fixed-buffer path. | Keep the historical peer fix as an adversarial shape lead, not as a current peer verdict or a format threshold. Continue using ODA §20.4.58 and local fixed-area writer controls for DWG; do not copy the peer's buffer sizes/patch into DXF code. |
| Autodesk [LTYPE table reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-F57A316C-94A2-416C-8280-191E34B182AC.htm), current [2027 group-code table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2027/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OARX-RefGuide-DXF_Group_Codes.html), and older [2015 group-code table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-2553CF98-44F6-4828-82DD-FE3BC7448113.htm) | The LTYPE table defines group 9 as one text string per element only when group 74 identifies embedded text. The 2027 general table gives code 9 a 255-character maximum (less for Unicode); the older table documents a 2049-single-byte exception for codes 0–9 following extended symbol names. The retrieved references therefore do not justify a single unversioned character/byte limit for every DXF target. | Add valid and malformed ASCII/Binary group-scope controls under the existing LTYPE owner. Record code page, target `$ACADVER`, Unicode scalar count, encoded byte count, and raw emitted length. Probe 254/255/256 and 2048/2049/2050 with generated inputs, but leave these diagnostic until a versioned producer/native witness selects the applicable rule. Do not silently truncate; after the profile is resolved, either enforce the right limit transactionally or document why the writer preserves a wider compatible value. |
| Local [`DRW_LType::parseCode`](src/drw_objects.cpp), [`dxfRW::writeLType`](src/libdxfrw.cpp), [`DRW_TableEntry`](src/drw_objects.h), and [`DxfReadRetainedBudget`](src/intern/dxfreader.h) | At the time of this research, DXF group 3 (`desc`) and valid group 9 (`segments.back().text`) were assigned/emitted as UTF-8 strings but were not charged to a long-lived table-entry lease. The parser checked that group 9 follows a segment with the text bit, but `validateDxf()` did not define a text-length policy. | The retained-owner gap is subsequently closed by `7S.2c.d.17.6`: shared lease charging now covers `desc` and each parsed segment string, with exact/one-under, replacement, copy/move/reset, repeated-group-73 release, callback refusal, and same-facade retry controls. Keep this bounded logical-retention contract distinct from process RSS and from the unresolved DXF wire field length. |
| ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.58 and current local `DRW_LType::encodeDwgResolved` | DWG complex-dash text is packed into a version-specific fixed string area (legacy 256-byte area versus 512-byte Unicode area) shared by the record's segments. This is not the DXF group-9 per-field rule and does not become 256/512 characters. The existing 7BF.2 writer preflight plans encoded bytes and terminators before publication. | Keep DWG encoded-area enforcement, exact-offset readback and atomic refusal within 7BF.2. Do not widen the DWG area based on DXF text length or treat successful DXF retention as proof a DWG target can encode the same text. |

## Implementation progress — 7K XDATA 1004 chunk boundary (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The existing focused XDATA writer test owner now includes generated ASCII and
Binary DXF cases with 126-, 127-, and 128-byte group-1004 payloads. The test
scans raw tags and requires exact uppercase hex chunks: one 126-byte chunk,
one 127-byte chunk, and a 127+1 split for 128 bytes. It then imports each file
and verifies chunk order/content, the APPID group, and the following LINE's
coordinates and absence of XDATA. This tests the local writer/reader wire
contract and cursor alignment only. Autodesk's [Extended Data reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A2A628B0-3699-4740-A215-C560E7242F63.htm)
specifies a maximum of 127 bytes per binary chunk, matching the test oracle;
the local generated test still does not establish independent producer/native
acceptance or a general XDATA/DWG EED limit.

Validation: `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests -j2`
passed, and `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --xdata-writer-validation`
passed. The full `libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures` CTest and full suite were not run, in
keeping with the fast-validation policy. No testing DWG/DXF file was added;
all output was generated under the system temporary directory and removed.
No CTest registration, production code, dependency, support claim, or public
API/layout changed. Findings/subplans remain 127/71; J256, J260, J268, J284,
J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

Receipt: [`xdata-1004-chunk-boundary-fast-slice-2026-10-17.json`](docs/research/xdata-1004-chunk-boundary-fast-slice-2026-10-17.json).

## Implementation progress — 7K DWG EED unsigned-size boundaries (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The existing `dwg_object_vectors_tests` target now emits generated AC1021
1000-string item streams whose EED data totals exactly 32,767, 32,768, 65,535,
and 65,536 bytes. The raw-envelope walk verifies unsigned BS lengths, the
application handle, exact chunk byte counts, item-boundary splitting, the
zero terminator, and a following-field sentinel. The 65,536 case splits as
65,407+129 because a 129-byte string item is indivisible. Production
`readDwgEed` then checks ordered distinct values and the same following-field
cursor. A 32,767-character indivisible item is refused before publishing
bytes; corrected data succeeds on the same writer buffer and decodes cleanly.

A second focused case creates a full AC1021 DWG under the system temporary
directory with one 65,536-byte EED payload followed by a second LINE. The
local reader recovers both lines, all values in order, the repeated APPID
group emitted at the physical chunk boundary, and no XDATA on the following
LINE. This is specifically a local wire/reader structural check: it does not
establish independent producer/native acceptance, and same-APPID continuation
semantics remain `LOCAL_WIRE_ONLY` / `EXTERNAL_ACCEPTANCE_PENDING`.

Validation: strict builds of `libdxfrw_dwg_object_vectors_tests` and
`libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip` passed. Both existing focused selectors,
`--dwg-eed-size-boundaries`, passed. No full CTest/full suite, new CTest
registration, production code, dependency, external drawing, or committed
test fixture was added. Temporary DWG output is removed by the test. The local
ODA PDF path documented in `AGENTS.md` was absent, so the byte-layout review
used the official ODA-hosted v5.4.1 specification (§2.2, §20.4.1, §28).

This closes only the local EED unsigned-size/cursor regression slice. It does
not resolve the Autodesk/ACadSharp peer reports as local defects, establish a
format-level 32,767-byte maximum, promote DWG/DXF support, or alter the six
external-only J items. Findings/subplans remain 127/71; J256, J260, J268,
J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. No
implementation order or validation cadence changed.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.6 LTYPE description and segment-text retained owner (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

`DRW_LType::parseCode` now admits group-3 descriptions and each parsed group-9
complex-dash string through the table-entry's existing shared
`DxfReadRetainedLease`. Replacement reserves the new logical value before
assignment, then releases the previous field charge. A repeated group 73
releases the parsed dash-text charges before replacing the segment arrays; a
dedicated repeated-group-73 control verifies that old segment text no longer
remains charged. Copy/move/reset continue to use the established shared-owner
lifetime model.
The string profile remains separate: this makes no claim about a normative
group-9 character maximum, and caller mutations after parsing remain outside
this read-retention accounting contract.

The existing hardening target generates ASCII and Binary DXF tag streams with
a name, a replaced description, two valid `74=2` text segments, and a replaced
second-segment string. The same generated TABLES owner also refuses code 9
when the active segment lacks the text flag, before callback publication. It
computes the minimum successful aggregate retained
cap, verifies one-byte-under refusal preserves the previous dash text, and
checks that the final lease accounts for the live name/description/all segment
strings only. Copy then move keeps the charge alive after the source resets;
the final owner reset releases it. Full generated TABLES inputs in both
encodings also contain a following `SENTINEL_LTYPE` row. One-byte-under refusal
produces no LTYPE callback; raising the budget on the same `dxfRW` facade
allows both rows and verifies the sentinel.

Validation: `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_hardening_tests
lc3_compat_check -j2` passed, as did
`build-gcc/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --dxf-ltype-retained-owner-budget`.
The existing `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests` target built and
`build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --ltype-mirror-authority` passed. No
full hardening CTest/full suite, new CTest registration, external fixture, or
committed test drawing was used. The generated Binary DXF file is temporary
and removed after each encoding. New private counters change the
public `DRW_LType` object layout; downstream consumers must rebuild and no
binary-ABI compatibility claim is made.

This closes only the local retained-owner gap. It does not settle the DXF
group-9 length conflict, qualify a native/independent producer, resolve the
peer reports as matching libdxfrw defects, or promote a feature-support claim.
Findings/subplans remain 127/71; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The implementation order and reduced
validation cadence are unchanged.

Receipt: [`ltype-retained-text-owner-fast-slice-2026-10-17.json`](docs/research/ltype-retained-text-owner-fast-slice-2026-10-17.json).

## Implementation progress — 7AP.2 proxy-cache provenance and explicit replay authorization (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

`DRW_Entity` now records whether the common proxy-graphics cache was supplied
by a caller or parsed from ASCII DXF, Binary DXF, or DWG, along with source
version, count group (92/160 for DXF), and declared byte count. Parsed bytes
remain unauthorized by default. An explicit caller acknowledgment is admitted
only when the current byte vector exactly matches its count; it can be revoked.
The acknowledgment is caller-owned policy, not an immutable source snapshot:
callers must revoke it before edits and re-acknowledge only after confirming
the cache is still appropriate. Copy retains this metadata; `reset()` clears it.
This adds a non-virtual source API and changes `DRW_Entity` layout, so downstream
binaries must be rebuilt; the 2D LibreCAD_3 source-compatibility compile gate
still passes. No writer consults the flag in this slice, so default output and
dedicated raw `ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY` capture/replay remain unchanged.

The common DXF entity writer now replays typed proxy bytes only with explicit
authorization and a narrow, verifiable closure: positive exact declared and
actual length within the existing payload cap; source DXF version exactly equal
to target; exact source/output codepage match; matching 92/160 count-code era;
and a complete stream with at least one recognized primitive and no unsupported
or resource-dependent chunks. Parsed ASCII/Binary DXF and caller-supplied caches
are eligible; DWG-origin caches are not. HATCH, MESH, MPOLYGON, and the dedicated
ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY carrier are excluded from the generic path. ASCII and Binary
output use the existing 127-byte group-310 chunk boundary. No cache is rewritten
in-place, and caller bytes/count remain unchanged.

The existing source-generated selector covers AC1021/group 92 and
AC1024/group 160, ASCII and Binary, lengths 0/127/128/255/256, exact literal
wire count/chunks, readback, and a following-LINE sentinel. Zero represents no
emitted proxy count/chunk; positive sizes exercise the replay path. Negative
controls reject target-version mismatch, codepage mismatch, stale declared
length, and an indexed-resource opcode. Focused validation passed:

* `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --proxy-graphic-loss-policy`

The full suite, native CAD, external peers, and independent semantic oracle were
not run. No drawing fixture, CTest registration, dependency, or support claim was
added. This proves only local generic DXF carrier emission for the tested
profiles—not edit tracking, general proxy regeneration, arbitrary proxy
opcodes/resources, DWG cache replay, rendering, or application acceptance.
The parsed-cache writer matrix and same-handle raw-plus-typed refusal are now
covered locally. Remaining 7AP.4 work is limited to relevant version/type
profiles and duplicate-source cases whose identity is missing or ambiguous;

## Implementation progress — 7AP.4 parsed-cache replay and raw/typed collision control (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The existing `--proxy-graphic-loss-policy` owner now exercises end-to-end
parsed-cache replay, not only caller-authored bytes. It generates complete
AC1021/group-92 and AC1024/group-160 source DXFs in both ASCII and Binary;
imports through `dx_iface`; checks the parsed origin, encoding, version,
codepage, count code, exact bytes, and default-deny authorization state; then
explicitly acknowledges the parsed cache and exports to both encodings at the
same version. Reopen and literal-wire probes verify exact payload/count, the
replay authorization does not leak into the new parsed object, and the
following LINE remains aligned. Across 2 source versions × 2 source encodings ×
2 output encodings this yields eight local generated paths.

A further generated strict-export control places a valid raw LINE record and a
typed proxy-cached LINE in one block with the same handle. The existing
adapter's raw/typed handle inventory refuses the collision before creating a
destination. This verifies the handle-backed duplicate policy; it does not
infer identity for handle-less or ambiguous source records. No production
behavior change was needed for this check.

## Deeper/broader DXF proxy-graphic class-code collision review (2026-10-17; research only)

This pass checked the generic proxy replay assumption against Autodesk's DXF
group tables and the current local parser dispatch. The common-entity table
defines groups 92/310 for proxy graphics, but those numeric codes are not
globally unique once an entity enters its class-specific grammar. Autodesk's
MLEADER table maps group 92 to text color; OLE2FRAME maps group 310 to its OLE
binary payload; TABLE has group 92 first as common proxy length and later as
AcDbTable column count. The local parser confirms these scope-sensitive
meanings: `DRW_MLeader::parseCode` maps group 92 directly to `styleTextColor`,
and `DRW_Ole2Frame`/`DRW_OleFrame::parseCode` collect group 310 as class
payload. Yet `canReplayTypedProxyGraphics()` currently admits those entity
types because its exclusions are limited to HATCH, MESH, MPOLYGON and
ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY. A caller can explicitly authorize a typed cache on these
classes. `writeMultiLeader`, `writeOle2Frame`, and `writeOleFrame` call the
common `writeEntity` path before emitting their class-local records; the reader
then consumes the same group codes through the MLEADER/OLE class parser. A
later read can therefore assign emitted proxy bytes to a different typed
field. This is a local source/spec-confirmed risk, not a runtime reproduction;
no production code or tests changed in this research pass.

| Evidence | What it establishes | What it does not establish |
|---|---|---|
| [Autodesk common entity codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3610039E-27D1-4E23-B6D3-7E60B22BB5BD.htm) | Groups 92/310 are common proxy-graphics count/data in the AcDbEntity scope. | That every later subclass parser/writer treats those codes as proxy data. |
| [Autodesk MLEADER codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-69B9139A-48B4-48A5-B3CF-A3233ABFBE49.htm) and local `DRW_MLeader::parseCode` | Group 92 also represents MLEADER text color; current local parse path has no common-vs-MLEADER subclass guard before that switch arm. | Runtime output corruption on a producer-authored MLEADER; that remains to be reproduced with a generated input. |
| [Autodesk OLE2FRAME codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2019/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-77747CE6-82C6-4452-97ED-4CEEB38BE960.htm) and local OLE frame parsers | Group 310 is OLE binary payload for these entity types; generic proxy replay cannot safely assume the consumer interprets it as proxy bytes. | Whether every existing OLE route can construct a caller-authorized proxy cache. The public entity cache/API permits the state, but the focused regression remains pending. |
| [Autodesk TABLE codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D8CCD2F0-18A3-42BB-A64D-539114A07DA0.htm) | The same group 92 changes meaning across `AcDbEntity` and `AcDbTable` subclass scopes. | That TABLE should be admitted to generic proxy replay; this is a required collision control only if proposed. |
| [ezdxf proxy implementation lineage](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dxfentity.py) and its [binary writer issue](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/issues/1412) | ezdxf retains `proxy_graphic` as bytes on generic entities and recently fixed ASCII/Binary carrier emission. | DWG decoding, custom-object semantics, MLEADER/OLE per-class compatibility, or native rendering. |

### Implementation-ready and fastest safe sequence

1. **Inventory before setup:** on each requested native platform, record the
   FreeCAD executable/version/build, bundled OCCT version, selected C++ or

   and explicit 3D entity control through the stock FreeCAD path; separately
   run an ACIS-only DXF control through the stock importer and expect an
   explicit unsupported/omitted disposition rather than silently calling it a
   failure of the converter. Keep converter output and FreeCAD import
   diagnostics as separate records.
3. **Optional add-on probe only if available:** first inspect the exact pinned
   `Law.evaluate` call path. Use a short-lived isolated process and a small
   locally generated control with independently known analytic bounds/volume;
   cover SAT and SAB, native and STEP strategies separately, and capture
   diagnostics, body count, shape validity, bounds, volume, and omission count.

   consumer route. Never use a rendered image or the add-on's own export/reopen
   as the expected result.
4. **Keep DWG AcDs as its own gate:** on an eligible DWG source, require
   per-solid source handle, AcDs record key, chunk count/length/hash, owner
   association, and transform closure before testing detached payload parsing.

   identified DWG reader) has extracted and joined the payload; it cannot
   establish the DWG key/owner edge.
5. Reuse the scheduled composed platform/consumer checkpoint; do not run this
   external route per implementation slice. No testing DWG/DXF is committed:
   use already-available repository/user samples or scratch files created
   locally from scratch and remove them outside the repository after the
   controlled run.

### Peer comparison fields tightened

For each peer result at the composed comparison checkpoint, capture:

1. Immutable release/commit or package hash, operating system/architecture,

   typed fields, opaque bytes, references, diagnostics, omission/refusal, and
