   closure, and whether output was complete or explicitly partial.
5. For 3D: explicit entities versus proprietary ACIS carrier; exact carrier
   digest versus parsed structure versus kernel shape; body count, validity,
   units/transforms and analytic metrics when that route actually exposes them.
6. Parser lineage and kernel lineage, so wrappers, forks and applications
   sharing a parser/kernel do not get counted as independent votes.

control, not to another peer’s output. Treat mutable documentation and issue
reports as route/discovery evidence until a pinned executable and source-bound

This pass refreshed primary-source evidence for a current open-source CAD
application, its codec/kernel dependency graph, one reported DWG writer failure
and repair, and a broad-format CAD project. The purpose is to distinguish
implementation lineage, application behavior, geometry processing and
independent acceptance—not to add another peer to the implementation loop.
No repository was cloned or built, no external DWG/DXF was downloaded, no peer
or native application was run, and no local test was run.

| Primary-source evidence | What it establishes | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCADStudio's [current README](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/README.md), [Cargo.toml](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/Cargo.toml), and [Cargo.lock](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/Cargo.lock) | The application advertises native DWG/DXF read/write and a 3D modeling/rendering route. The manifest names `opencadcodec` and `opencadkernel` as separate Git dependencies. In the reviewed source snapshot, the manifest's short `rev` values (`a01df94` and `0574444`) do not match the dependency revisions recorded by the lockfile (`325fa98d…` and `dfca3912…`). The mismatch makes mutable-main source an unsafe proxy for a particular published binary until the release artifact and effective dependency lock are bound. | Keep OpenCADStudio eligible only as an optional application/consumer route at the composed gate. Record artifact SHA-256, application source commit, lockfile, resolved codec/kernel commits, OS/architecture, operation, and actual input/output version/hash. If those do not correspond, mark the route `PROVENANCE_INCOMPLETE`; do not use the README feature table as qualification. |
| GitHub marks [`HakanSeven12/opencadcodec`](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/opencadcodec) as forked from [`hakanaktt/acadrust`](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust); OpenCADStudio's manifest and lockfile identify that codec as its DWG/DXF dependency. | OpenCADStudio and ACadRust-family codec routes have shared parser/writer ancestry, even where the fork has since diverged. A fork can offer useful current behavior, but it is not a second independent parser lineage. | Do not count OpenCADStudio, `opencadcodec`, ACadRust, or downstream wrappers that consume these as independent codec votes. Keep exact fork revision and operation in the lineage ledger; do not transfer a fork's reported bug/fix directly to libdxfrw. |
| [`opencadkernel` README](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/opencadkernel) and [manifest](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/opencadkernel/blob/main/Cargo.toml) | The kernel is a separate geometry layer with an optional ACIS bridge (`SatDocument` lift/lower), rather than a DWG/DXF parser. Its README describes the project as early and says most operations are not yet written; the application’s higher-level 3D claims therefore need an exact kernel revision and an operation-specific result. | The kernel may be recorded as a distinct geometry route, not an independent file-format reader or an automatic B-rep oracle. For any optional run, keep parser/carrier, body construction, per-face completion/fallback, topology/validity, units/transforms, and application rendering in separate fields. A tessellated preview or same-stack reimport cannot promote semantic support. |
| OpenCADStudio [issue #1078](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/issues/1078) | A user reported that an R2018/AC1032 DWG written by a specific OpenCADStudio build required AutoCAD RECOVER and lost `AcDbLayout` objects; a production case also reported MLeader, dynamic-block, handle/XDATA and XREF damage. The maintainer later reported fixes in codec/kernel/application commits and a source-pair comparison: 345 MLeader records and 8 Layout records matched semantically, with a 613-segment AcDs section byte-identical on same-version saves. The source pair and post-fix native acceptance were not independently checked in this review. | Reuse the issue as a peer-specific writer failure taxonomy and a candidate design for record-level checks; it is not evidence of a libdxfrw defect or complete release acceptance. At the existing composed gate, separate same-version preservation from cross-version conversion; compare record identity/type/owner and handle closure, layout/class links, XREF metadata, AcDs owner links and exact unchanged-carrier bytes, and native open/recovery disposition. Do not require byte-identical AcDs data after a version-changing rewrite. |
| CADKernel's [format matrix](https://github.com/kernalix7/CADKernel#supported-file-formats) | Its broad README compatibility headline is narrowed by its own detailed table: DWG is described as using a DXF fallback, while ACIS SAT/SAB is explicitly marked unsupported. The documentation is self-reported and was not exercised. | Do not admit CADKernel as an independent native DWG or ACIS semantic peer based on the headline. A future, pinned DXF fallback could at most be evaluated for the specific 2D operation/entity subset it actually reads and writes. |

### Implementation-ready use and evidence ceiling

1. Continue the existing local implementation order. This review adds no
   feature queue item and does not make optional peer availability a blocker.
2. Keep peer execution at the already-planned composed checkpoint. If an
   OpenCADStudio route is selected, first resolve the release artifact to its
   exact source commit and dependency lock. Record the codec fork and kernel
   revisions separately; the application is a consumer test, not a new codec
   lineage.
3. Use the #1078 failure pattern to structure the existing writer graph and
   native-acceptance matrix: same-version rewrite, cross-version rewrite,
   untouched opaque-carrier retention, semantic record/owner closure, and
   independent consumer result are different cells. A peer's corrected build
   is not an upstream fix requirement.
4. Do not add external binaries, external fixtures, CTest entries, dependencies
   or per-slice peer tests. Use locally generated controls for code changes;
   keep native/peer and broad sanitizer/full-suite checks composed or scheduled.
5. If the exact app artifact, dependency graph, or source-pair provenance is
   unavailable, record `NOT_RUN`/`PROVENANCE_INCOMPLETE` and proceed with local
   work rather than guessing which source the published binary contains.

consumer evidence gates only. It adds no finding or top-level implementation

### Implementation-ready use and evidence ceiling

## Deeper/broader Linux 2D consumer routes and shared-codec lineage review (2026-10-17; research only)

This pass screened two newly surfaced open-source CAD applications for a
potential downstream acceptance role and traced each format path to its actual
codec/converter lineage. The purpose is to broaden the optional 2D consumer
matrix without mistaking an application wrapper, port, or shared backend for an
independent DWG implementation. No repository was cloned, application or peer
runtime was installed/run, external drawing was downloaded, or local test was
run.

| Primary-source evidence | What it establishes | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| [IngeCAD repository README](https://github.com/ingelibre/ingecad) (status section, design pillars, source-build instructions) | The project describes itself as a Linux-first 2D CAD app. Its document model is a DXF database using ezdxf, and it says unrecognized data is preserved when saving. DWG is converted externally: packaged/patched LibreDWG is the only bundled engine, with ODA File Converter described as optional. Source-build guidance says its LibreDWG build is patched and directs users to the project patch/build scripts. The README reports broad UI and 2D drawing behavior, but those claims are not runtime qualification or a 3D semantic result. | Admit IngeCAD only as an optional, exact-version Linux downstream consumer and ezdxf-backed DXF route. For a direct DXF run, bind the app release/source, Python/ezdxf dependency set, input/output hashes and target `$ACADVER`; inspect per-source entity/handle/block path, layer, coordinates, text/dimension/style fields, diagnostics and whether untouched unknown tags survive. Treat explicit mesh entities such as `3DFACE` as a separate profile and only if the actual imported geometry can be inspected. Do not count the DWG wrapper as a new reader lineage: record its exact patched LibreDWG source/build/hash, selected ODA-vs-LibreDWG converter, argv/status and intermediate DXF before assessing the app model. |
| IngeCAD's [release/install/source-build documentation](https://github.com/ingelibre/ingecad) | The repository offers Linux artifacts and a source-build route; platform packaging may bundle different converter binaries, and a mutable `main` README does not identify which patch set or binary is in a particular artifact. | If the candidate is already available at the composed consumer checkpoint, record artifact hash, app source tag/commit, bundled `ezdxf` version, converter hash/version, and the patched LibreDWG commit/patch set. If any route component cannot be bound, mark that lane `PROVENANCE_INCOMPLETE`/`NOT_RUN`; do not infer upstream LibreDWG behavior from the app's bundled binary. Do not add it as a required install or CI dependency. |
| [Zephyr repository README](https://github.com/joseph-montanez/zephyr) (`SwiftDXFrw`, file-I/O and tech-stack sections) | Zephyr describes itself as a 2D CAD application. It says the Swift DXF module is a port of libdxfrw and DWG I/O uses LibreDWG. Its stated DXF target includes R2007; the repository's broad feature claims do not identify a pinned released artifact or establish independent semantic conformance. | At most use Zephyr as optional app/render/edit smoke for the route it actually ships. Its DXF port is derivative of libdxfrw and its DWG path is LibreDWG lineage, so neither counts as an independent codec vote. Pin the app/build, port commit, converter artifact and selected 2D operation; compare exact generated identities and typed values, not screenshots or its self-roundtrip alone. No Mac/Windows route substitutes for Linux consumer qualification or for LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/FreeCAD-specific gates. |
| LibreDWG's current [README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) and [manual](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | The project's own status language distinguishes broad version recognition from reliable writing: its README says R2010–R2018 writing can produce CRC errors, while the manual qualifies several writer directions/versions and notes AutoCAD may require recovery for generated output. These are project disclosures, not a verdict on a specific patched IngeCAD build. | Keep the existing writer matrix version- and operation-specific. An app's advertised DWG read/write, file-open success, or same-engine readback cannot qualify DWG output. Any optional test must check magic/target version, independent structural reopen, per-handle/type/owner disposition and diagnostics; native acceptance stays a separate composed result. |

### Implementation-ready disposition

1. Add no implementation item or routine validation step. Continue the local
   touched-target/focused-generated-test loop; do not install either app or a
   peer converter for an ordinary source slice.
2. If a Linux 2D consumer observation is useful at the existing composed gate,
   prefer one IngeCAD direct-DXF run first because its documented model parser
   (ezdxf) is distinct from libdxfrw. Use a tiny source-authored, scratch-only
   drawing and a prewritten manifest for ordinary 2D entities, blocks/INSERTs,
   layouts and selected text/dimension fields. Check consumer model identities
   and values before and after save/reopen; record unknown-tag retention
   separately from typed semantics.
3. Keep IngeCAD's DWG case as a separate chain: source DWG → exact selected
   converter → hashed/versioned DXF → ezdxf-backed app import. Do not credit a
   result to libdxfrw's DWG reader, or treat the bundled LibreDWG fork as the
   upstream release. If its patch identity cannot be resolved, skip that lane.
4. Keep Zephyr optional and correlated: only a downstream UX/render/edit result
   is available, since the DXF parser is a libdxfrw port and DWG depends on
   LibreDWG. A successful Zephyr open cannot serve as an independent
   differential or semantic 3D result.
5. Generate temporary test drawings locally from scratch; commit no external
   DWG/DXF artifact. Do not add CMake/CTest/CI integrations, dependencies, or
   per-slice application runs. Record `NOT_AVAILABLE`, `NOT_RUN`, or
   `PROVENANCE_INCOMPLETE` rather than blocking local implementation.

## Deeper/broader entity-specific DXF coordinate frames and arbitrary-axis boundary review (2026-10-17; research only)

This pass reconciled Autodesk's DXF frame contracts with current ezdxf,
FreeCAD, and ACadSharp implementation sources and audited the corresponding
local parser/helper and generated test vectors. It updates PAR-21 / 7H
readiness only. No peer was built or run, no drawing was downloaded, and no
fixture, dependency, test registration, or production change was made.

| Primary-source evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autodesk [OCS reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D99F1509-E4E4-47A3-8691-92EA07DC88F5.htm) and [arbitrary-axis algorithm](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-E19E5B42-0CC7-4EBA-B29F-5E1D595149EE.htm) | DXF coordinate frame is entity-specific. The OCS summary distinguishes planar entities, WCS 3D entities, mixed-frame DIMENSION, and WCS VIEWPORT. The arbitrary-axis polar-cap test is strict: both `abs(Nx)` and `abs(Ny)` must be `< 1/64`; equality selects `Wz × N`, not `Wy × N`. These are normative wire/coordinate rules, not a guarantee that every consumer API returns world-space geometry. | Keep raw entity fields, optional legacy projection, and consumer world-geometry as different observations. In PAR-21/7H, lock the strict 1/64 boundary and both coordinate predicates with locally generated vectors; do not derive frame behavior from a group number or C++ storage type. |
| Autodesk [ELLIPSE DXF table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-107CB04F-AD4D-4D2F-8EC9-AC90888063AB.htm), [INSERT DXF table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-28FA4CFB-9D5E-4880-9F11-36C97578252F.htm), and [LWPOLYLINE DXF table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-748FC305-F3F2-4F74-825A-61F04D757A50.htm) | ELLIPSE groups 10/11 are WCS despite group 210 being an extrusion/normal vector. INSERT group 10 is OCS and must remain distinct from subsequent block-transform application; scales default independently to 1. LWPOLYLINE groups 10/20 are OCS, group 38 is elevation, and 210 is its extrusion direction. The same group code is not enough to identify a frame across entity classes. | Preserve the already-implemented ELLIPSE no-second-transform behavior and its valid/invalid controls. Retain separate OCS/elevation, WCS geometry, and INSERT/MINSERT transform tests; keep dimensions in the mixed-frame lane. Avoid one generic `applyExtrusion` rule for all entities. |
| ezdxf [OCS/UCS usage tutorial](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorials/ocs_usage.html) | Documents OCS elevation and thickness separately; highlights LWPOLYLINE/HATCH's explicit elevation field; and notes ELLIPSE carries an extrusion direction without establishing an OCS for the center/axis values. This is a current peer-library explanation, not a substitute for the entity-specific Autodesk table or an independent native run. | Use ezdxf as a terminology/implementation cross-check only. Keep semantic fields and transformations typed by entity; do not compare a projected WCS point to a peer's raw OCS tuple. |
| FreeCAD [current Draft `placementFromDXFOCS` source](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDXF.py) and ACadSharp [Entity transform source](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/Entities/Entity.cs) | FreeCAD's mutable current source spells out the 1/64 arbitrary-axis branch and creates OCS placements for the selected importer path. ACadSharp's mutable source transforms through OCS/world matrices using `Matrix3.ArbitraryAxis`. They show the same class of transform concerns in downstream implementations, but neither source was pinned to a released runtime or executed here; FreeCAD's route is importer-specific and ACadSharp's helper does not alone prove every entity mapping. | Treat these as source-level route cross-checks, not support evidence or an implementation oracle. At the existing optional consumer checkpoint, pin exact app/parser revisions and score raw fields, projected points, and native acceptance separately. No peer run belongs in the leaf implementation loop. |
| Local `DRW_Entity::calculateAxis` / `extrusionUnitVector`, `dxfRW::processEllipse`, and `runDxfNonUnitExtrusionPolicy` in `tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp` | The local helper normalizes a temporary direction and uses the Autodesk strict `< 1/64` branch; it preserves the original extrusion field. `processEllipse` correctly does not apply the OCS helper to its WCS center/major-axis fields. Existing generated ARC/LWPOLYLINE vectors cover X below and above the cutoff, reflected normals, non-unit inputs, raw versus legacy read modes and ASCII/binary. They leave `Ny=0` in every cutoff vector, so they do not exercise the second predicate or equality. This is a generated coverage gap, not a reproduced parser defect. | Refine the existing 7H test, without adding a finding or CTest: add Y-only-below, X-below/Y-at, and X-at/Y-below vectors (with a unit normal and independently computed expected basis). Reuse the existing ASCII/binary and two-read-mode loop; assert raw and transformed results separately. Stop once this narrow matrix passes; no broad-suite rerun or native/peer gate is warranted by this source audit. |

### Implementation-ready and speedy disposition

1. Keep the feature owners and order unchanged: PAR-21 / 7H already owns
   accepted-normal policy, OCS projection, and the relevant typed tests. No new
   parser defect or plan subplan was established.
2. Extend `runDxfNonUnitExtrusionPolicy` or its existing focused selector with
   the three missing predicate/equality vectors. Generate expected basis and
   transformed coordinates from a small independent test oracle, not the
   production helper. Retain the existing unit/non-unit and negative-normal
   cases rather than duplicating them.
3. For the added vectors, run only the touched strict test target and focused
   selector; keep ASCII/binary plus `applyExt=false/true` in that owner. No new
   CTest/CI registration, full test suite, external fixture, peer install, or
   native app wait is needed. Update this progress row after implementation.
4. Do not change public 2D callback values, the ELLIPSE WCS rule, INSERT graph
   representation, units, or the 3D consumer contract based on source review
   alone. Existing nested INSERT/MINSERT, 3DFACE/MESH WCS, and mixed DIMENSION
   tests remain separate evidence lanes.

This refines only existing PAR-21 / 7H and the composed coordinate-consumer
interpretation. It adds no finding or top-level subplan, implementation queue

## Research update — standalone PLOTSETTINGS root and bounded next slice (2026-10-17)

Primary-source and independent implementation review resolves the previously
open standalone page-setup root/owner question. Autodesk's `Database` API
identifies `PlotSettingsDictionaryId` as the `ACAD_PLOTSETTINGS` dictionary;
its Plot Settings guide says standalone `PlotSettings` objects are stored in
that dictionary, iterates its named entries, and creates a named entry using
`PlotSettingsName`. Autodesk's DXF contract identifies the `PLOTSETTINGS`
record's handle, owner-dictionary/owner-object links, page-setup name, and
optional code-333 shade-plot handle. LibreDWG independently maps its
PLOTSETTINGS object family to `ACAD_PLOTSETTINGS`. This is sufficient to plan
the standalone object as an `ACAD_PLOTSETTINGS` dictionary entry keyed by its
page-setup name, owned by that dictionary; it supersedes older plan text that
treated the root/owner identity itself as unknown.

That evidence does **not** close the optional shade-plot edge. Autodesk's DXF
PLOTSETTINGS page documents shade modes 0–3, while current ObjectARX APIs
describe additional VisualStyle/RenderPreset modes and typed object IDs.
Therefore a non-null code-333 target still needs mode-, version-, and target-
type evidence plus handle remapping. Do not serialize a non-null code-333
reference from handle existence alone.

   comparison and require every object's parent handle to be that dictionary.

   named entries, and each PLOTSETTINGS record. Verify the writer applies the

4. Generate two named page setups with non-monotonic source handles and one

5. Run the focused adapter/DXF fixture selectors, targeted `-Werror` builds,

## Deeper research update — PLOTSETTINGS shade-mode target typing (2026-10-17)

The primary-source follow-up resolves one bounded part of code 333. Autodesk's
current `PlotSettingsShadePlotType` enum distinguishes `VisualStyle` (4) from
`RenderPreset` (5). Its `SetShadePlot` API states that AsDisplayed/Rendered do
not use an object ID, while VisualStyle/RenderPreset require an object ID of
the corresponding object family. Autodesk's DXF VisualStyle reference
identifies the standalone `VISUALSTYLE` record family. This makes a nonzero
PLOTSETTINGS code-333 target admissible for mode 4 only when it closes to one
rooted, owned, identity-consistent VISUALSTYLE; mode 5 must not be treated as a
VISUALSTYLE reference merely because its handle resolves.

The existing DXF-source exporter now implements that narrow mode-4 case. It
requires one ACAD_VISUALSTYLE NOD edge, one NOD-owned dictionary, one matching
dictionary entry, and exactly one typed plus raw VISUALSTYLE carrier with the
same owner and identity. Existing object-handle remapping is applied to code
333. Mode 5 remains rejected: this review did not establish the complete
RenderSettings carrier/owner/serialization route in this adapter. Broader
research now identifies versioned candidate families, but not a single
version-independent code-333 graph: Autodesk's pre-2016 guide describes
MENTALRAYRENDERSETTINGS in ACAD_RENDER_SETTINGS and a copied preset in
ACAD_RENDER_PLOT_SETTINGS for assignment to PlotSettings/Viewport; newer
guidance describes RapidRTRenderSettings under
ACAD_RENDER_RAPIDRT_SETTINGS, while its current sample assigns that ID to a
Viewport. The generic PlotSettings API requires a RenderSettings object ID,
but does not by itself settle which named dictionary entry a saved standalone
PLOTSETTINGS code 333 must target for each release. Therefore mode 5 remains
fail-closed pending version-specific wire evidence. Modes 0–3 remain restricted
to a null/omitted code 333. This is structural preservation, not proof that a
printer, plot configuration, rendering preset, or CAD application will execute
the requested plot behavior.

## Deeper/broader research update — PLOTSETTINGS RenderPreset graph and version boundary (2026-10-17)

This follow-up documents the candidate *named-object graph route* for shade
mode 5, but does not supply a producer-authored standalone-DXF witness for its
serialized code-76/code-333 form. Autodesk's official Render Presets guidance says the modern
RapidRT presets live in `ACAD_RENDER_RAPIDRT_SETTINGS`, and a second named
dictionary, `ACAD_RENDER_PLOT_SETTINGS`, stores the copy assigned to a
`Viewport` or `PlotSettings`. The same documentation labels MentalRay as the
pre-2016 family and describes its copy in `ACAD_RENDER_PLOT_SETTINGS`; the
2015/earlier guide states the same assignment contract. Autodesk's current
`PlotSettings.SetShadePlot` API requires a `RenderSettings` object for
`RenderPreset`, and its current enum assigns mode 5 to `RenderPreset`. The
primary-source combination supports the following bounded graph:

`NOD[ACAD_RENDER_PLOT_SETTINGS] -> DICTIONARY[key = preset name] -> one
MENTALRAYRENDERSETTINGS or RAPIDRTRENDERSETTINGS object <- PLOTSETTINGS code 333`

The target must be the copied record in `ACAD_RENDER_PLOT_SETTINGS`, not merely
a handle-resolvable global preset under `ACAD_RENDER_SETTINGS` or
`ACAD_RENDER_RAPIDRT_SETTINGS`. Require one NOD root edge, a NOD-owned complete
dictionary, one matching key/object, exact typed/raw identity and owner, and
the code-333 handle to that same target. Preserve the raw positional record
and map its self/owner handles and PLOTSETTINGS code 333 through the existing
source-to-output identity map. Restrict the first writer route to same-source
DXF version replay; do not infer support from DWG callbacks or down-version
conversion. Use the record's actual family as the discriminator: ACADVER alone
does not separate all products that use the same DXF generation.

An important evidence ceiling remains. Autodesk's current (2025) DXF
`PLOTSETTINGS` table still documents shade modes 0–3, whereas the current
ObjectARX/.NET API documents modes 0–5 and the optional shade-plot ID. This
disagreement means the official API establishes object typing and the
dictionary assignment route, but does not independently establish every
release's serialized code-76 value 5/code-333 wire behavior. A raw-preserving
same-version writer plus generated ASCII/Binary round-trip can establish local
structural behavior only. Keep mode-5 native save/reopen and actual plotting
as external semantic qualification; do not promote a general plotting or
RenderPreset support claim from this local route. LibreDWG's current object
catalog also marks RapidRT/MentalRay render records unstable, so it is a
family-name cross-check, not an independent semantic vote.

Implementation-ready slice (existing PAR-20/7G.3e; no new top-level item):

1. Admit standalone mode 5 only from DXF source when a PLOTSETTINGS code-333
   handle uniquely closes to a typed/raw RapidRT or MentalRay record in the
   NOD-rooted `ACAD_RENDER_PLOT_SETTINGS` dictionary. Require source/target
   DXF version equality, matching record name/key/owner, complete dictionary
   entries, and one-to-one typed/raw carrier identity. Keep modes 0–3 null-only
   and mode 4 VISUALSTYLE-only. Leave other RenderSettings types and DWG
   sources fail-closed unless their separate object-family graph is wholly
   rooted and same-version raw replay is proven.
2. Emit that record via `writeRawDxfObject` to preserve positional group order;
   keep the existing `writePlotSettings` field writer. Validate all identities
   before destination publication and remap raw group 5/owner 330 plus
   PLOTSETTINGS group 333. Reject duplicate roots, dictionary keys, handles,
   callback pairs, wrong family/owner, dangling references, or version mismatch.
3. Extend the existing in-memory adapter selector with one RapidRT positive
   and one MentalRay structural vector, ASCII and Binary export/readback,
   remapped code-333 target, fixed-handle collision, wrong-root/key/owner/type,
   dangling-handle and version-mismatch negatives, sentinel preservation, and
   same-adapter retry. Generate the vectors from scratch; do not add a checked-
   in DWG/DXF fixture or a new CTest registration.
4. Run the focused selectors, touched `-Werror` adapter/CLI targets, and
   `lc3_compat_check`. Defer full suites to their existing checkpoint and
   require a native AutoCAD/compatible save-reopen plus plotted result before
   any external semantic promotion.

Primary sources:

- [Autodesk Render Presets, 2016/current RapidRT and PlotSettings copy dictionary](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2016/ENU/AutoCAD-NET/files/GUID-A1309D38-A432-487C-B890-6666B891C701.htm)
- [Autodesk Render Presets, pre-2016 MentalRay and PlotSettings copy dictionary](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-NET/files/GUID-A1309D38-A432-487C-B890-6666B891C701.htm)
- [Autodesk `PlotSettings.SetShadePlot` object-type contract](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2022/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_PlotSettings_SetShadePlot_PlotSettingsShadePlotType_ObjectId.html)
- [Autodesk current `PlotSettingsShadePlotType` enum](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_PlotSettingsShadePlotType.html)
- [Autodesk current PLOTSETTINGS DXF fields](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-1113675E-AB07-4567-801A-310CDE0D56E9.htm)
- [Autodesk RAPIDRTRENDERSETTINGS DXF record](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-427599C5-9562-4384-82E6-8B7B87492C57.htm)
- [Autodesk MENTALRAYRENDERSETTINGS DXF record](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-69B42C9D-062D-4FEC-952E-CA0DDF7B4831.htm)

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.13 IMAGEDEF filename retained owner (2026-10-17; focused local verification, uncommitted)

`DRW_ImageDef::parseCode` now retains DXF group 1 (`name`) through the
existing `DRW_TableEntry` retained-string lease. The source class declares a
derived `name` that hides the base table-entry name, so this slice adds a
dedicated live-byte counter for the actual IMAGEDEF filename rather than
reusing the base name counter. Replacement bytes are reserved before mutation;
on refusal, the previous filename and charge remain unchanged. Reset clears the
derived counter before the base class releases the shared lease. Implicit copy
construction/assignment preserve both the derived counter and shared lease.
This changes public `DRW_ImageDef` layout: downstream consumers must rebuild;
binary ABI compatibility is not claimed. Accounting covers logical parsed DXF
filename bytes, not allocator capacity/RSS, caller mutation after callback,
DWG-owned strings, or writer/projection copies.

The generated `--dxf-imagedef-name-owner-budget` selector verifies ASCII and
Binary direct parsing, replacement exact/one-byte-under admission, preservation
of the previous value and charge on refusal, copy/assignment after source reset,
and final reset release. Full generated OBJECTS drawings exercise the actual
`linkImage` callback route: cap-minus-one refuses before callbacks with the
retained-byte `ResourceLimit` diagnostic; raising the same facade to the exact
cap retries and publishes both IMAGEDEF records including a following
sentinel. The binary source is generated under temporary storage and removed.

Focused local verification passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_hardening_tests lc3_compat_check -j2`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --dxf-imagedef-name-owner-budget`

No full suite, CTest registration, persistent fixture, peer runtime, or native
CAD run was used. No support claim or J disposition changes. This is a narrow
retained-owner closure only; IMAGEDEF/IMAGE entity semantics and external CAD
qualification remain governed by their existing rows. The shared checkout is
broadly dirty and this slice is uncommitted; unrelated hunks were not staged.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.12 STYLE font-name retained owner (2026-10-17; focused local verification, uncommitted)

`DRW_Textstyle::parseCode` now charges DXF group 3 (`font`) and group 4
(`bigFont`) to the existing shared `DRW_TableEntry` retained-string lease.
Per-field live-byte counters reserve replacement values before assignment and
keep prior values/charges on refusal. `reset()` clears the counters before the
base table-entry reset releases the lease, while preserving the established
default font name `txt` and empty bigfont. Ordinary implicit copy/assignment
share the lease and preserve the field counters. This adds private accounting
state to the public class layout: downstream consumers must rebuild; no binary
ABI compatibility is claimed. This accounts parsed DXF logical string length,
not capacity/RSS, public post-callback mutation, DWG strings, or writer copies.

The existing hardening target's generated `--dxf-textstyle-font-owner-budget`
selector checks direct parser input in ASCII and Binary DXF, old-to-new
replacement of both fields, a 256-byte bigfont, exact and one-byte-under
admission, preservation of the previous value on refusal, copy/assignment

also imports generated full STYLE TABLES drawings: one-byte-under refuses
before style callbacks with the retained-byte `ResourceLimit` diagnostic, and
raising the same facade to the exact budget retries successfully through a
following STYLE sentinel. The binary control is generated in temporary storage
and removed by the test.

## Implementation progress — 7AR.1 malformed CIF syntax and scalar safety (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

`DRW_Converter::encodeText` now accepts a CIF token only when it has exactly
the `\\U+` prefix and four ASCII hexadecimal digits. It decodes the complete
four-digit value without `scanf`/stream prefix parsing, so a malformed suffix
cannot turn `\\U+12G4` into U+0012. Malformed, truncated, whitespace, NUL,
and surrogate inputs remain literal in tolerant callbacks. Decode observations
mark malformed syntax as `MalformedEscape | UnrepresentedEscape`; NUL is
`UnrepresentedEscape`; surrogate code units are
`InvalidUnicodeOutput | UnrepresentedEscape`. This preserves source spelling
while making `RequireValidSource` refuse the ambiguous/unrepresentable input.
It also prevents invalid UTF-8 emission and C-string truncation through an
embedded NUL. Valid lowercase/uppercase CIF, adjacent escapes, and a following
hex-like suffix retain exact four-digit consumption. Tests exercise the
single-byte table, generic DBCS, Shift-JIS override and modern UTF-8 paths,
plus ASCII/Binary facade reads and strict-source admission. A paired surrogate
escape stays literal and unrepresented: Autodesk's published CIF overview
does not establish a pair-combination rule, so no supplementary-CIF
interpretation is claimed.

Focused validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests -j2`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests --text-read-observations`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests --source-text-admission`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests --target-text-transport`
- `cmake --build build-gcc --target dwg2dxf lc3_compat_check -j2`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_gbk_codepage$' --output-on-failure` — pass (1/1)
- scoped `git diff --check` (recorded in the receipt)

No full suite, native CAD, peer runtime, or Linux/Windows run was performed.
The generated source controls are in memory or temporary directories; no
fixture, CTest registration, dependency, or support claim was added. The
shared checkout contains extensive pre-existing changes, so this slice is
uncommitted rather than staging unrelated work. This closes the local
malformed-syntax/scalar behavior for 7AR.1; producer-specific surrogate-pair
semantics remain unresolved. 7AR.2's local source-bound matrix is unchanged;
native rendering and independent semantic interpretation remain separate.

## ASM BinaryFile8 parser lineage and profile review 2026-10-17 research only

This source review adds a useful *candidate route*, not a newly established
libdxfrw defect or a support gap suitable for a new implementation subplan. It
reconciles two recently visible open-source projects against the existing
carrier → payload parser → B-rep semantics → consumer evidence ladder.

### Route findings and evidence ceiling

| Route | Primary-source evidence | What it can add | What it cannot establish |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`ezf3d`](https://github.com/AlexSabaka/ezf3d) | The repository describes a clean-room MIT, alpha, headless Fusion `.f3d`/`.f3z` reader. Fusion `.smb` entries are identified as `ASM BinaryFile8`; its README reports B-rep traversal/analytic geometry and checks against edge/vertex and Fusion cached-display-mesh redundancy. GitHub currently shows no published releases. | A potentially distinct implementation for the exact ASM BinaryFile8 payload profile, if an admitted DWG/DXF payload is first shown byte/profile-compatible. Its clean-room claim and distinct parser are relevant implementation-lineage evidence. | Fusion container ingestion is not DXF or DWG parsing. The reviewed source does not map an ACIS DXF SAT/SAB carrier or DWG ACDSDATA/AcDs owner graph to the `.smb` dialect. Its four Fusion designs and cached meshes are from the same application/producer lineage, not independently authored semantic expectations. Alpha status and no published release require exact commit pinning before any optional run. |
| [`inventor-kit`](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/inventor-kit) + [`cq-acis`](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis) | Its documented pipeline is `IPT → CFB/RSe → saved SAB/ASM → acis-core → AcisModel → CadQuery`; it requires `cq-acis` and the `acis-core`/bridge crates, then exposes CadQuery geometry. Its current README identifies PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 for new material. | A bounded saved-geometry/container and assembly-reference route for Inventor inputs, subject to license and exact profile review. | Not a separate SAT/SAB decoder or geometry kernel from `cq-acis`/CadQuery/OCCT; not a DWG/DXF or AcDs route. It is not an acceptable new dependency for this project without a separate license decision. Its own validation guide says frozen metrics originate from the same converter; analytic cylinder/box checks have narrow scope; ezdxf checks SAB record boundaries only; STEP/XDE checks hierarchy and metrics, not native Inventor state; independent Apprentice/Inventor captures count only when a real provider capture and provenance exist. |
| Existing FreeCAD/InventorLoader lane | Stock FreeCAD's DXF/DWG route and optional InventorLoader path are already covered in the existing consumer-route research. | Retain the current separation between stock converter/importer behavior and optional add-on parser behavior. | Do not count a common OCCT kernel as an independent geometry vote; neither route supplies DWG AcDs owner/key/payload proof merely by opening a document. |

The important distinction is *parser lineage versus input-profile applicability*.
`ezf3d` may be genuinely separate from `cq-acis`, but that independence has no
value for a libdxfrw result unless the bytes/profile under test are actually
accepted by that implementation. Conversely, a common output kernel is not a
second independent geometry result. Do not infer that “ASM”, “SAB”, or a
matching modeler/version string means the envelopes, word widths, compression,
record framing, or semantic body model are interchangeable.

### Existing-checkpoint readiness refinement

Only at the already planned composed external-evidence checkpoint, and only if
an authorized existing or locally generated control payload is available:

1. Pin the target source file's provenance (producer/version, AC code, source
   entity handle, output/input route, hash) and independently inventory the
   carrier: inline SAT versus SAB chunks, or the DWG AcDs record/key/index and
   entity/owner join. Keep DWG container association as a separate result.
2. Preserve/hash the exact extracted bytes and record signature, container
   width (`BinaryFile4`/`BinaryFile8`/other as observed), modeler/save stamp,
   declared and actual lengths, framing, compression, and relevant offsets.
   Treat `ezf3d` as `NOT_APPLICABLE` unless its pinned reader accepts that exact
   payload profile; a similar name or version stamp is not admission evidence.
3. If the profile matches, run only the pinned `ezf3d` parser in an isolated
   scratch process and capture its per-body/topology inventory, failures,
   unsupported tokens, units, placements, and any incomplete/fallback status.
   Do not download or commit Fusion designs or peer fixtures for this step.
4. Compare the output to independent, source-authored expectations: at minimum
   analytic primitive dimensions/area/volume, expected shell/face/edge/vertex
   relationships, closure/orientation, and units/transforms. Do not use the
   parser's own Fusion cache, same-converter frozen metrics, nonempty output, or
   STEP roundtrip as the sole truth source. Record parser agreement separately
   from semantic agreement and consumer acceptance.
5. Do not install `inventor-kit` as a new dependency or count it as another
   parser/kernel vote. Its value is limited to documenting a shared
   `cq-acis`/OCCT lineage and a separate Inventor container route; any execution
   requires a license review and must not be represented as an independent
   ACIS oracle.

This is not a per-slice gate. Continue the plan's existing fast local tests and

native applications until the composed checkpoint and an applicable pinned
payload exist. A missing matching profile means `NOT_APPLICABLE`, not a blocker

Before a typed reader is considered, require the ODA specification plus an independently traceable, versioned producer witness and a following-object boundary check. Do not hardcode `546` from the peer or download/commit the issue's drawings. |

Its author describes three separate quadratic paths: exact-size handle-vector growth, ordered-reference insertion/movement, and repeated reference-cache resolution. The PR reports large speedups and unchanged output on its own tests/corpus, but those measurements and results are not reproduced here and are not a local libdxfrw performance result. | Reuse PAR-92/7BA/7S.3's existing deterministic work counters and bounded growth/visit checks. Keep vector growth, index insertion/comparison, reference resolution, and allocation admission as separate costs; preserve libdxfrw's source-order/ownership rules. Do not transplant LibreDWG's handle-first ordering or use its timings as thresholds. Run any scale experiment once at the existing composed checkpoint, only after a corresponding local hot path changes. |

Its patch is author-proposed and does not define a universal relaxed parser policy. Autodesk's references remain the field contract; peer output behavior is not normative. | Keep presence separate from numeric value in the existing HATCH owner. Keep attribute tag admission tied to its defined string/producer profile, and keep embedded-MTEXT scope controlled by its marker/grammar rather than a growing list of tolerated group codes. ### Implementation-ready refinements

1. **PAR-21/7H — geometry evidence:** retain the existing analytic transform oracle. A future optional ACadSharp comparison must pin its exact package/source revision and validate its ARC/ELLIPSE transform behavior against known analytic cases before that route contributes to geometric agreement. Field parse/readback and transformed geometry remain separate result columns.
2. **PAR-06 — unknown object policy:** keep PERSUBENTMGR opaque or explicitly unsupported. Reopen this decision only with authoritative layout evidence, a versioned producer sample whose provenance and object boundaries are known, and a non-speculative dispatch identifier captured from an eligible local trace.
3. **PAR-92/7BA — performance evidence:** keep the completed bounded-staging tests and work counters as leaf gates. At a planned composed checkpoint, a single representative scale profile may record input size, operation counts, allocation requests, output identity/owner census, and wall time as diagnostic only. Do not make wall time a pass threshold or re-run large scale cases per slice.
4. **HATCH/ATTRIB/MTEXT — parser policy:** preserve exact presence/value state, entity sub-scope, and record alignment. Use one generated minimal case only when a local change introduces an uncovered branch; a peer's accepted/rejected file or patch does not justify silently dropping the field or accepting arbitrary unknown codes.
5. **Evidence ledger:** for every peer result, record artifact/revision, format and direction, entity/class family, whether only fields or derived geometry were compared, full/reduced/recovery mode, diagnostics, and explicit source-to-output disposition. Peer self-roundtrip is not independent semantic proof.

## Cross-implementation research update — RenderPreset evidence ceiling (2026-10-17)

The broader implementation survey narrows what the preceding API research can
support. Autodesk's current ObjectARX/.NET contract is positive: shade mode 5
is `RenderPreset`, and its object ID must identify a `RenderSettings` object.
Autodesk's Render Presets guides also document the copied preset dictionary
`ACAD_RENDER_PLOT_SETTINGS` for assignment to `PlotSettings`/`Viewport`, with
the concrete renderer family changing from legacy MentalRay to RapidRT in
later product generations. These sources justify the *candidate named-copy
route*; they do not provide a producer-authored standalone DXF wire example
proving code 76 = 5 and code 333 for every release.

Independent open-source coverage is more conservative and does not close that
gap:

- The current Autodesk PLOTSETTINGS DXF field page and the ezdxf 1.4.5
  `PlotSettings` reference document shade modes 0–3. ezdxf also says it is
  unsure whether PLOTSETTINGS occurs as a standalone object, so its model is
  not evidence for standalone mode 5.
- ACadSharp's current `ShadePlotMode` enum lists only 0–3. Its PlotSettings
  model records code 333 as an ignored reference value; that is useful field
  mapping, not evidence of RenderPreset graph closure or plotting behavior.
- LibreDWG's object schema carries PLOTSETTINGS `shadeplot_type` (76) and
  `shadeplot` (333), while `dwggrep` cross-reference code categorizes the
  PLOTSETTINGS code-333 edge as VISUALSTYLE. Its object catalog marks the
  RapidRT/MentalRay settings families unstable. This is a DWG/implementation
  cross-check, not proof that RenderSettings targets are invalid in AutoCAD.
- Autodesk Community material reports mode-4/5 behavior in practice, but is
  user-authored rather than a normative DXF contract. Keep it as a lead for
  locating producer samples, not as a support gate.

Therefore distinguish three outcomes in implementation and reporting:

1. **Documented API intent:** mode 5 names a `RenderSettings` object and the
   copied preset dictionary route is documented.
2. **Local structural replay:** the adapter may preserve a complete,
   uniquely rooted, typed/raw RapidRT or MentalRay graph only for DXF input
   and identical source/target version. Generated ASCII/Binary controls now
   exercise each family, handle remapping, wrong-root/key/owner/family,
   dangling-reference and version-mismatch rejection, sentinel preservation,
   and same-adapter retry. This proves only this library's generated
   serialization/readback consistency.
3. **External semantic support:** still unqualified until a release-specific
   native save/reopen witness confirms code 76/333, the stored dictionary
   owner/key/target, and the resulting plotted output. Prefer one legacy
   MentalRay and one modern RapidRT witness; a single family cannot qualify
   the other. Include a peer reader/writer comparison, but do not let peer
   acceptance alone replace native behavior evidence.

Updated implementation sequence (existing PAR-20/7G.3e; no new finding or
subplan):

1. Keep the code route limited to the complete NOD-rooted
   `ACAD_RENDER_PLOT_SETTINGS` copy graph, exact record-name/key/owner/handle
   identity, paired typed/raw callbacks, and same-source-version DXF replay.
   Keep modes 0–3 null-only, mode 4 VISUALSTYLE-only, DWG source and version
   conversion fail-closed. Do not normalize opaque positional data or claim
   renderer semantics.
2. Run the two generated family vectors and fast adapter selectors at each
   implementation slice. Existing focused `-Werror` build targets and
   `lc3_compat_check` are the local gate; full suites stay at the plan's
   scheduled checkpoint. No fixture or CTest is needed for these generated
   controls.
3. Before expanding producer-version support, obtain minimal native DXF
   witnesses authored by AutoCAD/compatible CAD: one page setup per render
   family, with PLOTSETTINGS shade mode 5 and the referenced dictionary entry.
   Record producer/version, ASCII DXF code order, handle/owner graph,
   native reopen result, and plotted output. A VIEWPORT-only example does not
   substitute for the standalone PlotSettings case.
4. Compare those witnesses with at least one independent open-source reader
   and writer in fast targeted runs (ACadSharp and LibreDWG are already
   identified; ezdxf is useful only for its documented DXF subset). Capture
   exact acceptance/loss, not just process exit status. Promote only the
   specific producer/version/family rows actually verified; leave all other
   rows fail-closed.

This cross-check does not invalidate the documented Autodesk API route; it
lowers the ceiling from “wire graph resolved” to “candidate graph documented,
wire/consumer behavior still to be witnessed.” It adds no support claim and
does not change totals (128 findings / 71 top-level subplans). J256, J260,
J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.24 application-data writer copy overlay (2026-10-17; focused local verification, uncommitted)

`writeAppData()` no longer materializes a complete `std::list<std::list<DRW_Variant>>`
to resolve optional ACAD_REACTORS/ACAD_XDICTIONARY references. It validates all
source groups first, then resolves references in the established traversal order
into a compact index/decision vector before emitting any application data.
Unchanged groups and values stream directly from the caller's const source;
zero-target values and groups are omitted by indexed decisions, and replacement
handles are formatted only when emitted. With no resolver, no intermediate
application-data collection is built, and ordinary handle remapping allocates a
replacement string only when the handle actually changes. This preserves the
existing “all resolver callbacks before output” behavior and avoids a second
callback pass.

Generated ASCII and Binary writer controls pass for both resolver and
no-resolver paths. They verify direct/table/application-group resolver results,
callback counts, zero-target omission, foreign-group handling, normal
`setHandleRemap` behavior, literal framing, caller-source immutability, malformed
opaque XDATA preservation, resolver exceptions, and retry behavior.

## Deeper/broader DXF section framing and legacy-table recovery review (2026-10-17)

This pass triangulated the DXF top-level framing change against Autodesk's
format references, independent open-source parser/writer code, peer issue
reports, and the local reader. It found one local false-success defect
(PAR-129), now corrected in the focused 7BT.1 slice. It did not turn a peer's
unverified compatibility report into normative format behavior.

| Evidence | What it establishes | Plan disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk, [general DXF structure](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D939EA11-0CEC-4636-91A8-756640A031D3.htm) and [symbol-table group codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A66D0ACA-3F43-4B2E-A0C2-2B490C1E5268.htm) | A section is framed by group-0 `SECTION`, group-2 section name, and group-0 `ENDSEC`; symbol tables are shown inside `TABLES`, with `TABLE`/entry records/`ENDTAB`. | Treat a top-level orphan `TABLE` as malformed by default. Do not infer that the peer's reported export is conforming. |
| ezdxf [table loader](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/sections/table.py) and [R12 stream writer](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/addons/r12writer.py) | The loader expects a table head within the `TABLES` model. Separately, its minimal R12 writer can emit an `ENTITIES`-only document when `fixed_tables` is false; not having a `TABLES` section is therefore distinct from putting `TABLE` records outside one. This is source review, not a runtime result. | Add the no-`TABLES` R12 positive control so the new fail-closed framing check does not over-require optional symbol tables. Keep it alongside standard-table and orphan-table controls. |
| ACadSharp [issue #1128](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1128) | An open feature request describes older NC/CAM/plotting files with bare tables after `HEADER` and proposes warning-backed recovery. The issue includes no producer file, version, checksum, or independent reproduction. | Compatibility lead only. Recovery remains a separate future opt-in decision requiring a provenance-bound sample; default parsing rejects the out-of-section record instead of silently losing it. |
| LibreDWG [issue #1355](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1355) and [issue #1351](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1351) | Peer reports illustrate a different but related DXF-integrity class: a converter may emit a truncated document despite a successful process status, or break an INSERT/ATTRIB/SEQEND sequence. The latter report uses ezdxf readback to distinguish parseability from record completeness. These are peer reports, not reproduced libdxfrw failures. | Preserve the existing output-closure and independent readback checkpoint. Do not add peer defects to libdxfrw's findings absent a local reproducer. A process exit code or self-round-trip alone is not a complete output oracle. |
| Local `dxfRW::processDxf()` and generated regression | Before 7BT.1, unexpected top-level records could be skipped and later ENTITIES delivered with success. The parser now returns `BAD_READ_SECTION`. Generated ASCII/Binary controls cover minimal R12 without `TABLES`, normal `TABLES` with a `LAYER`, an orphan `TABLE`, a detached section name, and unmatched `ENDSEC`; they assert entity/table callbacks or rejection before later entity delivery. | 7BT.1 implements the bounded correction; reuse its existing executable and CTest. No downloaded or persistent drawing fixture, new dependency, or new test registration. |

### Implementation-ready consequence

1. Keep the outer-stream state machine fail-closed for unexpected records and
   malformed `SECTION`/section-name/`ENDSEC` framing. Record-level tolerant
   parsing inside a valid section remains a separate policy.
2. Keep controls paired in both encodings: minimal R12 with no `TABLES`, a
   standard `TABLES`/`LAYER` section followed by an entity, and malformed
   orphan `TABLE`, detached section-name, and unmatched `ENDSEC` records,
   each followed by a sentinel entity. Every malformed case must report
   `BAD_READ_SECTION` and must not deliver the later entity.
3. If an actual consumer requires legacy table recovery, first acquire a
   producer/version-attributed sample with a digest and inspect the exact
   record boundaries. Implement only an explicit compatibility policy that
   warns, is bounded to the evidenced grammar, and proves subsequent section
   alignment. Never synthesize wrappers for arbitrary top-level records.
4. Keep validation fast: strict-build the existing fixture target, run its
   `--top-level-section-framing` selector, the owning DXF-fixtures CTest, and
   scoped whitespace checks. Leave broad suites and peer/native qualification
   at the already-defined integration checkpoint.

The parser API does not roll back HEADER/TABLE callbacks emitted before a
later error; whole-output atomicity remains a separate CLI transaction
contract. This pass did not run ezdxf, ACadSharp, LibreDWG, or a native CAD
application, and does not establish legacy-recovery compatibility or a new
DXF support claim. It changes no DWG behavior. The ledger is now 129 findings
and 72 top-level implementation subplans. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.26 single-field strict text encode (2026-10-17; focused local verification, uncommitted)

The strict single-value `dxfWriter::fromUtf8String()` path previously reused
the chunk API by allocating a `vector<string>`, then materializing and moving
one chunk back out. The internal writer now has shared strict-profile and
per-scalar validation/encoding helpers; the single-value path appends those
validated scalars directly to one result string. Chunked output calls the
same helpers, keeping UTF8 validation, NUL/CR-LF refusal, version/profile
admission, CIF/MIF literal-backslash quoting, and encoder round-trip loss
checks aligned.

`writeUtf8String`, `writeUtf8Caps`, and `fromUtf8String` now accept a const
string reference. `writeUtf8Caps` makes one uppercase output copy instead of
first copying its input parameter and then creating the uppercase string.
The generated target-text test additionally verifies that symbol
capitalization does not mutate caller-owned input. These signatures are in
`src/intern/dxfwriter.h`, not an installed public header; no class layout or
virtual contract changed.

Focused verification on the configured GCC build:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests lc3_compat_check -j2` — passed.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests --target-text-transport` — passed (40 wire cases, 40 chunk cases, invalid/profile/framing and caller-preservation controls).
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_gbk_codepage$' --output-on-failure` — passed (1/1, 0.56 s).
- Scoped `git diff --check` for the touched code/test/plan files — passed.

No full suite, peer runtime, native CAD run, fixture or CTest registration was
added. This removes one temporary chunk container and redundant lvalue copies
on these single-field semantic text paths; it is not a general allocation,
RSS, MTEXT chunking, binary-hex scratch, or text-projection optimization.
Other 7S writer/projection copy sites remain open. The existing local worktree
is broadly dirty and Git metadata is read-only, so this slice is uncommitted.
The ledger and support claims are unchanged; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.28 borrowed raw DXF string sink (2026-10-17; focused local verification, uncommitted)

The internal `dxfWriter::writeString()` virtual boundary now accepts a
`std::string_view` instead of copying each caller's `std::string` by value.
The ASCII and Binary writers synchronously validate, stream the borrowed bytes,
and update record inventory before returning; neither writer retains the view.
The associated raw-string validators, record-name/owner inventory helpers,
and name/handle parsing helpers consume views as well, and obsolete
`std::move` calls into the sink were removed. This is an internal source/vtable
signature change only: it is not an installed/public interface, does not alter
`DRW_Interface` or object layout, and all local targets must be rebuilt.

The generated target-text selector now supplies a subview into mutable source
storage to both ASCII and Binary sinks, mutates the source immediately after
the call, and checks that the exact captured value was already emitted. This
protects the synchronous-borrowing contract alongside the existing wire
framing and semantic round-trip controls.

- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests --target-text-transport` — passed (40 wire cases, 14 rejection/modern controls, 40 chunk cases, 4 framing cases, 2 compatible MTEXT cases, 2 borrowed-view cases, and existing profile/cap/raw controls).
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_writer_primitives_tests` — passed.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_writer_primitives$|^libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures$' --output-on-failure` — passed (2/2; 4.27 s).

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.27 compatible MTEXT scalar view (2026-10-17; focused local verification, uncommitted)

Compatible-mode `writeUtf8MTextChunks()` previously copied each scalar-sized
`string_view` substring into a temporary `std::string`, then immediately
passed it to the codec. The internal `dxfWriter::fromUtf8String()` boundary
now accepts `std::string_view`, which both strict and compatible conversion
already consume; the MTEXT loop passes its scalar view directly. The encoded
scalar result and destination chunks still allocate because they hold output.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.29 contiguous encoded chunk backing (2026-10-17; focused local verification, uncommitted)

Strict `writeUtf8Chunks()` and the strict/compatible branches of
`writeUtf8MTextChunks()` previously collected one owning `std::string` for each
group-code value. They now retain one encoded backing string and a compact
vector of `(offset, length)` ranges. Chunk boundaries still follow encoded
byte and Unicode-scalar counts, and the strict MTEXT short-final-group rule
still splits the final complete scalar from an exactly full final continuation
chunk. Each range is passed to the synchronous raw writer as a view. All
encoding, bounds, and range construction finish before the first output field,
so a later oversized or unrepresentable scalar still emits no earlier group.

Generated ASCII/Binary controls exercise strict chunking, strict and
compatible MTEXT, empty explicit group-1 values, 249-byte DBCS boundaries,
the exact 250/249/1 short-final partition, semantic readback, and four
late-oversized-scalar failures with no partial output. No persistent drawing
fixture was created.

Focused verification on the configured GCC build:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests libdxfrw_writer_primitives_tests libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests lc3_compat_check -j2` — passed.

- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_writer_primitives_tests` — passed.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_gbk_codepage$|^libdxfrw_writer_primitives$|^libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures$' --output-on-failure` — passed (3/3; 4.43 s).
- Scoped `git diff --check` — passed.

## Implementation progress — VisualStyle candidate group-code type/width guard (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

Strengthened the existing `libdxfrw_visualstyle_slot_manifest` checker rather
than adding another test target. For each of the 58 VisualStyle source fields,
the checker now resolves every non-null R2010 group, R2013b candidate group,
and observed/spec/generated-metadata companion group to the generic DXF value
type declared by Autodesk's group-code ranges: string, binary64, int16, int32,
or Boolean. It checks that the groups used by the candidate crosswalk stay
within those classified ranges. It also requires an R2010 group to be present
for every specified or explicitly unresolved slot, absent for the 30
not-applicable extension slots, and retains the existing rule that all 58
R2013b semantic mappings and serializer admissions remain unresolved.

The distinction is deliberate: a group-code range gives a wire value type,
not the meaning of that group in a particular VISUALSTYLE slot. Thus the
31/33 importer/spec mismatch, slot 45 missing importer value, group-176
companion semantics, CMC policy, group 177, and source/value-to-output mapping
remain unresolved. No VisualStyle output is enabled by this change.

## Implementation progress — compatible uppercase-ASCII DXF symbol sink pass-through (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

`dxfWriter::writeUtf8Caps()` is used for symbol-like names that commonly
arrive already uppercase. In the compatible profile, the old path always
materialized a copy for ASCII uppercasing and then another encoded string,
even when the source was plain uppercase ASCII. Such bytes pass unchanged
through the table, DBCS, and UTF-8 DXF converters; the new guarded path sends
the caller's view directly to the synchronous raw writer. It is restricted to
ASCII with no lowercase letters or backslash, compatible text policy, and a
non-UTF-16 converter. Strict-lossless validation/quoting, UTF-16 conversion,
and all other input retain the prior path.

Generated controls compare direct-sink and optimized output for ASCII and
Binary DXF at AC1018 and AC1021 using ANSI_932, and verify source immutability.
A UTF-16 control verifies the old conversion route remains selected. Existing
strict-profile/capitalization and escape-quoting cases run in the same focused
selector. These are byte-equivalence controls; no allocation counter or
throughput benchmark was run.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.30 compatible MTEXT ASCII scalar conversion bypass (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

created an encoded `std::string` and called the configured converter for
every source scalar, including ASCII. The table, DBCS, and UTF-8 DXF

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.31 DIMSTYLE parsed-text retained owners (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

The DIMSTYLE parser retained seven string destinations without charging their
live text to the read budget: `dimpost`, `dimapost`, `dimblk`, `dimblk1`,
`dimblk2`, `dimtxsty`, and `dimldrblk`. These now reserve replacement bytes
on the existing shared `DRW_TableEntry` lease before assignment. DXF code
pairs 5/342, 6/343, and 7/344 are aliases for the same arrow-block
destinations and share the same counters. A failed replacement leaves the
prior value and charge intact. The private seven-counter array changes public
`DRW_Dimstyle` layout, so downstream consumers must rebuild; binary ABI is
not claimed.

DIMSTYLE's handwritten copy/move lifecycle was updated with the retained
owners: copies share the lease and copy counters, reset releases them, and
move operations transfer the stored strings/counters instead of copying
strings inside `noexcept` operations. Generated ASCII/Binary direct-parser
controls cover the seven fields, alias replacements, exact transient cap,
one-byte-under replacement preservation, copy/assignment/move lifetime, and
final reset release. Generated full TABLES drawings verify callback
suppression with a ResourceLimit diagnostic, exact-cap retry on the same
facade, and a following DIMSTYLE sentinel.

## Deeper/broader LibreDWG build-profile and per-class evidence review (2026-10-17; research only)

This pass went below project-level coverage and writer headlines to inspect
LibreDWG's primary-source build gates and its own class-stability taxonomy.
The material result is not a new libdxfrw defect or a new peer route; it is a
missing axis in comparator qualification. Build configuration changes which
classes are available, and an opaque same-version roundtrip can preserve data
without semantically decoding it. No peer was built or run, no drawing was
downloaded, and no local test, fixture, production code, dependency, or CTest
registration changed.

| Primary-source evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [README build options](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg#building-and-installing-the-library) | `--enable-release` disables features absent from official tarball releases, explicitly including unstable DWG features and unknown versions/objects. `--enable-debug` enables debugging classes for testing. Therefore two binaries from the same source revision can have materially different class coverage. | Bind each selected comparator result to immutable source/release identity **and** configure/build flags. Keep release/package-profile behavior separate from debug-enabled exploratory behavior; debug-only coverage cannot qualify ordinary released support. |
| LibreDWG [class documentation](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi#L3022-L3039) | The project's states are `stable`, `unstable`, `debugging`, and `unhandled`. It says unstable classes may be emitted to DXF/JSON but not always DWG, and may lower to `UNKNOWN_*`, `PLACEHOLDER`, `DUMMY`, or `POINT`. Debugging classes require `--enable-debug`; unhandled classes are ignored. | Add an explicit per-class disposition to the existing version/operation matrix: typed decode; opaque preservation; placeholder/lowering; omitted; or refused. Do not collapse all of these to “supported” or “round-tripped.” |
| LibreDWG [class documentation](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi#L3033-L3039) | It says same-version persistence of unstable classes requires the full known `unknown_bits` blob. This is a preservation path, not evidence that the class's fields or semantics were decoded. | Grade same-version unknown-bit replay as opaque carrier preservation only. Semantic support still needs typed field checks, source/output type+handle+owner closure, and an independent expected-value witness. |
| LibreDWG [project README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) | Broad reader/coverage statements coexist with caveats about advanced R2010+ objects being skipped and converter-specific limitations. The README does not provide a class-by-class, build-profile-specific test denominator. | Keep the existing per-version × entity/object × direction ledger. Aggregate percentages and tool names remain context, not completion evidence. |
| ACadSharp [issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) and ezdxf [XREF loader documentation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst#L242-L250) | ACadSharp's report is specifically against NuGet 3.4.9 and says its DWG→DXF writer silently omitted `3DSOLID`/`REGION`; the maintainer said those DXF entities were unsupported and linked unmerged work. ezdxf's documented XREF helper supports a narrower copyable/transformable subset and says unsupported ACAD_TABLE/unknown entities are ignored without exceptions. The latter is the XREF helper, not ezdxf's base file parser; neither source establishes current-release behavior for all routes. | Keep the existing source-to-output identity/loss ledger and operation-specific artifact pins. Record which stage performed typed parsing, opaque retention, copying, conversion, or omission. A quiet return/no exception does not establish a complete transfer, but these peer reports do not create a local libdxfrw finding without a local reproducer. |

### Implementation-ready refinement

1. Reuse the current S8/PAR-07 peer intake and 7S.3/S3.7 composed
   qualification checkpoint; add no peer work to the implementation-slice
   loop.
2. For each compared class, record `(format version, class/type, operation,
   build profile)` separately. At minimum, the peer receipt records the source
   commit/release and artifact hash; configure/build flags; relevant optional
   dependencies; requested and actual target version; class status where the
   peer publishes one; and the observed typed/opaque/lowered/omitted/refused
   result.
3. Keep route outcomes separate: input parse, extracted fields, emitted record
   identity/owner/payload, independent readback, native consumer result, and
   semantic geometry. For unknown classes, record raw-blob equality only as
   opaque preservation; never infer field semantics from a same-version replay.
4. Use the normal release/package profile for any released-capability row.
   A debug profile may be useful for diagnosis but receives its own row and
   cannot silently backfill release support. This is evidence bookkeeping at
   the already-composed checkpoint, not a new runtime prerequisite.
5. Continue focused generated local controls, owning CTest, and scoped
   `git diff --check` per implementation slice. Keep full-suite and bounded
   route-specific fuzz/sanitizer work at the planned checkpoint. Use
   in-memory or scratch-generated tests and do not commit external DWG/DXF
   fixtures.
6. When a peer's documented helper or a historical issue is used as a lead,
   scope it to the exact release, operation, and helper. Do not transfer an
   XREF-import limitation to a base parser, an older writer omission to a
   current release, or a debug-only class result to a package profile.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.32 DXF ACIS carrier retained-byte ownership (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

The resource review found that DXF ACIS carrier copies were bounded by a per-field/overall size ceiling but were not charged to the shared retained-byte budget. This slice makes the logical retained cost explicit before append, while reusing the existing `DRW_Entity` lease and adding no field to the public class layout.

| Carrier destination | Charged input/output ownership |
| --- | --- |
| `DRW_Surface::rawAcisData` | DXF groups 1/3 text bytes and decoded group 310 bytes |
| `DRW_ModelerGeometry::m_rawBytes` | DXF groups 1/3 text bytes, inserted inter-group separator newline, decoded group 310 bytes, and final text terminator newline |

Generated direct-parser controls verify exact lease values and rollback on an over-budget group. Generated complete-read ASCII and Binary files exercise both carriers, ordering/chunk offsets, exact minimum quota, one-byte-under callback suppression, `ResourceLimit/dxf-retained-byte-budget`, and successful same-facade retry. The test data is generated in memory/from scratch; no DWG/DXF fixture was added.

Validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_hardening_tests lc3_compat_check -j2`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --dxf-acis-carrier-retained-budget`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_hardening$' --output-on-failure` (1/1)
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_public_header_hygiene$' --output-on-failure` (1/1; corrects the stale 7BB status note above)

This is accounting for library-retained DXF bytes only. It does not parse/validate SAT or SAB semantics, establish DWG AcDs ownership, measure vector capacity/RSS, bound other raw carriers, or account for caller-owned copies made after callback. The broader worktree is already dirty; the slice and plan edits remain uncommitted. No full suite or sanitizer run was needed for this bounded change.

This is an explicit carrier/projection option, not an editable B-rep. | Use GDAL only as a raw-carrier/transform comparator with the option and target version bound. Compare exact binary payload/transform separately from typed geometry. |

The maintainer explains that stock FreeCAD cannot read ACIS blobs and closes native ACIS import as not planned. This is current product evidence, not a claim that no plugin or third-party extension exists. | Preserve FreeCAD as a 2D consumer-compatibility sentinel and converter-chain qualification target. Do not make FreeCAD native import the 3D ACIS pass criterion; for any external path, bind converter, output DXF identity, importer/backend, and resulting operation independently. |
| LibreDWG [README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) and [coverage documentation](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | LibreDWG advertises broad DWG reading but notes advanced R2010+ objects may be skipped; current docs distinguish handled, unhandled, unstable, and untested classes, and warn that later-version DWG writing has limits. A DWG→DXF conversion or object census is therefore a version/build-profile-specific comparison, not a complete semantic oracle. | At peer checkpoints record exact release/commit, build flags, source/target versions, per-entity typed/opaque/lowered/omitted/refused disposition, and warnings. No peer version or mutable master is a support vote. |

### Implementation-ready refinement

Keep the fast local sequence and validation cadence unchanged. Use two independent, explicit lanes:

1. **Explicit geometry lane:** verify existing 2D entities and explicit 3D point/line/face/mesh entities as typed geometry. Preserve LibreCAD and FreeCAD's 2D paths. For 3D explicit entities, test coordinate systems, extrusion/OCS, units, block transforms, topology/counts, and version gates separately from ACIS.
2. **Opaque modeler-carrier lane:** transport SAT/SAB/ASM bytes and their owner/history/transform associations without claiming that the library interprets the body. Start with generated ASCII and Binary DXF vectors for SAT group 1/3 continuations, binary group 310 chunks, empty/malformed payloads, multiple modeler records, block-only solids, and unsorted owner handles. Assert each source carrier is either reproduced byte-for-byte in a compatible same-version route or rejected/reported as a precisely identified loss before output.
3. **Versioned output lane:** build a small target-version matrix around AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027 and AC1032. Check the DXF subclass/field floor and SAT-versus-SAB/AcDs storage against the authoritative ODA spec and locally traceable vectors; peer PR #1150's `AcDb3dSolid` threshold and AcDs writer layout are hypotheses only. For version conversion, recode only a proven representation; otherwise fail closed or emit a loss diagnostic rather than silently writing an empty entity/block.
4. **Round-trip census/loss lane:** on generated controls, compare entity handle/type/block owner and carrier hashes before and after read→write→read for both ASCII and Binary DXF, including a block containing only 3DSOLID/REGION. Count output records and section data, not only callbacks. Add negative controls proving unsupported or invalid data is reported and does not create false success.
5. **Semantic and application lane:** keep ACIS syntax/graph extraction, topology closure, analytic B-rep checks, and native CAD behavior behind their existing separate gates. ezdxf, GDAL and FreeCAD results are admissible only for their documented lane; semantic acceptance needs a pinned independent reader/kernel with known analytic controls. Do not infer DWG AcDs association from a DXF carrier test.
6. **Fast validation policy:** each implementation slice runs only its strict touched targets, focused generated selector, `lc3_compat_check`, and owning CTest. No external fixture or dependency is needed. Reserve composed peer/native checks and full suites for the existing checkpoint, and keep J256/J260/J268/J284/J293/J295 `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` until their platform or independent semantic evidence exists.

This pass adds no confirmed local defect, finding, top-level subplan, fixture, dependency, test registration, peer execution, or support promotion. It refines existing writer-loss, carrier, consumer, and semantic evidence gates only. Totals remain 129 findings / 72 top-level subplans; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.41 DXF binary chunk stack buffer (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The common vector-backed `writeDxfBinaryChunks()` helper previously created a
new `std::string` for every 127-byte group-310 chunk, reserved up to 254
characters, and hex-encoded into it. The writer consumes `std::string_view`
synchronously, so the helper now encodes into one fixed 254-character stack

### Implementation-ready use and stop rule

1. **No queue change.** These candidates do not reveal a local defect and add

   screen adds no test, dependency, fixture, or CTest registration.

   temporary locally generated ASCII case with known sections, ordered tags,

   invocation, and route limits are recorded. If those are unresolved, record
   `VERSION_UNRESOLVED / NOT_RUN` and continue local implementation.
