## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.46 SAT text stack-buffer emission (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

`writeDxfSatTextValue()` previously allocated a `std::string` for each
group-code chunk. It now encodes into a fixed 255-byte stack buffer and passes
a `std::string_view` to the synchronous DXF writer. Caret escaping remains
atomic across chunk boundaries; SAT-v1 byte transformation and input
validation remain in the same per-byte path. A write failure still stops
emission immediately.

The existing hardening selector `--dxf-modeler-text-chunk-borrow` validates
ASCII and Binary DXF output for ordinary AC1024 modeler text, a caret escape
that exactly fills the 255-character group, a caret pair that must move intact
to the next group, and AC1015 SAT-v1 text whose transform creates caret pairs
with 254/2-character framing. It also checks decoded payload retention and a
following-record sentinel. No persistent DWG/DXF fixture or new CTest
registration was added.

Focused verification passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_hardening_tests lc3_compat_check -j2`

- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_hardening$' --output-on-failure`

## Implementation progress — 7AA.2 partial DXF MLEADER arrowhead-index preservation (2026-10-17)

`DRW_MLeader::ArrowHeadEntry` previously used only `isDefault` for both the
DWG legacy bit and DXF group 94. The local change adds `dxfIndex` plus
`hasDxfIndex`; DXF `parseCode` now records the signed 32-bit group-94 value
without changing `isDefault`. The AC1021 writer emits the exact stored group-94
index and the remapped group-345 handle in the original array order. Because a
DWG default bit does not establish a DXF index and this legacy array has no
modeled AC1027 representation, the writer fails closed before entity output
for entries without an explicit DXF index and for targets newer than AC1021.
DWG parse/encode byte paths were not changed.

The existing hardening selector now covers ASCII and Binary DXF with distinct
arrowhead handles and ordered indices 7/0/2, exact group-code order, parsed
values and handle identity, copy/reset, missing-index refusal, and modern-target
refusal. Existing MLEADER writer-remap validation also still supplies the
failure-before-publication reference control. No persistent fixture or CTest
registration was added.

Focused verification:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_hardening_tests libdxfrw_wave1_tests lc3_compat_check -j2` — passed.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --mleader-context-roundtrip` — passed.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_wave1_tests --mleader-writer-validation` — passed.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_hardening$' --output-on-failure` — passed (1/1).
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^(libdxfrw_wave1|libdxfrw_mleader_writer_version)$' --output-on-failure` — MLEADER writer CTest passed; `libdxfrw_wave1` failed with eight assertions in `testGeneratedDictionaryGroupCommonMetadata`. That test path was not edited in this slice; its current-checkout failure remains unresolved and is not reported as caused by this change.
- Scoped `git diff --check` passed for the touched source/test files and plan.

This is a partial 7AA.2 implementation, not a DWG↔DXF arrowhead semantic mapping or general MLEADER support claim. Adding fields changes the public nested struct layout; downstream consumers must rebuild and binary ABI compatibility is not claimed. The DWG default-flag relationship, producer-side index evidence, unknown/invalid index policy, and modern-version representation remain open. Findings/subplans remain 129/72; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The broad shared worktree remains uncommitted.

## Implementation progress — 7AA.1 partial DIMASSOC DXF group-70/71 mapping (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Autodesk's [DIMASSOC DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-C0B96256-A911-4B4D-85E6-EB4AF2C91E27.htm) assigns group 70 to the trans-space Boolean and group 71 to rotated-dimension type (parallel/perpendicular). No external DWG/DXF fixture or new CTest registration was added.

## Implementation progress — 7AA.1 DIMASSOC DXF reference remapping (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The prior group-70/71 correction left the DIMASSOC writer's object identity,
owner, dimension link, and ordered osnap links outside the DXF handle-remap /
reference-resolution pipeline. The writer now remaps its own nonzero handle and
owner, and resolves nonzero dimension/osnap references through the configured
reference resolver when installed (the resolver's result is final); otherwise
it applies the source-handle remap. All required links are resolved before a
record is staged, and a nonzero source link resolving to zero fails without
publishing DIMASSOC bytes. A record transaction also keeps later serialization
failures from leaking a partial object to the output stream.

Generated coverage exercises ASCII and Binary DXF, own/owner remapping,
resolver precedence over conflicting remaps (without remapping the resolver's
result a second time), remap-only fallback, ordered code-331 references, the
following-record sentinel, and failure-before-publication when a required
reference resolves to zero. No external fixture, persistent test drawing, or
CTest registration was added.

## Implementation progress — 7AA.1 DIMASSOC DXF emitted-graph closure (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Graph-managed DIMASSOC writes now fail closed unless each nonzero dimension or
osnap reference resolves to exactly one source entity that was actually
written. A planned source-to-output binding does not count as emission. Without
a configured reference resolver, the referenced source must be present,
non-ambiguous, marked written, and its normal remap must agree with the bound
output identity. With a resolver, its result remains the final identity and is
accepted only if it uniquely names an emitted entity; this permits a deliberate
redirect while rejecting zero, missing, duplicate, or object-only identities.
Validation happens before opening the DIMASSOC record transaction, so refusal
does not append bytes. Existing direct low-level writes with an empty entity
map intentionally retain their earlier behavior.

Generated controls cover ASCII and Binary DXF for valid dimension/geometry
links, an unemitted dimension, an unemitted osnap target, a preallocated-but-
unwritten target, a resolver redirect to an emitted entity, and a resolver
result outside the emitted graph. Every negative case checks output-prefix
preservation; successful readback checks final handle identities. No DWG bytes
or persistent drawing fixtures changed.

Focused verification:

intersection handle 332 still require role-aware relocation and remain under
the existing raw-preservation / typed-refusal path; intersection groups 74/92
and their required relationships are not yet implemented. No DWG parser or
byte layout changed.

| [`uncad`](https://github.com/iyulab/uncad) | The project README now explicitly says the package is read-only and does not convert DWG↔DXF. Its DWG reader calls LibreDWG through FFI; the vendored LibreDWG copy carries documented local patches. DXF takes a different route: ASCII and binary files (including R2007+) are read by `undxf`, a pure-Rust MIT parser, not LibreDWG's DXF importer. Its own caveats report 66/67 DXFs from the LibreDWG test corpus parsed, all 32 R2007+ examples parsed, and 28 DWG/DXF twins with matching normalized entity/table/block observations except for named format or source-data differences. These are project-reported self-corpus counts, not independent correctness evidence. | Split into `DWG_READER=LIBREDWG_LINEAGE` and a **candidate independent DXF reader=`UNDXF`**. It may be considered only at the existing optional composed checkpoint after exact source/lockfile pinning, license and dependency review, and a field-level audit. The DWG route adds no independent decoder; the shared normalized model and twin comparison are not an independent expected manifest. The full workspace is GPL-3.0-or-later even though the parser dependency is described as MIT; do not add the workspace as a production or test dependency for a comparator. |
| `uncad` 3D projection | Its caveats say 3DSOLID and REGION render as isometric wireframes, explicitly not B-rep reads; a body whose ACIS conversion fails is reported unsupported. Eight listed families, including MLEADER, MLINE, REGION, POLYLINE_PFACE, TOLERANCE, ACAD_TABLE, WIPEOUT, and LIGHT, are marked experimental and not exercised by real drawings. The caveats also say the DWG TABLE route is unknown because the vendored LibreDWG path only decodes that class in a debugging build, while DXF table content has a separate route. | Do not use the renderer, outline, skipped-edge count, or experimental tags as ACIS/AcDs, B-rep, TABLE, or general 3D semantic evidence. Preserve per-format and per-operation applicability. For a potential DXF parser run, capture unknown entities, diagnostics, and omissions; do not accept “unsupported” or absent as empty. |
| [`acad-ts`](https://github.com/node-projects/acad-ts) | Its README describes a TypeScript port of ACadSharp and names its base commit `3010994939c1bc21df0c9e2931e9baee4564815a`; it separately records the last compared upstream ACadSharp commit `3feabba4b2cbcb226f10b288aaee32442b03af6f`. Its reader guide says `failsafe` defaults true and `keepUnknownEntities` / `keepUnknownNonGraphicalObjects` default false. | Treat as the **same codec lineage as ACadSharp**, not a second DWG/DXF vote. At most it is a package/deployment compatibility route at a composed checkpoint. If exercised, pin both acad-ts package/source and the declared upstream base, turn failsafe off for strict assertions, retain unknown entities/objects, and capture notifications; otherwise recovery or default omission could make a successful read look like parity. |
| [`sch5182/dwg-reader`](https://github.com/sch5182/dwg-reader) | The public README says DXF is parsed directly but DWG requires an installed ODA File Converter or LibreDWG `dwg2dxf`; its downstream extraction/preview uses ezdxf/matplotlib. | Classify as an orchestration/converter pipeline, not a DWG parser. It adds no independent DWG vote and no kernel/B-rep evidence. Its DXF operation can be attributed only to the exact converter plus ezdxf stages actually selected. |

### Implementation-ready, speed-preserving comparator recipe

Do not add these routes to the per-slice loop. If a future scheduled/composed
checkpoint already needs an independent DXF parser, use `undxf` only after the
following one-time readiness checks:

1. Pin the `uncad` repository commit and lockfile, the resolved `undxf` package
   version/source and checksum, Rust toolchain, and build features. Record the
   route explicitly as `DXF_READER=UNDXF`; do not use `uncad`'s DWG path as a
   second peer because it is LibreDWG-backed. Audit the exact `undxf` source and
   dependency licenses before choosing a runnable artifact.
2. Use a tiny locally generated ASCII/Binary DXF control set with independently
   authored expected values. Start with common 2D records, a block/INSERT
   placement, a reference-resolution negative, an unknown-record/diagnostic
   control, and (only if needed) raw SAT/SAB carrier equality. Do not borrow or
   commit the peer's corpus drawings. Parse each operation directly through
   `undxf`; do not infer parser independence from `uncad`'s common model,
   `uncad diff`, or DWG/DXF twin results.
3. Compare exact source/output handles, entity kinds, owner/space/block path,
   layer/table resolution, coordinates, units, and relevant raw carrier bytes
   against the predeclared manifest. Record diagnostics and unknown/skipped
   counts. For every reported 3D carrier, assert only the carrier/structure
   question under test; no wireframe/render result promotes B-rep or native
   consumer support.
4. Keep `acad-ts` in the ACadSharp lineage bucket and converter wrappers as
   composed pipelines. Do not count distinct language, frontend, CLI, rendering
   output, or same-library roundtrip as an independent implementation.
5. No mandatory integration, dependency, test registration, routine peer
   execution, or queue change is warranted now. Revisit only when the existing
   composed comparator checkpoint is reached or a concrete local discrepancy
   identifies a row this route can test. This does not change the native
   Linux/Windows FreeCAD gate or independent ACIS/AcDs semantic requirements.

### Conclusion

This review identifies a narrow additional *candidate DXF parsing operation*
(`undxf`) while clarifying that `uncad`'s DWG route is LibreDWG-derived,
`acad-ts` is ACadSharp-derived, and converter wrappers are not parser peers. It
does not identify a new local defect, qualify any peer, or close a 3D evidence
gap. Findings/subplans remain 129/72; implementation order and fast per-slice
validation frequency are unchanged; no peer/native run, fixture, dependency,
support claim, or test was added. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

## Implementation progress — 7AA.1 DIMASSOC intersection-object DXF edge (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Following Autodesk's [DIMASSOC group table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-C0B96256-A911-4B4D-85E6-EB4AF2C91E27.htm), the typed DXF subset now admits intersection osnap types 6 and 11 only when nonzero group-331 main and group-332 intersection-object handles are present. It preserves optional group-74 intersection subentity type and group-92 GS marker, validates the group-74 short-width value, detects duplicate/orphan fields, and writes them in documented order before group 75. Non-intersection osnap types cannot carry these intersection-only fields.

Group 332 is resolved/remapped through the same reference path as group 331 and is subject to the same emitted-entity graph closure. A missing, zero, unmapped, ambiguous, or unemitted intersection entity fails before the DIMASSOC record is published. The DWG encoder explicitly refuses these DXF-only fields; no DWG byte layout or parser behavior was inferred. XREF string handles 301/302 remain on raw-preservation / typed-write-refusal path pending an explicit relocation contract.

Generated ASCII/Binary controls cover parsing and round-trip for an intersection record containing both geometry edges, groups 74/92, copy/assignment, DWG-encoder refusal before bytes, incomplete type-6 refusal without output, apparent-intersection type 11, missing-main-edge refusal, and graph-managed acceptance/rejection for emitted/unemitted group-332 targets. Existing XREF/unknown/orphan loss guards remain in place. No persistent sample or external DWG/DXF fixture was created.

Focused verification:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_hardening_tests libdxfrw_wave1_tests lc3_compat_check dwg2dxf -j2` — passed with strict warnings.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --dimassoc-documented-scalar-fields` — passed (includes intersection fields).
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --dimassoc-unsupported-detail` — passed.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_wave1_tests --dimassoc-graph-closure` — passed.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_wave1_tests --integer-valued-boolean-wire-kinds` — passed.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_hardening$' --output-on-failure` — passed (1/1).
- No full Wave1 CTest or peer/native run was performed; no test registration, dependency, or fixture was added.

This completes only one more portion of partial DXF DIMASSOC round-trip and graph closure. It does not model XREF handles, guarantee live associative updates, prove complete DIMASSOC semantics, or add DWG body support. Public osnap-reference layout changed, so downstream consumers must rebuild; ABI compatibility is not claimed. Findings/subplans remain 129/72, no support claim is promoted, and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The shared worktree remains broadly dirty and this slice is uncommitted.

## Implementation progress — 7AA.1 DIMASSOC XREF handle-string DXF preservation (2026-10-17; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Autodesk's [DIMASSOC DXF table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-C0B96256-A911-4B4D-85E6-EB4AF2C91E27.htm) identifies groups 301/302 as XREF-object handle strings; the [ObjectARX `setXrefHandles` contract](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OREF-AcDbOsnapPointRef__setXrefHandles_AcDbHandleArrayPtRef_.html) describes the XREF handle array associated with an osnap reference. This slice preserves the two DXF values as opaque strings. It deliberately does not infer their serialized grammar or reinterpret them as handles in the host drawing.

`DRW_DimensionAssociationOsnapRef` retains presence and text for group 301 and group 302. The DXF parser detects duplicate and orphan XREF fields as unrepresentable detail; the DXF writer emits each present string at its source-defined location without feeding it into local handle resolution, remapping, or emitted-entity graph closure. The DWG encoder rejects either field (including manually populated nonempty values) before writing bytes, because this DXF string representation does not establish a DWG field layout.

Generated in-memory ASCII/Binary controls cover exact parsing and writing, copy/assignment, exact preservation while local group-331/group-332 handles are remapped, duplicate/orphan refusal, and DWG-encoder refusal before output. No external DWG/DXF drawing was downloaded or added as a fixture.

Focused verification, as run for this slice:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_hardening_tests libdxfrw_wave1_tests lc3_compat_check dwg2dxf -j2` — passed with strict warnings.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --dimassoc-documented-scalar-fields` — passed.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --dimassoc-unsupported-detail` — passed.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_wave1_tests --dimassoc-graph-closure` — passed.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_hardening$' --output-on-failure` — passed (1/1).
- No full suite, peer runtime, or native CAD run was performed; no CTest registration, dependency, or persistent fixture was added.

This is opaque DXF text preservation only. It does not validate cross-database handle resolution, XREF availability, live associativity, or complete DIMASSOC behavior. Public osnap-ref layout changed, so downstream consumers must rebuild; ABI compatibility is not claimed. No DWG parser/writer bytes changed and no support claim is promoted. Findings/subplans remain 129/72; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

It requires Rust 1.88+. These are release claims, not a locally executed result or a complete parser audit. | Upgrade CADMPEG from a generic cross-read lead to a **conditional, exact-profile inner-stream parser candidate**. Before use, pin the 0.6.1 crate archive and dependency lock/source, audit the source for overlap with `acis-core`/`cq-acis`, record `SatCodec::inspect` stream kind/version/reference width, and require a zero/unexplained-loss-free result for the tested body. Do not use this crate as a DWG/DXF reader, AcDs container reader, writer, or native application. |
| CADMPEG versus `acis-core`/`cq-acis` | Existing project review establishes that `acis-core` is in the `cq-acis` ecosystem and can author limited scratch SAB profiles; CADMPEG is a separate Apache-2.0 workspace with separate `cadmpeg-asm`/`cadmpeg-ir` crates. The package dependency list alone does not prove source independence or wire-profile compatibility, and the shared project documentation/grammar lineage remains a potential correlation. | Require a narrow source/dependency overlap review and an exact producer-profile match before calling the cross-read independent. If source overlap, parser provenance, or profile cannot be resolved quickly, record `NOT_QUALIFIED / NOT_RUN` and continue; do not hold the local implementation queue. |
| [GDAL DXF driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) and [known issues](https://github.com/OSGeo/gdal/blob/master/ogr/ogrsf_frmts/dxf/KNOWN_ISSUES.md) | Current docs say Binary DXF input is available starting with GDAL 3.12. `EntityHandle` is exposed; `RawCodeValues` is off by default and contains only codes not already handled. `DXF_INLINE_BLOCKS=FALSE` separates block entities and exposes block name, scale, angle, OCS normal/coordinates, and attributes rather than expanding block geometry; block geometry merge is independently configurable. `DXF_3D_EXTENSIBLE_MODE=TRUE` exposes raw ASM bytes and a 12-value transform for AC1027+ 3D entities, but GDAL explicitly cannot translate them to OGR solid geometry and skips them by default. The driver projects many entities (e.g. curves to tessellated lines, dimensions to anonymous-block/fallback geometry) and documents unsupported entity/style/OCS cases. Its DXF writer targets AC2004. | Refine the existing optional GDAL comparison, not its support grade: pin GDAL release/build and open options; use direct reader output, not DXF→OGR→DXF as a round-trip oracle. For a block comparison, disable inline/merge and compare handle, source block path, insertion point, scale, rotation, OCS basis, attributes, and child identities. For raw 3D carrier checks, use AC1027+ only, capture `ASMData` and `ASMTransform` separately, and label this `DXF_CARRIER_ONLY`; an opaque byte match never establishes ACIS semantics, B-rep closure, or DWG AcDs association. Binary comparisons are inadmissible below GDAL 3.12. |
| GDAL [CAD](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/cad.html) versus [DWG](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dwg.html) | The `CAD` driver is built on libopencad and documents a read-only projected subset. The separate `DWG` driver requires Open Design Alliance Teigha. Thus the generic statement “GDAL DWG read” can refer to different parser/license routes; neither OGR projection route exposes complete DWG object graphs or solid semantics. | When recording any GDAL DWG observation, bind the exact driver name, build configuration, linked backend/library revision, version, and options. Count `CAD` only in the existing libopencad lineage; treat `DWG`/ODA as a separately licensed external route, not an open-source peer. Do not infer either route from an installed `ogrinfo` binary's product name alone. |

### Conditional implementation-ready comparator recipe

1. **No new routine work:** keep local strict build, focused selector, and the
   owning CTest as the per-slice loop. Do not add GDAL/CADMPEG to CMake, CI,
   dependencies, committed fixtures, or every-slice validation. Run this only
   at the existing composed evidence checkpoint when an exact DXF carrier or
   ACIS inner-payload question is ready.
2. **Qualify the parser artifact first:** for CADMPEG, pin crate 0.6.1 checksum,
   repository commit/source package, Cargo.lock, Rust toolchain/features, and
   the exact tested input profile. Compare packaged source with repository
   source and check for shared parser implementation, not just package names.
   Capture `inspect` output, decode losses, unknown-record spans, supported
   solved-record count, and body disposition.
3. **Use only scratch-authored controls:** generate a minimal known analytic
   body from scratch or use a generator profile already independently
   understood. Before decoding, check that its exact ASM/ACIS save profile and
   framing are admitted by the pinned CADMPEG release. Keep all generated
   SAT/SAB/DXF/DWG files outside the repository. Independently calculate
   expected units, placement, bounds, topology counts, and available analytic
   measures; a producer's self-read is not the oracle.
4. **Keep the carrier bridge explicit:** hash the DXF carrier extracted by
   libdxfrw and pass those exact bare bytes to CADMPEG only if the format is
   admitted. Record source entity handle → local owner/index → carrier hash →
   decoded body identity. This can independently challenge the inner stream;
   outer DWG AcDs section layout and entity-to-AcDs ownership remain local-only
   unless a separate external route exposes and verifies them.
5. **Use GDAL as a scoped structural/projection witness:** pin GDAL >=3.12 for
   any Binary-DXF comparison. For the direct read, explicitly enable
   `DXF_INCLUDE_RAW_CODE_VALUES`; disable `DXF_INLINE_BLOCKS` and block-geometry
   merge when graph/placement is under test; enable `DXF_3D_EXTENSIBLE_MODE`
   only for AC1027+ carrier controls. Record raw-carrier, projected-geometry,
   skipped/unknown, and owner/placement results separately. Do not expect
   `RawCodeValues` to duplicate handled tags or use OGR's tessellation as exact
   curve/B-rep truth.
6. **Stop at evidence boundaries:** successful CADMPEG decode or GDAL feature
   enumeration does not itself clear J256/J260/J268/J284/J293/J295. Promotion
   still requires the independently specified per-item semantic/platform
   evidence, full source-to-output graph disposition, and (where required)
   native Linux/Windows consumer qualification. A missing optional runtime is
   `NOT_AVAILABLE`, not a reason to pause local work.

### Conclusion

This review adds a potentially useful independent *bare ACIS stream parser*
and makes the existing GDAL DXF/DWG routes reproducible by mode, version, and
options. Neither route establishes complete document/container support or
closes an external semantic/platform gate. No new local finding or
implementation subplan is warranted; queue order, fast/full test cadence, and
the 129-finding / 72-subplan ledger remain unchanged. J256, J260, J268, J284,
J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and cannot be promoted by these
research-only observations.

This follow-up resolves the lineage and version ambiguity left by the broader
GDAL route inventory. It checked the original libopencad repository's
successor pointer, the successor's current README and public version enum,
and GDAL's current CAD driver documentation. The goal was to decide whether
the existing optional GDAL route can serve as a useful, sharply scoped DWG
comparison without overstating modern-file or semantic coverage. No peer was
cloned, installed, built, or run; no drawing, local test, or CAD application
was used; no production code, dependency, fixture, or test registration was
changed.

| Route/source | Finding and evidence ceiling | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Original [`sandyre/libopencad`](https://github.com/sandyre/libopencad) and successor [`nextgis-borsch/lib_opencad`](https://github.com/nextgis-borsch/lib_opencad) | The original repository identifies itself as abandoned and points to the successor. The successor's README says “Now supported only the DWG R2000 format.” Its public `CADVersions` enum lists AC1012 through AC1027 constants, but an enum is not implementation or test evidence; the repo README's stated runtime scope is the narrower ceiling. The old repository's R15/basic-geometry table must not be carried forward as current successor coverage. | Treat `lib_opencad` as a **conditional AC1015/ R2000 native-reader candidate only**. Before using it, pin the successor's exact commit/source and inspect the actual dispatch/read implementation; do not infer AC1012/14 or AC1018–27 support from constants, legacy docs, or a package name. If the exact source route cannot be established promptly, mark it `VERSION_UNRESOLVED / NOT_RUN`. |
| GDAL [`CAD` driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/cad.html) | The driver documentation identifies an internal libopencad dependency, marks the driver read-only, and documents a projected element subset: POINT, LINE, CIRCLE, ARC, and 3DFACE. LINE/rounded-polyline conversion may tessellate curved geometry. OGR features are a projection and do not expose the original DWG object/owner graph, full record payloads, or solid-kernel semantics. | If the already-planned optional checkpoint needs this route, use only scratch-authored **AC1015 2D** controls for the documented subset; compare geometry/count/layer and source identity only where the route exposes it. Record tessellation/projection and unsupported disposition explicitly. Do not make it a modern DWG comparator, full-graph oracle, or ACIS/AcDs semantic witness. |
| GDAL [`DWG` driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dwg.html) versus `CAD` | GDAL documents a separate DWG driver that depends on ODA Teigha; this is not the internal-libopencad `CAD` driver. A machine with GDAL installed can therefore expose materially different parser and license routes behind a generic “DWG” label. | Capture the exact GDAL driver short name, build configuration, linked backend and versions, open options, and input AC code. Count `CAD` only in the libopencad lineage. Treat `DWG`/ODA as a separately licensed external observation, never as an open-source peer. |

### Optional comparator recipe and stop rule

1. Keep the comparator at the existing composed checkpoint; do not add a peer
   build/run to the implementation-slice loop, CI, dependency set, or routine
   validation schedule.
2. Resolve the backend before generating an expected comparison: capture the
   GDAL release/build, selected driver, libopencad source revision and build
   options. Check the actual reader dispatch at that pinned source. A version
   enum, GDAL driver presence, or successful file open does not establish
   per-version/entity coverage.
3. If qualified, author a small AC1015 control locally from scratch with only
   documented 2D elements and known layers/coordinates. Use exact semantic
   geometry for LINE/CIRCLE/ARC/POINT; compare rounded polylines only under a
   separate tolerance/tessellation contract. Keep 3DFACE as planar face
   projection, not a B-rep or solid test. No external DWG/DXF fixture enters
   the repository.
4. Report parser status, projected feature inventory, layer/type/coordinates,
   approximation/tessellation, unsupported/unknown counts, and diagnostics as
   separate fields. Do not treat omitted OGR attributes as empty source data.
5. If source provenance, parser independence, or route coverage is unclear,
   record `NOT_QUALIFIED / NOT_RUN` and continue. This optional route cannot
   unblock J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, or J295.

### Conclusion

This research narrows an already-known GDAL/libopencad candidate rather than
adding a new required comparator. The useful possible cross-read is limited to
an audited AC1015 2D projection subset; no evidence here extends modern DWG,
object graph, write, ACIS/AcDs, or native-consumer claims. No new defect,

## Deeper/broader low-cost DXF tag-stream differential and audit cadence review (2026-10-17; research only)

This pass compared current ezdxf reader, tag-export, audit, and recovery
documentation with the plan's existing generated-wire tests and optional
composed peer checkpoint. The goal was to identify a faster way to diagnose a
DXF tag disagreement without making an external parser or a repair pass part of
every implementation slice. Sources reviewed: ezdxf's [document management
and JSON-tag API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/management.html),
[document audit API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/drawing.html),
and [DXF loading guidance](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/usage_for_beginners.html).
No package was installed or run; no external drawing, fixture, local test,
production code, dependency, or CTest registration was added or changed.

| Route/source | Finding and evidence ceiling | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ezdxf [`export_json_tags`](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/management.html) | The documented verbose mode (`compact=False`) exports a list of `[group-code, value]` pairs as a one-to-one representation of DXF tags, with values represented as strings. It preserves the decoded tag sequence for inspection, not the original ASCII spelling, binary group-code/value widths, record bytes, or exact file framing. | At the already-planned composed DXF peer checkpoint, pin one ezdxf artifact and use strict read + verbose tag export only when a generated case has a specific ordered-tag/value disagreement. Compare normalized ordered pairs against an independently authored expected manifest. Keep byte-level group-code/type-width, payload, and following-record sentinel assertions in local generated tests; JSON tag agreement cannot replace them. Do not add ezdxf to CMake, CI, or routine per-slice validation. |
| ezdxf [`Drawing.audit()` / `validate()`](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/drawing.html) and [strict/recovery loading guidance](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/usage_for_beginners.html) | The API says audit repairs fixable problems and records unfixable ones; `validate()` reports resolved and unrecoverable errors. Documentation characterizes audit as a potentially long-running task. Ordinary read and recovery are separate loading paths; recovery is recommended for flawed input rather than a substitute for strict read. A recovered/auto-repaired model is therefore not an unchanged writer round-trip. | Keep strict parse, recovery success, audit repairs/errors, saved output, and independent reopen as separate outcomes. Run audit only at the composed checkpoint when the output needs structural diagnosis, not for each local feature slice. Record repair counts and changed identities/fields; a clean audit still does not establish semantic completeness. |
| Existing local generated DXF controls | The current suite already checks selected ASCII/Binary group sequences, type widths, raw carrier bytes, handle closure, no-output refusal, and following-record sentinels in fast, generated tests. These directly exercise the changed code path and avoid a peer-runtime dependency. | Preserve the current fast validation order: strict touched target, focused selector, compatibility target when applicable, and owning CTest. Add no extra recurring work. Use the external tag-stream view only to triage an unresolved disagreement at a composed gate, then turn any independently understood defect into a local source-generated regression control. |

### Implementation-ready optional diagnostic recipe

1. Do not install or build ezdxf for this pass, add it as a project dependency,
   or run it during each code slice. Use it only if it is already available or
   at the existing composed peer checkpoint; bind the exact package version,
   artifact checksum, Python/runtime, and command/options.
2. Author the input/control from scratch or through an existing eligible local
   generator, and keep the emitted DWG/DXF in a scratch directory. Never add an
   external model as a repository fixture under this recipe.
3. Strict-read the output first. For a DXF tag-order/value question, export
   verbose JSON tags and compare ordered pairs with the source-authored
   expectation. Preserve a separate literal wire assertion for binary group
   widths, exact raw payloads, and record-boundary sentinels.
4. If strict read fails and recovery/audit is diagnostically useful, run it as
   a separate observation. Record strict result, recovered result, audit
   repairs/errors, changed entity/handle inventory, and post-save reopen as
   distinct fields. Do not fold repair success into the strict acceptance
   result.
5. Convert any confirmed local mismatch into a small in-memory or scratch-
   generated regression selector in the owning test target; keep the full
   suite, sanitizer/fuzz campaign, native application checks, and peer
   execution at their already-specified composed/scheduled gates.

### Conclusion

This is a validation-efficiency refinement, not a new codec implementation or
support finding. The verbose tag stream can shorten diagnosis for a narrow DXF
structure disagreement, while strict byte/sentinel tests remain the local
fast gate and potentially long-running repairs remain composed-checkpoint
diagnostics. No plan finding or top-level subplan is added; implementation
order and test cadence are unchanged. The ledger remains 129 findings / 72
top-level subplans. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.49 MLINESTYLE borrowed linetype names (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

`dxfRW::writeMLineStyle()` previously copied each element's resolved DXF
linetype into a temporary `std::string`, then moved it into an owning staging
vector before synchronous group-6 emission. The function now stores
`std::string_view`s. Each view refers only to an unchanged caller-owned
element string, a stable `m_writingContext.lineTypesMap` key, or the static
`BYLAYER` fallback; those owners outlive the function's immediate output
loop. `dxfSymbolNameKey()` now accepts a view and constructs the same owned
uppercase key, avoiding an additional by-value input copy while preserving the
lookup semantics.

line elements: a direct `CONTINUOUS` name, an empty name resolved through its
LTYPE handle, and the default `BYLAYER` case. It checks ordered group-6 output,
ASCII/Binary projection agreement, caller string immutability, and a following
MLINE record/sentinel. This is a bounded source-level copy avoidance change,
not an allocator-count, peak-RSS, throughput, or general writer-memory

## Deeper/broader peer format-matrix versus entity-survival review (2026-10-17; research only)

This source review checked whether public version-support summaries and a
successful DXF reopen are enough to infer that a conversion preserved the
source drawing. It refreshed ACadSharp's version matrix and the current
3DSOLID/REGION writer report, then compared ezdxf's base entity-export
contract with its separately scoped XREF-copy API. It found no new
libdxfrw defect; the practical result is a sharper completeness check for
the existing composed comparison gate.

| Source / route | Evidence and ceiling | Existing-plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ACadSharp [README version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) | The README lists DWG/DXF read/write availability by AC code, but not by entity, object, carrier, or operation. It is a format-version capability summary, not proof that every feature survives read→model→write. | Keep every local feature claim version × operation × entity-specific. Do not promote a parser/writer version checkmark into complete graph or content-preservation coverage. |
| ACadSharp [issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) and [PR #1150](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1150) | #1195 remains open in the reviewed public view and reports `3DSOLID`/`REGION` entities disappearing from DWG→DXF output, including children inside blocks, without notification. #1150 remains open; its Oct. 1 discussion says a DXF 2013+ `ACDSDATA` reader change retained only the last repeated group-310 chunk, and the maintainer preferred a schema-driven writer over raw replay. These are peer-specific reports/discussion, not a local reproduction or normative specification. | For ACIS-bearing paths, keep carrier length/chunk order, owning entity, block reachability, and independent solid semantics as separate checks. A count restricted to modelspace or a surviving block/INSERT is insufficient; the per-source entity-to-output mapping must include nested block children and every carrier chunk. Existing AcDs/ACIS owners already cover these checks; do not add a new peer-driven workstream. |
| ezdxf [`DXFEntity` export contract](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dxfentity.py) | The source says features unavailable in the selected DXF version may be ignored during export and ezdxf does not convert between DXF versions. A strict reopen can therefore validate the emitted file's parseability without proving no source feature was dropped. | At cross-version writer comparisons, pin source and target AC codes and label any expected projection/downgrade explicitly. Compare source and output inventories; record omitted fields/features rather than using reopen success as a preservation proxy. This describes ezdxf's route and is a caution for comparator interpretation, not evidence about libdxfrw's own output. |
| ezdxf [XREF loader contract](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst#supported-entities) | The XREF loader supports a narrower copyable/transformable entity set and documents that unsupported ACAD_TABLE and unknown-storage entities are ignored without exceptions. This is a cross-document copy operation, not the base DXF reader or writer contract. | Keep parse, same-document save, cross-document copy, and version downgrade as separate operations. For a copy/XREF result, capture diagnostics and exact source-to-destination identities; do not generalize the helper's omission behavior to ezdxf's base parser. |

### Implementation-ready disposition check

Apply this to the already-scheduled composed peer/consumer checkpoint or to
the focused local writer slice when that slice changes the relevant output
path. Do not install a peer or expand the per-slice test cadence for this
research result.

1. Start from a locally authored, versioned source manifest. Include stable
   handle/identity where available, owner, model/paper-space location, nested
   block path, entity/object type, and any opaque carrier digest/length.
2. Record a separate disposition for every manifest item at each stage:
   typed decode; exact opaque preservation; declared projection/down-convert;
   explicit refusal with a diagnostic; or omission. An unplanned omission is
   a failed preservation result, even if the parser/writer exits successfully.
3. For DXF output, record source and target AC codes, then check destination
   entity/object inventory and relevant ordered tags. For binary/raw carriers,
   additionally check exact byte/chunk sequence, complete length/digest,
   ownership association, and a following-record sentinel in the local fast
   test.
4. Strictly reopen the emitted file with a separately named reader when the
   composed gate warrants it. Report framing/read success separately from
   source-to-output completeness, audit/recovery changes, and application or
   geometry-kernel acceptance.
5. Where a target version intentionally cannot express a source feature,
   keep the exact allowed projection and diagnostic in the expected manifest;
   score that row as a declared lossy conversion, never native-entity parity.

### Conclusion

This is a completeness/measurement refinement of existing peer admission,
writer-loss, graph-closure, and composed-consumer checks. It creates no local
finding, top-level subplan, test registration, dependency, peer execution,
fixture, implementation-order change, validation-frequency change, or support
promotion. Findings/subplans remain 129/72. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Deeper/broader FreeCAD 3D consumer applicability and converter-success audit (2026-10-17; research only)

This pass revisited the native-consumer boundary using current FreeCAD
converter/importer source, FreeCAD's published importer and DWG guidance, a
maintainer response on proprietary ACIS payloads, and the public OCCT component
catalog. The goal is to determine which FreeCAD checks can establish useful
consumer evidence, which are inapplicable to stock FreeCAD, and how to keep the
one composed external check reproducible. No FreeCAD build or runtime, CAD
converter, peer executable, kernel, drawing, local test, or native application
was used; no source/test/fixture/dependency was changed.

| Evidence | Current-source finding and confidence boundary | Plan refinement |
|---|---|---|
| FreeCAD [`importDWG.py`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py), mutable `main` reviewed 2026-10-17 | The stock DWG open path calls `convertToDxf()` and then the selected `importDXF.open()`/`insert()` route. `convertToDxf()` may run LibreDWG, ODA, or QCAD according to the configured converter mode; in automatic mode the source attempts available routes in sequence. It calls `Popen()` and `communicate()` but does not inspect the process return code before treating the output path's existence as success. This is a wrapper behavior observation from mutable source, not a tested failure or a statement about every packaged FreeCAD build. | Keep `DWGConversion` pinned to one explicit backend during qualification; capture the FreeCAD source/build, converter path/version/hash, exact argv, return code and logs, and whether the output was newly created. Strictly validate and hash the intermediate DXF, including its actual `$ACADVER`, before importing it. A wrapper success message or file-exists check is handoff evidence only. Do not combine LibreDWG, ODA and QCAD results into one parser result. |
| FreeCAD [`Installing_additional_components.md`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Installing_additional_components.md) and archived [`FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md) | The current documentation distinguishes a native C++ DXF importer from the optional legacy Python importer and says the C++ route does not implement every DXF feature. The older documentation repository is marked archived (2026-04-01); its broad “only CAD Exchanger supports 3D DWG” wording is a dated workflow note, not a current universal consumer contract. | Record the exact importer implementation/selection and configuration alongside each result. Keep importer-specific source support and native runtime acceptance separate. The previously identified `3DFACE` C++-source versus published matrix discrepancy stays `SOURCE_SCOPE_SPLIT / RUNTIME_PENDING`; test the exact asymmetric geometry in the selected importer rather than choosing whichever importer has the more favorable table. |
| FreeCAD maintainer response in issue [#18454](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/18454) | The issue is closed as not planned. The maintainer distinguishes explicit entities (which open) from ACIS solids, describes the latter as proprietary blobs in DXF, and says stock FreeCAD has no reader for them. This is direct maintainer scope evidence, not proof that no separately installed workbench/plugin can ever consume ACIS. | Mark stock FreeCAD's ACIS/AcDs/SAB consumer cell `CONSUMER_NOT_APPLICABLE`, not `FAIL` and not a blocker that triggers repeated stock-application runs. Reopen that cell only after naming and pinning a separate modeler/import integration and identifying how it exposes full shape/topology. Keep explicit-face/mesh consumer tests as their own supported-subset candidate; neither result may stand in for ACIS semantics or the DWG entity→AcDs owner/key→payload join. |
| Open CASCADE's [`OCCT-Components` preview](https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT-Components/blob/main/ReadMe.md) and [ACIS exchange component](https://occt3d.com/components/acis-exchange/) | The repository identifies itself as a public preview/documentation hub for commercial extensions, directs readers to purchase full components, and lists ACIS SAT/SAB exchange among them. This is a possible separately licensed route, not an open-source implementation or a capability implied by stock OCCT/FreeCAD. | Do not count OCCT core, a FreeCAD build, or the public component-preview repository as an independent open ACIS reader. A licensed component may be an optional semantic observation only if its exact component/build, entitlement and permitted test use, platform, input profile, and inspectable shape/metrics API are confirmed. Do not acquire, install, or trial it as part of local implementation. |
| The existing source audit for [`CADKernel`](https://github.com/kernalix7/CADKernel#supported-file-formats) | The repo's detailed matrix still marks SAT/SAB read and write as planned/unsupported despite an overview that includes ACIS in broad format-category prose. This is consistent with its already-recorded `DISCOVERY_ONLY / ACIS_UNSUPPORTED` grade; it supplies no new runnable reader or kernel route. | Leave the existing disposition unchanged. Reconsider only after an immutable revision changes the specific detailed SAT/SAB rows and exposes a runnable route; do not spend build/install time or convert headline format counts into evidence. |

### Implementation-ready FreeCAD checkpoint

1. Keep two independent cases: (a) direct DXF import with the selected native
   or legacy importer and a source-authored explicit-geometry manifest; (b) DWG
   conversion through exactly one named converter, followed by strict
   intermediate-DXF validation and the same named importer. Do not let an
   automatic fallback obscure which backend produced the file.
2. For Linux and Windows, record immutable FreeCAD build/source identity,
   importer mode, OS/architecture, converter artifact and command, subprocess
   exit code/logs, fresh output path/hash/version, and parse/import diagnostics.
   Compare per-handle/type/owner/block placement and independently expected
   coordinates/topology for the explicit subset. A file that exists, a GUI
   document that opens, or an entity count alone is not a pass.
3. Keep stock-FreeCAD ACIS/AcDs `CONSUMER_NOT_APPLICABLE`; do not repeatedly
   schedule a check the current project says has no stock ACIS reader. A future
   modeler plugin or licensed OCCT component is a separately named route with
   its own availability/entitlement and no-fallback shape checks; it does not
   replace the independent document/carrier ledger.
4. Execute this only at the already-planned composed native checkpoint after
   local route controls are ready. No per-slice peer/native test is added; if
   the required build/backend is absent, record `NOT_AVAILABLE`/`NOT_RUN` and
   continue local implementation.

### Conclusion

The deeper source review narrows native FreeCAD qualification rather than
adding a new parser, kernel, defect, or local work item. It strengthens the
existing strict handoff and exact-backend provenance requirement, while making
stock-FreeCAD ACIS non-applicability explicit. No tests, persistent fixtures,
dependencies, or CTest registrations were added; implementation order and
fast/full-suite cadence are unchanged. Findings/subplans remain 129/72; J256,
J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and cannot be
promoted by this research.

### Refined readiness and cadence

1. **Leaf implementation:** choose the next already-ready local finding/subplan;
   make one bounded change; use generated in-memory or from-scratch data;
   assert the changed field's exact wire/model result, negative admission or
   refusal, and a following-record sentinel where parsing is involved.
2. **Fast validation:** run the focused selector, strict `-Werror` target, the
   directly owning CTest, `lc3_compat_check` when public API paths are involved,
   and scoped `git diff --check`. Do not add peer installs, CAD GUI runs, or
   full suites to this loop.
3. **Composed acceptance:** only after the relevant local route is ready, run
   one pinned external/native checkpoint and report distinct outcomes for
   wire validity, strict independent read, object/owner completeness, native
   audit/import, and geometric semantics. Missing tools or inaccessible
   samples are recorded `NOT_AVAILABLE`/`NOT_RUN`; implementation continues.

## Implementation progress — PAR-130 / 7BU.1 XDATA group-1009 string typing (2026-10-17; local fast slice)

Corrected the canonical DXF value-kind table in `src/intern/dxfcode.h`:
group codes 1000–1009 are strings, and 1010–1059 are doubles. Previously the
table started the double range at 1009, causing ASCII/Binary DXF readers and
raw typed capture/replay to interpret the last XDATA string code as an
8-byte real. The exact boundary is confirmed by Autodesk's [group-code value
type reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-2553CF98-44F6-4828-82DD-FE3BC7448113.htm)
and its [numerical group-code reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3F0380A5-1C15-464D-BC66-2C5F094BCFB9.htm).

Added generated controls to the existing `libdxfrw_wave1_tests` owner. They
assert group-1009 string typing and 1010/1059 double boundaries; parse ASCII
records; preserve group 1009 as a raw string variant; and parse Binary DXF
through group 1009, group 1010, and the following EOF sentinel. A focused
`--dxf-code-type-boundaries` selector, strict `libdxfrw_wave1_tests` target
build, and owning `libdxfrw_wave1` CTest pass (1/1). No fixture, test
registration, dependency, external runtime, or full suite was added.

This closes only the 1009/1010 classifier boundary. It does not establish that
all manually typed binary writer call sites match the official type table;
the planned source census and independent raw-width walker remain outstanding.
No DWG parser or `parseDwg` body changed. Findings/subplans now total 130/73
(PAR-130 / one new top-level 7BU subplan); J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The worktree is broadly
dirty, so this slice remains uncommitted and no unrelated files were staged.

The four typed edge ranges are translated when objects are copied; 1005 XDATA handles are treated as soft pointers. Code 330's target role also depends on object position/context (for example, common entity owner-dictionary versus BLOCK_RECORD owner). Autodesk says code-table order can vary. | Keep a field-level edge descriptor, not a “hex handle” or numeric-range-only rule: source owner kind, group code plus subclass/ordinal context, edge role (arbitrary, soft/hard pointer, soft/hard owner), expected target class, presence/null state, and mapping disposition. Preserve arbitrary IDs; remap typed edges only where the source and output object-set semantics require it. Resolve by target identity and class, not existence alone. Parse/census reordered groups. Keep ownership/reachability distinct from pointer-reference validity. |
| LibreDWG's current [`dwg_resolve_handleref`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dwg.c) | The DWG object model carries typed owner/pointer references and also decodes relative handle encodings before resolution. This is DWG reader evidence, not the DXF group-code grammar. | When bridging DWG-derived objects into DXF, preserve the decoded semantic edge role and absolute target identity; do not copy DWG wire handle codes into the DXF remap policy. This is especially important for per-version parser work, which remains gated by the local ODA specification. |
| Local [`dxfcode.h`](src/intern/dxfcode.h), raw/object writers in [`libdxfrw.cpp`](src/libdxfrw.cpp), and generated [`dxf_fixture_tests.cpp`](tests/dxf_fixture_tests.cpp) controls | The code already has `DxfHandleRole`/`dxfHandleRoleForCode`; XRECORD emission leaves role-`Arbitrary` values unchanged and remaps translated roles. Existing ASCII/binary extension-graph coverage checks group 320/329 arbitrary values, 330 owner/reactor closure, and XDATA 1005 remapping while identities change. | Reuse these role helpers and tests. The remaining gap is not a missing numeric classifier or a need to repeat 320/329/1005 coverage: extend 7G.2 with per-field/subclass target-class and null/absence semantics, and test only unrepresented role/context combinations plus ownership closure. Do not infer typed field expectations from the group-code range alone. |
| ezdxf's [`xref` scope and loader documentation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst) and [table audit implementation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/sections/table.py) | The cross-document loader supports a bounded copyable/transformable subset and explicitly ignores unsupported objects such as ACAD_TABLE/proxy content. It groups loading commands to keep resource renaming consistent. The table auditor repairs duplicate handles by reminting them and notes that this can break references. | Use ezdxf only as a pinned optional structural/differential observation. Capture raw output and diagnostics before any repair/audit mutation; an audited/repaired file that opens is not proof that the original handle graph was correct. Do not add a peer run to each leaf slice. |
| FreeCAD's current [`Draft/importDWG.py`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py) | The wrapper converts DWG to DXF with a selected external converter, then calls `importDXF.open()`. The current subprocess path waits for completion and tests whether the expected output path exists; that condition alone is not a semantic-conversion result. Converter choice is configurable and can be LibreDWG, ODA, or QCAD. | The native Linux/Windows checkpoint must record the exact FreeCAD build/importer backend, configured converter path and version/hash, arguments, process status/diagnostics, and a fresh output path. Validate output magic/version and strict DXF parse plus source-to-output inventory before attributing a result to the native importer. A converter file-exists message or successful import dialog alone is insufficient. |

### Refined 7G.2 sequence and fast validation

1. **Finish the typed-edge census before broad remapping.** Extend the current
   PAR-40 STYLE edge row with the exact source field context and target class.
   Then enumerate the remaining named table/object fields and common fields;
   distinguish code 320 arbitrary IDs, the 330–369 typed ranges, 1005 XDATA
   handles, name-valued compatibility fields, owner overrides, and generated
   destination handles. Do not mechanically route every 320–369 value through
   `remapObjectHandle` without recording its field role.
2. **Extend existing generated role controls without duplicating them.**
   Reuse the current extension-graph tests for arbitrary 320/329 values, owner
   and reactor 330 edges, and 1005 XDATA remapping. Add only the missing
   field-context matrix: soft/hard pointer and soft/hard owner cases whose
   expected target class is explicit, plus missing/explicit-zero/present
   states and permuted group ordering. Assert wrong-class targets fail and
   ownership edges are checked independently of pointer existence. Add one
   valid non-owning cycle and one invalid owner-cycle or unresolved hard-owner
   case according to the field schema. Exercise ASCII and binary DXF, output
   preservation on rejection, and the following-record/EOF boundary. Generate
   all controls locally; no existing arbitrary/pointer test should be copied
   into a parallel test owner.
3. **Define unresolved-target policy per edge.** A typed reference may be
   remapped to an emitted target, left unchanged only when the target is
   deliberately outside the copied/reminted set and remains present, treated
   as explicit optional-null, or rejected when its required target was lost.
   Hard-owner edges participate in ownership closure; pointers alone do not
   establish that an object is an emitted root. Unsupported opaque edges stay
   raw-preserved only when their identity namespace is demonstrably stable;
   otherwise fail closed. Do not infer that a soft reference to an omitted
   target is valid merely because the output contains the same numeric handle.
4. **Keep the patch small and validations fast.** Implement one schema-backed
   edge family at a time; run its focused selector, strict owning target, and
   owning CTest. Add `lc3_compat_check` only for public API/consumer contract
   changes. Do not run full suites or install peers for every edge. Keep the
   broader graph matrix, optional independent DXF audit, and native
   Linux/Windows FreeCAD qualification at the existing composed checkpoints.
5. **Keep support claims bounded.** A file that parses, a handle that resolves,
   an ezdxf repair, a converter output file, or a FreeCAD 2D projection does
   not establish complete ownership closure, ACIS/B-rep semantics, or 3D
   consumer acceptance. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; this research cannot promote them.

| [`xorgy/dxfscan`](https://github.com/xorgy/dxfscan) | Its README describes a single-pass, zero-copy, `no_std` binary-DXF parser for AC1015+ with typed support for a subset of common entities and `Unknown` retention for unrecognized entities. The repository page shows one commit, no listed release, and ISC licensing. Its documentation directs ASCII-to-binary conversion to a separate `dxfbin` tool. | At most a narrow optional binary-DXF structural comparator after pinning its exact source and checking test coverage. It can only speak to its admitted binary tags/entities and projection: it is not an ASCII-DXF route, DWG reader, writer, graph-preservation oracle, or semantic/3D vote. Do not add it as a dependency or invoke it per implementation slice. |
| [`iyulab/uncad`](https://github.com/iyulab/uncad) | Its README explicitly routes DWG through LibreDWG FFI and DXF through the pure-Rust `undxf` crate, then maps both into an application model and renderer. It documents Linux and Windows builds. | Do not count its DWG result as an independent parser vote; the DWG parser lineage is LibreDWG. It can be a composed application/render observation only if a future question needs that exact model/renderer route. Record the underlying parser, crate revisions, and downstream projections separately. Its `undxf` component is not a newly established independent route here; the plan's existing artifact/version-provenance check still applies. |
| [`seaflower205/Sea-DXF-Core`](https://github.com/seaflower205/Sea-DXF-Core) | The project describes a pre-1.0 DXF-only implementation and says the visible source is under a proprietary license that grants no use, modification, or redistribution rights. | Exclude it from the open-source peer set despite public source visibility. Do not clone, build, reuse code/schema/fixtures, or count its claims as independent support evidence. It does not add a DWG route. |

### Implementation-ready qualification sequence

1. **Do not add work to leaf slices.** These are discovery-only candidates. Keep
   the current local sequence and run neither peer during ordinary focused
   implementation validation. Do not add peer dependencies, persistent
   fixtures, test registrations, or copied foreign sample drawings.
2. **Admit a candidate only at the existing composed peer checkpoint.** Pin
   repository commit (or exact package checksum), license, build flags,
   dependency graph, platform, invocation, and source-lineage determination.
   A mutable `main` README or a successful build alone is not qualification.
3. **Use only locally authored, small controls.** For `ft_model`, cover one
   supported DWG release at a time plus a DXF control and record entity type,
   handle where exposed, block/layout path, and parser diagnostic before
   comparing the 2D projection. For `dxfscan`, use Binary DXF AC1015+ only and
   compare exact group/value framing and the subset it claims to type; preserve
   a following-record/EOF sentinel. Keep ASCII, DWG, writer, and semantic
   results `NOT_APPLICABLE` for that route rather than treating absence as a
   failure or pass.
4. **Separate the result layers.** Record bytes/strict parse, typed inventory,
   opaque/unknown retention, 2D projection/render, and any native application
   outcome independently. Any missing entity must be an explicit supported
   projection or reported loss; “opens” or “renders” does not close graph or
   payload preservation. None of these routes supplies an ACIS kernel or
   entity→AcDs→SAB ownership proof.
5. **Unblock without the candidates.** If source identity, licensing, build
   reproducibility, or a usable semantic inventory cannot be established,
   leave the optional route `UNQUALIFIED` and proceed with the already-ready
   local slice. No unresolved peer state blocks implementation.

1. **Repair carrier identity first.** Remove the VIEWPORT parser's code-349 alias to code 333 and prove the shade target is not overwritten; do not create a VIEWPORT `dragVisualStyleHandle`. Determine 0–3 and candidate 4/5 pair semantics independently for VPORT; the published table documents only 0–3 while current API exposes 0–5. Until producer/version witnesses resolve the delta, preserve reads without broadening write claims and fail closed on unsupported non-null targets or modes.
3. **Close all carrier edges in one context matrix.** For HEADER (including 345/346/349 VisualStyle refs), VIEW, VPORT, VIEWPORT, embedded LAYOUT PlotSettings, and standalone PLOTSETTINGS, record group code, semantic role, pointer/owner class, target kind, owning root, required/optional/null/absent rules, producer/version, parser field, writer field, handle map, and current disposition. Include code348 VisualStyle separately from shade-plot code333; include 332 Background, VIEW code334 LiveSection, HEADER VisualStyle refs, 361 SUN, and layer viewport-override codes only where the carrier-specific reference confirms them.
4. **Implement roots/ownership before positive emission.** Retain typed and raw Background/SUN objects and their owners. Emit Background only through a validated `ACAD_BACKGROUND` dictionary entry, enforce uniqueness/non-sharing between viewports, and validate concrete class/version. The documented defaults differ: Conceptual, 3D Wireframe, and null. | Treat the three as separate HEADER reference edges sharing a target class, not as VIEWPORT properties. Preserve null/absent/default distinctions and verify each target resolves to a rooted VisualStyle before output. Do not extrapolate a version gate from one variable to the others. |
| Autodesk [VIEWPORT DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-2602B0FB-02E4-4B9A-B03C-B1D904753D34.htm), [VIEW DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-CF3094AB-ECA9-43C1-8075-7791AC84F97C.htm), and [DXF group-code classes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3F0380A5-1C15-464D-BC66-2C5F094BCFB9.htm) | VIEWPORT assigns 345/346 to named/base UCS, 333 to shade target, 348 to VisualStyle, and lists no 349. VIEW assigns 334 to its optional LiveSection edge. The general code table only says 340–349 are hard pointers; that range alone cannot establish the semantic field or carrier. | Do not add `DRW_Viewport::dragVisualStyleHandle` or a VIEWPORT 334 field. Keep the `DRW_Viewport::parseCode(349)` alias as a parser defect: an unsupported/malformed VIEWPORT 349 must not overwrite shade code 333. Keep 345/346 meanings class-scoped. |
| Local source audit: `DRW_Viewport::parseCode`, `DRW_Header::parseCode`/`write`, and `DRW_Header::parseDwg`/`encodeDwg` | The viewport parser maps code 349 into `shadePlotHandle`; `writeViewport` then emits the resulting value as code 333. HEADER parsing has no 345/346/349 cases and drops those values; the explicit HEADER writer does not emit the three variables. In the R2007+ DWG header path, the three handles are read into temporary `CONTROL` values only for debug output; the writer emits null hard pointers for all three. | Land a no-corruption parser control first. Implement DXF HEADER retention/output as a separate graph closure with common identity remapping. For DWG, consult the repository's ODA specification sections for header variables and handles, then use version-matched sample traces before changing any `parseDwg`/encoder layout. |

This is useful corroboration for that variable only; it does not establish the other two variables' minimum version, wire representation for every target, or libdxfrw compatibility. | Use AC1021/R2007 as a test candidate for `$DRAGVS`, not as a blanket gate for all three variables. Confirm release boundaries from Autodesk/ODA documentation or producer-authored files before enabling output across versions. Peer API presence is not semantic support evidence. |

### Corrected implementation-ready sequence

1. **Prevent misclassification.** VIEWPORT code 349 is now rejected as out of schema, so it cannot change `shadePlotHandle`. The generated ASCII control places code 333 before code 349 and asserts rejection plus unchanged shade handle. Keep the existing valid 333 ASCII/Binary round trips; add bounded unknown-field retention only if the library adopts that policy across entity families.
2. **Add the HEADER trio on the DXF path.** Represent each HEADER hard pointer separately (345/346/349), preserve its code and raw handle identity, and emit it through the handle-remap plan. Add ASCII/Binary tests with distinct handles, present and null/absent targets, and collision cases where HEADER 345/346 must not be mistaken for VIEWPORT UCS. Gate positive output on a uniquely rooted VisualStyle target; negatives cover missing, wrong-class, duplicate, and unrooted targets with destination preservation and same-adapter retry.

The `$DRAGVS` R2007 peer note is a candidate lower bound, not a blanket rule.

Trace AC1021 and later samples to distinguish the handle kind, reference ordering, null encoding, and version gates. 5. **Fold into the context matrix and fast validation lane.** Include HEADER 345/346/349 alongside VIEW code334, VIEWPORT 345/346 UCS, VIEWPORT/VPORT 333, and VIEWPORT 348. Use generated temporary controls only. Run the strict touched target, one focused selector, compatibility target, and owning CTest; defer full suites to the already-planned checkpoint and do not add external fixture files.

3. If peer comparison is needed to adjudicate a concrete mismatch, select one route with a direct API/CLI for the missing observation. ## Deeper and broader cross-kernel semantic validation and topology-identity review (2026-10-18; research only)

This pass looked beyond parser feature matrices at how CAD interoperability research distinguishes model identity from shape interchangeability, then reconciled that evidence with the current SAT/SAB, AcDs, kernel, and native-consumer gates. It is a plan refinement only: no local code or tests changed, no external model was downloaded, and no third-party program was installed or run.

| Evidence | Verified contract and limitation | Plan refinement |
|---|---|---|
| Sap and Szabo, [“Representation and system-agnostic automated CAD interoperability testing based on model interchangeability”](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2590118425000516), *Computer-Aided Design* 85 (2025), DOI [10.1016/j.cola.2025.101365](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cola.2025.101365) | The authors describe representation-independent comparison using query/proxy models, configurable tolerances, and both local and global geometric/topological properties. Their method is a general CAD interoperability method, not a DWG/DXF conformance procedure, and its results do not certify libdxfrw, any particular ACIS profile, or a native consumer. | Make the metric family and tolerance explicit for each semantic case. Prefer independent analytic properties and bounded local comparisons over one aggregate count or visual screenshot. Keep the comparison's application purpose explicit; no metric set proves every downstream use. |
| Jones et al., [“B-rep Matching for Collaborating Across CAD Systems”](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.03169) | The paper treats geometric and topological changes as a cross-system correspondence problem, observes that neutral exchange often lacks internal CAD persistent-reference structures, and reports correspondence ambiguities including one-to-many cases. It addresses matching across model versions, not preservation of a specific DWG/DXF object graph. | **Inference for this plan:** exact cross-kernel face/edge/vertex IDs or counts should not be the universal shape-equivalence oracle. Keep handle, owner, topology, and carrier preservation as a separate structural contract; topology counts remain diagnostic unless the specific identity-preserving profile requires them. |
| NIST, [hybrid B-rep capability in ISO 10303](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/03/nist-contributes-new-modeling-capability-iso-product-data-interoperability) | NIST distinguishes explicit geometry and face-edge-vertex topology, and describes hybrid models that combine different geometric/topological representation types. This supports treating geometry and topology as related but independently observable properties; it does not establish an ACIS importer or a DWG mapping. | Preserve independent body validity/closure and expected topology checks where the target operation needs them. Do not collapse geometric shape equality, graph identity, and feature/history preservation into a single “3D pass.” |
| Existing [ACIS peer-route evidence](#deeperbroader-acadrust-acis-and-opencadkernel-semantic-route-review-2026-10-17-research-only), [OpenCADStudio tessellation boundary](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/docs/tessellation.md), and [cq-acis geometry limitations](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/docs/geometry-support.md) | The route inventory already identifies distinct parser/kernel/application stages: OpenCADStudio is ACadRust-lineage and can use fallback tessellation; `cq-acis` parses bounded SAT/SAB profiles into an OCCT-family kernel route and lists unsupported geometry and limits. A rendered or partially tessellated body does not prove full B-rep semantics; an OCCT-backed route is not an independent kernel from FreeCAD/OCCT. This pass found no newly qualified open-source route joining outer DWG/DXF/AcDs decoding to a genuinely independent kernel and native acceptance. | Add no peer or kernel dependency. Keep each route's exact parser, payload hash, kernel, fallback status, and application identity in one optional composed evidence record. Reject a partial-body/surface fallback as a complete-body semantic pass. |
| System-agnostic CAD interoperability article above and the current local 3D evidence matrix | A comparison can be much cheaper and more decisive when locally authored cases carry independently known dimensions/placement and bounded per-case tolerances, while source identity and owner/payload links are checked directly in the file graph. Expensive one-to-one topology matching and screenshots do not replace those tests. | Optimize readiness around a small generated analytic control and a predeclared metric manifest; do not add a per-slice peer build, broad corpus, geometric-learning matcher, or external fixture. |

### Updated implementation-ready semantic gate

1. **Keep structural preservation independent.** For each source entity, compare type/handle, owner and block path, payload bytes/hash, AcDs owner/key/page join where applicable, and output disposition. This remains required even when downstream geometry is equivalent.
2. **Define a bounded semantic case before running a peer.** Use a locally authored asymmetric analytic body with independently computed dimensions, placement, units, and expected bounds, volume/area/centroid. Record its source and emitted payload hashes. Choose tolerances from the target task and model scale; never infer them from the peer output.
3. **Require a complete body result.** Record parse result, body count, unsupported/raw records, conversion result, fallback count, valid/closed-shell status, and all diagnostics separately. Any missing required face/body, unsupported required record, or fallback that makes the model partial is `NOT_QUALIFIED` for complete-solid semantics even if a view renders.
4. **Compare shape properties, not universal B-rep identity.** Apply the declared analytic metrics and, where those metrics do not distinguish the case, a bounded distance/point-membership check. Record face/edge/vertex counts and adjacency as diagnostics; make them a pass criterion only when the case explicitly asserts topology-preserving transfer or the consumer operation depends on that topology.
5. **Keep the route boundary explicit.** A raw SAT/SAB parser result, DWG entity-to-AcDs binding, kernel B-rep, and FreeCAD/native application import are separate observations. Same-kernel results, same-project round trips, mesh silhouettes, and native open success cannot individually promote independent semantic support.
6. **Preserve the fast lane.** No change to per-slice validation frequency: strict touched target, focused generated selector, relevant compatibility target, and owning CTest. Run parser/kernel/native comparisons only at the existing composed checkpoint, with one selected question and exact artifact/profile capture. Create controls in memory or from scratch locally; do not add peer/customer fixture drawings.

This refinement touches the existing PAR-07/S8 semantic-evidence and composed-consumer gates only; it adds no finding or top-level subplan and changes no implementation order, test cadence, dependencies, or support claims. Ledger totals remain 130 findings / 73 top-level subplans. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; neither proxy-based metrics nor this research can promote them without their specific independent evidence.

## Implementation progress — PAR-40 / 7G.2 VPORT shade-plot fields (2026-10-18; local fast slice)

Added DXF-only retention for VPORT group 170 (shade-plot mode) and group 333
(soft-pointer shade target), including independent presence bits so missing
fields remain distinct from explicit zero. The parser accepts the Autodesk
API's syntactic mode range 0–5 and preserves the soft-pointer identity. The
writer currently emits only modes 0–3 with a null code-333 target, and only
for AC1021+; it rejects modern modes, any non-null target without an object
closure, and older target revisions before publication. This is a conservative
local read/write boundary, not full VPORT shade-plot support.

Primary documentation confirms that the [VPORT DXF schema](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-8CE7CC87-27BD-4490-89DA-C21F516415A9.htm)
defines code 170 as a shade-plot setting and code 333 as an optional soft
pointer. Autodesk's [shade-plot enum](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_PlotSettingsShadePlotType.html)
defines 0–5 and names modes 4/5 VisualStyle/RenderPreset; its
[SetShadePlot contract](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_PlotSettings_SetShadePlot_PlotSettingsShadePlotType_ObjectId.html)
requires VisualStyle/RenderSettings targets for those modes and nulls the
target for modes 0/3. These API details are not a VPORT producer/version
witness: the VPORT DXF page itself does not enumerate 170's values or establish
the first release for either field. Therefore modern modes and nonzero VPORT
code-333 output stay blocked pending a VPORT-specific typed-root/owner and
version contract; no relationship is inferred from VIEWPORT code 333.

Generated temporary ASCII/Binary controls cover modes 0–3 with explicit-null
333 round trips, absent-versus-null distinction, invalid mode rejection, and
atomic refusal for non-null target, modes 4/5, and AC1018 output. No persistent
DWG/DXF fixture, CTest registration, or DWG parser/encoder change was added.
