## Implementation progress — PAR-40 / 7G.2 VPORT and VIEW UCS-reference closure (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Closed the DXF adapter/writer gap for UCS references on the `VPORT` and `VIEW` symbol-table records. Autodesk's [VPORT schema](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-8CE7CC87-27BD-4490-89DA-C21F516415A9.htm) defines groups 345/346 as named/base `AcDbUCSTableRecord` handles, with 346 conditional on a nonzero orthographic type and implicit WORLD when omitted. The [VIEW schema](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-CF3094AB-ECA9-43C1-8075-7791AC84F97C.htm) makes its UCS fields conditional on group 72 and defines the same typed targets and implicit-WORLD base behavior.

The adapter now validates range/flag consistency, unique UCS target resolution, the required orthographic type for a nonzero base-UCS edge, and target-version representability before publication. The `VPORT` and `VIEW` serializers remap nonzero 345/346 references through the existing source-to-output handle map; standalone writers also fail rather than silently dropping these links when the target version or UCS flag cannot represent them. The change is DXF-only: no DWG parse/encode path, public callback, `DRW_Interface` virtual, or class layout changed.

Generated temporary ASCII/Binary controls add one VPORT and one VIEW referencing two UCS records. They verify typed readback, dangling/wrong-class target refusal with the old output preserved, invalid orthographic/has-UCS combinations, and reference closure after forcing the named UCS to collide with fixed handle `8`. The remap/readback matrix covers AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, and AC1027. No persistent drawing or fixture, CTest registration, or external application run was added.

### Refined peer-evidence and implementation-ready sequence

1. **Use an operation-specific evidence row.** For every optional peer result, bind exact source commit/release and runtime; source version and output version; entity/object family; operation (strict read, recovered read, write, cross-version conversion, or same-profile rewrite); source/output inventories; owner/block/handle disposition; warnings, repairs, and omissions; and the verifier actually used. Keep peer self-roundtrip separate from independent-reader and native-application evidence.
2. **Pick the cheapest peer that can answer the named question.** For a DXF group-code or raw-carrier ambiguity, use an exact-pinned strict structural/tag reader. For an emitted DWG, first screen the peer manual's exact write version and audit caveats; do not spend time running a known-experimental writer as though it were a native acceptance oracle. Run an expensive native or kernel route only at the existing composed qualification checkpoint.
3. **If `obj2cad` becomes useful, make one bounded pilot—not a dependency.** Pin its immutable commit and Rust dependency graph; inspect the distinct ACIS writer, linked readers, licenses, and `acis-samples` recipe. Generate plane/box/curved-surface controls only in scratch and record whether the payload is SAT or SAB plus the exact profile. Independently compute expected geometry; require full body and source-face disposition, valid closed-body checks where applicable, and independent bounds/area/volume/centroid/transform checks. A match of sampled surface vertices or a successful raw-carrier read is only partial evidence. Do not use its ACadRust-derived DWG output to claim independent DWG parsing/writing or AcDs coverage.
4. **Keep recovery in its own lane.** Strict source read, recovered read, audit repairs, write success, target-native audit, and semantic geometry are distinct outcomes. Never call an output conformant solely because a permissive recovery path reopened it.
5. **Preserve implementation speed.** The peer screen changes no local queue: continue the dependency-ready PAR-40 / 7G.2 generated DXF slices with the fast touched-target/focused-selector/compatibility gate; perform peer comparison only when a named ambiguity or composed checkpoint needs it. Do not add a new per-slice full suite, third-party package, persistent external drawing, or fixture from these repositories.

This research establishes no local defect and adds no finding or top-level subplan. It does not change implementation order, validation frequency, fixtures, dependencies, or support claims. while continuing to reject nonzero UCS references without the flag. No reset,
public layout, DWG parse/encode path, or record bytes were changed.

### Conditional implementation-ready evaluation

1. **Keep implementation moving.** This changes no local queue, prerequisite,

## Deeper/broader ACIS embedded-payload dialect and peer-independence audit (2026-10-18; research only)

This pass pins the newest published `cq-acis` artifact and re-evaluates the
external ACIS evidence ladder against the authoritative DWG wrapper description,
ACIS save-profile compatibility notes, and current consumer documentation. It
focuses on a recurring false shortcut: treating an AC1027+/AC1032 DWG version,
an `ACIS BinaryFile` marker, or a successful raw SAB parse as sufficient proof
that a particular geometry reader supports the enclosed dialect and shape.
No peer was installed or executed, no native CAD/kernel was run, no drawing was
downloaded, and no local code/test/fixture/dependency changed.

| Evidence | What is established—and what is not | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ODA [Open Design Specification v5.4.1, §20.4.41](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) and local authoritative copy | For the DWG `REGION`/`3DSOLID`/`BODY` carrier, the description distinguishes legacy blocked SAT text from a direct SAT/SAB stream; the direct stream is identified as SAB by its `ACIS BinaryFile` header, otherwise SAT, and SAB has an end marker. The same section says ODA does not completely decode the ACIS entity data and describes the typed group stream as not fully understood. This is a DWG carrier/wrapper description, not a complete SAT/SAB grammar, shape kernel, or validity oracle. | Use the spec for the DWG envelope and wrapper boundary only. Keep AcDs/page/owner closure, exact extracted carrier bytes, ACIS parsing, complete-body conversion, and geometry semantics as separate proofs. Do not infer the full ACIS payload grammar from ODA's reader or marker handling. Any DWG layout change still requires the relevant spec chapter and local trace. |
| ODA [Working with .sat and .sab Files in Teigha](https://www.opendesign.com/blog/2017/october/working-sat-and-sab-files-teigha) | This dated vendor note says save versions through 700 are compatible with Spatial ACIS; Autodesk's modified SAT/SAB profiles from 20800 and above are not native Spatial ACIS without conversion, and native Spatial ACIS profiles above 700 cannot be used in DWG/DXF as-is. The article's version table is historical and does not establish every current producer/version mapping. | Treat SAT/SAB dialect classification as a required intake step. Record the exact embedded header, save-format version, producer, and wrapper profile; do not equate a DWG AC version with an ACIS save version or pass arbitrary native SAT/SAB to a parser solely because its container has the expected marker. Confirm disputed version mappings with a pinned producer/reader control. |
| [`cq-acis` 0.3.12 PyPI publication](https://pypi.org/project/cq-acis/0.3.12/) | The release is dated 2026-10-16; PyPI provenance binds the sdist to source commit `e05a8f470d2f6799277f7b7df467d2fc35625889` and SHA-256 `eba52992abcf6afce57b0f3526c3afeeed29cc60fbbb61c275958703d597de3a`. Published wheels exist for Windows x86-64, Linux x86-64/aarch64, and macOS ARM64/x86-64. The project calls itself experimental, requires CadQuery/OCCT for conversion, and advertises only a supported analytic B-rep subset and selected SAB/ASM profiles. This refreshes artifact provenance and availability, not a successful run, exact profile qualification for our samples, or a separate kernel from FreeCAD. | Refresh the candidate identity to the latest exact 0.3.12 publication; it may be considered at the existing composed checkpoint when its accepted profile matches a locally authored/authorized body. Before any run, verify the wheel/sdist selected, hash, runtime, native dependencies, and exact source release. It is a parser/converter comparator, not a DWG/AcDs consumer and not a two-kernel result. No per-slice install/run is needed. |
| `cq-acis` [current SAB/ASM support notes](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/docs/sab-support.md), [geometry matrix](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/docs/geometry-support.md), and [third-party notices](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) | The project documents bounded SAB/ASM framing, separate active-table and opaque-history treatment, unsupported records preserved raw, and conversion failure when requested geometry is unsupported. Its notice says the SAB reader was written for the project and its grammar/layout was informed by CADMPEG project commit `faa73bfdaa29a7b4fb5c6998c1bdedfec8fac9d7`; it also cites ezdxf's SAB tag grammar and two public cube fixtures. This is explicit conceptual/source-reference lineage, not proof that the parser implementations are identical. The linked branch is mutable and must not silently substitute for the pinned release. | Treat `cq-acis`↔CADMPEG parsing as *correlated evidence pending source-level overlap audit*. Separate repositories/packages do not justify two independent grammar votes. A bounded cross-read can still expose implementation disagreements, but must disclose this reference lineage and is not an independent validation of ambiguous token layouts. Keep unsupported raw records, opaque history, incomplete conversion, and producer-current-state limits visible as non-passes for any required body. |
| [`ezdxf` ACIS tools documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) | ezdxf says it has no ACIS kernel, supports only a limited count of ACIS entity types, loads unsupported ones as `NONE_ENTITY` with data loss, and cannot load/re-export arbitrary ACIS data. Its polygonal face extraction loses curved faces. SAT/SAB authoring for its declared DXF version bands is useful as a narrowly scoped producer/structural control, not a general semantic oracle. | Keep ezdxf in the raw-tag/carrier and explicitly supported polyhedral lane. A successful ezdxf DXF parse, re-export, or planar extraction cannot close full body conversion or native 3D acceptance. Keep strict parse, recovery, audit, and projection outcomes separate. |
| FreeCAD [DWG import guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md), [converter implementation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py), and existing 3D importer notes | FreeCAD's documented DWG route is converter→DXF→its standard DXF importer; its stock DXF path does not establish embedded ACIS body decoding. OS/importer/backend differences remain relevant to the 2D qualification route. | Keep native Linux/Windows FreeCAD checks limited to the selected 2D converter/importer profiles unless a distinct supported 3D import route is demonstrated. Converter exit/output existence or a surviving `3DSOLID` shell does not qualify 3D geometry. |
| Ansys [ACIS interface documentation](https://ansyshelp.ansys.com/public/views/secured/corp/v261/en/ref_cad/cadACIS.html) | The 2026 R1 docs describe a stand-alone reader mode that does not require the ACIS system, reads SAT/SAB through version 2023 on Windows and Linux, and supports solid, surface, and line bodies. It does not support associativity and is not a writer. The documentation does not pin a locally available binary/license, exact binary identity, or a reproducible geometry-query/export path for our cases. | Retain Ansys only as an optional, non-open-source external-reader/consumer candidate. Before any use, verify lawful availability, exact installed component/build and OS, profile acceptance, and a way to capture complete geometry plus independent measurements. It cannot read the DWG AcDs owner join through a standalone SAT/SAB test, and its kernel/parser lineage is not established by this documentation. |

### Refined implementation-ready evidence sequence

1. **Resolve the outer container first.** For DWG, preserve entity handle, modeler wrapper, AcDs record key/page path, and the exact body association. For DXF, preserve the `3DSOLID`/`REGION`/`BODY` record and ordered SAT/SAB payload fields. Hash the exact extracted bytes and record whether extraction removed only the documented wrapper or performed any transformation.
2. **Classify the inner dialect before invocation.** Capture SAT versus SAB, exact save-format/profile marker, producer/version if available, and byte length/terminator. Never use AC1021/AC1027/AC1032 as a proxy for ACIS save version. Refuse to count a parser result when its accepted dialect cannot be shown to match the bytes supplied.
3. **At the existing composed checkpoint, pin one reader artifact.** For `cq-acis`, use the exact 0.3.12 PyPI provenance or a separately pinned later release, including package hash, source commit, wheel tag, Python/CadQuery/OCCT runtime, and invocation. For CADMPEG, bind the exact crate checksum, source, lockfile, Rust toolchain and profile. Do not add either to CMake/CI or routine slice tests.
4. **Audit correlation before voting.** Compare the relevant parser files/dependencies and disclose `cq-acis`'s stated CADMPEG and ezdxf references. A disagreement may guide debugging; agreement among these routes is not independent grammar corroboration until implementation overlap and common fixtures/profile assumptions are reviewed. OCCT-backed conversion shares geometry-kernel lineage with FreeCAD and is not a second kernel.
5. **Require total disposition and complete-shape checks.** Record every source body and every supported, raw, skipped, or failed record; require no unexplained record/body loss for the named profile, valid complete body/shell status, and independent expected units, placement, bounds, area/volume/centroid plus a bounded distance or point-membership check as appropriate. A parse count, raw bytes, partial analytic shape, tessellation, bounding box, or self-roundtrip alone is not a pass.
6. **Keep external/native cells separate and non-blocking.** A standalone SAT/SAB reader does not qualify DWG AcDs lookup, FreeCAD's 2D converter→DXF route, native Linux/Windows acceptance, or unsupported history/current model state. Ansys remains availability/license/profile-gated. Keep the local fast-slice cadence unchanged and never commit a downloaded peer drawing; use generated controls or already tracked, explicitly permitted samples.

This pass corrects only the evidence grade/readiness of the optional ACIS reader route and strengthens payload-profile separation. It establishes no local defect and adds no finding, top-level subplan, dependency, test, fixture, or implementation-order change. Support claims remain unchanged; totals remain 130 findings / 73 top-level subplans. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; neither a pinned package release nor its documentation resolves independent semantic evidence or external/platform qualification.

## Implementation progress — PAR-40 / 7G.2 VIEW/VPORT/VIEWPORT Background and SUN fail-closed export (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Closed a cross-carrier low-level DXF export gap without claiming Background or
SUN support. The existing adapter already refused unclosed Background/SUN
edges on paper-space VIEWPORT and VIEW records, but `dxfRW::writeViewport`
could still emit those source handles through direct callers. It now rejects
nonzero code-332 Background and code-361 SUN references before writing a
record. The VPORT path had the larger gap: `writeVport` emitted these fields,
while adapter preflight did not validate either edge. Both the adapter and
low-level VPORT writer now fail closed for nonzero references. Code 332 is a
documented VPORT Background reference; code 361 is not established for VPORT,
so this slice deliberately refuses it rather than endorsing that mapping.

The existing positive VIEWPORT handle-remap vector now tests only edges with a
qualified typed/remap route; it no longer treats unrooted Background/SUN
handles as valid. Added focused generated ASCII/Binary AC1027 controls for
VIEWPORT and VPORT. Each control checks refusal with an existing destination
preserved, then clears only the unsupported edge and retries successfully on
the same writer/adapter. VPORT controls exercise both adapter preflight and
the direct `writeVport` route; the neighboring VIEW Background/SUN control is
retained as a regression.

Validation passed: strict build of `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests` and the
`lc3_compat_check` target; `--viewport-background-sun-fail-closed`,
`--vport-background-sun-fail-closed`, `--viewport-typed-handle-remap`,
`--vport-shadeplot-retention`, and the existing
`--view-background-sun-fail-closed` selector; scoped `git diff --check`.
The VPORT shade-plot selector prints expected diagnostics from its negative
controls and passes. No full CTest/full suite, peer/native run, persistent
DWG/DXF fixture, registration, public API/layout change, or DWG parse/encode
change was added.

This closes only the direct-writer/adapter loss-prevention boundary for these
unretained references. It does not implement `ACAD_BACKGROUND` dictionary
capture, Background or SUN object serialization, prove VPORT code-361
semantics, qualify rendering/plotting, or promote 3D support. Continue the
remaining PAR-40/7G.2 reference-graph census using carrier-specific schemas;
external/native qualification remains separate and must not block local
fail-closed work. Findings/subplans remain 130/73. J256, J260, J268, J284,
J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The shared
worktree is broadly dirty, so this slice remains uncommitted and no unrelated
files were staged.

## Implementation progress — PAR-40 / 7G.2 Background and SUN typed and raw callback retention (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The DXF/DWG readers already publish `DRW_Background` and `DRW_Sun` through
non-pure `DRW_Interface` callbacks, but the concrete `dx_iface` adapter had no
overrides and `dx_data` therefore discarded both typed families. DXF object
records also arrived through `addRawDxfObject` without a retained owner. Added
typed `backgrounds`/`suns` collections and separate raw DXF carrier lists;
`dx_iface` now stores both callback paths and includes their handles in the
existing identity inventories. No `DRW_Interface` virtual contract changed.

This is an import-preservation stage, not a serializer completion. Export now
refuses typed or raw Background/SUN data before publishing output until the
`ACAD_BACKGROUND` NOD root and the carrier-specific SUN hard-owner graph can
be emitted coherently. This also covers DWG-origin typed callbacks, which have
no raw DXF companion. Generated AC1027 ASCII/Binary controls assert the
Background kind/version/color, SUN state/intensity, exact object handles and
raw record identities. They then prove that export leaves a pre-existing
destination untouched; removing only the unsupported object carriers permits
same-adapter retry. No external fixture or peer was used.

Validation passed: strict build of `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests` and
`lc3_compat_check`; `--background-sun-callback-retention`,
`--view-background-sun-fail-closed`,
`--viewport-background-sun-fail-closed`,
`--vport-background-sun-fail-closed`, `--vport-shadeplot-retention`,
`--header-visual-style-references`, and
`--vport-visual-style-reference`; scoped `git diff --check`. The VPORT shade
negative controls print expected parser diagnostics and pass. Full fixture
CTest/full suite, native CAD, and peer execution were not run. No DWG parser
or writer byte layout, `DRW_Interface` ABI, fixture, CTest registration, or
dependency changed; `dx_data` gained local storage fields and consumers of
that adapter data type should rebuild from source.

### Implementation readiness status for typed Background/SUN routes

1. **Completed locally:** DXF typed Background/SUN callbacks pair with exactly
   one raw carrier by handle, owner, record kind, and source revision. DWG's
   typed-only callback lane stays distinct; no DXF tags are fabricated from
   DWG raw frames.
2. **Completed locally:** Background publication requires a unique rooted
   `ACAD_BACKGROUND` dictionary, complete typed/raw child coverage, class and
   version checks, and supported Background secondary edges. Shared viewport
   targets and unsupported cross-links remain rejected.
3. **Completed at generated structural scope:** SUN serialization is admitted
   only for a uniquely paired raw SUN whose exact owner is one VPORT table
   record or VIEWPORT entity, with the typed group-361 target and raw code-330
   owner remapped together. The low-level owner-aware raw writer also requires
   a registered SUN identity and an already-emitted source owner; its original
   one-argument API remains intact for non-SUN carriers and refuses raw SUN
   replay without the validated owner route. VIEW group 361 is not admitted.
4. **Completed locally:** generated ASCII/Binary positive controls cover both
   VPORT and VIEWPORT owner routes; wrong-owner, direct owner-overload, and
   legacy one-argument raw-SUN refusal controls preserve an existing
   destination. Keep all controls in
   the existing focused DXF fixture executable, with no downloaded drawing or
   new CTest registration.
5. **Still composed/external:** run pinned native and independent consumer
   checks only at the existing qualification checkpoint. This evidence is
   separate and must not delay other dependency-ready local work.

These routes establish bounded structural DXF preservation only. No rendering,
plotting, DWG SUN parsing, 2D/3D semantic parity, or support claim follows.
Findings/subplans remain 130/73; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The shared worktree is broadly dirty,
so the slices remain uncommitted and no unrelated files were staged.

## Deeper/broader Background consumer and carrier-boundary update (2026-10-18)

This review reconciles the local Background replay slice against the current
implementation, Autodesk's DXF/ObjectARX contracts, and LibreDWG's published
object schema. The Autodesk material is normative for the consumer-facing DXF
contract; LibreDWG is a useful independent field-model cross-check, not a
semantic acceptance oracle.

| Area | Primary-source evidence | Plan impact |
|---|---|---|
| Dictionary ownership | Autodesk's [DXF OBJECTS example](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-1038FDE4-745D-469D-972E-1F977D674882.htm) describes dictionary key group 3 and child handle group 350. Autodesk's [Background class contract](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_Background.html) says each object belongs in `ACAD_BACKGROUND`, should have a unique name, and should not be shared among viewports. | Keep one validated NOD `ACAD_BACKGROUND` dictionary, unique key/handle pairing, and reject any Background target shared by viewport consumers. This validates graph preservation, not the background's visual/render behavior. |
| Consumer references | Autodesk documents optional group 332 Background IDs on [VIEW](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-CF3094AB-ECA9-43C1-8075-7791AC84F97C.htm), [VPORT](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-8CE7CC87-27BD-4490-89DA-C21F516415A9.htm), and [VIEWPORT](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-2602B0FB-02E4-4B9A-B03C-B1D904753D34.htm). The VIEWPORT schema separately lists optional group 333 shade-plot, 348 visual-style, and 361 SUN references. | Treat group 332 as a typed edge, never as an arbitrary numeric tag. Resolve it to a rooted Background and remap it on output. Keep the other reference slots independently validated; 333/348/361 evidence does not authorize Background/SUN interchange. |
| Background subclasses and secondary links | Autodesk's 2024 [Background class hierarchy](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_Background.html) enumerates Solid, Gradient, GroundPlane, IBL, Image, Sky, and Skylight types. The DXF [RAPIDRTRENDERENVIRONMENT schema](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2016/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-E0D55EE1-54C2-4C0E-A458-919E2E677595.htm) has group 340 for its custom-background edge; Autodesk's [IBL API](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2027/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OARX-RefGuide-AcDbIBLBackground__MEMBERTYPE_Methods_AcDbIBLBackground.html) limits that secondary background to Solid, Gradient, or Image and says its ownership is assumed. | The local same-version path now closes IBL group-340 edges only when typed and raw identities agree, the target is a unique rooted Solid/Gradient/Image object, handle remapping preserves the edge, and no direct VIEW/VPORT/VIEWPORT consumer also references the secondary target. GroundPlane/IBL/Sky targets reject. Keep Skylight-to-SUN closed until its separate owner semantics and remap path are qualified. |
| Cross-project schema check | LibreDWG's [published OBJECTS schema](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/OBJECTS.html) exposes parent/class-version and subtype data for Background objects, including IBL/Skylight reference fields. | Use it to build a field/edge checklist and to detect missing local captures. Do not infer complete DWG or DXF support from schema presence or another implementation's parser/writer. |

### Current implementation state and next slices

PAR-40 / 7G.2 now accepts VIEW, VPORT, and VIEWPORT group-332 edges only when
the target is present in the validated `ACAD_BACKGROUND` dictionary at the
exact captured DXF revision. VIEW references are resolved but do not count as
viewport owners; VPORT and VIEWPORT targets are counted together and duplicate
viewport ownership is rejected. Low-level writers remap group 332 only when
the adapter registers the rooted target set; direct codec calls remain
fail-closed by default.

The same graph now supports IBL group-340 secondary edges after typed/raw edge
identity checks. The target must be a distinct, uniquely rooted Solid,
Gradient, or Image Background; multiple IBL owners, direct view/viewport use of
the assumed-owned secondary target, other target classes, missing targets, and
typed/raw disagreement reject before publication. The raw writer remaps the
edge with its target object. Direct typed codec calls also refuse an
unregistered IBL target and refuse a non-null Skylight-to-SUN edge. Generated
ASCII/Binary controls round-trip all six Background kinds, IBL→Solid from the
source control, and IBL→Gradient/Image variants, together with all three
consumer group-332 slots. This proves structural serialization/readback and
handle closure only—not AutoCAD rendering, consumer acceptance, or semantic 3D
support.

Current fast-control status and remaining order (no full suite per slice):

   references are checked after readback against their remapped rooted handles.

   validate the wire/ownership assumptions against a native producer/consumer

   blocker to other local slices.
3. Independently qualify whether common reactor and extension-dictionary
   carriers can be included without widening replay unsafely. Until then, keep

4. **VPORT/VIEWPORT code-361 structural path now implemented locally.**
   Generated controls exercise each carrier's typed/raw owner edge and handle

   AcDbSun hard-owner contract; keep Skylight group-340→SUN refused until its

5. At the existing composed gate, run a pinned independent DXF reader and

## Deeper/broader Background ownership and type-census update (2026-10-18)

This follow-up checks the remaining Background object links against Autodesk's
DXF object contracts and current open-source field models, then closes the
locally provable extension-dictionary route. These sources inform wire
structure and implementation boundaries; none is treated as rendering or
semantic-3D acceptance evidence.

| Topic | Research evidence | Implementation consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Root dictionary versus extension dictionary | Autodesk's [DICTIONARY DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-40B92C63-26F0-485B-A9C2-B349099B26D0.htm) defines dictionary key/child pairs and owner behavior. Its [common object codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-6939D69E-04CB-4F4C-87B2-67BC540FCF58.htm) keep `330` common ownership, `{ACAD_REACTORS}` and `{ACAD_XDICTIONARY}` app-data groups distinct. The latter carries a `360` hard-owner link; reactors use `330` soft pointers. | Background's NOD `ACAD_BACKGROUND` entry remains a separately validated root. An extension dictionary is now admitted only when one raw `{ACAD_XDICTIONARY}` / `360` edge matches the typed `xDictHandle`, the generic typed dictionary graph is fully visited, and its parent is that Background handle. Keep reactors refused; never infer one edge class from another. |
| Raw reference remapping boundary | The local raw-object writer remaps recognized DXF handle groups when a source→output mapping exists, but opaque app-data/XDATA references do not have an application-specific semantic resolver. Autodesk's standard group definitions therefore do not justify remapping arbitrary numeric groups. | The Background raw-carrier gate now rejects extra translated-handle groups, any `{ACAD_REACTORS}` group, malformed/duplicate extension-dictionary edges, and XDATA `1005` references. This keeps same-version raw replay bounded to identities and the explicitly closed Background links. |
| Peer object-model maturity | LibreDWG's [current `objects.in` schema](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/objects.in) (mutable `master`, inspected 2026-10-18) lists Solid, Gradient, GroundPlane, Image, IBL, and Skylight Background classes as `UNSTABLE`; IBL is mapped to `RAPIDRTRENDERENVIRONMENT`. Its [published OBJECTS documentation](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/OBJECTS.html) describes object coverage levels and the limits of unsupported/unhandled classes. | Use LibreDWG for class/field census and differential test selection only. Pin a commit/release for optional runs. Schema recognition or a successful conversion cannot promote structural completeness, viewport acceptance, rendering, or semantic 3D support. |
| Independent DXF implementation boundary | ezdxf's [xref documentation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst) says unknown entities/objects may be retained as `DXFTagStorage` during transfer, while most OBJECTS-section features are outside that xref module's supported scope. Its [drawing add-on](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/addons/drawing.html) exposes a configurable canvas/layout background, which is distinct from reading or evaluating AutoCAD's Background object graph. | ezdxf is useful for an independent tag/structure reopen check only when the selected operation preserves these objects. It is not a Background semantic, viewport-rendering, or ACIS-kernel oracle; record what exact route was exercised. |
| Background subclass census | Autodesk's [Background hierarchy](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_Background.html) and [SkyBackground class page](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_SkyBackground.html) expose a `SkyBackground` API subtype. Two local AC1024 sample class tables (`visualization_-_sun_and_sky_demo.dwg`, `visualization_-_condominium_with_skylight.dwg`) map `AcDbSkyBackground` to the existing `SKYLIGHT_BACKGROUND` record name, with class instance counts 11 and 51. The local six-kind enum already models this as `DRW_Background::Skylight`; the inspected LibreDWG schema likewise lists `SKYLIGHT_BACKGROUND`, not a separate `SKY_BACKGROUND`. | The class-table census resolves the naming question: do not add a speculative seventh serialized kind. The earlier 2026-10-18 baseline said both reads stopped before callbacks; a post-7BE AC1024/MV37 recheck now reports `operationSucceeded=true`, `legacyError=0`, and one warn-only CLASSES CRC mismatch, then reaches object processing (13 and 54 object parse failures respectively). CLI export still refuses, and this is not typed Background instance/owner evidence. Keep the six-kind structural claim scoped to generated DXF controls and AC1024 DWG Background/SUN semantics unqualified. Updated receipt records the superseding observation. |

### PAR-40 implementation readiness after this review

1. **Completed local slice — Background extension dictionaries.** The bounded
   object-graph planner now roots each typed Background `xDictHandle`, accepts
   a Background as a legal owner only for the visited extension dictionary,
   and requires raw/typed group-360 identity to agree before replay. Generated
   AC1027 ASCII and Binary controls cover Background → DICTIONARY → XRECORD,
   output handle remapping/readback, typed/raw edge mismatch, and wrong-owner
   atomic refusal. The standalone typed `writeBackground` codec also rejects
   unregistered extension dictionaries/reactors and opaque handle-bearing
   app-data instead of silently dropping or replaying an unclosed edge.
   Reactors and opaque handle-bearing app-data remain refused on the adapter
   path as well.
2. **Completed bounded class-table census — Sky name.** The two local AC1024
   class tables identify `AcDbSkyBackground` as `SKYLIGHT_BACKGROUND`, matching
   the existing `DRW_Background::Skylight` kind. This resolves the separate-name
   question only. Their Classes-section CRC failure precedes object callbacks,
   so do not call it a DWG instance round-trip or use it to qualify SUN,
   viewport ownership, or full DWG Background parsing. Before changing any DWG
   parse code, read the relevant chapter of the repository-mandated ODA PDF and
   capture a passing trace.
3. **Separate edge lane — reactors and SUN.** Reactors require a typed target
   family, source/output identity closure, and safe deletion/share semantics;
   they are not a shortcut through extension-dictionary traversal. Resolve

4. **Qualification gate.** At the existing composed checkpoint, run the pinned

5. **Fast implementation loop.** For each small slice: update the plan and

   targets with `-Werror`; run the smallest relevant selector and compatibility

### Implementation progress — PAR-40 / 7G.2 VPORT and VIEWPORT→SUN owner-edge replay (2026-10-18; local fast slices, uncommitted)

The focused generated control found that `writeVport` reminted the source
VPORT table-record handle and emitted its code-361 reference through the
handle map, but generic `writeRawDxfObject` treated SUN's code-330 owner as an
opaque OBJECTS reference. The raw SUN therefore retained a dangling source
owner after conversion. The fix adds an overload that accepts a validated
source-owner identity while retaining the original one-argument API entry
point; the owner-aware path requires a SUN identity in the resolved-SUN set,
an already emitted table/entity owner mapping, and exactly one code-330 group
matching both the typed raw-carrier owner and the explicit source owner. It
emits that group using the writer's source-to-output mapping. Only the already
validated SUN graph uses this overload. The legacy one-argument method
continues to support other raw objects but now refuses raw SUN carriers unless
the owner-aware validated route is used, so it cannot bypass adapter graph
preflight. The adapter still refuses unknown handle-bearing payload, reactors,
extension dictionaries, XDATA, and unsupported object/owner graphs.

Separate generated AC1027 positive controls cover ASCII and binary
VPORT-owned and VIEWPORT-owned SUN graphs, including typed code-361 edges,
typed SUN owner identity, raw SUN code-330 ownership, and re-import after the
VPORT table-record or VIEWPORT entity handle is reminted. Each owner case also
checks a typed/raw owner mismatch against an existing destination sentinel to
prove refusal is atomic. Direct calls through both raw-SUN writer entry points
also refuse without graph registration and preserve a destination sentinel.
No downloaded or persistent DWG/DXF fixture was introduced.

Validation passed: strict `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests` and
`lc3_compat_check` targets; `--vport-sun-owner-graph`,
`--viewport-sun-owner-graph`,
`--background-sun-callback-retention`, `--vport-background-sun-fail-closed`,
`--viewport-background-sun-fail-closed`, and
`--view-background-sun-fail-closed`. The full CTest suite was not run. The
generated positive results qualify only the tested VPORT and VIEWPORT
structural replay paths; neither establishes native producer behavior,
viewport rendering, sun/shadow semantics, DWG SUN parsing, VIEW 361, or
Skylight→SUN. The worktree was already broadly dirty; no unrelated changes
were staged or committed. J256/J260/J268/J284/J293/J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`, with no support promotion.

### Refined peer-evidence record and conditional execution sequence

For any optional composed peer run, the evidence row must distinguish at least
these provenance axes instead of one `independent=true` flag:

1. **Implementation relation:** direct code dependency, fork/port, wrapper,
   algorithm cross-reference, or implementation-diverse source.
2. **Specification/source relation:** ODA/Autodesk reference, shared public
   reverse-engineered source, or independently authored producer evidence.
3. **Expected-value origin:** source-authored analytic manifest, peer output,
   same-codec round trip, or native-produced reference. Peer-derived expected
   values cannot validate that peer's own result.
4. **Consumer/kernel relation:** parser, converter, renderer, geometry kernel,
   and native CAD app identities must remain separate; a second UI over one
   parser or a second app over one kernel is not a second parser/kernel vote.
5. **Artifact/run identity:** exact commit/release, lockfile/submodules/build
   features, platform, input/output hashes, warnings/recovery/omission inventory,
   and named operation.

Conditional sequence: (a) select a concrete local question and one peer route;
(b) check source and dependency lineage before installing/running anything;
(c) use a locally authored in-memory/scratch control with an independently
written expected manifest; (d) record parse, typed/raw retention, graph closure,
projection, native acceptance, and semantic result as separate fields; (e) if
the exact input, provenance, or expected manifest is unavailable, record
`NOT_RUN` and continue local work. No peer setup or extra test is added to the
per-slice loop; touched-target strict build, focused fast selector, compatibility
check, and relevant atomic-refusal assertions remain the default.

### Refined composed-gate sequence; no change to the fast per-slice loop

1. Keep the fast implementation loop local: touched-target strict build,
   generated focused tests, 2D compatibility, raw carrier identity, graph
   closure, and fail-closed publication checks. Do not add a peer install,
   native CAD run, full suite, or external fixture to every slice.
2. At the existing composed consumer gate, run the *named* stock-FreeCAD
   converter/importer profile on Linux and Windows for its supported 2D and
   explicit-entity scope; record importer backend, source/output hashes,
   entity disposition, warnings and recovery. Do not use stock FreeCAD as an
   ACIS or AcDs semantic gate.
3. Keep CAD-kernel evaluation separate: use one pinned candidate only after
   source lineage, dependencies, accepted SAB profile, and required operations
   are verified. Measure the same source-authored analytic control and report
   parser completeness, body count, validity/closure, units, bounds, area and
   volume independently. Then separately verify source entity → owner/key →
   AcDs/ACDSDATA record → exact bytes.
4. For writer readiness, require all of: per-object disposition (including
   explicit refusal/diagnostic for unsupported data), entity and dictionary/
   owner-reference closure, strict independent readback, and native audit/open
   for the named target version. Keep LibreCAD 3's read-only DWG policy outside
   library writer acceptance until the consumer makes a separate decision.
5. Treat peer issues and open PRs as test-design signals only. Pin a released
   source artifact for comparison; label branch experiments separately and
   never use them to promote support.

## Implementation progress — PAR-39 / 7BU independent DXF chunk and legacy-width walk (2026-10-18; local fast slice)

Extended the existing generated binary writer boundary control with an
independent byte walk for group 1004 and the 310/319 binary-chunk range. The
walker checks ordered two-byte codes, each length byte, exact payload bytes,
all scalar widths (1/2/4/8), and complete EOF consumption without calling the
production group-code classifier. A separate fixed-byte expectation now
checks the explicit LibreCAD-legacy profile's group-260 one-byte Boolean,
group-482 eight-byte double, and following EOF record.

The owning Wave 1 test also exposed an outdated generic common-object vector:
it attached unrooted reactor/extension-dictionary edges and handle-bearing
app-data to `DRW_Background`, whose writer correctly refuses those unclosed
references. The generic test now exercises Background's representable common
text metadata only; rooted Background graph edges remain under the dedicated
graph-preservation controls. This changes no production writer behavior and
does not relax the fail-closed rule.

Validation passed: strict `libdxfrw_wave1_tests` build; focused
`--dxf-code-type-boundaries`; owning `libdxfrw_wave1` CTest (1/1); and

changed, so the LibreCAD compatibility target was not rerun for this test-only
slice. No full suite, external peer/native run, fixture file, dependency, or

qualification remain open. No format or 3D support claim is promoted;

## Implementation progress — PAR-34 / 7Q.2 HATCH gradient field grammar (2026-10-18; local fast slice)

Implemented presence-aware validation for the DXF HATCH gradient block in
ASCII and Binary parsing. A gradient block is now rejected when required
companions are missing or orphaned; duplicate numeric singleton controls,
invalid stop counts/order, invalid active mode/reserved values, non-finite
scalars, and out-of-range active single-color tint fail closed. Solid blocks
still require the documented companion fields and zero stop count, but the
other present values are ignored as Autodesk specifies. Active API gradient
payloads receive the corresponding preflight checks. Group 431 remains a
string/unknown-policy field, and 432/433's entity-specific name/book semantics
remain unresolved.

Compatibility detail: repeated group 470 is accepted with last-value-wins.
Autodesk's HATCH gradient rule requires the group but does not define duplicate
handling, while the existing reader contract tests transactional replacement
of retained text under an exact byte budget. A focused generated control now
locks that behavior for both ASCII and Binary instead of silently weakening
the pre-existing owner-lifetime test.

Validation passed: strict `libdxfrw_wave1_tests` and
`libdxfrw_hardening_tests` builds; focused
`--hatch-gradient-dxf-grammar`; owning `libdxfrw_wave1` and
`libdxfrw_hardening` CTests (2/2); rebuilt `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests` and
`libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures` CTest (1/1); `lc3_compat_check` from the earlier
public-header portion of this slice; and `git diff --check` / receipt JSON
validation. The initial hardening regression exposed that rejecting duplicate
470 bypassed the retained-text replacement contract; allowing the documented
presence requirement with compatible last-value-wins behavior resolved it.
No full suite, peer/native run, new fixture, dependency, CTest registration,
support claim, or J-item transition was added. The worktree remains broadly
dirty and this slice remains uncommitted; unrelated changes were not staged.

unqualified group range; the values remain on the public model for callers.

## Implementation progress — PAR-39 / 7X shared numeric sink-kind guard (2026-10-18; local fast slice)

Factored the active profile comparison into `dxfWriter::valueKindMatches()`
and applied it to the numeric typed methods in both writer formats. Binary
already enforced the classifier at its sink; ASCII now refuses mismatched
numeric method/group-code pairs before emitting the group or value. The active
classifier profile remains explicit, so the LibreCAD legacy overrides for
260–269 and 482–998 are still tested separately from the standalone-safe
profile. I16 range checks and finite-double checks are unchanged.

The generated ASCII boundary control exercises canonical string/double/I16/
I32/I64/Boolean/binary-chunk tags, parses the resulting ordered record stream
through its EOF sentinel, and checks wrong-kind and unassigned numeric routes
leave the output empty. A legacy-profile pair accepts Boolean 260 and double
482 while rejecting I32 260. Source inspection of numeric methods with
nonliteral codes records these owners: DIMSTYLE schema-driven dispatch;
appData assigned-kind dispatch; fixed code families for POLYFACE indices,
table-cell border arrays and MLEADER coordinate bases; version-paired proxy
count 92/I32 versus 160/I64; fixed XDATA 1070/1071 dispatch; and raw/typed
variant paths that classify before selecting the sink method. These remain
distinct routes rather than evidence that every DXF field's semantics or
version floor is qualified.

## Implementation progress — PAR-39 / 7BU ASCII string sink-kind guard (2026-10-18; local fast slice)

The numeric writer guard from the preceding PAR-39 slice covered `I16`,
`I32`, `I64`, double, and Boolean methods, but the ordinary ASCII string sink
still accepted a string at any legal group code. That allowed an API caller
to serialize a numeric/Boolean code through the wrong typed method, while the
Binary string sink already rejected that mismatch. Ordinary ASCII
`writeString()` now requires the active classifier profile to identify a
string or binary-chunk code. ASCII groups 1004 and 310–319 retain their text
hex spelling, with even-length, hexadecimal, and 127-byte chunk bounds checked
before output. The separate `writeRawString()` route preserves validated
source spellings for raw ASCII replay, including numeric/Boolean spellings and
unknown codes; the caller's raw-group preflight remains responsible for
lexeme/type/provenance validation. Binary behavior is unchanged.

Generated controls exercise valid string/numeric/binary-chunk records through
an EOF sentinel; reject ordinary string writes at integer, Boolean, and
unknown codes without emitting bytes; reject malformed or overlong chunks;
preserve explicit raw unknown strings; honor the legacy 260/482 profile; and
reject a dynamically selected numeric continuation code through both UTF-8
chunk helpers and the UTF-8 string wrapper.
The first full Wave 1 attempt exposed that raw ASCII replay intentionally
preserves validated source spellings even when a group is numerically typed;
the implementation was adjusted to preserve that established contract rather
than applying typed-sink policy to raw replay.

Validation: strict GCC `libdxfrw_wave1_tests` build; focused
`--dxf-code-type-boundaries`; owning `libdxfrw_wave1` CTest (1/1);
`libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests` strict build and `libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures` CTest
(1/1); strict `libdxfrw_writer_primitives_tests` and
`libdxfrw_writer_version_matrix_tests` builds; writer-primitives,
writer-version-matrix, and MLEADER-writer CTests (3/3);
`lc3_compat_check`; and `git diff --check`. No full CTest suite,
sanitizer/fuzz run, peer/native run, external fixture, dependency, new CTest
registration, or support claim was added. This is one local safety boundary
under existing PAR-39/7BU work, not completion of the whole group-code
contract. Counts remain 130 findings / 73 top-level subplans; J256, J260,
J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

The bounded literal census of direct `writeString(<integer>, ...)` calls in
`src/libdxfrw.cpp` and `src/intern/dxfwriter.cpp` found 38 distinct codes; the
only `Bin` codes are 1004 and 310, and the rest are `Str` under both supported
profiles. This is not a repository-wide or dynamic-call proof.

The initial bounded dynamic review of DIMSTYLE schema dispatch, appData
assigned-kind dispatch, UTF-8 chunk/string wrappers, and validated raw replay
was not exhaustive: a focused follow-up found that `writeAppData()` admitted
unknown string groups for ASCII but sent them through the ordinary typed
string sink, which correctly rejects unknown codes. The appData emission path
now uses the explicit raw sink only for that already-validated
`Unknown && !binFile` case; recognized strings, binary chunks, handles, and
all Binary unknown-code refusals retain their prior routes. Generated code-482
ASCII/Binary controls verify byte-exact ASCII output with a following EOF
sentinel and Binary refusal before any output. The rest of the dynamic census
remains bounded, not a proof for every call site or profile override. Next
unblocked local step: continue the PAR-39 inventory by writer family and
emitted-byte path, adding focused controls only for uncovered branches or
reproduced mismatches. For each route, verify that kind selection precedes
emission and raw preservation is admitted only after its existing validation.
Keep binary-chunk syntax separate and do not infer field semantics or version
floors from the generic group-code classifier. Full peer/native validation
remains at the composed checkpoint; unrelated local implementation continues
meanwhile.

for ASCII while refusing that representation for Binary, but the emitter
previously passed the ASCII value to ordinary `writeString()`, whose typed
sink rejects unknown group codes. After the same complete-group validation
and opaque-text preflight, only the `Unknown && !binFile` case now uses
`writeRawString()`; all assigned string/handle/binary kinds continue through
the typed sink, and unknown Binary values still fail before any group opener
is emitted.

The generated in-memory control writes code 482 inside a balanced appData
group, checks the exact ASCII spelling and a following group-0 `WIRE_END`
sentinel, and confirms the same unknown value is refused by Binary with an
empty destination. No persistent DWG/DXF fixture, CTest registration, public
header/API change, dependency, or output-profile change was added. This
closes only the validated unknown-string appData emission branch; it does not
complete the dynamic call-site census or establish support for arbitrary
unknown codes outside this prevalidated ASCII appData route.

## Implementation progress — PAR-39 / 7X.7 XRECORD coordinate-base and extended-code compatibility (2026-10-18; local fast slice)

The typed XRECORD writer now rejects `COORD` variants that do not begin at an
X component with valid Y/Z follower codes in the same point family used by
`DRW_XRecord::parseCode`. This prevents a model point at a Y/Z component code
from being serialized as a different, shifted point. The rule mirrors the
local parser's point-code families rather than imposing Autodesk's narrower
published XRECORD list as a blanket code filter.

That distinction preserves existing extension behavior: the local parser
classifies 480/481 as XRECORD handle values, and the Wave 1
`testDxfArbitraryHandlePayloads` control requires those values to survive the
typed XRECORD writer. An initial 1–369 cap failed that owner test and was
reverted; code 480/481 and other previously accepted scalar/string/handle
routes remain unchanged. Autodesk's [XRECORD reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-24668FAF-AE03-41AE-AFA4-276C3692827F.htm)
and [group-code table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2022/ENU/OARX-DevGuide/files/GUID-F8B4190D-CCC6-4CAB-BDAE-71A7094FB442.htm)
remain the documented standard profile; the extra local families are not
promoted to universal XRECORD compatibility.

Generated ASCII/Binary controls reject COORD bases 18, 20, 30, and 38 before
replacing an existing destination. Point base 17 round-trips. The typed
writer change does not affect raw-object replay or DWG XRECORD encoding. No
repository drawing, dependency, public API/layout change, or CTest
registration was added.

Validation passed: strict `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests` and
`libdxfrw_wave1_tests` builds with `-Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Werror`;

run exposed the overbroad code cap; after narrowing the change to COORD base
validation, both owners passed. No full suite, peer/native run, sanitizer/fuzz

J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. This slice remains

cannot encode safely: finite scalar values, finite coordinate components

## Implementation progress — PAR-59 / 7P.5b.1 IMAGEDEF source-callback retention (2026-10-18; local fast slice)

`dx_data` now owns full `DRW_ImageDef` callback values in a map keyed by the
current import generation and source handle. The generation is also captured
on each adapter IMAGE, so an IMAGEDEF callback only supplies a path to matching
images from the same import. Two definitions with the same filename but
different source handles remain separate, while multiple IMAGE instances may
still share one source definition. Invalid zero/sentinel handles mark that
generation; repeated handles are recorded as conflicts, retain the original
definition, and are not allowed to overwrite existing path bindings.

Generated adapter controls populate and inspect class version, pixel dimensions,
pixel sizes, loaded/resolution state, owner, extension-dictionary handle,
reactors, application data, and XDATA. They verify shared versus distinct
same-path definitions, copied ownership after callback-source mutation,
import-generation isolation, invalid-handle marking, and duplicate-handle
refusal. These controls run from the existing generated image-path CTest; no
fixture or test registration was added. Only CLI-internal adapter structures
changed; no installed `DRW_Interface` callback or library API changed.

list are emitted from the same graph. Duplicate basename dictionary keys are
made unique without rewriting the IMAGEDEF's original file name.

was added or committed.

## Deeper/broader ACIS consumer-route closure and independent-kernel boundary (2026-10-18; research only)

This pass broadened the route inventory from codec/kernel candidates to the
actual open-source application/plugin path available for DXF-carried solids,
then checked what a standard open-source OCCT installation can and cannot
provide. It reconciles the route roles rather than adding a new support lane.
Only primary project documentation, source/manifests, and the official OCCT
announcement were inspected; no peer was installed, built, or run, no drawing
was downloaded, and no local source or test changed.

| Route/evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Open CASCADE's [data-exchange component announcement](https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/discussions/1157) and [supported-format overview](https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/wiki) | OCCT's announcement separates open-source core formats from commercial extensions and explicitly lists ACIS SAT/SAB import/export among the commercial components. Therefore the open-source OCCT kernel used by FreeCAD is not, by itself, an ACIS reader. Older release-note entries for ACIS code do not establish that those proprietary exchange modules ship in a current public OCCT package. | Do not assume a FreeCAD or distro OCCT install contains a usable SAT/SAB reader. Treat a commercial OCCT ACIS component as an optional, separately licensed route; it is not a required open-source dependency or an independent-kernel result. |
| FreeCAD [Addon Reports](https://freecad.github.io/Addon-Reports/) and the [InventorLoader project README](https://github.com/jmplonka/InventorLoader), [DXF importer](https://github.com/jmplonka/InventorLoader/blob/master/importerDXF.py), and [SAT importer](https://github.com/jmplonka/InventorLoader/blob/master/importerSAT.py) | InventorLoader is a real, separate open-source plugin route: its DXF wrapper uses ezdxf to extract each 3DSOLID's SAT/SAB payload and its own `AcisReader` before constructing FreeCAD Part shapes. The project reports SAT/SAB and DXF-solid import, no export, and documented unsupported blend surfaces, some helix surfaces, and law-based interpolated geometry. The current FreeCAD addon catalog lists version 1.5.1 with a stale last-update indication; its README's minimum-FreeCAD guidance is also old. Public issue reports describe sample-specific SAT/SAB and face/normal problems; none was reproduced here. It does not read DWG or join DWG AcDs records. | Admit it only as an optional **DXF-carrier → independent SAT/SAB parser → FreeCAD/OCCT shape** probe, pinned to a source revision, add-on release, FreeCAD build, ezdxf version, and import strategy. Require every source entity to have a disposition; separate unsupported/missing geometry, invalid/open shapes, and transform/units mismatches. Do not call it a DWG reader, whole-document fidelity oracle, or second kernel. If the current FreeCAD/Python route is incompatible or not already available, mark `NOT_RUN` and continue. |
| OpenCADStudio's [current application manifest](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/Cargo.toml), [3D feature declarations](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio), and existing OpenCADKernel route review above | The current manifest identifies app version `2026.41.0`, pins its `acadrust`-named codec to OpenCADCodec `5d4f11a`, and pins OpenCADKernel `a60f18f` with the `acis` feature. The codec is an ACadRust descendant; the kernel is a separate, unreleased implementation candidate whose ACIS path has explicit loss/fallback reporting. These pins describe one composed application route, not independent parser votes or proof that a released binary used the same graph. | Preserve exact application/codec/kernel revision and feature identity. It may be considered as an optional downstream application/render observation, but only after per-handle payload and transform closure; record loss/fallback and do not treat the UI, mesh, or same-stack save/reopen as the independent expected geometry. |
| `cq-acis` [SAB/ASM support](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/docs/sab-support.md), [geometry limits](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/docs/geometry-support.md), and `acis-core` [model contract](https://docs.rs/acis-core/latest/acis_core/) | It is a distinct parser/model route for bare SAT/SAB with explicit profile admission; its model constructor proves index/reference closure, not B-rep validity. Its docs retain unknown records and SAB history opaquely, document finite conversion profiles, and identify history/current-state limitations. Conversion uses CadQuery/OCCT, so it is a potentially useful parser-plus-geometry check for an admitted exact payload, but not an independent geometry-kernel vote relative to FreeCAD. `cadmpeg-codec-sat` remains a separate optional read-only route with its own L1/profile limits; the projects cite some shared grammar references, so their source assumptions are not wholly uncorrelated. | Keep each package, source commit, platform wheel/build, parser result, loss/raw-record disposition, and kernel lineage separate. Use `cq-acis` only when the exact extracted signature/save profile is admitted; require complete requested-body/reference coverage, zero unsupported required topology, valid closed geometry, and independent analytic expectations. Never infer outer DWG AcDs ownership or history correctness from a bare-stream parse. |

### Shortest implementation-ready route gate

1. **Finish local carrier/graph proof first.** Keep inline DXF ACIS groups and
   DWG AcDs/DataStorage extraction as different routes. Before any external
   reader receives bytes, independently record source entity type/handle,
   owning block/INSERT path and transform, AcDs prototype/key when applicable,
   full payload hash/length, and exact SAT/SAB signature/save version.
2. **Select one eligible route for the unanswered question.** For stock FreeCAD,
   record only the selected Linux/Windows 2D backend and report solids as
   `NOT_CONSUMED_BY_STOCK_DXF_ROUTE`. For DXF-carried solids, InventorLoader is
   an optional older plugin/parser route if the exact current host can load it.
   For an admitted bare stream, prefer the already-scoped `cq-acis` or
   CADMPEG probe only at the existing composed checkpoint. Do not install or
   run the whole peer matrix after each code slice.
3. **Keep semantic expectations external to the codec.** Generate or use an
   already-authorized from-scratch analytic body; record units, placement,
   expected topology, closed/valid status, bounds, area, volume, and centroid
   before parsing. Require complete body/entity disposition and no unreported
   fallback, unsupported required records, or partial conversion. A parser's
   entity count, a valid mesh, a same-reader roundtrip, or an OCCT shape alone
   is not the expected answer.
4. **Do not conflate kernels.** FreeCAD, InventorLoader, and `cq-acis` share
   OCCT-family geometry. OpenCADStudio's kernel is a distinct but unreleased
   candidate coupled to an ACadRust-descended codec. Neither family currently
   supplies a released, reproducible, independent non-OCCT kernel result for
   the target source payloads. If the existing independent-kernel requirement
   cannot be satisfied, record `CARRIER_PRESERVED / SEMANTICS_NOT_QUALIFIED`;
   do not block local work or promote a support claim.
5. **Keep the cadence fast.** No ordinary slice gains an external app/kernel
   run, fixture, dependency, or full suite. Run a single composed route only
   after the local feature/profile gate is ready; record unavailable tools as
   `NOT_RUN`, and continue with the next implementation slice.

This route closure adds no local defect, PAR finding, or top-level subplan and
does not change the implementation queue or fast-validation cadence. Findings
and top-level subplans remain 130/73. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; source availability, app feature claims, and a
shared-OCCT result do not promote them.

This pass widened the peer comparison from codec declarations and 3D payload

reader/writer failure reports. It reviewed public project documentation and

This is current project policy documentation, not a new inspection of the pinned vendored source or a permanent policy promise. | Split library capability from LibreCAD 3 product support and by direction. Do not let this alter the local DXF/DWG implementation queue. |

Exercise a repeated-record case only when the corresponding loop is touched; never derive a parser cap from the peer's crash counts. Keep VERTEX subtype inference separate from the documented R12 grammar and existing R12 marker-omission writer control; only a source-backed/profile-specific local input witness can open a new parser change. |
| ACadSharp open [#1297](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1297) and [#1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) | #1297 reports AutoCAD 2025 rejecting an AC1032 file with MTEXT flag 90=16, while flag 90=17 and AC1027 work. The reporter says the serialized MTEXT object became byte-identical to an AutoCAD object after a change, yet the file still failed and the actual cause was not proven. #1195 reports ACadSharp 3.4.9 silently omitting DWG-read 3DSOLID/REGION entities from DXF output, including block-only solids. These are exact peer/version reports; neither is a libdxfrw regression or normative file-format rule. | For any native rejection, retain the whole-file boundary: entity bytes, classes/tables/dictionaries, referenced objects, and version profile must be considered; object-byte equality is not a whole-file pass. For PAR-59, count/identity-check every source solid and its output disposition, including nested block owners; separate opaque group-1/3 carrier preservation from geometric interpretation. Keep 90=16 as an optional reproducer lead only—no speculative DWG writer or MTEXT change from an unresolved peer report. |
| LibreDWG open [#1357](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1357), [#1409](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1409), and [#1351](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1351) | The reports describe distinct writer failure modes: an unresolved entity reference terminating the rest of a layout, mutation of an outer loop index skipping later block bodies, and an INSERT attribute-follow flag without an ATTRIB/SEQEND sequence. The #1351 report notes a later fix on LibreDWG master for its exact reproducer; none demonstrates a matching local defect. | Keep the existing writer closure checks as independent invariants: every source entity has exactly one emitted/explicitly refused disposition; each BLOCK_RECORD/BLOCK/ENDBLK and child owner is closed; INSERT flag 66 agrees with actual child and SEQEND framing; an error cannot be confused with end-of-list; and a neighboring-record sentinel follows every malformed/unsupported item. Use generated cases in existing owners, not peer/customer drawings or a new routine peer matrix. |

### Implementation-ready decision and test order

1. **Keep product claims directional.** Preserve the existing reader qualification
   and `WITH_DWG_IMPORT` boundary for LibreCAD 3. Do not promise app-side DWG
   writing unless the project explicitly reopens that decision. Library-level

2. **Close local structure before external comparison.** On each touched path,
   assert its source identity, owner/layout/block path, record count, output
   disposition, following-record alignment, and whole-output closure. For the

3. **Use the narrow owning fast test.** Add at most the relevant in-memory or

   when shared contracts change, and owning CTest; do not add a full-suite or
   native run to every item.
4. **Use peer/native routes only at a composed checkpoint.** Pin exact release
   or commit, direction, version, options, input/output hashes, diagnostics,
   and per-source disposition. A peer issue, parser success, exit code, object
   byte match, or aggregate entity count alone is not acceptance. Classify an

5. **No new local issue is opened by this review.** Reuse PAR-14/PAR-26,

   owners. Do not adopt ACadSharp's VERTEX recovery proposal or infer the

## Implementation progress — PAR-59 / 7P.5b.7 IMAGEDEF wire evidence and group-12 writer correction (2026-10-18; local fast slice)

The generated IMAGEDEF discriminator now locates and verifies its raw wire
fields without `dxfReaderAscii`, `dxfReaderBinary`, or another libdxfrw parser.
The ASCII test scanner parses group-code/value line pairs; the Binary DXF
scanner checks the 22-byte signature, R13+ 16-bit little-endian group codes,
and the documented value-width classes needed to walk the generated records.
The generated IMAGEDEF includes XDATA group 1001/1000 so the scanner exercises
those string-value types in both encodings. Both scanners capture literal
code-12/code-21 order before a separate fresh libdxfrw import checks the
current typed projection, XDATA, and following loaded/resolution sentinels.
This narrow scanner does not implement R12 one-byte/escape framing; it is not a
generalized DXF parser or normative mapping oracle. Separately, the versioned
Autodesk references listed in the evidence table settle the DXF wire mapping:
the writer now emits group 12 for `vp`, while `parseCode` retains both group
12 and legacy group 21 input handling. The ezdxf source-model discrepancy is
not treated as proof of emitted bytes, and its writer was not executed.

Validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests -j2`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --image-def-pixel-size-code-forms`
  (focused selector; generated ASCII/Binary × five-form matrix passed)
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^(libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures|dwg2dxf_image_path_cli)$' --output-on-failure` (2/2)
- `git diff --check -- tests/dxf_fixture_tests.cpp DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md`

An initial attempt to interpret `0xFF` as an extended group-code escape failed
the generated matrix. Inspection of the active AC1027 writer showed this
R13+-profile uses 16-bit little-endian group codes, so the helper was narrowed
to that profile instead of claiming R12 framing support; the focused matrix
then passed.

The IMAGEDEF DXF writer changed from group 21 to the documented group 12;
the reader remains dual-tolerant. No fixture file, dependency, support claim,
or J transition changed; no full suite or new CTest registration was run. Findings/subplans
remain 130/73 and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The remaining 7P.5b work is optional transformed U/V
bounds consumer observation and a native-producer witness if a future change
would narrow compatibility or claim native acceptance. The output mapping
change itself is supported by versioned primary DXF documentation. The broad
shared worktree remains uncommitted; unrelated changes were preserved.

## Implementation progress — PAR-59 / generated multi-chunk modeler carrier readback (2026-10-18; local fast slice)

The broader peer review surfaced LibreDWG's release-note report of a dropped
final SAT block. That report is not assumed to reproduce in libdxfrw. A local
coverage gap did exist at the public DXF readback helper: the direct
`DRW_ModelerGeometry` readback used only a short carrier, while the separate
writer matrix asserted long serialized tags but did not directly assert the
decoded retained bytes and chunk map.

The focused generated carrier now spans 511 printable bytes: two complete
255-byte DXF chunks plus a one-byte final chunk, with a distinctive
`FINAL-PAYLOAD` sentinel in the tail. It is exported and publicly read back as
ASCII AC1018 and Binary DXF AC1021. The assertion checks exact concatenated
carrier bytes, the final sentinel, the expected chunk count, contiguous
offsets, the group-1 initial chunk/group-3 continuation order, and the 255-byte
per-value limit. The existing multi-version ASCII/Binary writer matrix remains
the neighboring wire-output check. This is a generated opaque-carrier
preservation regression only; it does not parse SAT grammar, reproduce the
LibreDWG failure, or establish ACIS/solid semantics.

Validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip -j2`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip --modeler-dxf-long-carrier`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip --modeler-dxf-matrix`
- `git diff --check -- tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md`

The first strict build exposed a pre-existing test initializer made stale by
the newly explicit `m_hasObjectOsnapType` member: the old three-value
aggregate placed the object handle into the new `bool`. It was corrected to
initialize the presence flag as false, after which the target built cleanly.
No owning broad CTest, full suite, peer, or native application was run; there
was no new CTest registration, committed fixture, production-code change, or
support-claim promotion. Findings/subplans remain 130/73, and J256, J260,
J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. Continue with the next
dependency-ready local owner. The generated PAR-59 text-tail, chunk-map, and
following-record boundaries now pass; native and consumer qualification stays
at the composed gate and does not block other local work.

## Implementation progress — common DIMENSION Flags 1 parser direction (2026-10-18; local fast slice)

The parser-direction follow-up from the DIMENSION research pass is now covered
inside the existing `--verify-dimension-frames` owner. The test builds the
common DIMENSION fields from low-level DWG writer primitives rather than
calling `encodeDwgDimBase`, then patches Flags 1 as an independent raw RC. It
checks raw bytes 0, 1, 2, and 3 against decoded DXF flag states `0x80`, `0`,
`0xA0`, and `0x20` for AC1018, AC1021, and AC1024. Version framing includes
R2010's leading DIMENSION byte, the R2007+ detached UTF-16 string stream and
versioned text codec, object-size/handle boundaries, exact common-body cursor,
known text/point values, and a following-frame sentinel. The first run exposed
that the test reader lacked the R2007+ text codec; fixing the test setup made
the text assertion meaningful without changing production behavior.

Validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip -j2`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^dwg2dxf_dimension_frames_' --output-on-failure` (2/2)
- `git diff --check -- tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md docs/research/dwg-common-dimension-flag-parser-wire-fast-slice-2026-10-18.json`

This closes only the common DIMENSION Flags 1 base-parser mapping and its
versioned body boundary. It does not qualify concrete subclass fields,
AutoCAD edit/regeneration behavior, independent peer parsing, or general
dimension support. No production code, public API/layout, persistent fixture,

This pass rechecked current primary project documentation and release notes
against the existing peer matrix. Its main result is a sharper *admission and
scoring rule*, not another parser feature claim: the same file can pass a
container read, lose records during a converter or cross-document copy, and
then import only a subset into a CAD consumer. Those are separate outcomes.
No peer was installed, built, or run; no drawing was downloaded; no test,
fixture, dependency, source implementation, or support claim changed.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [0.14.1 `NEWS`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | The current release record gives concrete but distinct hardening cases: a decompression buffer shrinking below a still-larger logical stream, count×maximum-size arithmetic overflow, unvalidated R2004/R2007 section offsets/ranges, object pointers invalidated by container growth, and pre-R13 malformed-end no-progress loops. These are source/release-specific failure mechanisms; they do not establish a matching libdxfrw defect or a normative input limit. | Keep these under the existing bounded-section/decompression, checked-arithmetic, identity/ownership, and forward-progress owners (PAR-14/PAR-26/PAR-49 and the existing writer/modeler owners). For a changed local path, test only its invariant: capacity versus logical length, overflow/underflow edge, identity after growth, or cursor advancement, with the smallest useful following-record/object sentinel. Do not combine them into one generic size test or copy peer thresholds. |

Its DWG route converts through a selected external converter and then calls the DXF importer; the inspected LibreDWG wrapper path treats expected output-file existence as conversion success. This documents a composed route and a handoff risk, not a qualification result for any installed build. | Keep two consumer rows: (1) libdxfrw-produced DXF opened directly by the pinned selected importer; (2) DWG→named converter→fresh intermediate DXF→that importer. For row 2, record converter identity/arguments/status/logs, fresh output identity/hash, DXF version/strict parse, then importer result. Never attribute converter success to the DXF importer, or stock FreeCAD’s 2D route to ACIS/B-rep support. |

This does not describe ezdxf’s base document parser or general same-document read/write behavior. | Keep parser-open, same-document rewrite, cross-document XREF, downgrade, projection, and rendering as distinct peer operations. For XREF results, compare source-to-destination identities and report each unsupported/omitted item; success or no exception is not a complete-copy result. Do not broaden this operation-specific limitation into a claim that ezdxf’s base parser drops the same data. |

Do not spend a peer build/run unless it can answer a named unresolved container/field question with overlapping AC code and independently expected values; keep its skip/error/boundary counts and corpus date attached to the exact artifact. |

### Implementation-ready admission and execution rules

1. **Name the question before selecting a peer.** State the disputed field or
   record, source version, read/write direction, operation, and expected value.
   If no concrete disagreement exists, record `NOT_ADMITTED`; do not run a
   broad peer cohort to produce more aggregate percentages.

   build profile, platform, converter/importer options, and input hash. Identify
   parser, converter, projection, and kernel lineage separately. A result
   counts only for the operation and fields that exact artifact exposes.

   input with independently stated semantic values, bounded exact consumption
   and progress, plus a following-record/object sentinel. For a changed writer,
   inspect emitted physical tags/bytes with a test-side scanner and verify
   output closure. Run the owning focused CTest only; do not add a test
   registration or broad suite when an existing target owns the behavior.
4. **Report dispositions, not just process status.** Preserve per-source
   identity and classify each record as typed, raw-retained, projected,

   peer's model as a matching zero/default.
5. **Defer expensive evidence.** Full suites, fuzz/sanitizer campaigns,
   independent peer builds, and native Linux/Windows CAD runs remain at the
   already-planned composed checkpoints. Do not commit external peer/customer
   drawings; only use existing repository samples or local scratch controls
