## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.66 MPOLYGON fill-color name retention (2026-10-18; local fast slice)

The uncharged DXF group-430 `DRW_MPolygon::fillColorName` destination now uses
`replaceDxfRetainedStringField` with a private per-field byte counter on the
existing entity retained-text lease. Copy construction and assignment carry
the counter with the copied string, default move operations transfer the
lease/state, and `resetDwgState()` clears the counter before final release.
This adds private state to the public `DRW_MPolygon` layout; downstream
consumers must rebuild and binary ABI compatibility is not claimed.

Generated direct-parser tests cover the measured transient replacement peak,
exact-cap success, one-byte-under refusal with old-value/charge preservation,
reader teardown, copy construction/assignment, move construction/assignment,
and reset release. The first test run correctly showed that replacement peak
is larger than the final live string (the destination admission occurs before
the prior value is released); the control now measures that peak instead of
assuming final-size-only admission.

Validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_hardening_tests -j2`
- `cmake --build build-gcc --target lc3_compat_check -j2`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --dxf-hatch-text-owner-budget`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_hardening$' --output-on-failure` (1/1)
- `git diff --check -- src/drw_entities.h src/drw_entities.cpp tests/hardening_tests.cpp DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md docs/research/mpolygon-fill-color-name-retained-byte-owner-fast-slice-2026-10-18.json`

This pass expanded PAR-36/7U from a local skip-loop review into a format,
peer-architecture, and consumer-loss comparison. The result is a narrower
implementation contract: do not claim generic unknown-table preservation, but
make the existing well-framed skip observable and bounded. No peer was cloned,
built, or run; no external drawing was downloaded; no source, test, fixture,
dependency, or CTest registration changed.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not establish | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk [general DXF structure](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D939EA11-0CEC-4636-91A8-756640A031D3.htm), [symbol-table group codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A66D0ACA-3F43-4B2E-A0C2-2B490C1E5268.htm), and [symbol-table names and ordering](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2017/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-5AB9300F-F0AC-4ADE-89EA-A9D1D152D8B8.htm) | The documented TABLES section contains the named symbol tables APPID, BLOCK_RECORD, DIMSTYLE, LAYER, LTYPE, STYLE, UCS, VIEW, and VPORT. The grammar separates TABLE header, record stream, ENDTAB, and ENDSEC. Group 70 is a maximum/allocation hint, not an exact count/index. This is the published standard table set, not proof that vendor-specific table names cannot exist. | Keep standard-table dispatch explicit. Never use group 70 to skip, bound, or index the unknown body. Treat an unknown nested table as unsupported-but-well-framed, not as a malformed file and not as a typed standard-table callback. Preserve terminator and forward-progress validation. |
| Autodesk [TABLE entity reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D8CCD2F0-18A3-42BB-A64D-539114A07DA0.htm) | The graphical entity is named ACAD_TABLE and has entity/block-reference/table subclasses, cell payloads, and resource handles; it is not a symbol table declaration under TABLES. | Keep ACAD_TABLE entity and TABLES symbol-table support as separate PAR owners. A report or feature matrix about the graphical TABLE entity cannot establish nested unknown-symbol-table retention. |
| ezdxf current [TABLES implementation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/sections/tables.py), [table implementation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/sections/table.py), and [XREF scope](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst) | The reviewed source maps a fixed set of standard table names to explicit collections and writes those collections; it shows no generic opaque symbol-table writer. Its XREF operation separately documents ACAD_TABLE and preserved unknown tag-storage entities/objects as unsupported/ignored. The latter is a cross-document operation and says nothing about base-reader support for nested unknown symbol tables. No runtime behavior was reproduced. | Do not cite ezdxf as a positive arbitrary-table-preservation oracle or generalize XREF omission to its base reader. Its table model supports keeping libdxfrw's current public table callback contract unchanged. |
| ACadSharp open [issue #1128](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1128) | The request is for legacy files that place a bare TABLE record after HEADER without SECTION/TABLES framing; it reports silent skipping and proposes a warning/recovery path. It is not about an unknown table name inside a structurally valid TABLES section, and the issue provides no public sample. | Keep this as a separate malformed/nonstandard compatibility lead. No ACadSharp feature request or recovered file establishes valid-format PAR-36 retention or a local defect. Do not add recovery to the current critical path. |
| LibreDWG current [CLASSES/unknown-type documentation](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | Its description concerns DWG application-defined classes and opaque unknown-object bytes; retention is conditional on recognized class/profile and, for some classes, same-version rewrite with the complete unknown bit blob. That is a different binary object mechanism from ordered DXF symbol-table group pairs. | Do not transfer DWG unknown-class preservation into a DXF table contract or use its writer capability as an argument for a new callback/raw-table API. Keep class/proxy and symbol-table evidence separate. |
| Local `dxfRW::processTables()`, `DRW::OperationDiagnostic`, and `dx_iface::snapshotDxfReadOutcome()` | The nested unknown-table branch consumes through ENDTAB and rejects ENDSEC first. The public read diagnostic can carry a non-failing secondary advisory, but its list is bounded to 16 entries; the DXF adapter snapshots that diagnostic. These are current local source facts, not a completed warning implementation or proof that every frontend displays it. | Prefer a bounded skip plus observable diagnostic over retention or a new virtual callback. Add a deterministic summary/truncation outcome when more unknown tables occur than the secondary-entry budget; verify the adapter snapshot, and make frontend warning claims only after tracing its actual presentation path. |

### PAR-36 execution refinement

1. **Keep the scope narrow.** The pass is for a nested unknown table name in
   the standard TABLES framing. A malformed top-level bare TABLE remains the
   separate ACadSharp #1128 lead. ACAD_TABLE entity cells remain in their
   entity/parser and raw-carrier owners.
2. **Skip without semantic publication.** Consume recognized group-code/value
   records only through ENDTAB; do not publish guessed records, synthesize
   dependencies, or use group 70 as a body length. A structurally malformed
   terminator sequence still fails the tables phase.
3. **Make loss visible and bounded.** Emit a non-failing
   `unsupported-table-skipped` secondary advisory with phase, table name, and
   offset if available. The existing diagnostic capacity is 16 entries, so a
   capped aggregate must report total skipped count and that per-table details
   were truncated; it must not silently drop all advisories after the cap.
4. **Validate only the needed route.** Generated ASCII coverage uses repeated
   tags, group-102 application data, XDATA, and handle groups, followed by a
   known-table sentinel. Binary coverage is admitted only for codes whose
   widths the shared reader already knows. Keep ENDTAB/ENDSEC negatives and
   per-read diagnostic reset in the same focused owner; no persistent sample.
5. **Preserve the fast cadence.** Run the existing focused selector plus its
   owning DXF-fixture/hardening CTest. No complete-suite run, peer installation,
   native CAD run, or external drawing is needed for this leaf. No new public
   virtual, dependency, CTest registration, support promotion, finding, or
   top-level subplan is introduced.

This review resolves one implementation-choice ambiguity inside existing
PAR-36/7U. It adds no confirmed local defect or format claim; totals remain
130 findings / 73 top-level subplans. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295

## Deeper/broader AC1021 page-profile classification and reader-matrix review (2026-10-18; research only)

This pass rechecked the AC1021/R2007 page path against the official ODA
specification, LibreDWG's merged page fix and current source, and the exact
local decoder/test owners. It sharpens the earlier coverage question into a
source-confirmed classification asymmetry: local code has an AC18-format
compatibility branch, then assumes every other AC1021 page is RS-coded. A
legitimate no-RS page would therefore be rejected or misinterpreted unless it
happens to take the AC18 branch. The peer reports such pages for four metadata
sections in one corpus, but that has not been reproduced against a local file;
the plan still does not call it a confirmed libdxfrw defect. No code, test,
fixture, dependency, test registration, or support claim changed.

| Evidence | What is established—and what is not | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ODA [Open Design Specification v5.4.1 §§5.1, 5.4, 5.13](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) | §5.1 broadly says each page may be optionally RS-encoded, compressed, or encrypted. The detailed §5.4 data-page write sequence is more specific: compression is optional when it is not shorter, but RS encoding follows checksum/padding and uses section-selected interleave; §5.13 defines RS(255,251). The map has no per-page RS-present bit. The detailed writer does not define LibreDWG's observed no-RS exception as a normative profile. | Keep compression and RS independent: `cSize == uSize` means uncompressed, not necessarily unencoded. Require RS for compressed pages. Allow only the named compatibility profile observed by LibreDWG: uncompressed page plus physical extent unequal to the computed RS extent; retain CRC mismatch as a diagnostic, not a classifier. Resolve true geometry collisions with integrity evidence or fail closed. |
| LibreDWG merged [PR #1363](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/pull/1363) and its [AC1021 page decoder](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode_r2007.c) | The merged fix traces a large LWPOLYLINE/HATCH/LAYOUT corruption report to an early copy that treated uncompressed pages as unencoded. In the reported drawing, many `cSize == uSize` pages still contained RS parity. The same PR distinguishes four apparently verbatim SummaryInfo, Preview, AppInfo, and FileDepList pages by physical page-size geometry, reporting sane decoded metadata for those pages. Current peer code has an explicit size calculation for RS-coded pages and preserves the verbatim path when the physical extent does not match. This is maintainer-reported evidence on a finite corpus, not a format-wide rule or independent semantic proof. | Keep #1363 as cross-project failure-mode evidence, not an entity-parser regression or a source for unconditional heuristic copying. The raw-page exception is a concrete candidate profile to test; the four section names are provenance labels, not a claim that every producer/file has those raw pages. |
| Local [`dwgReader21::parseDataPage`](src/intern/dwgreader21.cpp), [`captureRawDwgDataSections`](src/intern/dwgreader21.cpp), and page metadata in [`dwgreader.h`](src/intern/dwgreader.h) | The earlier source audit found an AC18 page signature branch and otherwise unconditional RS decode. The new slice adds a narrow branch for uncompressed pages whose physical extent is not the computed RS extent; this matches the classifier in LibreDWG #1363. The same decoder is reused for some raw-section capture paths, but that does not prove which consumer requests the peer-reported metadata sections. | Keep semantic section parsing and unknown/raw-section capture as separate assertions. Preserve CRC/checksum diagnostics even when this named compatibility profile is selected. Continue failing closed on unsupported geometry and unresolved RS/raw collisions; do not infer semantic correctness from page classification. |
| Local corpus and existing reader tests | The repo already has six AC1021 samples under `tests/samples/AC1021/`; `/Users/dli/doc/dwg` also contains AC1021 files including `dwgreader21_230.dwg`. The existing tablet trace reports four metadata pages with `cSize == uSize` and physical extents unequal to computed RS sizes; SummaryInfo/AppInfo bytes begin with readable metadata. However raw-prefix CRC calculations do not match the recorded CRCs, and `dwg_read_AC1021_tablet_v2010` fails with 23 AC1021 CRC mismatches. This is a candidate profile observation, not authenticated or semantically validated raw-page support. | Reuse the existing matrix target and in-memory bytes; no fixture was added. Keep the tablet sample as unresolved compatibility/CRC evidence, not a passing smoke. Compare the failure against unmodified HEAD and verify CRC field/span/seed before making a support claim; keep other local samples out of per-slice testing unless they answer that exact question. |

### Implementation-ready sub-plan: AC1021 page-profile matrix

1. **Resolve the wire profile before production changes.** Use ODA §§5.1,
   5.4, and 5.13 plus a traceable producer/page-map witness. The normative
   writer path is optional compression followed by RS; the no-RS form is a
   compatibility profile observed by LibreDWG, not a general rule from §5.1.
   Document `page.size`, `dataSize`, `cSize`, `uSize`, `startOffset`, section
   encoding, and tail padding. The peer-reported compatibility profile is
   narrowly `cSize == uSize` and physical extent unequal to the computed RS
   extent; do not extend it to compressed pages or true extent collisions.
   Continue reporting CRC results separately, and require CRC evidence to
   disambiguate a collision rather than to veto this unambiguous profile.
2. **Extend the existing test owner only.** Add an AC1021 probe beside the
   current `DataPageDecodeProbe` in `tests/dwg_reader_matrix_tests.cpp`, plus a
   focused command-line selector; keep `libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix` as the
   sole registered CTest. The probe should exercise `parseDataPage` directly
   first, so the failing transform is isolated from section/entity parsing.
3. **Generate the smallest discriminating vectors in memory.** Cover (a) an
   AC18-format compatibility page, (b) an RS-coded but uncompressed page with
   `cSize == uSize`, (c) an RS-compressed page, (d) interleaved and
   non-interleaved R21 encodings, and (e) a no-RS page only after its
   section/profile is established. Choose lengths whose aligned raw extent
   and RS extent differ; include a second page/object sentinel so cursor and
   page-boundary correctness is observed. Cover extra physical tail padding
   and retain CRC mismatch as a warning for the identified profile. Expected
   logical bytes and checksum disposition must be authored independently of decode output; an
   encode-then-decode self-round-trip alone is not sufficient.
4. **Specify ambiguity and failure behavior.** Add negative controls for
   undersized/oversized physical geometry, unsupported encoding values, and
   invalid `cSize`/`uSize` relationships. Require bounded diagnostics, no
   partial section publication on structural/classification failure, and a
   successful same-reader retry. For the named uncompressed/no-RS profile,
   retain CRC mismatch as an integrity warning; for an extent collision,
   require CRC evidence to choose a unique transform or fail closed.
5. **Validate at slice speed.** Build only
   `libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests`, run the new focused selector, then its
   existing CTest. At the composed reader checkpoint, run exactly one
   existing AC1021 sample that is proven to contain the target profile. Defer
   other-version samples, complete suites, sanitizers, external peers, and
   native CAD qualification to their existing scheduled gates.
6. **Keep evidence lanes distinct.** This work tests page transformation and
   logical-byte recovery. Entity field semantics, object/reference closure,
   output completeness, and native consumer acceptance remain downstream
   gates; none can be inferred from a page decoder pass. No support claim is
   promoted and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

This refines existing 7BE / PAR-14 / PAR-26 page-reader ownership; it adds no
finding or top-level subplan. Findings/subplans remain 130/73. It does not

## Implementation progress — 7BE / PAR-14 / PAR-26 AC1021 page transforms (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The source comparison below refines the research-only entry above. ODA §5.4's
concrete writer procedure says a data page may skip compression when it is not
shorter, then it is padded and RS-encoded. LibreDWG's merged
[PR #1363](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/pull/1363) reports a real
compatibility exception: in one AC1021 corpus, four uncompressed metadata
pages (`SummaryInfo`, `Preview`, `AppInfo`, `FileDepList`) were stored
verbatim, while all compressed pages and the other uncompressed pages matched
the calculated RS extent. Its current decoder therefore takes RS for every
compressed page and for uncompressed pages whose physical page size matches
the RS size; otherwise it copies the declared uncompressed bytes. The PR
reports semantic parity against ODA File Converter 25.6 for its cited drawing
and a corpus sweep, but this is finite peer evidence, not a universal format
rule or an independent result for this repository.

The local `dwgReader21::parseDataPage` slice now keeps those dimensions
separate. It requires `cSize <= uSize`, routes compressed pages through RS
before LZ77, and considers the no-RS compatibility route only for uncompressed
pages whose physical extent is not the calculated RS extent. Verbatim pages
may have additional physical tail padding, so equality with `align32(cSize)`
is not required. CRC is still checked and a mismatch remains a bounded
integrity warning, but it does not veto this unambiguous profile. RS pages use
the section's non-interleaved/interleaved mode. For extent collisions the
decoder uses the compressed CRC to choose a unique transform, accepts a dual
match only when the payload prefixes are identical, and otherwise fails
closed. A missing CRC does not resolve a collision. This deliberately records
the peer profile as a candidate compatibility rule, not as a newly promoted
DWG support claim.

The existing `libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests` target now has an in-memory
AC1021 profile selector. It covers generated raw and RS-stored 300-byte pages,
both interleave modes, RS-before-decompress ordering, a generated compressed
page without RS (must reject), raw/RS extent collision cases, raw pages with
additional physical tail padding, raw-profile admission with a CRC warning
and with no CRC field, missing-CRC collision refusal, output preservation,
and retry with the same reader. These source-authored vectors validate
transform/control flow; they are not an independent DWG producer sample and
are not counted as semantic parity.

The existing `tests/samples/AC1021/tablet.dwg` trace is a local candidate
profile candidate, not a passing validation sample. `SummaryInfo`, `Preview`,
`AppInfo`, and `FileDepList` report `cSize == uSize` while their physical page
extent differs from the calculated RS extent. Direct byte inspection shows
plain metadata at the starts of the SummaryInfo and AppInfo payloads. However,
the raw-prefix CRC calculated with the local `updateSeed1`/mirrored-CRC path
does not match the recorded CRC for these four entries. The compatibility
classifier may select their raw path, but CRC warnings remain and the sample
does not establish semantic correctness. Resolve the CRC/metadata assumption
and compare against the unmodified decoder before calling this a reproduced
valid profile.

Validation this slice:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests -j2` —
  passed with the repository's warning policy.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests --r2007-data-page-profiles` —
  passed.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix$' --output-on-failure`
  — passed (one existing CTest; 1.49 seconds).
- The existing smoke `dwg_read_AC1021_tablet_v2010` was run three times,
  including after the raw-padding and CRC-warning refinements; all attempts
  failed. A clean build from the unmodified `HEAD` snapshot was also run
  twice (normal and debug). Both baseline and working tree report the same
  four system-page and 19 data-page CRC warnings, `operationSucceeded=true`,
  `legacyError=0`, and `Conversion failed`. The failure predates this slice;
  the persistent CRC issue remains unresolved and must not promote support.
- No full suite, peer executable, native CAD application, external drawing,
  fixture addition, or CTest registration was used.

Next implementation/evidence steps: (1) investigate the four system-page and
19 data-page CRC mismatches shared by clean HEAD and the worktree; resolve
page offsets, seed handling, field widths, and CRC span against ODA plus
trace; (2) verify the tablet metadata semantics against an independent
reader/expected record without promoting it as a support claim; (3) inspect
other existing AC1021 pages only if they can answer that exact question
without copying or modifying drawings. Until then keep generated local
coverage, mark the broader real-producer/semantic gate `NOT_RUN`, and do not
broaden the raw rule. Keep entity semantics,
reference closure, output completeness, and native application acceptance as
separate gates. Findings/subplans remain 130/73; no new finding or top-level
subplan is introduced. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and cannot promote support claims.

chain: a DXF parser, a DWG converter, a CAD application's selected DXF
importer, and a 3D modeler are distinct implementations and evidence stages.
The sources below were reviewed on their mutable primary-repository branches;
they were not installed, cloned, built, or run. No external drawing was
downloaded and no code, test, fixture, dependency, CTest, or claim status was
changed.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |

The docs list LibreDWG, ODA, and QCAD converter routes. The docs also describe CADExchanger as the available 3D-DWG route; that is a mutable documentation claim, not a universal or locally verified consumer fact. | Keep FreeCAD qualification composed and route-pinned: converter identity/argv/exit status/fresh output hash and `$ACADVER`, then importer backend/build/preferences and per-entity results. Stock FreeCAD's converter-to-DXF route is a useful 2D interoperability target, not an ACIS/AcDs semantic witness. Any 3D app route must be named separately and its exact converter/modeler/kernel lineage recorded. |
| FreeCAD's [closed issue #18454](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/18454), including the maintainer response | The maintainer distinguishes explicit DXF entities from proprietary ACIS blobs and states that stock FreeCAD cannot read those blobs. This is direct scope guidance for the stock route, not evidence about every plugin or future build. | Mark stock FreeCAD ACIS consumption `NOT_APPLICABLE`, not a failed libdxfrw carrier test and not a blocker requiring repeated stock-FreeCAD runs. Verify the intermediate DXF carrier independently; assess semantics only through a separately named qualified modeler route. |

At its composed gate pin the exact checkout, option state, bundled/upstream library identity, callback disposition and source-preservation behavior. |

Its XREF loader is a separate operation with narrower rules: it supports copyable/transformable entities and associated resources, identifies ACAD_TABLE/unknown storage and several object features as unsupported for that operation, and says unsupported entities can be ignored without raising. Neither parser feature claims nor XREF behavior establishes DWG parsing or ACIS B-rep semantics. | Admit ezdxf only for an exact direct-DXF parse/rewrite/read-back comparison with pinned package/source and independently authored expectations. Keep same-document read/write distinct from XREF import, version downgrade, rendering, and application import. On XREF cases require per-source disposition and identity/resource closure; “no exception” or absent peer output is not a pass. Do not require ezdxf as an ordinary dependency or per-slice peer run. |
| FreeCAD Issue [#31716](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/31716) (opened 2026-08-03) | A recent user report describes a purported 3D DXF appearing as lines rather than usable 3D geometry. It is an unverified issue report, not a reproduced parser defect or format fact. | Use it only to sharpen the consumer acceptance assertion: opening/rendering a file is insufficient. A named 3D route must report output object/entity types, body/face/edge/vertex counts, topology validity, placement/units, and analytic control metrics; preserve a source-to-output disposition for every tested record. Do not copy the report's attachment/sample into this repository. |

### Implementation-ready route refinement

1. **Keep the fast implementation loop local.** Continue generated in-memory
   controls, focused selectors, and the owning existing CTest only. This
   research adds no peer build/run, CI job, dependency, full suite, or fixture.
2. **Separate four DXF operations in reports and test plans:** direct parser
   open, same-document rewrite/read-back, cross-document/XREF copy, and native
   app import. A pass in one operation must not stand for the others. For
   unknown or unsupported content record `typed`, `raw-retained`, `projected`,
   `transformed`, `ignored`, `refused`, or `unavailable` per source identity.
3. **Use ezdxf selectively at an already-planned composed checkpoint.** Pin
   exact release/source, runtime and input hash; compare only fields the exact
   route exposes against local scratch-authored expected values. Audit output
   bytes/tags independently. Run XREF as a separate operation only when a
   named cross-document/resource question needs it; treat ignored/unsupported
   records as explicit losses.
4. **Keep FreeCAD in the 2D consumer lane unless a separate 3D route is
   identified.** Capture converter exit code and logs, require a fresh
   intermediate DXF, inspect its version and carrier records before import,
   then pin the importer backend and inspect semantic output. Do not attribute
   downstream omissions to the upstream DWG reader when the carrier is still
   present, and do not attribute converter success to the importer.
5. **For 3D, separate explicit geometry from opaque modeler data.** Qualify
   points/lines/faces/meshes by exact typed geometry and transforms; qualify
   3DSOLID/REGION only through carrier retention → AcDs/entity-owner join →
   exact SAT/SAB profile parse → independent topology/analytic geometry →
   named native consumer. Stock FreeCAD's documented route cannot satisfy the
   ACIS steps. Do not use a viewport screenshot or “document opened” as the
   semantic oracle.
6. **No queue or claim promotion.** This source refresh duplicates no finding

## Deeper/broader parser-assurance methods and validation-cost review (2026-10-18; research only)

This pass compared how mature open-source DWG/DXF projects structure fast
valid-input checks, malformed-input recovery, corpus sweeps, and fuzzing. The
goal is to reduce repeated expensive validation without confusing coverage or
successful parsing with semantic correctness. Sources were read, not executed;
their commands, corpus sizes, thresholds, and behavior are not transferred to
libdxfrw.

| Primary source | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [`HACKING`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/HACKING) and [`Makefile.am`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/Makefile.am) | Current source documents AFL, honggfuzz, and LLVM libFuzzer workflows, including AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer configurations and seed directories. Its make targets split DWG read, DXF conversion, Binary-DXF conversion, JSON output, and OSS-Fuzz corpora into distinct sweeps. This documents available assurance techniques and operation separation; it does not prove that every CI change runs those sweeps, that a seed corpus is complete, or that successful conversion preserves meaning. | Keep routine local work fast and route-specific. Schedule bounded corpus/fuzz/sanitizer work after shared parser boundaries or at composed reader/security gates; do not copy peer throughput claims, limits, CI cadence, corpus, or accepted behavior. A fuzz pass is robustness evidence, not semantic parity. |
| ACadSharp [reader documentation](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/docs/articles/samples/reading.md) and [sample-corpus discussion #520](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/discussions/520) | Reader notifications surface warnings and informational messages that a bare success/failure result omits; they do not guarantee a complete per-object loss/disposition report. The maintainer says the repository's sample drawings are used by its test project; this establishes fixture use, not that every sample is independently authored, normative, or accompanied by exact semantic expectations. | If ACadSharp is admitted for a named question at a composed checkpoint, capture its pinned release, notifications, object counts/identities, and only the exact fields with independent expected values. “No exception” or a peer's checked-in sample alone is not a pass. |
| ezdxf [recovery documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/recover.html), [launcher/audit documentation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/launcher.rst), and [feature summary](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/index.rst) | The documented strict path reads ASCII and Binary DXF; the recover module handles ASCII DXF only, repairs structural flaws, and runs an audit. The documentation describes recovery as slower and warns that decoding/rewrite can lose information or produce invalid DXF. Therefore strict parse, audit findings, repaired-document output, and rendering are distinct outcomes. | Use strict read for valid direct-DXF comparisons. Use recovery only for explicitly malformed ASCII recovery cases and score repaired/lost content separately; do not substitute recovery success for strict parsing, Binary-DXF support, or semantic parity. An audit result describes that peer's model and repair rules, not the file-format oracle. |

### Implementation-ready validation sequence

1. **Every implementation slice:** keep the changed behavior in the focused
   generated/in-memory selector, with independent literal expectations,
   bounds/progress checks, and a following-record/object sentinel where the
   parser or writer can affect one. Build the owning strict target and run its
   existing CTest once. For output changes, inspect physical group-code/byte
   framing and publication/rollback as well as local readback. Retain the
   existing `-Werror` and LibreCAD source-compatibility checks where applicable.
2. **At a composed reader or writer checkpoint:** run the smallest existing
   producer sample that exercises the completed path, then perform one
   question-specific peer check only if the peer overlaps on exact version,
   direction, and operation. Record diagnostics and source-to-output
   disposition; compare to independently authored values rather than peer
   output alone. Keep the existing fixture policy: no downloaded or copied
   peer drawings; use already-present project fixtures or scratch-generated
   local controls.
3. **At a shared parser-boundary/security checkpoint, not per slice:** run a
   bounded sanitizer/fuzz pass with a fixed time/size budget and an approved
   seed set (existing local fixtures plus scratch-generated inputs). Record
   build flags, seeds, elapsed budget, crashes/timeouts, and triage result. A
   failure yields a minimized local reproducer only when it can be created
   from scratch or is already in an allowed repository; do not add externally
   sourced DWG/DXF files. Keep long corpus sweeps and full suites at their
   already planned phase gates.
4. **Keep failure classes separate:** a valid-input parser mismatch, malformed
   strict rejection, ASCII recovery/audit repair, resource-limit refusal,
   timeout, sanitizer finding, and native application rejection are separate
   results. Do not turn recovery, a warning-free peer parse, a fuzz-clean
   window, or file-open success into a format-support claim.
5. **No reordering or external promotion:** this research adds no local defect,
   finding, top-level subplan, dependency, fixture, or required peer. It changes
   no per-slice validation frequency and does not interrupt the active AC1021
   CRC investigation. Findings/subplans remain 130/73; J256, J260, J268,
   J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and cannot promote support
   claims.

## R2007 CRC stage reconciliation and independent-peer eligibility (2026-10-18; research only)

This follow-up broadens the active AC1021 investigation from page-profile
classification to the exact CRC input pipeline and the quality of possible
independent cross-checks. It reconciles the local implementation with ODA
v5.4.1 §§5.3, 5.4, 5.12, and 5.13; rechecks the merged LibreDWG #1363 fix;
and assesses a second-language DWG reader as a future structural diagnostic.
It narrows the next experiment but does not identify the cause of the
worktree/clean-HEAD CRC mismatches. No production code, test, fixture,
dependency, CTest registration, or support claim changed in this research
pass.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ODA [Open Design Specification v5.4.1 §§5.3, 5.4, 5.12, 5.13](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) | For a data page, §5.4 calculates the 32-bit page checksum first, then optionally compresses and optionally encrypts; the 64-bit mirrored page CRC is over the resulting compressed-or-raw (and, if applicable, encrypted) bytes, using `UpdateSeed1(fileCrcSeed, payloadLength)`, before 8-byte padding and RS encoding (§5.4, pp. 49–50). For a system page, §5.3 calculates one CRC on the original uncompressed bytes and another on the resulting compressed-or-raw bytes, before padding/repetition/RS (§5.3, pp. 48–49). Section 5.12's 1–8-byte processing table resolves the apparent ordering concern: repeated 8-byte blocks use offsets `[6,7,4,5,2,3,0,1]`, and the 4-byte remainder uses `[2,3,0,1]`, matching local `calculateCrc64`. This settles the normative pipeline, but it does not prove local page bytes, seed extraction, physical page association, or interpretation of this sample's CRC fields are correct. | Do not change the CRC byte order based on the earlier table-reading suspicion. Check data and system page CRCs as separate lanes and use the exact ODA stage/length. Keep the data page's optional encryption state explicit. Do not CRC the 8-byte padding, repeated system-page copies, or RS parity when checking the stored page CRC. |
| Local `dwgReader21::parseDataPage`, `parseSysPage`, and `dwgUtil` | Current code computes a data-page CRC over the selected raw/RS-decoded prefix of `cSize` bytes, with `updateSeed1(r2007CrcSeed, cSize)`. System-page code checks the compressed-or-raw prefix and the uncompressed output separately. The clean-HEAD and worktree tablet traces both show four system-page and 19 data-page CRC warnings, so the page-profile slice did not introduce them. The generated matrix vectors compute their expected checksum with `dwgUtil`; they therefore test control flow and self-consistency, not the independent CRC value algorithm or the real sample bytes. | First add a small, independently expressed bit-at-a-time CRC reference and literal outputs for lengths covering 0–9 bytes, including the 4- and 8-byte special order, plus `UpdateSeed1` cases. Then inspect exactly one failing page from the existing tablet sample: record map/header offsets and raw bytes, stored CRC, decoded seed, `cSize/uSize`, page physical extent, encryption/section profile, and the precise CRC input span. Calculate with both the literal reference and production helper. Keep temporary byte dumps outside the repository; add no sample fixture. |
| LibreDWG merged [PR #1363](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/pull/1363) and [current `decode_r2007.c`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode_r2007.c) | The peer's fix provides strong AC1021 page-transform evidence: compression and RS are distinct, and exact physical extent is used to select RS for uncompressed pages. Its reported ODA File Converter comparison/corpus improvement is finite peer evidence. The change does not independently establish libdxfrw's CRC implementation, since the PR's main assertion is recovered object/geometry parity, not a page-level CRC oracle. | Retain #1363 for the narrow page-profile classifier. Do not treat the peer's successful decoded objects or its page-size heuristic as proof that CRC handling is correct. Keep CRC warning and semantic acceptance separate. |
| [dwg-rs](https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/dwg-rs) current README/source | This is a promising structurally separate Rust implementation, but its own README labels it pre-alpha, reports small per-version corpora and entity-decoder gaps, and says its R2007 RS decoder read-side fallback is pending. It also explicitly distinguishes container parsing, raw object walking, and semantic entity decoding. These are project-authored status statements, not independent qualification. | Do not add it as a dependency or required per-slice peer, and do not use its present CRC/container status as an AC1021 oracle. At a later composed checkpoint, a pinned revision may be considered only for a named raw-section/object-boundary comparison after verifying that the exact route is implemented; record its skipped/errored items and compare against independent expected values. |
| [ACadSharp `DwgCheckSumCalculator`](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/IO/DWG/DwgCheckSumCalculator.cs), [`CRC.cs`](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/IO/DWG/CRC.cs), and [`DwgSectionIO`](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/IO/DWG/DwgSectionIO.cs) | ACadSharp is a separate DWG reader and its current source contains checksum/CRC utilities, but the reviewed checksum calculator is a 32-bit sum using modulo 65521 and the reviewed section base handles version flags/sentinels; the reviewed files do not show it recomputing ODA R2007 page CRCs over the §5.3/§5.4 spans. The existence of a class named `CRC` is not sufficient to prove this route is used for page validation. | Keep ACadSharp as an optional structural/semantic differential only. Do not designate it a page-CRC oracle unless a concrete AC1021 call path is identified, its exact input span/seed is verified, and it is run against a known-profile sample. |

### Implementation-ready CRC isolation sub-plan

1. **Fast reference vectors — complete.** The existing reader-matrix target
   has an independently expressed bit-at-a-time reference and fixed literals
   for normal/mirrored CRC inputs of lengths 0–9 plus five `UpdateSeed1`
   cases. Keep these focused and run only their selector and owning CTest when
   touching this lane.
2. **Data-page trace — complete, result unresolved.** The existing tablet
   `AcDb:Header` page `0x1c` has independently corroborated map fields and
   `crc_seed=0`; its logical 32-bit checksum matches but its mirrored CRC does
   not. A source-derived (255,251) message-byte gather exactly matches the
   production decoder. Preserve the captured offset, extent, sizes, checksum,
   CRC, and computed values below; do not search arbitrary offsets, lengths,
   endian variants, or seeds for a match.
3. **System-page traces — complete, result unresolved.** Existing tablet and
   colorwh page-map descriptors independently corroborate the same
   (255,239)-decoded compressed prefixes as the production decoder. For each,
   check only the ODA §5.3 compressed-or-raw and uncompressed spans. Both
   stored fields mismatch on both pages; decoded file seed is zero. Do not
   use a system-page result to infer data-page behavior or FEC validity.
4. **Resolve with a real independent CRC witness before a production fix.**
   Inspect a concrete AC1021 page-CRC call path in a peer, or obtain a known-
   profile sample and page values from a tool that explicitly verifies the
   relevant CRCs. Pin the tool/source version and input hash; capture the
   physical page association, exact pre-padding/pre-RS bytes, decoded seed,
   and stored value. Compare only those exact spans. If no such witness is
   available, preserve the mismatch as unresolved, do not weaken checks, and
   do not let this side-investigation pause unrelated implementation slices.
5. **Classify the result before a fix.** If independent evidence shows the
   literal helper wrong, fix it with literal regressions. If the helper is
   right but page fields, association, transform, span, or encryption stage
   differ, change only the implicated code path and add the smallest
   generated in-memory vector. If a known-good independent sample still
   mismatches under the exact ODA pipeline, investigate sample provenance or
   profile rather than suppressing diagnostics.
6. **Keep validation narrow and claims gated.** Reuse the existing
   reader-matrix target, manual diagnostic selectors, and existing drawings;
   add no downloaded/copy fixture, persistent fixture, or CTest registration.
   After a demonstrated code change, build the owner, run its focused selector
   and owning CTest, then one relevant existing sample. Defer full suites to
   their planned composed checkpoint. A CRC pass establishes container
   integrity only, not entity semantics, output completeness, or CAD-consumer
   acceptance.
7. **No plan promotion.** This research adds no finding or top-level subplan,
   changes no queue order or validation frequency, and does not close the
   active AC1021 work item. Findings/subplans remain 130/73. J256, J260,
   J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; no result here can
   promote a support claim.

success and that cap-minus-one stops before overwriting the last prior value

move/reset lease lifetime. The two routes are isolated so an under-cap result
identifies which parser-owned field is admitted or preserved.

Keep source-distinct peer evidence, downstream UI/import behavior, and native DWG write acceptance separate. Any consumer check must bind the exact checkout and build/feature flags. |

### Implementation-ready route gate

1. **Before a peer run, name the exact question.** Bind AC version, input
   format, direction, operation, family/field, expected value source, peer
   artifact/source hash, build options, and fixture provenance. If that overlap
   does not exist, mark the peer `NOT_ADMITTED` and continue the local slice.
2. **For each writer route, observe the actual output.** Capture requested and
   emitted version independently; verify signature/header, required sections,
   terminal record, fresh output identity, and per-source-record disposition.
   Then use a distinct reader/native route where its exact operation is
   available. A self-roundtrip only checks internal consistency.
3. **For application routes, inspect every handoff.** Test generated DXF
   directly through the selected DXF importer to isolate the library writer.
   For DWG, validate converter completion and intermediate DXF before testing
   importer semantics. Do not blame or credit the wrong stage.
4. **Keep 3D evidence stratified.** Explicit point/curve/face/mesh geometry,
   opaque 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY payload preservation, AcDs owner/key association,
   SAT/SAB parsing, complete topology/analytic geometry, and native edit/open
   acceptance remain separate outcomes. Agreement on raw bytes or a visible
   tessellation cannot promote a semantic-solid claim.
5. **Do not add validation cost to every leaf.** Continue generated local
   controls plus the owning focused selector/CTest per implementation slice.
   Run independent peers, FreeCAD/native platform profiles, and bounded
   sanitizer/fuzz/corpus work only at the already planned composed gates. Do
   not add external drawings as committed fixtures; use existing eligible
   repository inputs or local-from-scratch controls.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c.d.17.70 MLEADER nested-text callback publication (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Extended the 17.69 direct-parser retained-text controls through full file-backed
DXF reads. The generated matrix covers AC1027 context text (group 304) and the
AC1021 legacy block-label route (group 302), each in ASCII and Binary DXF. The
callback immediately copies the published string values; a coordinate-distinct
LINE follows the MLEADER as the ordering/cursor sentinel. All drawing bytes are
created locally in the test and written only to a disposable temporary folder.

For each route, the test measures the minimum successful whole-read retained-
byte cap. Exact-cap reads publish MLEADER then LINE with the expected text
value(s) and all six LINE coordinates. At one byte under, the read fails with
`ResourceLimit/dxf-retained-byte-budget` before either entity callback; raising
the same facade to the measured cap and retrying publishes both in order.
This covers callback suppression and retry for both nested text owners, not
arbitrary memory retained by downstream consumers.

### Implementation-ready semantic checklist

Use this only on a touched family or at an already planned composed peer/native
checkpoint; it adds no per-slice external work:

1. **Bind the route.** Record exact input signature/version, producer, parser or
   converter identity and revision, requested and effective output version,
   selected importer, platform/build options, command and diagnostics. Mark a
   peer issue without an eligible reproducible artifact `LEAD_ONLY`.
2. **Check source-to-model identity.** Compare handle, concrete entity type
   (without confusing base-class `is-a` counts), owner/layout/block membership,
   and linked child records such as ATTRIB. Record expected, parsed, skipped,
   and unknown records separately.
3. **Check discriminating semantics.** Compare exact fields that control
   geometry or display—annotation dimensions, text, layer/style, coordinates,
   orientation, OCS/WCS, units, transforms, and references—not just counts,
   nonempty output, centers, extents, or rendered appearance.
4. **Check output and closure.** Inspect the emitted record/value and required
   object/owner links, then reopen with a source-distinct reader where available.
   Preserve every source record's disposition; process exit and self-roundtrip
   are consistency signals, not independent fidelity proof.
5. **Keep 3D evidence stratified.** Report explicit mesh/face/curve geometry,
   SAT/SAB bytes, AcDs association, ACIS parse, topology/analytic geometry, and
   native application acceptance in separate fields. An opaque payload that
   survives byte-for-byte does not prove a valid/editable solid; a missing
   stock consumer capability is not a parser failure.
6. **Keep the fast path fast.** Add no new corpus-wide run or full-suite
   cadence. Apply the narrow generated test plus its owning selector/CTest only
   when a local source trace or regression maps to the field; use existing
   fixtures or locally generated controls, never an unapproved external drawing
   as a committed fixture. Reserve peer, native, sanitizer and broad-corpus
   qualification for the established composed gates.

data in the data store, but does not define a universal per-modeler subtype
eligibility rule or a bijective record-key mapping. Therefore keep the exact
flag-to-payload check scoped to the locally admitted AC1027+ AcDs modeler
replay profile; do not generalize it to every modeler or call it a complete
typed DWG writer contract. This source review itself changed no local code,

InventorLoader has a distinct parser-to-FreeCAD route but documents unsupported blending/helix/law-defined geometry and shares OCCT with FreeCAD. cq-acis is experimental and explicitly profile/subset-dependent; it also converts into CadQuery/OCCT. Neither parses DWG section ownership or proves the entity→AcDs association. | Keep both optional and exact-profile only. Report raw-stream parser acceptance, unsupported records, produced shape count, validity/closure, units/transforms, and analytic checks separately. Neither counts as a second kernel relative to FreeCAD/OCCT or as a DWG/AcDs reader. |
| [ezdxf ACIS/recovery docs](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html), [GDAL DXF driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html), and [FreeCAD import workflow](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Import_Export.md) | These routes remain useful for narrower, named questions: DXF syntax/selected typed fields, projected geometry, raw carrier extraction, or native application behavior. They do not collapse to a common full-fidelity oracle: recovery can mutate; GDAL projects a subset; FreeCAD DWG conversion is an external stage; and raw ACIS extraction is not B-rep interpretation. | Preserve the existing per-operation comparator matrix. Select one route only after matching input format/version, direction, feature family, and expected-value source; record skipped/unsupported/lossy content as a result, not as a pass. |

### Implementation-ready evidence routing refinement

1. **Name the question before selecting a peer.** Separate container/page
   decoding, typed object/field semantics, DXF projection, raw ACIS carrier
   retention, DWG entity-to-AcDs join, B-rep/kernel construction, and native
   application acceptance. A route can answer one row without answering the
   next.
2. **Fingerprint every layer once at a composed checkpoint.** Record exact
   input/output SHA-256, source revision or package version, build/features,
   source/target versions, command/options, OS/application, codec, converter,
   kernel, diagnostics/recovery, per-handle disposition, and expected-value
   provenance. Count evidence by parser/kernel lineage, not by downstream app
   count.
3. **Use semantic manifests as a comparison envelope, not as the oracle.**
   Reopen the output and compare stable handle/type/owner references, typed
   fields, raw-carrier hashes, and geometry measures against an independent
   expectation. A peer's own `save_verified` or same-codec round trip is a
   useful loss detector but is not independent evidence by itself.
4. **Keep ACIS acceptance layered.** Require exact carrier bytes and owner/key
   closure first; then parser/profile acceptance; then complete-body shape
   count, validity/closure, transform/units, and analytic measures; then a
   native consumer result. A marker scan, tessellation, bounding box, partial
   body, or OCCT-family result cannot stand in for all layers.
5. **Keep implementation moving.** Use generated in-memory or scratch-only
   controls and the existing per-slice strict target + focused selector +
   owning CTest. Invoke one optional peer/native route only at the planned
   composed gate. If it is unavailable or cannot match the exact profile,
   record `NOT_RUN`/`NOT_APPLICABLE`, retain the narrow claim boundary, update
   this ledger, and proceed to the next local slice; do not create a new
   external blocker or add downloaded/committed fixtures.

This screen adds a possible downstream geometry-validation lane, not a new

newly surfaced STEP/B-rep implementation to explore an open-source geometry
check outside the OCCT lineage. The handoff is deliberately limited to the
existing one-time composed S8 checkpoint; per-slice validation and the local
implementation queue do not change.

| Route/source | Current evidence and limit | Plan use |
|---|---|---|

The profile docs are project claims and the reviewed `main` pages are mutable. | Use only after local extraction has closed the source entity→AcDs owner/key→exact payload join. Pin the v0.6.1 artifact or exact source tag/commit, dependency lock, toolchain, features, and output hash. Require admitted 217/218 input and a successful no-loss, geometry-transferred STEP conversion. Treat this as a conversion stage, not an independent ACIS oracle. |
| [OpenSolid README](https://github.com/MC-Meesh/opensolid-fable) | The project describes an independently implemented Rust hybrid F-Rep/B-rep kernel with STEP AP203 read/write, topology checking, and mass properties. It also documents a mesh fallback for STEP input and a shared-geometry re-import defect. Its README reports both 1,593 and 1,187 workspace tests in different sections, and the repo page shows no published release; aggregate test-count prose and mutable `main` are therefore not qualification. The documented STEP lane has no direct SAT/SAB, DWG, or DXF reader. | Consider only as a downstream non-OCCT kernel candidate. Pin an exact commit, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, build features and command. Audit whether this control stays on the exact B-rep import path; reject mesh fallback, refused/partial shapes, unknown transfer, or loss. Capture `check()` and analytic measurements per body. |
| CADMPEG→STEP→OpenSolid composed route | The two projects expose complementary conversion and import APIs, but neither route was built or run here. A valid STEP emitted by CADMPEG then accepted by OpenSolid would not establish that the original DWG/AcDs carrier was correct; source identity and expected values must bypass both implementations. Shared public format descriptions are not enough to establish code independence, and source/dependency lineage has not been audited in this pass. | Optional triangulation against a source-authored manifest only; do not count an OpenSolid result as an independent DWG parser, native CAD application result, or general ACIS compatibility claim. Keep the result below J-item promotion until all named external requirements are met. |

### Minimal implementation-ready composed check

1. Start from a locally generated asymmetric analytic control (or a control
   already in the named repositories). Keep all generated DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB/STEP
   outputs in scratch storage; do not add them as repository fixtures. Capture
   source-native dimensions, placement, units, topology expectation, and
   expected bounding box, area, volume, and centroid independently of the two
   readers—for example, from the source CAD API plus hand-checkable analytic
   formulas.
2. Preserve the existing libdxfrw gate first: exact source handle and block
   path, DWG AcDs key/index if applicable, exact payload length/hash, and the
   complete carrier join. A detached SAT/SAB file cannot prove this stage.
3. Resolve and record the inner stream signature/save profile. Run a pinned
   CADMPEG 0.6.1-compatible tool only for an admitted 217/218 profile. Require
   successful decode, `geometry_transferred`, no blocking loss or unsupported
   required topology, and a STEP export report with no semantic reductions.
   If CADMPEG cannot expose enough machine-readable detail to prove this,
   classify the route `NOT_QUALIFIED` and continue local implementation.
4. Feed the exact hashed STEP output to a pinned OpenSolid revision. Confirm
   the imported entity/body inventory and that every requested body is an exact
   B-rep, not a welded-mesh fallback; run its structural checker and collect
   units, transforms, topology counts, bounds, area, volume, and centroid. Do
   not accept STEP re-export/self-roundtrip alone as independent evidence.
5. Compare each result to the predeclared source manifest with explicit
   tolerances and per-body identity. Investigate any unsupported record,
   topology rewrite, unit/transform discrepancy, or disagreement; report
   `NOT_RUN`/`NOT_APPLICABLE` when the exact profile or toolchain is unavailable.
6. Keep the existing FreeCAD Linux and Windows checks, any licensed CAD audit,
   and source entity→AcDs→payload checks as separate lanes. This candidate
   requires no CMake/CI dependency and no repeated validation; it is considered
   once at the composed gate only. Continue the next ready local slice if the
   route is unavailable.

## Implementation progress — AC1027 DataStorage default schema and `schidx` table order (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Added the missing ODA §24.3 schema-only default profile as an in-memory
generated section in the existing `libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests` owner.
The profile has `segidx`, `schidx`, `schdat`, and `search` segments; the five
default schema records, four opaque unknown-property headers, an empty search
record, and no `datidx` or data records. Assertions cover schema indexes,
property types/values, header flags, segment classification, structural
validity/replay, and the zero-record state. Two malformed controls set the
first and second `schidx` table counts to `UINT32_MAX`; each verifies bounded
entry retention, a count-cap diagnostic, and disabled replay.

The new test first failed with out-of-range unknown-property references and
misdecoded schemas. Comparing the bytes to the local authoritative ODA v5.4.1
§24.2.2.5 resolved a production parser defect: the reader had treated the
first `schidx` table as schema references and the second as opaque
unknown-property-header references. It now stores the first table in
`schemaPropertyEntries` and the second table (whose field order is
segment-index, local-offset, index) in `schemaIndexEntries`. The bounded reserve
targets and diagnostic labels were corrected to track the actual destination
vectors. Existing generated schema vectors were updated to use ODA table order.

Validation passed: strict target build
`cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests -j2`,
focused owning CTest
`ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_graph_preservation$' --output-on-failure`
(1/1, 0.69 s after the malformed-count additions), and scoped `git diff --check`.
The full suite, peer runtimes, native consumers, and corpus sweeps were not run. Test bytes are authored
entirely in memory; no DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB fixture, new dependency, test
registration, or CTest was added. This closes the local schema-table-order
defect under existing PAR-07/S8.3; it does not resolve stale-index producer
behavior or promote support. Findings/subplans remain 130/73, and J256, J260,
J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

## Deeper/broader AcDs coordinate, parser-safety, and peer evidence review (2026-10-18; research update)

This review re-read the required local ODA v5.4.1 §24.2.2.3 and §24.2.2.5,
checked the merged ACadSharp Prototype1b reader discussion at the reported
edge locations, and screened a historical LibreDWG malformed-input report.
It adds no independent geometry oracle and does not use peer code as DWG byte
authority.

| Source | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Local ODA v5.4.1 PDF §24.2.2.5 and its [published copy](https://static.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) | ODA explicitly defines the first `schidx` table as unknown-property references (`index`, segment index, local offset), followed by the tag/property-count header, then schema references in segment-index/local-offset/index order. §24.2.2.6 places the opaque eight-byte unknown-property headers before schema records and the property-name table. The default schema-only section is therefore a valuable parser case independent of modeler bodies. The in-memory §24.3 test exposed that this checkout had reversed the two tables. | Keep the fixed role mapping in `readSchemaIndex()` and the test asserting both tables' distinct semantics. Preserve the fast graph-preservation target; no new suite or fixture. Do not infer that successfully reading the default schemas proves producer variation, data-record linkage, or ACIS semantics. |
| ODA v5.4.1 §24.2.2.3 local coordinate definitions and [ACadSharp PR #1154](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1154) | For a final data record, the formula line's plus sign conflicts with its own parenthetical. The data-start anchor is relative to segment start; record-local offset is relative to the anchor. Thus absolute start=`segment start + anchor + local offset`, absolute end=`segment start + segment size`, and span=`segment size - anchor - local offset`. The existing code's `segmentEndOffset - recordOffset` is exactly that result. PR participants reported this derivation against a corpus, which corroborates but does not replace the coordinate proof. | Mark the formula discrepancy resolved as an apparent documentation typo. Do not change the parser formula. Keep the existing generated explicit-anchor, next-record and terminal-sentinel controls; do not expand regular validation. |
| [ACadSharp PR #1154 discussion](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1154) | A contributor reports an unpublished customer DWG whose current header-selected `segidx` reportedly begins at `0x680` with size `0x300`, while an old index entry points to `0x80` with size `0x80`; their in-progress peer reader reportedly attempted 53 global entries in that stale 128-byte segment. The peer author disputed that the stale index is valid output. No DWG is attached, so this does not establish a legal producer profile or a libdxfrw defect. | Keep stale-index semantics open and external. Source inspection shows this reader consumes the header-selected segment-index table once; where present it uses the table's self-reference to bound its row loop and does not recursively parse every listed segment named `segidx`. If this surface changes, add only an in-memory bounded/non-recursion control and an explicit disposition; seek shareable producer evidence before choosing recovery semantics. Never add the private drawing. |
| [LibreDWG issue #695](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/695), [LibreDWG NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS), and [AcDs loss report #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411) | #695 is closed and labeled as intentional illegal/fuzz input; the report includes conflicting crash traces across a corrupted DWG and a 32-bit environment, so it is only a historical malformed-input signal, not a confirmed current `schidx` bug or current-release status. LibreDWG's release notes historically described Prototype1b as incomplete/brute-force, while #1411 is a separate report of R2013+ AcDs/SAB loss. These reports support separating parser safety, section extraction, association, and semantics; they do not measure this checkout. | Keep peer use optional and pinned. The new default-schema test also sets each table count to `UINT32_MAX` and verifies a count-cap diagnostic with replay disabled; do not copy LibreDWG code (GPL-3.0-or-later) or import its reports as support evidence. |

The resulting order remains: (1) bounded ODA-shaped table/segment decoding,
(2) index-to-record and entity-handle association, (3) complete raw payload
identity/page assembly, (4) independent SAT/SAB interpretation, (5) writer
reopen and per-platform consumer acceptance. The first local schema-table
defect is fixed under PAR-07/S8.3; stale `segidx` validity, independent ACIS
semantics, and external/native qualification remain open. Findings/subplans
remain 130/73. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain

FreeCAD, and LibreCAD 3, then reconciled them with the existing PAR-07/S8
carrier, writer, hardening, and native-consumer owners. It adds concrete
admission controls and route settings; it does not declare a defect in this
checkout or turn peer claims into support evidence.

| Source / exact evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| [LibreDWG R2007+ reader source](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode_r2007.c) routes `AcDsPrototype_1b` through `read_2007_section_acds()` and `acds_private()` / `acds.spec`. The project also maintains an [ODA 5.4.2/LibreDWG specification-difference document](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/ODA-5.4.2-libredwg-diff.pdf). | A distinct open-source AcDs parser and a list of candidate spec discrepancies exist. The mutable `master` URL is not a pinned comparator, and an implementation/spec diff is not authoritative over this repository's ODA v5.4.1 reference. The section reader does not, by itself, establish complete entity-owner joining or ACIS body semantics. | At a composed peer checkpoint, pin the LibreDWG commit, release/build options and exact input profile; compare section/index/payload association with the local ODA-derived manifest. Use its spec-diff only as an investigation index: adjudicate every byte-layout question against the repo-pinned ODA PDF and real sample trace. Keep raw carrier retention separate from decoded geometry. |
| [LibreDWG 0.14.1 NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) records fixes for an R2004 section-decompression heap overflow, a pre-R2004 VIEWPORT import use-after-free, and an R2004 header out-of-bounds read; its [project license is GPL-3.0-or-later](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg). LibreCAD's [README identifies its application license as GPLv2](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD). | These are peer-reported security fixes, not reproduced libdxfrw bugs. They show that mature DWG parsers remain exposed to size, lifetime, and page-map-boundary failures. GPL-3.0-or-later source is not an automatically safe source-port into the LibreCAD GPLv2 consumer. | Treat LibreDWG as an optional behavioral comparator unless exact revision and build are pinned. Do not copy/derive source into the LibreCAD upgrade without a separate maintainer/license-compatibility review; prefer spec-led clean implementation. Map the three failure classes to existing checked-size/decompression, object-lifetime, and section-page-map hardening owners. First audit existing guards; if a gap is confirmed, add one minimal generated/in-memory regression to the owning fast test target. Keep sanitizer/fuzz/corpus execution at the existing composed assurance gate. |
| [IxMilia.Dxf's compatibility notes](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf#autocad) list typed 3DSOLID, BODY, and REGION types but explicitly warn that AutoCAD might not open files written with those entities. | Entity-model presence or successful parser read is not output conformance. This is a project-level warning, not proof that every IxMilia output is invalid. | Use a pinned IxMilia build as a source-distinct DXF reader/tag comparator only for fields it exposes. Never use its same-library or peer-writer readback as the positive writer gate for modeler entities. Keep strict raw output checks and independent native/third-party opening plus per-body association/semantic checks in their existing separate lanes. |
| Official [FreeCAD converter docs](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md), [DXF preferences](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Import_Export_Preferences.md), [additional-components docs](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Installing_additional_components.md), and [FreeCAD issue #18454](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/18454) describe DWG as external converter → DXF → selected importer, configurable C++/legacy Python DXF readers with differing feature coverage, and the stock importer limitation for ACIS blobs. | “FreeCAD opens this DWG” is a configuration-specific end-to-end result. The selected converter, intermediate DXF revision/content, importer backend, and import preferences can each change the result. The issue is a route-boundary report, not a general geometry-format specification; stock FreeCAD is not the ACIS/B-rep witness. | For each required Linux and Windows qualification, record exact FreeCAD build/hash, converter binary/version/hash and requested/actual output version, DXF hash, importer backend and relevant preferences. Check the intermediate DXF before importing. Qualify only the backend/configuration the product claims to support; run the alternate importer as an additional matrix cell only if it is part of the promised route. Compare 2D entities/blocks/layers/annotation by identity and properties. Score explicit 3D entities separately from ACIS/AcDs opaque retention and from solid semantics. |
| [LibreCAD 3 DWG support policy](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/blob/master/docs/dwg-support.md) states DWG import is behind `WITH_DWG_IMPORT`, off by default, and read-only; its evidence ledger is reader-direction only. | LibreCAD 3 is a real downstream compatibility consumer when the feature is enabled, but a default build or a DWG write test is not an applicable route. This policy does not imply that its 2D drawing model consumes ACIS bodies. | Pin the LibreCAD 3 commit and explicitly enable its documented import option for the downstream read-compatibility check. Exercise the shared callback/filter path for the existing 2D contract; do not require DWG write support or infer 3D solid rendering. Preserve the older LibreCAD 2 adapter/API path independently. |

### Implementation-ready refinements under existing plan owners

1. **Peer admission (PAR-07/S8):** before comparison, save a compact run record
   containing repository URL, immutable commit/tag, license, executable hash,
   build flags, OS, input/output format and version, exact command, and all
   diagnostics. Mark unavailable, unpinned, or license-ineligible peers
   `NOT_RUN`/`NOT_QUALIFIED`; do not block the local implementation queue.
2. **Stage-specific evidence:** for a source-authored case, compare source
   manifest → local parse → emitted DXF/DWG → independent reopen. Record each
   object as typed, raw-preserved, skipped-with-diagnostic, or fatal and join
   by source handle, physical owner/block path, AcDs key/index, and complete
   payload length/hash. Count equality alone and a successful open are not
   enough. Keep DWG inline SAT/SAB, AcDs section payloads, DXF SAT, DXF
   SAB/ACDSDATA, explicit geometry, and B-rep semantics as distinct rows.
3. **2D consumer protection:** the standard per-slice check remains the
   strict owning target, focused selector, and one owning CTest. Reuse the
   existing generated ASCII/Binary DXF and DWG-object controls for legacy
   entities, tables, blocks, layers, annotation, handles, and encoding; assert
   callbacks and following-record boundaries. A 3D carrier change must not
   regress these 2D consumer-visible fields or make a new `DRW_Interface`
   callback pure virtual.
4. **Security-cost control:** map a specific size/lifetime/progress concern to
   its existing hardening test owner before adding code. Prefer bounded,
   in-memory byte vectors and exact owning CTest selection; no downloaded or
   newly authored DWG/DXF fixture is needed. Full suites, fuzzing, sanitizers,
   corpus sweeps, peer runs, and native-app matrices remain composed-checkpoint
   work, not per-slice requirements.
5. **Self-updating and unblock rule:** after each implemented plan item,
   record the code/test/receipt result, remaining evidence boundary, and the
   next locally actionable item in the same plan; if an external route is
   unavailable, mark only that evidence cell and immediately select the next
   ready local item. Report progress after each actual commit, but do not
   create a commit that would include unrelated pre-existing worktree changes.

No format rule was inferred from peer source; the local ODA v5.4.1 PDF remains
authoritative for DWG bytes. This review adds no local finding or top-level
subplan, does not reorder implementation or increase routine test frequency,
adds no dependency or DWG/DXF fixture, and promotes no support claim. Plan
totals remain 130 findings / 73 top-level subplans. J256, J260, J268, J284,
J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and cannot be promoted by these
sources. LibreCAD 2D compatibility, 3D typed-data access, opaque ACIS/AcDs
preservation, ACIS parsing, solid semantics, and native-platform qualification
remain separate claims.

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8.3 aggregate AcDs payload retention cap (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Applied the existing 8 MiB retention ceiling cumulatively across inline and
blob-backed `DRW_DataStorageRecord::payload` copies. Blob descriptors, page
metadata, source section bytes, record identities, and structural replay remain
available when the typed payload-copy budget is exhausted; the first omitted
copy adds a `SupportedOpaque` diagnostic and clears `payloadsRetained` without
invalidating the section.

The generated in-memory fan-out control reuses the two validated blob pages
from a section smaller than the cap across five records. It verifies that the
first four ~2 MiB copies are retained, the fifth payload is omitted, the exact
diagnostic is present, and the section remains structurally valid and
replayable. This bounds aggregate record-payload copies for this parser call;
it does not bound transient page-copy buffers, raw section storage, or later
copies made while linking payloads to entities. Those remain under the separate
7S.3 operation-accounting work.

Validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests -j2`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_graph_preservation$' --output-on-failure` (1/1)
- Scoped `git diff --check` is recorded with the receipt.

No full suite, peer, native application, committed fixture, new CTest, or
support claim was added. All generated section bytes are built in memory.
Findings/subplans remain 130/73; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

### Refined readiness and speed rules

1. Maintain separate evidence identities for released peer artifacts, mutable
   development heads, open PRs, and issue repro reports. A capability matrix or
   an issue's “master” claim never substitutes for an immutable run receipt.
2. Before any peer comparison, freeze a source-authored manifest and compare
   per handle/type/physical owner/block path. At each stage classify the object
   as typed, raw-preserved, skipped-with-diagnostic, or fatal; include complete
   payload length/hash for modeler carriers. Counts and successful file-open
   status are supplemental only.
3. Keep the smallest touched local owner as the routine gate: strict target,
   focused selector, owning CTest, and a following-record/graph sentinel where
   applicable. Existing relevant controls already cover the newly refreshed
   peer failure shapes, so this research adds no test, fixture, CTest, or
   dependency.
4. Run the pinned peer/native matrix once at the existing composed
   checkpoint. If an artifact, sample, platform, or observable disposition is
   unavailable, record only that cell as `NOT_RUN`/`NOT_QUALIFIED` and continue
   with the next local slice.
5. At the time of this review, the locally open 7S.3 costs included the
   finalizer's retained parse copy and in-tree consumer staging. The later
   implementation entries below remove the redundant finalizer parse copy,
   raw-frame parse-peer copies, and one in-tree modeler event/adapter copy.
   The writer-owned pending modeler payload copy remains necessary under the
   callback lifetime contract. Arbitrary external-consumer copies, allocator
   capacity, and process RSS remain outside the library's direct control.

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8.3 7S.3 linked AcDs payload-copy accounting (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Bound and measured the second reader-owned AcDs payload copy made when a
retained record is attached to its modeler entity. `dwgReader` now tracks
`m_dataStorageLinkedPayloadBytes`, refuses a link that would exceed the same
8 MiB cumulative payload-copy ceiling, and increments only after a successful
link. The parser captures one Prototype/AcDs section per reader path; section
payload retention already caps the sum of source record payloads, and
`m_dataStorageLinkedRecords` prevents any source record from being linked a
second time. The new guard makes those assumptions explicit and resistant to
future multiple-section or repeated-traversal changes.

Link publication is transactional at the allocation boundary: payload and
string values are staged and the unique section/record claim is inserted
before entity fields are published. An allocation/claim failure increments
the existing link-failure count and leaves the entity and byte counter
unchanged. The generated fan-out test links the four retained ~2 MiB records,
checks the exact aggregate count stays under the cap, retries one already
linked entity without double-accounting, and confirms the over-budget fifth
record remains orphaned.

Validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests -j2`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_graph_preservation$' --output-on-failure` (1/1)
- Scoped `git diff --check` is recorded with the receipt.

This accounts for reader-owned source-record payloads and entity attachment
copies. It does not account for consumer callback/document copies, writer-side
pending AcDs payloads, or whole-process allocator overhead; those remain
separate 7S.3 work. No full suite, fixture, CTest registration, peer/native
run, or support promotion was added. Findings/subplans remain 130/73; all six
J items remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8.3 metadata-only AcDs writer preflight (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Added a source-compatible `DRW_parseDataStorage(..., retainPayloads)` overload.
The existing three-argument API keeps its original symbol and defaults to full
payload retention; the explicit `false` route still validates segment/index/
record structure and preserves handles, page references, and record metadata,
but does not copy the record payload vectors. `dwgWriter18::addRawDwgSection()`
uses this metadata-only route because its preflight checks only parse status,
structural validity, and replay eligibility. Finalization still uses the
retaining route, since its pending-record verifier currently compares exact
payload bytes.

The generated blob control verifies the no-retention parse remains structurally
valid/replayable, retains both records and two-page metadata, and leaves the
payload vectors empty. Strict graph-preservation target build and focused CTest
pass (1/1); no new test registration, fixture, dependency, full suite, or
support promotion was added.
