## Deeper/broader FreeCAD subprocess and support-boundary check (2026-10-18; research only)

This pass traced the currently published FreeCAD DWG import wrapper down to
its child-process success condition, then compared that contract with this
checkout's CLI and existing fast/optional tests. It adds an execution-quality
constraint to the existing FreeCAD gates; it does not identify a new local
converter defect.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not establish | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| FreeCAD's current [`Draft/importDWG.py`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py), converter branch around lines 1500–1558 | The LibreDWG route creates a temporary output directory, invokes `dwg2dxf <input> -o <output>`, waits with `communicate()`, and uses output-path existence as its success condition; the visible wrapper does not test the child process return code before returning that path. This is FreeCAD wrapper behavior, not a defect in libdxfrw. | A native integration result must independently require a zero child exit status, a fresh output under a unique temporary directory, successful DXF parse/readback, and the expected identity-level manifest. The GUI's “conversion successful” message or file existence alone is not a pass. For expected failures, require nonzero status and no published partial DXF. |
| FreeCAD's [DWG import documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md), [current format overview](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Manual_Import_and_export_to_other_filetypes.md), and [import/export preferences](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Import_Export_Preferences.md) | The standard DWG path is an external converter followed by the selected DXF importer, whose limitations apply. The documentation describes stock DXF/standard DWG handling as 2D-only for proprietary ACIS content and documents CADExchanger as a separate 3D DWG route. These docs do not prove that every FreeCAD build/plugin behaves identically or that an ACIS payload has valid B-rep semantics. | Preserve two separate consumer rows: stock FreeCAD converter + DXF importer for the advertised 2D/explicit-entity profile; an explicitly named modeler-capable add-on/backend for 3D semantic evidence. Stock FreeCAD opening a file cannot promote ACIS/AcDs semantic support. Where ACIS is outside the selected stock importer, report `CONSUMER_NOT_APPLICABLE` for the solid-semantics cell while still checking emitted carrier bytes and DXF structure independently. |
| Local [`dwg2dxf/main.cpp`](dwg2dxf/main.cpp), [`dwg2dxf_cli_contract_tests.py`](tests/dwg2dxf_cli_contract_tests.py), [`run_freecad_dwg2dxf_compat_test.cmake`](tests/run_freecad_dwg2dxf_compat_test.cmake), and optional [`run_freecad_dwg2dxf_failure_test.cmake`](tests/run_freecad_dwg2dxf_failure_test.cmake) | The local CLI implements the exact `[input, "-o", output]` argument shape used by the FreeCAD wrapper. The fast contract already exercises the FreeCAD-mode defaults/argument behavior, and the optional real-wrapper failure gate explicitly checks that a failed conversion cannot hand off a partial DXF. These are local harness/CLI controls, not a Linux/Windows FreeCAD runtime result. | Reuse these owners; do not duplicate them or add a default FreeCAD dependency. At the composed native checkpoint, run the installed artifact on each requested OS and retain the actual argv, process status, converter hash/version, fresh output hash, parse/readback result, importer backend, and entity disposition. Keep failure-path and native checks optional and out of the per-slice fast loop. |

### Revised implementation-ready acceptance sequence

1. **Fast local gate:** keep the existing CLI compatibility check and touched
   focused test. No FreeCAD installation or repeated application start is
   needed for routine code slices.
2. **Native converter gate (Linux and Windows, composed checkpoint only):**
   call the installed `dwg2dxf` using FreeCAD's exact argument vector in a
   newly-created output directory; assert return code, fresh output identity,
   nonempty/parseable DXF, actual `$ACADVER`, and per-handle/type/owner
   dispositions before opening it in FreeCAD. Record the importer backend and
   relevant preferences.
3. **Native consumer gate:** compare 2D entities and explicit 3D entities only
   against the scope claimed for that exact importer. Separate unsupported
   ACIS/AcDs entities from malformed conversion and from semantic-solid
   results; never treat entity shells or successful open as geometry success.
4. **Independent modeler gate:** use a separately pinned ACIS-capable reader
   for B-rep validity/closedness and analytic measurements, and separately
   verify DWG AcDs owner/key/prototype/history linkage. A FreeCAD add-on that
   shares OCCT with FreeCAD is one geometry lineage, not two independent
   semantic readers.

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8.3 DataStorage move callback for in-tree converter (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

`libdwgr` now transfers each completed typed DataStorage section through an
additive rvalue callback after entity/object parsing has finished. The default
`DRW_Interface` implementation forwards to the existing const-reference
callback, preserving source behavior for existing consumers such as LibreCAD.
The in-tree `dx_iface` overrides the rvalue form and moves the section into
`dx_data::dataStorageSections`, avoiding a deep copy of the section's schema,
index, record, and payload vectors. The legacy const-reference adapter callback
continues to copy when called directly.

The adapter control exercises both callback routes, including exact payload,
schema-name, and handle-index readback. This avoids only the consumer's section
staging copy; reader-owned data, modeler-entity payload copies, callback-time
copies made by other consumers, allocator capacity, and whole-process RSS are
not bounded by this change. The source rvalue transfer is issued only after
`readDwgObjects()` succeeds, so parsing and entity linking have already
consumed the reader-owned section data.

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8.3 zero-copy raw-frame parse input (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The retained raw object owns the immutable byte vector for the full duration of
`replayRawObject()`. The previous code copied that frame into a mutable
`sourceFrameBytes` vector only because the in-memory `dwgBuffer` constructor
accepted `std::uint8_t*`. Changed the internal `dwgCharStream` and `dwgBuffer`
memory-input signatures/storage to `const std::uint8_t*`, then passed
`object.m_rawBytes.data()` directly to the semantic parse. The byte stream
advances its own cursor and copies bytes only into caller-provided output
buffers; clones/forks retain the borrowed const pointer and remain inside this
parse lifetime. No source mutation or public API change is possible through
this input path. Together with the preceding parse-peer vector-copy removal,
the raw frame is no longer redundantly materialized during this validation.

Existing replay controls still verify inline AcDs payload, two-page Blob01
payload with a split marker, exact semantic state and finalization, and orphan
marker refusal. No test source, fixture, or CTest registration changed.

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8.3 AcDs modeler ownership-transfer callback (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Removed two selected library-owned deep copies for completed DWG modeler
entities. `DwgEntityOutput` now journals REGION/3DSOLID/BODY through a
single-delivery owned event, moving the parsed `DRW_ModelerGeometry` into the
event. The event publishes through a new trailing, non-pure rvalue callback;
its default forwards to the pre-existing const-reference callback, so
consumers that only implement the old method continue to receive the entity.
Before moving the typed value, dispatch now constructs the paired
`DRW_UnsupportedObject` view from the complete source entity. This preserves
reactor/common-link vectors and flags that would otherwise be left in the
moved-from object. The in-tree `dx_iface` override then moves the typed value
into block storage instead of copying all retained payload/frame vectors. The
separately budgeted DataStorage-record-to-entity payload copy, the independent
raw-view carrier, and arbitrary consumer-owned copies remain unchanged.

Generated AC1027 coverage asserts that modeler shell and two-page AcDs dispatch
use the rvalue callback and preserve exact typed/raw identity, owner, reactor
handle, AcDs flag, frame, and payload bytes. A focused adapter control verifies
the in-tree transfer and default forwarding to a legacy const-reference
override. The interface method is trailing and
non-pure, but downstream binaries must rebuild; no binary ABI compatibility
is claimed.

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8.3 modeler raw-frame ownership transfer (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

REGION/3DSOLID/BODY parsing and AcDs linking complete before the typed modeler
entity takes ownership of the object-frame body with a vector move. The paired
raw `DRW_UnsupportedObject` is then copied once from the typed entity's frame
and moved into the previously added owned journal event. This removes the
typed entity's former `tmpByteStr` deep copy while retaining two independent
callback values whose complete raw-frame byte vectors match exactly. The

all other raw-entity callers keep their existing source and behavior.

callback and byte equality between its frame and the typed modeler's frame,
alongside the existing handle, owner, AcDs key, and payload assertions. The
move occurs after all parser reads and data-storage linking; the branch does
not subsequently access the moved-from parser body or its `dwgBuffer` view.

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8.3 raw-object journal ownership transfer (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Completed the owned raw-object journal path through the consumer boundary.
Added a trailing, non-pure `DRW_Interface::addUnsupportedObject(
DRW_UnsupportedObject&&)` callback whose default forwards to the existing
const-reference callback. `MoveValueEvent` now uses that route and has an
explicit one-shot guard, so replay cannot redeliver a moved-from raw frame.
Existing `appendValue(..., &DRW_Interface::addUnsupportedObject)` callers
remain source-compatible: a typed internal callback overload disambiguates
the legacy const-reference member pointer without changing those call sites.

The generated reader-matrix control covers both receiver contracts. A
const-reference-only `ModelerDispatchSink` observes the original frame through
the default forwarding implementation; a move-aware sink retains the same
256 KiB vector allocation by move. Both check callback count, payload size,
handle/content, and that replaying the event a second time returns false and
does not invoke the callback again.

Focused verification passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests dwg2dxf lc3_compat_check -j2`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests --acds-modeler-move-callback` (`PASS`)
- `build-gcc/tests/libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests --modeler-geometry-move-callback-fallback` (exit 0)
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix$' --output-on-failure` (1/1)
- Scoped `git diff --check` for the changed interface, journal, and test sources

No new CTest registration, fixture, dependency, full suite, peer/native run,
or support promotion was added. This is a trailing virtual and preserves
source-level legacy forwarding, but it is not a binary-ABI compatibility
claim; downstream consumers must rebuild. It removes no copies for a
const-reference-only consumer and does not alter the `dx_iface` raw-entity
policy. Remaining payload attachment, section retention, and arbitrary
consumer-owned storage are separate costs. Findings/subplans remain 130/73;
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The shared
worktree is broadly dirty; this slice was not staged or committed.

## Deeper/broader independent implementation and consumer route crosswalk (2026-10-18; research only)

This pass compares the current public contracts of independent DWG/DXF
implementations and downstream consumers by executable route, not by broad
format labels. It resolves several tempting but invalid comparator joins:
GDAL's DWG reader is not its DXF driver, FreeCAD's DWG import is not a native
DWG decoder, and a libdxfrw fork is not an independent parser. These are
route-scope refinements; no peer binary or external drawing was run.

| Implementation / primary source | What the source establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| [LibreDWG README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg), [manual coverage/unknown-object discussion](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi), and [NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | The project describes a broad DWG reader and multiple DXF/JSON/SVG output tools, but also says advanced R2010+ objects may be skipped. Its README/manual describe different write ceilings and caveats for R2007 and R2010–R2018, while the manual says unknown classes may remain raw object blobs without DXF codes. Those are source-level scope statements; they do not provide a single immutable per-entity conformance matrix or an expected semantic answer for every input. LibreDWG is GPL-3.0-or-later, which also makes direct code reuse a separate license decision for this GPL-2.0-or-later project. | Keep LibreDWG as an optional, separately implemented DWG decode/DXF conversion differential. ## Implementation progress — PAR-23/7J DIMENSION DSTYLE canonical writer emission (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Completed canonical DXF writing for the same modeled DSTYLE subset used by the
reader. Ordinary DIMENSION, ARC_DIMENSION, and LARGE_RADIAL_DIMENSION paths now
place values in one ACAD/DSTYLE subsection, not in the legacy direct groups.
The writer maps 12 public fields to variables 47, 48, 71, 72, 146, 272, 274,
279, 283, 284, 285, and 286, with the documented typed values/ranges. It merges
into an existing ACAD group and DSTYLE subsection, replaces a known pair when
the typed field differs, preserves unchanged pairs (including explicit zero),
and preserves unknown pairs and their order. When there is no DSTYLE subsection,
it adds one to the existing ACAD app group or creates the ACAD group. Malformed
DSTYLE, malformed app grouping, and invalid modeled ranges fail before DIMENSION
record output. The standalone group-code classifier remains unchanged; numeric
groups 80–84 are not emitted.

The generated Wave 1 matrix checks all 12 field mappings in ASCII and Binary,
asserts exact ordered DSTYLE key/value subsequences and absence of the old direct
groups, verifies an edited typed value replaces its raw pair while an unknown
pair and matching explicit-zero pair remain unchanged, verifies that a new
subsection is inserted into an existing ACAD app group, and checks malformed or
out-of-range input is rejected before output. The existing generated reader
selector independently verifies the same input grammar and callback projection.

## Implementation progress — PAR-23/7J DIMENSION style-resource closure (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Strict modern full conversion now resolves a DIMSTYLE's group 340 text-style
reference to an emitted STYLE row, and groups 341–344 to planned BLOCK_RECORDs
whose BLOCK/ENDBLK bodies actually emitted. When a parsed source handle is
available, source handle→name and emitted handle identity are checked before
the output references are written. Empty arrow names remain defaults; the
closed-filled / zero-handle sentinel is represented as handle `0`; a named
arrow must resolve to a real planned block body. A mismatch, absent STYLE or
BLOCK_RECORD, or bodyless arrow block rejects the strict conversion atomically.

Generated-from-scratch ASCII and Binary full-conversion controls cover the
positive named resources, all four arrow slots, dynamic DIMSTYLE variables,
DXF import→re-export handle remapping, and negative missing-style,
missing-block, missing-body, and source name/handle mismatch cases. No
persistent DWG/DXF fixture or new CTest registration was added. This is
resource-reference/body closure only; no built-in arrow block is synthesized,
and it does not establish all DIMSTYLE version fields, dimension geometry,
constraint classification, rendering, or external/native semantics.

## Implementation progress — PAR-23/7J DIMENSION picture body closure (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Strict modern conversion now distinguishes a planned picture BLOCK_RECORD from
an emitted and closed BLOCK body. During the BLOCKS phase, a nonempty DIMENSION
group-2 name is checked against the planned-name map and recorded as a pending
reference; this permits forward references within BLOCKS. Each user block is
added to the emitted-body index only after its ENDBLK is written, and the two
fixed model/paper space bodies are registered after their output succeeds. At
the BLOCKS boundary, every pending picture name must resolve to an emitted
body. A subsequent modelspace DIMENSION is admitted only if its named body is
in that completed index. Missing bodies report
`incomplete-dimension-picture-block` and fail atomically.

The emitted and pending indexes participate in the existing write-attempt
mutation journal. Failed BLOCKS output rolls them back with the record scope;
the outer destination transaction preserves existing bytes. The guard is
limited to strict modern conversion. Empty names stay unclassified, R12 and
standalone legacy writer behavior is unchanged, and this work does not claim
constraint semantics.

Generated ASCII/Binary tests cover all three supported DIMENSION writer routes
(ordinary, ARC_DIMENSION, LARGE_RADIAL_DIMENSION), missing body refusal,
complete body admission, a forward picture reference inside another block,
modelspace use after BLOCKS, and an unresolved forward target with unchanged
output and rolled-back indexes. No DWG/DXF fixture was added.

- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_wave1$' --output-on-failure` (1/1)
- `jq empty` for the implementation receipt
- Scoped `git diff --check` for the plan, source/header/test, and receipt

This is deliberately only the name→BLOCK_RECORD→closed-body boundary. It does
not yet prove source-child identity/owner preservation, nested INSERT targets,
arrow/style/linetype resource closure, anonymous constraint classification,
full `dxfRW::write`/CLI conversion behavior, picture geometry, or consumer
rendering. The next local 7J/7G work remains child-owner and nested-resource
closure plus the full conversion route; independent ezdxf/FreeCAD/native gates
stay at the composed checkpoint. No new CTest registration, dependency, full

### Evidence and implementation-readiness refinement

The issue set supports four independent result columns, and the plan must not
collapse them into a single “conversion passed” bit:

1. **Value meaning:** compare authoritative/source bytes or tags to the decoded
   field and an independently authored expected value (for example CMC method,
   codepage byte-to-scalar, or a curve parameter). A plausible picture or
   palette lookup is not a value oracle.
2. **Framing and progress:** verify record order, encoded lengths, exact cursor
   consumption and a following record/object sentinel. For writers, also
   require terminal group-0 `EOF`, complete required sections and a truthful
   failure status; EOF alone does not establish source completeness.
3. **Identity and graph/carrier closure:** account for each source handle/type,
   owner/block/layout path, required references and opaque payload, with an
   explicit emitted, refused or unsupported disposition. A surviving shell,
   block name, or global count does not prove children or ACIS/AcDs data.
4. **Consumer semantics:** record the exact native application/platform,
   version, backend/options, open/recovery state, audit repairs/deletions and
   resulting geometry. A peer self-roundtrip or raw ASM exposure cannot
   substitute for this result.

Implementation speed remains the current policy: select the owning local test
target and smallest generated selector; make one path change; run the strict
target build, selector and owning fast CTest; update the progress ledger and
receipt immediately. Only after that local slice is green should an unresolved
composed checkpoint consume a pinned peer or native application. If peer
reports disagree with the primary specification, keep that support cell
unqualified and continue independent work; do not block unrelated slices or
guess at wire semantics. This pass changes neither existing implementation
order nor validation frequency and adds no new peer dependency.

The review found no unrepresented confirmed local defect and adds zero findings
or top-level subplans. Existing pending fast controls (including terminal EOF
assertion, LAYOUT shade-DPI DWG retention, and encoded CP8/UTF-16 length edges)
remain under their current owners, not duplicated here. J256, J260, J268,
J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; none of these sources promotes
their support claims.

goal was to decide whether a new local defect or routine validation lane is

| ODA [Open Design Specification §28, pp. 260–261](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) | Each application EED block begins with a bit-short data length, an APPID handle, and a typed item stream; the length excludes its own encoding and APPID handle. Item types have specific byte widths, including length-prefixed strings/binary and fixed-width handles, points, doubles and integers. The specification defines wire framing, not an allocation strategy or a per-process memory target. | Keep the outer application-data length, typed item span, APPID identity and next-field/object boundary as distinct checks. A peer's allocation formula is not normative DWG grammar. |

The PR is still open/unmerged in the reviewed state, has one approving review and a maintainer comment that a `pslib` installation issue remains. These are author-reported LibreDWG measurements, not a local reproduction, general peer release result or format limit. | Use this as a resource-risk/test-shape lead only. Do not transfer the reported RSS values, sample sizes or proposed `realloc` code to libdxfrw; pin exact peer state if an optional comparison is later run. |
| Local `src/intern/dwgreader.cpp::readDwgEed`, `src/intern/dwgreader.h::DwgEedChunk`, `src/drw_objects.cpp::DRW_TableEntry::parseDwgImpl`, `src/drw_entities.cpp` EED publication, and `src/intern/dwgsafety.h` | The parser reads a bounded outer chunk into one byte vector, decodes item types against that chunk's remaining bytes with per-type bounds, stages typed `DRW_Variant` values and layer-reference indexes, and publishes only after parsing succeeds. Existing ceilings are 65,536 chunks, 65,536 items per chunk and 1,000,000 total EED items. Table-entry and entity publication then allocate public variant nodes from the staged items. The source mechanism inspected is not the peer's per-item allocation of the entire remaining chunk; however the temporary bytes, typed chunk vector and public staging create multiple linear representations, and the peak-memory constant has not been measured. | Do not register a new local finding from the peer report. Keep bounded item count and transactional publication. If the local path becomes an evidenced bottleneck, first account for simultaneous representations and copy counts; optimize ownership/streaming only while preserving rollback, APPID/layer handle resolution, item order and exact cursor consumption. Avoid per-item shrink/realloc churn unless a measured allocator profile warrants it. |
| Existing local EED controls and PAR-92/7BA scale lane | The plan already has generated DWG EED unsigned-length boundaries (32,767/32,768/65,535/65,536 bytes), exact split/order checks, refusal/retry coverage, and a following-LINE full-file sentinel. PAR-92/7BA already owns composed scale measurement and bounded work-counter reasoning. The current leaf does not establish peak RSS for one object with many small numeric values. | Do not duplicate the wire-boundary test or add a permanent external drawing. On the next EED parser/publication change, extend the existing fast selector only if needed to assert a dense, generated item sequence and following-object integrity. At the single composed scale checkpoint, use one locally generated, scratch-only dense EED case (20,000 small numeric items is a peer-inspired case, not a format threshold) and report process/runtime/build identity, decoded item count, output disposition, elapsed time and peak RSS. Treat the measurement as diagnostic—no brittle absolute RSS gate—and run it only if EED code changed or profiling identifies EED as a bottleneck. |

### Implementation-readiness refinement

1. Keep ordinary per-slice validation fast: changed strict target, smallest
   EED owner selector, owning fast CTest and compatibility check. Existing
   length-boundary coverage remains sufficient when an unrelated code path is
   changed.
2. For a touched EED decoder/publication path, require exact item order and
   values, APPID and layer-reference resolution, byte-exact chunk consumption,
   the following field/object sentinel, and same-reader retry after malformed
   input. Use an in-memory generated control in the existing test executable;
   do not commit a peer/customer DWG or create a new CTest target for this.
3. If a local dense-EED cost is suspected, inspect whether cost comes from
   repeated tail-sized allocations, vector growth, `DRW_Variant` copies,
   per-node ownership, APPID/layer resolution, or retained public storage
   before changing code. A local optimization must have a bounded ownership
   plan and retain fail-closed publication semantics; preserve all six wire
   and handle-resolution invariants above.
4. Run the generated 20,000-item scratch scale observation once at the
   existing PAR-92/7BA composed checkpoint, only when an EED change or local
   profile makes it relevant. Record raw output/diagnostics and exact process
   identity; do not assert peer-reported memory ratios or make large RSS,
   sanitizer, peer, or native runs part of each implementation slice.

## Implementation progress — PAR-23/7J nested INSERT body closure (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Strict modern conversion now records non-emitted INSERT targets encountered
inside BLOCKS and checks the pending target names against the body index after
the final ENDBLK. This accepts forward nested references when a matching block
body is emitted later in the section, while refusing a BLOCK_RECORD that has
no emitted body. Once BLOCKS is complete, a modelspace INSERT is admitted only
when its target body is present. The pending-name index uses the existing
write-mutation journal and is cleared/reset with the write session, so a failed
record or failed BLOCKS transaction does not retain attempt-local state.

The existing ASCII/Binary strict full-conversion selector now exercises a
picture block containing a nested INSERT whose target body is emitted later;
readback checks the INSERT target name, nested block-record/body association,

### Refined peer admission and implementation order

For every optional peer/native evidence row, include its declared unsupported,
unstable, unhandled, and untested limits alongside the exact repository
revision/package, direction, format version, tool options, dependency/license,
lineage, and observed record disposition. Grade the local pipeline in separate
stages: bytes/version recognized → record/class decoded → callback/model
published → graph/reference closure → raw carrier integrity → independent
geometry semantics → target consumer acceptance. A dropped/ignored/unsupported
result is not a pass; an undocumented or unavailable route is inconclusive.

The practical consequence is to stop screening general-purpose repositories
for an ACIS semantic oracle based on broad README claims. No reviewed open-source
route in this pass supplies an independent, demonstrated end-to-end DWG
AcDs/SAB-to-valid-B-rep result: LibreDWG documents ACDS records as unhandled,
FreeCAD's stock importer documents ACIS as unreadable, and standard open-source
OCCT does not include the commercial ACIS exchange component. Continue searching
only when a candidate has a concrete, independently testable exact route; if
none is available, record `NOT_AVAILABLE` and continue the local implementation
queue. This does not remove the existing external/native qualification gates.

## Implementation progress — PAR-26/7S DWG string-length writer boundaries (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The existing `libdxfrw_writer_primitives` test now exercises the actual
length-prefixed DWG text sinks at their encoded-unit boundaries. Generated
inputs cover:

1. CP8 and ENC: 65,534 payload bytes plus the required terminator, producing
   the maximum unsigned BS count (`0xFFFF`); byte payload, trailing NUL, and a
   following `0xA5` sentinel are checked through the bit-level reader.

   represented by a surrogate pair. The test checks the encoded unit count,
   exact terminal code units, surrogate bytes, and following sentinel.
3. Rejection: 65,535 payload bytes for CP8/ENC and 65,535 UTF-16 payload units
   are rejected before a length or payload byte is emitted; writer error state
   remains visible.

character report. Inputs are created in memory; no fixture, dependency, test

### Implementation-ready one-time check

1. **Artifact admission:** only at the existing composed S8 checkpoint, resolve
   the exact `cadmpeg-codec-sat` 0.6.1 archive/integrity, matching source commit,

   `ACIS BinaryFile` 217/218, `ASM BinaryFile4/8`, or text. Require the pinned
   decoder to report the exact admitted branch and version, all required
   bodies, and no unexplained geometry-transfer loss. Any unverified dialect,
   unknown required topology, incomplete body, or `geometry_not_transferred`

3. **Independent expected values:** author the expected dimensions, placement,
   unit conversion, bounds, volume/area, topology counts, orientation, and
   permitted tolerances before decoding. Compare these to the CADMPEG result;
   parser self-roundtrip and its own “direct-carrier parity” statement are
   useful scope evidence, not an independent expected-value oracle.
4. **Prove the outer join first:** for DXF, retain entity handle plus ordered
   inline group-1/3 or ACDSDATA group-310 chunks and keys; for DWG, retain the
   entity handle plus inline modeler frame or AcDs section/key/owner/index.

   CADMPEG. Keep its payload result separate from carrier preservation and
   object-graph closure.
5. **Keep consumer evidence separate:** CADMPEG does not satisfy the native
   Linux/Windows FreeCAD gate. The stock FreeCAD route is converter→selected
   DXF importer and documents no stock ACIS solid import. If another safe,
   pinned modeler-capable consumer is unavailable, mark that consumer stage
   `NOT_AVAILABLE` and continue; do not hold local implementation or promote
   a support claim.
6. **Preserve speed and provenance:** no CADMPEG install/build in ordinary
   slices, no CMake/CI dependency, no persistent or downloaded DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB
   fixture, and no repeated full suite. Use only generated scratch bytes at
   the composed gate. After the optional check, report a compact receipt with
   exact source/payload/output hashes, diagnostics/losses, body disposition,
   independent expected-value comparison, and the remaining consumer gate.

### Implementation-ready PAR-12/S13 addition

1. Reuse the existing hardening/writer test owner; do not create a new CTest
   registration or add a third-party tool. Generate small inputs in memory:
   supported valid typed graphs plus nearby invalid cases (unresolved owner or
   resource, duplicate/ambiguous handle, unsafe line break, and a value that
   cannot be represented in the selected output profile). Keep the generator
   deterministic and explicitly cap case count, entity count, and output bytes.

   framing scan over the emitted bytes: every group-code/value pair is complete,

   of the intended role. Compare the small semantic manifest to the existing
   exact writer assertions; do not infer all-feature semantics from framing.

   replacement or partial append, repair the model, and retry through the same
   writer/output path. This checks publication safety, not merely an error
   return.
4. Run the focused selector only when generic writer framing, validation,
   transaction, or handle allocation changes, or at one existing scheduled
   hardening checkpoint. Keep the ordinary per-slice loop on one owning fast
   test, strict build and relevant consumer-compatibility compile; no full
   suite, broad mutation campaign, peer runtime or native CAD run is added.
5. Consider coverage-guided writer mutation only if this deterministic property
   test demonstrates a named branch/state-space gap. Keep any future campaign
   opt-in, scratch-only and locally seeded; never commit fuzz-generated DXF or
   peer/customer samples.

## Implementation progress — PAR-12/S13 generated whole-output DXF property (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Implemented the bounded writer-output property recommended by the cross-project
conversion and cross-language writer reviews. Its independent tokenizer reads
ASCII and Binary DXF bytes directly; it does not invoke libdxfrw's own reader.
The generated AC1027 controls assert complete group pairs, balanced required
sections, one terminal EOF, unique emitted self-handles, the `*Model_Space`
BLOCK_RECORD identity, and LINE owner closure to that record. Zero and fixed-
low source handles are included. No drawing fixture was added; all output is
generated in a uniquely named system-temporary directory and removed on test
exit.

The property exposed a local defect in `dxfRW::writeEntity`: a repeated,
non-ambiguous source handle on ordinary typed entities could reuse the first
entity's emitted handle. The writer now atomically refuses that case. A
source handle explicitly marked ambiguous before entity emission retains the
existing behavior: each entity is minted a distinct output identity and the
ambiguous key is not used for reference remapping. Tests also seed an existing
destination, force a lossless-text refusal, verify byte-for-byte preservation,
then repair the model and retry through the same `dxfRW` instance.

Validation was intentionally local and fast: strict `libdxfrw_hardening_tests`
build passed; focused `--dxf-writer-output-property` passed; owning
`libdxfrw_hardening` CTest passed (1/1, 0.32 s). The full suite, independent
peer, native CAD applications, and fixture ingestion were not run. No CTest
registration or dependency was added. This slice changes output behavior only
for an unqualified duplicate source identity; no DWG/DXF feature-support or
consumer-acceptance claim is promoted. Because the shared worktree contains
extensive pre-existing user changes, this slice remains uncommitted and
unstaged.

## Implementation progress — AC1027 DXF ACDSDATA raw owner-key retry control (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Corrected the retry assertion in the existing generated
`runDxfAcdsMultipleDataStorageProjection` owner. DXF import retains the
ACDSDATA section as raw groups; it does not attach each SAB body to
`DRW_ModelerGeometry::dataStorageData`, which is the typed DWG DataStorage
carrier. For this DXF route, the association contract is the ACDSRECORD group
320 owner key resolving to the emitted modeler entity handle, together with
exact section payload and chunk preservation.

Validation passed: strict build of `libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip`, focused
`--dxf-acds-multiple-data-storage` selector (ASCII and Binary), and owning
`libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip` CTest (1/1, 3.23 s). The selector
covers the valid multi-record raw section, omitted-middle-chunk and
reordered-chunk refusal, preservation of the pre-existing destination
sentinel, then repaired export through the same exporter and strict readback
of all five records with owner-key closure. The prior assertion incorrectly
required the raw DXF SAB also to appear in the DWG-only typed payload field;
the production parser/writer was not changed.

No CTest registration, external or committed fixture, dependency, production
change, or support promotion was added. The full suite was not run in this
slice. Synthetic SAB framing and raw association do not
establish valid ACIS geometry or solid semantics. The shared worktree remains
uncommitted and unstaged; findings/subplans remain 130/73 and all six external
items remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3/S3.7 shared-loop coedge-count memoization (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Rooted SAB wireframe extraction now caches each source loop's coedge-ring
cardinality for the duration of one extraction. Multiple faces can reference
the same loop graph, so the previous path walked each coedge ring once per
face/loop occurrence even though its count is invariant for the immutable
model. The cache does not deduplicate output: every face still receives its
own ordered `DRW_AcisFaceLoop` rows, and each face's loop-chain cycle guard
remains independent. Each cache entry consumes one `maxOutputItems` unit before
the map insertion; allocation failure remains distinct through the existing
`bad_alloc` outcome path. This bounds cache entry count, not allocator bytes or
RSS.

The generated 4-face/4-loop/4-coedge control now verifies all four faces retain
the same ordered source loop identities and count 4 on every row. Its measured
extraction-work counter remains higher than the one-face control because face
projection is still per-face, but is below four times that control, detecting
the removed repeated coedge-ring traversal. Existing 8×8 shared-cycle output
and exact-budget/one-under ResourceLimit controls remain in the same executable.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3/S3.7 shared-vertex point-result memoization (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Wireframe extraction now resolves each source vertex's point once per
`extractAcisWireframeImpl` invocation and caches both resolved coordinates and
unresolved results. Edge endpoints that refer to the same vertex reuse the
cached result instead of rescanning the vertex's pointer list and point-token
sequence. The vertex and edge output loops remain unchanged: every source
vertex/edge is emitted in its prior order, every endpoint keeps its original
coordinate, and unresolved-vertex diagnostics still occur once at the vertex
row. No transform, units, topology, or semantic policy changed.

Each vertex-result cache entry reserves one existing `maxOutputItems` unit
before lookup/materialization and map insertion. Existing projected vertex and
edge rows and diagnostics retain their own accounting. This bounds entry
count, not `std::map` allocator bytes, node overhead, or RSS; any
`std::bad_alloc` remains reported through the existing allocation-failure
path. The generated one-edge/eight-edge ACIS 21800 streams share one vertex
and point. Readback asserts all eight edge endpoint pairs retain the same
coordinates, and deterministic extraction work remains below eight times the
one-edge baseline. An exact work/cache-item budget passes; one fewer work unit
refuses and clears the projection.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3/S3.7 shared intcurve control-polygon memoization (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Each referencing edge previously re-read the shared `intcurve-curve` record's
NUBS/NURBS subtype and knot sequence before appending the same control polygon.
The extractor now caches the parsed control-point vector by source curve-node
index. It still assigns an independently owned vector to every edge; the
cache is not exposed in the public model or shared across extractions.

The cache node and parsed points are charged before/while they are retained,
and every edge's copied control points are separately charged to
`maxOutputItems`. Copy work is charged by control-point count. The generated
ACIS 21800 SAB contains 16 knot doubles and two known control points, with one
curve referenced by one edge and by an eight-edge fan-out. Tests preserve both
point tuples for every edge, assert distinct vector storage, show fan-out work
below eight times the one-edge case, admit exact work/output-item limits, and
refuse one work unit below the measured bound with cleared output.

- `git diff --check -- src/drw_acis.cpp tests/graph_preservation_tests.cpp`

This is a deterministic work-counter result, not a wall-clock benchmark or a

## Deeper/broader question-specific peer independence and directional support matrix (2026-10-18; research only)

This review widened and reconciled the open-source comparison by asking two
questions per candidate: exactly which operation/version/record path does its
source establish, and along which dimensions is its evidence independent of
libdxfrw and of the expected result? A repository or product is not a single
independent vote: implementation ancestry, shared specification/algorithm
references, sample producer, expected-value author, wrapper, projection,
geometry kernel, and native consumer can have different provenance.

| Project/route and primary source | Source-grounded scope and caveat | Plan use |
|---|---|---|
| [LibreDWG manual](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi), [project test/fuzz entry points](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg), and [DWG reader CLI](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/programs/dwgread.1) | LibreDWG is a distinct C DWG/DXF implementation with broad version claims, structured warning/error behavior, corpus tests, and fuzzing workflows. Its own manual describes implementation coverage as ongoing and distinguishes stable, unstable, debug-only, and unhandled classes; broad percentages and same-library rewrite/re-read do not prove each type's semantic or writer correctness. | Keep LibreDWG as a broad independent C DWG peer, but compare only a named version/entity/direction. Capture its exact release or commit, class maturity, diagnostics and skip/error state, and compare against an independently authored manifest. Reuse its assurance *method categories* (corpus, unit, fuzz) only at existing planned gates; do not make its corpus or full suite a per-slice prerequisite. |
| [ACadSharp README/version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) and [reader notification API example](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/docs/articles/samples/reading.md) | The current matrix varies by format direction and release: for example, AC1009 is DXF read-only; AC1012 has DXF read/write but no DWG read/write; AC1021 lists DWG read but not write. A returned `CadDocument` and notifications are useful observations, not a complete per-handle loss ledger or proof of resource/3D closure. Current open reports also remain version- and entity-specific. | Keep direction × version explicit in every peer admission row. Capture notifications plus source-record/handle disposition; do not infer a missing write path from a read checkmark, or a clean read from the absence of a thrown exception. Select ACadSharp only where the exact overlapping route answers a current local question. |
| [`dwg-rs` README and measured coverage report](https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/dwg-rs) | Its current project page labels the reader pre-alpha, reports decoded/skipped/errored counts over its own versioned sample set, and documents major per-entity gaps and no external CAD acceptance for its experimental DWG writer. It says the decoder is based on ODA's published spec and that one LZ77 detail was cross-checked against ACadSharp documentation; it also states no LibreDWG source was consulted. | Treat it as a distinct, spec-derived structural/decoder route, with the shared ODA-spec basis and limited algorithm cross-reference recorded rather than collapsing independence to yes/no. Its counters demonstrate a useful denominator/disposition reporting format, not a comparable score until sample identities and type mix match. Do not use the pre-alpha writer as output acceptance. |
| [ezdxf support overview](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/), [DXF entity source](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dxfentity.py), and [ACIS documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) | ezdxf is a DXF reader/writer with a version-specific feature model; its source explicitly says changing output version does not convert unsupported features and such features may simply be ignored. Its ACIS path exposes SAT/SAB carrier handling and limited flat-face polygon projection, not a general ACIS kernel or complete curved B-rep semantics. | A DXF peer comparison must record source and target DXF versions and classify each input field as represented, retained opaque, projected, omitted, rejected, or transformed. Treat ACIS byte/carrier and flat-face checks separately from exact solid geometry; do not use a version override or successful save as a conversion-fidelity claim. |
| [IxMilia.Dxf compatibility README](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf) and [changelog](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) | It declares DXF read/write from R10 through R2014 with explicit missing MESH, MLEADER, SURFACE, TABLE, and VIEWPORT support; it separately warns that output for types including 3DSOLID/BODY/REGION may not open in AutoCAD and notes R13 output caveats. | Use only as an optional structural/field comparator for a matching legacy DXF question. A constructible class or library round-trip is not target-application writer acceptance. No .NET install/build is added to the ordinary implementation loop. |
| [GDAL DXF driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) and [FreeCAD DWG wrapper](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py) / [Draft DXF documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) | GDAL produces OGR geometry projections with documented omissions/tessellation and can expose raw ASM for a restricted modern-DXF route; it is not a CAD document graph or B-rep result. Stock FreeCAD composes an external DWG converter with a selected DXF importer; its documentation says stock DXF import does not consume embedded ACIS solids. | Keep parser, converter, intermediate DXF, importer/backend, and resulting model as separate stages. Use GDAL only for explicit supported projection fields; qualify FreeCAD 2D consumer behavior with exact platform/build/settings, while leaving its stock route out of ACIS/B-rep promotion. |
| [UnCAD README](https://github.com/iyulab/uncad) and [codelibs/libdxfrw fork](https://github.com/codelibs/libdxfrw) | UnCAD's DWG parser is vendored LibreDWG via FFI while its DXF path is a distinct `undxf` route; its current output is model/JSON/rendering rather than DWG/DXF write. codelibs identifies as a fork of original SourceForge libdxfrw, advertises a separate test suite but points at external `fess-testdata`; it is a correlated fork, not independent parser ancestry. | Deduplicate at the underlying parser, not at app/repository count. For UnCAD, attribute DWG results to the exact LibreDWG artifact and consider `undxf` only for a named DXF question. For codelibs, inspect immutable fork/base diffs only if a specific patch can resolve a local gap; external corpus claims do not authorize importing or committing sample files. |

### Implementation-ready comparator admission and fastest route

1. Represent evidence independence as a per-question tuple, not a boolean:
   (a) parser source ancestry, (b) normative-spec/shared-algorithm lineage,
   (c) input producer and sample provenance, (d) expected-value authorship,
   (e) wrapper/projection lineage, and (f) geometry-kernel/native-consumer
   lineage. Mark each `independent`, `shared`, `derived`, or `unknown` for the
   question under review. This prevents a separate app, language, or package
   from creating a false independent vote.
2. Make the comparison key explicit before selecting a peer:
   format/container + exact version + ASCII/binary mode + read/write direction
   + entity/object family + owner/reference graph + payload/carrier + selected
   semantic fields + loss/disposition class. A peer that does not overlap this
   key is not a useful validation target for that slice.
3. Prefer the lowest-cost evidence order: (i) source/API and version-matrix
   screen; (ii) compare to the already generated local control and independent
   literal/spec expectation; (iii) run one exact-pinned peer only at the
   existing composed checkpoint if it can distinguish the unresolved result;
   (iv) run a native consumer only for the separately planned platform gate.
   If artifact/runtime, input mode, provenance, or expected semantic values
   cannot be bound promptly, record `NOT_RUN` and return to the local queue.
4. For a selected peer result, inventory every source record/handle and report
   `typed`, `opaque-preserved`, `projected`, `unsupported`, `skipped`,
   `rejected`, or `lost`; retain diagnostics and owner/resource links. Score
   parser acceptance, serialization, re-open by a different implementation,
   geometric semantics, and native application acceptance separately. An
   aggregate success percentage is not a substitute for the per-route
   denominator and dispositions.
5. Keep the implementation-speed contract unchanged: one focused local test
   selector/owning CTest per slice; no peer installation, download, full suite,
   native app, new fixture, or new dependency in that loop. Run broad suites,
   fuzz windows, and selected peer/native gates only at existing integration
   boundaries. Preserve the local-generated-only fixture policy and continue
   unrelated ready work when any optional route is unavailable.

implementation ordering and test cadence are unchanged. Findings/subplans

`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and cannot promote support claims. The broad worktree
remains uncommitted; no files were staged.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3/S3.7 single-pass SAB candidate classification (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The wireframe extractor previously made three complete passes over the same
candidate-node sequence, filtering once each for vertices, edges, and faces.
It now classifies and projects candidates in a single pass. Each output vector
still preserves the source order of its own node category. Diagnostics are
buffered by category and joined in the established vertex, edge, then face
order, so mixed record ordering does not change the externally observed
diagnostic sequence. Vertex-point, curve, surface, and shared-loop caches
remain per extraction with their previous item/work accounting.

Generated one/eight SAB controls contain otherwise unprojected local record
types. The extraction-work delta is exactly seven, proving one candidate-scan
unit per additional node rather than the former three category scans. Exact
work/output-item limits admit the eight-record case; a one-unit-under work
limit refuses and clears caller-visible output. A separately generated
in-memory model orders a face before a missing-point vertex and a degenerate
edge, then verifies diagnostic order remains vertex → edge → face. These are
deterministic operation counters and semantic checks, not a wall-clock
benchmark.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3/S3.7 combined SAB edge-reference scan (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

Edge projection previously traversed each edge's ordered reference list to
find its first two vertex refs, stopped, then started a second full scan at
the first ref to find the first `-curve` node. It now records those two
independent first matches in one pass and stops once both have been found.
Endpoint ordering, first-curve selection, missing-endpoint behavior, point
resolution, curve projection, diagnostics, and output order are unchanged.
The scan continues after the second vertex when no curve has yet been found,
matching the old full curve search in that case.

Generated one/eight SAB controls contain two distinct endpoint vertices, a
shared straight-curve node, and a full five-slot edge reference row in the
order null/pattern, start vertex, end vertex, null/coedge, curve. Both shapes
preserve exact endpoint and curve values. The deterministic work delta is
exactly six per added edge: one candidate visit plus one pass over five
references, versus the prior endpoint scan plus a second curve scan. Exact
work/output-item limits admit; a one-unit-under work cap refuses and clears
the output. This is a source-counter comparison, not a wall-clock benchmark
or memory/RSS claim.

Validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests -j2`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_graph_preservation$' --output-on-failure` (1/1, 0.59 s)
- `git diff --check -- src/drw_acis.cpp tests/graph_preservation_tests.cpp DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md`

No DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB fixture, CTest registration, dependency, public API/layout
change, full suite, peer/native run, or support promotion was added. Findings
and top-level subplans remain 130/73; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The shared worktree remains broadly modified and
uncommitted; no files were staged.

Next local action: continue the existing dependency-ready 7S.2c–d/7S.3
retention/accounting queue. Inspect one concrete source-level repeat or
unaccounted owner at a time, add a focused generated control, and update this
progress ledger after its owning fast test. Do not add further caching unless
the source demonstrates another repeated invariant traversal; if the next
candidate needs unavailable peer/native evidence, mark only that evidence
cell `NOT_RUN` and continue with a ready local item.

The existing FreeCAD Linux/Windows qualification remains the required consumer gate where applicable. |

### Implementation-ready optional-use checks

1. Do not build or install KumCAD merely to add another comparison point. First
   name the specific unresolved 2D consumer behavior and establish that the
   current required consumer route does not already answer it.
2. If admitted, pin the application commit, build configuration, OS/toolchain,
   Qt/runtime dependencies, and exact LibreDWG source or binary version. Treat
   the README's LibreDWG 0.13.3 recipe as a discovery lead until the built
   executable's linked codec and effective output are verified.
3. Use only an existing eligible repository sample or a tiny locally authored
   case; do not import or commit external/peer/customer drawings. Write expected
   entity identity, owner/block/layout path, geometry, units, and text values
   independently before executing the app.
4. Record DWG import, DXF import, DWG export, and DXF export as separate
   operations. For output, capture the requested target and actual DWG magic or
   DXF `$ACADVER`, output hash, process result, diagnostics, strict reopen, and
   per-source-record disposition. A successful open/render or aggregate count
   alone is not a semantic pass.
5. Keep explicit planar entities (`SOLID`, `3DFACE`, mesh polylines) separate
   from modeler entities (`3DSOLID`, `REGION`, `BODY`) and from raw AcDs/SAB
   retention. No KumCAD result can promote ACIS/B-rep claims without a
   documented import path and independent per-body semantic comparison.
6. Do not use KumCAD for macOS qualification based on its CI statement alone;
   the project itself says the physical macOS package has not been exercised.
   Keep its optional result out of fast tests and the current per-slice queue.

### Readiness refinements

1. Add a lightweight peer-refresh record only when a peer is actually selected
   at an existing composed checkpoint: immutable release/commit or PR head,
   base/master SHA, merge-base, build options, platform, sample hash/provenance,
   conversion direction/version, diagnostics, and result manifest. Do not
   poll or rebuild all peers during every local slice.
2. For chunked carriers, assert each layer independently: source declared
   length; all chunks retained in original order; reconstructed byte count and
   hash; owning entity and AcDs key join; block/INSERT reachability; and
   independent semantic geometry. Keep a sentinel after the carrier to catch
   parser over-consumption. Empty shells, equal entity counts, and successful
   process exits do not pass the carrier gate.
3. Use locally generated asymmetric analytic solids for controls (for example
   a non-cubic polyhedron with an offset, non-unit transform), but preserve the
   repo's existing no-new-external-fixture policy. A scratch DXF/SAB control
   validates carrier mechanics; it does not supply an independently authored

### Implementation-ready acceptance sequence

1. Freeze a locally generated asymmetric analytic manifest before
   serialization: entity role/handle, source units, expected bounds/topology,
   area/volume where applicable, and requested DWG/DXF version.
2. Score output at three boundaries: codec readback plus identity/owner
   closure; source-distinct ACIS parse plus kernel conversion; then external
   application open/audit. A mismatch stops only that exact route/version
   row and records the first divergent stage.
3. If rendering is an explicit consumer goal, add an optional fourth check:
   open the same hash in a pinned app/build, enable a non-wireframe style,
   reveal target layers, and record geometry visibility and renderer
   diagnostics. For large files, separately record bytes, entity/face counts,
   peak RSS, duration, and hardware; do not infer a generic memory ratio from
   a peer application.
4. Keep implementation speed: no peer checkout, native GUI, dependency,
   external fixture, or full suite during ordinary local slices. Run the
   route matrix only at the existing composed checkpoint; continue independent
   local work when an optional lane is unavailable.

## Deeper/broader cross-peer validation-protocol and DXF loss-boundary audit (2026-10-18; primary-source research only)

This pass widened the comparison from parser feature lists to the behavior of
peer validation and document-transfer paths. It looked for places where a
nominal “round trip,” successful document return, or application import can
hide normalization, repair, projection, or dropped metadata. Public
documentation and scripts define route boundaries; they do not establish a
libdxfrw defect or independent expected semantics.

| Primary source | Finding and evidence limit | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [`test-dxf.sh`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/test-dxf.sh), [project README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) | The helper builds and converts a selected DWG, filters the generated DXF, then pipes a textual diff through LibreDWG's comparator and `less`. This is a useful maintainer inspection workflow, but the script does not itself establish a machine-verifiable semantic-pass result. The README separately documents direction/version limits (including narrower DWG writing than reading), so headline coverage and a successful conversion are not entity-level completeness evidence. | Use LibreDWG only for an exact pinned conversion/read route. Keep original output, any normalized/filtered output, diagnostics, and a pre-authored identity/value manifest distinct. Do not adopt the interactive script's exit status or textual normalization as a local semantic oracle. Existing per-handle disposition and output-transaction gates remain the local acceptance path. |
| ezdxf [recovery documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/recover.html) | Recovery is a repair path for structurally flawed ASCII DXF and runs an audit; it may return a document while reporting unrecoverable decoding errors, including binary XRECORD data. The docs warn that writing the recovered document can invalidate the file or lose information; `errors='strict'` rejects undecodable data. Recovery is explicitly slower than ordinary reading. | For a valid-input peer comparison use the strict reader and preserve raw binary payload expectations. Exercise recovery only as its own malformed-ASCII diagnostic route, and report parser status, audit findings, recovered changes, and save/readback separately. A recovered document is never a positive preservation result; do not add recovery to ordinary local fast tests. |
| ezdxf [legacy `Importer` contract](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/addons/importer.html) | This compatibility add-on is deprecated in favor of `xref` and states its purpose is graphical cross-document transfer. It intentionally removes Extension Dictionaries, AppData, and XDATA; does not import OBJECTS; does not support some DIMSTYLE overrides; and requires `finalize()` to bring in dependencies such as tables and blocks. These are explicit operation limits, not evidence that ezdxf's base document reader drops the same data. | Do not use cross-document import as a same-document DXF round-trip or opaque-preservation comparator. If this legacy route is selected for a named consumer question, treat it as lossy projection and measure source-to-target identity, resources, and dropped metadata; capture finalization and output validity as separate steps. Prefer no new route unless an existing composed question requires it. |
| ACadSharp [reader guide](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/docs/articles/samples/reading.md) and [version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) | The reader API exposes notifications during `Read()`, while the matrix reports only broad per-version/direction capability. Notifications are useful diagnostics but the guide does not promise a complete per-object omission or semantic-difference ledger. | At an already planned exact-version comparator checkpoint, collect notification text alongside source/output per-handle disposition and independent expected values. Do not promote from a returned document, a clean process exit, or a matrix checkmark. Do not install/build/run ACadSharp during normal implementation slices. |

### Implementation-ready peer scoring protocol

At the existing composed peer/native checkpoints, record each route with a
single explicit outcome, not a generic “round-trip passed” label:

1. `STRICT_READ`: exact input hash, source and target format/version,
   operation, process status, parser diagnostics, and per-record disposition.
2. `RECOVERY_DIAGNOSTIC`: only for intentionally malformed ASCII DXF; retain
   pre/post hashes and audit/recovery findings, and never count this as strict
   acceptance or preservation.
3. `PROJECTION_OR_IMPORT`: selected importer/operation, finalization status,
   source-to-output identity and dependency closure, and explicit omission or
   transformation ledger.
4. `SELF_ROUNDTRIP`: same-codec read→write→read consistency only; no
   independent semantic credit.
5. `INDEPENDENT_SEMANTIC_READBACK`: distinct implementation plus an expected
   manifest authored before serialization; compare handles/types, owner and
   block/layout edges, typed values, ordered opaque tags and payload hashes,
   and analytic geometry only where that lane has a qualified kernel.

Apply this protocol by selecting the smallest route that answers the active
question; do not run the full matrix per slice. Keep generated controls in
memory or temporary scratch, do not import peer corpora, and retain the fast
owning-test → focused-selector → owning-CTest cadence. An unavailable peer
lane is recorded `NOT_RUN` and does not stop independent local implementation.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3/S3.7 ACIS diagnostic publication-slot accounting (2026-10-18; local focused slice, uncommitted)

The wireframe extractor already charged each diagnostic when it was created in
the vertex/edge/face category staging vector. `appendDiagnostics` then moved
each string into `DRW_AcisBrep::diagnostics`, retaining another vector slot
without charging it. The publication loop now charges one output item before
each destination append. This keeps the cumulative output budget aligned with
both staging and public-result slots; the string payload itself is still moved,
not copied.

A paired generated SAB control compares a valid vertex point against a missing
point. The unresolved case produces one diagnostic and must account for
exactly two more output items than the otherwise equivalent valid case: one
staging slot and one published diagnostic slot. Existing exact-budget and
one-under-budget controls use the resulting outcome counters and still verify
successful exact admission and fail-closed clearing on refusal.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3/S3.7 ACIS reference-count planner-slot accounting (2026-10-18; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The graph builder reserves `referenceCounts` with one `std::size_t` slot per
SAB record so the later node-copy pass can reserve each node's reference
vector exactly. That temporary allocation was not included in
`graphItemsAccounted`, even though the same budget already counts node slots,
copied token slots, and resolved pointer references. The builder now charges
one graph item per record before the planner-vector reserve. The outcome
comment names planner slots explicitly; this is logical item accounting, not
an allocation-byte, allocator-capacity, or resident-memory measurement.

The generated in-memory vertex SAB control independently computes the expected
count as two per-record slots (graph node plus planner), all token slots, and
all pointer-reference slots. This would fail against the previous counter,
which omitted the planner vector. Existing exact-cap and one-under controls
continue to verify admission at the measured total and fail-closed refusal one
item below it.

## Implementation progress — PAR-132/7CB AC1024 proxy-entity dispatch (2026-10-18; local focused slice, uncommitted)

The generated AC1024 frame control now drives `dwgReader::readDwgEntity` for
`ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY`, instead of testing only a hand-built public object. It
asserts application class metadata, the fixed carrier ID 498, subclass and
drawing-format metadata, entity-data bit-size presence, exact 5-bit and 3-bit
payloads, ordered typed object-ID references, absent/present common proxy
graphics, typed plus raw callbacks, and a following LINE sentinel.

The positive frame exposed two metadata omissions: DWG `PROXY` parsing did not
mark entity-data bit-size presence, and the first proxy-specific bit-long was
not mapped to the application class ID (DXF group 91). The non-byte-aligned
payload assertion also caught `copyDwgBitRange` reading a whole final octet
past the proxy data boundary, copying bits belonging to subsequent detached
streams. The parser now uses the ODA-backed 498 carrier ID, records the
application class ID and size-presence flag, and copies only the admitted tail
bits with zeroed padding. A generated malformed typed handle inside an
otherwise valid outer frame and a separately truncated physical frame both
fail before typed or raw callback publication.

## Deeper/broader peer version claims, build profiles, and downgrade semantics (2026-10-18; research only)

This pass rechecked current primary project documentation for a subtle but
high-impact false-positive path: broad version claims and successful output
files do not necessarily mean the peer converted every source feature or
validated its own output independently. The evidence sharpens admission rules
for the existing composed comparator and downstream-consumer gates; it does
not identify a new local parser defect.

| Source | Evidence and limits | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) and [command overview](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | The current README says the decoder reads all DWG versions but notes that some advanced R2010+ objects fail and are skipped; it also says R2007 writing is an exception and R2010–R2018 writing has CRC errors. The same README's build-option section says write support works only through R2004, while the `dwg2dxf` / `dxf2dwg` tool descriptions give rough 90% / 80% coverage estimates. The text therefore contains different levels of scope and should not be collapsed into one pass/fail claim. Stable package configuration also disables unstable features, whereas debug configuration can enable them. | Every optional LibreDWG run must bind release/commit, configure flags, tool, source/target version, direction, object family, diagnostics, and per-record dispositions. Report the stable and debug profiles separately. Treat the percentages as project-level estimates, not semantic coverage. Never infer that a broad reader claim validates advanced objects, or that a successful DWG→DXF operation proves writer support. |
| LibreDWG [`dwgrewrite` documentation](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | The documented command reads a DWG, writes it, then reads the output back for confirmation. That is useful internal consistency evidence, but both passes use the same implementation and profile. | Label this as peer self-reread only. It cannot satisfy independent readback, producer/native audit, or semantic parity gates. |
| ezdxf [current entity source](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dxfentity.py) | Its `DXFEntity` module documents that changing/overriding the document version is allowed but unsupported features are ignored during export; it explicitly says ezdxf does not convert between DXF versions. This source contract is more specific than an API call that merely selects a target header version. | Do not use `doc.dxfversion = ...` or an export override as a cross-version conversion oracle. An optional ezdxf target-version run is comparable only when each source record is independently inventoried and any unsupported/ignored feature is recorded as loss; prefer same-version structural checks for parser comparisons. |
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF contract](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and [DWG route](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py) | The current documentation distinguishes a built-in C++ importer from a legacy Python importer: both claim file-version reach from R12, but their entity lists differ. It says stock FreeCAD cannot read embedded ACIS solids. Its DWG path converts to DXF and then invokes the selected importer. The two exporters are also bounded (R12 legacy and R14 C++), so import claims cannot be reused for export. | Bind the exact FreeCAD release/platform, DWG converter, selected importer preference, input/output direction, entity family, and resulting object type. Score importer reach and per-entity construction, not merely “file opened.” Do not make stock-FreeCAD ACIS/B-rep support a required expectation; test its documented 2D/3DFACE subset separately from optional ACIS add-ons or kernels. |

### Implementation-readiness delta

1. Add the peer-profile fields above to the existing composed route manifest;
   do not run or install peers in the ordinary fast-slice loop.
2. For every peer output, separate `self-reread`, independent strict read,
   recovery/audit, native open, and semantic comparison. A success at one stage
   cannot stand in for another.
3. Treat target-version reassignment as a declared output profile only, never
   as proof of entity conversion. Compare input/output identities and count
   omissions, approximations, unsupported records, and warnings explicitly.
4. Keep FreeCAD importer selection and platform in the route identity. A
   2D-import success, raw SAT/SAB output, and constructed valid 3D solid remain
   separate outcomes.
5. No implementation order, routine validation frequency, CTest registration,
   dependency, persistent fixture, or support statement changes. This research
   adds no local finding or top-level subplan; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293,
   and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and cannot be promoted by these sources.

not a new support finding: multiple public implementations that appear to be
separate readers are ports or forks of the same parser family, and the one
independent DWG peer reviewed here explicitly does not label this class stable.

### PAR-133 type-528 implementation-ready gate

The dynamic-block residual is now sequenced so a future implementation slice
can begin immediately once the wire evidence exists, without speculating from
peer class names or partial output:

1. **Bind the witness.** Record the source file's hash, AC code, application
   maintenance/version, class-record identity, object type code, object handle,
   data-bit boundary, and handle-stream boundary. A fixture may be used only if
   it is already in LibreCAD/libdxfrw or LibreDWG, or was generated locally
   from scratch; otherwise keep the sample external and hash-bound.
2. **Resolve the grammar.** Read the applicable ODA chapter and all relevant
   cross-references for the `BLOCKLOOKUPACTION` base/action/table data. Use
   commit-pinned ACadSharp/acad-ts or LibreDWG source only to enumerate
   candidate fields, flags, and references. Reconcile every candidate against
   the ODA source and a versioned producer trace; unknown/reserved data stays
   bounded opaque data until resolved.
3. **Implement one version/profile at a time.** Add only fields supported by
   that witness, retain per-record warn-and-continue behavior, and keep the
   handle stream bounded. Do not hardcode an object type from third-party
   tables; capture it from the sample's class/type trace. Keep any newly added
   `DRW_Interface` callback non-pure and preserve existing 2D consumer
   compatibility.
4. **Add generated fast controls.** Build in-memory positive and malformed
   vectors for field values, ordered object references, end-bit alignment,
   truncation, and a following sentinel object. Check local writer/readback
   separately from input parsing. Do not add a new persistent fixture or run
   the full suite for this slice.
5. **Keep conversion fail-closed.** Verify the unsupported or unclosed object
   continues to be reported and prevents strict `dwg2dxf` success. A retained
   raw object, visible proxy graphics, and a same-library roundtrip are not
   semantic dynamic-block support.
6. **Check the feature graph, not just the action object.** For a semantic
   lookup-action claim, validate its associated lookup parameter, action/table
   references, input/output columns and values, unmatched/default behavior,
   and (where reverse lookup is enabled) the expected block-reference custom
   property or displayed geometry. If the consumer only supports static 2D
   geometry, record that as a projection/fallback rather than live dynamic
   behavior or full graph preservation.
7. **Promote only on independent semantics.** Require an independently
   implemented parser/producer or native application result for the same
   versioned profile and expected lookup behavior/graph references. Record
   parser lineage so ACadSharp plus acad-ts, or LibreDWG plus libredwg-web,
   cannot be counted as two independent confirmations.

No parser code, test, fixture, dependency, queue order, full-suite cadence, or

## Implementation progress — DIMENSION groups 80–84 input-side framing guard (2026-10-18; generated local fast slice, uncommitted)

### Defect and scope

The DXF group-code classifier assigns groups 80–89 the string wire kind. The
DIMENSION parser nevertheless read groups 80–84 from the reader's integer
cache into `tolZero`, `altTolDecimals`, `altZero`, `altTolZero`, and `textMove`.
Since `readRec()` had already consumed a string, those getters could reuse an
integer left by a prior record field and create false semantic values. The
fields' implemented typed source is the ACAD/DSTYLE XDATA mapping; no
source-backed direct-tag mapping for 80–84 was established.

### Implemented control

- Route direct codes 80–84 through the ordinary unknown entity-tag behavior
  after their classified string values have been consumed.
- Document each public field's canonical DSTYLE variable code alongside the
  declaration. Preserve the typed ACAD/DSTYLE parser and writer behavior.
- Add in-memory ASCII and Binary DXF controls. Each begins with valid integer
  group 71, follows with string groups 80–84, and ends with a distinctive
  group-0 sentinel. Assert strings, unchanged DSTYLE-backed fields, and
  sentinel alignment. The generated stream is not saved or committed.
- Make the adjacent generated picture-BLOCK writer probes explicitly clear
  the default DIMSTYLE name. This isolates their intended BLOCK admission and
  body-closure assertions from the independent strict DIMSTYLE gate; no
  production writer behavior is relaxed.
- Add a focused `--dimension-unassigned-direct-groups` selector; no new CTest
  registration or external fixture is required.

### Validation and remaining boundary

The strict library/test target built; the new focused selector, the DXF
code-type boundary selector, `libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures`, and the owning
`libdxfrw_wave1` CTest all passed. The initial Wave1 run exposed an unrelated
test-precondition issue: picture-BLOCK probes inherited a default `Standard`
DIMSTYLE name but emitted no DIMSTYLE record, so strict conversion correctly
stopped at that earlier gate. Explicitly clearing the style in those generated
BLOCK-only probes made the test exercise its intended subject; it did not
change production writer policy. No full suite, peer, native CAD, or external
fixture was run. `git diff --check` passed for the touched source/test/plan
files. This closes only the stale-integer interpretation bug; it does not
promise preservation or semantics for unassigned direct tags 80–84, establish
vendor behavior, or promote any support claim. The existing DSTYLE route
remains the typed semantic route.

No finding or top-level subplan was added; totals remain 133/76. J256, J260,
J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. No
dependency, committed fixture, public API change, stage/commit, or support
promotion was made. The worktree remains broadly dirty; this slice is
unstaged/uncommitted.
