   peer install, or native suite belongs in ordinary feature slices.
2. **Native FreeCAD consumer checkpoint:** use an explicit converter setting
   (not automatic fallback), pin the FreeCAD build/OS/importer/backend and
   settings, capture subprocess status and fresh intermediate DXF hash/version,
   then record the importer result and per-record/per-handle object/geometry
   disposition. Run Linux and Windows as distinct cells. A successful open or
   visible drawing alone is insufficient.
3. **3D-family separation:** ordinary 2D entities, explicit `3DFACE`, mesh and
   PFACE/POLYMESH, and `3DSOLID`/`REGION`/`BODY` ACIS carriers remain separate.
   Stock FreeCAD ACIS semantic consumption is `CONSUMER_NOT_APPLICABLE` unless
   the exact named importer/plugin demonstrably supports it. Raw carrier
   presence never implies a valid solid.
4. **Peer evidence:** at the already composed checkpoint, select at most one
   peer route for the unresolved question and pin the exact release/source,
   version, direction, operation, options, diagnostics, and fixture lineage.
   Capture skips as `NOT_RUN`; unsupported, transformed, omitted, or refused
   records may not disappear inside aggregate counts.
5. **Implementation speed and fixture policy:** keep validation to the touched
   strict target, one focused generated selector, its owning fast CTest, and a
   scoped diff check. Reserve full suites/native/peer runs for existing
   composed gates. Use repo-owned inputs or locally-from-scratch temporary
   controls only; do not commit external peer/customer drawings.

This review confirms route/evidence constraints but no new local parser or
writer defect. It adds no finding, top-level subplan, fixture, test, CTest

## Implementation progress — DICTIONARYWDFLT/default PLACEHOLDER serializers and import provenance (2026-10-18; local, uncommitted)

Added `dxfRW::writeDictionaryWithDefault` as a typed record-level serializer;
the format-specific sequence is `AcDbDictionary`, optional R2000+ group 281,
ordered 3/350 pairs, `AcDbDictionaryWithDefault`, and group 340. Own, child,
default, and owner handles are remapped. Authored keys and child targets use
the same bounded uniqueness admission as DICTIONARY. Because the official
WDFLT DXF grammar has no group 280, nonzero inherited `hardOwner` is rejected
instead of lost. Because group 281 is unavailable in R14 output, nonzero
cloning is rejected for AC1014 rather than silently discarded; values outside
Autodesk's enumerated 0–5 cloning range are rejected for all targets.

Added `dxfRW::writeAcDbPlaceholder` for the independent documented
`ACDBPLACEHOLDER` shape: code 0/5, optional persistent-reactor groups, and a
required code-330 owner. It rejects ownerless placeholders and inherited
XDATA/extension-dictionary state because the published object grammar has no
such carrier. The generated direct-edge control makes the WDFLT code-340
default identity equal the placeholder's remapped code-5 identity, and makes
the placeholder's code-330 owner equal the WDFLT's remapped code-5 identity.
See Autodesk's [WDFLT table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A6605C05-1CF4-42A4-95EC-42190B2424EE.htm)
and [PLACEHOLDER table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3BC75FF1-6139-49F4-AEBB-AE2AB4F437E4.htm).

The broader adapter trace found a separate import gap: the DXF readers pass
both records through `addRawDxfObject`, but the concrete `dx_iface` retained
only four ordinary named-resource classes, so WDFLT and PLACEHOLDER raw tags
were discarded in production imports. The existing named-resource receipt is
deliberately scoped to those four classes; expanding its raw list would make
its exact-family proof reject unrelated additions or weaken its contract.
Instead, this slice adds dedicated raw collections and a separate
`dx_dictionaryDefaultImportReceipt` with independent typed/raw ranges. Its
validator binds each DXF-origin typed WDFLT to the exact raw identity/owner and
code-340 target; validates the placeholder's published tag domain and owner;
and requires the default handle to identify one placeholder owned by that
WDFLT. The DWG-origin branch validates typed callbacks only and is policy-tested
with generated data, not promoted as a real DWG witness.

The generated in-memory source is emitted as ASCII and Binary DXF at AC1014,
AC1015, and AC1027. Literal-wire checks assert subclass order, 350 child
roles, the 340 default pointer, absence of group 280, allowed cloning values,
R14/R2000 cloning gates, placeholder owner/subclass shape, and remapped
identities; typed WDFLT parseback checks the complete payload. Production
adapter import tests assert both raw companion collections and the independent
one-generation receipt, then reject owner mismatch and duplicate placeholder
identity; a synthetic DWG-origin receipt control exercises typed-only pairing.
Hard-owner, unsupported-cloning, AC1014-cloning, and ownerless-placeholder
controls each preserve a seeded destination and succeed on same-writer retry
after correction. The next bounded output slice is now implemented: exact
`ACAD_PLOTSTYLENAME` NOD admission, source-origin raw/typed selection,
WDFLT/default-placeholder graph closure, remapping, CLASS counts, and
parent-before-child scheduling. A generated production-adapter test covers
ASCII and Binary AC1027 output and atomic refusal when the root edge is
removed. That route is intentionally narrow: unknown WDFLT entry targets and
placeholder reactors/extensions still fail closed, and no real DWG-origin
WDFLT witness or native CAD result is established. The import receipt and
generated DXF round trip do not promote a broad support claim.

No finding/subplan or ledger count changed (133/76). J256, J260, J268, J284,
J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. This slice is
still uncommitted pending safe isolation from the pre-existing broad worktree.

## Implementation progress — rooted DICTIONARYWDFLT/default PLACEHOLDER adapter route (2026-10-18; generated local fast slice, uncommitted)

The concrete exporter now inventories WDFLT and PLACEHOLDER typed/raw
carriers separately from ordinary dictionaries. It requires the one-import
dictionary-default receipt and exact source-origin route, then admits only
one WDFLT and one default PLACEHOLDER. The WDFLT must be referenced exactly
once by the `ACAD_PLOTSTYLENAME` NOD entry, with no NOD alias. The independent
code-340 pointer must resolve to a placeholder whose owner is the WDFLT.
DXF-origin inputs emit the retained raw WDFLT and placeholder once each;
DWG-origin inputs emit typed records only. Unknown or ambiguous family
records, unknown WDFLT child targets, raw placeholder reactor groups, and
typed placeholder reactors/XDATA/extension dictionaries are refused before
publication. These constraints are deliberate semantic boundaries, not
evidence that other ACAD_PLOTSTYLENAME payloads are unsupported by the file
format.

The graph traversal stages the default pointer as its own edge (it is not
required to also be a named code-350 dictionary entry), retains existing
dictionary child-edge traversal, and includes WDFLT parents in owner closure.
Output planning reserves/remaps both identities, regenerates the NOD edge,
registers exact WDFLT/PLACEHOLDER CLASS instance counts, and writes the parent
before the child. No duplicate typed/raw output occurs across the DXF/DWG
origin split.

Added a generated-from-scratch production-adapter control; no drawing fixture
was committed. ASCII and Binary AC1027 conversions are re-imported and checked
for one root edge, one WDFLT, one placeholder, remapped default identity,
matching owners, and exact CLASS counts. The test also seeds the destination
and verifies that removing the canonical root edge refuses without replacing
it, then restores the root key and retries successfully on the same adapter.

## Implementation progress — raw DXF object references to reminted table records (2026-10-18; generated local fast slice, uncommitted)

raw DXF objects translated hard-pointer codes such as MLEADERSTYLE code 342
through structural and object-handle maps, but omitted the source-table-record
map populated when STYLE/LTYPE/BLOCK_RECORD handles are reminted during
output. The raw object therefore retained the source STYLE handle while the
emitted STYLE record had a different handle. Raw translated references now
consult `sourceHandleToWrittenTableMap` before the generic minted-object map,
while preserving structural-collision remaps as the higher-priority mapping.

its BLOCK_RECORD target and code 342 at its STYLE target. Its typed-only
serializer case now states explicitly that the synthetic successful-DWG
receipt exercises the serializer only; it is not a DWG read or external
support evidence. The existing readback assertions validate that the raw

and Binary output. No fixture was added or downloaded.

   the graph preflight admits each scoped reference. Initially limit support
   to targets already present in the emitted closure; do not silently add an
   arbitrary object family or allow an unresolved soft pointer. Keep rejection
   atomic and verify same-adapter retry after fixing the graph.
4. Extend the existing generated WDFLT round trip with one in-closure reactor
   and negative controls for malformed markers, duplicate/missing owner,
   unresolved reactor, and a 330 located outside the reactor scope. Assert
   ASCII and Binary output preserve the reactor/owner distinction and remap
   each handle to exactly one emitted target. Run only the touched adapter
   target and its focused CTest selector; no full suite or native CAD run is
   needed for this slice.
5. Before broadening beyond one reactor target, reconcile the object-specific
   table with the authoritative ODA versioned layout and a repository/local
   DWG/DXF trace. Keep results generated locally; do not add externally
   obtained fixture files.

This is a refinement of the existing WDFLT/PLACEHOLDER sub-plan, not a new
ledger finding: counts remain 133 findings / 76 top-level subplans. No local
reactor behavior has yet been accepted, and the generated WDFLT controls still
test writer consistency only. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. This research does not block adjacent
local implementation work.

## Deeper/broader cross-project test architecture and route-boundary review (2026-10-18; research-only plan refinement)

This pass compared the current project-owned guidance and source for LibreDWG,
ACadSharp, ezdxf, and GDAL. The focus was not another feature-count survey;
it was identifying where a peer's test/repair/conversion pipeline can hide a
loss or accidentally collapse distinct claims. No peer repository was cloned
or built, no peer executable or native CAD/kernel was run, no drawing was
downloaded, and no code or test changed.

| Source / route | Source-backed implementation detail | Plan refinement |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [`HACKING`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/HACKING), [`libredwg-fuzz`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg-fuzz), and [`dwgrewrite`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/programs/dwgrewrite.c) | The project documents separate DWG, ASCII-DXF, Binary-DXF, JSON, and decode/encode/re-decode fuzz entry points. The fuzz setup separates instrumented and ordinary ASan builds, classifies crashes/hangs/leaks, and has explicit replay of previously collected failures. Its unknown-field workflow requires paired DWG/DXF controls with distinctive names and numeric values; uniform zero-valued fields make field attribution ambiguous. | Keep each local fast test tied to one parser/writer route and its owning behavior. For the composed security checkpoint, split fuzz targets by public input route and decode-only versus rewrite/redecode behavior, bound resources, and replay only locally relevant minimized failures. For generated mapping probes, use distinct sentinels per field and handle; preserve old-cursor/following-record checks. Do not run a broad peer fuzz corpus per implementation slice. |
| ACadSharp [version/direction matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp), [reader API](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/docs/articles/samples/reading.md), and [sample-corpus maintainer answer](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/discussions/520) | The project declares reader/writer eligibility separately by AC code, exposes per-read notifications, and says its repository samples are used by its reader tests. The feature matrix, test sample, and a `Read()` return are separate evidence: a version may have a reader but no writer, and diagnostics can report skipped/partial content. | Admit a peer case only where version, direction, record family, and operation overlap the local question. Record every notification and source-object disposition. A peer sample can be used only if already present/authorized; do not copy it into this repository. Do not infer semantic completeness from its declared matrix or test completion alone. |
| ezdxf [`DXFEntity` export contract](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dxfentity.py), [`xref` limits](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst), and [table audit implementation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/sections/table.py) | The exporter documents that overriding the target DXF version does not convert unsupported features and may ignore them. `xref` is a selective copy route and can ignore unsupported raw/proxy records. The auditor may replace duplicate table handles; its source explicitly notes this can break references while making the file readable. | Keep strict parse, version conversion, xref/copy, repair/audit, save, and independent reopen as separate result rows. If a peer repair is used diagnostically, capture before/after handles, references, repairs, deletions, and warnings; a repaired or readable output is not unchanged preservation. For ordinary parity comparisons, use strict routes and an independently authored identity/value manifest. |
| GDAL [DXF driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | The DXF reader projects records into OGR; curves may be tessellated. Binary DXF is documented from GDAL 3.12. Its AC1027+ 3D-extensible option exposes raw `ASMData` and a separate 12-number `ASMTransform`, but the driver skips these solids by default and does not make OGR solid geometry from them. | Retain GDAL only for the exact 2D projection, Binary-DXF parser, or raw-carrier question. Record version/options and compare source identity, raw payload, affine transform, projected feature, and omission status independently. Never count one OGR feature, carrier byte match, or successful import as a B-rep/AcDs semantic pass. |

### Implementation-ready route protocol

Use the following sequence when an existing plan item calls for a peer or
consumer check; it narrows execution without adding a new dependency or
changing the per-slice test cadence:

1. Name the exact operation and its version/direction intersection first:
   DWG read, DWG write, ASCII-DXF read/write, Binary-DXF read/write, conversion,
   repair, projection, or native import. Exclude peers that do not implement
   that exact route/version rather than treating a missing matrix cell as a
   failure or a pass.
2. For a local implementation slice, use a scratch-generated minimal pair
   with distinct field values, handles, owners, and a following-record
   sentinel. Keep it local and temporary unless it was already in the source
   repository; do not add downloaded peer/customer files. Check raw/typed
   value, identity, graph closure, output transaction, and readback as distinct
   assertions.
3. Capture stage outcomes separately for DWG→DXF: binary decode; typed/raw
   callback inventory; adapter graph/materialization; output preflight and
   publication; independent DXF parse; and downstream/native geometry. A
   later stage cannot retroactively certify an earlier one, and a partial
   result must retain a per-source disposition rather than only an aggregate
   entity count.
4. Use strict peer parsing for preservation comparisons. If recovery, audit,
   or repair is necessary to diagnose a malformed input, run it as a second
   route and report changed handles, references, erased objects, and repaired
   values alongside the original strict result.
5. Keep fast implementation validation as-is: touched target build, focused
   selector, owning CTest, scoped diff/receipt checks. Run peer matrices,
   fuzz campaigns, sanitizer sweeps, complete corpus checks, and native
   Linux/Windows CAD qualification only at their already scheduled composed
   gates; split those gates by route and retain resource/time bounds.

This is an evidence-protocol refinement of existing parser, writer, graph,
3D-carrier, and consumer subplans, not a new local defect or subplan. Ledger
counts remain 133 findings / 76 top-level subplans. No support claim is
promoted. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting; peer source/test architecture does not
resolve native platform qualification or independent semantic support
evidence.

### Optional Open CAD Studio route (new candidate; not a new support claim)

Open CAD Studio's [project README](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio),
[automation contract](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/docs/automation/README.md),
[tessellation route map](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/docs/tessellation.md),

describe a useful optional downstream route. Its manifest pins the codec to
`opencadcodec` revision `5d4f11a` and the separate `opencadkernel` to
`a60f18f`. The application documents DWG/DXF R14–2018 read/write targets,
per-record manifests and `dropped_on_save`, a `save_verified` operation that
reopens and compares a semantic manifest, and an ACIS-to-kernel-body
tessellation path that marks incomplete fallback meshes. It publishes desktop
builds for Linux, Windows, and Apple Silicon macOS.

This route is useful but has strict evidence ceilings:

1. It is an application/consumer route, not a second independent parser vote
   from ACadRust: the application directly depends on its `opencadcodec` fork.
   Count the parser lineage once. The separately pinned kernel is a candidate
   source-distinct geometry consumer, but its ACIS lift, topology, units,
   tolerances, and analytic results have not been independently qualified here.
2. `audit` and `save_verified` are excellent loss-auditing surfaces, but the
   app's own reopen still shares its codec. Use the audit manifest and
   `dropped_on_save` against libdxfrw-produced bytes as a downstream observation;
   do not call its self-reopen an independent writer or native-CAD pass.
3. At the existing composed consumer checkpoint only, pin the exact app tag,
   executable/package hash, codec/kernel revisions, OS, and import/export
   route. Feed scratch-generated controls with independently recorded source
   handles and analytic values; collect diagnostics, manifest, dropped/raw
   dispositions, kernel completeness, and geometric metrics separately. Keep
   files temporary and do not use a green viewport alone as topology proof.
4. Keep stock FreeCAD Linux/Windows qualification and every `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`
   J gate unchanged. Open CAD Studio is optional additional evidence and cannot
   substitute for FreeCAD, resolve an external-only J item, or promote a
   broad DWG/DXF/ACIS support claim.

## Implementation progress — Binary-DXF primitive/group-width guard (2026-10-18; generated local fast slice, uncommitted)

### Scope

This slice closes the direct low-level coverage gap identified in the existing
ACadRust Binary-DXF width report. It changes tests and test registration only;
production writer behavior is unchanged. All controls are generated in
memory; no external or committed drawing fixture was added.

### Controls

- Wrong primitive/code pairs (I32 for groups 73/74; I16 for group 90) must
  return failure, set the writer error, and emit zero bytes.
- Valid I16 groups 73/74 and I32 groups 90/93 must emit the expected wire
  widths and values.
- A following group-0 string sentinel must remain exactly aligned after the
  valid integer records.
- The selector `--dxf-binary-group-width-guard` is included in
  `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests`; CTest registration is labeled `fast;dxf;binary`.

### Validation and remaining boundary

Passed under the existing strict build configuration:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests -j4
build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --dxf-binary-group-width-guard
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dxf_binary_group_width_guard$' --output-on-failure
```

The controls prove the low-level type guard and byte alignment. They do not
prove every serializer propagates a rejected write or every production caller
uses the correct primitive; add a family-level test only when that owner is
next changed. No full suite, peer runtime, native CAD app, staging, or commit
was performed. Findings/subplans remain 133/76 and all six J items remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

## Implementation progress — PAR-39/7X Binary-DXF LWPOLYLINE group-width family guard (2026-10-18; generated local fast slice, uncommitted)

Extended the existing `--dxf-binary-group-width-guard` selector with an
end-to-end family-level control. It constructs a three-vertex LWPOLYLINE and
a following LINE in memory, exports through the public `dx_iface::fileExport`
route to a temporary Binary DXF, and scans the serialized stream using the
test-owned group-width table. The control requires exactly one LWPOLYLINE
group 90 value with a four-byte value equal to 3, group 70 with a two-byte
value equal to 1, the immediately following record name to be LINE, and EOF
to consume the complete file. Temporary output is removed by scope cleanup.

Validation passed under the configured strict build:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests -j4
build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --dxf-binary-group-width-guard
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dxf_binary_group_width_guard$' --output-on-failure
```

This verifies one concrete serializer family in addition to the sink-level
primitive guard across AC1014, AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and
AC1032 targets. It does not close the full typed numeric call-site census,
dynamic group-code audit, other serializer families, chunk/raw replay paths,
or LibreCAD-legacy classifier qualification. No production code, fixture, new CTest
registration, dependency, peer/native run, full suite, or support claim
changed. Findings/top-level subplans remain 133/76; J256, J260, J268, J284,
J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The slice is uncommitted because
the shared worktree contains extensive unrelated user/work-in-progress
changes; nothing was staged.

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 simple HATCH gradient CMC read/write (2026-10-18; generated local fast test slice)

The reader now interprets each AC1024+ gradient stop as an ODA §2.11 CMC:
reserved BS must be zero, the packed BL high byte selects C2 RGB or C3 ACI,
and the RC continuation flags must be zero on this bounded route. C2 stores
only the low 24-bit RGB in `GradientStop::rgb`; C3 stores only its low-byte ACI
in `aciColor`. Unsupported packed methods and nonzero reserved/flag bytes fail
the entity parse rather than being normalized into a different color.

The DWG encoder now uses the shared CMC writer. It accepts simple C2/C3 stops,
rejects simultaneous ACI+RGB, unknown method metadata, and names/books whose
HATCH string continuation is not yet qualified. A failed active-gradient
HATCH or MPOLYGON write marks the staged file operation failed so an adapter
cannot publish the remaining drawing with that entity silently omitted;
ordinary non-gradient skipped-entity behavior is unchanged. The DXF writer
accepts the recognized DWG-side C2/C3 metadata only when consistent with the
normalized stop fields and continues to emit groups 421/63 without guessing a
group-431 mapping.

Generated tests use no committed DWG/DXF fixture. A source-authored test-local
bit walker checks both packed writer colors (`0xC200A600` and `0xC30000FF`),
both reserved zero shorts, RC=0, the following bit sentinel, and the AC1024 TU
gradient-name cursor. A generated AC1024 DWG is then read through the real
bounded parser; typed C2/C3 values and a following LINE are checked. Invalid
method, simultaneous ACI/RGB, and named-color cases preserve a pre-existing
destination and succeed after corrected same-`dwgRW` retry. Separate ASCII and
Binary DXF writer/parser checks assert that group 63 belongs to the ACI stop
and group 421 to the RGB stop.

The AC1024 detached-string control assembles both valid and malformed vectors
from scratch. The malformed string area contains the complete `LINEAR` gradient
name followed by a length-one UCS string whose payload is truncated; parsing
must fail after the parsed gradient name, leave the source cursor at bit zero,
clear the partially populated HATCH state, and preserve a physically following
sentinel. This exercises the detached R2007+ stream bounds without adding a
committed drawing fixture or changing parser behavior.

Strict `libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip` and `libdxfrw_wave1_tests` builds pass;
`--hatch-gradient-cmc`, the Wave 1 executable, and owning CTests
`libdxfrw_wave1` and `libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip` pass. Scoped `git diff
--check` passes. No full suite, committed test fixture, new CTest registration,
external executable, native CAD application, sanitizer run, or support claim
promotion was made. This is partial PAR-134 completion: direct malformed-input
AC1018 nonzero reserved-BS/RC controls and the AC1024 detached-string bounds
control are now exercised. Named/book read mapping, other CMC methods, full
gradient semantics, and external consumer qualification remain open.
Finding/subplan totals remain 134/76;
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

lists to the actual operation and evidence each project documents: strict
parse, recovery, typed model, raw retention, cross-document import, projection,
write, independent readback, and fuzzing. The reviewed upstream pages are
mutable unless a release is called out. No peer repository was cloned or run;
no external sample was downloaded. The local source, tests, fixtures, and
support claims were not changed by this research pass.

| ezdxf [feature/version summary](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/index.rst), [entity export contract](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dxfentity.py), [XREF/import scope](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst), and [drawing limits](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/addons/drawing.rst) | The project documents ASCII/Binary DXF read/write over named DXF releases, third-party content retention, and explicitly says it does not convert between DXF versions; unsupported attributes can be ignored on export. Its XREF/import workflow has a narrower copyable/transformable entity subset and ignores ACAD_TABLE, raw-only unknown objects/entities, and several document/OBJECTS features. Its renderer has no 3D engine and does not render ACIS. These are distinct routes within one DXF implementation, not a contradiction in its core parser. | When using ezdxf, pin operation and mode. Score direct read/write separately from XREF import and rendering. Record unsupported/export-ignored fields and raw-storage presence; never treat a successful projection or imported subset as full document retention. Preserve a strict parse result separately from any recovery-mode result. |

A missing/projected geometry result must be labeled as that route's documented limit before it is considered a candidate local gap. Keep wire-level entity fields, source graph, and rendered/projected geometry as independent assertions. |

It is a useful separate C++ DXF parsing path for fields that reach callbacks, but callback success cannot observe unreported records, unknown data, or retained object-graph closure. Its age/version scope must be checked before selecting an output profile. | Keep dxflib as an optional callback-level compatibility probe only. Do not use it for full-file preservation, unknown-record retention, DWG, modern object graph, or 3D/ACIS semantics. Capture callback count and explicit unhandled records alongside field values. |
| LibreDWG [README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg), [package spec](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/libredwg.spec), [manual/testing and fuzz paths](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi), and [fuzz repository](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg-fuzz) | The README broadly says the reader covers all versions with advanced R2010+ objects sometimes skipped and describes a writer caveat around R2007; the current package spec instead describes writer capability through R2000 and CRC issues for R2010–R2018. The manual enumerates separate `dwgfuzz` input/output modes and an external fuzz-campaign repository. The maturity statements therefore differ by document/package context, while a listed fuzz target proves neither executed coverage nor semantic correctness. | Before any peer result is used, bind release/source commit, build options, exact tool and direction, and executed test/fuzz command. Treat README/package discrepancies as a freshness/provenance warning; do not quote a generic writer ceiling or fuzz-target presence as a result. Retain the existing per-version/per-class and separate reader/writer evidence gates. |

### Implementation-ready comparator and test refinement

1. For every optional peer/native observation, record one row per exact route:
   repository and immutable revision or release; build/runtime/options; input

## Implementation progress — PAR-65/7AM.1 BLOCK transparency group 440 (2026-10-18; generated local fast slice, uncommitted)

Autodesk's [common entity group-code reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3610039E-27D1-4E23-B6D3-7E60B22BB5BD.htm)
defines group 440 as the entity transparency field, and its [DXF value-type
reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3F0380A5-1C15-464D-BC66-2C5F094BCFB9.htm)
classifies codes 440–447 as 32-bit integers. The ordinary entity writer emits

writer omitted them. BLOCK now uses that same version gate and typed Int32
write.

vector shape is based on ezdxf's [source encoding
helper](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/tools/__init__.py),
while Autodesk's [AcCmTransparency API](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2019/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OREF-__MEMBERTYPE_Methods_AcCmTransparency.html)
documents alpha values as 0 transparent through 255 opaque. The raw ASCII and

## Deeper/broader OpenCADStudio self-check versus external CAD audit harness review (2026-10-18; research only)

This pass examined the current OpenCADStudio automation contract and its
published acceptance scripts, then reconciled their assertions with the
existing codec-lineage, native-consumer, and 3D evidence gates. The project
publishes two materially different checks: `save_verified` reopens output in
the same app/codec stack and compares a semantic entity manifest, while a
separate Windows-only script is documented to open DWG 2000/2013/2018 in a
reference CAD command-line console and run `AUDIT` without repairs. Neither
route was run in this review; the reference script body and the exact v2026.42
tagged automation files were not independently retrieved, so this is a
current-main documentation/source claim, not a pinned execution result.

| Source / route | Evidence established—and limit | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCADStudio [`mcp_acceptance.py`](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/docs/automation/mcp_acceptance.py) and [automation README](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/docs/automation/README.md) | The checked-in current-main harness authors a closed PLINE, two CIRCLEs, a LINE and TEXT in a new drawing. It requests DWG 2000, 2013 and 2018 plus DXF 2000, calls the app's `audit` and `save_verified`, checks the verified flag/output file, and records a viewport PNG/report. The test does not declare an independent expected per-handle geometry manifest in the script; the save verifier uses the same app codec. | Admit as a bounded optional 2D application control only after pinning app commit, binary hash, platform, codec/kernel dependencies, exact generated output hash/version, and all warnings/losses. To compare libdxfrw, open the exact libdxfrw-produced bytes in the peer app; do not count files emitted by the peer's own writer as an independent writer comparison. Use locally authored per-handle expectations for geometry and metadata. Do not infer block/XREF/object-graph, explicit 3D mesh, ACIS/AcDs, or B-rep coverage from this four-type 2D control. |
| OpenCADStudio [automation API contract](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/docs/automation/API-SPEC.md) | `save_verified` is specified to write the selected target version, reopen it, check actual version, compare semantic entity manifests, audit raw DXF handle references and return a SHA-256. Those are valuable self-consistency/loss-detection checks, but both serialization and readback are the app's own codec lineage; the manifest is not independent expected truth. | Classify results as `SAME_CODEC_VERIFIED_SAVE`. They can expose internal regressions and provide a hash-bound artifact for a later route, but cannot alone count as an independent read, semantic oracle, or native application acceptance. Preserve source/output identity and disposition data separately. |
| OpenCADStudio [automation README's `reference_acceptance.ps1` route](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/docs/automation/README.md) | The current documentation says the script consumes the three app-generated DWGs, launches a reference CAD command-line console in isolated profiles, opens read-only, runs `AUDIT` without repairs, and saves one log per target version; it is explicitly Windows-only. The README is the evidence available here—the script was not retrieved or executed. A clean native AUDIT would be structural/file-integrity evidence for that exact application/version, not a per-object semantic or solid-geometry comparison. | At the existing composed native checkpoint only, first inspect/pin the script and console binary, then run it against scratch-only libdxfrw outputs (not just the peer's outputs). Preserve exact command/profile, input SHA-256 and DWG signature, stdout/stderr/logs, timeout/forced termination, error/fix/deletion counts, and final process status. A missing console, missing script, unreported skip, or forced termination before an audit result is `NOT_RUN`, not a pass. Do not add this Windows-only route to every local slice or substitute it for the required FreeCAD Linux/Windows routes. |
| Current FreeCAD [DXF importer scope](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and [DWG workflow](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md) | FreeCAD documents DWG as external converter → DXF → selected importer, with distinct C++ and optional legacy Python DXF routes; its DXF documentation says embedded ACIS/SAT solids cannot currently be read. This route therefore cannot turn an OCS audit or converter exit into ACIS/AcDs semantic acceptance. | Keep the existing required FreeCAD acceptance cells bound to platform, exact converter/intermediate DXF, chosen importer/backend and entity disposition. The OpenCADStudio route is additive only; it cannot satisfy the FreeCAD gate, resolve J256/J260/J268/J284/J293/J295, or promote a 3D/ACIS support claim. |

### Implementation-ready optional comparator sequence

1. Keep per-slice work local and fast: the touched strict build target, the
   smallest generated selector, and its owning CTest. Do not launch peer apps
   or native CAD for each BLOCK/entity/writer slice.
2. At the scheduled composed writer checkpoint, generate the input from
   scratch or existing repository fixtures, write it with libdxfrw, and freeze
   the source expectations before comparison. Record input/output hashes,
   actual file signature/version, entity handles/types, ownership/block
   membership, supported property values, and explicit omissions/refusals.
3. If OpenCADStudio is already available, pin its exact source/artifact and
   open the libdxfrw artifact. Record its `audit`/load diagnostics and
   unsupported/dropped dispositions. Treat `save_verified` only as a separate
   same-codec stability result; do not rewrite the input before preserving the
   original hash and parser observations.
4. If a reference CAD console is already available on Windows, run the
   reviewed external `AUDIT` lane at the composed milestone. A clean AUDIT
   does not replace entity-by-entity expected geometry, owner/reference
   closure, or a separate native FreeCAD run on Linux and Windows.
5. For 3D cases, extend the generated manifest and score each stage
   independently: entity shell/flags → AcDs section/index/key → entity-owner
   association → exact SAB bytes/disposition → parser losses and topology →
   independently authored analytic measures → named native consumer result.
   A viewport PNG, tessellation, entity count, non-empty payload, or successful
   self-reopen is never the semantic-solid pass condition.

## Implementation progress — PAR-65/7AM.2 ENDBLK source owner identity validation (2026-10-18; local fast follow-up, uncommitted)

The footer owner is now checked against the actual output owner at the emission
boundary. For versions that encode group 330, a retained source owner must
resolve through the source-to-output handle map to the BLOCK_RECORD that owns
the containing BLOCK; a nonmatching explicit owner aborts the output
transaction. Missing owner metadata remains allowed for caller-authored
carriers that have no source identity, and versions before AC1015 do not emit
the owner group. This prevents the current writer's canonical owner emission
from silently masking a wrong or unresolved retained source owner.

fixed-space footer owners after semantic re-import. It also mutates an XREF
footer to point at the model-space BLOCK_RECORD, verifies export failure leaves
the destination sentinel intact, then proceeds through the existing duplicate
self-identity rejection and repaired same-adapter retry. The source fixture is
modified only in memory; no new DWG/DXF fixture was added.

inside a closed XRECORD. The specialized BLOCK writer now emits the shared

group-320 values remain opaque XRECORD payload, not graph edges.

typed references, and opaque group-320 values are checked. An unresolved BLOCK
extension root must fail without replacing a sentinel destination, after

## Implementation progress — PAR-20/7G.3 DWG LAYOUT viewport-list reverse membership (2026-10-18; generated local fast slice, uncommitted)

The prior preflight proved every handle declared by a DWG LAYOUT resolved to
a retained viewport, but did not prove the reverse direction: a retained
paper-space VIEWPORT could belong to that same LAYOUT and still be omitted
from its list. A generated two-layout control reproduced that acceptance in
both ASCII and Binary DXF when the Sheet A list retained `0x700` but omitted
same-layout viewport `0x705`; this was the regression case before the fix.

The adapter now builds a sorted viewport-handle-to-LAYOUT ownership index,
rejects duplicate declarations, requires every emitted paper-space viewport
to appear under its resolved reciprocal LAYOUT, and compares each LAYOUT's
declared list size with the emitted owned viewport set. This remains a
membership check only: DXF groups 68/69 continue to derive from the
independent established output-order projection, not DWG list order. The
generated test asserts rejection leaves an existing destination sentinel
unchanged; its valid ASCII/Binary graphs still project and read back.
An additional control temporarily removes every retained paper-space
VIEWPORT while keeping non-empty LAYOUT lists; the composed export still
rejects atomically because `validateLayoutGraph` resolves list targets before
the projection preflight's no-viewport fast return. This confirms that edge
case is already covered by the earlier graph gate and required no extra
production change.

Validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests -j4                    PASS
build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --dwg-viewport-projection                    PASS
build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --layout-graph-read-contract                 PASS
build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --block-record-xdata-roundtrip               PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures$' --output-on-failure      PASS (1/1)
git diff --check -- dwg2dxf/dx_iface.cpp tests/dxf_fixture_tests.cpp             PASS
```

This CTest result is the current-checkout result; it supersedes the earlier
receipt's recorded XDATA-retry failure, whose cause was not attributed to
this LAYOUT change. No full suite, native CAD application, external peer,
newly registered fixture, copied external drawing, or support promotion was
performed. The generated order-reversal control establishes that the current
composed serializer projection is independent of DWG list ordinal; it gives
no basis to synthesize groups 68/69 from that ordinal. Native/editor
reconstruction of the DWG-only list remains for the existing composed
consumer checkpoint. Continue with the next locally ready PAR-20/7G.3 item
without waiting on that external result. Findings/subplans remain 134/76. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293,
and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The shared worktree is

## Cross-format paper-space viewport representation crosswalk (2026-10-18; primary-source research)

The DWG-side field is a counted sequence of viewport handles, but the DXF
`LAYOUT` schema does not expose a corresponding count/list field. Autodesk's
complete [LAYOUT group-code table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-433D25BF-655D-4697-834E-C666EDFD956D.htm)
identifies code 330 as the associated paper-space BLOCK_RECORD, code 331 as
the last viewport active when that layout was current, and codes 333/345/346
as separate shade-plot/UCS references. For graphical records, Autodesk lists
common code 330 as the owner BLOCK_RECORD and code 410 as the layout tab
name ([common entity codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3610039E-27D1-4E23-B6D3-7E60B22BB5BD.htm)).
The `VIEWPORT` schema separately assigns code 68 to active/off-screen/off
state and positive stacking order, and code 69 to viewport identity
([VIEWPORT group codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-2602B0FB-02E4-4B9A-B03C-B1D904753D34.htm)).
The independent ezdxf implementation likewise exposes all `VIEWPORT` entities
in a paperspace layout and a separate `main_viewport()` accessor
([layout API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/layouts/layouts.html));
this corroborates the entity-space model but is not normative format evidence.

The target class for the DWG-side repeated handles received a separate
cross-check. ODA §20.4.84 calls each repeated reference a “Viewport handle”
without naming the class in that table. Autodesk's
[`AcDbLayout::getViewportArray()` API](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/OARXMAC-RefGuide/files/OREFMAC-AcDbLayout__getViewportArray.html)
specifies IDs of `AcDbViewport` entities in that layout's paperspace. A
static LibreDWG [`dwggrep.c` matcher](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/programs/dwggrep.c)
labels `LAYOUT.viewports[i]` as `VPORT`, but a read-only LibreDWG 0.14 JSON
run over all 10 already-admitted `tests/samples/AC1024/*.dwg` files resolves
all listed handles in the 8 populated files to `VIEWPORT` entities; 2 files
have empty lists. In `title_block-iso.dwg`, list handle `0x52` resolves to a
`VIEWPORT` entity (and is also the `active_viewport` target), while a separate
`VPORT` table record has handle `0x7f`. This static/runtime peer discrepancy
does not outweigh ODA or Autodesk API evidence and does not justify changing
the local typed target gate. It does bound the observation to AC1024 and this
corpus; other version/profile semantics still need their own traced target.

### Implementation-ready consequence

1. Keep the new DWG count/list validator as an input-graph closure gate. DXF
   output represents membership through the complete paper-space entity set,
   each entity's mapped BLOCK_RECORD owner/space/layout identity, and the
   LAYOUT's separately typed code-331 last-active reference; do not invent a
   DXF count/list field or serialize the DWG handle array as unrelated raw
   tags.
2. Do not infer that the DWG sequence order maps to DXF group 68 stacking
   order or group 69 identity. The local projection's deterministic output
   traversal remains an adapter policy; source-list-order equivalence and
   native editor behavior remain unqualified until matched producer/consumer
   evidence exists. A native qualification vector must compare source list
   order, emitted VIEWPORT 68/69 values, layout ownership, and reopened active
   viewport separately.
3. The generated fast lane now covers both directions of closure: missing
   listed targets (including when no viewport entity remains), and retained
   same-layout entities omitted from the list. Keep ASCII/Binary round-trip
   and atomic-destination checks in the existing fixture executable. Do not
   add downloaded drawings or per-slice full-suite, peer-binary, or native
   runs; defer those to the named composed consumer checkpoint.
4. This crosswalk adds no confirmed defect, finding, subplan, fixture,
   dependency, or support claim. Findings/subplans stay 134/76; J256, J260,
   J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.
   The LibreDWG run used only the repository's existing sample files and
   added no persistent fixture or routine peer dependency.

## Implementation progress — PAR-20/7G.3 LAYOUT viewport-list order independence (2026-10-18; generated local fast slice, uncommitted)

The existing generated two-layout DWG-origin projection covered exact
viewport-list membership and output group 68/69 values, but did not directly
assert that reordering the DWG list leaves that DXF projection unchanged. The
control now reverses both Sheet A and Sheet B handle sequences in memory,
exports and re-imports the ASCII and Binary outputs, and compares each
generated viewport identity (unique center-X marker) together with its
paper-space owner name and `(vpstatus, vpID)` pair. This binds the comparison
to viewport and layout identities while allowing output handles to be
reminted. Source lists are restored before subsequent controls run.

This result supports a bounded output rule: preserve the complete viewport
membership through the existing layout/owner closure, keep `LAYOUT` 331's
last-active viewport separate, and do not derive DXF groups 68/69 from DWG
list position. It does not establish how AutoCAD or another native editor
reconstructs a DWG-only viewport list from DXF; that remains an existing
composed-consumer question, not a blocker for local implementation.

Validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests -j4                    PASS
build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --dwg-viewport-projection                    PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures$' --output-on-failure      PASS (1/1)
git diff --check -- tests/dxf_fixture_tests.cpp DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md PASS
```

The strict target, selector, and owning CTest were rerun on 2026-10-19 after
the comparison was strengthened to include layout-owner identity. No new
fixture file or CTest registration was added; test output is generated under
a temporary directory and removed by the test. No full suite, external peer,
native CAD application, or support promotion was performed. Findings /
top-level subplans remain 134/76. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The worktree is broadly dirty;
nothing was staged or committed.

Next local action: proceed through the existing dependency-ready PAR-20/7G.3
queue; keep native/editor semantics at the composed checkpoint and do not
wait on external qualification to continue local items.

Preserve input/output versions and unsupported/unknown counts, and compare emitted fields against an independently authored manifest. Do not equate a clean audit or successful write with feature-preserving conversion. |

FreeCAD's converter selector can try LibreDWG, ODA, then QCAD in Automatic mode; `DWGConversion=1` selects the LibreDWG-converter branch only, whose executable is resolved from the configured path or PATH. The non-GUI C++ DXF importer had a stale-Python-exception bug; PR #20328 merged as `0986dad` on 2025-03-31, added a regression, and fixed the non-GUI layer/view handling. This is upstream code evidence, not proof that a particular packaged FreeCAD build contains the fix or that every headless importer path succeeds. | Add a faster optional FreeCAD object-level checkpoint using a pinned `FreeCADCmd` build that contains the fix, the C++ importer, and an explicitly configured local `dwg2dxf`. Set `DWGConversion=1` and the exact converter path; avoid Automatic fallback. Capture converter argv/exit/diagnostics and hash the intermediate DXF rather than trusting FreeCAD's success message. If the selected packaged build cannot execute the exact headless route, mark that cell `NOT_RUN` and use the existing GUI route; do not block code slices waiting on it. |
| [FreeCAD headless guidance](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Headless_FreeCAD.md), [Draft DXF guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md), and [LibreCAD_3 DWG policy](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/blob/master/docs/dwg-support.md) | Headless FreeCAD exposes an App document but has no GUI document/view providers. FreeCAD's documented C++ and optional legacy DXF importers have different entity coverage; stock DXF import does not consume embedded ACIS/SAT solids. LibreCAD_3 deliberately keeps DWG import opt-in/read-only until separate write claims and external acceptance are promoted; it consumes libdxfrw and is not an independent codec lineage. | Scope the fast FreeCAD pass to its document/object and geometry data, not view-provider/render assertions. Keep one GUI smoke per required native platform at the composed gate if the user-facing `Open` path is claimed. Record `3DSOLID`/`REGION`/ACIS as unsupported by the stock importer rather than treating their absence as converter loss. Keep LibreCAD_3 compatibility as a downstream consumer check, not writer evidence or another parser vote. |

### Implementation-ready FreeCAD sub-plan

1. **Pin and preflight once per platform.** Record OS/architecture, exact FreeCAD build/commit, whether it includes FreeCAD commit `0986dad` or a verified equivalent, importer backend, and the effective converter-selection preference. The headless path is eligible only after a minimal locally authored DXF smoke proves that the packaged C++ importer creates the expected App document without a pending Python exception.
2. **Force the path under test.** Put the built libdxfrw `dwg2dxf` at a test-local absolute path and configure FreeCAD's `TeighaFileConverter` path to it with `DWGConversion=1`. This bypasses Automatic mode's LibreDWG→ODA→QCAD fallback chain. Verify the resolved executable before opening the file. Capture subprocess arguments, exit status, stdout/stderr, and produced-file existence; the FreeCAD wrapper treats output-file existence as conversion success and does not use the child exit code as the sole result.
3. **Reuse the existing generated/local control.** Use one locally generated DWG profile already covered by the plan, with distinctive 2D geometry, two layers, and explicit expected units/coordinates. Do not add downloaded DWGs or a new permanent fixture. Preserve the converter's intermediate DXF in the temporary acceptance packet and check its `$ACADVER`, hash, exact entity/handle/owner/value disposition, and any refused/opaque records before FreeCAD import.
4. **Assert consumer output independently.** In `FreeCADCmd`, inspect the App document's object `TypeId`, layer/group assignment, placement, curve/vertex data, and measured bounds/lengths against a manifest written before conversion. Keep converter success, DXF structure, FreeCAD object creation, and geometry measurements as separate columns. The headless test cannot claim GUI/view-provider behavior.
5. **Batch native acceptance.** Run this profile once on Linux and once on Windows at the existing composed checkpoint, after related reader/writer slices are ready. Keep a single user-facing GUI `Open` smoke per platform only if claiming that path; use the explicitly pinned converter/backend and capture fallbacks. Continue fast generated selectors for per-slice work and do not run the full suite or install optional peers for each slice.

This refines the existing consumer gate rather than adding a new parser finding or changing implementation order. It adds no fixture, peer dependency, mandatory per-slice test, or support promotion. The top-level finding/subplan counts remain 134/76. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; this research does not satisfy their platform or independent semantic evidence requirements.

## Deeper/broader route-capability reconciliation across DWG readers, DXF projections, and geometry consumers (2026-10-19; primary-source research)

This pass compared the implementation boundaries—not headline “format
support”—of the current open-source DWG readers, DXF parsers, GIS projections,
and geometry consumers. It reviewed project-owned manuals, API documentation,
known-issue inventories, and a public security report. No peer was cloned,
built, or run; no peer/customer drawing or attachment was downloaded or copied.

| Route | Primary-source evidence | Plan consequence and evidence ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| [LibreDWG manual](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi), [class table](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/objects.in), and [0.14.1 NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | The manual's broad DWG coverage statement coexists with version/type-specific unhandled classes and explicit missing test coverage; it says unknown classes/types may remain binary blobs without DXF codes. It also documents a distinct GeoJSON projection that omits 3D entities and selected curve/entity families, and the current release notes retain version- and direction-specific writer caveats. | Keep DWG decoding, object-graph retention, DXF serialization, and alternate projections as separate stages. A reader's retained opaque blob does not imply a DXF record was emitted. At any selected differential record decoded, skipped, unsupported, opaque, and emitted counts per source identity, plus version/direction and build options; do not use a project-level coverage percentage or GeoJSON result as DWG/DXF semantic qualification. |
| [GDAL DXF driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) and [known issues](https://github.com/OSGeo/gdal/blob/master/ogr/ogrsf_frmts/dxf/KNOWN_ISSUES.md) | GDAL exposes an OGR feature projection, not an entity-preserving CAD document: spline/curve geometry is tessellated, HATCH fill styling is omitted, MLINE element styling and caps are omitted, and INSERT can be exploded or inlined. `INCLUDE_RAW_CODE_VALUES` exposes unhandled group codes and handles/paperspace fields can help locate some losses. AC1027+ 3D-extensible mode exposes opaque ASM bytes plus a 12-value transform, but the driver explicitly cannot build OGR geometry from them. Its writer emits AutoCAD 2004 DXF; the known-issues list separately names unsupported entities and 3D/OCS gaps. | Retain GDAL as an optional, exact-route projection check only. If selected for a concrete 2D DXF question, open the produced DXF directly, pin GDAL version/options, enable raw code values, and compare pre-authored expected records separately from projected geometry. Treat tessellation, block expansion, and omitted fields as declared transformations, not parser loss. For ASM, compare only payload/hash and transform at the carrier stage; do not call it solid interpretation. Do not use its writer for versioned or full-fidelity output acceptance. |
| [BRL-CAD DXF conversion documentation](https://brl-cad.github.io/docs/tutorials/converting/chapter4.html), [current issue #228](https://github.com/BRL-CAD/brlcad/issues/228), and [open-source source tree](https://github.com/BRL-CAD/brlcad) | `dxf-g` converts polygon/mesh input to BOT primitives, maps each DXF layer to a BRL-CAD region, maps lines/circles/arcs to NMG objects and points to spheres, and assumes millimeters if units are absent. It is therefore a useful geometry-consumer route but deliberately aggregates and transforms the DXF model rather than preserving entity identity. The open issue reports an out-of-bounds read from malformed POLYLINE face indices in the normal importer path; this remains peer-specific reported evidence, not a libdxfrw defect or a local test oracle. | Admit `dxf-g` only as a conditional geometric projection for valid, scratch-generated DXF profiles that it documents. Before comparison, pin source/build, units/scale/tolerance and the layer-to-region aggregation; compare geometry against an independently authored manifest, not per-entity counts or metadata. Do not feed malformed face-index controls or external untrusted files to this optional route while the report is unresolved. Keep local malformed-input tests generated in-process and under local ownership. |
| [ezdxf entity model](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/tree/master/docs/source/dxfentities), [XREF limitations](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst), and [export contract](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dxfentity.py) | ezdxf provides typed DXF entity data, including 3DSOLID/REGION carrier classes and detailed HATCH paths/gradients, but explicitly does not convert unsupported features when changing DXF versions. Its XREF importer supports a documented subset and ignores unsupported records; associative HATCH relationships are not managed by the entity API. | Use ezdxf only for the typed DXF fields it exposes at the exact input/output version. A successful parse, audit, write, or same-library reread does not establish unknown-record retention, associative graph closure, version conversion, or ACIS/B-rep interpretation. Keep source identity, references, and opaque data under libdxfrw's own preservation ledger. |
| [gdsestimating/dxf-parser](https://github.com/gdsestimating/dxf-parser) [README](https://github.com/gdsestimating/dxf-parser/blob/master/README.md) and [LibreDWG JSON/GeoJSON tools](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | The JS parser documents a typed object projection for common DXF entities and does not claim all entity/object families; 3DSOLID is outside its documented typed set. LibreDWG's JSON/GeoJSON tools are different projections from its DWG reader and have their own omissions. | These are optional syntax/field observations only for documented subsets. Unexposed content is `NOT_OBSERVED`, never presumed absent or successfully preserved. Do not count multiple wrappers/projections of one parser lineage as independent implementations. |
| Cross-route conclusion | The surveyed implementations cover separate portions of the evidence ladder: DWG structure, typed DXF values, GIS geometry projection, opaque ACIS/ASM transport, and geometry-kernel interpretation. None of the reviewed routes independently proves the complete chain `DWG object/entity → AcDs owner/key → exact modeler payload → complete solid topology → native Linux/Windows consumer`. | The plan's separated carrier, semantic, writer, and platform gates remain necessary. No new local defect is demonstrated; research changes comparator admission and interpretation only. In particular, GDAL raw ASM and ezdxf carrier classes cannot satisfy the independent ACIS/AcDs semantic gate, and BRL-CAD's mesh conversion cannot satisfy native CAD acceptance. |

### Fast, implementation-ready use of this research

1. For every optional peer result, bind one route fingerprint before execution:
   project and immutable revision/artifact; lineage; input format/version;
   read/write/convert operation; exact entity/object families; enabled
   options; transformations and unsupported/opaque policy; and the independent
   expected-value source. If any field is unknown, record `NOT_ADMITTED` or
   `NOT_RUN` rather than a pass.
2. Prefer a single direct-DXF GDAL projection only when a named local DXF
   semantic question remains after generated fast tests. Record both OGR
   geometry and raw-code observations; retain tessellation, inlining,
   precision, units, and omitted-feature accounting. Do not run it per slice.
3. Use `dxf-g` only if a valid generated geometry profile needs a downstream
   3D-model projection. Compare aggregated layer-region geometry with analytic
   expectations and explicit units/tolerance. Never use it for malformed
   POLYLINE security vectors, and do not make optional availability a blocker.
4. Do not add peer packages, fixtures, permanent CTests, or full-suite runs.
   Existing local generated/in-memory tests remain the fast implementation
   loop; selected external readers and consumers remain at their existing
   composed checkpoints. Continue the dependency-ready local queue when an
   optional route is unavailable.
5. No finding or top-level subplan is added because no local mismatch was
   reproduced. Findings/subplans remain 134/76; J256, J260, J268, J284,

## Deeper/broader open-source comparison: round-trip evidence, identity normalization, and route readiness (2026-10-19; primary-source review)

This pass looked beyond feature badges and test counts at what selected peer
round-trip tests actually compare, which identity/provenance fields they
normalize away, and what their published DWG coverage numbers mean. The goal
is to make the existing composed comparator smaller and more decisive. Sources
were read-only; no peer was installed, built, or run, and no peer/customer
drawing or attachment was downloaded or copied.

| Route/evidence | What the primary source establishes | Plan consequence and evidence ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| [ACadRust round-trip comparator](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/blob/main/tests/roundtrip.rs#L3221-L3295) | Its general entity comparator clones both sides and normalizes before equality. The helper clears common handles, owner handles, reactors, extension-dictionary handles, internal entity mode, and raw-record provenance; its entity-specific normalization also clears nested handles/references and sorts or canonicalizes selected values. This is an intentional semantic-field comparison, not a whole graph-identity check. | At an optional cross-peer comparison, collect source-handle → output-handle mapping and owner/reference membership before invoking normalized field equality. Score those as separate columns. Do not call a peer's normalized document equality a preservation pass, and do not add a new local graph test where the existing identity/owner closure controls already cover the edge. |
| [ACadRust ACIS/DWG tests](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/blob/main/tests/roundtrip.rs#L3798-L3855) | The suite contains a marker-bearing fake SAB helper and a separate generated planar-body path, and the basic DWG round-trip helper invokes ACadRust's own writer followed by its own reader. The generated planar body and same-codec check can exercise internal serialization/parsing and selected body construction; the fake marker case exercises only a synthetic carrier profile. | Keep four results distinct: synthetic carrier/framing, same-codec internal round-trip, separately implemented parser/kernel with an independently authored geometric expectation, and native application acceptance. None of these peer tests alone proves AutoCAD/FreeCAD acceptance or the full DWG entity→AcDs owner/key→SAB→B-rep chain. This refines the existing S8/composed gate only. |
| [DWG-RS coverage and verification contract](https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/dwg-rs) | Its current README distinguishes a more mature container/object walk from alpha/partial entity decoding, provides per-version decoded/skipped/errored counts on a small local corpus, and explicitly says DWG writing lacks automated external CAD acceptance. The aggregate percentages therefore depend on this corpus, selected versions, and decoded-record denominator. | If used as a read-side observation, record the immutable commit, exact input hash/version, total enumerated objects, decoded/skipped/errored counts by type and handle, and reader stage reached. Never compare aggregate percentages across different corpora or treat a clean container walk as typed entity success. Keep its alpha writer out of the acceptance denominator. |
| [IxMilia.Dxf compatibility notes](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf) and [IxMilia `dxf-rs` integration tests](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf-rs/blob/main/src/misc_tests/integration.rs) | The C# library publicly lists DXF entity/version exclusions and warns that AutoCAD may reject some emitted types, including modeler carriers. The Rust project says its converter/AutoCAD interop tests are conditional on Windows and installed tools; absent tools can leave those branches unexecuted. | Use either only for an exact overlapping DXF syntax/writer question. Capture test-level `PASS`, `FAIL`, `SKIP`, or `NOT_RUN`, identify the producer of each intermediate file, and pin the peer and any ODA/AutoCAD executable separately. A successful test process with a skipped external-tool branch is not native acceptance. |
| Cross-route conclusion | These projects expose distinct evidence layers—container parsing, typed-field comparison, graph identity, carrier framing, independent geometry, and native acceptance. Their own test source shows that round-trip equality can deliberately omit identity while their high-level summaries remain broader than that test proves. | Retain the current plan's operation/version/lineage matrix and evidence grades. The only refinement is to require identity/owner/reference closure to be captured before normalized semantic-field comparison in the existing composed peer protocol; no new defect or top-level implementation subplan follows. |

### Fast, implementation-ready comparator protocol

1. Use one locally authored/generated input for a selected composed checkpoint;
   never import a peer/customer file as a repository fixture. Before writing,
   produce an expected manifest with source identity, owner/block path, record
   family, expected version transformation, and fields that are in scope.
2. Inspect the local emitted wire/record inventory first. Then map each source
   identity to peer-visible identity and compare owner/reference closure. Only
   after that compare the explicitly selected typed fields, with normalization
   rules listed rather than hidden in equality helpers.
3. Record parsed, retained-opaque, intentionally transformed, skipped with a
   diagnostic, errored, and not-run counts separately by source identity and
   record type. A normalized field match cannot cancel a missing identity or
   an unexplained skipped/opaque record.
4. At most one pinned peer route is run for one named question at the existing
   composed checkpoint. Record immutable source/artifact, version, direction,
   options, runtime/toolchain, OS, intermediate producers, and explicit
   conditional-test outcomes. Do not put peers, native apps, or full suites in
   the per-slice fast loop.
5. Keep independently authored analytic geometry and native application audit
   as later evidence stages. Same-library geometry builders, same-codec
   round-trip, fake SAB markers, projected meshes, and drawing renders cannot
   promote B-rep or complete-document support.

This review found no new local defect and adds no finding, top-level subplan,
test, fixture, dependency, peer/native execution, full-suite run, or support
promotion. The existing local identity/graph and transactional output owners

## Deeper/broader BODY/AcDs source reconciliation and modern BODY boundary (2026-10-19)

This pass resolved the exact evidence ceiling around modern `BODY` ACDSDATA
without treating broad peer type predicates as a format contract. It reviewed
the official ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1, Autodesk's BODY DXF
reference, current LibreDWG AcDs source, and ACadRust's current entity contract
and round-trip test. No peer was built or run; no remote drawing or fixture was
downloaded.

| Route/evidence | Primary-source observation | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| [ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1, §§20.4.41 and 24.2.2.3](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) | §20.4.41 groups REGION, 3DSOLID, and BODY as ACIS entities with a shared, partly-understood modeler record. The AcDs section is introduced as storing ACIS data for regions/solids; its §24.2.2.3 data-record rule explicitly says that for each REGION or 3DSOLID a record is made with its SAB stream. It does not specify BODY's modern AcDs record/key/owner association. | This is a specification coverage gap, not proof that no producer ever stores BODY data in AcDs. Do not extrapolate the REGION/3DSOLID join to BODY, and do not change the qualified modeler-class predicate from this absence alone. Keep modern BODY `NOT_QUALIFIED / PROFILE_DISCOVERY_PENDING` until a normative clarification or traceable real producer profile binds entity handle, schema/index, key, and SAB record. |
| [Autodesk BODY DXF definition](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-7FB91514-56FF-4487-850E-CF1047999E77.htm) | The documented BODY grammar is the `AcDbModelerGeometry` subclass, modeler-format version, proprietary group-1 text, and optional group-3 continuation. This is the legacy inline DXF carrier; it does not define the modern AcDs join. | Preserve and test legacy BODY SAT group-1/3 behavior independently. Do not reinterpret inline text chunks as an AcDs record or silently change the entity family to REGION/3DSOLID. |
| LibreDWG [`common_entity_data.spec`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/common_entity_data.spec), [`dwg.c`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dwg.c), and [`acds.spec`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/acds.spec) | The current DWG reader sets up its AcDs SAB association queue for entities with `has_ds_data` whose `dwg_obj_is_3dsolid()` predicate includes 3DSOLID, REGION, BODY, and several surface classes. `acds.spec` then scans the data-store byte stream for SAB markers and associates spans through the queued handles. This is useful evidence that a peer implements a broad shared AcDbModelerGeometry route; it is not an independent producer trace or proof that BODY's schema/semantic interpretation is correct. | Record this as `PEER_IMPLEMENTATION_ROUTE`, not a normative rule or parity pass. A future comparator must distinguish route admission, exact owner/key/payload association, and independently checked BODY geometry. Do not count a generic handle predicate or marker scan as BODY semantic support. |
| ACadRust [EntityCommon docs](https://docs.rs/acadrust/latest/acadrust/entities/struct.EntityCommon.html) and [round-trip tests](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/blob/main/tests/roundtrip.rs#L3798-L3928) | The current docs/comment state that R2013+ 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY geometry is carried by AcDs. This pass rechecked the exact DWG DataStorage specification text against the

cross-referenced the current LibreDWG 0.14.1 security notes, and screened
ezdxf's published DXF preservation/ACIS boundaries. No peer was cloned,

| Official [ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1, §24.2.1 and §24.2.2.3](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) | The segment header's object-data alignment offset is expressed in 16-byte units from the segment start. The data-record grammar places a data-start marker after the record headers, defines each record start from that marker plus its local offset, and gives a maximum-size calculation for the last record. | Keep ODA as the governing contract. The exact coordinate interpretation of the last-record expression is disputed in the ACadSharp review discussion below; do not replace the documented formula on a peer comment alone. For any future parser edit, write down the absolute segment/header/data-marker/record-start coordinates explicitly and prove each subtraction is nonnegative before reading. |
| ACadSharp merged [Prototype1b reader PR #1154](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1154), its [issue #1152 discussion](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1152), and closed [Blob01 follow-up #1156](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1156) | #1154 replaced marker-scanning DWG extraction with a whole-section `DataStorage` model, schema/handle access, and Blob01 resolution. The discussion records an initial four-record/alignment-offset failure, a stale segment-index snapshot over-read, and then contributor-reported byte-for-byte per-handle payload comparisons on later revisions; another report covers Blob01 payloads up to 14 MiB across 13 pages. These are useful regression shapes and contributor reports, not independently reproduced results or a proof of every producer profile. The older #1139/#1146 signature/offset fallback is not the current merged DWG reader architecture. | Compare the local section model and entity→owner/schema/key→payload join separately. Continue to classify data-directory references and stale/unreferenced historical sections explicitly; never infer payload identity from an ACIS marker scan or aggregate entity counts. Existing generated 0/1/4/12-record, padding, Blob01, handle, and payload-identity controls remain the local fast owner; do not add duplicate tests or wait for ACadSharp execution. |
| ACadSharp open [writer PR #1150](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1150) and the linked [#1154 review exchange](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1154) | #1150 remains an unmerged proposal. Its contributor reports that a field-by-field ODA audit found the search-segment per-handle index must store the rank in sorted-handle order, not the record's directory position; these values coincide only when directory order already matches sorted handles. Later comments say the proposal needs rebasing/adaptation after the schema refactor and its tests include same-reader readback. | Retain a locally generated permuted-handle control as a distinct invariant from directory traversal order. The peer report is a test-shape lead, not authority to port code or evidence of a released writer. The current local replay path preserves parsed section bytes rather than synthesizing a schema-aware AcDs search index, so this does not create a new local writer task unless that architecture changes. |
| ACadSharp #1154 contributor [alignment-offset discussion](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1154) | A contributor argues that ODA's last-record maximum-size expression is a typo and describes additional data headers/unreferenced bytes in some files. The public discussion supplies an interpretation and producer observations, but not an ODA erratum, an independently rerun minimal DWG, or a formal rule for all such extra bytes. | Record this as `SPEC_DISCREPANCY_UNRESOLVED`, not an implementation instruction. Keep the current checked alignment-anchor implementation and local generated edge controls. If the parser is next changed, compare both candidate coordinate interpretations using a locally authored vector and a traceable producer/independent consumer result; preserve the raw section and fail closed on ambiguous bounds. |
| LibreDWG [0.14.1 NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) and [fuzzing setup](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg-fuzz) | The current release notes enumerate distinct failure classes: decompression allocation/logical-size disagreement, invalid page offsets and integer multiplication, a 3DSOLID block-size overflow, non-finite MLINE angles causing unbounded normalization, stale pointers after container growth, and record-loop/OOM progress defects. LibreDWG also documents separate DWG/DXF decode, encode, and round-trip fuzz routes. | Treat these as adversarial bug classes, not evidence of a libdxfrw defect. Local source review finds checked alignment/range arithmetic and bounded allocation/progress in the corresponding DataStorage, modeler SAT-block, and reader paths; the local MLINESTYLE writer rejects NaN/Inf and has ASCII/Binary refusal controls. Keep fuzz/sanitizer replay at the scheduled composed checkpoint, and add only the specific missing control when a touched parser owner lacks one. A peer fuzz campaign or successful parse cannot prove semantic completeness. |

Its optional DWG route is ODA File Converter. | Keep syntax/tag retention, raw ACIS carrier transport, B-rep interpretation, and native rendering/import as separate support dimensions. Do not use an ezdxf parse/audit/render as a 3D semantic pass or count its ODA-mediated DWG route as an independent DWG parser. |

### Implementation-ready reconciliation

1. **Preserve existing fast controls:** reuse the local 0/1/4/12-record and

   dependency-ready local queue.
3. **Resolve a future alignment edit from evidence:** use ODA §24.2.1/§24.2.2.3
   first; then record segment start, header end, object-data alignment anchor,
   header-directory end, data-start marker, record local offset, and segment
   end as separate coordinates. An apparent ODA typo may be promoted only
   after exact-profile producer data and independent readback corroborate it.
4. **Keep writer scope honest:** no AcDs writer is implied by section parsing

5. **Keep cadence and compatibility fixed:** strict focused target/selector

   scheduled gates. Preserve LibreCAD and LibreCAD_3 2D compatibility, the
   Linux/Windows FreeCAD qualification boundary, and the rule against
   committing external DWG/DXF fixtures.
