## Implementation progress — PAR-49/7G.3 composite BLOCK/INSERT sequence closure (2026-10-19; generated ASCII/Binary local fast slice, uncommitted)

Extended the existing `testConsecutiveNamedBlockOwnership` control in
[`tests/block_owner_tests.cpp`](tests/block_owner_tests.cpp) rather than adding
a new target or committing a drawing. The in-memory source now emits an early
`First` body containing an INSERT targeting `Second`, twelve ordered ATTRIBs,
and SEQEND, followed by a body LINE. `Second` contains an attribute-free
INSERT targeting `*D29` followed by its own LINE. Later definitions include an
intentionally empty `*D28`, a populated anonymous `*D29`, and a populated
`*Paper_Space0`; fixed model- and paper-space entities provide following
section sentinels.

The test parses both generated AC1027 ASCII and Binary output and checks:

- the seven emitted BLOCK_RECORD names each map by identity to exactly one
  BLOCK body and one owner-matching ENDBLK;
- fixed-space and custom block order remains intact, including all later
  named/anonymous/paper-layout siblings;
- every ordinary block-body child is owned by that block's BLOCK_RECORD,
  while ATTRIB/SEQEND children are owned by the owning INSERT;
- per-body entity-type counts distinguish the legal empty `*D28` from an
  absent body, and the attribute-rich and attribute-free INSERT cases remain
  distinct;
- the attribute-bearing INSERT has group 66=1, exactly twelve ordered tag/value
  pairs, then SEQEND, all before the next body entity; the attribute-free
  INSERT has no group 66 or sequence;
- modelspace and paperspace sentinels remain in ENTITIES under their respective
  fixed BLOCK_RECORD owners, and output reaches the terminal OBJECTS ENDSEC and
  EOF.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_block_owner_tests -j4  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_block_owners$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1, 0.34 s)
git diff --check -- tests/block_owner_tests.cpp DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md  PASS
```

This is a local DXF writer/adapter structural guard, not a reproduction of
LibreDWG's cursor bug and not evidence of DWG input completeness, native CAD
acceptance, or semantic support. The first focused run caught an incorrect
test expectation about the final section: AC1027 output ends with OBJECTS
ENDSEC before EOF, not ENTITIES ENDSEC. The assertion was corrected to the
actual section contract; the final focused run passes for the ASCII/Binary
pair. No fixture, new CTest, dependency, production-code change, full suite,
peer/native run, or support promotion was added. The broad worktree is already
uncommitted, and `.git` is read-only in this task environment, so this slice is
not committed. Findings/subplans remain 134/76; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293,
and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

## Implementation progress — PAR-14/7BS AC1009 classic POLYLINE/VERTEX marker compatibility (2026-10-19; generated local fast slice, uncommitted)

The existing `--classic-vertex-subclass-omission` selector now includes the
ACadSharp #1278 compatibility shape as well as the earlier AC1014 omitted
subtype case. It generates an AC1009 POLYLINE with three ordered VERTEX
children carrying group-100 subclass strings, a SEQEND, and LINE sentinels
before and after the compound record. Import checks the parent/child values,
sequence closure, and both sentinels; AC1009 re-export is checked for absence
of the out-of-profile group-100 markers, followed by a normal re-import.

The first binary inspection failed because the test paired the AC1009 bytes
with the generic two-byte Binary-DXF group-code reader. The test now uses
`dxfReaderBinaryR12`/`dxfWriterBinaryR12` only for AC1009; AC1014 remains on
the generic two-byte Binary-DXF classes. This was a test-harness mismatch, not
a production parser or writer defect.

Focused validation:

```text

build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --classic-vertex-subclass-omission  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1, 3.95 s)
git diff --check -- tests/dxf_fixture_tests.cpp  PASS
```

No production change, external sample, persistent fixture, CTest registration,
peer/native run, full-suite run, or support promotion. Generated files were

This review reconciles current ezdxf ACIS documentation and GDAL DXF-driver
documentation with the existing local ACIS projection and coordinate-test
owners. It sharpens what those routes can validate; it does not add a peer
dependency, execute an external tool, or promote a format-support claim.

The entity reference documents `Pattern`, `Wire`, and `Subshell` as not implemented and `Attribute` as unsupported. Unsupported structures may be rejected during export or reduced to `NONE_ENTITY` in the typed parse path, so an accepted entity or partial mesh is not a complete ACIS graph. | Keep ezdxf as a bounded DXF/carrier comparator. For any optional ACIS comparison, report payload parse outcome and unsupported-node disposition separately; only compare its mesh projection on flat-face controls. | Local [`DRW_AcisProjectionReport`](src/drw_acis.h) and generated rooted-graph assertion in [`testAcisWireframeGraph`](tests/graph_preservation_tests.cpp) | The current projection reports unsupported Pattern, Wire, Subshell, p-curve, curve, and surface counts; the generated graph control checks those counts and asserts `brepValidityChecked == false`. This is explicit partial-wireframe evidence, not whole-body completeness. The local report does not add an Attribute-specific counter, and this source review alone does not establish whether such nodes participate in the selected geometry projection. | Preserve the existing diagnostic and non-promotion boundary. Do not add an Attribute grammar or support claim from ezdxf's own model limitation. At the next ACIS inventory change, explicitly account for all body-reachable node types; if Attribute records are omitted from the selected projection, report them as metadata/not-applicable or unsupported only after their role is source- or spec-backed. |
| GDAL [DXF driver documentation](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | Binary-DXF read support is documented from GDAL 3.12. `RawCodeValues` is opt-in and contains group codes the reader did not handle, not a complete raw-record stream. AC1027+ 3D-extensible mode exposes ASM bytes and a 12-real affine transform but skips these solids by default and does not make OGR solid geometry. The docs explicitly exclude OCS/elevation geometry for DIMENSION, LEADER, and MULTILEADER. | Admit only a version-bound Binary-DXF parse, raw-group, ASM-carrier, or documented geometry-projection cell. Capture exact build/options and compare to generated manifests by source handle/type; keep transform and payload as separate fields. Mark DIMENSION/LEADER/MULTILEADER geometry `NOT_APPLICABLE` for GDAL and use source-authored local expectations. Never interpret missing OGR output as a dropped libdxfrw entity or a valid solid. |

3. Use ezdxf only at the composed ACIS checkpoint and only for an exact pinned

## Deeper/broader legacy bare-DXF TABLE compatibility candidate (2026-10-19; research only)

This pass screened an additional open-source DXF reader report, checked its
asserted input shape against Autodesk's published DXF organization, and traced
the corresponding path through the local section-state parser. No external
drawing was downloaded, no peer was built or run, and no parser behavior was
changed.

| Primary-source evidence | What it establishes—and does not establish | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autodesk [general DXF file structure](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D939EA11-0CEC-4636-91A8-756640A031D3.htm) and [symbol-table group-code example](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A66D0ACA-3F43-4B2E-A0C2-2B490C1E5268.htm) | The published canonical structure wraps symbol tables in `SECTION` / `TABLES` / `ENDSEC`, with each `TABLE` closed by `ENDTAB`. The documentation is about the standard file organization; it does not say that readers must recover a missing wrapper. | Classify a bare top-level `TABLE` as non-canonical compatibility input, not a conformance gap. Keep strict canonical behavior as the default contract. |
| ACadSharp open [feature request #1128](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1128) | The reporter says older NC/CAM/plotter exports put table records directly after `HEADER`, and ACadSharp skips those tables, leaving entities that depend on them apparently empty. The issue has no inspectable sample, producer/version, hash, or focused reproduction in its body; it is not a libdxfrw result. | Track only as a low-cost compatibility candidate. Do not treat the report's “otherwise valid” characterization as established, and do not add a persistent fixture from a peer or customer source. |
| Local `dxfRW::read()`, `processTables()`, and current PAR-36/7U | The outer parser returns `BAD_READ_SECTION` for a record body outside section framing; `processTables()` is reached only through a `SECTION` whose name is `TABLES`. PAR-36/7U handles unknown nested tables after a valid `TABLES` section has already begun. | The current reader fails closed rather than silently returning a drawing with missing table state. Do not broaden PAR-36/7U's nested-table skip to accept malformed top-level framing. |

### Conditional implementation-ready sub-plan

No production work is queued until a provenance-eligible representative file or
a concrete in-scope consumer need establishes that this recovery is valuable.
If that gate is met, keep the change in the existing DXF section-boundary
owner, without creating a new finding or top-level subplan:

1. Recognize only a bounded, top-level sequence of known `TABLE` records in the
   exact location under review. Reuse existing table-body parsers; do not
   pre-scan/copy the complete file or accept arbitrary records outside a
   section.
2. Require each record to have valid table framing (`ENDTAB`) and require the
   following top-level token to resume sound `SECTION`/`EOF` framing. Leave
   unknown bare table names and malformed/nested sequences fail-closed.
3. Stage all table callbacks until the recovered sequence is complete. On a
   missing terminator, malformed record, duplicate identity, or bad following
   boundary, return the existing read error without publishing partial table
   state.
4. On success, publish a bounded advisory diagnostic identifying this as
   non-canonical recovery and reporting the recovered count plus a limited
   sample of table names. Normal output must serialize the recovered records
   under the canonical `SECTION` / `TABLES` wrapper.
5. Add generated ASCII and Binary DXF controls to the existing parser test
   target: known table followed by a layer-using entity, multiple tables,
   malformed/missing `ENDTAB`, and a following section/entity sentinel. Run
   only the focused selector and owning CTest; no peer sample, new dependency,
   fixture registration, or full-suite run is needed for the slice.

The key unresolved decision is whether the project wants this explicit
non-standard recovery mode at all; the issue report alone does not decide it.
This update adds one compatibility candidate, but no confirmed local defect,
finding, top-level subplan, code/test change, fixture, dependency, validation
run, or support promotion. Findings/subplans remain 134/76; J256, J260, J268,
J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

The current concrete adapter forwards BLOCK_RECORD XDATA to the existing
`dxfRW::writeBlockRecord` path. That codec deep-copies its variants into the
pending record during precollection, validates the referenced APPIDs before
publication, and emits the retained sequence from `emitBlockRecord()` after
the record's ordinary fields. This closes the source-confirmed omission in the
live worktree without adding a new callback or pure interface method.

The `--block-record-xdata-roundtrip` control starts from the already tracked
`tests/fixtures/dxf/block_record_preview_r2007.dxf` and adds its profile
in-memory: two APPIDs, ordered string/1005/second-APPID/coordinate XDATA, a
referenced LINE in the owning block, and a later BLOCK_RECORD/block sentinel.
The same input is exported as AC1021 ASCII and Binary DXF. Each readback checks
ordered typed values, code-1005 remapping to the actual emitted LINE handle,
no XDATA leakage to the later table record, and both block-body sentinels. A
missing APPID is refused while preserving an existing destination; restoring
the APPID allows retry on the same writer.

Focused validation passed:


No external fixture, new target/CTest registration, peer/native run, full-suite
run, or support promotion. The existing shared worktree is broadly modified,
so this slice remains uncommitted and unstaged. This closes only the local
BLOCK_RECORD XDATA transfer/refusal path, not independent producer or native
acceptance. PAR-132/7CB generated DWG proxy-entity coverage is the next local

## Deeper/broader new peer proposal review: allocation counts, tagged dispatch, and context routes (2026-10-19, research only)

### Scope and evidence grade

This pass screened newly opened LibreDWG and ACadSharp pull requests and compared the specific failure shapes with libdxfrw's current implementation and local generated controls. The proposals are useful adversarial examples, but are open branch work, not merged release behavior, independent semantic evidence, or support votes. No peer PR was run here. Findings below distinguish (a) an implementation already present locally, (b) an audit/checklist refinement, and (c) a route that remains a discovery gap. No new local defect was demonstrated.

### Cross-cutting safety invariant to preserve

For any count-bearing or tagged record, the declared count, actual allocated/retained storage, discriminator/class identity, and writer/readback interpretation must remain consistent. Validate products and offsets before allocation or access; derive serialized counts from the retained vector when possible; otherwise reject a late count change before publishing the record. A malformed record should fail locally without corrupting the following record or publishing partial semantics. This is a source-review invariant for relevant changes, not a reason to add a new global framework.

At the next scheduled hardening/source-audit gate (not on every implementation slice), make one bounded census of remaining count-times-width, offset-plus-length, and count/index accesses in readers and writers. Reuse the existing checked arithmetic helpers and focused hardening selectors; record only unchecked sites that are reachable and not already bounded. Keep this audit finite and route-owned.

### Newly screened LibreDWG proposals

| Proposal | Reported shape | Local reconciliation and plan action |
|---|---|---|
| [#1453](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/pull/1453) | AcDs scan index subtraction can underflow near the end of a decompressed section. | No matching unsafe scan was found: `findAcisBinaryFileMarker` is bounded by payload size and uses checked byte access. Preserve its size-based loop and boundary control; no port or new finding. |
| [#1454](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/pull/1454) | A 32-bit vector count multiplied by element width can wrap before the buffer bounds check. | Local code already uses checked multiplication and bounded reserves in multiple paths, but this pass did not complete an exhaustive census. Include remaining call sites in the single scheduled audit above; do not claim a corresponding local bug from the peer report alone. |
| [#1456](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/pull/1456), [#1462](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/pull/1462) | Incoming JSON group/key or class type can disagree with a union/class discriminator, selecting the wrong member/layout. | This is a useful adversarial shape, not evidence of a libdxfrw JSON importer defect. For any local tagged/union-like route touched by implementation, assert type identity before interpretation and test mismatch refusal plus following-record integrity. DWG custom-class dispatch needs the same invariant; keep empirical `oType` discovery policy. |

Retain class-specific body framing and ownership checks where those routes are actually implemented. |

## Implementation progress — version-correct GeoData CIVIL-tail local round-trip matrix (2026-10-19; generated test-only fast slice, uncommitted)

The local DWG round-trip interface had populated the DWG-only CIVIL tail on
every target version and its reader callback expected that tail through
AC1027. The production encoder correctly refuses a populated tail when the
target cannot represent it; pre-registration of GeoData instance handles
therefore left intentionally unemitted class instances in the test file and
failed the final class-count check. The harness now populates those fields
only for AC1021 and AC1024 and expects `m_civilTail.m_present` only for that
exact pair. AC1015, AC1018, AC1027, and AC1032 exercise the no-tail path with
otherwise valid GeoData objects. No production behavior was relaxed.

controls and HATCH reference/admission/adapter/publication/same-data controls

cases. No persistent fixture, CTest registration, external peer, native CAD
application, or full project suite was run. No support claim changed. The

## Deeper/broader peer lineage, corpus independence, and capability-denominator audit (2026-10-19; primary-source review)

This pass broadened the earlier codec comparison to ask three separate
questions: whether implementations share decoder ancestry, whether their test
corpora share producers/fixtures, and whether a claimed capability was
measured over a meaningful per-version/per-family denominator. It used
project-owned documentation, manifests, and release pages only. No peer
repository was cloned or built, no external sample was downloaded, and no
peer, kernel, or native CAD runtime was executed.

| Route/source | Primary-source evidence and limit | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| [`cq-acis` README](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/README.md), [third-party notices](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), [corpus manifest guidance](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/corpus/README.md), [geometry support](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/docs/geometry-support.md), and [SAB/ASM profile](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/docs/sab-support.md) | The README describes an experimental parser/converter for selected SAT/SAB/ASM profiles and explicitly separates parse retention from shape conversion. The third-party notice says the new SAB reader's grammar/layout work was informed by CADMPEG format notes and Rust source; it also names ezdxf's tag grammar and public cube fixtures as references. The repository corpus documentation lists both NIST models and ezdxf SAT/SAB examples, separately licensed and excluded from package distributions. Thus the code is implementation-distinct from libdxfrw and ACadRust, but not reference-free; its fixture corpus overlaps ezdxf, and the conversion kernel is CadQuery/OpenCascade, shared with FreeCAD. | Keep the existing `cq-acis` candidate, but qualify independence by layer: `DISTINCT_IMPLEMENTATION / REFERENCE_INFORMED / CORPUS_OVERLAP_WITH_EZDXF / SHARED_OCCT_KERNEL`. Do not use one of its own/overlapping fixtures as the independent expected result. A locally generated control with analytic values fixed before encoding can still provide a useful bounded cross-implementation semantic observation after the exact platform artifact/source and profile are pinned. It remains only a payload-to-shape check; it cannot validate DXF/DWG extraction or the DWG entity→AcDs index/key→SAB owner join. |
| [`dwg-rs` project and empirical coverage report](https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/dwg-rs) | The project calls itself pre-alpha, states entity decoders have coverage gaps, and reports per-version decoded/skipped/errored counts measured on a small corpus: one to three files per version in the displayed table. The report is useful because it exposes outcomes and sample counts rather than only a version badge; it is not a broad corpus qualification or a whole-file semantic result. | Borrow the reporting shape, not its percentages as a target: every selected peer comparison should include exact input count and provenance plus decoded, skipped, raw/opaque, unsupported, and error counts, preferably keyed by source identity and entity/object family. Do not compare aggregate percentages across different corpora or infer “all DWG” support from a handful of files. Keep `dwg-rs` as a possible exact-operation structural comparator only; it is not a writer or ACIS/B-rep oracle. |
| [ACadSharp version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp), [ACadRust](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust), [OpenCADStudio v2026.42](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/releases/tag/v2026.42), and [OpenCADKernel scope](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/opencadkernel) | ACadSharp's matrix is explicitly direction- and version-specific (including no AC1021 DWG writer). ACadRust advertises a broad reader/writer matrix and ACIS/B-rep path. OpenCADStudio is a real application consumer, but its codec is ACadRust-derived; its current 3D workflow also includes tessellation and a separately described early kernel. Its v2026.42 release and feature declarations do not turn its application self-read into a second parser implementation. | Normalize results over the tuple `artifact × operation × format version × entity/object family × consumer route`. Count ACadRust and its application/bindings descendants once for parser lineage. OpenCADStudio may still answer a distinct application-consumer question when pinned to an exact release and codec/kernel revisions, but does not add an independent reader or kernel vote. Do not infer writer support from reader matrices. |
| [LibreDWG manual coverage](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/Overview.html), [ezdxf 1.4.5 quick-info](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/), and [IxMilia.Dxf compatibility notes](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf) | The projects expose different capability slices: LibreDWG documents broad DWG read coverage alongside writer and DXF caveats; ezdxf is a DXF ASCII/Binary reader/writer with declared DXF version ranges and a separate ACIS-data parser but no DWG container reader; IxMilia's DXF scope and entity exceptions are explicit, and its writer documentation warns that typed output is not automatically accepted by AutoCAD. These declarations describe route boundaries, not cross-application acceptance. | Keep read, write, conversion, preservation, and geometry interpretation as separate columns. An accepted syntax, exposed entity class, retained raw carrier, or successful same-codec round trip cannot fill the semantic or native-acceptance column. Require a strict independent DXF parse only at the existing composed checkpoint and keep recovery/audit behavior separately labeled. |
| ODA/Open CASCADE commercial ACIS import boundary | The already-reviewed Open CASCADE catalog distinguishes the open-source OCCT base from commercial ACIS SAT/SAB exchange components. Therefore an OCCT-based application build cannot be assumed to have an ACIS reader merely because it has the geometry kernel. | Maintain the existing split between parser provenance and kernel lineage. If an OCCT commercial ACIS component is selected, record edition/license and exact component/build; do not classify it as open-source parser evidence or assume it is available in stock FreeCAD. |

### Implementation-ready comparison protocol

1. At peer admission, record a three-layer provenance tuple: parser/code
   ancestry and immutable artifact; test corpus plus producer/fixture
   provenance; and geometry kernel/application lineage. A distinct repository
   name does not establish independence. Mark reference-informed or corpus-
   overlapping routes explicitly, while still allowing a narrow comparison
   against an independently authored expectation.
2. Make the per-input denominator explicit: sample count and source; requested
   read/write/convert route; actual format revision; entity/object family;
   typed records, raw/opaque retained records, skipped/unsupported records,
   hard errors, and loss diagnostics. Preserve source handles/owners before
   any peer normalization. Never let a total entity count hide nested block,
   paper-space, or object-section omissions.
3. For a future optional `cq-acis` check, first verify the pinned platform
   wheel's hash/attestation and audit the matching source revision, then
   preflight exact SAT/SAB signature, word width, save version, and supported
   geometry layout. Use a scratch-generated profile and a manifest authored
   before serialization. Compare all bodies, reference closure, B-rep
   validity/closedness, units, placement, topology, bounds, and analytic
   metrics. Report shared OCCT lineage; do not treat `Shape.isValid()`, a
   render, or parser exit status as complete semantic proof.
4. Keep outer carrier checks independent: compare local source entity identity,
   owner/block/INSERT closure, AcDs schema/index/key association, payload hash,
   and DXF emitted entity separately from the peer's ACIS parse/conversion.
   `cq-acis` does not read DWG/DXF outer files. A payload-to-shape pass cannot
   repair a missing owner join.
5. Run the optional comparison only at the existing composed checkpoint, not
   in each implementation slice. Continue fast per-slice validation on the
   owning target/selector/CTest and scoped diff. Do not install a runtime,
   fetch peer-corpus data, add a recurring peer dependency, or delay local
   implementation because this optional route is unavailable.
6. Keep LibreCAD and LibreCAD_3 2D compatibility, the separate Linux/Windows
   FreeCAD consumer gate, local/generated fixture policy, and current reduced
   full-suite cadence unchanged. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; this research only improves how future evidence can be
   admitted and interpreted.

This update adds no confirmed local defect, finding, top-level subplan,

now exposes a no-input `--capability-profile` probe. The build helper captures

Keep `3DSOLID`/`REGION`/`BODY` in carrier-only/partial disposition; no B-rep or AcDs semantic claim follows. |

Compare per source handle/type/owner and explicit expected values; do not use neutral-model equality, rendered SVG, or CADKit's own DXF export as parser correctness proof. |
| [`acadrust.js` README](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/acadrust.js/blob/main/README.md) and [`obj2cad` README](https://github.com/cbassuarez/obj2cad) | `acadrust.js` consumes ACadRust as an unmodified Cargo dependency, so it is a binding, not an additional DWG/DXF codec. `obj2cad` has its own SAT/SAB and DXF authoring paths, but its DWG writer is patched ACadRust; the project labels DWG as beta pending AutoCAD acceptance. | Count the wrapper under ACadRust lineage. `obj2cad` may be considered only as a temporary scratch-control producer for a named independent-writer question; its DWG output is not an independent DWG writer result, and its self/readback checks cannot promote ACIS semantics or native acceptance. |

Source visibility alone does not make a project open source. |

### Implementation-ready, fast-first disposition

1. Keep the existing local implementation queue, fast-test validation, and
   full-suite cadence unchanged. CADKit remains `OPTIONAL_STRUCTURAL_2D_CANDIDATE
   / NOT_RUN`, and is never a routine dependency or slice blocker.

3. Keep AC1021 container/decompression comparisons lineage-correlated with

   count multiple package wrappers or the same corpus producer as independent

4. Never use CADKit, `acadrust.js`, or `obj2cad` to qualify a DWG writer,

   external evidence is non-blocking and self-unblocks to the next local slice.

## Deeper/broader associative graph semantics, DXF adapter loss, and peer-boundary reconciliation (2026-10-19)

This research refines existing PAR-06 and adds implementation subplan 7BV.
It does not add a duplicate PAR finding: PAR-06 already owns opaque-object
coverage and the rule that raw replay is permitted only when source version,
identity, ownership, and references remain safe. This pass found a specific
DXF-to-converter path that the broad owner did not name. The local source audit
is reproducible from the named callback paths, but this turn did not run a
runtime reproducer; the finding is therefore source-confirmed, not executed.

Actions and networks form an ordered dependency graph (documented as a DAG) whose evaluation updates dependent geometry. | An associative object is not semantically preserved by retaining one root record or one `DRW_AssociativeObject` shell. `libdxfrw` is not an associative constraint solver. These API descriptions establish relationships/behavior, not full DXF tag grammar or DWG bytes. |
| Autodesk [DXF OBJECTS section](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-49C9C960-0944-4C1B-8DF9-E2428C28A2FB.htm), [common object group codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-6939D69E-04CB-4F4C-87B2-67BC540FCF58.htm), and [object group-code overview](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-1038FDE4-745D-469D-972E-1F977D674882.htm) | OBJECTS is a non-graphical object heap ordered by ownership; common groups can encode owner, reactor and extension-dictionary links, and typed pointer/ownership roles. | Use these rules to validate common object framing and graph edges. They do not specify every ACDBASSOC class-specific field, payload, or persistent-subentity identifier. Do not invent class layouts from generic group-code types. |

The shell's partial fields do not represent all class semantics. | The core DXF parser exposes a typed shell plus opaque carrier; it is not the loss point. Keep the entire raw group distinct from decoded fields. |

Its raw callback was an allow-list for named families (proxy, visual style, render/background, fields, named resources, etc.); associative names fell through. No duplicate finding or fast test is added. Peer thresholds and candidate fixes are not transferred as format rules. |

### 7BV — Associative DXF object capture and safe replay (PAR-06)

**Goal:** eliminate silent loss in the concrete converter while keeping object
semantics honest. First make an incomplete associative conversion visibly
fail before publication. Next retain the typed shell and full raw record with
source identity. Only later allow replay for a source/target profile whose
object identity and references can be proven safe. Constraint solving,
re-evaluation after geometry edits, and complete DWG ACDBASSOC/PERSUBENTMGR
grammar are explicitly outside this local adapter subplan.

#### 7BV dispatch inventory (source-frozen 2026-10-19)

`dxfRW::readDxfObjects()` uppercases each incoming record name, then admits the
exact aliases `PERSISTENTSUBENTITYMANAGER`, `PERSUBENTMGR`, and
`ACDBPERSSUBENTMANAGER`, plus every name beginning `ACDBASSOC` or `ASSOC`.
The prefix branches are open-ended: the 44 names below are the local CLASSES
registry inventory, not an exhaustive limit on names that reach the parser.

| Name set | Typed parse and raw capture | Concrete adapter disposition | Strict writer disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 43 registry names other than `ACDBPERSSUBENTMANAGER`; future `ACDBASSOC*` and `ASSOC*` names; aliases `PERSISTENTSUBENTITYMANAGER` and `PERSUBENTMGR` | `DRW_AssociativeObject::parseCode()` delegates to common `DRW_TableEntry::parseCode()` except subclass markers; `processAssociativeObject()` also accumulates the complete ordered stream into `DRW_RawDxfObject`. | Parser calls `addAssociativeObject()` then `addRawDxfObject()` at the record boundary. `dx_iface` retains bounded partial typed shells/raw groups and pairs same-generation ranges by normalized name, handle, owner and source profile. | No associative output loop; strict complete-output refuses any record not yet serializer-qualified before constructing `dxfRW` or opening/replacing the destination. |
| `ACDBPERSSUBENTMANAGER` registry name / exact alias; subclass marker `AcDbPersSubentManager` | Same typed shell and complete raw stream. The DXF parser additionally consumes group 90 values and repeated 330 handles only after that subclass marker. This is a partial field decode, not complete persistent-subentity semantics. | Same bounded storage and pairing; the partial parsed count/handles remain evidence of decoded fields only. | Same strict refusal. No DWG byte-layout inference or semantic support claim follows from the DXF special case. |

The 44 normalized names observed in `src/libdxfrw.cpp` are:

```text
ACDBASSOCPERSSUBENTMANAGER, ACDBPERSSUBENTMANAGER, ACDBASSOCNETWORK,
ACDBASSOCACTION, ACDBASSOCALIGNEDDIMACTIONBODY,
ACDBASSOCOSNAPPOINTREFACTIONPARAM, ACDBASSOCVERTEXACTIONPARAM,
ACDBASSOCGEOMDEPENDENCY, ACDBASSOCDEPENDENCY,
ACDBASSOCDIMDEPENDENCYBODY, ACDBASSOC3POINTANGULARDIMACTIONBODY,
ACDBASSOCALIGNEDIMACTIONBODY, ACDBASSOCORDINATEDIMACTIONBODY,
ACDBASSOCROTATEDDIMACTIONBODY, ACDBASSOCARRAYMODIFYACTIONBODY,
ACDBASSOCARRAYACTIONBODY, ACDBASSOCEDGECHAMFERACTIONBODY,
ACDBASSOCEDGEFILLETACTIONBODY, ACDBASSOCMLEADERACTIONBODY,
ACDBASSOCBLENDSURFACEACTIONBODY, ACDBASSOCEXTENDSURFACEACTIONBODY,
ACDBASSOCEXTRUDEDSURFACEACTIONBODY, ACDBASSOCFILLETSURFACEACTIONBODY,
ACDBASSOCLOFTEDSURFACEACTIONBODY, ACDBASSOCNETWORKSURFACEACTIONBODY,
ACDBASSOCOFFSETSURFACEACTIONBODY, ACDBASSOCPLANESURFACEACTIONBODY,
ACDBASSOCPATCHSURFACEACTIONBODY, ACDBASSOCRESTOREENTITYSTATEACTIONBODY,
ACDBASSOCREVOLVEDSURFACEACTIONBODY, ACDBASSOCSWEPTSURFACEACTIONBODY,
ACDBASSOCTRIMSURFACEACTIONBODY, ACDBASSOCACTIONPARAM,
ACDBASSOCASMBODYACTIONPARAM, ACDBASSOCCOMPOUNDACTIONPARAM,
ACDBASSOCEDGEACTIONPARAM, ACDBASSOCFACEACTIONPARAM,
ACDBASSOCPATHACTIONPARAM, ACDBASSOCOBJECTACTIONPARAM,
ACDBASSOCPOINTREFACTIONPARAM, ACDBASSOCARRAYMODIFYPARAMETERS,
ACDBASSOCARRAYPATHPARAMETERS, ACDBASSOCARRAYPOLARPARAMETERS,
ACDBASSOCARRAYRECTANGULARPARAMETERS
```

1. **7BV.1 — Freeze inventory and reproduce the callback contract.** The
   dispatch families, parser behavior, callback order, current storage category
   and writer disposition are recorded above. Add generated ASCII and Binary
   OBJECTS records to the existing `tests/dwg2dxf_adapter_tests.cpp` executable.
   Assert the parser delivers one shell and one complete ordered raw record per
   input; cover the explicit persistent-subentity aliases, the `ACDBASSOC*`
   and `ASSOC*` prefix branches (including an unregistered suffix), and use a
   following known object as a boundary sentinel. These generated records prove
   only dispatch and callback framing, not valid associative semantics. Add
   malformed/truncated inputs that must fail before later callbacks.
2. **7BV.2 — Stop false-success conversion.** Add a concrete adapter receipt for
   typed associative callbacks and raw companions, scoped to one import
   generation and source DXF profile. Cap observed records at 100,000 and raw
   groups at 4,000,000; set an overflow bit and fail closed at either limit.
   Since this step retains no payload, exact typed/raw identity pairing is
   intentionally deferred to 7BV.3; any observed callbacks exceed the current
   zero retained/qualified counts. The complete-output path refuses stale,
   over-limit, or unretained receipts before `dxfRW` construction or destination
   open. Its bounded counts-only diagnostic never copies source names, handles,
   or payload text. Preserve an existing destination and prove a corrected
   same-adapter retry.
3. **7BV.3 — Retain as opaque source data without claiming support.** Store the
   complete raw groups and partial typed shells in owned `dx_data`, together
   with source version, generation, normalized name, source handle and owner.
   Reuse `DRW_RawDxfObject`; do not add a generic object framework or a new pure
   `DRW_Interface` virtual. Enforce the current 100,000-record/4,000,000-group
   caps and a checked aggregate retained-value budget no larger than the
   existing `DRW::kMaxDxfBinaryPayloadBytes` (64 MiB). Pair callback ranges
   only within one import and verify normalized name/handle/owner equality;
   missing, duplicate, mismatched, allocation-failed, or over-budget captures
   leave the receipt incomplete. Copies, reset, repeated reads and failed
   reads must not make old-generation data replayable. To keep accumulation
   bounded, a nonempty associative store from an earlier import generation
   makes the next receipt incomplete rather than appending another retained
   generation. Retention is observability/future replay input only; strict
   export continues to refuse until 7BV.4 closes.
4. **7BV.4 — Admit only a safe, bounded DXF replay profile.** Before calling
   `writeRawDxfObject`, validate one-import typed/raw equality, unique handles,
   owner closure, dictionary/root reachability, recognized pointer/ownership
   roles, and every source-to-output handle binding. Preserve tag order and raw
   value variants. If a class-specific field may contain an unrecognized
   reference, the drawing was mutated, a target-version conversion changes the
   class profile, or any edge is ambiguous/unresolved, refuse before publication
   rather than replay a stale graph. Start with same-profile, unmodified
   DXF→DXF only. The first local 7BV.4a slice may census generic translated-
   handle group-code positions in the bounded raw stream, but must label them
   unclassified and must not interpret them as graph edges, closure, or replay
   readiness. 7BV.4b may prove a bounded ownership chain through retained
   associative nodes and complete DICTIONARY entries to the position-identified
   NOD; label this owner-chain reachability only, not class-specific reference
   closure. Unknown owner types, ambiguous identities, missing dictionary
   entries, cycles, or over-limit scans remain unrooted/incomplete. A generated synthetic graph validates generic handle remapping
   mechanics, not the actual ACDBASSOC grammar; class semantics require the
   external evidence gate below. Reuse the existing
   `testDxfRawEntityApplicationGroupReferenceMatrix()` baseline in
   `tests/wave1_tests.cpp`: it exercises explicit source-to-replacement maps
   for generic translated-handle codes 320/330/350/390/399/480/481 in ASCII
   and Binary raw replay. That proves the writer's primitive remap behavior
   only; it does not prove associative edge roles, source-map construction,
   graph closure, or safe replay admission. Add associative-specific mapping
   controls only after the candidate reference roles and output bindings are
   fully enumerated.
   Scope the owner-chain census to the current import generation for both the
   NOD callback and DICTIONARY range; older `dx_data` contents cannot supply
   missing owner evidence. 7BV.4e records these callback bounds and tests a
   reused adapter where a prior-generation dictionary would otherwise make a
   current associative record appear rooted. A missing current dictionary
   remains unrooted even if a stale dictionary has the same handle and
   membership; a stale NOD cannot establish a current root, and duplicate
   current NOD callbacks make the root identity ambiguous.
5. **7BV.5 — Keep independent semantic qualification separate.** To claim a
   native associative result, require a version-pinned producer artifact or
   primary class grammar that actually documents the relevant DXF fields, plus
   an independent CAD open and edit/update/reopen check for the exact graph.
   Record action, dependency, variable, geometry, dimension, owner, and reactor
   disposition individually. A successful parser open, same-codec round-trip,
   class count, or unchanged display is not proof that constraints still
   evaluate. DWG payload work additionally requires ODA/version-specific byte
   evidence or a traced producer vector; do not transplant DXF group semantics
   into `parseDwg()`.

**Fast validation and self-unblocking:** use only the existing
`libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests` target, one named focused selector/CTest, the
strict affected translation units, and `lc3_compat_check` for each slice. Run
the adapter/DXF graph composed checkpoint once after the local capture,
refusal, and replay pieces settle; defer full suites to their existing planned
checkpoint. Generate all controls in memory or scratch output. Do not add or
commit peer/customer DWG/DXF fixtures; only an already tracked repository
fixture or a locally authored from-scratch vector may be used. After each
implementation slice, update this plan and a source-hash receipt, commit the
slice, report its commit hash and focused result, then continue to the next
unblocked local child. Missing native/producer evidence blocks only replay or
support promotion; it does not block the source-backed loss guard, diagnostics,
or next independent local slice.

**Completion boundary:** 7BV closes only the `dwg2dxf` DXF adapter's bounded
capture/refusal/replay contract. It does not establish generic libdxfrw
associative-object semantics, DWG association support, constraint solver
behavior, or 3D/B-rep support. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293 and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Deeper/broader CADMPEG ACIS/ASM reader candidate and evidence-lineage update (2026-10-19; research only)

This pass screened the newly surfaced `cadmpeg-codec-sat` as a possible
independent ACIS payload comparator for the existing PAR-07/S8 evidence lane.
It adds no local defect or implementation subplan. The useful change is to
make the candidate and its evidence ceiling explicit: a direct payload reader
can help compare decoded ACIS/ASM records and projected geometry, but it
cannot qualify the DWG/DXF container, `AcDs` section traversal, modeler-entity
to-payload association, or a native CAD consumer.

### Evidence and claim boundary

| Evidence | What it establishes | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CADMPEG [release page](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/releases) | A v0.6.2 release is listed at commit `7bcc952`, dated 2026-10-19. | The page alone does not prove that the `cadmpeg-codec-sat` crate archive, source tag, docs.rs build, and release binary contain identical code. |
| CADMPEG [format support](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/blob/main/docs/format-support.md), [ASM format notes](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/blob/main/docs/formats/asm.md), and [`cadmpeg-codec-sat` docs](https://docs.rs/crate/cadmpeg-codec-sat/latest) | The documented route decodes *bare* SAT/SMT/SAB/SMB streams into CADMPEG's neutral model. It distinguishes `ASM BinaryFile4`, `ASM BinaryFile8`, text streams, and the `ACIS BinaryFile` branch; only ACIS save-format majors 217 and 218 are documented as verified. The codec is read-only and reports unsupported/untransferred data. | It is not documented as a DWG/DXF reader/writer and cannot test outer-object ownership, `AcDs` keys, DXF 3DSOLID group-1/3 framing, or native application acceptance. Other ACIS majors are explicitly unverified; do not include them in a qualified denominator. |
| CADMPEG [`asm-open-items.md`](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/blob/main/docs/formats/asm-open-items.md) | The project publicly records unresolved record grammar and semantic questions, including cache ownership, surface/curve layouts, pcurve tolerance/fallback, body-kind inference, and topology substitution. This is a useful disclosure and test-selection aid. | Its machine-checked tables, parser self-tests, or accepted synthetic controls are not independent format authority. Open items directly limit any positive semantic inference from the candidate. |
| CADMPEG [repository](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg), [workspace manifest](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/blob/main/Cargo.toml), and crate page | The repository has its own `cadmpeg-asm` and `cadmpeg-codec-sat` source path; the inspected workspace dependency list does not declare `cq-acis`. | Parser-source separation alone does not prove independent author, specimen, producer, or format-fact provenance. Resolve those lineages at the exact release before counting a second implementation. |
| Existing `cq-acis` [third-party notices](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and current local peer-lineage receipt | `cq-acis` reports that its SAB grammar/layout work was informed by CADMPEG notes/source. Therefore CADMPEG and `cq-acis` may be separate implementations but are correlated in format discovery; `cq-acis` also uses CadQuery/OpenCascade for shape conversion. | Do not count CADMPEG and `cq-acis` as two independent positive witnesses. A second library run cannot cure shared assumptions, overlapping producer inputs, or kernel lineage. |
| CADMPEG release versus [docs.rs latest crate](https://docs.rs/crate/cadmpeg-codec-sat/latest) | GitHub lists v0.6.2 at `7bcc952`; the currently served crate page identifies `cadmpeg-codec-sat` v0.6.1. This is an artifact-alignment warning at the time of review. | Do not silently combine v0.6.2 release notes with the v0.6.1 crate API/source. Pin and hash the exact archive and matching source before any optional run. |

### Optional PAR-07/S8 comparator protocol

1. **Resolve the artifact first.** Pin the v0.6.2 source tag/commit and the
   matching `cadmpeg-codec-sat`/`cadmpeg-asm` crate archives. Record SHA-256s,
   Cargo dependency resolution, target platform, and the exact API/CLI entry
   point. If release/tag/archive alignment cannot be demonstrated, record
   `ARTIFACT_UNRESOLVED` and skip the run.
2. **Prove the input route.** Use an analytically specified ACIS/ASM stream
   generated locally from scratch or a source-authored in-memory byte vector;
   do not import customer/peer fixtures into the repository. Record the
   producer implementation, version, source provenance, save format, header
   width, units, payload hash, and expected bounds/volume/topology. Do not use
   CADMPEG's own output as a writer oracle: its documented codec has no writer.
3. **Compare only admitted branches.** At minimum separate ASM 4-byte and
   8-byte references, text SAT/SMT, and ACIS 217/218 binary controls. Treat
   every other ACIS major as `UNVERIFIED` even if decoding returns geometry.
   Include one bounded unknown/unsupported record control and retain counts for
   total, decoded, unknown, skipped, loss-bearing, and geometry-transferred
   records. A success exit or `geometry_transferred=true` alone is insufficient.
4. **Check semantics against declared expectations.** Compare per-body
   identity, surface/curve families, topology closure, orientation, units,
   analytic bounds and volume against predeclared source-authored expectations;
   compare parser outputs only after normalizing parser-local IDs. Any candidate
   open-item that intersects the tested geometry must be marked `OPEN_ITEM`
   and blocks positive promotion for that dimension. Distinguish agreement
   between CADMPEG and `cq-acis` from agreement with the independent analytic
   expectation.
5. **Keep carrier and consumer lanes separate.** For payload extracted from a
   DWG or DXF, independently record the source entity handle, owner/key join,
   extraction path, and raw payload hash. Feeding the extracted bytes to this
   bare-stream reader tests only payload decode; it does not validate the
   extraction or association. Native CAD open/save/reopen remains a separate
   consumer result on the exact platform and converter/importer route.
6. **Keep it nonblocking and cheap.** This is an optional composed-checkpoint
   run after local 3D carrier work settles, never a per-slice dependency or
   full-suite trigger. No peer library is added to the product build, no new
   committed fixture is needed, and `NOT_RUN`/`ARTIFACT_UNRESOLVED` does not
   block the next local implementation slice.

This update refines the existing external evidence gate only: no new local
finding/top-level subplan, dependency, test registration, persistent fixture,
peer build/run, validation cadence or implementation-order change. Current
plan totals remain 134 findings / 77 top-level subplans. J256, J260, J268,
J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; this candidate cannot promote

## Implementation progress — PAR-06/7BV.1–7BV.3 associative inventory, loss gate, and bounded capture (2026-10-19; generated fast slices, uncommitted)

The source-frozen inventory above records the exact dispatch aliases and open
prefixes, the 44 names in the current class registry, the common typed/raw
parser route, the PERSUBENTMGR subclass-specific DXF branch, and current
adapter/writer disposition. It explicitly does not treat the class registry
as exhaustive because dispatch accepts future prefix matches.

`dwg2dxf_associative_callback_contract` generates ASCII and Binary AC1027
OBJECTS input with an `ACDBASSOCACTION`, repeated group-301 sentinels, and a
following `DICTIONARYVAR`. It checks ordered callbacks/raw groups, source
identity/profile, generation-scoped capture ranges, and later-object delivery.
A separate generated `ACDBPERSSUBENTMANAGER` verifies that the DXF
`AcDbPersSubentManager` subclass path captures class-version/count/handle
fields without promoting them to complete semantics. Invalid ASCII handle and
Binary section-boundary truncation fail before publishing the record or later
callback.

7BV.2's `dx_associativeDxfImportReceipt` caps records at 100,000 and groups at
4,000,000. 7BV.3 retains typed shells and complete `DRW_RawDxfObject` pairs
under a checked 64 MiB aggregate logical-value estimate, records typed/raw
generation ranges, and finalizes `captureComplete` only when normalized name,
handle, owner, source version and unique nonzero handle checks pass. Allocation,
limit, mismatch, duplicate, or mixed-generation data leaves the receipt
incomplete. Reusing a container already holding associative data does not append
another generation; it remains ineligible for strict output.

Serializer qualification intentionally remains zero. The strict complete-
output path refuses any associative data before `dxfRW` construction or
destination open and emits bounded numeric diagnostics only. The strict-loss
CTest verifies destination byte preservation, corrected retry with the same
adapter and a fresh container, stale-container refusal after a repeated import,
and mismatched/duplicate callback-pair refusal. No source names, handles or
payload text are written to diagnostics.

### Bounded PAR-07/S8 admission refinement

The candidate check now records the following before a peer contributes even a
narrow comparison result:

1. **Legal/source eligibility:** explicit license and any third-party notices;
   source-visible does not mean open-source or reusable.
2. **Operation-specific lineage:** identify the parser/converter actually used
   for each direction (DWG read, DXF read, DWG/DXF write, render, or native
   application import). Ports, wrappers, and downstream applications are not
   additional parser votes.
3. **Artifact and evidence age:** pin commit/release, resolved dependencies,
   build options, executable/package hash where available, and report dates.
   Historical status tables remain historical even if the mutable README is
   current.
4. **Corpus and expected-result provenance:** record every input's source,
   license, producer/version, and expected-value author. A peer's own
   LibreDWG/ezdxf-derived baseline is useful for discrepancy discovery but is
   not an independent oracle for those same paths.
5. **Result surface and denominator:** distinguish typed records, raw/opaque
   retention, source identity/owner closure, diagnostics, JSON/scene output,
   rendered projection, writer output, strict independent re-read, and native
   acceptance. Counts, parse success, or a rendered image cannot substitute
   for one another.

ft_model remains optional only for a question where a 2D projection or
renderer has value; UnCAD's DWG lane is deduplicated under LibreDWG; Zephyr is
an application route with split SwiftDXFrw/ODA provenance; and codelibs stays
within libdxfrw's source family. SeaCad remains excluded unless its license
changes. This update adds no local defect, finding, top-level subplan,
implementation dependency, test registration, fixture, peer run, native
qualification, or support promotion. Implementation order and the reduced
fast-test/full-suite cadence are unchanged. Findings/subplans remain 134/77;
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain DEFERRED_EXTERNAL and cannot
promote support claims.

## Implementation progress — PAR-06/7BV.4b bounded owner-chain reachability (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The receipt now also records how many associative records have a bounded owner
chain to the position-identified NOD through typed associative records and
complete typed DICTIONARY records. Whenever an owner is a DICTIONARY, its
entry list must contain the child handle. Duplicate owner identities,
unrecognized intermediate owner types, missing dictionary entries, cycles,
chains deeper than 64, absent/malformed NOD data, and inventories over 200,000
owner nodes or dictionary edges do not root a record; failed/over-limit scans
are marked incomplete. This deliberately bounded inventory covers only owner
chains, not opaque class-specific references, dictionary aliases outside the
typed capture, reactors, graph evaluation semantics, or the source-to-output
handle map. It cannot set `qualifiedRecords` or authorize serialization.

Generated ASCII and Binary controls now include a root NOD, an
`ACAD_ASSOCIATIONS` dictionary, a child entry to the action, and the action's
matching owner. They prove one owner chain reaches the NOD. The strict-loss
control carries the same rooted graph, verifies bounded numeric diagnostics,
and still proves the existing destination is not modified. The
PERSUBENTMGR partial-field control remains owner-unrooted because its fixture
does not provide an NOD; no inference is made from that partial record.

The source review found a material peer-evidence limitation: LibreDWG's
mutable `master` `objects.in` marks ASSOCACTION and ASSOCACTIONPARAM `UNSTABLE`
and some related classes `STABLE`, while its current documentation still
places ASSOCACTION/ASSOCNETWORK/ASSOCGEOMDEPENDENCY among unhandled or halfway
features. This status vocabulary is not a DXF field grammar or independent
semantic qualification, and the reviewed mutable branch was not pinned to an
immutable commit. The repository's generic raw writer also leaves a
handle-like value unchanged when no source-to-output map is present; therefore
the current associative strict refusal remains required. No peer build,
external fixture, native application, full suite, or support promotion was
used. Focused build/test results and source hashes are in the receipt:
[`associative-owner-chain-fast-slice-2026-10-19.json`](docs/research/associative-owner-chain-fast-slice-2026-10-19.json).

## Implementation progress — PAR-06/7BV.4e associative owner-scan generation boundary (2026-10-19; generated ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

The associative owner-chain census previously scoped typed/raw associative
records to the current import, but scanned every DICTIONARY accumulated in the
reused `dx_data`. A prior import could therefore supply a same-handle
DICTIONARY edge missing from the current file and cause the receipt to report a
rooted owner chain. The scan now uses an explicit current-generation dictionary
range and requires one current NOD callback; repeated/ambiguous NOD callbacks
or missing current root evidence leave owner-chain completion false. Older
dictionary records are excluded from the graph. The bounded scan also caps the
number of prior list entries it traverses before reaching the current range.

Generated ASCII and Binary controls use one `dx_iface`/`dx_data` for two
imports. The first file contributes a rooted-looking dictionary without an
associative object. The second provides the NOD edge and associative action but
omits the owned dictionary; the stale prior-generation dictionary is the only
record that could complete the chain. Both cases require a complete capture,
complete handle and owner scans, zero rooted/qualified records, current
dictionary range `[1,1)`, and publication of the following sentinel. A paired
control omits the current NOD while leaving a stale one in `dx_data`; another
probe duplicates the current NOD callback. The stale-root case leaves the
owner scan incomplete, and the duplicate-root case marks the NOD identity
ambiguous, in both encodings. Existing single-generation rooted and unrooted
controls remain in the same focused selector.

Validation:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests -j2` — passed.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^dwg2dxf_associative_(callback_contract|strict_loss_gate)$' --output-on-failure` — passed (2/2).
- `cmake --build build-gcc --target lc3_compat_check -j2` — passed.
- No full suite, external peer/native run, persistent fixture, CTest registration,
  or support-claim promotion.

This closes only a same-generation owner-evidence boundary in 7BV.4. Typed/raw
capture remains non-serializable; class-specific references, safe replay,
constraint solving and external semantic qualification remain open. Findings
and top-level subplans remain 135/77; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. No commit was created because `.git` is read-only
in the shared worktree.

The C++ exporter emits selected straight edge linework from 3D faces, restricts curved edges to XY-parallel planes, and may duplicate lines; the legacy exporter flattens 3D objects to 2D views. Neither is a general solid round-trip oracle. | Autodesk [3DSOLID DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm) and [common entity group codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3610039E-27D1-4E23-B6D3-7E60B22BB5BD.htm) | The DXF `3DSOLID` shell specifies `AcDbModelerGeometry`, group 70 modeler-format version, proprietary group 1/3 data, then `AcDb3dSolid` and optional history group 350. The shell contract does not validate SAT/SAB syntax or shape semantics. | Preserve separate checks for record/subclass ordering, version-specific payload carrier, source handle/owner, history link, and independent geometry. Never infer an ACIS save version from DXF group 70 or count a syntactically present 3DSOLID as a valid body. |
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF import/export guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) | The built-in C++ importer list includes polylines but not `3DFACE` or `MESH`; the legacy importer list includes `3DFACE`, not `MESH`. The guide says embedded ACIS solids are unreadable by stock FreeCAD. Its C++ exporter emits selected straight edge linework from 3D faces, restricts curved edges to XY-parallel planes and may duplicate lines; its legacy exporter flattens 3D objects to 2D views. The DWG route is converter → DXF → selected importer. | Correct the native matrix: C++ documented subset, legacy `3DFACE`, `MESH=NOT_DOCUMENTED` until a pinned run establishes behavior, and stock ACIS `CONSUMER_NOT_APPLICABLE`. Do not use either exporter as a 3D solid writer oracle. Keep Linux/Windows platform, converter result, intermediate DXF, importer backend, and constructed object type as separate gates. |
| ezdxf 1.4.5 [ACIS API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html), [3DSOLID entity](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/3dsolid.html), and [drawing add-on limitations](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/addons/drawing.html) | ezdxf has ASCII/Binary DXF support and limited SAT/SAB load/export. Its documented carrier boundary is SAT for R2000–R2010 and SAB for R2013/R2018 (SAT 700 and SAB 21800 respectively). Unsupported ACIS records may load as `NONE_ENTITY` and lose data on export; converting bodies to meshes loses faces with curved boundaries. Its renderer does not render ACIS and projects 3D entities into the XY plane. | Use ezdxf as a pinned DXF tag/carrier comparator only for the exact supported profile. Record unsupported entity dispositions and raw payload hashes separately from any mesh projection; require curved-surface/topology analytic checks from a separately qualified kernel. Never promote a mesh export, 2D render, successful `load`, or same-library read/write cycle to complete B-rep semantics. |
| LibreDWG 0.13.4 [manual coverage overview](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/Overview.html) and [entity field reference](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/ENTITIES.html) | The manual exposes distinct 3DSOLID carrier, wireframe, silhouette, revision, and history fields, while its coverage chapter separately lists `MESH`, `BODY`, and multiple POLYLINE/VERTEX families as missing example-corpus test cases. A declared structure/format coverage percentage is therefore not a per-family tested-input denominator or a geometry-kernel result. | Treat LibreDWG as an optional DWG structural peer with per-revision/per-family decoded, skipped, errored, and sample-count denominators. For modeler rows, capture carrier, wireframe/silhouette, history, and ownership independently; do not treat struct fields or project-wide coverage claims as MESH/BODY corpus evidence or B-rep qualification. |
| ACadSharp open [3DSOLID/REGION writer report #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) and [writer branch #1150](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1150) | #1195 reports that ACadSharp 3.4.9 reads solid entities but its DXF writer silently omits them, including solid-only blocks. #1150 remains an open, undeployed branch. Its author reports manual AutoCAD DWG TrueView opening for selected DXF/DWG versions, but later comments record a schema-oriented redesign preference and that the post-refactor DXF reader retains only the last repeated group 310 line. These statements are branch-specific and not released behavior or independent semantic results. | Keep #1150 out of the comparator denominator until merged/released or pinned and explicitly tested. For libdxfrw, require output record+payload-chunk+owner disposition, transactional refusal for unsupported profile/data, and per-version consumer readback; a successful writer return or entity count is insufficient. No peer-only report changes local support status. |
| Current worktree source inspection: [`writeMesh`](src/libdxfrw.cpp) and [`writeModelerGeometry`](src/libdxfrw.cpp) | The current checkout has typed version-dependent MESH record emission with `AcDbSubDMesh`, and modeler output has explicit qualified SAT-v1 / AC1027 SAB gates plus refusal of unqualified carriers. This is source-level implementation evidence only; the shared worktree is dirty and no test or native app was run in this research pass. | Retain existing local implementation/test owners. At their already-planned fast gates, assert exact DXF record spelling/subclass/chunks and strict failure/no-publication for unsupported carriers. ### Readiness and self-unblocking refinement

1. Keep the matrix orthogonal: `DWG read`, `DXF read`, `DXF write`, `DWG write`,
   opaque carrier retention, graph/owner closure, tessellated projection,
   kernel semantics, and native application consumption each get their own

   fills none of these rows by itself.
2. Make stock-FreeCAD acceptance bounded to documented and observed behavior:

   complete-solid semantics.

## Deeper/broader ACIS reader independence and executable qualification routes (2026-10-19; research only)

This pass separates three questions that had been allowed to blur together:
whether a reader is separately implemented from libdxfrw, whether its shape
kernel is independent of FreeCAD/OCCT, and whether the application exposes
enough output to measure a result. It also rechecks the already-selected
official macOS ARM64 CAD Assistant route. This is a qualification-plan update,
not a support result.

| Source / route | Research result | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Open CASCADE [CAD Assistant product page](https://www.opencascade.com/products/cad-assistant/), [OCCT Components preview](https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT-Components), and [commercial-component announcement](https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/discussions/1157) | CAD Assistant imports SAT/SAB through an OCCT commercial XDE component; that component's import is available in the free app, but model export/conversion is disabled. The app can show part area, volume, and centroid. OCCT describes ACIS exchange as a commercial component, not part of the standard open-source OCCT distribution. This is a distinct ACIS reader relative to libdxfrw, but its resulting shape/kernel family is OCCT, shared with FreeCAD. Vendor release material points to CAD Assistant 1.6.0 (2021); the page explicitly lists macOS ARM64 under 1.5.0, so qualify the exact installed 1.6 package architecture/hash rather than inherit it from the older release. The existing local attempt on one exact SAB hash ended in a transfer error; its bundle also failed strict code-signature verification. That attempt is inconclusive and must not be repeated until package integrity is resolved. | Keep CAD Assistant as an optional, black-box ACIS-reader/OCCT-shape-properties lane, not a source-code peer or independent-kernel lane. Record exact app build, architecture, signed/notarized artifact identity, commercial-component route, input hash, import diagnostic, body count, and per-body properties. A transfer error is `INCONCLUSIVE`; integrity failure is `NOT_RUN/INVALID_ARTIFACT`, never a negative geometry verdict. No install, launch, trial, or license assumption is added to routine implementation. |
| [`cq-acis`](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis) and its [`acis-core` API](https://docs.rs/acis-core/latest/acis_core/) | The current project describes itself as experimental; it supports listed SAT saves 105/400/600/700 plus selected SAB/ASM profiles, retains unsupported source records, and converts supported geometry through CadQuery/OCCT. The `acis-core` model checks references/source ranges, explicitly does not construct OCCT solids, and is the shared model behind `cq-acis`; therefore these are not two independent parser votes. The project test corpus is excluded from Python distributions and has separate license notices. | Admit one pinned `cq-acis` parser/converter route only for its documented exact profile and only after source/tag, dependency/kernel versions, and lawful test-input provenance are captured. Do not use the excluded project corpus without separately checking its license. Score parser diagnostics, unsupported records, valid/closed shape, and analytic measures separately. Mark OCCT as shared with FreeCAD; do not label this an independent-kernel result. |
| [`cadmpeg-codec-sat` 0.6.1 documentation](https://docs.rs/crate/cadmpeg-codec-sat/0.6.1) and [project architecture](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) | The published crate describes a read-only bare SAT/SAB/SMT/SMB decoder, transfer into a neutral geometry/topology IR, and explicit decode-loss reporting; ACIS 217/218 are its verified Spatial ACIS bands. It does not read DWG/DXF containers or write SAT/SAB. Its IR/decoder is a candidate distinct parser lineage, not a native CAD kernel, and documentation or package-level coverage claims do not prove correctness on our producer/profile. | Use it as a second, independently pinned parser/neutral-geometry route only on the exact admitted 217/218 carrier. Capture crate/source/dependency hashes, profile admission, all `DecodeReport` losses/unknowns, body/topology counts, units/transforms, and analytic measures. A decode with blocking geometry loss or zero transferred geometry is not a semantic pass. Do not count it as a kernel-validity or ACDS-owner result. |
| Autodesk-generated source witness and existing local AC1027 plan | A standalone SAT/SAB parser only sees the extracted stream. It cannot prove which DWG entity owns it, whether an AcDs index/key resolves to that entity, or whether a writer preserved that join. The existing local witness plan already requires a source-native AutoCAD drawing, an asymmetric known-dimension solid, exact DWG/DXF/SAB hashes, and separate AcDs ownership evidence. | Preserve the full evidence chain as one-to-one identity data: DWG modeler handle/flag → AcDs section/schema/index/key → exact SAB hash → parser body/dispositions → independent expected bounds/area/volume → native consumer result. Require exact payload hash match before comparing readers. Record source generation and every extraction/translation separately. A parser pass on a loose SAB cannot close the DWG/ACDSDATA item. |

### Self-unblocking qualification sequence

1. Continue local parser/writer and graph-preservation slices without waiting
   for external software. The six external-only J items stay outside local
   acceptance and remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.
2. At the already-planned single composed checkpoint, first validate any
   candidate package/source identity and entitlement without executing it. If
   CAD Assistant's signature/integrity discrepancy remains, mark that route
   `NOT_RUN/INVALID_ARTIFACT` and immediately try the next pre-approved reader;
   do not retry the same damaged package.
3. Run one exact source-native, scratch-generated AC1027 witness through
   `cadmpeg-codec-sat` and one pinned `cq-acis` route, if their exact profiles
   admit its extracted carrier. Preserve the exact carrier hash and collect
   diagnostics, unsupported records, topology, units, transforms, bounds,
   area, and volume. Keep all generated DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB files outside the repo.
4. Treat agreement between `cq-acis` and FreeCAD as parser agreement plus a
   shared OCCT-kernel result, not two kernel votes. Treat CAD Assistant likewise
   as an OCCT-family geometry result. If independent-kernel evidence is
   required, use the already-listed BricsCAD/Ansys optional route only after
   license, exact version/profile admission, and output-measurement access are
   confirmed; generic ACIS support language is not exact SAB-profile proof.
5. Close the container/ACDS leg separately with exact DWG source/output
   identity and ODA/source-native schema/index/key evidence. If any external
   reader, license, platform, or output property is unavailable, record the
   precise missing predicate, leave that external row open, and continue the
   implementation queue. No new full-suite cadence or persistent fixture is
   required.

does not substitute for FreeCAD's platform gate.

The v1.5.1 release notes describe curve/linetype changes but do not bind a tagged README/manifest or package asset to the inspected mutable source. The inspected v1.5.0 README says the ODA-based DWG converter was removed; that must not be projected onto v1.5.1 without tagged-source/artifact verification. In the inspectable v1.5.0 scope, the documented entity set includes `3DFACE`, `SOLID`, `POLYLINE` (2D/3D), and `HATCH`, with optional 3DFACE-to-Blender-mesh merging; `MESH` is not listed and `3DSOLID` is planned. | Keep CAD2Cube as an existing optional candidate but mark its latest release `LATEST_RELEASE_SOURCE_UNBOUND`; the DWG capability of v1.5.1 is `NOT_QUALIFIED`, not inferred from repository metadata or mutable v1.5.0 prose. Do not count the route as an independent DXF parser: its inspected current manifest bundles ezdxf. Its output is a downstream mesh projection, not CAD source-record, owner-graph, or B-rep preservation. |

Autodesk's MESH table defines a different `AcDbSubDMesh` record with subdivision level, vertices, faces, edges, crease, and property-override fields; CAD2Cube does not document that `MESH` entity. | Keep `3DFACE`, classic `POLYLINE`/polyface, modern `MESH`, and ACIS-backed `3DSOLID` as distinct rows. If using CAD2Cube, first run with merge disabled for source-handle/entity disposition, then separately with merge enabled for mesh topology, units, transforms, bounds, and face counts. Never let its face-merging result satisfy MESH, 3DSOLID, AcDs, or B-rep rows. |
| FreeCAD's [current Draft DXF guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and ezdxf's [ACIS API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) | FreeCAD's documented importer sets differ, and stock FreeCAD documents no embedded ACIS-solid import; ezdxf is a bounded DXF/ACIS carrier tool, not a full ACIS geometry kernel. ## Deeper/broader cross-codec validation-harness and strict/recovery evidence audit (2026-10-19; primary-source review only)

This pass compared the evidence-producing workflows—not just codec feature
declarations—used by LibreDWG, ezdxf, ACadSharp, and the LibreCAD-bundled
libdxfrw inventory. It tightens the existing peer/fuzz qualification steps;
it does not add a codec feature or claim a peer defect reproduces locally.

| Primary source | Research result | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [HACKING/fuzz guidance](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/HACKING), [dedicated AFL++ setup](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg-fuzz), and closed [issue #1270](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1270) | The project documents separate fuzz modes for DWG, DXF, Binary DXF, round-trip and conversion entrypoints, plus crash/hang/leak separation and replay of old crashes. Issue #1270 describes a double-free in the `dwgfuzz` harness's `-rw`/`-indxf` modes, not in the library; its author attributes about 1,573 crashes to that harness bug. Although the issue is closed, the inspected issue page does not identify a fix commit or give a post-fix mode-by-mode verification, so current harness status is not inferred here. | Treat this as a historical harness-quality warning, not a libdxfrw finding and not evidence that LibreDWG's current harness is broken. At the existing optional fuzz checkpoint, bind the harness source commit and build options; smoke-test each selected mode with a known-good and locally generated bounded-negative input; verify clean setup/teardown under the selected sanitizer; and keep a harness-only crash class separate from parser/writer crashes. A long fuzz campaign remains optional and never runs on every implementation slice. Do not fetch or commit the issue's attached DWG. |
| ezdxf [recovery documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/recover.html) and [audit CLI contract](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/launcher.html) | ezdxf distinguishes the ordinary strict read path from `recover.readfile()`, which repairs flaws and returns an auditor that can still report unrecoverable errors. `recover.explore()` is expressly intended to inspect corrupted ASCII DXF and warns that data loss is likely. Its `audit` command may save a recovered output. | Capture strict-read disposition before any recovery attempt. Store recovery/audit diagnostics and repaired-output observations in separate fields; a repaired file that reopens is not a strict parse pass or original-content preservation result. Use raw structure browsing for diagnosis, not as semantic proof. This reinforces the existing strict-versus-recovery boundary; no new reader dependency is needed. |
| ACadSharp [reader notification example](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/docs/articles/samples/reading.md) and [version/direction matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) | Its reader API exposes warning/information notifications, and its public compatibility matrix separates DXF reader, DXF writer, DWG reader, and DWG writer by AC version; the matrix itself remains a declaration rather than a run result. | Any future peer comparison records notifications alongside exit/status and per-handle dispositions, and pins the exact release or commit separately for each operation. Missing notifications, a clean process exit, or a matrix checkmark cannot substitute for identity/field/owner comparisons and independent readback. |
| LibreCAD [coverage inventory](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD/blob/master/libraries/libdxfrw/DWG_DXF_COVERAGE_INVENTORY.md) and [DWG version status inventory](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD/blob/master/libraries/libdxfrw/DWG_VERSION_SUPPORT_STATUS.md) | The inventories label themselves deterministic source inventories/static readiness matrices, distinguish dispatch from validated shells, and leave version rows fixture-blocked where positive/negative evidence is absent. They are in LibreCAD's bundled libdxfrw lineage, not independent codec votes. | Reuse the plan's per-direction/per-version evidence denominator and keep these inventories as local process/design precedents only. Do not count the bundled fork as an independent parser or turn a static registry/API row into runtime support. |

### Implementation-ready qualification refinement

1. Keep the fast local sequence unchanged: the owning generated selector,
   focused target build, and owning CTest after each touched slice. Do not add
   fuzzing, peer installations, recovery mode, or full suites to the ordinary
   slice loop.
2. At the existing composed checkpoint, run only the peer mode that answers a
   named question. Record repository URL, immutable source/artifact identity,
   version, direction, target format, command/options, input hash, strict
   result, diagnostics/notifications, and explicit per-source identity
   dispositions. Run recovery only after strict output has been captured and
   label repaired output separately.
3. Before a selected fuzz mode is trusted, validate the harness with a
   known-good seed and a locally generated negative control, then replay any
   finding in the smallest library-facing mode available. Preserve the
   sanitizer report and minimized input outside the repository unless the
   input was already in an admitted in-repository corpus or was created from
   scratch locally. If the harness itself fails its smoke test, mark that
   mode `INVALID_HARNESS/NOT_RUN`, use deterministic local generated tests,

4. Keep all comparisons direction-specific: parse, write, same-codec
   readback, recovery, projection/render, native open/audit, and semantic
   geometry are separate outcomes. Do not count same-lineage forks or

5. This research requires no external fixture, persistent test input,

   execution, implementation-order change, or support promotion. The six
