## Deeper/broader nested-INSERT consumer scaling and peer-test denominator audit (2026-10-19; research only)

This pass followed a fresh open-source CAD consumer report from file parsing
through block expansion and compared the reported evidence with libdxfrw's
adapter contract, the existing generated block-owner tests, and peer test-data
disclosures. It is a downstream resource/evidence-boundary update, not a new
format defect. No external drawing, peer binary, CAD application, or kernel was
run; no local code or test was changed.

| Evidence | Research result and limit | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCADStudio open [issue #1698](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/issues/1698) and maintainer-reported fixes [`29c0d1d`](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/commit/29c0d1d) / [`df22824`](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/commit/df22824) | The reporter says the AC1032 DWG parsed in about 1.9 seconds, but eager rendering expansion of 12,012 model-space INSERTs and nested definitions reached 6,128,569 primitives and about 8.94 GiB before allocation failure. The customer drawing is unavailable. ## Implementation progress — PAR-136/7AR ASCII DXF semantic control strings (2026-10-19; generated fast slices, uncommitted)

Implemented the semantic ASCII-DXF caret convention at the typed text/codepage
boundary. The writer emits `^ ` for a literal caret, `^` plus the standard
ASCII control letter for C0 controls (except refused NUL and the existing
CR/LF policy), and `^?` for DEL. The reader reverses recognized spellings only
for semantic ASCII values and inside the selected converter's ASCII branch;
legacy DBCS lead/trail decoding therefore remains authoritative. `^@` is kept
visible and records an unrepresented-escape observation rather than injecting
an embedded NUL. Unknown caret text is preserved.

The shared `writeUtf8String`/chunk paths apply the transformation once. The
uppercase-symbol shortcut now bypasses it only when there is no caret/control
to encode. Raw-string access/replay and Binary DXF are unchanged. The typed
XDATA encoded-length and round-trip preflight now accounts for ASCII caret
expansion; the bounded GeoData text-size check uses the encoded size too.

Generated controls cover AC1018 and AC1021, both compatibility and strict
writer policies, group 1 and XDATA 1000, BEL/ESC/tab/US/DEL, literal and
adjacent carets, raw spelling/getters, unknown and NUL spellings, DBCS trail
bytes, following LINE/EOF framing, ASCII/Binary MTEXT group-3 boundaries, and
public TEXT/XDATA/ATTRIB/ATTDEF round trips. A 255-byte XDATA case verifies
that caret expansion is rejected before replacing the destination. All files
are generated in memory or temporary directories; no persistent fixture or
CTest registration was added.

Focused verification passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests lc3_compat_check --parallel 4`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_gbk_codepage_tests --target-text-transport` — pass (56 table-driven wire cases plus raw, DBCS, Binary-DXF, MTEXT chunk, public consumer, and preflight controls)
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_gbk_codepage$' --output-on-failure` — pass (1/1)
- Scoped `git diff --check` for the touched source and test files

This proves local codec self-consistency and transaction/preflight behavior,
not AutoCAD acceptance, other CAD reader behavior, C1-byte semantics, or a
general DXF support claim. No full suite, peer runtime, native CAD application,
or kernel was run. Counts remain 136 findings / 77 top-level subplans; J256,
J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.
The shared worktree remains broadly dirty and uncommitted.

### PAR-137 — generated/no-chunk SAT caret escape symmetry (implementation-ready refinement)

**Owner:** existing PAR-07/S8 modeler text-carrier branch. **Status:** the local writer/reader asymmetry is fixed and public-path reproduction passes; external/native acceptance and ACIS geometry semantics remain unqualified. This does not claim that every SAT payload is valid, that a native CAD application accepts the record, or that ACIS geometry is semantically supported.

1. Extend `runModelerDxfWriterMatrix` with generated AC1018 and AC1024 ASCII and Binary DXF cases. Construct `DRW_ModelerGeometry` with a valid text payload containing a literal caret followed by a space and no `m_dxfPayloadChunks`. Add an exact payload assertion in the same slice as the fix; verify the raw source object remains unchanged and a following entity plus EOF is aligned.
2. Make the no-chunk fallback use the SAT-specific escape atom and bounded chunking behavior already used for explicit chunk maps. Preflight the complete payload before record publication; preserve the 255-character DXF group limit, keep `^ ` pairs indivisible across group-1/3 boundaries, and propagate refusal transactionally. Do not route SAT bytes through `writeUtf8String` or the PAR-136 semantic codec.
3. Add boundary controls with the caret pair at the final two positions of a group and at the 254/255-byte split. Re-import and re-export once, comparing ordered group codes/values and exact payload reconstruction. Keep the existing explicit-chunk and qualified AC1015 SAT-v1 controls as regression coverage; use the direct matrix selector as the sole public round-trip run for this leaf, not the unfiltered local-roundtrip executable.
4. Add a SURFACE raw-payload negative control (ASCII and Binary) so its existing exact raw path remains untouched. Keep CR/LF/NUL refusal and unsupported-carrier transaction behavior unchanged; if empty-map inputs contain line breaks or another unsupported form, test fail-closed behavior rather than silently emitting partial tags.

Validate the touched strict target and run `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip --modeler-dxf-matrix` directly, plus scoped `git diff --check`; run `--dxf-modeler-text-chunk-borrow` only if the shared chunk-boundary primitive changes. Do not add a CTest registration. Run the broader owning `libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip` CTest at its existing validation cadence, not as an added per-slice full-suite prerequisite; run `lc3_compat_check` only if the public surface/layout changes. No external sample, native app, peer runtime, or kernel is a prerequisite. At the existing composed checkpoint, record any external strict-read/native result separately from this local carrier round trip.

### Implementation progress — PAR-137 synthesized SAT caret-escape symmetry (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The first local slice closes the identified writer/reader mismatch without
changing the public model or applying the semantic-string codec to opaque
carriers. `writeDxfSatTextPayloadChunks` preflights the complete payload and
uses `writeDxfSatTextValue` both when parsed chunk metadata exists and when the
payload is synthesized with an empty chunk map. Literal carets are encoded as
an indivisible two-character atom before 255-character groups are emitted.
The representability preflight rejects NUL, non-ASCII bytes, and ASCII-DXF
line breaks before the modeler record is published; Binary DXF retains its
ability to carry CR/LF bytes.

Generated public-writer/import tests cover AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, and AC1024
in ASCII and Binary modes. They exercise no-chunk caret-space payloads,
caret-pair placement at and across the 255-byte boundary, unchanged source
payloads, ordered group-1/3 chunk ranges, exact reconstruction from those
ranges, import/re-export stability, and a following LINE followed by EOF.
Binary cases additionally carry embedded CR/LF. ASCII line-break rejection is
checked against a pre-existing destination sentinel. A raw SURFACE caret
payload is a negative control in both encodings.

The first matrix assertion compared `m_rawBytes` directly with source bytes
and exposed an existing parser convention: after the final group-1/3 value,
`DRW_ModelerGeometry::parseCode` appends one terminal LF to this raw carrier.
The final check therefore expects that framing LF in `m_rawBytes`, while
requiring the parser's ordered `m_dxfPayloadChunks` ranges to reconstruct the
exact original SAT payload without it. This is a carrier/framing distinction,
not loss of payload data.

**Validation:** `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip
--parallel 4` passed with the project's strict warnings; direct selector
`build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip --modeler-dxf-matrix` passed; the
already-built hardening target's
`build-gcc/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --dxf-modeler-text-chunk-borrow` passed;
and scoped `git diff --check` passed. No full suite or owning CTest was run,
consistent with the plan's lower-frequency cadence. No CTest registration,
fixture, dependency, public API/layout change, peer/native execution, commit,
or support-claim promotion was made. The shared worktree was already broadly
modified; unrelated changes were preserved. J256/J260/J268/J284/J293/J295
remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

## Deeper/broader LAYOUT viewport-list and last-active audit (2026-10-19; research/readiness update)

This pass reconciles the normative DWG/DXF field contracts with current
independent open-source implementation work, then traces those fields into
the local parser, writer, adapter, and test owners. A bounded same-cursor bit
probe across three existing AC1024 files now confirms that the observed
R2010-profile count is decoded as BL: BL lands on the object-body boundary,
while interpreting the same bits as raw RL yields implausible counts and
crosses that boundary. LibreDWG and ACadSharp master both implement the count
as a bit-long; ACadSharp's inline comment nevertheless says RL, matching the
ODA v5.4.1 table. This narrows the implementation decision for the observed
profile but does not establish an ODA erratum or every producer/version
profile. A local two-handle structural vector now covers the generated writer
and reader route. No native CAD application, downloaded drawing, new fixture,
or production-code change was used in this research pass.

| Evidence | Cross-check and limits | Plan update |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ODA DWG specification v5.4.1 §20.4.84 and Autodesk [LAYOUT DXF group-code reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-433D25BF-655D-4697-834E-C666EDFD956D.htm) | ODA specifies the R2004+ LAYOUT viewport count as `RL`; §2 defines `RL` as raw long, not bit-long. It then specifies that many repeated viewport handles. The common handle sequence separately includes 331 as last-active viewport. Autodesk describes DXF 331 as the viewport last active when that layout was current. Neither contract says to replace the list with 331, or makes 331 equivalent to current interactive editor state. ODA specifies repetition/count but does not assign semantic meaning to list ordering such as “overall viewport.” | Preserve and assert `viewportCount`, ordered `viewportHandles`, and `lastActiveViewportHandle` as separate values. Treat the normative `RL` label as unresolved against the observed bytes and convergent peer code; do not claim an ODA correction. Do not infer “overall” or native pane restoration from vector position. |
| OpenCADStudio [issue #1670](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/issues/1670) with maintainer-linked [application change](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/commit/2c329b2) and [codec change](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/opencadcodec/commit/d57097c) | The current peer report separates a stored last-active link from live active viewport/UCS context. Its maintainer says the codec had treated that link as the overall viewport and changed that derivation to use the layout viewport list. This is valuable route-specific evidence, but the report, implementation, and tests are peer-authored; they do not establish a libdxfrw defect or independent native-format acceptance. | Retain the separate existing qualification lanes: typed link closure, DWG list interpretation, DXF VIEWPORT status/ID and UCS values, and native save-close-reopen behavior. Do not turn peer implementation behavior into a normative list-order rule. |
| ACadSharp merged [layout/viewport refactor #1024](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1024) and [ActiveStatus change #1068](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1068) | The peer work adds a Layout `LastActiveViewport` mapping, ensures paper layouts retain a paper viewport, expands layout tests, and handles DXF VIEWPORT code 68 separately. This corroborates that layout link, paper viewport, and status projection are separate implementation concerns. It is not an independent conformance oracle; peer issue #1023/#1068 discussion also documents writer/default pitfalls. | Keep paper-canvas/overall-viewport behavior separate from last-active link handling. Use this only to shape locally generated controls and optional pinned peer probes, never as expected-value authority. |
| Independent open-source reader implementations: LibreDWG [`src/dwg.spec`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/master/src/dwg.spec) and ACadSharp [`DwgObjectReader.readLayout`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/master/src/ACadSharp/IO/DWG/DwgStreamReaders/DwgObjectReader.cs) | Current LibreDWG master uses `FIELD_BL(num_viewports)` with a 10,000 bound, then reads the repeated viewport handles. ACadSharp master calls `ReadBitLong()` and uses the result to read the repeated handles, although its adjacent comment calls the field `RL`. These are separate codebases and agree on the implementation primitive, but their specs/comments are not independent normative authority and may share lineage. | Record this as convergent implementation evidence only. It raises confidence that the `RL` label is a documentation/notation discrepancy for the observed layout profile, but neither peer implementation nor comments can amend the ODA specification. |
| Local source and same-cursor sample trace: `DRW_Layout::parseDwg` / writer in `src/drw_objects.cpp`; `testLayoutVectors` in `tests/dwg_object_vectors_tests.cpp`; generated DWG route in `tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp`; adapter controls in `tests/dxf_fixture_tests.cpp`; local AC1024 samples | Three existing AC1024 files were hashed and probed at the same count-field cursor. `architectural_example-imperial.dwg` (`52d14a7b…34cce7`) has Model `RL=17857956` vs `BL=0`, and Layout1 `RL=276669504` vs `BL=2`; `title_block-iso.dwg` (`b874d82c…f793bc2`) has Model `RL=28847524` vs `BL=0`, and Architectural Title Block `RL=3089982528` vs `BL=1`; `visualization_-_conference_room.dwg` (`0579e4b5…0132c4`) has Model/Layout1/Layout2 `BL=0`, while each same-cursor raw `RL` is `20451748`. In the architectural sample, Layout1's parsed list is exactly `{0x28B, 0x290}`, its body cursor equals the declared body end (2393/2393 bits), and the handle cursor ends four bits before its frame boundary (3812/3816). LibreDWG 0.14 JSON independently reports the same two Layout1 handles. The strict local conversion still exits nonzero later because the read disposition is incomplete (unsupported associative-dimension dependency classes); this trace is not a successful full-conversion result. | The observed AC1024 samples now resolve the implementation gate for the current BL path; the ODA `RL` discrepancy remains documented, not corrected. Preserve the existing production reader/writer representation unless new version-specific sample evidence or an authoritative ODA correction requires a change. This proves structural read/write coverage, not complete target closure or viewport/editor semantics. |

## Deeper/broader open-source comparator route applicability and operation-specific coverage (2026-10-19; research only)

This review widened the peer set from codec declarations to the concrete
operations through which common open-source consumers expose DWG/DXF. The
comparison reconciles current primary documentation and source/issue evidence
with the existing PAR-07/S8 evidence rules. It produces a small readiness
refinement, not a new libdxfrw defect: several routes are intentionally
projections/import subsets, so a missing result can be either an expected
consumer exclusion or a real parser/adapter loss depending on the selected
operation. No peer binary, FreeCAD installation, or native CAD application was
run; no external drawing was downloaded.

| Project and source | Route-specific result | Plan consequence |

| ACadSharp [feature/version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) and [issue #1131](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1131) | The public matrix separates DXF read, DXF write, DWG read, and DWG write by AC version; for example, its current declaration omits AC1021 DWG writing. Its custom-object issue also reports a case where notifications described unknown entities that did not reach the final document. These are declaration and issue evidence, not a run of a pinned artifact or proof of a libdxfrw failure. | Keep exact artifact, direction, requested/actual version, final membership, and per-handle dispositions in the peer manifest. A matrix checkmark, warning, or entity total is not proof of delivered semantics. This reinforces the already specified delivery ledger; it does not create a second codec implementation lane. |
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF importer/exporter documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md), [import/export preferences](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Import_Export_Preferences.md), and [DWG route](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md) | Stock DWG import converts DWG to DXF first and then invokes the selected importer. FreeCAD documents separate C++ and legacy Python DXF importers, both starting at R12; their entity lists differ: the documented legacy list includes 3DFACE, while the C++ list does not, and the C++ block path skips text, dimensions, and attributes. The documentation says embedded ACIS/SAT solids are not read by the stock importer. | A FreeCAD qualification row must pin converter, platform/build, importer mode, preferences, and input/output version. State the intended 2D consumer profile and mark unsupported families `OUT_OF_PROFILE` before running; do not fail the libdxfrw route for an expected FreeCAD exclusion or claim 3D-solid support from successful explicit-entity import. Keep Linux and Windows results separate. |
| GDAL [DXF driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) and its [known-issues ledger](https://github.com/OSGeo/gdal/blob/master/ogr/ogrsf_frmts/dxf/KNOWN_ISSUES.md) | OGR explicitly omits several entity families (including MESH, MPOLYGON, RAY, TABLE, TOLERANCE, and XLINE) and documents missing 3D/OCS behavior for dimension, leader, and multileader projection, along with styling/projection limitations for HATCH, MLINE, WIPEOUT, text, and 3DFACE. | Admit GDAL only for named supported projection fields/geometry. For unsupported or transformed families, mark the comparator cell `NOT_APPLICABLE`; never treat its OGR feature count or absent geometry as a parser-level pass/fail, raw preservation result, or native CAD oracle. |
| ezdxf [supported-version/scope documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/introduction.html), [XREF import documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/xref.html), and [recovery documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/recover.html) | ezdxf documents structured ASCII/Binary DXF read/write and retention of third-party content, but its XREF/import operation deliberately supports a smaller copyable/transformable subset and ignores unknown/proxy objects and several document features. Its recovery path repairs structurally flawed files and can still report unrecoverable data. | Record `STRUCTURAL_READ_WRITE`, `XREF_IMPORT`, `STRICT_READ`, and `RECOVERY` as distinct operations. Test opaque retention only through a read/write route that claims it; do not infer it from selective XREF import, and do not count a repaired output as strict input preservation. |
| LibreDWG [README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) and current [ACDS issue #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411) | The README's DWG write claim is direction/version-limited (writing is documented only through earlier versions and rewriting most files through R2004 is described as usually working). #1411 reports a specific LibreDWG 0.14.8593 build preserving modern solid entity shells while losing R2013+ AcDs SAB payload in a scratch-generated and a private-file scenario. The issue is a build-specific report, not a universal statement about current LibreDWG. | Keep DWG read, DWG write, DXF conversion, entity-shell publication, and AcDs payload preservation separate. Reuse the existing AcDs carrier/owner gates; do not turn a peer issue into a claim about all LibreDWG releases or a local defect without an exact local reproduction. |

An OCCT-based application or shared OCCT kernel therefore does not imply an available open-source ACIS reader. | Preserve the existing parser/kernel provenance split. Treat any commercial component as an optional, explicitly licensed route with exact edition/build; it cannot be described as an open-source parser or independent kernel result. |

### PAR-07/S8 route-applicability manifest refinement

At the existing composed comparison checkpoint, add one small manifest row
per selected tool operation—not one row per test case—with these fields:

1. **Artifact and route:** project/repository, immutable source or release,
   binary/package identity, OS/architecture, build options, and any converter
   or dependency between the source file and the consumer.
2. **Operation:** exact direction and mode (for example DWG→DXF conversion,
   strict DXF read, recovery read, XREF import, OGR projection, or native
   open/audit), requested and actual format version, and relevant options.
3. **Applicability:** intended entity/object families, expected container,
   owner and transform behavior, explicitly unsupported families, and any
   deliberate projection or repair. Set exclusions before the run; label them
   `OUT_OF_PROFILE` or `NOT_APPLICABLE`, not silently skipped.
4. **Observed disposition:** exit/result and diagnostics, then use the existing
   per-handle ledger for source identity → callback/opaque/skip/error → final
   destination membership. Preserve strict input, recovered output,
   same-codec readback, independent parse, and semantic geometry as separate
   evidence columns.
5. **Claim boundary:** state whether the result is syntax, structural
   preservation, 2D projection, native acceptance, or independent geometry
   semantics. Shared parser/kernel lineage and unrun modes must be explicit.

Do not broaden the per-slice validation loop. Implementation slices still use

fixtures or dependencies. If an expected consumer route is unavailable, mark
`NOT_RUN` and continue the local implementation queue.

Its own docs distinguish the raw and high-level APIs, a small modern native entity-decoder cohort, ezdxf-backed DWG→DXF export, and a native AC1015-only DWG writer subset. | If a direct DWG field question remains and artifact provenance is resolved, prefer this one route over running several similar peers. Current source/package mismatch remains a preflight blocker where unreconciled. |

Its unknown tag-storage entity is deliberately not generally copyable or transformable; preservation is not equivalent to semantic editing/import support. | Select for strict DXF syntax or named-field/opaque-tag read-write checks. LibreCAD_3 is a downstream libdxfrw consumer with an explicitly read-only, opt-in DWG policy. | Keep the existing separate FreeCAD Linux/Windows composed qualification and LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3 source-compatibility lanes. Neither is a second DWG parser implementation; FreeCAD's unsupported 3D cohort must be marked out-of-profile rather than counted as a libdxfrw conversion loss. |

### Fast comparator selection for existing plan owners

At an already scheduled composed checkpoint, select at most one optional
external route for a concrete unresolved question:

1. DWG section/container framing or object census: use the existing local ODA
   spec and generated controls first; if a peer observation is still needed,
   choose one exact-pinned DWG reader (LibreDWG or `dwg-rs`) and record its
   decode/skip/error disposition.
2. A named common 2D DWG field or placement: choose one source-distinct reader
   whose exact artifact/version covers the entity (`ACadSharp` or `ezdwg`).
   Do not add OpenCADStudio/CADCraft wrappers as additional parser votes.
3. DXF record syntax or unknown-group retention: use strict `ezdxf` parsing;
   use GDAL only when the expected result is explicitly an OGR geometry or
   projected field.
4. ACIS/AcDs: establish local owner/key/payload closure before any kernel.
   Then use one profile-matched standalone ACIS route for parser/shape
   evidence. No standalone SAT/SAB parser can validate the DWG AcDs join or
   stock FreeCAD's converter/importer behavior.
5. Native consumer claims: run only the specified consumer path at the
   composed checkpoint, recording process exit, exact intermediate file,
   selected importer, platform, and per-source disposition. Do not add a
   consumer smoke to every implementation slice.

For every route, resolve immutable source and executable/package identity,
version, platform, build features, input provenance/hash, and exact operation
before execution. If any required identity cannot be matched cheaply, mark
`NOT_RUN / UNBOUND` and continue the local implementation queue. Prefer a
scratch-generated in-memory case or an already-admitted repository sample; do
not add externally sourced/customer DWG/DXF fixtures. Peer issue bodies and
capability matrices prioritize questions but do not establish local defects,
support promotion, or closure of J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, or J295.

This is a consolidation/refinement of existing PAR-07/S8 and peer-lineage
owners, not a new finding or top-level subplan. It changes no local code,

ordering; no support claim is promoted. Findings/top-level subplans remain

`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

### PAR-20/7G.3f.4b.2 — implementation-ready MATERIAL sequence

Keep this as one existing leaf. The recommended order is deliberately short and
keeps the DXF-origin path independently useful while avoiding an incomplete
DWG-to-DXF material projection:

1. **Retain the existing callback (DXF only).** `dxfRW::processMaterial()`
   already captures ordered raw groups alongside the typed
   name/description projection and calls both interface callbacks at the same
   object boundary. Add adapter storage for the raw callback and a
   generation-bound receipt requiring one raw/typed match per handle and
   owner. Preserve duplicate codes, order, values, subclass boundaries,
   source version, and ASCII raw spellings. Reuse the reader's existing
   retained-byte and typed-node budgets; do not modify the parser, reparse the
   file, or duplicate a callback.
2. **Close the resource graph.** Emit exactly one `ACAD_MATERIAL` NOD entry
   for the admitted material dictionary, emit each MATERIAL with a valid
   group-330 owner, and require every non-default entity group-347 target to
   resolve to exactly one emitted material after handle remapping. Reject
   missing, duplicate, ambiguous, or unsupported owner/edge cases before
   destination publication. Reuse the established dictionary and output
   transaction helpers; never output both typed and raw copies of one handle.
3. **Replay complete DXF payload.** For DXF-origin records, serialize the
   retained ordered fields, rewriting only the common handle/owner identity
   fields through the known remapper. Keep repeated map codes in their original
   order. Fail closed if the selected writer version cannot represent the
   captured profile or if any handle-bearing field lacks a classified remap
   role. For DWG-origin materials, do not use the opaque DWG body tail as a DXF
   payload; defer cross-format visual fields until their versioned DWG layout
   is read against ODA and grounded in real/local authorized samples.
4. **Test one closure, not a new corpus.** Extend the existing
   `tests/dxf_fixture_tests.cpp` owner with scratch-generated ASCII and Binary
   DXF containing one root dictionary, one material with contextual repeated
   groups/matrix values, and one entity referencing it. Assert exact ordered
   payload, NOD/owner closure, handle remap, and re-import identity. Add
   negative missing/duplicate-target cases that preserve a sentinel output,
   plus same-adapter corrected retry if the existing harness pattern applies.
   Do not commit any external test drawing; generated data is built from
   scratch in temporary storage.

**Validation budget:** use the existing strict build target, direct focused
selector, and the owning `libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures` CTest at the slice boundary.
Avoid the unfiltered suite at each slice; use the plan's normal full-suite
checkpoint. An ezdxf differential is optional once, at the existing composed
checkpoint, and must pin executable/version plus input/output hashes. Native
material rendering is a later consumer result, not a prerequisite for the
local record-preservation slices.

This review confirms one existing source-level gap but no new finding or
top-level subplan. It changes neither implementation priority beyond making
the current MATERIAL leaf executable in ordered slices, nor the six external
qualification dispositions. No production/test code changed; no local build,

## Deeper/broader ACAD_TABLE R2010+ placement-wire conflict and resolution gate (2026-10-19; research only)

This follow-up supersedes the 2026-10-17 title-only review of LibreDWG #1425. The full issue body and current LibreDWG decoder specification are now available, and they disagree about the R2010+ ACAD_TABLE wire prefix. The existing local AC1024 vector is authored in the same layout as the local parser, so it cannot resolve this disagreement. The result is a bounded `OPEN_SPEC_RECONCILIATION` gate under existing 7G.3d/PAR-126, not a new defect declaration.

| Primary source / local path | Evidence and limits | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ODA v5.4.1 [Open Design Specification](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf), §§20.4.96.1–20.4.96.2, pp. 229–237 | §20.4.96 says ACAD_TABLE inherits INSERT. §20.4.96.1 explicitly lists insertion point, the four R2000+ scale encodings, rotation, extrusion, and the ATTRIB-presence bit before the pre-R24 table payload. §20.4.96.2 starts with an ellipsis described as “Common entity data,” then lists R2010+ RC/H/BL fields, the R2010 B and R2013 BL fields, inline TABLECONTENT, and later table data; it does not restate the INSERT placement fields as explicit R24 rows. The inheritance statement and the omission do not, by themselves, settle whether those inherited fields physically precede the R24-specific fields in each version. | Keep ODA as the byte-layout authority, but record this exact R24 field-order ambiguity rather than claiming that the table's general inheritance sentence explicitly specifies the R24 byte prefix. No production change until a real sample trace can be reconciled with the spec text. |
| LibreDWG [issue #1425](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1425), open at review time | The reporter describes the repository test files `example_2010.dwg`, `example_2013.dwg`, and `example_2018.dwg` with paired DXFs. For TABLE handle `4F2` in `example_2018.dwg`, the reported `unknown_bits` begin after common entity data and decode at offset zero as insertion point `(3298.7947769117454, 839.6133480853896, 0)`, scale flag `11` (unit XYZ), zero rotation, and default extrusion; the point agrees with DXF group 10 to printed precision. The report says the same offset/values occur in 2010 and 2013 examples. It does not decode past extrusion, identify the TABLE-to-`*T` BLOCK_HEADER handle from its handle stream, or provide an independently rerun/native result; the author says *T pairing used handle order. The DWG/DXF files were not downloaded or hash-pinned in this pass. | Treat this as a concrete sample-trace lead, substantially stronger than the formerly available issue title, but still a reporter-authored observation rather than a verified local decode or normative rule. Verify file magic, hashes, table identity, all references, and literal bit offsets before relying on it. Never use “next unreferenced *T block by handle order” as a graph rule. |
| LibreDWG [current `dwg2.spec` TABLE implementation](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dwg2.spec#L457-L481), mutable `master` as fetched 2026-10-19 | Its R2010+ branch begins with RC, a table-style handle, BL, version-gated B/BL fields, then TABLECONTENT fields; it does not decode the reported INSERT placement prefix there. The pre-R2010 branch does explicitly decode an `AcDbBlockReference` subclass with insertion, scale, rotation, and extrusion. This is a meaningful source disagreement but not independent validation of either branch: the issue itself proposes extending this decoder, and the fetched master SHA was not resolved. | Pin a commit before using the implementation as a comparison result. For now record the branch as the competing parser hypothesis, not as proof that the sample report is wrong. Do not import its field order or class maturity labels into libdxfrw. |
| Local [`DRW_Table::parseDwg`](src/drw_entities.cpp), [`testR2010EmbeddedTableContentVector`](tests/dwg_object_vectors_tests.cpp), and [placement-prefix fast-slice receipt](docs/research/table-placement-prefix-fast-slice-2026-10-17.json) | The local parser reads insertion point, scale flag/data, rotation, extrusion, and attribute presence before the AC1024+ table-specific prefix. The generated AC1024 frame is built with that same assumed order and verifies decoded values, handles, content, and cursor position. This proves regression consistency for the selected local layout; it is not independent producer evidence. A diagnostic read of local `tests/samples/AC1024/title_block-iso.dwg` returned AC1024 and no parser-failure counts, but its full CLI export stopped at strict-complete disposition and the trace had no ACAD_TABLE parse marker, so it is not a positive TABLE witness. | Keep the existing four-mode tests, but constrain their claim to local generated parser/vector behavior. Add the captured producer-derived prefix only after independent byte offsets and references are established; retain AC1021 coverage separately. No acceptance, TABLE completeness, or 2D/3D support claim follows from the current generated R24 vector. |
| Other open-source routes already screened: ACadSharp [#1264](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1264), ezdxf [XREF/import scope](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst), and GDAL [DXF driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | ACadSharp #1264 concerns TABLECONTENT block-cell value representation, not the R24 entity prefix. ezdxf's documented XREF operation does not support typed ACAD_TABLE import, and GDAL is an OGR projection rather than a DWG TABLE parser. None resolves the R2010+ DWG placement bytes. | Do not add these routes as substitute evidence. Use them only for their existing, distinct TABLE/DXF projection questions. |

### 7G.3d / PAR-126 — sample-first, fast resolution sequence

1. **Bind the source material in scratch.** Use the public LibreDWG repository sample pair named by #1425 (or an already-admitted local producer sample if one is found). Record repository commit, each file's SHA-256 and first-six-byte AC code, sample license/provenance, and the exact ACAD_TABLE handle. Keep downloaded source files outside this repository; do not add them as committed fixtures.
2. **Trace one record end-to-end.** Compare the raw entity data after common entity data against the reported INSERT field sequence; independently decode bit-coded doubles and scale modes. Match insertion, scale, rotation and extrusion to the same handle's DXF groups 10/41–43/50/210. Resolve the table-style handle, owner/block-record, TABLECONTENT boundary, handle-stream entries, and actual `*T` BLOCK_HEADER reference from explicit identity edges. Do not infer table-to-block membership from handle ordering.
3. **Use cross-version discriminators before changing production.** At minimum inspect one sample each for AC1024/R2010, AC1027/R2013 and AC1032/R2018. Capture the bit offset and exact cursor/body end before and after the candidate prefix and R24 fields. If the prefix exists in all three, document how that observation maps to ODA's inheritance and “Common entity data” wording; if it varies, add explicit version/profile gates only where the bytes prove them. Do not use a dual-parser/heuristic fallback that accepts whichever branch yields plausible numbers.
4. **Turn the observation into small generated tests.** Extend the existing `dwg_object_vectors_tests` builders with a locally authored-from-scratch vector whose field order and expected values come from the hash-pinned trace, plus a discriminating no-prefix or wrong-version negative where valid. Retain the AC1021 vector and the existing four scale modes. Assert literal field values, exact body cursor, owner/style/block identities, following sentinel, and callback delivery. No downloaded DWG/DXF is committed and no new CTest registration is needed.
5. **Keep validation fast.** For a production change, build only `libdxfrw_dwg_object_vectors_tests`, run the direct TABLE selector and its owning `libdxfrw_dwg_object_vectors` CTest, then scoped `git diff --check`; run `lc3_compat_check` only if public data/API changes. Do not add peer-runtime or native-CAD runs to the implementation slice. Defer a pinned peer comparison and native placement/render check to the existing composed checkpoint.

Until steps 1–3 resolve the actual bytes, mark AC1024+ INSERT placement as **implementation pending independent wire trace**. Preserve current code and tests as existing local behavior; the trigger does not justify a production parser edit. This adds no finding or top-level subplan, changes no queue/cadence, adds no fixture/dependency/registration, and promotes no feature claim. Totals remain **137 findings / 77 top-level subplans**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

output route. Before output publication the adapter requires one successful,

handle-aware raw-object writer. ACAD_MATERIAL root targets are remapped before

## Implementation progress — PAR-20/7G.3f.4b.2 model-document view-style resource closure (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The previous capture slice is now followed by a separate resource-target gate.
`dx_data::hasClosedModelDocViewStyleResourceReferences()` checks every
non-null reference in the typed DETAILVIEWSTYLE and SECTIONVIEWSTYLE records
against the adapter's LTYPE, STYLE, and BLOCK_RECORD target collections. A
target must occur once across those three expected table-entry families and
cannot resolve through a wrong family; zero-valued optional references remain
allowed. This is deliberately not a global object-handle census, dictionary
root proof, output remap proof, field-completeness proof, or writer receipt.

The `fileExport()` preflight now requires a valid one-generation capture and
closed resource references, then refuses these records before opening or
publishing output because there is still no qualified style serializer. Thus
the new closure gate cannot be mistaken for output support, and the adapter no
longer silently drops a captured style on export.

Primary schema cross-check: Autodesk's [`DetailViewStyle` properties](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-__MEMBERTYPE_Properties_Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_DetailViewStyle.html)
and [`SectionViewStyle` properties](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-__MEMBERTYPE_Properties_Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_SectionViewStyle.html)
classify identifier and label styles as text-style table records, arrow
symbols as block table records, and the view/section line types as linetype
records. Autodesk's [DXF group-code reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3F0380A5-1C15-464D-BC66-2C5F094BCFB9.htm)
classifies 340–349 as hard-pointer handles. These API-level role definitions
support the DXF reference-family mapping only; they do not qualify the DWG
binary field layout or any style writer.

The existing generated ASCII/Binary selector now parses concrete 340 edges
and LTYPE/STYLE/BLOCK_RECORD table targets. It verifies all six detail and
six section-style reference roles, rejects a missing target, a handle resolving
to the wrong target family, and a duplicated target, and checks that a broken
reference reaches the export preflight and preserves an existing destination.
It also confirms that even a closed valid graph is refused because no
serializer exists. Inputs remain scratch-authored and temporary; no fixture or
CTest registration was added.

Focused validation passed:

```text

build-gcc/tests/libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests --retain-named-object-callbacks  PASS

git diff --check -- dwg2dxf/dx_data.h dwg2dxf/dx_iface.cpp tests/dwg2dxf_adapter_tests.cpp DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md  PASS
```

This closes only the typed STYLE/LTYPE/BLOCK_RECORD reference-role gate and a
safe output refusal boundary. It does not prove global handle uniqueness,
NOD-root closure, target block-body closure, handle remapping, complete style
payload semantics, serializer readiness, cross-version replay, or native
rendering. No fixture/dependency/support promotion or full-suite run occurred.

## PAR-138: ModelDocViewStyle NOD dictionary hierarchy (2026-10-19 research only)

This pass cross-checked the active DETAILVIEWSTYLE/SECTIONVIEWSTYLE path
against Autodesk's ObjectARX ownership contract, then audited the local
generated input and output gate. It found that the prior positive replay
selector encoded the wrong NOD graph shape. The previous same-version
structural-replay completion is therefore superseded; the local implementation
and tests have not yet been corrected.

| Evidence | Direct observation | Plan consequence and boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk [`getDetailViewStyleDictionary`](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2019/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OREF-AcDbDatabase__getDetailViewStyleDictionary_AcDbDictionary___AcDb__OpenMode.html) and [`getSectionViewStyleDictionary`](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2019/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OREF-AcDbDatabase__getSectionViewStyleDictionary_AcDbDictionary___AcDb__OpenMode.html) | Each API opens an `AcDbDictionary` under its named NOD key; that dictionary contains the corresponding `AcDbDetailViewStyle` or `AcDbSectionViewStyle` objects. The graph is NOD → named style dictionary → style object, not NOD → style object. | This is authoritative object-ownership/API evidence. It invalidates a direct-style root edge as a positive AutoCAD-shaped case; it does not specify every serialized field, record order, version delta, or DWG byte layout. |
| Autodesk [dictionary object/entry guide](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/RUS/AutoCAD-AutoLISP/files/GUID-24E52678-513E-4322-8070-B23C8945DC3D.htm) | Its sample NOD listing shows `ACAD_DETAILVIEWSTYLE` and `ACAD_SECTIONVIEWSTYLE` as dictionary keys with child style names (for example, `Imperial24`) listed inside. A dictionary entry is a name plus a hard-ownership reference to the entry object. | Generated controls must construct both container dictionaries and child name→style edges. Preserve dictionary child keys from the input; do not synthesize a key by assuming a style's handle or use the root key as the style's name. |
| Local [`retainModelDocViewStyleCallbacks`](tests/dwg2dxf_adapter_tests.cpp) generated control and [`fileExport()` root preflight](dwg2dxf/dx_iface.cpp) | The control writes `ACAD_DETAILVIEWSTYLE → handle 105` and `ACAD_SECTIONVIEWSTYLE → handle 106`, with each style owned directly by NOD handle `C`. `fileExport()` accepts those exact direct typed targets only when their `parentHandle` is the NOD, then writes the root key to the style's remapped handle. | This is a confirmed local structural defect in the current implementation/test contract, not just a missing research question. Do not use it as a clean-room independence claim or reproducible release qualification until provenance is bounded. |

| Local semantic checklist | Autodesk's DetailViewStyle and SectionViewStyle API inventories name the switches, but do not give these DWG bit positions or the exact mapping of the repeated SectionViewStyle group-290 fields. The local parser currently retains aggregate flags and the two booleans; the generated DXF output gate retains raw records. | Keep a per-property result of typed-and-mapped, raw-only, unsupported, or unresolved. ## Implementation progress — PAR-138 SectionViewStyle hatch-angle count consistency (2026-10-19; generated ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

`DRW_SectionViewStyle::parseCode()` already captured the group-90 hatch-angle
count into `m_dxfExpectedHatchAngles`, and captured subsequent group-40 angle
values into `m_hatchAngles`, but the DXF object path never reconciled them.
Malformed counts could therefore reach the typed callback with an incomplete
or contradictory typed projection while the raw carrier retained the source
groups.

Added one bounded validation path: a negative or greater-than-100,000 declared
count is rejected while parsing; before publishing the typed/raw callback pair,
the record must have a declared count when angle values are present and that
count must equal the retained angle vector. The 100,000 bound is now shared
with the existing DWG hatch-angle count guard. A subgroup with no declared
count and no angle values remains accepted.

The existing generated ModelDocViewStyle ASCII/Binary control now includes a
valid one-angle SectionViewStyle record, checks the parsed angle/transparency,
and exercises four refusal cases: count mismatch, negative count, over-limit
count, and angles with no count. Each malformed source fails import before a
SectionViewStyle callback is issued. The selector also retains its existing
raw replay, root graph, owner/resource, and valid following-record assertions.

## Implementation progress — PAR-138 order-independent view-style name association (2026-10-19; ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

Implemented the DXF style-name handoff using the documented dictionary graph.
The OBJECTS parser now resolves the first-position NOD's fixed
`ACAD_DETAILVIEWSTYLE` / `ACAD_SECTIONVIEWSTYLE` keys case-insensitively,
validates the referenced child dictionary's owner, and indexes its entry names
by target handle. The original child-entry spelling is passed to the typed
style callback. It is not read from an assumed style-object group 2.

When a style record appears before its child dictionary, the parser stages its
typed/raw callback pair in a bounded queue (maximum 100,000) and drains the
queue in source order once earlier names are resolvable; unresolved entries
are published with an empty typed name at OBJECTS end. Normal dictionary-first
callbacks remain immediate. Duplicate root keys, shared detail/section child
dictionary handles, duplicate case-insensitive child keys, duplicate target
handles, absent keys/dictionaries, and wrong child owners do not produce
guessed names. Raw object groups remain available. Child-key duplicate
comparison intentionally uses ASCII case folding only; this is not a claim of
full Unicode case folding for arbitrary dictionary names.

The existing generated selector now covers ASCII and Binary DXF for normal
and reversed style/dictionary order, callback order, exact typed names,
key-renaming, lowercase fixed root keys, missing/duplicate root and child
entries, duplicate targets, wrong ownership, missing child dictionary, and a
shared child dictionary. The reversed-order profile is also exported and
re-imported at the same version to verify that the typed names survive the
existing raw replay path.

## Implementation progress — AC1024+ TABLE merged-range projection (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Implemented the existing 7G.3d.3e / PAR-126 slice. The AC1024+ TABLECONTENT parser now validates the rectangular grid, range coordinate order/bounds and overlap using a bounded two-dimensional difference grid. Valid ranges project to top-left cell merge markers and inclusive spans before typed publication. Invalid ranges keep the raw DWG frame available, mark the semantic subrecord incomplete and leave the typed grid unpublished. The DXF writer's strict merge/range agreement check remains unchanged.

The generated AC1024 vector covers horizontal, vertical, rectangular and multiple disjoint ranges, untouched cells, inverted and out-of-bounds coordinates, overlapping ranges, and an immediate body-tail sentinel. The existing adapter merge matrix now covers the same valid shapes in ASCII and Binary DXF, inspects literal 173/175/176 groups before parser readback, and verifies readback ranges, cell spans and values. No repository drawing, fixture, CTest registration, dependency, public API change, or external tool was added/run.

## Deeper/broader cross-implementation feature and failure-mode review (2026-10-19; research only)

This pass compares the current local 3D/modeler carrier and writer routes with
the independently maintained LibreDWG, ACadSharp and ezdxf projects. The goal
is to improve comparator selection and implementation readiness, not to turn
peer feature tables or issue reports into local support claims. ODA v5.4.1
remains the authority for DWG byte layout; each peer is evidence only for its
own named source/build, format, version, direction and exercised object.

| Evidence | Cross-project result and evidence ceiling | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg), [manual class maturity and coverage inventory](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi), and [NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | The README describes broad DWG read coverage but notes advanced R2010+ objects may be skipped and that R2010–R2018 writing still has CRC problems; the manual separately classifies classes as stable, unstable, debugging or unhandled and lists types without test coverage. The historical v0.11 NEWS section records incomplete R2013+ `AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b` extraction and brute-force SAB recovery. These are project-scope statements that differ by release/build and do not qualify an arbitrary current-master run. | Keep LibreDWG as a candidate independent DWG structural comparator, pinned by source commit, built artifact, build options and exact profile. For every comparison capture warnings, skipped/unknown classes, object identity/owner, and inline versus AcDs carrier disposition. Do not map a version-reader claim or `STABLE` class label to object completeness, semantic correctness or native acceptance. |
| ACadSharp [version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp), [issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195), and [current issue index](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues) | The matrix advertises directional DWG/DXF reader/writer support by AC version and omits DWG writing for AC1021. Issue #1195 reports that a DWG reader retained 3DSOLID/REGION shells while its DXF writer omitted them without a loss notification; the current issue index also contains version-specific native-writer, parser-boundary and recursive-work reports. These are ACadSharp claims/reports, not local reproductions, normative limits or evidence that every current peer release has the same behavior. | Keep the matrix as a route-selection aid only. On local export, score exact source object identity, owner, block membership, geometry shell, inline payload, external AcDs payload/key/owner, writer disposition and independent readback separately. A shell/count-only check must fail the payload-completeness gate; a skipped object with success and no observable loss is an adverse outcome. Do not import peer-specific limits (for example, its reported XDATA or recursion thresholds) into local format caps. |
| ezdxf [XREF/import contract](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst), [3D renderer limitations](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/addons/drawing.rst), and [ACIS entity creation guidance](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/tasks/add_dxf_entities.rst) | ezdxf is an independent DXF model/read/write route, not a DWG reader. Its XREF import intentionally ignores unsupported entities including ACAD_TABLE; its renderer projects 3D entities to XY and does not render ACIS; creating ACIS payloads requires an external library. Its ACIS/raw inspection utilities can help with a specific DXF carrier question but do not establish general B-rep semantics. | Admit ezdxf only for an exact DXF parser/writer or carrier question with version, options, payload bytes and ignored/unsupported records recorded. Do not score its XREF transfer as whole-document preservation, its 3D rendering as geometry truth, or its ACIS payload inspection as a kernel result. Keep `ACAD_TABLE`, ACIS semantics and native application outcomes on their existing independent gates. |
| Local [`writeModelerGeometry()`](src/libdxfrw.cpp), [`dx_iface::writeEntity()`](dwg2dxf/dx_iface.cpp), [modeler writer matrix](tests/modeler_dxf_writer_matrix_tests.cpp), and [SAT carrier comparator](tests/modeler_sat_dxf_compare.cpp) | The local DXF route has a typed 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY dispatch and version/profile-specific raw modeler payload handling; unsupported or unqualified carrier combinations are refused rather than accepted as an empty successful body. Existing generated and sample-backed owners cover local structure, carrier bytes, chunking and some FreeCAD handoff outcomes. They do not establish arbitrary ACIS validity, all AcDs joins, a complete editable 3D model, or native CAD acceptance. | Retain the current fail-closed target matrix and source/output carrier census. At the composed comparator checkpoint, bind one exact version/profile and compare every source modeler identity and owner to its emitted entity and complete ordered payload chunks; inspect AcDs records/keys/owners separately. Run external semantic/native lanes only after these local structural gates pass. This peer review adds no reason to weaken preflight or expand the per-slice test cadence. |
| Cross-lineage audit: [UnCAD README](https://github.com/iyulab/uncad), [cq-acis](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis), ACadRust/CADCraft notes already recorded under PAR-07/S8, and the LibreCAD bundled fork documented in this repository | UnCAD's DWG route uses LibreDWG, so it is not a second DWG vote; ACadRust-based applications share a parser lineage. cq-acis is a distinct ACIS parser/converter but uses CadQuery/OpenCascade, the same kernel family as FreeCAD, and its documented geometry profiles are bounded. LibreCAD's bundled libdxfrw is a related source fork, not an independent implementation result. | Preserve the evidence-provenance graph. Count independent parsers and geometry kernels, not product names or wrappers. A cq-acis check can answer a pinned SAT/SAB profile question but cannot simultaneously qualify libdxfrw's DWG/AcDs extraction and FreeCAD-native geometry acceptance. ## Implementation progress — PAR-138 typed same-version DXF view-style field overlay (2026-10-19; generated ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

Implemented the next PAR-138 writer slice without changing the public
`dxfRW` API. `dx_iface::writeDetailViewStyleRaw()` and
`dx_iface::writeSectionViewStyleRaw()` operate on a local copy of each captured
raw OBJECTS record. The field walker follows the existing `parseCode()`
subclass/group/occurrence rules and substitutes the corresponding current
typed values into existing recognized groups. Handle references continue
through the shared raw-object remapper and the existing NOD/dictionary closure
and exact-source-version gates remain in force.

Unchanged ASCII raw spellings are retained. When a typed value differs, only
that group's ASCII lexeme is updated in the copied carrier; Binary DXF uses the
typed group value as before. Unrecognized groups remain in their original
position with their captured values. Changes to a typed field that has no
representing source group are rejected unless the value is still that class'
default. SectionViewStyle hatch-angle values must still match the captured
angle-group count and its count marker. These rules prevent the current raw
carrier path from silently dropping unrepresentable edits; adding/inserting
missing groups and changing repeated-field cardinalities remain unsupported.

DetailViewStyle description, identifier height, and label pattern, plus

typed ASCII/Binary readback, all group codes/order/values after expected

sentinel. It also verifies publication refusal for a changed absent Detail

sentinel. No repository fixture or CTest registration was added.

| GNU LibreDWG [DXF manual](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/DXF.html), [program/manual inventory](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/Programs.html), and [official repository test-dxf.sh](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/test-dxf.sh) | The versioned 0.13.4 manual says ASCII DXF output is broad but reports that AutoCAD fails to import some generated files (approximately 10% in that project statement); it describes DXF reading as working for most objects, Binary DXF reading as complete but untested, and Binary DXF output as under construction. LibreDWG exposes fuzz frontends for DWG, DXF, DXFB, and related formats, as well as conversion/round-trip scripts. These are project scope and test-method disclosures, not a current pinned binary run or a libdxfrw result. | Never treat writer completion, parseback, or object-count parity as native acceptance. Keep strict parse, same-codec reopen, independent codec read, and native open/audit separate in the existing evidence ledger. Keep fuzzing at the already scheduled hardening/composed checkpoint; do not add a fuzz or peer suite to each fast implementation slice. Bind exact version, encoding, and operation when selecting LibreDWG as a comparator. |
| ezdxf [`DXFEntity` source](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dxfentity.py), [XREF/import contract](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst), and [resource mapping source](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/xref.py) | ezdxf preserves unfamiliar records through a raw tag-storage representation in supported document read/write paths, but documents that its XREF/import operation ignores unknown/proxy entities and supports only a smaller copyable/transformable subset. Known handle-bearing resources are mapped during copy; raw unknown types are not generally semantically transformable. Thus “unknown retained” is operation-scoped, not an end-to-end transfer guarantee. | Make the route manifest distinguish unchanged in-place serialization from XREF/import/copy, transform, and version conversion. For changed identity or owner, require classified reference remapping and closure; if a retained raw object contains references that cannot be safely rewritten, refuse the transformation instead of claiming graph preservation. Use ezdxf at the composed checkpoint only for the exact direct-DXF syntax/tag question; never score its XREF projection as full-document preservation. |
| IxMilia.Dxf [README compatibility cautions](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf) and [changelog](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) | The project warns that some emitted entity types may not open in AutoCAD or require additional fields; its changelog separately records fixes for handle resolution within BLOCKs, valid handle assignment, XDATA placement, and encoding/version-specific writer behavior. This is useful evidence that typed class presence is not a writer-acceptance result, not proof of a libdxfrw defect. | Preserve per-object validity/required-field selectors in local fast tests when touching those paths. At the composed checkpoint, compare source→destination handle/owner identity, required structural fields, and consumer diagnostics rather than only class totals. Do not add IxMilia as a per-slice dependency or broad test lane. |
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and [DWG route documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md) | FreeCAD documents DWG import as external DWG→DXF conversion followed by its selected DXF importer, and explicitly says embedded ACIS/SAT solids are not read by the stock DXF importer. The consumer result therefore measures a converter-plus-importer route, not the DWG reader alone or ACIS body semantics. | Keep platform qualification pinned to converter, target/intermediate DXF version, importer backend/settings, and output manifest. Keep stock FreeCAD's documented route in the 2D-consumer lane; it cannot resolve the separate ACIS/AcDs semantic gate merely by opening a converted drawing. |

### Implementation-ready refinement

1. For every planned peer/native checkpoint, record the operation tuple:
   input format/version → exact tool artifact and options → operation → output
   format/version → observed per-object disposition. Separate strict read,
   recovery, in-place rewrite, copy/import, transformation, cross-version
   conversion, and native acceptance. Mark unrun or unsupported modes
   `NOT_RUN` / `OUT_OF_PROFILE`, not successful.
2. Continue PAR-138's existing typed overlay over the raw carrier. Interpret a
   repeated group code only within its exact subclass, marker, and occurrence;
   insert a missing field only when the surrounding sequence uniquely proves
   the intended slot. Preserve cardinality and unrelated sentinels. If a
   handle-bearing field is duplicated/ambiguous or its target cannot be
   resolved/remapped, fail closed and retain the source bytes rather than
   publish a potentially dangling graph.
3. Keep per-slice validation to the generated ASCII/Binary selector, focused
   target build, owning CTest, and scoped diff check. Use one pinned direct-DXF
   comparator and the required native consumer rows only at the existing
   composed checkpoint, where they answer named questions. Run fuzzing only
   at the existing hardening checkpoint; this research adds no validation
   frequency or full-suite requirement.
4. No new finding or top-level subplan is warranted: these sources validate
   the existing operation-aware disposition ledger and fail-closed PAR-138
   design. Findings/subplans remain **138 / 77**; J256, J260, J268, J284,

## Implementation progress — PAR-138 insertion of missing DetailViewStyle group-1 handle references (2026-10-19; generated ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

Extended the existing same-version `DetailViewStyle` typed-over-raw serializer
to insert missing group-1 identifier-style and arrow-symbol references
(DXF group 340). The local parser assigns these repeated references by
occurrence, so insertion preserves their order. When the identifier reference
is absent/default-null while a nonzero arrow reference is edited, output now
inserts a group-340 `0` placeholder before the arrow handle; this keeps the
second occurrence mapped to `m_arrowSymbolHandle` instead of changing its
meaning. Zero/sentinel values are not admitted as newly inserted resource
targets, and existing raw fields continue through the prior overlay/remap
path.

The generated adapter control removes both group-1 references from a primary
DetailViewStyle in source ASCII and Binary DXFs. It then checks (a) insertion
of the edited identifier+arrow pair and (b) the arrow-only case with a null
identifier slot. Both routes re-import with the intended typed handles and
closed resource references. The test compares the complete ordered raw style
groups, including ASCII raw lexemes/Binary alignment, confirms the untouched
SectionViewStyle carrier remains identical, and verifies the following POINT
still survives. All test inputs/outputs live in a temporary directory and are
removed.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests -j2  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^dwg2dxf_named_object_callback_storage$' --output-on-failure  1/1 PASS (0.52 sec)
```

This is only same-source-version DXF typed-field insertion/replay. It does not
qualify DWG-origin typed serialization, cross-version projection, ambiguous
partial-occurrence inference, native style rendering, or other unimplemented
style properties. No repository fixture, CTest registration, dependency,
full-suite run, peer/native execution, or support promotion was added. The
shared worktree remains uncommitted; `.git` is read-only. Findings/subplans
remain **138 / 77**, and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

identifier-height, arrow-size, and identifier-offset values (DXF group 40).

<a id="deeperbroader-peer-test-maturity-and-operation-gates-2026-10-19-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader peer test maturity and operation gates (2026-10-19; research only)

This pass examines not just peer feature declarations, but what their
published tests actually execute and what a reported pass can establish. It
adds an implementation-readiness refinement to the existing PAR-07/S8
comparator gate; it does not identify a new local defect, finding, or
sub-plan. The purpose is to avoid treating a test name, reader sample,
successful conversion, or recovery result as end-to-end format parity.

| Primary source | Direct observation and evidence ceiling | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| GNU LibreDWG [`test-dxf.sh`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/test-dxf.sh) | The script invokes `dwg2dxf` on a corpus DWG, filters/normalizes output, then compares to a paired DXF through `diff` and a custom comparator piped to `less`. This is useful paired-output investigation, but the script as written is human-review oriented and does not itself assert a machine-readable semantic pass or native-CAD acceptance. The project also exposes `dwgread` JSON output as a distinct structured route. | At the composed comparator checkpoint, keep paired DXF text comparison as a diagnostic only. For automation, capture structured peer records (where available), compare selected fields and identities with explicit tolerances, and retain tool logs/exit codes. Do not count an interactive diff or conversion exit as an automated parity gate. |
| ACadSharp [version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) and maintainer response on [sample corpus purpose](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/discussions/520) | The README advertises separate DXF/DWG reader/writer capability by AC version. The maintainer says the repository `samples` are files used by the `Tests` project to check that DXF and DWG readers work properly. That description does not establish writer round trips, preservation of unmodeled records, or native acceptance for each matrix cell. | Treat the matrix as candidate route selection. At any peer run, identify the exact test and operation for the selected cell; if relying on samples, classify their provenance and whether a test actually reads, writes, or compares semantics. Never infer writer evidence from reader sample coverage. |
| IxMilia.Dxf [compatibility notes](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf/blob/main/README.md) | The project distinguishes broad DXF version support from types it lists as potentially rejected by AutoCAD, including 3DSOLID, BODY, REGION, proxy entities, dimensions and MTEXT; it also names entities whose output may fail when required data is missing (for example, LEADER vertex count). It explicitly leaves MESH, MLEADER, SURFACE, TABLE and VIEWPORT outside its stated R10–R2014 support. These are the project's own scope/compatibility statements, not a libdxfrw result or independently rerun test. | Keep writer tests entity-specific and include minimal required-field/structural-validity controls for the local types in scope. Compare serialization, independent parser acceptance, and native acceptance separately. Reuse existing local vectors/CTest owners; do not add IxMilia as a dependency or per-slice test lane. |
| ezdxf [file loading guidance](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/tutorials/getting_data.rst), [recovery guidance](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/usage_for_beginners.rst), and [audit CLI](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/launcher.rst) | The docs recommend strict `readfile` for trusted valid files and a separate recovery API for flawed input; recovery returns an auditor and may still report unrecoverable errors. A recovered object model is therefore not evidence that strict parsing accepted the input unchanged. | Record strict parse, recovery parse, repair diagnostics, and recovered output as distinct operations. If recovery is exercised, compare before/after object and handle dispositions and report repair/deletion counts; do not fold it into a successful strict-read result. |
| FreeCAD [DWG import route](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md) and [Draft DXF limits](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) | FreeCAD documents DWG conversion to DXF before importer processing, offers separate importer backends, and documents that stock DXF import does not read embedded ACIS/SAT solids. This is an application route with distinct converter and importer loss boundaries, not a direct DWG semantic oracle or ACIS kernel result. | Preserve the existing consumer manifest: pin converter, DXF target version, importer/backend/settings, platform, and per-source object disposition. Keep stock FreeCAD qualification scoped to its actual supported import set; do not use an openable file or entity-count summary to resolve the ACIS/AcDs semantic gates. |

### Implementation-ready follow-through

1. For every composed peer row, record the exact input and output format/version,
   encoding, operation (strict read, recovery, same-version rewrite, copy,
   transform, or conversion), tool/package commit or release, runtime/build
   options, test command, exit status, diagnostics, and per-source handle/type/
   owner disposition. If any of these are unknown, mark the result `PARTIAL`
   or `NOT_RUN`, not `PASS`.
2. Keep peer disagreements spec-led. For a DWG field conflict, first read the
   relevant ODA v5.4.1 section and trace the local offsets/bit positions; next
   use an admitted producer sample with a paired DXF or another independent
   raw trace. Peer implementation counts are corroboration, not a vote. If the
   sources still conflict, preserve the current behavior as
   `OPEN_SPEC_RECONCILIATION` and fail closed on support promotion.
3. Keep fast slice validation unchanged: generated local ASCII/Binary controls,
   focused target build, owning CTest, and scoped diff check. Do not run peer
   repositories or full suites per slice. Use one pinned peer/native matrix at
   the existing composed checkpoint; keep fuzzing at the already planned
   hardening checkpoint.
4. Use only existing in-repository fixtures or locally generated scratch
   inputs for commits. Downloaded peer samples may be inspected transiently
   when permitted, but do not add them to the repository; record hashes and
   provenance if a composed result depends on them.
5. No new finding/sub-plan is warranted from these project-level test
   disclosures. Findings/subplans remain **138 / 77**; J256, J260, J268,
   J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and cannot be promoted by
   these sources. This research changed only the plan and receipt: no code,
   tests, CTest registration, fixture, dependency, peer execution, native run,
   validation frequency, or support claim changed.

## Deeper/broader source-lineage-qualified peer independence and evidence tiers (2026-10-19; research only)

This primary-source review revisits the word *independent* across the open-source
DWG/DXF comparison set. A repository, binary, language, or CAD application is
not by itself an independent parser or semantic oracle. The key new
qualification is historical: GNU LibreDWG says its code came from QCAD
Community Edition; LibreCAD documents that it began as a QCAD CE fork; and
libdxfrw describes itself as created by LibreCAD contributors. Those sources
show a shared product-history path, but do **not** establish that current
LibreDWG and libdxfrw DWG reader code shares implementation. Treat the
relationship as ancestry-uncertain rather than either proven reuse or proven
clean-room independence.

| Route / source | Provenance observation | Evidence label and plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| GNU [LibreDWG overview](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/Overview.html), [LibreCAD project history](https://docs.librecad.org/en/latest/appx/licenses.html), and [libdxfrw README](https://github.com/LibreCAD/libdxfrw) | LibreDWG documents origin in QCAD Community Edition; LibreCAD documents its QCAD CE fork history; libdxfrw documents development by LibreCAD contributors. The records do not show file-level or algorithm-level reuse between the current LibreDWG decoder and libdxfrw. | For the PAR-138 `children-room-decoration.dwg` result, replace unqualified *independent decode* with **source-distinct structural cross-check; historical product ancestry unresolved**. It remains useful corroboration of the observed object values and graph, but is not a clean-room assurance, source of normative semantics, or independent semantic oracle. |
| [`dwg-rs` README](https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/dwg-rs) and [ACadSharp](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) | `dwg-rs` describes a spec-first implementation and says it did not import ACadSharp code, but it explicitly cross-checked an ambiguous LZ77 offset description against comments in ACadSharp. It also discloses that its entity decoders have per-version gaps. | Score independence per algorithm/path: container, section-map, and object-stream code may be a distinct structural route; do not count its LZ77 behavior as an independent algorithm witness. Keep its pre-alpha/version/corpus limits attached to every comparison. |
| [`acad-ts`](https://github.com/node-projects/acad-ts) and ACadSharp | `acad-ts` identifies itself as a TypeScript port of ACadSharp. A different language, package, or UI does not create a second parser lineage. | Deduplicate both under ACadSharp for parser evidence. It may still be a separate deployed artifact when testing a platform/runtime consumer, but that is consumer/runtime evidence only. |
| [`ezdxf`](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf) [ODA File Converter add-on](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/addons/odafc.rst) | ezdxf's native model is DXF; `odafc` invokes an installed external ODA File Converter for DWG/DXB conversion. | Admit ezdxf as a DXF implementation only. Any DWG result belongs to the exact ODA executable, version, arguments, and conversion profile—not to an open-source DWG reader. |
| LibreCAD_3 [DWG support policy](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/blob/master/docs/dwg-support.md) and current bundled libdxfrw | LibreCAD_3 routes experimental read-only DWG through libdxfrw and deliberately does not write DWG. | Keep its build/import checks under downstream compatibility. They are valuable for the LibreCAD consumer contract but are not an independent format implementation or writer witness. |

### Implementation-ready update to the existing PAR-07/S8 evidence manifest

1. Add four separate provenance fields to each optional peer result: (a) exact
   parser/writer implementation and immutable source or package pin; (b) shared
   or consulted algorithm/helper sources; (c) external converter/kernel/importer
   actually invoked; and (d) provenance of the expected values. Missing fields
   mean `LINEAGE_UNRESOLVED` or `NOT_RUN`, never `INDEPENDENT_PASS`.
2. Maintain distinct result labels: `SAME_IMPLEMENTATION_SELF_CHECK`,
   `SOURCE_DISTINCT_CROSSCHECK`, `ALGORITHM_INDEPENDENT_CROSSCHECK`,
   `INDEPENDENT_EXPECTED_SEMANTICS`, and `NATIVE_CONSUMER_ACCEPTANCE`. A result
   may satisfy more than one only when each dimension is separately evidenced.
3. Retain the existing PAR-138 peer decode and its measured values, but qualify
   the record as source-distinct structural corroboration. To claim semantic
   independence, bind expected values to an authored producer/native toggle,
   authoritative specification, or independently measured geometry—not to
   another codec's output alone.
4. At the already planned composed checkpoint, choose only the peer needed for
   the unresolved question. Do not add peer builds, dependencies, full-suite
   runs, or native-app checks to each implementation slice; keep generated
   ASCII/Binary fast tests and owning CTests as the routine gate.
5. This changes no implementation order, finding/subplan count, consumer
   contract, fixture policy, or support claim. No source checkout, peer binary,
   native CAD app, external drawing, or local test was run. The six external
   items J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.
