| ODA [DWG specification v5.4.1, §7 R2013 organization](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) | The published specification describes the `AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b` data section as introduced in R2013 and containing ACIS data. This addresses container-level presence, not the complete local extraction/association algorithm or the semantic correctness of each body. | Keep AC1024 inline-SAT and AC1027+ SAB/AcDs as separate test profiles. A converter-authored pair may be used only after inspecting target signature, actual payload signature, owner/reference chain, and exact emitted bytes; any converter re-encoding is a recorded transform, not byte-identity evidence. |

### Ready-to-run sequence for the optional composed semantic checkpoint

1. **Smallest gate first:** in an isolated temporary environment on macOS ARM64,
   verify the exact wheel hash/attestation, Python/CadQuery/OCCT versions, and
   one already supported release-profile body. Start with a closed planar
   polyhedron whose independently written manifest specifies body/lump/shell/
   face counts, bounds, volume, and orientation. Do not use cq-acis's own
   corpus expectations as the semantic oracle.
2. **Cheap independent structure check:** run the same SAT/SAB payload through
   the pinned ezdxf API only if the case is all-planar and within its documented
   subset. Require no unsupported records and compare its mesh to the authored
   manifest. If the profile is curved or outside ezdxf's subset, skip this
   comparator rather than weakening the expected result.
3. **Compose the file route only after the small gate passes:** author scratch
   DXF controls locally, convert them with a pinned external converter to
   AC1024 and AC1027 (or AC1032) DWG, and inspect whether the converter emitted
   inline SAT versus an AcDs/SAB route. Checkpoint source entity identity,
   owner/handle edges, section/index references, payload hash/length, and each
   transformation independently. A converter that strips or changes the
   modeler payload makes the case `NOT_EXERCISED`, not a libdxfrw failure.
4. Feed each exact extracted payload to cq-acis and bind its body result back
   to the originating DWG handle. Require all source solids to have an explicit
   disposition, no unreported raw/unsupported geometry, valid closed shapes,
   and analytic bounds/area/volume within stated tolerances. Keep the parser's
   OCCT result labeled as a shared-kernel-family measurement with FreeCAD, not
   as an independent kernel vote.
5. Run the FreeCAD Linux/Windows consumer matrix only at the scheduled external
   checkpoint. Capture converter, intermediate DXF, importer backend/settings,
   native object inventory, and visible/semantic solid outcome separately. A
   stock importer's documented ACIS omission is an expected route boundary,
   not grounds to claim the DWG carrier was absent.
6. Keep generated files, downloaded wheel, and temporary environment outside
   tracked fixtures. Do not add a runtime/CI dependency or run this expensive
   route per implementation slice. If tool/platform access is unavailable,
   mark that external row pending and continue the local implementation queue.

### PAR-139 implementation-ready sequence

1. **139.1 — strict typed-field admission (small local codec slice).** Keep the
   DWG body order bound to ODA §20.4.94: point count and points, extrusion and
   origin, flags, conditional front/back distances, exactly two 12-value
   matrices, then common handles. For DXF, require at least two points and a
   group-70 count consistent with the repeated point pairs when group 70 is
   present; any present count must be unique, nonnegative, and within the
   existing boundary-point cap. Require groups 71–73 to be 0/1. Stage
   group-40 occurrences until the record is complete, then accept exactly 24
   values when front clipping is off or exactly 25 when it is on (first value
   is front distance, remaining 24 are the matrices). Require the conditional
   front/back distance fields to agree with their flags. Require finite
   doubles and preserve group-40 order. Do not let a lone
   front-distance tag disappear, do not zero-pad missing matrices, and do not
   allow malformed typed records to enter an admitted writer path; retain raw
   bytes only under the existing explicit raw-policy/receipt. Extend the
   existing hardening/parser test path with generated malformed and boundary
   controls—no new CTest registration.
2. **139.2 — adapter capture and loss visibility.** Add bounded storage for
   typed `DRW_SpatialFilter` callbacks in `dx_data` and a `dx_iface` override.
   For DXF-origin callbacks, retain the complete raw companion with an
   import-generation receipt, byte/group/callback accounting, and typed/raw
   handle/owner identity checks. For DWG-origin callbacks, retain typed fields
   plus explicit source format/version; never reinterpret an unsupported DWG
   frame as DXF. Keep new public callbacks non-pure. Until graph closure and
   writer admission are implemented, any detected filter must produce a
   bounded diagnostic/refusal before publication, not silent success.
3. **139.3 — order-independent owner-graph preflight.** Index dictionaries,
   INSERTs, filters, and extension dictionaries by unique non-null handle.
   Resolve INSERT → extension DICTIONARY → exact `ACAD_FILTER` child → exact
   `SPATIAL` filter entry; verify every dictionary owner and filter
   `parentHandle`. Also follow an extension dictionary attached to the
   `SPATIAL_FILTER` itself, including opaque `ACAD_XREC_ROUNDTRIP` XRECORD
   children when present. Preserve typed reactors/EED and XRECORD children.
   Until traversal and writers exist for arbitrary sibling objects, reject
   sibling entries on the INSERT's `ACAD_FILTER` route or its `SPATIAL`
   dictionary rather than emit an incomplete graph; broaden that admission
   only with a source-to-output disposition for every sibling.
   Require one unique owning INSERT per filter; test two INSERTs of the same
   block with separate filters so block-definition identity cannot be
   mistaken for instance ownership. Reject ambiguous/case-conflicting keys,
   duplicate handles, cycles, dangling/wrong-kind edges, orphan filters, and
   unsupported raw children. Do not infer ownership geometrically or create
   synthetic dictionaries.
4. **139.4 — same-version graph serializer and transactional refusal.** The
   first implementation slice now schedules the filter plus its admitted
   dictionary/extension-dictionary and typed XRECORD nodes, remaps their
   handles, and emits them only after the complete graph is admitted. It
   starts with an exact source-version match; rejects unfamiliar raw
   SPATIAL_FILTER tags and unsupported sibling dictionary objects; and keeps
   record bytes transactional. Extend typed/raw sibling closure before
   widening that supported shape. Preserve both exact
   12-value matrices; never default absent values to zero. Preserve the
   conditional front distance only when group 72 enables it and the back
   distance only when group 73 enables it; preserve the two-point rectangle
   versus polygon boundary, OCS normal/origin, and group-40 occurrence order.
   Preserve group 71 as a raw Boolean without promoting its semantic label:
   ODA and Autodesk's DXF table call it boundary display, while Autodesk's
   `SpatialFilterDefinition.Enabled` API describes making the clip volume
   effective (and its .NET clipping guide describes showing/hiding the
   boundary); ezdxf also exposes it as clipping-enabled. These descriptions
   conflict and must be resolved with native behavior, not naming inference.
   `$XCLIPFRAME` is a separate drawing-level frame display/plot policy; prove
   field preservation independently from effective clipping and rendered
   frame behavior. Start with same-version replay and add cross-version
   targets only when every value and graph edge is representable. Any
   unsupported field, version, or edge must fail before replacing an existing
   destination and permit a corrected retry on the same adapter/writer. Do
   not geometrically clip, explode INSERTs, or rewrite block contents here.
5. **139.5 — generated ASCII/Binary regression controls.** Extend existing
   hardening and `dwg2dxf_named_object_callback_storage` targets; add no
   registration or committed fixture. Build an in-memory block with inside
   and outside LINEs and two INSERT instances using nonzero translation,
   rotation, nonuniform scale, and distinct nontrivial matrices/clip paths.
   Cover a rectangle and a polygon, a non-default normal/origin, group 71 on
   and off, front-only, back-only, both planes, and their disabled-field
   controls. Assert literal typed fields, invalid non-Boolean flags, 24-vs-25
   group-40 sequence, exact
   matrix order, dictionary keys/owners, one filter per INSERT, remapped
   handles, and separate raw preservation of group 71 and `$XCLIPFRAME` in
   ASCII and Binary output; reimport and verify the same graph plus a following-record
   sentinel. Permute OBJECTS callback order. Generated missing/duplicate/
   wrong-owner/wrong-kind/cyclic/dangling/count-mismatch/partial-matrix cases
   must refuse and preserve an existing destination; then correct the same
   adapter and verify a successful retry. Keep payloads in-memory or in
   deleted test-temp outputs only.
6. **139.6 — optional composed clipping semantics, not a per-slice gate.** At
   the existing peer/consumer checkpoint, pin exact ezdxf and independent
   reader revisions, strictly read the emitted DXF, and inspect the owner
   graph and 2D non-inverted path. Use affine matrices with nonzero
   translation, rotation, and nonuniform scale—not identity or arbitrary
   sequential doubles—and compare each 12-value matrix against a separately
   derived expected point mapping. Test both DXF→DXF and DWG→DXF (when an
   independently generated DWG witness exists); per-format round trips alone
   cannot detect cross-format transpose or matrix-role swaps. Compare analytic
   inside/outside segments in block and WCS coordinates under INSERT
   transformation, and observe group 71's effect on clipping separately from
   frame visibility. Exercise `$XCLIPFRAME` values 0/1/2 against group 71 on
   and off; assert only serialized preservation until a native app establishes
   display, plot, and clipping outcomes. Treat ezdxf as a secondary comparator
   only: its open #1305 reports a WCS-path mismatch for an attached drawing,
   and its docs say inverted-clip structure is not fully understood. The open,
   unmerged ACadSharp #1230 reports lost/transposed matrices and explicitly
   notes that identity matrices masked its defect; use its proposed affine
   cross-format assertions as a test-design warning, not as deployed peer
   behavior or proof of a libdxfrw defect. Do not infer inversion semantics
   from ezdxf's `ACAD_XREC_ROUNDTRIP` convention or emit its experimental,
   documented AutoCAD-incompatible form. Record strict-read failures, audit
   repairs, dropped entities, geometric results, and renderer outcomes
   separately; keep native LibreCAD/AutoCAD display at composed gates. No new
   renderer dependency.

**Fast implementation cadence:** routine validation for 139.1–139.5 is only
the affected strict library/adapter target build, its focused selector, the
owning existing hardening or adapter CTest, and scoped `git diff --check`.
Run only the affected serializer/graph selector when that slice changes it.
Do not run the full suite after each slice; reserve cross-peer, renderer,
FreeCAD, and native-CAD work for existing composed checkpoints. After every
implemented item, update this plan with the closed part, focused result,
remaining gaps, and next unblocked item; after each committed slice, report
progress. Continue independent local slices while optional external/platform
evidence is pending.

## Implementation progress — PAR-139.4 same-version SPATIAL_FILTER graph serialization (2026-10-19; generated ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

The codec-level `writeSpatialFilter()` now rejects unsupported target versions,
invalid typed fields, null/overflow owners, zero/fixed output handles, and
duplicate reservations before emitting a record. It remaps and reserves the
self handle, stages the complete object in `DxfWriterRecordScope`, checks each
group write, preserves the exact 12+12 matrix order, and emits front/back
distances only under their respective flags. A failed record cannot publish a
partial SPATIAL_FILTER record.

The adapter owner-graph gate now requires an exact source/target version match
and returns output closures for the owning INSERT extension dictionary, its
`ACAD_FILTER` dictionary, the `SPATIAL_FILTER`, and typed XRECORDs under the
filter's own extension dictionary. The object writer emits those typed nodes
in dependency-safe OBJECTS order and remaps the fixed output-handle collision
for the filter. Before admission, it rejects cross-type/entity handle
collisions, unrecognized source raw group codes, and unsupported sibling
entries on the two INSERT clipping dictionaries. This is deliberately
fail-closed: arbitrary sibling-object traversal and raw XRECORD preservation
are not yet implemented. Typed reactors/EED and the filter-owned typed
XRECORD payload are retained; no inversion semantics are inferred.

Generated ASCII and Binary inputs exercise two INSERTs of one block with
separate owner chains, distinct boundaries/matrices, front-only and back-only
distances, and a filter-owned `ACAD_XREC_ROUNDTRIP` dictionary/XRECORD carrying
opaque metadata. Controls verify same-version output/reimport, fixed-handle
remapping, transactional refusal for a target-version mismatch, dangling
target and cross-owner rejection with destination preservation, then a
corrected retry on the same adapter. No external/repository fixture or new
CTest registration was added; all generated files are temporary and removed.

Validation: strict builds of `libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests` and
`libdxfrw_hardening_tests`; `libdxfrw_hardening_tests
--spatial-filter-dxf-validation` passes; existing
`dwg2dxf_named_object_callback_storage` passes 1/1 (0.55 sec); scoped diff
check passes. No full suite, peer executable, native CAD application, or
FreeCAD run was performed. This establishes bounded field/graph serialization
and DXF reimport only—not visible clipping, inversion, DWG-origin export
qualification, or consumer support. Continue PAR-139.5 with broader generated
field/topology controls and PAR-139.6 at the composed semantic checkpoint.
Findings/subplans remain 139/77; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c GEODATA newline escape preservation (2026-10-19; generated ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

The focused hardening selector reproduced two failures: AC1021 and AC1032
ASCII output changed GEODATA's established newline notation from `^J` to
`^ J`. The new modern ASCII text sink correctly quotes ordinary literal
carets, but `writeGeoData()` had already normalized field newlines to the DXF
`^J` escape, so routing that value through the generic literal-text encoder
quoted the escape a second time.

Added a field-specific UTF-8 writer path that preserves normalized `^J` as an
atomic escape while applying the selected compatible/strict encoding policy
to other scalars. The continuation-group path uses the same atom-aware encoder
and keeps UTF-8 scalars and `^J` pairs intact at the 255-byte boundary. The
existing generated control now checks AC1021/AC1032, ASCII/Binary, both
compatible and `RequireLossless` policies, exact group-301 content, source
immutability, and a following-record sentinel.

Validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_hardening_tests -j2`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --dxf-geodata-modern-text-preflight`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_hardening$' --output-on-failure` (1/1)
- Scoped `git diff --check` on the changed implementation and test files.

No persistent fixture, CTest registration, dependency, peer runtime, native
application, or full suite was added/run. This fixes a local text-sink
regression; it does not establish native GEODATA interoperability or promote
support. Findings/subplans remain **139 / 77**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293,
and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The typed-projection constructor audit
that followed this slice closed pre-copy name admission for associative,
dynamic-block, and AcSh history OBJECTS. The next 7S.2c action is the remaining
retained-output/callback-copy census, keeping parser operation leases separate
from adapter-owned retained-byte estimates. PAR-139.6 remains a composed
semantic checkpoint only and does not block local implementation. The shared
worktree remains uncommitted; no staging or commit was attempted.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c typed OBJECTS record-name retained-byte ownership (2026-10-19; generated ASCII fast slice, uncommitted)

The typed-projection audit found that `processDynamicBlockObject()` and
`processAcShHistoryObject()` constructed their typed records directly from
`nextentity` before the raw companion's name lease was charged. The associative
object route had the same issue and was corrected in the preceding slice.
Dynamic-block and AcSh history records now start with their default
constructors, reserve `nextentity.size()` against the operation's retained-byte
budget, then copy the name; dynamic-block kind classification follows the
admitted assignment. Allocation/admission failure returns a bounded parse
error before either typed or raw callback publication.

The generated ASCII selector
`--dxf-typed-object-name-retained-budget` exercises one
`BLOCKVISIBILITYPARAMETER` and one `ACSH_HISTORY_NODE` OBJECTS record. For each,
it finds the exact minimum successful budget, verifies raw-carrier plus typed
name charges, clears raw callback storage and confirms the typed name remains
charged, then releases the typed callback value and confirms the charge drops
to zero. One byte below the threshold must report
`ResourceLimit/dxf-retained-byte-budget` before either callback. Inputs are
constructed in memory; no fixture or CTest registration was added.

Validation passed:

callback forms and verifies that the rvalue route is selected and the adapter
retains the modeler entity. The existing fallback selector separately checks
legacy callback compatibility. No external or persistent drawing fixture was
used; the change does not alter modeler parsing or qualify ACIS semantics.

## Deeper/broader ACIS carrier generation, FreeCAD consumer limits, and DWG AcDs controls (2026-10-19; research only)

This pass compared stock FreeCAD's documented importer boundary with its
optional InventorLoader ACIS path, inspected ezdxf's documented SAT/SAB
generation and parser limits, and revisited the LibreDWG AcDs documentation
and generated issue reproducer. The aim is to make the modeler/AcDs checks
reproducible without importing external drawings, and to prevent a consumer
that cannot read ACIS from being treated as a semantic oracle. Mutable
`main`/`master` documentation was reviewed; no external project was cloned or
run, no drawing or issue attachment was downloaded, and no repository fixture
was added.

The guide explicitly says its DXF import path cannot read ACIS/SAT solids. Separately, InventorLoader reads DXF via ezdxf, extracts SAT/SAB into a custom `AcisReader`, then offers native or STEP import strategies. This add-on is a distinct parser path, but its native shape construction remains in FreeCAD/OCCT and its README records unsupported geometry features. | Split the FreeCAD checkpoint into stock 2D/explicit-entity acceptance and optional ACIS-add-on investigation. Treat it as a useful independent parsing path for a bounded profile, not an independent kernel-family vote or general DWG oracle. |
| ezdxf [ACIS tools](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html), [ACIS-based entity constructors](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/layouts/layouts.html), and [ACIS browser/version notes](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/launcher.html) | ezdxf documents SAT for DXF R2000–R2010 and SAB for R2013/R2018. Its ACIS package targets simple, known structures, has no ACIS kernel, maps unsupported ACIS records to `NONE_ENTITY` with data loss, and cannot round-trip arbitrary ACIS data. `body_from_mesh` provides a local source-generation route for polyhedral bodies; `mesh_from_body` emits only flat polygonal faces and loses curved boundaries. | At the existing optional generated-peer checkpoint, pin the exact ezdxf package and generate scratch-only AC1015/AC1018/AC1021/AC1024/AC1027/AC1032 controls from a deliberately asymmetric closed polyhedron. Do not add ezdxf as a production/test dependency or commit generated fixture files; keep generation and outputs under the temporary test directory unless a generated fixture is explicitly accepted under the repository's fixture policy. |
| LibreDWG [AcDs issue #1411 and its generated reproducer](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411), [manual coverage matrix](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi), [NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS), and [R2007 AcDs reader source](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode_r2007.c) | The issue describes a generated AC1032 DXF `REGION` carrying a cube-derived SAB body; a named LibreDWG build reportedly preserves the entity but loses the 5,489-byte SAB on DWG→DXF and does not create an AcDs section on DXF→DWG. The issue is an unreproduced peer report for the named build, not a libdxfrw result. The historical v0.11 NEWS section describes incomplete `AcDsPrototype_1b` support and brute-force extraction of some newer SAB blobs, while current source contains an AcDs section reader; this documents a version/build-sensitive implementation history, not one universal outcome. | Reuse the issue's shape only as a test-design lead at the composed peer checkpoint. Generate the SAT/SAB control locally, bind exact generator and LibreDWG versions/commits, and assert the actual DWG section name, record/handle association and bytes before judging conversion. After conversion, independently inspect DXF `ACDSDATA` records and entity-to-record joins; entity count and `has_ds_data` alone are insufficient. Label any mismatch by peer version/build and direction. Do not copy the reported size, offsets, or alleged defect into parser behavior or promote local support from the peer report. |

`dx_iface::addRawDxfEntity` previously copied every unsupported/raw DXF entity
into a block's ordered event vector and only rejected callbacks without an
owning block. It now admits each event against per-`dx_data` aggregate limits:
100,000 records, 4,000,000 raw groups, and 64 MiB of logical event plus copied
record storage. The estimate charges the event slot once, then the raw record's

sticky for the retained model and export refuses to publish a partial DXF; the
old per-import reset of that sticky flag was removed so an existing incomplete
capture cannot become exportable merely by starting another read into the same
`dx_data`.

and independent byte-, record-, group-, and owner-context rejection paths. It
also verifies no output is published after an over-budget capture. No external
or persistent drawing fixture was introduced.

A primitive's expected geometry must be specified independently of its author and checked after decoding; a peer's own readback or a nonempty payload is not a semantic pass. |
| ACadSharp [issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) and [PR #1240](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1240) | The issue reports ACadSharp 3.4.9 reading 3DSOLID/REGION entities but silently omitting them from DXF output, including solid-only block definitions. The writer proposal remains a separate branch/PR in the reviewed listing; it is not evidence that the behavior is fixed in a released artifact. | Keep the existing source-handle → emitted entity/carrier → block/INSERT owner disposition ledger. A surviving block shell or process success cannot count as retained geometry; require exact payload disposition or an actionable refusal before publication. Bind any peer observation to the exact release/commit and conversion direction. |
| [FreeCAD Draft DXF guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md), [ezdxf ACIS authoring guidance](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/tasks/add_dxf_entities.rst), and [ezdxf ACIS tools](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) | FreeCAD's documented C++/legacy importers have different explicit-entity sets; the legacy list includes 3DFACE, neither published list names MESH, and stock FreeCAD does not read embedded ACIS/SAT solids. ezdxf says creation of ACIS data requires an external library and documents limited ACIS parsing/projection rather than general B-rep semantics. | Preserve entity-family/backend-specific FreeCAD rows and keep stock ACIS as `CONSUMER_NOT_APPLICABLE`. An ACIS author, carrier parser, mesh projection, and native CAD consumer are distinct roles; no new candidate fills the missing independent semantic or platform gate. |

### Implementation-ready disposition

1. Do not change the implementation queue or add a required external step. Keep
   local fast validation and the existing composed peer/native checkpoint as
   planned; inability to bind or run this fork does not block the local queue.
2. If the candidate is revisited, first bind an immutable commit, license,

   scratch-generated primitive case, outside the repository. Capture target
   DXF version, entity type/handle/owner, SAT/SAB signature and exact bytes,
   and any DWG AcDs key/owner association separately.
3. Require a separately authored analytic manifest (topology counts, bounds,
   volume/orientation where applicable) and a distinct admitted parser/kernel
   path. Do not use the fork's `208/208` headline, same-codec reopen, README
   primitive list, or FreeCAD stock importer as the semantic oracle.
4. Continue using existing local and composed gates for block/INSERT closure,
   carrier retention, semantic validity, and native acceptance. No permanent
   external DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB fixture or production dependency is warranted by
   this discovery.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c shared typed named-resource callback capture bounds (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The typed `SCALE`, `DICTIONARYVAR`, `MLINESTYLE`, and `MLEADERSTYLE`
callbacks now share one container-lifetime admission budget of 100,000
records and 64 MiB logical retained bytes. `MLINESTYLE` keeps its separate
one-million-item cap and per-element DXF validation-mask accounting; its
successful deep copy also consumes the shared record/byte budget. Estimators
charge table-entry metadata and variable strings, as well as nested MLINE
elements. Counts/bytes advance only after a successful copy. Stale DXF import
generation, allocation failure, per-family MLINE limit, or shared record/byte
limit leaves sticky capture evidence; the named-resource receipt becomes
unsuccessful and export refuses before publication. This is a retention guard,
not a wire-schema, object-graph, serializer, or consumer qualification.

Generated controls cover exact callback accounting and deep-copy ownership for
all four families, null MLEADERSTYLE input, cross-family aggregate record
admission, byte and record boundary refusal, sticky retry, stale-generation
retry, and no-output export refusal. The existing generated ASCII/Binary
named-resource import evidence also verifies that the new receipt counters
close for DXF input; synthetic DWG provenance controls were updated to match
the additional receipt accounting. No repository/external DWG/DXF fixture was
added.

### Local crosswalk and implementation-ready subplan

The local test inventory already includes raw-DXF rejection of missing and zero self-handles and duplicate-handle checks, plus record-inventory duplicate-emission checks (`tests/wave1_tests.cpp`). This is useful local evidence about parsing/replay/inventory controls, not proof that every DXF writer route emits valid handles. `src/libdxfrw.cpp` allocates nonzero handles for normal table records, while any eventual writer qualification should still inspect actual emitted records through an independent strict parser and verify uniqueness and required owner/reference closure.

The go-cad ≥18 MB report maps first to the existing R2004+ page-map, section framing/capacity, and bounded decompression work. Do not import the reported threshold or peer opcodes as spec facts. If a locally supported path later reproduces a failure, capture the exact AC version, first failing stage, section/page geometry, and bounded trace; use a scratch-generated in-memory control at below/at/above the suspected boundary where feasible, and assert bounded refusal/no partial publication. Add a new issue only after local reproduction and source/spec reconciliation; do not add peer DWG fixtures.

For any future optional go-cad comparison, make it a single question-specific checkpoint rather than a standing dependency or test lane:

1. Pin the upstream commit, Go version, build flags, exact executable/package hash, and all input hashes; record the reader/writer operation and format version.
2. Use only repository-existing drawings or locally generated scratch inputs. Keep independent expected values/identities separate from the implementation's own output; report parse errors, skipped/unsupported records, missing, extra, wrong-type, and compared-value mismatches independently.
3. Compare the union of expected and observed handles/types before any per-value percentage. A skipped or unclassified expected record cannot silently disappear from the denominator; fail closed if the manifest does not account for every record.
4. For DXF output, independently strict-reopen ASCII and Binary variants as applicable; assert nonzero unique handles, class/type agreement, and owner/reference closure. A peer reader's acceptance alone is not semantic correctness.
5. For DWG-to-DXF ACIS/AcDs, score raw carrier retention and owner association separately from independent parse, native open/regeneration, and analytic B-rep semantics. go-cad explicitly reports no ACIS kernel, so it cannot qualify that route.
6. Preserve ordinary fast local validation order; run this peer check only at an already-composed external checkpoint when it answers a named gap. Do not add a peer installation, dependency, CI matrix, or full-suite cadence.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c typed DATALINK callback capture bounds (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The typed `DRW_DataLink` callback copy was the next uncovered persistent OBJECTS store identified in the 7S.2c census. The callback already retained connection metadata and nested custom-data text, but its `dx_data::dataLinks` collection had no adapter-owned aggregate budget. The slice adds container-lifetime limits of 100,000 records, 1,000,000 custom-data items, and `DRW::kMaxDxfBinaryPayloadBytes` logical bytes (64 MiB). Accounting includes `DRW_TableEntry` dynamic state, DATALINK metadata strings, custom-data vector slots, and each nested text value; only successfully copied records advance counters.

Limit, estimate, or allocation failure sets a sticky capture-failed bit. `fileExport` checks that state immediately after validating the source container and refuses before later preflight or destination publication. The existing nonempty-DATALINK refusal remains in place because callback retention is not a DATALINK/TABLE graph serializer or linked-range qualification.

Generated fast controls verify exact record/item/byte accounting, deep-copy independence after mutating the source, record/item/byte refusal, sticky retry refusal, the specific export-preflight diagnostic, and preservation of an existing destination. The existing parse-to-adapter DATALINK test continues to cover ASCII callback fields and fail-closed export. The first adapter-test build also exposed a preexisting `-Werror=unused-function` issue: the generated ModelDocViewStyle typed-capture test function had neither a command selector nor a CTest registration. This slice wires that existing function into its selector and focused CTest; its test logic was not changed.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c typed DICTIONARYWDFLT/PLACEHOLDER callback capture bounds (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The 7S.2c typed-callback audit found that `addDictionaryWithDefault` and
`addAcDbPlaceholder` already routed through a shared aggregate admission guard,
but there was no focused selector/CTest locking that behavior down. Added a
generated adapter test and registration for that existing guard; production
serializer/parser behavior was not changed in this slice.

The generated dictionary has two entries, dynamic base-table state and a
reactor handle; the placeholder carries its own base-table name and reactor.
The successful case verifies independent callback destinations, deep-copy
ownership after mutating both source objects, and exact logical record/item/
byte counters. Additional cases seed the aggregate admission counters at
exactly the three boundaries (100,000 records, 1,000,000 dictionary-entry
items, and 64 MiB logical retained bytes) and confirm exact-fit admission,
then attempt a further callback and confirm sticky refusal without advancing
counters. One-over record, item, and byte cases also verify resource-limit
classification and that no rejected typed record is appended. These seeded
counter tests exercise the logical admission boundary; they are not an RSS or
allocator measurement.

A stale DXF import generation remains a sticky capture failure after the
receipt generation is corrected, and is distinguished from a resource-limit
failure. The byte-limit refusal is additionally required to stop export at
the typed-capture preflight, emit its specific diagnostic, and preserve an
existing destination sentinel. All controls use generated in-memory objects;
no DWG/DXF fixture, peer dependency, or support claim was added.

## Implementation update — XRECORD typed callback retention bounds (2026-10-19)

Closed one concrete gap in the 7S.2c common OBJECTS callback-store census:
`dx_iface::addXRecord` previously copied every typed XRECORD callback into
`dx_data::xRecords` without aggregate admission. The callback now applies
container-lifetime caps of 100,000 records, 1,000,000 retained typed entries,
and `DRW::kMaxDxfBinaryPayloadBytes` (64 MiB) of conservative logical retained
bytes. Accounting covers common table-entry payloads, typed and ordered
variant values (including strings and binary data), handle pairs, opaque raw
data bytes, and the additional dynamic payload retained by an immutable DWG
source snapshot. The snapshot's payload is charged per callback copy even
though the source snapshot allocation is shared, so repeated callbacks cannot
understate the adapter's retention budget.

Limit or allocation failure is sticky. DXF export checks that state before
publishing output and refuses with a specific diagnostic. Parsing and
`DRW_Interface` callback semantics are unchanged; this bound does not qualify
XRECORD graph closure, serializer fidelity, or DWG-origin output.

Generated fast coverage checks payload accounting and copy independence,
exact-fit admission across all three aggregate caps, over-budget refusal, sticky
failure, and preservation of an existing output destination. No drawing

### Cross-route interpretation

This refresh found no new confirmed libdxfrw defect and no unowned peer
failure domain. It does sharpen a common false-positive risk: one codec can
successfully decode a record into a native/raw view, then lose or normalize it
in a separate neutral projection or writer. A single “reader succeeded” or
“output reopened” result would hide which stage changed the source. The
existing PAR-07/S8 identity and loss ledger already supports this distinction;
the plan delta is to make the stage boundary mandatory when a peer exposes
both native and projected models.

For a future named `cadkit` comparison, collect a row per source record with:

1. Source file SHA-256, AC magic, selected artifact/package SHA-256, exact
   source commit (or explicit unbound-artifact status), lockfile, compiler,
   target, enabled features, and reader options.
2. Native-view disposition: handle, raw type/class, decoded/unknown/error
   state, byte span or raw-byte hash when available, owner/reference result,
   and emitted warning/diagnostic.
3. Neutral-projection disposition: mapped kind, retained native ID, owner/block
   membership, coordinate/OCS mapping, and any value or geometry conversion.
4. Output disposition: exact DXF target version and ASCII route, source handle
   to emitted handle/type/owner map, strict independent reopen, unsupported or
   refused records, and final section/EOF closure.
5. For a supported 3D face/mesh subset only, compare explicit coordinates,
   topology and transforms against independently expected values. `cadkit`
   has no DWG writer and no documented ACIS/B-rep semantic gate; do not score
   its neutral projection as a modern solid oracle.

### Implementation-ready and speed-preserving plan delta

1. **No new finding or subplan.** Keep this as a refinement of the existing
   PAR-07/S8 comparator and loss-accounting rows. The current plan remains
   139 findings / 77 top-level subplans.
2. **Eligibility gate first.** Before installing or invoking an optional
   reader, verify the exact package checksum, embedded VCS revision, source
   tag/commit, lockfile, compiler/target and corpus provenance. Mismatch or
   missing metadata makes the candidate advisory only; do not spend time
   debugging an unbound artifact.
3. **Smallest useful composed run.** At the existing cross-codec checkpoint,
   select one already-admitted or locally generated file that exercises the
   exact owner under review. Run one native/raw decode and, only where needed,
   one neutral projection plus ASCII-DXF strict-reopen. Do not run the peer for
   every local slice, add it to mandatory CI, fetch its corpus, or commit an
   external DWG/DXF fixture.
4. **Version fence.** Do not select AC1012 from the advertised matrix alone;
   require a positive, artifact-bound R13 route first. For the remaining
   published AC1014–AC1032 band, record actual per-file dispositions instead
   of converting the matrix into coverage evidence.
5. **Keep the 3D evidence boundary.** Raw modeler bytes, a 3DSOLID/REGION
   shell, mesh projection, native CAD acceptance, and ACIS B-rep semantics are
   distinct evidence. The `cadkit` candidate can inform structural reader or
   2D/explicit-face questions only; it cannot satisfy J256, J260, J268, J284,
   J293, or J295.
6. **Implementation order and validation cadence unchanged.** Continue
   generated fast tests after each local slice. Reserve focused peer checks
   for a real disagreement at the composed gate; reserve full suites and
   native/platform checks for their already planned milestones.

Assessment: this is a provenance/readiness refinement, not a new local defect.
No code, tests, CTest registration, fixture, dependency, peer execution,
platform/native run, support statement, or validation cadence changed.
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and
non-promoting.

Preserve `NOT_AVAILABLE`, `NOT_QUALIFIED`, and unsupported-body states. No result from this candidate alone can promote J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, or J295. |

### Low-cost, implementation-ready optional spike

1. **Eligibility first:** only consider the pinned v1.0.0 tag if its license,
   build toolchain, and host platform are acceptable and already available.
   Record the tag, full commit hash, build options, compiler, OS/architecture,
   and dependency versions. A missing build is `NOT_AVAILABLE`; do not add it
   to CI or block local implementation.
2. **Prove the adapter before testing ACIS:** start with one locally authored,
   asymmetric, analytic solid whose independent face/edge/vertex graph,
   coordinates, bounds, and volume are fixed in the test description. Compare
   the source neutral model with the transferred SMLib model before asking the
   kernel to validate it. Scratch outputs stay under the temporary directory;
   do not download or commit peer DWG/DXF fixtures.
3. **Run one exact-profile payload only if ready:** bind the already-qualified
   SAT/SAB digest to the originating entity, modeler flag/version, and AcDs
   owner/key chain. Require complete parser dispositions and no blocking
   unknown shape records. Do not use the current CADMPEG 0.6.2 binary until its
   embedded codec/source alignment is resolved; a separately pinned 0.6.1
   crate is a different artifact and must be scored as such.
4. **Keep expected values independent:** disable healing; check input/reference
   closure and transferred body counts; compare bounds, analytic volume and
   selected surface/curve evaluations with independently authored values.
   Record SMLib validity/measurement outputs as one kernel observation. Do not
   use tessellated triangle count or `is_manifold_solid()` by itself.
5. **Stop after the decision:** if the adapter cannot faithfully preserve the
   selected topology/profile, mark the route `NOT_QUALIFIED` and retain the
   current HOOPS/Ansys/FreeCAD gates. No additional peer matrix, external
   fixture, build integration, or per-slice validation is justified.

No new local defect, finding, top-level subplan, code, test, CTest, fixture,
dependency, or implementation-order change is warranted. Findings/subplans
remain 139 / 77. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
DEFERRED_EXTERNAL and non-promoting. The candidate adds a future optional
independent-kernel route, not a DWG/DXF or ACIS support claim.

<a id="typed-entity-modeler-and-block-byte-capture-bounds-2026-10-19-implementation"></a>

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c typed entity/compound-geometry and BLOCK byte capture bounds (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The earlier typed callback ceiling limited entity, BLOCK, and TABLE record
counts but did not bound byte-heavy copies. Typed entity admission now uses a
container-lifetime 64 MiB logical retained-byte estimate in addition to the
100,000-record cap. The estimate includes the concrete callback type's inline
size and common `DRW_Entity` dynamic state: layer/linetype/color/proxy strings,
proxy graphics, reactors, data-storage key/data/marker, pending handle
resolution slots, XDATA variants, and nested 102 application-data groups.
`DRW_ModelerGeometry` additionally accounts for its SAT/SAB/raw-frame buffers,
DXF payload chunk/range arrays and marker text, and any already-decoded ACIS
wireframe vertices, edges, faces, controls, loops, and diagnostics. Admission
is checked before the copy; counters advance only after successful insertion.
The `DRW_Surface` family also accounts for ACIS carrier bytes, payload chunks,
cross-section/guide handles, decoded wireframes, and each subtype's binary or
reference data. `DRW_Mesh` accounting includes subdivision and cage vertices,
nested face indices, edges, creases, and override-property vectors.
Further family accounting covers SPLINE knot/weight/control/fit arrays;
POLYLINE and LWPOLYLINE vertex copies, with vertex XDATA and SEQEND state;
HATCH pattern dashes, gradient strings, seeds, loops, boundary handles, and
deep-copied LINE/ARC/ELLIPSE/SPLINE/LWPOLYLINE boundary entities; MLINE's
nested segment/fill parameters; TEXT/MTEXT strings and R2018 arrays; and INSERT
names, attribute handle arrays, deep-copied ATTRIB/embedded-MTEXT records, and
SEQEND state. DIMENSION name/text/style strings, LEADER vertex coordinates,
and nested MLEADER roots, leader lines, break pairs, block labels, text, and
columns are also covered. The legacy POLYLINE handle-list count is exposed
read-only so its copied list nodes are included without changing wire behavior.
`DRW_Table` cell/content trees are now charged for columns, rows, cells,
attributes, content variants/raw values, text, merged ranges, and subrecord
ranges. Its extra `dx_data::tables` snapshot is debited from the same aggregate
typed-entity byte budget before copying; the normal block-entity copy is then
admitted against the remaining budget separately.

BLOCK metadata has a separate 64 MiB aggregate estimate. It covers the inline
`dx_ifaceBlock` storage once, common entity state, block name/xref/description,
preview bytes, and dynamic state copied from each ENDBLK record. ENDBLK budget
or assignment failures are sticky, so export refuses before publication. The
estimates are conservative logical payload/slot accounting, not allocator,
capacity, or RSS limits.

Generated fast controls verify common proxy-string accounting, distinct
modeler raw/SAB/DataStorage payload accounting, surface and mesh payloads,
curve and compound-entity deep-copy accounting, byte-budget refusal without
partial retention, populated TABLE snapshot/entity accounting, BLOCK-start
and ENDBLK accounting/refusal, the existing record-count boundary, sticky
failure, and preservation of an existing output destination. No
committed/downloaded DWG or DXF fixture was used or added.
Strict `-Werror` targets built; the typed-capture selector and focused block
owner/modeler move-dispatch CTests passed (4/4). The full suite was not run.

This advances only the 7S.2c adapter-retention census. Entity-specific dynamic
members outside the paths listed above (including RTEXT, OLE/underlay, and
other compound families) and remaining auxiliary stores still need a fresh
owner-by-owner audit and bounded estimates. Existing parser/member ceilings do
not automatically account for adapter copies. No complete-memory-bound,
serializer, semantic, or 3D support claim is implied. Findings/subplans remain
**139 / 77**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

| Autodesk [3DSOLID DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm) and [common entity codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3610039E-27D1-4E23-B6D3-7E60B22BB5BD.htm) | The 3DSOLID entity has an AcDbModelerGeometry subclass, format version code 70, proprietary modeler data carried as group 1 lines with optional additional group 3 lines, then AcDb3dSolid and a group 350 soft-owner handle to history. The common-entity code 92/310 sequence is specifically proxy graphics, not the 3DSOLID body. Autodesk also cautions not to depend on the displayed order of common group codes. | Treat the modeler payload, version, ordered text fragments, proxy graphics and history reference as distinct fields. Add generated exact carrier controls for repeated group 1/3 boundaries and group-350 resolution/remapping. Never count code 92/310 proxy graphics as ACIS body preservation. Parse fields by code/context, not an assumed global ordering. This proves carrier shape only, not that the payload decodes to valid ACIS or equivalent B-rep geometry. |
| ODA [Open Design Specification 5.4.1](https://static.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) | The R2007 delta introduces the AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b data-storage section for ACIS data; this storage is outside the inline DXF 3DSOLID group-1/3 representation. | Keep DWG inline modeler data and R2007+ AcDs owner/key/payload joins as separate versioned routes. Do not convert one route's positive result into evidence for the other. The checked-in/local specification named by AGENTS.md remains authoritative for byte-layout changes. |
| ACadSharp [declared direction/version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) and open reports for [DWG→DXF SPLINE data](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1299), [DXF writer rejection](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1253), and [R2009 GeoData writer omission](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1261) | The README has separate reader/writer columns by version. The reports identify different failure classes and bind at least #1299 to package 3.8.0 and #1261 to 3.8.0 plus a named master SHA; #1261 describes a missing versioned field tail and a reader/writer field mix-up, while #1253 says permissive readers accepted output that AutoCAD rejected. These are reporter-supplied cases, not independently reproduced results. | Retain existing SPLINE route, versioned writer, DXF group-order/type, GeoData field/roundtrip, and strict-consumer owners. Crosswalk the report shapes to those controls; do not create a new local finding from a peer report or import its fixture/threshold. In peer comparisons, bind exact artifact/source SHA, direction, version, consumer, and expected per-record outcome. |
| LibreDWG [NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | The 0.14 entry documents R2004/AC1018 DWG writer support and separately states R2007 output falls back to R2010; the 0.14.1 entry is a later patch/security release. This makes the implementation's direction and exact output version materially important even within one named family. | Report support at the (input version, operation, output version, feature) level. A successful R2007 read or R2010 fallback write is not direct R2007 writer support. Preserve the existing per-version admission and output-version assertions; do not accept an umbrella “DWG read/write” badge. |
| ezdxf [xref documentation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst) and [DXF entity inventory](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/dxfentities/index.rst) | The xref importer documents only copyable/transformable entities and associated resources, while ACIS entity classes existing in the package do not imply arbitrary-body reconstruction or support in every transfer operation. | Use ezdxf as an optional DXF syntax/carrier comparator for a named operation and profile. Record skipped/unsupported entities. Do not treat class registration, xref copy, SAT/SAB string access, or a flat-face projection as complete semantics. |
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and [import/export preferences](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Import_Export_Preferences.md) | FreeCAD offers built-in C++ and optional legacy Python DXF importers with different feature sets. DWG import invokes an external converter to produce DXF, then selects an importer. The docs state that stock FreeCAD DXF import cannot read embedded ACIS solids. | Keep Linux and Windows native checks at the composed consumer gate, with converter, intermediate DXF, importer backend/preferences, and object result separately recorded. Run the two importer backends as separate rows only where both are in scope. Score their documented 2D and explicit entity subset; classify stock ACIS import as UNSUPPORTED_CONSUMER rather than a failed or successful B-rep result. |

### Implementation-ready plan delta

1. **Use one route row per claim.** The evidence key is now explicitly the
   tuple: input format/version, operation and direction, entity/object family,
   source identity/owner, payload profile, output format/version, and consumer
   platform/backend. Each row records seven non-substitutable stages:
   decode; native/raw capture; neutral-model projection; output-carrier
   emission; strict independent syntax/reopen; independent semantic result;
   and native consumer result. A stage may be `NOT_RUN`, `UNSUPPORTED`,
   `FAILED`, or `PASS`; absent evidence must never be inferred as a pass.
2. **Close the local retention census first.** Continue the active 7S.2c
   fast-slice queue for adapter-owned copies and auxiliary stores. This is
   lower-cost than starting another peer matrix and protects the current
   implementation before adding modeler-geometry breadth. For each concrete
   gap, add only an in-memory generated boundary/ownership test and its owning
   focused CTest; update the progress ledger after the slice. Keep parser
   bounds, post-callback mutation, output serialization, graph closure, and
   semantic support as separate claims.
3. **Close exact DXF 3DSOLID carrier vectors at the existing PAR-07/S8
   owner.** Existing generated `modeler_dxf_writer_matrix_tests` cover format
   version 70, ordered group-1/group-3 emission, following subclass/entity
   sentinels, history handle 350, and ASCII/binary paths across the admitted
   output-version matrix. The generated AC1027
   `dwg2dxf_modeler_dxf_move_dispatch` control now separately covers the
   version-specific common proxy count/data (160/310), group-1 then group-3
   modeler body, following `AcDb3dSolid`/350 fields, and a following LINE;
   assertions prove the proxy bytes do not enter the modeler payload. Keep
   this as carrier/parser evidence only. The typed proxy writer deliberately
   does not authorize 3DSOLID proxy replay, so do not infer proxy-output
   support or relax its fail-closed policy from these controls. Remaining
   profile-specific writer/reference-remap cases must be generated at test
   runtime; do not commit a new DWG/DXF fixture. None of these vectors proves
   ACIS parseability or geometry.
4. **Keep the DWG AcDs route separate.** For each admitted DWG version with
   data storage, assert source entity→history/owner→AcDs key→all payload chunks
   closure, uniqueness, following-record alignment, and output disposition.
   R2007+ section storage must not be synthesized from or credited to the
   inline DXF test. Use the ODA PDF before changing DWG parse/write bytes, and
   use real already-admitted samples or test-time locally-from-scratch data;
   external downloaded samples remain advisory and excluded from commits.
5. **Require semantic evidence only after carrier closure.** For ACIS, keep
   the sequence: exact source/owner/payload closure → exact-profile independent
   parser → validated transfer into the comparison model → analytic topology,
   transform, unit, bounds, and volume expectations → optional native consumer
   that actually consumes that geometry. A same-codec read/write or entity
   shell is not a semantic result. Where no qualifying parser/sample exists,
   preserve `NOT_AVAILABLE`/`NOT_QUALIFIED` and do not promote J256, J260,
   J268, J284, J293, or J295.
6. **Spend validation time at the narrowest useful stage.** After each code
   slice, run the strict build targets and owner-focused generated test(s),
   then the directly adjacent fast regressions. Run a full suite only at the
   plan's existing integration checkpoints; platform FreeCAD, peer releases,
   sanitizers, fuzzing, and independent kernels stay at their composed/phase
   gates. This research adds no per-slice peer/runtime dependency and no full
   suite frequency increase.
7. **Use peer reports as negative-control shapes, not work tickets.** Map
   ACadSharp #1299 to the existing spline read→neutral→DXF route; #1253 to
   exact DXF type/order plus strict independent reopen; and #1261 to versioned
   GeoData field-tail/read-write symmetry. Map LibreDWG's version/direction
   notes to output-version claims. Add a new libdxfrw finding only after an
   admitted local input or generated control demonstrates a specific defect.
   Do not download peer issue attachments or commit external test drawings.

This research adds no confirmed local defect, finding, or top-level subplan;
the plan ledger remains **139 findings / 77 top-level subplans**. It changes
the readiness detail for existing PAR-07/S8 modeler carrier/semantic gates,
the DWG/DXF writer matrix, spline/GeoData owner checks, and FreeCAD consumer
qualification. No support claim is promoted. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; all external/platform
qualification and independent semantic evidence remain advisory until the
existing support gates are met.

<a id="raw-dxf-section-adapter-capture-bounds-2026-10-19-implementation"></a>

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c opaque DXF section callback retention bounds (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The callback census found that `addRawDxfSection` copied every unmodeled DXF
section into `dx_data::rawDxfSections` without adapter-side aggregate limits.
The parser's per-section group and source-text budgets do not bound the second,
persistent adapter-owned vector/string/binary copy. The callback now admits at
most 100,000 retained sections, 4,000,000 aggregate groups, and 64 MiB of
logical retained bytes. The estimate includes the copied section name, group
and raw-value vector slots, string-valued groups, binary group payloads, and
ASCII source spellings. Exceeding a limit or allocation failure sets a sticky
capture-failure flag; DXF export refuses before publication rather than
silently omitting the section.

The in-memory generated test checks exact accounting and deep-copy ownership,
then exercises each limit and verifies a byte-limit failure leaves an existing
destination unpublished. No drawing fixture was added. The already registered
CLI section-passthrough test also exercises locally generated input, output
reopen, ACDSDATA retention, and the section/solid identity relation. Its RAY /
XLINE vector assertion compared decimal strings exactly to 0.6/0.8 even though
the importer/exporter correctly normalizes WCS directions and emits adjacent
binary64 decimal representations on repeated conversion. The matcher now
accepts the small representation drift while retaining checks for both
direction fields and the 3D base point.

Validation passed:

- `cmake -S . -B build-gcc -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5`
- `cmake --build build-gcc --target dxfrw dwg2dxf libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests -j2`

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c IMAGEDEF auxiliary status-key capture bound (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The fresh direct-store census found that invalid IMAGEDEF callbacks insert
their import generation into `invalidImageDefinitionGenerations`. The typed
definition map and its payload are already bounded, but a caller can reuse one
`dx_data` across arbitrarily many imports, making this status set grow once per
invalid generation. Conflicting-definition keys are tied to the already
bounded definition map, but they share the same new aggregate auxiliary-key
budget so the two status sets cannot escape adapter accounting. At most
100,000 unique invalid/conflicting status keys are retained; repeated status
callbacks deduplicate without charging extra keys. Exhaustion marks
IMAGEDEF capture incomplete and the typed-entity gate sticky, so export
preflight refuses rather than treating unrecorded identity failure as clean.

The existing generated image-path control now checks repeated-invalid-key
deduplication, deterministic status-key-limit refusal, and no-output export
refusal. No external image or drawing fixture is added. The rest of the direct
`cData` append census covers typed blocks/entities/tables/images and typed/raw
OBJECTS callbacks; those paths already have record, item/group, logical-byte,
or shared aggregate bounds. This closes this identified auxiliary set-growth
gap but is not a claim that callers cannot mutate public `dx_data` containers
after callbacks.

## Deeper/broader peer test boundaries and faster qualification selection (2026-10-19; research only)

This pass compared current primary project documentation and test tooling for
LibreDWG, ezdxf, and GDAL, then checked the findings against the existing
PAR-07/S8 and writer qualification sequence. The purpose is to select each
peer only for the layer it can measure and avoid turning broad peer test
infrastructure into per-slice work. No peer executable, external drawing,
native CAD application, or geometry kernel was run; no external fixture was
downloaded.

| Source | Current source-backed behavior | Qualification consequence |
|---|---|---|
| [LibreDWG manual](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) and [NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | The manual's approximate coverage headline coexists with an explicit entity/object list lacking test coverage and a statement that unknown types may be retained as opaque blobs without DXF codes. NEWS separately records the R2004 writer addition and says R2007 output falls back to R2010. | Do not use coverage percentages, version ranges, or unknown-blob retention as per-family read/write proof. Pin release/commit and require exact operation, input/output version, and object disposition. A fallback output version is not direct target-version support. |
| ezdxf [loading design](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/develop/pkg-design.rst), [recovery guide](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/recover.html), and [ACIS entity authoring guide](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/tasks/add_dxf_entities.rst) | Loading has a structural/tag stage followed by section/layout creation and owner linking; the recovery/audit route is a distinct API/CLI; ACIS entity factories can carry modeler data but authoring the ACIS payload is delegated to an external library. | Strict read acceptance, repaired/recovered read, owner-graph closure, modeler-carrier preservation, and ACIS semantics must be separate result fields. Do not count a recovery output or entity shell as strict or semantic acceptance. |
| [GDAL DXF driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) and [vector-driver inventory](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/index.html) | The DXF driver reads into OGR features, offers optional unhandled-code capture, reads Binary DXF starting in GDAL 3.12, and writes AutoCAD 2004 DXF from a constrained geometry/style model. Curves may be tessellated; unsupported CAD records/styles are omitted or projected. | Use GDAL only for a named explicit-geometry projection or syntax-consumer question, and record version/options and the expected projection. Its writer or `RawCodeValues` field cannot qualify full-fidelity entity/object serialization, references, or preservation of all unknown codes. |
| [LibreDWG fuzz setup](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg-fuzz) and current [test tooling inventory](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/tree/master) | The published AFL++ setup separates fuzz targets by input/output route, classifies crashes/hangs/leaks, and replays collected regressions through dedicated scripts. | Borrow the phase separation and minimized-regression discipline only at the existing hostile-input/security checkpoint. Do not add peer fuzz runs, peer installations, sanitizer expansion, or full-suite execution to ordinary fast implementation slices. |

### Implementation-ready delta to existing owners

1. **PAR-07/S8 strict reopen:** use a strict parser entry point for the
   independent syntax gate. Record recovery/audit as a separate outcome; if
   recovery is used for diagnosis, preserve the original input hash and list
   every repair before examining the recovered output. Continue the remaining
   profile-specific modeler handle-remap controls locally before the single
   composed independent-reopen checkpoint.
2. **Writer matrix and claims:** add no broad “peer supports DXF/DWG” row.
   Key each evidence row by exact file version, read/write direction, entity or
   object family, strict/recovery mode, raw-versus-projected representation,
   and output version actually observed. A peer's fallback target or opaque
   record retention cannot close a typed serialization claim.
3. **GDAL optional check:** keep its generated AC1027+ modeler path limited to
   the documented ASM bytes/transform projection and ordinary explicit
   geometries. Record Binary DXF capability only for a pinned GDAL >=3.12
   build. Never use OGR feature count as a source-entity conservation check;
   reconcile identity and omissions before evaluating projected geometry.
4. **Speed and validation cadence:** select one peer per unresolved question;
   generate the smallest local control from scratch; build the touched strict
   target, run its fast selector and owning CTest, then defer peer/native/full
   matrix work to the already named composed checkpoint. Expand validation
   only when a shared parser, writer, publication, or resource-boundary owner
   changes. This preserves the plan's reduced full-suite frequency.
5. **Compatibility and scope:** preserve existing 2D LibreCAD and
   LibreCAD_3 behavior while keeping optional 3D carrier and semantic evidence
   separate. Add no peer dependency or fixture. Existing tracked fixtures and
   locally authored scratch/generated controls remain the only fixture
   sources eligible under the current policy.

This research establishes no new local defect and adds no finding or top-level
subplan. It sharpens the existing peer-admission, strict-reopen, writer-version,
and composed consumer gates only; implementation order and per-slice
validation frequency are unchanged. Findings/subplans remain **139 / 77**.
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; this
research does not promote a support claim.

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8 modeler writer cross-profile handle and history remap controls (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The existing modeler writer matrix checked that each output handle was
nonempty and that group 350 matched the first output record, but it did not
assert the source-to-minted remap or verify that the importer restored the
same history edge. The generated matrix now parses the emitted handle and
asserts every modeler source handle `0xFC00 + index` changes on first export
for AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, and AC1027 in both ASCII and Binary DXF.
It then matches imported modeler entity handles to the raw output records and
asserts that the AC1021+ `3DSOLID` history handle resolves to the imported
remapped first modeler; records without history must read back with no history
handle. The existing exact group-350 check therefore verifies the serialized
edge and the local readback verifies the parser-side edge.

The matrix remains generated-from-scratch and does not add persistent DWG/DXF
fixtures. It validates local writer/remap/parser behavior only; the parser used
for local readback is not independent. A local availability probe found no
`ogrinfo`, `gdalinfo`, `ODAFileConverter`, or installed `ezdxf`, so the strict
independent-reopen stage remains for its existing composed checkpoint. No
external runtime was installed.

Validation passed:

- `cmake -S . -B build-gcc -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5`
- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip -j2`

- Scoped `git diff --check` for CMake, test, and plan edits

No full suite, peer runtime, native consumer, or external drawing was used.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c IMAGE/WIPEOUT adapter clip-boundary capture accounting (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The typed entity estimate previously covered common entity strings and the
IMAGE/WIPEOUT inline object size but omitted the dynamically allocated
`DRW_Image::clipPath` coordinates copied into the adapter-owned entity. IMAGE
callbacks also retained a `std::list<dx_ifaceImg*>` lookup node outside the
aggregate typed-entity budget. Both copies are now charged: clip coordinates
are included for IMAGE and inherited WIPEOUT records, and IMAGE preflights the
entity plus list-node estimate together before retaining either. The list
charge includes the stored pointer and two link pointers. If the combined
estimate cannot fit, the callback sets sticky capture failure before partial
entity publication; allocation failure remains fail-closed.

Generated controls use in-memory entities only. They verify exact logical
accounting for an empty IMAGE and its lookup node, a three-point IMAGE clip
path, and a four-point WIPEOUT clip path; they also check deep-copy values and
separate aggregate-budget refusals for the clip payload and IMAGE lookup node.
The vector accounting is logical size-based, not allocator-capacity or RSS
accounting.

## Deeper/broader consumer projection boundaries and operation-specific peer evidence (2026-10-19; research only)

This pass revisited the open-source comparison through three concrete
implementation routes: FreeCAD's documented DXF import profiles, GDAL's
distinct Binary-DXF transport and OGR projection paths, and LibreDWG's own
class-status and fuzz-target model. It used primary project documentation and
repository pages only. No peer was cloned or run, no FreeCAD or GIS
application was installed, and no external drawing was downloaded.

| Source | Newly reconciled evidence | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| [FreeCAD Draft DXF documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and [DWG route](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md) | The documentation repository is archived (read-only) and its Draft DXF page describes two materially different import profiles, both starting at R12. Its C++ importer lists 2D geometry, text, dimensions, leaders, layers and paper-space objects, but block imports retain geometry only and skip text, dimensions and attributes inside blocks. The legacy importer has a different list, including 3DFACE. The page says stock FreeCAD cannot read ACIS/SAT solids and routes DWG through an external converter followed by the selected DXF importer. Its broad sentence that DXF permits 1:1 DWG conversion without loss conflicts with the same page's explicit converter/entity/ACIS limitations. | Treat that broad no-loss sentence as non-evidence. At the existing FreeCAD checkpoint, bind the exact application build, converter and importer backend/settings; predeclare the in-profile entity denominator and block-child behavior. Record skipped or unsupported children as explicit dispositions rather than converter loss or a successful whole-document import. FreeCAD's stock route remains 2D/profile consumer evidence, never ACIS geometry evidence. Because the documentation is archived, use it to define candidate profiles; the pinned application source and runtime result decide actual qualification. |
| [GDAL DXF driver documentation](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | Since GDAL 3.12 the driver can read Binary DXF. The documentation distinguishes a direct Binary-DXF-to-ASCII translation path from OGR feature projection. OGR may tessellate curves, simplify text, drop MLINE styling/HATCH fill, apply INSERT inlining/merging, and skips 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY/SURFACE by default; optional AC1027+ 3D-extensible mode exposes raw ASM bytes plus a transform, not a shape. Raw unhandled group values are opt-in, and the documented DXF writer targets AutoCAD 2004. | Keep two optional route labels: `BINARY_DXF_TRANSPORT` for the direct translation question, and `OGR_DXF_PROJECTION` for an explicitly bounded feature subset. The former can check input/output signatures, strict syntax and ordered tag disposition; it does not establish geometry semantics. For OGR, pin GDAL and the driver/options, enable raw-code capture only when relevant, and set block/text/modeler options deliberately. Do not use its AutoCAD-2004 writer to qualify modern DXF target versions or full-document round trips. Run only the route answering a named open question at the existing composed checkpoint. |
| [LibreDWG manual](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | The manual separates stable, unstable, debugging and unhandled classes; unknown types may be retained as binary blobs without DXF group codes. It separately documents that R2007 DWG writing is unavailable and pre-R13 DXF remains work in progress. | A LibreDWG command that succeeds is not a complete-object or cross-version writer result. In the existing per-source ledger record class status, typed/opaque/ignored disposition, operation and actual output version. Unknown raw blobs without a DXF representation cannot count as emitted DXF objects or as semantic preservation. |
| [LibreDWG fuzz setup](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg-fuzz) and [manual fuzz targets](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | The project separates input and output targets (`indxf`, `injson`, `rw`, `outdxf`, and additional render/serialization targets), and its campaign workflow distinguishes crashes, hangs and leaks and replays prior failures as regressions. | Refine the existing scheduled hardening lane so parser-input, conversion, and writer/output fuzz outcomes remain separately attributable. A parser-only campaign does not qualify serializer paths. Triage saved failures by category and retain only minimized, locally generated regression controls under the plan's existing fixture policy; keep long fuzz outside each implementation slice. This is a cadence/readiness clarification, not a new always-on job. |

### Implementation-ready refinement under existing PAR-07/S8 and 7S owners

1. Before a consumer/peer run, write one route row with the exact binary or
   source revision, platform/build/options, operation and direction, input and
   actual output version, selected importer/driver, and a pre-authored list of
   in-profile source handles plus expected out-of-profile items.
2. For the required FreeCAD row, use the intended backend and converter
   explicitly. Keep modelspace, paperspace, block definitions and INSERT
   instances separate. Include at least one block containing both geometric
   children and text/attribute/dimension children so the documented omission
   boundary is visible. Score only the declared profile; report skipped items
   rather than silently shrinking the denominator.
3. For an optional GDAL question, choose either direct Binary-DXF transport or
   OGR projection, never infer one from the other. In projection mode, capture
   the exact open options and compare source identity/owner, field disposition
   and geometry separately; ASM bytes remain carrier-only evidence. Check the
   emitted `$ACADVER` before interpreting output, and exclude GDAL-authored
   DXF from target-version writer acceptance because its documented writer is
   AutoCAD 2004.
4. For a LibreDWG comparison, record class status and opaque/unhandled counts
   alongside decoded and emitted handles. Bind actual six-byte DWG magic and
   DXF `$ACADVER`; requested CLI version and process exit alone are
   insufficient.
5. Preserve the implementation-time fast loop: focused generated selector,
   touched strict target, owning CTest, scoped diff/receipt checks. Run one
   selected peer route only at the composed checkpoint; keep cross-platform
   native tests and operation-specific fuzz campaigns scheduled there, not
   after each slice. Do not add external drawings, dependencies, or routine
   fixture files in this research update.

### Implementation-ready gates and expedited sequencing

1. **Keep local implementation moving.** This research does not add a blocker or
   reorder the current local queue. Maintain the existing fast slice loop and
   planned composed-checkpoint cadence; do not install a peer, wait for an
   external response, or expand the test suite after each code slice.
2. **Run ACadRust only for a named differential question.** Pin a release or
   commit and toolchain first. Begin with one already-present or locally
   generated benign file per route; store only hashes and manifests in the
   receipt. Do not commit third-party test DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB files unless they
   already belong to this repository or were created locally from scratch and
   pass the existing licensing/provenance policy. Record every object as
   decoded, transformed, preserved opaque, skipped, rejected, or relocated.
3. **Run `cq-acis` only for semantic profiles it accepts.** Extract the
   candidate SAT/SAB bytes through the already-qualified libdxfrw carrier path,
   retain their source entity/AcDs owner-key join, and verify exact stream
   framing/version before invocation. Compare complete supported bodies to
   expected analytic invariants; partial body/entity counts, raw unknown
   records, tessellation alone, or failure of an out-of-profile profile do not
   count as a positive or negative semantic result. Keep the package and its
   large CadQuery/OCCT dependency external to the core library and CI.
4. **Use CAD Assistant narrowly.** The selected macOS ARM64 app may provide a
   native visual/shape-validity observation for a compatible standalone
   SAT/SAB or 3D-DXF input, with exact build and import route recorded. Its
   commercial reader lineage and restricted export mean it cannot establish
   round-trip writer correctness; do not combine it with the separate
   FreeCAD Linux/Windows gate.
5. **Keep support adjudication conjunctive.** A positive 3D claim still needs
   the local versioned carrier/owner association, complete semantic body
   interpretation, expected shape invariants, and the intended consumer route.
   Peer/parser results are individually labeled and cannot substitute for a
   missing stage. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` until their stated external/platform evidence is
   actually captured and reviewed.
