## Deeper/broader peer strictness, recovery, and CI evidence boundaries (2026-10-19; research only)

This pass reviewed current primary project documentation and workflow sources
for LibreDWG, ezdxf, and IxMilia.Dxf. It focuses on a recurring qualification
error: treating a successful parser, recovery tool, project-wide compatibility
claim, or CI badge as proof of strict validity, writer interoperability, or
consumer semantics. No peer was cloned or run, no drawing was downloaded, and
no local test or full suite was run for this documentation-only update.

| Source | Source-backed behavior | Readiness consequence |
|---|---|---|
| [LibreDWG CI workflow](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/.github/workflows/main.yml), [test tree](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/tree/master/test), and [manual](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | The current workflow has distinct debug, release, coverage, ASan, UBSan, 32-bit, and Windows build paths. The `make check` step is conditional on selected Linux matrix configurations, while Windows jobs invoke CTest. The manual separately describes reader/writer coverage and limitations. CI success therefore describes that workflow's tested configuration and corpus, not all format routes or every object family. | Keep local per-slice validation small and deterministic. At scheduled/composed checkpoints, record exact peer commit, workflow/job, compiler/sanitizer, operation, corpus, and output version. Borrow a sanitizer lane only when a shared parser/writer/security boundary changes; do not rerun peer-wide matrices after routine local slices. |
| [ezdxf recovery guide](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/recover.html), [loading design](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/develop/pkg-design.rst), and [DXF data model](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxf_data.html) | The regular loader is the faster strict path; `recover.readfile` is a slower repair/audit path and is documented for ASCII DXF only. Recovery may accept decoding errors in binary payloads such as XRECORD data while reporting audit errors; saving such a document may make it invalid or lose information. The loader also builds sections/layouts and owner links after low-level tag parsing. | In the PAR-07/S8 peer row, report strict-read, recovery-read, audit, owner-graph, and save/reopen outcomes separately. Recovery is diagnostic only and cannot satisfy strict-read, preservation, or support criteria. Never route Binary DXF through this ASCII-only recovery gate. When recovery is used to inspect a failure, keep the original input immutable and record every repair/loss warning before using the recovered result. |
| [IxMilia.Dxf README](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf) and [changelog](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) | The project declares DXF/DXB rather than DWG scope, lists R10–R2014 support with MESH, MLEADER, SURFACE, TABLE, and VIEWPORT exceptions, and states that some generated entities may not open in AutoCAD or may need required child data. Its changelog records compatibility fixes over time, including handle, XDATA, table, and writer behavior. | Admit IxMilia only as a pinned, named DXF syntax/field comparator for a family and version it declares. Record read and write separately; strict-open and target-CAD acceptance separately; preserve entity-level omissions and required-child validation. A green peer parse or broad “complete” status cannot qualify DWG, unsupported DXF families, or AutoCAD interoperability. |

### Implementation-ready, faster peer-check subplan

1. **Every implementation slice:** keep the existing local loop—strict target
   build, one generated focused selector, and its owning CTest. Do not invoke a
   peer, recovery path, native CAD UI, sanitizer matrix, or full suite unless
   the changed owner is a shared security/publication boundary or the plan's
   scheduled composed checkpoint is due.
2. **At a composed DXF checkpoint:** generate one minimal specimen locally
   from scratch for each unresolved family/encoding/profile. First validate
   with libdxfrw's strict reader and inspect the emitted group-code stream;
   then run at most one pinned peer that declares the exact profile. Compare
   source identity, handles/owners, relevant group order and values, and
   per-record disposition—not just exit status or entity count.
3. **Recovery branch:** run ezdxf recovery only after the strict peer read
   fails and only for ASCII DXF. Store the original file hash, recovery
   diagnostics, audit errors, repaired-record list, and whether the recovered
   output reopens strictly. Keep recovery evidence diagnostic and non-promoting.
4. **Writer/consumer branch:** reopen output with a strict parser first; only
   then evaluate the exact target application or converter route at a composed
   checkpoint. Version fallback, recovery, projection, or unsupported-record
   omission is an explicit outcome, not a pass.
5. **Expensive validation trigger:** reserve the broad CI/sanitizer/fuzz lane
   for changes to shared byte readers, token/group-code classification,
   object/entity dispatch, handle/owner closure, serialization/publication, or
   resource-bound enforcement. Otherwise run only focused local tests and
   defer broad qualification, preserving the plan's reduced validation time.

adds no tests, fixture, dependency, peer execution, or support promotion.

## Deeper/broader open-source route identity, independence, and fast peer selection (2026-10-19; research only)

This pass cross-checked current primary project documentation for GDAL's
separate DWG/DXF drivers, FreeCAD's DXF import/export backends and DWG
converter route, and LibreCAD 3's consumer policy. The purpose is to make the
existing PAR-07/S8 peer matrix faster and harder to misattribute: a product
name is not a parser identity, and a conversion pipeline is not one codec
result. This is a documentation/source review only. No repository was cloned,
no peer/native application was run, and no DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB sample was
downloaded or added.

| Route/source | Evidence from current primary sources | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| GDAL [`DXF` driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html), [`CAD` driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/cad.html), [`DWG` driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dwg.html), and [build dependency guide](https://gdal.org/en/stable/development/building_from_source.html) | These are three materially different routes. `DXF` is the built-in DXF reader/writer and since 3.12 accepts Binary DXF; its OGR model is a lossy projection with optional raw-code capture. `CAD` is read-only and is built on internal or externally selected libopencad; it emits only POINT, LINE, CIRCLE/ARC, and 3DFACE geometries in its documented subset, tessellating curved polylines. The separate `DWG` driver uses ODA Teigha rather than the open-source `CAD` backend. The successor [libopencad project](https://github.com/nextgis-borsch/lib_opencad) currently states support only for DWG R2000. | Record `driverShortName`, exact backend/library, versions, build flags, open options, and input AC code for every GDAL run. Never count GDAL `CAD` and direct libopencad as two peer votes; do not identify either as GDAL's separate ODA-backed `DWG` route. Keep `CAD` eligible only for a named AC1015/R2000 geometry-projection question after the exact source/build is pinned. The ODA-backed driver is a separately licensed external route, not an open-source peer. A GDAL DXF transport result and an OGR projection result stay separate. |
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md), [additional-components guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Installing_additional_components.md), and current [`importDXF.py`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDXF.py) | FreeCAD documents two DXF importers (built-in C++ and optional legacy Python) with different supported entity/object profiles. The C++ importer skips text, dimensions, and attributes inside blocks; the legacy list includes 3DFACE. Its exporters are also not interchangeable: documented C++ export targets R14 and omits text/dimensions/colors, while legacy export targets R12 and has its own curve and 3D-flattening limits. Stock FreeCAD does not read embedded ACIS/SAT solids. DWG is processed by an external converter into DXF and then by a selected DXF importer. The guide's broad no-loss sentence conflicts with its explicit converter, backend, and entity limitations. | Treat a FreeCAD result as the complete named pipeline `(converter, output DXF version, importer/exporter backend, application build, options)`. Import and export are separate directions; do not use FreeCAD's own DXF exporter as a libdxfrw writer oracle or infer DWG converter success from the downstream importer. Predeclare a source-entity denominator and expected block-child omissions. Mark the broad no-loss statement non-evidentiary. Stock FreeCAD remains a consumer check for its declared 2D/explicit-entity profile, not an ACIS semantic witness. |
| LibreCAD 3 [DWG support policy](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/blob/master/docs/dwg-support.md) and [build configuration](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/blob/master/README.md) | LibreCAD 3 documents DWG reading through libdxfrw's `dwgRW`, disabled by default behind `WITH_DWG_IMPORT`; it explicitly does not write DWG. This is a downstream application integration path using the same codec family, not an independent parser. | Keep LibreCAD/LibreCAD 3 build and callback checks in the consumer-compatibility lane. They can catch API, adapter, and model-projection regressions in the named consumer, but cannot add an independent DWG parse vote or qualify DWG writing. Enable the option explicitly in the test configuration and capture the libdxfrw revision actually linked. |
| Open-source and proprietary route independence | The GDAL driver split, FreeCAD conversion chain, and LibreCAD 3 policy show that parser, intermediate translator, projection model, writer, consumer, and geometry kernel may be separate implementations or shared dependencies under a single UI/tool name. | Extend the PAR-07/S8 receipt with a small route graph and evidence role for each stage: `input_parser`, `translator`, `projection_or_model`, `writer`, `native_consumer`, and `geometry_kernel`. Mark each edge `same`, `distinct`, or `unknown` by source/build evidence. Only count distinct, version-bound parser implementations as parser comparisons; a wrapper, same-codec reopen, or a second interface over the same backend is correlated evidence. Unknown lineage is `UNKNOWN_NOT_INDEPENDENT`, not assumed independent. |

### Fast route-selection subplan

Apply this once at the plan's already-scheduled composed checkpoint, not after
each implementation slice:

1. **Name the unresolved question first.** Select exactly one lane: DWG byte
   parsing/object disposition; DXF raw syntax or binary transport; supported
   geometry projection; actual downstream application import/export; or 3D
   modeler semantics. Do not run a general peer matrix when a focused local
   generated control and ODA-spec cross-check settle the issue.
2. **Choose the narrowest route that can observe it.** For Binary-DXF transport
   or raw-record grammar use the existing LibreDWG DXB candidate; for selected
   DXF geometry use GDAL's DXF OGR projection only with an explicit expected
   projection; for AC1015/R2000 DWG geometry only, consider pinned libopencad
   through GDAL `CAD`; for native consumer behavior use the exact selected
   FreeCAD converter plus importer, or the named LibreCAD consumer build. Do
   not use GDAL `CAD` for modern DWG or solid semantics.
3. **Bind every pipeline edge before execution.** Record source revision or
   package checksum, build/configuration, driver/backend, OS/architecture,
   source hash/provenance, input magic or `$ACADVER`, requested and actual
   output version, options/preferences, and per-source-entity disposition.
   For FreeCAD DWG import, force the desired converter instead of Automatic
   fallback; verify the actual output file and `$ACADVER` before import.
4. **Compare like with like.** For raw transport compare ordered tags and
   record disposition; for projection compare only predeclared geometry and
   fields, accounting for tessellation, expansion, omission, and owner loss;
   for native import compare per-handle native objects and explicit skips.
   Counts, successful process exit, a rendered view, and a reopened file alone
   are not semantic parity.
5. **Keep 3D qualification conjunctive.** Carrier extraction, complete
   ACIS/AcDs ownership, payload parsing, valid complete body topology, analytic
   invariants, and the target consumer remain separate gates. None of the
   newly reviewed routes closes the independent ACIS/AcDs semantic condition
   or native Linux/Windows FreeCAD condition.
6. **Keep implementation speed.** A peer run is optional and question-driven;
   no runtime dependency, CTest, fixture, or per-slice peer invocation is
   added. Generate any minimal controls locally from scratch in temporary
   storage; retain only hashes/manifests under the current fixture policy.
   Leave broad suites, cross-platform FreeCAD, and native/3D observations at
   their existing composed checkpoints.

This update reconciles source-level route identity and directionality; it
identifies no new confirmed libdxfrw defect and adds no finding, numbered
subplan, test, fixture, dependency, required peer run, or support promotion.
Findings/subplans remain **139 / 77**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. No local build or test
was run for this research-only update.

each source `DRW_SortEntsTable`, including both source handle vectors, then

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c lazy raw-section projection copy (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Previously, every export copied `dx_data::rawDxfSections` into a mutable
working vector before checking whether AcDs projection would append anything,
then copied that vector again into the codec. The projection helper now reads
the source sections by const reference and builds a working copy only after a
candidate AcDs section has passed its existing graph/schema checks. On the
common no-append path, the original collection is copied once directly into
the codec. On the append path, the isolated source copy plus generated section
is moved into the codec. Copy/allocation failure returns a preflight failure;
source sections are never mutated. This removes one full source-section clone
from every no-op export without changing projection eligibility or raw replay
rules.

disposition is recorded in [the superseding 2026-10-20 section](#deeperbroader-cadmpeg-v062-tag-source-release-digest-and-sat-comparator-refresh-2026-10-20-research-only).
The historical table below remains as an audit trail; its recommendation to
treat v0.6.2 as unconfirmed is no longer current. No package was downloaded
and no peer was executed.

against the currently indexed upstream release page, the published Rust
packages, and the project's release configuration. The practical result is

was executed, and no local code, test, fixture, finding, or support claim

Do not count ACadSharp and CADKit as independent votes for those stages; other CADKit stages may be source-distinct but remain unaudited here. Before any optional invocation, resolve the exact crates.io version, immutable source commit/tag, package checksum, full workspace lockfile, and the version actually executed. Its DXF-only route may be considered separately for a named 2D projection question, but it does not add DWG or 3D/ACIS evidence. |
| CADKit [repository README](https://github.com/TNYCL/cadkit) and [CI history](https://github.com/TNYCL/cadkit/actions) | The project describes allocation/size limits, warning-based recoverability, and fuzz targets for each reader in CI; the repository page shows a young project with a small commit/release history. These are implementation and maturity signals, not local security verification. | Carry forward bounded-allocation, explicit-unknown, and malformed-input-fuzzing patterns as review prompts only. Do not import the project, add a dependency, or treat its CI history as proof of this library's safety. |

### Fast optional procedure at the existing composed peer checkpoint

1. Do not add CADKit to normal builds, CTest, dependencies, slice gates, or
   external blockers. Revisit only if a named 2D/structural differential
   question remains after local fast checks.
2. Resolve one exact version and immutable source revision first. Record the
   package checksum, Cargo lockfile, Rust/toolchain version, target OS/arch,
   runtime version output, and the reported source-provenance overlap. If the
   0.2.0/0.2.1/0.3.0 surfaces cannot be reconciled, skip without delaying work.
3. Use only locally authored controls or already-approved repository samples;
   keep generated controls in a temporary directory. Do not copy CADKit, Tika,
   ACadSharp, or other external sample bytes into this repository.
4. Compare exact supported type/version profiles by handle, owner/layout,
   source coordinates and normalized values against a separately authored
   expectation. Record `Unknown`, warning and unsupported dispositions rather
   than counting them as decoded. Keep the candidate's own DXF oracle separate
   from its DWG reader result.
5. Treat R2007 container results as lineage-correlated with ACadSharp. Treat
   ACIS as opaque-carrier-only; CADKit does not decode its B-rep semantics,
   does not read/write DWG, and cannot qualify AcDs links or native FreeCAD.

it adds no implementation finding, numbered or top-level subplan, required

<a id="deeperbroader-cross-project-solid-carrier-failure-chains-and-evidence-ceilings-2026-10-19-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader cross-project solid-carrier failure chains and evidence ceilings (2026-10-19; research only)

This review compares the *operation and stage* each project documents, not its
headline file-format list. It refines the existing PAR-07/S8 modeler-carrier,
semantic, and native-consumer gates; it does not add a local defect, finding,
top-level subplan, dependency, fixture, test, peer-run requirement, or support
claim. Primary sources reviewed include the [LibreDWG 0.14.1 NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS), its [open AcDs loss report #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411), [ezdxf 1.4.5 ACIS API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) and [FAQ](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/faq.html), the [ACadSharp version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/README.md) and its [open issue list](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues), and [GDAL's CAD](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/cad.html) and [DXF](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) driver documentation.

| Route / evidence | What the current source supports | Readiness boundary for libdxfrw |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG reader/writer and `dwg2dxf` / `dxf2dwg` | NEWS records improvements to ACIS carriers and 2004+ sections but also says the AcDsPrototype_1b datastore was not fully decoded and SAB extraction used brute-force search. Open issue #1411 reports that a pinned LibreDWG 0.14.8593 Linux build preserves `REGION` records yet drops AC1027+ AcDs/SAB payloads in both directions; its reproducible case is generated from scratch, and its separate real DWG is confidential and unavailable. This is a specific peer failure report, not a verified current-master result. | Do not use entity count, conversion exit status, or that peer's result to qualify libdxfrw. If the peer is run at an existing composed gate, bind exact source/build, test only a locally generated control, and compare the full entity-to-section association and payload hashes. A peer failure is a comparator limitation, not a libdxfrw defect. Keep independent local expected values. |
| ezdxf 1.4.5 DXF and ACIS APIs | The API documents SAT/SAB loading and export functions, a mesh-to-ACIS body path, and version routing (SAT through R2010, SAB for R2013/R2018). It explicitly warns that only a limited subset of ACIS entities is parsed and unsupported data is lost; its mesh conversion emits only flat polygonal faces and cannot tessellate curved surfaces without a kernel. Its FAQ still says SAB cannot be written and no ACIS creation is provided, contradicting the current API page. | Resolve the documentation contradiction against the exact immutable package/source before using ezdxf as a scratch producer. Even then it is a useful exact-profile DXF transport/parser route, not a semantic oracle for its own output, arbitrary ACIS, curved surfaces, DWG AcDs joins, or native acceptance. Author expected geometry independently and report unsupported ACIS nodes explicitly. |
| ACadSharp | Its README declares DWG/DXF reader/writer support through AC1032, but current open reports include an AC1032 INSERT reader loss (#1172), 3DSOLID/REGION omission in the DXF writer (#1195), and AutoCAD rejection of specific DXF group-code output (#1253). These are issue reports, not independently reproduced tests here. | Treat its matrix as route candidacy only. Any differential run must name direction, version, entity family, immutable package/source, and exact result denominator. Require missing, extra, wrong-type, skipped, and lossy entities to remain visible; do not let a broad version check stand in for writer acceptance or solid semantics. |
| GDAL / OGR | The `CAD` DWG driver is read-only and documents POINT, LINE, CIRCLE/ARC, and 3DFACE projection. The DXF driver can optionally expose AC1027+ 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY/SURFACE as raw ASM bytes plus a transform, while explicitly saying those are not converted to OGR geometry. Blocks and other data are projected according to its options. | Use GDAL only for its named 2D projection, 3DFACE geometry, or raw-carrier transport questions. Raw bytes/transform are not a decoded B-rep, topology result, complete drawing, or DWG AcDs association. Count direct DXF and OGR projection as separate stages, not separate semantic votes. |

### Implementation-ready gate refinement

Apply this only inside the existing 3D/PAR-07/S8 checkpoints. Keep ordinary
implementation slices on fast local tests; no external project becomes a
per-slice prerequisite.

1. For each local generated control, key the expected/observed ledger by
   `(container, AC code, direction, entity family, carrier route, source
   handle)`. For modeler carriers, record SAT versus SAB, modeler version,
   inline versus section-level storage, history/owner handles, record and
   chunk counts, payload byte length/hash, and an explicit disposition for
   absent, empty, unsupported, malformed, and successfully retained bodies.
2. Keep routes separate: DXF AC1015–AC1024 inline SAT/chunks; DXF AC1027+
   ACDSDATA/SAB records and owner keys; DWG AC1024 inline SAB; and DWG
   AC1027+/AC1032 AcDsPrototype_1b/DataStorage association. Passing one row
   never promotes adjacent versions, entity types, or carrier layouts.
3. At the carrier gate, assert source entity identity, exact bytes/hash,
   version/frame metadata, history/reference closure, and strict emitted-DXF
   reopen. A matching payload hash establishes preservation only. Do not
   infer that a valid solid, complete body, closed shell, or correct placement
   was produced.
4. At the semantic gate, require an exact-profile independent parser/kernel
   route with separate provenance from both the scratch producer and the
   libdxfrw writer. Compare independently authored analytic expectations:
   expected body/lump/shell/face counts where stable, closedness/manifold
   status, volume and bounds within declared tolerance, orientation, and
   placement. Preserve a per-source-handle `decoded / partial / fallback /
   unsupported / rejected` outcome; a mesh preview or nonempty entity is not
   a pass. If the independent route cannot parse the exact profile, leave the
   semantic row `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and continue the local queue.
5. At the native-consumer gate, record the complete pipeline and platform
   (converter, output DXF version, importer/backend, application build,
   options, modeler/kernel path). LibreCAD and LibreCAD_3 2D compatibility
   remains its own consumer lane. Stock FreeCAD DXF import and GDAL's OGR
   projection cannot certify ACIS B-rep support.
6. Optional peer work stays bounded: first resolve ezdxf's SAB documentation
   conflict against a pinned artifact; then, only if a named question remains,
   run one peer at the existing composed checkpoint. Use a temporary
   locally-generated control, never a confidential or downloaded peer
   drawing. Do not install a peer, add a dependency/CTest, or add a recurring
   full-suite run for this research. Re-open the peer screen only after a
   release/source change, a merged fix, or a new reproducible report changes
   one of these exact route boundaries.

This review did not clone or execute any peer, install ezdxf/CADMPEG/ACadSharp,
download a drawing, or run a local build/test. It changed no support statement

<a id="deeperbroader-peer-failure-taxonomy-and-fastest-evidence-path-2026-10-19-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader peer failure taxonomy and fastest evidence path (2026-10-19; research only)

This source refresh adds a cross-project test-selection and failure-taxonomy
crosswalk to the existing implementation plan. It does not promote project
issue reports to local defects. Sources reviewed were LibreDWG's
[format/API documentation](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi),
[test registration](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt),
and [fuzzing guidance](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/HACKING);
ezdxf's [format scope](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf) and
[test instructions](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/setup.rst);
and ACadSharp's open [#1281](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1281)
and [#1279](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1279) reports.

| Peer source | Verifiable observation | Local plan consequence / evidence ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG | Its manual states that unhandled classes/invalid object types are non-critical and unknown types may be kept as binary blobs without DXF codes. CMake separately registers shell-level `alive`, DXF, JSON, DWG-filter and SVG tests plus unit tests; its HACKING guide describes parser fuzz targets as a separate activity. | Preserve unknown data only as the exact opaque route actually implemented; do not count it as typed support or claim it will appear in DXF. Keep fast owning tests and composed converter/fuzz checkpoints separate. A successful peer parse or blob count is not parity evidence. |
| ezdxf | Its README declares DXF ASCII/Binary read/write across named releases, with older revisions read-only and upgraded on write. Its documented test command separates `tests` and `integration_tests`; the repository is a DXF implementation, not a DWG codec or ACIS kernel. | Use it only for a named DXF structural/typed route with a pinned package/source. Do not make installation or its full test suite a per-slice prerequisite; no same-library self-read can prove independent semantic correctness. |
| ACadSharp #1281 | The open report describes recursion proportional to consecutive comments, XDATA application blocks, and WIPEOUT clip groups; the reporter gives 15–85 KB examples and states ASCII/Binary share affected reader paths. It names ACadSharp 3.8.0 and says the same code is on master; no local reproduction occurred. | The actionable local invariant is bounded iterative progress and controlled record-level failure, not the peer's file sizes/counts. If these parser paths change, use a small generated ASCII/Binary pair and check the next entity/section sentinel; retain existing parser hardening owners. |
| ACadSharp #1279 | The open report describes AC1014 2D POLYLINE child VERTEX records with `AcDbVertex` but no more-specific subtype marker; a peer placeholder-to-typed cast then aborts the whole file. The reported workaround infers from parent flags, which is not itself format authority. | Retain the local existing parent/child/sentinel route and authoritative-format gate: infer only where the format contract justifies it; otherwise refuse/drop only the malformed record with a diagnostic and continue safely. Do not treat this recovery control as valid-format support. |

### Implementation-ready test selection

For each behavior-bearing slice, select one narrow layer and reuse the
existing focused test target/selector. Keep the following order:

1. **Parser/model change:** a tiny locally generated input proves exact fields,
   bounded progress, diagnostics, and a following-record sentinel. Exercise
   ASCII and Binary only when both encodings traverse the changed code.
2. **Adapter/graph change:** exercise owner/handle closure and callback
   publication/rollback on generated data, including same-object retry if the
   public operation promises retryability.
3. **Writer change:** assert required section/record framing, target version,
   source-to-output identity, and a strict local re-open. A successful exit or
   entity count alone is insufficient; any intentionally unsupported or
   opaque record needs an explicit disposition.
4. **Claim requiring independence:** defer one pinned external parser or
   native consumer to its already-composed checkpoint. Bind its exact
   executable/package, operation, version, and source hash; never add it as a
   routine dependency of fast slices.
5. **Security/resource claim:** keep sanitizer/fuzz work at the planned
   composed checkpoint unless a slice changes a memory-safety boundary. A
   peer's crash threshold is a test shape, not a format/resource limit.

This keeps a useful distinction explicit throughout implementation:
`decoded` is not `typed`; `opaque-retained` is not `re-emitted`; `emitted` is not
`strictly reopened`; `reopened` is not semantically correct; and semantic
correctness is not native-consumer acceptance. No implementation order or
validation frequency changes: the smallest relevant local check remains the
per-slice gate, with broad suites and external/native routes at composed gates.
The existing total is unchanged at **139 findings / 77 top-level subplans**.
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain explicitly
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; no peer evidence can promote them.

This was a read-only source review plus plan crosswalk: no peer was cloned or
run, no external drawing was downloaded, and no local build/test was run.
No fixture, dependency, test, finding, or top-level subplan was added.

### Implementation-ready bounded procedure

At the existing composed PAR-07/S8 checkpoint only:

1. Select the platform wheel from the hashes above; verify the file hash and
   PyPI provenance, then record a locked Python 3.11+ environment and exact
   CadQuery/OCCT runtime versions. Do not add any of these dependencies to the
   library, standard build, fast tests, or CI.
2. Generate a temporary, from-scratch analytic control with an independently
   authored expected manifest (body count, source units/tolerance, topology,
   bounds, orientation/closure, and analytic volume). Keep the producer, DXF
   or DWG container extractor, cq-acis parser, and expected-value authoring
   provenance separate. Do not use or commit cq-acis corpus files.
3. For each exact route, log container/version/direction/entity type/handle,
   owner and insertion path, carrier kind/signature/save version, byte length
   and SHA-256, and every parser/converter diagnostic. For modern DWG AcDs,
   record the independently decoded section record/key and the entity-handle
   association before extraction; for DXF, record the independently parsed
   entity/record framing and raw carrier source.
4. Accept a semantic row only if all referenced geometry for every expected
   body converts; report raw/unknown/unsupported nodes, failed bodies, topology
   and validity, shell closure/orientation, bounds, volume, units, and placement.

   omitted auxiliary body or unresolved source handle.
5. Run native FreeCAD Linux/Windows only in its separate planned product
   checkpoint, through the intended converter and importer, and report its
   unsupported ACIS profile explicitly. Use the already-selected official
   macOS ARM64 CAD Assistant only as the separate optional native-reader
   observation. A failure or unavailable route remains NOT_QUALIFIED; continue
   local implementation without waiting for it.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c Background/SUN handle-list callback retention (2026-10-19; generated local fast slice, uncommitted)

The 7S.2c lifetime audit found that `fileExport()` moved
`m_backgroundHandlesToWrite` and `m_sunHandlesToWrite` into the codec before
`dxfW->write()`. During that write, `dx_iface::writeObjects()` still needs
those adapter-owned lists to emit the paired raw OBJECTS carriers; the codec
also needs independent copies for reference validation. Moving the vectors
left the ACAD_BACKGROUND dictionary/root intact while omitting Background/SUN
raw objects from ASCII and Binary output.

The adapter now retains both lists through `writeObjects()`, passing them to
`dxfRW` via the existing const-reference setters, which make the separate
writer-side validation copies. The newly collected Background handle vector
moves into adapter ownership only after its consumer-reference validation,
avoiding the earlier local-to-member copy without sacrificing the callback's
required lifetime. No API, layout, graph rule, or handle-remap policy changed.

Validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target dwg2dxf libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests -j2`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --background-sun-callback-retention`
  (ASCII and Binary graph, carrier, and reference cases)
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures$' --output-on-failure`
  (1/1, 3.84 sec)
- `cmake --build build-gcc --target lc3_compat_check -j2`
- Scoped `git diff --check` and receipt `jq empty`

No new test or CTest registration, fixture, dependency, full suite, peer/native
run, or support promotion was added. Findings/subplans remain **139 / 77**;
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and
non-promoting. The broader 7S.2c retained-output/callback-copy census continues
in the uncommitted shared worktree.

<a id="deeperbroader-ft-model-2d-dwg-renderer-evidence-ceiling-and-comparator-admission-2026-10-19-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader ft_model 2D DWG-renderer evidence ceiling and comparator admission (2026-10-19; research only)

### Why this peer is worth tracking

The already-tracked `hhcme/ft_model` entry is rechecked here against its current README and the two dated status/review records. The project advertises direct DWG/DXF input, an entity scene graph, and Canvas/WebGL-style 2D rendering with JSON scene export; the README names R2000, R2004, R2007, R2010, R2013, and R2018 families. This remains a potential observer for the same narrow projection question—whether selected 2D geometry and presentation survive into a rendered scene—not a new parser vote or a substitute for reader/writer, raw-record, or application interoperability evidence.

This remains a *candidate*, not a qualified implementation. The project README's “Full DXF Support” and multi-version claims are project-authored statements, not independently reproduced results. `PROJECT_STATUS.md` explicitly labels itself historical and superseded by the V1.0.0 plan; its dated 2026-04-23 snapshot reports 99.8% / 99.99% / 97.0% matches for selected R2010/R2013/R2007 files but only 37.8% for one R2004 file, with a major object-map gap and missing entities. The May 2026 final review also records the R2004 loss and unresolved block/insert issues. These dated reports demonstrate why headline feature lists and one aggregate percentage cannot establish current, version-wide support; because the status document is explicitly historical, its numbers must not be represented as current project status.

### Independence and evidence ceiling

The project describes its parser as self-developed, but the consulted material is not a source-level provenance audit. More importantly, its historical regression method compares entities against LibreDWG DWG-to-DXF output extracted with ezdxf, and its format notes explicitly use LibreDWG source as a read-only format-understanding reference. Therefore classify the route as **implementation-distinct candidate / expected-value lineage correlated / source provenance not audited**. It may expose a different parser's disagreement, but agreement with its output is not independent semantic corroboration. Do not use its output as a golden file or assert that its semantics are independent of LibreDWG.

The relevant output is a rendered/scene projection. It cannot establish complete entity/object coverage, preservation of unknown records, exact raw DXF/DWG fields, writer round trips, 3D topology, ACIS/ACDS body semantics, ownership/history closure, or acceptance by LibreCAD, LibreCAD_3, or FreeCAD. The README documents JSON scene export and an active export-format workstream; no DXF writer behavior was established in this review. Treat absent documentation as “not evidenced,” not as proof a capability does not exist.

### Implementation-ready admission sub-plan

1. **Freeze before execution.** Resolve and record an immutable upstream commit (not `main`), archive the exact README/status/test-strategy documents used, record the source tree hash, build configuration, compiler/toolchain, executable hash, and license. Inspect source attribution and dependency history sufficiently to label provenance; do not copy code or add a dependency. If source revision or executable cannot be bound, keep the route at `SOURCE_REVIEW_ONLY`.
2. **Clear input provenance.** Use only an already-owned, license/provenance-cleared DWG that overlaps the local matrix, or a control created locally from scratch and independently described by analytic expected values. Do not fetch/copy `ft_model`'s `test_dwg`, third-party fixtures, screenshots, reference JSON, or golden outputs into this repository. If no eligible DWG overlaps, do not run the DWG comparator; the repository's synthetic DXF controls may assess only its DXF/rendering route and must not be reported as DWG evidence.
3. **Name the claim and boundary.** Record source file hash, AC version, input operation, supported entity subset, units/coordinate frame, layout/model-space selection, and rendering options. Capture parser diagnostics, dispatched/success/skip counts when exposed, JSON scene entities, and rendered geometry separately. Do not flatten an unreported skip into success. Compare only agreed 2D primitives and explicit transforms/styles with tolerance and independently authored expected values; exclude text/font appearance unless font resources and renderer configuration are fixed.
4. **Run only at an existing composed checkpoint.** Build/run the pinned optional tool outside the production build and only when a specific unresolved PAR/S8 projection question benefits from it. Keep its run out of per-slice gates and normal fast validation. A mismatch becomes a localized investigation lead; first identify which stage differs (decode, scene projection, block expansion, or rendering), then reproduce locally with an owned/generated minimal control before changing libdxfrw.
5. **Promote no support claim from this lane.** A passing visual/scene comparison is one observation only. Any claim still needs the plan's applicable parser/raw preservation, output/reopen, independent semantic, and named native-consumer gates. Keep the lane optional if environment/build cost exceeds the question's information value.

| Evidence lane | Allowed use | Not established |
|---|---|---|
| Source/document review | Identify architecture, stated version families, claimed scene/render features, and candidate test methods | Current correctness, code provenance, or any libdxfrw behavior |
| Pinned runtime on eligible overlapping DWG | Optional 2D scene/render differential for named primitives and explicit placement/style | Full DWG semantics, 3D/ACIS, complete preservation, or native acceptance |
| ft_model regression output / LibreDWG-derived expected data | Explain the peer's own historical comparison method | Independent truth, a gold oracle, or support promotion |
| ft_model DXF controls | Optional DXF parse/render observation only, with local expected geometry | DXF writing, lossless round trip, DWG parsing, or writer parity |

### Plan delta and current disposition

Retain the existing `ft_model` optional peer entry and refine its evidence label to `IMPLEMENTATION-DISTINCT-CANDIDATE / CORRELATED-ORACLE / PROVENANCE-UNVERIFIED / NOT-QUALIFIED`. Do not create a new finding, local test, CTest, dependency, fixture, generated reference output, or recurring peer-validation step. Do not change the fast local test order or frequency; full suites and native/peer qualification remain at their existing composed gates. No local source, support matrix, or issue disposition changed during this research pass. Findings/subplans remain **139 / 77**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; this source cannot promote their status or any DWG/DXF/3D support claim.

All are mutable `main`-branch pages; no immutable commit, checkout, build, fixture inspection, or runtime was performed.

research. It reconciles current ezdxf API documentation with its explicitly
old FAQ, checks LibreDWG's public modern-ACIS reproduction and reader source,
and maps a reported AcDs schema-index vulnerability shape to the local
bounded parser. No peer binary, CAD application, kernel, or downloaded
drawing was run or installed.

SAT v700 is the documented carrier for DXF R2000–R2010; SAB v21800 is documented for R2013/R2018. The API specifically supports mesh-derived flat polyhedra; it says unsupported ACIS entities become NONE_ENTITY and are lost, arbitrary load/re-export is unsupported, and curved-face tessellation requires a kernel. Its documentation reports polyhedra exported as SAT/SAB loading in Autodesk products or BricsCAD, but this review did not reproduce that result. | Admit ezdxf as an optional, pinned scratch producer for mesh-derived polyhedral DXF controls only. The current, detailed ACIS API documents a narrower mesh-derived authoring route. A separate AutoCAD R2018 file is confidential and unavailable. The issue is not an independently reproduced current-master result; the reported byte length is not a golden payload hash. | Use the public generated example as an optional regression-profile recipe at the existing composed carrier checkpoint. Generate in disposable scratch, record the exact ezdxf artifact, target AC code, source entity handle, ACDSDATA key/association, payload length and digest at each hop, and strict reopen diagnostics. Construct expected geometry and metrics independently; never use the expected 5,489 length alone as a correctness oracle. Do not download or commit the confidential drawing. |

Do not transfer LibreDWG's implementation or limitations into libdxfrw. Use the ODA v5.4.1 specification—not peer code—as the authority for local DWG field layout and legal values. |

Verify adjacent valid segment/record handling only where the current boundary policy proves safe continuation. Do not add a persistent DWG/DXF fixture or new CTest registration. |

### Implementation-ready, fast-first follow-through

1. **Small local safety slice:** extend the existing in-memory DataStorage
   schema builder and owning graph-preservation test. Keep a valid type-15
   control, then malformed type-16 and UINT32_MAX cases. Assert the named
   diagnostic, bounded failure, stable surrounding state, and no type-table
   access on invalid input. Build the owning target and run its focused
   selector/CTest only; do not run the full suite for this isolated guard.
2. **Optional carrier-source slice at the composed checkpoint:** use a pinned
   ezdxf package in an isolated environment to create an AC1032 DXF from
   scratch. Prefer an explicitly dimensioned closed mesh with an independently
   authored metric manifest; keep REGION and 3DSOLID as separate entity-family
   rows. Confirm actual $ACADVER, non-empty SAB, ACDSDATA section/record
   association, and output hash. The issue's cube recipe is a reproducible
   starting profile, not a committed or byte-for-byte golden fixture.
3. **Route ledger:** compare source DXF ACDSDATA→libdxfrw parse→DWG AcDs
   write→libdxfrw DWG read→DXF ACDSDATA. At every boundary record source
   handle, entity type, owner/key, body disposition, payload byte count and
   hash, plus unrelated sentinel entities and strict parse status. Separate
   legacy inline SAT from modern section-level SAB; a pass in one route does
   not qualify the other.
4. **Semantic boundary:** ezdxf generation plus ezdxf readback is one
   implementation lineage and can only establish its generated carrier
   shape. A semantic pass requires an independently authored expected model
   and a distinct parser/kernel/native route with all unsupported records
   disclosed. Flat-face mesh extraction cannot qualify curved geometry.
5. **Peer/security boundary:** if a LibreDWG comparison is useful, run one
   immutable release/commit at the existing composed checkpoint, record
   platform/build options and exact executable hash, and do not generalize
   issue #1411's 0.14.8593 report to a later release or mutable master. The

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c ACIS-history proxy direct index (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

`collectAcdsHistoryProxyGraph()` indexed each source proxy handle to a vector
of candidate pointers, then performed a second map lookup to append the sole
candidate. Duplicate handles were already rejected during initial insertion,
so the vector could only contain one item and its per-proxy allocation did
not provide ambiguity handling. The index now stores one direct pointer per
handle, reserves for the admitted source count, and catches index-allocation
failure as a graph rejection. The existing missing/duplicate/wrong-owner
refusal and diagnostic context are preserved; no accepted history graph or
serialized output changes.

three-object proxy-history closure, duplicate proxy-handle rejection, mixed
class rejection, and malformed-edge refusal. No new selector or CTest was
needed, and no DWG/DXF fixture was added.

This pass broadened the source comparison across ACadSharp, LibreDWG, ezdxf,

sections for the one report that conflicts with the format reference. Peer
issues and support matrices are discovery evidence, not format authority or

| Evidence | What it establishes—and does not | Plan consequence |

| ACadSharp open [#1277](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1277) and ODA v5.4.1 §§20.4.71, 20.4.86, 20.4.89 | ACadSharp 3.7.16’s reporter describes AutoCAD LT 2026 AUDIT failures after an AC1032 no-op DWG round-trip, including loss of standalone `AcDbMLeaderObjectContextData`; two writer changes were needed in the reported private drawings. The suggested removal of a bit between context version and default flag conflicts with ODA §20.4.89, which specifies the R2010+ base sequence `BS version`, `B has file to extension dictionary` (default true), `B default flag` (default false). §20.4.71 adds the scale hard-pointer; §20.4.86 specifies the MLeader context’s root/line counts and content fields. The peer’s AutoCAD result and proposed field removal do not supersede ODA or establish a libdxfrw repro. | Keep the exact peer fix out of the implementation. Add a focused ODA-profile check to existing PAR-20/7F.1 before any MLeader context expansion. Distinguish the context’s base bit from the common object extension-dictionary-present flag; they are separate fields. Where a producer trace conflicts with the specified profile, identify the exact version/class/profile and preserve both raw evidence and the disputed cursor before deciding on compatibility behavior. |
| ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.86 `MLeaderAnnotContext` and local [`parseMLeaderRoot`](src/drw_entities.cpp) | The table specifies flags 290/291 followed directly by 3BD connection point and 3BD direction, with no `IF` guards. A full table review confirms ODA marks conditions explicitly on conditional fields elsewhere in the same description. The embedded local parser instead gates each point on its corresponding flag, and the nearby comment cites LibreDWG `dwg2.spec`. ODA therefore settles the specified embedded-body profile; the absence of a producer-authored local sample leaves only producer-specific deviations unqualified. | For the ODA-profile embedded MLeader entity, parse and write both 3BD fields unconditionally after the two flags, and cover all flag combinations with cursor/following-field sentinels. Do not use this result to reuse the embedded body as a standalone `AcDbMLeaderObjectContextData` body: its base preamble, scale link, owner graph, and publication path remain distinct and the adapter remains fail-closed. |
| Local [`DRW_ObjectContextData::parseDwg`](src/drw_objects.cpp), [model](src/drw_objects.h), [DWG object dispatch](src/intern/dwgreader.cpp), and [adapter callback](dwg2dxf/dx_iface.cpp) | At this research snapshot, the parser read `m_classVersion` then `m_defaultFlag` without ODA’s intervening R2010+ context bit, and the model had no field for it. The generated implementation follow-through below now adds the field and gates its read at AC1024+; this closes that local base-profile mismatch for the specified profile. <a id="deeperbroader-dwg-eed-unsigned-size-and-same-appid-continuation-boundary-2026-10-19-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader DWG EED unsigned-size and same-APPID continuation boundary (2026-10-19; research only)

This pass reconciles a fresh peer writer failure against ODA's EED field
definition, LibreDWG's public bitcode types and EED model, and the existing
local encoder/reader tests. The key correction is that ACadSharp's reported
32,768-byte failure must not be turned into a 32,767-byte format limit. The
remaining uncertainty is specific to the local writer's repeated same-APPID
blocks above one unsigned-BS maximum. No code, test, fixture, dependency, peer
binary, or native CAD application was run or changed in this research pass.

| Evidence | Finding and confidence boundary | Plan disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ODA v5.4.1 [§28, Extended Entity Data](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf), p. 269 | ODA defines each EED block as `Length | Application handle | Data items`; `Length` is a 16-bit `BS` counting item bytes, excluding the length field, its bit-pair, and the APPID handle. Blocks repeat until a zero length. This establishes an unsigned-width boundary for each block, but does not state whether a writer may split one application's payload across consecutive blocks that repeat the same handle. | Keep the per-block maximum at the full `uint16_t` range, not signed `INT16_MAX`. Keep same-APPID continuation above 65,535 bytes pending a producer/consumer witness; do not reinterpret the omission as a standards-defined per-APPID cap. |
| LibreDWG [public `BITCODE_BS` definition](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/include/dwg.h) and [EED model documentation](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | LibreDWG declares `BITCODE_BS` as `uint16_t`. Its documentation models repeated EED blocks with a length and APPID handle on the first entry of each block; its published example uses several different APPID handles. This is independent source corroboration for unsigned BS and a repeated-block list, but not a demonstrated repeated-handle continuation case. | Use only as a type/model cross-check. Do not take the peer's data model or example as proof that duplicate consecutive APPID handles are merged semantically by AutoCAD/ODA. |
| ACadSharp open [#1282](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1282) | The report says its DWG writer stores an EED block length through `(short)mstream.Length`; a one-APPID 32,768-byte record wraps and the writer's own reader then drops the LINE. The report identifies ACadSharp 3.8.0 NuGet and current `master`, but this pass did not fetch the package, run it, or independently bind release/source artifacts. The mechanism explains a signed-conversion failure in that peer; its suggested “format limit” is not an ODA rule. | Do not copy the signed 32,767 ceiling or treat a peer self-round-trip as evidence against libdxfrw's unsigned representation. Keep the report as a comparator/hardening lead, not a local finding. |
| Local [`getBitShort()`](src/intern/dwgbuffer.cpp), [`putBitShort()`](src/intern/dwgbufferw.cpp), [`encodeDwgEed()`](src/drw_entities.cpp), and existing [7K generated controls](#implementation-progress--7k-dwg-eed-unsigned-size-boundaries-2026-10-17-local-fast-slice) | The local type path is `uint16_t`; `encodeDwgEed()` bounds each emitted payload to `UINT16_MAX`, flushes only between complete items, repeats the same APPID handle on a continuation block, and terminates the block stream with zero. Existing generated vectors check 32,767, 32,768, 65,535, and 65,536 bytes; the last case splits 65,407+129. A local full-file AC1021 write/read keeps the following LINE. These checks prove local wire/cursor behavior, not interoperability of same-APPID continuation. | Keep the completed local boundary slice. Do not duplicate its 32,768 test or promote the 65,536 result. At the next existing composed EED checkpoint, inspect every emitted block length/handle and require an independent reader/native audit to retain the entity and the exact ordered XDATA items across the repeated APPID group. |

### Implementation-ready decision gate

1. No production change is needed for the peer's reported 32,768-byte signed
   cast: the local writer already encodes that range as unsigned BS and has a
   generated exact-boundary control. Preserve this test as a fast gate.
2. Keep local same-APPID continuation behavior isolated to complete-item
   boundaries and retain the zero terminator. The 65,536-byte same-codec
   readback remains `LOCAL_WIRE_ONLY`; it cannot be used to claim peer/native
   or general EED semantic support.
3. At the already scheduled composed checkpoint, emit one scratch-only
   AC1021-or-newer entity with one APPID and payloads at 65,535 and 65,536
   encoded data bytes. Bind source/output hashes, the sequence of unsigned BS
   lengths, every repeated APPID handle, item order, entity count, and following
   entity sentinel. Run only a source-distinct writer/reader or native CAD
   acceptance path that can independently inspect the output; ACadSharp is not
   an eligible positive witness until #1282's signed-size issue is fixed in
   the exact pinned artifact.
4. If the independent consumer rejects or drops the repeated-handle case,
   change the API writer to refuse an APPID payload that cannot fit one
   65,535-byte block, before publication, while retaining read-side handling
   for valid multi-block files. If it accepts and preserves the exact item
   sequence, record that exact version/profile only; do not generalize across
   all DWG versions or claim that an unrelated consumer's success resolves
   any `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` J item.
5. If the external executable/platform is unavailable at the composed gate,
   retain `EXTERNAL_ACCEPTANCE_PENDING` and continue the next local
   implementation-ready item. Do not repeat external setup or a full suite in
   each slice.

This research corrects peer-limit attribution and narrows the existing 7K
external acceptance question; it adds no finding ID or top-level subplan. It
does not change local implementation order, reduced validation cadence,
fixture policy, dependencies, support claims, or any deferred-J disposition.
Findings/subplans remain **139 / 77**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain explicitly **DEFERRED_EXTERNAL**. The shared worktree remains broadly
dirty; the plan and receipt changes are uncommitted.

## Implementation progress — PAR-49/7G.3 AC1015 paper-space chain walker regression (2026-10-19; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Added a focused selector to the existing `libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests`
executable and registered the same function in its ordinary matrix run. The
direct vectors use local writer-generated entity frames and supply table-level
`DRW_Block_Record`/layout metadata to `walkBlockRecordEntities()`. The new
integration also calls `readDwgBlocks()` with generated BLOCK/ENDBLK/entity
frames and in-memory records, thereby covering more than the direct walker but
still not full DWG BLOCK_RECORD table or LAYOUT object decoding.

The AC1015 vectors cover an empty default paper-space chain, a two-line
`Sheet A` chain, a one-line `Sheet B` chain (`firstEH == lastEH`), exact
layout-handle/block-record/entity identity and order, paper-space mode, and an
unowned following sentinel. An AC1027 control assigns those same entity
identities through explicit owner handles and compares normalized manifests.
A bounded AC1015 range omits the middle handle; traversal stops at the gap and
leaves the later frame unconsumed. The `readDwgBlocks()` integration dispatches
an empty default paper layout, a two-entity `*PAPER_SPACE0`, and a singleton
`*PAPER_SPACE1`, then verifies callback identities/counts and an unowned
sentinel.

That integration reproduced and fixed a production gap in
`isSpaceBlockRecordName()`: the reader recognized only the exact
`*PAPER_SPACE`, not standard numbered records. The classifier now accepts the
exact base token or a nonempty decimal suffix. Autodesk's [BLOCK DXF
reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-66D32572-005A-4E23-8B8B-8726E8C14302.htm)
documents `*Paper_Space`, `*Paper_Space0`, `*Paper_Space1`, and subsequent
numbered names. ODA v5.4.1 §§20.4.1–20.4.2 separately supports the explicit
legacy entity-link wire form used by the cycle vector ([official ODA
specification](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf)).
These sources support the name and chain contracts, not broad producer
compatibility.

The explicit-link follow-up is now covered in the same selector. ODA v5.4.1
§20.4.1 states that `nolinks` is 1 when major links are assumed as adjacent
handles and 0 when explicit links are stored; §20.4.2 specifies the pre-R2004
previous/next entity references as relative soft pointers ([official ODA
specification](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf)).
The generated AC1015 frames set `nolinks=0`, encode previous/next relative
handles into the handle stream, and form a two-entity cycle before a distinct
last-handle sentinel. The reader decodes the links, emits exactly the two
reachable lines, detects the repeated handle, reports one bounded chain
failure, and leaves the sentinel frame in `ObjectMap`. This confirms the
existing cycle guard against the explicit-link wire form; it does not test
whole-file BLOCK_RECORD/LAYOUT decoding or any native producer's cycle policy.

Validation completed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests --parallel 2` — passed with strict project warnings.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests --legacy-layout-block-chains` — passed.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix$' --output-on-failure` — passed, 1/1 (1.51 s).
- `git diff --check -- src/intern/dwgreader.cpp tests/dwg_reader_matrix_tests.cpp DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md docs/research/pre-ac1018-paper-space-layout-chain-fast-slice-2026-10-19.json` — passed.

No persistent fixture, new CTest registration, peer binary, external drawing,
or native CAD application was used. The local PDF copy is absent, but the
official ODA-hosted v5.4.1 §§20.4.1–20.4.2 was available and reviewed. The
generated integration uses supplied in-memory table/layout metadata; full
BLOCK_RECORD/LAYOUT section decoding and real producer interoperability remain
open. This slice proves the local generated route and fixes one specific
paper-space name gap; it does not justify a broad support claim. Findings /
top-level subplans remain **139 / 77**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain explicitly **DEFERRED_EXTERNAL** and non-promoting.

<a id="implementation-progress-par-19-1410-dxf-to-dwg-cross-codec-slice-2026-10-19-generated-fast-test-uncommitted"></a>

### Implementation progress — PAR-19/#1410 DXF-to-DWG cross-codec slice (2026-10-19; generated fast test, uncommitted)

**Implementation.** Added a focused mode to the existing DWG local-roundtrip
executable and a single fast CTest. The harness writes temporary AC1024 and
AC1032 ASCII DXFs, imports each through `dx_iface.fileImport`, dispatches the
small fixture model through `dwgRW::write`, and reopens through the production
DWG importer. The AC1024 profile checks an HATCH line edge with explicit Y=0,
a hash-bearing ATTRIB tag, and following LINE. The AC1032 profile checks
multiline embedded-MTEXT on both ATTRIB and ATTDEF, including group-46 defined
height, background flags/scale, ACI/truecolor/name/transparency and multiline
text. Both profiles check the INSERT attribute list and SEQEND, named block
membership, and following-LINE continuity.

The round trip found two production gaps. DXF parsing left embedded
ATTRIB/ATTDEF host type at its single-line default, so the R2018 DWG encoder
omitted the nested text; parsing now derives the host type (2 for ATTRIB, 4
for ATTDEF) from the host subclass after the embedded-object marker. The
embedded-MTEXT DWG reader and writer also used an ACI-only background CMC
path, discarding true color and names; they now use the existing bounded CMC
reader and R2004+ CMC writer overload, including separate-stream color/book
names. The official ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.46 description was checked before this
DWG parser/encoder change. When DXF supplied both ACI and true color, DWG CMC
stores the true color; readback reports ACI index 256 while preserving RGB,
name and transparency. The test asserts that documented codec projection,
not byte-identical redundant group values.

**Validation.** The strict target build succeeded:


### Fast diagnostic order

1. Establish artifact provenance, exact source/output hashes, DWG version, ACadSharp package/build, GDAL version/options, exit status, and complete diagnostics. A missing/unlicensed attachment is `NOT_RUN`, not a blocker to local work.
2. Validate DXF syntax independently of geometry projection. Capture the first failing record and handle; verify that a later group-code/value pair or entity sentinel remains correctly framed.

Check count-to-occurrence consistency, knot/control/fit/weight cardinalities, flags, tangents, finite values, and the distinction between omitted and explicit-zero fields. Its binding accepts the optional positional fields after the filename as document name, ignore-errors Boolean, and option-source path. It is therefore permissive by default unless the caller supplies `False`. This is a source/API fact, not a runtime outcome for any libdxfrw output. | For strict direct-DXF qualification through the C++ importer, invoke the binding explicitly as `Import.readDXF(path, document_name, False, option_source)`; if the GUI/menu or default Python wrapper is the target, report it as a separate permissive consumer observation and retain its warnings, statistics, and created-document inventory. | FreeCAD current [`ImpExpDxf.cpp`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Import/App/dxf/ImpExpDxf.cpp) | The importer selects an `optionSource`, calls `setOptions()`, and records settings including import mode, scaling, annotations, points, paper-space objects, hidden blocks, layers, and colors. Its source also has a text-line `PreScan` counting values following literal `0` group lines; that helper is not the full DXF parser or a reliable source-record/identity oracle. Import modes can aggregate shapes, so FreeCAD document-object counts need not match DXF entity counts. | Pin and record importer backend, `optionSource`, and every relevant option. Do not use `PreScan` or aggregate FreeCAD object counts as the completeness denominator. Keep the C++ and legacy Python profiles separate; published entity lists are candidate scope, not a runtime qualification. |
| FreeCAD current [`Draft/importDWG.py`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py) and archived [`Draft_DXF` capability page](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) | The wrapper selects a configured LibreDWG, ODA, or QCAD converter and then feeds the produced DXF to a DXF importer. In these paths the wrapper calls `communicate()` and treats output-file existence as conversion success; this is not evidence of strict DXF syntax, complete conversion, or native CAD acceptance. The documentation repository was archived Apr. 1, 2026 and describes different C++/legacy feature subsets, so use it only to predeclare candidate profiles; current source and pinned runtime decide actual behavior. | Separate `DWG_TO_DXF_CONVERTER` from `FREECAD_DXF_IMPORT`. Do not assume the result of the FreeCAD wrapper equals a manual `dwg2dxf -v2010` (or any other requested target). <a id="deeperbroader-hatch-rational-weight-ownership-across-dwg-and-dxf-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>
## Deeper/broader research — HATCH rational-weight ownership across DWG and DXF (2026-10-20; research only)

### Conclusion and local route

This pass confirms the already tracked PAR-115/7N.2 loss rather than adding a new finding. The local HATCH parser reads an ODA-rational spline's weight into `DRW_Coord::z` and leaves `DRW_Spline::weightlist` empty; `dxfRW::writeHatch()` emits the nested HATCH spline's group-42 values from `weightlist`. Consequently, a rational DWG HATCH can retain the legacy carrier but lose its canonical weights on DXF conversion. Existing `runDxfHatchSplineWeights(false/true)` controls cover literal DXF HATCH/MPOLYGON syntax, explicit/omitted weights, array validation, ASCII/Binary output and reread. They do not prove the DWG parser fills both model fields. Existing generated DWG HATCH exercises that only assert file/read outcome are not a weight-semantic oracle.

### Evidence crosswalk and authority

| Evidence | What it establishes | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1, §20.4.75, printed p.196; local copy `~/doc/dwg/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf` (workspace copy has `(1)` in its filename) | The authoritative DWG order is `isrational B`, `isperiodic B`, bounded knot/control counts, knots as `BD`, then for each control `2RD` followed by conditional weight `BD`. Rational weight is not a third point coordinate. The subsequent R24 fit section is explicitly versioned. | Does not resolve the observed R24 zero-fit tangent producer/spec discrepancy; that remains separate 7N.3 work. |
| [Autodesk Boundary Path Data (DXF)](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2017/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-DC5215D6-E73F-4DFF-8BE9-01CA9610FAEE.htm), spline-edge table | HATCH has a distinct nested grammar: 94 degree, 73 rational, 74 periodic, 95/96 counts, 40 knots, 10/20 OCS XY controls, group 42 optional weights defaulting to 1, then 97 fit data and 11/21 points. This is not standalone SPLINE's group-41 encoding. | Specifies interchange tags, not what every consumer chooses to materialize for omitted unit weights. |
| [ACadSharp current master `readHatch()`](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/IO/DWG/DwgStreamReaders/DwgObjectReader.cs#L2318-L2367) | A source-distinct DWG implementation reads the same per-control `2RD` then rational `BD` sequence and carries the scalar in the third coordinate of its HATCH XYZ control-point object. It also gates R2010+ fit points/tangents on positive fit count. | Mutable master is not an immutable release artifact; useful as an implementation comparison, not authority. Its tangent policy is explicitly not a reason to collapse 7N.3. |
| [LibreDWG 0.13.4 manual: HATCH objects](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/OBJECTS.html) and [current NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | Its documented model separates `Dwg_HATCH_ControlPoint.point: 2RD` and `weight: BD`; current NEWS records a DXF/HATCH fix for rational spline knots versus weights. This is an independently structured model and useful adversarial case for keeping knot and weight counts/streams distinct. | The manual is release documentation; the NEWS entry is mutable current source history and does not prove any specific packaged binary or local defect. LibreDWG is not a normative wire authority. |
| [ezdxf HATCH reference](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/dxfentities/hatch.rst#spline-as-boundary-edge) | HATCH point coordinates are documented as OCS `(x,y)` tuples; `SplineEdge` exposes a separate read/write `weights` list alongside control points, fit data, rationality and periodicity. This is an independent DXF consumer/modeling shape. | DXF-only evidence; not a DWG reader or geometric oracle. |
| Local source/test audit (`src/drw_entities.cpp`; `tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp`) | Confirms the local handoff split and that existing focused HATCH spline weight tests exercise DXF parsing/writing, while the needed DWG-to-neutral weight assertions are absent. The local DWG encoder also sources its compatibility wire weight from nested control Z, so 7N.2a should not silently rewrite that writer behavior. | Source inspection only in this research pass; no test was executed and no claim is made that every prior generated HATCH read path was re-run. |

### Ready implementation slice and exit criteria

1. Keep the change scoped to the existing 7N.2a reader handoff: for rational `ncontrol`, store exactly one finite wire weight in both `weightlist[i]` and the legacy `controllist[i]->z`; preserve XY bit values and rational/periodic flags. For a nonrational edge, leave `weightlist` empty and do not invent a Z/weight value.
2. Retain the parser's bounded-count/body-end discipline and local temporary object. Reserve `weightlist` only after the control count is accepted, and do not append/publish the spline until each pair and applicable fit payload validates. Reject truncation transactionally at the edge/entity boundary; do not add a positive-weight constraint absent from the existing profile contract.
3. Use from-scratch, ODA-order vectors: AC1018 rational zero-fit; AC1027 rational one-fit with tangent fields so 7N.3 cannot confound this change. Include non-unit and explicit-unit weights, a quarter-circle with weights `1, sqrt(0.5), 1`, a truncated BD, a later edge, and following object/handle sentinel. Independent expected values must not be generated by calling the production HATCH encoder alone.
4. Pass the parsed object through ASCII and Binary DXF export/readback. Assert group 42 per weight (all-unit omission remains semantically legal), unchanged OCS XY, no group-30 Z leak, callback visibility of the legacy Z mirror for 2D consumers, canonical array cardinality, and the analytic midpoint. Keep DWG writer canonical-vs-legacy authority in 7N.2b; keep modern zero-fit tangents in 7N.3.
5. Add no proprietary/external drawing and no committed fixture: generate temporary controls from scratch and remove them. Use one focused selector plus its existing executable/CTest owner, then only the scheduled composed gate; do not run a full suite for this narrow slice. After the implementation slice, update statuses/receipt and continue to the next local-ready item instead of waiting on external qualification.

No code, tests, fixtures, dependencies, peer executables, or native CAD applications were changed or run for this research-only update. Findings/subplans remain **139 / 77**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; this evidence cannot promote any DWG/DXF, ACIS/AcDs, native-platform, or 3D support claim.

## Deeper/broader cross-repository DWG/DXF fault patterns and AcDs gate (2026-10-20; research only)

### Decision

This cross-project refresh confirms the existing PAR-115 HATCH weight
handoff work and adds one source-confirmed local field-loss finding,
PAR-140/7N.4: DWG HATCH/MPOLYGON path boundary references are discarded on
read and zeroed on write. Current inventory is 140 findings / 78 top-level
subplans. It also sharpens ACIS/AcDs acceptance: qualify modern modeler data
by its external data-store linkage and payload, not by the surviving entity
record; treat peer issues and unmerged peer PRs as risk signals rather than
support evidence. Validation cadence, dependency policy and fixture policy
are unchanged; no support claim is promoted.

### Implementation-ready refinements to existing subplans

1. **PAR-115 / 7N.2a-b HATCH weights.** The DWG reader/writer rational-weight
   handoff is implemented locally. Retain the independent boundary-bit check,
   the now-explicit group-21 zero-presence census, and the AC1018/AC1027
   HATCH/MPOLYGON continuity controls. The existing `--hatch-references`
   ASCII/Binary DXF selector already checks path flags 7/0/2 and source-handle
   lists `{0x31}`, `{0x32,0x33}`, and empty; reuse it rather than duplicating
   those DXF controls. Keep the R24 zero-fit tangent policy in 7N.3.
2. **PAR-140 / 7N.4 DWG path references.** Add one generated fast selector
   and one narrowly filtered CTest to the existing DWG local-roundtrip target.
   Build independent AC1018 and AC1024-or-AC1027 bit/handle-stream literals;
   exercise uneven per-path counts, empty path, distinct flags and values,
   HATCH plus MPOLYGON, and exact soft-pointer codes. Check parser loop
   ownership, independent raw writer output, DXF ASCII/Binary group 97/330
   roundtrip, and next-path/entity sentinels. Test truncated handles, wrong
   relation code, bounded count overflow and public-handle width before any
   callback or output mutation. Do not require the source entities to exist
   in the codec-only literal; test owner-graph closure in the adapter layer.
   Keep native associative edit/recompute as a later consumer qualification.
   No proprietary or downloaded file; scratch controls are temporary and
   deleted. Run the strict target build, direct selector and its owning CTest,
   not the full suite. Update the plan/receipt after the slice and continue
   with the next local-ready item.
3. **ACIS/AcDs carrier and semantic gate.** Partition generated controls by
   storage era: pre-R2013 entity-inline SAT/ACIS and R2013+ AcDs/SAB external
   storage. For each, check entity identity and disposition, referenced

   gate; a candidate that extracts the payload but cannot independently

4. **Evidence and unblock rule.** ODA remains the DWG byte-layout authority;

## Implementation progress — PAR-115 / 7N.2a HATCH DWG rational-weight handoff (2026-10-20; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The DWG HATCH spline reader now stores each rational control's bounded finite
wire weight in both `DRW_Spline::weightlist` and the compatibility
`DRW_Coord::z` mirror, preserving XY and existing 2D consumer behavior. The
wire source remains the ODA-defined 2D control followed by conditional BD;
the DWG writer's existing source/authority behavior was not changed.

The generated local control exercises independently authored ODA-order
AC1018 zero-fit and AC1027 one-fit records, quarter-circle and non-unit
weights, an independently decoded boundary literal, truncated-weight
transactional refusal/retry, following-edge/path/object sentinels, DWG
write/read callbacks, and ASCII/Binary DXF group-42 export/readback. DXF checks
also verify zero elevation and no geometric-Z leakage. No external or
committed drawing fixture was used; all generated files are scratch outputs
removed by the test harness.

The first selector run exposed a test-scanner setup issue: its standalone DXF
reader had not enabled the same DIMSTYLE name/reference compatibility mode as
the normal library import path, so scanning stopped in TABLES before
ENTITIES. Enabling that mode (and wide handle lexemes) makes the independent
wire census reach the HATCH and following LINE; the library writer was not
changed for this correction.

No full suite, fixture, dependency, peer/native run, new finding, top-level

<a id="implementation-progress-par-115-7n2b-hatch-dwg-writer-weight-authority-2026-10-20-local-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>
## Implementation progress — PAR-115 / 7N.2b HATCH DWG writer weight authority (2026-10-20; local fast slice, uncommitted)

`DRW_Hatch` now has a documented-in-code source-compatible DWG weight rule:
the complete finite canonical `weightlist` wins and signals rationality; an
empty list with the rational flag set retains the historical control-Z weight
carrier; an empty list with a clear flag stays non-rational even if control Z
is nonzero. Conflicting mirrors do not mutate the source. Partial canonical
arrays and non-finite effective weights fail validation before the output
buffer receives bytes. No positivity or closed-solid rules were invented.

The existing local-roundtrip selector now exercises AC1018 zero-fit and AC1027
one-fit output for quarter-circle, near-unit, non-unit, and all-unit weights,
using canonical-only, legacy-Z-only, matching, conflicting, and unmarked-Z
inputs through both HATCH and MPOLYGON object wrappers. A test-local independent
bit reader checks rational bits, exact 2RD XY, weight order/values, fit fields,
following edge, and loop trailer; full generated DWG readback verifies the
neutral model, correct entity callback, following LINE, and unchanged source
spline fields.
ASCII/Binary DXF write/read and analytic quarter-circle midpoint checks remain
in the same selector. Partial and non-finite input controls confirm refusal
with a zero-bit output buffer.

Validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip dwg2dxf -j4`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip --hatch-dwg-spline-weights`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^dwg_hatch_rational_spline_weight_handoff$' --output-on-failure` (1/1, 0.37 s)
- Scoped `git diff --check` for implementation, test, plan, and receipt
- `jq empty docs/research/hatch-dwg-rational-weight-writer-authority-fast-slice-2026-10-20.json`

No full suite, external fixture, dependency, native/peer qualification, new
CTest target, or support promotion was added. The valid-zero coordinate and
two-path state-isolation controls are now covered by the generated PAR-115 /
PAR-140 selectors described above; this older queue note is superseded by
those results. Findings/subplans at this slice remain **139 / 77**; J256,
J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. PAR-141 / 7S.2c
has since been implemented locally and focused-validated; its progress record
