<a id="deeperbroader-text-script-and-layout-consumer-boundary-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>
## Deeper/broader text script and layout consumer boundary (2026-10-20; research only)

### Decision

This peer-source pass adds no libdxfrw defect or implementation slice. It
sharpens the existing PAR-05/7AR and PAR-90/7AZ evidence boundaries: byte
decoding and Unicode scalar preservation are file-codec behavior; mapping
those scalars to legacy SHX glyphs, right-to-left shaping, and MTEXT line
layout are separate resource/consumer behavior. Keep Unicode text round-trip
claims scoped to the tested DXF version, field, and byte/scalar contract. Do
not make SHX availability or an MTEXT explode engine a codec prerequisite.
Finding/subplan inventory remains 140/78. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

### Evidence crosswalk and limits

| Source | What it establishes | Plan consequence | Evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| ezdxf open [issue #1271](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/issues/1271) | The reporter initially described Farsi text that did not appear as Persian after extraction, including after trying CP1256. The maintainer compared R2004 CP1256/CIF and converted R2018 UTF-8 text and reported the extracted strings looked the same; the reporter then concluded the source used a customized Unicode-to-Persian glyph map independent of ordinary Arabic Unicode. The maintainer separately states ezdxf does not support RTL rendering. | Do not change CP1256 selection, expand `\U+` escapes globally, or transform text based on STYLE font names from this report. Treat exact source bytes, decoded Unicode scalars, font-resource mapping, bidi shaping, and visual glyph output as separate observables. Reuse the existing generated CP1256 scalar anchor in `tests/gbk_codepage_tests.cpp` and the existing PAR-05/7AR target-version matrix. | Open peer issue with an uninspected confidential drawing and SHX attachment; the reporter's final diagnosis is informative but not independently verified. It is not a libdxfrw reproduction, normative encoding rule, SHX specification, or visual rendering oracle. |
| ezdxf [DXF File Encoding](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfinternals/fileencoding.html), [Unicode Decoder](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/low_level_tools/dxf_unicode_decoder.html), and [DXF tags](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfinternals/dxftags.html) docs | The independent DXF implementation documents pre-R2007 codepage-selected byte encoding plus `\U+nnnn` Unicode escapes, R2007+ UTF-8, and a separate explicit Unicode-escape decoder; its tag docs also distinguish string storage from application interpretation. | Preserve the existing source-version × target-version × field matrix. For each test, assert raw emitted bytes and expected scalar separately; do not byte-compare when a version-appropriate CIF escape legitimately carries the same scalar. Keep generic object strings and MTEXT inline-control strings under their already separate field contracts. | Useful independent implementation documentation, not a substitute for the plan's Autodesk DXF authority. The ezdxf docs are versioned but can change; pin an exact package only if later used as an executable comparator. |
| ezdxf [Font Resources](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/concepts/fonts.html), [Fonts](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tools/fonts.html), and [STYLE table](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfinternals/tables/style_table.html) docs | DXF styles identify external font files by name; the library does not bundle those resources, and rendering depends on installed/resolved fonts or substitutes. SHX/shape resource identity is not carried by Unicode text bytes alone. | Do not auto-fetch or silently substitute fonts during codec import/export. If a later consumer offers resource resolution, make the selected file identity, licensing/provenance, glyph mapping, and unresolved outcome explicit. Keep text-style fonts distinct from `T_SHAPE`/SHAPEFILE numeric glyph identity owned by PAR-90/7AZ. | Documentation describes ezdxf's font workflow, not all CAD applications or a universal SHX mapping contract. No SHX resource was downloaded or used. |
| ezdxf open [issue #1389](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/issues/1389), [MText](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/mtext.html), and [MTextExplode](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/addons/mtxpl.html) docs | #1389 reports continuous CJK text overflowing the specified MTEXT width when converted by ezdxf's explode/layout helper; it is marked `wontfix`. The docs define a reference width for wrapping and describe explode as an approximate layout replication utility with limitations, including left-to-right flow. | Keep MTEXT payload/chunk preservation and control-string parsing under PAR-05/7AR/7M separate from paragraph breaking, CJK break opportunities, bidi/vertical layout, and exploding MTEXT into TEXT entities. Add no parser test for a consumer-only layout symptom. If a product later claims MTEXT layout/explode, add a separate optional consumer gate with pinned engine/version, locally authored CJK/Bidi inputs, expected line placement, and bounded runtime. | This is a peer utility behavior, not a DXF wire rule, native CAD result, or evidence about libdxfrw (which has no text layout engine). The issue's proposed tokenizer fix is reporter speculation, not adopted behavior. |
| Local `tests/gbk_codepage_tests.cpp`, `src/intern/drw_textcodec.cpp`, and the existing 7AZ contract | The generated codepage matrix already includes `ANSI_1256` byte `C7` → Unicode U+0627 and checks reverse byte encoding; the local text codec keeps UTF-8 and legacy codepage routes distinct. The 7AZ plan explicitly separates shape-file identity, numeric index, and DXF glyph-name alias and does not claim SHX resolution. | Reuse these owners; no duplicate CP1256 scalar case is needed. If a later gap is found, add only a generated control under its current owner: assert raw legacy bytes/codepage or modern UTF-8, exact Unicode scalar sequence, and following-field integrity. Native font appearance is a separate result. | Source/test inspection only in this pass; tests were not run. This does not establish Arabic shaping, private glyph mapping, actual font lookup, or native display. |

### Implementation-ready evidence rules

1. **Fast codec slice:** retain the existing CP1256 anchor and PAR-05/7AR
   version/field matrix. Any future text-codec change must have an independent
   byte literal, expected Unicode scalar sequence, target `$ACADVER`/codepage,
   valid UTF-8 check where applicable, and a following-tag/entity sentinel.
   Reuse the existing codec executable and one narrow selector/CTest; no full
   suite for a text leaf.
2. **Text-resource mapping:** do not infer glyph mapping from a style name or
   Unicode scalar. Any future opt-in resolver must identify the exact local
   resource and glyph mapping, be bounded and non-networked, and report an
   unresolved mapping without corrupting or silently rewriting stored text.
   Keep this separate from 7AZ's legacy SHAPE identity and its output guard.
3. **Text layout:** keep line breaking, shaping, glyph metrics, and MTEXT
   explosion outside low-level read/write acceptance. If this becomes an
   explicit product requirement, qualify it in a consumer-specific harness
   with pinned engine/font versions and generated text cases; do not install a
   peer package in per-slice validation or commit external drawings/fonts.
4. **Evidence and claims:** use Autodesk for normative DXF field/code rules;
   use ezdxf docs/issues only for independent implementation architecture and
   adversarial consumer cases. Neither peer report can promote DWG/DXF, font,
   rendering, native-platform, ACIS/AcDs, or 3D support. Do not inspect or
   redistribute #1271's confidential attachments without a provenance/rights
   basis.

<a id="implementation-progress-par-140-7n4-dwg-boundary-reference-retention-2026-10-20-generated-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>
## Implementation progress: PAR-140 / 7N.4 DWG boundary-reference retention (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

`DRW_Hatch::parseDwgBoundaryData()` now records one boundary-reference count
per path. HATCH and MPOLYGON parse the bounded post-common-entity handle stream,
validate absolute/relative soft-pointer roles and resolved 32-bit width, then
publish references to their original loops only after the complete stream has
parsed. Their shared DWG writer emits each loop's actual count and ordered
soft-pointer values in the correct pre-/post-AC1024 handle area.

The focused generated selector covers AC1018 and AC1024 for HATCH and
MPOLYGON; three paths use counts `2/0/1`, distinct flags, and references to
three generated LINE entities. It independently checks path counts and raw
handle tails, full DWG readback and target identities, following-entity
continuity, and ASCII/Binary DXF references. An end-to-end result exposed that
`dxfRW::writeMPolygon()` had no object-reference resolver/remapper for group
330, unlike HATCH. The writer now resolves those references and refuses an
unresolved handle. MPOLYGON group 71 remains its solid-fill flag, not
associativity.

Raw helper controls verify absolute code 4 and documented relative codes
6/8/A/C, and reject hard-pointer code 5, a physically truncated handle, an
absolute or relative result above `uint32_t`, a per-path count above the
bounded limit, and an aggregate count above the limit. Every negative case
preserves the original loop handle lists. The generated writer also rejects
oversized path lists before producing body/handle bytes.

Validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip dwg2dxf --parallel 2`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip --hatch-dwg-boundary-references`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^dwg_hatch_dwg_boundary_references$' --output-on-failure` (1/1)
- Adjacent `--hatch-references` and `--hatch-dwg-spline-weights` selectors.

No full test suite, external fixture, dependency, peer executable, or native
application was used. The generated DWG/DXF files are temporary and removed;
no fixture was committed. No commit was created, so there is no commit
progress to report. The first slice closed the focused PAR-140 codec path;
the following composition slice extended the existing 7F.1 DXF-export graph
gate to MPOLYGON and added the generated DXF-import→DWG→readback route. Its
same-type negative matrix and target remapping now pass. Exact geometric
boundary agreement and native associative editing remain outstanding.
Inventory remains **140 / 78**, and all six
external-only J items remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

missing-target refusal with destination-sentinel preservation in ASCII and

with exact per-path references and target-handle remapping. The test adapter
clears stale imported source identities for fresh DWG allocation, maps each
DXF target handle to its newly emitted DWG handle, and restores the imported
DXF entity identities/references after the write.

<a id="deeperbroader-resource-complexity-peer-patterns-and-attributed-insert-staging-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>
## Deeper/broader resource-complexity peer patterns and attributed-INSERT staging (2026-10-20; research + local source audit)

### Decision

This pass adds one source-confirmed local performance finding, PAR-141, under
existing 7S.2c; it does not add a new top-level subplan. LibreDWG's open
#1395/#1402 proposal is not merged and cannot be used as a result for this
library, but its source-level analysis identifies three distinct complexity
classes worth checking separately: exact-size handle-vector growth, ordered
reference-index insertion in the middle of an array, and repeated full
reference-resolution sweeps caused by an invalidation flag. Local inspection
found analogous but independently evidenced risk in DWG INSERT/ATTRIB
staging and commit ordering. LibreDWG's merged #1268/#1261 class-count DoS fix
is an adversarial prompt, not a matching local defect: the local R13–R2000
class loop is section-byte-bounded and successful `DRW_Class::parseDwg()`
consumes fixed bit fields plus variable-text length prefixes; the R2004+
reader bounds its declared count, reserves before the loop, and validates
class/string cursors against their section spans. Do not copy the peer's
numeric cap or alter those readers without a local reproducer.

Findings/subplans now total **141 / 78**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; this research does not promote any format,
performance, security, native-platform, ACIS/AcDs, or 3D support claim.

### Implementation-ready PAR-141 slice

1. Add a handle-to-staged-attribute index to both pending-owner and
   child-first orphan state. For modern profiles, build/retain a declared
   handle membership index once from `attribHandles`; for R13–R2000 retain
   the documented first/last endpoint membership rule. Reuse the source-order
   list for callbacks and DXF/DWG output; the index is lookup-only.
2. Before any vector/map mutation, validate the owner handle, expected-child
   rule, duplicate status, max attribute count, checked capacity growth, and
   aggregate per-reader budget. Stage the active source frame only after
   reservations succeed. If insertion or callback/journal preparation fails,
   erase any newly indexed identity and preserve the existing frame
   terminalization/rollback rules.
3. Replace commit-time `find_if` with indexed lookup, then separately assert
   that each declared ref resolves once and that the ordered callback list
   exactly follows the DWG declaration. Do not sort output attributes or
   weaken the existing duplicate-child marker/SEQEND logic.
4. Add scratch-generated many-attribute parents in both parent-first and
   child-first encounter order, use deliberately nonmonotonic handles, and
   check identical callback order/ownership after reader commit. Negative
   controls cover duplicate declared refs, duplicate observed identity,
   missing child, wrong parent, overflow/budget refusal, and a later ATTRIB,
   SEQEND, and LINE sentinel. Do not add or commit external files.
5. Validate with the strict DWG reader/local-roundtrip targets, one focused
   selector and its narrow owning CTest, plus scoped `git diff --check` and
   receipt JSON validation. No wall-clock threshold, full suite, peer runtime,
   external file, native app, or platform qualification is required for this
   local optimization. Update the plan/receipt and self-unblock to the next
   local-ready item after the slice.

### Implementation progress — PAR-141 / 7S.2c (2026-10-20; local, uncommitted)

The implementation uses `m_stagedAttributeIndex`, an ordered map from unique
ATTRIB handle to owner and stable staged-vector ordinal. Modern INSERT declared
references are sorted and duplicate-checked once per pending owner; an
aggregate reader counter bounds those projections, and the shared ordered map
is bounded by `MaxDwgReadObjectCount`. Pending/orphan `attlist` and staged
attribute vectors now use geometric growth. Parent adoption verifies the
existing owner/ordinal index instead of rebuilding a duplicate-scan vector.
Completion, commit ordering, and final staged-state validation use indexed
lookups; declaration order, child-first adoption, rollback, callback
transactionality, and the legacy R13–R2000 first/last endpoint rule are
preserved.

Generated test controls in `tests/dwg_reader_matrix_tests.cpp` exercise 257
unique nonmonotonic ATTRIB handles in parent-first and child-first order,
declared callback order, duplicate declared and observed identities, missing
children, wrong ownership, aggregate-budget refusal, SEQEND gating, and
neighboring ATTRIB/LINE frames. No DWG/DXF fixture was added.

## Deeper/broader OpenCADStudio AC1027 ACIS and FreeCAD platform-gate refresh (2026-10-20; research only)

### Decision

This source refresh adds no new PAR finding and no new top-level subplan. It
sharpens the existing PAR-07/S8 composed consumer and ACIS/AcDs qualification
gates. OpenCADStudio is now a useful optional cross-platform consumer because
it publishes Windows, Linux, and macOS builds and documents ACIS entity
tessellation; its parser/writer is ACadRust-derived, however, so it is not a
second independent parser vote relative to ACadRust. Its same-stack
`audit`/`save_verified` path is consistency evidence only. A new open AC1027
3DSOLID failure report has no public DWG attachment, so it cannot be reproduced
or used to establish whether the source record is valid. Do not download or
commit a peer/customer DWG.

FreeCAD's published DXF documentation places a decisive boundary on native
qualification: its stock importers do not decode ACIS SAT/SAB solids; the
built-in C++ importer has a listed entity subset, while the legacy importer
adds 3DFACE but still not ACIS. Its DWG helper converts through DXF and inherits
those importer limits. The requested Linux and Windows FreeCAD checks therefore
qualify only the exact DWG converter route plus the exact FreeCAD importer and
fields it supports. They cannot unblock or promote ACIS/AcDs semantic support.
The independent semantic gate remains separate and profile-specific.

Current inventory remains **141 findings / 78 top-level subplans**. J256,
J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.
No local support claim, test cadence, implementation order, fixture policy, or
2D consumer contract changes.

### Evidence crosswalk and limits

| Source | Fresh evidence | Plan disposition |
|---|---|---|

This is an unverified peer failure report, not proof of valid DWG syntax, an ACIS bug, or a libdxfrw failure. The application advertises native R14–R2018 DWG/DXF and ACIS tessellation, but those project claims are not independent geometry results. | Reuse the report only as an adversarial test-shape prompt for the already-existing bounded-record/ACIS owner: if a local source audit identifies an exact comparable field, generate a valid AC1027 record and a one-field malformed twin, then assert bounded refusal, no fabricated array, and valid neighboring-record continuity. Both currently cannot read ACIS solids. Do not count ezdxf self-read, payload presence, or mesh tessellation as ACIS support. |

### Implementation-ready, fast-first platform and semantic gates

1. Continue local implementation using the existing fast selectors and focused
   CTests; do not pause for OpenCADStudio, FreeCAD, a peer issue attachment, or
   an external drawing. The platform checks belong once at the composed
   PAR-07/S8 checkpoint, not after every local slice.
2. Run the same pre-admitted local DWG set on Linux x86-64 and Windows x86-64
   with a named FreeCAD release/build. Record OS/architecture, FreeCAD version
   and build id, selected C++/legacy DXF importer, converter selection, exact
   converter executable path/version/hash, relevant preferences, locale, and
   full command. Keep ODA/QCAD fallback disabled or otherwise prove which
   executable ran.
3. Before invoking FreeCAD, call `dwg2dxf` directly with the exact intended
   arguments. Require exit code zero, output existence and nonzero size; hash
   the result; parse it with the local strict DXF path; and compare source vs
   DXF using a per-handle/type/owner/reference manifest. Then invoke the actual
   FreeCAD DWG-open helper and compare only its supported subset. Record both
   known importer omissions and all unexpected loss/exception counts. This
   avoids conflating converter success with FreeCAD import success.
4. Use existing tracked fixtures or controls generated locally from scratch;
   never add externally sourced test drawings or issue attachments. Include
   a negative converter-exit/missing-output control in any wrapper test, but
   do not run it as a repeated full platform suite.
5. Keep the ACIS/AcDs gate separate: prove modeler-handle → AcDs object/key →
   exact SAB span/hash → emitted neutral/DXF carrier, then pass the extracted
   bytes to one pinned profile-compatible external decoder and compare against
   independently authored analytic expectations. Record parser lineage and
   geometry-kernel lineage separately. The current FreeCAD DXF route is not an
   ACIS shape oracle; if no suitably independent route accepts the exact
   carrier profile, retain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and the narrow opaque-byte
   disposition.
6. After either composed checkpoint, update its evidence row and continue the
   next local-ready slice automatically. Keep the fast-test-first schedule;
   this research adds no full-suite run, new dependency, permanent fixture, or
   additional native-platform execution.

## Implementation progress: PAR-140 / 7N.4 MPOLYGON metadata reference roundtrip (2026-10-20; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The previous ASCII/Binary MPOLYGON metadata failures were test-fixture and
assertion defects, not a production-code loss. The generated associated
polyline case supplied boundary handle `0xB0` but left the MPOLYGON handle at
zero; graph preflight correctly refused the invalid identity graph. Giving the
MPOLYGON its own unique handle makes the local graph valid. The DXF writer then
collision-safely remaps source handles, so the correct roundtrip invariant is
that the imported loop's group-330 reference resolves to the imported
polyline's handle—not that it numerically equals the original `0xB0`.

The existing `runDxfMPolygonMetadata()` matrix now tests that invariant in
ASCII and Binary along with pixel size, seed points, loop type, and ordinary
edge-path metadata. A focused `--mpolygon-metadata` selector and the narrow
`dxf_mpolygon_metadata_boundary_roundtrip` CTest were added. Both pass. The
failure diagnostic reports export/import outcome and decoded reference details
if this generated control regresses.

## Deeper PAR-116 zero-fit HATCH tangent witness screen (2026-10-20; local corpus research)

ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.75 (pp. 196–197) lists the R2010+ HATCH spline boundary
sequence as `Numfitpoints`, that many fit-point payloads, then start and end
tangents. The published pseudocode does not condition the tangent pair on a
positive fit count. The local parser currently reads the pair only when
`nfit > 0`, citing ACadSharp behavior and a zero-fit boundary observed in
`svg/export_sample.dwg`. The reference and peer implementation therefore do
not yet agree with the current local compatibility gate.

A fresh trace screen covered all ten AC1024 files locally present under
`tests/samples/AC1024`. They are untracked in this worktree, so their
repository provenance is not inferred; they were read only and not modified.
The screen found no HATCH boundary-spline/tangent trace marker; the condominium drawing
had a general SPLINE parse marker only, which is not evidence about a HATCH
edge. The converter declined strict-complete DXF export for all ten after
observing unsupported custom classes. That export refusal does not mean the
DWG parser failed, and absence of a trace marker is not proof that no HATCH is
present. Nine additional AC1024 files were identified in `~/doc/dwg`, but are
not repository fixtures and were not counted as fresh witnesses in this pass.
No external drawing was fetched and no fixture was created or committed.

Disposition: keep PAR-116 / 7N.3 open and unchanged. Do not remove the `nfit`
gate from the written sequence alone, and do not treat ACadSharp or a
same-stack write/read as independent producer evidence. Resume this exact
question only with a locally generated or provenance-cleared AC1024 witness
whose HATCH boundary bytes, fit-count cursor, tangent bytes, and enclosing
record boundary are independently verified. Other local-ready slices continue
without waiting for this witness. This adds no finding or support claim; all
six J items remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

Research receipt:
[`par116-ac1024-local-corpus-witness-screen-2026-10-20.json`](docs/research/par116-ac1024-local-corpus-witness-screen-2026-10-20.json).

## Deeper/broader open-source peer capability matrix and 3D evidence boundaries (2026-10-20; research only)

This refresh checks peer documentation and current issue reports against the
existing PAR-07/S8 carrier, semantic, and consumer gates. It is intentionally
operation-specific: an open-source DWG/DXF project may be useful for one
stage and unsuitable for the next. Issue reports are leads, not local
reproductions or format authority. A source/test-owner inventory found no
new local defect in this pass. No peer repository or executable was installed
or run.

| Peer/source | Evidence and confidence boundary | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [manual](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi), [project README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg), and [fuzzing setup](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg-fuzz) | The project documents a capable DWG reader and DWG/DXF tooling, while also distinguishing stable/unstable/unhandled class states and saying R2010–R2018 DWG output still fails CRC/audit checks. Its fuzz setup separates crashes, hangs, and leaks and replays saved failures. This is project documentation, not a run against the current local corpus. | Keep LibreDWG useful for pinned read-side census and selected DXF structure checks; do not treat its modern DWG writer as a general positive/native oracle. Borrow the failure-classification and minimized-regression idea only for locally generated controls at an already scheduled hardening checkpoint; do not import peer fuzz corpus files or add fuzzing to every implementation slice. |
| ACadSharp open [issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) and current [version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) | The issue report says ACadSharp 3.4.9 reads `3DSOLID`/`REGION` objects but its DXF writer silently omits them, including objects inside solid-only blocks; the reporter says a LibreDWG census confirmed the source objects. No customer drawing is attached, and the result is a report for a named package, not an independent reproduction. | Preserve PAR-07/S8's per-source identity and owning-block no-loss check. Count emitted modeler records and inline carrier bytes separately from process success and block-shell survival; every omitted record must have an explicit `UNSUPPORTED`, `REJECTED`, or `ERROR` disposition. Do not add a local defect from this report: local source inventory already shows an explicit modeler-geometry DXF writer path, whose correctness still requires the existing cross-route gates. |

## Deeper/broader DWG/DXF consumer-route and peer-coverage maturity refresh (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass expands the existing PAR-07/S8 comparator matrix in three directions:
the exact FreeCAD DXF importer selected after conversion, the difference
between explicit faceted geometry and ACIS/ASM modeler carriers, and the gap
between peer headline coverage and the peer's tested/stable class states.
Sources were current upstream project documentation or project-maintained
manuals; no peer was cloned or run, and no external drawing was downloaded.

### Evidence crosswalk and interpretation

| Route/source | Fresh primary-source evidence | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) | The docs describe two selectable importers: the built-in, faster C++ importer and a legacy Python/add-on importer. Both claim DXF versions from R12, but their listed families differ: the C++ list includes dimensions, blocks, and paper-space objects, while the legacy list includes `3DFACE`. The same docs explicitly say ACIS/SAT solids cannot currently be read by FreeCAD. DWG import/export is converter → DXF importer/exporter → converter. | A FreeCAD test result is not fully described by “FreeCAD opened it.” Record converter, FreeCAD version/build, platform, importer backend and preference/add-on state. For ordinary platform qualification, test the importer selected by the shipped/default configuration on both Linux and Windows; test the alternate backend only if it is an in-scope supported installation profile. Treat explicit 3DFACE/mesh import as a separate bounded geometry case. Do not count ACIS bytes being present in DXF as successful FreeCAD solid import. Keep converter read and write as separate legs, verify exit code and fresh output existence, strictly reopen the output, and compare source identities/dispositions. |
| FreeCAD [DXF implementation report](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/18454) | The project discussion distinguishes explicit entities from ACIS blobs and says FreeCAD cannot interpret the latter as geometry. This is consistent with the maintained documentation, but is a project discussion, not a format specification. | Use it only to corroborate the consumer boundary. The normative claim remains the exact versioned importer behavior observed in a local native run; do not turn a discussion or UI result into broad CAD-format support. |
| LibreDWG [published manual coverage section](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) and [project NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | The manual reports broad revision coverage but partitions classes into unstable/undertested, broken/undertested, halfway, unhandled, and lacking test coverage. It explicitly lists `BODY`, `MESH`, and other 3D types among classes missing the manual's sample test coverage, and `ACDSRECORD`/`ACDSSCHEMA` among unhandled classes. The NEWS history also documents incomplete `AcDsPrototype_1b` extraction and a brute-force SAB recovery path; because this is historical release-note material, it is a risk signal rather than a claim about every current build. | Never use a peer's aggregate “coverage percent,” class declaration, or stable label as support evidence by itself. For any LibreDWG comparison, bind the exact build and input hashes, record per-type decode/write disposition and test-corpus membership, and separately compare source entity ↔ AcDs record/key/owner ↔ exact SAB payload. A passing DWG/DXF conversion or surviving entity count cannot close AcDs or solid-semantic evidence. Keep LibreDWG as an optional version-bound structural comparator, not the only independent oracle. |
| GDAL [DXF driver documentation](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | The OGR projection maps `3DFACE`, `SOLID`, and `TRACE` into polygonal/simple geometries and maps polyface meshes to polyhedral-surface geometry; several curves are tessellated, INSERTs are inlined by default, text and HATCH presentation are simplified, and raw unhandled group values are opt-in. Separately, AC1027+ 3D-extensible mode can expose raw ASM bytes and a 12-value transform, but the docs say it cannot transform `3DSOLID`/`REGION`/`BODY`/`SURFACE` into OGR geometries and skips them by default. | Split GDAL evidence into `OGR_EXPLICIT_GEOMETRY_PROJECTION` and `RAW_ASM_CARRIER_EXTRACTION`. The former can check a declared subset using normalized geometry and explicit options, but not exact CAD record/reference preservation. The latter can assist with raw payload/transform cross-checking only; it is not a B-rep or native-consumer result. Pin GDAL version, options (`INLINE_BLOCKS`, `MERGE_BLOCK_GEOMETRIES`, `INCLUDE_RAW_CODE_VALUES`, `3D_EXTENSIBLE_MODE`), and expected projection for any optional composed run. Do not place GDAL in per-slice tests. |

### Implementation-ready refinement to PAR-07/S8

Use one generated analytic control (created in scratch, never committed as a
new DWG/DXF fixture) with separate, unambiguous cohorts:

1. **Explicit 3D primitives/facets:** `3DFACE`, polyface `POLYLINE`/`MESH`,
   and already-supported explicit surface/NURBS entities. Record source type,
   handle, owner/block, coordinates, transform, and the expected neutral
   geometry. Compare the explicitly declared geometry subset with tolerances;
   do not infer ACIS/B-rep success from facets or a tessellated preview.
2. **Modeler carriers:** `3DSOLID`, `REGION`, `BODY`, and `SURFACE` where the
   source profile actually carries ACIS/ASM. Record entity identity, modeler
   flags, inline-vs-AcDs location, section/key/owner edges, exact payload
   digest, transform, and per-object disposition. Carrier preservation is
   structural evidence only; shape validity, topology, analytic measures,
   and native display/editability remain later independent gates.
3. **Consumer route:** for each Linux/Windows run, record the converter and
   its version/hash, FreeCAD version/build, selected DXF importer backend,
   importer preference/add-on presence, command/arguments, exit code, output
   existence, reopened document identity/counts, unsupported warnings, and
   output digest. The minimum platform gate uses the configured production
   importer; alternate importers are optional and explicitly labeled.

Keep the writer direction separately observable: FreeCAD DXF export followed
by the DWG converter is not implied by a successful DWG→DXF import. Verify
conversion status, the actual output file and version, independent reopen,
and per-source/output disposition. A wrapper return code, document-open event,
entity count, or view screenshot alone is insufficient.

This is a composed milestone only. It adds no default peer invocation, CTest,

## Deeper/broader peer claim ledgers, transformation boundaries, and harness trust (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass looks beyond whether an open-source project says it supports a
format. It checks what the project's own evidence ledger qualifies, what
operation a comparator actually executes, and whether the test harness can
misclassify failures. The sources below are project-maintained documentation
and a peer issue report. They inform comparator selection and plan readiness;
they are neither DWG/DXF normative authority nor a reproduction of a local
libdxfrw defect.

| Peer/source | Deeper finding | Plan consequence and limit |
|---|---|---|
| LibreCAD 3 [DWG support policy](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/blob/master/docs/dwg-support.md) | The policy says `WITH_DWG_IMPORT` is off by default and routes read through `dwgRW`. At its stated pinned revision, the qualification ledger contains 15 read claims (11 `EXPERIMENTAL`, 4 `PENDING_NATIVE`), no `PROMOTED` claims, and no write-direction claims. It describes DWG writing as intentionally unavailable, not merely unimplemented. | Keep two LibreCAD compatibility lanes distinct: the existing 2D source/API and callback compatibility checks, and any pinned LibreCAD 3 DWG-read consumer check. Neither is an independent parser vote; neither can qualify DWG writing. The current policy does not imply a consumer failure in this workspace or permission to promote the library's own claims. A future LC3 receipt must bind the exact library revision, build option, claim ledger, input profile, and source-to-imported disposition. |
| ACadSharp [repository version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) and [API reference](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/docs/api/index.md) | The README declares different read/write support by DXF/DWG revision: for example, its table marks AC1012 DWG read/write unsupported, AC1021 DWG writing unsupported, and several adjacent revisions supported. The API identifies distinct `DwgReader`, `DwgWriter`, `DxfReader`, and `DxfWriter` routes. These are useful operation/profile declarations, but the matrix is not accompanied there by per-entity denominators or external acceptance receipts. | Select ACadSharp only for a version and direction explicitly declared by the pinned package/source; record the exact runtime, build, revision, and entity/object dispositions. Treat a matrix checkmark as a candidate route, never as semantic conformance. Keep the previously recorded ACIS writer-omission report package-specific and unresolved by documentation alone. |
| ezdxf [file-loading guidance](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/tutorials/getting_data.rst), [XREF/transfer scope](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst), and [ACIS browser](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/launcher.rst) | ezdxf distinguishes strict `readfile` from the repair-oriented `recover` path. Its XREF transfer documentation says unsupported entities (including preserved unknown `DXFTagStorage` entities/proxy content and `ACAD_TABLE`) are ignored, and several OBJECTS features are outside that transfer operation. ## Deeper/broader ACIS-reader ecosystem and independent-semantics boundary (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass expands the ACIS/AcDs comparator search from DWG/DXF libraries to
standalone SAT/SAB readers and geometry-kernel integration. It updates the
existing PAR-07/S8 and J256/J260/J268/J284/J293/J295 external-evidence gates;
it is not normative DWG layout evidence, a local defect report, or runtime
qualification. The current ODA DWG specification remains authoritative for
the DWG container/owner/reference bytes. ACIS/ASM payload interpretation needs
its own independently recorded parser/kernel evidence.

### Candidate and independence crosswalk

| Candidate/source | What the project says or source inspection shows | Evidence value and boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Open CASCADE Technology (OCCT) [data-exchange policy](https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/discussions/1157) and [components preview](https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT-Components/blob/main/ReadMe.md) | The OCCT project lists STEP, IGES, glTF, BREP, STL, VRML, PLY and OBJ among open-source core exchange formats. It lists ACIS SAT/SAB and DXF among separately sold commercial exchange components. | Do not assume an unmodified open-source OCCT install is itself an ACIS reader. If the previously selected official/native ACIS runtime is used, pin its exact binary/version, platform, license/availability, and the API/import path. A commercial component route is a candidate semantic oracle, not open-source peer evidence. |
| [`cq-acis`](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis) [README](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/README.md), [geometry limits](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/docs/geometry-support.md), [SAB/ASM profile](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/docs/sab-support.md) | The project describes an experimental SAT/SAB parser with SAT save versions 105/400/600/700, ACIS BinaryFile 21800, and selected ASM BinaryFile4 versions 22000/22300/22600/22700/22900/23200. It types a bounded set of analytic geometry and topology, retains unknown records, and says unsupported geometry may fail conversion. It documents bounded precision/topology checks and explicitly limits NURBS and selected ASM profiles. Its public corpus README says sources are pinned by commit/blob hash and carries separate license notices for NIST/ezdxf source data. | Candidate independent parser for exact admitted profiles and diagnostics; potentially useful to compare payload decoding, topology references and analytic invariants. It is experimental and does not imply general ACIS/ASM coverage. It converts to CadQuery/OCCT shapes, so its B-rep validity/volume is not an independent-kernel verdict from FreeCAD. Pin a commit and test only an explicitly intersecting profile. Do not copy its corpus into this repository; if used externally, record exact source commit, blob/SHA-256, upstream provenance/license, build/runtime and per-input result. |
| [FreeCAD InventorLoader](https://github.com/jmplonka/InventorLoader), [SAT reader](https://github.com/jmplonka/InventorLoader/blob/master/Acis.py), [native importer](https://github.com/jmplonka/InventorLoader/blob/master/importerSAT.py) | The add-on contains its own Python `AcisReader`, advertises SAT/SAB and DXF 3D-solid import, and offers native-part and STEP-conversion routes. Its documentation says export is unsupported, lists omitted blending/helix/law-defined geometry, and includes older FreeCAD prerequisites. Source inspection shows reference linking can set a reference to `None` on lookup failure without a typed hard-failure at that site. | A distinct parser/importer candidate for comparison only after pinning the add-on and FreeCAD builds, instrumenting diagnostics, and verifying every reference resolves. Its Part/Shell/Face construction and STEP route execute through FreeCAD/OCCT; do not count it as a second kernel oracle or substitute it for the configured stock FreeCAD DXF importer. Old declared prerequisites make current-version/platform compatibility an explicit preflight, not an assumption. |
| FreeCAD [source architecture](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/The_FreeCAD_source_code.md) and CadQuery [kernel description](https://github.com/CadQuery/cadquery/blob/master/doc/primer.rst) | FreeCAD's documentation describes OCCT as its solid-geometry kernel; CadQuery describes itself as based on OCCT. Therefore `cq-acis`→CadQuery and InventorLoader→FreeCAD share the underlying OCCT kernel family with FreeCAD semantic-consumer tests. | Count parser diversity, geometry-kernel diversity, and application-consumer diversity as separate axes. A disagreement between independent decoders can reveal grammar/profile/association issues; agreement in the resulting OCCT shape does not independently validate the kernel's interpretation. |
| ezdxf [ACIS browser](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/launcher.rst) and [entity index](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/dxfentities/index.rst) | ezdxf documents raw SAT/SAB inspection/export and has modeler entity classes; this inspection route does not claim B-rep reconstruction. | Keep ezdxf useful for DXF tag/carrier extraction and strict parse/write checks, not as a B-rep semantic oracle. |

### Implementation-ready external gate (existing composed checkpoint only)

1. **Keep local implementation moving.** Do not add any of these readers as a
   production dependency, default CTest, per-slice check, or blocker. Continue
   the existing local fast-first queue; an unavailable external lane is
   `NOT_RUN/UNBOUND`, then self-unblock to the next local item.
2. **Preflight comparators once, before the composed ACIS gate.** Pin source
   commit/release and artifact hash; OS/architecture; compiler/runtime; OCCT,
   FreeCAD, CadQuery and add-on versions; importer/converter selection; exact

   provenance; and whether an independent kernel is actually in use. Reject
   any unpinned or unsupported profile as `NOT_RUN/UNBOUND`, not pass.
3. **Use a bounded witness set.** Prefer locally generated-from-scratch,
   analytic SAT/SAB witnesses where the chosen writer can produce them, or

4. **Score each layer separately:** (a) libdxfrw DWG owner/handle/AcDs graph
   association and exact payload digest; (b) peer parser active-record count,
   typed record families, reference closure, unsupported/raw counts and
   diagnostics; (c) independently known analytic measures/topology/orientation
   and transform; (d) target application import, document contents and
   disposition. A matching digest proves carriage only. A parsed graph does

5. **Make failure observable.** Include one intentionally unsupported-profile

6. **Keep native consumer qualification distinct.** The required Linux and
   Windows FreeCAD runs still use the configured production DXF importer and

   InventorLoader is an optional alternate-importer experiment only, and a

7. **Promote nothing from research availability.** These sources only identify

   J260, J268, J284, J293, or J295; those remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. No
   support claim, finding ID, or subplan is added or promoted.

## Implementation progress — PAR-138 DWG ModelDocViewStyle dictionary-derived name join (2026-10-20; local fast slice, uncommitted)

The dwg2dxf adapter now completes a post-read, order-independent join from the
DWG header-resolved NOD to `ACAD_DETAILVIEWSTYLE` / `ACAD_SECTIONVIEWSTYLE`,
their NOD-owned child dictionaries, and each typed style's unique dictionary
entry. It requires complete dictionary entries, unique NOD keys and child
handles, correct dictionary/style owners, nonempty unique names, and no
conflicting style handles. Names are prepared and applied only after the whole
current-import join validates; ambiguous or malformed graphs leave typed names
unchanged and keep the name-resolution receipt false. Newly retained name
bytes are admitted against the existing aggregate typed-style budget, and
repeating the resolution does not charge them twice. DXF name resolution stays
on its existing parser path.

The generated fast control uses the existing locally generated style graph,
clears the typed names, and builds a DWG-origin adapter envelope with the
child dictionaries retained in reverse order. It verifies both Detail names
and the Section name resolve from dictionary keys, then checks idempotent
accounting. Wrong-owner, duplicate style-target, and exhausted-retention-budget
controls all refuse without partially assigning any name. This exercises the
adapter's post-read graph association; it is **not** an actual DWG parse or
producer qualification, and it adds no `DRW_Interface` callback or changes to
LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3 callback ordering.

## Autodesk named-object dictionary owner crosswalk (2026-10-20; local control refinement)

The previous corpus review found that peer sample folders alone do not establish
the expected object graph. A targeted check against Autodesk's DXF and ObjectARX
references now pins several named-object owner routes that the generated
`retainNamedObjectCallbacks()` control exercises:

| Family | Autodesk evidence | Required control shape |
|---|---|---|
| `MLINESTYLE` | The DXF reference says group 330 is the owning dictionary and always the `ACAD_MLINESTYLE` entry of the NOD. | NOD entry `ACAD_MLINESTYLE` -> dictionary -> named style; the style's group 330 names that dictionary. |
| `TABLESTYLE` | The DXF reference says group 330 is the `ACAD_TABLESTYLE` entry of the NOD. | NOD entry -> `ACAD_TABLESTYLE` dictionary -> style entry; typed and raw style identities use that dictionary as owner. |
| `MLEADERSTYLE` | ActiveX creates/accesses the style through `Dictionaries.Item("ACAD_MLEADERSTYLE")`; ObjectARX exposes the named-object MLeader-style dictionary. | Keep a dictionary between the NOD and style records; callback identity must retain that owner. |
| Detail/section view styles | ObjectARX methods state that `ACAD_DETAILVIEWSTYLE` and `ACAD_SECTIONVIEWSTYLE` keys in the NOD open dictionaries containing the corresponding style objects. | Keep the named dictionary and typed style parent links explicit. |
| Scale list and plot style names | Autodesk's dictionary-object example lists `ACAD_SCALELIST` and `ACAD_PLOTSTYLENAME` as NOD dictionaries with named children. | Model these as dictionary routes rather than direct typed-object NOD targets. |
| Dictionary variables | The same Autodesk example lists `AcDbVariableDictionary` as an NOD child, with variable names such as `FIELDEVAL` below it. | Use the documented `AcDbVariableDictionary` root key and retain the variable's dictionary parent. |

This crosswalk updates only the locally generated in-memory DXF control: its
NOD now points to the family dictionaries, and style/resource records point
back to their direct dictionary owner. It does not add a binary fixture or
promote DWG semantic support. The callback test also no longer requires the
writer to change a non-conflicting source handle: the check is referential
closure (NOD -> dictionary -> entry -> typed/raw record), while preserving a
valid source identity is acceptable.

The research and test refinement do not add a new finding or top-level
subplan; totals remain **141 / 78**. The focused
`dwg2dxf_named_object_callback_storage` CTest passed (1/1) after the in-memory
control was corrected. Keep the fast-first cadence; full suites remain
reserved for the plan's composed checkpoints. J256, J260,
J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

Primary references: Autodesk [MLINESTYLE DXF](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3EC12E5B-F5F6-484D-880F-D69EBE186D79.htm),
[TABLESTYLE DXF](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-0DBCA057-9F6C-4DEB-A66F-8A9B3C62FB1A.htm),
[MLeaderStyle ActiveX](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2022/CHS/AutoCAD-ActiveX-Reference/files/GUID-14AC2D0B-EBFC-44B9-982D-9112539F8DE8.htm),
[MLeader-style dictionary ObjectARX API](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2019/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OREF-AcDbDatabase__getMLeaderStyleDictionary_AcDbDictionary___AcDb__OpenMode.html),
[detail/section view style dictionaries](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2019/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OREF-__MEMBERTYPE_Methods_AcDbDatabase.html), and
[AutoLISP dictionary example](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/AutoCAD-AutoLISP/files/GUID-24E52678-513E-4322-8070-B23C8945DC3D.htm).

## Deeper/broader dictionary owner-link semantics and peer convergence (2026-10-20; research + local guard refinement)

This pass cross-checks the dictionary-variable route at three distinct layers:
the Autodesk DXF object contract, an independent DWG implementation's lookup
path, and a mature DXF library's object-graph behavior. Agreement is useful
for implementation shape, but does not turn peer code into format authority
or semantic support evidence.

| Evidence | Finding | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk [DICTIONARYVAR DXF](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D305303C-F9CE-4714-9C92-607BFDA891B4.htm) and [DICTIONARY DXF](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-40B92C63-26F0-485B-A9C2-B349099B26D0.htm) | A DICTIONARYVAR's group 330 is the `ACDBVARIABLEDICTIONARY` owner. A DICTIONARY has its own owner-object group 330 and entries represented as name/group-3 plus group-350 soft-owner handles. These edges have different roles and must not be collapsed into a single “handle exists” check. | Require both edges: NOD key to a child DICTIONARY, then the dictionary entry to the variable; independently verify the variable's owner handle equals that child DICTIONARY. Preserve NOD-to-child owner validation and the exact typed-object identity check. |
| Autodesk [About Object Ownership](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-CC1D6F91-42BF-4946-8D4B-6FC6A39100C5.htm) and [Object Group Codes example](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-1038FDE4-745D-469D-972E-1F977D674882.htm) | The NOD is the first OBJECTS record; subsequent non-graphical objects may be owned by it or by other objects. | Keep first-record NOD identification as a format invariant. Test order independence only for child dictionaries and DICTIONARYVAR records after that required root record; a file placing the NOD later is invalid-input coverage, not a positive reordered-graph case. |
| LibreDWG [`dwg_variable_dict`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dwg.c) | The independent DWG library's helper finds `AcDbVariableDictionary` through its dictionary lookup, resolves the named child entry, then explicitly requires the target object's fixed type to be `DICTIONARYVAR` before returning its value. This corroborates the traversal/type-check shape; it does not establish correctness of this repository's DWG reader or writer. | Keep a two-stage lookup and typed-target validation in generated controls and graph preflight. Do not infer all variables from one matching name or accept a same-handle object of the wrong type. |
| ezdxf [`Dictionary` implementation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dictionary.py) | ezdxf requires dictionary contents to be OBJECTS-section objects, sets an object's DXF owner to the containing dictionary when linked, and audits/removes dictionary links to missing objects. Its parser recognizes entry references in group 350 and group 360. New dictionaries default to group 350, while loaded entry-code state is retained at dictionary level for serialization; the source comments explicitly call 360 observed but undocumented by the Autodesk DICTIONARY table. | Keep group 350 as the Autodesk-documented/default generated form. Treat group-360 acceptance as a separate permissive-input compatibility case, not a normative format rule. For any rewrite test, assert the selected writer's actual rule rather than assuming all libraries canonicalize to group 350. |
| Local `DRW_Dictionary::parseCode`, `dxfRW::writeDictionary`, reserved-root writer (`src/libdxfrw.cpp`); strict graph guard (`dwg2dxf/dx_iface.cpp`) | The parser accepts either group 350 or 360 for dictionary entries. Ordinary child dictionaries emit group 360 when `hardOwner == 1`, otherwise group 350; mixed source codes are not preserved there. The NOD is regenerated through a separate reserved-root path and its root entries emit group 350 regardless of the source root's hard-owner flag. The guard requires one case-insensitive canonical NOD key, a NOD-owned DICTIONARY target, and matching group-330 owners. | No second production parser change is indicated. Test expected output separately for regenerated NOD edges and ordinary dictionary edges: NOD entry code 350; child entries follow the emitted dictionary's `hardOwner` flag. Continue to test permissive mixed-code input independently of writer normalization. |

### Readiness additions

1. The local guard slice is implemented and fast-validated. It covers positive
   canonical routing plus direct-NOD, wrong-variable-owner, provenance,
   output-preservation, duplicate-root-key, wrong-target-kind, missing-target,
   and corrected-retry controls.
2. The generated parser-compatibility control now uses group 360 on the NOD
   child link and one child entry, group 350 on its sibling, then imports and
   rewrites in both ASCII and Binary. It also places DICTIONARYVAR records
   before their referenced child dictionary to verify subordinate-object
   order independence while retaining the NOD as the first OBJECTS record.
   The latter is a format requirement: Autodesk defines the NOD as first, so
   moving it later is invalid-input coverage only. The 360 case is labelled
   compatibility-only because Autodesk's cited DICTIONARY schema documents
   350, not 360. The test asserts libdxfrw rewrite output as
   group 350 for regenerated NOD entries and `hardOwner == 1 ? 360 : 350`
   for ordinary child-dictionary entries; it does not claim universal
   normalization across peers.
3. Keep dictionary entry key/reference validation, dictionary object's parent
   owner, and child DICTIONARYVAR group-330 owner as three separate assertions.
   A passing `DICTIONARYVAR` payload parse or an existing handle alone is not
   sufficient.
4. Leave malformed, ambiguous, missing, or wrong-kind routes fail-closed for
   strict export. For permissive import, record whether the parser preserves,
   ignores, or diagnoses each condition; never silently synthesize the
   canonical owner edge from a variable's name.

This is a local graph-correctness refinement only. It adds no finding ID,
top-level subplan, external sample, dependency, full-suite run, peer execution,
native CAD run, or support promotion. Findings and top-level subplans remain
**141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and cannot promote claims. Continue with the next local
ready slice while retaining the scheduled low-frequency composed validation.

## Deeper/broader application-wrapper and port-lineage audit (2026-10-20; research only)

### Decision

This pass expands the existing peer ledger from libraries and CAD consumers to
newly surfaced browser applications and language ports. Product count is not
parser independence: the reviewed routes resolve to ACadRust, ACadSharp, or
LibreDWG lineages already represented in PAR-07/S8. A newly surfaced
application can still serve as a useful downstream 2D consumer, but only when
its parser dependency, version, platform, and selected import/render path are
bound. No new local defect or top-level subplan is justified.

The strongest implementation-specific lesson is version refusal: `acad-ts`
documents a historical DWG writer path that emitted an R2004 container with
an R2007 signature, which external CAD engines reject; its current matrix
marks AC1021 DWG writing unsupported. This is peer evidence, not a local
libdxfrw defect. It reinforces the existing exact-target check: a requested
version, a header signature, and the actual container version are separate
observations, and a writer must reject a target it cannot encode rather than
publish a mismatched file.

This research changes no local implementation order, validation cadence,
fixture policy, dependency, test, or support claim. Keep the 2D consumer
contract and all six J items unchanged: J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. Findings/subplans remain
**141 / 78**.

### Cross-project evidence and route disposition

| Project/source | Current source evidence | Plan disposition |
|---|---|---|
| CodeCAD [`cadview-core/Cargo.toml`](https://github.com/backkem/codecad/blob/main/crates/cadview-core/Cargo.toml), [`Cargo.lock`](https://github.com/backkem/codecad/blob/main/Cargo.lock), and [README](https://github.com/backkem/codecad) | The app describes a DWG viewer/editor and renderer, but its core depends on `acadrust = "0.3"`; the checked-in lock resolves that to `acadrust` 0.3.4. That is the same parser lineage as ACadRust and is older than the 0.6.4 release already reviewed in this plan. | Classify as `ACADRUST_DERIVATIVE_CONSUMER`, not an independent DWG parser. At the existing composed checkpoint it may be considered for a narrow 2D editor/render projection only, and only after pinning the app commit, release binary hash, locked crate checksum, platform, and exact visible-object denominator. Never use its render result to establish raw-record preservation, DWG writer conformance, or 3D/ACIS semantics. |
| `acad-ts` [README and interoperability notes](https://github.com/node-projects/acad-ts/blob/master/README.md) | The project calls itself a TypeScript port of ACadSharp, identifies its source ACadSharp commit and last-compared commit, and maintains a commit audit. Its matrix excludes AC1021 DWG writing; the notes say earlier releases emitted an R2004 container carrying an R2007 signature and were rejected by external CAD engines. | Classify as `ACADSHARP_PORT`, not an independent parser vote. The commit audit can help localize a suspected ACadSharp-derived mapping difference, but any comparison must bind both source histories and exact package artifacts. Retain target-version refusal and independently check actual DWG magic plus `$ACADVER`/strict reopen; never count a requested AC1021 save as AC1021 output without those checks. |
| MLightCAD [open-source DWG viewer documentation](https://github.com/mlightcad/cad-viewer) and [parser/licensing route note](https://github.com/mlightcad/cad-viewer/blob/main/PROPRIETARY-PARSER.md) | The documented default open-source DWG path uses `libredwg-web` / `@mlightcad/libredwg-converter`; DXF uses a separate in-house data-model parser. The proprietary DWG parser is a distinct licensed package and documents only partial SAB decode with wireframe/bounding-box fallback, not full B-rep tessellation. | Count the default DWG path under LibreDWG lineage, not as a new DWG parser. Keep the separate DXF parser potentially useful for one specific DXF projection question, but not as whole-document parity or B-rep evidence. The proprietary parser is not eligible for this open-source peer set; do not acquire a license or add a dependency for this plan. |
| [`flyfish-dev/cad-viewer`](https://github.com/flyfish-dev/cad-viewer) and related LibreDWG-WASM viewers | Their public README describes DWG ingestion through `@mlightcad/libredwg-web` / LibreDWG WebAssembly and conversion to a scene/document model. | Treat each as an application/renderer on the LibreDWG parser lineage. A visible-scene comparison may diagnose a specific 2D rendering projection at the composed gate, but it cannot add another parser vote or prove file-graph preservation. |
| [CADKernel README](https://github.com/kernalix7/CADKernel) | The mutable README presents broad DWG/DXF format checkmarks, while its ACIS SAT/SAB table marks read and write unchecked and its FAQ says proprietary-format import is planned. This is an internal claim-scope inconsistency; no source implementation, supported test corpus, or external acceptance evidence was admitted in this review. | Mark `NOT_ADMITTED_CLAIM_CONFLICT`. Do not cite its version checkmarks as peer coverage or use it to change a finding. Reconsider only after a source-linked implementation, exact released artifact, tested version/direction matrix, and per-family results are available. |
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and [DWG converter implementation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py) | The reviewed documentation snapshot describes external DWG conversion followed by one of two selectable DXF importers. The docs state their feature subsets differ and stock import does not read ACIS solids. The Python adapter invokes converters and its observable route depends on configured preference/fallback. The documentation repository is archived, so a later runtime qualification must bind the application build and actual importer/converter route. | No change to the existing platform gate: record exact converter, importer backend, preferences, executable/build, exit result, intermediate DXF, and imported-object dispositions. A successful UI open is only the selected consumer projection. ACIS remains out of stock FreeCAD's documented DXF semantics. |

### Implementation-ready refinement with no per-slice cost

1. Keep the active local queue moving. These newly discovered products create
   no prerequisite, mandatory peer run, new test registration, or delay to a
   fast implementation slice.
2. At the already-scheduled composed PAR-07/S8 checkpoint, add or fill one
   route-lineage row before interpreting results. Record `application`,
   `parser implementation`, `parser version/commit`, `wrapper/port lineage`,
   `build hash`, `platform`, `input hash/provenance`, `requested output
   version`, `actual magic / DXF $ACADVER`, `strict reopen`, and per-source
   entity/object disposition. For 3D routes also record the geometry kernel
   and unsupported/fallback state.
3. Do not run every app. Select a peer only to resolve a named remaining
   question: the same-source `acad-ts` port for a narrow ACadSharp-derived
   drift check; CodeCAD or another viewer for a specific 2D consumer
   projection; MLightCAD's open-source path only as a LibreDWG-derived
   rendering route. If no question remains, mark it `NOT_RUN / NOT_NEEDED`.
4. For any writer comparison, verify output freshness, actual target version,
   strict independent parse, and full expected source disposition. A matching
   signature string without a compatible container is failure, not
   compatibility. Reject unsupported target versions atomically before
   creating or replacing output.
5. Keep product-level results advisory. They do not change PAR-07/S8's stages
   (DWG decode → graph/owner closure → DXF carrier → strict reopen → supported
   semantics → native consumer), do not promote a peer's marketing matrix, and
   cannot resolve any deferred J item by themselves.

No peer repository was cloned or built; no peer executable, native CAD app, or
external drawing was run or downloaded. No code, tests, fixtures, dependency,
or CTest registration changed. The only plan effect is a more accurate
implementation-lineage map and a stronger explicit output-version assertion
at the existing composed gate.

## Deeper/broader follow-up: forked DXF reader and ACIS renderer evidence boundary (2026-10-20; research only)

### Decision

This follow-up deepens the 2026-10-17 `kedazo/dxf-go` candidate review; it does
not add another peer or independent DWG codec. It clarifies the candidate's
unknown-record writer limitations and its LibreDWG-correlated DWG diagnostic,
and rechecks that a documented edge projection is not an ACIS/ACDS semantic
validator. Keep comparator eligibility operation-specific:
format parsing, raw-carrier retention, writer round-trip, geometric
interpretation, and native-consumer acceptance are separate claims.

| Route / artifact | Evidence found in primary project material | Admission and limits |
|---|---|---|
| `kedazo/dxf-go` (candidate already inventoried 2026-10-17) | Its current package README declares text and binary DXF read/write from R12 through AC1032, typed entities including HATCH, MESH, and 3DFACE, and `UnknownEntity` raw group-code retention. It explicitly says it is a fork of `ixmilia/dxf-go`. The `UnknownEntity` API documentation qualifies retention: application group 102 is dropped when referenced objects are not written, and other references (for example, to OBJECTS-section styles) may not survive. The package index displays v0.3.3 and says this version is not the latest module version. | Retain the existing `IXMILIA_DXF_FORK / OPTIONAL` classification; this is not an independent parser lineage. Add a whole-graph no-loss check to any future unknown-entity writer probe; raw code-pair retention alone is insufficient. Pin package and immutable source commit, runtime, and exact input. The API/docs remain capability claims, not conformance evidence. |
| `kedazo/dxf-go/cmd/dxfcheck` | The package documentation says DWG input/xrefs are converted with LibreDWG `dwg2dxf`, then checked against the DWG's own entity counts; the conversion and `dwgread` are selected as LibreDWG tools. | `LIBREDWG_CONVERSION_AND_COUNT_DIAGNOSTIC`, not an independent DWG parser, writer, or semantic oracle. Counts can locate candidate omissions, but do not establish record identity, handle/reference closure, typed values, or geometry. For a needed check, capture exact LibreDWG binary/version and compare per-handle/per-record expected dispositions in addition to counts. |
| `dxf-go` DXF writer | The project declares ASCII and binary DXF writes and HATCH read/write; the README does not, by itself, establish independent expected-value comparisons or native interoperability. | A potential third-party serialization comparison only after exact version pinning and per-field expected-value assertions. Do not accept self-read/self-write equality or shared-ancestor agreement as independent semantic evidence. No package was downloaded or executed in this research pass. |
| ProCad / ProGPU CAD document IO | ProCad identifies its IO as ACadSharp-backed. ProGPU's architecture document says ACadSharp owns the DWG/DXF file-format object model. | `ACADSHARP_DERIVATIVE_CONSUMER` for document import/export and typed object coverage, not an independent DWG/DXF codec. Product UI, rendering, and performance claims remain consumer observations, not parser votes. |
| ProGPU ACIS/SAB renderer path | A separate ProGPU DXF technical document describes `AcisSabParser` scanning binary SAB tokens, isolating `edge` records, tracing vertex references to points, and outputting `Acis3dEdge(Start, End)` records for projection. This corroborates the already-recorded edge-projection scope, but the inspected description does not claim complete shells/faces/loops/coedges/surfaces, validity checking, solid operations, or independent expected-volume tests. | Keep the existing `PROJECTION_ONLY / NOT_ADMITTED_AS_READER` boundary. It is a possible narrow edge-render comparison, not proof of ACIS/ACDS decoding, manifold B-rep semantics, or an independent semantic oracle. Require source-and-test review, unresolved-reference accounting, topology closure, analytic expected geometry/volume, and an independent kernel/native acceptance route before any stronger claim. |
| `Solid3D` / `Region` model fields in `dxf-go` | Public model docs expose `Solid3D` format version, `CustomData` / `CustomData2`, and a history-object handle; `Region` exposes `CustomData` / `CustomData2`. Names and raw-carrier fields alone do not show that ACIS topology is interpreted. | Treat as possible structural-carrier comparison only if a pinned implementation and tests confirm actual wire mapping. Do not use model type names, field presence, or a successful write as ACIS/ACDS semantic support evidence. |

### Implementation-ready refinement with no per-slice cost

1. Keep the local implementation queue and fast-validation cadence unchanged.
   These projects add no prerequisite, mandatory peer run, new CTest, or pause.
2. At the already-scheduled composed PAR-07/S8 checkpoint, add a route row only
   if a named unresolved claim benefits from it. Record the parser lineage,
   exact package/source identity, runtime/build, platform, input provenance and
   hash, ASCII/binary variant, requested and actual output version, strict
   reopen result, and per-source entity/object/handle disposition.
3. If `dxf-go` is selected, choose one exact DXF question (for example, a
   bounded MESH, HATCH, or unknown-entity write case), pin the immutable source
   and package, and prepare expected values independently before execution.
   Its DWG helper route must be recorded as LibreDWG-derived. Do not expand this
   into a per-slice peer matrix.
4. Keep opaque 3DSOLID/REGION carriage separate from ACIS interpretation:
   verify actual payload group/chunk mapping, size and version behavior,

## Implementation progress — PAR-87/7AW residual DWG entity ordering (2026-10-20; local generated fast slice, uncommitted)

HEAD `de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9` still selected the minimum
source-order entry by rescanning the remaining `ObjectMap`; this pass closes
that locally actionable gap without changing DWG layouts or entity decoding.
The reader now snapshots bounded immutable `(sourceOrdinal, loc, handle)` keys,
sorts the snapshot once, and re-finds each handle before processing it. It
retains the existing map-mutation behavior for BLOCK/compound consumption,
checks the captured map/source identity before touching a frame, caps visits at
twice the admitted key count, and fails if unexplained entries remain. Only an
unchanged, unpublished `Pending` frame restored after a soft false read can be
retried, at most once; no unordered-map iterator survives parsing or detach.
The complexity statement is intentionally limited: sorting is O(r log r),
while individual hash-map lookups do not carry a deterministic worst-case
O(r log r) guarantee for the whole sweep.

The implementation is backed by the repository's generated fast controls:
512-key comparison envelope; equal-ordinal/location handle tie-break; atomic
count/byte/peak-capacity admission refusal; injected scratch allocation
failure; retry-policy predicates for allowed and disallowed states; and 64
locally generated AC1021
LINE frames with an exact source-order callback transcript and empty-map check.
A separate locally generated AC1015 VERTEX test drives the actual legacy
`readDwgEntities` take-frame path: its first virtual read restores the exact
source key and returns a soft failure, the second read publishes one frame receipt,
and a negative control that restores again is rejected after exactly two
attempts without publication. This exposed and fixed an ordering defect in
which the legacy wrapper marked the frame `Failed` before the residual retry
guard could observe its required `Pending` disposition. The owning
`libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix` and adjacent insert-staging owner also pass. The
comparator does not include skipped/unused records or rewrite the file layout.

One synthetic legacy probe was explicitly rejected as an oracle: the generic
AC1015 LINE frame encoder failed typed-body parsing for its generated frames.
The passing 64-frame runtime transcript is AC1021, not AC1015. The separate
AC1015 VERTEX control uses its own generated encoder and only asserts the
restoration/retry/receipt lifecycle; it does not qualify external legacy
compound semantics. Historical isolated-commit evidence for `0ee3bff2` remains
historical and is not substituted for this worktree's test result.

The authoritative ODA specification copy available in this environment was
`/Users/dli/dev/ACadSharp/reference/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf`
(v5.4.1); the repository-preferred `~/doc/dwg/` copy was absent. The relevant
chapters were read before changing `src/intern/dwgreader*`: §23.1, R13–R15
object map (p.251); §20.1 object section (p.103); §20.4.1–2 common entity and
handle data (pp.109–111); and §20.4.8, §20.4.11–17 for SEQEND, VERTEX and
POLYLINE compound references/order (pp.115–122). This is a worklist-ordering
change, not new DWG format evidence.

direct `--residual-entity-sweep` passed; focused CTest selection

passed. The full suite, large-file timing, native CAD, external producer,
