<a id="deeper-broader-xref-state-identity-and-overlay-boundary-2026-10-20"></a>
## Deeper/broader XREF state, identity, and overlay boundary (2026-10-20; research plus local fast-slice correction)

This pass found and corrected a semantic conflation in the current PAR-65 / 7AM.4
implementation. The ODA DWG `Loaded Bit` is not DXF BLOCK group-70 bit 32.
Group 70 bit 32 denotes a resolved external reference/dependent record and is
documented as ignored on input; the unload state is a separate DXF BLOCK
group-71 bit. An unloaded flag can therefore coexist with either value of the
group-70 resolved bit. The plan and local model now keep these states separate.

| Evidence | Primary-source result | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ODA v5.4.1 [§20.4.52, pp. 164–165](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) | The R2000+ `BLOCK_HEADER` body has a `Loaded Bit`; zero means loaded for an XREF. The same record also has XREF-reference/index/dependency/overlay fields, the pathname, and a common NULL hard-pointer slot. ODA does not define this loaded bit as the DXF resolved-status bit. | Decode the wire bit into a distinct `xrefUnloaded` property: `0 → false`, `1 → true` for XREFs. Never synthesize or clear DXF `BLOCK` group-70 bit 32 from it. Keep the NULL pointer invariant and DWG-only index/pointer fields separate. |
| Autodesk [BLOCK DXF table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-66D32572-005A-4E23-8B8B-8726E8C14302.htm), [BLOCK_RECORD table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A1FD1934-7EF5-4D35-A4B0-F8AE54A9A20A.htm), and ObjectARX [`setIsUnloaded`](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OREF-AcDbBlockTableRecord__setIsUnloaded_bool.html) | BLOCK group 70 assigns distinct bits to XREF (4), overlay (8), externally dependent (16), resolved (32; ignored on input), and referenced (64; ignored on input). ObjectARX explicitly says the XREF `isUnloaded` property is the first bit of BLOCK group 71 and is set when unloaded. BLOCK_RECORD has separate insertion units, explodability, scalability, and preview fields. | Model group 70 and group 71 independently. Preserve existing BLOCK_RECORD metadata as its own record; do not collapse the BLOCK entity and BLOCK_RECORD into a single flags/path bucket. Group 71 true is valid only on an XREF and is emitted only for a target profile that carries it; reject unsupported target combinations before publication. |
| Autodesk [BLOCKS section](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A3E4F1D3-79C9-489C-B7EC-3924DA7F25C9.htm), [attach/detach and paths](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-Core/files/GUID-A987D2FF-45BD-474E-99C1-E6316A42F667.htm), and [nested/overlay rules](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2022/ENU/AutoCAD-LT/files/GUID-0D7D1315-B58A-4BCD-9953-282FF578B144.htm) | DXF stores an XREF as a BLOCK definition with group-1 path; paths can be full, relative, or absent. A relative nested-XREF path is relative to its immediate host. Attachments can nest and flow through a containing drawing; overlays do not flow when that host is itself referenced. The external file is a live link whose contents are loaded/reloaded by a consumer, not inline geometry in the host block definition. | Keep literal path retention separate from path resolution, file existence, load/reload, transmittal packaging, and visible geometry. Do no filesystem probing or path normalization in the codec slice. Keep attach/overlay nesting and per-INSERT transforms in a separate composed consumer test; a block flag/path roundtrip is not XREF application support. |
| ezdxf [XREF documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/xref.html), ACadSharp reader/writer sources ([DWG reader](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/IO/DWG/DwgStreamReaders/DwgObjectReader.cs), [DXF BLOCK writer](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/IO/DXF/DxfStreamWriter/DxfBlocksSectionWriter.cs)), and LibreDWG [current NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | ezdxf describes an XREF as a flagged/path-bearing BLOCK without inline contents, referenced by one or more INSERTs; its cross-document loader is a distinct operation with documented omissions. ACadSharp carries `IsUnloaded` separately from `BlockTypeFlags` and writes group 71 separately. LibreDWG's recent rename from `loaded_bit` to `xref_loaded` is a useful field-name cross-check. These peer sources corroborate the separation but do not replace ODA/Autodesk or prove interoperable output. | Admit peers only as crosswalks for named field/operation questions. Distinguish direct parse/write from XREF `embed`/import/resolve operations, record ignored items, and do not use same-library reread, feature names, or a successful XREF loader as independent support evidence. No peer binary, external drawing, or dependency is added to the fast slice. |

### Implementation-ready plan correction

1. **PAR-65 / 7AM.4 current local correction:** `DRW_Block` and
   `DRW_Block_Record` now carry `xrefUnloaded` separately; DXF `BLOCK` parses
   and emits group 71; DWG `BLOCK_HEADER` parsing copies the raw loaded bit
   directly into the separate property; and the DWG writer serializes it from
   that property, not from `flags & 32`. Group-70 resolved/dependent bits stay
   in the group-70 field and are not a proxy for unload status. Since the
   public structures gained fields, downstream binaries must be rebuilt; no
   `DRW_Interface` virtual was added.
2. Generated fast controls cover AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and
   AC1032 with both unloaded values, while keeping group-70 bit 32 set in the
   source metadata so the two states are deliberately crossed. A test-local
   raw-body bit walker checks the emitted DWG `BLOCK_RECORD` fields before
   production parseback. Existing locally authored ASCII/Binary DXF coverage
   carries BLOCK flags and group 71 together and checks the following ENDBLK.
   These tests establish only the covered fields/cursors, not full object
   framing or string-stream conformance.
3. **DXF-origin routing is a distinct, conditional integration—not an
   existing in-tree adapter slice.** Source audit confirms `dwg2dxf` imports
   either DXF or DWG through `dx_iface::fileImport`, but its export path creates
   `dxfRW`; no production `dx_iface` route invokes `dwgRW::write`. The public
   `dxfRW` reader callbacks and callback-driven `dwgRW` writer can be composed
   by a consumer, but libdxfrw does not currently provide that bridge. Do not
   block the direct `dwgRW::defineBlock(DRW_Block_Record)` contract or add a
   speculative converter. If a built-in DXF-to-DWG route is explicitly in
   scope, give it a separate implementation subplan: capture BLOCK and
   BLOCK_RECORD independently, pair by source handle/owner/name evidence with
   a unique one-to-one result, reconcile conflicts before opening/publishing
   output, then preserve group-70 flags, group-71 unload state, group-1 path,
   record-level units/description/preview, and DWG-only XREF index fields in
   distinct members. Keep empty-path policy target-profile-specific; never
   fabricate a path. Validate that optional route with locally generated
   DXF→adapter→DWG controls and pre-publication conflict sentinels. Until that
   adapter is in scope, identity pairing is a downstream integration
   requirement, not a current libdxfrw code blocker or a support claim.
4. At the later composed application gate, exercise at least one attachment
   and one overlay with a nested reference, multiple INSERT transforms, a
   relative nested path resolved from the immediate host, and missing-file
   behavior. Record actual opened objects, warnings, and path resolution. This
   consumer-only qualification is not added to every local slice and does not
   require checking external files during codec read/write.
5. Findings and top-level subplans remain **141 / 78**. J256, J260, J268,
   J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; nothing here promotes DWG,
   DXF, XREF resolution, ACIS/AcDs, 3D, or native-platform support claims.

The following focused gates passed after the correction: the strict GCC
`-Werror` build of `libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip`,
`libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests`, and `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests`; direct
`--block-record-xref-roundtrip`, `--block-record-xref-index`, and
`--block-xref-path-roundtrip`; and the four-Ctest selector for those three
owners plus `libdxfrw_block_owners`. The full suite, peer tools, and native CAD
were not run. No new fixture, dependency, or CTest was added; test DWGs/DXFs
are generated in temporary directories or derived in-memory from existing
repository fixtures. The shared tree remains uncommitted.

## Deeper/broader GDAL DWG/DXF route matrix and 3D evidence ceiling (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass refreshed the GDAL routes against its current primary driver
documentation and cross-checked those operation boundaries against the local
PAR-07/S8 evidence gates. It found no new local codec defect. GDAL is useful
only when its selected driver and OGR projection are made explicit: the
similarly named `CAD` and `DWG` registrations do not represent the same
implementation, and the DXF driver's raw-carrier mode is not a solid-model
reader. No GDAL build or executable was run and no drawing was downloaded.

| Route / source | Current primary-source observation | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| GDAL [CAD — AutoCAD DWG driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/cad.html) and [vector-driver index](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/index.html) | The `CAD` driver documentation says its DWG route is based on libopencad and read-only. Its listed projection is narrow: POINT, LINE, CIRCLE/ARC, and 3DFACE; lines/arcs are mapped to OGR geometries, and bulged polylines may be tessellated. The vector-driver index separately lists `CAD` with internal libopencad and `DWG` with the ODA Teigha library. The driver docs do not promise a stable source-handle attribute for the CAD projection. | Treat `CAD` and `DWG` as distinct routes. The open-source libopencad route can be considered only as a narrow read/projection cross-check for an exact supported cohort. Before comparison, verify the registered driver name, build/runtime version and linked backend; do not infer the route from `.dwg` input or a generic claim that “GDAL opened it.” Do not compare only aggregate entity counts or attribute-free geometry where duplicate entities can alias. If the projection exposes no stable identity for the selected build, restrict it to a uniquely discriminating scratch control and keep it advisory. It cannot qualify writing, full DWG preservation, unsupported entity behavior, or 3D semantics. |
| GDAL [DXF driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | The driver reads ASCII DXF and writes DXF in the AutoCAD 2004 format (its docs describe interoperability with AutoCAD 2004 and later). Binary DXF input is documented beginning with GDAL 3.12 (Binary DXF is not DWG). The OGR model projects the document into layers/features; raw unhandled code values are opt-in, handles are exposed as `EntityHandle`, and block inlining is a configurable route. | Use only as an optional, version-pinned DXF parser/projection comparator. Capture GDAL version, driver identity, ASCII/Binary encoding, `$ACADVER`, configuration options, entity handles, raw-code option, layer/block mode, and warnings. Compare exact source-handle and selected field/tag values only; OGR geometry, tessellation, styling, and feature counts are not a lossless document oracle. Do not use its R2004 writer output to qualify libdxfrw DXF writing. |
| GDAL [DXF 3D extensibility mode](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html#3d-extensibility) | The documentation states that 3DSOLID, REGION, BODY and SURFACE carriers are skipped by default because GDAL cannot make OGR geometries from them. With `DXF_3D_EXTENSIBLE_MODE=TRUE`, it exposes `ASMData` and `ASMTransform` (12 column-major reals) only for AC1027 and later. This is carrier exposure, not a kernel/B-rep result. | A missing solid in default mode is an expected skip, not proof of corrupt data or libdxfrw loss. At the already-scheduled composed checkpoint, enable the option explicitly only for an AC1027+ DXF carrier question. Compare source handle, exact bytes/digest and transform components against an independently specified expected value; separately record whether the route was unavailable, skipped-by-default, exposed, malformed, or failed. Do not call a byte match a valid solid, a transform extraction a geometry result, or raw ASM preservation semantic 3D support. |
| GDAL general format output and vector data model | The DXF route is an OGR projection: the driver maps CAD records to spatial features and may tessellate or simplify fields that do not fit that model. A DXF writer exists, but it writes the OGR model rather than an arbitrary complete DWG/DXF object graph. | Keep parser-level group/tag inspection, projected OGR geometry, and output/reopen evidence as separate stages. Any future GDAL-based comparison must declare the exact question and expected disposition before invoking the peer. Do not add GDAL as a required dependency, convert all repository samples for a census, or turn its support table into a capability checklist for libdxfrw. |

### Implementation-ready refinement to existing PAR-07/S8

1. Keep the implementation queue and its fast validation cadence unchanged.
   No GDAL install, peer process, online file, or full suite becomes a
   prerequisite for a local code slice. Use GDAL only at the already-planned
   composed comparison checkpoint and only if a suitable pinned build is
   available there.
2. Before each optional run, pre-register a compact route row containing
   `GDAL version/build + driver name/backend + input hash/provenance + format /
   AC code / encoding + operation + options + expected source identities +
   per-identity disposition`. The `CAD`/libopencad DWG projection and the DXF
   driver are separate rows, not interchangeable “GDAL” observations.
3. For a DXF raw-group question, run direct parse mode with
   `DXF_INCLUDE_RAW_CODE_VALUES=TRUE`; compare selected raw groups and stable
   entity handles. For Binary DXF, require GDAL 3.12 or newer and record the
   exact build. For an ACIS carrier question, require AC1027+ and explicitly
   enable `DXF_3D_EXTENSIBLE_MODE`; separately assert raw carrier bytes and
   transform values. Default-mode omission is a declared skip disposition.
4. For a narrow DWG projection, select the `CAD` driver deliberately and
   limit inputs/assertions to its documented POINT, LINE, CIRCLE/ARC and
   3DFACE subset. Assert per-object identity where the build exposes it;
   otherwise use a scratch-generated single-discriminator input and leave the
   result advisory. Do not use ODA-backed `DWG` as open-source peer evidence.
5. Maintain the existing evidence firewall: a GDAL projection can help locate
   a field or transform mismatch, but only ODA/spec-backed layouts, local
   byte-level controls, an independent semantic witness, and the applicable
   consumer route can establish the relevant claim. GDAL raw ASM bytes,
   feature counts, or successful conversion cannot promote any of J256,
   J260, J268, J284, J293 or J295.

This update changes only the existing PAR-07/S8 route-admission and composed
checkpoint instructions. It adds no finding or top-level subplan, code, test,
fixture, dependency, or support claim. Totals remain **141 findings / 78
top-level subplans**; all six J items remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. No peer
repository was cloned, built or run; no external file was downloaded; no
tests or full suite were run.

<a id="deeperbroader-dxf-only-peer-lineages-and-projection-boundaries-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>
## Deeper/broader DXF-only peer lineages and projection boundaries (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass expands the peer screen to DXF-only parsers and callback libraries
that can help diagnose narrow tag/field questions but cannot validate the
DWG reader/writer or establish full-document/3D support. It also distinguishes
two related `dxf-parser` packages so a port is not accidentally counted as a
second independent parser. Sources were reviewed online; no peer was cloned,
built, or run, and no external drawing was downloaded.

| Route / primary source | Source-backed scope and limits | Plan disposition |
|---|---|---|
| QCAD [dxflib overview](https://www.qcad.org/doc/dxflib/2.5/reference/overview.html), [feature list](https://www.qcad.org/en/dxflib), and [programmer guide](https://www.qcad.org/doc/dxflib/2.5/reference/overview.html) | `dxflib` parses DXF by invoking application callbacks; its guide explicitly says it does not store entities/document information. Its feature page lists a selected set of entities/objects and documents DXF R15 (2000) as the writer version. The listed classes include some explicit 3D records (`3DFACE`, `SOLID`, `TRACE`, POLYLINE), but this is not ACIS/ACDS B-rep support. | Admit only as an optional callback/projection cross-check for selected legacy DXF fields, and only when the expected values are declared independently. It cannot qualify unchanged rewrite, unknown-record preservation, whole-document graph closure, DWG, Binary DXF, or modern 3D/modeler semantics. Do not treat its feature list as a support score. |
| GDS Estimating [`dxf-parser` README](https://github.com/gdsestimating/dxf-parser) | The JavaScript package parses DXF text into a JavaScript object and lists HEADER, layers, LTYPE, blocks/INSERT, text/some MTEXT, some XDATA, and most 2D entities. It explicitly lists 3DSOLID and some less-common entities/objects as unsupported. The API example accepts file text; this is a parser/projection route, not a writer or raw-byte-preservation contract. | Optional ASCII-DXF parser cross-check for a small selected field/entity cohort only. Pin package version/commit and Node runtime; record unknown/skipped entities. Do not use parse success, JSON shape, or rendering downstream of this object as a document-preservation or DWG/3D result. |
| PyPI [`dxf-parser`](https://pypi.org/project/dxf-parser/) | The project describes itself as a dependency-free parser for ASCII AutoCAD DXF and explicitly says its JSON-serializable representation is compatible with the JavaScript `dxf-parser` output; it is inspired by that project. It lists headers, tables, blocks, common entities, indexed colors, and XDATA. PyPI classifies it as alpha; the page reports a 2026-09-03 release. | Treat the Python package and JavaScript parser as one related schema/output lineage, not two independent votes. The Python port may be a convenient executable route at a composed checkpoint, but only for ASCII DXF and only after pinning the wheel/source hash and Python version. Binary DXF, DWG, writer conformance, and independent expected semantics remain out of scope. |
| BRL-CAD [DXF conversion guide](https://brlcad.org/w/images/5/5f/Geometry_Conversions.pdf) and [GCV architecture](https://brlcad.org/docs/cad/articles/gcv.html) | BRL-CAD documents `dxf-g` as a conversion from DXF into its own geometry database and notes that its historical importer predates ACIS use and does not support ACIS objects. GCV explicitly converts through a BRL-CAD in-memory geometry database; its own guidance warns that not every source object has a direct analogous target primitive. | Keep this within the already-existing faceted-geometry projection lane. It is not a DXF document roundtrip, an ACIS reader, or an identity/owner-preservation oracle. Do not add a BRL-CAD run to routine slices; any optional run must compare a declared explicit-geometry subset with per-source dispositions and account for projection/loss. |

### Implementation-ready comparator refinement

1. Keep the local fast loop unchanged: self-authored ASCII/Binary controls,
   the touched strict target, its owning CTest, and scoped diff validation.
   No package install, peer process, downloaded drawing, full suite, or
   cross-platform/native checkpoint is added to an ordinary slice.
2. If a composed checkpoint still has a specific legacy ASCII-DXF question,
   admit at most one selected parser route (`dxflib`, JavaScript
   `dxf-parser`, or its Python port) and record exact version/commit, runtime,
   encoding, input hash/provenance, entity handle/type, selected group values,
   unsupported dispositions, and parse diagnostics. Use expected values from
   the scratch-control manifest, not from another library's output.
3. Keep callback projection, normalized parser object, strict parse/rewrite,
   cross-codec read, and CAD-consumer acceptance as separate operations. A
   parser that lacks a document writer cannot validate preservation; a writer
   that only writes R15 cannot validate modern-version serialization; a 3D
   record class or geometry projection is not ACIS/ACDS semantic support.
4. Do not add an aggregate peer-support percentage. Keep source identities and
   owners where exposed, and record loss/refusal/failure per identity. DIME's
   existing separate row remains the best current candidate for unknown-tag
   retention questions; this update does not duplicate or broaden that route.
5. This is comparator selection only. It adds no finding, top-level subplan,
   code, test, fixture, dependency, validation cadence, or support claim.
   Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78** and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
   J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Deeper/broader release-pinned OpenCADStudio ACIS kernel and peer-writer boundaries (2026-10-20; research only)

### Decision

This pass resolves the source dependency identity for the OpenCADStudio
`v2026.42` tag and rechecks the current ACadSharp modeler-writer proposal. It
does not resolve the six external qualifications or add another parser vote.
The tagged app's `Cargo.lock` pins `acadrust` 0.6.4 from
[`opencadcodec`](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/opencadcodec) commit
`5d4f11ae38758caec540bc9819ff2c4120eeadb4`, `opencadkernel` commit
`a60f18ff033b5a3f7d842e2398f393e4d6cfcd32`, and `opencadgraph` commit
`d9f2aeeaaffa9f4972cb10a07e039f4512e8572f`. This replaces the prior
`DEPENDENCY_REVISION_UNBOUND` status for the tagged source graph. It does not
bind the distributed executable's hash to a reproducible build in this review;
the mutable `main` manifest already names different codec/kernel revisions.
Keep release artifact and tag source as separate identities.

The locked kernel's README describes an early B-rep project, says most
operations are not written, and describes the ACIS bridge as lifting/lowering
a `SatDocument`. OpenCADStudio's product README advertises ACIS entity
tessellation, but that claim does not override the kernel's narrower pinned
scope or prove complete geometry for an arbitrary body. Current `pid-cad`
tessellation documentation further distinguishes a kernel mesh path from a
per-surface fallback and marks incomplete output; because that document is a
mutable separate source route, it is an implementation warning, not evidence
about the exact `v2026.42` binary. In all cases, an OpenCADStudio observation
is within the ACadRust-derived parser family, not an independent second parser
vote.

ACadSharp issue [#1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) remains
open. Its maintainer says `Solid3D`, `CadBody`, and `Region` are not yet
supported as DXF entities, and linked PR
[#1240](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1240) is still open and
depends on schema/storage work in #1174. Do not treat that branch as a
released positive DXF writer route. LibreDWG's 0.14.1 NEWS independently
records both a `3DSOLID` SAT-block-size overflow fix and a DXF-export fix for
dropping the final SAT block. The local modeler writer already has generated
group-boundary cases and following-record checks; this peer note reinforces
those assertions without creating a new local defect or test owner.

Findings and top-level subplans remain **141 / 78**. The implementation queue,
fast-test cadence, no-external-fixture policy, and 2D consumer contract are
unchanged. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Deeper/broader CADMPEG v0.6.2 tag-source, release-digest, and SAT comparator refresh (2026-10-20; research only)

### Decision

The previous release-index correction was based on a stale listing that
omitted v0.6.2. The official release API now resolves the discrepancy: the
v0.6.2 release was published 2026-10-19 at exact source commit
`7bcc95276548de4e4876894b9a650a84ea9c4d6d`, and the release exposes
platform-specific asset SHA-256 digests. The tagged root manifest is also
available and says workspace version 0.6.2; `cadmpeg-codec-sat` is a workspace
member and `sat` is enabled in the binary's default feature list. The tagged
release workflow builds on a pushed version tag. This resolves the earlier
release/tag uncertainty and confirms the SAT feature in the tagged build
configuration, but no binary was downloaded or executed and no clean
reproducible rebuild was performed.

The exact-tag format profile still bounds this route: the SAT codec reads bare
SAT/SMT/SAB/SMB streams outside their containers, is read-only, and verifies
Spatial ACIS majors 217 and 218. Other ACIS majors are unverified. Its format
support ladder is L1 even though the source documents additional geometry
transfer as a profile-limited extra; neither the project's own score nor its
machine-checked layout table is independent format authority. The tag's
`asm-open-items.md` keeps relevant geometry and topology questions open.
CADMPEG is therefore a candidate parser/neutral-geometry cross-check, not a
general ACIS kernel, DWG/DXF parser/writer, AcDs extractor, owner/key oracle,
or native-consumer result. Its format research is also correlated with
`cq-acis` source notes, so do not count their agreement as independent format
discovery.

The stale docs.rs/latest view still returned crate 0.6.1 in this research pass.
That is a separate registry/documentation artifact, not evidence that the
v0.6.2 GitHub source tag or release binary is absent. Do not silently use the
0.6.1 package source/API as the implementation identity for a v0.6.2 binary;
if the package route is selected, bind its version and checksum independently.

No new finding, top-level subplan, peer run, external input, fixture,
dependency, test registration, validation-cadence change, or support claim is
added. Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293,
and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

implementation lineage and no evidence that closes the full chain from DWG

blocking local implementation.

The repository separates a relatively mature container/object walker from incomplete per-entity decoding, publishes corpus-dependent decoded/skipped/error counts, has no DXF parser, and disclaims automated native DWG-writer acceptance. <a id="deeperbroader-freecad-importer-scope-and-acis-writer-candidate-refresh-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>
## Deeper/broader FreeCAD importer-scope and ACIS-writer candidate refresh (2026-10-20; research only)

### Decision

This pass rechecked the native FreeCAD DXF route and ACadSharp's public
ACIS-writer work against the existing PAR-07/S8 gates. It does not identify a
new libdxfrw defect or a newly qualified peer. It does tighten the planned
consumer run so the exact importer and converter are explicit, and it closes
one recurring ambiguity: a stock FreeCAD ACIS/SAT import failure is expected
from the documented route and is not a semantic-solid result.

FreeCAD documents two separately selectable importers. Both accept DXF from
R12 onward, but their record subsets differ: the built-in C++ importer lists
common 2D entities and imports only geometry from blocks (omitting block text,
dimensions, and attributes); the legacy Python importer additionally lists
3DFACE. The same documentation says stock FreeCAD cannot read ACIS/SAT solid
payloads. DWG is not a native reader route there: an external converter first
produces DXF, then the selected importer consumes it. Accordingly, any
FreeCAD result must bind the exact app build, importer preference, converter
binary/version/hash, source version, and per-source-entity disposition. The
result can qualify only the explicit supported subset on that route; it must
not be counted as a full-DXF, DWG, proxy, or ACIS semantic pass.

The FreeCAD #28905 mirrored-block report is closed by its reporter, who later
identified the supplied DXF as corrupted. It remains a useful reminder to
separate malformed-file recovery from valid-file interoperability, but it is
not evidence of a FreeCAD or libdxfrw transform defect. Do not put its attached
file into the test corpus. Use the existing locally generated asymmetric and
nested INSERT controls for any transform qualification.

ACadSharp #1195 still reports silent 3DSOLID/REGION omission in a named older
package. The earlier contributor PR #1150 remains open and undeployed; its
discussion says the initial implementation conflicts with the later
ACDS/ACIS storage refactor and notes that a refactored DXF path retained only
the last repeated group-310 chunk. The maintainer prefers a schema-driven
writer over raw replay. The separate #1240 proposal also remains open and is
not a released positive route. Statements in either PR about TrueView checks,
versioned SAT/SAB placement, token-safe chunking, or section indexing are
candidate design evidence only—not shipped behavior, an independent
acceptance result, or format authority.

### PAR-07/S8 implementation-ready refinement

1. Keep the local implementation queue and fast validation unchanged. The
   existing `modeler_dxf_writer_matrix_tests` source constructs local
   ASCII/Binary DXF cases across AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, and AC1027,
   and checks ordered modeler groups, chunk boundaries, and the version-gated
   3DSOLID history pair. This is generated syntax/field regression evidence;
   it does not establish a native application accepting the output. Avoid
   duplicating these controls unless a later source trace exposes a missing
   version/field row.
2. At the existing composed native-consumer checkpoint, record separately:
   exact FreeCAD build/platform; selected C++ or legacy importer; exact DWG
   converter path and binary identity; DXF input version/encoding; exact
   source entity identity and owning block/layout; and emitted/imported,
   skipped, unsupported, or failed disposition. Check each importer only
   against its documented entity subset. Include a locally authored,
   asymmetric nested-block case so transform errors cannot hide behind
   identity transforms.
3. For 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY, score the converter separately for emitting the
   expected opaque carrier and owner association. The stock FreeCAD importer
   is documented not to read ACIS/SAT, so record that importer outcome as
   unsupported; do not require a B-rep or count the result as a solid semantic
   pass. Keep opaque carrier byte identity, ACIS/AcDs ownership/key
   association, independent analytic geometry, and native consumer semantics
   as separate evidence cells. Use an independently profiled ACIS
   parser/kernel only at the already planned composed gate.
4. Recheck ACadSharp #1150/#1240 only if a released/pinned artifact becomes
   available or a specific unresolved question warrants one optional peer
   run. Before scoring a modern ACDSDATA route, verify all repeated binary
   chunks, exact reconstructed payload length/hash, owner-key joins, and
   non-monotonic handle-vs-directory ordering; never accept same-peer
   readback as the only writer oracle.
5. Keep source/fixture policy unchanged: the local generated vectors remain
   the test inputs; no issue attachment or peer drawing is committed. Full
   suites, peer runs, and native runs stay at their existing composed gates.
   If a chosen external route is unavailable, record `NOT_RUN` and return to
   the local-ready queue.

class-version (group 70) and flags (group 90) in the class-header order already
used by DetailViewStyle. The shared helper remains bounded to the named style
subclass and known header fields; it refuses unfamiliar header prefixes rather
than guessing an insertion point. Class versions above the signed DXF int16
range fail closed. High-bit flags are serialized through the existing signed
DXF-long representation and recover the original uint32 value on re-import.

drawing, edits the typed values, and exercises ASCII and Binary DXF export and
re-import. It checks exact ordered raw-carrier output, typed values, unchanged
DetailViewStyle data, closed resource references, and following POINT

header prefix verify refusal without replacing an existing destination. No persistent DWG/DXF fixture,
external drawing, new CTest registration, dependency, peer/native run, or
support claim was added.

<a id="deeperbroader-dwg-acds-association-peer-fallback-native-consumer-boundaries-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>
## Deeper/broader DWG AcDs association, peer fallback, and native consumer boundaries (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass reconciled the DWG DataStorage wire contract in ODA v5.4.1 with
LibreDWG's current mutable `master` implementation, then rechecked current
FreeCAD and OpenCADStudio consumer routes. It sharpens existing evidence and
does not create a new local defect, gate, top-level subplan, or support claim.

### Normative association crosswalk and peer boundary

ODA §24 defines a multi-stage lookup, not a global byte search: the file
header selects the segment-index, data-index, schema-index, and search
segments; each DataIndex row carries `(segment index, local offset, schema
index)`; the data-segment record header carries its own 64-bit handle and a
local offset relative to the data-start marker; payload is either inline or
the `0xbb106bb1` blob
reference whose ordered Blob01 page list reconstructs a larger payload. ODA
specifies direct data records up to `0x40000` bytes and versioned SAB envelope
markers. Schema-search data can be ignored when reading, but ODA says AutoCAD
ignores an entity if the schema-search records are not created. Therefore,
reader-side raw preservation, typed entity-to-record association, and
writer-side consumer visibility are separate proof obligations. The spec is
the byte-layout authority, while exact source drawings remain necessary to
qualify producer-specific and later-version behavior.

| Evidence | Finding | Admission boundary |
|---|---|---|
| ODA [Open Design Specification v5.4.1, §24](https://static.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) | Defines the segment/DataIndex/record-handle/blob-page route and the schema-search visibility requirement. It explicitly allows a reader to ignore search data; it does not make marker scanning equivalent to a keyed join. | For typed extraction, prove DataIndex row → exact record header handle → complete inline/blob bytes → entity/owner association. For any future writer, separately validate schema-search rows and strict consumer visibility. For opaque read/replay, retain the source section losslessly and avoid inventing semantic ownership. |
| LibreDWG current [`acds.spec`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/acds.spec) and [`decode_r2007.c`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode_r2007.c) | Source parses the section header, segment catalogue, indexes/schema/search structures, but leaves `_data_` and `blob01` segment bodies marked unhandled in `acds.spec`; the decoder subsequently searches decompressed section bytes for `ACIS BinaryFile`/`End-of-ASM-data` and associates matches with queued `acis_sab_hdl` handles in encounter order. That is a fallback, not the ODA keyed lookup, and current `master` source is mutable. | Keep the existing no-peer-promotion decision. Do not port the marker/queue association or count current LibreDWG as an exact AcDs join oracle. An optional peer run must pin a commit/build and compare each entity handle, DataIndex row, record handle, full page chain, payload hash, and owner independently. |
| OpenCADStudio [v2026.42 release](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/releases/tag/v2026.42), its [locked dependency graph](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/v2026.42/Cargo.lock), and [OpenCADKernel](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/opencadkernel) | The release advertises a separate SAT/ACIS model-import workflow and pins `acadrust` 0.6.4 plus `opencadkernel` commit `a60f18f`; OpenCADKernel describes itself as early, with most operations not yet written. A standalone SAT import is not evidence of DWG AcDs association, and this is an ACadRust-family consumer/parser lineage already tracked. | Optional application-level observation only, bound to the exact release/platform/input and imported disposition. Do not count it as a second independent DWG parser or as ACIS semantic proof until the exact profile, code path, test corpus, and independent analytic expectations are demonstrated. |
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF route](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and [DWG import route](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md) | FreeCAD converts DWG to DXF and then uses a selected DXF importer. Its published route says the built-in and legacy DXF importers do not read the ACIS/SAT blob; the documentation repository is archived, so this is route documentation, not current-build runtime proof. | Preserve the existing Linux/Windows native checkpoint for explicit supported entities and converter/importer behavior. Treat ACIS as expected unsupported on stock FreeCAD; this run cannot close independent ACIS/ACDS semantic evidence. Capture converter output version/hash and importer/platform separately. |

### Implementation-ready refinement (inside existing PAR-07/S8; no new subplan)

1. Reuse the local generated controls already in the tree: the DWG
   `testModelerAcDsDataIndexOrder` distinguishes directory-row order,
   physical-record order, numeric-handle order, and entity callback order;
   `testDataStorageBounds` and `testDataStorageBlobPages` cover direct/blob
   boundary and page reconstruction. Do not duplicate those tests or add

2. Keep the next implementation/evidence slice as a strict dependency chain:
   validate segment-index ranges and DataIndex row bounds; resolve the record

   valid envelope bytes, or shell survival alone is insufficient.

4. Keep fast local tests as the per-slice gate. At the composed checkpoint,

   bare-SAB analytic profile separate, and OpenCADStudio optional. Neither
   FreeCAD nor an ACadRust-family wrapper can promote the independent

<a id="deeperbroader-independent-dxf-reader-and-acds-peer-route-boundary-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>
## Deeper/broader independent DXF reader and AcDs peer-route boundary (2026-10-20; research only)

This scan looked for a genuinely useful additional open-source comparison
route, rather than treating every CAD application that advertises DWG/DXF as
an independent reader. The strongest new candidate is `uncad`, whose own
documentation separates its backends and publishes unusually explicit
failure/disposition limits. The evidence is documentation/source-page review
only: no repository was cloned, no binary was built or run, and no drawing was
downloaded.

### Route and evidence crosswalk

| Project/route | Primary-source observation | Admission boundary |
|---|---|---|
| [`iyulab/uncad`](https://github.com/iyulab/uncad) DWG path | Its README says DWG reads use LibreDWG through Rust FFI. Its caveats document local patches to a vendored LibreDWG and explain that an earlier global signature scan attached R2013 solids by encounter order, swapping a 3DSOLID and REGION in `example_2013.dwg`; it also missed `ASM BinaryFile4` bodies in an R2018 file. The documented correction resolves DataStorage record handles to solid handles. | This is a valuable implementation/test-shape corroboration of exact handle association, but not an independent DWG parser: it shares LibreDWG lineage, and the cited file outcomes are the project's own documentation, not a reproduction here. Do not count it as a second DWG vote or an oracle for the ODA wire contract. |
| `uncad` DXF path (`undxf`) | The project states that ASCII and Binary DXF are parsed by a separate pure-Rust `undxf` reader rather than LibreDWG. It says the path reads pre-R2013 SAT groups and R2013+ SAB carried in ACDSDATA; the common `uncad-model` code derives ACIS wireframe edges. | This is a candidate independent DXF structural/carrier observer, especially for the R2013+ `ACDSDATA` route. It has not been pinned or run here. A model-level wireframe is not B-rep validity, topology/volume qualification, DWG AcDs record association, or native CAD acceptance. Admit only after immutable source/lockfile pinning and one exact-profile generated-control run. |
| `uncad-model` ACIS path | Its project documentation says it has no file parser, renderer, or native dependencies; it provides SAT/SAB-to-wireframe functions in the neutral model. `uncad` reports unsupported bodies as `Unknown` and skipped edges explicitly rather than presenting them as empty solids. | Useful evidence-disposition design and a possible raw-wireframe comparator, not a solid kernel. Require per-entity `read / unknown / unsupported / skipped-edge` results and exact payload identity; never promote semantic support from a nonempty wireframe. |
| [`mlightcad/cad-viewer`](https://github.com/mlightcad/cad-viewer) and [`iyulab/uncad`](https://github.com/iyulab/uncad) application/tool wrappers | The viewer documents that its default open-source DWG route is opt-in LibreDWG WASM, with entity-coverage and large-file limitations. `uncad` documents the same underlying DWG engine while selecting a separate DXF reader. | Count parser lineage by the actual route, not by product count. The viewer adds no independent DWG parser vote; `uncad` adds a distinct DXF parse route only. |
| [`gdsestimating/dxf-parser`](https://github.com/gdsestimating/dxf-parser) and [`dxfjs/parser`](https://github.com/dxfjs/parser) | The former explicitly says 3DSolids are not yet supported. The latter lists 3DSOLID among input entities, but its README does not establish Binary DXF coverage, ACDSDATA linkage, ACIS parsing, or an independent geometry result. | The first is excluded for 3D modeler comparisons. The second is at most a low-confidence DXF token/entity-presence candidate until a source-pinned profile and actual tests prove more; neither closes an ACIS/AcDs or semantic gate. |

|---|---|---|

Its README states that it reads ASCII and Binary DXF from R12 through AC1032; preserves unsupported entity types as `UnknownEntity` with raw group codes; and reads selected OBJECTS such as LAYOUT and IMAGEDEF. It also states that this is a fork of `ixmilia/dxf-go`, with BLOCKS, selected OBJECTS, and other changes. | A candidate independent DXF parser for a one-time, exact-pinned structural comparison—not an independent DWG reader. Before use, pin source commit/module checksum and inspect whether the direct parser completes a locally generated AC1024/AC1027 binary file through EOF, retains all group-310 chunks in order, and exposes ACDSDATA payload plus key/owner association. `UnknownEntity` raw-tag retention alone does not prove ACDSDATA support. |
| [`xorgy/dxfscan`](https://github.com/xorgy/dxfscan) | Its repository describes a one-pass, zero-copy Binary-DXF scanner for R13+ with typed data and lookups; the supported-entity list includes ordinary geometry such as LINE, SPLINE, HATCH, and 3DFACE, but not 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY. It says other entity types are represented as `Entity::Unknown`. The repository currently shows one commit and no tagged release. | Screened as a narrow candidate for a locally generated Binary-DXF ordinary-entity/handle syntax probe only. Do not use it for modeler carriers, ACDSDATA, a full-document acceptance result, or semantic parity unless source inspection proves unknown-record and terminal-EOF behavior for the exact input. Pin the commit before any optional run. |

At most a scratch-only pair-encoding utility after its supported group-code rules are checked; do not add it as a test dependency or use its output as independent expected data. |
| [`kedazo/dxf-go` DWG/xref helper route](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/kedazo/dxf-go@v0.3.3) | The same README says DWG xrefs are converted with LibreDWG `dwg2dxf` before the Go DXF reader checks them. | Count this route as LibreDWG-lineage for DWG inputs. Keep its value confined to a pinned, target-file structural/boundary comparison; not a 3D geometry, writer-acceptance, or ACIS semantic oracle. |
| [`gallowaysoftware/dxf`](https://github.com/gallowaysoftware/dxf) writer | Already inventoried: a narrow R2010 2D-only writer without a reader or modeler carrier support. | No new peer route. Retain only its previously documented small-writer test-design lessons; do not broaden parity claims. |

<a id="deeperbroader-acadsharp-prototype1b-reader-merge-freecad-dwg3d-route-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>
## Deeper/broader ACadSharp Prototype_1b reader merge and FreeCAD DWG/3D route refresh (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass refreshed the exact ACadSharp AcDs reader state, checked the
corresponding LibreDWG report and source boundary, and reconciled current
FreeCAD documentation with its DWG adapter. It corrects an earlier peer-status
snapshot: ACadSharp PR #1154 is no longer an open proposal.

The format contract was cross-checked against the public ODA v5.4.1
specification, §24: the segment index locates segments; DataIndex rows select
the data segment/local record offset/schema; record headers carry the object
handle and payload offset; large records reference Blob01 pages. This supports
the plan's keyed association and complete-page-chain requirements. The spec
does not make an unreferenced stale segment an accepted payload, nor justify
associating data by signature scan or encounter order.

### Current evidence and limits

| Route/source | Refreshed observation | Plan consequence / evidence limit |
|---|---|---|
| ODA [Open Design Specification v5.4.1](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf), §24 | The primary layout describes a handle-keyed DataStorage route through the segment index, DataIndex, record headers, and optional Blob01 pages; it says schema-search data may be ignored by readers. | Use this as the byte-layout authority over either peer's observed behavior. Require exact record handle and full reconstructed bytes before a modeler join; don't infer owner identity from a nearby marker or directory order. Treat questionable/stale segment entries as bounded parse/diagnostic cases unless a valid source demonstrates their role. |

## Implementation progress — AcDs stale-secondary segidx live-extent bound (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The generated `--acds-dataindex-order` owner previously tested reordered
DataIndex rows and Blob01 pages, but not a live `segidx` whose row zero points
to an older secondary index or a valid unindexed data segment. Added an
in-memory AC1027 section where the stale index remains valid at row zero, the
live index occupies row three, and a trailing valid data segment is absent
from the live directory. A separate negative control increases the live entry
count beyond its declared segment extent. It failed before the parser change,
confirming the old section-wide bound admitted directory reads from following
segments.

`readSegmentIndex` now uses the live segment header's declared size as its
primary bound, validates nonzero extents against the section, and preserves the
existing self-reference fallback only for producers that leave the header size
unset. The regression verifies the valid section still retains all four
segments/records and modeler-payload joins while ignoring the unindexed
record; the malformed count produces a bounded count diagnostic, six bounded
directory slots, and non-replayable structural status. An out-of-bounds
nonzero header extent is also checked for fail-closed behavior before any
directory row is consumed.

The existing generated four-record ACdS profile already checked explicit
object-data alignment anchors, unordered record offsets, exact handle/payload
associations, and entity links. It did not exercise a DataIndex row that points

<a id="implementation-progress-par07s8-dataindex-rejects-blob01-as-record-segment-2026-10-20-generated-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>
## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8 DataIndex rejects Blob01 as record segment (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The prior audit found that `isDataSegment` treated both `_data_` and `blob*`
segments as valid targets for DataIndex rows. ODA §24.2.2.2 says those rows
index objects in a Data file segment; §24.2.2.3–.4 describe Blob01 segments as
pages referenced by a blob descriptor inside a data record. Narrowed the
record-segment predicate to `Data` only. Blob pages remain eligible through
the separate descriptor page-reference path. A nonzero DataIndex row that
targets another segment kind now emits
`datastorage-record-segment-kind-invalid`; the spec's segment-index-zero stub
row remains ignored.

Extended the existing runtime-generated AC1027 record/alignment profile with
an unused fourth `blob01` segment. The negative case moves one DataIndex row
to that segment, installs plausible record-header and payload bytes there, and
requires a structural diagnostic, non-replayability, absence of the redirected
record, and exact retention of the three neighboring valid record payloads.
The companion positive case points a different row to segment index zero with
a nonzero local offset/schema index; it verifies that the spec-defined stub is
ignored, the section remains structurally replayable, and the other three
records retain exact payloads. The ordinary profile and prior payload-region
boundary control remain valid. This is a kind/association check, not Blob01
page reconstruction or ACIS-semantic evidence.

## Deeper/broader DWG AcDs versus versioned DXF SAT/SAB route review (2026-10-20; plan update)

This pass reconciled ODA v5.4.1 §§24.2.2.2–.7 with the current LibreDWG
`master` AcDs decoder, Autodesk's public DXF 3DSOLID group-code reference,
and the current documented capabilities of ezdxf, FreeCAD, and `cq-acis`.
It also checked the local reader, DataStorage parser, DXF writer, adapter,
generated tests, and existing PAR-07/S8 contract. This is source/spec research
only: no peer was cloned or executed, no external drawing was downloaded, and
no CAD application or ACIS kernel was run.

| Evidence | What it establishes | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [ODA DWG specification §24.2](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) | DataIndex rows select Data segments and carry a segment-stream-relative offset to a record header. The record header's local offset is relative to the data-start marker; the next sorted payload offset bounds a record. Blob01 is reached through a blob descriptor's page references, not through ordinary DataIndex record rows. The page header separately carries total length, page start, page index/count, and page data length. | The text calls the record-header second UInt32 unknown (ODA writes 1); that producer value is not a safe universal validation rule. Section layout does not define ACIS topology or prove a consumer can interpret the bytes. |
| Current [LibreDWG `acds.spec`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/acds.spec), [`decode_r2007.c`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode_r2007.c), [`common_entity_data.spec`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/common_entity_data.spec), and [`dwg.c`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dwg.c) | The checked-in decoder recognizes the segment directory and parses DataIndex/schema/search metadata. Its segment switch still logs `_data_` and `blob01` as unhandled; a later pass scans for ACIS/SAB start/end markers and consumes queued modeler handles. The helper's eligible entity/object families include 3DSOLID, REGION, BODY and several surface types. | This is not proof that a file's record offset, page chain, payload-to-owner association, or every eligible type is correct. The queue/signature path is a useful adversarial comparator, not an expected-value mapping rule. ODA explicitly names REGION/3DSOLID in §24.2.2.3; other families still need producer-backed evidence. |
| [Autodesk DXF 3DSOLID reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm) and [ezdxf ACIS documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) | Autodesk describes the modeler subclass, format version, proprietary group-1 text with optional continuation group-3 strings, and the 3DSOLID history pointer. ezdxf documents SAT data for R2000–R2010 and SAB for R2013+, and explicitly says its reader supports a limited number of ACIS entities; unsupported ones become NONE_ENTITY and lose data. | DXF SAT text, DXF SAB bytes, and DWG AcDs DataStorage are not interchangeable syntax. A DXF parse, ACIS browse, or successful raw save cannot establish geometry semantics or arbitrary ACIS round-trip support. |
| [FreeCAD Draft DXF documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md), [FreeCAD documentation repository](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation), and [`cq-acis` profile limits](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/docs/geometry-support.md) | The checked-in FreeCAD page says stock DXF import cannot read ACIS; its documentation repository is archived, so this is a route snapshot and not a live contract for a later build. `cq-acis` documents an experimental bounded SAT/SAB/ASM geometry subset with explicit failures for unsupported profiles. | Neither source provides native FreeCAD qualification for a selected current build, nor a general B-rep oracle. `cq-acis` converts through CadQuery/OpenCascade and is not an independent-kernel vote for an OCCT-based consumer. |

### Plan refinements under existing PAR-07/S8 (no new ledger item)

1. **Keep the wire formats and claims orthogonal.** The qualification row for
   each exact version/operation must name the carrier: DWG inline modeler
   fields, DWG AcDs record/blob, legacy DXF SAT group 1/3, or DXF AC1027+
   ACDSDATA/SAB. Record type, source/target version, encoding, section/record
   owner identity, byte length/digest, conversion result, and consumer route
   separately. A carried payload is not an interpreted solid.
2. **Boundary-index poisoning is now covered by a generated control.** A
   DataIndex row points to an in-range header-shaped byte sequence whose
   record-local offset lands inside a neighboring payload. The parser reports
   the payload crossing and implausible fake record, marks the section
   structurally invalid/non-replayable, withholds the overlapping records, and
   retains exact bytes for independently bounded records. This is a conservative
   disposition, not proof that a malformed source record can be recovered;
   do not heuristically slide boundaries to salvage geometry. Do not reject
   solely because the record-header unknown field differs from ODA's written
   value.
3. **Keep the association proof identity-based.** Permute segment physical
   order, DataIndex order, record-header order, numeric handles, and entity
   callback order independently. Require exact handle-to-offset-to-payload

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8 in-range overlapping DataStorage boundary control (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Extended the existing generated AC1027 DataStorage alignment profile with a
header-shaped DataIndex target in the unused header padding. Its record-local
offset deliberately points inside the second valid inline payload. The parser
uses the declared candidate offset as a boundary, then rejects the crossed
payload and the fake record's over-limit size; it does not publish either
record. The section is structurally invalid and non-replayable, while two
independently bounded records retain exact handles and bytes. This establishes
the fail-closed behavior for this malformed/ambiguous profile. Do not guess a
replacement boundary from record size or neighboring payload bytes. ODA marks
the adjacent header field unknown (ODA writes 1), so the control does not rely
on treating that value as a normative discriminator.

No production code changed, no drawing fixture/dependency/peer/native runtime

### PAR-07/S8 composed-checkpoint decision procedure

1. **Finish local framing and join evidence first.** Require valid DWG section
   framing, DataIndex-to-Data record resolution, record-header handle match,
   ordered Blob01 page reconstruction where applicable, explicit entity
   handle/schema/key join, and exact payload digest. If any stage is ambiguous,
   refuse/retain diagnostics and return to the local queue; do not ask an ACIS
   parser to infer ownership.
2. **Choose the peer by the open question, not by a generic “3D support” badge.**
   For byte/profile parsing without shape construction, choose one pinned
   parser (e.g. CADMPEG or `acis-core`); for supported-subset shape construction,
   choose one pinned `cq-acis` or authorized commercial OCCT route. Avoid running
   correlated parsers by default. If the selected tool is unavailable, license
   blocked, unsupported for the exact ACIS/ASM version, or cannot account for
   all records, record `NOT_RUN`/`UNSUPPORTED` and self-unblock to local work.
3. **Use a source-authored scratch model and independent expectations.** Keep
   generated SAT/SAB/DXF/DWG artifacts in scratch space only; do not commit
   them as fixtures. Predeclare primitive dimensions, units, frame/transform,
   expected closedness, topology counts where stable, bounds, area, volume, and
   tolerances before parsing. The generator/parser under test must not be the
   sole source of its expected values.
4. **Separate carrier from semantic dispositions.** Record exact SAT/SAB bytes,
   ACIS/ASM version, decoded/unknown/unsupported/lost record counts, body and
   topology counts, `valid`/closed status, and analytic measures. A raw-byte
   match or reference-closed model is only carrier/parser evidence; a B-rep
   result for one authored body is only that exact semantic profile.
5. **Keep writer/reimport and consumer gates distinct.** Any round-trip must
   reopen with a different pinned implementation or a named native consumer;
   same-writer/same-reader roundtrip is an internal consistency check only.
   Stock FreeCAD’s ACIS path remains `UNSUPPORTED_CONSUMER`; qualify its selected
   2D importer and converter separately. No result here promotes DWG-wide,
   arbitrary ACIS, or platform-wide support.
6. **Do not block implementation on the composed checkpoint.** Preserve the
   fast local selector/build per slice, run expensive peer/kernel/native checks
   once at their already-planned checkpoint, write the observed disposition and
   self-unblock to the next local item immediately. Do not add a CTest, new
   fixture, dependency, full-suite run, or per-slice external test from this
   research result.

<a id="implementation-progress-par07s8-single-identity-and-unversioned-section-link-controls-2026-10-20-generated-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>
## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8 single-identity and unversioned-section link controls (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Extended the existing `testDwgModelerDataStorageLinking` hardening owner to
exercise the remaining exact-identity branches. A modeler with only the
lexical DataStorage key and one with only the numeric DataStorage handle each
resolve their exact record even though the entity's own handle identifies a
different record. Missing explicit key/handle values are refused rather than
repaired from the entity handle. A section whose version is `UNKNOWNV` is
accepted only when the explicit record identity still resolves uniquely. An
AC1024 reader does not link an AC1027 section, while the existing AC1027
profile succeeds; an AC1027 entity with handle-looking fields but no
`hasDsData` advertisement leaves the record unclaimed. Unclaimed records
remain visible to orphan accounting.

All bytes and sections are generated in memory. No production code, persistent

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8 final duplicate-record diagnostic selection (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The local index audit found that `buildRecordIndex` updated the preferred
record maps for every duplicate but emitted the informational diagnostic on
the first duplicate only. For three records with the same handle, the selected
map entry could therefore point at the third record while the diagnostic
still named the second. Diagnostic creation now occurs after the full index is
built and reports the final selected record, handle, and record offset.

The existing generated AC1027 record-disposition case now has three
same-handle records. It verifies that the preferred lookup still returns the
third payload under the existing deterministic local policy, both source-order
indexes retain all three positions, the other two records remain orphaned
after linking, and the diagnostic reports record index 2 and its offset. A
focused `--acds-record-dispositions` selector reuses the existing test target;
no CTest registration was added.

### Evidence boundary

ODA v5.4.1 §24.1 and §24.2.1 identifies DataStorage and per-segment revision
fields; §24.2.2.3 describes data-record headers keyed by object handle and
states that each ACIS entity has a data record. §24.2.2.7 describes one search
index per handle, but also says readers may ignore search data. These sections
do not define a duplicate-handle winner or establish revision precedence.
Accordingly, the current deterministic duplicate selection is preserved only
as compatibility behavior; the diagnostic accurately reports it, while the
duplicate case itself remains non-conforming/ambiguous evidence and cannot
promote a DWG, AcDs, or semantic support claim. See the [ODA specification,
§24](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf).

<a id="implementation-progress-par07s8-overlapping-record-headers-2026-10-20-generated-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>
## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8 partially overlapping DataStorage record headers (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The next DataStorage index audit found that `readDataIndex` rejected exact
duplicate `(segment, localOffset)` entries, but `readDataRecords` did not
reject distinct local offsets whose fixed-size 20-byte record headers
partially overlap. A generated AC1027 section changed the second row's
header offset from 20 to 1 byte. Before the parser change, the focused control
failed because no overlap disposition was emitted. The malformed rows could
also contribute bytes to the sorted payload-boundary index.

The parser now gathers in-bounds `(segment, localOffset)` pairs into bounded
sorted vector scratch, finds overlapping fixed-size header ranges before
using any of those rows to build payload boundaries, marks the section
structurally invalid, and skips each row in an overlap cluster. The sorted
scratch avoids a per-entry hash-node set for this check. A third independently
bounded row is still decoded with its exact payload. Diagnostics are emitted
in original DataIndex order. The ODA layout describes DataIndex local offsets
as locations of repeated record headers and specifies the header's fixed
field sequence; overlapping interpretations are not treated as partial valid
records. See [ODA v5.4.1 §24.2.2.2–.3](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf).

The bytes are generated in memory. No downloaded/external DWG or DXF, new
persistent fixture, CTest registration, dependency, peer executable, or native
application was added or run.

A parsed byte vector alone is insufficient evidence of the outer association or ACIS semantics. <a id="implementation-progress-par07s8-malformed-entry-boundary-sentinel-2026-10-20-generated-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>
## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8 malformed record-header boundary sentinel (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The next DataStorage pass examined how the parser builds payload-stream
boundaries from DataIndex-targeted fixed-size record headers. Before the fix,
the boundary prepass skipped a header when its declared `entrySize` was less
than the 20-byte fixed header size. A generated control made the following
indexed record malformed and enlarged the preceding inline payload to cross
that record's payload offset. The regression failed before the parser change:
the predecessor did not receive an out-of-record disposition.

The prepass now retains the payload offset of every fully bounded indexed
header, even when that header declares an invalid entry size. The record pass
still rejects the malformed header with `datastorage-record-entry-invalid`;
the preserved offset also fences the predecessor, which is rejected with
`datastorage-record-payload-out-of-record`. The generated assertion verifies
that neither ambiguous payload is published and a later valid record remains
available for diagnostics. This is a conservative local boundary invariant,
not a new ODA claim that malformed producer records are otherwise meaningful.
ODA v5.4.1 §24.2.2.2–.3 says DataIndex offsets select the data-record headers
and bounds each payload by consecutive data-stream offsets; it lists `Entry
size` but does not specify how malformed entry-size values affect that
boundary calculation. See the [ODA specification, §24](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf).

Validation:

- Before production change, `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests --acds-dataindex-order` failed on the new assertion as expected.
- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests --parallel 2` — passed after the fix.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests --acds-dataindex-order` — passed.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_acds_dataindex_order$' --output-on-failure` — 1/1 passed (0.02 s).
- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests --parallel 2` — passed.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_graph_preservation$' --output-on-failure` — 1/1 passed (1.09 s).
- Scoped `git diff --check` for the parser and test — passed.

No full suite was run. No persistent DWG/DXF fixture, new CTest, peer runtime,
dependency, or support claim was added. The generated section is created in
memory. Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293,
and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. No files were staged or committed because
the shared worktree contains extensive pre-existing modifications and Git
metadata is read-only in this environment. Self-unblock: continue the local
PAR-07/S8 record-offset/owner audit at the next uncovered source-backed
invariant; external qualification remains optional and non-blocking.

### Implementation-ready PAR-14 arithmetic audit refinement

1. **Inventory only parser-relevant expressions.** In `dwgreader*.cpp`,
   `dwgbuffer.cpp`, `drw_entities.cpp`, and `drw_objects.cpp`, identify
   input-derived count/length × element-width and byte↔bit conversions that
   lead to an allocation, cursor advance, or buffer read. Do not turn unrelated
   geometry arithmetic into this security pass.
2. **Classify the proof at each owner.** Record one of `PRE_CAPPED`,
   `CHECKED_HELPER`, `WIDENED_BEFORE_MULTIPLY`, or `GAP`; include the source
   width/signedness, cap or available-span check, resulting type, and whether
   the value reaches an allocator or cursor API. A cast applied after an
   already-overflowing product does not count as widened arithmetic.
3. **Test only an identified gap.** Construct the smallest in-memory vector
   that crosses the specific overflow/boundary and its immediately valid
   neighbor. Assert rejection occurs before allocation/publication, the
   failing cursor/state is deterministic, and a following record/handle stays
   aligned. Keep the generated control with the existing owner; add no
   downloaded/peer DWG or DXF fixture and no new CTest registration unless a
   distinct public integration contract requires it.
4. **Keep validation proportional.** Strict-build the touched target, run its
   focused selector and owning existing CTest, then check the scoped diff and
   receipt. Do not schedule a full suite, fuzz campaign, or general sanitizer
   run for a source-only audit. Escalate to a focused sanitizer only if the
   local changed expression is an actual memory-safety boundary.
5. **Self-unblock.** If all inspected expressions classify safely, record the
   source paths reviewed, close this PAR-14 audit pass with no new finding,
   and continue the existing implementation queue. A missing optional peer,
   Windows host, or external sample does not block local work.

<a id="implementation-progress-par14-checked-eed-byte-to-bit-cursor-2026-10-20-generated-arithmetic-fast-slice"></a>
## Implementation progress — PAR-14 checked EED byte-to-bit cursor (2026-10-20; generated arithmetic fast slice, uncommitted)

The finite parser-arithmetic pass traced the EED application-chunk cursor in
`src/intern/dwgreader.cpp`. `eedCurrentBit` multiplied the stream's 64-bit byte
position by eight and added the intra-byte position directly, then
`eedHasBits` compared the result to the declared enclosing end bit. A byte
position above `UINT64_MAX / 8` could wrap before that bounds check. ODA
v5.4.1 §28 defines EED as repeated length-delimited application chunks directly
following the entity handle; the stream-size conversion is local arithmetic,
not a new wire-format rule.

Added `dwgSafety::bitPosition`, which checks both multiplication and addition
and rejects a bit offset outside `[0, 7]`. The EED bounds helper now fails
closed if the absolute cursor cannot be represented; the speculative handle
reader uses the same checked conversion before publishing its cursor. The
existing EED field parsing and chunk behavior are unchanged.

Validation:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_hardening_tests libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests --parallel 2` — passed with the project's strict warning settings.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_hardening_tests` — passed.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests` — passed; this includes existing bounded EED and following-entity sentinel controls.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_(dwg_reader_matrix|hardening)$' --output-on-failure` — 2/2 passed (2.29 seconds).
- `git diff --check -- src/intern/dwgsafety.h src/intern/dwgreader.cpp tests/hardening_tests.cpp` — passed.

No full test suite, persistent drawing fixture, new CTest registration,
external peer, native CAD application, or kernel was used. The new boundary
controls are integer-only unit cases for the largest representable absolute
bit position, the next byte's multiplication overflow, and bit offset 8.
Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`, and no support claim is promoted. Self-unblock:
continue the bounded PAR-14 expression inventory; classify remaining
input-derived multiplications by pre-cap, checked helper, or widen-before-
multiply, and add no test where the existing source proof is sufficient.

### Bounded implementation and validation refinement

<a id="implementation-progress-par14-wide-dwg-writer-bit-count-accounting-2026-10-20-generated-fast-slice"></a>
## Implementation progress — PAR-14 wide DWG writer bit-count accounting (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The bounded arithmetic inventory rechecked non-pointer multiplication sites
in `dwgreader.cpp`, `dwgreader18.cpp`, `dwgreader21.cpp`, and `dwgbuffer.cpp`.
The inspected input-derived products are already bounded: modular-char readers
consume at most five 7-bit groups, modular-short consumes at most two 15-bit
words, EED UTF-16 lengths widen the 16-bit code-unit count before multiplying
by two and compare against the containing chunk before allocation, and the
staging-capacity products test the available budget by division before
multiplying. The file-size-to-bit conversions in the reader's bounded object
paths use the checked helper or a buffer already capped below `UINT64_MAX / 8`.
No additional parser-side defect was confirmed in this finite source set.

The adjacent writer audit found a concrete representational mismatch:
`dwgBufferW::bitCount()` narrowed `m_buf.size()` to `uint32_t` and then
multiplied by eight. At exactly 512 MiB, the resulting `2^32` bit count wrapped
to zero, while the library's general buffer ceiling is larger. The internal
measurement is now `uint64_t`, calculated with the checked
`dwgSafety::bufferBitCount` helper. The 32-bit serialized header handseed
offset and legacy object bit count remain 32-bit and are explicitly range
checked before narrowing; the on-disk format and normal output bytes are
unchanged. Bit-range patching also validates the total and requested range
before converting to platform `size_t` indexes.

Generated tests exercise the exact 512 MiB arithmetic boundary without
allocating a large buffer, plus aligned/partial-byte counts, invalid cursors,
and 64-bit multiplication overflow. Validation:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_writer_primitives_tests --parallel 2` — passed with strict warning settings.
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_writer_primitives_tests` — passed.
- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_object_vectors_tests libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip --parallel 2` — passed.
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_(writer_primitives|dwg_object_vectors|dwg_local_roundtrip)$' --output-on-failure` — 3/3 passed (3.63 seconds).
- Scoped `git diff --check` for changed source/test files — passed.

No full suite, 512 MiB allocation, persistent fixture, new CTest registration,
peer runtime, native CAD app, or kernel was used. Findings/subplans remain
**141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`, and no support claim is promoted. Self-unblock: continue
the PAR-14 cursor/count audit at the direct object-body bit-position helpers
in `src/drw_objects.cpp`; compare each byte-to-bit multiplication with the
existing `MaxBufferSize` admission and local boundary tests before changing
any parser path.

## Implementation progress — PAR-20/7G.3 GROUP adapter closure (2026-10-20; generated ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

The codec already emitted GROUP objects and regenerated the `ACAD_GROUP`
dictionary, but the concrete `dx_iface` adapter dropped `addGroup`, so a
DXF→adapter→DXF pass lost every group. The adapter now retains typed GROUP
callbacks under record/member/byte bounds, joins each imported group handle to
its name through the positional NOD's normalized `ACAD_GROUP` key and the
referenced dictionary's key→handle entries, and refuses export if that
identity join is incomplete or ambiguous. Export passes the retained GROUPs
to the codec. The codec rejects empty/colliding names, duplicate/invalid member
handles, and any member 340 that does not map to an emitted entity; it no
longer silently filters unresolved group members.

The generated control starts from a locally constructed LINE and GROUP, then
imports, exports, and imports again in both ASCII and Binary AC1032 DXF. It
checks the dictionary-derived group name, description, and member-entity
identity after each pass. Negative controls cover a missing member, duplicate
members, case-folded duplicate names, and an input whose `ACAD_GROUP`
dictionary entry does not resolve to the GROUP object. Every refusal
preserves an existing destination sentinel. The malformed dictionary case
confirms import can retain the decoded object while separately recording
identity-resolution failure and refusing export. All drawings are created
under the system temporary directory and removed by the test; no binary
fixture or test data file is committed.

Validation:

```text
cmake --build build --target dwg2dxf libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests -j2  PASS
cmake --build build --target lc3_compat_check -j2                      PASS
build/tests/libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests --group-adapter-roundtrip  PASS
ctest --test-dir build -R '^libdxfrw_group_adapter_roundtrip$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1)
```

This pass re-opened the current LibreDWG and ACadSharp reports and compared
their exact failure stages and candidate fixes with the local implementation
and tests. The central readiness correction is to distinguish a peer's
initial hypothesis from its later measured correction: a proposed patch is a
research lead until it changes the reported output on the exact route.

| LibreDWG [issue #1415](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1415) | The issue remains open. The reporter says its first suggested guard to preserve the separately read R2004+ CMC short produced byte-identical output across 184 drawings: that index is vestigial for this profile. The later measured rule uses the packed CMC method: `0xC3` encodes indexed ACI in the low byte; `0xC2` is true color and has no ACI index to recover that way. Reverse RGB-palette lookup can turn ACI 104 into a colliding palette entry and can produce an invalid DXF layer color for RGB with blue=0. The reported 184-file improvements are author-measured peer results, not independently reproduced here. | Reject the no-op proposed guard as a port candidate.
