## Implementation progress — PAR-20/7G.3 DWG GROUP dictionary graph (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The writer now has a dedicated `registerDwgGroupDictionaryEntry()` path,
separate from physical NOD children. It rejects case-folded duplicate keys,
duplicate handles, reserved dictionary identities, and attempts to put a
registered GROUP handle directly under the NOD in either registration order.
The deferred OBJECTS phase emits those entries inside the fixed
`ACAD_GROUP` dictionary and records dictionary/frame receipts in the compound
write checkpoint. Final validation requires each registration to have exactly
one emitted GROUP frame and object-map occurrence. `writeGroup()` fails closed
for an unregistered or mismatched key/handle, wrong parent, repeated frame,
duplicate member, or member that was not emitted as an entity. Ordinary NOD
child registration remains a separate path.

The GROUP payload now preserves the format distinction: DWG's TV group name is
parsed and written through `DRW_TableEntry::name`; DXF group 300 remains
`DRW_Group::m_description`. The adapter requires the ACAD_GROUP dictionary
entry and both owner edges, compares the parsed DWG TV name with its dictionary
key, and no longer accepts a direct-NOD fallback. DXF import continues to
resolve the GROUP name from the dictionary and preserves group-300 description
separately.

The generated selector covers zero- and one-GROUP dictionaries in AC1015,
AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032. The one-GROUP case uses two ordered
member entities, distinct dictionary/name/description values, exact owner and
flag checks, plus a following XRECORD sentinel. AC1024 negatives cover a
direct-NOD alias before and after GROUP registration, case-folded duplicate
keys, unregistered frame, registration without a frame, duplicate emission,
wrong owner, and missing member. All drawings are generated under a unique
temporary directory and deleted; no fixture or peer drawing was added.

<a id="deeper-broader-peer-object-graph-survival-and-output-loss-boundary-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader peer object-graph survival and output-loss boundary (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass rechecked the next open PAR-20/7G boundary after the generated GROUP
dictionary writer slice. The useful cross-project result is not a new codec
feature claim: mature readers/writers make object survival conditional on class
maturity, target route, and a valid owner path. A successful parse, a matching
class name, or retained opaque bytes is therefore insufficient evidence that a
named OBJECT survives a conversion in a usable, referentially closed form.

| Evidence | Observed boundary | Consequence for libdxfrw |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [class-stability documentation](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi#L3022-L3039) | The current manual distinguishes stable, unstable, debugging, and unhandled classes. It says unstable objects may be represented as unknown objects/entities and written as placeholder-like classes; only same-version rewrites with the complete known unknown-bits blob may preserve some classes as such. Debugging/unhandled classes can be ignored. | Treat peer class support and a broad peer read/write claim as advisory. A same-codec no-op rewrite and DXF export are separate operations; do not infer cross-version or semantic retention from a successful read. |
| ezdxf [object lifecycle model](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/develop/pkg-design.rst#L223-L225) and [OBJECTS ownership rules](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/develop/pkg-design.rst#L314-L318) | Non-graphical OBJECTS records have a parent, most often a DICTIONARY; the root dictionary is the exception allowed to have owner `0`; objects with a missing/destroyed owner are orphaned and its audit destroys/removes them. | The output gate must verify root reachability and reciprocal owner identity, not only object-map presence or serialization callbacks. |
| ezdxf [XREF owner-path design notes](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/xref.py#L2453-L2504) | The implementation notes distinguish objects whose ownership path terminates at a graphical entity (for example, entity → extension dictionary → XRECORD) from NOD-rooted object-only paths; copying a rooted object family may require reconstructing missing dictionary ancestors. | Keep entity-owned extension graphs separate from NOD resource graphs. A root-key closure pass cannot silently treat an extension-dictionary child as a named-root child or vice versa. |
| LibreDWG [writer-operation documentation](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg#readme) | The current README qualifies DWG writing as working only through R2004 and says most rewrites up to R2004 usually work; it also separately describes partial conversion coverage. | Match any optional comparison to the exact writer version, operation, and class. This does not qualify our DWG writer and must not become a routine peer dependency. |
| Local [support boundary](README.md#support-boundary), [writer/adaptor implementation](src/libdxfrw.cpp), and [7G graph plan](#deeperbroader-nod-entry-order-keyed-closure-2026-10-20-research-only) | Local claims already distinguish typed/raw carrier retention from independent semantics; the latest GROUP slice now closes one specific `NOD → ACAD_GROUP → GROUP → members` route, while broader NOD root and nested dictionary closure remains open. | Continue under existing PAR-20/7G; do not add a finding, expand the release claim, or duplicate already-covered field/handle tests. |

### PAR-20/7G implementation-ready refinement

1. **Classify before replay.** For each source NOD key discovered by the existing
   reader/adapter audit, record one disposition: fixed/regenerated root;
   typed route with a closed owner/reference graph; opaque route with proven
   owner and handle-remapping rules; or unsupported route that is explicitly
   reported and refused in strict output. Never infer the disposition from a
   callback having fired or a byte vector being non-empty.
2. **Keep graph families separate.** For NOD roots, verify normalized
   key→target identity, dictionary class, target kind, exact owner reciprocity,
   duplicate/case-folded key handling, all outgoing handle roles, and
   reachability from the regenerated NOD. For entity extension dictionaries,
   start at the owning entity and independently verify the extension-dictionary
   edge and descendant path. Do not relocate between these graphs to make an
   otherwise dangling item appear reachable.
3. **Use an explicit minimal route table.** Extend the existing 7G inventory
   with the expected immediate owner kind and treatment for each currently
   admitted root key; do not introduce a generic schema framework. Keep
   fixed roots (`ACAD_LAYOUT`, `ACAD_GROUP`, and other regenerated roots) on
   their dedicated writer paths. Admit other keys only when their target
   family has an existing typed/raw capture and output owner; otherwise emit a
   deterministic diagnostic and fail strict publication rather than silently
   dropping or guessing a dictionary container.
4. **Add focused generated controls only where coverage is absent.** Reuse the
   existing named-object and graph-preservation selectors. Assert one positive
   closed multi-level dictionary route and negatives for an orphan/non-root
   owner `0`, wrong dictionary parent, dangling remapped handle, duplicate
   normalized key, and an unsupported unknown root. Use in-memory/from-scratch
   data and temporary output only; add no peer or external DWG/DXF fixture.
5. **Keep the fast loop local.** Build only changed targets and run the owning
   selector/CTest, `git diff --check`, and the existing compatibility check
   only when a public callback/API changed. Reserve broader suites, peer
   binaries, and native CAD applications for already-defined composed
   checkpoints; their absence is not a reason to pause local work.
6. **Self-update and self-unblock.** After each implemented graph item, update
   this route table, the owning PAR-20 status row, and a small receipt with the
   exact tests and remaining gaps. Report slice progress when committed; when
   a route cannot be admitted from available local/spec evidence, leave it
   explicitly unsupported/refused and advance to the next implementation-ready

## Implementation progress — PAR-20 generic unmodeled OBJECTS strict-loss refusal (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The source audit found that `dxfRW::processObjects()` already routed an
unrecognized OBJECTS record through the generic raw capture, but
`dx_iface::addRawDxfObject()` had no general storage/output path and silently
ignored that callback. Rooted records often failed later graph validation;
unrooted records had no such guard. Inferring “unknown” from the raw callback
was incorrect because typed routes also publish raw companions, and
`ACDBPLACEHOLDER` intentionally uses a raw-only adapter route.

The parser now queries an optional
`DRW_UnmodeledDxfObjectHandler` side-interface only from the generic
unknown-object fallback; it does not add or reorder any `DRW_Interface` virtual.
`ACDBPLACEHOLDER` takes the same bounded raw capture path without the unknown
marker. `dx_iface` sets a sticky
container-lifetime marker; strict `fileExport(..., requireResolvedOwners=true)`
refuses before output publication when that marker is present. Existing
permissive export mode and explicitly modeled/raw-only callbacks are not
changed. This is detection/refusal, not raw replay; broad unknown-object
preservation remains unimplemented.

The focused regression parses a generated minimal OBJECTS section containing
the NOD and one unknown object, then asserts strict output refusal and absence
of the requested destination file. The existing named-object callback control
also asserts that recognized typed/raw families do not set the unknown marker.
Generated input and output live in a unique temporary directory removed by
the test; no persistent or external DWG/DXF fixture was added.

Focused validation:

```text

```

It does not replay the unknown object, prove arbitrary owner/reference
semantics, or qualify writer/consumer support. Generic raw OBJECTS replay,

`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. No full suite, peer binary, external
drawing, or native CAD application was used. The shared worktree is broadly

confirmed by this review.

It also distinguishes entity-owned extension dictionaries from NOD-rooted object-only paths. | Test output reachability and ordering for the same admitted owner graph; do not rely on a later consumer audit to repair a misplaced or orphaned child. Keep graphical-owner extension graphs separate from NOD routes. |

The reporter supplies claimed comparisons and proposes resolving the header NOD handle, with unowned-DICTIONARY fallback. Keep DWG root-handle identity separate from DXF's position-defined NOD. |

The existing ASCII/Binary DICTIONARYVAR control deliberately places the variables before their owner DICTIONARY in the source and verifies output owner closure/readback, but it does not inspect emitted OBJECTS record ordinals. Source inspection suggests parent-first order for this route, not a proven regression. | Extend that existing generated selector with raw output-order assertions. This converts an implicit ordering property into a regression guard without adding a new CTest, a generic graph framework, or an external fixture. |

### PAR-20/7G implementation-ready refinement

1. Keep root selection and record scheduling separate. First emit the one

   dictionary key→remapped-target association independently of that schedule.
2. Build ordering constraints from semantic owner roles, not code-number ranges
   alone: an object's group-330 owner, an `ACAD_XDICTIONARY` group-360
   extension-dictionary owner, and DICTIONARY group-350/360 entry edges under
   the dictionary's ownership policy are owner edges. Ordinary hard/soft
   pointer references are not ordering constraints. An entity or other owner
   emitted in an earlier DXF section satisfies the cross-section predecessor

4. Keep unsupported, missing-owner, duplicate-identity, or cyclic owner paths

## Implementation progress — PAR-20/7G generic NOD-root owner reciprocity (2026-10-20; generated ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

Strict extension-graph preparation now resolves each admitted non-fixed NOD
entry to exactly one captured supported target and requires that target's
`parentHandle` to equal the decoded NOD handle. A missing/ambiguous target or
wrong owner returns a specific invalid-graph diagnostic before publication;
the existing `hasParent(0)` allowance remains available only to other
separately validated graph contexts and no longer authorizes an ownerless
NOD child.

The existing root-dictionary closure selector now also has a simple generic
`CUSTOM_ROOT` positive case (owner = NOD) and a negative case (owner = `0`).
The negative asserts both the precise `NOD dictionary entry target does not
name the NOD as its owner` failure and preservation of the preexisting
destination. These controls run in ASCII and Binary alongside the previous
NOD-first/owner-before-DICTIONARYVAR checks. The generic route is deliberately
empty and does not imply support for arbitrary unknown OBJECTS.

## Deeper/broader DXF DICTIONARY entry-ownership and FIELD route (2026-10-20; research only)

This review revisits PAR-20/7G after the NOD-root and OBJECTS owner-order
controls. The entry-kind audit below supersedes the previous generic
`hardOwner -> 360` expectation: official DXF references distinguish the
dictionary-wide flag from each entry's group code, and the current local data
model discards source entry-code identity. Keep the following relationships
independent:

**Supersession note:** the generic `hardOwner` output expectation and the
implementation sequence in this historical subsection are superseded by the
newer [entry-kind preservation refinement](#deeperbroader-dxf-dictionary-entry-kind-preservation-and-field-route-2026-10-20-research-only)
below. Use that newer sequence for implementation; this section remains as the
record of the earlier, narrower FIELD-route audit.

1. **Containing-object ownership:** group 330 identifies the owning object on
   a DICTIONARY; an entity's `{ACAD_XDICTIONARY}` attachment uses a separate
   hard-owner group-360 edge.
2. **Dictionary-entry edge kind:** a repeated group-3 key is paired with its
   own group-350 soft-owner or group-360 hard-owner handle.
3. **Dictionary-wide policy:** group 280 says whether the dictionary's
   elements are to be treated as hard-owned. Do not infer a key's emitted edge
   code from group 280 alone without checking the exact route/profile.
4. **FIELD-internal references:** a FIELD's child fields use group 360 and its
   expression object IDs use group 331; neither is a DICTIONARY key edge.

The OBJECTS example emits group 350 for the root dictionary. These official sources are not fully aligned on a universal code rule; version, object route, and producer output matter. | Retain the existing `NOD → ordinary entry = 350` expected output and child entries selected by dictionary-wide flag as current libdxfrw writer policy. Do not infer from the older NOD prose that every root edge must become 360, and do not infer from the current table that every special extension-dictionary edge must be 350. Resolve only the named route below. |
| Autodesk [FIELD DXF table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-51B921F2-16CA-4948-AC75-196198DD1796.htm) and Autodesk Developer [field-list description](https://blog.autodesk.io/how-to-find-all-fields-in-a-drawing/) | FIELD child references are explicitly hard-owner 360; FIELD expression object IDs are soft-pointer 331. The comment, historical release summary, and current output behavior are therefore not a license to generalize the exception. | Treat `ACAD_FIELD` as a narrowly scoped generated-output candidate only. If a peer check is needed, pin the exact 0.6.5 source/package and ask only whether its `ACAD_FIELD` output matrix matches the proposed local contract; do not install/run it per implementation slice. |
| LibreDWG [current NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | The release history records an older “DICTIONARY: fix hard_owner DXF 350/360” writer fix. Do not re-run a peer or infer current behavior from historical NEWS; only compare an exact release/source when the composed validation checkpoint reaches a named question. |
| Local `dxfRW::writeDictionary`, the reserved NOD writer in `src/libdxfrw.cpp`, and `populateAutoCadFieldGraph` / `validateAutoCadFieldGraph` in `tests/dwg2dxf_adapter_tests.cpp` | The reserved NOD writer currently emits each regenerated root entry as 350. This update supersedes the generic edge-code assumptions in the preceding
research entry. It compares current Autodesk documentation, the local parser
and writers, ezdxf's actual dictionary codec, and the latest ACadRust release
source. The defensible local objective is **per-entry source-code preservation**;
the default code for newly constructed dictionaries and application-specific
exceptions remain separate policy questions.

Group 281 is a duplicate-cloning flag. The published tables do not establish that flag 280 alone determines every entry's group code. | Stop presenting `hardOwner == 1 ? 360 : 350` as a universal/normative rule. Characterize it as existing construction behavior only. Any change to defaults needs a route-specific expected-value source. |
| Local `DRW_Dictionary::parseCode`, `DRW_Dictionary::Entry`, `dxfRW::writeDictionary`, the named-dictionary writer, and reserved NOD writer | The parser accepts either 350 or 360 but retains only a key and handle; comments note files mix codes independent of the wide flag. Both ordinary output paths regenerate entry code from `hardOwner`; the special NOD route separately emits 350. The typed data model therefore cannot reproduce a mixed-code dictionary after parse/write. This is a source-confirmed information-loss path, not yet an output-level reproduction or demonstrated external rejection. | Make preservation of the parsed per-entry code the first local change. Do not infer original edge kind from flag 280. Keep the regenerated NOD route separate, and test actual emitted pairs rather than only the typed graph. |
| ezdxf [current `dictionary.py`](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dictionary.py) and [DICTIONARY documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfobjects/dictionary.html) | `load_dict()` accepts both 350 and 360 but records one `_value_code` for the whole dictionary, overwritten by each encountered entry; `export_dict()` emits that one code for every key. This corrects the earlier source-availability note. Its FIELDLIST writer documents that the reference application omits id-set flag 290 and emits it only when the stored unknown flag is true. This is exact peer source behavior, not a native-run or raw AutoCAD sample. | Keep the source as a scoped expected-output lead for default FIELDLIST flag omission. Characterize local output for false/true in ASCII/Binary before changing production behavior, and reserve native/pinned-peer execution for a later composed checkpoint only if source/local evidence does not settle the policy. Do not let this specific note generalize DICTIONARY entry-code rules. |
| Autodesk [FIELD DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-51B921F2-16CA-4948-AC75-196198DD1796.htm), [developer field-list description](https://blog.autodesk.io/how-to-find-all-fields-in-a-drawing/), and ODA [FIELD/FIELDLIST object layouts](https://static.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) | FIELD child handles use 360 and expression object IDs use 331. FIELDLIST is an AcDbIdSet: it has a count and 330 soft-pointer field-membership handles. The developer note also describes the NOD `ACAD_FIELDLIST` route and typical host extension-dictionary access. Common object owner 330 precedes the subclass body, so the repeated member 330s must be parsed by state, not conflated with the owner. The ODA listing leaves the FIELDLIST unknown boolean without a DXF group-code mapping. | Assert five distinct roles: NOD entry to FIELDLIST; FIELDLIST 330 membership; host extension-dictionary attachment; `ACAD_FIELD` dictionary entry; FIELD child-360 and expression/value soft-pointer references. Preserve the existing subclass-aware parser control and add explicit 290 false/true wire characterization. Do not infer owner semantics from a matching group number. |
| LibreDWG [historical NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) and [current DXF writer source](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/out_dxf.c) | NEWS records an old hard-owner 350/360 fix; current object writing is partly macro/generated. Only compare a pinned release at the composed checkpoint if it answers a named question. |

This pass widens the PAR-20/7G dictionary-entry review across a second
independent parser and the OBJECTS root contract. It sharpens the goal from
"make every peer round-trip preserve the same edge code" to two separately
measured properties: preserve each source `(key, handle, 350|360)` tuple in
libdxfrw's own round trip, and preserve the semantic target/owner graph across
consumers that normalize that wire detail.

| Evidence | Finding and evidence ceiling | Plan consequence |

The docs therefore describe related but non-identical object policy and serialized reference type. | Keep three assertions separate: serialized entry code, dictionary's flag-280 policy, and target/owner graph lifecycle. Do not call retention of a 360 code proof that the dictionary's ownership policy is semantically correct, or derive all entry codes from flag 280. |
| ACadSharp [DXF OBJECTS reader source](https://coveralls.io/builds/81353195/source?filename=src%2FACadSharp%2FIO%2FDXF%2FDxfStreamReader%2FDxfObjectsSectionReader.cs) | The inspected source snapshot handles codes 350 and 360 in the same branch and assigns the handle to the latest dictionary key; the in-memory entry map shown there does not carry the original group code. This is useful independent implementation evidence that consumer normalization exists, but it is a mutable coverage snapshot, not a pinned release or AutoCAD semantic oracle. | At the composed checkpoint, use ACadSharp only for target/key graph and read acceptance unless its exact version/source is pinned. Never require a peer rewrite to preserve mixed wire codes when that peer's model discards the distinction. Record version and compare literal tags before/after if output behavior is material. |

## Implementation progress — PAR-20/7G per-entry DICTIONARY code retention (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Implemented the first local slice from the dictionary-entry plan. The public
`DRW_Dictionary::Entry` now carries a typed `DxfHandleCode` value
(`Unspecified`, `SoftOwner`, or `HardOwner`). `DRW_Dictionary::parseCode`
records group 350 or 360 on the matching key/handle pair, completeness checks
reject invalid enum values, and ordinary direct and registered named-dictionary
writers emit each parsed code. New/DWG-origin entries remain `Unspecified` and
retain the previous `hardOwner` fallback. The regenerated NOD path remains its
explicit group-350 route; DICTIONARYWDFLT retains its object-specific group-350
writer grammar.

The existing `--dictionary-key-admission` selector now creates ephemeral
ASCII/Binary inputs with mixed entry codes under both flag-280 values and in
both entry orders. It verifies parsed typed values, copy/assignment retention,
literal code/key/handle output through direct and named-dictionary writers,
and typed readback of the target handles/objects. No persistent drawing or
fixture was added. This establishes the local parse/write preservation path;
it does not prove that any native CAD consumer requires or semantically
interprets the mixed codes differently.

### ABI and version decision

This field changes the public `Entry` element layout. The implementation keeps
the repository's intended 2.0.0 development boundary rather than introducing
a 3.0 version churn: the local tag list has no 2.0.0 tag, and the official
[GitHub release page](https://github.com/LibreCAD/libdxfrw/releases) currently
lists no releases. This is not a complete search of external package
registries. Before publishing a shared 2.0.0 package, recheck for any already
distributed ABI-2 artifact; if one exists, apply the documented release-time
ABI/SOVERSION policy before publishing. Downstream binaries must be rebuilt
against the public header that carries this field.

<a id="deeper-broader-3d-modeler-cross-peer-capability-and-loss-notification-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader 3D modeler cross-peer capability and loss-notification boundary (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass compares current standards references, released peer claims, source tests,
and issue/PR state to sharpen the existing PAR-07/S8 implementation queue. The
newly useful cross-project signal is not evidence for a new local parser bug:
several independent routes can retain a modeler entity shell while omitting,
discarding, or refusing its ACIS payload. Therefore “entity survived” must not
be the only writer success criterion, and carrier presence must not be called
semantic 3D support.

| Evidence | What it establishes—and evidence ceiling | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ODA [Open Design Specification v5.4.1, §§7 and 24](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) and Autodesk [3DSOLID DXF group-code reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm) | ODA identifies the post-R2013 DWG `AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b` DataStorage route for ACIS payloads; the Autodesk DXF entity table documents the modeler subclass/version, proprietary group-1 text with optional group-3 continuation, and history handle. These sources establish distinct outer carrier/record layouts, not that an ACIS body is valid or that every reader/writer supports each version. | Preserve the route matrix: legacy inline SAT, versioned DXF SAT/SAB/ACDSDATA, and DWG AcDs DataStorage must be tested as separate profiles. Record entity/version, carrier kind, ordered chunks/pages, hashes, handle/key/owner join, and disposition. Never use a DXF ACDSDATA result as evidence for DWG DataStorage or vice versa. |
| ACadSharp [issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) and [PR #1240](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1240) | The issue reports ACadSharp 3.4.9 reading hundreds of DWG `3DSOLID`/`REGION` entities but emitting none in DXF, leaving solid-only blocks empty without notification. The PR remains open and undeployed; its visible commit message says `DwgObjectWriter`, so it does not establish a fix for the reported DXF-writer omission. These are peer-reported states, not local reproductions. | Treat read, write, and no-loss notification as separate capabilities. Audit libdxfrw's current strict/permissive modeler-export behavior; where a payload/profile cannot be represented, require deterministic loss diagnostics or strict refusal before destination publication. Do not add a duplicate diagnostic mechanism if the existing route already refuses correctly. |
| ezdxf [ACIS tools documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) | The current docs say only a limited set of ACIS records is supported; unsupported records load as `NONE_ENTITY` and lose data, while exporting those unsupported records raises `ExportError`. This is an explicit failure/disposition contract, not arbitrary ACIS preservation or a geometry kernel. | Reuse this as a fail-closed test-design reference: assert that unsupported modeler content cannot be reported as successful complete output. A generated ezdxf carrier can be an optional source input only after exact package pinning; its own limited parser is not the semantic oracle. |
| LibreDWG [issue #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411) | The report pins a scratch-generatable AC1032 DXF `REGION`/SAB control to LibreDWG 0.14.8593 at commit `8a1ae764`: the REGION survives conversion while its 5,489-byte SAB/ACDSDATA payload does not. This is a version-specific issue report, not a result for current LibreDWG master or libdxfrw. | Use the small generated case as a design reference for assertions that inspect the full payload and its owner/index association independently of the entity count. Do not import the confidential real DWG described in the issue or classify the report as current peer-runtime evidence. |
| ACadRust [v0.6.5 release](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/releases/tag/v0.6.5) and [round-trip tests](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/blob/main/tests/roundtrip.rs) | The release is pinned to commit `289a616` and advertises ACIS modeler improvements. Its published R2018 planar-body test generates a cube from explicit vertices/faces, writes and re-reads through ACadRust, and asserts the 3DSOLID survives with ACIS data. That is a useful generated producer/transport control, but same-codec readback plus `has_data()` does not independently prove B-rep validity, exact topology, native acceptance, or DWG DataStorage association for arbitrary input. | If the composed gate needs a peer run, this is a candidate for one exact pinned control. Keep separate expected analytic values (for a 2×2×2 cube, volume 8 and bounds [0,2]³); assert record/payload identity and the DataStorage join separately; require an independent parser/kernel or native result before promoting semantic support. Do not add this peer to routine tests or dependencies. |

### Refined PAR-07/S8 sequence for implementation readiness and speed

1. **Continue local slices immediately.** Reuse current generated owners for
   modeler DXF chunk preservation, DWG DataIndex/Blob01 association, bounds,
   and loss refusal. Add no persistent peer fixture, build dependency, or
   second CTest unless an audit shows a missing assertion in the exact owner.
2. **At the writer boundary, check disposition before publication.** For each
   selected version/profile, either preserve the complete carrier and its
   graph, or fail/diagnose unsupported content before replacing the requested
   output. An emitted `3DSOLID`/`REGION` shell with zero/missing carrier is a
   loss, even when entity counts match and the command exits successfully.
3. **Keep route axes explicit.** Record (a) format/version/profile, (b) carrier
   grammar and ordered bytes, (c) exact record/page reconstruction, (d) owner,
   handle, history and dictionary association, (e) geometry record disposition
   and B-rep validity, (f) writer outcome, and (g) named-consumer acceptance.
   Mark unexercised cells `NOT_RUN`/`NOT_QUALIFIED`; do not collapse them into
   a single “3D supported” status.
4. **Use a single composed peer checkpoint, not a per-slice matrix.** If
   needed, pin ACadRust v0.6.5/source `289a616` for a generated planar control
   after checking license/artifact availability and exact test scope. Compare
   literal carrier bytes and independently authored analytic geometry values;
   same-codec roundtrip is only a transport check. Do not use ACadSharp #1240's
   open branch as a released comparator or LibreDWG #1411 as a current result.
5. **Make semantic and consumer gates independent.** A geometry-semantic pass
   requires complete disposition of all body-reachable records, valid closed
   topology where expected, exact units/transforms, and comparison against
   independent bounds/area/volume. Stock FreeCAD ACIS import remains
   out-of-profile per the existing consumer contract; its platform run cannot
   discharge the ACIS/AcDs semantic gate.
6. **Preserve cadence and self-unblock.** Touched-target build, the owning
   generated fast selector, and scoped diff checks remain the per-slice lane.
   Reserve full suites and external/native checks for existing composition
   checkpoints. Update the receipt after each local slice; if an external
   artifact or platform is unavailable, record that cell and continue to the
   next runnable local PAR-07/S8 item. Support claims remain gated on all
   required evidence, not on plan completion.

This refines existing PAR-07/S8 and the loss-reporting contract; it adds no
finding or top-level subplan and does not establish a new libdxfrw defect.
Inventory remains **141 findings / 78 top-level subplans**. J256, J260, J268,
J284, J293, and J295 remain explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.
No code, tests, fixtures, dependencies, or external drawings changed; no peer
repository was cloned or built, and no peer executable, native CAD application,
or geometry kernel was run. The plan does not promote 3D support from carrier
retention or same-codec tests.

<a id="deeper-broader-peer-capability-archetypes-strict-recovery-and-validation-evidence-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader peer capability archetypes, strict/recovery, and validation evidence (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass widens the current comparison across format libraries, converters,
projection tools, and the downstream application route. The key plan update is
to stop treating a project's format/version matrix as a proxy for feature
parity: each project exposes a different product boundary and several of the
routes deliberately normalize, project, repair, or omit data. The findings
below refine existing evidence and validation gates; they do not identify a
new local defect.

| Primary source | What it establishes and its evidence ceiling | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [agent testing guide](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/AGENTS.md) and [format/class manual](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | The project recommends focused tests and `make check`; its DWG→DXF helper compares the source read, encoded DXF, and reread result, while its guide says JSON round trips are useful only through R2000. Its class documentation distinguishes stable, unstable, debug-only, and ignored types. This is strong evidence for test strategy and explicit support tiers, not evidence that a particular current peer binary preserves every object. | At a composed comparison, bind exact peer revision/build and operation, then inspect the input, converted DXF, and independent reread as separate stages. Record per-class/per-record disposition; do not infer preservation from a supported class list, successful conversion, or same-codec JSON round trip. Keep GPL-3+ source reuse subject to a separate compatibility review. |
| ezdxf [version/format README](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf) and [recovery documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/recover.html) | The project declares ASCII/Binary DXF read/write across R12 and R2000–R2018, with older DXF read-only conversion paths. Its recovery API can load structurally damaged ASCII DXF, but warns that decode errors (notably binary data in XRECORD) can be unrecoverable and that writing a recovered document may produce invalid DXF or lose information; `errors="strict"` is available to reject such input. These are DXF-library behaviors, not DWG or arbitrary 3D semantics. | Keep strict parse and recovery/repair as separate evidence modes. A recovery success must retain its diagnostics and any repaired/omitted content in the output disposition; never count it as a strict compatibility pass or use its rewrite as the fidelity oracle. Use ezdxf for a precisely scoped DXF tag/object comparison, not DWG. |
| ACadSharp [repository feature/version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) and [reader example/notifications](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/docs/articles/samples/reading.md) | Its README declares both DWG and DXF readers/writers, but the matrix itself is direction- and version-specific (for example, AC1021 DWG writer is not checked). Reader warnings are delivered as notifications. The matrix and notification API do not make a per-entity completeness or native acceptance claim. | Keep ACadSharp as a conditional object-model differential only. Capture the exact release/commit, chosen format direction/version, warnings, and entity/object dispositions. An unchecked matrix cell is `NOT_DECLARED`, not a libdxfrw defect or a peer pass. |
| GDAL [current DXF driver documentation](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | GDAL documents Binary-DXF reading beginning with 3.12 and a `RawCodeValues` option for unhandled tags. Its main output is an OGR feature projection; many CAD properties are mapped or approximated. For AC1027+ it can optionally expose raw ASM bytes and an affine transform, but states it cannot construct OGR geometry from 3D modeler data and skips those records by default. | Use GDAL only for a named projected geometry/field question. Enable and capture raw values when relevant, keep tessellated/projected results separate from exact CAD records, and never count raw ASM extraction as B-rep semantics, complete graph preservation, or DWG support. |
| FreeCAD [DXF importer documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md), [DWG import documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md), and [current `importDWG.py`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py) | FreeCAD documents selectable C++ and legacy Python DXF import/export paths with different feature coverage. DWG is a converter→intermediate-DXF→selected-importer chain, not a direct DWG parser; the stock DXF import route does not consume embedded SAT solids. The current wrapper's completion therefore cannot establish that intermediate conversion or import preserved every object. | Preserve the named consumer gate as a multi-stage manifest: converter identity/args/exit/diagnostics and intermediate DXF hash/version; selected importer backend/preferences/build; source-to-intermediate-to-imported identity and disposition. Keep Linux/Windows FreeCAD qualification distinct from libdxfrw parser tests and from ACIS semantics. |

### Revised implementation-ready and speed rules

1. **Represent capability by route tuple, not a project badge.** For every
   existing PAR family, qualify only the relevant tuple:
   `(input format, AC code, operation/direction, record family, parser mode,
   output format/version, consumer)`. Use explicit states such as
   `PARSED_TYPED`, `RAW_ONLY`, `PROJECTED`, `REPAIRED`, `OMITTED_WITH_DIAGNOSTIC`,
   `REFUSED`, and `NOT_RUN`; keep output identity/owner joins separate from
   aggregate entity counts.
2. **Fast local slice remains the default.** Reuse the owning generated test
   selector and target CTest. Assert the source field/tag or DWG value, typed
   value, emitted wire value, identity/owner association, one following
   sentinel, and exact fail/diagnostic disposition where applicable. Add a
   new test only for a demonstrable uncovered local route; avoid a second broad
   matrix executable or routine peer installation.
3. **Keep recovery out of strict acceptance.** If an existing parser exposes
   recovery/repair, record it as a separate run and preserve diagnostics and
   loss/repair counts. Strict mode must be evaluated independently. A recovery
   result may inform robustness but cannot promote lossless read/write support.
4. **One composed peer checkpoint.** Only when a remaining named question
   cannot be resolved from the format source and local generated oracle, run
   one exact-pinned peer operation at the existing composed checkpoint. Bind
   source/output hashes, release/commit, build flags/runtime, input provenance,
   format/version, mode/options, process status/diagnostics, and per-record
   disposition. If unavailable, write `NOT_RUN`/`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and
   immediately resume local implementation.
5. **Consumer checks stay downstream and optional until ready.** For the
   requested FreeCAD Linux/Windows gates, separate converter output validity,
   importer/backend behavior, and application object inventory. Do not ask a
   stock 2D importer to qualify ACIS semantics; do not treat application open
   or save success alone as a no-loss result.
6. **Queue and validation cadence are unchanged.** The next local action
   remains PAR-20/7G.3 root/owner closure after the FIELD wire candidate and
   malformed-graph refusal controls. Keep full-suite runs at existing
   composition/release checkpoints; no extra external dependency, peer build,
   persistent fixture, or test DWF/DXF file is introduced by this research.

### Local queue reconciliation

A read-only scan of `prepareExtensionObjectGraph()`, the `fileExport()` NOD
root builder, and the existing generated adapter/codec tests found that the
generic root route is not one undifferentiated serializer: known root
dictionaries, directly owned XRECORD/DICTIONARYVAR/SCALE-family entries, and
special GROUP, LAYOUT, MATERIAL, BACKGROUND, and FIELD paths have separate
admission/emission behavior. Existing tests already exercise representative
nested MLINESTYLE, TABLESTYLE, PLOTSETTINGS, VISUALSTYLE, and
DETAIL/SECTIONVIEWSTYLE closures, as well as direct/nested XRECORD and root
owner negatives. The current public peer documentation does not justify
promoting an untested root target type to output support. No additional code or
test was added from this scan; continue the queued PAR-20/7G.3 audit from the
next source-backed route and require an exact gap before expanding the
serializer.

This is a research refinement under the existing PAR ledger: no new finding,
top-level subplan, code change, test change, fixture, dependency, or support
promotion. Counts remain **141 findings / 78 top-level subplans**. J256, J260,

## Deeper/broader FIELDLIST membership and DXF version/flag boundaries (2026-10-20; research refinement)

This pass adds producer, version, and graph-topology detail to the existing
PAR-20/7G FIELD route. The main correctness risk is treating every occurrence
of group 330 as the same edge, or treating presence of a parsed carrier as
proof that the selected target DXF version can represent it.

| Evidence | Finding and limit | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ODA [Open Design Specification v5.4.1, sections 20.4.76–20.4.77](https://static.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf) | FIELD and FIELDLIST are R18 classes. FIELD child fields are hard-owner 360; FIELD object references are soft-pointer 331. FIELDLIST inherits AcDbIdSet and has a 90 count plus repeated 330 soft-pointer members; it is stored at the NOD `ACAD_FIELDLIST` entry. The unknown DWG bit has no DXF group-code mapping in the table. | Keep version floor, FIELD child/reference edges, FIELDLIST membership, and the NOD dictionary edge independent. A FIELDLIST member 330 is not an owner relation. Use AC1018/R18 as the first target-version candidate and test the AC1015 boundary before emitting either class there. |
| Autodesk [FIELD DXF table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-51B921F2-16CA-4948-AC75-196198DD1796.htm) and [developer field enumeration note](https://blog.autodesk.io/how-to-find-all-fields-in-a-drawing/) | Autodesk documents FIELD child 360, expression soft-pointer 331, and group 330 as the ID-valued field value when the value type is ID. The developer article says the NOD's `ACAD_FIELDLIST` identifies a FIELDLIST, that each field is typically accessible from an entity extension dictionary, and that enumerating FIELDLIST code-330 members yields AcDbField objects. “Typically” is not a guarantee that every field has an extension-dictionary route. | The complete graph model must preserve the aggregate FIELDLIST index, typed ID-valued cache references, and each concrete host route (entity, TABLE, or other supported owner) as separate associations. Do not require a field's extension dictionary to equal FIELDLIST membership, infer list membership from host reachability, or confuse group 330 roles across object state. |
| ACadRust [v0.6.5 published package/source](https://docs.rs/acadrust/0.6.5/src/acadrust/io/dxf/writer/section_writer.rs.html) and [release commit](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/commit/289a616da6c68518218594aa80802cbe7fa71309) | The docs.rs package index resolves `latest` to 0.6.5 dated 2026-10-18; the exact-version section writer says the reference application does not write id-set flag 290 and emits it only when `unknown` is true. This is pinned peer source behavior, not an observed AutoCAD DXF or an executed peer output. | Add a fast default/true flag characterization to the existing ASCII/Binary writer selector. Treat absence of 290 for the default false value as a strong candidate output policy; do not describe local 290:0 as a confirmed interoperability defect before an independent emitted-wire/native check. Do not map the DWG bit to a new DXF meaning. |
| Autodesk [Field feature introduction note](https://blog.autodesk.io/autocad-lno-code-solution-field/) and ODA class-version rows above | Autodesk describes Fields as introduced in AutoCAD 2005; ODA lists FIELD and FIELDLIST with DWG version R18. The local `dxfRW::writeField()` and `writeFieldList()` guards currently allow DXF targets from AC1015. This is a source-confirmed version-floor discrepancy candidate; no AC1015 AutoCAD rejection was reproduced. | Make the local writer's minimum version explicit in the existing direct-writer control. First assert AC1015 is refused and AC1018 is admitted for both FIELD and FIELDLIST; if any documented target exception is found, capture it before changing the guard. Reader behavior and imported older custom class records remain a separate question. |
| Local `dxfRW::processFieldList()`, `writeFieldList()`, `DRW_FieldList`, adapter graph validator, and current generated tests | The parser uses `Preamble → AcDbIdSet → AcDbFieldList` state to distinguish common-object owner 330 from member 330. It validates the declared 90 count against members and has a following-record sentinel. Graph closure requires unique list membership covering the admitted typed fields; adapter export still explicitly refuses FIELD/FIELDLIST. The direct writer remaps owner/member handles but unconditionally emits 290 even when `m_unknown == 0`; the typed value currently does not retain whether an input explicitly contained `290:0`. The existing low-level FIELD candidate asserts expression 331 but does not put an ID-valued cache (330) in that generated graph. | Preserve subclass-aware parsing and the existing bounded tests. Extend only the existing writer selector: false/true flag policy; explicit-presence versus canonical-output decision; AC1015/AC1018 floor; and exact ASCII/Binary `(code,value)` order for owner 330, FIELDLIST member 330, FIELD ID value 330, expression 331, FIELD child 360, count 90, and sentinel. Keep strict adapter refusal as the positive boundary; a low-level writer pass does not enable `dx_iface`. |

### Implementation-ready order (existing PAR-20/7G; fastest local slices)

1. **Version gate first.** Reuse the current FIELD writer characterization in
   `tests/wave1_tests.cpp`. Add four generated calls (FIELD and FIELDLIST at
   AC1015/AC1018); assert pre-R18 refusal is atomic and AC1018 emits bounded
   records. This is a tiny, deterministic source/spec check with no fixture.
2. **Default id-set flag.** In the same selector, write FIELDLIST with
   `m_unknown = 0` and `m_unknown = 1` to ASCII and Binary. Scan literal tags:
   count 90, optional 290 only under the chosen policy, owner 330 before
   `AcDbIdSet`, members 330 after the count, `AcDbFieldList`, and the trailing
   sentinel. Decide whether `290:0` is canonicalized away or retained as input
   presence; add public presence metadata only if strict typed tag round-trip
   requires it, with the documented ABI review. Use current peer 0.6.5 source
   as an expected-value lead; keep a peer/native run out of per-slice
   validation.
3. **Parser/graph closure.** Reuse the existing generated FIELD parser and
   adapter graph controls. Extend the direct candidate with an ID-valued
   FIELD cache value whose group-330 soft pointer is checked separately from
   the preamble owner and FIELDLIST member slots. Retain cases where a FIELD
   is reachable from the list but not an extension dictionary, and where an
   owner extension dictionary links a FIELD not otherwise confused with the
   list root. Check exact handle identity and uniqueness. Add a case only if
   the current controls do not already cover it; do not create a second graph
   test lane.
4. **Keep operation boundaries explicit.** Continue low-level writer and
   strict DXF reader checks while `dx_iface` refuses FIELD/FIELDLIST graph
   export. Enable adapter output only after root traversal, all owner routes,
   handle reservation/remap, emitted-wire assertions, and typed strict
   readback are implemented together.
5. **Fast validation and self-unblock.** Build the touched library/wave1 and
   adapter targets, run only their existing FIELD/named-resource CTests, and
   run scoped `git diff --check`. No full suite, persistent sample, peer
   executable, or native application is needed per slice. Update the receipt
   immediately, report a completed slice at its requested commit boundary,
   then continue to the next local PAR-20/7G item; external qualification is
   advisory and must not stop implementation.

The evidence is sufficient to make the two local output questions actionable,
but it does not establish that `290:0` causes a native failure, that AC1015
output has been rejected by a real reader, or that every field is host-attached
through an extension dictionary. The exact group-0 FIELD spelling also remains
separate from these graph/code questions: Autodesk's table labels the name
`ACAD_FIELD`, while the current local writer emits `FIELD`; keep the existing
literal candidate separate until a source-backed native-produced DXF resolves
the spelling. No production policy changed in this research pass.

This refines existing PAR-20/7G without a new finding or top-level subplan.

native CAD application, or external drawing was used. The generated adapter
positive-structure/strict-refusal control remains independently validated as

This pass corrected an erroneous freshness conclusion in the immediately
preceding FreeCAD review and tightened the type of evidence each 3D consumer
row can establish. The relevant distinction is not simply “2D versus 3D”:
DXF has lightweight face and planar-fill entities, ACIS modeler carriers, and
presentation/boundary records, each with different geometry and retention
contracts.

| Evidence | Finding and limit | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md), [DWG import guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md), and the repository's GitHub archive banner | The pages are publicly accessible, but GitHub marks `FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation` archived/read-only from 2026-04-01. The previous section wrongly treated accessibility as evidence that this documentation repository was active. The separate FreeCAD application source remains a different repository and can still be inspected, but mutable `main` source is not a version-pinned release contract. | Treat the documentation as an archived profile snapshot. Use it to select candidate route/backend cases, then bind the FreeCAD application build, converter, importer preference, and actual runtime disposition for any consumer result. Do not cite page accessibility or updates to cached page content as evidence that the documentation repository is maintained. This correction supersedes the contradictory status sentence in the prior section. |
| Autodesk [3DFACE reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-747865D5-51F0-45F2-BEFE-9572DBC5B151.htm) and [3DFACE command reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2022/ENU/AutoCAD-Core/files/GUID-5E88BB23-9110-45FB-B54A-3FF2E2002585.htm) | `3DFACE` carries three or four explicit WCS corner tuples; corner four repeats corner three for a triangle, and group 70 controls the four invisible-edge bits. This describes a face/surface primitive, not a closed B-rep solid or ACIS history. | Keep the existing `DRW_3Dface` field contract and generated controls focused on exact corners, triangular/quadrilateral topology, and the edge-visibility mask. Consumer acceptance of a face must not satisfy a solid-body claim. |
| Autodesk [SOLID reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-E0C5F04E-D0C5-48F5-AC09-32733E8848F2.htm) and [3DSOLID reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm) | The DXF record named `SOLID` is defined by four corners plus optional thickness (39) and extrusion vector (210–230); it is not the `3DSOLID` ACIS carrier. `3DSOLID` instead carries the modeler subclass/version, proprietary group-1 data with optional group-3 continuation, and a history-object handle (350). `HATCH` remains a boundary/fill entity, not an ACIS body. | Keep separate test and result rows for `3DFACE`, planar `SOLID`/`TRACE`, `HATCH`, mesh/polyface geometry, and ACIS-backed `3DSOLID`/`REGION`/`BODY`/`SURFACE`. A count or successful parse for one family cannot be substituted for another. For `3DSOLID`, retain the separate SAT/SAB/ACDSDATA and DWG AcDs association requirements. |
| Prior local [3D support status](docs/3D_SUPPORT_STATUS.md), [optional FreeCAD consumer macro](tests/freecad_dwg2dxf_import_check.FCMacro), and its opt-in CTest registration | The status record says that one existing, user-owned AC1021 DWG produced 48 `3DFACE`, 81 planar `SOLID`, and 24 `HATCH` records through both libdxfrw and ODA File Converter 27.1.0.0. FreeCAD 1.1.3 revision `20260725` on macOS arm64 created 4,868 objects from either DXF, while logging 38 `3DFACE`, 69 `SOLID`, and 22 `HATCH` entities as unsupported and reporting entity-read exceptions. The aggregate report does not map every source handle to an imported object or establish the fate of the unlisted records. The optional generated tilted-`3DFACE` check separately pins a C++ importer negative expectation to an exact FreeCAD revision; it has not been run in this research pass. | The shared unsupported report is evidence that downstream FreeCAD omissions are not unique to libdxfrw's output for that sample. It does not prove output equivalence, semantic geometry survival, or general FreeCAD support. Preserve the source-handle denominator and per-handle dispositions in future probes; do not infer acceptance from the identical 4,868-object total. Reuse the existing opt-in one-face negative test only when that exact pinned FreeCAD profile is under qualification. |
| FreeCAD mutable [`ImpExpDxf.cpp`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Import/App/dxf/ImpExpDxf.cpp) and its application-facing importer boundary | The current source contains a generic `TopoDS_Shape` construction path with a `3DFACE` comment, but a downstream generic-shape case does not prove that all `3DFACE` records or flags reach that path. The archived guide's C++ list omits `3DFACE`, and the pinned one-face macro expects unsupported behavior for its named runtime revision. | Avoid a timeless statement that C++ FreeCAD either fully supports or categorically cannot support every `3DFACE`. Classify by exact backend/build and entity profile. The existing local parser/writer tests remain the codec oracle; the app route is a bounded external disposition check, not a reason to relax or duplicate those tests. |

## Broader open-source peer representation versus 3D semantics and geometry wire gates (2026-10-20; research refinement)

This pass compares what selected open-source peers represent, what they
actually interpret, and which downstream claims their documented behavior
can support. A recognized record, typed API structure, raw ACIS carrier, or
mesh extraction is not by itself proof of a valid analytic solid or a
consumer-visible 3D result.

| Evidence | Finding and limit | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG public [`dwg_api.h`](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/refman/dwg__api_8h_source.html) and current [`dwg.c`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dwg.c) | The API publishes typed `3DFACE` and `3DSOLID` object structures, while current helper code classifies `3DSOLID`, `REGION`, `BODY`, and selected modeler/history objects as modeler/solid-related. That establishes a useful DWG object-model and dispatch comparison. It does not establish that every version is decoded completely, that proprietary modeler bytes have been converted to a valid B-rep, or that a DXF export retains all associations. | Use LibreDWG as a bounded reader/object-classification peer for a specifically named DWG question. Keep decoded-record, raw carrier, association-closure, DXF-output, and analytic-geometry evidence as separate rows. Do not make a general “LibreDWG supports 3D solids” claim from the public typedef/helper surface. |
| ezdxf [`3DSOLID` and ACIS documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html), [`drawing` limitations](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/addons/drawing.html), and [entity creation guidance](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tasks/add_dxf_entities.html) | ezdxf can store SAT/SAB data, expose portions of the ACIS object graph, and extract polygonal meshes from some bodies. Its documentation explicitly marks ACIS `Wire`, `Subshell`, `PCurve`, and other constructs as not implemented; extraction of flat polygonal faces loses curved-face geometry; the drawing frontend does not render ACIS and has no 3D engine (its 3D entities are projected to XY). The author also says required ACIS data creation must be supplied by an external library. | Treat ezdxf as a strong DXF wire/container and limited parser/mesh peer, not an independent complete ACIS kernel. Mesh fallback must be labeled approximate/lossy and separately compare bounds, connected components, face counts, and deviation; it cannot certify analytic surfaces, volume, or topology. Avoid a routine peer install/run when source behavior answers the narrow question. |
| ezdxf [`SOLID` entity reference](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/solid.html) and [layout API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/layouts/layouts.html) | Planar DXF `SOLID` vertex slots are OCS points; the documented entity accessor corrects an unusual stored order, and a triangle repeats its final vertex in the wire representation. These details are easy to lose if tests inspect only a converted polygon or normalized accessor result. | In any uncovered direct `SOLID` tests, assert literal group-code vertex slots and OCS values first, then independently assert the normalized vertex order and WCS result for a non-default extrusion axis. Preserve thickness and extrusion independently. Use an audit of existing tests before adding cases; do not duplicate the existing generated writer/round-trip controls. |
| Autodesk [3DFACE](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-747865D5-51F0-45F2-BEFE-9572DBC5B151.htm), [SOLID](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-E0C5F04E-D0C5-48F5-AC09-32733E8848F2.htm), and [3DSOLID](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm) references | The standard itself distinguishes individual explicit faces, planar filled 2D primitives, and ACIS modeler carriers. A successful parse/count of one family cannot satisfy another family's contract; HATCH and mesh/polyface are also separate representations rather than substitutes for a valid ACIS B-rep. | Maintain distinct support-profile rows for wire parse, wire write, graph/handle retention, world-space geometry, topology/analytic semantics, rendering/import, and round-trip acceptance for each family. Negative results identify the exact failed stage rather than reducing all 3D entities to one pass/fail number. |
| FreeCAD current [`ImpExpDxf.cpp`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Import/App/dxf/ImpExpDxf.cpp), compared with archived [FreeCAD DXF importer documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) | The mutable importer source has a generic `TopoDS_Shape` path with an example comment for `3DFACE`; a source search of that file did not locate a direct `3DSOLID` route. The documentation repository is archived, and neither source inspection nor the old aggregate runtime probe is a pinned release guarantee. | Keep FreeCAD evidence version/backend specific. Do not infer ACIS support from its use of `TopoDS_Shape`, a generic shape comment, total object count, or a successful DWG-to-DXF conversion. For future consumer qualification, record per-source handle/type, intermediate-DXF disposition, created-object identity/type, geometry signature, and explicit skip/error reason. |

### Implementation-ready refinement of existing PAR-07/S8 and geometry-family rows

No new finding or top-level subplan is needed. Apply this dependency order to
existing slices, and first audit the current focused selectors so completed
coverage is reused rather than reimplemented:

1. **Typed expectation ledger.** For each entity family, freeze the expected

<a id="deeper-broader-datastorage-parser-projection-peer-and-librecad3-consumer-boundary-2026-10-20-research-refinement"></a>

## Deeper/broader DataStorage parser, projection-peer, and LibreCAD_3 consumer boundaries (2026-10-20; research refinement)

This pass widens the peer review beyond “does a project expose a 3D type?” to
the exact layer each implementation can evidence: DWG section parsing, record
association, DXF carrier handling, geometry construction, projection, writing,
and application consumption. It adds no support claim or required peer run.

| Primary evidence | Finding and limit | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ACadSharp [Prototype_1b issue #1152](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1152) and [merged PR #1154](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1154) | The merged PR adds a structured DWG `Prototype_1b` section reader and retains segment/index/schema/data records; the PR description says some values remain unknown and that edits would require correctly rebuilding related search-schema and data-index references. It explicitly leaves the prior DXF extraction path in place, and its author notes that mapping `DataStorage` entries to entity payloads is a separate join. The issue thread surfaced real adversarial shapes—stale secondary segment-index rows, multiple schemas, nontrivial `_data_` start/alignment, unreferenced data headers, and out-of-handle-order search references. The thread contains peer-reported corpus and AutoCAD/TrueView results, but these were not reproduced here; an intermediate branch failure is not evidence of a defect in the merged release. | Admit the reader as an optional **section-structure comparator**, not as proof that a given entity received the correct SAB or that any body is valid. Compare section header, chosen segment-index anchor, segment identities/ranges, schemas, DataIndex rows, record-local offsets, Blob01 page references, handle joins, and payload hashes separately. Preserve a compatibility distinction between strict indexed resolution and any heuristic recovery; a signature match alone must not satisfy a strict payload association or support claim. Where peer statements conflict with ODA v5.4.1, read the relevant ODA chapter and capture an exact local trace before changing byte-layout logic; do not copy peer constants or promote an unresolved discrepancy to a format rule. |
| LibreDWG [issue #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411), [AcDs decoder](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode_r2007.c), and [NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | Issue #1411 reports that LibreDWG 0.14.8593 on Linux/x86-64 retained AC1032 `REGION` entity records while losing their 5,489-byte SAB body and AcDs section. It supplies a scratch recipe that creates a polyhedral SAB `REGION` through ezdxf, converts DXF→DWG→DXF, and checks the carrier length. The issue is version-pinned and unverified by this pass; it does not characterize every current LibreDWG revision or any libdxfrw behavior. | Use this recipe only as a **locally regenerated, temporary** optional negative-control shape if a composed peer comparison is warranted. Hash the authored SAB and check source entity, AcDs record/owner key, output section, and output carrier independently. The generated polyhedron can exercise byte/association survival; because it starts as a faceted mesh, it is not evidence for curved analytic faces or general B-rep semantics. Do not download or commit customer drawings or the issue's repro output. |
| GDAL [current DXF driver documentation](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | The current documentation says Binary DXF reading arrived in GDAL 3.12. OGR exposes generic feature projections: selected curves are tessellated, `3DFACE`/planar `SOLID`/`TRACE` become polygon-like geometry, some HATCH fill styling is omitted, and block INSERTs can be merged into compound geometries. For AC1027+, optional 3D extensibility exposes raw ASM bytes and an affine transform, while the driver explicitly cannot construct OGR geometry from those modeler entities. | Use an exact-pinned GDAL build only for a named projection/coordinate question on explicit geometry, or to inspect a raw carrier boundary. Never use OGR geometry, entity counts, or ASM extraction as lossless DXF round-trip, DWG AcDs association, analytic topology, or native-CAD acceptance evidence. Record whether blocks were inlined, geometry tessellated, and styling/fill discarded. |
| ezdxf [ACIS tools documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) | The current stable docs say its ACIS tools target simple/known structures and not arbitrary editing; unsupported records may load as `NONE_ENTITY` with data loss. `mesh_from_body()` returns flat polygonal faces and loses curved-face geometry; ezdxf does not provide an ACIS kernel. The same project can author a cube/polyhedron SAB control, as used in #1411's repro. | ezdxf remains a useful carrier inspector and generated-input producer for bounded profiles. Do not use its partial parser or mesh as a B-rep oracle. For analytic semantics, state expected dimensions/volume/bounds independently from the generation recipe and retain topology/curved-surface expectations separately. |
| LibreCAD_3 [DWG support policy](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/blob/master/docs/dwg-support.md), alongside the existing [3D consumer contract](docs/3D_CONSUMER_CONTRACT.md) | The current LibreCAD_3 document says DWG reading is through `dwgRW`, experimental, and disabled by default; it intentionally does not write DWG until separate interoperability/risk conditions are met. This is an application-policy statement, not a libdxfrw library capability test. | Keep LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3 compatibility scoped to the existing source-compatible 2D adapter and explicit callback/data-delivery guarantees. Qualify the application's DWG reader setting and DXF save workflow separately. Do not require DWG writing as a consequence of reader support, and do not infer UI projection/edit/display behavior from library callback coverage. |
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and [DWG import guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md) | FreeCAD's archived route guidance distinguishes its C++ and legacy Python DXF importers and states that stock FreeCAD cannot read the ACIS blob in `3DSOLID`; DWG import is a converter-to-DXF-to-selected-importer chain. The documentation repository is archived, so these pages are route-selection evidence, not a current runtime qualification. | Keep native Linux/Windows FreeCAD runs optional and exact-profile. For any composed run, capture converter identity/arguments and exit, intermediate DXF version/hash, importer backend/preferences/build, and per-source-handle outcome. A successful converter exit or equal aggregate object count does not establish import fidelity. The documented stock ACIS route is `UNSUPPORTED_CONSUMER`; it cannot block local AcDs implementation or promote modeler semantics. |

### Updated implementation-readiness gates (existing PAR-07/S8 and consumer rows)

1. **Use the existing layered family matrix.** For `3DFACE`, planar
   `SOLID`/`TRACE`, HATCH, mesh/polyface, and ACIS-backed
   `3DSOLID`/`REGION`/`BODY`/`SURFACE`, report distinct results for wire parse,
   typed/raw retention, graph/owner association, coordinate transform,
   semantic geometry, write/reopen, and named consumer import/render. One
   family or one successful layer cannot promote another.
2. **Audit before adding tests.** The current generated suite already contains
   DataStorage segment/schema controls, multi-page Blob01 controls (including
   nonsequential physical segments), and direct DXF SOLID slot / TRACE OCS
   controls. Reuse those. Add a single focused test only after the audit finds
   an uncovered assertion such as the direct SOLID non-default-OCS `ext=true`
   path or a missing strict-vs-recovery boundary; do not create a new broad
   suite or duplicate a DWG fixture.
3. **Keep expected values independent.** For generated cubes, define bounds,
   closedness, component count, and volume from the mathematical construction,
   not from the serializer or the same ACIS parser that authored the bytes.
   Classify tessellated meshes as approximate and compare a stated tolerance;
   they do not establish analytic surfaces, volume preservation, or exact
   topology for curved bodies.
4. **Make extraction failure visible.** For strict conversion, an entity with
   `hasDsData` but no unique, validated section record/payload association
   must not be presented as a valid empty solid or silently skipped. Preserve
   raw carrier+graph or refuse before publishing output, with a structured
   diagnostic. Permissive/recovery behavior, if retained, must carry an
   explicit loss/recovery disposition and cannot pass strict compatibility.
5. **Keep peer work at the composed checkpoint.** Do not install/build
   ACadSharp, LibreDWG, GDAL, ezdxf, FreeCAD, or a kernel per local slice.
   If one exact question remains after local tests, select at most one pinned
   route and record source/artifact hash, version, operation, options, and
   per-handle disposition. Missing platform/tool availability becomes
   `NOT_RUN`/`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; immediately self-unblock to the next local
   source/spec-backed item.
6. **Preserve the fast cadence and fixture policy.** Each local slice remains
   one invariant, one touched target/selector, one owning CTest, a scoped diff
   check, and an updated receipt. Run full suites only at composed integration
   or release checkpoints. Any new DXF/DWG input must already belong to this
   repository/LibreDWG or be generated locally from scratch; keep external
   peer repros in temporary build paths and commit no external fixture.

This pass audits a practical cross-codec route for the existing PAR-07/S8
composed checkpoint. The goal is not to promote ACIS support from a peer's
round-trip test, but to turn the no-external-fixture policy into a runnable
from-scratch semantic witness with independently owned stages and expected
values.

Its self-round-trip and marker-only helper do not prove valid SAB grammar, body topology, an AcDs-to-entity join in libdxfrw, or native CAD acceptance. Before any run, pin the source/archive and verify the exact generator API is present in that artifact; do not assume mutable `main` test content equals the release tag. |

These are issue-author reports against their named versions/branches, not findings in libdxfrw and not automatically attributable to v0.6.5. | Use only the bounded generated cube path for a controlled temporary producer if it succeeds under resource/time limits. Do not treat ACadRust as a general corpus oracle or as proof that malformed DWG handling is safe. Record its exact revision and result; a producer failure is `NOT_RUN`/`NOT_APPLICABLE`, not evidence against libdxfrw. |

It retains unknown records raw and fails conversion when referenced geometry is unsupported; successful parsing alone is not a complete shape. It consumes bare SAB bytes, not a DWG container or AcDs section. Its CadQuery conversion uses OCCT, the same kernel family used by FreeCAD. | Use it only after profile-probing the exact extracted payload. It can independently check supported active-table B-rep semantics, but cannot validate libdxfrw's DWG section parser, DataStorage index, entity handle/key association, history/current model state, or FreeCAD application import. Do not count `cq-acis` and FreeCAD as independent kernel votes. Keep `cq-acis` external to the library and normal CTest/CI. |
| ODA [DWG specification v5.4.1, §20.4.41](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf), local [DataStorage implementation](src/drw_datastorage.cpp), and existing [AcDs graph controls](tests/graph_preservation_tests.cpp) | For modern DWG modeler data, geometry bytes and their DWG entity association are separate facts: a valid SAB-like payload does not prove the section/index/key join selected the right `3DSOLID`/`REGION`, and a complete section parse does not prove the bytes form a body. The existing local generated tests already cover several schema, record-anchor, and Blob01-page cases; this research does not claim those cover every producer profile. | At the composed checkpoint, retain a per-source-handle ledger through: generated DWG identity → libdxfrw object/owner and DataStorage record/key → extracted payload length/hash/profile → output DXF entity/carrier → `cq-acis` body/conversion result. Keep the ODA specification authoritative for DWG layout and require exact trace/spec support before changing parser bytes or joins. |

### Bounded, implementation-ready composed procedure

1. Pin ACadRust v0.6.5 by full commit/archive hash and pin the
   `cq-acis` 0.3.12 wheel plus Python, CadQuery, and OCCT versions. Keep both
   outside the library dependency graph. Check wheel platform availability
   before scheduling; missing tooling is an immediate `NOT_RUN`, not a reason
   to stop local PAR-07 work.
2. Generate one asymmetric analytic box in a temporary directory only. Define
   its eight vertices, six oriented faces, expected one-body/closed-shell
   topology, bounds `[0,2]^3`, and volume `8` in a small manifest authored
   independently of either codec. Save the DWG generation recipe and source
   handle; do not copy or commit a peer corpus, sample, or generated DXF/DWG.
3. Run the pinned producer once to create AC1032 DWG. If it does not produce a
   usable AcDs payload, stop only this optional comparator route, record the
   reason, and continue the local implementation queue. Do not amend the
   expected geometry to match the output.
4. Run libdxfrw on that file and reconcile source handle → decoded entity type
   → AcDs record/key/segment → payload bytes. Independently record SHA-256,
   byte count, and exact SAB/ASM signature/save version. A payload with no
   unique owner/key association, or a signature outside the pinned reader's
   documented profiles, is not a semantic pass.
5. Feed only the extracted bare SAB into `cq-acis`. Require every body-reachable
   reference to resolve, no unsupported/raw body dependency, full conversion,
   valid closed shape, expected body/component count, bounds, orientation, and
   volume within a declared tolerance. `has_data`, parsed-record counts,
   partial faces, tessellation, or successful same-codec readback are not
   substitutes.
6. If a DXF output is also under test, verify its handle/type/carrier and raw
   group-chunk reconstruction separately before passing the carrier to the
   semantic reader. This does not establish DWG rewrite parity or native
   FreeCAD/AutoCAD acceptance.
7. Keep this optional comparison at the existing composed PAR-07/S8 checkpoint
   only. Local feature slices still use one fast selector/CTest; this research
   adds no per-slice external runtime, full-suite run, peer dependency, or
   persistent fixture. Report each layer's result independently and self-unblock
   to the next local item if a tool/profile is unavailable.
