<a id="deeper-broader-cross-project-silent-loss-finalization-and-objects-root-acceptance-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader research — cross-project silent-loss, finalization, and OBJECTS-root acceptance (2026-10-20; research-only)

### What the new source pass establishes

The current [LibreDWG NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS)
is unusually useful because it separates several easily conflated capabilities:
its release notes say that the `AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b` DataStorage parser is
not yet complete, that R2013+ SAB extraction is still done by brute force, and
that converting SAB v2 to encrypted SAT v1 is a separate compatibility step
for pre-R2013 DXF. This is evidence about those named LibreDWG routes only; it
does not justify copying a heuristic into libdxfrw or treating successful byte
extraction as valid B-rep semantics.

LibreDWG [issue #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411)
provides a reproducible, from-scratch AC1032 DXF input recipe: create a `REGION`
with a cube-derived SAB body, whose reported expected SAB size is 5,489 bytes,
then exercise the named LibreDWG 0.14.8593 DXF→DWG→DXF route. The issue reports
that the REGION shell survives but its SAB/ACDSDATA does not. This is a useful
generated adversarial carrier case for a future local DXF read/write slice; it
does not by itself produce an independent valid DWG fixture, prove current
LibreDWG master behavior, or validate topology in a modeler kernel. Do not
download the issue's confidential customer drawing.

Two other LibreDWG reports sharpen whole-file acceptance independently of
ACIS. [Issue #1355](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1355) reports
an AC1032 `dwg2dxf` run that returns success while the output lacks complete
sections and `EOF`, despite a nonzero entity inventory in a separate converter.
This is a peer-reported defect shape, not a libdxfrw reproduction. The local
plan already has strict EOF, transactional publication, and source-disposition
owners; retain them as independent predicates: valid process status, closed
sections/final marker, strict parse, and exactly accounted source objects.
File existence or a good entity count alone cannot stand in for any of these.

[Issue #1413](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1413) reports that
selecting the first DICTIONARY by lowest handle can place an extension-owned
dictionary before the Named Objects Dictionary, so readers resolve the wrong
root and layouts collapse. The issue reports an exact root-first reorder on 2
of 43 production drawings, preserving object/tag content, and all 141 shipped
DWG samples satisfying the new first-object rule. Treat those figures as the
reporter's evidence, not a locally reproduced corpus result. The structural
lesson matches Autodesk's [object-ownership contract](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-CC1D6F91-42BF-4946-8D4B-6FC6A39100C5.htm)
and ezdxf's [OBJECTS section contract](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfinternals/sections/objects_section.html),
and is distinct from general owner-topology: root identity must be established
before checking that each owner precedes its children.

### Plan refinements and ready execution order

1. **Keep the three object-level acceptance dimensions separate.** For every
   admitted `OBJECTS` graph route, first assert the actual NOD identity and
   first-record position; then assert parent-before-child physical order for
   ownership edges; separately verify dictionary key, handle, owner, and target
   identity. Do not infer root identity from handle order or dictionary entry
   order, and do not schedule non-owning pointer edges as if they were owners.
2. **Reuse the new generated route controls.** The PlotSettings and
   VisualStyle fast slices now assert NOD-first and owner-dictionary-before-
   child order in ASCII and Binary DXF. They close only those exact generated
   routes. Continue the next already dependency-ready PAR-20/7G.3 graph family;
   add a cross-family scheduler or extra CTest only if source audit identifies
   a supported route without an existing owner and a generated negative case
   can distinguish the behavior.
3. **For the PAR-07/S8 modeler carrier lane, use the scratch DXF recipe only
   for DXF carrier behavior.** Record source entity handle/type, exact ordered
   group-1/3 or group-310 bytes and total length, root/key/owner join, emitted
   entity identity, and strict readback disposition. For a DWG AcDs test, use a
   separately qualified producer; do not treat LibreDWG 0.14.8593's reported
   missing AcDs output as a usable positive fixture. Keep schema/index/search
   association separate from concatenated payload equality and B-rep semantics.
4. **At conversion boundaries, score completion before semantic comparison.**
   Require a successful process result, all section terminators and final
   `EOF`, strict reparse, source-object disposition accounting, and no
   publication of partial output after a fatal conversion error. Reuse the
   existing fast EOF/atomic-output controls; do not add a duplicate
   peer-sized fixture or invoke a full suite for every implementation slice.
5. **Preserve the cheap-to-expensive queue.** Generated selector and the
   owning fast CTest are the per-slice gate; exact-pinned independent parser or
   producer checks run only at the existing composed checkpoint; native app or
   kernel qualification remains a named external gate. Record the artifact,
   version, direction, options, warnings, and disposition for any later peer
   run. A pass at one layer never promotes the next layer's claim.

This is a refinement of existing PAR-07/S8, strict-conversion/finalization, and
PAR-20/7G.3 owners; it adds no finding, top-level subplan, dependency, fixture,
or local defect. Current generated PlotSettings and VisualStyle selectors plus
their focused CTests passed as recorded immediately above. The research did
not run LibreDWG, download any external drawing, or execute a native CAD
application/kernel. Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268,
J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`, and no support claim is
promoted.

<a id="deeper-broader-capability-axes-recovery-and-consumer-semantics-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader capability axes, recovery, and consumer semantics (2026-10-20; research only)

This source pass compares implementation boundaries rather than ranking
projects by a single “DWG/DXF support” label. It sharpens existing plan rows;
the evidence does not establish a new libdxfrw defect.

| Primary source | Fresh observation | Plan consequence and limit |
|---|---|---|
| [LibreDWG README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) and [NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | The README's broad reader headline is qualified nearby: advanced R2010+ objects may be skipped; DWG write support is described as working only through R2004, with R2010–R2018 CRC issues; its converter coverage estimates and DXF→DWG version scope are distinct from its read-version claim. NEWS separately labels some classes stable/unstable and notes incomplete AcDsPrototype_1b / heuristic SAB extraction. | PAR-07 and the format-status matrix must keep *format version*, *read/write direction*, *route*, *object family*, and *semantic depth* separate. Peer-wide coverage percentages or “all versions” headlines cannot promote a libdxfrw cell. A skipped/unstable object is not equivalent to decoded, preserved, or semantically interpreted. This is project-authored capability documentation, not a normative DWG specification. |
| [ezdxf recover/audit documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/recover.html) | ezdxf documents a fast normal read and a slower explicit recovery path; recovery returns audit diagnostics, can tolerate decoding failures, and warns that writing recovered material can create invalid DXF or lose information. It exposes a strict decoding option. | Keep normal conversion success, recoverable parse, audit warnings, strict rejection, and output writeback as different outcomes. Recovery must never silently convert an input into a clean-success or preservation claim. Reuse existing strict/transactional controls; add recovery behavior only for an identified local requirement. |
| ezdxf [xref support boundary](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst) and [document loading/owner model](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/develop/pkg-design.rst) | The xref operation supports a bounded copy/transform subset, ignores unsupported entities, and preserves unknown entities as raw `DXFTagStorage`; the broader loader binds entities and then builds sections/layouts and links owners, with a single parent/layout ownership model. | Treat operation scope and whole-file fidelity separately. For PAR-20/7G.3, preserve the logical ownership graph and root identity; use physical owner order as a serialization acceptance check where required, not as a substitute for correct key/handle/owner links or semantic interpretation. ezdxf's xref scope is not its whole-document support claim. |
| [FreeCAD Draft DXF documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md), [DWG import documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md), and [issue #18454](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/18454) | FreeCAD routes DWG through an external converter to DXF, then applies its own importer limits. Its built-in C++ DXF importer is faster but handles fewer features than the optional legacy Python importer. The docs say 3D solids in DXF carry ACIS/SAT blobs that FreeCAD cannot currently read; issue #18454 distinguishes explicit line/arc geometry from opaque ACIS solids. | A DWG-converter pass and a FreeCAD import pass are separate receipts. FreeCAD's standard importer is a useful 2D consumer-compatibility check but cannot serve as the ACIS/SAB semantic oracle. Record which DXF importer and preferences were actually used; do not interpret downstream omission as proof that the source carrier was absent. |
| [InventorLoader README](https://github.com/jmplonka/InventorLoader/blob/master/README.md), its [DXF ACIS extraction route](https://github.com/jmplonka/InventorLoader/blob/master/importerDXF.py), and [open issues](https://github.com/jmplonka/InventorLoader/issues) | This optional FreeCAD add-on extracts SAT/SAB from DXF and offers native or STEP-based modeling. Its README lists omitted blending/helix/law-defined geometry; the issue board currently includes SAB parse, SAT shell, and plain-SAT completeness reports. The source route uses ezdxf to extract payloads before its ACIS reader. | This is a candidate exploratory consumer/parser, not a qualified independent oracle: pin the code and inputs, separate raw carrier extraction from geometry conversion, declare unsupported-record policy, and require independently authored body metrics. Because the modeler integration is FreeCAD/OCCT-based and the add-on has active parser limitations, it cannot alone satisfy independent-kernel or J-item evidence. |
| [LibreCAD_3 DWG support policy](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/blob/master/docs/dwg-support.md) | The sibling consumer explicitly enables experimental DWG reading behind an opt-in, keeps DWG writing disabled, and qualifies direction-specific claims with blockers and native gates. | Maintain directional consumer compatibility: an adapter that reads must not imply write safety or symmetric support. Use the sibling policy as a compatibility/evidence design reference only; it does not promote or transfer claims to this repository's current branch. |

### Refined implementation-ready sequence

1. **Finish cheap structural coverage already in flight.** Continue the
   generated PAR-20/7G.3 owner/root route queue. Each local slice asserts NOD
   identity, graph reciprocity, parent-before-child where required, and strict
   ASCII/Binary readback in its existing focused selector. Avoid a generic
   scheduler or new framework until source audit finds a concrete supported
   route that current route-level controls cannot represent.
2. **Normalize evidence dimensions before expanding claims.** For each
   implemented route, record version, direction, entry point, family, and
   semantic layer (container parse, typed decode, opaque retention, converted
   output, independent interpretation, consumer import). Use explicit
   outcomes: supported, partial, preserved-opaque, omitted-with-diagnostic,
   refused, malformed, or not-run. Do not collapse these into one support bit.
3. **Keep strict and best-effort behaviors disjoint.** The default import or
   conversion result remains strict and fail-closed for malformed structure;
   if a recovery mode exists or is later requested, it must be opt-in, return
   diagnostics, preserve the original on fatal errors, and never satisfy a
   strict-support gate by itself. Prefer existing fast parse/negative controls
   over adding a slow recovery dependency.
4. **Qualify a consumer pipeline stage by stage.** For FreeCAD, report
   converter resolution/version/exit and output closure separately from
   FreeCAD importer identity, import warnings, and resulting entity/body
   inventory. Use the standard importer for relevant 2D cases; keep ACIS
   semantic validation on a separate capable parser/kernel route. Do not add
   GUI/native runs to per-slice validation.
5. **Use optional peers as scoped differential tools.** LibreDWG can generate
   or compare named direction/version cases, but its own README records
   directional and version caveats. ezdxf is useful for DXF structural
   parsing/auditing and raw unknown-tag behavior; InventorLoader is a candidate
   ACIS route with explicit limitations. Pin exact revisions, use scratch
   inputs, record warnings and unsupported records, and treat missing tools or
   incompatible profiles as `NOT_RUN` while continuing local work.
6. **Keep validation cheap and progressive.** Run the changed target, one
   selector, and its owning fast CTest after each slice; run a composed local
   graph/semantic checkpoint only when its dependencies are present. Reserve
   full suites and external/native application checks for milestone gates,
   not each fix. No persistent peer/test drawings are needed for these
   crosswalks.

This is a research refinement of existing PAR-07/S8, PAR-20/7G.3,
format-status, strict-finalization, and consumer-qualification owners. It adds
no finding, top-level subplan, production behavior, peer dependency, fixture,
or support claim. The research updated interpretation/readiness, not the
current implementation order: finish the dependency-ready generated owner
routes, then re-audit the remaining local route inventory before widening the
external checkpoint. Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268,
J284, J293, and J295 remain explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and
non-promoting. No peer executable, external drawing, native CAD application,
or geometry kernel was run.

### Implementation-ready, low-cost execution route

1. Finish local generated tests for DWG entity → DataStorage section/index/key
   → exact carrier → DXF entity/owner. Those are libdxfrw responsibilities and
   are not covered by a bare-SAB peer.
2. At the existing composed semantic checkpoint only, first audit the pinned
   parser source, dependencies, and test/expected-value provenance for
   independence from libdxfrw and from the producing route. Then select an
   already available v0.6.1 release binary for the host, verify its published
   checksum, record `--version`/build identity, and first confirm that its

   implemented comparator observation, not an independence vote.

   recorded) to `cadmpeg`; require every body reference to resolve, no

   geometry-transfer diagnostic. Compare independently authored body count,

4. Optionally compare that same carrier with the already pinned `cq-acis`
   route if its supported profile accepts it. Report parser and modeler
   results separately: `cadmpeg` has no documented OCCT dependency; `cq-acis`
   shape construction shares the OCCT family with FreeCAD. Disagreement is a
   diagnostic for narrowing the profile, not a majority vote.
5. Keep the candidate external and conditional. Do not install it for every
   local slice, add its toolchain/package to CMake or CTest, copy its corpus,
   or let a successful bare-SAB parse promote DWG/DXF or ACIS/ACDS support.

That is consistent with a container/association limitation, not an ACIS parser verdict. | Keep the end-to-end evidence chain split into DWG section read → DataStorage index/key → entity ownership → exact payload bytes → DXF carrier → external parser/kernel. No stage's success substitutes for the next. |

### Implementation-ready differential protocol

1. **Pin the comparator before interpreting it.** Capture repository commit or
   released package, executable hash, OS/architecture, command/options, source
   hash, AC code, and route direction. A current issue is not evidence about a
   past release unless the commit relation is established.
2. **Use source-identity ledgers, not raw type totals.** For generated or
   lawfully available controls, compare `(handle, exact type, owner/block,
   layout, subtype, salient values)` across input parse, typed model/callback,
   output serialization, and independent reopen. Explicitly separate
   inheritance families such as INSERT/TABLE and composite ATTRIB/SEQEND data.
3. **Score losses by stage and semantic depth.** Record `decoded`,
   `preserved-opaque`, `converted`, `omitted-with-diagnostic`, `refused`,
   `malformed`, or `not-run`; attach diagnostic severity/count and source
   identities. A successful exit or same-codec reread alone is not a pass.
4. **Use reports to choose bounded probes, not port prescriptions.** Require a
   public scratch control or locally generated minimal object, a normative
   spec check, and a local gap before creating a fix/test lane. If peer
   evidence lacks an input or exact version, retain it as a risk note and move
   to the next independent local item.
5. **Keep the cadence cheap.** Each change runs its owning fast target and
   focused selector; run the pinned external reopen only at the composed
   milestone and the full suite less frequently. Do not add peer dependencies
   to CMake/CTest or commit external fixtures. If a peer is unavailable, record
   `NOT_RUN` and self-unblock by continuing local work.

This crosswalk adds no numbered defect, top-level subplan, local test, fixture,
dependency, or support claim; it refines existing PAR-07/S8, version/direction
matrices, PlotSettings, and output-finalization gates. Findings/subplans remain
**141 / 78**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

This pass checked the active PAR-20/7G.3 OBJECTS-order queue against the
normative DXF object/handle references and two independently structured open
source DXF implementations. It narrows the meaning of the current generated
order assertions: owner/key relationships are semantic graph invariants;
physical record position is a separate serializer or consumer-compatibility
property unless a version-specific requirement proves otherwise.

| Primary source | Evidence and ceiling | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk [Object Group Codes in DXF Files](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-1038FDE4-745D-469D-972E-1F977D674882.htm), [Common Group Codes for Objects](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-6939D69E-04CB-4F4C-87B2-67BC540FCF58.htm), and [group-code reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3F0380A5-1C15-464D-BC66-2C5F094BCFB9.htm) | The Object Group Codes page gives a minimal OBJECTS example whose first record is the named-object root DICTIONARY, then describes its named entries and subsequent objects. Common object codes describe 330 as an optional owner-dictionary pointer and later 330 as the owner-object pointer; group-code ranges distinguish soft/hard pointers and owners. These references establish identity and relationship encodings and the example's root-first layout, but they do not state a universal ordering constraint for every owner/child pair in the OBJECTS section. | Keep an explicit root-dictionary identity/root-first assertion because the reference example and local writer contract make that boundary meaningful. Do not label generic parent-before-child record order a DXF format rule, and do not use it alone to promote an object's support status. For each object, independently validate handle uniqueness, dictionary key → exact child handle, owner pointer → expected parent, and any specified reciprocal pointer/reactor. |
| ezdxf [document loading and owner model](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/develop/pkg-design.rst), [entity base/export contract](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dxfentity.py), and [xref graph reconstruction](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/xref.py) | The maintained implementation describes linking objects to one parent owner, identifies the root dictionary as the OBJECTS object with owner `0`, treats other missing/destroyed owners as orphans, and reconstructs owner paths when importing dependent resources. Its exporter explicitly preserves tag ordering inside an object; those sources describe object graph validity and per-record tag order, not a global parent-before-child ordering rule across OBJECTS records. ezdxf is an implementation comparison, not the normative DXF specification. | Make typed graph closure/readback the reusable PAR-20/7G.3 acceptance layer. Treat cross-record physical ordering as a second, narrower assertion and add it only where the local serializer promises it or a pinned consumer/regression demonstrates it is required. Keep unknown/opaque object preservation distinct from typed graph closure. |
| Autodesk [GROUP object reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-5F1372C4-37C8-4056-9303-EE1715F58E67.htm) and [MATERIAL object reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-E540C5BB-E166-44FA-B36C-5C739878B272.htm) | The per-object references specify required owner-dictionary identities (e.g. GROUP under `ACAD_GROUP`, MATERIAL under `ACAD_MATERIAL`) and distinguish that pointer from other owner/object references. This is stronger and more directly testable than inferring ownership from record position. | For root routes, validate exact key name and owner identity rather than merely “some DICTIONARY before child.” For extension-dictionary routes, validate the source entity's extension-dictionary reference and the dictionary's owned child references; retain physical order only as an observed serialization property unless a consumer-specific contract applies. |
| LibreDWG [current DXF/DWG manual](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/LibreDWG.pdf) and [writer CLI route](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/programs/dwg2dxf.c) | LibreDWG exposes DWG→ASCII/Binary DXF as explicit writer routes, while its own manual classifies class stability and unhandled/unstable behavior separately. A successful writer route therefore says nothing by itself about typed closure or semantic support for every emitted object. This pass did not run LibreDWG or inspect a pinned executable. | At the composed peer milestone, compare object identities and owner/key edges across parsed model, output, and independent reopen; record unsupported/opaque/omitted diagnostics. Do not add a LibreDWG command to every fast slice and do not convert writer exit status into a local support claim. |

### Refined implementation route

1. Keep existing passing physical-order checks as **local deterministic
   serialization regressions**; this research does not justify deleting them.
   Remove or narrow only an assertion shown to encode an unsupported
   format-wide assumption or that causes avoidable runtime without guarding a
   stated contract.
2. For each remaining PAR-20/7G.3 root/owner family, first run the owning
   generated ASCII/Binary round-trip and assert: unique emitted handles; the
   actual root DICTIONARY; exact dictionary key → child handle; exact child
   owner → parent; reciprocal references only where defined; and strict
   readback without orphan/missing-owner diagnostics. Root-first may be
   asserted separately. This is the minimum useful slice and should replace
   any order-only coverage gap.
3. Add a physical-order assertion only when (a) it is a documented local
   writer invariant, such as the root-first OBJECTS shape, or (b) a pinned
   consumer/version regression demonstrates reliance on the ordering. Label
   the assertion with that specific contract; do not describe it as generic
   DXF conformance.
4. Preserve the speed policy: reuse each route's already-running fixture or
   adapter selector; prefer a single object scan plus indexed lookups to
   repeated full scans; no new fixtures, peer dependencies, per-slice native
   consumers, or broad-suite runs. Run only the changed target, selector, and
   owning fast CTest for each slice.
5. At the composed interoperability checkpoint, use a pinned peer to reopen
   one locally generated dependency-complete graph. Report root identity,
   dictionary key resolution, owner closure, diagnostics, and whether the
   consumer repaired/dropped records separately. A difference is a scoped
   compatibility lead, not proof of a normative order requirement.

<a id="deeper-broader-libredwg-security-advisory-crosswalk-and-generated-negative-controls-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader LibreDWG security-advisory crosswalk and generated negative controls (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass broadens the peer comparison from semantic loss and feature claims to
versioned parser-safety failures. LibreDWG's [0.14.1 release notes](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS)
record a second R2004 section-decompression heap overflow after an earlier
fix, an out-of-range R2004 header page-map read, a pre-R2004 DXF VIEWPORT
use-after-free across object-array reallocation, and a pre-R13 loop/allocation
fix that was incomplete in 0.14. The same release notes list other boundedness,
NULL-check, signed-count, and stale-pointer fixes. These are source-pinned
peer failures and adversarial test-design inputs; they do not establish a
libdxfrw defect or imply that C-level object-array failures share a C++ cause.
The issue and advisory histories for [R2004 decompression](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1180),
[R13–R2000 class-count complexity](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gp83-hcvh-g255),
and [the pre-R13 loop/resource fix](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS)
provide bounded reproducer context. No peer PoC drawing was downloaded or
added to the repository.

| Peer failure shape | Evidence ceiling | Local source/test crosswalk and plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| R2004 compressed-section output buffer was shrunk to a per-section size while its logical cursor/section size still described a larger stream; 0.14.1 records the follow-up overflow fix ([NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS), [issue #1180](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1180)). | A LibreDWG decoder regression, not proof that libdxfrw has the same allocator/cursor lifetime. | `dwgCompressor::decompress18` receives an explicit output-window size and writes through its bounded decoder path; `dwgReader18::parseDataPage` builds page-local decoded storage and bounds page ranges. Reuse the existing decompressor and DWG reader-matrix tests first. If coverage misses the *reader-level* capacity-versus-logical-size invariant, generate a local valid seed, mutate one section/page size relationship, and assert bounded failure and the documented callback/publication behavior. Do not add the published external DWG as a fixture. |
| An R2004 header page-map offset caused an OOB read; the release notes identify the missing range validation. | A concrete peer parser safety fix; no normative offset rule inferred from the advisory. | `dwgReader18` resolves the section-map address with checked addition and validates the mapped file range; `dwgReader21` checks page-map base-plus-offset and map sizes before parsing. The generated AC1018 `testR2004SectionMapPublication` control now sets the R2004 offset to `UINT64_MAX - 0xFF`, reseals the header CRC, and verifies FileHeader/PageRange refusal, no descriptor/callback publication, and corrected-input retry through both the probe and public facade. This closes that exact offset-overflow/publication control only; other page-map mutations still require route-specific coverage inventory. [Implementation entry](#implementation-progress-par14-r2004-file-header-page-map-offset-overflow-control-2026-10-20-generated-fast-slice-uncommitted). |
| LibreDWG's R13–R2000 `num_classes` value drove a `realloc` on every class iteration without a sanity check; the same peer release history separately records a pre-R13 entity-end loop/resource fix ([GHSA-gp83-hcvh-g255](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gp83-hcvh-g255), [pre-R13 GHSA-7625-26gc-xqvp](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/security/advisories/GHSA-7625-26gc-xqvp), [NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS)). | The class advisory is a peer-specific allocation strategy. Pre-R13 is outside the qualified-support denominator, but AC1.40 and experimental AC1006/AC1009 reader paths exist locally; the pre-R13 report is therefore an audit lead, not an out-of-scope path. | **`DIFFERENT_ARCHITECTURE` for the class-count trigger; `PARTIAL_ANALOG`, now regression-covered, for pre-R13 end/progress safety.** ODA DWG Specification 5.4.1 §10.1 defines R13–R15 CLASSES as an RL payload byte size followed by records until the data is exhausted—there is no `num_classes` header. Locally, `dwgReader15::readDwgClasses` copies only a section-size-bounded payload (`MaxBufferSize`), parses until that payload is consumed, and stages classes in an amortized vector plus an index. `DRW_Class::classNum` is `uint16_t`, parsed from BS; IDs below 500 and duplicates are rejected, so the representational ID domain permits at most 65,036 unique accepted IDs (500–65,535), not an on-wire count or a chosen policy limit. For AC1.40, `dwgReaderR1_40::readFileHeader` rejects `dwg_size` outside `[0x202,fileSize]`, and `readDwgEntities`/`readEntity` walk against that same validated `m_dwgSize`; there is no separately clamped end plus independent loop-size counter. For AC1006/AC1009, `dwgReaderR11::readFileHeader` validates section ranges, `readEntitySection` requires bounded forward progress, and `readEntityR11` confines each body to its declared 16-bit size. The existing `libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix` controls already include a locally authored 496-byte AC1.40 input with a declared end beyond physical input, an end below the entity start, a truncated header/body, exact-boundary records, no callback on header refusal, and same-reader corrected-input retries. Thus the advisory's end-boundary pattern has a matched local regression, although this does not prove total-memory bounds for arbitrarily large *valid* input or reproduce LibreDWG's allocation behavior. Keep aggregate-memory profiling conditional, do not copy peer limits/code, and keep AC1009 outside the support denominator. |
| VIEWPORT and MLINESTYLE readers/writers retained an object pointer across a container growth operation. | A peer-specific pointer invalidation pattern; no cross-project defect conclusion. | Before touching local object-graph staging, check whether any pointer/reference into a growable vector survives insertion, callback, or rehash. Prefer stable handles/indices or reacquire after mutation. This is a source-review checklist, not a mandate for duplicate tests when local code has no equivalent lifetime shape. |

### Implementation-ready refinement to existing PAR-14 / PAR-07/S8

1. **Coverage inventory first.** Map each peer failure class to an existing
   libdxfrw implementation path and fast selector. Mark it `DIRECT_ANALOG`,
   `PARTIAL_ANALOG`, `DIFFERENT_ARCHITECTURE`, or `OUT_OF_SCOPE`; do not infer
   safety from the peer's fix or from a test with a similar name.
2. **Close this class-count peer analog without a speculative limit.** The
   authoritative ODA R13–R15 layout has no count field, while local work is
   section-bounded and class IDs are a finite BS domain. Do not add a peer-
   shaped `num_classes` mutation or arbitrary maximum. If the implementation
   later needs a deterministic duplicate check, `stagedMap` is used only for
   duplicate detection; a 65,536-bit seen set is a semantics-preserving,
   allocation-free alternative, but treat it as optional performance
   hardening until a generated scaling probe shows a meaningful win. Keep the
   existing `classesmap` check for collisions with already published IDs.
3. **Profile aggregate memory only when policy or evidence calls for it.**
   Account for the bounded raw section copy, transient per-string buffers,
   decoded UTF-8 strings, class objects, coverage entries, and indexes. Do not
   infer a tight aggregate-memory ceiling from `MaxBufferSize`; if that shared
   ceiling changes or measurements show pressure, add a separately justified
   budget and small arithmetic-boundary tests before any allocation-heavy
   stress case.
4. **Add one generated mutation only for an uncovered invariant.** Start from
   locally generated serializer bytes or an in-memory scratch builder, mutate
   one count/offset/size/progress field at a time, and check bounded refusal,
   no sanitizer-visible memory error, and existing transaction/publication
   semantics. No external DWG/DXF fixture or PoC is needed or admitted.
5. **Consult the authoritative ODA DWG specification before changing a DWG
   parse body.** Confirm the version-specific field width, address space,
   count meaning, and record boundary there; advisories identify failure
   patterns, not wire-format semantics.
6. **Keep validation proportional.** Build the owning target and run its fast
   selector plus focused CTest for a changed path. Run ASan/UBSan or the
   existing fuzz harness at a composed parser-safety checkpoint, not for every
   unrelated slice; retain the plan's infrequent full-suite cadence.
7. **Self-unblock.** If an advisory has no direct local analog, its PoC is
   unavailable, or the relevant format version is unsupported, record the
   classification and continue the next dependency-ready local item. External
   tool/platform availability does not block implementation.

The class-count architecture classification above supersedes the earlier
crosswalk wording that called the local R13–R2000 reader an “explicit count
ceiling.” Its actual limits are the bounded section payload plus the finite
class-ID domain; these are not an explicit record-count field or a separately
tuned policy cap. A focused source proof is sufficient for the peer-specific
realloc trigger, while aggregate-memory measurement remains conditional and
separate.

malformed DataStorage handling, and scheduled parser-safety checkpoint. It

<a id="implementation-progress-par14-32-bit-dwg-decompressor-size-admission-2026-10-20-generated-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>

## Implementation progress — PAR-14 32-bit DWG decompressor-size admission (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The bounded parser-safety source audit found a concrete width mismatch in
`dwgCompressor`: `decompress18` and `decompress21` accept `uint64_t` compressed
and decompressed sizes, but their input/output cursor and size members are
`uint32_t`. The previous implicit assignments silently reduced values modulo
2^32. Locally generated valid AC1018 and AC1021 streams demonstrated that both
algorithms could accept a declared `2^32 + N` input or output size after it
wrapped to the small valid test buffer.

Both decoders now reject either size above `UINT32_MAX` before retaining
caller pointers or decoding, clear their prior decode state on that refusal,
and use explicit casts only after representability is established. Generated
tests cover oversized input and output sizes for both algorithms and verify
that output sentinels remain unchanged, decoded-byte state is cleared, and the
same instance accepts a subsequent valid retry. The normal bounded AC1021
literal/back-reference control and AC1018 extended-copy control remain
positive cases.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_wave1_tests --parallel 2  PASS
build-gcc/libdxfrw_wave1_tests --dwg-decompressor-size-bounds  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_decompressor_size_bounds$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1)
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1; 1.49 sec)
cmake --build build-gcc --target lc3_compat_check --parallel 2  PASS
git diff --check -- src/intern/dwgutil.cpp tests/wave1_tests.cpp CMakeLists.txt DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md DWG_DXF_3D_SUPPORT_PLAN.md  PASS
```

Before the production fix, the broad `libdxfrw_wave1_tests` run failed on all
four new size-boundary assertions and 60 unrelated object/metadata assertions
in the current worktree. After the fix, the focused decompressor selector,
owning CTest, DWG reader-matrix CTest, and `lc3_compat_check` were rerun; no
full suite is claimed. One focused fast CTest was registered so this safety
invariant has an isolated owner. No persistent DWG/DXF fixture, external PoC,
dependency, peer executable, native app, or support claim was added.
Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The shared tree remains uncommitted and broadly
dirty.

<a id="implementation-progress-par14-r2004-decompressor-extended-length-overflow-2026-10-20-generated-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>

## Implementation progress — PAR-14 R2004 decompressor extended-length overflow (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The existing R2004 decompressor accepted extended copy/literal lengths into
32-bit counters. Source arithmetic shows that an extended long-copy token can
exceed `UINT32_MAX` after its fixed opcode bias is added, while a long literal
length can independently exceed that limit; either value can wrap before
window clipping. With 16,843,008 zero continuations, the old long-copy
calculation wraps to 31 bytes and the old literal calculation wraps to 16.
Generated AC1018 controls exercise both shapes against a 64-byte output
window.

The R2004 extended-length helpers and copy/literal counters now use 64-bit
unsigned values. The output checks compare each length with the remaining
window (`size - cursor`) before clipping, so no cursor-plus-length addition can
wrap. The long-copy control now fills all 64 bytes, retaining the exact
18-byte literal prefix and repeating its final `C` byte; the long-literal
control preserves its expected 64-byte sequence. The existing oversize-size
refusal/retry controls and normal AC1018 extended-copy / AC1021
literal-back-reference positives remain in the same focused selector.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_wave1_tests --parallel 2  PASS
build-gcc/libdxfrw_wave1_tests --dwg-decompressor-size-bounds  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_decompressor_size_bounds$|^libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix$' --output-on-failure  PASS (2/2; 1.82 sec)
cmake --build build-gcc --target lc3_compat_check --parallel 2  PASS
git diff --check -- src/intern/dwgutil.cpp src/intern/dwgutil.h tests/wave1_tests.cpp CMakeLists.txt  PASS
```

The two 16 MiB controls are generated in memory and are not committed as
DWG/DXF fixtures. They prove the local decompressor's length arithmetic and
window clipping only; they are not producer-derived DWG witnesses, a full
security audit, or semantic-support claims. No full suite, peer executable,
native CAD app, external PoC, dependency, or persistent fixture was used.
Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The shared worktree remains
broadly dirty and uncommitted.

## Implementation progress — PAR-14 R2004 file-header page-map offset overflow control (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The LibreDWG security-advisory crosswalk identified unchecked R2004 page-map
offsets as a useful adversarial shape. Local source already used checked
addition for `sectionPageMapOffset + 0x100`, but the existing generated
`testR2004SectionMapPublication` covered duplicate map names rather than this
overflow boundary.

The existing in-memory AC1018 DWG writer witness now has a generated mutation
that sets the section-page-map offset to `UINT64_MAX - 0xFF`, reseals the
file-header CRC, and leaves all other bytes untouched. `dwgReader18` rejects
the `+0x100` operation in the FileHeader phase with `PageRange` before
publishing section descriptors. The test verifies no CRC warning, no known or
unknown descriptor publication, no callbacks from the public `readBuffer`
facade, and successful retries with corrected bytes on the same low-level
reader and facade. This closes a focused coverage gap around the existing
checked-add guard; it does not add a production defect or change parser policy.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests --parallel 2  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1; 1.74 sec)
git diff --check -- tests/dwg_reader_matrix_tests.cpp DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md DWG_DXF_3D_SUPPORT_PLAN.md  PASS
```

The source drawing is generated in memory and no DWG/DXF fixture or external
PoC was added. No full suite, peer executable, native CAD app, dependency, or
support claim was added. Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78**; J256, J260,
J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The
shared worktree remains broadly dirty and uncommitted.

1. Before adding any peer result, label its role as `DWG_CODEC`,

### Implementation-ready safety and acceptance procedure

1. Label every local generated input before dispatch: `POSITIVE_INTEROP`,
   `MALFORMED_NEGATIVE`, or `EXTERNAL_PROVENANCE`. Keep malformed controls out
   of native CAD runs unless there is an explicitly authorized isolated
   security exercise and the selected product is confirmed mitigated.
2. For native acceptance, capture product/build/update, OS, architecture,
   options, input hash, and the result (`OPEN`, `AUDIT`, repair/discard counts,
   and semantic inventory where available). Missing or affected-version
   metadata makes the native result `NOT_RUN`/`NOT_QUALIFIED`, not a pass.
3. Keep parser robustness evidence at the local owning fast selector and
   focused CTest; use sanitizer/fuzz checks at the existing parser-safety
   checkpoint. Do not schedule a full suite or peer runtime for unrelated
   implementation slices.
4. When an advisory has no public reproducer or root cause—as here—record the
   boundary and proceed. Do not manufacture a wire-format mutation from the
   CVE title, change a reader based on a downstream application's crash, or
   block independent local work on an external native build.

adds an independently implemented, automatable semantic witness—not whether
its overview page lists DWG, DXF, or ACIS among many formats. The screen changes

This is a possible manual inspection route, not an open-source parser API or a current automated oracle. | Do not add CAD Assistant or commercial OCCT components as a dependency or required gate. If an already-installed, license-authorized build is used later, record exact build/platform and treat visible shape/property checks as supplemental manual evidence only; lack of a machine-readable per-body report is not a pass. |

Use the issue's scratch-generation recipe only as a local control design; do not treat its body, peer report, entity count, or a successful conversion exit as geometry semantics. Continue to require source/dependency lineage review before counting an independent vote. |

## Deeper/broader cross-peer failure taxonomy and implementation-readiness reconciliation (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass refreshed a set of recent open-source issue reports against their
primary issue text, normative references already used by the plan, and the
current local source/test owners. The useful result is a sharper separation
of failure stages—not a new claim that libdxfrw has the same defects. Issue
reports and downstream application errors remain leads until reduced to a
local, specification-backed control.

| Failure stage and source | What the evidence supports—and limits | Existing plan owner and consequence |
|---|---|---|
| DWG modeler carrier: LibreDWG [#1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411) | The issue remains open in the reviewed snapshot. Its generated ezdxf recipe creates an R2018 DXF REGION with a reported 5,489-byte SAB payload, then reports that the LibreDWG DXF→DWG→DXF route returns the entity with an empty body and no AcDs records. This is a useful reproducible *carrier-loss shape*, but the round trip uses the same peer codec in both directions; ezdxf's ACIS authoring is not an independent B-rep oracle. Its confidential AutoCAD drawing was not obtained. | Keep PAR-07/S8's exact join ledger: source entity/modeler flag → AcDs section/schema/key/owner → payload span/hash → DXF carrier and explicit disposition. A surviving REGION count or same-codec readback cannot qualify ACDS/ACIS semantics. The recipe may guide a locally generated, scratch-only carrier control; do not download or commit the issue's drawing or elevate its generated mesh body to analytic topology evidence. |
| DWG value decoding: LibreDWG [#1415](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1415) | The open report distinguishes CMC method `0xC3` (ACI encoded in the method word) from `0xC2` (RGB), and reports palette collisions plus a bad group-62 fallback when RGB's blue byte is zero. Its initial suggested guard was later corrected by the author after recognizing that the R2004+ BS index is reserved/vestigial for this route. This is peer analysis, not a new ODA rule. | Reuse PAR-66/7AN's ODA-shaped generated C2/C3 controls, exact group 62/420 output, off-state, and readback. Do not copy the superseded BS-index fix, infer ACI from RGB palette lookup, or duplicate the existing CMC suite. |
| DXF object graph: LibreDWG [#1413](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1413), Autodesk [OBJECTS section](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-49C9C960-0944-4C1B-8DF9-E2428C28A2FB.htm), and ezdxf [OBJECTS internals](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfinternals/sections/objects_section.html) | The peer issue gives a concrete root-selection failure: an extension DICTIONARY at handle `3`, owner `2`, precedes the NOD at handle `B`, owner `0`; ezdxf then identifies the first object as the root. Autodesk's example and ezdxf docs support the positional NOD-first convention. The reviewed references do not unambiguously establish a universal parent-before-child order for every OBJECTS record; later plan review therefore keeps that as a local writer/consumer assertion unless a specific profile requires it. Neither ordering rule permits discovering DWG NOD identity from minimum handle or source-array position. | PAR-20/7G.3 already distinguishes actual NOD identity from physical DXF OBJECTS order and has generated NOD-first, graph-owner, and unique-handle checks. Keep NOD-first distinct from the per-route owner-before-child regression assertions; do not present the latter as a format-wide rule, sort dictionaries by handle, or infer a DWG root from record order. No new test or finding. |
| DXF string integrity: LibreDWG [#1412](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1412) | The open peer report describes a capacity-terminated C buffer followed by `strlen`, allowing allocator fill bytes into output. Its `MALLOC_PERTURB_` demonstration is specific to that C string path. Local `dxfWriter` uses length-aware `std::string` writes and the existing ASCII/Binary framing controls already check exact boundaries, sentinels, rollback, and destination preservation. | Keep PAR-05/PAR-14's current exact-length and transactional checks. Do not add allocator perturbation or claim a matching local bug without a new capacity-based C-string path. |
| Source-text form × target-DXF encoding: LibreDWG [#1414](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1414) | The issue remains framed as an unresolved question: equivalent `TV` and `TU` inputs can treat literal `\U+XXXX` differently when targeting R2007+ DXF, and lone-surrogate text raises a UTF-8 validity concern. Its own corpus comparison is reporter evidence, not a normative escape policy. Local generated tests already expose TV/TU source routes, target bytes, decoded values, and following-record sentinels; they label the cross-route result observational rather than a policy ruling. | Preserve PAR-05/7AR's storage-path × output-version × field-kind matrix. Do not globally expand `\U+` substrings or change behavior from the issue alone; resolve literal-vs-inline escape semantics per field against the relevant Autodesk/ODA contract. Reuse the existing generated selectors. |
| Strict DXF consumer and writer profiles: ACadSharp [#1253](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1253), [#1299](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1299), and Autodesk DXF tables | #1253 reports AutoCAD rejection of ACadSharp 3.6.35 output and separates CLASSES fields, HATCH group 47, and a DIMSTYLE table-subclass sequence. A later comment narrows one reported HATCH case: TrueView required group 47 on derived boundaries (path flag 92=7), so the original simple “omit when zero” proposal is not a general rule. Raw producer files were not independently inspected here. #1299 is an open report against ACadSharp 3.8.0 whose DWG/DXF attachments and Claude explanation were not downloaded or treated as diagnosis; a GDAL rejection is downstream evidence, not by itself proof of invalid spline data. | Keep PAR-05/7BQ.5 as profile-specific strict-consumer candidates and preserve the unresolved HATCH presence predicate; do not change the current writer from an issue comment alone. At the composed checkpoint pin the exact writer/consumer versions, compare complete ordered DXF records, and separately report strict parse, native open, and geometry/count outcomes. Keep spline changes tied to ODA plus a local generated or repository-owned trace. |
| Peer release/lineage boundary | The cited issue pages were open at review time. No peer executable, fix branch, or linked customer drawing was run or downloaded in this pass. FreeCAD's stock DWG path remains converter→DXF→selected importer; it is not an ACIS semantic oracle. | Treat issue state, peer master code, released packages, importer behavior, and independent geometry interpretation as separate evidence fields. No new peer lineage or support result is admitted. |

2. Reuse existing focused owners for NOD ordering, CMC method/value fidelity,

requires the identified NOD's `parentHandle` to be zero and exactly one typed
EVALUATION_GRAPH record, while retaining the existing NOD-first, unique
OBJECTS-handle, exact graph-owner, single expression-target, and over-budget

The test-first dangling-owner control showed strict export accepting an
EVALUATION_GRAPH whose group-330 owner was changed to a missing handle. Added
owner validation in `dx_iface::prepareExtensionObjectGraph`: ordinary graph
owners must be an accepted empty/default root (0/C/D), the NOD, a registered
BLOCK_RECORD, or an owner already traversed through a supported object route;
refusal preserves the existing destination. The ACDS history graph remains on
its separate typed BOX closure path. Autodesk documents group 330 as an optional owner-dictionary pointer
and owner-object pointer, and ObjectARX documents EvalGraph as either a global
object or attached to another object ([common object codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-6939D69E-04CB-4F4C-87B2-67BC540FCF58.htm), [ObjectARX graph ownership](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2022/ENU/OARX-DevGuide/files/GUID-B520F4A9-20D0-420D-B4A3-FBEC835D0E42.htm)).

NOD. The generated output contains no such entry, and this slice found no
authoritative requirement that one must exist. That speculative assertion was
not retained; key semantics remain an explicit source-backed follow-up rather
than being inferred from this local route.

peer vulnerability into a libdxfrw finding.

| VulnCheck-assigned [CVE-2026-111167](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-111167) and [technical advisory](https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/gnu-libredwg-through-0.14.8612-out-of-bounds-read-in-acds-private-acds-decoder) | The CVE record, published 2026-10-15 by VulnCheck, reports that LibreDWG versions through 0.14.8612 can read beyond a static AcDs schema type-size table when `acds_private()` consumes an oversized `schdat` property type. ## Deeper/broader EvaluationGraph semantic contract versus local wire closure (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass separates dynamic-block graph semantics from the current typed
carrier/ownership work. It identifies a concrete implementation-readiness
boundary in PAR-20/7G.3, without treating an incomplete semantic audit as a
format defect or adding a new support claim.

| Source / route | Evidence and limits | Existing local owner and plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk ObjectARX [AcDbEvalGraph reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2027/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OARX-RefGuide-AcDbEvalGraph.html), [Graphs guide](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2022/ENU/OARX-DevGuide/files/GUID-B520F4A9-20D0-420D-B4A3-FBEC835D0E42.htm), and [Node Dependencies and Edges](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2022/ENU/OARX-DevGuide/files/GUID-74E0EB04-41BF-4E56-85A8-2318B25C9BBE.htm) | Autodesk describes the dynamic-block evaluation graph as directed, with unique node IDs; edges identify start and end nodes; the resulting active dependency subgraph is expected to be acyclic and is topologically sorted for evaluation. An edge is oriented E2→E1 when expression E1 depends on E2. This is the semantic/API contract, not the DXF serialization map for group codes 91–95/92–94, nor a claim that ObjectARX's graph API automatically detects or rejects cycles. | Keep graph semantics distinct from record-shape capture and handle closure. A valid semantic fixture must have unique IDs and closed edge endpoints and should include a small acyclic dependency chain with the direction independently asserted. Do not infer serialized sentinel values, node-list ordering, or exact edge endpoint fields solely from this API prose. |
| LibreDWG [OBJECTS manual / EVAL structures](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/OBJECTS.html) and [published EVAL_Node API fields](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/refman/struct__dwg__EVAL__Node.html) | The peer manual maps EVAL nodes to `id` (DXF 91), `edge_flags` (93), `nextid` (95), and `evalexpr` handle (360); its edge layout includes `id` (92), `nextid` (93), `e1` (94), and additional integer fields under group 91/92. These are useful structural field-name crosswalks from an implementation/manual, but do not define a normative sentinel for `nextid` or fully establish which repeated integers are endpoint IDs. LibreDWG 0.13.4 is also not a current artifact execution. | Add an explicit `FIELD_MAP_UNCONFIRMED` step before semantic validation: resolve the repeated 91/92/93/94/95 sequence against the ODA specification if present, otherwise a minimal independently authored/exported DXF/DWG trace and a second reader's decoded values. Do not hard-code endpoint or sentinel rules from peer naming alone. |
| Local [DRW_EvaluationGraph parser/finalizer](src/drw_objects.cpp), [DXF writer](src/libdxfrw.cpp), and [adapter capture vector](tests/dwg2dxf_adapter_tests.cpp) | At the time of this research entry, the adapter route used one node (`id=1`, `nextid=2`) with default-zero group-91 edge values. The later same-day wire-sequence update expanded it to two opaque node records and two opaque edge records; it verifies capture, owner/expression handle closure, repeated-group ordering, readback and atomic refusal, but still does not establish graph connectivity or dynamic-block behavior. | Mark the selector as `WIRE_CAPTURE_AND_HANDLE_CLOSURE`, not `SEMANTIC_GRAPH_VALIDATION`. Source review still confirms no semantic graph checks. The newer two-node/two-edge values are opaque transport sentinels, not an authored valid DAG; because semantic field meanings remain unresolved, register no new numbered defect yet and preserve fields unchanged. |

### Implementation-ready refinement for PAR-20/7G.3

1. **Lock the wire map first.** Record the exact group-code sequence for graph
   header counts, node ID/flags/next ID/expression handle/data, and edge ID,
   link, endpoint and metadata values. Confirm the meaning of `nextid` and its
   terminal value from an authoritative serialization source or an
   independently authored minimal trace. If that evidence is unavailable,
   leave internal integer references opaque and describe the route as field
   preservation only.
2. **Keep transport and semantic controls distinct.** The generated adapter
   selector already checks two node records and two edge records with opaque
   values, separate LINE expressions, exact group order, expression-handle
   closure, and strict ASCII/Binary readback. Do not relabel these arbitrary
   values as a valid DAG. After step 1 resolves the serialized fields, add a
   separate two-node/one-edge acyclic semantic control with known edge
   direction and independently authored expectations, still generated at
   runtime with no committed DWG/DXF.
3. **Add fail-closed negatives only after step 1 resolves the fields.** Exercise
   duplicate node ID, missing referenced node, malformed/cyclic `nextid` chain,
   and an invalid edge endpoint with the following-record sentinel retained.
   Test graph cycles separately from `nextid` list cycles; they are not
   interchangeable. Require destination-preserving refusal for strict export.
4. **Bound cost and validation.** Use existing `kMaxEntries`/retained-byte
   admission; build one temporary ID→node index rather than quadratic scans.
   Run the existing EvaluationGraph selector in ASCII and Binary, its owning
   CTest, and `lc3_compat_check` for a public-layout change. Do not run a full
   suite or native CAD dynamic-block test per leaf; keep Autodesk/LibreCAD
   dynamic-block behavior at the existing composed qualification gate.
5. **Claim boundary.** Parsing/writing the mapped fields is not equivalent to
   evaluating dynamic blocks. A local pass requires semantic node/edge
   assertions; native edit/visibility behavior remains external. This does not
   qualify any `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` J item.

## Deeper/broader CADMPEG F3D carrier route and evidence-independence boundary (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass separates three F3D routes that otherwise look like corroborating
votes. CADMPEG's F3D and bare-stream paths share one ASM decoder. The already-
tracked `ezf3d` project is a separately implemented MIT reader for Fusion's
contained ASM BinaryFile8 profile, so it is a potential independent parser
comparison for that exact input profile after execution. Neither path is a DWG
reader or evidence for a DWG-side AcDs join. A third viewer advertises F3D
support, but its own notices classify the reader as proprietary and its output
is tessellated display geometry.

| Source / route | Evidence and limits | Plan disposition |
|---|---|---|
| [CADMPEG v0.6.2 release](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/releases/tag/v0.6.2), exact [tag commit](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/tree/7bcc95276548de4e4876894b9a650a84ea9c4d6d), [F3D codec source](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/blob/7bcc95276548de4e4876894b9a650a84ea9c4d6d/crates/cadmpeg-codec-f3d/src/lib.rs), [F3D manifest](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/blob/7bcc95276548de4e4876894b9a650a84ea9c4d6d/crates/cadmpeg-codec-f3d/Cargo.toml), and [CLI feature manifest](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/blob/7bcc95276548de4e4876894b9a650a84ea9c4d6d/crates/cadmpeg/Cargo.toml) | The tag resolves to commit `7bcc95276548de4e4876894b9a650a84ea9c4d6d`. It packages both F3D and SAT features in the CLI default feature set. The F3D crate describes typed B-rep topology, analytic/cached NURBS geometry, transforms, design/history records and appearances, and directly depends on `cadmpeg-asm`. The same lower-level ASM decoder is used by the existing bare SAT/ASM candidate. | Admit F3D only as a distinct *container/profile coverage lead* for the same implementation lineage. It may help expose ASM carrier, body-selection, transform, unit, and feature-context cases; it is not another parser/kernel vote and is not independent validation of CADMPEG's ASM decoder. |
| Exact v0.6.2 [format-support profile](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/blob/7bcc95276548de4e4876894b9a650a84ea9c4d6d/docs/format-support.md) and [evaluation ledger](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/blob/7bcc95276548de4e4876894b9a650a84ea9c4d6d/docs/evaluations.toml) | The published profile marks `f3d:manifest-3-2-0-0` as L4 and states that F3D selects `.smb`/`.smbh` geometry through a Design body map. against the local harness. This is qualification-method research, not a new
libdxfrw defect report.

Its ODA command requests `ACAD2000` DXF, so the converter route can deliberately downgrade the intermediate file; `convertToDwg()` similarly waits for LibreDWG/ODA/QCAD but its helper returns the requested path without checking the resulting file. The module docstring still describes an ODA-only route, while the code supports several configured backends. The guide lists different C++ and legacy Python entity subsets, says the legacy route includes 3DFACE while C++ does not list it, and says stock FreeCAD cannot read ACIS/SAT solid blobs. Verify a new non-empty intermediate DXF, exact `$ACADVER` and intended downgrade policy, strict independent parse, converter status/diagnostics, and per-source-object disposition. <a id="deeperbroader-dxf-modeler-carrier-authority-boundary-and-peer-status-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader DXF modeler-carrier authority boundary and peer status (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass rechecked the ACIS/modeler route against the public Autodesk DXF
entity reference, ODA DWG specification v5.4.1, and current LibreDWG,
ACadSharp, and FreeCAD sources. It narrows one authority boundary in the
existing PAR-07/S8 writer plan; it does not add a new format rule, defect,
support claim, or external qualification gate.

| Source | What the primary source establishes | Plan treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk [3DSOLID DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm) | The published 3DSOLID entity table lists `AcDbModelerGeometry`, modeler format version 1, proprietary group-code 1 data split into lines shorter than 255 characters, optional group-code 3 continuation lines, then `AcDb3dSolid` and history soft-owner 350. This describes the documented inline entity route; it does not document a modern `ACDSDATA` section, data-record schema, or its association rule. | Keep group 1/3 inline SAT and modern DXF `ACDSDATA` as different version/profile routes. Treat the latter as implementation-observed unless a matching normative source is found; require pinned native/reference-produced evidence for semantic claims. Do not infer DXF `ACDSDATA` layout from the DWG AcDs chapter. |
| ODA [Open Design Specification v5.4.1](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf), §24.2.2.3–24.2.2.4 | For the DWG `AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b` DataStorage route, the spec describes SAB data records, handle-associated record headers, large data-blob references, and Blob01 pages. It gives the `ACIS BinaryFile` prefix and version-dependent terminal marker. The spec explicitly leaves detailed ACIS/SAB semantics outside its scope. | Continue using ODA as the DWG byte-layout authority for section/index/blob work, but require separate payload-profile and semantic evidence. Do not treat DWG’s AcDs record rules as a DXF serialization specification or a geometry-kernel contract. |
| LibreDWG [NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS), [issue #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411), and [source](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode_r2007.c) | NEWS documents historical incomplete/heuristic R2013+ AcDs SAB extraction and a separate fix for dropping the last SAT block on DXF export. Issue #1411 reports empty SAB/AcDs output for the named 0.14.8593 route and remains an issue-level observation; the visible source has an AcDs reader path, so the issue’s summary should not be repeated as proof that no section reader exists at all. | State the limitation at the actual failing layer: profile-specific decode/extraction, entity association, or DXF/DWG write. Pin release/commit and route. The peer report is a useful generated-carrier discriminator, not a blanket current-master verdict, proof of valid geometry, or prescription to copy brute-force extraction. |
| ACadSharp [issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195), [PR #1150](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1150), and [PR #1240](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1240) | The issue reports that DWG-read solids disappear from DXF output, including solids that are the sole contents of blocks. Both visible writer PRs remain open; #1150 proposes multiple carrier/version paths and reports branch-specific reader/writer interaction problems, while #1240 is a separate dependent implementation path. These are not merged-release results. | Maintain per-source identity/disposition and solid-only block checks. Credit neither branch as shipped interoperability or semantic evidence. Require complete route-specific carrier reconstruction or an explicit fail-before-publication result; same-library readback is not an independent geometry oracle. |
| FreeCAD [DXF guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and [issue #18454](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/18454) | The documented stock DXF importer does not read embedded ACIS/SAT solid blobs; DWG is converted to DXF before the chosen DXF importer. Explicit 3D primitives/surfaces and opaque ACIS carriers therefore have different consumer outcomes. | Keep native Linux/Windows FreeCAD qualification scoped to the selected converter/importer and entity profile. Do not use stock FreeCAD to grade ACIS B-rep semantics; preserve its 2D route as an independent compatibility requirement. |

### PAR-07/S8 implementation-ready refinement

1. **Freeze the versioned carrier map before changing code.** For each test
   vector, record source format/version, entity handle/type, owner/block path,
   carrier route (`DXF-inline-1/3`, `DXF-observed-ACDSDATA`,
   `DWG-inline`, or `DWG-AcDs`), exact byte/chunk spans, expected entity
   identity, and disposition. Do not collapse these four routes into one
   `ACIS supported` checkbox.
2. **Keep the version boundary source-backed.** Use ODA §24 for modern DWG
   DataStorage layout and local traces for the supported reader versions. Use
   Autodesk’s public 3DSOLID group table for documented inline DXF fields.
   Treat any DXF `ACDSDATA`/group-310 association as observed profile data
   until a public normative source or pinned native output establishes its
   contract. No speculative type code, key, or handle association.
3. **Test the serialization routes separately with generated controls.** Reuse
   existing selectors to cover group-1/3 continuation and terminal-block
   boundaries, modern-DXF binary chunk completeness and handle association,
   and DWG AcDs schema/index/record/Blob01 traversal. A carrier hash pass proves
   byte preservation only; separately assert owner/key join and explicit
   semantic disposition. A shell entity with empty/missing modeler bytes is a
   loss, not a passing entity-count match.
4. **Do not use the peer repositories as routine dependencies.** At the
   existing composed PAR-07/S8 checkpoint only, capture an immutable peer
   release/commit, executable/package hash, exact source artifact, route,
   diagnostics, and per-record outcomes. Label unmerged PR results as design
   leads. If a peer or native tool is unavailable, record `NOT_RUN` and
   continue the local queue.
5. **Preserve the fast implementation cadence and fixture policy.** Each
   local slice uses its owning generated ASCII/Binary selector and fast CTest;
   full suites remain sparse at composed milestones. Add no external DWG/DXF
   fixture: use existing repository fixtures or controls generated locally
   from scratch. Keep 2D callback/API compatibility intact while tracking
   3D carrier and semantic evidence separately.

This is a correctness/readiness refinement to the existing PAR-07/S8 and
PAR-14 owners only; it adds no defect, finding, top-level subplan, test,
fixture, dependency, peer run, or support promotion. Findings/subplans remain
**141 / 78**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain explicitly
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. Local queue order and validation
cadence are unchanged; no full suite was run.

<a id="deeperbroader-open-source-codec-workflow-and-comparator-selection-gates-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader open-source codec workflow and comparator-selection gates (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass compared primary project documentation for LibreDWG, ACadSharp,
ezdxf, and FreeCAD to make the existing PAR-07/S8 peer checkpoint more
selective and execution-ready. It does not add a repository-level support
claim or infer a local defect from another project's status statement.

| Primary source | What it establishes | Plan treatment and limits |
|---|---|---|
| GNU LibreDWG [manual: JSON](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/JSON.html), [programs](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/Programs.html), and [fuzzing setup](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg-fuzz) | LibreDWG describes its JSON as a readable 1:1 mapping of its DWG structures with more information than DXF; it exposes separate DWG/DXF/JSON input, read-write, and output fuzz routes. It also documents unknown classes/objects as possible binary blobs without DXF codes and route/version caveats for writers. | Use its JSON only as a pinned peer-decoder inventory/field-differential view for an exact artifact; it is LibreDWG's internal representation, not a neutral interchange standard, normative field map, or geometry oracle. Select a fuzz target matching the changed input/output route and keep fuzzing at the existing hostile-input milestone, not per implementation slice. |
| ACadSharp [feature/version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) and [reader notifications example](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/docs/articles/samples/reading.md) | Its current README declares compatibility per DXF/DWG reader/writer and version; individual matrix cells differ by direction. Its example exposes warnings/information via reader notifications. | Use the matrix to identify a candidate version/direction for a named differential, not to claim entity completeness or native acceptance. Pin an immutable release/source and artifact, capture notifications, and compare only the families/fields actually exercised. A blank matrix cell means not declared there, not local failure or proof of peer failure. |
| ezdxf [loading guidance](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/usage_for_beginners.html), [recovery](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/recover.html), [entity inventory](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/index.html), and [XREF scope](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/xref.html) | The project distinguishes ordinary loading of trusted DXF from an explicit recover path for flawed files; recovery/audit diagnostics are a different result. Its entity documentation includes 3DSOLID, REGION, BODY, proxy and other classes, while its XREF module documents a narrower copyable/transformable subset and limitations for unsupported entities/objects. | For a DXF output question, run strict parse first; record recover/audit separately and never use recovered output as a strict pass. Distinguish raw tag retention during load/save from XREF/copy/transform behavior. Do not use an entity index or XREF result as a whole-file support matrix. |
| FreeCAD [import/export preferences](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Import_Export_Preferences.md), [format inventory](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Import_Export.md), and [DXF guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) | FreeCAD documents DWG processing through a selected external converter and describes DWG/DXF capability at the application/importer layer; documented DXF 3D-carrier limitations are distinct from conversion. | Keep converter selection/output, the chosen DXF importer/backend/options, resulting object identity, and geometry interpretation as separate records. Use the stock consumer only for its declared 2D/entity routes; it cannot settle ACIS/SAB semantics. Documentation is a test-selection aid, not native Linux/Windows qualification. |

### PAR-07/S8 implementation-ready comparator procedure

1. **Name the unanswered stage before selecting a peer.** Use ODA v5.4.1 and
   Autodesk DXF references for normative layout questions. Select LibreDWG for
   a DWG decode/conversion question, ACadSharp for a bounded object-model
   read/write differential, ezdxf for direct DXF syntax/tag/recovery behavior,
   FreeCAD for a specific installed-consumer route, or a matching ACIS parser
   only for the payload profile it actually accepts. Do not run all peers by
   default.
2. **Freeze a compact artifact envelope.** Record immutable source revision,
   release/package or executable hash, build/runtime, source and output hash,
   file version/encoding, operation direction, command/options, warnings, and
   exact input provenance. If the artifact cannot be bound to source, label it
   unbound and do not count it as an independent implementation vote.
3. **Compare identities before aggregate counts.** Build a per-source ledger
   keyed by handle plus raw type/class and owner/block path. For each source
   item, record decoded typed fields, opaque bytes, explicit unsupported/skip
   or refusal, emitted target identity, and independent reopen result. Compare
   the shared fields both implementations actually expose; report unobservable
   and normalized fields as such rather than treating them as equal.
4. **Keep parse, recovery, conversion, and meaning separate.** A strict peer
   parse and an audit/recovery parse are different outcomes; a successful
   conversion plus reparse does not prove application import; an imported
   object or retained SAB bytes do not prove valid B-rep semantics. Native
   application and geometry-kernel results remain separate named receipts.
5. **Keep the fast lane local and progressive.** Continue the changed target,
   generated selector, and owning fast CTest as the per-slice checks. Invoke an
   optional peer only at the existing composed checkpoint for a predeclared
   unresolved question; run route-matched fuzzing only at the existing safety
   milestone. Missing/incompatible tools become `NOT_RUN` or
   `NOT_APPLICABLE`, then implementation self-unblocks to the next local
   source-backed slice. No peer install, full suite, native app, or external
   drawing is a per-slice dependency.
6. **Do not change support accounting from this research.** Peer matrices,
   project documentation, issue reports, structured dumps, same-codec reopen,
   and recovered files remain bounded evidence for their stated route only.
   No result here qualifies J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, or J295 or promotes
   DWG/DXF/3D support.

This refines existing PAR-07/S8, PAR-14 safety scheduling, and the peer
artifact/evidence ledger only. It adds no defect, finding, top-level subplan,
test target, fixture, dependency, peer run, or validation-cadence change.

remain explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. No peer executable,

Record build/commit, direction, source profile, warnings, entity↔section joins, exact carrier bytes, and output disposition. A surviving entity or a `has_ds_data` flag is not payload or geometry evidence. |

At the semantic checkpoint, record parser/profile disposition, shape validity, and independently authored topology/analytic expectations separately; an OCCT validity pass or successful FreeCAD open cannot alone prove geometric equivalence. |

### Revised implementation-ready procedure for existing PAR-07/S8 and PAR-14

1. **Keep the local fast queue primary.** Reuse the completed DataStorage
   record-anchor, Blob01-page, schema-type, and stale-secondary-index controls
   under their current test owners. For a changed parser boundary, run its
   strict target, selector, owning CTest, and scoped diff check. Do not rerun
   the full suite or add an external drawing for each slice.
2. **Select ACadSharp only for a concrete unresolved stage.** At the existing
   composed checkpoint, pin a release/source commit and executable/package
   hash, then compare only the relevant input/output operation. A missing,
   crashing, recovery-only, or warning-skipped peer result is `NOT_RUN`,
   `NOT_APPLICABLE`, or `COMPARATOR_LIMITATION` as appropriate; continue the
   local plan without waiting for the peer.
3. **Use a reference-closed comparison tuple, never just a total count:**
   `current file-header index → live segment-index entry → DataIndex/SchemaIndex
   entry → schema/key → DataField/DataHeader → direct record or Blob01 page
   references → ordered reconstructed bytes/hash → owning modeler handle/type →
   output entity/carrier`. Capture the active index identity, segment offsets
   and declared extents, record key/handle, direct-versus-blob route, page
   offsets/sizes/order, entity owner/block path, and per-stage disposition.
4. **Account for non-live material explicitly.** Keep stale secondary segment
   indexes, unreferenced DataHeader entries, pre-2013 inline payloads, and
   current referenced AcDs records in separate buckets. They may explain
   count deltas but cannot be silently counted as recovered entity payloads.
   Only compare byte hashes after the live DataIndex/schema/reference join is
   established; only compare semantic bodies after entity association is
   established.
5. **Preserve evidence ceilings and speed.** A peer section parse can inform
   structural fields; payload equality can establish carrier preservation;
   a pinned parser can establish only its admitted profile; kernel validity
   plus separately authored analytic/topology expectations can support a
   bounded semantic case. None alone establishes the next stage. Keep native
   Linux/Windows FreeCAD qualification and independent semantic evidence at
   the existing composed gate, preserve the 2D consumer route, and do not add
   peer installs, routine peer builds, or full suites to per-slice work.
