## Implementation progress — PAR-20/7G.3 XRECORD hard-pointer closure to DICTIONARYVAR (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Closed an existing source-backed gap in strict XRECORD graph validation. The
writer already traversed the NOD's canonical `AcDbVariableDictionary` and
collected its emitted DICTIONARYVAR handles in `visitedDictionaryVars`, but
the XRECORD group-code handle-target validator omitted that visited set. A
valid group-340 hard pointer to a retained DICTIONARYVAR was therefore
rejected even though the target was part of the output graph. The validator
now admits only DICTIONARYVAR handles reached in the validated graph; it does
not admit arbitrary or unresolved handles.

Extended the existing generated `--named-resource-import-evidence` ASCII and
Binary selector. The positive control roots an XRECORD at the NOD, points its
group-340 value at the `ROOT_SOURCE_VALUE` DICTIONARYVAR, then requires strict
readback to show: the NOD key points at the emitted XRECORD; the XRECORD is
NOD-owned; the target DICTIONARYVAR has its remapped handle and canonical
owner; and group 340 equals that remapped target. The negative control points
group 340 at absent handle `0xDEAD`, requires refusal, and verifies that the
pre-existing destination remains byte-for-byte unchanged.


`ACAD_GROUP` root survived, but it did not exercise an ambiguous input graph.

non-null unique canonical root to resolve to exactly one dictionary owned by

dictionary. Authored GROUPs without a source NOD root remain supported; the

both malformed cases in ASCII and Binary. Each refusal must preserve a seeded
destination byte-for-byte; after reloading the valid source, the same adapter
must retry successfully and strict readback must retain exactly one GROUP,
its name, and its member entity identity.

<a id="deeperbroader-consumer-route-semantics-and-documentation-conflict-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader consumer-route semantics and documentation conflict (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass reconciles current primary project documentation across FreeCAD,
LibreCAD_3, and ezdxf. The important finding is not a new libdxfrw defect:
consumer behavior is narrower and more route-specific than a format-level
“can exchange” statement implies. Converter success, strict DXF readability,
consumer object retention, and editable 3D model semantics must stay separate.

| Source | Evidence found | Plan disposition |
|---|---|---|
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) | The page documents two importer paths: a faster C++ importer and a legacy Python importer with some stronger entity handling; both are documented for DXF R12 onward. The C++ importer lists explicit omissions, including text, dimensions, and text/dimensions/attributes inside blocks. The same page says DXF ACIS solids cannot currently be read by FreeCAD. It then makes a broad statement that same-version DWG↔DXF conversion has “no data loss.” | Treat the broad exchange statement as a format-level generalization, not proof that a particular converter-plus-FreeCAD importer retains all records. Route-specific omissions and observed object dispositions govern consumer qualification. Test the intended importer setting; run another backend only if that backend is part of the supported product route or is needed to explain a failure. |
| FreeCAD [DWG import documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md) and [import/export preferences](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Import_Export_Preferences.md) | DWG processing is described as an external converter producing DXF followed by FreeCAD’s DXF importer; the documentation explicitly says the DXF importer’s restrictions apply. It names LibreDWG, ODA File Converter, and QCAD Pro as converter options, and notes CADExchanger as the route for 3D DWG conversion. | FreeCAD qualification is a composed pipeline, not a single “opens DWG” result. Record converter identity/version/hash, process status/diagnostics, fresh output hash and DXF `$ACADVER`, strict intermediate parse, selected importer/backend/settings, and per-source consumed/skipped disposition. Keep stock FreeCAD ACIS/B-rep semantics `NOT_APPLICABLE`/unsupported unless a separately identified 3D route is actually selected and independently qualified. |
| LibreCAD_3 [`docs/dwg-support.md`](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/blob/master/docs/dwg-support.md) | Current `master` documentation says DWG import is behind `WITH_DWG_IMPORT` and off by default; DWG writing is deliberately not offered. It describes its pinned libdxfrw ledger as read-only claims with none promoted, and enforces Save As to DXF for DWG-origin documents. The documentation itself is mutable and is not a native run receipt. | Keep LibreCAD_3 as an opt-in, read-only consumer route and do not turn its presence into a DWG writer or 3D-consumer requirement. For compatibility, test the opt-in import route only at the existing composed consumer gate, retain the Save-As-to-DXF policy, and qualify 2D persisted semantics separately from any opaque 3D carrier retained by the library. |
| ezdxf [XREF documentation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/xref.rst), [ACIS browser documentation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/launcher.rst), and [project README](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/README.md) | XREF loading/copying supports a documented subset of copyable/transformable DXF entities and required resources; unsupported ACAD_TABLE, preserved unknown/proxy content, and many OBJECTS features may be ignored without exceptions. The separate ACIS browser exposes SAT/SAB content for inspection/export, while the README describes DXF read/write and audit tools. | Do not treat ezdxf XREF copying, a successful parse/audit, or raw SAT/SAB inspection as whole-document retention, writer round-trip, ACIS interpretation, or solid semantics. Select it only for a concrete DXF operation and record that operation’s documented and observed denominator. |

### PAR-07/S8 and 3D consumer-gate refinement

1. Keep the evidence lanes separate: file-format structural parse; typed
   records and owner/reference graph; converter output; raw modeler carrier;
   consumer-imported object inventory; geometry/kernel validity; independent
   expected topology/volume/placement; and native acceptance. A success at an
   earlier lane cannot promote a later lane.
2. At the composed FreeCAD checkpoint, first use the intended default importer
   configuration. Bind the exact OS/build, converter and importer settings,
   input/output hashes, process statuses, diagnostics, output version, and
   source-handle-to-consumer-object/skipped mapping. Exercise the second
   importer only if it is an advertised route or needed to diagnose a specific
   discrepancy; do not double the routine matrix by default.
3. Use a scratch-generated or already-admitted input with a predeclared
   source-object manifest. Include a supported 2D object/resource set, an
   explicitly unsupported/ignored control, and separate 3D carrier controls.
   Score FreeCAD’s reported 2D importer behavior only against that route’s
   expected subset. Stock FreeCAD ACIS inability is a route limitation, not a
   libdxfrw parse failure; a rendered wireframe or tessellation is not a B-rep
   witness.
4. Preserve LibreCAD and LibreCAD_3 2D consumers as compatibility constraints.
   LibreCAD_3’s opt-in DWG reader must remain read-only; Save As to DXF is the
   expected policy. Do not infer 3D editing support from callback/API
   availability or opaque modeler-data retention.
5. No per-slice FreeCAD/LibreCAD_3/ezdxf builds, external fixtures, or new
   dependencies. Keep fast generated local checks first and invoke external
   consumer routes only at the existing milestone. Unavailable or unpinned
   routes remain `NOT_RUN`; continue local work. No result here changes any
   support claim or the external J-item state.

This pass adds no finding, top-level subplan, production/test change, fixture,

<a id="deeper-broader-dxf-viewer-parser-lineage-and-projection-boundary-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader research — DXF viewer parser lineage and projection boundary (2026-10-20; research only)

### Findings and source crosswalk

The repository search surfaced `opendxfviewer`, a Rust/Makepad DXF viewer with an independently implemented display pipeline. Its README explicitly limits the product to viewing DXF (no editing, conversion, or CAD kernel) and says it does not read DWG. The README lists supported drawing entities and transformations, but also says HATCH is not parsed by its `dxf` crate, fit-point-only splines are approximated, MLINE is rendered as a centerline, and other unsupported types are counted. It documents input budgets for primitive count, vertices, INSERT-array cells, and retained text bytes, plus generated malformed/degenerate fixture coverage and a no-GPU unit-test suite. These are useful renderer- and hostile-input design observations, not proof of this repository's current guard completeness or comparative performance.

The viewer does not supply an independent parser vote: its third-party notice lists the Rust `dxf` crate; that crate's published manifest names `https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf-rs` as its repository. The viewer contains custom file-loading/encoding handling, so any future run must still pin and inspect the exact app and parser versions; the lineage classification follows the declared dependency, not a claim that every parsing step is delegated unchanged.

`vagran/dxf-viewer` remains a distinct renderer route, using JavaScript/WebGL and `dxf-parser`. Its own current README describes it as a 2D viewer and enumerates incomplete areas including stream parsing, styles/MTEXT, line patterns, hatching, arrayed blocks, dimensions/leaders, legacy code pages, full OCS, and paper-space layouts. It identifies Autodesk's online viewer as its primary appearance reference and says exact rendering issues depend on sample-driven reports and local corpora. That project guidance is evidence about the renderer's scope and its own verification model, not an independent truth oracle for this library.

### PAR-07/S8 and PAR-14 implementation-ready refinement

1. Keep source decoding, code/value preservation, handle/owner graph closure, writer disposition, strict output parsing, and application import as separate evidence rows. A screenshot or scene projection cannot replace any of those checks.
2. Do not run either viewer in a normal implementation slice. If a composed checkpoint has a specific unresolved 2D display question, select at most one viewer whose declared support includes the relevant entities and transformations; record the exact source/release revision, parser dependency, runtime, options, and unsupported/ignored counts.
3. Generate a minimal DXF from scratch or use only a drawing already eligible in this repository. Compare predeclared projection observables for an allowlisted entity subset (such as transformed endpoints, bounds, and curve samples) under a fixed view. Exclude unsupported entities and report them explicitly; do not judge exact raster equality across different tessellation/font/rendering stacks.
4. Treat an `opendxfviewer` result as IxMilia-parser-lineage plus a distinct scene/render stage, not as a second independent parse. Treat `vagran/dxf-viewer` as `dxf-parser` lineage plus its renderer. If either tool is unavailable, unpinned, or cannot consume the chosen DXF profile, record `NOT_RUN`/`NOT_APPLICABLE` and continue local work.
5. Reuse existing PAR-14 resource-limit and generated-input controls; audit any unresolved amplification vector separately (expanded primitives, generated vertices, INSERT array cells, and retained text) rather than inferring safety from one total-output counter. Do not introduce another peer dependency, persistent fixture, or routine render test for this research item.

This is a comparator-boundary refinement only. It creates no local defect, numbered finding, top-level subplan, required tool, peer run, downloaded drawing, fixture, test, dependency, or support promotion. Findings and top-level subplans remain **141 / 78**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Deeper/broader peer capability-matrix and DWG-lineage screen (2026-10-20; research only)

This screen adds two current projects to the existing PAR-07/S8 comparator
inventory and, more importantly, sharpens the pre-execution admission rule.
Marketing labels, a format matrix, a 3D renderer, or a GUI that opens DWG do not
by themselves establish which parser, writer, converter, or geometry kernel
processed the file. The candidate must be traceable from source artifact to
operation and output before it costs a local clone/build or enters an evidence
receipt.

| Candidate | Current primary-source evidence | PAR-07/S8 disposition |
|---|---|---|
| [CADKernel](https://github.com/kernalix7/CADKernel) | Its README overview advertises 60+ formats including ACIS and says DWG/DXF read/write are supported. The same README's [format matrix](https://github.com/kernalix7/CADKernel#supported-file-formats) marks ACIS SAT/SAB read/write as planned, while the [FAQ](https://github.com/kernalix7/CADKernel#faq) says proprietary CAD import is planned. | Do not admit based on the headline or unchecked compatibility claim. First require a concrete source path, tagged artifact, and operation-specific test for the exact DXF/DWG profile. Until reconciled, no clone/build and no parser, writer, or semantic credit. This is a documentation-evidence inconsistency, not a confirmed implementation defect. |
| [mlightcad/cad-viewer](https://github.com/mlightcad/cad-viewer) | Current README says DXF loading uses its built-in MIT parser; default DWG loading is not registered, and open-source DWG loading requires an opt-in GPL-3.0 LibreDWG converter. It describes a 2D-only optimized rendering pipeline, while R12-to-latest version compatibility remains in progress. The README mentions Three.js but does not identify ACIS parsing or a B-rep semantic route. | Keep as a conditional independent DXF-parser/2D-projection candidate only, for entities actually in its implemented subset and only at a composed checkpoint. If the LibreDWG converter is used, classify DWG evidence under that parser lineage, not as a second independent DWG implementation. No 3D, ACIS/AcDs, exact owner-graph, DXF writer, or native CAD acceptance credit. |
| [cq-acis](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis) | Its own README calls the project experimental, lists bounded SAT/SAB/ASM versions and a limited analytic B-rep subset, and says parsing alone does not guarantee shape conversion. | Retain the already documented exact-profile candidate for raw ACIS payloads only. It does not read DWG/DXF containers or establish AcDs record-to-entity ownership; the kernel and independent analytic-oracle limitations already recorded in the exact-artifact gate still apply. |

### Revised low-cost admission and execution procedure

1. **Documentation sieve before tool setup:** inspect the current source/manifest,
   release tags, license, exact reader/writer/converter route, and tests for the
   requested operation. Resolve contradictions between overview, matrix, FAQ,
   and roadmap. If the route is only a roadmap item or cannot be located, record
   `NOT_ADMITTED` and continue local implementation without cloning or building.
2. **Draw the lineage graph:** record parser, converter, projection, and geometry
   kernel separately. A GUI or renderer may compose multiple libraries. Count
   shared code and shared kernels as correlated evidence; do not count a
   LibreDWG-based app as a second DWG parser, or an OCCT-backed parser as an
   independent kernel.
3. **Admit only a matching operation/profile:** name source kind and version,
   carrier type, entity subset, read/write direction, strict/recovery mode, and
   output surface. Capability tables and broad version ranges are discovery
   leads only. Missing route-specific test/reproduction evidence means
   `NOT_APPLICABLE` or `NOT_RUN`, not inferred support.
4. **At most one peer execution at a composed checkpoint:** choose the one
   source-distinct route that can answer the unresolved question. Pin source
   commit and released artifact/runtime hashes; capture diagnostics, every
   source entity's output disposition, unsupported/repair/fallback counts, and
   output identity. Compare against generated or already-eligible local data;
   do not import peer test drawings.
5. **Keep the implementation queue moving:** no new mandatory dependency, test,
   or per-slice external run follows from this screen. A rejected/unavailable
   peer does not block any local slice. For 3D, retain independent checks for
   explicit mesh topology, opaque SAT/SAB byte/owner transport, B-rep validity
   and analytic metrics, and selected consumer acceptance.

This refines comparator selection under existing PAR-07/S8 and its 3D evidence
boundary only. It adds no local defect, numbered finding, top-level subplan,
test, fixture, dependency, peer execution, or support promotion. Findings and
top-level subplans remain **141 / 78**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The six external items
do not block local implementation.

## Deeper/broader peer validation workflow and corpus-provenance crosswalk (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass looked beyond feature matrices and issue reports at how another
open-source DWG/DXF implementation organizes evidence and contributor
validation. The useful result is a faster, clearer validation ladder for this
plan—not another peer capability claim.

| Primary source | Current evidence and limits | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/AGENTS.md) | The project recommends `make check` for ordinary changes, identifies its ASan build as very slow, and documents separate ODA File Converter round-trips with audit for interoperability checks. The instructions are project-specific and do not establish results for libdxfrw or a particular peer build. | Keep each implementation slice on the changed target, one generated focused selector, and its owning fast CTest. Defer broad suite, sanitizer, fuzz, and converter work to their existing route-specific checkpoints; do not run a peer or full suite merely because a leaf changed. |
| LibreDWG [`test-dxf.sh`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/test-dxf.sh) and [`dxf-roundtrip.sh`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/dxf-roundtrip.sh) | The first script generates DXF, filters/normalizes it, then compares it with an expected DXF when one exists. The second composes LibreDWG DWG→DXF, an ODA File Converter DXF→DWG conversion, and a `dwgread` reopen. This is a layered mixed-toolchain workflow, not an independent single-codec or semantic result. | At the composed checkpoint, label each stage and exact tool separately: source read, adapter/writer output, normalized structural comparison, optional external conversion, strict reopen, and per-source identity/disposition. Do not collapse a successful round-trip into proof that every stage preserved data. |
| LibreDWG [manual coverage notes](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) and [`HACKING`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/HACKING) | The manual explicitly lists typed entity/object families without test coverage and distinguishes unhandled pass-through data. HACKING describes fuzz and sanitizer workflows and says unknown-layout reverse engineering needs DWG/DXF pairs. This is the project's own coverage disclosure and workflow, not a standards requirement or a measured libdxfrw gap. | A version support matrix, declared class, or opaque pass-through must not imply tested semantic support. Unknown byte layouts require ODA authority or a producer-authored pair/trace; a generated vector is admissible only for rules independently known well enough to encode it. Never reverse-infer a missing grammar from a self-authored vector. |

### Revised implementation-ready validation ladder

1. **Fast leaf (every slice):** identify the exact read/write direction,
   version, record family, and evidence claim before editing. Add or reuse one
   source-authored generated case only when the wire rule is known. Require the
   positive case, a bounded negative or refusal/retry where applicable, and a
   following-record/owner sentinel. Build the narrow production/test targets,
   run the owning selector and CTest, and inspect only the scoped diff.
2. **Pair-backed differential (only for a producer-specific question):** use
   an already eligible repository sample or a scratch-only pair created from
   scratch. Record producer/version, file hashes, input and output versions,
   diagnostics, exact source-to-output identity/disposition, and normalization
   rules. A peer-generated file can establish producer interoperability for
   its tested route; it does not become a normative layout source.
3. **Composed checkpoint (once for a completed route/batch):** select at most
   one source-distinct peer for the unresolved question. Separate the stages
   (decode, callback/model projection, write, strict reopen, optional consumer)
   and preserve per-record outcomes. Run a full format matrix only when a
   milestone closes a version-family slice, not for unrelated leaf changes.
4. **Safety checkpoint (low frequency and path-triggered):** run the planned
   sanitizer/fuzz campaign when parser bounds, allocation, ownership, or
   lifetime code changes, or at the scheduled integration checkpoint. Keep
   hostile generated vectors local; do not send malformed inputs to native CAD
   applications as ordinary compatibility tests.
5. **Self-update and self-unblock:** after every implemented item, update its
   status/evidence and choose the next locally actionable item. If no eligible
   producer pair, peer binary, platform, or native application is available,
   mark only the affected external claim `NOT_RUN`/`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`, preserve
   its support ceiling, and continue the local queue. Do not let this external
   gap stop implementation.

### Refined route-acceptance sequence (existing PAR owners; no new subplan)

1. **Artifact result:** record reader result, diagnostics, writer result, and
   publication outcome separately. Require complete DXF section closure and
   final `EOF`; when the read is incomplete, fail/refuse explicitly rather
   than publish a truncated file as successful conversion.
2. **Syntax:** run the existing strict DXF validation route at the composed
   checkpoint (or the qualified independent runtime when available). Check
   physical group-code framing separately from semantic string preservation.
   ASCII refusal of unsupported CR/LF data must remain an explicit refusal,
   never be scored as a successful text round trip.
3. **Graph and ownership:** compare source and output record identities by
   block/layout/owner, with an explicit disposition for every source object.
   Assert each block's member identities and reference closure; aggregate
   counts and block-shell existence are insufficient.
4. **Modeler carrier and meaning:** compare ACIS entity identity, carrier
   version/path, payload association, and bytes independently from geometry
   validity, topology, and consumer interpretation. Opaque-byte parity cannot
   promote ACIS semantic support.
5. **Cadence and self-unblock:** keep focused targets/selectors as the normal
   per-slice validation. Run the composed strict-parse/identity check once at
   the existing route or family checkpoint, not after every unrelated leaf.
   If a peer artifact, build, or native platform is unavailable, mark only
   that external cell `NOT_RUN`/`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and continue local work.

This is an acceptance-boundary refinement of existing PAR-06, PAR-07/S8,
PAR-14, PAR-20, and PAR-49 only. The local generated CR/LF, ownership,
modeler-carrier, transactional-output, and independent-DXF controls already
cover their focused dimensions; this pass found no need to duplicate those
tests or run them again. It adds no local finding, top-level subplan, code,
test, fixture, dependency, peer execution, or support promotion. Findings and
top-level subplans remain **141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

previously bounded nodes, references, staged handles, and source-record
inventory, but a selected XRECORD could require linear scans of scalar/text
payload slots that were not graph edges and therefore did not consume any
budget. Added a distinct `maxXRecordPayloadSlots` policy and
`inspectedXRecordPayloadSlots` counter; reaching it produces the named

representation is charged when actually scanned: ordered `m_dataEntries`,
fallback `m_values`, and each `m_handleValues` pass, while handle references
continue to consume the separate edge budget. The diagnostic includes the new
counter. Retained-byte limits in 7S and graph topology semantics are unchanged.

graph fixed and vary only payload slots. Both ordered and fallback value views
pass at cap−1/cap and refuse at cap+1 with the seeded destination unchanged;
the corrected graph retries successfully through the same adapter. A
fallback-handle-view control confirms both actual scans are charged and a
one-slot cap refuses before the second scan, then retries at cap. No persistent
fixture or new CTest registration was added.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3 DWG block-list validation and scratch reuse (2026-10-20; focused round-trip gates, uncommitted)

The deferred DWG BLOCK_RECORD closure path in
[`dwgWriter15::emitDeferredBlockControl()`](src/intern/dwgwriter15.cpp) had
three input-sized costs: every member linearly searched the complete object
map for a frame, duplicate detection rescanned the already-visited owner-list
prefix, and block/model/paper handle vectors were copied even when modern
versions preserve their source order. At a maximum one-million-handle owner
list, the two nested scans could perform quadratic comparisons before writing
the final ownership graph.

The writer now sorts its existing object-map vector before closure validation
and uses `lower_bound` for exact frame membership. This adds no object-map
clone or side index; the later `writeDwgHandles()` sort remains authoritative
because structural frames are appended after closure. Each list is copied to
one reusable scratch vector, sorted once, checked for adjacent duplicates,
then checked against the sorted map. The copy helper refuses lists above the
existing `dwgSafety::MaxOwnedObjectCount` cap before allocation. The scratch
payload is therefore at most 1,000,000 `uint32_t` slots (4,000,000 bytes;
approximately 3.82 MiB), and legacy optional-entity filtering, contiguous-chain
checks, and sorted emission reuse that same allocation.

For AC1018 and newer, BLOCK_RECORD output borrows the original entity-handle
vectors, preserving callback order without an owner-list copy. AC1015 and
earlier continue to emit sorted handle lists, as before. No DXF/DWG fields,
handle roles, admission policy, public API, or support claim changed.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip --parallel 2  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^(libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip|libdxfrw_dwg_block_record_xref_roundtrip)$' --output-on-failure  PASS (2/2)
git diff --check -- src/intern/dwgwriter15.cpp DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md docs/research/7s3-dwg-block-list-validation-scratch-reuse-fast-slice-2026-10-20.json  PASS
```

The local round-trip test exercises valid legacy and modern writes, including
non-empty user-block membership and generated large POLYLINE chains; the XREF
gate covers BLOCK_RECORD version-specific metadata. Neither is a performance
benchmark or independent-producer/native-application qualification. No new
CTest, fixture, dependency, or full-suite run was added.

The insertion path `recordBlockOwnedEntity()` still linearly scans its owner
vector before appending each typed entity, and `recordRawBlockOwnedEntity()`
has a related membership scan. Those are distinct remaining source-backed
hot paths; the scratch refactor does not claim to remove their cumulative
quadratic work. **Self-unblock:** continue 7S.3 by evaluating a bounded,
rollback-safe insertion-time membership index against the existing global
object-count limits, then update the byte/work receipt before adding any
indexing state. Keep the DXF-copy audit and other DWG live/work owners open.

slice. Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and

## Implementation progress — 7S.3 DWG block-owner membership index (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Replaced the insertion-time owner-vector scans in
[`dwgWriter15::recordBlockOwnedEntity()`](src/intern/dwgwriter15.cpp) and
[`dwgWriter15::canRecordRawBlockOwnedEntity()`](src/intern/dwgwriter15.cpp)
with an owner+entity-handle membership set. Pairing the handle with its
BLOCK_RECORD preserves the previous per-owner duplicate contract, including
the prior behavior for malformed callers that repeat one handle under two
different owners. Raw and typed entities share the same membership index.
Index insertion precedes vector publication; allocation failure in the vector
append removes the inserted key before propagating the exception.

The index is bounded by `dwgSafety::MaxDwgReadObjectCount` (1,000,000 entity
memberships), matching the existing reader's aggregate object-count budget.
Compound rollback erases membership keys for every modelspace/paperspace or
user-block vector tail it truncates, and for entity lists belonging to
user-block records created after the checkpoint. It leaves list entries
untouched where the existing rollback logic intentionally does not resize
those lists. Serialized handle-list order and wire fields are unchanged.

The generated `--block-owner-membership-index` selector checks duplicate
refusal for typed and raw entities, per-owner scoping, and typed/raw rollback
followed by retry. No persistent DWG/DXF input or output was added.

`dx_iface::prepareExtensionObjectGraph()` previously scanned the shared
`rawNamedResourceObjects` vector independently for DICTIONARYVAR, SCALE,
MLINESTYLE, and MLEADERSTYLE. Each scan normalized every source name, even
when it belonged to a later family; only matching records consumed the

unbudgeted earlier full-vector scans before the configured work cap stopped

source-order pass after the typed family maps have been built. It uppercases
each name once, charges each candidate exactly once with
`examineSourceRecord()`, validates the raw handle spelling plus typed
identity/owner, and inserts the pointer into the existing family map. Family
coverage checks remain explicit and family-specific. The implementation adds
no second pointer vector, copy, new counter, or persistent fixture. The
`dx_iface` test friend is non-virtual and adds no object state or public
callable API.

The generated `--extension-graph-limits` control constructs one typed
MLINESTYLE and its mixed-case raw carrier in memory. A one-record budget
admits the typed record but refuses on the raw carrier at exactly the cap; a
corrected two-record budget succeeds through the same adapter and reports two
source records, proving the raw projection is charged once.

The extension-graph walker scans the NOD entries once to find and validate the
special `AcDbVariableDictionary` root, then traverses the same entries and
charges accepted graph edges. Unlike regular DICTIONARY and
DICTIONARYWDFLT pre-scans, this first NOD pass previously had no bound against
the remaining edge budget and could walk a large list before the later edge
loop stopped.

The NOD cardinality pass now compares its entry count with the remaining
`maxEdges` budget before scanning. It refuses with `EdgeLimit` if the
pre-traversal work cannot fit; it does not increment `examinedEdges`, so the
actual traversal continues to account accepted reference slots once. This
matches the existing conservative pre-scan policy for dictionary entries and
adds no format rule or public state.

The generated `--extension-graph-limits` control creates a two-entry NOD with
two valid dictionary targets under a one-edge budget. It verifies refusal
before any edge is charged or node visited.

## Deeper/broader research — DXF wire-order, reference-role, recovery, and comparator-maturity boundary (2026-10-20; research only)

### Primary-source findings

| Source | Evidence | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk [common DXF entity group codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3610039E-27D1-4E23-B6D3-7E60B22BB5BD.htm) and [group-code description](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-89CB823D-614D-4D1E-8204-568EC72DF869.htm) | Autodesk explicitly says not to rely on the display order in entity-code tables: order can vary. A DXF record is still a stream of group-code/value pairs with structural record/section markers; omitted fields use defined defaults. | Reader acceptance should separate allowed tag-order variation from schema-defined ordering of repeated tuples, nested application groups, subclass scopes, and record boundaries. A writer’s stable output order is a serialization regression contract, not proof that readers accept legal alternate orderings. |
| Autodesk [persistent reference handles](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-582ECC55-155A-48CC-A8B1-7D75FDF4ECC9.htm) and [DXF group-code ranges](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2027/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OARX-RefGuide-DXF_Group_Codes.html) | 320–329 are arbitrary IDs; 330–339 soft pointers; 340–349 hard pointers; 350–359 soft owners; 360–369 hard owners. XDATA group 1005 has soft-pointer translation behavior. Those roles are not interchangeable merely because values are handle-shaped. | Continue PAR-16/7A and PAR-20/7G role-aware remapping/closure; in composed readback, check reference role and target identity, not just a resolvable hex token. Preserve external/arbitrary handles without pretending they are local graph edges. Reuse existing role/remap and HANDSEED coverage; add a leaf only if source review identifies a concrete uncovered pair. |
| ezdxf [handle model](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfinternals/handles.html), [strict/recovery loader](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/recover.html), and [audit API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/drawing.html) | ezdxf documents unique drawing handles, one owner per object, and `$HANDSEED` above the greatest handle. Its recovery path repairs some structural flaws, may accept decoding errors as unrecoverable diagnostics, and warns that rewriting recovered files may lose information or create invalid output; audit is distinct from strict loading. | At PAR-07/S8’s existing composed checkpoint record strict-load result, recovery/audit result, and any repairs/errors separately. A recovered document or a same-codec rewrite is diagnostic only and cannot satisfy strict output acceptance. Keep handle uniqueness, owner cardinality, reference reachability, and header seed as separate assertions. |
| LibreDWG [current repository guidance](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) and [`dwgwrite` manual](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/programs/dwgwrite.1); ACadSharp [published direction/version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp#compatible-dwgdxf-versions) | LibreDWG’s README contains broader writer claims and caveats, while its current tool documentation describes `dwgwrite` as R2000-only and the repository describes `dxf2dwg` as R2000-only. ACadSharp’s matrix marks AC1021 DWG reading supported and AC1021 DWG writing unsupported. These are different tools and declared project contracts, not proven per-feature results. | Every optional differential row must bind repository/tool, exact revision or release, operation, direction, target version, and class/property under test. Do not use a reader capability as a writer oracle, a repository-level checkmark as semantic evidence, or an unavailable version row as a negative result. |

### Implementation-readiness refinement (existing owners only)

1. **Fast leaf audit:** when touching a DXF parser family, first reuse its existing generated ASCII/Binary selector. If source inspection finds that only the usual table order is covered, add at most one small locally generated alternate-order case in that same test owner. Permute only independent fields whose order is not prescribed; retain group-0/entity boundaries, group-100 subclass scope, balanced group-102 controls, and the ordering of repeated/vector payloads. Assert the parsed values and the following-record sentinel. Do not create a Cartesian permutation suite.
2. **Output closure:** use existing PAR-16/7A, PAR-20/7G, and HANDSEED checks. For an admitted edit/remap, independently verify output handle uniqueness/high-water seed, owner role/cardinality, local translated references, and XDATA 1005 behavior. Do not require arbitrary 320–329 references to resolve locally or remap. Check output text order only where a format rule or an explicit stable-writer contract requires it.
3. **Composed differential:** run one exact-pinned comparator only for a still-unresolved named property/version/direction at the existing PAR-07/S8 checkpoint. Capture emitted artifact hash and parser diagnostics. Run strict parsing first; recovery/audit can follow as a separate diagnostic, with its repair list and errors retained. An audit that repaired the output, an exit code alone, or a same-library reopen does not convert a strict failure to a pass.
4. **Self-unblock:** absent a comparator build, platform, or external drawing, keep that cell `NOT_RUN`/`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and continue to the next locally actionable source-backed implementation slice. Do not import or commit peer fixtures; use existing repository fixtures or scratch vectors generated locally from scratch.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3 DWG GROUP member-target index (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

`dwgWriter15::writeGroup()` previously checked each referenced member by
searching both space-entity vectors and then every user-block entity vector.
For `M` total GROUP references and `E` emitted entities, this repeated
owner-vector traversal scaled with `M × E` in the large case.

The writer now lazily builds one sorted, deduplicated vector from
`m_blockOwnedEntityHandles`, the existing owner+handle ledger already bounded
by `MaxDwgReadObjectCount`. Each GROUP member check uses binary search. Entity
recording and compound-transaction rollback invalidate this derived view, so a
retry or later admitted entity cannot use stale membership. The temporary
view is bounded to at most one million 32-bit handles (about 3.82 MiB); it
adds no per-entity persistent owner state. This is an algorithmic reduction in
repeated scans, not a benchmarked speedup claim.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3 DWG user-block owner lookup index (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Repeated entity admission, raw-entity replay, block-scope entry, and INSERT
reverse-reference operations searched `m_userBlocks` linearly by
BLOCK_RECORD handle. With `Q` lookups over `B` registered blocks, that owner
resolution could repeat `O(Q × B)` scans.

The writer now lazily builds a sorted handle-to-vector-index view and uses
binary search for those lookups. The view is invalidated when block creation
appends a record or compound rollback removes records. Changes to block
metadata and entity-list tails do not move vector entries and therefore keep
the index valid. If index allocation or uniqueness validation fails, the
lookup falls back to the original linear search. Successful construction costs
`O(B log B)` once per block-vector generation and subsequent lookups cost
`O(log B)`; this is an algorithmic bound, not a measured speedup. The view
stores one handle/index pair per registered block. Wire layout, ownership-list
ordering, admission rules, and API are unchanged.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3 DWG emitted-object handle membership index (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Several writer paths re-scanned the full `m_objectMap` for every frame to
reject duplicate handles; modeler and dictionary/class closure also counted
frames by repeated scans. That made cumulative duplicate admission quadratic
in the number of emitted frames.

The writer now maintains an emitted-handle set coupled to object-map
publication for the legacy and R2007+ frame writers and raw replay. Per-frame
duplicate checks and exact-one closure checks use the same set. Compound and

publication removes a tentative key if appending the map entry throws. This
also replaces the temporary sorted handle vector from the preceding modeler
replay slice. Final object-map preflight reuses this synchronized set rather
than rebuilding another ordered set; the final HANDLES path retains its
independent sort and adjacent duplicate validation. Set operations are
average `O(1)` (with the standard unordered-container worst-case); final map
sorting remains `O(E log E)`. No timing benchmark is claimed.

## Deeper/broader cross-implementation 3D capability and loss-accounting audit (2026-10-20; research only)

This source review compares the current public contracts for explicit DXF
geometry, ACIS/SAT/SAB, DWG conversion, and downstream projection. It is a
capability-boundary audit, not a run of peer binaries or a new libdxfrw
conformance result.

| Primary source | Verified contract and evidence ceiling | Plan consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autodesk [POLYLINE DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-ABF6B778-BE20-4B49-9B58-A94E64CEFFF3.htm) and [Polyface Meshes reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-96B6288E-F413-46C0-968A-A314171C0AAE.htm); existing `runDxfPolyfaceCompletedPool` | The bit-coded parent distinguishes 3D polyline, polygon mesh, and polyface modes; a 2D polyline elevation is OCS while a 3D polyline elevation is WCS. Polyface header vertex/face counts need not be accurate; writers should place coordinate vertices before faces, while readers must tolerate unusual child ordering. At the review baseline, generated ASCII/Binary cases covered stale counts, interleaved/forward face placement, signed indices, and canonical output, but stopped at EOF after `SEQEND`; no following-entity resynchronization was asserted and the leaf lacked a focused fast selector. | Reuse PAR-37/7V, not a new finding: append a distinct LINE sentinel after `SEQEND`, assert its identity/XYZ after initial read and strict write/readback, and expose this existing control through one focused fast selector/CTest for both encodings. Keep canonical writer ordering and actual-coordinate-pool validation. A passing parser vector proves wire interpretation only, not rendered topology or DWG support. |
| [ezdxf 1.4.5 ACIS API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) | The public API reads SAT/SAB and writes ACIS records only when all structures are supported; export raises for unsupported entities. Its ACIS-to-mesh route explicitly emits flat polygonal faces, says curved faces are lost, and `vertices_from_body()` bounds are exact only for polyhedra, approximate for curved faces. | Admit ezdxf as an exact-version carrier/parser observer only for records its API actually decodes. Do not use flat-face output, mesh-derived bounds, or successful `load()` as a curved B-rep oracle. Preserve per-body unsupported-node/error counts and exact input/output hashes; keep analytic dimensions and closed-solid results on the independent semantic-reader/kernel lane. |
| [IxMilia/dxf public support matrix and writer caveats](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf) | The repository declares DXF R10–R2014 coverage with named entity omissions (including MESH and SURFACE) and separately warns that several typed entities, including 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY, may not open in AutoCAD when written. This is a project declaration, not a peer execution for libdxfrw's file. | Use IxMilia only for matched direct-DXF cells where its own matrix says the operation/entity/version is in scope. A peer parse or save is not an acceptance result; for a positive writer result, require strict reopen plus the existing target-consumer gate and compare source-handle disposition rather than total entity counts. |
| [LibreDWG repository contract](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) | The repository describes broad DWG reading but notes some advanced R2010+ objects can be skipped; it also reports newer DWG writer limitations/CRC failures. Tool directions differ: `dwg2dxf` coverage is not `dxf2dwg` coverage, and `dxf2dwg` is documented as R2000-only. | Keep LibreDWG comparisons bound to exact tool, revision, direction, target version, entity, and property. It remains a useful independent structural comparator for eligible fields, but cannot serve as a generic modern-DWG writer oracle or ACIS semantic oracle. Never count an unavailable version/direction as a negative test. |
| ACadSharp [issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) and linked [PR #1240](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1240) | The open issue reports silent loss of DWG-read 3DSOLID/REGION records during DXF writing, including blocks that then contain no geometry. The report names ACadSharp 3.4.9; linked work and current releases are different revisions, so it is a peer failure report, not verified behavior of current master or a libdxfrw defect. | Retain the existing modeler object/owner/INSERT census and output-disposition requirement. Each source body must be classified as preserved, explicitly refused, or omitted with a diagnostic; verify both block definition contents and INSERT references after strict reopen. Do not infer semantic success from document load, global counts, or a peer issue. |
| GDAL [DWG driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dwg.html) and [DXF driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | GDAL's DWG route depends on ODA Teigha. The DXF OGR route tessellates several curves and inlines/merges INSERT geometry by default; `INLINE_BLOCKS=FALSE` exposes block/reference fields, while 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY/SURFACE are skipped unless AC1027+ 3D-extensible mode returns raw ASM bytes and a transform. | Keep GDAL optional and dependency-attributed. For any future block-graph comparison, pin `INLINE_BLOCKS=FALSE`; for modeler carriers, pin `3D_EXTENSIBLE_MODE=TRUE` and score only the raw bytes/transform. Record OGR projection/tessellation losses; exclude the DWG route as independent of ODA-based comparison and exclude either route as a whole-document CAD or B-rep oracle. |

owner/payload links, interpreted B-rep, and rendered/imported geometry as

## Deeper/broader LibreDWG/ezdxf SAT DXF framing and terminal-block crosscheck (2026-10-20; research only)

This source-level pass expands the prior SAT-boundary review from a single
question (“space-aware or byte-budget cuts?”) into separate, observable
questions: which group codes carry SAT lines and continuations, where a
serializer cuts each value, how SAT-v1 caret escapes are represented, whether
SAB-to-SAT conversion retains its terminal block, and what an independent
reader reconstructs. Source inspection is not execution or acceptance evidence.

| Primary source | Source observation | Evidence limit and plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk [2024 3DSOLID DXF table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm) | The published table describes group 1 as proprietary data in multiple lines under 255 characters, and group 3 as additional lines when the preceding group-1 string exceeds 255 characters. | This is the published DXF carrier contract; it does not specify token-aware cut points, the SAT-v1 caret transform, or downstream acceptance of a payload split at a particular byte. Do not infer SAT grammar from the carrier table alone. |
| ezdxf [v1.4.4 ACIS source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozman/ezdxf/v1.4.4/src/ezdxf/entities/acis.py) | `tags2textlines()` treats group 1 as the start of a SAT line and appends following group-3 chunks. `textlines2tags()` writes each line as group 1 up to 255 characters, then group 3 chunks of up to 255. The same source documents SAT on older DXF profiles and SAB/ACDSDATA for 2013+. | A pinned independent serializer/parser gives a useful structural reconstruction comparator for group-1/3 streams. It is not an ACIS geometry kernel or native CAD acceptance oracle; its profile and release must be recorded. |
| LibreDWG mutable [`out_dxf.c` master source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/master/src/out_dxf.c#L2641-L2728) | In `dxf_3dsolid()`, each emitted SAT line uses `GROUP(1)`; it prefers an existing newline before the current value limit, otherwise uses a maximum 255-byte cut. It applies the SAT-v1 caret-space transformation while writing. This implementation path does not emit group 3 for these SAT chunks. | For a long logical SAT line, this differs from the group-1/group-3 continuation behavior described by Autodesk and used by ezdxf. Whether LibreDWG's repeated-group-1 form is accepted for such lines remains unverified. Treat it as an implementation observation, not a normative alternative or proof of native acceptance. `master` is mutable; capture an exact commit/tag and tool version before any comparator run. |
| LibreDWG SAB conversion and [`NEWS`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | `dwg_convert_SAB_to_SAT1()` splits converted data into 4096-byte storage blocks, records the final block, and writes a zero-size/null terminator. Its source comment says the prior missing `+1` dropped the final block and could make a one-block SAT body empty; NEWS independently records the 3DSOLID/REGION DXF-export fix. | This demonstrates a concrete peer regression class and a valuable generated boundary case. It is not evidence that libdxfrw shares the defect. Reuse the local length/boundary matrix and assert all bytes, including the tail, survive; do not add a persistent fixture. |
| ACadSharp [PR #1150](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1150), existing local [`writeDxfSatTextValue`](src/libdxfrw.cpp) and [writer matrix](tests/modeler_dxf_writer_matrix_tests.cpp) | The open ACadSharp proposal reports SAT before-2013 output using groups 1 and 3 and proposes whitespace-aware cuts. Local libdxfrw uses group-1/3 values with a 255-byte budget, preserving SAT-v1 caret-space pairs atomically while otherwise allowing a token to cross a value boundary. Existing generated cases already check boundary lengths, token-crossing/adjacent-space, ASCII/Binary encoding, reconstruction, and refusals. | The proposal is unmerged, local tests prove only local round-trip, and LibreDWG's group-1-per-line policy differs for long-line framing. There is no newly confirmed local defect. Reuse existing tests; compare source wire tags separately from reconstructed SAT lines and from consumer acceptance. |

### Implementation-ready refinement — one composed checkpoint, no per-slice peer gate

1. Keep the current local fast-test cadence and production writer behavior.
   The newly surfaced group-code disagreement is a research question, not a
   reason to block the next implementation slice or change serialization.
2. At the existing PAR-07/S8 composed SAT checkpoint, create ephemeral inputs
   locally from scratch. Cover: multiple short SAT lines; a line exactly at
   the 255-character edge; a long line with a token spanning that edge; spaces
   immediately before/after the edge; a SAT-v1 caret escape at the edge; and a
   payload whose SAB-to-SAT conversion leaves a final partial 4096-byte block.
   Reuse the existing matrix and add coverage only if an exact source/test
   inventory shows one of these controls is absent.
3. For each candidate, record (a) exact ordered group-code/value lengths,
   (b) group-1/group-3 reassembly into SAT line boundaries, (c) exact payload
   hash and final-byte/tail preservation, (d) strict parser result, and
   (e) native/ODA disposition only at the already planned composed checkpoint.
   Keep structural parsing, SAT byte preservation, ACIS semantic geometry,
   and native acceptance as distinct evidence lanes.
4. At that checkpoint only, pin the LibreDWG commit/tag and ezdxf release;
   run no more than the minimum generated discriminator set needed to tell
   repeated-group-1 framing from group-1/3 continuation and to expose a lost
   terminal block. Do not download or commit third-party DWG/DXF files. If an
   optional binary or application is unavailable, record `NOT_RUN` /
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; retain local results and move to the next ready local
   plan item.
5. After each implementation slice is committed, update the progress ledger
   and its receipt, report the passing fast checks and remaining queue, and

   availability a stop condition. Only revise the serializer policy if

## Implementation progress — 7S.3 DWG GROUP dictionary indexes (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

GROUP admission repeatedly scanned pending NOD and GROUP vectors; each GROUP
frame then scanned the emitted dictionary and emitted-frame vectors again.
Registration also requested an exact-size frame-vector reserve on each GROUP,
which could repeatedly move all earlier frames.

The writer now keeps lazily derived hash indexes for pending NOD names/child
handles, normalized GROUP names/handles, emitted GROUP dictionary handles,
and emitted GROUP frame handles. Authoritative vectors retain their prior
insertion order and validation semantics; rollback invalidates derived views
after restoring checkpoint state. `writeDwgObjects()` reserves the frame vector
once after callbacks have registered all groups. Frame membership is staged
before output and removed if frame emission fails. The existing generated
GROUP selector now includes 128 groups and checks dictionary order, callback
order, handles, names, owner, and ordered member handles across AC1015, AC1018,
AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032. This is an average-complexity improvement,
not a wall-clock benchmark or a format support claim.


## Implementation progress — 7S.3 entity-frame checkpoint (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

`dwgWriter15::encodeEntity()` previously called the comprehensive compound
checkpoint for every entity. That copied document-wide class, object, block,
table, GROUP, and owner ledgers whose size grows with the drawing, making
ordinary entity emission repeat work proportional to accumulated state.

Entity writes now take a bounded checkpoint of the byte buffer, object-map
length, sticky frame/EED flags, and current/pending frame provenance. On a
failed frame, rollback removes only that frame's published object handle and
the owner/INSERT membership actually appended by the current write. The full
checkpoint remains in use for class-associated entity handles and for all
larger compound/public transaction boundaries. The existing generated
ownership-index selector now verifies that a normal line write does not
request a full checkpoint and exercises byte/map/owner-membership rollback.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip --parallel 2  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_block_owner_membership_index$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1)
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_block_record_xref_roundtrip$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1)
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1, 3.18 sec)
git diff --check -- src/intern/dwgwriter15.cpp src/intern/dwgwriter15.h tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md  PASS
```

No persistent fixture, external drawing, peer runtime, native CAD application,
full CTest suite, wall-clock benchmark, or support promotion was added/run.
This is a complexity reduction supported by the checkpoint-call control, not a
quantified throughput claim. Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78**; J256,
J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and

An end-to-end call-path audit found that `dwgRW::encodeEntityForWrite()`
still created and retained a full `CompoundWriteCheckpoint` around every
entity, negating the writer-local checkpoint reduction for actual facade
callbacks. Added a writer capability for retained last-entity rollback:
AC1015+ writer15 and the AC1024+ writer24 path now retain only frame bytes,
object-map length, error/provenance state, and the exact owner/INSERT
membership appended. The facade uses that record for its own failure guard
and `rollbackLastDwgObjectWrite()`; unknown/custom writer implementations
continue using the full compound snapshot. Compound INSERT/POLYLINE and
explicit public transactions remain on their existing full boundaries.

The existing generated owner selector now exercises facade writes at AC1015
and AC1024, asserts zero full checkpoint calls, injects a post-frame facade
failure, and calls explicit last-write rollback; each case checks that bytes,
object map, and model-space membership return to the pre-write state.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3 fixed-frame OBJECT transaction fast path (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

An OBJECT callback audit found that fixed one-frame objects still entered
`writeObjectTransaction()` and cloned the growing document-wide writer
checkpoint for each callback. Added a shared bounded frame-only transaction
for the fixed `ACDBPLACEHOLDER`, `VBAPROJECT`, `IMAGEDEF`, `LAYOUT`, `DICTIONARY`,
`XRECORD`, and `BLOCKREPRESENTATIONDATA` routes. It snapshots
the current frame boundary and keeps full rollback for any explicit handle
associated with a custom DWG class. IMAGEDEF's caller-owned table state is
captured/restored on failure and remains tracked for an outer user transaction;
LAYOUT, VBA PROJECT, ACDBPLACEHOLDER, DICTIONARY, XRECORD, and
BLOCKREPRESENTATIONDATA are encoded from local/copy state and do not mutate the
caller object. The seven audited encoders
emit no deferred GROUP, MLineStyle, or custom-class ledger entries after their
frame.

The existing generated `--block-owner-membership-index` selector now verifies
all seven ordinary facade routes produce frames with zero comprehensive
checkpoints. It makes the facade's frame-receipt step fail after valid IMAGEDEF, DICTIONARY,
XRECORD, and BLOCKREPRESENTATIONDATA frames have been emitted, then verifies frame bytes, object-map /
emitted-handle-index cardinality, and (for IMAGEDEF) the caller's original
handle/owner fields are restored. DICTIONARY and XRECORD are admitted only
after checking their writers: each uses a fixed ODA type, local EED/reference
vectors, one frame, and no post-frame side ledger. This exercises the same
rollback boundary the production facade uses if a writer reports an incomplete
frame receipt. A separate negative control gives DICTIONARY an explicit handle
already associated with a custom class; its reserved-handle rejection occurs
under exactly one comprehensive checkpoint, proving the safety fallback is
still active.


## Implementation progress — 7S.3 single-frame INSERT rollback checkpoint (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

`dwgRW::writeInsert()` used a comprehensive writer snapshot even when the
record had no ATTRIB children and no SEQEND, although that route emits exactly
one entity frame. For writers advertising `supportsLastEntityWriteRollback()`,
that shape now uses the retained frame checkpoint already used by ordinary
entities. INSERTs with attributes, preserved legacy empty sequences, or writers
without the rollback contract keep the existing comprehensive path. Class-
associated handles still take `dwgWriter15::encodeEntity()`'s internal full
fallback.

The facade snapshots the caller's pre-allocation state before assigning an
automatic handle or normalizing the empty SEQEND metadata. On frame-receipt
failure it restores that original state after writer-frame rollback. On
success it replaces the post-normalization mutation entry with the original
state in both implicit rollback and an enclosing caller-mutation-tracking
transaction. The existing `--block-owner-membership-index` selector verifies:

- one ordinary no-attribute INSERT adds a frame and owner/insert-index entries
  with zero full checkpoints;
- a forced missing frame receipt removes frame bytes, object-map/emitted-handle
  membership, owner membership, and insert-reference membership, while
  restoring caller handle and SEQEND fields;
- an auto-handle INSERT inside an explicit outer transaction rolls back to the
  original caller state and removes its frame/index entries, with exactly the
  outer transaction checkpoint and no additional facade-level snapshot.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip -j2  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^(libdxfrw_dwg_block_owner_membership_index|libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip|libdxfrw_dwg_block_record_xref_roundtrip|dwg_dxf_issue_1410_cross_codec)$' --output-on-failure  PASS (4/4)
```

No fixture, CTest registration, dependency, external runtime, native CAD
application, full suite, wall-clock benchmark, or support promotion was added
or run. The checkpoint count is deterministic work evidence, not measured
throughput. Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284,
J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The shared
worktree remains broadly dirty and `.git` is read-only, so this slice is
uncommitted.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3 POLYLINE frame-batch rollback (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

`dwgRW::writePolyline()` emitted its parent, vertices, and SEQEND as atomic
frames but wrapped the entire chain in a document-wide `CompoundWriteCheckpoint`.
For `dwgWriter15`-family writers that advertise retained entity rollback, and
only when none of the preallocated frame handles is explicitly class-associated,
the facade now retains the compact per-frame checkpoints and rolls the contiguous
batch back in reverse order. The writer verifies the object-map suffix, emitted
handle set, common BLOCK_RECORD owner, owner-list suffix, and absence of INSERT
references before mutating any rollback state. This preserves one-owner ordering
and derived GROUP-target-index invalidation without copying document-wide class,
block, dictionary, and object ledgers for each polyline.

Writers without the retained-frame contract and polylines with class-associated
handles continue through the comprehensive checkpoint fallback. Explicit outer
transactions still use their one full public checkpoint; the polyline adds no
second facade snapshot. Failed encoding, failed frame receipts, and injected
SEQEND failure restore frame bytes/maps/indexes and the original caller handles
and vertex state.

The existing `--block-owner-membership-index` selector was extended (no new
CTest registration) to assert:

- a two-vertex polyline writes four correctly-role-labeled frames with zero full
  checkpoints, then implicit rollback preserves a pre-existing LINE and restores
  the entity/map/owner state;
- a missing vertex frame receipt and an injected SEQEND-stage failure each roll
  the entire successful frame prefix back and restore all caller handles;
- an enclosing caller-mutation-tracking transaction adds exactly its one
  checkpoint and rolls back the polyline state.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip -j2  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_block_owner_membership_index$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1)
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^(libdxfrw_dwg_block_owner_membership_index|libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip|libdxfrw_dwg_block_record_xref_roundtrip|dwg_dxf_issue_1410_cross_codec)$' --output-on-failure  PASS (4/4)
```

No drawing fixtures, CTest registrations, dependencies, peer runtimes, native
CAD applications, full suite, or wall-clock benchmark were added or run. The
zero-checkpoint count is deterministic work evidence, not a throughput claim.

## Deeper/broader text-output boundary and source-path review (2026-10-20; generated fast controls)

This follow-up traced the open LibreDWG #1408 and #1412 reports from their
primary issue pages, inspected the two linked #1412 commits, revisited the open
#1414 TV/TU policy question, then matched each reported layer against local
writer and generated-test owners. No peer executable or issue drawing was
downloaded or run. These are implementation comparisons, not normative DXF
rules and not evidence that the same defect exists here.

| Peer report / layer | Local source and test evidence | Plan disposition |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [#1408](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1408), ASCII physical-record framing for CR-bearing TEXT/MTEXT | The report says some complex CR-bearing values produce a literal CR in a DXF value line, an empty physical line at the next group-code boundary, and a dropped adjacent character; its drawing is not publicly attached and the reporter says a simple bare-CR case does not reproduce the reported shape. Local `dxfWriterAscii::writeStringImpl` rejects CR/LF/NUL before emitting a group. MTEXT’s field-aware path maps LF/CRLF to `\\P` and refuses a bare CR. The existing MTEXT selector now includes a generated issue-shaped payload containing formatting, caret commands, a CR, and following text across AC1018/AC1021/AC1032, ASCII/Binary, and both writer policies; each case requires refusal before any bytes are written. Existing facade controls also verify unchanged destination on refusal. | No local defect found. Retain fail-closed ASCII framing and field-specific MTEXT newline semantics; do not adopt blanket caret escaping or claim semantic parity with the unavailable drawing. Do not add another generic framing suite. If the TEXT writer route changes, add a focused TEXT semantic/sentinel case under its existing owner. |
| LibreDWG [#1412](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1412), transformed C-string length / zero-length value framing | The issue reports a peer C helper that writes transformed bytes without terminating at the final byte and later calls `strlen`; it also identifies a zero-length transformed-value case. Linked commits [5abbe5d](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/commit/5abbe5dc25208c87e7c2da2b6aa402d54f2193b1) and [aafb376](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/commit/aafb376e0bd0b75b5b06a2e04a7c7dd65a741474) respectively add the terminator and emit the empty group. Both commits exist, but the issue remains open and this does not identify which published peer release contains them. Local DXF string writing is length-bearing (`std::string_view`/explicit `ostream::write`); no analogous `cquote()`→`strlen()` path exists. New generated controls send C0 bytes and a literal `\\M+` sequence through transformation in AC1018/AC1032 ASCII and Binary, assert exact expected bytes and typed roundtrip, and read a following group as a sentinel. | No matching local C-buffer defect. Keep explicit-length writes and exact framed-value checks. Do not add allocator poisoning or port a C-specific workaround. Revisit only if a capacity-based or NUL-scanned transformed buffer is introduced. |
| LibreDWG [#1414](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1414), pre-R2007 `TV` versus R2007+ `TU` escape expansion | The report remains an unresolved policy question: its peer `VALUE_TV` and `VALUE_TU` paths disagree for `\\U+XXXX`, while the issue itself notes that generic strings and MTEXT may not share one harmless interpretation. Existing local generated integration covers source AC1018/TV and AC1021/TU DWGs with TEXT, MTEXT, rooted XRECORD, and following LINE/XRECORD sentinels, exporting strict AC1027 ASCII and inspecting both semantic values and raw target bytes. The selector passes, but it is a local reader/writer roundtrip, not an independent policy oracle. | Preserve the source-storage-path × target-version × field-role split. Keep current escaping behavior observational until a normative field-specific rule or independent reader/native witness resolves the policy. Do not blanket-expand every `\\U+` substring or promote text interoperability from self-roundtrip. |

### Cross-project evidence reconciliation

A broader source refresh against [LibreDWG 0.14.1 NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS), the current [ACadSharp issue reports #1297](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1297) and [#1299](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1299), and [ezdxf 1.4.5 documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) does not justify a new local finding. LibreDWG's release history records concrete HATCH path-state, rational spline-knot/weight, bounded 3DSOLID arithmetic, and final inline-SAT-block export fixes; use these as existing PAR-05/PAR-07/PAR-19/PAR-22 regression selectors, not evidence of a matching libdxfrw defect. ACadSharp #1297 is an unresolved AC1032 whole-file AutoCAD rejection with no established causal field; #1299 is a versioned DWG→DXF spline complaint without public knot/control/weight expectations. Keep them attached to the existing native-writer and SPLINE evidence gates. ezdxf's release is a DXF route (R12–R2018 by its docs), and `ezdwg` explicitly uses it as the DXF serializer; that makes the two outputs one DXF-writer lineage, not independent votes. None supplies ACIS/AcDs semantic or B-rep evidence. These mutable documentation/issues are scoped by their stated release/profile and remain non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3 INSERT/ATTRIB frame-batch rollback (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Attribute-bearing INSERTs and preserved legacy empty-ATTRIB sequences previously
used a comprehensive `CompoundWriteCheckpoint` around every write, even though
the encoded parent/child/SEQEND records are contiguous entity frames. For
`dwgWriter15`-family writers advertising retained entity rollback, `writeInsert()`
now retains one compact checkpoint per published frame for both compound
shapes. `rollbackEntityFrameBatch()` validates the complete object-map suffix,
emitted-handle membership, common BLOCK_RECORD owner list, and (only on the
first INSERT frame) the reverse block-reference vector/index before changing
any state. Frames are then removed in reverse order. Writers without that
contract and class-associated frames still use the comprehensive fallback;
ordinary single-frame INSERT behavior remains unchanged.

The existing `--block-owner-membership-index` generated selector now verifies:

- a two-ATTRIB INSERT publishes Parent, Attribute, Attribute, and SEQEND receipt
  roles, records one target-block reverse reference, and uses zero full
  checkpoints;
- explicit last-write rollback removes bytes, object-map/emitted-handle state,
  owner membership, and the target block's insert-reference indexes while
  restoring the caller's INSERT and ATTRIB state;
- an injected missing receipt after the parent and first ATTRIB, and an injected
  SEQEND failure after both ATTRIBs, each roll back the exact successful prefix
  and allow a clean retry;
- a class-associated INSERT using explicit handle `0xF100` and class 500 takes
  the comprehensive fallback; a missing receipt after the INSERT and first
  ATTRIB restores class-owner/raw-instance/emission ledgers and both block
  ownership/reference indexes, then retry and explicit rollback succeed;
- a preserved AC1015 empty-ATTRIB sequence uses the same two-frame rollback
  contract and restores its original sentinel handles;
- an enclosing caller-mutation-tracking transaction adds exactly its single
  comprehensive checkpoint, with no additional INSERT snapshot.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip -j2  PASS
build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip --block-owner-membership-index  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^(libdxfrw_dwg_block_owner_membership_index|libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip|libdxfrw_dwg_block_record_xref_roundtrip|dwg_dxf_issue_1410_cross_codec)$' --output-on-failure  PASS (4/4)
```

No external or new persistent drawing fixture, CTest registration, dependency,
peer runtime, native CAD application, full suite, or wall-clock benchmark was
added/run. Zero full-checkpoint counts are deterministic work evidence, not a
throughput measurement. Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78**; J256, J260,
J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The
shared worktree is broadly dirty and `.git` is read-only, so this slice is
uncommitted.

**Self-unblock:** the class-associated INSERT fallback and injected-failure
rollback are now covered by the generated selector, including retry and
explicit rollback. Continue the 7S.3 transaction audit at the next compound
public writer boundary; keep full snapshots wherever the bounded receipt does
not enumerate every mutated ledger. External qualification and semantic
evidence remain non-blocking.

<a id="implementation-progress-7s3-image-compound-receipt-and-rollback-boundary-2026-10-20-generated-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>

## Implementation progress — 7S.3 IMAGE compound receipt and rollback boundary (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The existing `writeImage()` outer `CompoundWriteCheckpoint` is required: the
operation emits IMAGEDEF, class-registered IMAGEDEF_REACTOR, and IMAGE entity
frames as one public transaction. The direct writer calls for the first two
frames previously trusted only their boolean results; they now also require a
valid object-frame receipt. A missing intermediate receipt rolls back the full
envelope before returning failure. On success, `writeImage()` now marks its
retained facade transaction as compound-checkpoint-owned; this corrects the
last-write rollback selector, which otherwise chose the entity-only rollback
and left IMAGEDEF/REACTOR records and custom-class ledgers behind.
Known unsupported DataStorage flags on supplied IMAGEDEF/REACTOR inputs are
rejected before taking that document-wide snapshot, because this preflight
cannot mutate writer state.

The existing `--block-owner-membership-index` generated selector now checks:

- injected IMAGEDEF_REACTOR receipt failure after IMAGEDEF emission restores
  all object bytes/maps, emitted handles, and class-instance ledgers;
- injected IMAGEDEF receipt failure restores the first emitted frame and
  caller-visible IMAGE state before later frames can be written;
- unsupported DataStorage flags on either supplied definition preflight to
  refusal with zero comprehensive snapshots and no writer/caller mutation;
- injected final IMAGE receipt failure after all three frames were emitted
  restores the same graph and caller-visible IMAGE state;
- a clean retry creates the expected three-frame graph and class association,
  then explicit last-write rollback removes all three frames and restores the
  original caller fields;
- every admitted file-backed IMAGE attempt takes exactly one comprehensive
  checkpoint (the outer atomic boundary), including failures and retry, while
  known unsupported-payload refusals take zero.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip -j2  PASS
build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip --block-owner-membership-index  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^(libdxfrw_dwg_block_owner_membership_index|libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip|libdxfrw_dwg_block_record_xref_roundtrip|dwg_dxf_issue_1410_cross_codec)$' --output-on-failure  PASS (4/4)
```

No external or new persistent drawing fixture, CTest registration, dependency,
peer runtime, native CAD application, full suite, or wall-clock benchmark was
added/run. The single full checkpoint is retained for atomicity; deterministic
checkpoint counts are not throughput measurements. Findings/subplans remain
**141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The shared worktree is broadly dirty and
`.git` is read-only, so this slice is uncommitted.

**Self-unblock:** IMAGE transaction coverage is now closed for intermediate
receipt failure, final-frame failure, retry, and explicit rollback. Continue the
facade audit found no additional multi-frame public writer boundary beyond the
already-audited INSERT, POLYLINE, and IMAGE paths. The remaining generic OBJECT
wrappers are single-frame but can mutate shared ledgers, so retain their full
snapshots unless each callback's affected ledgers and rollback receipt are

## Implementation progress — 7Y.2b typed/raw finite-underflow parity (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The raw ASCII numeric validator in `src/libdxfrw.cpp` previously rejected every
`ERANGE`, although the typed ASCII reader accepts finite underflow. Raw numeric
preflight now rejects only failed/full-token parses and nonfinite results, so
underflow to zero and finite subnormal values follow the typed-reader policy.
The raw lexeme remains emitted exactly as supplied; this changes admission, not
formatting or precision. Overflow remains rejected. The separately
string-backed ARCALIGNEDTEXT parser retains its legacy `std::stod`-compatible
`ERANGE` behavior, as specified by 7Y.2's context split.

Generated numeric controls cover typed and raw underflow-to-zero, the smallest
positive subnormal, exact raw spelling preservation, malformed/comma-decimal
input and overflow refusal, and destination preservation on failure.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_numeric_locale_tests -j2  PASS
build-gcc/tests/libdxfrw_numeric_locale_tests  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_numeric_locale$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1)
```

No fixture, CTest registration, dependency, peer runtime, native CAD application,
full suite, or support promotion was added/run. Findings/subplans remain
**141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The shared worktree is broadly dirty and
`.git` is read-only, so this slice is uncommitted.

gate passes. Keep ARCALIGNEDTEXT's legacy conversion semantics isolated, and
continue with the next implementation-ready local item; external platform
