## Deeper/broader open-source route completeness and 3D semantic ceiling (2026-10-20; research only)

This source review reconciles the screened DWG/DXF and ACIS projects by the
stage they actually implement. It extends the existing PAR-07/S8 comparator
and consumer gates; it does not establish a new defect or imply that the
screened set represents every open-source project. Sources reviewed include
the [LibreDWG project contract](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg), the
[ACadSharp operation/version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp), its
[reported 3DSOLID/REGION DXF-writer omission](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195),
the [ezdxf ACIS API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) and
[renderer limits](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/addons/drawing.html),
[CADMPEG's format pipeline](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg),
[`cq-acis`'s parser/shape contract](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis),
the [OCCT commercial-component boundary](https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/discussions/1157),
and [FreeCAD's DXF/DWG consumer documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md).
No peer binary, native CAD application, kernel, package, or external drawing
was run or downloaded for this pass.

| Route | What the source supports | Evidence ceiling and plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG | Its current project documentation separates broad DWG decoding (with some advanced R2010+ objects potentially skipped) from DWG writing and the narrower version support of individual tools. Its NEWS describes AcDs/AcDsPrototype_1b support as incomplete and records a brute-force extraction path for newer SAB payloads. | Keep it as a direction-, revision-, version-, and object-scoped structural comparator. A decoded entity shell, emitted DXF, or successful process exit does not prove AcDs carrier preservation or solid semantics. |
| ACadSharp | The README publishes distinct DWG/DXF read/write version columns (including no declared AC1021 DWG writer); its issue #1195 reports 3DSOLID/REGION omission during DXF output in a named older release. Reader APIs expose notifications, but the matrix and issue do not establish current per-entity behavior. | Select only exact supported route cells and record notifications plus source-handle disposition. Treat the old issue as a failure shape, not a claim about current master. Do not infer geometry from document load or aggregate counts. |
| ezdxf | The DXF library exposes ACIS SAT/SAB records and inspection/export routes; its ACIS documentation limits parsed structure, requires an external library to create ACIS data, and its drawing add-on says it does not render ACIS or provide a 3D rendering engine. | Useful for strict DXF structure, exact carrier extraction, and bounded record-level checks. Not a general ACIS editor, B-rep kernel, or semantic/native acceptance oracle. |
| CADMPEG / `acis-core` / `cq-acis` | These projects parse selected bare SAT/SAB/ASM profiles; CADMPEG and `acis-core` also expose bounded record/reference or neutral-B-rep paths, while `cq-acis` constructs only its documented geometry subset through CadQuery/OCCT. | Feed them only an independently associated extracted carrier after profile/signature selection. Parsing, reference closure, a valid kernel shape, and independently expected geometry metrics are separate outcomes. Check parser/source and kernel lineage before counting independent evidence. |
| OCCT | The open-source core and the separately distributed commercial exchange components have different format coverage; the official component catalog puts ACIS SAT/SAB exchange outside the ordinary open-source core. | Do not assume a stock OCCT/FreeCAD install is an ACIS reader. Any authorized commercial translator is an optional, license-bound route, not a reproducible open-source gate or a required dependency. |
| FreeCAD | The documented DWG route converts to DXF and then uses the selected DXF importer. The current documentation says the stock importer cannot read ACIS/SAT solids and gives only a subset of supported explicit DXF entities. | Keep native FreeCAD Linux/Windows qualification on explicitly supported 2D/3D DXF entities, keyed by converter, importer, build, and platform. It cannot unblock the ACIS/AcDs semantic gate. |

### Refined evidence handoff (existing plan owners only)

For each modeler body, retain the already planned staged result rather than a
single “3D supported” boolean:

1. **DWG/DXF container:** strict parse, version/profile, and byte-range bounds.
2. **Object graph:** source entity identity, owner/block membership, AcDs
   record key, unique record selection, and no ambiguous or orphan association.
3. **Carrier:** exact SAT/SAB bytes, encoding/signature, save version, record
   family, transform, and target-output disposition.
4. **Independent parser:** only an exact admitted bare-carrier profile; report
   unknown/unreachable records and diagnostics, not just successful parse.
5. **Geometry semantics:** require a complete supported body and independently
   authored analytic expectations (for example, dimensions, volume, area,
   centroid, bounds, and transform). Kernel validity alone is insufficient.
6. **Consumer:** pin the actual application/import route and assert the
   observable object/shape. Keep this independent from parser readback.

Use existing generated fast tests for the local container, graph, carrier, and
writer contracts per slice. Spend the composed external checkpoint only when
one exact payload matches a candidate's published profile and a separate
expected-value path exists. A missing profile, application, platform, or
independent expectation is `NOT_APPLICABLE`/`NOT_RUN`/`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`, then
self-unblock to the next local item; do not add dependencies or externally
sourced drawing fixtures, and do not let any one stage promote another.

This review adds no numbered finding, top-level subplan, test, fixture,
dependency, peer execution, or support promotion. Findings/subplans remain
**141 / 78**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain explicitly
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. ODA v5.4.1 and Autodesk references
remain authoritative for DWG/DXF byte-layout claims.

## Deeper/broader peer-route reconciliation and evidence ceilings (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass widened the source screen across independent DXF parsers, spec-led
DWG readers, ACIS decoders, and downstream CAD consumers, then reconciled each
route with the existing PAR-07/S8 comparator register. Most candidates were
already inventoried; this is a completeness and evidence-grade correction,
not an exhaustive census of every CAD project. Sources reviewed include
[`dxf-parser`](https://github.com/gdsestimating/dxf-parser),
[Kabeja](https://github.com/jpgiance/Kabeja),
[QCAD's bundled `dxflib` source](https://github.com/qcad/qcad/blob/master/src/3rdparty/dxflib/src/dl_entities.h),
[`dwg-rs`](https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/dwg-rs),
the versioned [`go-cad` module report](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/unitedrhino/go-cad%40v0.0.0-20261001090957-ddd91eea9618),
[`cq-acis`](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis), and the
[FreeCAD DXF importer contract](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md)
plus its [confirmed multi-layout report #22214](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/22214).
For the carrier boundary, Autodesk's [3DSOLID DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm)
remains the format source; peer pages are not normative.

| Route family | Source-grounded result | Plan consequence / evidence ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| DXF parsers and callback readers | `dxf-parser` documents a text-in/object-model-out parser with “most 2D entities,” partial MTEXT/XData, and explicit 3DSOLID and leader gaps. Kabeja describes DXF-to-SVG conversion, incomplete entity coverage, and text problems. QCAD `dxflib` exposes callback/data structures for supported records, not a complete retained document model. | These are useful only for named DXF fields/entities and projection behavior. A parse/render success, missing output object, or callback count cannot certify full drawing retention, binary DXF, DWG, or modeler semantics. Select only a route that actually represents the property under test. |
| Spec-led DWG readers | The current `dwg-rs` README labels the reader pre-alpha and reports 19 sample drawings with per-version decoded/skipped/errored counts (3,911/525/9); it also describes exact per-record data-stream boundary checks and names remaining decoder failures. The aggregate changes when the corpus denominator changes. | Use its exact pinned revision for container/record-boundary or named decoder differentials only. Report version-specific denominators and each record disposition; never translate decoded percentages into semantic support or compare changing aggregate rates as a benchmark. |
| LibreDWG-derived gold comparisons | The versioned `go-cad` report advertises 37 DWG files, 34 strict rows, and field-level agreement with LibreDWG JSON. That is evidence of another implementation path and a reproducible differential procedure, but the expected values are still the selected LibreDWG oracle. | Admit as a question-specific structural comparator after pinning module/source and corpus provenance. Shared oracle output does not constitute independent ground truth, independent geometry expectations, or native-consumer acceptance. |
| ACIS readers and kernels | `cq-acis` describes an experimental SAT/SAB reader and conversion of a selected geometry subset to CadQuery/OCCT; unsupported records remain raw or fail conversion. It does not read DWG containers or establish AcDs-to-entity ownership. | Keep its stages separate: profile recognition, record/reference closure, shape construction/validity, and analytically expected geometry. No stage can substitute for container association or consumer acceptance. |
| Native DXF consumers | FreeCAD documents separate C++ and legacy Python DXF importers, an explicit C++ entity subset, and no stock ACIS-solid import. Confirmed issue #22214 reports a multi-layout import limitation on a named C++ importer route. Autodesk's 3DSOLID contract separately lists proprietary modeler data and a soft-owner history handle (group 350). | Pin importer/backend, build, platform, options, and entity family. The layout report is a consumer-route limitation, not proof of malformed libdxfrw output; test layout fidelity at the application stage separately from emitted DXF structure. Preserve ACIS bytes, history references, owner association, and semantic geometry as separate assertions. |

### Readiness delta (existing PAR-07/S8 and consumer owners only)

1. Keep the route register closed to candidates that fail the exact-operation
   test: identify direction, version, entity/object family, and whether the
   tool returns raw records, a typed model, rendered projection, or native
   geometry before scheduling a comparison.
2. For any selected peer, record immutable source/artifact identity, license,
   source lineage, input provenance, decoder diagnostics, and per-source-record
   disposition. Same-family forks, wrappers, and consumers do not add
   independent codec votes; a shared gold oracle must be labelled as such.
3. Preserve the existing fast-first sequence: generated local leaf controls
   and affected focused selectors per slice; one composed comparator or native
   checkpoint only when the exact route and independent expected-value path
   exist. Do not add peer runtime dependencies or externally sourced drawing
   fixtures. A missing platform/profile/oracle is recorded `NOT_RUN` or
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`, then implementation self-unblocks to the next local
   source-backed item.
4. No candidate in this pass changes any support claim. J256, J260, J268,
   J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

This reconciliation adds no numbered finding, top-level subplan, test,
fixture, dependency, peer execution, or support promotion. Findings/subplans
remain **141 / 78**. ODA v5.4.1 and Autodesk references continue to govern DWG
and DXF format-layout claims; the source review cannot replace local tracing,
independent semantic expectations, or platform qualification.

## Deeper/broader capability-matrix and evidence-denominator reconciliation (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass rechecked public capability statements from four complementary
open-source routes against the plan's existing PAR-07/S8 comparator and
consumer gates: [ACadSharp](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp),
[IxMilia.Dxf](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf),
[GNU LibreDWG](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/), and
[ezdxf](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/). The result is a stricter
interpretation of peer claims, not a new libdxfrw defect. These projects expose
different file forms, version ranges, read/write directions, entity coverage,
and recovery/retention behavior; a version matrix or broad entity count alone
cannot establish parity.

| Route | Current primary-source statement | Evidence limit and plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ACadSharp | Its mutable README publishes separate DXF/DWG reader/writer matrices across AC1009–AC1032. The matrix claims DWG read/write for many versions, but not DWG writing for AC1021; it also advertises ASCII and binary DXF. | Treat as a candidate route for exact pinned, direction-specific structural comparisons only. A matrix cell is a project declaration, not a test result for every entity, object graph, file profile, or consumer. Record the immutable source/package and the tested file/entity denominator before using a result. |
| IxMilia.Dxf | Its README describes DXF/DXB, not DWG; declares DXF R10–R2014 support except MESH, MLEADER, SURFACE, TABLE, and VIEWPORT; and documents AutoCAD writer caveats, including entity-specific required fields and R13 compatibility concerns. | Limit any use to a named DXF version/entity and direction. Do not use it as an AC1021+ or DWG comparator, nor treat successful typed parsing as preservation of unsupported records. For writer checks, include strict target-consumer acceptance separately from peer self-read. |
| LibreDWG | The current manual documents broad DWG/DXF tooling but explicitly qualifies DXF writer stability and AutoCAD interoperability; its own reader/writer coverage statements are version- and operation-specific. The manual also describes DXF and DWG command-line conversion routes. | Keep it as a useful, distinct structural comparator only for the exact supported operation/version. A successful conversion, decode count, or LibreDWG-generated expected value is not independent semantic ground truth; retain per-record decoded/skipped/errored/unsupported dispositions and provenance. |
| ezdxf ACIS | The current ACIS documentation states that only a limited set of ACIS entities is supported; unsupported entities become `NONE_ENTITY` and their data is lost, and arbitrary ACIS cannot be loaded and re-exported. It documents SAT for DXF R2000–R2010 and SAB for R2013+. | Admit only an exact supported-carrier profile for raw/typed-structure comparison. Require explicit unsupported-record counts and payload-retention checks. Do not treat this path as a general SAT/SAB oracle, analytic B-rep witness, or consumer qualification. |

### Implementation-readiness refinement (existing PAR-07/S8 and consumer owners)

Before a peer result enters the evidence ledger, bind it to the tuple
`(file form, version, direction, entity/object family, strict-or-recovery
mode, retention disposition, peer revision/artifact, consumer route)`. Record
per-source-record outcomes as decoded, preserved raw, intentionally skipped,
rejected, recovered, or unresolved; never collapse these into an aggregate
“supported” count. Keep these independent acceptance layers separate:

1. strict container/section parse and bounded record framing;
2. typed field values plus raw preservation/refusal for unsupported content;
3. object ownership, dictionary/reference closure, and block membership;
4. exact SAT/SAB or other carrier bytes and save-version/profile;
5. independent geometry semantics where the claim is 3D; and
6. named application/importer acceptance on the stated platform.

Use this refinement in the existing source-selection and composed-checkpoint
steps only. Fast local generated controls remain the implementation loop;
pin/build a peer only when its exact route covers a current question, and run a
consumer checkpoint only when its input profile and expected result are
available. If not, record `NOT_RUN` or `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and self-unblock to
the next local item. Do not add peer runtimes, external drawing fixtures,
tests, or a larger routine validation gate from this documentation refresh.

This review adds no numbered finding or top-level subplan, changes no
implementation order or support claim, and leaves counts at **141 findings /
78 subplans**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain explicitly
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. ODA v5.4.1 and Autodesk references
remain authoritative for format-layout claims; peer capability pages only
select candidate routes and do not supersede normative field layouts or local
trace evidence.

was cloned or built, no peer binary or CAD application was run, and no external

## Implementation progress — 7F.1b schema-3 observation count-domain matrix (2026-10-20; generated fast self-test, uncommitted)

The 7F.1b typed-result validator applies unsigned range checks to scalar
counters, nested named summaries, integrity rows, byte-prefix lengths and
frame-coverage totals. Its previous fast mutation controls exercised
bool/negative/overflow values at a scalar counter, but did not directly prove
those same domain rules across the nested observation families.

Extended the existing dependency-free runner self-test with a valid synthetic
schema-3 observation containing retained named and integrity rows, then built
a deterministic list of 50 unsigned-count paths. For each path, the self-test
rejects `true`, `-1`, and `2**64` (150 malformed variants total). This covers
both named-summary families, row-local instance and prefix lengths, all
integrity aggregate counts and uint64 row values, the logical-handle bound,
all frame dispositions, and each scalar observation counter. The positive
seed validates before mutation, so a malformed test fixture cannot make the
negative controls pass for an unrelated reason.

Focused validation:

```text
python3 -B tools/run_qualified_differential_v2.py --self-test  PASS (0.28s)
python3 -B -m py_compile tools/run_qualified_differential_v2.py    PASS
git diff --check -- tools/run_qualified_differential_v2.py        PASS
```

No production behavior, schema, manifest, fixture, dependency, CTest, peer or
native run, or support claim changed. Findings/subplans remain **141 / 78**;
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and
non-promoting. No commit was created in this shared worktree.

**Self-unblock:** count-domain validation is locally covered across every
schema-3 observation family. Continue the remaining 7F.1b readable
partial/opaque/readback integration gates and 7AG.4 compile-contract
qualification; missing external/native routes do not block those local steps.

This freshness pass revisits the existing provisional ACadRust comparator
screen. It checks the issue lifecycle, published crate, matching mutable

onto local parser-hardening, ownership, and writer-disposition owners. The
published crate and `Cargo.toml` identify 0.6.5 (released 2026-10-18),
but the fetched docs.rs `latest` source and repository README identify 0.5.5;
this audit's initial claim that docs.rs also served 0.6.5 is superseded by the
source-freshness correction below. Older issue reports still name 0.6.3 or
0.6.4; the distinction matters because 0.6.5's changelog claims several
relevant fixes, while those reports remain open or have no public
private-corpus retest. These are comparator-admission inputs, not measured
libdxfrw gaps.

| Peer report / route | Fresh source finding as of this review | Implementation-ready consequence and limit |
|---|---|---|
| ACadRust issue [#124](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/124), malformed header-section size | Open issue, originally reproduced against crate 0.6.3 with an AC1024 drawing emitted from a small local-from-scratch model and single-bit mutations to the header-section size. The report distinguishes unchecked header slicing and a possible negative-size-to-`usize` conversion from object-record count problems. Maintainer commits `3097271`, `4838a42`, and `a80defa` are linked, with a request to re-check; no public independent retest is recorded. | Keep this separate from object-body count/allocation checks. At the existing DWG hardening owner, verify checked-add/range validation for header subsection offsets and lengths, then use a locally generated input plus a small set of field-targeted mutations. Require a bounded `BAD_READ_FILE_HEADER`/equivalent failure, never process termination or an out-of-range slice. Do not copy peer-specific byte offsets; derive locations from the local generated encoding or test the bounded helper directly. |

The recipe describes both a misread count clamped to 100,000 with zero-filled reads and a stream-derived allocation request reported at about 12 TiB. Commit `53007f3` and a maintainer request to re-check are present, but the issue is not closed and no independent current-package result is published. | Existing object-frame/parser-hardening coverage remains the owner: check count × element-size overflow before allocation/iteration, bound reads by the frame and remaining input, and ensure failed reads cannot become plausible zero-valued geometry. Preserve strict failure unless the local object is known optional and its complete frame boundary is established. A peer's cap or threshold is not a format rule. |
| ACadRust issue [#133](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/133), missing owner re-homed into model space | Open issue based on a private 351-file corpus and a same-reader comparison of ODA-converted DXF; the report alleges a 0.6.3 recovery path placed orphaned anonymous dimension-block contents into model space. Never invent model-space membership merely to increase entity counts. Retain or reject/report the orphan according to the local preservation contract; exclude it from valid model-space geometry and consumer counts until resolved. Keep ODA comparison advisory and do not use the private corpus. |
| ACadRust issue [#134](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/134), AC1032 auxiliary-object bounds | Open issue reports 70/351 private AC1032 inputs rejected by 0.6.4 at MLeader context or associative records after stricter record bounds. Commit `0e46236` is described as preserving bounded auxiliary objects after decode failures; the maintainer says it may help and requests a private-corpus retest. The issue supplies neither those files nor a public aggregate retest. | Do not weaken record/section bounds to recover apparent compatibility. In the existing bounded object-frame owner, reject an object-local parse only when the frame remains trustworthy; preserve a bounded opaque/unsupported record with a warning and continue only when the remaining boundary is independently known. Otherwise retain strict stage failure. No blanket “failsafe success” or global decoder recovery is justified. |

The commit title indicates that unknown records may be reported unsupported rather than preserved byte-for-byte. | Treat the closed report as a historical failure shape, not proof that the current release is lossless. In any exact pinned comparison, count each source handle and table record as preserved, intentionally refused with a diagnostic, omitted with a diagnostic, or silently lost. A diagnostic is acceptable where raw-to-DWG conversion is unsupported; silently dropping it is not. Compare named colors and table XDATA independently from custom-class payload retention. |

Do not claim those mutable views and the release are aligned. The package is MPL-2.0 and lists parser/compression/encoding/parallel dependencies; its broad version matrix remains a declaration, not per-family measured coverage. Release notes and a self-round-trip are not independent verification. Do not install it or add a peer CI lane for routine local slices. |

### Readiness delta for existing plan owners

1. **PAR-07/S8 comparator admission:** pin crate checksum and matching source

   zero-filled/fabricated entity. If the current fast owners already prove an
   invariant, link them and do not add a duplicate test or CTest.
3. **Record recovery:** recovery may retain an auxiliary record only if its
   raw bytes and exact frame end are trustworthy. Test one damaged optional
   frame followed by a valid sentinel record; assert the sentinel remains
   aligned. If the boundary cannot be established, fail closed rather than
   scanning for a plausible next marker.
4. **Graph and output loss:** owner closure and writer loss are separate
   denominators. Generated controls should distinguish resolved/null/missing
   owners and preservation/refusal/diagnostic/silent omission for unknown
   classes, color-book names, and table/block XDATA. Counts alone cannot
   conceal re-homing or field loss.
5. **Cost and continuation:** run only the existing generated selector and
   its owning fast CTest for any uncovered invariant. Full suites, sanitizers,
   fuzz budgets, peers, and native consumers remain at their scheduled
   checkpoints. If an external peer artifact or proprietary corpus is
   unavailable, mark that route `NOT_RUN`, retain the candidate gate, and
   continue local work.

tag sequence, intact modeler carrier, decoded ACIS graph, valid B-rep, and
named-consumer acceptance are five different outcomes.

It does not establish B-rep validity or authorize treating proxy graphics as modeler bytes. | Keep subclass-local parsing, payload ordering, history-target resolution, and proxy-graphic accounting as separate assertions. The group-350 target must be checked after strict output/readback, not inferred from payload equality. |
| Current local `DRW_ModelerGeometry::parseCode` and `dxfRW::processModelerGeometry`, plus `tests/modeler_dxf_writer_matrix_tests.cpp`, `tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp`, and `tests/dwg2dxf_adapter_tests.cpp` | Code dispatches groups by tag and retains ordered payload chunks, history handle, and proxy graphics separately. Existing controls cover canonical writer order, group-350 retention, proxy group-310 separation, chunk boundaries, and following-record continuity. A new generated AC1027 input now places ordered group 1/3 chunks before group 70 within the modeler subclass and asserts the proxy/history/sentinel values; it also rejects odd-length group-310 data before callback publication. This is a test-coverage refinement, not a reproduced parser defect. | Keep the permutation case in the existing modeler test owner/focused selector; do not add a new subsystem or numbered finding. ## Implementation progress — 7S.3 OBJECT frame-receipt freshness (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The remaining facade OBJECT audit found that both
`writeObjectTransaction()` and `writeFixedObjectFrameTransaction()` used the
writer's last committed frame receipt as proof for the current call. A
successful no-op could therefore inherit an older receipt. Both transactions
now require a valid receipt with a new producer generation and growth past
their pre-write output boundary.
The only intentional no-frame success is exposed explicitly for `MLINESTYLE`,
whose writer returns success for an already emitted same-name/same-handle
style; the no-op must leave output size unchanged.

The generated `--block-owner-membership-index` selector proves both sides:
an identical MLINESTYLE retry returns success without changing bytes or the
object map, and both generic and fixed-frame transactions that append a non-frame
byte are rejected despite the still-available prior receipt; rollback restores
the original buffer and object map. Both rejections also clear
the receipt through their existing rollback boundaries. The caller audit found
no other intentional no-frame success among the generic/fixed
OBJECT adapters; GROUP and handle-less PLOTSETTINGS retain their previously
documented full-checkpoint requirements for side-ledger correctness.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip -j4  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dwg_block_owner_membership_index$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1)
git diff --check -- src/intern/dwgwriter.h src/intern/dwgwriter15.h src/intern/dwgwriter15.cpp src/libdwgr.h src/libdwgr.cpp tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp DWG_DXF_3D_SUPPORT_PLAN.md DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md docs/research/7s3-object-frame-receipt-freshness-fast-slice-2026-10-20.json  PASS
```

No full suite, external/native runtime, persistent drawing fixture, dependency,
or support promotion was added/run. Findings/subplans remain 142/78; J256,
J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. The shared
worktree is broadly dirty and Git metadata is read-only, so this slice is
uncommitted.

**Self-unblock:** the generic/fixed OBJECT caller audit is complete: only the
documented MLINESTYLE duplicate route intentionally succeeds without a new
frame, while GROUP and handle-less PLOTSETTINGS retain their side-ledger-safe
checkpoint policy. Continue to the next locally actionable implementation
item; preserve strict frame freshness by default and do not wait on deferred
external qualification.

## Implementation progress — 7S.3 single-frame custom-class OBJECT rollback (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Extended the fixed-frame OBJECT transaction helper to retain only the class-
instance ledger state for its explicit registered handle. If frame receipt
validation fails after `finishObject()` has moved a custom-class instance from
pending to emitted, the helper now rolls back the byte/object-map suffix and
restores that one handle's owner, pending/emitted membership, and class emission
count. It no longer copies the document-wide class maps for this bounded case;
full checkpoints remain for compound writes and malformed/inconsistent class
associations. `writeDbColor()` now uses this audited one-frame route.

The generated `--block-owner-membership-index` control registers a DBCOLOR,
injects a missing receipt after frame emission, verifies its complete class
ledger and frame rollback, then retries and verifies exactly one successful

It does not provide an authentic external CAD-produced sample, prove all modern carriers share one layout, or qualify libdxfrw semantics; keep it advisory and do not rely on LibreDWG conversion to produce modern AcDs positives. |

### Implementation-readiness and time-saving rules

1. Before any optional peer execution, inspect the manifest/lockfile and classify (a) container parser, (b) entity decoder/model, (c) downstream projection/renderer, (d) geometry kernel, and (e) native-consumer layer. Same-codec applications stay in one PAR-07 lineage even when their later rendering or output code is separate. Record exact version/commit; mutable `main` and advertised matrices are not pins.
2. Prefer source inspection and the existing fast local tests over installing multiple same-lineage apps. A new peer run is justified only by a concrete unmet question (for example, an exact DXF projection or native application acceptance case) and must state input hash/version, scope denominator, unsupported/skipped records, strict versus recovery mode, and output disposition. No periodic full-suite run is added.
3. Where a downstream output is useful, compare only the shared documented subset and use locally authored expected geometry/semantics. Raster pixels, GeoJSON, a successful parse, and same-parser round-trip are supplemental; each loses or transforms information, and each requires a declared projection denominator. Preserve unknown/unrendered content as a separate outcome.
4. For 3D, keep DWG/DXF container extraction and AcDs ownership separate from SAT/SAB/ASM parsing, shape construction, topology validity, analytic expectations, and consumer acceptance. Do not substitute commercial OCCT exchange for the requested independent open-source evidence without explicit approval and an exact entitlement/build route. Keep unresolved external-platform gates `NOT_RUN` / `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`, then self-unblock to a bounded local task that does not assert the missing claim.
5. Peer drawing corpora remain external. Tests may use only fixtures already present in LibreCAD/libdxfrw or locally generated from scratch with documented generator parameters and independently authored expected values. The new consumer routes add no fixture, CI dependency, runtime, test code, or validation cadence.

No top-level subplan, finding, or support status changes result from this screen. Historical totals remain **141 findings / 78 subplans** as cited in the current top-level register; this research does not recompute the older count discrepancy. ## Deeper/broader AC1024 BLOCKLOOKUPACTION peer-sequence crosswalk and semantic boundary (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass refreshes PAR-133 from four different evidence layers: the local
authoritative ODA specification, a current peer DWG reader, that peer's DXF
writer, LibreDWG's object inventory/manual, and Autodesk's public behavioral
description. It does not decode or publish a new object.

### Cross-source findings and limits

* The local reference copy is ODA *Open Design Specification for .dwg files*,
  v5.4.1. A text extraction search for `BLOCKLOOKUPACTION`, `BlockLookupAction`,
  dynamic blocks, lookup actions, and lookup tables finds no class-specific
  layout. This is only a search result, not proof that no general object or
  custom-class rule applies; ODA remains authoritative, and the exact field
  order is unresolved.
* ACadSharp's mutable `master` DWG object reader reads the common block-action
  prefix, row and column BitLong counts, `rows × columns` variable-text row
  values, then `columns` column records. Each candidate column record is three
  BitLongs, a bit, variable text, a bit, variable text; one final bit follows.
  Its current DXF writer serializes a corresponding model as group codes 92/93,
  row-major group-302 values after a group-301 marker, then one column sequence
  (94/95/96/282/305/281/304) per column, and group 280 at the end. Reader/writer
  agreement within one implementation is useful internal consistency, not an
  independent producer or normative DWG source.
* LibreDWG 0.13.4's manual inventories `numrows`, `numcols`, a `lut` array,
  `exprs` as variable text, and the final B280 flag. It does not specify their
  exact byte/bit ordering or all version-dependent cardinalities. LibreDWG's
  current `objects.in` marks `BLOCKLOOKUPACTION` `UNSTABLE`, and current NEWS
  says unstable objects are not preserved via DXF. Thus its type recognition
  and field inventory are not a round-trip oracle.
* Autodesk's Block Editor help describes a lookup action as creating a lookup
  table associated with a lookup parameter. This establishes the feature's
  user-level role, not DWG field order, dynamic evaluation semantics in this
  sample, or 3D geometry behavior.
* The existing local AC1024 trace has exact class/object identity and bounded
  cursor diagnostics, but stops at a preflight before the first candidate
  value. That failure plus peer differences identifies a plausible local
  shape/count issue; it does not prove ACadSharp's ordering for this object,
  explain every data/string cursor boundary, or justify a production decoder
  change. The sample's partial read and unrelated Classes CRC mismatch further
  prohibit using conversion as a complete-file result.

Sources: [ACadSharp DWG reader](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/master/src/ACadSharp/IO/DWG/DwgStreamReaders/DwgObjectReader.Objects.cs), [ACadSharp DXF writer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/master/src/ACadSharp/IO/DXF/DxfStreamWriter/DxfObjectsSectionWriter.cs), [LibreDWG 0.13.4 OBJECTS manual](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/OBJECTS.html), [LibreDWG current object registry](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/objects.in), [LibreDWG NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS), and [Autodesk Block Editor help](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENG/AutoCAD-Core/files/GUID-B69D58AD-7920-4198-AB2A-0E24B944F6CD.htm).

### PAR-133 implementation-readiness refinement

1. Preserve the current fail-closed parser and raw/opaque fallback. Do not
   substitute ACadSharp's peer layout or weaken the preflight based only on
   these sources.
2. Implement the next diagnostic as a non-publishing cursor probe on the
   already-local AC1024 sample. Snapshot/restore or clone both the object-data
   and versioned string buffers independently; record the starting and ending
   bit for each, plus the object data end and computed handle-stream start/end.
   Try only the peer-described candidate sequence and stop at the first bad
   buffer/read or declared-bound crossing. No semantic field or typed object
   may escape the probe.
3. A candidate is eligible for a production patch only if all required row
   strings and column records decode within their own stream bounds, the final
   bit is available, the data cursor does not enter the handle stream, and the
   result is repeatable on a second independently authored sample or an
   authoritative field-order source. A cursor that merely lands inside the
   body is not enough.
4. After field order is established, add generated non-square matrices (so
   row-major versus column-major order is observable), empty and long strings,
   zero/maximum/rejected dimensions, truncated string/data/handle streams, and
   a following-object sentinel. Keep resource limits checked before allocation;
   failures remain transactional and the following record remains readable.
   Register/use only the owning fast CTest for this narrow leaf, not the full
   suite per implementation slice.
5. Test lookup-table text retention separately from parameter dependency
   linkage, evaluator behavior, and resulting block-instance geometry. This
   object is dynamic/parametric block metadata; parsing it is not a 3D solid,
   ACIS, or B-rep capability claim. Require known lookup inputs and expected
   resulting block entities before claiming dynamic-block semantics.

This refines existing PAR-133 and PAR-07/S8 evidence boundaries only. It adds
no finding or subplan and does not change implementation order or validation
frequency. No external executable or drawing was run/downloaded; no fixture,
dependency, or support claim was added. The historical plan log contains both
141- and 142-finding assertions; this pass intentionally records no canonical
count until a plan-wide reconciliation. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. ODA v5.4.1 remains
authoritative for DWG byte layout.

### Readiness decision

Keep InventorLoader `SCREENED_NOT_ADMITTED` as an optional, exact-profile
candidate until it passes an unmodified, source-pinned run and the existing
untrusted-input review is resolved. Earlier plan work already identified a
reachable Python `eval` path, shell/face fallback, unsupported blend/helix/law
cases, and shared FreeCAD/OCCT kernel lineage; this refresh does not clear any
of those limitations. Do not execute the add-on against customer data or
downloaded payloads. The candidate can only witness that a declared generated
SAT/SAB profile decodes into a measured shape through this parser/kernel path.
It cannot establish the DWG container, the DWG `AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b`
section, entity-to-AcDs key mapping, history-owner closure, arbitrary B-rep
validity, or native FreeCAD core acceptance.

### Implementation-ready sequence (optional composed checkpoint only)

1. **Admit the artifact before running it.** Resolve and record the exact
   InventorLoader commit SHA and source hash; check the active LICENSE and
   dependency closure; pin the FreeCAD and OCCT build; inspect the current
   `eval` call path and resource bounds. If direct `readText()` still needs
   the issue #110 caller-side lifecycle workaround, record the stock route as
   failed/unready and do not apply a local patch while calling it an
   independent pass. Keep a STEP-conversion result in a separately named
   profile.
2. **Reuse the existing known-body scratch recipe.** At the composed
   checkpoint, reuse the plan's already-scoped, pinned ezdxf 1.4.5
   AC1032/SAB recipe for two independently specified asymmetric rectangular
   prisms (`2×3×5` and `1×4×2` at distinct non-origin placements) and its
   analytic manifest. Do not add a duplicate unit-cube or routine CTest lane.
   Generate only in a unique temporary directory and only after the exact
   producer-artifact probe succeeds. The public #1411 `REGION` example is an
   alternate lead, not the default recipe or format authority. Do not add an
   AC1024/SAT profile until a separate exact producer/decoder profile is
   demonstrated. Record generator revision, input geometry, output file hash,
   DXF version, entity type, ordered payload lengths, and any group-350
   history reference. Never copy the issue attachment or persist a test
   DWG/DXF fixture in the repository.
3. **Isolate codec preservation from interpretation.** Parse the generated
   DXF with libdxfrw, serialize it, then compare the exact available SAT/SAB
   carrier bytes and entity/history references. For the modern DWG case, test
   AcDs section decoding, entity/key join, and SAB bytes as distinct stages;
   the InventorLoader parser does not cover these stages. Keep `3DSOLID`,
   `REGION`, and any other entity family as separate denominators.
4. **Measure semantic output without self-derived expectations.** Feed only
   the generated payload to the pinned candidate, first through its direct
   ACIS parser/build path and separately through its STEP-conversion path.
   Capture every source body/lump/shell and output shape; reject an apparent
   success that degrades to faces, wires, or open shells. For each authored
   prism assert non-null closed solid topology, kernel validity, positive
   volume, the authored analytic area/volume/bounds, and placement within the
   already-declared tolerance. These expectations come from the independent
   vertex manifest, not from the candidate's decoded mesh. Record units and
   transforms independently.
5. **Use fast negative controls, not a broad-suite gate.** Mutate only the
   generated payload (truncate a terminal chunk; remove or duplicate a
   generated AcDs association in the DWG-only lane) and require an explicit
   failure/disposition with no fabricated solid. Keep malformed tests gated
   behind the parser-safety review because this candidate is not yet trusted
   for arbitrary untrusted bytes. Run this lane once at the existing
   composed PAR-07/S8 checkpoint; do not add it as a routine dependency or
   full-suite job.
6. **Report narrow outcomes and self-unblock.** Record parser, carrier,
   semantic-kernel, optional STEP, stock-FreeCAD, and add-on consumer results
   separately. A passing prism profile does not qualify other ACIS classes,
   DWG versions, or the six external gates. If the optional route cannot be
   pinned, audited, or run, mark it `NOT_RUN`/`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and continue
   local bounded parser, graph, and loss-disposition work.

## Deeper/broader AC1024 SORTENTSTABLE and associative sibling graph (2026-10-20; research, local diagnostic, and bounded implementation progress)

### Decision and evidence boundary

This pass refines existing **PAR-06 / 7BV associative-object closure** and
**PAR-49 / 7G.3 owner-graph validation**; it adds no numbered finding or
top-level subplan. It corrects the interpretation of the next local blocker
after PAR-142: a SORTENTSTABLE owner extension dictionary is not necessarily a
single-entry dictionary. Autodesk documents `ACAD_SORTENTS` as the SORTENTS
table key and separately documents an object's associative network as a
network object owned by a special subdictionary under the object's extension
dictionary, with default key `ACAD_ASSOCNETWORK`. Therefore the simultaneous
presence of these keys is structurally plausible and should not, by itself, be
classified as malformed or as a SORTENTSTABLE alias. The exact associative
leaf graph and its preservation policy still need proof.

The local diagnostic used the existing
`tests/samples/AC1024/architectural_example-imperial.dwg` without copying or
modifying it. After PAR-142, the partial read reaches `validateSortEntsGraph()`.
The trace reports SORTENTSTABLE handle 8336, extension-dictionary/parent
handle 8331, owner `*U7` BLOCK_RECORD handle 8311, one reactor to 8331, and an
owner dictionary with two complete entries: `ACAD_ASSOCNETWORK` → 8332 and
`ACAD_SORTENTS` → 8336. The exact trace then shows dictionary 8332 owned by
8331, one persistent reactor to 8331, and one `ACAD_ASSOCNETWORK` entry →
8333. The object callback identifies 8333 as `ACDBASSOCNETWORK` with owner
8332. This is consistent with Autodesk's documented nested subdictionary
route, but the trace does not decode or prove every network/action/dependency
edge, does not establish semantic safety of omission, and does not establish
external sample provenance. The read remains partial-observed; the
associative-network shell is not retained by the DWG-to-DXF adapter.

The bounded validator change now accepts only the documented sibling-key
topology (`ACAD_SORTENTS` plus one `ACAD_ASSOCNETWORK`) after validating the
nested dictionary's identity, owner, reactor, sole key, and completeness.
It then rejects at the explicit stage
`SORTENTSTABLE ACAD_ASSOCNETWORK lacks safe DXF replay closure`. This moves
the local failure from a false topology/cardinality rejection to the actual
serializer-readiness boundary; it does not make the graph exportable.

The same run reports `operationSucceeded=true`,
`semanticCoverage=partial-observed`, 663 observed/published source frames, zero
entity/object parse failures, and 14 skipped `ASSOCDIMDEPENDENCYBODY` records.
The conversion still exits nonzero at export preflight. This is useful
diagnostic evidence only; it is not a successful conversion, completeness
result, regression fixture, or support claim. The sample remains where it was
and was neither copied nor modified.

### Broader implementation comparison

| Source | Current evidence | Consequence and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Autodesk [`AssocNetwork.GetInstanceFromObject`](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_AssocNetwork_GetInstanceFromObject_ObjectId__MarshalAsUnmanagedType_U1__bool__MarshalAsUnmanagedType_U1__bool_string.html), [`Networks of Actions`](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/OARX-DevGuide/files/GUID-BD833D49-DD90-4815-B576-8E7B5831A5BC.htm), [`DICTIONARY` DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-40B92C63-26F0-485B-A9C2-B349099B26D0.htm), and [`SORTENTSTABLE` DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-462F4378-F850-4E89-90F2-3C1880F55779.htm) | A BTR-associated network is reached through its extension dictionary and a special subdictionary, by default keyed `ACAD_ASSOCNETWORK`. A dictionary entry is a unique name/object mapping; the dictionary's hard-owner flag controls entry ownership, while object ownership, persistent-reactor links, and associative network/action membership are distinct edge roles. The SORTENTS table uses `ACAD_SORTENTS` and has its own owner/entity references. | This primary documentation supports accepting the two distinct keys and requires a typed edge model rather than a one-hop name/handle check. It does not supply the complete field grammar for every associative subtype or prove that dropping the branch is safe. |
| LibreCAD current bundled [`DWG_DXF_COVERAGE_INVENTORY.md`](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD/blob/master/libraries/libdxfrw/DWG_DXF_COVERAGE_INVENTORY.md) | The inventory calls itself deterministic source inventory, not byte-level conformance. Its DXF-object row for `ASSOCNETWORK` is `raw-preserved / yes / yes / fixture-needed`; its DWG custom-class row for `ACDBASSOCNETWORK` is `typed-custom / no / no / fixture-needed`. Other associative DXF rows have the same fixture-needed ceiling. | The DXF and DWG rows describe different adapters and must not be collapsed into a claim that the bundled fork retains a usable DWG associative graph. This is a source/dispatch map, not semantic correctness or standalone-upstream parity. |
| LibreDWG mutable [`objects.in`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/objects.in), [`NEWS`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS), and [manual](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | Current `objects.in` labels `ASSOCNETWORK` and `ASSOCGEOMDEPENDENCY` `STABLE`. The current manual still groups `ASSOCNETWORK` among “Unhandled (fields spec'ed, but broken/undertested)”; NEWS describes it in an older/new unstable inventory. | Status signals conflict across mutable source/docs. Before comparator use, pin an exact release/commit and inspect matching reader, DXF writer, tests, build flags, and class disposition. Neither a `STABLE` enum nor successful serialization is independent semantic qualification; no type layout or implementation code is copied. |
| Local `dwg2dxf/dx_iface.cpp`, `dwg2dxf/dx_data.h`, and generated adapter tests | DWG SORTENTSTABLE has a separate bounded typed membership receipt, distinct from the DXF raw companion. The validator accepts only the named sibling topology and rejects an incomplete/non-replayable associative route before publication. The DWG associative callback logs but does not retain this shell. | Keep DWG and DXF evidence routes separate: a DXF raw capture receipt cannot stand in for DWG decoding, and a parsed DWG shell cannot stand in for complete identity/owner/reference closure. Preserve fail-before-publication until the typed/raw graph is closed or an explicit atomic-omission policy is demonstrated. |

### Implementation-ready refinement (PAR-06/7BV × PAR-49/7G.3)

1. **Separate legal topology from serializer readiness.** Index the owner
   extension dictionary by normalized key and identity. Permit `ACAD_SORTENTS`
   plus the documented `ACAD_ASSOCNETWORK` sibling as distinct branches, but
   do not reduce the check to `entries.size() == 1`, ignore extra entries, or
   infer ownership from the key name alone. Preserve duplicate-key,
   duplicate-handle, cross-owner, and cycle rejection.
2. **Close the associative subdictionary before export.** Start from the
   exact observed route (BTR extension dictionary → `ACAD_ASSOCNETWORK`
   subdictionary → `ACDBASSOCNETWORK`) but do not generalize it to all
   drawings. Build typed edges for dictionary membership, object ownership,
   persistent reactors, network/action membership, and dependencies; preserve
   logical versus physical ownership as separate relations. Verify identity,
   version-specific field completeness, backlink reciprocity, and every
   referenced action/dependency under existing PAR-06/7BV bounds. Do not add
   guessed DWG type codes or parser fields; capture them from a real sample
   trace and check byte layouts against ODA v5.4.1. For any unparsed or
   unretained leaf, make the exact unsupported disposition visible.
3. **Choose an explicit output policy.** Preferred strict behavior is to
   retain and remap the complete associated branch, with exact graph identity
   readback. If the 2D converter intentionally permits partial output, only
   omit a branch when a bounded atomic projection removes its nested
   dictionary, every owned/linked child that cannot be emitted, and all
   inbound references—including any top-level-network relationship—and when
   the remaining evaluated 2D geometry is independently shown to be valid.
   This last requirement is an inference from Autodesk's documented network
   evaluation role, not a finding about this sample. Report each omitted
   source handle. If safe omission is not proven, refuse before destination
   publication; never strip just the `ACAD_ASSOCNETWORK` key.
4. **Generated test status and next discriminators.** The bounded slice now
   exercises the documented two-key/nested-dictionary shape in DWG-source
   and DXF-source graphs, both ASCII and Binary DXF output modes; checks
   fail-before-publication with a sentinel; and repairs the graph on the same
   adapter instance before a successful retry. Existing cases also cover
   extension-key aliases and owner/target failures. Still required when a
   serializer or omission route is implemented: a closed/resolved network
   readback; missing/non-dictionary subdictionary; dangling leaf;
   duplicate/case-folded alias; wrong owner/reactor; cycle; cross-linked
   top-level network; and full action/dependency closure. Keep these generated
   in-memory graphs; do not add/import a persistent fixture.
5. **Fast validation and self-unblock.** Build only
   `libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests` and `dwg2dxf` with the existing
   warning-as-error configuration; run the direct SORTENTSTABLE selector,
   `libdxfrw_sortents_adapter`, and the existing `libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures`
   regression once the shared adapter code is touched; run scoped
   `git diff --check`. On one later composed diagnostic, confirm only that
   export advances to the next graph guard or fails with the new explicit
   associative disposition. Do not run the full test suite or the 30-case
   AC1024 matrix for this bounded graph change. Then report the slice status
   and continue to the next local item; native and external qualification is
   not a prerequisite.

## Deeper/broader model-layout group-331 target-role audit (2026-10-20; research + local diagnostic)

### Decision

This pass identifies one local DXF-export preflight false rejection and adds
**PAR-142** under the existing **PAR-49 / 7G.3 layout-graph owner**; it does
not add a top-level subplan. The current validator interprets every non-null
LAYOUT group-331 handle as a retained, paper-space `DRW_Viewport` entity. A
local AC1024 trace instead captures `Model` LAYOUT handle 34 with group 331
target 148 (`0x94`), and captures handle `0x94` as a `DRW_Vport` table record.
The explicit `--allow-partial-dwg-read` conversion reaches export preflight and
is rejected because handle 148 is not an entity. This establishes a local
false-rejection path; it does not establish complete input reading or DXF
consumer compatibility.

The evidence is deliberately layered. ODA v5.4.1 describes the common 331
reference as a soft pointer to the last-active viewport and separately lists
the R2004+ layout viewport count/list; that passage does not name one target
class for every layout. Autodesk's DXF LAYOUT table likewise describes 331 as
the ID/handle to the viewport last active when the layout was current, without
specifying a universal class. ezdxf's internal layout documentation says the
modelspace layout requires (?) a VPORT table entity at group 331, explicitly
qualified as an apparent requirement rather than a normative rule. These
sources corroborate the observed model-layout route, but the proposed fix is
bounded by the local typed identity and must not relax the established
paper-layout checks. ([ODA DWG specification v5.4.1](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf),
[Autodesk LAYOUT DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-433D25BF-655D-4697-834E-C666EDFD956D.htm),
[ezdxf layout-management notes](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfinternals/layout_management.html))

The local diagnostic used
`tests/samples/AC1024/architectural_example-imperial.dwg` without copying or
modifying it. Its read observation reports `operationSucceeded=true`,
`semanticCoverage=partial-observed`, 663 observed/published source frames,
zero entity/object parse failures, and 14 skipped unsupported associative
class instances. Even with explicit partial mode, export fails at the LAYOUT
331 class check. The sample's provenance is not established in this review;
it remains diagnostic-only and is neither a new regression fixture nor
evidence for a support claim. Output was directed to a disposable temporary
directory and was not retained.

### PAR-142 — model LAYOUT 331 may reference the VPORT table

**Status:** `FAST_SLICE_IMPLEMENTED_AND_VALIDATED_UNCOMMITTED`; the original
local false rejection is corrected for the narrowly evidenced Model/VPORT
route, with paper-layout checks unchanged.

The route is in
[`validateLayoutGraph()`](dwg2dxf/dx_iface.cpp), where
`hasOwnedViewport()` searches only `mBlock`/block entity containers and then
requires `dynamic_cast<DRW_Viewport*>`, `PaperSpace`, and matching paper-space
BLOCK_RECORD ownership (with the narrow DWG current-paper-space ownerless
exception). The layout graph tests already cover paper layouts, missing or
wrong-class group-331 targets, cross-layout VIEWPORTs, reciprocal owner links,
and the current-paper-space exception, but the generated `Model` layout does
not set 331 to a VPORT table handle. The omission leaves a model-layout
reference shape untested.

Keep the correction inside existing PAR-49 / 7G.3; do not change DWG parsing,
DWG object type dispatch, `prepareDwgViewportProjection()`, or paper-space
ownership policy in this slice.

### Implementation-ready slice and speed boundary

1. Resolve the associated BLOCK_RECORD for each LAYOUT and classify the
   model-space route only when both identities agree: normalized layout name
   `MODEL` and normalized associated record name `*MODEL_SPACE`, including the
   reciprocal record-to-layout link. Do not branch on the LAYOUT name alone.
2. For that model-space route only, resolve nonzero group 331 by handle to
   exactly one captured `DRW_Vport` table record. Include VPORT handles in
   this target's identity/ambiguity check and reject null, duplicate, or
   cross-record collisions; do not require a particular VPORT name such as
   `*ACTIVE`, synthesize a `DRW_Viewport`, or treat the soft pointer as an
   ownership edge. Preserve zero/absent 331 behavior.
3. Leave paper layouts on the existing rules: target must be a unique
   paperspace `DRW_Viewport`, with its current owner/layout consistency or the
   already-bounded DWG current-`*PAPER_SPACE` ownerless case. A VPORT-table
   target on a paper layout, and a paper VIEWPORT/LINE/missing handle on the
   model route, remain rejected unless a separate source-backed rule later
   establishes otherwise.
4. Extend the existing generated
   `--layout-graph-read-contract` selector with an ASCII/Binary positive
   case whose Model LAYOUT 331 points to one VPORT table handle and whose
   paper layouts retain their existing VIEWPORT targets. Assert group 331
   survives strict re-import as the same typed handle role after output
   handle remapping. Register emitted VPORT table-row handles before writing
   LAYOUT objects so references use the actual emitted handle. Add negative
   controls for missing VPORT, wrong target class, duplicate/colliding handle,
   and the same VPORT target attached to a paper layout; every refusal must
   preserve the preexisting destination. Retain the present missing, LINE,
   cross-layout, and ownerless-DWG controls rather than replacing them.
5. Build only `libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests` and `dwg2dxf`; run the direct
   `--layout-graph-read-contract` selector, its existing
   `libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures` owner test, and scoped `git diff --check`. This
   bounded validation passed. Do not repeat the 30-case AC1024 matrix or full
   suite for this bounded graph change. At the later composed AC1024
   diagnostic, verify only that this preflight advances; the sample remains
   partial and has separate unresolved associative/SUN graph outcomes.
6. Record focused progress and a receipt, then self-unblock to the next local
   AC1024 object/carrier or PAR-07/S8 owner slice. This broad pre-existing
   dirty worktree includes overlapping files, so this slice is documented as
   uncommitted rather than risking an unrelated commit; isolate it before a
   later commit. Missing Linux/Windows native qualification, external geometry
   semantics, or any J-item evidence does not block this local correction and
   cannot be promoted by it.

This finding is a model-layout target-class false rejection, not a DWG reader
byte-layout defect. It adds no external-drawing fixture, dependency, peer
execution, native run, or support claim. The rest of the multi-layout graph
remains strict. Plan totals are now **142 findings / 78 top-level subplans**;
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain explicitly
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

### PAR-142 implementation progress (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

`validateLayoutGraph()` now builds a unique VPORT handle index and routes a
nonzero Model LAYOUT 331 through it only when the normalized layout name,
associated `*MODEL_SPACE` BLOCK_RECORD name, and reciprocal layout backlink
all agree. Duplicate/invalid VPORT handles, structural collisions, missing
targets, and collisions with retained entities fail closed. Paper LAYOUTs
continue to require their existing unique paperspace VIEWPORT and ownership
checks. The DXF VPORT writer now registers valid source table-row handles so
LAYOUT 331 is serialized against the emitted row handle rather than a stale
source value.

Generated ASCII and Binary controls cover valid Model 331 import/export/readback,
missing and entity-class targets, duplicate VPORT identity, VPORT/entity handle
collision, and refusal to attach a VPORT target to a paper layout. Existing
paper VIEWPORT ownership and negative cases remain active. Verified:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests dwg2dxf --parallel 2`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --layout-graph-read-contract`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures$' --output-on-failure`
- `git diff --check` scoped to the touched implementation/test/plan files

The selector and owning CTest pass; the two requested build targets compile
with `-Werror`. No external drawing fixture was added, and no full suite or
AC1024 matrix was run. This local behavior does not qualify the partial AC1024
diagnostic or any consumer semantics. No commit was made because many
pre-existing unrelated changes occupy the shared worktree and these source
files overlap prior implementation work. Next, self-unblock to the next
bounded AC1024 carrier/graph issue. All six external items remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — PAR-49/7G.3 AC1024 paper-space delimiter owner (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

A debug trace of the existing repository sample
[`visualization_-_sun_and_sky_demo.dwg`](tests/samples/AC1024/visualization_-_sun_and_sky_demo.dwg)
reached `readDwgBlocks` and then failed with `BLOCK/ENDBLK owner does not match
BLOCK_RECORD`. The trace showed the active `BLOCK_RECORD` named `*Paper_Space`
at handle `0x58`; its `BLOCK` and `ENDBLK` delimiters are named
`*Paper_Space0` and carry parent handle `0x58`. The reader classified the
delimiter name as paper space and required a null owner, rejecting the exact
owner handle of the active record.

The delimiter gate now accepts either the matching `BLOCK_RECORD` handle or,
for recognized model/paper-space names, the legacy ownerless form. A different
nonzero handle remains rejected, and the existing BLOCK/ENDBLK reciprocal
owner equality check remains in force. This is grounded in ODA v5.4.1 §20.2
(common entity handle/entmode rules) and §20.4.6–7 (BLOCK/ENDBLK common handle
data); those sections distinguish owner-bearing block definitions from
ownerless legacy model/paper-space forms. The generated test uses the library
writer to encode an AC1027 `*PAPER_SPACE0` BLOCK/ENDBLK pair owned by its
`*PAPER_SPACE` BLOCK_RECORD and exercises the full `readDwgBlocks` path.

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8 owner-reference disposition and null-owner contract (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The semantic adapter already emitted `owner` edges and typed `ownerHandle`
fields, but every edge remained only `observed`. The adapter now classifies a
nonzero owner target as `resolved` when its handle equals a captured record's
`sourceHandle`, and `unresolved` otherwise. Classification happens at result
serialization over the final captured record list, so an owner record reported
before its target is still resolved. Handle and block graph-node targets are
accepted by the disposition helper.

Null-owner representation follows the actual adapter contract: `DRW::NoHandle`
is zero, `addOwnerEdges()` emits no owner field or edge for it, and the result
uses `ownerHandle: null`. A zero-valued owner field, if received in an external
schema-3 result, is also validated as null and must have no owner edge. There is
no synthetic `null` edge disposition. The previous synthetic runner baseline
had an owner edge pointing to handle zero despite a null owner; it was corrected
to match the producer contract and its graph cardinalities.

The schema-3 validator now recomputes owner-edge resolution from the captured
records. Controls cover resolved and unresolved nonzero owners, target records
captured after the source, handle and block target nodes, absent/zero owners
with no edge, plus missing, duplicate, wrong-target, stale-disposition, and
zero-owner-edge rejection. A final review removed the unreachable legacy
`null`-disposition branch so the validator and schema vocabulary now agree:
null owners have no edge, and only nonzero edges are classified as
resolved/unresolved. These statuses establish handle-to-record presence only;
they do not establish that the target has the correct owner class, that the
target's reciprocal/container membership is valid, or that the document's
ownership graph is closed.

Focused validation:

```text
python3 -B tools/run_qualified_differential_v2.py --self-test  PASS
python3 -B -m py_compile tools/run_qualified_differential_v2.py  PASS
python3 -B tools/build_semantic_adapter.py --self-test  PASS (locked target and fresh standalone builds)
git diff --check -- tests/semantic_differential_adapter.cpp tools/run_qualified_differential_v2.py DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md  PASS
```

No full suite, peer executable, native CAD/kernel, or external drawing was
run. No fixture or dependency was added; production reader/writer behavior and
callback ABI are unchanged. The accepted schema-3 edge-disposition vocabulary
is now `observed`, `resolved`, and `unresolved`. Findings/subplans remain
**141 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain explicitly
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The slice remains uncommitted because
the shared worktree already contains broad unrelated modifications; committing
its source files would also include existing work. **Self-unblock:** continue
the next locally testable PAR-07/S8 carrier/owner item without waiting for
external semantics or native consumer availability.

This pass rechecked primary project documentation and issue evidence to
challenge whether a headline claim can be used as a parity denominator. It
found no new libdxfrw defect: the useful delta is a tighter rule for admitting
peer and downstream evidence. No peer checkout, executable, package, native
CAD application, geometry kernel, test corpus, or external drawing was run or
downloaded. Public `master` pages are mutable; where the source itself names a
release or pinned dependency, that identity is preserved below rather than

| Source / route | Fresh evidence and limits | Existing plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| GNU LibreDWG [repository README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) and [Texinfo manual source](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | The repository README describes `dwg2dxf` as about 90% coverage and `dxf2dwg` as about 80%, with `dxf2dwg` limited to R2000 and DWG writing to earlier versions through R2004. The manual separately says approximately 99% read/mostly-write coverage through R2018, while also stating that R2007 DWG writing is not implemented and the default writer uses R2004 or earlier. The pages do not publish a common entity/object denominator or a reconciled operation/version matrix. | Treat every percentage as non-scoring context. A LibreDWG comparison must pin the exact executable/source revision and score one direction × version × family × operation. Keep `dwgread`/DWG-to-DXF, `dxfwrite`/DXF-to-DWG, and DWG writer routes separate; don't use a project-wide percent or one route's read pass to qualify its writer. |

Issue #1253 reports that AutoCAD 2027 rejected DXF emitted by ACadSharp 3.6.35 even though more permissive readers accepted it; the report says it was checked with `accoreconsole` and compared against AutoCAD `DXFOUT`. Its individual HATCH group-47 discussion has a later correction for derived boundaries, so issue comments do not establish one universal writer predicate. This remains peer-reported evidence, not a run against libdxfrw. | Use it only to justify a distinct strict-consumer/output-syntax gate at the existing PAR-05/7BQ.5 checkpoint. The current libdxfrw README, by contrast, reports a specifically scoped FreeCAD 1.1.3 macOS arm64/C++-importer/PATH route using a generated AC1015 nonzero-Z LINE and explicitly leaves native Linux/Windows unqualified. **Plan inference from those documented limits:** the archived guide is route discovery only; its broad file-format statement cannot establish end-to-end fidelity for the listed importer routes or a current binary. | Keep FreeCAD evidence split into converter process/artifact, exact importer backend and settings, imported per-source records/coordinates, and modeler semantic outcome. ## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8 modeler history-target resolution disposition (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The preceding history-reference slice preserved each nonzero
`MODELER_GEOMETRY.historyHandle` as a typed graph edge, but labeled every edge
only `observed`. That was insufficient to distinguish a placeholder handle
node from a target record actually captured by the adapter. The result writer
now emits `resolved` when the target handle exactly matches a captured
record's `sourceHandle`, and `unresolved` otherwise. The classification runs
after read callbacks have populated the complete record list, so an object
appearing after its owning 3DSOLID is handled correctly.

The runner recomputes the same classification from `records` and requires
the edge disposition to agree. Nonzero handles still require one exact
`historyReference`; zero handles require none. Non-history edges remain
`observed`. These values mean only handle-to-record presence: they do not
prove the resolved record has the correct history-object class, that reciprocal
ownership/reference closure is complete, or that the ACIS B-rep is valid.

Fast controls cover both positive states (target record present after the
modeler and no captured target), null-handle/no-edge, missing and duplicate
edges, mismatched targets, stale resolved/unresolved labels, null-handle with
an edge, and misuse of a resolution disposition on an identity edge. The
linked C++ self-test checks target resolution independent of record order; the
dependency-free runner self-test checks disposition recomputation and rejects
tampering.

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S8 modeler history-reference evidence edge (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The semantic adapter already captured `MODELER_GEOMETRY.historyHandle` as a
typed field, but the normalized object graph omitted the corresponding
reference. That left group-350 history bytes/field evidence disconnected from
the graph used for closure and source/output comparison. The adapter now emits
an explicit `historyReference` edge from the modeler record to the exact
handle node for every nonzero history handle. The edge kind is distinct from
the record's identity `handleReference` and its database `owner` edge. A
missing target record is still represented as a handle node and is not
misreported as resolved.

The schema-3 validator now requires a typed `historyHandle` on each
`MODELER_GEOMETRY`, exactly one matching `historyReference` for a nonzero
handle, and no such edge for a zero handle. It rejects a missing edge,
duplicate edge, wrong target, null-handle edge, and a history edge attached to
a non-modeler record. This validates the observed handle relation only; target
object existence/type and history-graph closure remain separate evidence and
are not promoted by this slice.

The linked adapter self-test creates a synthetic modeler with a nonzero
history handle and verifies the edge independently of its payload carriers.
The dependency-free runner self-test directly checks a valid relation and the
negative controls above. The test-generated handle is not a valid ACIS model
or a fixture; it exists only to test evidence plumbing.
