<a id="deeperbroader-dxf-acis-carrier-history-and-consumer-geometry-evidence-2026-10-20-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader DXF ACIS carrier, history, and consumer-geometry evidence (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass separates four things that broad “3D support” statements can
accidentally collapse: the DXF entity record, its proprietary ACIS payload,
the entity's history-object reference, and a consumer/kernel's geometric
interpretation. The Autodesk DXF reference identifies `3DSOLID` as an entity
with an `AcDbModelerGeometry` subclass, modeler-format version group 70,
proprietary text payload in groups 1 and 3, then an `AcDb3dSolid` subclass
with group 350 as a soft-owner handle to a history object. Thus byte-preserved
payload alone does not prove history-edge preservation, and neither proves
valid solid semantics. ([Autodesk 3DSOLID DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm))

Current ezdxf documentation is useful as a route/capability screen, not a
format authority or semantic oracle. It documents SAT for DXF R2000–R2010 and
SAB for R2013+, says its ACIS interface reads both but writes SAT only, and
describes its solid-to-mesh example as losing faces with non-straight
boundaries; the bounding-box tool explicitly does not support ACIS entities.
The first two statements identify a capability asymmetry to test per
direction/version. The latter two mean a mesh or bounding-box result from that
route cannot be scored as exact curved B-rep equivalence. ([ezdxf ACIS tools](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html), [ACIS FAQ](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/faq.html), [ACIS entity limits](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/3dsolid.html), [bounding-box limits](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/bbox.html))

### Refined evidence record for PAR-07/S8

For every admitted producer/consumer run, record these dimensions separately:

1. **DXF record/carrier:** source and output DXF version; entity kind (`3DSOLID`,
   `BODY`, `REGION`, or a specific `SURFACE` subtype); presence/count/ordered
   byte lengths of groups 1 and 3; modeler-format group 70; and, for a modern
   carrier, whether the `ACDSDATA` section and SAB payload are present. Each
   field is `present`, `absent`, `malformed`, `unsupported`, or `not inspected`,
   not an implicit zero. Treat ezdxf's SAT/SAB version table as a test selector
   until version-authentic examples or authoritative format material confirms
   the precise transition.
2. **History/ownership edge:** capture group 350 exactly and classify its
   target as `null`, `resolved`, or `unresolved`; independently record whether
   the referenced object survived output and whether its own references close.
   Do not merge the group-350 history edge with the payload byte comparison or
   silently repair a missing edge. Use the normative “soft-owner” role from the
   Autodesk table; no stronger ownership semantics are inferred here.
3. **Payload disposition:** per entity, compare available source/output
   carrier bytes and report `byte-identical`, `transformed-with-recorded
   conversion`, `explicitly refused`, `diagnosed omission`, or `silent loss`.
   Keep SAT text and SAB binary as distinct encodings; a one-way ability to read
   SAB and write SAT is not a same-version round trip.
4. **Semantic result:** separately capture decoded topology/reference counts,
   independent analytic expectations (for example known primitive volume,
   area, and bounds), kernel validity, and named-consumer import result. Mesh
   projection, vertex extraction, or unsupported bounding-box calculations are
   diagnostic observations only; they cannot stand in for curved surface,
   closed-shell, or B-rep validity.
5. **Consumer configuration:** for FreeCAD, pin build/revision and direct
   importer route, record requested/effective options and import statistics,
   then inspect actual document properties. The confirmed open FreeCAD #30043
   report says the C++ importer can apply the active Draft Scale Multiplier to
   DXF text; retain the generated known-height TEXT control at the composed
   native checkpoint and classify this consumer-specific calibration outside
   ACIS semantics. Do not treat it as a libdxfrw defect. ([FreeCAD issue #30043](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/30043))

### Implementation-ready refinement and fast-path boundary

1. Extend the existing PAR-07/S8 evidence ledger—not the production API—with
   the five dimensions above. Reuse the current exact-route candidate record;
   only the denominator fields are added. Keep source blob/hash, exact
   producer/reader/writer builds, command/options, errors, and per-record
   dispositions alongside the dimensions.
2. For the local fast path, use generated-from-scratch controls only. Exercise
   group-1/group-3 continuation framing and group-70/group-350 capture with
   small synthetic records, plus negative controls for truncated continuation,
   duplicate/missing history target, and payload/output omission. These are
   wire/ledger controls, not valid ACIS geometry or format compatibility
   evidence. Keep temporary sample files outside the repository and clean them
   automatically; do not add downloaded/private drawings or external fixtures.
3. Admit SAT/SAB semantic comparisons only when the exact producer and
   consumer can decode the declared encoding. A route that converts a body to a
   polygon mesh must carry a lossy-projection label and cannot pass the exact
   geometry comparator. Require independently sourced expected geometry and a
   kernel validity result before making a B-rep semantic claim.
4. At the composed native checkpoint, run the small version/record cohort once
   per declared consumer route and report missing routes as `NOT_RUN` or
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. Keep FreeCAD's text-scale calibration as a separate
   option-sensitive control. Do not increase routine full-suite frequency or
   block local work on unavailable native applications.
5. If Autodesk's entity reference and pinned implementation sources do not
   establish the meaning or version gating of a byte, record `UNRESOLVED`, do
   not change parser/writer rules speculatively, and self-unblock to the next
   local 2D or carrier-disposition slice.

This research refines existing PAR-07/S8 carrier, ownership, semantic, and
consumer gates only. It adds no finding or top-level subplan, changes no
implementation order, changes no validation frequency, and adds no code, test,
fixture, dependency, peer run, or support claim. Counts remain **141 findings
/ 78 subplans**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain explicitly
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. No external drawing was downloaded or
committed. The ezdxf route observations are mutable project documentation and
must remain capability hints; Autodesk's DXF reference governs the documented
entity group layout, while ODA v5.4.1 remains authoritative for DWG byte-layout
questions.

## Implementation progress — 7F.1b schema-3 optional-field/capability consistency (2026-10-20; generated fast self-test, uncommitted)

Closed a schema-3 harness gap in the existing 7F.1b typed-result gate. The
runner now binds the optional modeler and surface fields to the already
validated side capability contract. For the reviewed target profile, absent
optional fields must remain absent and have exactly one matching
`semanticFields` / `excluded` / `adapterFieldCoverageExcluded` disposition.
For the standalone profile, each declared field must be present with the
expected type, including zero-valued chunk counts; zero data is not confused
with an unavailable adapter API. The check covers DWG source version, modeler
payload status, inline ACIS presence/byte count, DXF payload chunk count,
surface ACIS chunk count, and each declared payload-range bit offset.

Range-index iteration is bounded by the result's field denominator, and both
field and exclusion indexes must equal the declared range set. Thus fabricated
out-of-range bit-offset data and inflated range counts are rejected before a
large validation loop. The
runner self-test now covers valid target/standalone profiles plus negative
mutations for a fabricated target field, a missing target exclusion, inflated
range count, extra out-of-range target exclusion, fabricated target surface
field, out-of-range standalone bit-offset field, and omitted standalone
zero-counts for modeler and surface chunks.

## Deeper/broader FreeCAD effective import options and text-scale calibration (2026-10-20; research only)

This pass refreshed the native FreeCAD consumer lane against current primary
source and one current, confirmed DXF-import report. It does not revise any
DWG/DXF wire-format rule. It narrows an existing consumer qualification: an
application preference receipt is not by itself proof that the selected
importer applied that setting as intended, and a visible importer discrepancy
must not be misattributed to libdxfrw when the converter's DXF has already
passed independent syntax and structural checks.

### Source observations and evidence ceilings

| Source | Observation | Evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|
| FreeCAD `Import.readDXF` [binding](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Import/App/AppImportPy.cpp) | The current binding accepts a filename, optional document name, `ignore_errors` flag, and `option_source`; the source defaults `ignore_errors` to true, calls the DXF reader, recomputes the document, and returns importer statistics. The reader records several effective settings in its import-statistics structure. | Source/API inspection only; this was not run against an installed FreeCAD build. Use the explicit false value for the strict direct-binding profile and keep GUI/Open/Insert behavior as a separately named permissive route. |
| FreeCAD `ImpExpDxfRead` [implementation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Import/App/dxf/ImpExpDxf.cpp) | The C++ importer selects an option-source path and records options such as annotation import, manual scaling, layout objects, hidden blocks, layers, and colors in its statistics. | Returned statistics and an explicit configuration path improve reproducibility, but they do not prove semantic correctness of every imported property. Capture actual object properties as well. |
| FreeCAD issue [#30043](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/issues/30043) | Still open and labeled confirmed when reviewed. The reporter says C++ DXF import on FreeCAD 1.1.1 and a 1.2 development build applies the Draft Scale Multiplier to DXF text height; the expected result in the report is to retain the height supplied by the DXF TEXT record. | Peer-reported, confirmed consumer behavior, not reproduced here and not a normative DXF interpretation. The issue's sample was not downloaded. Pin any future run to its exact FreeCAD build and record actual imported properties. |
| FreeCAD [DXF importer guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and [import/export preferences](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Import_Export_Preferences.md) | The application has separately selectable C++ and legacy Python DXF importers with different feature sets; the stock importer does not interpret embedded ACIS/SAT solids. | Backend identity must remain explicit. This source does not provide ACIS/B-rep evidence and does not make either backend an independent DXF writer oracle. |

The source-backed improvement is test observability, not a new codec feature:
record the exact FreeCAD build, importer backend, `ignore_errors` setting,
`option_source`, requested preference values, returned import statistics,
warnings, and the final imported-object properties. A preference that was
requested but is not surfaced in returned statistics must be marked
`NOT_EXPOSED`; do not silently treat the requested value as the effective one.

### Existing-plan refinement and implementation-ready sequence

1. Keep this check at the existing composed native FreeCAD Linux/Windows
   checkpoint. Do not add a FreeCAD dependency, routine CTest, or peer/native
   run to implementation slices. Local parser and writer work continues while
   the platform gate is unavailable.
2. If the declared FreeCAD profile includes text, generate a small ASCII DXF
   from scratch in a temporary directory with a known-height TEXT entity and
   an independent geometric sentinel. Do not copy the issue attachment or
   commit the generated file. Independently parse and inventory the exact
   intermediate DXF before import.
3. Invoke the intended C++ profile explicitly through
   `Import.readDXF(path, document_name, False, option_source)`; capture the
   importer statistics and the imported TEXT's object type, height, placement,
   and text content. Pin and record the exact option-source tree and the
   Scale Multiplier value. If a non-unit multiplier changes file-authored
   TEXT height, record a FreeCAD consumer limitation for that build/profile;
   do not classify it as a libdxfrw serialization failure unless the
   independently parsed intermediate itself differs from the declared
   expected DXF values.
4. If the legacy Python importer is an intended supported consumer route,
   execute it as a separate profile with its own options and denominator. Do
   not blend its result with the C++ importer or infer one backend's behavior
   from the other's settings.
5. Preserve the existing 2D/3D separation: a FreeCAD import pass can qualify
   only the selected consumer profile. It cannot promote opaque ACIS carrier
   preservation, AcDs owner/key closure, B-rep semantics, or native solid
   acceptance. All absent independent routes remain `NOT_RUN` or
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and self-unblock to local implementation work.

## Implementation progress — explicit bounded partial DWG-read policy (2026-10-20; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Implemented the first local policy slice from the updated PAR-06/PAR-07/S8
sequence. `dx_iface::fileExport` now accepts a trailing source-compatible read
completeness policy: `Legacy` retains prior library behavior, the CLI selects
`RequireComplete` by default, and the exact `--allow-partial-dwg-read` opt-in
selects `AllowPartial`. Partial admission requires a successful, source-matched
DWG read receipt; finalized complete/partial frame status; zero pending,
deferred, staged, unresolved, or unrecognized dispositions; an exact bounded
frame-disposition denominator; a complete non-saturated integrity ledger; and
no retained integrity error. A generated negative control mutates a published
frame to pending and proves the incomplete ledger is refused without replacing
the destination. It does not weaken strict owner/reference checks,
source/target text gates, or output publication safeguards; unrecognized enum
values also fail closed before publication. The CLI warns that
partial output may omit source content and is not a completeness/support claim.

The existing locally generated malformed-HATCH/following-LINE control now
proves strict mode refuses without replacing a sentinel, explicit partial mode
can write the one following valid LINE, and an unmodeled OBJECTS record still
fails with the destination preserved. CLI option controls prove exact-token
acceptance in positional and FreeCAD `-o` forms, reject a suffixed token, and
prove the option grants no overwrite authority. No DWG/DXF fixture was added.

Two diagnostic checks against existing user-held samples kept the policy
boundary honest: one AC1018 input failed the DWG read with `BAD_READ_BLOCKS`
and remains rejected in both modes; one AC1024 input read successfully with
501/501 terminal frames but `semanticCoverage=unknown`, then partial export
still failed strict LAYOUT last-active-viewport owner closure. Neither result
created an output or promotes support. The generated API control is the
positive test for the partial policy; the real local checks are negative
controls for read-operation and independent graph failures.

**Focused current-worktree recheck (2026-10-22):** rebuilt `dwg2dxf` with
`-Werror`, then ran only the 17 registered `dwg_read` tests. Fourteen passed;
the three remaining AC1024 visualization cases failed the strict conversion
expectation with `operationSucceeded=true`, `legacyError=0`, and partial frame
coverage (2–3 object parse failures each). Their traces retain the class CRC
warning separately from those later object dispositions; the sun/sky sample
identifies `BLOCKLOOKUPACTION` type 528 and `PERSUBENTMGR` type 515 as unresolved

was copied or committed; no external drawing was downloaded.

### Implementation-ready sequence and speed constraints

1. **Separate conversion policies without weakening graph checks.** In the
   current CLI, `fileExport(..., requireResolvedOwners=true, ...)` drives both
   owner-closure checks and the `strictDwgReadOutcomeIsComplete()` gate. Add a
   source-compatible completeness policy (strict by default) as a distinct
   parameter/enum. An explicit partial opt-in may emit a bounded diagnostic
   result only when record boundaries and owner closure remain valid; it must
   not silently turn on for FreeCAD-compatible invocation. Keep existing
   transactional output and strict default behavior.
2. **Reuse existing generated fast selectors.** Extend the current CLI/adapter
   contract selector with one strict-refusal/no-publication assertion and one
   explicit partial-policy case using a generated partial-read control plus a
   following valid LINE sentinel. Add a separate unresolved-owner negative
   control that still fails in partial mode. Keep the malformed HATCH only as
   policy plumbing, not valid-format coverage. Run the owning focused CTest(s)
   and `git diff --check`; do not add a fixture, CTest registration, or full
   suite gate.
3. **Resolve the four visualization cases independently.** Preserve only
   local trace summaries/hashes if a later audit needs comparison; never copy
   these externally sourced files into `tests/samples`. First establish the
   physical section envelope and checksum span using the authoritative ODA
   material, then make a minimal generated control only if it faithfully
   isolates the observed field. If the uncertainty cannot be resolved from
   spec plus trace, record `UNRESOLVED` and self-unblock to a different local
   implementation slice.
4. **Do not duplicate peer-reported behavior already covered locally.** The
   existing #1409 block census, #1410 zero-HATCH/attribute/embedded-MTEXT
   controls, #1412 exact-length text controls, #1355 terminal-output checks,
   and AcDs payload/owner gates remain the local owners. Recheck peer issue/PR
   states only at the composed comparator checkpoint.

This research adds no numbered finding or top-level subplan and does not
promote support. It refines PAR-06/PAR-07/S8, PAR-14, PAR-19/PAR-28 and the

## Deeper/broader ACadRust 0.6.5 release, issue, test-denominator, and ACIS-claim freshness correction (2026-10-20; research only)

This section supersedes the package-version observation in the preceding
same-day issue audit. The v0.6.5 release tag (commit `289a616`) and mutable
upstream `Cargo.toml` identify ACadRust 0.6.5, released 2026-10-18; the earlier
statement that the ACIS documentation page displayed 0.6.4 was stale. A later
source refresh found that the repository README and the fetched docs.rs
`latest` source page still identify 0.5.5. Therefore do not say that the live
README, docs.rs `latest`, manifest and release source are all version-aligned.
Treat v0.6.5/`289a616` as the candidate release identity, but require a matching
source/archive checksum before using source evidence. The package manifest
identifies MPL-2.0 and lists its dependencies. ([v0.6.5 release](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/releases/tag/v0.6.5),
[manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/main/Cargo.toml),
[docs.rs source page](https://docs.rs/acadrust/latest/src/acadrust/io/dwg/dwg_stream_readers/object_reader/class_object.rs.html))

### Release claims versus independently measured behavior

The 0.6.5 changelog claims (a) malformed-header errors are reported, (b)
bounded auxiliary DWG records can be preserved after decode failures, (c)
orphaned geometry stays out of model space, and (d) named colors and
table-record XDATA are preserved while unsupported custom records are
reported. The versioned issue state is not equivalent to independent
verification: #123 and #124 remain open for malformed object allocation/count
and malformed header slicing; #133 and #134 remain open for orphan membership
and AC1032 auxiliary-record compatibility; #132 is closed as completed after
the linked change, but neither the issue nor release note publishes an
independent retest of the affected private corpus. Preserve both facts in the
evidence ledger: “maintainer claims fix in 0.6.5” and “external regression
retest not public / not run here.” Do not project 0.6.3/0.6.4 reproductions
onto 0.6.5 as current failures, and do not promote the 0.6.5 claims to verified
support. ([0.6.5 changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/main/CHANGELOG.md),
[#123](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/123),
[#124](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/124),
[#132](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/132),
[#133](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/133),
[#134](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/134))

### Correct evidence denominator and route boundaries

The public docs list DXF/DWG read/write from AC1009 through AC1032, but also
say entity availability varies, AC1009 DWG fidelity is incomplete, and a
document merely tagged AC1009 is still written as R13 by default unless the
explicit R12 writer is selected. The docs say the project's GitHub Actions
run stable Rust checks on Linux, Windows, and macOS (plus wasm build checks),
but drawing-dependent tests for files absent from the repository are
`#[ignore]`d. Therefore a green standard CI job does not establish the
ignored real-drawing denominator. For plan scoring, capture each run's exact
release/commit, platform, feature flags, command, file hash/version, direction,
entity/object denominator, ignored/skipped count, diagnostics, and strict vs
recovery mode; distinguish explicit R12 DXF output from the default writer
route. ([0.6.5 support matrix and test notes](https://docs.rs/crate/acadrust/latest),
[0.6.5 changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/main/CHANGELOG.md))

The changelog's ACIS statements concern preserving binary face/edge colors,
splitting SAT bodies, and fixes to wireframe/pcurves/history. The separate
ACIS primitive API documents builders that construct topology for standard
primitives; this is useful structural evidence, but it is not by itself an
independent geometric-kernel validity result or acceptance by FreeCAD, LibreCAD,
or another named consumer. This distinction is an inference from the stated
builder/API scope, not a claim that the implementation is invalid. Keep the
existing three-dimensional gate layered: (1) raw SAT/SAB carrier and version
preservation, (2) decoded topology/reference closure, (3) independent analytic
or kernel semantic checks with expected values not generated by the candidate
reader/writer, and (4) named consumer acceptance. Do not merge those layers
into “ACIS supported.” ([ACIS primitive API](https://docs.rs/acadrust/latest/acadrust/entities/acis/primitives/index.html),
[0.6.5 changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/main/CHANGELOG.md))

### Implementation-readiness delta

1. Update the existing PAR-07/S8 candidate record with a correction flag for
   the stale docs-version note; pin version 0.6.5 only if a future task admits
   this route, and record checksum, source revision, license, dependencies,
   test commands, platform/feature matrix, ignored tests, and exact file
   denominator before scoring.
2. For malformed inputs, keep header subsection ranges separate from object
   record counts/allocations. Assert checked arithmetic, in-frame bounds,
   bounded allocation/work, stable first-stage errors, and no process abort,
   fabricated zero-filled geometry, or false successful recovery.
3. For recovery, preserve optional auxiliary bytes only when the record end is
   proven; test a damaged optional frame followed by a valid sentinel. If the
   boundary is uncertain, fail closed rather than scanning for a plausible
   next marker. Record dropped/preserved/unsupported outcomes per handle.
4. For ownership and writers, distinguish null, resolved, and unresolved
   owners, prohibit automatic model-space re-homing of unresolved entities,
   and separately count raw unknown classes, named colors, and table/block
   XDATA as preserved, explicitly refused, diagnosed omission, or silent loss.
5. For ACIS, treat generated primitive topology as a candidate structural
   control only. Require independently sourced expected values and a direct
   external semantic/kernel or named-consumer path before any B-rep support
   claim; missing routes remain `NOT_RUN` / `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and self-unblock
   to local work.

This correction refines existing PAR-07/S8 and parser-hardening, owner-closure,
writer-disposition, and 3D-semantic gates only. It adds no numbered finding or
top-level subplan, does not change implementation order or validation
frequency, and adds no test, fixture, dependency, runtime, or peer execution.
Counts remain **141 findings / 78 subplans**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293,
and J295 remain explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. No external
DWG/DXF was downloaded or committed. ODA v5.4.1 remains authoritative for DWG
layout questions.

   existing composed checkpoint, generate the asymmetric polyhedron in a

### Implementation-ready refinement

1. **Fast local/API loop:** for a `DRW_Interface` or entity change, build the
   owning libdxfrw target, run the focused existing selector/CTest, and run
   `lc3_compat_check` when its public surface is touched. Keep callbacks
   optional/non-pure; do not add a 3D callback requirement to LibreCAD_3.

   commits; source-overlay libdxfrw into a disposable consumer checkout; build
   `persistence` before the full app. Use the default 2D profile

   separate `WITH_DWG_IMPORT=ON` smoke only if DWG-import integration is in
   scope, and label it experimental/read-only. Do not inherit the consumer's

3. **Mixed-content assertion:** use generated temporary content or an already
   repository-owned fixture; include ordinary 2D records around unsupported
   3D/modeler records and verify source-order/block behavior for the supported
   subset. The consumer's intentional no-op is an explicit disposition, not
   evidence that the library may silently drop data in its own read/write

4. **Spline quality without slow per-slice peer runs:** keep deterministic
   ASCII/Binary and relevant DWG-version curve controls in the local fast

5. **Self-unblock:** if the current downstream source, platform toolchain, or
   optional consumer is unavailable, record the exact `NOT_RUN` reason and
   continue the next local source-backed slice. Do not wait on LibreCAD_3 or
   the peer spline report to proceed with local implementation.

sharper separation of entity/carrier/semantic gates; it does not discover a

only. No peer checkout or executable, application, kernel, package,
DWG/DXF attachment, or new runtime was fetched, installed, or executed;
public source and documentation pages were reviewed only.

Autodesk's [entity-code guidance](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A35B8C2A-1885-4A8E-8533-E61D8A423D62.htm) says not to assume group-code order and to tolerate undefined codes. | Keep independent implementation/test rows for explicit surfaces/meshes, curves, and modeler-backed entities. Preserve repeated-array order and codes 1/3 separately from group-350 history. Add permutation/unknown-code generated controls only where the current selector audit finds a gap; never treat 3DFACE or MESH as an ACIS solid, or a 3DSOLID record count as geometry validity. Autodesk tables specify DXF fields, not the internal DWG object bit layout; ODA v5.4.1 remains authoritative for that. |
| [ezdxf ACIS API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html), [entity-generation task guide](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/tasks/add_dxf_entities.rst), and [drawing limitations](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/addons/drawing.rst) | The API documents a bounded mesh-to-planar-body generator and reports SAT for DXF R2000–R2010 versus SAB for R2013+; the task guide says arbitrary ACIS-data creation requires an external library. The drawing add-on says ACIS rendering is unsupported and has no 3D engine (3D records are projected into XY). Its documentation also describes unsupported ACIS record loss and does not claim an ACIS kernel. | Admit ezdxf as an optional, exact-version, scratch-only producer/structure inspector. Record declared DXF version, observed SAT/SAB type, exact bytes/hash, and independent analytic expectations. Treat the version mapping as a producer-documentation profile to verify on the exact output, not a general DWG layout rule. Do not use ezdxf as the semantic decoder, kernel, renderer, or independent acceptance oracle; do not treat an XY preview as 3D validation. |
| Current [LibreDWG `decode_r2007.c`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/master/src/decode_r2007.c), [`acds.spec`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/master/src/acds.spec), [`common_entity_data.spec`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/common_entity_data.spec), and [issue #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411) | Source review found an AcDs section read and schema/segment parser. The data-segment path then scans the section bytes for `ACIS BinaryFile` and a tagged terminator, consumes a queued reference collected from `has_ds_data` modeler entities, and attaches each found payload to the resolved solid; it warns on count mismatch, and comments that wires/silhouettes may also exist. Open issue #1411 reports silent geometry loss with named LibreDWG 0.14.8593. The source refs are mutable and no current-master run was made. | This is useful differential evidence, not a reliable semantic oracle. Check all AcDs source records are dispositioned before claiming complete retention; do not silently equate an extracted SAB body with all AcDs-owned data. |

The README advertises broad SAT/SAB and B-rep capabilities, but a capability statement or same-implementation round trip does not independently validate arbitrary input or geometry. | Reuse only the test-design pattern—two unequal payloads, reversed traversal/order, wrong/missing/duplicate owner and strict readback. | FreeCAD [Draft DXF docs](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and [InventorLoader docs/source](https://github.com/jmplonka/InventorLoader) | The documented stock FreeCAD DXF importer cannot read embedded ACIS solids; backend matters for other 3D families. InventorLoader is a separate add-on that advertises SAT/SAB from DXF and supports native or STEP conversion paths, but its public limitation list excludes blending surfaces, helix surfaces, and law-defined curves without spline data. Both routes eventually create geometry through FreeCAD Part/OCCT; this pass did not pin or run its mutable source. | Preserve the stock importer as a named consumer route, not the ACIS oracle. Keep InventorLoader as a candidate *parser-plus-OCCT-output* route with exact release/source and mode pinned; native versus STEP output is two routes but not two independent kernels. Admit only profiles actually tested with asymmetric expected topology/volume/bounds, and record unsupported constructs as partial/refused rather than successful full conversion. |

### Refined implementation sequence

1. **Audit once, then avoid duplicate tests.** Crosswalk current fast selectors
   against the five dimensions `entity family × source version × carrier ×
   direction × operation`. Mark each as covered, missing, or intentionally
   unsupported. Existing 3DFACE, MESH/PFACE, SPLINE, typed modeler, AcDs,
   writer, and consumer controls remain the starting point; add no duplicate
   target for coverage already present.
2. **Keep local transport checks surgical.** For any missing DXF ordering or
   framing case, generate scratch ASCII/Binary controls with reordered legal
   group codes, repeated 1/3 carrier chunks, unrelated group-350 references,
   unknown codes, and an adjacent sentinel. Compare exact per-source arrays,
   history edges, and readback, not only entity counts. For AcDs, use unequal
   body payload markers and owner keys with reversed record/entity order,
   then wrong/missing/duplicate/orphan keys; require atomic refusal on
   ambiguity and explicit disposition for non-SAB/wire/silhouette records.
3. **Separate geometry from carriage.** A semantic case must have an
   independently authored analytic expectation (asymmetric points, bounds,
   area/volume, and topology as applicable). Record parser, kernel, and
   consumer separately. A parser success, exact SAB hash, or OCCT shape alone
   is insufficient without profile admission, expected-value comparison, and
   source-to-payload closure.
4. **Use one bounded external semantic checkpoint.** At the existing composed
   milestone, test a pinned released SAT/SAB profile through one admitted
   parser route; where useful, the InventorLoader route is a parser cross-check
   but its Part/OCCT result shares a kernel family with FreeCAD/CadQuery. Run
   native consumer/platform checks only at their existing scheduled gates.
   Unavailable or unsupported optional routes become `NOT_RUN` or
   `PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED`; implementation continues locally.
5. **Keep status honest.** A full support row requires explicit disposition
   for every source record, stable owner/history graph, accepted target
   profile, geometry expectation, and named consumer result. Preserve the
   current 2D/API compatibility lane and never promote a 3D claim from a
   downstream no-op, tolerant parse, synthetic marker, or peer feature badge.

This refines existing PAR-05/7BQ.5 strict DXF output, PAR-07/S8 peer and
per-source disposition, S2/S3 modeler carrier work, S3.7 SAB parsing, and
S8.15 consumer gates only. It adds no numbered finding, top-level subplan,
code, test, fixture, package, peer execution, or validation-cadence change.
Finding/subplan counters remain unreconciled. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293,
and J295 remain explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. No native
Linux/Windows FreeCAD or independent new semantic evidence was acquired in this
pass; ODA v5.4.1 remains the DWG byte-layout authority.

## Deeper/broader research — SAB common record header and type-field alignment (2026-10-21; source audit)

This pass follows the ACIS/SAB path below the DWG AcDs envelope. ODA v5.4.1
§24 remains authoritative for DWG DataStorage framing, handle/blob association,
and the SAB stream prefix/terminator convention; it does not specify the
detailed per-entity SAB field grammar. The pinned ezdxf implementation source
provides independent implementation evidence for the currently projected
`ACIS BinaryFile` 21800 profile, not normative ACIS authority.

| Evidence | Result | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ODA [Working with .sat and .sab Files in Teigha](https://www.opendesign.com/blog/2017/october/working-sat-and-sab-files-teigha) and [Open Design Specification §24.2.2.3](https://static.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf#page=246) | ODA maps R27/2013 to save version 21800 and states that formats 20800+ are Autodesk-modified, not native Spatial ACIS; native versions above 700 are likewise not directly interchangeable with DWG/DXF. The spec says an ACIS SAB payload begins with `ACIS BinaryFile` and, when save version is >=21800, ends with `End-of-ASM-data` (otherwise `End-of-ACIS-data`). It specifies this envelope convention, not the detailed entity-field grammar. | Name the supported scope precisely as the Autodesk-modified `ACIS BinaryFile` 21800 profile. Keep the stream terminator version-aware in generated controls. Do not use a native ACIS decoder assumption, the `ACIS` label alone, or a matching number to admit another signature/version. Keep AcDs transport/owner association separate from SAB record decoding. |
| Pinned ezdxf [`sab.py` export path](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/dd7f6cc34983fdbf0b2b910f2497e0720d06dd16/src/ezdxf/acis/sab.py#L265-L286) and [`entities.py::export_sab()`](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/dd7f6cc34983fdbf0b2b910f2497e0720d06dd16/src/ezdxf/acis/entities.py#L48-L66) | The R2013+ export path sets the ASM terminator flag, and `SabBuilder.dump_sab()` writes `header.sab_end_marker()` after the record stream. This independently corroborates the ODA terminator transition for the ezdxf-produced 21800 profile. | Generated 21800 parser controls must use `End-of-ASM-data`; keep `End-of-ACIS-data` only for profiles where it is valid (e.g. the local version-1 framing control). The parser may recognize both marker spellings, but acceptance of a marker is not by itself proof that the signature/version/terminator combination is a valid producer profile. |
| Pinned ezdxf [`sab.py::build_entities()`](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/dd7f6cc34983fdbf0b2b910f2497e0720d06dd16/src/ezdxf/acis/sab.py#L307-L325) and [`Decoder.read_record()`](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/dd7f6cc34983fdbf0b2b910f2497e0720d06dd16/src/ezdxf/acis/sab.py#L117-L170) | The raw record retains the entity-type token at `[0]`; non-marker records then have a shared attribute-pointer at `[1]` and, for the current >=700 branch, an integer entity ID at `[2]`. Entity-specific data starts at `[3]`. Thus the two shared fields occupy raw indexes 1 and 2, while the semantic suffix starts at index **3**. The version predicate in ezdxf is broader than this plan's admitted profile; it is not a format-wide rule. | Derive the local semantic offset internally as 3 for validated non-terminal `ACIS BinaryFile` 21800 wire records. Preserve all raw tokens and the installed public `DRW_SabRecord` layout; do not add an offset member. Validate tag shape before using the offset; do not use 2, infer malformed parsed records, or extend this layout to legacy SAT/SAB or ASM. |
| Pinned ezdxf [`entities.py` common-field layouts](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/dd7f6cc34983fdbf0b2b910f2497e0720d06dd16/src/ezdxf/acis/entities.py#L203-L229) and [`Face.restore_common()`](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/dd7f6cc34983fdbf0b2b910f2497e0720d06dd16/src/ezdxf/acis/entities.py#L337-L365) | A version-gated pattern pointer can precede a type's own fields; the face layout then reads its linked face/loop/shell/subshell/surface fields and sense/sidedness flags in a specific order. | Keep shared header fields, feature-gated common fields, and type-specific fields distinct. Rooted projections must use semantic field ordinals derived from the right start offset; they must not sort by record index or assume all pointers in a raw record are body links. |
| CADMPEG [v0.6.2 release](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/releases/tag/v0.6.2), its pinned [`format-support.md`](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/blob/7bcc95276548de4e4876894b9a650a84ea9c4d6d/docs/format-support.md) / [`asm.md`](https://github.com/cadmpeg/cadmpeg/blob/7bcc95276548de4e4876894b9a650a84ea9c4d6d/docs/formats/asm.md), and ODA's 20800+ classification above | CADMPEG calls ACIS 217/218 its verified Spatial ACIS bands and documents ACIS BinaryFile framing, while ODA classifies 20800+ SAT/SAB as Autodesk-modified. Numeric band and `ACIS BinaryFile` magic alone do not resolve whether every record/profile is equivalent; this pass did not run CADMPEG against a native 21800 payload. | Keep CADMPEG as an optional exact-byte parser/geometry route, not as a normative authority or a support claim based only on “217/218 verified.” Before any comparison, bind the exact 21800 payload hash, parser release/source, record grammar, diagnostics and geometry result; if not admitted, report `NOT_APPLICABLE`/`PROFILE_UNVERIFIED`, not a peer failure. |
| Local [`DRW_SabRecord`](src/drw_acis.h), [`readRecord()` / `parseSabPrefix()`](src/drw_acis.cpp), and [`buildAcisModelImpl()` / `readPointers()`](src/drw_acis.cpp) | The parser appends the initial `EntityType` token and all subsequent fields to one `tokens` vector. It does not represent a semantic offset. The model builder currently counts/copies every pointer token, including token `[1]` when it is the shared attribute pointer, and rooted validation walks all raw pointer tokens as type-specific ordinals. Hand-built `DRW_SabData` tests omit the wire prefix, so they do not test this parser/model boundary. This is a source-audit risk, not yet a failing native-file reproduction. | Add a local S3.7 structural slice: validate exact 21800 non-terminal raw prefix `[0]=EntityType(type), [1]=Pointer, [2]=Int`, then derive semantic start 3 in a private helper; preserve raw tokens and do not add a member to installed `DRW_SabRecord` (which would alter its public layout). Use the suffix for ref planning/resolution, point and curve/surface cursors, intcurve extraction, transform classification, and rooted pointer-row ordinals. Keep complete raw-token budgets and snapshots. Caller-built records without that wire prefix keep offset zero; terminal records are exempt. |
| [`cq-acis` corpus manifest](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/corpus/manifest.jsonl), [project README](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/README.md), [OCCT exchange component](https://www.occt3d.com/components/acis-exchange/), and prior [ACadRust release/source audit](#deeperbroader-acadrust-065-release-and-issue-freshness-2026-10-20-research-only) | The public `cq-acis` corpus gives per-source commit/blob/SHA and separate NIST-PD/third-party notices, but the repository says the corpus is not in its wheel. `cq-acis`/InventorLoader shape output shares the OCCT kernel family; ACadRust supplies a distinct structural parser lineage, while its README/test claims and package/source artifact must remain separately bound. | At most, use a corpus sample later as an optional, provenance-recorded external semantic probe; do not vendor it or commit it as a libdxfrw fixture. None of these routes independently qualifies an ACIS kernel, native FreeCAD, DWG AcDs association, or this parser's generic-header handling. No peer package/run belongs in the local fast slice. |

### Implementation-ready S3.7 sub-slice

1. Preserve the installed `DRW_SabRecord` layout. Keep the exact raw token
   vector, including the leading entity-type marker; add only a private helper
   deriving semantic start 3 for non-terminal records in the supported
   Autodesk-modified `ACIS BinaryFile` 21800 profile after validating raw
   token `[0]` as `EntityType` matching `record.type`, `[1]` as `Pointer`
   (attribute pointer), and `[2]` as `Int` (entity ID). A caller-built record
   without that complete prefix keeps offset zero. The wire parser rejects a
   malformed/ambiguous 21800 prefix; it must never guess. Terminal markers
   are exempt. Unsupported SAB/ASM profiles remain raw and outside rooted
   projection.
2. Apply the semantic start consistently in reference counting/resolution,
   point and curve/surface cursors, intcurve control-point extraction,
   transform-token interpretation, and `readPointers()` ordinal verification.
   Resource accounting still covers the complete raw token vector, including
   the type marker, shared attribute pointer, and entity ID; only semantic
   graph references exclude the attribute pointer and entity ID.
3. Add from-scratch, in-memory wire-form 21800 controls for an attribute-null
   record and a non-null attribute record. Assert the exact decoded type,
   preserved type marker, attribute pointer, entity ID, type-specific pointer
   ordinals, raw transform snapshot/index, and successful rooted body
   projection; include malformed prefix,
   terminal-marker, and caller-built offset-zero controls. Update only the existing
   `libdxfrw_graph_preservation` target; do not add or commit DWG/DXF/SAB files.
4. Validate with the graph-preservation target/CTest, `lc3_compat_check`, and
   scoped diff/receipt checks. Run the focused modeler block projection only
   if the change touches that reader/writer path. No full suite, peer package,
   native FreeCAD, or large external corpus run is needed for this local
   structural correction; retain those at their existing composed gates.
5. Keep all resulting claims at raw/typed graph-structure level. A correct
   shared-header offset does not establish complete SAB grammar, attribute
   semantics, transform/unit application, B-rep closure, volume/area, or
   external application acceptance. Add no finding or top-level subplan;
   all six J items remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

uses `End-of-ASM-data`; it does not define detailed entity records. In pinned
ezdxf, `Decoder.read_record()` retains the entity type, shared attribute
pointer, and entity ID at raw indexes 0, 1, and 2; semantic type fields begin

is not generalized to native Spatial ACIS, other SAB versions, or ASM.

parser boundary and derives semantic token start 3 in a private helper. It
uses that start consistently for semantic pointer planning/resolution, point

include the full record. The installed public `DRW_SabRecord` layout is
unchanged; caller-built records without the wire prefix retain historical
offset zero, and terminal records are exempt. Generated in-memory tests
exercise non-null attribute-pointer exclusion, parsed wireframe and rooted

## Deeper/broader research — DXF group order and repeated-coordinate assembly (2026-10-21; primary-source review + local source audit)

This follow-up turns the existing “do not assume DXF group-code order” rule
into a focused implementation sequence. Autodesk's [2024 Object and Entity
Codes guidance](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A35B8C2A-1885-4A8E-8533-E61D8A423D62.htm)
explicitly says not to assume code order inside an entity, notes that group
code 0 delimits the next entity/section, and recommends table-driven dispatch
that ignores undefined codes. Its [2023 common entity-code
reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3610039E-27D1-4E23-B6D3-7E60B22BB5BD.htm)
says the displayed order may change by conditions or future releases. This is
a field-dispatch requirement; it is **not** permission to sort all tags,
reorder repeated same-code arrays, move subclass/context delimiters, or relax
entity framing.

| Evidence | Finding | Implementation consequence / limit |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk DXF references above | DXF readers must dispatch on each group code rather than assume table/display order; entity end remains the next group-0 record. | Build generated permutations by moving distinct point-component groups while preserving same-code occurrence order, entity group-0 boundaries, subclass markers, and nested context markers. Unknown codes must follow the existing declared ignore/preserve/refuse policy; do not globally reorder records. |
| [ezdxf entity loading](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/dxfentity.py) and [ACadSharp code mappings](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/Entities/Entity.cs) | The reviewed peers expose code-keyed tag/subclass processing and property-to-group-code metadata. These source patterns are compatible with field dispatch, but this source-only review did not run either peer or establish that every parser handles all permutations. | Use as architectural context, not as a pass/fail oracle. No peer execution is needed for the local fast loop; pin exact revisions only if a later differential question justifies a composed run. |
| Local [`DRW_Spline::parseCode`](src/drw_entities.cpp) and generated [`testDxfSplinePointComponentOrder`](tests/hardening_tests.cpp) | The original parser constructed control/fit points only when X group 10/11 arrived, so earlier Y/Z groups were lost or misbound. The fix now tracks independent X/Y/Z occurrence ordinals, assembles components into point slots, and validates counts without requiring X to be the first code encountered. | Completed local regression slice: ASCII and Binary generated controls reorder all control-point components and all fit-point components independently, assert exact asymmetric points, and verify a following LINE sentinel. Missing optional components retain zero defaults; count/cap validation remains enforced. No DXF fixture was added. |
| Autodesk [MESH DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-4B9ADA67-87C8-4673-A579-6E4C76FF7025.htm), [group-code point definitions](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3F0380A5-1C15-464D-BC66-2C5F094BCFB9.htm), and local [`DRW_Mesh::parseCode`](src/drw_entities.cpp) | Autodesk defines group 92 as level-0 vertex count, group 10 as vertex position, and group 93 as face-list size; general code-order guidance applies while the stream/count boundaries remain entity-specific. A generated ASCII/Binary test reproduced the parser's X-first rejection: a valid vertex with Y and Z components preceding X failed before callback. | Implemented per-axis occurrence counters; the face/edge/crease phase machine and group 92/93/94/95 delimiters remain intact. The test moves all Y values, then all Z values, then all X values, preserving each same-code occurrence order; it asserts exact topology and the following LINE. Existing missing-Y, missing-Z, and excess-Y controls still refuse before callback publication. MESH is no longer an unverified candidate; only the other source-audit rows below remain unconfirmed. |
| Autodesk [LWPOLYLINE DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-748FC305-F3F2-4F74-825A-61F04D757A50.htm) and local [`DRW_LWPolyline::parseCode`](src/drw_entities.cpp) | Autodesk defines group 90 as vertex count and repeated 10/20 as X/Y arrays with one entry per vertex; optional groups 40/41/42/91 are also repeated per-vertex values. The old parser created a vertex only on X and routed all optional fields through the last-X cursor. Generated ASCII/Binary input grouped each per-vertex field by group code and reproduced value loss/misbinding before the following LINE. | Implemented independent ordinal counters for 10/20/40/41/42/91, bounded by the existing one-million vertex cap and declared count; missing optional entries retain zero defaults. Exact asymmetric points, widths, bulges, identifiers, following LINE, and excess-Y refusal-before-callback are covered. No persistent DXF fixture was added. |
| Autodesk [LEADER DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-396B2369-F89F-47D7-8223-8B7FB794F9F3.htm) and local [`DRW_Leader::parseCode`](src/drw_entities.cpp) | Autodesk defines group 76 as advisory for OPEN and groups 10/20/30 as repeated 3D vertex components. The old parser created a point only on X and ignored earlier Y/Z. Generated ASCII/Binary permutations reproduced loss while retaining group-76 compatibility behavior. | Implemented independent 10/20/30 ordinals under the existing 5,000-vertex cap; X occurrence count must match materialized points, while Y/Z defaults remain zero when omitted. Exact asymmetric tuples, following LINE, and excess-Y refusal-before-callback pass. No fixture was added. |
| Autodesk [HATCH boundary-path schema](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-DC5215D6-E73F-4DFF-8BE9-01CA9610FAEE.htm) and local [`DRW_Hatch::parseCode`](src/drw_entities.cpp) | Schema pins spline-edge framing: 94 degree, 95 knots, 96 control points, 40 knot values, 10/20 control points, 42 optional weights, 97 fit data, 11/21 fit points, and 12/22 + 13/23 tangents. Generated ASCII/Binary input with Y-before-X control and fit arrays reproduced the old parser's loss/rejection. | Fixed with independent control-X/Y and fit-X/Y ordinals, bounded by declared counts and the existing item cap. Only active spline coordinate arrays bypass the ordinary HATCH adjacent-pair transition; loop, edge, knot, weight, fit, tangent, and group-0 framing stay intact. Exact spline fields, following LINE, and excess-Y refusal-before-publication pass. No fixture added. |
| Autodesk [MLEADER context](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-EC56D0DE-026D-46AB-87B1-9692393B0C22.htm), [leader node](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-8648B8F7-5BD3-445B-A1B2-6F65EC4ECB3E.htm), and [leader line](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-B2E6436A-F17D-4F59-9DE8-DBDB61AD36C6.htm) schemas; local [`DRW_MLeader::parseDxfContextCode`](src/drw_entities.cpp) | The official tables reuse point groups across distinct scopes: context base/plane vectors, leader-node last point/dogleg/breaks, and leader-line vertices/breaks. ezdxf documents a structured context with WCS leader-line vertices and break records, but also calls MULTILEADER context data complex. Local parser mutates last entries in some arrays and has explicit presence flags and `LEADER{}` / `LEADER_LINE{}` framing. | Still a candidate, not a reproduced defect. Next probe only one complete, canonical context and permute components within one documented point slot/scope at a time. Keep all 300/301/302/303 braces, flags, branch order, same-code ordinal, and group-0 sentinel fixed; assert exact root/line/break tuples and malformed-closure refusal before callback. Do not globally permute reused codes across scopes. |
| Autodesk [MLINE DXF schema](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-590E8AE3-C6D9-4641-8485-D7B3693E432C.htm) and local [`DRW_MLine::parseCode`](src/drw_entities.cpp) | Schema defines repeated arrays for group 11/21/31 vertex coordinates, 12/22/32 segment direction vectors, and 13/23/33 miter vectors, one record per vertex; counts and per-element 74/41, 75/42 sequences add framing. Local parsing creates a vertex on 11 and assigns later components to the current vertex, so grouped Y/Z-before-X is a source-identified candidate. | Not reproduced yet. Build one two-vertex ASCII/Binary MLINE with unequal vector components and minimal valid per-element parameter lists; move only 21/31, then 22/32, then 23/33 before their matching X arrays while preserving count/group-74/75 blocks. Check exact payload and following LINE; fix only if the valid-profile control demonstrates loss or rejection. |
| Local [`DRW_NurbsSurface::parseCode`](src/drw_entities.cpp) | Existing NURBS-surface coordinate masks record components independently for each fixed vector, providing a useful local pattern; the grid/control-point array still needs its own selector audit. | Reuse existing mask/count checks where the schema is fixed-field. Audit repeated grid points separately; do not duplicate tests for already-covered fixed vectors. |

### Implementation-ready sequence and speed rules

1. **Keep the contract narrow.** For each affected entity, consult its exact
   Autodesk DXF schema and existing count/default rules. Shuffle only distinct
   coordinate group codes; preserve occurrence order among repeated 10/20/30
   (and corresponding 11/21/31) values because those ordinals define the
   point sequence. Keep group-0 entity boundaries, group-100 subclass markers,
   and MLEADER/HATCH nested framing untouched.
2. **Close the confirmed SPLINE, MESH, LWPOLYLINE, LEADER, and HATCH slices.** Their generated ASCII/Binary
   component-order controls, exact field/topology comparisons, following
   LINE sentinels, owning fast CTests, and `lc3_compat_check` pass. SPLINE
   reuses its two private cursor slots; MESH reuses its three phase-counter
   slots, with size/alignment assertions; LWPOLYLINE and LEADER use private
   per-code bounded occurrence counters without changing public fields or
   virtuals. HATCH uses private bounded control/fit X/Y ordinals and preserves
   its ordinary adjacent-coordinate rule outside active spline edges
   (consumers rebuild for updated private class layouts).
   Re-run owning tests after relevant edits; no full suite is warranted for
   these isolated parser changes.
3. **Self-unblock through small local probes.** Audit existing selectors once;
   HATCH spline edges are now complete. Probe nested MLEADER's scoped context
   arrays and MLINE's three repeated vector families next; use one generated
   profile per schema and change production only after a valid-profile failure
   reproduces.
   For every reproduced case, implement one family slice, add or
   extend the existing fast selector, assert exact semantic points and an
   adjacent sentinel, run the owning CTest and compatibility compile, and
   record the result before moving to the next family. A negative control must
   verify count/cap/cardinality refusal occurs before callback publication.
4. **Keep implementation fast and non-invasive.** Use generated in-memory
   ASCII and Binary DXF; do not commit external samples or create new CTest
   lanes when an existing owning target can carry the control. Do not run
   independent peers or native CAD on each slice; keep those at the existing
   composed consumer checkpoint. Avoid a universal tag-buffer rewrite unless
   several confirmed schemas require it and the owner review shows a clear
   smaller alternative is inadequate.
5. **Progress, evidence, and self-unblock.** After each implemented slice,
   refresh this plan and its small receipt with the exact selector/CTest and
   remaining source-audit candidates. If an optional peer, OS, or CAD
   application is unavailable, record `NOT_RUN` and continue to the next local
   slice. Keep 2D compatibility as a separate consumer lane; point-order
   parsing establishes neither rendered geometry nor full 3D semantic support.

This research refines existing PAR-05/7BQ.5 DXF syntax/ordering, PAR-22/7AB
SPLINE/NURBS, and existing entity-specific DXF implementation owners only. It
adds no numbered finding or subplan and changes no support matrix. Remaining
source-audit candidates are nested MLEADER, MLINE repeated vectors, and the
NURBS-surface grid-point array; these are not yet confirmed defects. Peer
documentation/source was reviewed but no peer executable or runtime, CAD
application, geometry kernel, or customer fixture was used.
No support claim is promoted; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. Peer documentation/source
was reviewed as architectural context, but no peer executable/runtime was
run. ODA v5.4.1 remains the authority for DWG byte layout.

Research receipt:
[`deeper-broader-dxf-group-order-coordinate-assembly-2026-10-21.json`](docs/research/deeper-broader-dxf-group-order-coordinate-assembly-2026-10-21.json).

## Implementation progress — DXF SPLINE component-order regression (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Applied the confirmed local code-order fix to standalone `DRW_Spline` control
and fit points. Per-component occurrence cursors associate group codes 10/20/30
and 11/21/31 by their own array ordinals, so a legal Y/Z-before-X sequence no
longer disappears or shifts the point. Declared-count and item-cap validation
remain active; absent Y/Z components retain their existing zero defaults.
The two parser-private pointer slots were reused with a private cursor type,
guarded by compile-time size/alignment assertions; no public field, callback,
or virtual was added.

Generated ASCII and Binary DXFs each contain a control-point SPLINE, a
fit-point-only SPLINE with distinct non-square coordinates, and a following
LINE. The selector asserts all point components and the LINE values exactly.
The order was deliberately changed by component arrays while repeated-code
occurrence order was preserved.

Validation:

```text
cmake --build build --target libdxfrw_hardening_tests lc3_compat_check -j4  PASS
build/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --dxf-spline-point-component-order  PASS
ctest --test-dir build -R '^libdxfrw_hardening$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1)
```

No fixture, peer run, CAD/kernel run, full test suite, or support claim was
added. The source audit identified HATCH spline edges and nested MLEADER
coordinates as follow-up candidates; they remain unreproduced and unmodified.
The worktree is broadly dirty and Git metadata is read-only, so this entry is
uncommitted. **Self-unblock:** continue with a schema-checked generated HATCH
spline-edge probe, then nested MLEADER without waiting for peer or native
qualification.

## Implementation progress — DXF MESH vertex component order (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The Autodesk MESH schema and general DXF group-code guidance support
dispatching coordinate components by code while preserving stream framing.
The generated regression first reproduced a real local failure: in both
ASCII and Binary DXF, legal vertex Y/Z groups before X were rejected before
the MESH callback. `DRW_Mesh::parseCode` now assigns each coordinate component
by its own occurrence ordinal, so groups 10/20/30 independently populate the
same vertex slots. The existing level-0 vertex count, face-list size, edge and
crease sections (groups 92/93/94/95), and topology parsing remain in place.
The three pre-existing private parser-counter slots are reused across parser
phases and guarded by size/alignment assertions; no public member, callback,
or virtual was added.

The generated ASCII and Binary controls reorder the first MESH's coordinate
records to all Y, then all Z, then all X, preserving same-code occurrence
order and every count/section delimiter. They assert exact vertex/topology
payload and a following LINE sentinel. Existing missing-Y, missing-Z, and
excess-Y negative controls still refuse publication. No persistent fixture
was added.

## Implementation progress — DXF LWPOLYLINE per-vertex group order (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Autodesk's LWPOLYLINE schema defines group 90 as the vertex count and groups
10/20 as repeated OCS X/Y values, one entry per vertex; optional 40/41/42/91
values are also per-vertex arrays. The generated ASCII/Binary test grouped
these records by group code, preserving occurrence order within each array.
The original parser's X-created `vertex` cursor lost Y-before-X values and
attached repeated optional fields to the last X point. The regression failed
in both encodings before the production change.

`DRW_LWPolyline::parseCode` now indexes groups 10, 20, 40, 41, 42, and 91
using independent bounded occurrence counters. The existing million-vertex
cap and group-90 declared count bound every field; X occurrences still define
the required vertex sequence, optional omitted fields keep their zero
defaults, and `validateDxf` confirms parsed X count matches materialized
vertices. No public data member or virtual changed. (As with any installed
class private-state change, consumers should rebuild against the updated
header/library; the source-compatibility compile passed.)

The generated three-vertex polyline uses asymmetric coordinates, distinct
start/end widths, bulges, and identifiers. ASCII and Binary tests reorder the
per-vertex arrays, compare every exact field, and assert a following LINE
sentinel. A generated excess-Y negative control fails before the polyline
callback in both encodings. No persistent DWG/DXF fixture was added.

Validation:

```text
cmake --build build --target libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests lc3_compat_check -j4  PASS
build/libdxfrw_dxf_fixture_tests --lwpolyline-point-component-order  PASS
ctest --test-dir build -R '^libdxfrw_dxf_fixtures$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1)
```

This demonstrates parser field association only, not rendered 2D/3D geometry
or external consumer acceptance. No peer, CAD/kernel, full-suite run, fixture,
or support claim was added. The worktree remains broadly dirty and `.git` is
read-only, so this slice is uncommitted. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. **Self-unblock:** continue to HATCH spline
edge-array probes, then nested MLEADER; keep each as an independent fast
slice and do not wait for external qualification.

## Implementation progress — DXF LEADER 3D vertex component order (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Autodesk's LEADER DXF table defines group 76 as the vertex count (ignored for
OPEN) and groups 10/20/30 as one X/Y/Z component per vertex. The old parser
created points only on group 10 and ignored earlier Y/Z components. A
scratch-generated ASCII/Binary test grouped all Y, then Z, then X records and
reproduced that loss while keeping the advisory group-76 behavior intact.

`DRW_Leader::parseCode` now assigns 10/20/30 by independent bounded
occurrence ordinals. The existing 5,000-point cap still applies; X occurrences
define the materialized point sequence, omitted Y/Z remain zero, and
`validateDxf` rejects component-only placeholder points without X. The group
76 count remains advisory as before. No public field or virtual changed;
consumers should rebuild for the updated private class layout.

The generated controls assert all three exact asymmetric 3D points and a
following LINE in ASCII and Binary. An excess-Y mutation is rejected before
the LEADER callback in both formats. No persistent fixture, CAD/kernel run,
or support claim was added.

generated test checks exact knots, control/fit point tuples, the following
LINE, and rejection of an excess control-Y before `addHatch` publication. No

layout; downstream consumers must rebuild, with no public field or virtual

## Deeper/broader research — open-source DXF peer risk crosswalk and fast sequence (2026-10-21; research-only)

This follow-up broadens the audit from group ordering to adjacent semantic
failure modes reported by independent open-source implementations. It refines
existing DXF/HATCH, MLINE/MLEADER, 3DSOLID carrier, and modeler owners; it does
not add a numbered finding or promote a support claim.

| Primary source / implementation evidence | Finding | Plan consequence and evidence ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk [general entity ordering](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A35B8C2A-1885-4A8E-8533-E61D8A423D62.htm), [common entity codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3610039E-27D1-4E23-B6D3-7E60B22BB5BD.htm), and [group-code types](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-2553CF98-44F6-4828-82DD-FE3BC7448113.htm) | Display/table order is not a wire-order guarantee. Entity end is group 0; point group ranges identify numeric components, but meaning is entity- and scope-dependent. | Keep the existing per-entity parser dispatch. Reorder only schema-approved distinct codes; retain repeated-code ordinal order, group-0/subclass boundaries, and local count/brace/record delimiters. Never globally sort tags or treat a generic point triplet rule as sufficient for nested records. |
| Autodesk [MLINE schema](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-590E8AE3-C6D9-4641-8485-D7B3693E432C.htm) | Positions (11/21/31), segment directions (12/22/32), and miter vectors (13/23/33) are each repeated once per vertex; 74/41 and 75/42 encode nested per-element parameter lists. Group 2 and handle 340 are redundant style references, and the schema says a style entry must exist and these references must remain consistent. | Keep MLINE a candidate until the control contains a rooted MLINESTYLE entry and matching 2/340 references. Generate a two-vertex/two-element control with asymmetric vector components and non-empty 41/42 lists, then permute one vector family at a time without moving parameter/list boundaries. Compare all vectors, nested list cardinalities/values, style identity, and a following LINE in ASCII and Binary. Reject an excess component before callback publication. Do not use an unrooted/hand-minimal MLINE as conformance evidence. |
| Autodesk [MLEADER context schema](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-EC56D0DE-026D-46AB-87B1-9692393B0C22.htm) and [common MLEADER schema](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-69B9139A-48B4-48A5-B3CF-A3233ABFBE49.htm); ezdxf [MLEADER internals](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfinternals/entities/mleader.html) and [entity model](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/mleader.html) | Reused point codes appear in context data, leader nodes, and line vertices. The independent implementation models context, nodes, lines, and break records as nested objects and explicitly describes the context as complex; it documents WCS leader vertices and warns that style override flags may not correspond to stored entity overrides. | The MLEADER probe must select a single scope and tuple, preserve braces, flags, repeated-code order, break indices, and all other scopes, then assert the exact decoded context and style/presence fields. A rendered comparison is not an oracle for override-flag semantics; use raw entity fields for syntax/retention and native consumer behavior only in its separate gate. |
| LibreDWG [`NEWS`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS), current `master` as reviewed 2026-10-21 (including the 0.14-era history) | The peer changelog records fixes for HATCH association-handle index reset across paths, `has_derived` being ORed across paths, rational spline knot/weight association, and dropping the final SAT block on DXF export. These are concrete classes of scope/cardinality/terminal-record mistakes in adjacent code. | Treat them as peer-reported risk patterns, not defects in libdxfrw. Re-audit the existing HATCH association/reference tests and modeler DXF group-1/3 writer matrix for path-local handle identity, per-edge rational knot/weight counts, and final-block preservation. Reuse the owner tests; add only a scratch-generated control if the exact gap is uncovered. Record the reviewed peer revision/date for any future code-level comparison. |
| ezdxf [ACIS API documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html), [3DSOLID entity limits](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/3dsolid.html), and [ACIS FAQ](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/faq.html) | ezdxf documents limited ACIS record support, inability to load/re-export arbitrary ACIS data, and no ACIS kernel. The API page documents `export_sat()` and `export_sab()` for supported polyhedral bodies (SAT for DXF R2000–R2010; SAB for R2013/R2018), while the FAQ's SAT-only statement is stale/contradictory. | Keep ezdxf in the syntax/raw-carrier/selected-profile lane. It can generate/inspect bounded SAT/SAB profiles, but cannot independently qualify arbitrary ACIS/AcDs preservation, curved B-rep semantics, transformations, or native 3D support. Pin the exact package and inspect the emitted carrier; retain separate independent-reader/kernel and consumer gates. |
| ezdxf [MESH model](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/mesh.html) and [HATCH model](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/hatch.html) | The peer exposes explicit mesh vertices/faces/edges/creases and HATCH boundary path/edge/spline records; its entity model is useful for field-by-field inspection but does not certify native CAD behavior. | Use it selectively as a field-schema and exact-data observer where its documented model retains the target fields. Pin the exact package/source revision for composed differential runs; do not add it to every fast slice or treat successful parse/save as semantic support evidence. |

### Refined implementation-ready sequence and evidence gates

1. **Close cheap source/test audits first.** Check the existing HATCH reference
   tests and `modeler_dxf_writer_matrix_tests` for the peer-reported
   path-local handle, rational knot/weight, and terminal SAT-block cases.
   Reuse tests where exact coverage exists. For a gap, add only a locally
   generated scratch control to the owning test; do not commit a new DWG/DXF
   fixture or create another CTest lane.
2. **Resolve MLINE with a valid owner graph.** Build the smallest generated
   MLINESTYLE dictionary/style record that satisfies the required style name,
   handle, and entity reference. Preserve that graph while testing each of
   the three repeated vector families separately. The previous incomplete
   unrooted probe is discarded and contributes no positive or negative
   evidence. If the rooted ASCII/Binary control does not reproduce a mismatch,
   record the negative result and proceed without changing production code.
3. **Probe MLEADER by scope, not by tag bucket.** Choose one context point and
   one leader-line vertex only after the root context/control strings and
   child counts are explicit. Mutate one component family at a time, retain
   nested tags and breaks byte-for-byte, assert exact context/node/line values,
   and include a following entity sentinel plus a malformed-closure negative.
4. **Audit NURBS-surface grid points separately.** First map each repeated
   coordinate group to its declared U/V/control-point dimensions and current
   parser counters. Generate an asymmetric grid with distinct coordinate
   components; preserve knot/weight counts and surface flags. Reuse existing
   fixed-vector masks only if they match the grid's independent cardinality.
5. **Keep fast and composed validation separate.** Per slice: build the one
   owning test target and `lc3_compat_check`, run the direct selector and its
   owning CTest, then update this plan/receipt and move on. Run independent
   peers only at the composed, exact-version-pinned checkpoint and only for
   fields the peer retains. Run native CAD/kernel qualification at the
   existing consumer checkpoint, not for every local parser slice.
6. **Keep claim promotion gated.** Parser field association, exact raw carrier
   preservation, independent semantic interpretation, and native-consumer
   acceptance remain separate evidence tiers. An upstream issue/changelog,
   a passing peer parse, or a local generated parser test cannot alone promote
   a DWG/DXF or 3D support claim. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

No peer executable, CAD application, kernel, customer drawing, or persistent
fixture was used in this review. LibreDWG `master` and ezdxf stable/master links
are moving targets; the receipt records the review date and treats them as
source/doc observations rather than a pinned runtime result. ODA v5.4.1
remains authoritative for DWG byte-layout questions.

## Implementation progress — DXF MLINE repeated-vector component order (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The peer-risk audit found the adjacent cases already have direct owners and
coverage: `dwg_hatch_reference_graph` checks path-local HATCH references,
per-path flags, and exact rational spline knot/weight values; the modeler DXF
writer matrix checks exact group-1/group-3 SAT chunks and payload readback for
multi-chunk values, including the final chunk. The focused audit CTests pass
4/4, so no duplicate coverage or CTest lane was added.

The MLINE candidate was then generated with the existing rooted
MLINESTYLE-object pattern: a valid NOD → `ACAD_MLINESTYLE` dictionary → style
record, matching entity group 2/340 references, two vertices, and two style
elements. The first ASCII position-array permutation reproduced rejection in
the old parser. `DRW_MLine::parseCode` now indexes the nine repeated
position/direction/miter components independently by their own occurrence
ordinals, bounded by group 72 and the existing vertex cap. Parameter-list
association is no longer driven by the last group-11 vertex: group-74/75
parameter blocks advance by the declared element count, and blocks arriving
before group 73 are held boundedly and attached when that count is read.

Generated ASCII and Binary controls cover all three vector families with
unequal values, two elements per vertex, non-empty segment and fill parameter
lists, and an exact following LINE sentinel. A late group-73 control verifies
that the parameter blocks remain associated when the count follows them.
Excess group-21, -22, and -23 arrays are refused before `addMLine` callback.
No persistent fixture or new CTest lane was added. No public fields,
callbacks, or virtuals changed; the private class layout changed, so consumers
must rebuild.

Validation:

```text
cmake --build build --target libdxfrw_dwg2dxf_adapter_tests lc3_compat_check -j4  PASS
ctest --test-dir build -R '^libdxfrw_named_resource_import_evidence$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1; generated ASCII/Binary controls)
cmake --build build --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip -j4  PASS
ctest --test-dir build -R '^(dwg2dxf_modeler_dxf_writer_matrix|dwg_hatch_reference_graph|dwg_hatch_rational_spline_weight_handoff|dwg_hatch_dwg_boundary_references)$' --output-on-failure  PASS (4/4)
```

This establishes local DXF field association and bounded nested-list
preservation only. It does not establish MLINE rendering or native CAD
acceptance. No peer runtime, CAD/kernel, full suite, external drawing, or
support claim was added. The worktree remains broadly dirty and `.git` is
read-only, so the slice is uncommitted. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. **Self-unblock:** continue with one scoped
MLEADER context-array probe, then the NURBS-surface grid audit; do not wait for
