## Deeper/broader open-source DXF peer and consumer-boundary refresh (2026-10-21)

This refresh reconciles the MLINE implementation slice with a wider source
and consumer review. Autodesk's common-entity guidance says group-code tables
are not guaranteed wire order and recommends code-driven dispatch; this does
not make nested sequence boundaries optional. MLINE's schema explicitly
defines three repeated per-vertex vector arrays and count-framed 74/41 and
75/42 parameter lists, while its style name/reference fields are redundant
with the style dictionary and handle. Thus component ordinals may be assembled
independently within each documented family, but repeated-value order,
declared counts, parameter blocks, style identity, and entity framing remain
invariants. The generated rooted MLINE controls now cover this profile in
ASCII and Binary DXF.

The same official reference says SPLINE group-41 weight values are optional
for unit weights. The existing generated SPLINE/HATCH knot-domain owners
already check omitted unit weights, explicit unit weights, non-unit rational
weights, and an independently evaluated curve point; this is covered and
should not become a duplicate implementation slice. Keep this as a schema
cross-check when touching the shared spline representation.

The broader peer sweep yields three plan constraints:

1. **Treat peers as typed observers, not authorities.** LibreDWG's current
   changelog records concrete HATCH path/index/derived-state, rational
   knot/weight, and final SAT-block writer fixes; these remain targeted risk
   patterns, not libdxfrw defects. Its manual also self-identifies areas where
   behavior/test coverage is incomplete. Pin immutable peer revisions and
   compare only overlapping fields with a complete source disposition ledger;
   neither a changelog nor a peer's successful self-read promotes support.
2. **Score FreeCAD on the supported profile.** Its current DXF documentation
   describes separate C++ and optional legacy importers, enumerates their
   explicit entities, and says embedded binary ACIS/SAT solids cannot
   currently be read. Therefore the native FreeCAD/DWG-converter acceptance
   lane is a bounded 2D and explicit-entity conversion/roundtrip check. It
   cannot qualify 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY ACIS semantics; those require a separate
   exact carrier, independently calculated geometry, and an independent
   reader/kernel or another consumer that can actually ingest that profile.
3. **Compare retained semantics, not just file survival.** ezdxf documents
   itself as not being a CAD application and says unsupported version
   features are ignored on export. Peer tests must report (a) source records,
   (b) parsed/retained typed and raw fields, (c) peer-dropped/unsupported
   fields, and (d) independent semantic outcomes separately. A parse-save
   cycle or rendered image cannot cover an unretained field or certify exact
   geometry.

Implementation order is now explicit: the generated MLEADER leader-line
vertex probe also reproduced and fixed Y/Z-before-X loss in one preserved
`LEADER_LINE{}` scope; its receipt follows. Next map NURBS-surface grid-point
selectors against authoritative schema/source before writing any new probe;
if no concrete gap is identified, record the negative audit and self-unblock
to the composed checkpoint. Keep the known HATCH/modeler peer risks under
their existing owners. At the composed checkpoint only, pin one independent
DXF peer and run a field-retention matrix; do not run peer builds or full
suites per local slice. Maintain the family × version × carrier × operation
matrix and separate native 2D acceptance from solid semantics.

No external peer runtime, native CAD, or geometry kernel ran; no external
drawing or persistent fixture was added. No support claim changed. J256,
J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.
The MLINE implementation changed private class layout only, so downstream
consumers must rebuild; public callbacks and virtuals are unchanged.

## Implementation progress — DXF MLEADER scoped vertex component order (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The next candidate was narrowed to the repeated `10/20/30` vertex components
inside a single `LEADER_LINE{}` scope. Autodesk's MLeader context and leader
line tables identify these as vertex coordinates; nested `CONTEXT_DATA{}`,
`LEADER{}`, and `LEADER_LINE{}` delimiters and same-code order were held fixed.
The old parser created a vertex only on group 10, so generated ASCII and
Binary controls with repeated group-20/group-30 arrays before group 10 lost
the Y/Z values. The pre-fix focused selector failed for both encodings.

The parser now assembles each X/Y/Z component by its own bounded occurrence
ordinal, scoped to the current leader line. Closing group 305 checks that the
X slots define the point count and that Y/Z arrays do not exceed it. The
generated two-point control checks exact asymmetric tuples, closes the nested
state machine, then reads entity-level group 270 as a post-context sentinel.
An excess Y component is refused at closure in both encodings. No new CTest
lane or persistent file was added; this is parser-local context retention,
not proof of MLEADER style graph validity, CAD rendering, or native acceptance.

Validation:

```text
cmake --build build --target libdxfrw_hardening_tests lc3_compat_check -j4  PASS
build/libdxfrw_hardening_tests --mleader-context-roundtrip  PASS (ASCII/Binary, exact two-point values and excess-component rejection)
ctest --test-dir build -R '^libdxfrw_hardening$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1)
```

The private `DRW_MLeader` class layout changed; public callbacks and virtuals
did not, so downstream consumers must rebuild. No peer runtime, full suite,
native CAD, or geometry kernel ran. No support claim changed. J256, J260,
J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. **Self-unblock:** audit
NURBS-surface grid-point selector semantics next; change production only if a
primary schema/source plus a valid generated control reproduces a mismatch.

## Deeper/broader research — NURBSURFACE DXF wire-schema negative audit (2026-10-21)

The last item in the local group-order queue was incorrectly described as a
repeated NURBS-surface grid/control-point array. That premise is not supported
by the available DXF schema or the independent field map. Autodesk's published
[SURFACE DXF page](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-BB62483A-89C3-47C4-80E5-EA3F08979863.htm)
documents common surface modeler data (groups 1/3) and U/V isoline counts
(71/72), but no repeated NURBS control-point grid. The [LibreDWG 0.13.4
ENTITIES field map](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/ENTITIES.html)
maps NURBSURFACE's additional explicit DXF fields as scalar 170/290 and four
fixed 3D vectors at groups 10–13 (`uvec1`, `vvec1`, `uvec2`, `vvec2`); it does
not list grid dimensions, knot arrays, or repeated CV points. Its separate
modeler payload fields are not a control-point array. This independent map is a
peer cross-check, not a replacement for Autodesk's wire-format authority.

The ObjectARX `AcDbNurbSurface::get` API describes an in-memory control-point
array and says its v index varies first. That describes the object API's data
model; it does not establish a serialized DXF group-code sequence. Do not
transfer that in-memory ordering into the DXF parser without a wire schema.
Locally, [`DRW_NurbsSurface::parseCode`](src/drw_entities.cpp) handles the
fixed vector groups by independent X/Y/Z component masks and has no repeated
grid-point selector. The corresponding writer emits those same fixed vectors
for AC1027+; it does not serialize a grid array.

**Disposition:** close the grid-point permutation probe as not applicable,
not as a demonstrated parser defect or broad NURBSURFACE support result. Do
not add a synthetic grid, modify production, or add a test lane. If a future
wire source exposes additional NURBSURFACE fields, first map their exact
version/subclass and cardinality; then test with a locally generated
ASCII/Binary control only when the schema predicts an independently
permutable repeated array. Keep NURBS/ACIS geometry semantics in the existing
separate consumer/kernel qualification gate.

The local component-order queue is now complete: the reproduced SPLINE,
MESH, LWPOLYLINE, LEADER, HATCH spline-edge, MLINE, and scoped MLEADER cases
have fast generated controls; this NURBSURFACE candidate produced a negative
schema audit. Self-unblock to the existing composed checkpoint: review exact
source/typed/raw/dropped-field dispositions under current owners, then run the
already-planned single pinned peer comparison. Do not block local work on
native Windows/Linux FreeCAD or ACIS/kernel availability; do not make either a
substitute evidence claim. No new fixture, peer runtime, full suite, finding,
or support promotion. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Deeper/broader cross-implementation route-boundary refresh (2026-10-21)

The broader comparison confirms that the next peer check must be selected by
evidence question and exact route, not by the most impressive project-level
version matrix. [LibreDWG's current NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS)
shows continued object-specific DXF/DWG corrections alongside parser safety
work; its published documentation distinguishes read/write capabilities and
records skipped advanced objects. It remains the best open DWG conversion
observer here, but a version-level pass does not imply per-family or per-field
completeness. Locally available LibreDWG 0.14 command-line tools are identified
by exact executable SHA-256 in the linked receipt. A later scratch-only attempt
is recorded below; it was not an admissible peer comparison.

[ACadSharp's current version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/README.md)
claims DWG/DXF read/write through AC1032, but that matrix is only route
availability. It says nothing by itself about object payload coverage, modern
AcDs owner/key mapping, or semantic geometry. [IxMilia.Dxf's published
matrix](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf) is a more bounded DXF-only observer
(R10–R2014) and explicitly excludes MESH, MLEADER, SURFACE, TABLE, and
VIEWPORT; use it only for an overlapping cohort, not for current modeler
families. The [LibreCAD bundled coverage inventory](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD/blob/master/libraries/libdxfrw/DWG_DXF_COVERAGE_INVENTORY.md)
is useful for discovery but calls itself an inventory, not byte-level
conformance; `typed-dispatch`, `raw-preserved`, or `fixture-needed` labels do
not demonstrate field round-trip or consumer behavior, and the fork is not an
independent parser vote.

Current [ezdxf ACIS documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html)
and its [3DSOLID reference](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/3dsolid.html)
make the structural/semantic boundary explicit: it handles only a limited
ACIS subset, can lose unsupported records, and does not supply a general
analytic geometry kernel. Although the stable documentation is now at 1.4.5,
keep this repository's existing executable differential pinned to 1.4.4 until
its runtime, configuration, hashes, and expected field map receive a deliberate
refresh. The current host has no ezdxf runtime; do not turn that into a
blocking dependency. If the local LibreDWG binaries are used instead, record
their exact hashes and restrict the comparison to their chosen converter
direction/version and a generated scratch cohort.

The [FreeCAD importer documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md)
further constrains consumer claims: its C++ and optional legacy importers have
different explicit entity subsets; DWG arrives through a converter-to-DXF
route; and embedded ACIS/SAT solids are not read by the documented stock
importer. Keep native FreeCAD as a named 2D/explicit-entity consumer check,
separate from ACIS/ACDS semantics and independent kernel evidence.

**Readiness delta:** for the one composed peer checkpoint, select a single
implementation based on the question (LibreDWG for a pinned DWG/DXF conversion
route; ezdxf for DXF structure/carrier retention; ACadSharp for a pinned DWG
object cohort; FreeCAD for a named native 2D consumer profile). Record the
source denominator and local typed/raw/emitted dispositions separately from
peer typed/raw/dropped/unsupported fields, diagnostics, and any independent
semantic metrics. A peer pass can qualify only that route/cohort. If the peer
cannot run, self-unblock to local implementation/readback work; do not wait on
external installs, native platform qualification, or ACIS/kernel availability.
No new parser defect, test lane, dependency, persistent fixture, or support
claim was found. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — peer-control fixture closure negative control (2026-10-21; scratch-only, not a support result)

To self-unblock the planned peer checkpoint without installing a dependency, I
generated an AC1015 ASCII DXF from scratch with asymmetric LINE/3DFACE/sentinel
coordinates and converted it through the locally available LibreDWG 0.14
tools. `dxf2dwg`, `dwgread`, and LibreDWG `dwg2dxf` returned success, but the
local `dwg2dxf` stopped at `BAD_READ_OBJECTS` (12), reporting a remaining object
frame routed as an entity. The peer JSON identified that frame as type 49,
handle `0x31`, a `BLOCK_HEADER` named `*Model_Space` beyond the model/paper
headers reported by its `BLOCK_CONTROL`.

The hand-authored DXF-to-DWG generator did not establish a complete
`BLOCK_CONTROL`/`BLOCK_HEADER` graph. ODA v5.4.1 §§20.4.51–20.4.52 defines the
block-control handle list separately from the two special model/paper handles
and the block-header record; the observed duplicate/unlisted header makes this
input inadmissible for a compatibility conclusion. Therefore this is a
fixture-generation negative control—not a libdxfrw finding, peer pass, or
support result. No source fix is warranted from it. The experimental parser
classification change was reverted, and the generated DXF/DWG/output files were
removed.

**Updated peer preflight:** before interpreting any peer result, verify the
source denominator and closure of each block control/header/entity relation:
ordinary block-header handles must match the control list; model/paper handles
must match their special references; each header must resolve to exactly one
BLOCK/ENDBLK identity; and every source entity must have an explicit disposition.
Peer success alone is not a source-validity oracle. If a locally generated
control fails this preflight, discard it and self-unblock to another local
owner/readback task rather than changing production code to accept an
unreconciled graph. Exact tool hashes and observations are in the linked
research receipt. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Deeper/broader research — open-source peer admission, license, and codec-lineage refresh (2026-10-21)

This source-only pass revisits candidates that appeared in the broader DWG/DXF
search and asks whether they qualify as open-source comparators, independent
parser implementations, or semantic consumers. A project name, public GitHub
repository, file-format badge, or visible source is not enough: the plan needs
the license, actual route, codec ancestry, supported operation, and explicit
failure/drop behavior before it can assign evidence weight.

| Source reviewed | Evidence and boundary | Plan disposition |
|---|---|---|
| [SeaCad / Sea-DXF-Core](https://github.com/seaflower205/Sea-DXF-Core) current README and repository license disclosure | The README calls the source proprietary despite public visibility and describes a pre-1.0 ASCII/Binary DXF-only core, AC1009–AC1032. It explicitly says DWG is not implemented, complete entity CRUD is not claimed, and neither a renderer nor native B-rep kernel is implemented. Its project-reported POINT completion and strict-reparse claims are not independently reproduced here. | Exclude from the open-source implementation census, comparator runs, and dependency options unless its license changes. Do not infer DWG, full DXF entity, or 3D support from the broad version range or “lossless” framing claim. Its stated plan is not a libdxfrw defect source. |
| [mlightcad/cad-viewer proprietary parser disclosure](https://github.com/mlightcad/cad-viewer/blob/main/PROPRIETARY-PARSER.md) | The project distinguishes its open viewer/model from a licensed DWG parser. Its default open-source DWG route uses LibreDWG; the proprietary route claims 3DSOLID extraction and partial SAB decoding but says full B-rep tessellation is unavailable and exposes best-effort wireframe or bounding-box fallback. | Count the default DWG route under LibreDWG lineage. Exclude the licensed parser from open-source peer counts. Even if an authorized exact package is later used, score only its admitted structural/carrier behavior; wireframe/bounds do not qualify analytic geometry, topology, or B-rep validity. |
| [UnCAD](https://github.com/iyulab/uncad) current README and route notes | The project states that DWG goes through LibreDWG FFI, ASCII/Binary DXF goes through the separate `undxf` crate, and output is JSON/SVG/PNG; the DWG/DXF writer API was removed. | Deduplicate DWG observations with LibreDWG and exclude it from writer comparisons. Keep `undxf` as an optional, separately pinned DXF syntax/value observer only if a concrete unresolved route question remains; rendered projection is not modeler semantics. |
| [OpenCADStudio](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio) latest release page, current issue index, and existing release/lock audit | The latest listed release at this review is v2026.42 (2026-10-18), already bound elsewhere in this plan to an ACadRust-derived codec. The current issue index lists #1896 (opened 2026-10-19), reporting one AC1027 ACIS-solid file rejected at handle `0x5B87`, type code 37. The input is unavailable here and the report postdates the pinned release. | Keep #1896 as a codec-lineage-specific failure-shape lead under the existing AC1027 modeler/ACIS gates. ### Evidence-layer model and implementation-ready delta

Use these independent result columns in the existing PAR-07/S8 composed
receipt; do not collapse them into a single “3D pass”:

1. **Container/carrier:** source DWG version or DXF `$ACADVER`; section/record
   extents; exact 3DSOLID/REGION owner key; ordered DXF groups 1/3; group-350
   history references kept separately; raw byte hash and explicit disposition
   for every AcDs/DataStorage record.
2. **Profile/framing:** SAB signature, save-format word, word width, record
   count, terminator, and exact profile admission. A numeric 23200 under ASM
   BinaryFile4 is not the same row as ACIS BinaryFile 21800.
3. **Parser/model:** typed-reference closure, rooted body coverage,
   unsupported/raw records, transform candidate, and per-owner association.
   Reference closure or a parser success is structural evidence only.
4. **Geometry semantics:** separately authored asymmetric expected topology,
   bounds, area/volume, units, and transform. A CADMPEG model/analytic helper

   outputs are not an independent-kernel vote from FreeCAD.
5. **Consumer/platform:** exact converter, native build/platform, selected
   importer, settings, warnings, and expected imported-source disposition.
   Stock FreeCAD ACIS is `UNSUPPORTED_CONSUMER`, not a codec failure or pass.

Use these five independent result lanes in the existing PAR-07/S8 composed
record; do not add a combined “3D supported” boolean:

## Implementation progress — S3.7c parser-fed non-finite ACIS location rejection (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Extended the generated complex ACIS BinaryFile 21800 stream matrix with NaN,
+infinity, and -infinity variants in a rooted point `LocationVec`. Each
generated stream is parsed into SAB records, built into the ACIS model, and
sent through rooted body projection. The wire-fed values reach the model, but
projection fails with `InvalidModel` at the owning body and clears
pre-seeded output. This verifies the existing finite-value guard end-to-end;
it does not change parser policy, B-rep semantics, or support status.

## Deeper/broader research — ezdxf ACIS subset-reader route correction (2026-10-21; source review)

This pass rechecked the exact current ezdxf release documentation after earlier
plan entries had classified ezdxf as a raw-carrier observer only. The
versioned v1.4.5 ACIS API documents a limited SAT/SAB graph parser, supported
subset export, mesh-to-ACIS generation, and flat-polygon-face extraction. This
is a meaningful open-source parser/converter route for a narrow polyhedral
subset, but not a general ACIS kernel. No package was installed or run, and no
external drawing or repository fixture was used.

| Primary source | New evidence and ceiling | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ezdxf [v1.4.5 release/tag](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/releases/tag/v1.4.5) (`84ae319`), [ACIS API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html), and [versioned documentation index](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) | `acis.load()` accepts SAT or SAB, `body_from_mesh()` creates a restricted ACIS Body from a mesh, `export_sat()` and `export_sab()` serialize supported structures, and `mesh_from_body()` extracts meshes from flat polygonal `Face` records. The API documents the topology vocabulary (Body/Lump/Shell/Face/Loop/Coedge/Edge/Vertex) and says unsupported ACIS entities become `NONE_ENTITY`, their data is lost, and arbitrary ACIS cannot be loaded and re-exported. Curved faces (including spline surfaces, tori, and cones) require an ACIS kernel and are not tessellated by this route. | Correct ezdxf's status from `RAW_CARRIER_ONLY` to `CONDITIONAL_LIMITED_ACIS_GRAPH_AND_POLYHEDRAL_CONVERTER`. It may be an optional independent parser check for the documented subset, with per-entity unsupported counts; it is not an independent geometry kernel, arbitrary SAT/SAB preservation oracle, curved-surface oracle, or native CAD acceptance route. Pin the exact 1.4.5 artifact/source and checksum before execution. |
| ezdxf [v1.4.5 FAQ](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/faq.html) versus the more specific [ACIS API reference](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) | The FAQ still says ezdxf has no ACIS creation/editing functionality and only writes SAT, while the v1.4.5 API explicitly exposes `body_from_mesh()`, `export_sat()`, and `export_sab()`. The FAQ is stale or overly broad relative to the current module reference; this pass did not inspect or execute the release artifact to resolve implementation details. | Prefer the version-specific module API for candidate discovery, but make an isolated source/package inspection and a smoke check the entry condition. Do not treat the documentation inconsistency as proof that every documented SAB path is present in a chosen wheel or works for a target profile. |
| [AutoCAD 2026 DXF `3DSOLID` reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm) and ezdxf [ACIS API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) | Autodesk's carrier fields remain modeler version 70, proprietary group-1 lines, optional group-3 continuations, then `AcDb3dSolid` and optional history handle 350. This carrier framing is distinct from the limited SAT/SAB record parser. The API accepting `bytes`/text directly does not by itself validate DXF group ordering or modern DWG `AcDsPrototype_1b` associations. | Keep byte-carrier reconstruction, raw ACIS parsing, graph/topology inspection, polyhedral mesh extraction, DWG AcDs owner/key closure, and consumer acceptance as separate result rows. An ezdxf `load()` result cannot close the DWG AcDs lane. |
| LibreDWG [0.14.1 NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) and open [issue #1398](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1398) | NEWS says LibreDWG fixed missing `num_subents`/`subents` parsing for a **DXF** `PERSUBENTMGR` path. Issue #1398 remains open and describes a separate **DWG** class-object layout where a proposed field sequence yields an implausible subentity count; the reporter explicitly distinguishes `AcDbPersSubentManager` from `AcDbAssocPersSubentManager`. | Do not read the DXF importer fix as resolving the DWG layout or as evidence for local type-515 dispatch. Use the exact peer release only for a DXF field-retention comparison if that question is in scope; keep the DWG object bounded-opaque/unsupported until the ODA spec or independent producer evidence settles its wire order. |

### Optional implementation-ready qualification recipe

1. Add no mandatory dependency, CI job, fixture, or per-slice external run.
   At the existing composed external-semantic checkpoint only, bind ezdxf
   v1.4.5 to an immutable package/source identity and checksum, inspect the
   selected artifact's license and ACIS modules, and smoke-test availability
   in an isolated environment. If this is not immediately available, record
   `NOT_RUN/UNAVAILABLE` and self-unblock to local implementation.
2. Start with one locally generated asymmetric closed polyhedron (for example,
   a non-cubic prism) whose vertex coordinates, face loops, orientation,
   connected components, and bounds are independently specified. Do not use
   a downloaded drawing or commit generated DXF/SAT/SAB fixtures. Exercise
   the SAT v700 and SAB v21800 APIs separately; the latter is a direct SAB
   payload comparison, not proof of AC1027+ DWG AcDs decoding.
3. Compare source handles and ordered raw carrier bytes separately from the
   parsed ACIS graph. For the supported polyhedron, compare Body/Lump/Face/
   Loop/Coedge/Edge/Vertex reachability and the mesh's vertex/face incidence,
   winding, connected components, and expected bounds against the independent
   source model. Record `NONE_ENTITY`, parser errors, ignored nodes, and
   incomplete graph closure as explicit failures/unsupported outcomes; never
   count a partial mesh as a complete solid pass.
4. Include one curved-face negative control and one unsupported-node control.
   The expected result is an explicit unsupported/partial classification, not
   a fabricated mesh or a support promotion. Do not use `mesh_from_body()` for
   analytic surface dimensions, curved tessellation, volume, manifold validity,
   or B-rep-kernel agreement.
5. Run this only as a bounded optional comparator and report the exact package,
   Python/runtime, source/output hashes, profile, and per-source entity
   disposition. It can raise confidence only for the exact tested SAT/SAB
   polyhedral subset; native application behavior and all DWG/AcDs semantics
   remain separately gated.

Do not infer changed profile support, parser maturity, geometry correctness, or a new independent semantic result from the version bump.

### One-time checkpoint procedure

At the already-planned composed PAR-07/S8 checkpoint—not during each fast slice—use this bounded process:

1. Resolve the exact v0.6.3 tag/source manifest and read its SAT/ASM support and open-items documents. Record the source commit, declared codec/profile, and relevant limitations. If exact-tag documentation cannot be inspected, stop this optional comparison as `NOT_QUALIFIED`; do not fill gaps from `latest` docs or older release behavior.

## Implementation progress — DWG class string-footer unaligned bit offsets (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA DWG specification v5.4.1 §§10.2 (p. 87) and 20.1 (p. 104) describe
the R2007+ class/object string-stream footer using bit-relative offsets and a
low size word whose high bit signals an additional high-size word. The
existing local regression covered the extended size only when the footer was
byte-aligned. Extended that generated helper test across all seven nonzero
bit offsets; each case writes the high word, flagged low word, and terminal
bit at the selected bit position, then checks the reconstructed size, start
bit, and returned cursor. No production parser behavior changed.

As a bounded corpus check, the current locally available AC1024 DWGs under
`/Users/dli/doc/dwg` did not reproduce the known classes-stage error 8 in the
observed traces. Their strict `dwg2dxf` conversions still failed at the
separate complete-read-disposition/export-preflight gate; several also report
incomplete frame coverage, and one reports a classes CRC warning. These are
not successful conversion or support results, and do not resolve the known
RTM-save report without the exact failing inputs. No local DWG/DXF was copied
into the repository.

references and the current ezdxf entity model, then verified that the existing
generated POLYFACE fast test exercises the consequential reader/writer
asymmetry. It found no uncovered local defect. The distinction is important:
the explicit-facet entities have different wire identities and topology
contracts, so their results must not be collapsed into one “mesh supported”
claim. No external drawing or peer executable was used.

| Source / local evidence | Contract established | Plan consequence |

Header groups 71/72 may be incorrect; readers must tolerate unusual vertex/face ordering, even though producer-generated records should put coordinate vertices before face records. Face index signs encode invisible edges; face records are limited to four vertex references by the AutoCAD entity structure. | Keep separate reader tolerance and writer normalization criteria. Do not treat advisory 71/72 counts as the completed coordinate pool, force reader input into writer order, or reject a valid drawing solely because face records are interleaved/forward-referencing. When writing, emit a stable coordinate pool followed by stable face records while preserving face indices, sign/visibility, face metadata, and caller-owned list order. |
| Autodesk [3DFACE DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-747865D5-51F0-45F2-BEFE-9572DBC5B151.htm) and 2026 [3DFACE reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-747865D5-51F0-45F2-BEFE-9572DBC5B151.htm) | `3DFACE` is a separate WCS-corner primitive with three or four corners; a missing fourth corner duplicates the third. Group 70 encodes per-edge invisibility bits. | Keep corner identity, degenerate-triangle convention, and hidden-edge flags in the `3DFACE` family lane. An emitted face count or triangulated projection alone does not prove these fields survived. |
| Autodesk [MESH DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-4B9ADA67-87C8-4673-A579-6E4C76FF7025.htm), ezdxf [MESH model](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/mesh.html), and [POLYFACE guidance](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorials/polyface.html) | MESH has its own counted vertex, face-list, edge, crease, and subentity-override fields; its faces support n-gons, unlike POLYFACE's 3/4-index face records. ezdxf exposes MESH indices as zero-based indices into its vertex array. Its 1.4.5 page calls R2000 the minimum, while older ezdxf internals text gives a conflicting introduction-era statement; neither resolves Autodesk's historical target-name/profile boundary for every release. | Maintain separate index-base, version, record-name, and class-profile assertions. Preserve the existing unqualified status for pre-AC1024 MESH output; do not infer acceptance from a local readback or from conflicting peer docs. |

This does not authorize sorting tags or normalizing unlike entity types into one mesh representation. | Keep group-code component assembly distinct from child-record ordering. Preserve group-0 and `SEQEND` framing; only normalize the POLYFACE coordinate/face pools at the writer boundary. Continue to use exact entity references for per-family field semantics. |
| Local [`validatePolyfaceDxf`](src/drw_entities.cpp), [`processPolyline` / `processVertex` / `writePolyline`](src/libdxfrw.cpp), generated [`runDxfPolyfaceCompletedPool`](tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp), and its focused [`dxf_polyface_completed_pool`](tests/CMakeLists.txt) CTest | Source and test cover actual-pool index bounds, stale/zero advisory header counts, interleaved and face-first/forward face records, one-/two-index wireframe records, first-zero termination, stable writer normalization, caller-vector non-mutation, ASCII/Binary readback, invalid-index transactional refusal, and following-entity preservation. The test does not assert manifoldness or generic solid validity, correctly keeping those outside this DXF syntax guard. | Reuse this focused owner for changes to PFACE parsing/writing and hostile-index validation. No duplicate test is justified by peer/security reports alone. Add a new generated control only if a local audit finds an uncovered distinct path (for example an alternate API bypassing the completed-pool validator). |

## Deeper/broader research — ezdxf SAB authoring ceiling and AcDs loss-stage attribution (2026-10-21; research only)

This pass reconciled the public LibreDWG #1411 reproducer against the current
ezdxf ACIS API, FAQ, and DXF-structure documentation. The sources contain a
material version/documentation conflict: the stable 1.4.5 ACIS API documents
`export_sab()` and R2013/R2018 SAB export for polyhedra, while the same-version
FAQ says ezdxf only writes SAT and provides no ACIS-data authoring. The API
also explicitly limits its model to known/simple records and flat polygonal
faces; it has no ACIS kernel. Consequently, pin and inspect the actual
generator artifact/output instead of assuming either prose statement is the
runtime contract. The public #1411 DXF→DWG→DXF recipe is a useful peer loss
shape, but because its first conversion uses the peer DWG writer, it cannot
by itself isolate the peer DWG reader. The separate reported AutoCAD DWG case
is confidential and not independently inspectable. No peer code was run, no
external file was fetched, and no local behavior or claim changed.

|---|---|---|

The docs say generated polyhedra load in Autodesk products/BricsCAD, but this does not imply arbitrary B-rep, curved-face, or kernel-level semantic coverage. | Admit ezdxf as an optional scratch-only carrier author for its exact documented profile, not as an arbitrary SAT/SAB oracle. Use asymmetric, explicitly specified polyhedra for raw carrier and bounded face/topology controls; classify each test by exact DXF version and entity class (`3DSOLID`, `REGION`, or `BODY`). Keep curved surfaces, general B-rep validity, and independent semantic qualification outside this route. |
| ezdxf [FAQ 1.4.5](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/faq.html) versus the above ACIS API | The FAQ says ezdxf reads SAT/SAB but only writes SAT, and says it cannot create/edit ACIS data; the current ACIS API exposes `export_sab()` and `export_dxf()` and shows a polyhedron-generation example.    referenced rows from stale, dangling, and unreferenced rows. Never use
   signature scanning as a substitute for the strict indexed route.
2. **Payload join:** resolve each supported modeler entity by the exact
   handle/key/reference path, not sorted position or encounter order. Test
   inline records, Blob01 single- and multi-page payloads, repeated chunks,
   multiple schema rows, empty/missing payload, duplicate/ambiguous owner,
   reordered records, stale index entries, and exact maximum/truncation
   boundaries. Preserve source-owner, payload hash, and disposition in the

   entity and block/INSERT occurrence in output. The result must be preserved,
   transformed under a documented supported rule, or refused with a diagnostic

   or the converter exit code look successful. Keep schema-aware DWG writing

<a id="deeperbroader-open-source-dxf-reader-diversity-and-libredwg-loss-boundaries-2026-10-21-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader research — independent DXF reader diversity and LibreDWG loss boundaries (2026-10-21; research only)

This pass screened two additional open-source DXF readers and refreshed the
official LibreDWG conversion caveats. The important new distinction is that
`uncad` is not an independent DWG implementation: its DWG path is LibreDWG
through FFI, while DXF is parsed by the separate `undxf` crate. Its published
3DSOLID/REGION path can therefore be a candidate DXF carrier/parser differential,
but not a second DWG codec, writer check, ACIS kernel, or native-CAD result.
The new `dxfscan` project is a much narrower Binary-DXF subset parser. A
source-visible DXF core with a proprietary license was excluded from code and
implementation comparison. No peer repository was cloned or built, no external
drawing was fetched, and no local code, fixture, dependency, or support claim
changed.

| Project/source | Direct evidence and limits | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|

### Implementation-ready refinement — existing PAR-06/PAR-07/S2/S7/S8 owners

1. **Keep parser lineages separate.** The primary DWG contrast remains the
   local reader versus one pinned LibreDWG/ACadSharp route. `uncad` shares
   LibreDWG for DWG and must not be counted as an independent vote. For DXF,
   `undxf` is the newly identified optional independent parser; do not assume
   its normalized model preserves every raw group, omitted-field state, or
   extension payload.
2. **Do the fast local work first.** Inventory existing generated ASCII/Binary
   DXF controls and fill only missing version/encoding/owner cases. Keep all
   new drawings and SAB bytes generated in memory or under a temporary path;
   do not add a persistent external fixture. Run the owning focused selector
   and CTest after each slice; defer full tests and peer matrices to existing
   composed gates.
3. **Use a bounded optional DXF differential.** If `undxf` is already
   available at the composed gate, pin crate, model, and toolchain versions;
   feed a scratch-generated file that exercises ordinary 3D entities and a
   separate modern ACDSDATA modeler record. First require complete parse and
   source identity; then compare ordered raw groups, owner/key/payload hashes,
   typed field values plus absent/unstated distinctions, and block occurrence.
   Treat differing parser diagnostics as evidence to investigate, not as a
   reason to normalize away bytes.
4. **Bound the Binary-DXF subset candidate.** `dxfscan` may be tried only if
   already installed and only for a supported common-entity control. Inspect
   its complete-document behavior before admitting it; unknown entity
   preservation is not proof that OBJECTS, ACDSDATA, or terminal EOF are
   validated. With no source audit or eligible run, mark `NOT_QUALIFIED` and
   self-unblock.
5. **Preserve loss-stage accounting.** When comparing DWG→DXF peers, snapshot
   source object/class IDs and per-block membership before conversion; then
   inspect converter diagnostics and the emitted file before opening it with a
   second reader. An absent entity can arise in decode, class dispatch,
   conversion, writer dispatch, or consumer import. Do not assign it to a
   reader based only on final counts.
6. **No evidence promotion from this pass.** A DXF parser differential can
   strengthen syntax/carrier/association confidence only. It cannot establish
   DWG codec parity, B-rep validity, correct transforms/units, independent
   kernel semantics, or FreeCAD/native acceptance. All six J items remain
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S3.7 ACIS pointer range-before-narrowing guard (2026-10-21; generated in-memory fast slice, uncommitted)

Closed a local integer-safety gap in the model builder. A caller-built
`DRW_SabToken` can carry a signed 64-bit pointer value even though resolved
graph indices are `int`. `buildAcisModelImpl` previously converted the value
to `int` before checking whether it was inside the node table; an extreme
positive value could therefore be implementation-defined at the conversion
boundary, even though rooted projection later rejected the raw/reference
disagreement. The model builder now compares the nonnegative raw value to the
node count in an unsigned wide domain and narrows only an in-range index.
Out-of-range and negative values continue to map to unresolved `-1`; the raw
token remains unchanged, so the rooted validator reports the exact invalid
pointer and ordinal.

Added a generated in-memory graph regression with `LLONG_MAX`. It verifies the
model reference remains unresolved and rooted projection refuses the raw
reference transactionally with `InvalidReference`, the source node, and
pointer ordinal 0. This is a graph-boundary correctness/safety check only; it
does not extend SAB grammar, DWG/DXF carrier support, or geometry semantics.
No DWG/DXF/SAB fixture, dependency, peer run, or CTest registration was added.

Fast validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests --parallel 2`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_graph_preservation$' --output-on-failure` (1/1)
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests` (PASS)
- `jq empty` for the research receipt and scoped `git diff --check`

No full suite or external/native test was run. The broadly dirty worktree
remains uncommitted; this slice did not stage or commit other work. Findings
and top-level subplans remain 143/78; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`. **Self-unblock:** continue to the next distinct
locally evidenced PAR-07/S3.7 or PAR-07/S2/S8 gap; do not wait for an optional
peer or native consumer run.

### Research-to-implementation crosswalk

1. **Keep support multidimensional.** For every route record format/version,
   direction, encoding, entity type, source handle, owner and block occurrence,
   raw-carrier disposition, parsed fields, geometry/semantic result, and
   destination-consumer outcome. “Reads DWG/DXF” and entity totals are not
   pass criteria.
2. **Reuse existing local fast owners first.** ACadSharp's codepage, VERTEX,
   repeated-record, and modeler-loss reports already map to generated local
   controls in `tests/gbk_codepage_tests.cpp`,
   `tests/dxf_fixture_tests.cpp`, `tests/hardening_tests.cpp`,
   `tests/modeler_dxf_writer_matrix_tests.cpp`, and related ownership tests.
   Before adding any vector, confirm the current test does not already cover
   that exact encoding/version/parent role/record boundary. A peer issue alone
   never justifies duplicating a test or changing production parse behavior.
3. **Choose one optional peer per unanswered question.** Use LibreDWG or
   ACadSharp for a DWG operation only at a supported exact version/direction;
   use IxMilia.Dxf or ezdxf only for their DXF profiles. If no exact artifact,
   input, or operation is available at the composed checkpoint, write

4. **Sequence gates without adding test cost.** For a code edit, run the owning
   `-Werror` target and smallest generated selector/CTest. Run a complete suite

   remains optional and never blocks local slices.
5. **Preserve the evidence ceiling.** A second parser can confirm only its
   exact syntax/field/carrier scope. Topology parsing, polyhedral extraction,
   complete output, independent-kernel agreement, native consumer acceptance,
   and cross-platform behavior each require their own evidence. This research
   cannot close or promote J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, or J295; each remains
   explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — PAR-07/S3.7 ACIS signed pointer-limit controls (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Added the negative signed-limit companion to the existing generated
`LLONG_MAX` pointer regression. `DRW_SabToken::ival` is signed; an in-memory
body pointer set to `LLONG_MIN` must remain unresolved in the constructed
model rather than narrowing or becoming a valid node index. Rooted projection
must then reject the preserved raw value transactionally and report the exact
body node and pointer ordinal. The production guard already checked
nonnegative raw values before narrowing; this slice closes the opposite limit
in its regression coverage. It is a graph-boundary check only, not SAB grammar,
carrier, or geometry support.

Fast validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests --parallel 2`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_graph_preservation$' --output-on-failure` (1/1)
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests` (PASS)
- `jq empty` for the receipt and scoped `git diff --check`

No DWG/DXF/SAB fixture, dependency, CTest registration, full suite, or external
peer/native run was added. The shared worktree remains broadly dirty. Git
metadata is read-only (`.git/index` is not writable), so this slice is recorded
but cannot be committed in this environment. Findings/subplans remain 143/78;
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.
**Self-unblock:** continue to the next distinct source-backed local PAR-07/S3.7
or PAR-07/S2/S8 slice; do not wait for an external peer or platform gate.

## Deeper/broader research — BRL-CAD current DXF converter profile and security gate (2026-10-21; primary-source review)

This refresh replaces the older, narrower BRL-CAD tutorial description with
the project's current converter manuals and rechecks the open POLYFACE safety
report. It sharpens BRL-CAD's possible role as an optional explicit-geometry
consumer; it does not establish a new libdxfrw defect, ACIS route, or required
peer gate. No BRL-CAD executable or external drawing was run.

| Primary source | Evidence and ceiling | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| BRL-CAD [`dxf-g(1)` manual](https://brlcad.org/docs/html/man1/dxf-g.html) | The current manual says the converter expects ASCII DXF as defined by the AutoCAD 2006 manuals. It lists POLYLINE subtypes including 3D polyline, 3D polygon mesh, and polyface, plus LWPOLYLINE, 3DFACE, LINE, CIRCLE, ARC, ELLIPSE, SPLINE, and selected annotation entities. It describes per-layer object aggregation and optional coordinate scaling/vertex merge tolerance. It does not list Binary DXF, `MESH`/`AcDbSubDMesh`, `3DSOLID`, `REGION`, `BODY`, surfaces, DWG, or whole-document/raw-tag preservation. | Bound any optional BRL-CAD read comparison to a pinned ASCII-DXF input and one documented explicit family at a time. A successful import is geometry projection, not entity/handle/block/reference preservation. Use a uniquely isolated layer per control, record scale and merge tolerance, and predeclare normalized coordinates/units before comparing geometry. Leave unlisted families `NOT_ESTABLISHED`, not implicitly supported. |
| BRL-CAD [`g-dxf(1)` manual](https://brlcad.org/docs/html/man1/g-dxf.html) | The inverse route tessellates BRL-CAD regions to triangles and emits either 3DFACE or POLYFACE MESH, with explicit unit and chord/normal/distance tolerances. It is not a typed CAD-entity round-trip or ACIS/SAB writer. | Do not use `g-dxf` as a DXF writer-parity oracle. At most, compare its faceted output to an independently authored expected tessellation under a recorded tolerance; keep its intentional representation change separate from libdxfrw's record-preserving writer contract. |
| BRL-CAD open [issue #228](https://github.com/BRL-CAD/brlcad/issues/228) and open [PR #245](https://github.com/BRL-CAD/brlcad/pull/245) | The issue reports a full-path heap out-of-bounds read from attacker-controlled POLYFACE indices in `dxf-g`; the PR remains open/unmerged in the reviewed snapshot. The proposed positive-index checks must be reviewed against DXF's legal negative signed indices (invisible-edge flags) and zero terminator before being treated as a complete fix. This is peer-reported security evidence, not a libdxfrw defect or an executed result here. | Keep malformed/adversarial inputs out of BRL-CAD until a pinned merged revision is source-audited and its importer path plus signed-index behavior are checked. Do not copy the PR's policy as the format rule. The existing local `validatePolyfaceDxf()` and `dxf_polyface_completed_pool` generated ASCII/Binary tests already cover the local actual-pool boundary; no duplicate vector is justified. |
| Local [`validatePolyfaceDxf()`](src/drw_entities.cpp) and focused [generated test owner](tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp) | The local reader validates after the completed POLYLINE child pool is known; the writer validates before emission. Existing fast cases cover legal signed visibility values, zero termination, actual-coordinate-pool range checks, extreme negative magnitude, atomic invalid-output refusal, both encodings, and a following-record sentinel. | Reuse the existing focused owner if PFACE code changes. Only add a new local test if source tracing finds a distinct reachable path that bypasses this validator; do not add a peer reproducer or persistent fixture. |

### Implementation-ready peer admission and self-unblock

## Deeper/broader research — ACIS peer validator and normalization boundary (2026-10-21; primary-source review)

This pass drills into what an ACIS peer's public validator and parser actually
establish, and how mutating convenience APIs can contaminate a differential.
It also rechecks whether the newest ACadRust repository tests constitute an
independent geometry oracle. The result is a tighter optional structural-peer
protocol, not a new local defect, a kernel result, or a reason to add peer work
to ordinary implementation slices. No peer runtime, geometry kernel, CAD
application, or external drawing was run or fetched.

| Primary source | Evidence and ceiling | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| ACadRust [`SatDocument` API](https://docs.rs/acadrust/0.5.5/acadrust/entities/acis/types/struct.SatDocument.html), [`SabReader` API](https://docs.rs/acadrust/0.5.5/acadrust/entities/acis/sab/struct.SabReader.html), and [ACIS module docs](https://docs.rs/acadrust/0.5.5/acadrust/entities/acis/index.html) | The versioned 0.5.5 API says `validate()` checks pointer targets and topology consistency; `complete_brep_links()` fills missing vertex-edge and edge-coedge links; `strip_for_sab()` removes non-core records and remaps references; `SabReader::read()` produces a `SatDocument`. This is a potentially useful independent *structural* implementation, but not a geometric-kernel test. The published API is 0.5.5, not proof of the moving repository's 0.6.5 surface. | If this optional route is used, pin the exact crate/archive/source and reconcile docs/API versions first. Parse an untouched copy, capture parser disposition and record/reference graph, then run validation before any repair or subset conversion. Treat `complete_brep_links()` and `strip_for_sab()` as mutations: never use their post-state alone to claim source topology was valid or fully preserved. |
| ACadRust [current `roundtrip.rs`](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/blob/main/tests/roundtrip.rs) | The source contains a helper that fabricates marker-shaped SAB bytes for AcDs transport tests and a generated planar cube built by ACadRust, then written and reread by ACadRust's own DWG writer/reader. These are useful transport/self-consistency controls; they are not independent input truth, an independent parser vote, or native CAD acceptance. The branch is mutable and must be pinned before assigning these tests to a release. | For any peer report, label evidence separately as generated self-roundtrip, opaque byte retention, parser acceptance, graph validation, external geometry measurement, or native open/audit. Do not promote a row from the first two categories. |
| `cq-acis` [README](https://github.com/monozukuri-ai/cq-acis/blob/main/README.md) and [`acis-core` API](https://docs.rs/acis-core/latest/acis_core/) | `acis-core` documents a Rust-owned model, bounded SAB/ASM profiles, retained raw records, and explicit statement that it constructs no OCCT solids; `cq-acis` documents conversion of a supported subset through CadQuery/OpenCascade. They form one parser/converter route, not two independent votes, and share OCCT lineage with other OCCT-based checks. Unsupported geometry and approximate/healed conversion remain visible limitations. | Keep the route as one optional parser-plus-kernel lane. Require raw-record/unsupported accounting before conversion, exact parser profile, kernel/version/options, validity checks, and independently expected geometric measures. Do not combine `acis-core`, `cq-acis`, CadQuery, and FreeCAD Part as independent kernel confirmations. |
| FreeCAD [current DXF guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and [DWG converter source](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py) | The guide lists differing built-in C++ and legacy importer entities and says embedded binary ACIS/SAT is not read by stock DXF import. The DWG helper runs a separately selected external converter before the DXF importer; file creation is used as its success indication on those paths. Thus an imported document may validate the converter/DXF/explicit-entity path while saying nothing about solid-body consumption. | Maintain distinct result rows for converter completion, strict DXF parse, explicit-entity import, modeler-carrier retention, and actual solid semantic import. A FreeCAD pass that has no solid importer is not an ACIS semantic result; capture per-source-handle dispositions and the importer backend. |

## Deeper/broader research — explicit-facet peer geometry and subdivision evidence boundaries (2026-10-21; primary-source review)

This pass separates three DXF 3D representations that can otherwise be
mistaken for interchangeable “mesh/solid” support: classic POLYFACE geometry,
the `MESH`/`SUBDIVISION` `AcDbSubDMesh` cage, and ACIS modeler carriers. It
also tightens the optional GDAL comparison recipe to avoid projection defaults
that can collapse identities or cap block expansion. This is an evidence and
implementation-readiness refinement only; no local defect or new support
claim was found.

| Primary source / route | Evidence and limits | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk [POLYLINE DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-ABF6B778-BE20-4B49-9B58-A94E64CEFFF3.htm), [POLYFACE mesh reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2016/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-96B6288E-F413-46C0-968A-A314171C0AAE.htm), and [VERTEX reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-0741E831-599E-4CBF-91E1-8ADBCFD6556D.htm) | POLYFACE is a POLYLINE with coordinate VERTEX records followed by face-definition VERTEX records; face indices are one-based, negative indices encode invisible edges, and zero terminates a face's index list. Autodesk says writers should emit all coordinate vertices before face records while readers should tolerate noncanonical order. Face records are limited to four indices, so larger polygons require triangulated/wedge representation. | Keep source-record order, parent/child identity, signed edge-visibility indices, terminators, winding, and any triangulation disposition separate from the resulting surface. The existing generated local PFACE tests own signed-index/zero/bounds/order cases; do not duplicate them. A projected closed surface is not evidence that the original PFACE record graph or invisible-edge flags were retained. |
| Autodesk [2024 MESH DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-4B9ADA67-87C8-4673-A579-6E4C76FF7025.htm) | `MESH` uses subclass `AcDbSubDMesh`; its published groups include subdivision level, level-0 vertex/face/edge counts, crease values, and per-subentity property overrides. That is a subdivision control-cage representation, distinct from a POLYFACE's explicit face surface and from an ACIS B-rep carrier. Preserving the level-0 cage/metadata alone does not prove the evaluated subdivision surface is correct. | Report distinct outcomes: `polyface_explicit_surface`, `subdmesh_base_cage_retained`, `subdmesh_evaluated_surface`, and `acis_modeler_carrier/shape`. Only claim the exact level implemented and checked. Preserve crease and override records in addition to coordinates/face lists; keep MESH/SUBDIVISION version spelling as its own version-profile invariant. |
| GDAL [DXF driver documentation](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | The current driver documents POLYFACE as an OGR `POLYHEDRALSURFACE` projection and `3DFACE` as a polygon projection. It exposes `EntityHandle` and optional raw unhandled codes, but maps records into OGR features, tessellates some curves, and by default may inline/merge block geometry. Its inserted-feature limit is 10,000 per block unless `DXF_FEATURE_LIMIT_PER_BLOCK=-1` is set. Binary DXF reading is documented only from GDAL 3.12. The supported-entity list does not establish `MESH`/`AcDbSubDMesh` parsing or evaluated-subdivision semantics. | GDAL can be considered as a one-time independent projection for a narrowly matched ASCII-DXF POLYFACE control, not as a document-preservation or MESH/ACIS oracle. Pin exact build/options and bind every projected feature to source handle/block occurrence before comparing. If handle/occurrence identity is unavailable or ambiguous, keep the result advisory. |
| IxMilia.Dxf [project compatibility and status](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf) | Its README lists MESH among the exceptions to its R10–R2014 DXF coverage and warns that its writer may emit 3DSOLID, REGION, and BODY entities that AutoCAD does not open. | Admit IxMilia only as a version-matched parser differential for entity families it actually supports. Do not use its MESH parser absence or modeler writer output as a positive 3D interoperability result. This corroborates the existing parser-versus-writer evidence boundary; it is not a new libdxfrw defect. |

### Implementation-ready refinement — existing POLYFACE, MESH, and PAR-07/S8 owners

1. Keep the local fast-test owners unchanged. For POLYFACE, reuse the existing
   completed-child-pool test matrix for vertex/face ordering, signed visibility
   flags, zero termination, actual-pool index bounds, and following-record
   framing. For MESH, reuse the generated ASCII/Binary version-profile tests
   for record spelling, `AcDbSubDMesh` class identity, base-cage fields,
   overrides, and following-entity continuity. No peer-inspired fixture or
   duplicate test is justified by this research.
2. If GDAL is already available at the existing composed checkpoint, use only
   a locally generated ASCII POLYFACE file for the optional geometry
   projection. Record exact GDAL version/build, DXF driver, `$ACADVER`, file
   hash, and options. For block-graph identity, use `INLINE_BLOCKS=FALSE` so
   INSERTs remain reference points and definitions remain in the `blocks`
   layer. For a separate INSERT-expansion observation, use
   `INLINE_BLOCKS=TRUE`, `MERGE_BLOCK_GEOMETRIES=FALSE`, and
   `DXF_FEATURE_LIMIT_PER_BLOCK=-1` to avoid merged geometry and the documented
   10,000-feature cap. Set `INCLUDE_RAW_CODE_VALUES=TRUE` where raw-tag
   evidence is needed. For Binary DXF, require GDAL 3.12 or later and record
   the encoding explicitly.
3. Compare by source handle and block occurrence, then separately compare the
   normalized OGR surface to independently known generated coordinates and
   face topology. Do not use feature count alone. OGR projection does not
   establish that DXF child order, signed invisible-edge flags, raw group
   values, styles, or arbitrary object graph were retained; assert those with
   the existing local raw/typed tests. If the route changes representation or
   cannot preserve identity, record that disposition instead of treating it as
   an entity-by-entity pass.
4. Never send `MESH`/`SUBDIVISION` input through a POLYFACE oracle and call the
   result subdivision support. For `AcDbSubDMesh`, require base-cage and
   crease/override equality for a retention claim; evaluated-surface claims
   need an implementation that actually evaluates the cage and a separate
   geometric oracle. Keep ACIS SAT/SAB/AcDs entity association and B-rep
   validity on their existing independent PAR-07/S8 gates.
5. No GDAL install, peer runtime, persistent fixture, CI lane, or full suite is
   added to ordinary implementation slices. If the optional build is absent,
   record `NOT_RUN / PEER_UNAVAILABLE` once and immediately self-unblock to the
   next local implementation item. A projected POLYFACE pass does not promote
   J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, or J295.

This refinement adds no finding, top-level subplan, code, test, fixture,
dependency, peer execution, or support claim. Findings/subplans remain
143/78; validation cadence and implementation order are unchanged. J256,

<a id="deeperbroader-multi-layout-dwg-writer-source-confirmed-capability-gap-2026-10-21-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader research — multi-layout DWG writer source-confirmed capability gap (2026-10-21; research only)

### Decision

The current worktree's DWG writer has a source-confirmed **multi-layout
capability gap**, not a reproduced case of silently misplacing user data.
`dwgRW::writeLayout()` can serialize a `DRW_Layout` record, but the current
writer rejects a `DRW_Block_Record` carrying a nonzero `layoutHandle`, writes
the BLOCK_RECORD layout-handle slot as null, and its deferred BLOCK_CONTROL
path emits only the fixed `*Model_Space` and first `*Paper_Space` owners.
Consequently, a file containing multiple standalone LAYOUT objects or an
ordinary user block named `*Paper_Space0` is not evidence of a valid
multi-layout DWG graph. The current writer fails closed for the reciprocal
link rather than claiming it can write that feature.

This audit was against the current **working tree** on branch
`codex/dwg-dxf-open-source-parity` at HEAD `de27a33`; the inspected DWG writer
and tests have substantial uncommitted changes. Treat the source locations
below as a working-tree capability assessment, not as an assertion about
`origin/master` or a clean checkout. Before implementing, reconcile the exact
target branch/commit and recheck these anchors; preserve all unrelated local
changes.

### Cross-project evidence and limits

| Primary source | Verified observation | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Local [`dwgWriter15::defineBlock(DRW_Block_Record)`](src/intern/dwgwriter15.cpp), [`emitBlockRecord()` / `emitDeferredBlockControl()`](src/intern/dwgwriter15.cpp), [`prepareBlockOwnedEntity()` / `recordBlockOwnedEntity()`](src/intern/dwgwriter15.cpp), and [`dwgRW::writeLayout()`](src/libdwgr.cpp) | `defineBlock(record)` rejects every nonzero `record.layoutHandle`; `emitBlockRecord()` writes a null hard-pointer in the layout slot; deferred output creates only the fixed Model and first Paper owners. Entity placement is keyed by model, first paper, or a normal user block. `writeLayout()` emits one object frame without itself closing the LAYOUT dictionary ↔ LAYOUT ↔ BLOCK_RECORD graph. | Register **PAR-144** under the existing 7G.3 layout-graph implementation owner. Do not mark the present behavior as a corrupt-output bug: the API refuses the unrepresented association. Keep read-side coverage and standalone LAYOUT object roundtrips as narrower capabilities. |
| Local [`testConsecutiveNamedBlockOwnership()`](tests/block_owner_tests.cpp) and standalone LAYOUT cases in [`dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp`](tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp) | Existing coverage proves DXF can preserve a `*Paper_Space0` BLOCK body and that the DWG object writer can encode selected LAYOUT fields. These tests do not produce a DWG where that BLOCK_RECORD is reciprocally associated with its own LAYOUT and owns layout-specific entities. | Extend the existing generated test owner. Do not add a downloaded drawing, persistent fixture, new test target, or redundant CTest registration. Existing DXF multi-layout tests remain useful but cannot close the DWG writer gap. |
| Autodesk [entity ownership](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2022/ENU/OARX-DevGuide/files/GUID-A0FDAE4E-9DAE-4256-8CE0-E3BD8D81A058.htm), [BLOCK_RECORD DXF contract](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A1FD1934-7EF5-4D35-A4B0-F8AE54A9A20A.htm), and [LAYOUT reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-433D25BF-655D-4697-834E-C666EDFD956D.htm) | Autodesk documents entities as owned by a `BlockTableRecord`, predefined `*MODEL_SPACE`, `*PAPER_SPACE`, and `*PAPER_SPACE0` records, a hard-pointer association from BLOCK_RECORD to LAYOUT (DXF group 340), and separate layout properties/links. | Model entity owner, layout identity, current/active layout, BLOCK_RECORD identity, and LAYOUT identity as separate data. Do not infer the active layout solely from a name suffix or a global `PaperSpace` bit. |
| ODA [DWG specification v5.4.1](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf), §§20.4.2, 20.4.51–20.4.52 | The common entity handle data and entity mode are versioned; BLOCK_CONTROL's child-list shape distinguishes fixed Model/Paper roots from other block headers; BLOCK_HEADER records a hard-pointer Layout Handle. In particular, do not generalize the R13–R14 ownerless entity-mode notes in §20.4.2 to later versions. | Before changing any writer byte layout, derive each target-version field/owner sequence from these sections and the current writer path; verify version-specific details with generated byte walks or sample traces. Keep R13–R14 first/last chains separate from R2004+ explicit owned-object lists. |
| CADCraft open [#1463](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/issues/1463) and merged [#1080](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/pull/1080) | The synthetic three-layout report says same-ACadRust reread retained membership while ZWCAD 2025 placed the paper entities on the first tab. A later comment says the application's #1080 change made non-active layout entities block-owned instead of treating all as the active paper-space mode. This remains a project report, not a local reproduction or normative rule. | Use distinct per-layout marker entities, views, and owners; a same-codec roundtrip is only internal consistency. Verify the correct mode/owner contract against ODA for each supported version before choosing an encoding. |
| ACadRust [#143](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/143), now closed as completed; current source at pinned commit [`a106f1e`](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/commit/a106f1e087233851bfd31c38ee0c6755ed50e213) | The issue reports duplicate `*Paper_Space` names after suffix stripping, an 11/11 ACadSharp 3.8.0 read failure, and cautions that simply preserving every source suffix can leave the active paper-space record unnamed. The current pinned source has a `dwg_block_name()` helper documented as reserving the bare paper-space name for the active record without colliding with other layouts. The commit merges a broad batch; its code comment and issue closure are not a reproduced external acceptance result. | The useful peer lesson is joint handling of **unique names plus active-layout identity**. Do not copy a suffix-strip or suffix-preserve rule alone. Keep the peer's fix as a future pinned comparator lead; do not count it as an independent parser/consumer vote or as proof that libdxfrw's wire output is correct. |
| LibreDWG [documented object/space model](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) | Its manual describes ModelSpace, PaperSpace and Blocks as distinct entity containers and discusses BLOCK_CONTROL / BLOCK_HEADER access. The reviewed text is not a version-by-version multi-layout writer conformance result. | Retain LibreDWG as a candidate independent structural reopen at the composed checkpoint only after pinning exact source/build/version and confirming that its observable model exposes the layouts under test. Do not use its broad capability statement as a pass. |

The closed ACadRust issue and the open CADCraft report expose different layers:
the former concerns writer naming collisions plus active-layout selection;
the latter concerns emitted ownership/mode interpreted by an application.
Neither is the exact local failure. The local source audit independently shows
that this writer does not yet represent or emit the reciprocal multi-layout
DWG graph at all.

### PAR-144 — emit a closed multi-layout DWG ownership graph

**Status:** `IMPLEMENTATION_IN_PROGRESS / RECIPROCAL_LAYOUT_GRAPH_PARTIAL`.
**Parent:** existing 7G.3 layout graph and DWG writer owner ledger; do not add a
new top-level subplan.

#### Implementation slices

1. **Reconcile target and pin the contract.** At the first implementation
   slice, verify the target branch/commit and re-read the current writer,
   `DRW_Block_Record`, `DRW_Layout`, facade, and tests. Read ODA §§20.4.2,
   20.4.51–20.4.52 for the specific output version. Write a compact contract
   table for AC1015 legacy chains and AC1018+ owned-object lists before editing
   bytes. Stop only if current source no longer matches this gap; otherwise
   mark the changed premise in this plan and self-unblock to the next step.
   **Completed 2026-10-21:** worktree branch `codex/dwg-dxf-open-source-parity`
   at base `de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9`; local
   `origin/master` is `d68fb1ed937ad2a74a54f6208277ec10a1b031b0`. Rechecked
   both target and worktree anchors; the source-confirmed gap is unchanged.
   ODA §20.4.2 distinguishes R13–R14 owner-relative entity modes from the
   R2000+ owner handle stream; §20.4.51 excludes fixed Model/Paper roots from
   the counted block-header entries; §20.4.52 ends BLOCK_RECORD with the
   LAYOUT hard pointer; §20.4.84 gives LAYOUT its reciprocal paperspace
   BLOCK_RECORD soft pointer. No entity-mode or BLOCK_CONTROL count rule was
   changed in this slice.
2. **Add explicit layout-owner state.** Represent each paper layout with a
   stable source/output layout identity and its associated BLOCK_RECORD handle.
   Keep Model, active/default Paper, inactive Paper layouts, and ordinary user
   blocks as distinct owner kinds. Do not infer these identities from
   `DRW_Entity::space`, ownerless entmode, or `*Paper_SpaceN` suffixes alone.
   Reuse existing handle allocation, owner membership, insert reverse-link,
   and rollback ledgers where their keys fit; otherwise add one indexed
   owner abstraction rather than rescanning every entity for each layout.
3. **Emit reciprocal records and names.** Preallocate all required handles
   before encoding references. Emit the LAYOUT dictionary root and one entry
   per layout, each LAYOUT object, each corresponding BLOCK_RECORD/BLOCK/
   ENDBLK group, and reciprocal references. Keep the active/default
   `*Paper_Space` role unique; allocate distinct inactive names deterministically
   without collapsing source identities. A parsed nonconsecutive suffix is
   not an identity source. Reject duplicate names/handles, missing endpoints,
   conflicting roots, or nonreciprocal links before publication. Complete the
   LAYOUT-to-viewport side of the graph as well: preserve its common
   last-active-viewport reference and, for R2004+, the versioned viewport
   count/list. Keep plot-settings payload validation as a separate concern;
   don't let a peer's plot-setting failure masquerade as a layout-graph result.
4. **Route all owned content by exact owner.** Place each layout's marker,
   VIEWPORT, annotation, and ordinary entities into its associated block
   record; keep INSERT target (`blockRecH`) distinct from the INSERT entity's
   owner. Ensure compound children such as ATTRIB/SEQEND follow their INSERT
   and that model/current paper-space defaults retain existing behavior. Derive
   entity mode and handle stream from the per-version ODA contract; do not
   apply the CADCraft workaround globally without this check.
5. **Make finalization atomic and complete.** Validate one-to-one
   LAYOUT↔BLOCK_RECORD association, unique object handles and reserved block
   names, exactly one BLOCK/ENDBLK pair per record, correct block-control
   membership, entity-owner membership, INSERT target/reverse links, active
   paper-space identity, and dictionary reachability before committing output.
   A refusal must preserve a preexisting destination and report a typed
   diagnostic. Keep existing single-layout and ordinary-block output
   byte/semantic behavior stable.
6. **Use generated fast tests first.** Extend the existing DWG local roundtrip
   owner with a from-scratch in-memory case: Model plus active and two inactive
   layouts; distinct LINE/TEXT sentinels; in AC1024, two paper-space VIEWPORT
   entities per layout with exact LAYOUT handle references; one ordinary block
   and a ModelSpace INSERT/ATTRIB/SEQEND crossing neither layout owner;
   deliberately shuffled input order; and one nonconsecutive source suffix.
   Assert unique emitted names, reciprocal handles, correct layout dictionary
   membership, exact marker/viewport owner and count by layout, viewport
   handle references, correct active-layout selection, object-map uniqueness, and
   terminal section integrity. Independently inspect old-version first/last
   entity chains and modern owned-object lists; a reader-only roundtrip cannot
   substitute for that check. ODA §20.4.38 does not serialize DXF group 69
   (`vpID`) in the DWG VIEWPORT entity; keep ID-1/ID-2 checks in a separate DXF
   compatibility profile, not the DWG object test. AC1015 generated coverage
   now includes type-34 VIEWPORT frames as well as line/text; require reader
   retention, but do not infer independent byte correctness from a
   same-library writer/reader result. The observed reader warning was fixed by
   retaining the inline body bound check before common-handle parsing and
   applying the post-handle string-end check only when the string stream is
   detached. Keep raw frame/handle-map inspection and an independent reader or
   native checkpoint as separate qualification work. Add malformed missing/duplicate/
   nonreciprocal owner controls with destination-preservation and corrected
   same-writer retry. No external or binary fixture file is needed: generate
   the inputs locally from scratch inside the existing test.
7. **Validate by boundary, then compose once.** Start with AC1015 and AC1024
   (legacy chain vs. modern owned list), then extend only the narrow encoding
   matrix to AC1018/AC1021/AC1027/AC1032 as required by touched writer branches.
   Build the strict library/test target, run only the focused selector and its
   owning CTest, `lc3_compat_check` if an installed surface changes, and scoped
   `git diff --check`. At the composed checkpoint, select one exact-pinned
   independent structural reader per applicable version profile and record
   diagnostics, layout count/name/tab-order, active name, and per-owner entity
   handles. ACadRust's reported AC1015 reader defect is not evidence against
   emitted writer bytes; avoid using versions before its chain-reader fix is
   confirmed in the pinned artifact. ACadSharp's open ShadePlotDPI report can
   discard LAYOUT objects on read, so qualify its diagnostics and plot-settings
   input before interpreting missing layouts. `dwg-rs` is a newly refreshed
   optional structural candidate: pin an exact commit and use its raw object
   walker only if an admission probe proves it exposes the generated profile's
   object types/handles and sufficient payload/handle-tail bytes; its own README
   reports six real-corpus VIEWPORT typed-decode failures, so typed VIEWPORT
   success is not an acceptance criterion and its application writer is not
   qualified. If the raw API cannot inspect the needed tail, record
   `NOT_QUALIFIED` and continue with the local bounded frame walk. LibreDWG
   conversion exit status alone is insufficient: require complete DXF
   sections/EOF and expected entities. Keep native CAD audit separate; do not
   repeat a full suite or peer/native run for each slice.
8. **Update and self-unblock.** After each implementation item, update this
   plan and a research/implementation receipt with evidence, exact tests,
   changed support disposition, and remaining next action. After each slice
   is committed, show the user a compact progress summary and commit identity.
   Do not stop at external-platform or independent-semantic gates: record an
   unavailable optional comparator once as `NOT_RUN`/`NOT_QUALIFIED` and
   continue the next local-ready item. Preserve the user's existing dirty
   changes; isolate commits by precise paths once safe.

## Deeper/broader research — multi-layout viewport closure and peer-reader failure isolation (2026-10-21; research only)

### Decision

Refine existing **PAR-144**; do not add another finding or top-level
subplan. The most important uncovered acceptance boundary is not just the
reciprocal `LAYOUT` ↔ `BLOCK_RECORD` pair: `LAYOUT` also carries viewport
references, and each layout's entities must be attributed through the
version-appropriate owner structure. The immediate fast-test target remains
generated, scratch-only data. Independent reader behavior must be interpreted
with parser diagnostics and known version-specific defects in view.

The ODA specification is normative for the binary layout. Autodesk API docs
confirm the user-facing distinctions among current layout, selected tab, and
the special active Paper Space block. ezdxf's main-viewport-ID-1 note is useful
as a compatibility test shape, but that documentation itself uses tentative
language and is not a DWG wire-format authority.
