## Deeper/broader research — independent reader and FreeCAD consumer boundaries (2026-10-21; research only)

### Decision

Refine **PAR-144**'s composed qualification, not the local implementation
scope. A peer is useful only for the layer it actually exposes: binary object
and owner traversal, DXF layout semantics, or application import behavior.
FreeCAD is an important downstream consumer, but its current multi-layout DXF
import limitation prevents it from serving as the sole oracle for the DWG
writer's multiple-layout graph. Converter completion, DXF parsing, layout
preservation, and semantic import remain separate observations.

### Broader findings and consequences

| Source | Evidence from the source | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [reader API/manual](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi), [owned-entity traversal](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dwg.c), and [versioned object model](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dwg.spec) | Its manual shows independent traversal through `BLOCK_CONTROL` entries and `get_first_owned_entity()` / `get_next_owned_entity()` for per-`BLOCK_HEADER` membership. The documented `dwg_paper_space_ref()` is a convenience for the paper-space root, not a demonstration that every named paper layout was resolved. The current manual separately says its DWG writer omits R2007 and that R2010–R2018 writer output can fail CRC/audit checks. | At a composed checkpoint, LibreDWG may independently witness decoded object/owner structure only for exact versions where its **reader** accepts the output and exposes the needed references. Enumerate block records/layout associations; do not use only the active-paper convenience API. Record parse diagnostics, version, and per-owner handle census. Its writer limitations do not establish reader limitations, but disqualify LibreDWG-generated files or write/read self-roundtrips as a cross-version normative oracle. Pin the executable and source revision before use. |
| ezdxf [layout manager](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/layouts/layout_manager.html), [layout model](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/layouts/layouts.html), and [layout structures](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfinternals/layout_management.html) | The API exposes layout names in tab order, active paperspace selection, and an entity-to-owner-layout lookup; its model explicitly distinguishes `Modelspace`, each `Paperspace`, and reusable `BlockLayout`. The technical page documents that active paper content is serialized in the DXF `ENTITIES` section while inactive paper layouts live as BLOCKS content. | Use ezdxf as an independent **DXF** semantic parser for a DXF directly emitted by libdxfrw, or for a separately identified converter output. Assert tab-order names, active layout, per-layout entity membership, and block-vs-layout distinction. It is not a DWG parser; a DWG→DXF converter result must be reported as a two-stage observation, not attributed to the DWG writer alone. |

The documentation lists paper-space objects among importer capabilities, but does not promise preservation of every layout as a separate FreeCAD object. | A FreeCAD import pass/failure cannot alone accept or reject PAR-144's multi-layout graph. Keep `DXF parser preserves layout graph` separate from `FreeCAD importer presents every layout`; capture the importer path/version and expected one-layout limitation. A FreeCAD result may still qualify other supported consumer behaviors (e.g. explicit 2D entities) but not complete multiple-layout preservation until the upstream limitation is resolved or a verified newer version changes it. Do not download/commit the issue's sample archive; continue using local generated tests. |
| FreeCAD [DWG converter implementation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py) | The current LibreDWG and ODA converter branches wait for the subprocess and then report conversion success if the expected DXF path exists; those branches do not check the subprocess return code or validate DXF sections/content before returning the path. | For FreeCAD-path testing, add external harness assertions for converter exit status, complete DXF structure/EOF, expected layout names, and owner-specific marker counts before importing. Log converter identity/options and importer backend separately. Output-file existence, UI success text, and a rendered view are not sufficient evidence of converter or multi-layout correctness. |
| ACadSharp [current `Layout` model](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/Objects/Layout.cs), [`BlockRecord` model](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/Tables/BlockRecord.cs), and merged [attribute-link PR #446](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/446) | Its source has an explicit `Layout.AssociatedBlock`, makes the paper viewport a member of that associated block, carries `LastActiveViewport`, and exposes a `BlockRecord.Layout` association. PR #446 fixing attribute-definition synchronization was merged in January 2025; an earlier discussion about DWG attribute limitations therefore must not be repeated as a current master fact without checking the selected release. | Treat ACadSharp as a candidate independent semantic/structural reader, not a normative byte-layout source. At qualification time pin a release/commit that contains the relevant fixes; use valid default plot settings to avoid the separately known ShadePlotDPI reader issue; inspect exact owner and attribute dispositions. Do not infer attribute interoperability solely from the historical issue or merged PR. |

### DWG VIEWPORT scope correction — ODA §20.4.38 and local codec audit

The earlier ID-1/ID-2 test wording applies only to a DXF compatibility profile,
not to the DWG VIEWPORT entity itself. ODA §20.4.38 lists the DWG VIEWPORT
entity's center, paper width/height, view state, and common handle data; it does
not list DXF group 69 (`vpID`). ODA §§20.4.69–20.4.70 describe separate
VIEWPORT ENTITY CONTROL (type 70) and VIEWPORT ENTITY HEADER (type 71)
objects. The local [`DRW_Viewport::parseDwg` and `encodeDwg`](src/drw_entities.cpp)
also do not read or write `vpID`; DXF parsing/writing does. Therefore DWG
assertions compare exact viewport entity handles, owner membership, common
LAYOUT last-active reference, and R2004+ count/list. Keep DXF group 69 / main
viewport-ID conventions in an independent DXF-only test.

The first generated experiment found that AC1024 readback delivered the
viewport entities but naturally left `vpID` at its default, while AC1015
type-34 frames were warned and omitted despite document-level read success.
The follow-up writer receipt proved the frames were emitted. Code tracing then
localized the AC1015 reader failure: `sBuf` aliases `buf` for inline-string
versions, but after `DRW_Entity::parseDwgEntHandle` the parser compared that
advanced shared cursor with `stringEndBit == bodyEndBit`. Common handles are
outside the data-body range, so this false boundary rejection ran before the
viewport-specific handle sequence. Guarding only that post-handle comparison
when the string stream is detached preserves the earlier body/string bounds
while allowing AC1015's handle tail to be read. The generated same-library
roundtrip now retains all four AC1015 VIEWPORT entities. This closes the
observed local failure, not independent correctness: same-library readback is
not an independent parser or raw handle-map proof.

- The generated in-memory DWG roundtrip now places distinct LINE/TEXT markers
  in two named paper-layout block owners, plus a separate ordinary block with
  a ModelSpace INSERT, one ATTRIB, and SEQEND. This tests that the insert target
  block, insert owner, and layout owners do not collapse into one relationship.
- AC1024 adds two VIEWPORT entities to each named paper layout and verifies
  the exact handles in each `LAYOUT` count/list and last-active reference, as
  well as per-block readback ownership. It intentionally does not assert a
  DWG viewport ID. AC1015 also emits two type-34 VIEWPORT entities per named
  paper layout and requires generated reader retention; it does not assert

- The generated writer now checks its completed `DwgBlockWriteResult` during

- The reader callback now checks parsed `BLOCK_RECORD` fields against that

### Current-paper-layout serialization boundary (2026-10-21)

Autodesk documents CTAB as a drawing-saved system variable, but its published
DXF HEADER-variable table does not list `$CTAB`. The native LayoutManager also
exposes current layout and the associated BlockTableRecord, while Autodesk's
layout guide says the canonical `*PAPER_SPACE` BlockTableRecord points to the
last active Paper layout. Keep those claims at their proper layers: inspect the
canonical record-to-LAYOUT association in serialized DWG/DXF structure, and
query CTAB/CurrentLayout in a native host. Do not make a missing literal
`$CTAB` header pair a serialization failure. The generated test does not yet
exercise a non-default current paper layout; it does assert that the canonical
paper-space record is associated with the default `Layout1` in the original
compound-owner control. A separate generated AC1024 case now associates the
canonical record with a non-default `LOCAL_LAYOUT_DPI` layout and checks the
serialized links plus active-owner entities. Native CTAB/current-tab state
remains a separate, unqualified external observation until a native host
check is available.

### Decision

Refine existing **PAR-07/S8 carrier, semantics, and peer-admission gates**;
do not add a finding or top-level subplan. This pass is a current-source
cross-check, not a newly discovered route: `obj2cad`, `cq-acis`/`acis-core`,
ezdxf, OCCT commercial exchange, ProGPU, LibreDWG, and LibreCAD_3 are already
covered elsewhere in this plan. Their evidence ceilings remain unchanged.
Separate the project-maintained 3D status matrix from an independent execution
receipt, and peer-wide capability claims from tested per-family/version/
direction coverage.

### Implementation-ready, low-overhead sequence

1. Continue the owning local fast tests for each changed codec invariant. Do not
   add optional peers to the ordinary build/CTest path or run full suites per
   slice.
2. At the composed ACIS checkpoint only, first ask whether a specific producer
   or carrier-dialect question remains after local byte, owner/key, parser-fed,
   and generated semantic controls. If not, record `NO_ADDITIONAL_PEER_NEEDED`
   and self-unblock to the next local-ready item.
3. If an already-screened or new peer is genuinely needed, pin its exact source
   commit, artifact/build hash, dependency set, license, and call path before
   use. Generate only locally authored asymmetric analytic geometry in a
   unique temporary directory. Record the DXF version/encoding, SAT or SAB
   profile, source entity, payload length/hash, warnings, and every
   unsupported/omitted body record. Do not download or commit fixtures or
   generated DWG/DXF files.
4. Compare only the exact route: raw payload/framing and strict target-format
   reopen first, then compare parsed topology and independent analytic
   expectations. Do not
   derive expected geometry from the writer's readback, infer general curved
   support from one analytic case, or count the ACadRust-derived DWG route as an
   independent codec. If exact source/artifact/profile or expected geometry
   cannot be established, record `NOT_QUALIFIED` and continue.
5. Keep semantic-kernel and application results separate. A successful
   ezdxf flat-face mesh, FreeCAD import, OCCT commercial conversion, or
   screenshot is not a complete B-rep result. Require complete per-source
   disposition, independently authored topology/analytic measures, explicit
   tolerances and transforms, and a named application/backend when consumer
   behavior is the question.

### Implementation-ready refinement — exact-stage, fast-first checks

1. **Reuse existing generated controls first.** Audit the PAR-07/S8 generated
   carrier, ACDSDATA association, parser-fed, and analytic controls before
   adding anything. Do not add a test that merely mirrors LibreDWG issue #1411
   if current local tests already cover that distinct invariant.
2. **If a peer differential is still needed, isolate each hop in scratch.** Use
   only a locally authored/generated input (or a sample already tracked by
   this repository or the peer). Record hashes and dispositions for source
   DXF groups/ACDSDATA, intermediate DWG section map and all AcDs records,
   entity `has_ds_data` flags and exact owner/key mapping, and final DXF
   groups/payload. Do not commit generated DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB files.
3. **Select peers by stage, not headline.** Do not choose current LibreDWG
   `dwg2dxf` as a positive modern-AcDs writer oracle while its ACDSDATA output
   block remains disabled. An independent DWG reader can be considered only
   when an independently inspected DWG has a known-good AcDs carrier. Use
   `cq-acis` only after the exact raw payload is captured; do not count
   ACadRust self-roundtrip or an OCCT-backed route as independent semantic
   confirmation.
4. **Fail closed on a flag without a body.** A modeler entity with
   `has_ds_data=true` but no uniquely joined payload must be reported as
   missing/incomplete (or refused under the existing policy), not counted as
   a complete empty solid. Conversely, unreferenced/ambiguous AcDs records
   must remain visible in per-source disposition totals.
5. **Keep gates inexpensive and honest.** Run only the owning focused local
   selector for any implementation slice. Defer full suites, native FreeCAD,
   and optional peer executables to existing composed gates. If the exact
   independent input/build is unavailable, record `NOT_RUN` or
   `NOT_QUALIFIED`, finish dependency-ready local work, and self-unblock.

## Deeper/broader research — ACIS DXF version lanes and silent-loss prevention (2026-10-21; primary-source review)

### Decision

Refine existing **PAR-07/S8 and PAR-59** only. DXF ACIS transport is versioned
and must not be represented by one generic “solid round trip” result. This
cross-check adds a concrete implementation boundary and a faster validation
sequence, not a new defect in libdxfrw. No source, test, or fixture was changed
in this research pass.

### Cross-project evidence and limits

| Source | Verified observation | Implementation consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Autodesk [3DSOLID DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-19AB1C40-0BE0-4F32-BCAB-04B37044A0D3.htm), [group-code reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2027/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OARX-RefGuide-DXF_Group_Codes.html), and ezdxf 1.4.5 [Body API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/body.html) / [ACIS FAQ](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/faq.html) | Autodesk documents the entity-local 3DSOLID modeler fields (subclass, modeler version, proprietary data, optional continuation strings, history handle). ezdxf documents `acis_data` as SAT for R2000–R2010 and SAB for R2013+, and its FAQ locates modern SAB in the ACDSDATA section. ezdxf explicitly reads SAT/SAB but writes SAT only; its API does not promise arbitrary ACIS authoring or B-rep interpretation. | Treat the two serialization lanes separately: AC1015/AC1018/AC1021/AC1024 use entity-local SAT text; AC1027/AC1032 use entity-to-ACDSDATA SAB association. Do not emit an empty inline entity or claim a SAB write merely because a payload is retained in memory. Use ezdxf only as a pinned raw-carrier/association comparator for the exact feature it documents. |
| LibreDWG [`out_dxf.c`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/master/src/out_dxf.c) and open [issue #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411) | The prior source pass found current `dxf_acds_write()` has its sole section emission body behind `if (0 && _obj->num_segidx)`, despite the call site returning success. Issue #1411 demonstrates the danger of counting entity records or a successful converter exit when ACIS payload/section bytes are absent, but its public chain does not independently prove the intermediate DWG contained the section. | Keep LibreDWG out of the positive current-source ACDSDATA-writer lane. Require a strict output/section check and inspect intermediate DWG presence before attributing loss to a later read stage. |
| ACadSharp [issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195), [open PR #1240](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1240), and [prerequisite #1174](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/pull/1174) | The open issue reports `DwgReader` exposing `3DSOLID`/`REGION` entities while `DxfWriter` omits them, including solid-only block definitions. The proposed writer remains open and depends on schema work; it is not a released or independently accepted capability. | The output contract must account for every input modeler handle and its block owner: emitted with payload, deliberately transformed, explicitly diagnosed as lost, or cause refusal. Add no test solely to mirror the peer issue; reuse the existing local generated entity-disposition/block controls. |
| CADCraft [v0.10.0 release](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/releases), current [`cadcraft-dwg` manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/storytold/cadcraft/main/crates/dwg/Cargo.toml), and open [AutoCAD 2027 report #604](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/issues/604) | The release notes include merged #781 (“Keep the ACIS geometry … on save (ACDSDATA)”), but the current bridge manifest still depends on ACadRust 0.6.4, so this is an application/retention observation on a shared codec lineage, not an independent DWG parser vote. The separate #604 report says the requested AC1032 source was saved as AC1018 and AutoCAD reported six AUDIT errors; it is not an ACIS-specific test and does not establish a universal CADCraft failure. | If the route is used at the existing composed gate, pin the app release, lockfile, ACadRust artifact, input and output signatures. Record requested versus actual target DWG/DXF version, audit/importer path, per-handle carrier disposition, and whether the case was untouched retention or newly authored geometry. Treat #604 as a target-version/audit caveat, not a new libdxfrw defect. |
| Archived [netDxf changelog](https://github.com/haplokuon/netDxf/blob/master/doc/Changelog.txt) | The project records a historical fix for reading the ACDSDATA section and describes it as an undocumented DXF section affecting 2013+ databases; the repository is archived. This supports the need for a section-level parser lane, not a current writer or semantic capability claim. | Keep it discovery/history only. Do not add it as a routine dependency or current acceptance gate. |

### Fast, implementation-ready version matrix

| Target DXF lane | Required carrier/association | Fast local acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024 | Ordered SAT text stored on each supported ACIS entity; preserve modeler version and history reference, with group-1/3 continuation/chunk boundaries respected. | Generate in-memory SAT cases at continuation boundaries; serialize, parse, and compare exact ordered payload plus entity handle/type/block ownership. Cover `3DSOLID`, `REGION`, and `BODY` only where the existing implementation actually supports that carrier. |
| AC1027 and AC1032 | SAB bytes stored in ACDSDATA with a unique entity↔record/key association; entity flags, object ids, section records, and group-320/310 relationships must close. In the entity stream, apply the group-92/group-160 proxy-byte budget first; only the correctly ordered remaining group-310 bytes may be assigned to modeler data. Group 320 is an arbitrary ID, not a translated owner pointer. | Reuse existing generated ACDSDATA association/index controls; assert exact owner/key/payload hashes, duplicate/ambiguous refusal, missing-record refusal, and source-to-output disposition. Keep proxy and ACIS byte counts separate. Do not use a same-codec geometry result as semantic proof. |
| Cross-version downgrade | Exact SAT conversion requires a supported converter/semantic codec; raw SAB bytes cannot simply be relabeled as SAT. | If no authorized supported conversion exists, require a structured warning/loss disposition or an atomic refusal. Ensure success status cannot coexist with a silently empty solid. Record actual output signature, not requested target alone. |

Implementation order for the next relevant PAR-07 slice:

1. Audit the current DXF ACIS parse/write dispatch and reuse the extant generated
   carrier and ACDSDATA association controls; map their selectors to the matrix
   above before adding tests.
2. Implement only the first uncovered local boundary. Preserve legacy SAT code
   paths while handling modern SAB section/key associations independently.
   Keep writes transactional so a malformed/ambiguous association cannot leave
   a partial entity or section in the output.
3. Add a regression only for a proven uncovered invariant, generated in memory
   or scratch. Do not commit new external DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB fixtures.
4. Run the owning fast selector and its focused CTest only. Defer the full suite,
   peer binaries, and native CAD qualification to the already-defined composed
   gate. Record slice progress when committed; after each item, update this plan
   and self-unblock to the next locally executable item rather than waiting on
   peer releases or platform access.

No new finding or top-level subplan is warranted; counts remain **144 / 78**.
The current peer set does not provide an independent, universally capable ACIS
kernel: carrier retention, parser recovery, subset topology, kernel validity,
and native CAD acceptance remain distinct ledger outcomes. No support claim is
promoted. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain explicitly
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

### Decision

Refine existing **PAR-07/S8 carrier/semantics/consumer gates and PAR-59
evidence ordering**; do not add a finding or top-level subplan. This pass

### Readiness update — shortest honest path

1. **Baseline without duplicate work:** reuse the existing 0.3.12 SAB receipt
   and its fast verifier. It already executes a bounded geometry conversion;
   no package install, repeated peer run, or new default test dependency is
   needed.
2. **Candidate selection:** read the pinned `cq-acis` corpus lock/manifest,
   then choose one smallest NIST SAT artifact whose exact save profile is
   accepted by the pinned package and whose body-reachable record set can be
   completely classified. If those checks fail, record `NOT_QUALIFIED` and
   continue with locally authored generated vectors; do not spend time trying
   to force an unsupported corpus model through the converter.
3. **Scratch-only carrier path:** if an eligible SAT file is found, wrap its
   unchanged payload as entity-local DXF SAT only through an existing supported
   adapter; capture original and emitted bytes, chunk order, handle/type, and
   block owner. Reopen with libdxfrw and compare exact payload identity. Keep
   the source SAT/DXF and all derived DWG/DXF files in a unique temporary
   directory and remove them after recording hashes/results. Never commit an
   external fixture.
4. **Semantic oracle gate:** run the pinned `cq-acis` reader against original
   and preserved payloads only after the carrier comparison. Require complete
   body reachability, zero unclassified geometry/raw records, supported
   profile diagnostics, valid closed topology where the model expects a solid,
   and independent expected metrics. If no independent expectation exists,
   report “shape constructed” only—not a semantic parity pass. A SAT self-read
   or matching output from the same parser is not independent expected truth.
5. **Keep lanes independent:** this bare-payload route cannot validate
   AC1027+ ACDSDATA section/index parsing, entity↔key↔payload joins, DWG
   DataStorage, model history/current state, native FreeCAD behavior, or any
   deferred J item. Those keep their existing native/platform and independent
   evidence gates.
6. **Fast implementation cadence:** use only the owning generated selector
   after any code change; run optional peer conversion at the composed semantic
   checkpoint, not per implementation slice. Update this plan after each
   implemented item, self-unblock to the next local-ready task if a peer or
   platform result is unavailable, and report progress after each slice is
   committed.

<a id="implementation-progress-par144-ac1015-viewport-reader-boundary-correction-2026-10-21"></a>

## Implementation progress — PAR-144 AC1015 VIEWPORT reader-boundary correction (2026-10-21; scratch-only fast slice)

The generated AC1015 writer probe already established that four type-34
VIEWPORT frames were emitted and each frame carried the expected single block
owner token. Extending that generated case through readback reproduced a local
reader warning for every viewport. ODA §20.4.38 confirms the AC1015 type-specific
reference sequence is clip boundary, viewport header, named UCS, and base UCS;
there is no R2000+ frozen-layer prefix. The failure occurred before this
handle sequence, so the writer's four null references were not the cause.

Cursor tracing found the defect in `DRW_Viewport::parseDwg`: for AC1015 the
entity and string buffers alias, but the post-common-handle check compared the
advanced shared cursor with `stringEndBit`, whose value is the earlier
data-body end. Common handles are outside that body range. The parser now
performs this post-handle string-end comparison only when the string stream is
detached; existing body/string bounds still protect field parsing before the
common handle pass. The generated AC1015 roundtrip now retains all four
VIEWPORT entities, and its owner/content graph checks pass.

The strict `libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip` target builds; focused
`dwg_block_record_layout_association` passes 1/1 in 0.43 seconds, and the
existing generated `libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix` passes 1/1 in 1.75 seconds;
scoped `git diff --check` passes. The test creates and removes its unique
scratch DWG.
An available local AC1015 `simple.dwg` was also tried through `dwg2dxf`, but
fails earlier at `BAD_READ_TABLES` (error 9), before any entity/VIEWPORT
qualification; it is not evidence for or against this fix. No full suite,
external peer, native CAD application, or persistent sample fixture was used.
This is a generated same-library regression, not independent format
qualification: no support claim is promoted, counts remain **144 / 78**, and
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

Next self-unblocking action: add a generated test-only structural check for
AC1015/AC1024 object-map, frame, and owner-handle spans, compared against the
existing frame receipts and block-owner ledger. Then continue the next
dependency-ready local PAR-144 graph-closure gap without waiting on native or
external qualification.

## Implementation progress — PAR-144 generated VIEWPORT raw-frame boundary cross-check (2026-10-21; scratch-only fast slice)

Added a generated test-only type-34 VIEWPORT frame probe for AC1015 and AC1024.
It reads the writer's in-memory serialized object frame rather than trusting
only `DwgObjectFrameReceipt`: it decodes the modular body-size prefix, the
AC1024 handle-bit count and separate data/handle byte spans, the AC1015
object-size bit boundary and merged trailing handle tokens, and the stored
CRC. Every captured handle occurrence is decoded again from its bounded
physical byte segment and compared for code, reference, and end bit; the
owner's code-4 handle is required exactly once in the encoded handle stream.
The test also checks that the committed in-memory object-map entry points to
the generated frame at offset zero.

The focused binary selector `--viewport-object-frames` passes. The strict
`libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix_tests` target builds, and owning CTest
`libdxfrw_dwg_reader_matrix` passes 1/1 in 1.50 seconds. `jq empty` validates
the research receipt and scoped `git diff --check` passes. This is a generated
in-memory frame check: it does **not** parse the final file-level HANDLES
section, establish full-file object-map closure, use an external drawing, or
qualify native CAD behavior. No persistent fixture, full suite, external peer,
or native application was used; no support claim is promoted. Totals remain
**144 / 78**, and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

The worktree already contains broad mixed changes and these tests depend on
the current uncommitted writer/receipt implementation. To avoid creating a
partial commit that cannot build from HEAD or bundling unrelated changes, this
slice remains uncommitted.

Next self-unblocking local action: add a generated scratch-only **full-file
HANDLES-section** check through the writer's normal finalization path. Parse
the serialized handle map and page CRCs, verify every handle/offset pair is
unique and lands on the corresponding frame prefix, and compare the final
map against the emitted per-frame receipts. Keep the current raw-frame test as
the fast lower-level invariant and leave peer/native qualification at the
existing composed checkpoint.

### Decision

Refine the existing **PAR-07/S8 peer-admission gate** and the **PAR-144
composed structural checkpoint** only. The newly useful distinction is that a
partial DWG parser may still expose a separately useful raw-object layer, while
its typed VIEWPORT decoder is known to fail; do not let either layer inherit
the other's evidence ceiling. No new finding, subplan, dependency, fixture, or
per-slice validation is warranted.

### Source findings and disposition

| --- | --- | --- |

Its matrix marks an object-stream walker shipped across eight releases; `all_objects()` is described as returning raw type codes, handles, and payload bytes. The same README reports partial graph resolution and six real-corpus VIEWPORT decoder failures, including a 266-of-1125-bit boundary result. It states there is no DXF parser and no automated external-CAD acceptance for its writer. | Add it as an **optional raw structural candidate**, not a semantic or writer oracle. The typed VIEWPORT failure is an explicit reason not to gate on typed viewport success. If the raw API cannot support the question, record `NOT_QUALIFIED` and self-unblock. The README's self-described provenance and mutable aggregate figures are not independently audited or current release evidence. |
| [`uncad` scope](https://github.com/iyulab/uncad) | The read-only Rust facade routes DWG through LibreDWG FFI and DXF through the separate pure-Rust `undxf` crate, including ASCII/Binary DXF and R2007+. | Deduplicate all DWG observations under LibreDWG. Keep `undxf` as an optional, exact-version/checksum-pinned DXF-only parser candidate; no writer, DWG, 3D, or ACIS conclusion follows from the wrapper. |
| [`OpenCADStudio` README and automation guide](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio) and [application source](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/src/app/document.rs) | The mutable README advertises a desktop DWG/DXF editor, R14–2018 save targets, multiple desktop platforms, and an automation `audit`/`save_verified` path that reopens output and compares a semantic manifest. The application source imports `acadrust` document and entity types. | This can be an optional **consumer/application smoke** at a composed checkpoint, not an independent parser vote. Pin both app release and codec commit; separate app repair/reopen results from LibreCAD, FreeCAD, and raw parser evidence. ### Implementation-ready gate refinement

At PAR-144's existing composed checkpoint, use `dwg-rs` only if a one-time
admission probe resolves an exact repository commit and confirms the raw object
API can inspect both generated AC1015 and AC1024 drawings. Compare object
counts, type-34 handles, raw frame extents, and owner-handle occurrences only
where those bytes are actually exposed. Do not infer that the partial typed
decoder accepted a viewport from the raw walk, and do not infer semantic
support from enumeration alone. If the probe cannot see a required handle-tail
span, the plan already has a self-unblocking local fallback: a bounded
test-only decoder over generated scratch bytes, with peer/native qualification

For OpenCADStudio, one explicit-version import/export/reopen/audit run could
answer application-consumer questions, but every result must include app
release, `acadrust` commit, source/output hashes, diagnostics, and per-entity
disposition. Its shared codec lineage makes it correlated evidence. For
`undxf` or mlightcad's DXF parser, pin package version, source checksum,
dependencies, input flavor (ASCII/Binary), and supported DXF version before
admission; run only at the composed DXF checkpoint, not after each local slice.

No peer runtime, new dependency, downloaded sample, or native app was run in
this research pass. No 3D/ACIS support statement is promoted. Counts remain

## Deeper/broader research — FreeCAD consumer gates and DWG-to-DXF loss attribution (2026-10-21; primary-source review)

### Decision

Refine existing **PAR-07/S8**, **PAR-144**, and the external FreeCAD
qualification condition only; no new defect is inferred from another
project's limits. The key readiness change is to make three outcomes
independently reportable: (1) converter process and DXF artifact validity,
(2) the exact selected FreeCAD DXF importer/backend's supported projection,
and (3) ACIS/B-rep semantic interpretation. Stock FreeCAD documentation
currently marks the third outcome unsupported, so native FreeCAD runs must not
be made a prerequisite for local progress or used as a negative ACIS semantic
oracle.

### Broader source findings

| Primary source | Evidence and limit | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md), [DWG import guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md), and current [`importDWG.py`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py) | DWG import is an external converter call followed by `importDXF.open`; FreeCAD's documentation lists a faster built-in C++ DXF importer and an optional legacy Python importer with different entity coverage. The C++ list includes common drawing entities, blocks/layers, and paper space; the legacy list additionally names 3D faces. The same guide explicitly says embedded ACIS/SAT solids cannot currently be read by FreeCAD. Thus converter exit success, DXF parse acceptance, entity projection, and solid semantics are distinct. These are mutable upstream docs/source and must be pinned at qualification time. | Split the FreeCAD condition into converter interoperability and backend-specific consumer checks. Record FreeCAD build/commit, OS/architecture, exact converter path/version, selected importer backend and preferences, produced DXF version/signature, process status, diagnostics, imported-object census, and per-source-handle disposition. Do not require ACIS B-rep construction from stock FreeCAD; keep it under the separate independent semantic-reader gate. |
| FreeCAD [import/export preferences](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Import_Export_Preferences.md) and [`importDWG.py`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py) | The converter is selected from settings or platform search paths; the FreeCAD wrapper can convert through LibreDWG, ODA File Converter, or QCAD Pro depending on configuration. Import preferences also choose importer behavior. A result without the exact selected route is not reproducible and cannot be attributed to libdxfrw alone. | In Linux and Windows qualification, pin the converter explicitly to the libdxfrw-built `dwg2dxf`; disable automatic converter fallback. Pin C++ versus legacy importer and relevant options. Capture argv, exit code, stderr/stdout, temporary DXF hash/signature, and FreeCAD object census. A fallback to ODA/QCAD or a different backend is a distinct test row, not a pass for the requested route. |
| LibreDWG [NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS), [`decode_r2007.c`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode_r2007.c), and open [issue #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411) | Current source includes a named `AcDsPrototype_1b` reader, while NEWS describes the datastore as incomplete and newer ACIS extraction as brute-force. #1411's public DXF→DWG→DXF control reports missing SAB/ACDSDATA but the first conversion's writer status determines whether the later reader was tested at all. The issue's confidential AutoCAD DWG observation is not available for independent reproduction. | Keep stage attribution mandatory: independently inspect the source DXF carrier; inspect the intermediate DWG section/page/index/record and entity flag/key association; then inspect libdxfrw extraction and final DXF. Only diagnose a reader gap if the intermediate proves the section and payload were present. Do not infer broad reader parity from a decoder code path or matching entity counts. |
| ezdxf [DXF overview](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/index.rst), [ACIS browser](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/launcher.rst), and [drawing limitations](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/addons/drawing.rst) | ezdxf documents broad DXF ASCII/binary read/write version coverage and an ACIS content browser, but its drawing add-on explicitly does not render ACIS and has no 3D rendering engine. It is useful for file/carrier inspection, not a B-rep semantic or native-CAD oracle. | Retain ezdxf only as a pinned, version-specific DXF carrier/parser comparator. For any result, bind package/source hash and raw payload hashes; do not count browse success, entity preservation, or 2D drawing output as 3D semantic support. |

### Implementation-ready qualification lanes

1. **FreeCAD converter lane (Linux and Windows):** use a generated local DWG
   only when the existing writer can make a valid input for the exact feature
   under test; otherwise use an already-tracked repository fixture. Explicitly
   configure FreeCAD to use this project's `dwg2dxf`, record actual output
   signature and DXF hash, and verify the converter returned success without
   fallback. Do not commit external or generated DWG/DXF fixtures.
2. **FreeCAD importer lane:** lock the exact FreeCAD build, C++/legacy backend,
   and preferences. Use backend-specific expected subsets; for example, do not
   expect the C++ backend to behave like the legacy backend for 3DFACE. Compare
   imported entities and geometry to the intermediate DXF, and separately
   list ignored/unsupported entities. This lane qualifies the consumer path,
   not the converter's entire semantic model.
3. **ACIS semantic lane:** stock FreeCAD currently documents ACIS/SAT solids as
   unreadable. Record this as `UNSUPPORTED_CONSUMER` for that exact build; do
   not treat it as a converter failure or a failed libdxfrw semantic reader.
   Continue using the existing independent external semantic-reader evidence
   gate, with exact carrier-to-body association, independently derived
   expectations, unknown-record disposition, and kernel-lineage accounting.
4. **DWG loss localization:** compare each stage's entity count, owner/key,
   payload byte count/hash, and diagnostics. The decisive order is source DXF
   → intermediate DWG section/map/record → decoded semantic object → output
   DXF carrier → FreeCAD import. Stop diagnosis at the first proven loss; a
   successful exit or surviving `3DSOLID`/`REGION` header cannot mask an empty
   or missing payload.
5. **Fast execution and self-unblocking:** do not run native FreeCAD after
   every local slice. Keep the normal per-slice gate to a focused generated
   test and owning CTest. Run Linux/Windows FreeCAD only at the already-planned
   composed checkpoint when those hosts/builds are available. If unavailable,
   record `NOT_RUN` with the missing host/build detail and continue local work;
   do not wait or claim qualification.

This research changes no support claim and closes no external item. Findings
and top-level subplans remain **144 / 78**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
J295 remain explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. No FreeCAD,
LibreDWG, or ezdxf runtime, native CAD application, external drawing, new
dependency, or full suite was used in this research pass.

Extended the focused `--viewport-handles-section` selector to retain the

section-map/page decoder and 1,200 uniquely named VPORT table records emitted
through the public table callback; their production reader maps exactly match
the writer's emitted object maps. AC1021 uses the independent R2007
page-map/data-page path and 1,200 public-callback VPORT records. Since the
concrete `dwgWriter21` is final and has no public full-map snapshot, that row
compares the production reader's map with an independent logical HANDLES
decode and confirms all emitted table/control and generated VPORT handles are
present. In all six version rows, map entries are unique and land on bounded,
non-overlapping, CRC-valid frames in the decoded OBJECTS section.

The version-specific frame detail matters: AC1015's frame begins with the
object size; AC1024 adds a UMC handle-stream bit length before the data/handle
bytes; AC1018 uses the pre-AC1024 merged-handle frame; AC1021 uses the R2007
page format and merged data/handle frame; AC1027/AC1032 share the AC1024
three-stream frame. The AC1024-family check consumes and validates the UMC
handle-bit length and includes it in CRC coverage. Applying one framing rule
to all versions would mislocate frame boundaries or CRCs.

## Deeper/broader research — AC1009 paper-space DWG→DXF route and writer-path correction (2026-10-21; primary-source review)

### Decision

Correct the earlier “AC1009 is outside the current AC1012+ reader scope”
disposition. The current worktree dispatches AC1009 to `dwgReaderR11`, so this
route is in scope for a bounded compatibility audit. The `HAS_PSPACE` meaning
has a strong cross-implementation semantic lead, while local source inspection
shows that `readEntityR11` consumes the flag's extension byte but its
`applyAttrs` lambda does not assign `DRW_Entity::space`. The writer-side audit
also corrects the earlier suspected container gap: `dxfRW::writeBlocks()`
already writes the fixed legacy `$MODEL_SPACE` and `$PAPER_SPACE` BLOCK records
for AC1009, and entity emission writes group 67 and selects the paper-space
owner from `ent.space`. Therefore classify this as a **candidate entity-space
projection loss**, not a missing output-container defect, pending a generated
full-route control. Do not create a new finding/subplan or change parsing until
the control and pre-R13 contract evidence are reviewed. This is separate from
PAR-144's R13+ LAYOUT graph and PAR-143's unsupported REPEAT/ENDREP/LOAD
markers.

### Evidence and plan consequences

| Source | Evidence and limit | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Current [`dwgRW::createReaderForVersion`](src/libdwgr.cpp), [`dwgReaderR11::readEntityR11`](src/intern/dwgreaderR11.cpp), and [`dxfRW::writeBlocks` / entity writer](src/libdxfrw.cpp) | AC1009 dispatches to `dwgReaderR11`; a generated control now confirms flag `0x40` projects to `DRW::PaperSpace`, while unflagged points remain model-space and the following point stays aligned. The 2D adapter's AC1009 export emits group 67 only for the flagged point; reopening retains the exact three-point split. This confirms the local code path, not the producer's byte contract. The DXF writer already emits the legacy fixed space BLOCK pair. | Keep the generated callback→adapter export→DXF reopen regression. The separate CLI/independent-parser check of `$ACADVER`, the fixed legacy BLOCK pair, and exact output membership remains a composed follow-up; do not add a second container-synthesis change. Keep AC1006 separate until its flag contract is established. |
| LibreDWG [`common_entity_data.spec`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/common_entity_data.spec#L1679-L1688), [issue #1337](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1337), and [PR #1368](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/pull/1368) | The peer's pre-R13 decoder source sets `entmode = 1` and emits DXF group 67 when `FLAG_R11_HAS_PSPACE` is set. <a id="deeperbroader-acad-table-dwg-writer-identity-and-peer-route-refresh-2026-10-21-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader research — ACAD_TABLE DWG writer identity and peer-route refresh (2026-10-21; source audit)

### Decision

Extend only existing **PAR-126 / 7G.3d**. The current reader and DXF model have
TABLE-specific paths, but the DWG entity writer does not: `DRW_Table` derives
from `DRW_Insert` and declares no `encodeDwg` override; the inherited
`DRW_Insert::encodeDwg` selects ordinary DWG object type 7 (INSERT) or 8
(MINSERT), then emits the INSERT body. The DWG writer dispatches through the
virtual `encodeDwg` call, and `dwgRW::writeTable` forwards to the generic
entity writer. Source therefore confirms a DWG output-completeness gap: typed
TABLE-specific content is not encoded as TABLE by this path and may be
silently represented as an INSERT-shaped frame. This source audit is not a
runtime reproduction or producer-authored wire trace.

Do not alter the existing `parseDwg`, `parseCode`, DXF write behavior, or
LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3 2D consumer contract as a side effect. First make unsupported
DWG TABLE output fail closed and atomically; then add version-specific wire
encoding and reference closure from the ODA specification and a real producer
trace. A display `*T` block is not a substitute for semantic rows, cells, and
linked object references.

### Evidence and limits

| Evidence | What it establishes | Limit / plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Local [`DRW_Table`](src/drw_entities.h#L1851), [`DRW_Insert::encodeDwg`](src/drw_entities.cpp#L6171), [`dwgWriter15::encodeEntity`](src/intern/dwgwriter15.cpp#L5723), [`dwgWriter24::encodeEntity`](src/intern/dwgwriter24.cpp#L234), and [`dwgRW::writeTable`](src/libdwgr.cpp#L2318) | `DRW_Table` has a TABLE `eType` and TABLE-specific parser/model fields, but no writer override. The inherited encoder assigns `oType` 7/8 and serializes insert fields. Both writer families invoke the virtual encoder, and the facade treats `writeTable` like a generic entity write. | This is sufficient to add an implementation task under PAR-126. Before changing bytes, add a generated regression that checks the actual frame type and whole-write disposition. Do not infer the producer's TABLE type code from `DRW::TABLE`, peer source, or a DXF group code. |
| ODA DWG Specification v5.4.1, the existing PAR-126 TABLE/TABLECONTENT crosswalk, and the local `DRW_Table::parseDwg` / `DRW_TableContentObject::parseDwg` paths | DWG TABLE has version-dependent data and object relationships; R2010+ has a separate TABLECONTENT path in the existing model. ODA remains the byte-layout authority. | Build separate pre-AC1024 and AC1024+ encoder lanes. Re-read the exact ODA sections for each lane before editing. Capture the actual object type from an existing producer DWG's `Remaining object Handle, loc, type=` trace as required by the repository instructions. If no producer trace is available, retain the affected lane as unsupported rather than inventing a type code. |
| Autodesk [TABLE DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D8CCD2F0-18A3-42BB-A64D-539114A07DA0.htm) and [AcDbTable API reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2027/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OARX-RefGuide-AcDbTable.html) | The DXF record has distinct `AcDbEntity`, `AcDbBlockReference`, and `AcDbTable` subclass data, including TABLESTYLE and owner BLOCK pointers, grid dimensions, per-cell types/values, FIELD and block-cell references, and cell/table overrides. The API class derives from `AcDbBlockReference` but has its own cell model. | Inheritance explains shared placement/display fields; it does not license writing a TABLE as INSERT. Preserve table identity, semantic content, and display-block graph separately. Autodesk's DXF mapping is not the DWG binary grammar. |
| ACadSharp open [issue #1321](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1321), filed 2026-10-20 | A peer reports a no-op AC1032 read/write/read changing two TABLEs to one, losing a cell edit, and producing output AutoCAD 2020 rejects with ErrorStatus 53. The issue's no-table control reportedly succeeds. | This is a useful failure-shape and priority signal, not proof of a libdxfrw defect, not normative layout evidence, and not an independent reproduction. The author offers the sample pair but none was attached or imported; do not fetch or commit it. Use a local generated minimal TABLE control. |
| LibreDWG's pinned [`src/dwg2.spec`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/f860b0fb76d5f8effb5a70769a3389cb1e0308c8/src/dwg2.spec) | The peer spec source distinguishes the TABLE entity and notes a separate R2010+ TABLECONTENT object lane. | Corroborates the need for version separation only. It is a peer implementation/spec transcription, not a replacement for ODA and not grounds to hardcode `oType`. |
| [CodeCAD architecture](https://github.com/backkem/codecad/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) and [`dxfscan`](https://github.com/xorgy/dxfscan) | CodeCAD states it reads DWG through ACadRust and builds a 2D projection; dxfscan is a Binary-DXF-only parser with a fixed common-entity list and `Unknown` fallback. | Neither is an independent DWG TABLE writer oracle. Keep CodeCAD as same-lineage optional 2D consumer evidence and dxfscan as a conditional Binary-DXF syntax comparator only; neither warrants a dependency, routine test, or delay to implementation. |

### Implementation-ready, fast-first subplan

1. **Add one characterization selector before changing the encoder.** Reuse
   the existing generated DWG local-roundtrip harness and its owning target.
   Create a minimal `DRW_Table`, an ordinary `DRW_Insert`, and a distinctive
   following entity entirely in memory. Check exact entity kind, source/output
   handle, owner block, frame count, and sentinel alignment. Include a small
   table with text and a block cell if the existing model can express both.
   Exercise one representative from each currently supported writer family:
   legacy AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, and AC1024+, adding AC1027/AC1032 only where
   the existing target already covers those profiles. Keep all bytes scratch-
   generated; no external drawing is needed.
2. **Close the silent-loss path first.** Until a version lane has a mapped
   encoder, a TABLE with unencoded semantics must refuse the write atomically;
   it must not return success as type-7/8 INSERT. Assert unchanged object
   buffers, object/handle maps, block-owner ledger, class-instance ledger, and
   caller-owned TABLE state on refusal. Surface an explicit unsupported/loss
   result through the existing writer contract. Ordinary INSERT behavior is a
   negative control and must remain unchanged. Keep this guard version-scoped
   if a lane is implemented incrementally.
3. **Bind wire identity before encoding.** Trace a producer-authored TABLE in
   an already available repository/local sample, using the required debug
   handle/location/type output. Record DWG version, class/type, owner, TABLE
   handle, display-block handle, TABLESTYLE, TABLECONTENT and child links.
   Read the ODA profile for that version and compare actual cursor/handle
   boundaries. If no admissible producer sample exists, finish the fail-closed
   guard and self-unblock to the next implementation item; do not block all
   work or guess a type value from LibreDWG/ACadSharp.
4. **Implement by wire family, not by application inheritance.** Share only
   proven common entity and insertion-placement fields. Implement the legacy
   inline TABLE profile separately from the AC1024+ TABLE/TABLECONTENT object
   graph. For each lane, encode in the correct DATA/string/handle stream and
   close every required owner/pointer edge: TABLESTYLE, owning BLOCK_RECORD,
   TABLECONTENT, FIELD/DATALINK where mapped, block-cell target, and its
   attribute-definition/value associations. Keep the display `*T` block's
   rendered primitives distinct from semantic cell content. Preserve
   `EMPTY`, `UNKNOWN`, text, FIELD, block reference, and incomplete content as
   distinct states; never fabricate defaults for unmodeled data.
5. **Make partial support explicit.** Require the existing semantic-complete
   state before a strict round-trip/export can claim full table preservation.
   If a linked object or cell variant is unsupported, either reject before
   emitting any part of that TABLE graph or retain it only through an
   explicitly documented opaque-preservation path with stable ownership.
   Do not silently drop TABLECONTENT, FIELD, DATALINK, or cell attributes.
6. **Validate cheaply per slice.** For each change, run the strict `-Werror`
   build of the owning target, its direct selector, the one registered owning
   CTest, and scoped `git diff --check`. Add no peer dependency and no imported
   fixture. Do not run the full suite for each subtask; run the planned
   composed regression set once after the version lanes and reference graph
   close. At that checkpoint, independently inspect generated framing and run
   any already-installed consumer/native TABLE audit once, recording exact
   version, object count, cell edits, owner graph, diagnostics, and rejected
   object identities. A native pass is qualification evidence, not permission
   to skip local frame/semantic checks.
7. **Self-update and self-unblock.** After each implementation slice is
   committed, update this plan and its research/implementation receipt with the
   exact version lane, fast tests, observed result, remaining limitation, and
   next ready slice; report the committed-slice progress. If a producer sample
   or external application is unavailable, label only that evidence gate
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`, finish all dependency-ready generated/local work, and
   continue to the next slice without waiting or stopping implementation.

### Scope and completion boundary

This research does not implement the guard or encoder and did not run tests,
builds, peer binaries, or CAD applications. No DWG/DXF fixture, peer attachment,
dependency, source edit, or support claim was added. Findings/subplans remain
**144 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain explicitly
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The only new plan work is nested under
existing **PAR-126 / 7G.3d**; LibreCAD and LibreCAD_3 2D behavior stays in scope
as a compatibility constraint.

<a id="deeperbroader-freecad-dwg-wrapper-success-semantics-and-route-pinning-2026-10-21"></a>

## Deeper/broader research — FreeCAD DWG-wrapper success semantics and route pinning (2026-10-21; primary-source review)

### Decision

Refine the existing **PAR-07/S8 FreeCAD consumer gate** and its Linux/Windows
qualification condition. The current FreeCAD wrapper's visible “Conversion
successful” result is not proof that its selected converter exited
successfully or emitted a complete DXF: the reviewed source waits for the
process, then checks only whether the expected output path exists. Its
automatic converter mode can also try a different implementation after the
requested path fails. The composed test must independently identify the
converter, inspect process status and diagnostics, validate the artifact, and
then score the selected FreeCAD DXF importer separately. This is a test-route
precision update, not a libdxfrw defect or support promotion.

### Cross-project evidence and limits

| Primary source | What it establishes | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| FreeCAD current [`importDWG.py`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py), especially `convertToDxf()` | LibreDWG is invoked as `dwg2dxf <input> -o <temporary-output>`; the wrapper calls `communicate()` but does not inspect the child's return code, and treats output-path existence as success. With automatic converter selection, the code can proceed from LibreDWG to ODA and then QCAD. The ODA route explicitly requests `ACAD2000` DXF. | For a libdxfrw qualification, set FreeCAD's converter preference explicitly to this build's `dwg2dxf`; do not use automatic selection. Capture the child exit status and stdout/stderr outside the wrapper, and independently inspect the produced file even when FreeCAD reports success. Any ODA/QCAD fallback is a separate test route and cannot pass the libdxfrw row. |
| FreeCAD current [`importDXF.py`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDXF.py) and its [DXF import guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) | `importDWG.open()` passes the converter output to `importDXF.open()`. The importer supports a selectable C++ and legacy Python backend, records importer statistics, and documents different entity subsets: the legacy list includes 3DFACE; the documented C++ list does not and says text, dimensions, and attributes inside blocks are skipped. The guide says embedded ACIS/SAT solids cannot currently be read. | Record FreeCAD build, OS/architecture, importer backend, preferences/add-on version, import statistics, and the exact DXF hash/signature. Define expected imported geometry per backend; mark unsupported features separately. Treat stock FreeCAD ACIS as `UNSUPPORTED_CONSUMER`, never as a failed DWG converter or an ACIS semantic oracle. |
| ACadSharp current [issue #1299](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1299), [issue #1297](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1297), and [issue #1264](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1264) | #1299 is reported against the NuGet v3.8.0 DWG→DXF route and alleges malformed spline output, but its private input and expected control arrays are not available for independent inspection. #1297 reports AC1032 whole-file AutoCAD rejection even after the reported MTEXT frame matched the producer object byte-for-byte, leaving other file/object graph stages unresolved. #1264 uses paired repository DWG/DXF samples to report a block-cell model-value discrepancy; ODA's versioned tagged-content grammar remains the layout authority. | Keep peer findings exact-build, operation, and entity scoped. Use them to select local generated negative controls only where an existing owner lacks coverage; do not infer a format rule, transfer a master-source result to a package release, or import attached/private drawings. A successful entity-frame comparison does not replace full-file structural/owner closure; DWG block content and DXF value mapping remain distinct assertions. |
| LibreDWG [project README](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) and [NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS); ezdxf [DXF entity index](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/dxfentities/index.rst), [ACIS browser](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/launcher.rst), and [drawing limitations](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/addons/drawing.rst) | LibreDWG is a distinct DWG codec with version- and direction-specific limitations documented by its project; it is not a blanket correctness oracle. ezdxf is a broad DXF parser/writer and raw SAT/SAB inspection route, but its drawing add-on documents no 3D renderer and no ACIS rendering. | Retain these peers only for their operation-specific optional comparisons. Pin artifact/source revision and feature direction. Parser recognition, raw-carrier visibility, geometry projection, native application import, and solid semantics stay separate evidence columns. No peer run is required in the per-slice loop. |

### Implementation-ready qualification sequence

1. **Pin the converter route.** On each available Linux/Windows FreeCAD host,
   configure `DWGConversion` to LibreDWG and set the exact `dwg2dxf` path. Record
   FreeCAD build, platform/architecture, converter version/hash, and the actual
   argv. Disable automatic fallback; if preferences cannot guarantee that,
   instrument the wrapper invocation or mark the route `NOT_QUALIFIED`.
2. **Validate conversion independently.** Capture process exit status and
   stdout/stderr because the wrapper itself accepts an existing output file
   without checking exit status. Require exit code zero, a newly produced
   nonempty DXF, recognized `$ACADVER`/encoding, and strict parser/structural
   validation. Record the DXF hash and each source handle's preserved,
   transformed, unsupported, omitted, or refused disposition. Do not accept
   FreeCAD's success message or a file's mere existence as the pass criterion.
3. **Pin the consumer backend.** Set C++ versus legacy Python importer
   explicitly and record add-on availability/version and relevant preferences.
   Compare the imported object/statistics report only against the documented
   subset for that backend; 3DFACE is not a shared expected feature in the
   current documentation, and block-contained text/attributes may be skipped
   by the C++ route. Do not auto-download an importer dependency during a
   qualification run.
4. **Keep semantics staged.** Compare source DWG → `dwg2dxf` artifact → FreeCAD
   imported projection. For ACIS/SAB, keep exact carrier/owner association and
   an independent semantic reader as separate gates; stock FreeCAD's DXF
   importer is not expected to create a solid. Stop loss attribution at the
   first independently demonstrated stage.
5. **Keep the loop fast and self-unblocking.** Continue per-slice validation
   with the focused local selector, owning CTest, and scoped diff check. Run
   native FreeCAD only at the composed checkpoint, not after each slice. If a
   host, importer, or exact converter artifact is unavailable, record that
   condition as `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`/`NOT_RUN` and continue local implementation.

This review changed no production code, tests, fixture set, peer dependencies,
or support claims. Findings/subplans remain **144 / 78**; J256, J260, J268,
J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. The update
is nested under the existing consumer-qualification work, preserves the
LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3 2D compatibility requirement, and adds no new blocker or

## Deeper/broader research — independent STEP kernel cross-check candidate (`smlibpy` / NVIDIA SMLib) (2026-10-21; research only)

### Decision and evidence ceiling

Refine the existing **PAR-07/S8 independent semantic-evidence gate** with an
optional downstream STEP re-import candidate. `smlibpy` 0.3.5 packages the
NVIDIA SMLib NURBS B-rep kernel behind Python bindings, and its documented
`import_step(path, heal=False)` path can check whether a STEP B-rep exported
after the existing SAT/SAB parser→OCCT path remains a valid, quantitatively
consistent solid in a different kernel family. A published wheel makes this
candidate materially cheaper to provision than the previously screened
source-build-only SMLib route, but does not make it a DWG/DXF/ACIS reader.

This check cannot establish that libdxfrw correctly parsed SAT/SAB bytes,
preserved a DXF ACIS carrier, followed an ACDSDATA index/key to the right
record, or preserved the owner/handle graph. It only sees the STEP handoff;
STEP export itself may already have lost source distinctions. A matching
SMLib result is meaningful only when compared with expected geometry derived
independently of the libdxfrw/OCCT path. It is corroboration at one composed
semantic checkpoint, not a support-claim promotion or a substitute for native
FreeCAD/Linux/Windows qualification. Do not change the six external findings:
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 stay explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

### Primary-source findings and limits

| Primary source | What it establishes | Limit / plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| PyPI [`smlibpy` 0.3.5 release](https://pypi.org/project/smlibpy/0.3.5/) | Released 2026-10-17; declares Python ≥3.10; has CPython 3.10–3.14 wheels for Windows x86-64, Linux x86-64/aarch64, and macOS x86-64/arm64. All 26 files have PyPI provenance metadata. The release is classified Alpha and its license expression is `MIT AND Apache-2.0 AND OFL-1.1`. The CPython 3.14 macOS ARM64 wheel is `smlibpy-0.3.5-cp314-cp314-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl`, SHA-256 `03824146913b002f8089544a8447e766e2b4ea77bcff75bef808efb54573858b`; the source archive SHA-256 is `a7b7ef62caf0689dc3398fdf3ab7e15e1401291ef13586f7d18cf99282e06217`. PyPI provenance ties the release workflow to source commit `316514b421285ae5abdfe5ed24936bd24ed9dec1`. | This is a convenient, auditable optional test artifact, not a production dependency. At qualification time use the wheel matching the host's Python/platform, record its exact SHA-256 and attestation, and pin the source commit and SMLib submodule/patch state. If the exact wheel cannot be used, record `NOT_RUN`; do not block implementation or fetch/build from source just to clear the gate. |
| [`smlibpy` file-format documentation at the PyPI source commit](https://github.com/awv-informatik/smlibpy/blob/316514b421285ae5abdfe5ed24936bd24ed9dec1/docs/files.md) | The STEP importer accepts AP203/AP214/AP242, reads solids and surfaces with units and names, and offers `heal=False` to skip its default healing of invalid bodies. The project says its importer is checked against OpenCASCADE on more than 400 files from several CAD systems and CAx-IF models. | The file-format and test-coverage statements are project-maintainer claims; they were not independently rerun here. Use the explicit importer with healing disabled, and treat the published corpus comparison as readiness evidence only—not proof that the current local DWG/ACIS route is correct. Avoid generic `load()` if it hides importer options. |
| [`smlibpy` kernel documentation at the same source commit](https://github.com/awv-informatik/smlibpy/blob/316514b421285ae5abdfe5ed24936bd24ed9dec1/docs/kernel.md) and NVIDIA [`usd-brep`](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/usd-brep) | The wrapper is built over NVIDIA's SMLib kernel, whose kernel family is separate from OCCT. The source documentation says the package compiles the kernel as a submodule and carries local patches for two kernel source files; `smlibpy` also supplies its own measurement implementation. | Do not identify the test engine only as “SMLib.” Receipt the exact package, wheel hash, upstream SMLib submodule revision, and patch manifest/hashes. Numerical measurements and shape validation are still implementation-specific, so compare with independently authored expected values and record the returned error estimate. |
| Existing PAR-07/S8 `cq-acis==0.3.12` receipt | An exact SAB 21800 generated control already became a valid closed OCCT solid, but the receipt explicitly says it is not qualification-eligible: the source was ezdxf-authored, OCCT is shared with the FreeCAD lineage, and the test does not parse outer ACDSDATA ownership. | The SMLib STEP re-import can add one independent-kernel downstream check to that already-run control if the optional package is available. It does not repair the input's qualification ineligibility, broaden `cq-acis`'s profile, or establish the native DWG/AcDs path. Keep the current receipt status unchanged. |

### Implementation-ready, fast-first qualification slice

1. **Keep it optional and composed.** Do not add `smlibpy` to libdxfrw's
   runtime, build, or required CI dependencies. Run one bounded check only at
   the existing PAR-07/S8 composed ACIS-semantic checkpoint, after the local
   supported-profile parser has produced an OCCT shape and a STEP artifact.
   No peer installation belongs in per-slice validation; implementation
   proceeds if this external package or a compatible wheel is unavailable.
2. **Pin the runnable artifact before interpreting output.** Prefer the
   matching 0.3.5 wheel with PyPI provenance. On CPython 3.14/macOS ARM64 use
   the hash above; on another host select the release's matching wheel and
   copy its published hash/provenance into the receipt. Record Python,
   OS/architecture, package version, wheel filename/hash, provenance result,
   source commit, SMLib submodule revision, and all source patches. Do not
   silently replace 0.3.5 with mutable `main`, a source build, or another
   kernel wrapper.
3. **Bind every stage by digest.** Record the original DWG/DXF carrier hash,
   entity handle and owner/key context; exact SAT/SAB payload hash; parser
   version/profile; OCCT version; exported STEP hash; SMLib artifact identity;
   and importer settings. Use only an existing repository fixture or a
   scratch-generated control. Do not add a newly downloaded peer fixture to
   this repository; do not commit scratch artifacts.
4. **Import without repair.** Call `import_step(step_path, heal=False)` so
   healing cannot make an invalid export appear valid. Record import errors,
   body count, solid/shell classification, each body's validity, units,
   bounding box, volume, surface area, centroid, and inertia where exposed.
   Keep names/body ordering as diagnostics rather than sole identity keys.
5. **Use independent, profile-appropriate expectations.** Compare those
   measurements against exact analytic expectations for scratch-generated
   controls or source-authoritative independent measurements for producer
   files. Choose numerical tolerances from the source precision and reported
   measurement error before running the comparison; do not tune them after
   seeing a failure. Do not require identical face/edge counts or topology
   ordering across kernels. If no independent expected geometry exists, label
   the result `CORROBORATION_ONLY`, not a semantic pass.
6. **Preserve staged outcomes and self-unblock.** A STEP parse/validity/metric
   mismatch is localized to the exported STEP handoff or downstream kernel
   until earlier raw-carrier and expected-geometry checks isolate the cause.
   Record a per-stage disposition, update this plan/receipt after the bounded
   check, report progress after the slice commit as already required by the
   plan, and continue dependency-ready implementation. Missing platform,
   package, sample, or independent expected geometry is `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`/
   `NOT_RUN`; it never blocks local work.

### Scope boundary

This is research/readiness only: no package was installed or run, no source,
test, fixture, peer dependency, or CI workflow changed, and no support claim
was promoted. Findings/subplans remain **144 / 78**. The addition is nested in
the existing PAR-07/S8 semantic-evidence work; it adds no full-suite run and
does not alter LibreCAD or LibreCAD_3 2D compatibility requirements.

These are valuable implementation and corpus leads, not independently reproduced results for an exact release. | Upgrade the existing optional structural checkpoint from simple section/payload presence to: (a) one and multiple schemas; (b) a small record plus payload crossing a blob-page/chunk boundary; (c) deliberately non-sequential blob references; (d) distinct blob versus indexed data-entry accounting; and (e) entity-handle attachment after extraction. Pin the exact package/source revision and report separate section-record, payload-byte, and attached-entity denominators. Keep ODA v5.4.1 and local producer traces authoritative for wire rules; do not copy peer formulas or type codes. |
| [OpenCADKernel README](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/opencadkernel) and its described [ACIS layer](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/opencadkernel/tree/main/src) | OpenCADKernel proposes lifting a `SatDocument` into its own B-rep and lowering it again, which could eventually provide a geometry-kernel route distinct from OCCT/CadQuery/FreeCAD Part. The project labels itself early and says most operations are not yet written. Its ACIS feature depends on `opencadcodec`, so outer DWG/DXF parsing is not independent of the ACadRust-derived codec family. | Mark as **candidate / not qualified**, not as an available J-item resolver. At a later composed checkpoint, inspect a commit-pinned public API and tests; feed it the exact locally admitted SAT/SAB body (not a same-codec roundtrip); require complete body/face disposition, valid topology, and pre-authored analytic metrics. If only lift/lower or partial meshing is available, record structural/preservation evidence only. No new dependency or wait condition. |

The app's release notes add a SAT/ACIS import workflow. This is a useful observable projection route, but it is not a DWG decoder vote: the app uses the ACadRust-derived codec lineage, a display mesh is not a B-rep, and fallback output is not full semantic success. | If used, pin app, codec, and kernel commits; record for each source handle whether every face was kernel-lifted, fallback-sampled, omitted, or failed. Use only as a downstream visualization/projection diagnostic. Do not count it as independent DWG/DXF parsing, arbitrary ACIS support, or a shape-validity oracle. |
| LibreDWG [R2007+ AcDs section source](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode_r2007.c), [project format notes](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi), ezdxf's [ACIS authoring boundary](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/tasks/add_dxf_entities.rst), and its [ACIS tools documentation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/acis.rst) | LibreDWG has a real modern AcDs section/parser path; its explicit incomplete-datastore/brute-force SAB warning is in the historical NEWS 0.11 entry, not the current 0.14.1 release entry. ezdxf preserves raw SAT/SAB and can create/extract simple known flat polyhedra, but explicitly has no general ACIS kernel and does not target arbitrary ACIS structures. | Retain LibreDWG only as a version-pinned structural differential route; first prove the candidate input contains the target AcDs section. Use ezdxf as a DXF carrier/parser or bounded polyhedral control producer, not an arbitrary-solid semantic oracle. Do not infer B-rep semantics from carrier access or broad version labels. Keep native FreeCAD's documented embedded-ACIS limitation as `UNSUPPORTED_CONSUMER`, separate from the DWG converter gate. |

### Implementation-ready, fast-first refinement

1. **Continue local implementation without external waits.** Run the owning
   generated fast selector for each parser/writer slice. Do not install or
   build a peer in the normal workflow; optional comparators remain at the
   existing composed checkpoint.
2. **Strengthen only the modern-AcDs composed probe.** When that checkpoint is
   reached, create scratch-only controls for one/multiple schemas, blob/data
   distinctions, split and reordered blob spans, alignment/count boundaries,
   and missing/duplicate keys. Use a separate expected map from entity handle
   to section key to exact payload hash. Keep malformed cases fail-closed or
   explicitly recovered without fabricated attachment.
3. **Separate the evidence stages and denominators.** Report section/index
   framing; record bytes; payload reconstruction; owner/key association;
   semantic body construction; and native consumer outcome independently.
   A positive earlier stage never implies a positive later stage.
4. **Admit independent kernels only on capability, not project labels.**
   Revisit OpenCADKernel only after a pinned build exposes an exercised ACIS
   lift path and complete analytic-solid tests. If it is unavailable, record
   `NOT_READY` and continue with existing local controls, the already-recorded
   OCCT-family baseline, and the optional STEP downstream check; do not block
   implementation or relax the independent-evidence condition.
5. **Preserve the support boundary.** Keep explicit DXF 3D entities, opaque
   SAT/SAB retention, AcDs transport, B-rep semantics, native application
   acceptance, and 2D-consumer compatibility as separate ledger rows. No
   fixture from an external repository may be committed; generated controls
   stay in tests or scratch only if created locally from scratch under the
   existing fixture policy.
6. **Self-update and self-unblock.** After each implemented slice, update this
   plan and its machine-readable receipt, run its fast owning test, report
   progress after the slice is committed, then move to the next dependency-
   ready local item. An unavailable peer, kernel, sample, or platform is a
   recorded `NOT_RUN`/`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` condition—not a reason to stop.

This is research and readiness refinement only. No source/test/fixture,
dependency, or CI change was made; no peer executable or native CAD
application was run; the full suite was not run. Findings/subplans remain

## Implementation progress — PAR-126 DWG TABLE fail-closed gate (2026-10-21; current-worktree verification)

The current uncommitted worktree contains the planned first safety slice:
`dwgRW::writeTable()` refuses a non-null TABLE, latches DWG write failure,
and emits `unsupported-table-dwg-encoding` rather than dispatching through
`DRW_Insert::encodeDwg`. Its generated full-write test covers AC1015, AC1018,
AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032. For each version it checks TABLE identity
and semantic payload remain unchanged, the neighboring INSERT and LINE entity
callbacks still execute, the refusal diagnostic/skip count is correct, and a
pre-existing destination sentinel is preserved instead of publishing a
partial DWG.

Validation passed:

- `cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip -j4`
- `build-gcc/libdxfrw_dwg_local_roundtrip --dwg-table-writer-refusal`
- `ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^dwg_table_writer_refusal$' --output-on-failure` (1/1)
- `git diff --check -- src/libdwgr.cpp tests/dwg_local_roundtrip_tests.cpp tests/CMakeLists.txt`

An additional debug trace of the already tracked
`tests/samples/AC1021/blocks_and_tables_-_imperial.dwg` (SHA-256
`3c95e8a82d5c8c251483fabc61efa8ca904f4e4bc8c2fce4786d74e812284d07`)

at `/Users/dli/doc/dwg/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf` in this
session. Keep all TABLE DWG writes fail-closed; do not implement bytes from
peer code or guess a class ID. **Self-unblock:** continue to the next
dependency-ready local PAR-07/PAR-14 item, and resume the TABLE encoder only
after the authoritative ODA sections and a complete producer profile are
available. No new fixture, full-suite run, peer dependency, or support claim
was added. The mixed worktree remains uncommitted; this slice was not
committed.

These tables describe DXF fields, not subdivision evaluation, arbitrary ACIS interpretation, or DWG AcDs ownership. | Keep MESH separate from classic POLYLINE/PFACE and 3DFACE. Never use its renderer or same-codec readback as an independent solid-semantic result. |
