selector beyond the BLOCK_RECORD→LAYOUT link. It captures actual generated
LINE member frames, the BLOCK_RECORD frame, and a following LINE sentinel.
Each child's owner and self-handle receipt is decoded against that child's
serialized bytes; BLOCK_RECORD first/last references (AC1015) and hard-owned
references/count (AC1018+) are decoded against the serialized BLOCK_RECORD
frame and resolved in order to the captured child-frame handles. The test
checks frame CRCs, adjacent offsets, and the following sentinel boundary.
For AC1015 it also parses the entity common header and confirms
`nolinks=1`: this writer profile has endpoint references but no previous/next
chain to traverse. AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032 pass.
The `independentLayoutViewportHandlesMatch` control now emits two distinct
LAYOUT/BLOCK_RECORD groups in one object stream, each with two actual VIEWPORT
frames and its own following LINE sentinel. For each group it validates the
viewport self/owner handles, exact BLOCK_RECORD owned references, reciprocal
BLOCK_RECORD→LAYOUT hard pointer, and LAYOUT viewport-list/last-active tokens
against the group's actual captured frames. It rejects a reference to the
other layout's record, layout, or viewport handles and checks adjacency within
each group. AC1015 exercises actual last-active references but expects no
viewport list; AC1018+ verifies list references/count. This generated probe
passes alongside the original per-version BLOCK_RECORD member-frame probe.

- Scoped `git diff --check` and receipt JSON validation — PASS

## Deeper/broader research — open-source cross-peer failure boundaries and implementation readiness (2026-10-21; primary-source review)

### Decision

This pass compared current source-level support declarations and fresh peer
failure reports across LibreDWG, ACadSharp, ACadRust, and ezdxf, then mapped
their failure shapes onto the existing local owners. The new evidence is useful
for sharpening evidence admission and slicing—not as a vote that libdxfrw has
the same defects. No peer binary, CAD application, or external drawing was
run/imported. No new finding or support claim is justified.

| Source | Fresh evidence and limit | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [0.14.1 NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | Its release notes identify R2004/AC1018 DWG writing as newly implemented and explicitly say R2007/AC1021 encoding falls back to R2010/AC1024; the same release history includes container, decompression, and security fixes. Thus a requested output version and the actual serialized version are separate observations even for a mature open-source codec. | Preserve the per-direction/per-version matrix. Any writer qualification records the file's actual AC code, not just the requested `DRW::Version`, and checks that down-conversion is exact or reported/refused. Keep version fallback and read/write coverage distinct. |
| ACadSharp [README version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) and current [issue index](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues) | Its general feature statement says DWG read/write, while its table is direction-specific: AC1021 has a reader but no DWG writer, AC1012 is DXF-only, and AC1009 DXF is read-only. Current issues include AC1032 table loss/open rejection (#1321), native-consumer failure from missing VisualStyle/Material graph objects (#1074), and earlier silent ACIS DXF omission (#1195). These are project declarations and user reports, not normative format evidence or verified local behavior. | Keep the existing table-writer/graph owners (PAR-126/7G.3, PAR-20/7G.3) separate from entity-field parsing. The composed output gate must inspect required object roots and graph edges as well as entity counts; a successful same-library reopen is not consumer acceptance. Do not create parallel tests unless local audit finds an uncovered field/edge. |
| ACadRust [README](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/blob/main/README.md) and current reports [#145](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/145), [#146](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/146), [#149](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/149), [#123](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/123), and [#124](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/issues/124) | Its README advertises broad DXF R12–R2018+ and DWG R13–R2018+ read/write. Fresh open reports separately describe DWG→DXF omission of unknown custom-class entities and proxy graphics (#145), DXF→DWG objects rejected by BricsCAD even though a direct DWG→DWG route opens (#146), page/section sizes trusted before allocation (#149), object-count/size handling (#123), and malformed-header panics (#124). The repro reports are not independently audited here; their route distinction is the relevant evidence. | Refine existing PAR-06/PAR-07/PAR-14/PAR-132/PAR-49 gates to label route and stage on every observation: reader recognition, adapter/raw retention, writer emission, output structure/identity, independent parser, native open/audit, and geometry semantics. A direct-source rewrite cannot stand in for a DXF-mediated route. Keep unknown data/proxy graphics and semantic custom-class meaning separate. |
| ezdxf [ACIS contract](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) and [proxy contract](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/acad_proxy_entity.html) | The documentation explicitly says its ACIS model covers only a limited subset: unsupported structures become `NONE_ENTITY` with data loss and arbitrary ACIS re-export is not supported. Proxy graphics are a display representation whose explosion destroys original proxy meaning. This is valuable DXF/raw-payload evidence, not DWG parsing or a general B-rep kernel. | Retain PAR-07/S8's separate raw carrier, body-reachable record accounting, interpreted subset, and independent geometric semantics. A proxy-graphic count or ezdxf parse result cannot promote custom-object or solid semantics. |

### Local applicability audit

The reviewed reports map onto existing plan owners rather than creating a new
queue: unknown/proxy retention to PAR-132/PAR-06; malformed lengths, count
bounds, and strict structural completeness to PAR-14/PAR-07 S8; DWG→DXF and
DXF→DWG route distinctions and native acceptance to PAR-49; TABLE/object-graph
closure to PAR-126 and PAR-20/7G.3; multi-layout ownership to PAR-144; and
ACIS/modeler evidence to PAR-07/S8 and PAR-59. The local source review also
confirmed named ceilings in `dwgSafety` for DWG buffers, object/owned-object
counts, and EED staging, with R2004/R2007 page/section code checking sizes
against bounds before the reviewed allocations. This is not an exhaustive
audit of every file-derived allocation or conversion, so it does not close
PAR-14.

The peer reports do not establish a matching libdxfrw defect. The current plan
already contains generated loss/refusal, unknown-object, graph-closure,
multilayout, malformed-container, and per-version controls. Therefore this
pass adds no new numbered finding, CTest, dependency, or implementation slice;
it makes the existing evidence/intake procedure more explicit and prioritizes
the current local-ready PAR-144 byte-walk continuation.

### Implementation-ready peer triage and fast path

For each newly surfaced peer issue, before changing code:

1. Record the repository, immutable commit or release artifact, observed date,
   DWG/DXF version, direction (`DWG→DXF`, `DXF→DWG`, same-format roundtrip),
   and exact failed stage. Treat issue text as a scenario report, not proof of
   its diagnosis.
2. Bind the affected source object to a stable identity tuple where available:
   source handle, type/class, owner/block/layout, expected references, and
   expected output disposition. Keep opaque bytes, graphics, typed meaning,
   and native acceptance in separate columns.
3. Map that tuple to the existing PAR owner and fast selector. If already
   covered or inapplicable, receipt the reason and self-unblock. If a local
   invariant is uncovered, make the smallest generated in-memory control with
   a following sentinel; assert exact preservation or explicit refusal,
   diagnostic, and destination atomicity. Do not import peer/customer DWGs or
   commit external fixtures; generated fixtures must be created locally from
   scratch or already exist in a repository.
4. Run only the owning fast target/CTest and scoped diff/receipt checks per
   slice. Update the plan and receipt, report the slice's progress after its
   commit, and continue to the next dependency-ready item without waiting for
   unavailable peers or platform qualification. Reserve full suites and one
   exact-pinned independent/native run for composed checkpoints.
5. At that checkpoint, pin parser/writer/app version and architecture; inspect
   actual output version, diagnostics/repair status, per-object graph and
   content disposition, and consumer acceptance. Do not use same-codec
   readback, a wrapper that shares its codec lineage, a static feature matrix,
   or a peer's open issue as a support promotion.

This is a readiness refinement only. Findings/subplans remain **144 / 78**;
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain explicitly
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. No external fixture was added, no peer
runtime or native CAD app was run, and no full suite was run. The local
PAR-144 fast selector and its two owning CTests pass as recorded in the
implementation receipt above.

<a id="deeperbroader-consumer-route-contracts-open-source-class-dispositions-and-harness-integrity-2026-10-21-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader research — consumer-route contracts, open-source class dispositions, and harness integrity (2026-10-21; primary-source review)

### Decision

The new evidence sharpens existing qualification gates; it does not establish
a libdxfrw defect or justify another finding. The main implementation risk is
route conflation: FreeCAD's DWG path is converter → DXF → a selected importer,
the two FreeCAD DXF importers have different documented entity coverage, and
neither currently supplies ACIS-solid semantics. LibreCAD 3's documented DWG
contract is opt-in read/import, not writing. Independent parser results also
depend on class-stability/build flags, while fuzz results depend on harness
integrity. Keep these dimensions explicit and pin mutable upstream sources
before any composed qualification run.

### New evidence and plan consequences

| Source | Source-level evidence and limit | Existing plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| FreeCAD [Draft DXF documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) | It documents a fast built-in C++ importer and an optional legacy Python importer, with differing object lists: 3DFACE appears in the legacy list but not the documented C++ list. It says embedded ACIS/SAT solids cannot currently be read. Its exporters also have separate output profiles and limitations. This describes FreeCAD behavior, not libdxfrw correctness. | Refine PAR-07/S8 and PAR-49's FreeCAD matrix: identify importer backend/version for each result; treat 3DFACE/importer outcomes separately; never use FreeCAD DXF import as the ACIS semantic oracle. Keep direct-DXF import distinct from DWG-converter qualification. |
| FreeCAD [`importDWG.py`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py) and [DWG documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md) | DWG is mediated through an external converter that produces DXF, which is then passed to the DXF importer. The selected converter may be LibreDWG, ODA, or QCAD, so a successful FreeCAD import alone does not prove the libdxfrw/LibreDWG route ran. | For the Linux/Windows native gate, force the LibreDWG converter with fallback disabled; record exact converter binary/build, arguments, return status, actual DXF `$ACADVER`, structural completion, diagnostics, FreeCAD build, and importer backend. Validate converter output before importing; record imported-object counts and unsupported-entity diagnostics separately. |
| LibreCAD 3 [`DWG support contract`](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/blob/master/docs/dwg-support.md) | The project documents `WITH_DWG_IMPORT` as off by default and DWG reading through libdxfrw `dwgRW`; it explicitly says DWG writing is not implemented, exposed, or planned until separate evidence and project decisions reopen that choice. Its claims are direction-specific and tied to a pinned library revision. | Refine the LibreCAD 3 consumer gate only for the import/read path and adapter compatibility. Do not make DWG writer parity a prerequisite for LibreCAD 3 compatibility, and do not infer 3D display/edit behavior from the existence of `dwgRW`. Pin the consumer revision and option state for any run. |
| LibreDWG [manual: class stability and unknown classes](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/doc/LibreDWG.texi) and [build options](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg) | The manual separates stable, unstable, debugging, and unhandled classes. Some unknown/unstable classes can become UNKNOWN records or placeholder/dummy/point output; its manual says some unknown payloads persist only for same-version rewrites with the complete `unknown_bits` blob. The README documents `--enable-release` as excluding unstable features/unknown versions and `--enable-debug` as enabling unstable classes. Broad coverage percentages therefore do not identify a reproducible per-class parser profile. | Refine PAR-06/PAR-07/PAR-132/PAR-144 peer receipts: pin commit, release/debug/default flags, version, and enabled class set; compare only the admitted typed subset; separately record raw bytes, proxy graphics, typed interpretation, and conversion disposition. A peer downgrade/placeholder is not byte preservation or semantic equivalence. |
| LibreDWG [fuzz setup](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg-fuzz) and historical [harness issue #1270](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1270) | The fuzz project separates input/output modes and crash/hang/leak regression replay. Issue #1270 reports a harness double-free in a specific 0.13.4.8229 build that polluted crash counts; it is a historical harness report, not a current libdxfrw defect or proof about current LibreDWG. | Refine PAR-14's optional security checkpoint: keep deterministic bounded tests as the per-slice default; if a sanitizer/fuzz run is used at a composed checkpoint, pin the harness/mode, smoke-test valid and malformed inputs, distinguish harness crashes from library crashes, and replay known crash regressions. Do not add a fuzzer dependency or run a full campaign for every slice. |

### Implementation-ready route checklist

1. Keep local implementation slices on their owning fast selector and scoped
   diff/receipt checks. Existing generated controls remain the fast evidence;
   this research adds no new fixture or per-slice full-suite requirement.
2. At a FreeCAD DWG checkpoint, make the route explicit:
   `DWG hash/version → pinned LibreDWG dwg2dxf → complete DXF and actual
   $ACADVER → pinned FreeCAD build + importer backend → per-entity disposition`.
   Run a separate direct-DXF lane when testing DXF, and do not let automatic
   converter fallback silently change the tested route.
3. For 3DFACE and other 3D entities, record the exact FreeCAD importer backend;
   the documented C++ and legacy entity lists are not interchangeable. For
   3DSOLID/REGION/BODY, treat FreeCAD import as carrier/diagnostic evidence
   only—the documented importer cannot parse the embedded ACIS/SAT blob.
   Keep independent analytic/kernel semantic evidence under PAR-59.
4. For LibreCAD 3, qualify only the consumer behavior it exposes: opt-in DWG
   read/import and the existing callback/API contract. DWG writing remains a
   separate library capability and project-policy decision.
5. For LibreDWG comparison, pin binary, source commit, configuration, target
   version, and object-class status. Inspect output version and per-object
   disposition; same-library rewrite or nominal format coverage is not an
   independent writer acceptance result.
6. Keep fuzzing separate from semantic qualification and optional/timeboxed.
   Reuse no external crash/sample artifact in the repository; retain only
   locally generated controls or fixtures already in LibreCAD/libdxfrw or
   libdxfrw's existing peer repository.

This is a research/readiness refinement only. It adds no finding, subplan,
dependency, fixture, test registration, source change, or support promotion.
Findings/subplans remain **144 / 78**. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
remain explicitly `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. No external runtime,
FreeCAD application, LibreCAD 3 application, or fuzz campaign was run in this

Refresh the existing PAR-07/S8 modeler route, PAR-59 loss-attribution ledger,
and PAR-144 optional peer checkpoint only. ACadSharp's open work is useful
implementation evidence, but its current PR state is not a released or
validated parity result. In particular, a new modeler-writer PR depends on an
open schema/storage refactor whose review thread reports a failing
payload-attachment test on the tested branch. This sharpens peer admission
and sequencing; it does not establish a libdxfrw defect or resolve external
qualification.

The PR depends on #1174. Thus the proposed patch spans more than the issue's DXF-write symptom and crosses separate input/output routes. | Keep the existing peer issue as a version-scoped failure shape, not a local defect. If #1240 is ever tested, create separate rows for DWG read, DXF write, DWG write, target-version result, and per-handle disposition. Do not mark the feature available from the PR title or branch code; pin both base and head commits and rerun the exact tests after any rebase. |

A public review comment reports that, on the branch tested with .NET 9, `DxfAcdsDataSectionTests.ReadAcdsDataAttachesAcisPayloadToOwnerEntity` failed because `readAcdsRecord` threw `NotImplementedException`, and says the tested branch lost post-2013 DXF payload attachment. This is a branch-specific report, not a verified failure of current master or every later PR head. | Treat #1174 as an unmet comparator prerequisite until the exact candidate head builds and proves payload-record parsing plus entity attachment. Capture exact head SHA, test output, source entity/owner/key/payload hashes, and warnings. If it fails or cannot be run, mark that peer cell `NOT_QUALIFIED` and continue local work. |

A candidate read test is `NOT_EXERCISED` until section presence is established. Distinguish ezdxf's bounded polyhedral authoring/extraction from arbitrary ACIS interpretation. Keep exact carrier bytes, AcDs schema/index/key join, entity association, B-rep construction, analytic semantics, and target application acceptance as distinct evidence. |

### Implementation-ready peer checkpoint

1. **Freeze candidate identity.** Record repository URL, base commit, candidate
   head commit, build/runtime, target file version, compiler configuration,
   and whether the tested artifact includes #1174, #1240, or neither. Never
   blend `master` output with an unmerged feature branch in one result.
2. **Establish the ACDS prerequisite first.** Run the candidate's narrow
   payload-attachment test. Require the exact entity handle → schema/index/key
   → payload byte-span/hash join; distinguish direct DXF-carried SAT/SAB from
   DWG AcDs-carried SAB. On a missing attachment or `NotImplementedException`,
   stop only that peer lane and record `NOT_QUALIFIED`.
3. **Test writer directions independently.** For a fixed locally generated
   modeler input, census each source handle, owner/block, modeler class, and
   carrier. Exercise DWG→in-memory→DXF separately from DWG→in-memory→DWG;
   record output magic/`$ACADVER`, downgrade, warnings, and emitted/omitted/
   refused state for every source handle. Verify solid-only block definitions
   and INSERT reachability after strict reopen.
4. **Keep semantic claims downstream.** Only send exact recovered carrier
   bytes to the already admitted semantic route after owner/key closure. Check
   complete shape/face disposition and pre-authored analytic metrics; do not
   count ACadSharp's schema/parser work, ezdxf's carrier parser, LibreDWG's
   entity shell, or a same-kernel shape import as independent proof by itself.
5. **Fast-first and self-unblocking.** This peer work remains at the existing
   composed checkpoint, not the per-slice loop. Keep local owning fast tests
   as the default, update this plan/receipt after any implemented slice, and
   continue to the next dependency-ready local item if a peer prerequisite,
   platform, or sample is unavailable. No peer fixture may be copied into
   this repository; use existing eligible fixtures or controls generated
   locally from scratch.

Extended the existing parser-fed complex SAB graph check to inspect the
unsupported `parabola-curve` branch independently of the spline-surface case.

### Decision

candidate status or repeat the previous witness. The prior local receipt
reports a valid one-body/one-shell OCCT conversion for a scratch ACIS 21800
box, but `qualificationEligible=false`: the input was ezdxf-authored, the
route shares the OCCT kernel family with FreeCAD, and the run did not parse a
DWG or establish AcDs owner/key association. This pass adds source-lineage,
NIST cross-format, platform-artifact, and explicit-DXF-carrier boundaries.

finding, top-level subplan, fixture, dependency, code, or promoted claim.

### Implementation-ready optional checkpoint

1. **Keep the regular loop unchanged and reuse existing evidence.** The exact
   0.3.12 scratch box witness has already run; do not rerun it for this research
   update. Run local generated fast tests first. Invoke the peer only at the
   existing composed checkpoint in an isolated environment; no normal slice
   should wait on installation, native apps, or the full suite.
2. **Use a stronger scratch-only analytic control only if needed.** The next
   useful semantic input is a non-rectangular prism/body authored locally from
   scratch, with expected extents, volume, orientation and intended boundary
   counts recorded independently of either parser. The prior box remains a
   useful smoke control, not a general geometry profile. Do not use shipped
   peer corpus files or commit externally sourced SAT/SAB/DWG/DXF fixtures.
   Use only documented release profiles; `SUPPORTED_VERSION` alone is not
   acceptance.
3. **For the DWG route, compose structural and semantic checks.** On a
   locally-generated DWG containing the exact target AcDs profile, use the
   pinned ACadSharp v3.6.51 release as the optional section/record reader; pin
   its package/runtime too. Record section presence and schema/index rows,
   exact recovered SAB hash/size, owner/key/entity-handle join, and per-handle
   loss separately. Feed only the extracted bytes to cq-acis. `cq-acis` does
   not parse the DWG container or AcDs datastore, so it cannot establish the
   section lookup or attachment on its own.
4. **Compare geometric semantics, not just parser status.** Require full
   source-body closure for the declared profile, valid nonempty shape(s), and
   agreement with independent analytic metrics (volume, bounds, orientation,
   and profile-appropriate topology checks). The existing one-body observation
   is not a full-file semantic pass. Neither positive volume, successful exit,
   raw-byte retention, nor a self-roundtrip suffices. Keep cq-acis conversion
   separate from source DWG/DXF carrier checks and do not count its OCCT result
   as an independent kernel vote from FreeCAD.
5. **Keep routes and claims scoped.** Report SAT, stand-alone SAB, DWG AcDs
   extraction, DXF carrier write/read, explicit 3DFACE/POLYFACE fallback, and
   native consumer import as distinct matrix rows. An unsupported or
   ambiguous profile remains `NOT_QUALIFIED`/`REFUSED`, not zero-loss.
6. **Self-unblock and preserve the fixture policy.** If the package/runtime or
   exact DWG section profile is unavailable, record the skipped gate and
   continue dependency-ready local implementation. Keep any external corpus
   outside the repository; only scratch-generated local controls may become
   persistent fixtures. Update this plan/receipt after a gate result and do
   not change the six external statuses without independent, route-specific
   evidence.

## Implementation progress — S3.7c SAB 21800 sphere-surface ordered fields fail closed (2026-10-21; generated parser-fed fast slice, uncommitted)

The existing sphere parameter projection used the shared `TokenCursor`, which
searches forward for the next token of a requested tag. A malformed record
could therefore skip an unexpected field and bind a later `Double` as the
sphere radius. The pinned ACadRust 0.6.4 typed-record documentation describes
the field order as center, radius, U direction, and pole; this is peer
implementation evidence for the narrow record profile, not normative ACIS
authority. The local projection now requires those ordered field tags and
skips only pointer tokens (whose links are validated separately in the graph).
Unknown trailing tokens remain retained and uninterpreted; surface sense,
parameter bounds, transforms, topology, and geometry are not promoted.

Generated parser-fed controls cover (1) a literal inserted where the radius
belongs with a later double present to tempt the old scan-ahead cursor, and
(2) a truncated record missing its pole vector. Both streams remain valid at
the generic SAB framing layer, but rooted projection now refuses as
`InvalidModel`, clears pre-seeded output, and reports the exact sphere-surface
node. The existing positive signed-radius/oriented-frame control and the
30-case NaN/+infinity/-infinity field matrix continue to pass.

Focused validation:

```text
cmake --build build-gcc --target libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests lc3_compat_check -j4  PASS
ctest --test-dir build-gcc -R '^libdxfrw_graph_preservation$' --output-on-failure  PASS (1/1, 1.13 seconds)
git diff --check -- src/drw_acis.cpp tests/graph_preservation_tests.cpp  PASS
```

No persistent DWG/DXF/SAB fixture, CTest registration, dependency, peer runtime,
native application, full-suite run, or support claim was added. The shared
worktree remains broadly modified and uncommitted; no files were staged.
Findings/subplans remain **144 / 78**; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295

### Implementation-ready refinement (existing plan owners only)

1. **Keep implementation dependency-free.** Use the latest peer research only
   to select questions for already-owned local slices. No dependency, peer
   installation, external fixture, or peer run belongs in the ordinary
   generated fast-test loop. Self-unblock whenever a peer artifact is
   unavailable or its exact route is out of scope.
2. **Make version and direction explicit.** Preserve separate cells for ASCII
   DXF, Binary DXF, DWG read, DWG write, same-version rewrite, and each
   conversion direction. Bind each cell to exact file version, entity/object
   type, and source-to-output disposition; a headline `R/W` or a successful
   parser open cannot fill sibling cells.
3. **Keep lossy down-save honest.** For any R12 or other downgraded output,
   capture which source handles were preserved, approximated, expanded,
   refused, diagnosed, or lost. Use locally authored controls with independent
   expected bounds/counts for any polygonal approximation. Do not require
   pixel-perfect renderer agreement or silently equate a polyline expansion
   with exact spline/ellipse/helix semantics.
4. **Bound optional peer execution.** If ACadRust is later selected, use the
   immutable release/source identity, verify crate checksum correspondence,
   set explicit mesh/record limits, never enable unlimited-mesh mode on
   untrusted input, and keep failsafe recovery separate from strict reads.
   Record skipped/ignored inputs and exact diagnostics. If any identity, limit,
   or reproducible input is missing, mark the peer cell `NOT_RUN` and continue
   local work.
5. **Preserve support and consumer boundaries.** Do not infer 3D solid/B-rep
   semantics from ACIS carrier preservation, self-roundtrip, render output, or
   broad version tables. Keep the required LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3 2D callback/API
   contract intact; keep all six external J findings explicitly
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting until their route-specific independent
   evidence exists.

<a id="implementation-progress-s37c-sab-21800-ordered-scalar-curve-fields-fail-closed-2026-10-21-generated-parser-fed-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>

## Implementation progress — S3.7c SAB 21800 ordered scalar curve fields fail closed (2026-10-21; generated parser-fed fast slice, uncommitted)

Straight-curve and ellipse-curve parameter extraction used the tolerant
`TokenCursor`, which searches forward for the next vector/scalar tag. In the
admitted `ACIS BinaryFile` 21800 projection, this could let a malformed field
be skipped or leave a recognized curve silently unresolved. The existing
parameter sequence was retained but is now read positionally: two vectors for
a straight curve; three vectors and a double for an ellipse curve. Both
recognized vector tags remain accepted because generated/existing 21800
streams use both `LocationVec` and `DirectionVec` tags for vector-valued
fields. Other signatures/versions keep the legacy reader.

The current ACadRust typed-layout documentation lists straight-curve origin /
direction and ellipse center / normal / major-axis / ratio sequences, but the
page is mutable `latest` SAT documentation and does not establish the SAB
21800 wire tags. It is corroborative layout context only, not normative
format authority or an independent file sample. No type-specific continuation
tokens are discarded; only pointer slots are skipped by the ordered cursor.

Parser-fed generated controls now verify: (1) valid straight-curve projection
retains the expected point/direction; (2) valid ellipse projection retains
center/frame/ratio; (3) a shifted straight-curve field refuses instead of
scanning ahead; and (4) a shifted ellipse field refuses instead of scanning
ahead. Malformed rooted projection clears pre-seeded output and reports the
exact curve node. The first test run exposed an existing stream using both
vector tag variants; the strict cursor was corrected to enforce vector
position without over-constraining the tag variant.

## Implementation progress — S3.7c SAB 21800 non-finite scalar-curve node attribution (2026-10-21; generated parser-fed fast slice, uncommitted)

Strict straight-curve and ellipse-curve field readers previously accepted
non-finite values into the temporary edge projection and relied on the final
whole-body finite scan to reject them. That was fail-closed, but it reported
the owning body instead of the exact malformed curve record. The admitted
SAB 21800 reader now validates every consumed vector component and the ellipse
ratio before setting `hasCurve`; its existing caller records that curve node
as the failure location. Other signatures/versions retain the established
legacy path.

Parser-fed generated tests now cover NaN, +infinity, and -infinity in all
coordinates of straight origin/direction and ellipse center/normal/major axis,
plus the ellipse ratio: 48 malformed cases total. Every case parses and builds
at the generic SAB/model layers, then rooted projection refuses with
`InvalidModel`, clears pre-seeded output, and identifies the exact curve node.
This expands the previous x-only vectors and body-scoped diagnostics without
claiming geometric validity for finite but degenerate curve frames.

<a id="deeperbroader-dwg-peer-security-raw-reader-denominator-and-wrapper-lineage-2026-10-21-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader research — DWG peer security, raw-reader denominator, and wrapper lineage (2026-10-21; primary-source review)

### Decision

Refresh the existing PAR-07/S8 peer-evidence gate and PAR-14/PAR-26 parser-safety crosswalk. The source review found no newly confirmed libdxfrw defect. The peer evidence does, however, justify two explicit controls: (1) treat coverage denominators and sample identities as part of every comparative result, and (2) count wrappers around one DWG engine as that engine's lineage, not as independent readers. No new finding, top-level subplan, test target, or peer dependency is added. Local implementation remains fast-test-first; fuzzing, sanitizer runs, and peer/native checks stay at their scheduled or composed gates.

### Broader peer evidence and local applicability

| Primary source reviewed | Evidence and limits | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [0.14.1 NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS), [security advisories](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/security/advisories), and [0.14 milestone](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/milestones?state=closed) | The July 25, 2026 release records multiple concrete failure classes: an R2004 decompression buffer could shrink while a larger logical cursor remained live; a 32-bit `section_count × max_decompressed_size` product could under-allocate; an R2004 section-page-map offset was not validated before use; a prior pre-R13 end-boundary/no-advance mitigation was incomplete; and object pointers could become stale across vector growth. The same release records HATCH repeated-path state, DXF `3DSOLID`/`REGION` final-SAT-block truncation, and further fuzzer-found cleanup/bounds defects. These are LibreDWG-specific observations and release notes, not evidence those defects exist here or format requirements. | Keep these as risk patterns under existing PAR-14/PAR-26/PAR-49 and modeler-carrier owners. Do not port fixes mechanically or create a generic “security” implementation epic. For any locally changed route, retain its narrow invariant: capacity versus logical length, checked multiply/range, stable object identity across growth, cursor progress, or exact terminal payload inclusion. A peer crash class becomes a local finding only after a local source path and generated reproducer demonstrate a gap. |
| Local [`dwgReader18::parseDataPage`](src/intern/dwgreader18.cpp), [`dwgSafety`](src/intern/dwgsafety.h), and [`decompress18`](src/intern/dwgutil.cpp) | Static audit found page count/capacity multiplication and total section capacity checked before a single bounded decoded-buffer allocation; output pages write into that fixed capacity rather than resizing it while a decompressor cursor is live. `decompress18` validates 32-bit input/output bounds, compressed input minimum, back-reference origin, and output-window limits. Existing reader-matrix/hardening vectors cover section-capacity overflow and R2004 logical-tail/page behavior; compressor tests cover short/null/oversized inputs and length controls. | No matching capacity-shrink or unchecked-product defect is established. Preserve the existing generated page/decompressor selectors as first checks when this path changes; add only an uncovered mutation if a reproducer identifies a specific missing guard. Do not equate a peer's `uSize` policy with this repository's documented input-bounded data-page profile. |
| Local [`dwgReader18::readDwgClasses`](src/intern/dwgreader18.cpp), [`dwgReader15::readDwgClasses`](src/intern/dwgreader15.cpp), and [`dwgReaderR1_40`](src/intern/dwgreaderR1_40.cpp) | Source inspection found an explicit `<499` class-number underflow refusal, bounded class/string cursors and count-to-storage checks for the R2004 family, input-range checks around R13/R15 class bytes, and a legacy R1.40 walk ending at the declared `dwg_size` with each successful record advancing the cursor to its consumed byte position. This is source review, not exhaustive proof of all parser loops. | Keep the peer's no-progress/OOM report mapped to the existing bounded cursor and object-count work. Do not copy its exact count limits. If a later edit introduces a repeated-record loop or count-derived reserve, add a small zero/one/exact-cap/one-over generated control with an adjacent-record or frame sentinel. |
| [`dwg-rs` current README](https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/dwg-rs) and its [coverage report source](https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/dwg-rs/blob/main/examples/coverage_report.rs) | The README labels the project pre-alpha and reports one dated sample table: 19 files total, with per-version decoded/skipped/errored counts and 88.0% aggregate decoded coverage. Its separate capability matrix says “real-file aggregate currently 95.6%” and describes broader synthetic coverage; the README does not bind both summaries to one immutable sample manifest in the rendered page. It also says the raw object-stream walker covers eight versions while typed entity decoding, graph traversal, writer behavior, and external-CAD acceptance remain incomplete. This is an ODA v5.4.1-derived route; shared format specification is not independent normative evidence. | Do not combine 88.0% and 95.6%, infer a delta, or use either as a peer support score. At an existing optional structural checkpoint, bind the exact commit/toolchain, sample hashes and provenance, operation, and per-version/per-family denominator; keep decoded, skipped, errored, and untested dispositions separate. Use only raw section/object-boundary output for a matching structural question, not its typed geometry, writer, or aggregate percentages. |
| [`dwg2dxf-converter`](https://github.com/JosephESSEY/dwg2dxf-converter) README and its stated embedded [LibreDWG 0.13.4](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/releases/tag/0.13.4) WebAssembly engine | The wrapper advertises cross-platform zero-system-dependency conversion and R12–2018+ coverage, but its README identifies the embedded codec as LibreDWG 0.13.4. This is a wrapped converter route, not a new parser implementation; the wrapper's headline claims are not per-version/per-entity measurements, and its bundled engine predates the reviewed 0.14.1 fixes. No package was installed or executed. | Count it as LibreDWG lineage and as a possible downstream packaging/converter route only. Do not use it as a second DWG vote or assume its version headline equals verified codec coverage. Any optional run must pin the npm package, WASM digest, embedded LibreDWG source/release, runtime, input hash, requested/emitted DXF version, and per-source disposition. Do not add it to routine CI. |

### Implementation-ready refinement

1. **Local queue:** continue existing dependency-ready implementation items. The peer security refresh adds no confirmed bug and does not block local code work. For a touched reader/writer path, reuse the owning focused test first; add one generated edge only when local source/test audit shows it is absent. Keep fixtures external to the repository unless already present upstream or authored locally from scratch.
2. **Peer denominator:** at the existing PAR-07/S8 composed checkpoint, reject aggregate coverage claims unless the exact sample list, hash/provenance, version/family, operation, and decoded/skipped/error/untested counts are bound together. If project summaries disagree, preserve each as a separate source statement and mark the metric `NOT_COMPARABLE`; do not average or choose the favorable number.
3. **Lineage:** record wrapper → engine → version/digest. LibreDWG-WASM products remain one LibreDWG decoder lineage even if their host language, browser UI, package API, or platform support differs. A wrapper may add a consumer observation but cannot add an independent parser vote.
4. **Speed:** retain generated in-memory fast tests and one owning CTest per changed invariant. Do not add the wrapper, `dwg-rs`, external corpus files, full-suite runs, or sanitizer/fuzz work to each slice. Run the existing scheduled hardening lane only at its planned checkpoint; if an optional peer cannot be pinned or built, record `NOT_RUN`/`NOT_QUALIFIED` and self-unblock.
5. **Claim boundary:** fuzz/crash freedom, successful decompression, raw object-frame extraction, or a DWG→DXF conversion does not qualify entity semantics, DXF writer acceptance, ACIS/AcDs association, B-rep validity, native CAD acceptance, or any of J256/J260/J268/J284/J293/J295.

This source and local-code audit refines existing PAR-07/S8 and PAR-14/PAR-26 owners only. No local defect was reproduced; no code, test, fixture, dependency, peer build/run, native application, finding, top-level subplan, implementation order, or validation cadence changed. <a id="implementation-progress-s37c-loop-coedge-identities-2026-10-21-generated-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>

## Implementation progress — S3.7c exact face-loop coedge identities (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The rooted ACIS wireframe previously retained each face's ordered loop nodes
and each loop's coedge count, but not the coedge node identities that formed
that ring. `DRW_AcisFaceLoop` now also exposes those exact node indices in the
source `next`-link order. The loop projection cache stores the ordered ring

<a id="deeperbroader-binary-dxf-peer-maturity-and-cpp-lineage-2026-10-21-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader research — Binary-DXF peer maturity and C++ lineage (2026-10-21; primary-source review)

### Decision

Refine the existing PAR-07/S8 and PAR-144 evidence-admission rules only. The
review adds no local implementation defect and does not justify another test
or peer dependency. Binary DXF is a separate transport route from ASCII DXF;
peer support must be admitted by exact operation, artifact, and record
disposition rather than by a format-wide feature label.

### Source findings and plan consequence

| Primary source reviewed | Evidence and limits | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [current `dwgwrite.c`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/programs/dwgwrite.c) and [0.14 NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) | The current source recognizes DXB/DXFB and routes it to `dwg_read_dxfb`, but the verbose read path itself prints “still highly experimental and untested.” The 0.14 NEWS records DXB input/output support and a `dxfb.test`; this coexistence is not a contradiction to resolve by choosing the favorable statement—the source warning limits confidence, while the test establishes only that a test exists. No binary was built or run. | Do not treat LibreDWG DXB as a positive cross-parser parity oracle by default. If it becomes useful for a narrow syntax question, pin source commit, build flags, test/build identity, exact input/output hash, actual binary signature and `$ACADVER`, then label the result advisory unless independent expected record values and strict framing are checked. This restriction applies to its binary-DXF route, not to its separately assessed ASCII-DXF or DWG routes. |
| ACadSharp [README and direction/version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) | The project advertises Binary and ASCII DXF read/write, and its table separates reader and writer availability by AC code (for example, AC1009 is DXF-reader-only; AC1021 has a DWG reader but no DWG writer). These are project declarations, not measured per-entity results, and do not by themselves state how unsupported data is retained. | Keep the existing optional ACadSharp candidate, but bind its exact release/source, binary-vs-ASCII route, target AC code, entity/object family, notifications, and source-handle disposition. A successful reopen or version-table cell cannot establish opaque payload preservation or broader support. |
| ezdxf [project capability declaration](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/index.rst), [file management documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/drawing/management.html), and [ACIS drawing limitations](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/docs/source/addons/drawing.rst) | ezdxf declares ASCII/Binary DXF read/write across its stated DXF versions, with older read-only files upgraded to newer internal versions; its renderer explicitly does not render ACIS and has no 3D rendering engine. The docs state capability scope, not independent acceptance or an ACIS semantic result. | Keep ezdxf eligible for a pinned Binary-DXF parser/writer observation and exact raw-carrier inspection. Record input encoding and output encoding separately, actual `$ACADVER`, upgrade/downgrade behavior, and unsupported/lost fields. Do not use render success, mesh extraction, or its own round-trip as a B-rep or application acceptance oracle. |
| [C++ `libezdxf` repository](https://github.com/mozman/libezdxf) | GitHub marks the repository archived/read-only since 2023. Its README calls it a C++ learning project “not for production usage,” describes the goal as a C++ interface “like” Python ezdxf, lists ASCII/Binary DXF and raw-tag preservation as design goals, and explicitly says there is no DWG exporter. This suggests related design lineage rather than an independent peer implementation. | Classify as `DESIGN_REFERENCE_ONLY` under the ezdxf lineage. It may inform API/design questions about raw DXF-tag retention, but do not build or run it as a parity gate, add it as a dependency, count it as an independent parser vote, or infer DWG support. |

### Implementation-ready refinement

1. Preserve the local leaf-slice queue and its fast generated tests; this
   source review does not authorize adding peer packages or external files.
2. At the existing composed peer checkpoint, model DXF route identity as
   `(peer revision/artifact, operation, ASCII-or-Binary encoding, input/output
   AC code, entity/object family, disposition)`. Do not collapse Binary DXF
   into an ASCII result or infer round-trip quality from read support.
3. For any admitted Binary-DXF observation, record the binary signature,
   `$ACADVER`, exact source handles/types and block membership, raw group-310
   or other binary payload bytes and order where relevant, terminal framing,
   diagnostics, and strict reopen in a different implementation. Compare
   only predeclared fields; same-peer write/read remains a self-consistency
   observation.
4. Prefer ACadSharp or ezdxf for a future optional binary-DXF comparison only
   after source/release pinning and input-route audit. Keep LibreDWG DXB
   `NOT_QUALIFIED` as a positive oracle unless a pinned build and independent
   controls resolve its own warning. Treat `libezdxf` as source archaeology.
5. No test was added because the local Binary-DXF MESH/modeler and proxy-byte
   owners already exercise generated encoding, exact payload/chunk order,
   strict readback, and following-record alignment. Reuse those selectors if
   a relevant production path changes; do not rerun the full suite for this
   research-only refinement.

No findings or top-level subplans were added; findings/subplans remain
**144 / 78**. No local tests, peer runtimes, native applications, fixtures,
dependencies, or code were used or changed. ODA v5.4.1 remains authoritative
for DWG byte layout. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain explicitly
`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting. Self-unblock: continue the existing
dependency-ready local implementation queue; do not wait for optional Binary-
DXF peer qualification.

## Implementation progress — S3.7c exact coedge next-ring closure (2026-10-21; generated parser-fed fast slice, uncommitted)

The rooted SAB 21800 projection now follows exact zero-based pointer ordinals
for the face's first loop (2), a loop's next loop (1), a loop's start coedge
(2), and a coedge's next coedge (1). Previously the coedge walk selected the
first coedge-typed reference; when the next pointer was null, that could
silently borrow the previous or partner slot. The exact walk now records
`hasCoedgeRingClosure` and `coedgeRingClosed` on each projected face loop. It
reports closure only when the walk returns to its start; a null next link or a
cycle entering another seen coedge remains visible as an unclosed structural
gap. Non-21800 behavior remains on the prior type-search path.

multi-loop graph. A parser-fed negative removes one coedge's next pointer while
leaving its previous/partner references populated; the projected row does not
borrow either link, remains one coedge long, reports unclosed status, and
classifies as `ProjectedSubsetWithKnownGaps`. The parser-fed comparison also
checks closure fields against direct graph projection.

### Decision

provenance: a fix listed in a development NEWS file or observed on mutable

### Local applicability and non-duplication audit

* **SummaryInfo:** local DWG code recognizes/locates the section but exposes no
  typed custom-property authoring route. Existing generic DWG string-length
  tests do not qualify SummaryInfo serialization. Leave the route
  unsupported/unqualified; if it is implemented later, start a distinct
  versioned section parser/writer item with encoded-unit boundaries, explicit
  no-silent-loss disposition, and an independent reader/native check.
* **ARC/ELLIPSE transform:** preserve source parameters and use the existing
  Autodesk-derived analytic expectations in PAR-21/7H. A transform report in a
  peer's object model is neither a local defect nor a DXF/DWG byte-layout
  authority. Add no duplicate test unless local transformation behavior is
  introduced or changed.
* **DWG parser/release comparison:** existing local page, bounds, identity,
  ownership, framing, and transactional-output controls remain the owners for
  the relevant LibreDWG failure patterns. Match the exact source commit to the
  reported fix before interpreting peer agreement/disagreement. No downloaded
  peer drawing or user-private attachment is needed.
* **3D/ACIS denominator:** no reviewed source establishes the entire
  DWG→AcDs owner/key/payload join→independent B-rep semantic result→native
  acceptance chain. Keep SAB node/graph preservation, carrier association,
  geometry/kernel interpretation, and consumer acceptance as four separate
  observations; a peer's version matrix, self-roundtrip, entity count, or raw
  carrier match cannot promote the later stages.

### Fast implementation/readiness handoff

1. Continue the dependency-ready local S3.7c topology/semantic-identity queue;
   do not wait for a peer release or external platform result.
2. When a relevant local owner changes, run its existing target, one selector,
   and owning CTest. Do not add peer packages, downloaded DWG/DXF fixtures, or
   a full-suite run to that leaf slice.
3. At the existing composed optional-comparison checkpoint only, freeze the
   exact source/tag/package digest, toolchain/runtime, direction, AC code,
   encoding, input/output hashes, warnings, and per-source disposition. A
   peer's own reopen is a separate same-lineage result; independent/native
   reopen is required for those stronger claims.
4. If the peer route is already covered locally or does not exercise the same
   representation, record `COVERED_BY_EXISTING_OWNER` or
   `NOT_APPLICABLE_LOCAL_PATH`, then self-unblock to the next local item.

The rooted projection now exposes `DRW_AcisFaceLoop::coedgePreviousNodeIndices`
and `coedgePartnerNodeIndices`, aligned with the exact coedge identities in
next-link order. For the admitted SAB 21800 profile, these rows resolve only
coedge pointer ordinals 2 and 3 respectively; a missing/null slot is retained
as `-1`, counted as a known projection gap, and charged through the existing
extraction/output budgets. The identity capture is structural only: it does
not validate reciprocal links, adjacent-face ownership, manifoldness, or
partner-cycle semantics.

Generated multi-loop assertions verify the exact per-row previous and partner
targets. Parser-fed null controls independently preserve a previous slot and a
partner slot as aligned `-1` entries and classify the projected subset as
having known gaps. A wrong-type partner target is rejected earlier by the
SAB 21800 graph validator as `InvalidReference`, with the exact source node
and pointer ordinal 3 and transactional output clearing. Parser-fed and
in-memory rooted projections are compared including both new rows. Coverage
tests also prove that either misaligned row is classified as a known gap. The
exact output-item budget admits the full rows and a one-under budget rejects
and clears the caller output. The `libdxfrw_graph_preservation_tests` and

## Implementation progress — S3.7c SAB 21800 open coedge-chain disposition (2026-10-21; generated parser-fed fast slice, uncommitted)

The rooted projection previously treated every non-circular next-link walk as
a known gap. Public ACIS implementation documentation describes open loops:
the last coedge's `next` and first coedge's `previous` are null, while
interior coedges remain linked in both directions. The projection now exposes
`DRW_AcisFaceLoop::coedgeRingOpen` only when the exact SAB 21800 rows show
those null endpoints and reciprocal next/previous identities across the
retained chain. `coedgeRingClosed` remains reserved for a cycle returning to
its start. Coverage permits only the two boundary nulls of an observed open
chain; a mid-chain null, mismatch, misaligned row, or cycle into another
coedge remains a known gap.

Generated parser-fed SAB controls distinguish a three-coedge reciprocal
open chain from a broken ring whose first next pointer is null but whose
previous pointer still targets another coedge. Coverage tests verify that
open endpoint nulls alone do not produce a gap, while the interrupted ring
remains a known gap. Parser-fed/in-memory equivalence now compares the open
state as well.

The external reference is ezdxf's public ACIS data-model documentation, which
states the open-loop endpoint convention and double-linked coedge model:
[ACIS Tools](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html). This is
semantic/model guidance, not authority for SAB 21800 byte layout; exact
pointer ordinals remain local generated-test assumptions for the admitted
profile. `coedgeRingOpen` describes only the observed retained chain and does
not prove the absence of detached owner-linked coedges, source-loop
completeness, face/shell validity, manifoldness, trim closure, B-rep validity,
or native acceptance.

The public `DRW_AcisFaceLoop` layout changed, so downstream consumers must

For each projected edge in the admitted SAB 21800 profile, the extractor now
builds a bounded source-ordered index of every parsed `coedge` record whose
exact ordinal-4 target resolves to that edge. It restricts retained index
storage to edges in the current projection while scanning the model once,
then compares the selected edge's ordinal-3 coedge partner walk against that
index. `coedgePartnerRingMatchesEdgeUseIndex` is true only for a closed
walk whose identities equal the explicit back-reference set; equal counts,
unique traversal, and source-index membership are all checked. A detached
coedge that explicitly names the edge but is absent from its partner ring,
or a partner member that names another edge, remains a known projection gap.

and all exact edge-use references agree, an extra detached coedge that makes

Coverage rejects a missing, unsorted, or falsely matching use index. The
existing exact/one-under output-budget control now also accounts for the
index, and extraction-work accounting includes the bounded model scan and
membership checks.

The census is limited to parsed model records with a well-typed explicit

malformed/untyped links excluded from that index, or an omitted peer to which

## Implementation progress — S3.7c SAB 21800 edge-use census completeness (2026-10-21; generated parser-fed fast slice, uncommitted)

The edge-use index now distinguishes its rows from its completeness. During
the single bounded scan of the parsed model, every `coedge` is checked for an
exact ordinal-4 target that resolves to an `edge`. Missing slots, null targets,
and wrong-type/unresolved targets increment an unclassified count and retain
the first source node index. Each projected edge carries this parsed-model
completeness observation alongside its source-ordered use row. A partner-ring
comparison is true only if every parsed coedge was classifiable and the
closed-ring identities exactly equal the row for that edge. This prevents a
partial typed-reference index from looking complete merely because its
surviving members match.

Generated parser-fed SAB 21800 controls cover a missing ordinal-4 slot and a
wrong-type ordinal-4 target outside the rooted ring. Both keep the positive
edge's valid-reference row intact while marking the model census incomplete,
reporting the exact first unclassified node, preventing a ring/index match,
and classifying the projection as a known gap. The prior full positive,
detached-use, cross-edge, parser-fed/in-memory equivalence, and exact/one-under
output-budget controls remain in the same fast owner. This check does not infer
that the source ACIS record set itself is complete and does not validate
geometry, manifoldness, trims, or B-rep semantics.

## Implementation progress — S3.7c SAB 21800 face-loop use census completeness (2026-10-21; generated parser-fed fast slice, uncommitted)

The admitted rooted profile now builds a single bounded source-order index for
both typed coedge→edge ordinal-4 references and typed loop→face ordinal-3
references. For each projected face, `loopUseNodeIndices` exposes the parsed
loop records whose exact owner slot resolves to that face. The census also
records whether every parsed loop has a classifiable owner slot, its
unclassified count, and the first affected node. `faceLoopChainMatchesUseIndex`
is true only when the full parsed-model census is complete and its identities
exactly match the face's observed next-loop chain. An extra detached loop that
names the face, or a missing/null/wrong-type owner slot anywhere in the parsed
model, prevents a match and remains a known projection gap.

Parser-fed generated controls cover a multi-loop positive whose source-index
order differs from next-chain order, a detached extra loop naming the face, a
missing ordinal-3 owner, and a wrong-type owner target. Coverage mutations
reject false or incomplete census metadata. A budget-boundary control finds
the minimum successful output-item limit for the generated graph and verifies
that one item less refuses transactionally. Parser-fed/in-memory equivalence
also compares the face census state and row.

The ezdxf ACIS source model is useful structural corroboration: its public
classes expose `Face.loop`, `Loop.face`, and ordered `next_loop` traversal.
However, ezdxf explicitly limits ACIS parsing to selected known entities,
loads unsupported entities as `NONE_ENTITY` with data loss, and says arbitrary
ACIS editing is not a goal. Its typed model therefore does not prove the
complete SAB 21800 source grammar or B-rep validity. The local census covers
only records already represented in `DRW_AcisModel`; it cannot detect source
records omitted during parsing, nor certify face/shell geometry, trims,
manifoldness, or B-rep validity.

<a id="deeperbroader-acis-topology-crosswalk-and-peer-evidence-ceilings-2026-10-21-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader research — ACIS topology crosswalk and peer-evidence ceilings (2026-10-21; primary-source review)

### Finding and decision

The broader source review found no newly confirmed libdxfrw defect and no
independent open-source route that closes the full DWG/DXF carrier, ACIS graph,
independent geometry semantics, and native-consumer chain. It does sharpen
which project is useful for which question. Keep the existing **144 findings /
78 subplans**; add no duplicate issue-mirroring item, dependency, required
peer run, or support claim.

### Peer source comparison

| Primary source | Evidence obtained | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| [ezdxf 1.4.5 ACIS tools](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) and [typed ACIS entity model](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/acis/entities.py) | The docs limit parsing/creation to simple known structures, say unsupported entity types become `NONE_ENTITY` and lose data, and explicitly exclude arbitrary ACIS editing or providing an ACIS kernel. The implementation model gives useful structural vocabulary: face→first loop, loop→face owner, ordered next-loop links, and coedge next/previous/partner/edge relationships. | Keep ezdxf as a pinned DXF/SAT/SAB syntax and selected-structure observer only. Its field model can cross-check relationship names and test shape, not establish SAB byte ordinals, arbitrary-record completeness, solid semantics, or a valid B-rep. The current face-loop census remains bounded to the local parsed model and exact admitted 21800 profile. |
| LibreDWG [current `acds.spec`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/acds.spec), [R2007+ reader source](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode_r2007.c), and open [issue #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411) | Source has an AcDs section reader; the issue's public generated DXF reproduction first passes through LibreDWG's own DXF→DWG writer, and the issue says that intermediate file lacks AcDs. Thus the generated route does not exercise reader-side AcDs extraction. The issue's claimed AutoCAD-authored sample is confidential/unavailable. | Preserve the existing PAR-07/S8 staged gate: prove the source DWG contains the target section before scoring reader behavior; then separately assess section/schema/blob decode, source-object owner/key association, DXF writeback, and external acceptance. Classify an absent-section input as `NOT_EXERCISED`, not a reader failure or pass. |
| ACadSharp open [issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) | The report describes the DWG reader materializing ACIS-bearing `3DSOLID`/`REGION` objects while its DXF writer silently omits them, including solid-only block definitions. It is a peer-version/user report, not an independently reproduced current behavior or evidence about libdxfrw. | Keep per-source entity disposition and block-owner membership in PAR-07/S8. A successful entity count or surviving INSERT is insufficient; each modeler object must be emitted, explicitly transformed, reported lost, or cause refusal. Reuse existing controls instead of adding a duplicate. |
| ACadRust [published round-trip tests](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/blob/main/tests/roundtrip.rs), [OpenCADStudio plugin/architecture docs](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio/blob/main/docs/plugin-architecture.md), and [OpenCADStudio project README](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio) | ACadRust's public tests include same-codec DWG writer→reader checks and a fabricated SAB marker payload; the OpenCADStudio docs explicitly identify `acadrust` as its document-model dependency. A separate application or repository therefore does not create an independent DWG parser vote. | Keep both on the ACadRust lineage for DWG decode and raw transport. OpenCADStudio can be a separately named application/consumer observation only when the exact build, parser dependency, platform, and operation are recorded. Same-codec results do not qualify external geometry semantics. |

### Readiness and speed refinement

1. For the current face-loop census, retain only the fast generated parser-fed
   graph controls: complete multi-loop row, source-order versus chain-order,
   detached owner reference, missing owner, wrong-type owner, coverage
   mutation, and exact/one-under output cap. Run its owning graph CTest and
   `lc3_compat_check`; no full suite or new fixture is needed.
2. Keep the next local implementation slice focused on one source relationship
   or topology invariant with a discriminating parser-fed negative. Do not
   promote a census over records that did not reach `DRW_AcisModel`.
3. At the existing composed checkpoint only, run optional pinned peers with a
   per-source disposition ledger and explicit lineage. A peer's self-roundtrip
   may establish internal consistency; an application result may establish
   acceptance of that exact build/input/operation; neither alone establishes
   independent geometry semantics.
4. Keep the six external/platform conditions explicitly deferred and
   non-promoting until their prescribed native Linux/Windows qualification
   and independent semantic evidence are recorded. If a candidate peer lacks
   an eligible sample or exact reproducible route, record `NOT_EXERCISED` /
   `NOT_QUALIFIED` and continue local work.

No source code was changed by this research subsection. J256, J260, J268,
J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

## Implementation progress — S3.7c SAB 21800 coedge-oriented endpoint identities (2026-10-21; generated parser-fed fast slice, uncommitted)

The rooted face-loop projection now exposes
`coedgeOrientedStartVertexNodeIndices` and
`coedgeOrientedEndVertexNodeIndices`, aligned with the ordered coedge rows.
The values are derived from the existing exact edge ordinal-1/2 vertex
identities and the retained coedge sense. ACIS defines a coedge as traversing
its associated edge either in the same direction or in reverse
([ACIS Topology Manual](https://manualzz.com/doc/23441667/acis-modeling-software-topology-manual)); the projection keeps raw edge
endpoint rows unchanged and applies only this coedge-to-edge direction.

Sense 0 preserves raw start/end identities; sense 1 swaps them. A null or
unresolved raw endpoint stays `-1` at the corresponding traversal endpoint.
Unknown or misordered sense produces `-1` for both derived endpoint identities
rather than guessing. Rooted coverage now checks both row alignment and the
derived/raw/sense relationship, so mutated or inconsistent derived rows are
reported as known gaps. The new cached and emitted rows are charged to the
existing extraction/output budgets.

The same slice records endpoint-chain continuity for an observed reciprocal
coedge ring. Closed rings compare every oriented end identity to the next
coedge's start, including the wraparound join; open chains compare internal
joins only. The observation is withheld if any endpoint or sense is unknown.
Known disconnected joins produce a count and first-coedge identity, and rooted
coverage marks the projection as having a known gap. This compares topological
vertex identities only; it is not curve coincidence or pcurve/trim continuity.

Parser-fed generated controls cover forward and reversed coedges, a connected
closed cycle, a disconnected cycle with exact first-gap reporting, a missing
raw start and end independently, unknown/misordered sense, projection/in-memory
equality, coverage refusal after inconsistent derived-row/observation mutations,
and exact/one-under work/output budgets. No
DWG/DXF fixture, peer dependency, native application run, or support promotion
was added. `DRW_AcisFaceLoop` public layout changed; downstream consumers must
rebuild. This does not evaluate pcurves/trims, establish face-normal winding,

## Implementation progress — S3.7c analytic straight-curve projection (2026-10-21; generated/parser-fed fast slice, uncommitted)

Added the public `drw_projectPointToAcisStraightCurve` helper. Given a decoded
straight curve and a finite WCS point, it computes the orthogonal projection
onto the infinite line, returning both the raw `p0 + t*p1` parameter and the
projected point. The direction remains unnormalized and the parameter is not
clamped to edge endpoints. It applies no modeler tolerance; callers decide
whether the source point is sufficiently close to the projected result.

The implementation scales the direction and point offset before dot-product
calculation, then uses `frexp`/`ldexp` exponent arithmetic for the parameter
and projected coordinates. This avoids avoidable intermediate overflow and
underflow for large/small but representable cases. Unsupported/unresolved
curve kinds, zero direction, non-finite input, unrepresentable point offsets,
or non-finite results return false without changing either output.

Generated tests cover an off-line point and its raw parameter, a near-axis
extreme-scale case whose small projected component remains representable,
wrong type, zero direction, non-finite input, and offset overflow. A
parser-fed SAB 21800 rooted graph uses a straight edge whose exact start/end
vertices project to parameters 0 and 1; `lc3_compat_check` and the focused
graph-preservation CTest pass. No persistent drawing fixture, public struct
layout, `DRW_Interface` vtable, 2D callback, dependency, or support claim
changed. Consumers must rebuild to link the new exported symbol.

Added `drw_projectPointToAcisPlaneSurface` to orthogonally project a finite
point to the infinite plane described by a decoded plane face's origin and

unrepresentable output refuses without modifying the caller's point.

## Implementation progress — S3.7c sphere-surface point projection (2026-10-21; generated/parser-fed fast slice, uncommitted)

Added `drw_projectPointToAcisSphereSurface` for closest-point projection onto
the geometric sphere locus described by the decoded center and signed radius.
The locus uses the radius magnitude; its sign/frame orientation is not changed
or interpreted by this operation. Projection refuses the center because the
nearest direction is not unique, and refuses zero radius as a degenerate
surface. It rejects missing/wrong surfaces, non-finite input, and an output
coordinate that cannot be represented, leaving the caller output unchanged.

Direction normalization uses the largest component of `point - center`; when
direct subtraction overflows, it derives the direction from coordinates scaled
by their largest absolute value. The output is assembled only after all three
coordinates are finite. Rooted projection coverage now classifies a zero or
non-finite sphere radius as a known gap but accepts finite signed radii without
imposing a positivity convention.

The parser-fed SAB 21800 sphere record (center `(4,5,6)`, radius `-7.5`) is
projected and compared with the equivalent positive-radius locus. Generated
controls cover the ambiguous center, zero radius, non-finite input, output
overflow, and an extreme coordinate-difference fallback.

## Implementation progress — S3.7c sphere-surface tolerance predicate (2026-10-21; generated/parser-fed fast slice, uncommitted)

Added `drw_pointWithinToleranceOfAcisSphereSurface`. For a decoded sphere face,
it reports signed radial distance from the point to the sphere locus: negative
inside, zero on the locus, positive outside. It uses the magnitude of the
stored signed radius without modifying the source face and requires an
explicit finite, nonnegative caller tolerance; no ACIS/modeler default is
introduced. Unlike closest-point projection, distance at the sphere center is
well-defined and returns the negative radius magnitude. A zero radius remains
degenerate and refuses.

When the radial distance is directly representable, the implementation
subtracts the radius from that computed distance to preserve exact boundary
comparisons. If the radial length itself would overflow, a scale-normalized
difference computes the signed result without requiring the larger intermediate
to fit in `double`. Invalid/missing/wrong surface, non-finite data, negative or
non-finite tolerance, unrepresentable signed distance, and an out-of-tolerance
point return false without changing the output.

Parser-fed SAB 21800 controls cover inside, outside, exact tolerance boundary,
and center distance. Additional controls cover just-outside refusal, invalid
tolerance/input/surface/radius atomicity, and point-center subtraction that
overflows even though the signed radial result remains representable.

## Implementation progress — S3.7c ellipse-curve closest-point projection (2026-10-21; parser-fed generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Added `drw_projectPointToAcisEllipseCurve` for the full, untrimmed geometric
locus described by a decoded ellipse edge. It reuses the evaluator's explicit
frame contract: normalize a temporary normal, check the major-axis residual
against a caller-supplied finite nonnegative dimensionless tolerance, and
remove only a tolerated residual. Positive ratios above one are handled by
sorting the two geometric radii for the solve while retaining their original
3D axis directions.

The closest point is found by solving the monotone Lagrange-multiplier
constraint with bounded bisection after scaling the axes and query
coordinates. The external-query bracket is based on the scaled
axis/query products, so a tiny but representable ellipse queried from far
away remains projectable. An ellipse-constraint residual check prevents a
bounded but ill-conditioned solve from publishing an interior point. For a
noncircular ellipse, the in-plane medial-axis segment has two equally close
points; the function refuses those cases (including the center) instead of
choosing one by accident. Circle-center ambiguity is also refused. Outputs
remain unchanged on all refusals.

The parser-fed generated SAB 21800 control checks major/minor exterior and
interior queries, normal-offset removal, the medial-axis cusp, exact-locus
projection, an oblique non-unit frame with an independent expected point, an
axis ratio above one, and a tiny ellipse/far query. A deterministic grid of
generated points compares each accepted result against 1,024 evaluations of
the full ellipse locus and verifies the known medial-axis refusals. Invalid
curve type, ratio, query, frame, frame tolerance, and overflowing
query/center difference refuse atomically.

## Implementation progress — S3.7c ellipse-evaluator cancellation correction (2026-10-21; parser-fed generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The ellipse evaluator previously normalized the already-derived right-handed
minor basis a second time and added the center before two large in-plane
offsets. For a finite, oblique ellipse this could create a one-ULP basis
mismatch, magnified into a large residual, and could discard a small
representable center when the offsets canceled. The evaluator now computes
the minor vector directly as `unitNormal × projectedMajor`, so both basis
vectors share the same scaled frame, and sums major/minor offsets before the
center.

A parser-fed generated SAB 21800 control uses a large finite oblique ellipse
and an angular/radius pair whose x offsets cancel; it asserts that the small
decoded center survives while the other large coordinate remains finite.

frame, and unrepresentable-output controls remain enabled. Focused validation:

Added `drw_evaluateAcisConeFaceNormal` for the existing explicit local cone
surface parameterization. The normal is derived from `dP/du cross dP/dv` in

cone-angle terms. A scale-safe sum computes the signed radial factor

unrepresentable radial factor fail without mutating output.

### Decision

Correct the existing PAR-14 cross-project classification; do not create a
new local vulnerability finding or duplicate test. LibreDWG 0.14.1 says the
earlier fix for its pre-R13 entity-end loop/OOM problem was incomplete. The
local AC1.40 reader is a different implementation and already has a generated
496-byte, locally authored end-boundary regression plus truncated-record,
exact-end, and retry cases. The local AC1006/AC1009 reader is also
implemented experimentally, though these old-format routes remain outside the
qualified-support denominator. This review changes the route/evidence
classification only.

### Decision

Refine existing PAR-07/S8 and PAR-144 comparator/readiness rules only. This
pass found no newly confirmed libdxfrw defect and no basis to add a finding,
top-level subplan, dependency, fixture, peer run, or support claim. The main
implementation consequence is to prevent a default FreeCAD DWG import from
being mistaken for a 3D ACIS qualification, and to prevent peer-owned sample
files from becoming local semantic goldens without provenance and independent
expected values.

| Primary source | Evidence and ceiling | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| FreeCAD's current [`importDWG.py`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py), [DWG-import guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md), [Draft DXF guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md), and [file-format limitations](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Manual_Import_and_export_to_other_filetypes.md) | The source implements DWG open as conversion to DXF followed by `importDXF.open`; documentation says the ordinary DXF route imports/exports 2D data and flattens 3D objects into 2D views. The DWG guide separately describes external converter choices and says converter output is subject to the selected DXF importer’s limits. These are descriptions of the stock route, not proof about every optional workbench or a runtime result. | Split the FreeCAD comparator into `stock DWG-converter → DXF → importer (2D projection)` and any separately named 3D-capable workbench/import route. For the stock route, record the exact converter (force one; disable fallback), process result/diagnostics, output DXF version/hash, importer backend/preferences, and per-source 2D disposition. Do not use it to promote ACIS carrier interpretation, B-rep validity, 3D semantics, or any `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` J item. The response does not identify who authored each drawing, the producer/version, transformation history, redistribution rights for each file, or independent expected object/geometry values. Thus repository use establishes a regression-input role, not golden-reference provenance. | Treat these as `PEER_SMOKE_INPUT_ONLY` candidates. Do not import, redistribute, or commit them as libdxfrw fixtures; do not score matching the peer's own parsed model as an independent semantic result. | ACadSharp current [issue index](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues) entry #1283, “new Insert(BlockRecord) deep-copies nested blocks: quadratic time and stack overflow” | The public index exposes the report title; the issue body was not retrieved in this pass, so no detailed trigger, measured threshold, or current fix status is asserted. It is a candidate application/model-copy performance issue, not by itself a DXF/DWG wire-format defect. | Keep it as a peer threat-model prompt only. Local [`DRW_Insert`](src/drw_entities.h) stores `blockRecH`/name and copies its attached ATTRIB/SEQEND state; it does not recursively clone the referenced block graph. The in-tree adapter uses visited block handles when walking block definitions. No equivalent recursive deep-copy path was found, so add no local issue or duplicate test. If a future API introduces recursive expansion/copy, test a shared nested-block DAG, repeated INSERTs, cycle handling, depth/work budget, and stable identity there. |

This is a narrow source audit, not a performance benchmark or proof of every possible consumer traversal. | Keep block-definition membership and INSERT occurrence transforms in the existing graph/disposition tests. Do not add nested-block cloning, expand the public API, or introduce an arbitrary depth limit absent a matching recursive local route. Any future traversal change gets a generated shared-DAG/cycle fast control and its owning CTest only. |

### Implementation-ready and self-unblocking refinement

1. Continue the existing local implementation queue independently of peer-file
   availability. For stock FreeCAD, run only the already-planned 2D consumer
   cohort; score converter invocation, DXF validity, importer behavior, and
   2D entity disposition as separate stages.
2. Reserve 3D native qualification for an explicitly selected importer that
