## Implementation progress — DXF MLINE vector component order (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Added an independently authored complete MLINE control for both ASCII and
Binary DXF. The two-vertex entity deliberately orders each Y/Z vector component
before its matching X component for the position, vertex-direction, and
miter-direction arrays. Distinct coordinate values make accidental cross-
occurrence pairing observable; the entity also carries different per-vertex
segment/area-fill parameters and is followed by a sentinel LINE. Full import

## Implementation progress — S3.7c rooted ACIS projection-coverage field validation (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Closed a false-negative in `drw_acisProjectionCoverage`: a manually mutated or
otherwise inconsistent rooted projection could keep all parser diagnostic
counters at zero while carrying absent observations, non-finite coordinates,
or degenerate analytic fields, and still be classified
`ProjectedSubsetNoKnownGaps`. The coverage helper now directly requires edge
endpoint/curve and face surface/loop observations, and checks finite vertex
coordinates and edge endpoints; line origin/direction; ellipse
center/frame/ratio; non-empty finite intcurve control points; and the finite,
nondegenerate fields required to describe plane, sphere, cone, and torus loci.
Cone classification only rejects an angle pair that is non-finite or
identically zero; it does not impose an undocumented normalization tolerance.
Torus locus classification does not require a U direction because the
untrimmed locus is defined by center, axis, and radii.

Generated snapshot controls cover missing edge endpoint/curve and face
surface/loop observations with zeroed diagnostic counters, non-finite
vertex/edge/curve/surface fields, empty intcurve control data, zero
line/ellipse/cone/torus axes, invalid ellipse ratio, invalid cone ratio/angle
pair, zero/negative torus radii, and valid plane/sphere/cone/torus baselines.
The gap-free test baseline now explicitly supplies a generated straight-curve
profile, rather than hiding its absent curve behind a zeroed report counter.
Existing projection diagnostics and all graph-incidence checks remain intact.
Focused validation:

## Implementation progress — PAR-03 XDATA 1006–1009 and XRECORD type-context audit (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The source audit found a documentation conflict that the earlier PAR-130 /
7BU.1 slice had not accounted for. Autodesk's 2020 Group Code Value Types
Reference assigns the full 1000–1009 range as strings. The 2024 reference
instead lists 1000–1003 strings, 1004 binary, and 1005 string, then starts
the next assigned range at 1010; the 2025 numerical reference likewise lists
1000–1005 and then jumps to 1010. Accordingly, the standalone-safe classifier
now assigns only code 1005 in that gap and leaves 1006–1009 `Unknown`; the
explicit `LibreCadMasterLegacy` profile keeps the earlier string-width
interpretation. This narrows the binary claim without discarding ASCII source
spelling or pretending that the newer omission proves every private producer
use invalid.

ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.104 describes DWG XRECORD data as DXF group-code/value pairs
and identifies code 1005 as an entity-handle reference. The XRECORD-specific
classification had been broader than that contract: it treated 1005–1009 as
handles and 210–269 as 3D points. The decoder/writer helpers now limit the
first to code 1005 and the second to 210–239. Typed encoding rejects any code
for which the XRECORD-specific mapper has no payload contract, instead of
writing a group-code word with no value bytes. Parsed, bounded unsupported
XRECORD data is still retained as an opaque full data block and may be replayed
only with the existing exact same-version/source-record provenance checks.
Independent generated vectors cover unknown codes 1009 and 240 taking that
opaque path; typed output rejects 1009/240 and continues to accept 1005.

This does not change `dwgResbufValueKind`, used for associative-action values:
that is a separate DWG value context and needs its own ODA passage/trace before
changing its widths or handle-stream behavior. The 2020-versus-2024 Autodesk
classification conflict also remains documented rather than erased. No
producer-authored evidence for 1006–1009 was available in the tracked corpus;
therefore no standalone binary width or support claim is inferred for them.

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 HATCH gradient CMC ByLayer/ByBlock methods (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The existing CMC reader/writer handled C2 RGB and C3 indexed colors but
rejected the two standard methods already represented by the shared DWG color
decoder: C0 ByLayer (ACI 256) and C1 ByBlock (ACI 0). The bounded gradient
reader now accepts those packed methods only when their 24-bit payload is zero,
and maps them to `rgb=-1` with the corresponding ACI sentinel. The CMC writer
emits the method byte and zero payload for matching explicit C0/C1 tuples;
invalid method/value combinations remain fail-closed. Gradient validation and
DXF group-63 parsing/writing preserve 256 and 0 as ByLayer/ByBlock, including
the otherwise easy-to-drop ACI-zero value. The method decode is cross-checked
against the existing `dwgBuffer::getCmColor()` mapping.

Generated controls independently inspect the C0/C1 CMC bytes and reserved
field, exercise direct AC1018 same-stream parsing, exercise an AC1024 DWG file
roundtrip with detached string handling and a following LINE sentinel, and
write/read both ASCII and Binary DXF with explicit group-63 values 256 and 0.
The first run exposed an incomplete test-side AC1018 cursor: optional C2/C3
color/book strings are inline between stops. The independent verifier now

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 R2010+ zero-fit HATCH/MPOLYGON spline tangent alignment (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The generated AC1024 MPOLYGON gradient roundtrip added for the CMC C0/C1
slice used a spline boundary with zero fit points and failed to read its
following edge. The local writer and ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.75 serialize the R2010+
fit-count field, zero or more 2RD fit points, then both 2RD tangents. The shared
HATCH/MPOLYGON boundary parser had incorrectly skipped the tangents when the
fit count was zero, so the next edge type was read from tangent bytes. The
parser now reads both tangent vectors unconditionally for R2010+ after the fit
array, with the same bounds and finite-value checks as populated-fit parsing.
No writer change was needed.

The independent boundary-wire control now emits a zero fit count and zero
tangents for the no-fit case. The existing generated HATCH and MPOLYGON DWG
writer/reader matrix verifies both no-fit and populated-fit paths, including
boundary continuation and following-entity framing. This is spec-backed local
wire/readback evidence, not independent producer qualification. The previous
peer-derived conditional assumption is not used as the byte-layout authority.

## Research refinement — PAR-134 CMC method bytes C0–C8 (2026-10-21; source audit, no semantic promotion)

ODA v5.4.1 §2.11 defines the generic R2004+ CMC wire structure (reserved BS,
method-packed BL, RC name/book flags, and optional strings) but does not
enumerate all `AcCmEntityColor::ColorMethod` values. Autodesk's documented
[`ColorMethod` enum](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2019/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OREF-AcCmEntityColor__ColorMethod.html)
starts at `kByLayer = 0xC0` and lists the contiguous methods through `kNone`;
its documentation identifies C4/ByPen, C6/LayerOff, C7/LayerFrozen, and
C8/None as internal-only for third-party applications. `kForeground` is C5;
Autodesk separately defines ACI foreground as 7. Autodesk's [`AcCmColor::color`
contract](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/OARX-RefGuide/files/OREF-__MEMBERTYPE_Methods_AcCmColor.html)
states the high byte is the color method. This is API semantic evidence, not a
DWG producer sample for the low 24-bit payload of every method.

The local `dwgColor` enum now names C3 as `ACI` (retaining `ACIS` as a
historical alias), adds the documented C4-C7 names, and renames C8 from the
unsupported `WINDOW_BG` label to `NONE`. This is an internal nomenclature
correction only: no decoder, writer, normalized projection, API, or support
claim changed. The general `getCmColor()` fallback still returns ACI 256 for
methods other than C0-C3; that fallback is not independent semantic support.
`DRW_VisualStyle` retains raw method/value metadata for exact same-version
replay, while the generated `0xC8` vector's normalized view currently becomes
256. Treat that view as a fallback/loss risk, not a valid ByLayer interpretation.

LibreDWG's mutable
[`dwg_color_method_name()` source](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dwg.c)
also names C5 Foreground and C8 None, but labels C2/C3 differently from the
local ODA/Autodesk-backed RGB/ACI mapping. This source-level divergence is a
reason to keep method/value vectors explicit; the name helper is not a binary
format authority or runtime oracle.

Implementation-ready disposition:

1. Keep C0/C1/C2/C3 as the only semantically projected CMC methods in the
   current HATCH gradient path. Keep the independent C0-C3 vectors and their
   exact DXF group-63/421 associations unchanged.
2. Treat C5 Foreground as a candidate mapping to ACI 7, but do not read/write
   it in HATCH gradients until an ODA example or eligible real DWG proves the
   packed low-24-bit payload and optional-name behavior. Then test its method,
   payload, and group-63 output separately from C3 ACI 7.
3. Keep C4 and C6-C8 opaque/unsupported for third-party semantic projection;
   do not normalize them to ByLayer. Preserve raw source metadata and exact
   same-version replay where the owning data class already supports it. Any
   fail-closed change to the shared `getCmColor()` fallback needs a consumer
   inventory first because that decoder feeds many DWG object/entity paths.
4. Add no new finding count or peer dependency in this research pass. Findings
   and top-level subplans remain 144/78; J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and
   J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 standalone MTEXT background CMC retention (2026-10-21; generated AC1024/AC1032 fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.46 defines MTEXT background color as CMC; §2.11 defines
CMC RGB and optional color-name/color-book strings. The standalone MTEXT DWG
parser previously retained only the normalized scalar even though its existing
public model has RGB/name fields, and the standalone writer emitted only that
scalar. This silently changed a parsed truecolor background to ByLayer.

Standalone parsing now retains C2 RGB and optional color/book names from the
bounded string stream. Standalone and embedded DWG writers share validation and
method selection for C0/C1/C2/C3, preserve name-only CMC values, and reject
out-of-range or unrepresentable state before writing the MTEXT common prefix.
The shared CMC preflight also rejects a non-finite background scale before
standalone output; the embedded writer uses the same validation.
R2007+ named colors require a distinct detached string stream. The embedded
writer's text-frame flag gate now mirrors the parser's AC1032-only interpretation.
No public layout or virtual interface changed.

Generated AC1024/AC1032 vectors independently inspect named C0 ByLayer, named
C1 ByBlock, C3 ACI, and named black C2 RGB, including text/name stream order and
the following transparency value. Production parsing retains background
scalar/RGB/name/book state and leaves the following-handle sentinel aligned;
a second local round trip is also checked. Invalid RGB and missing detached
strings fail before the common prefix. The existing issue-1410 composed
DXF→DWG→DWG-readback control passes after the shared embedded-writer change.
The NaN background-scale control also fails before standalone output. No
persistent drawing fixture was added.

**Adjacent unresolved spec discrepancy:** ODA §20.4.46 labels the background
scale factor `BL` while specifying a default of 1.5; the current parser/writer
and existing fast controls use `BD`. A locally authored AC1018 scratch drawing
from GNU LibreDWG 0.14.0 with background scale 2 emits the field as `BL 45`,
and the peer's read-to-DXF route reports group 45 as 2.0. This is a useful
peer-specific trace, but not an AutoCAD/ODA producer sample. LibreDWG's
published structure agrees with `BL`, while ACadSharp's writer uses
`WriteBitDouble` despite its `BL` comment and another binding reports `BD`.
libdxfrw rejects the scratch AC1018 file at `BAD_READ_FILE_HEADER` before
object parsing, so the sample does not qualify its own MTEXT path. The default
and type remain internally inconsistent in ODA; leave the current `BD` path
unchanged until a producer-authored non-integral sample or authoritative trace
resolves the conflict. [Detailed trace receipt](docs/research/mtext-background-scale-finite-fast-slice-2026-10-21.json).
The source/method identity beyond normalized C0/C1/C2/C3, HATCH C5 producer
behavior, class-specific DXF mappings, and external/native qualification remain
separate gates.

<a id="implementation-progress-par134-dwg-header-cmc-metadata-retention-2026-10-21-generated-ac1024-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 scalar-only DWG HEADER CMC metadata retention (2026-10-21; generated AC1024 fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA v5.4.1 §9 lists the six HEADER variables `CECOLOR`, `DIMTFILLCLR`,
`DIMCLRD`, `DIMCLRE`, `DIMCLRT`, and `INTERFERECOLOR` as CMC. §2.11 defines
the CMC method byte, RGB payload, optional color name, and optional color-book
name. The parser previously kept only the normalized integer returned by
`getCmColor`; the writer consequently regenerated an indexed method and lost
truecolor/name/book distinctions.

`DRW_Variant` now retains an immutable DWG CMC sidecar (method, flags, index,
RGB, names, and source version) alongside its existing scalar value. Variant
copy/move and HEADER copy/assignment preserve the sidecar; replacing the
scalar clears stale DWG provenance. HEADER parsing reads optional names from
the bounded R2007+ detached string stream and verifies the cursor stays within
its declared extent. HEADER writing validates normalized scalar/method/RGB
consistency, name flags, the specification-reserved zero index, supported
C0–C3 methods, and required detached output before emitting each field.
Scalar-only DXF-origin values keep the existing writer behavior.

The DXF mapping was intentionally not extended. The reviewed Autodesk DXF
HEADER reference establishes scalar group-code mappings, but did not establish
class-specific truecolor/color-name/color-book extensions for these variables.
The DWG sidecar therefore does not promote RGB/name/book into undocumented DXF
groups. The new member changes public `DRW_Variant` size/layout; downstream
consumers must rebuild. No virtual interface changed.

A generated AC1024 file exercises all six fields through the production writer
and reader: C0 ByLayer, C1 ByBlock, C2 RGB with and without optional names,
and C3 ACI. The control verifies scalar and sidecar values, header copy and
assignment, refusal of unsupported C4 and nonzero reserved index while
preserving seeded destinations, and successful retries on the same writer.
The file is generated in the system temporary directory and removed by the
test; no persistent DWG/DXF fixture was added.

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 MPOLYGON fill CMC name/book retention (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA v5.4.1 §2.11 defines the CMC method, RGB payload, optional color name,
and optional color-book name. The existing MPOLYGON parser already retained
the normalized scalar, C2 RGB, and color name, but discarded the separate book
name. Its DWG writer used the RGB convenience overload and an empty book name;
that overload falls back to the indexed form when RGB is absent, losing named
C0/C1/C3 state as well.

`DRW_MPolygon` now retains `fillColorBookName` through copy/assignment and DWG
reset, and the typed `dx_iface` callback budget charges both dynamic strings.
Before writing the common entity prefix, the encoder validates the normalized
scalar domain, absent/present RGB sentinel and C2 scalar pairing, supported
C0/C1/C2/C3 method selection, combined bounded text size, and the detached
R2007+ string-stream requirement. Pre-R2004 output refuses RGB or names rather
than silently dropping them. The R2004+ writer explicitly emits the method and
both optional strings; existing scalar-only C0/C1/C3 output remains canonical.
`dwgRW::writeMPolygon` escalates a refused color-bearing entity to a required
write failure, preventing a non-gradient MPOLYGON from being silently omitted
while the rest of the drawing is published.

The reviewed Autodesk MPOLYGON DXF table establishes fill ACI group 63 but not
a separate fill color-book group. Existing DXF groups were not extended; a
book-bearing MPOLYGON now fails preflight and preserves the destination. This
is a deliberate class-mapping boundary, not a claim that all MPOLYGON truecolor
DXF extensions are qualified.

Generated production-writer/reader roundtrips cover AC1018, AC1024, and AC1032
for named C0 ByLayer, named C1 ByBlock, named black C2 RGB, and named C3 ACI.
They verify normalized values, RGB/name/book retention, callback capture, and
the following LINE sentinel. An invalid C2 scalar/RGB pair on a non-gradient
MPOLYGON refuses the whole transaction, preserves a seeded destination, then
succeeds after correction on the same writer. A generated DXF control verifies the unsupported
book-bearing write is refused with destination preservation and that a
corrected no-book write succeeds on the same `dxfRW` instance. Files live in
the test's temporary directory and are removed; no persistent fixture was
added.

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 MTEXT CMC source-method retention (2026-10-21; generated AC1024 fast slice, uncommitted)

Autodesk's `ColorMethod` reference names `0xC5` as Foreground. The existing
shared `getCmColor` projection maps C5 to the scalar ACI foreground value 7,
but standalone and embedded MTEXT parsing discarded the method byte. Their
DWG writers therefore regenerated the normalized scalar as C3, changing the
source method without retaining evidence that its payload was equivalent.
ODA v5.4.1 §2.11 remains authoritative for the CMC field envelope (reserved
BS, packed BL, RC flags, optional text names); it does not qualify C5's packed
payload semantics.

`DRW_MText` now appends `m_backgroundColorDwgMethod`, using `0xFF` to mean no
DWG-specific method was captured and allowing the legacy canonical writer
selection. Both standalone and embedded MTEXT parsing retain the raw method
for R2004+ backgrounds; pre-R2004 input has no CMC method and keeps the
sentinel. Reset clears it, ordinary copy/assignment preserves it, and DXF
updates to groups 63/421/431 clear stale DWG provenance. Before writing, the
shared standalone/embedded CMC preflight requires an explicit C0-C3 source
method to agree with scalar/RGB state. It permits representable C0/C1/C3
indexed output on a pre-R2004 path only when no RGB or names would be lost. C5
and other unqualified methods remain visible to callers but refuse where a
CMC payload would otherwise be emitted. DXF projection remains based on the
documented scalar and truecolor groups and does not consume this DWG-only
method field.

Generated AC1024 vectors now mark C0/C1/C2/C3 source methods explicitly and
verify read/rewrite retention. A generated C3 MTEXT body is then changed only
at the packed CMC method byte to C5. Production parsing projects it to ACI 7,
retains C5, and leaves the following handle aligned. Copy, assignment, reset,
and fail-before-output refusal are checked. This is a generated parser control,
not producer evidence for C5 encoding; no persistent fixture was added.

## Research refinement — PAR-134 MLEADER line-color DXF group and override bit (2026-10-21; no code change)

The Autodesk MLeader Leader Line DXF table lists vertex groups 10/20/30,
break-index group 90, break-start groups 11/21/31, break-end groups 12/22/32,
and leader-line index group 91; it does not list a color field. The common
MLeader table separately defines entity-level leader-line color as group 91,
text color as group 92, and block color as group 93. Read in isolation, these
tables leave an apparent conflict with the local nested line group-92 writer.

The local authoritative ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1 §20.4.86 resolves
the nested field: an R2010+ `LEADER_LINE{}` record contains `CMC` DXF group 92
for line color and `BL` group 93 for override flags, with bit 2 denoting a
line-color override. §20.4.48 independently gives group 91 as the MLEADER
entity-level leader color. The groups have different class scopes; current
parser/writer scalar mapping is supported by the ODA field tables. The
references are [Autodesk leader-line groups](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-B2E6436A-F17D-4F59-9DE8-DBDB61AD36C6.htm),
[Autodesk common MLeader groups](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-69B9139A-48B4-48A5-B3CF-A3233ABFBE49.htm),
and the [ODA specification](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf).

This resolves the scalar group assignment only. The reviewed DXF tables and
ODA mapping do not establish nested group-420/430 encodings for per-line RGB,
color name, or book name. The implementation therefore retains scalar group
92 and refuses richer metadata until a class-specific DXF producer/spec
witness establishes that representation. Generated vectors remain local
writer controls, not native producer evidence. No code, fixture, external
gate, support claim, or plan count changed. Findings/subplans remain 144/78;
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`.

Self-unblock: continue the PAR-134 CMC caller inventory and class-specific DXF
loss audit; the scalar line-color question no longer blocks local work.

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 LAYER CMC raw flags/index and book-only retention (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

BS and retained no separate color-name/book-name strings. It also projected a
book-only CMC to an empty `colorName`, so a read/rewrite silently lost the book.
ODA v5.4.1 §2.11 defines the R2004+ CMC shape as a leading BS index that is
always zero, a packed method/RGB BL, and an RC whose bit 0 indicates a color
name TV and bit 1 indicates a book-name TV.

strings with an explicit source-metadata marker. The joined public spelling
uses `BOOK$ENTRY` when the book is present, including `BOOK$` for a book with
an empty entry name. Copy/assignment retain the new fields; reset and DXF
color-group parsing clear the DWG-only provenance. Typed callback memory
estimation charges both retained private strings in addition to the existing
public `colorName` payload.

The DWG encoder validates a parsed source method against the current scalar /
RGB projection, requires the reserved index to be zero, accepts only the two
ODA-defined flags, and checks that unset name/book bits do not carry strings.
Unmodified parsed names replay their exact separate values and flags. An
intentional edit through public `colorName` is split using the existing
`BOOK$ENTRY` convention and receives flags consistent with the edited value.
`dwgBufferW::putCmColorWithFlags` preserves source flags, including a flagged
empty string; unsupported flag bits or inconsistent string/flag pairs fail
before the CMC bytes are written. No CMC method outside the locally-supported
C0–C3 set was added.

Generated AC1024 and AC1032 full DWG writer/reader routes cover named C2 and C3
colors plus a book-only C3 color, checking raw flags/index, separate names,
joined public spelling, copy/reset, rewrite, and reread. Generated ASCII and
Binary DXF controls check group 430 round-trip for the book-only spelling and
that importing DXF clears DWG-only metadata. Low-level generated bytes verify

flags bit and a nonzero reserved index and prove refusal before any output

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 VIEW/VPORT ambient CMC metadata and class-specific DXF projection (2026-10-21; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The bounded R2007+ VIEW and VPORT parsers already captured scalar, optional
RGB, and name/book values, but dropped the CMC method byte, optional-string
flags, and leading BS index. The DWG writers could therefore normalize an
unsupported source method, lose named indexed colors, lose book-only or
empty-book state, and silently omit non-default ambient fields when writing a
pre-R2007 version. Adapter byte estimates also omitted the newly-retained
separate CMC names/books.

Both table-record models now retain CMC method/flags/index, separate name/book
strings, and a source-metadata marker. Copy/reset behavior follows the model's
normal value semantics; DXF color-group parsing clears DWG-only provenance.
DWG encoding preflights the complete ambient projection before any bytes,
replays supported C0-C3 source methods and name/book flags, and refuses
unknown flags, a nonzero reserved R2004+ BS, method/value disagreement,
unsupported methods, or non-default ambient state in versions without the
ambient field. Adapter retained-byte estimates charge the separate name/book
strings.

The class-specific DXF decision is deliberately asymmetric. Autodesk's current
[VPORT DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-8CE7CC87-27BD-4490-89DA-C21F516415A9.htm)
lists ambient groups 63/421/431, so the VPORT output keeps that projection.
Autodesk's group-code table classifies 430–437 as strings used for named
truecolors; keep VPORT's documented 431 as the single color-name value (the
existing `BOOK$ENTRY` spelling) rather than inventing a separate group 430
field for this record.
ODA v5.4.1 maps VIEW ambient CMC to group 63, while Autodesk's current
[VIEW DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-CF3094AB-ECA9-43C1-8075-7791AC84F97C.htm)
does not list ambient 421/431 fields. VIEW therefore emits only the ODA-listed
scalar group 63; rich RGB/name/book values fail atomically instead of being
written using undocumented class fields. Legacy DXF similarly refuses
non-default ambient data where the target cannot represent it.

Generated AC1024/AC1032 full DWG routes cover VPORT named RGB, VIEW book-only
ACI, and an explicitly empty VIEW book name; parser assertions inspect method,
flags, raw index, separate strings, joined spelling, copy/reset, rewrite, and
reread. ASCII and Binary DXF controls inspect literal VPORT 63/421/431 and
VIEW scalar-63 fields, verify parse-back clears DWG-only metadata, and prove
atomic refusal for legacy ambient data and rich VIEW RGB/name state. Direct
encoders reject invalid flags/index, C5, and legacy ambient-color loss before
changing their output buffers. No persistent fixture was added.

## Implementation progress — generated DWG partial-read outcome sentinel repair (2026-10-21; scratch-only fast slice)

The previous generated partial-read outcome control tried to create a malformed
HATCH by clearing a spline's rational flag while retaining its weight list.
That is no longer malformed: `DRW_Hatch::encodeDwg` treats a nonempty
`weightlist` as canonical and emits the rational bit, so the reader correctly
accepts the HATCH. The earlier stage-1 failure therefore exposed a stale test
assumption, not a reader recovery defect.

Both generated partial-read controls now emit a LINE with a NaN coordinate,
then emit a finite LINE. `DRW_Line::encodeDwg` serializes the authored scalar;
the bounded reader's finite-value check rejects the first record while the
entity loop continues and publishes the following LINE. The control verifies
one entity parse failure, one successful LINE callback, finalized partial frame
coverage, and the diagnostic's partial-read disposition. All files are
generated under temporary directories and removed by the test; no persistent
DWG fixture or production parser change was made.

existing narrow `--dwg-read-outcome` selector. The semantic adapter's partial
readback control uses the same generated malformed-LINE shape, keeping both

ODA v5.4.1 §2.11 defines the generic R2004+ CMC envelope as a reserved BS
index, packed BL method/value, flags byte, and optional color-name/book TV

so this slice leaves the established SUN field order unchanged and only
captures the already-parsed CMC metadata. Autodesk's SUN DXF reference lists
group 63 for color, but no group 421 or CMC name/book group; Autodesk's color

presence, RGB, and separate color/book names. Its DWG encoder validates and

stream; it refuses malformed metadata and unsupported methods before output.

output admits faithful scalar group-63 colors (including the documented C5 to
ACI-7 projection), and refuses RGB, optional names/flags, invalid indices, or
unsupported methods before record publication. The writer no longer emits the
undocumented SUN group 421 extension; the parser continues to accept it but
the typed writer fails closed when that value cannot be projected by the

strings, and the following SUN fields; the production parser checks retained

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 SECTION_SETTINGS geometry CMC retention and DXF schema correction (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA v5.4.1 §2.11 defines the generic R2004+ CMC envelope, including the
reserved BS index, packed method/value, flags, and optional TV name/book
strings. The existing bounded SECTION_SETTINGS DWG reader already consumed
that envelope for each Section Geometry Settings record but retained only
normalized ACI/RGB. This change does not alter the SECTION_SETTINGS DWG field
order; it carries the decoded CMC details through the typed model and inverse
writer.

`DRW_SectionGeometrySettings` now retains source method, flags, reserved
index, color name, and color-book name. DWG encoding preflights every geometry
color before writing the record: it checks normalized method/value/RGB
consistency, zero reserved index, known flag bits, name/flag consistency,
bounded names, and detached string-stream availability. It replays supported
C0-C3 CMC, including flagged-empty optional names. Unsupported methods and
malformed metadata fail before output. The appended fields change the public
struct size; downstream consumers must rebuild.

Autodesk's class-specific [Section Geometry Settings DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-21E53626-0F28-4787-A109-86B9FFE0C149.htm)
identifies group 63 as color data and lists no truecolor, color-name, or
color-book field for this subclass. The typed DXF writer therefore emits
scalar color only as group 63 and refuses RGB/truecolor, CMC names/books,
flags (including flagged-empty strings), nonzero reserved index, unsupported
methods, and inconsistent color state before writing. The parser reads the
documented group 63 and continues to accept the historical local group-62
spelling for compatibility; newly emitted DXF is canonical group 63. It also
continues accepting an incoming group 420, but the typed writer refuses that
RGB state because the class-specific DXF schema provides no such mapping.

Generated controls write/read an AC1024 SECTION_SETTINGS object with a named
RGB C2 color, book-only C1 color, and flagged-empty C0 name; they check parser
retention, copy/assignment, and atomic refusal for C5, nonzero index, unknown
flags, mismatched flags/strings, and out-of-range RGB. Separate ASCII/Binary
writer controls verify scalar ACI uses group 63 and refuse each unprojectable
CMC form before emitting bytes. A focused parser control checks group 63 and
the legacy group-62 read alias. No persistent DWG/DXF fixtures were added.

## Deeper/broader research — open-source peer route and artifact-status refresh (2026-10-22; primary-source review)

### Decision

Refresh the existing PAR-07/S8 peer-routing matrix, PAR-14 external-artifact
pinning rule, and native-consumer qualification sequence. This pass clarifies
the distinct current statuses of two LibreDWG milestones and sharpens the usable scope of
libopencad, GDAL DXF, ezdxf, ACadSharp, and FreeCAD. It found no new local
defect, no reason to add a finding or top-level subplan, and no evidence that
promotes a DWG/DXF/3D support claim. ODA v5.4.1 remains the DWG byte-layout
authority; peer sources are route-selection and cross-check evidence only.

### Peer routes and evidence ceilings

| Primary source reviewed | Current observation (2026-10-22 snapshot) | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [0.14 release](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/releases/tag/0.14), [NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS), separate [0.14](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/milestone/22) and [0.14.1](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/milestone/23) milestones, and [release list](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/releases) | The 0.14 release at `d9468ae` says R2004 DWG writing is supported and R2010/R2013/R2018 writing is experimental, with CRC errors reported on import. The 0.14 milestone closed Sep 8, 2026, though its description still lists TODOs; the separate 0.14.1 milestone remains open at 67% with 13 open items. The 0.14.1 NEWS is labeled beta, and the latest listed `0.14.8612` at `f860b0f` is explicitly a prerelease/nightly. These are distinct milestone/release/source identities, not contradictory claims to average. | Preserve the milestone distinction in the artifact-status row above. At optional peer checkpoints, pin the exact release/pre-release commit and record operation, AC version, output hash, strict independent reopen, and per-object disposition. Do not treat milestone closure, a newer version string, or mutable source as a writer pass. |
| ACadSharp [release history](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/releases), [v3.8.0](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/releases/tag/v3.8.0), and open [issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) | v3.8.0 at signed commit `3a1c66b` remains the latest formal release in the reviewed page. Its v3.7.1 predecessor includes release notes for reading ACIS payloads from 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY and reading the AcDs payload-area offset. Issue #1195 reports silent DWG-read→DXF-write solid/region loss against ACadSharp 3.4.9; it remains open, but the report is not a test of v3.8.0 and must not be projected onto that release without reproduction. | Use ACadSharp only for the exact reader/writer route and pinned release tested. For a future optional modeler probe, compare every source handle and block owner through decode→DXF emission→independent parse; include solid-only blocks. Do not use an old issue report as a current-release result or accept entity count/same-reader roundtrip as carrier-preservation evidence. Existing PAR-07/S8 owner/disposition work already owns this check; add no duplicate local case absent a specific coverage gap. |
| [libopencad](https://github.com/nextgis-borsch/lib_opencad) and GDAL's [DWG/CAD driver documentation](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/cad.html) | libopencad's project README states that it supports only DWG R2000. GDAL documents its DWG/CAD driver as based on libopencad, read-only, and exposing a small OGR geometry subset (for example POINT, LINE, CIRCLE/ARC, and 3DFACE). By inference from that projected schema and listed entity set, this route does not expose a complete DWG object graph. | Mark this as a narrow AC1015-era geometry-projection route, not a competitive current-version DWG parser, DWG writer, AcDs, arbitrary-object, or solid-semantic oracle. Avoid spending a peer-build slot on AC1018+ or ACIS claims; a local generated AC1015 2D case is sufficient if a specific projection question remains. |
| GDAL [DXF driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | GDAL 3.12+ reads Binary DXF, not DWG. The DXF driver converts many source records into OGR geometries (including tessellated curves and merged/inlined blocks by default), omits some styling/schema details, skips 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY/SURFACE by default, and offers an opt-in `ASMData`/`ASMTransform` projection for AC1027+ without converting ASM into OGR geometry. Raw-code-value capture is optional. | Permit GDAL only as an exact-version, configured, downstream projection or limited raw-carrier observer. When used, disable block inlining/merging if identity matters, enable raw-code capture as needed, record every open option, and compare source handles, placements, transform, payload bytes, and omitted-feature diagnostics. Never treat successful OGR output, tessellation, or raw ASM bytes as full DXF preservation, B-rep semantics, or DWG evidence. |
| ezdxf [ACIS glossary](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/glossary.html), [ACIS tools](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html), and its [DXF version capabilities](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/introduction.html) | ezdxf is a useful broad ASCII/Binary DXF reader/writer and can inspect/create selected SAT/SAB carriers, but its docs explicitly exclude arbitrary ACIS editing/processing and state it has no ACIS kernel. The project does not supply a DWG codec; an ezdxf-to-DWG route invokes a separately installed converter and belongs to that converter's lineage. | Use ezdxf for normal DXF parse/field/raw-carrier observation, keeping any recovery/audit path separately labeled, and only locally authored simple payloads within the documented profile. Keep it out of arbitrary ACIS/B-rep semantics, DWG parser counts, and independent geometry votes. Record any external converter separately. |
| FreeCAD [current `importDWG.py`](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py), [DXF guide](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md), and [local support status](docs/3D_SUPPORT_STATUS.md) | FreeCAD's DWG route is converter→DXF→selected DXF importer. The current wrapper can try LibreDWG, ODA, and QCAD according to its preference; the LibreDWG conversion branch checks output-path existence after `communicate()` rather than proving process success. The stock DXF importer is a separate consumer stage and does not acquire capabilities merely because the converter emitted an entity/carrier. | Native Linux/Windows qualification must explicitly select the converter, pin the exact importer/backend/build, capture converter exit status and logs outside the wrapper, independently inspect output DXF, and assert native per-source disposition. Treat fallback as another route. Keep imported object counts separate from geometry validity and preserve the existing 2D-consumer regression lanes. |

### Implementation-ready, fast-first refinement

1. **Do not repeat the broad survey.** The current route matrix is sufficient
   to select one peer only when a local implementation slice leaves a precise
   unresolved question. No peer binary, package, or external corpus belongs in
   each-slice validation.
2. **Resolve local questions against ODA/spec and generated controls first.**
   For code changes, run the owning fast selector and its focused CTest; add a
   generated in-memory or locally-from-scratch control only for a demonstrated
   uncovered invariant. Use broader suites at their already scheduled
   checkpoints.
3. **At the single composed peer checkpoint, choose by question:** use
   LibreDWG/ACadSharp for a version-matched DWG structure or object-disposition
   comparison; ezdxf for DXF tag/raw-carrier behavior; GDAL only for selected
   OGR projection; and a native FreeCAD run only for the separately pinned
   converter/importer route. Do not count wrappers or downstream apps as
   independent codec lineages.
4. **Bind evidence per source object, not only aggregate counts.** Record
   source handle, owner/block/layout, family/version, decoded disposition,
   serialized disposition, output handle, payload hash when applicable, and
   omission/refusal diagnostic. Preserve separate stages for transport,
   typed semantics, geometry/kernel, and native acceptance.
5. **Keep the repository fixture policy.** Do not download or commit samples
   from peer issue trackers or their regression corpora. Use already-tracked
   fixtures or controls generated locally from scratch, and keep confidential
   or third-party-origin drawings in the protected local corpus.
6. **Self-update and self-unblock.** After each implementation slice, update
   this plan and its receipt, run the fast owner test, report progress after
   the slice commit, and immediately continue with the next locally actionable
   item. Missing peers/platforms/samples remain `NOT_RUN` or
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; all six J gates remain explicitly non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 AC1021 TABLE override CMC semantic-completeness gate (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The AC1021 TABLE reader structurally consumed per-cell and table-level
override values, including CMC colors, but did not retain those values in its
typed projection. It could therefore leave `m_semanticContentComplete` true
and make the typed TABLE adapter eligible to emit a snapshot missing the
overrides. ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.96.1 documents the applicable cell override bits,
the title/header/data row color bits, and the 18-entry border color,
lineweight, and visibility masks.

Cell and table override parsing now receives semantic-completeness state.
Any nonzero unretained mask disqualifies typed TABLE output while preserving
structural parsing and the existing anonymous-block INSERT fallback. The
reader now tracks structural cell-parse success independently from semantic
completeness: after discovering an override it continues through subsequent
cells and table masks, preserving the object cursor and handle/string
alignment. Bits outside the ODA-documented AC1021 mask ranges fail closed
instead of being silently ignored.

Generated AC1021 frames cover a cell background-color CMC override and a
table title-row-color CMC override, each with a following tail sentinel. Both
controls assert successful structural parsing, `m_hasSemanticContent`,
`!m_semanticContentComplete`, and exact cursor alignment. Existing no-override
text and block-cell cases continue to assert complete semantic parsing. No
persistent fixture was added.

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 ENC reserved-bit refusal (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA v5.4.1 §2.11 enumerates the ENC flags for inline RGB (`0x80`), an
AcDbColor reference (`0x40`), and transparency (`0x20`). The local decoder
previously ignored bits `0x04`, `0x08`, and `0x10` and returned the normalized
ACI value without consuming any payload for them. A bounded caller could then
interpret an unknown extension as the next entity field. The decoder now
invalidates its candidate buffer before reading any following field when one
of those three undocumented bits is present. The existing `0x01`/`0x02` local
name/index behavior and documented high-bit paths are unchanged.

Generated in-memory controls cover ordinary ACI, the ACI 256/ByLayer index
bit, the current inline-RGB path, the AcDbColor reference flag pair, and
transparency. Each valid route asserts a following 3-bit sentinel. Separate
controls set each reserved flag and assert that the reader becomes invalid
before the sentinel can be interpreted. These controls exercise the local
decoder only; they are not producer-authored DWG evidence.

**Adjacent unresolved ODA text discrepancy:** the local ODA v5.4.1 PDF's ENC
paragraph describes the inline RGB value as `BS` while specifying that it
contains the last 24 bits. A bit-short cannot represent an arbitrary 24-bit
RGB value, while the existing local decoder consumes this slot as `BL`. This
slice does not change that width or claim that the generated `BL` vector
settles the format. Resolve it only with an authoritative erratum or an
eligible producer trace and a traceable drawing.

The R2007+ TABLECONTENT path also structurally consumes CMCs in cell content
formats and populated cell styles without retaining their values. ODA v5.4.1
§20.4.97 describes TABLECONTENT; §20.4.101.3 specifies content color as CMC;
§20.4.101.4 specifies the populated cell style's background CMC, inherited

the cell-style data flag above the documented 0/1 range are refused rather
than interpreted as the presence bit.

## Deeper/broader research — ACIS/SAB producer scope and AcDs test-route correction (2026-10-22; research only)

This review reconciles the current ezdxf ACIS API with its contradictory FAQ,
re-reads the public LibreDWG AcDs loss report as a staged pipeline, and turns
those findings into a low-cost, implementation-ready probe. It refines PAR-07/S8
and PAR-144 only: no new local defect, finding, top-level subplan, or support
promotion is justified by peer documentation or issue reports.

| Primary source / route | Finding | Plan consequence and evidence ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| ezdxf [1.4.5 ACIS API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html), [FAQ](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/faq.html), and [ACIS entity limits](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/dxfentities/3dsolid.html) | The specific API lists `export_sat()` and `export_sab()`, `export_dxf()`, and `body_from_mesh()`. Its supported version profile is SAT for DXF R2000–R2010 and SAB for R2013/R2018. `body_from_mesh()` generates polyhedral ACIS bodies; `mesh_from_body()` returns only planar polygonal faces and loses curved faces. Unsupported ACIS records can become `NONE_ENTITY` and lose data; ezdxf has no ACIS kernel. The FAQ's “only write SAT” and “no creation” wording conflicts with that detailed API. | Prefer the more specific API over the stale FAQ, but admit only exact version-pinned behavior and verify actual emitted DXF version, carrier, entity association, and payload hash. Use ezdxf as a bounded SAT/SAB scratch producer and carrier inspector—not as an arbitrary ACIS round-trip oracle, curved-surface evaluator, B-rep kernel, or semantic witness for its own generated body. |
| LibreDWG [issue #1411](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1411) | The open report gives a source-generated AC1032 DXF procedure: create a polyhedral body through ezdxf, confirm a non-empty entity SAB and `acdsdata.has_records`, then invoke LibreDWG `dxf2dwg` and `dwg2dxf`. The report observes the DWG has no `AcDsPrototype` section and the output DXF has no SAB. This demonstrates a loss on the reported writer route. Because its intermediate DWG lacks the target section, that public chain does not exercise DWG reader extraction. The issue's separate AutoCAD DWG is confidential and unavailable. | Keep this as a version/commit-scoped peer report, not an independent test result for current releases and not evidence of a reader failure. Split producer input validation, DWG writer section emission, DWG reader extraction, and DXF re-emission into distinct cells. Before scoring any reader, prove the tested DWG has the AcDs section and payload association. |
| ACadSharp [public version matrix](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) | The mutable project matrix explicitly separates DxfReader/DxfWriter/DwgReader/DwgWriter: it declares AC1021 DWG read but not write, while AC1024/AC1027/AC1032 are declared for both. The table is a project capability declaration, not class-level runtime coverage. | Preserve direction × version × class as separate dimensions in the peer matrix. Use the declaration to select a candidate route only; before comparison pin release/commit and report per-handle emitted/retained/refused outcomes. Do not infer that a broad “supported version” includes AcDs or semantic modeler support. |
| FreeCAD current [Draft DXF documentation](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md) and [DWG wrapper](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py) | DWG open composes an external converter with `importDXF.open`; the converter selection can differ by preference and can fall through to another executable. The stock DXF route is a downstream consumer, so converter success cannot establish its entity or 3D interpretation. | Keep the already-defined native Linux/Windows checks staged: force and identify this `dwg2dxf`, capture subprocess outcome and DXF artifact independently, then test selected importer behavior and per-source disposition. Preserve the existing 2D-consumer compatibility lane. Do not use FreeCAD's stock route as an ACIS semantic gate. |

### Implementation-ready probe order

These are gates within existing PAR-07/S8 work, not new scheduled suites or
external blockers:

1. **Fast local regressions remain first.** Continue generated in-memory
   parser/writer controls and focused CTests for each changed slice. Do not add
   ezdxf as a required build or CI dependency, and do not run full suites for
   this research-derived profile.
2. **Optional scratch generator (only when a pinned ezdxf runtime is available).**
   Generate temporary DXF controls for AC1024/SAT and AC1027 or AC1032/SAB.
   Start with an asymmetric closed polyhedron; if inexpensive, add a disconnected
   second component and an open shell to exercise multiple-lump and shell
   dispositions. Reopen only to inspect source version, SAT/SAB storage,
   ACDSDATA presence, entity-to-record association, and bytes/hash. Write them
   under a temporary directory and delete only those exact generated files after
   preserving the receipt; never commit generated drawings or their binary
   payloads.
3. **DXF carrier check.** Exercise libdxfrw's existing ASCII/Binary DXF reader
   and writer separately from DWG. Assert exact supported carrier bytes and
   owner/key association, no silent empty entity, and a following-record
   sentinel. If the route does not preserve a field, require an explicit
   incomplete/refusal result rather than a positive semantic claim.
4. **DWG writer check.** When testing DXF→DWG, inspect the produced DWG before
   attempting readback. It must contain an identifiable AcDs section and the
   expected record-to-owner/key association; absent section is writer loss and
   makes the reader cell `NOT_EXERCISED`.
5. **DWG reader check.** Use a source whose AcDs section is independently
   established before invoking the local reader. Score extraction, record
   boundaries, owner/key join, and DXF carrier reconstruction separately. A
   reader round-trip through the same writer is not an independent positive.
6. **Semantic check.** Compare the bounded polyhedral profile against analytic
   expectations (component count, closed/open topology, bounds, and volume)
   using a separately admitted kernel/reader and independent expected values.
   ezdxf self-readback and `mesh_from_body()` are carrier/selected-structure
   checks only; neither closes curved-surface, arbitrary ACIS, or solid-validity
   claims.
7. **Native consumer check.** Run FreeCAD only at the existing composed Linux
   and Windows qualification gates. Capture the converter artifact before
   importer projection, and count it solely for the selected FreeCAD backend.
   If only the stock 2D importer is available, classify ACIS semantics as
   `UNSUPPORTED_CONSUMER`/`NOT_EXERCISED`, not a codec pass or failure.

artifact was downloaded or executed. Current plan totals remain 144 findings /
78 top-level subplans. Native FreeCAD Linux/Windows qualification, independent
ACIS/ACDS semantic evidence, and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain
separate; all six J items stay `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` and non-promoting.

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 R24 TABLESTYLE data-flag domain validation (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.101.4 defines the R24 TABLESTYLE cell-style data flag as a
bit-short with exactly two values: `0` means no data and `1` means data is
present. The R2018+ parser previously converted every nonzero value to `true`,
so an out-of-domain value could be accepted as a populated style when the
remaining bytes happened to form a complete style record.

`readTableStyleCellStyle` now refuses negative or greater-than-one decoded
values before mutating the style projection. This matches the existing
TABLECONTENT cell-style flag validation and keeps the parser strict at the
shared ODA-defined semantic boundary.

The generated AC1032 TABLESTYLE frame contains a complete no-data style and a
complete populated-style payload (background/content CMCs, content format,
text-style handle, margins and border count). Controls assert that `0` and `1`
parse, while `2` and `65535` fail even though the rest of their payload is
otherwise well-formed. Invalid parses also prove stale typed state is cleared.
No persistent DWG/DXF fixture was added.

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 TABLESTYLE property-override and content-layout flag domains (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA v5.4.1 §§20.4.101.3–.4 enumerate the property-override bits used by
content-format and cell-style records (highest documented bit `0x40000`), and
the content-layout bits Flow `0x1`, Stacked horizontal `0x2`, and Stacked
vertical `0x4`. The reader previously retained unknown high bits in both
property-override fields and the content-layout field.

Both property-override fields now reject bits outside `0x7ffff`; content
layout rejects bits outside `0x7`. Generated populated AC1032 frames cover
zero and the complete documented property-override mask independently at

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 TABLESTYLE border flag and active value domains (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.101.4 defines six border-edge bits and six border property
override bits. It identifies border types as Single `1` and Double `2`, and
the invisibility property as `1` or `0`. The parser previously accepted
undocumented bits in both masks. It also accepted out-of-domain type and
visibility values when those corresponding properties were active.

the border-type override bit is active, only `1` or `2` is accepted; when the
invisibility override bit is active, only `0` or `1` is accepted. Unoverridden
type/visibility storage remains untouched by this semantic gate. Generated
AC1032 full-object frames check zero/known/full masks, invalid next/high bits,
both border types, and visibility values 0/1/2. Invalid cases prove the
TABLESTYLE projection is cleared atomically. No persistent drawing fixture
was added.

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 MLINESTYLE CMC reserved-index retention (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA v5.4.1 §2.11 specifies the R2004+ CMC BS index as reserved zero. The
MLINESTYLE reader previously rejected an object as soon as that field was
nonzero, while other CMC-bearing records retain anomalous source metadata and
refuse lossy rewrites. MLINESTYLE now appends raw-index fields for its fill
color and each parallel-line element, captures them only on R2004+ inputs (the
older field remains a real color index), and keeps the rest of the object
readable. Both DWG encoding and the typed-only DXF writer preflight these
fields and refuse any nonzero source index before writing body, string, or
handle bytes; neither silently normalizes the source to zero. The typed DXF
gate is exercised with a synthetic DWG-origin receipt because DXF-origin
exports intentionally replay their validated raw MLINESTYLE carrier instead
of serializing edited typed projections.

Generated AC1024 controls mutate the fill and a middle element's two-bit BS
encoding from reserved zero to 256 without shifting the body. They assert the
raw values survive parsing, angles and later element linetype indexes remain
aligned, copy/assignment/reset preserve lifecycle behavior, DWG rewrite is
refused atomically, and typed-only DXF export refuses fill/element anomalies
without replacing a pre-existing destination. No persistent DWG/DXF fixture
was added.

## Deeper/broader research — open-source implementation and ACIS semantic-route refresh (2026-10-22; research only)

### Decision

Extend the existing PAR-07/S8 peer-routing and PAR-14 artifact-pinning rules
with a newly surfaced direct DWG/DXF implementation (`acadrust`), its
application/kernel family (OpenCADStudio / OpenCADKernel), and a separate
experimental SAT/SAB-to-OpenCascade path (`cq-acis`). Also pin the current
ACadSharp release identity and keep `dxflib` in the narrow 2D-DXF consumer
category. This is route-selection and test-design research only: peer claims,
peer issue reports, and peer self-roundtrips do not establish a local defect,
interoperability pass, or support claim. Findings/subplans remain 144/78.

### Fast, implementation-ready use of the new research

1. **No survey-driven code change.** The new peer reports and feature tables do
   not establish any local issue. Audit the local parser/writer, existing
   selectors, and plan inventory first; add a finding only after a local,
   reproducible gap is shown.
2. **Select exactly one external route for a precise question.** Prefer
   `acadrust` or ACadSharp for version-pinned DWG object/record comparison;
   use ezdxf for DXF tag/carrier inspection; use `cq-acis` (or another pinned
   geometry evaluator) only for a bounded semantic shape question; use
   dxflib only for narrow 2D callback behavior. `OpenCADStudio` inherits its
   codec route from the pinned `opencadcodec` fork and is not a second parser
   vote.
3. **Use a compact generated case matrix only when uncovered:** one unknown
   class plus adjacent known entity sentinel; one table-record XDATA/named
   color case; one AC1032 custom-object failure/opaque-retention case; one
   malformed count/length boundary; one solid-only block with an INSERT; and
   for ACIS one closed asymmetric polyhedron with a disconnected/open-shell
   negative control. Match each to an existing local fast selector before
   writing a new test. Keep all new DWG/DXF controls locally generated from
   scratch or use already-admitted repository samples; never import a peer's
   regression drawing into the tree.
4. **For each external probe, bind identity and stages:** exact package/tag or
   commit, build flags, OS/architecture, command/options, input/output hashes,
   source handle+owner, output handle, status (preserved/typed/opaque/refused/
   omitted), payload hash where relevant, and independent-reopen diagnostics.
   For geometry, additionally capture topology, bounds, volume, and exact
   refusal/unsupported result. An entity count or same-codec readback is not
   sufficient.
5. **Keep test cadence focused.** Run the local fast selector and focused
   CTest first. A peer executable, native CAD app, full suite, or external
   corpus is an optional composed checkpoint, not a per-slice dependency.
   Update this plan/receipt after each completed slice and keep the six J gates
   `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL` unless their separately stated evidence is actually
   produced; peer research cannot promote them.

<a id="implementation-progress-par134-dimstyle-dimclr-cmc-ac1021-correction-2026-10-22"></a>

## Research correction and implementation progress — PAR-134 DIMSTYLE DIMCLRD/E/T CMC (2026-10-22; existing AC1021 sample plus generated fast tests; uncommitted)

### Corrected format finding

The prior `DIMCLRD/E/T = BS` conclusion was based on a misread of the local
ODA extract and a self-generated wire test that encoded and decoded the same
incorrect assumption. Rechecking the authoritative ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.68 table
shows all three fields are `CMC` under “Common”; §20.4.68 separately places
`DIMLWD` and `DIMLWE` as `BS`. This matches the source layout in the existing
AC1021 sample. The official [Open Design Specification](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf)
is authoritative for the DWG layout.

Independent source comparison supports, but does not replace, that ODA
finding: LibreDWG master defines `FIELD_BSd` as a signed cast of `BS` in
[`dec_macros.h`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dec_macros.h),
while its read trace of the repository-owned
`tests/samples/AC1021/architectural_-_annotation_scaling_and_multileaders.dwg`
decodes `DIMCLRD/E/T` as CMC fields (index, packed method/RGB value, and flags)
and reaches `DIMLWD/E` at the expected following positions. That corroborates
the wire interpretation on this exact producer-authored file; it does not
qualify general semantic support. The previous offset at the beginning of
`DIMLWD` was 1006 bits; with the CMC widths corrected, the parser reaches the
field at bit 988 and parses both lineweights and the final flag.

Autodesk's [DIMSTYLE DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-F2FAD36F-0CE3-4943-9DAD-A9BCD2AE81DA.htm)
lists groups 176–178 for these colors but no class-specific truecolor or
color-book companion. The generic [entity color groups](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3610039E-27D1-4E23-B6D3-7E60B22BB5BD.htm)
describe 420/430 as AcDbEntity/class-level data; that is not proof that those
groups are legal for DIMSTYLE. Therefore the implementation retains richer
DWG CMC detail and refuses DXF downgrade when RGB/name/book information would
be lost; it does not invent a 420/430 mapping.

### Completed implementation slice

- Replaced the three modern bounded BS reads with bounded CMC reads and
  retained method, RGB, flags, reserved index, color name, and book name in
  `DRW_Dimstyle::dimColorCmc`.
- Encoded the fields as CMC for supported DWG versions, including their
  optional strings in the R2007+ detached string stream. Copy, assignment,
  move, and reset carry/clear the new metadata.
- Added `canWriteDxfDimensionColors()` and a DIMSTYLE writer preflight. Plain
  ACI/ByBlock/ByLayer projections remain writable; RGB/name/book or unknown
  methods fail before the DIMSTYLE record is emitted.
- Replaced the misleading generated BS test with a CMC walker covering
  ACI/name/book, RGB, ByBlock, ByLayer, following-field alignment, metadata
  copy/assignment, and conservative DXF downgrade admission. The existing
  DIMTFILLCLR CMC wire test now also reads the neighboring fields as CMC.
- No persistent DWG/DXF fixture was added; only the repository's existing
  AC1021 sample was used. No public virtual was added. `DRW_Dimstyle` layout
  grew, so downstream binaries must rebuild.


## Implementation progress — PAR-03/PAR-04 associative reserved-code refusal and PAR-134 CMC caller audit (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

### Evidence and correction

The exact-source CMC caller audit covered every `readCmColorWithinBounds`
consumer in `src/drw_objects.cpp`. Modern consumers retain RGB when present,
method, flags, reserved index, and optional names/book names, or (for
`DRW_VisualStyle`) retain the raw CMC prefix separately together with those
decoded strings. The DIMSTYLE scalar-only path is limited to its

mistaken for the preferred API in future work. This audit found no grounded
remaining live scalar-only CMC parse gap. It does not close class-specific DXF
projection or producer-semantic questions such as HATCH C5.

The associative-value audit found the classifier used broad numeric ranges
that accepted group codes 80–89 as Int32, 101 as String, and 106–109 as
Point3d. Autodesk's primary [Group Code Value Types Reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-2553CF98-44F6-4828-82DD-FE3BC7448113.htm)
enumerates the neighboring ranges but does not assign these codes. The
existing LibreDWG mapping at local commit
`6d6a33987a1a97095b069c799c3d8a793320f812` was used as a peer cross-check, not
as authority for DWG payload widths. No DWG variant width or field order was
changed; this correction narrows invalid-code acceptance only.

## Deeper/broader research — CADMPEG 0.6.3 exact crate profile and semantic-probe refinement (2026-10-22; research only)

### Finding and evidence ceiling

The previous v0.6.3 release-freshness note correctly recorded that the GitHub
release announcement alone did not establish ACIS profile coverage. The
versioned [`cadmpeg-codec-sat` 0.6.3 crate documentation](https://docs.rs/crate/cadmpeg-codec-sat/0.6.3)
is now available and published 2026-10-21. It describes a read-only bare-stream
reader for text SAT/SMT, ASM BinaryFile4/8, and ACIS BinaryFile 217/218; it
transfers supported records through `cadmpeg-asm` into `cadmpeg-ir`. It also
exposes a geometry-transfer result and structured losses. This resolves the
earlier *documentation freshness* gap for the crate version; it does not bind
the crate source/dependency graph to the separately distributed CADMPEG CLI
archive recorded in the 2026-10-21 receipt, nor does it establish runtime
behavior on any local payload.

The v0.6.3 docs sharpen the admission boundary. ACIS majors 217/218 are the
documented verified bands. Other ACIS bands may be decoded using a substituted
217/218 grammar only as `Admission::Unverified`, with a dialect-unverified
loss; a successful parse/body count on that path is not a qualified semantic
result. A future probe must record the admission state and every loss, not just
`geometry_transferred` or entity totals. The documented binary framer starts
from the declared record-stream boundary and reference width and stops at the
declared solved-record limit or stream terminator; this is useful design
context for parser comparison but is not proof that every producer profile is
covered.

The codec is a distinct optional reader/neutral-model implementation from
libdxfrw, ACadRust, and `cq-acis`; its own crate and `cadmpeg-asm` are one
implementation lineage, not multiple peer votes. It does not read DWG/DXF
containers, locate AcDs sections, associate a carrier with a drawing handle,
write SAT/SAB, or provide an independently qualified general geometry kernel.
The crate docs show bodies/faces and loss reporting but do not by themselves
certify closed/manifold B-rep validity or native CAD acceptance. `cq-acis`
remains a separate parser/OCCT shape-conversion route, but prior research
records format-note/corpus overlap with CADMPEG and shared OCCT lineage with
FreeCAD; do not count project names as independent evidence votes.

<a id="implementation-progress-ac1024-tablestyle-standard-identities-2026-10-22"></a>

## Implementation progress — AC1024 TABLESTYLE standard repeated identities (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

### Evidence and change

The existing AC1024 `architectural_example-imperial.dwg` sample failed while
parsing TABLESTYLE object handle 135. Trace-level identity capture showed a
repeated style ID of `1` and raw style-class value `0`. The parser required
every repeated style ID to be at least 101 and allowed only style classes 1
or 2, so it rejected a standard R24 style and counted the object as failed.

ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.101.2 documents standard R24 style IDs 1–4 and custom IDs
starting at 101. ACadSharp's `DwgObjectReader.readTableStyle()` independently
reads the repeated style index, cell-style fields, ID, class, and name without
requiring IDs ≥101. The reader now accepts standard IDs 1–4 or custom IDs
≥101. It also retains class value 0 as raw input alongside 1/2 without
assigning it data/label meaning; the ODA profile still documents only 1/2, so
class-zero semantics remain unresolved. Added generated AC1024 identity
vectors cover the observed class zero and reject IDs 5/100 and invalid class
values. No DWG/DXF fixture, public API, class layout, or support claim was
added or changed.

<a id="implementation-progress-par03-par04-associative-action-1005-1009-fail-closed-correction-2026-10-22"></a>

## Implementation progress — PAR-03/PAR-04 associative-action 1005–1009 fail-closed correction (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The prior generic `resbufValueKind()` range treated every code from 1005
through 1009 as a string. Its AC1024 generated action vector consequently
called code 1005 an `XDataHandleString` and treated it as successfully decoded.
That was stronger than the evidence: ODA DWG Specification v5.4.1 §28 says
1005 is an entity-handle reference in EED, while targeted text extraction found
no `AcDbAssocAction`, `ACDBASSOCACTION`, or `AcDbEvalVariant` value-layout
entry. The EED rule does not establish how an associative-action variant is
represented across its data, string, and handle streams.

The generic value-kind helper now classifies 1005 as `Handle`. A separate
`associativeActionValueKind()` consumer gate rejects 1005–1009 as `Invalid`
until that class-specific wire grammar is authoritative. The action parser
therefore fails the typed frame instead of interpreting an unproven value as
a string or guessing a handle-stream rule. Existing bounded failed-frame
handling retains the exact object as opaque with typed payload validation
false; strict complete conversion still refuses that record. Generated
controls move 1005 out of the action parser's supported values, require
consumer-specific refusal for 1005–1009, and preserve the existing body
sentinel checks for supported categories. No persistent DWG/DXF fixture,
public layout, dependency, or support claim changed.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c modeler DXF text direct append (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

`DRW_ModelerGeometry::parseCode` previously copied the `getString()` result a
second time into a payload-sized `decodedText` string, then copied that string
into `m_rawBytes`. It now makes a bounded first pass to count the output bytes
after `^ ` decoding, checks the aggregate payload limit and vector index limits,
reserves the final payload/chunk capacities, and charges the exact retained
logical length before appending. The decode pass writes each byte directly to
`m_rawBytes`; it preserves the legacy rule that a later group 1 inserts one LF
between payload chunks, while group 3 remains concatenated. Chunk offsets
continue to exclude the separator and identify only their source payload.
Rollback retains the old raw-byte size if chunk publication unexpectedly
throws. This removes one payload-sized temporary and also makes the chunk
append atomic with respect to the retained-byte lease.

concatenation, the group-1 separator, exact chunk offsets/lengths, and exact

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c remaining group-310 parser paths (2026-10-22; generated ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

### Evidence and change

The exact-source audit found six remaining binary-payload parsers that copied
the current DXF hex token and/or decoded into a staging vector before
publishing it. OLE2FRAME and OLEFRAME now borrow the current record's
`dxfReader::getStringView()` and append decoded bytes directly to
`m_payloadBytes`. Their 128-MiB guard and `m_payloadTooLarge` disposition are
preserved: malformed token spelling or allocation failure does not mark a
valid-size payload oversized. EXTRUDEDSURFACE and REVOLVEDSURFACE decode into
`dxfBinaryData` only after even-length and declared-remaining-size checks.

declared remaining size, and decodes directly into that vector.

allocation is already moved into the final variant, so a mutable public
variant accessor would add API surface without eliminating a payload copy.
That route now borrows the record token and checks the aggregate variant-data
limit before decoding; the resulting vector is moved into the owning variant.
`decodeHexBytes` now accepts `std::string_view` and writes transactionally into
that destination vector. The now-unused staged `appendBytesChecked` helper was
removed. No borrowed view escapes `parseCode`.

Generated in-memory controls exercise all six parsers with 300-byte payloads
split at the binary-DXF 127-byte chunk boundary, in both ASCII and Binary DXF.
They assert the exact reconstructed payload, LOFTEDSURFACE variant ordering,
typed-surface finalization, and a following-record sentinel. Separate
declared-size overrun cases for EXTRUDEDSURFACE, REVOLVEDSURFACE, and
SWEPTSURFACE confirm rejection without discarding an already accepted prefix.

## Implementation progress — 7S.2c MTEXT borrowed chunk view (2026-10-22; generated ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

### Evidence and change

`DRW_MText::parseCode` previously copied the current group-1/group-3 reader
token into a temporary `std::string` and then appended it to `text`. MTEXT
continuations can span many physical groups, so this repeated temporary owner
was unnecessary: `dxfReader::getStringView()` is valid until the next
`readRec()`, and this parser consumes each chunk synchronously. The parser now
borrows that view and appends its bytes directly to the final MTEXT owner. The
existing group-1 UTF-8 conversion, group-3 deferred assembly, decode-work
charge, retained-byte reservation/rollback, and public data layout are
unchanged. No view escapes the parse call.

The generated control writes three heap-sized chunks (groups 3, 3, and 1) and
a following-record sentinel through both ASCII and Binary DXF writers. It
checks exact concatenation after the reader has replaced its current record,
sentinel alignment, retained-owner accounting after reader destruction, and
release after owner destruction. The same focused selector also executes the
existing MTEXT exact-budget and one-byte-under refusal control. No persistent
fixture was added.

### Evidence and change

The exact-source DXF ownership audit found that entity and table-entry typed
XDATA copied `dxfReader::strData` into a temporary return string, then moved
that temporary into the final `DRW_Variant`. Added internal `takeString()` to
transfer raw current-token storage directly into that owner. For semantic
codes 1000, 1001, and 1003 it calls the same version-aware decoder as
`getString()` before clearing the reader token; codes 1002, 1004, and 1005 keep
their existing raw/control/binary/handle spelling. Only the entity and
table-entry XDATA routes that immediately retain the string use this method.
No borrowed view escapes the record and no public installed header or model
layout changes.

owners. They assert token transfer (the reader's current string view is empty
after parse), exact retained value contents after reader teardown, exact
byte-budget usage, copy/reset lease lifetime, and one-byte-under rejection.

the canonical hex spelling. The focused test creates no persistent fixture.

having bit 1 set when the six margin values are present. The same specification
uses `Flags & 0x01` for bit 1 in §20.4.99. The parser previously treated every
nonzero signed bit-short as presence, so a complete invalid flag value could

flag as exactly `0` (no break data) or `1` (break data present). The parser
previously interpreted any nonzero signed value as true, allowing malformed
flags to enter the optional break-data branch.

well-formed break-data payload so refusal is due to the Boolean domain, not
truncation. The negatives verify the cell content remains available and the

ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.97 documents TABLE cell-state bits `0x01` through `0x40`:

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 AC1021/AC1024 TABLE CadValue kGeneral flag (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

`kGeneral` (type 512), and the common data-type field is omitted when that
flag is set. Type 512 carries a bounded `BL` byte count and raw byte array.

treated format flags `0x01`/`0x02` alike as an empty value. A generated

not decoded as text. Tests assert flags, inferred type, data size, exact raw
bytes, binary variant, unit/text fields, complete semantics, and the
AC1024 following-table-tail bit boundary. The frame builders synthesize all
bytes in memory; no DWG/DXF fixture was added. A focused
`libdxfrw_table_cell_general_value_format_flag` CTest was registered.

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 AC1021/AC1024 FIELD CadValue `kGeneral` format flag (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1 §20.4.99 defines the `CadValue` used by
FIELD as a common value: for R2007+, flag `0x01` selects `kGeneral` (type 512),
the ordinary data-type BL is absent, and the body contains a BL byte count
followed by that many bytes. The same rule is already exercised in the TABLE
routes. FIELD's shared reader instead treated any low two format bits as an
empty value while still requiring the data-type BL; its writer likewise
emitted the type and suppressed the payload for flag `0x01`.

omit the data-type field when bit `0x01` is set. The empty-value handling now
tests only bit `0x02`, matching the existing TABLE implementation. Unflagged
type 512 retains its explicit data-type field. The writer rejects the
contradictory combination of `kGeneral` flag and a non-512 type, and checks a
provided `m_dataSize` against the retained raw byte count. Updated the stale
writer comment to state that undocumented buffer layouts fail closed.

Added `libdxfrw_field_cadvalue_general_format_flag` and generated AC1021 and
AC1024 frames. Controls cover root and child general values, exact raw bytes,
format/value strings on the detached string stream, explicit type 512 when the

FIELD bounded-child-count regression remains in the focused cohort. No

## Research and regression update — FIELD `kGeneral` DXF projection remains fail-closed (2026-10-22)

The official [Autodesk FIELD DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-51B921F2-16CA-4948-AC75-196198DD1796.htm)
describes group 90 as the FIELD value data type and groups 92/310 as binary
buffer size/data. It does not enumerate the FIELD value-type numbers or state
that DWG `kGeneral` type 512 / R2007+ flag `0x01` maps to that DXF binary
representation. DWG ODA §20.4.99 therefore cannot by itself authorize a DXF
grammar change.

The current FIELD DXF writer rejects type 512 because no class-specific DXF
mapping is implemented, and the parser's required-payload check rejects types
outside its defined DXF projection. A read-only check of the sibling LibreDWG
source at revision `6d6a33987a1a97095b069c799c3d8a793320f812` found its DXF
FIELD type-512 branch unimplemented/commented; this peer state is corroborative
only and is not authority for the format. No external drawing was obtained or
converted in this pass.

Added a generated `kGeneral` writer-preflight negative control to the existing
FIELD CTest owner. ASCII and Binary export both refuse before emitting any
bytes. This locks down the current safe boundary without asserting that DXF
cannot represent the value. The focused `libdxfrw_acad_field_writer_candidate`
