## Research update — FIELD format flag `0x02` semantics remain unqualified (2026-10-22)

Read the local ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1 §20.4.99. Its complete
flag statement is `Flags & 0x01 => type is kGeneral`; the subsequent common
data-type field is omitted when bit 1 in Flags is set. The section does not
define bit `0x02` as an empty value or identify any other meaning. Autodesk's
public FIELD DXF reference lists the serialized long, double, object-ID, and
binary forms, but is silent on the DWG format flag. LibreDWG's shared
`TABLE_value_fields` implementation suppresses payload for low bits in
`format_flags`, while its macro and NEWS entry do not name bit `0x02` or
establish that it means “empty.” The bundled LibreCAD implementation is a
downstream code lineage and is not independent normative evidence.

Disposition: preserve the already documented `0x01` general-value behavior,
but keep `0x02` semantically unqualified. Existing local controls that encode
and parse the bit establish only internal agreement; they do not verify the
wire meaning. Do not advertise empty-value support or use it to promote a
support claim. A future behavior change requires a direct authoritative
specification, a traceable producer-authored DWG with independent byte/semantic
interpretation, or equivalent independent evidence. No code, fixture,
dependency, or support claim changed.

Self-unblock: keep unrelated implementation slices moving; route any current
`0x02`-dependent assertion as characterization only until the meaning is
resolved. In particular, keep type-0 unknown values refused by writers even
when `0x02` suppresses a payload, since the unknown semantic kind is itself
unsupported.

Sources: ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.99 (local authoritative PDF); [Autodesk FIELD DXF
reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-51B921F2-16CA-4948-AC75-196198DD1796.htm);
[LibreDWG shared `TABLE_value_fields` source](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/665b8dde6c018825f8098309f8983e6ef39451b5/src/dwg_spec_shared.h);
[LibreDWG NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS).

PlotStyleName object used when `$CEPSNTYPE` is 3. The existing generic HEADER
parser retained the variable in `vars`, but the writer omitted it; a non-null

retains a well-formed explicit null handle (`0`) and emits it as group 390 in
ASCII and Binary DXF. Absent remains absent. Non-null references remain
available in the parsed header but fail the writer preflight until the
referenced plot-style object graph can be closed and remapped. Present values
are refused for targets before AC1015, the first version whose current HEADER
writer path emits this family; this is a conservative no-loss gate, not a
claim about the variable's exact introduction release.

and bare aliases, malformed API-provided values, and invalid handle lexemes
cannot be written. `clearDxfPlotStyleId()` explicitly clears the retained
field and malformed-source state so a caller can repair it. Malformed source
groups follow the repository's tolerant-read / fail-closed-rewrite pattern;
invalid group-390 handle lexemes are rejected by the DXF reader itself. This
adds public `DRW_Header` methods and a private state bit; downstream consumers
must rebuild, and no binary ABI compatibility is claimed.

## Implementation progress — PAR-27/7L.4 `$CEPSNID` default-plot-style graph closure and handle remap (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The preceding HEADER slice retained null `$CEPSNID` handles but still refused
all non-null values. The current adapter already has a closed, narrowly
supported PlotStyleName default graph: one NOD `ACAD_PLOTSTYLENAME` edge to a
`DICTIONARYWDFLT`, with the validated default `ACDBPLACEHOLDER` child. The
graph-aware export path now accepts `$CEPSNID` when and only when it refers to
that exact default placeholder and `$CEPSNTYPE` is 3. This also requires a
32-bit handle representable by the current remapper. A HEADER reference itself
now requests named-object-root validation, so a missing graph cannot bypass
the graph preflight.

During `writeHeader`, the verified source handle must occur in the staged
placeholder set, then is remapped through the same writer map as the emitted
OBJECTS graph. The low-level HEADER codec retains and serializes syntactically
valid non-null handles; graph closure remains the adapter's responsibility.
Mismatched targets, absent/incomplete/ambiguous graphs, malformed values,
wrong `$CEPSNTYPE`, and pre-AC1015 output fail before destination publication.
This does not add arbitrary named PlotStyleName objects or expand the one
default-placeholder profile.

The existing dictionary-default adapter regression now generates a source
HEADER reference to its default placeholder in ASCII and Binary DXF. It checks
the imported handle, successful graph validation, target remap and strict
readback identity; it mutates the reference to another handle and the type to
2 in separate negative cases, verifies sentinel destination preservation, and
then retries with the corrected source graph on the same adapter. The
standalone HEADER selector separately verifies direct syntax retention and
that an unclosed adapter reference remains refused.

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 FIELD unqualified format flags fail closed (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.99 documents format bit `0x01` as the `kGeneral` selector,
but does not define bit `0x02` as an empty-value flag or assign semantics to
other bits. The previous implementation skipped the typed payload whenever
`0x02` was present, then treated the remaining FIELD record as complete. That
was an unsupported semantic inference and could misalign the bounded FIELD
body if the bit has a different meaning.

A fresh peer-source cross-check did not resolve the bit. ACadSharp's current
`CadValue.IsEmpty` property treats bit `0x01` as empty, while its DWG reader
reads the data-type BL before using that property to gate the payload;
LibreDWG's current `TABLE_value_fields` reads the data-type BL and skips the
payload when either low bit is set. Those behaviors conflict with ODA's
documented `0x01` kGeneral/type framing and with each other on `0x02`. They
are implementation observations, not independent producer semantics, so
they do not justify choosing either peer's interpretation. See [ACadSharp
CadValue](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/CadValue.cs),
[ACadSharp DWG object reader](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/IO/DWG/DwgStreamReaders/DwgObjectReader.Objects.cs),
and [LibreDWG shared spec](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dwg_spec_shared.h).

For AC1021/AC1024, `readCadValue()` now interprets only the documented `0x01`
bit. Any other format bit returns `Unsupported` before parsing a guessed
type/payload layout; the FIELD reader keeps an incomplete bounded shell and
does not publish typed child values. The typed writer rejects any modern
format mask outside `0x01` before emitting body, string, or handle bits. The
documented `0x01` kGeneral path remains unchanged. Generated controls patch a
valid in-memory FIELD frame to flags `0x02`, `0x03`, and `0x04`, and assert
incomplete read state plus writer refusal for both modern versions. Existing
kGeneral positive controls and kUnknown incomplete/refusal controls are also
retained.

from Apple's vendor mapping published by Unicode; its 2005 update maps the
Mac OS 8.5+ `0xDB` byte to U+20AC, and byte `0xF0` to Apple's U+F8FF corporate
character. Cross-project comparison adds a useful boundary: LibreDWG exposes

Macintosh, while noting that modern `$DWGCODEPAGE` meaning is unclear.

or qualify these Macintosh labels. Therefore the local exact mapping is
corrected while the exact-source support gate remains closed; producer
recognition and native application support are not asserted. Sources:

<a id="implementation-progress-par-05-exact-iso-8859-15-decoder-2026-10-22-generated-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>

### Implementation progress — PAR-05 exact ISO-8859-15 decoder (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Added the exact ISO/IEC 8859-15:1999 Latin-9 mapping from the Unicode
Consortium's [ISO8859/8859-15.TXT table](https://www.unicode.org/Public/MAPPINGS/ISO8859/8859-15.TXT).
The primary table retains identity mappings for C1 controls and defines the
Latin-9 replacements, including Euro at 0xA4, S/Z carons, OE ligatures, and
capital Y diaeresis. All 128 production upper-byte entries match Python's
strict `iso8859_15` codec.

ExactNamed resolves compact and hyphenated labels, case-insensitively, to the
distinct `Iso8859_15` decoder/profile. Compatible behavior remains unchanged:
both `ISO8859-15` and `ISO-8859-15` select Windows-1252. Generated ASCII/Binary
DXF imports record the exact consumed profile; clean exact ISO-8859-15 remains
`UnsupportedProfile`. No persistent fixture or support claim was added.

Generated tests independently transcribe all 128 positions, check exact
decode and inverse encoding for all four spelling/case variants, validate
resolver metadata, distinguish the Euro byte from the prior Windows-1252
fallback, and verify source-profile partitioning and strict-admission refusal

<a id="deeper-broader-open-source-peer-defect-crosswalk-2026-10-22-research-only"></a>

## Deeper/broader research — peer defect crosswalk and implementation readiness (2026-10-22; research and local source audit)

### Result

This pass compared recent LibreDWG, ACadSharp, and ezdxf primary project
sources against the actual current libdxfrw writer/parser paths and tests. It
found one concrete local DXF HATCH writer mismatch, two semantic object-model
gaps that are already partially protected by raw-net preservation, and several
peer-only reports that should remain qualification signals rather than local
defects. The earlier generated R2018 section-map extent control and patterned
associative HATCH round-trip from the previous crosswalk now have their own
implementation records above; neither remains an open test-gap item.

Peer reports are version- and route-specific. LibreDWG `master` NEWS is mutable
and labels 0.14.1 (2026-07-25) beta; ACadSharp issues describe specific commits,
packages, or AutoCAD builds. They supply adversarial cases and comparison
leads, not proof that libdxfrw has the same defect. The local ODA v5.4.1 PDF
remains the authority for DWG byte layouts; the Autodesk DXF reference is the
authority used here for documented DXF groups. No peer binary, customer file,
or native CAD application was run.

### Cross-repository findings joined to local code

| Peer evidence | Local source/test crosswalk | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| LibreDWG [0.14.1 NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) records recent HATCH path-state/rational-spline fixes, MATERIAL color/mapper and TABLESTYLE row true-color DXF import fixes, and an off-by-one that dropped the final SAT block on DXF export. | HATCH already has generated ASCII/Binary path/reference, rational-weight, final SAT-chunk, and patterned multi-path owners. MATERIAL's `DRW_Material::parseCode` intentionally models only name/description while the DXF raw-net preserves the complete source groups; its DWG parser likewise keeps an opaque body tail. TABLESTYLE's DXF parser reads top-level scalars while nested cell/row styles remain raw-net-only. | Do not duplicate the already-covered HATCH/SAT work. Add explicit typed MATERIAL visual-field and TABLESTYLE nested-row subplans below. Opaque preservation supports pass-through, not typed semantic-consumer support. NEWS is a regression-source signal, not a compatibility certification. |
| ACadSharp [#1253](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1253) reports strict AutoCAD rejection at CLASSES, HATCH, and DIMSTYLE-table boundaries; the report's own follow-up supplies a peer-repository AC1032 HATCH sample and clarifies that group 47 is needed for paths marked derived (group 92 value 7), even when pixel size is zero. | `DRW_Class::write` emits the documented 0/1/2/3/90/91/280/281 groups and has no 92/93 route. The AC1024 DIMSTYLE-table writer emits the count and per-row 340 references, and generated table-census controls assert that versioned output; other versions deliberately retain their distinct legacy header shape. `dxfRW::writeHatch` emits group 47 only for a nonzero `pixelSize`, even though `DRW_HatchLoop::type & 4` is the derived-boundary bit and the DWG reader/writer already derives pixel-size presence from that bit. Existing `testHatchPixelPresence` currently expects no group 47 for a zero-sized type-7 path. | **Confirmed local HATCH writer gap:** emit group 47 with value zero if any boundary path has the derived bit, and retain nonzero-pixel output for other paths. Update the generated ASCII/Binary regression so the type-7 zero case expects group 47 and the type-3 zero case remains absent. Do not change CLASSES. Keep the DIMSTYLE handling version-specific; do not generalize AC1024's 71/count + 340/handles rule to other revisions without a producer/spec trace. Use the ACadSharp case as a lead, not as the norm for every version. |
| ACadSharp [#1281](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1281) reports process-ending recursive DXF handling for long runs of comments, XDATA application blocks, and WIPEOUT/IMAGE clip-count groups. | The local DXF tokenizer skips comments iteratively; generated hardening controls exercise 20,000 comments, 20,000 XDATA application/value pairs, and bounded/rejected clip-count runs while checking later-record alignment and callback atomicity. | Already addressed by the local architecture and stress tests. Reuse those tests; no duplicate recursion patch or fixture. The peer issue remains evidence for preserving these checks when refactoring parsers. |
| ACadSharp [#1234](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1234) reports SummaryInfo string loss/corruption at a 16,382/16,383-character boundary in that peer's AC1032 writer. | libdxfrw has no typed SummaryInfo property-writing model; SummaryInfo is a named opaque DWG section, not the ACadSharp `WriteTextUnicode` route. | Scope review only. Do not add a speculative public property model or copy the peer's numeric limit. If a future writer starts materializing this section, derive bounds from ODA and test exact/over boundaries plus an independent reader; otherwise preserve/refuse opaque bytes explicitly. |
| ACadSharp [#1261](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1261) reports an R2009 GEODATA Civil-tail omission in its DWG writer; [#1297](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1297) reports an AC1032 MTEXT frame-only rejection with a confounding missing-VisualStyle path; [#1299](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1299) reports malformed spline output on an attached but uncommitted customer DWG. | Local generated GEODATA version/tail controls, MTEXT flags 0/16/17 across AC1027/AC1032, and spline wire tests cover parser/writer invariants, but they do not reproduce those external producer/consumer paths. The #1297 author explicitly could not isolate flag 16 as the cause; the issue also notes omitted VisualStyle objects. | Keep these as separate native/external qualification candidates. Do not infer a local defect, download/commit customer files, or promote support from local same-library re-encoding. A future local regression must be generated from scratch or sourced from an already-admitted repository fixture and must isolate the responsible field/graph. |
| ACadSharp [#1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) reports silent 3DSOLID/REGION omission on an older DXF writer route and describes solid-only blocks becoming empty. ezdxf [ACIS documentation](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) says its parser supports only a limited set of ACIS entities; unsupported entities become `NONE_ENTITY`, and it explicitly cannot load/re-export arbitrary ACIS data. | libdxfrw already has modeler-carrier export/reporting and block-graph ownership gates; the modeler census checks source handles, carrier bytes/associations, and block ownership rather than entity count alone. | Reuse PAR-07/S8 carrier/disposition gates. Treat ezdxf as a limited SAT/SAB syntax/face-mesh observer, never a general semantic ACIS oracle. Keep opaque carrier preservation, kernel semantics, and native CAD geometry as separate evidence levels. |

### New implementation subplans

1. **RPP-3 — HATCH derived-path group-47 correction (P1, local code mismatch).**
   In `dxfRW::writeHatch`, compute derived presence from the complete
   `looplist` (`loop != nullptr && (loop->type & 4) != 0`) and emit group 47
   before group 98 whenever any path is derived, including a zero-valued
   `pixelSize`. Keep existing nonzero group-47 output for non-derived paths;
   do not make group 47 unconditional. Update the existing generated presence
   test in `tests/hatch_reference_tests.cpp` for ASCII and Binary DXF: type 3,
   pixel 0 => absent; type 7, pixel 0 => present with value 0; type 3 or 7,
   pixel 0.125 => present; explicit input group 47 equal to zero remains
   readable. Assert group order, following LINE alignment, and parsed model
   state. This is a locally testable fix and does not require an external file.
2. **RPP-4 — MATERIAL semantic color/mapper fields (P1, confirmed model gap; documented unambiguous DXF slices 4a–4l implemented below; procedural table remains open).**
   Start with Autodesk's [MATERIAL DXF field reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-E540C5BB-E166-44FA-B36C-5C739878B272.htm)
   and the applicable ODA DWG object chapter before changing binary parsing.
   Slice the work by field group: (a) ambient/diffuse method and factor
   (groups 70/40 and 71/41; implemented below), (b) unsigned CMC values
   (groups 90/91, including the full UINT32 boundary; implemented below),
   (c) diffuse-map blend/source/file/projection/tiling/auto-transform
   (groups 42/72/3/73/74/75; implemented below), and (d) the 16-value mapper
   transform (group 43; implemented below), and (e) specular gloss/color
   controls (groups 44/76/45/92; implemented below), (f) specular map
   controls/mapper transform (groups 46/77/4/78/79/170/47; implemented
   below), (g) reflection-map controls/mapper transform
   (groups 48/171/6/172/173/174/49; implemented below), (h) opacity fields/map
   (groups 140/141/175/7/176/177/178/142; implemented below), (i) bump map
   (groups 143/179/8/270/271/272/144; implemented below), and (j) refraction
   index/map (groups 145/146/273/9/274/275/276/147; implemented below).
   Slices 4k/4l cover the unambiguous physical, Normal Map, and uniquely
   mapped tail fields. The generic procedural-property sequence
   (300/291/271/469/301/292/62/420/430) remains raw-preserved rather than
   typed; these codes are reused and need a bounded context-state parser plus
   producer-backed vectors before promotion. The Autodesk table lists the
   value group codes but does not define the complete per-property
   name/type/value cardinality or how optional color components associate.
   A source audit of LibreDWG's pinned `in_dxf.c` revision
   [`e0a152d`](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/e0a152d728cd5b794dc9361a65417fa12d920509/src/in_dxf.c#L9598-L9605)
   explicitly says its procedural-texture variants are not written by its
   DXF writer and remain unhandled by its generic MATERIAL import; the
   handler returns unrecognized pairs to the generic object path. This
   corroborates a peer support gap but supplies no wire semantics, so it is
   not a typed implementation oracle. Keep this local sequence raw until a
   product-authored, versioned witness or another normative schema resolves
   the full sequence. Group 90/149 self-illumination
   remains untyped because Autodesk's DXF reference and LibreDWG's DWG schema
   disagree; resolve with an authoritative, version-specific DXF witness
   before mapping. Extend the typed
   model only with explicit defaults/presence where needed, preserving
   unknown DXF groups and DWG tail bits. DXF typed-field slices use generated
   ASCII/Binary controls; any AC1021/AC1024/AC1032 DWG body mapping is a
   separate spec- and sample-traced task, not implied by DXF coverage. Add
   copy/reset/budget and transactional writer refusal controls before any
   callback/API claims. A typed MATERIAL parse is not a rendering or
   ACIS-kernel qualification.
3. **RPP-5 — TABLESTYLE nested DXF row/cell styles (P1/P2; bounded row projection, TABLECONTENT column/row/cell style-ID capture/domain checks, typed CELLSTYLEMAP retention, same-version replay, name-only DXF-origin edits, and AC1021 object-graph writing implemented; cross-object style-ID resolution, complete custom-cell authoring, production handoff, and DWG version-upconvert semantics remain open).**
   Generated slices 5a–5c cover legacy DWG row colors/roles/text-style handles,
   R24 malformed nested-count refusal with a following-object sentinel, and
   ASCII/Binary raw-net order/replay/refusal. Slice 5d now parses the
   documented repeated DXF row-style groups into `DRW_TableStyle` while
   retaining their exact ordered raw carrier, with generated ASCII/Binary
   projection and incomplete-row/following-object controls. Preserve raw order
   for every record and keep malformed nested state out of the typed callback.
   RPP-5e verifies that duplicate group-430 color names and group-431 book
   names fail closed, and typed row copy/reset. RPP-5f adds exact-budget and
   one-byte-under retained-string controls and proves that a typed row edit
   which diverges from the raw DXF-origin carrier refuses export without
   replacing the destination. RPP-5i–5k extend the DXF-origin raw-carrier route
   with bounded edits to existing core and documented row slots while keeping
   group order and unchanged source spellings; omitted border slots stay
   absent, and edits to them refuse rather than being discarded. The DWG-origin
   route continues to use its separate bounded typed writer. Complete custom
   cell-style authoring is not inferred from the repeated row groups and needs
   a separately evidenced schema; unsupported nested content remains raw.
   Public
   model/parser state grows C++ object layouts; compatibility checks are
   source-level only, and downstream consumers must rebuild. Keep
   R2010+ DWG write capability distinct: current generated local writer tests
   gate TABLESTYLE DWG writing at AC1021, so do not claim the peer's TABLESTYLE
   upconvert is already supported here. RPP-5g validates the official
   FlowDirection and title/header suppression domains (0/1), duplicate core
   scalar-field occurrences, and finite table margins; malformed typed state
   is withheld while the complete raw carrier remains available. The
   generated ASCII/Binary canary covers duplicate and out-of-domain
   FlowDirection values plus invalid header suppression, followed by a valid
   sentinel. RPP-5h adds a duplicate pre-body class-version group-280 case and
   confirms that the following valid sentinel is still projected. RPP-5i
   merges edits to existing top-level scalar slots; RPP-5j/k extend that
   merge to documented row values with bounded domains and optional-border
   presence rules. Existing raw slots are edited in place; absent slots are
   never synthesized. Groups 90/91 remain equality-only because the current
   typed writer does not support nonzero data/unit values. Group-3 description
   editing remains gated on source-encoding evidence. No separate custom-cell
   style schema is inferred from the repeated row sequence. See Autodesk's
   [TABLESTYLE group-code table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-0DBCA057-9F6C-4DEB-A66F-8A9B3C62FB1A.htm).
4. **RPP-6 — Strict DXF grammar canary (P2, local audit complete; native
   acceptance remains external).** The generated exact writer-wire census now
   covers CLASSES at AC1014/AC1015/AC1018/AC1024 in ASCII and Binary, including
   the writer's AC1015→AC1018 group-91 boundary. The existing DIMSTYLE census covers its
   version-specific table header and row subclasses across AC1018/AC1021/AC1024
   in both encodings; both have focused CTests. For CLASSES, compare against
   Autodesk's [official group list](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-42E19B4F-61E1-4795-93E7-C8769CE2D7C0.htm);
   for HATCH/DIMSTYLE, use their official per-object references. Keep the
   optional AutoCAD `accoreconsole` import as a composed native qualification,
   not a routine test prerequisite. A permissive reader or same-library
   readback is not a strict ordered-writer oracle.

### Fast execution order and gates

1. RPP-3 is implemented and its ASCII/Binary HATCH presence matrix plus
   patterned multi-path sentinel passed; rerun only those owners if its code
   changes.
2. RPP-4 slices 4a–4l have generated ASCII/Binary parser/writer and raw-replay
   coverage. The generic procedural-property sequence and disputed 90/149
   self-illumination mapping remain explicitly untyped until producer-backed
   evidence resolves context and wire meaning. RPP-5's bounded typed parser
   now exists; continue hardening that local lane without waiting on external
   gates. Each new slice should retain raw fallback and a following-record
   sentinel.
3. RPP-5 slices 5a–5k provide legacy DWG controls, bounded DXF row projection,
   raw-net preservation, malformed/duplicate metadata callback refusal,
   copy/reset, retained-text budget controls, top-level field domains, and
   bounded typed edits to existing core and row slots. Optional border-slot
   presence is preserved; edits to absent slots fail closed. Continue with
   documented row fields only where their domains and presence are evidenced.
   Groups 90/91 remain unchanged; group-3 editing and any complete custom
   cell-style authoring need separate encoding/schema evidence. Keep generated
   ASCII/Binary tests and add no persistent fixtures.
   RPP-6 CLASSES and DIMSTYLE writer-wire canaries are implemented; keep
   optional AutoCAD/native import outside the routine fast loop.
3. Run full CTest, sanitizers, external binaries, or native CAD only at a
   composed checkpoint or when a changed path requires it. Do not add
   downloaded peer/customer drawings; use in-memory generators or existing
   repository samples under the established fixture policy.
4. No support claim is promoted by this research. J256, J260, J268, J284,
   J293, and J295 remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; FreeCAD Linux/Windows native
   qualification and independent ACIS/ACDS semantic evidence remain
   `NOT_RUN` and separate from local generated carrier tests.

The research update above identifies one concrete HATCH writer mismatch and
two bounded semantic implementation tracks; peer-only failures remain
advisory/qualification inputs. Its evidence does not promote support claims.
The HATCH mismatch has since been corrected and verified. RPP-4's documented
unambiguous fields through 4l now have local generated coverage; generic
procedural fields and the 90/149 conflict remain raw/untyped. RPP-5d/e project
documented nested TABLESTYLE DXF row fields into typed state while retaining
raw source groups, fail closed for incomplete and duplicate CMC metadata,
and preserve copy/reset behavior. RPP-5f verifies the row-string budget edge
and refuses a write when supported typed row values diverge from their raw
carrier. RPP-5g validates bounded core-field domains/multiplicity and retains
malformed wire data raw; RPP-5h rejects duplicate pre-body class-version
group-280 values from the typed projection. RPP-5i–5k merge bounded edits to
existing TABLESTYLE core/row slots while preserving raw group order and
optional border presence. Group-3 editing, nonzero data/unit values, and full
typed custom-cell-style authoring remain separate follow-ups. RPP-6's CLASSES and DIMSTYLE wire
canaries pass in focused ASCII/Binary tests.

## Implementation progress — RPP-4b MATERIAL unsigned color values (2026-10-22; generated ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

`DRW_Material` now retains ambient/diffuse group-90/91 color values as
`uint32_t`, with separate presence flags. The DXF reader enables unsigned
32-bit parsing only while processing a MATERIAL record and only for groups
90/91; signed I32 parsing elsewhere remains unchanged. Raw MATERIAL capture
stores those values without sign loss, and raw replay emits four-byte bit
patterns in Binary DXF or unsigned decimal spelling in ASCII DXF. The typed
writer follows the same encoding rule. This supports same-encoding replay and
ASCII↔Binary projection through the existing MATERIAL graph gate; map fields,
mapper fields, and DWG body semantics remain untyped.

Generated ASCII/Binary controls exercise UINT32_MAX and 0x80000001, parsed
typed values and raw-net pairing, copy/reset behavior, explicit-default and
explicit-zero typed writer output, invalid-factor refusal/retry, same-encoding
graph replay, and both cross-encoding directions. The source drawing has a
following LINE sentinel, so MATERIAL group alignment is checked beyond the
object.

## Deeper/broader research update — peer route and consumer evidence boundaries (2026-10-22)

This pass cross-checked current primary project documentation and source for
LibreDWG, ACadSharp, ezdxf, GDAL/OGR, FreeCAD, and LibreCAD 3. It refines the
existing PAR-07/S8 peer-comparison and PAR-14 evidence-admission rules; it
does not add a new implementation finding or promote a support claim.

### What the broader cross-check changes

| Route | Current primary-source boundary | How this plan may use it |
|---|---|---|
| [LibreDWG NEWS](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/NEWS) / [0.14 release](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/releases/tag/0.14) | Its mutable `master` NEWS describes both peer-side hardening and targeted HATCH, MATERIAL, TABLESTYLE, and final-SAT-block fixes. The 0.14 release notes limit DWG writing to AC1018 as supported, describe later targets as experimental, and state AC1021 encoding falls back to AC1024. | Select adversarial and regression dimensions; compare only the pinned release/source and exact direction/version. A NEWS item or peer self-round-trip is not evidence of a local defect or independent semantic correctness. Keep existing RPP-3/RPP-4/RPP-5 scoped to local source crosswalks. |
| [ACadSharp](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp) / [issue #1195](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/issues/1195) | The project publishes separate DXF/DWG read/write version claims. Issue #1195 reports silent omission of 3DSOLID/REGION on a named 3.4.9 DXF-writer route; the report is not evidence about current v3.8.0 behavior. | Use versioned issues as candidate route tests only. Before adding a local regression, reproduce a field/object-graph mismatch against current local source with a locally generated control or an already-admitted sample. |
| [ezdxf ACIS API](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/acis.html) | The ACIS API supports a limited set of known structures and polyhedral-body generation/extraction; it explicitly has no ACIS kernel and cannot load/re-export arbitrary ACIS. Its bounded export supports SAT on R2000–R2010 and SAB on R2013/R2018. | Use it optionally to generate a bounded carrier or inspect known planar-polyhedron cases. Do not count its own export/readback as independent semantics, and do not use it as a general B-rep or curved-surface oracle. Keep any expected geometry independent of the exporter. |
| [GDAL DXF/OGR driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | The reader is a geometry projection: it tessellates several curves, may inline/merge blocks, and does not preserve all styling. ACIS-bearing entities are skipped by default; optional `DXF_3D_EXTENSIBLE_MODE` exposes raw ASM data and a 12-value transform only for AC1027+—not OGR solids. Binary DXF reading is explicitly distinct from DWG. | Use only as an independently implemented observer for the specific projected primitive, topology, block, or raw-carrier field being checked. Preserve source handles and compare only records the route actually emits; never grade a skipped/raw ASM record as semantic solid support. |
| [GDAL CAD / libopencad driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/cad.html) | The documented DWG route is read-only and projects a small entity set (POINT, LINE, CIRCLE, ARC, 3DFACE) into OGR geometries. | It may be a narrow additional read observer for those named entity families. It cannot qualify DWG writing, full object-graph preservation, ACIS/ACDS, or unlisted entities. |
| [FreeCAD DWG helper](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py), [DXF importer docs](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/Draft_DXF.md), and [DWG docs](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD-documentation/blob/main/wiki/FreeCAD_and_DWG_Import.md) | Its DWG helper composes an external converter with the selected DXF importer. Its current DXF documentation says ACIS solid blobs are not read by the standard importer; its DWG documentation states that the converter route inherits DXF-importer limits. | Keep native Linux/Windows qualification split into converter invocation/output and FreeCAD importer outcomes. FreeCAD can qualify the exact non-ACIS consumer cases exercised, but it is not an ACIS semantic oracle; record the importer implementation/version and count unsupported/lost records explicitly. |
| [LibreCAD 3 DWG-support note](https://github.com/LibreCAD/LibreCAD_3/blob/master/docs/dwg-support.md) | Its current DWG-support note describes DWG reading as experimental and off by default; DWG writing is not implemented or planned absent separate promoted write claims and independent acceptance. | Keep `lc3_compat_check` as a source-contract regression only. It does not imply binary ABI, UI, general 3D, or DWG-write compatibility. Preserve existing 2D callback behavior while 3D typed data remains an opt-in experimental consumer path. |

The main practical change is evidentiary, not architectural: an external
application can only answer the question its route reaches. A successful DWG
conversion followed by a 2D DXF importer is not a solid-kernel test; a GDAL
geometry result is not an object-graph round-trip; a raw ASM/SAB match is not
shape equivalence. This distinction must remain visible in per-family,
per-version, per-direction results and in any future README/support table.

### Implementation-readiness refinements to existing subplans

1. **RPP-4c MATERIAL map controls (implemented below; DXF only).** The
   diffuse-map blend/source/file/projection/tiling/auto-transform groups
   (42, 72, 3, 73, 74, 75) are now typed. Generated ASCII and Binary DXF
   objects use deliberately different diffuse and normal-map values for
   repeated codes; tests assert the diffuse typed fields, retained raw-net
   ordering, exact same-encoding replay, cross-encoding replay, copy/reset/
   presence, bounded filename parsing, and a following LINE sentinel. The
   `464` Luminance delimiter starts the later block; group `465` Normal Map
   Strength is a fallback delimiter if luminance is omitted. Do not use `271`
   alone because that group also occurs earlier as Bump Map Tiling. Keep the
   Normal Map duplicate groups opaque until a separately specified typed
   model exists. Do not infer DWG MATERIAL body semantics from this DXF
   implementation.
2. **RPP-4d mapper transforms / remaining MATERIAL fields (group 43 implemented below).**
   The diffuse map transform is a 16-value row-major field, parsed only before
   the Normal Map boundary. Generated tests cover a non-identity matrix,
   default/reset presence, non-finite writer refusal, short/long count refusal,
   raw preservation of the later Normal Map matrix, and sentinel alignment.
   Before typing additional physical or DWG-only fields, cite the applicable
   Autodesk DXF reference or ODA DWG chapter and capture a version-matched
   source trace. Unknown fields continue through the ordered raw-net path; no
   partial typed writer may silently discard them.
3. **RPP-4e specular controls (implemented below; DXF only).** Type gloss
   factor (44), specular color method (76), factor (45), and unsigned CMC value
   (92), preserving group-92's unsigned 32-bit value only within MATERIAL
   parsing/capture/replay. Generated ASCII/Binary tests cover distinct values,
   UINT32 high-bit cross-encoding replay, exact group order, defaults/copy/reset,
   invalid method/factor/non-finite gloss/ASCII overflow refusal before
   callback, typed-writer round-trip, transactional refusal/retry, and the
   following LINE sentinel. Continue to leave the later map families opaque.
4. **RPP-4f specular map (implemented below; DXF only).** Type blend/source/
   filename/projection/tiling/auto-transform and the 16-real row-major mapper
   transform (groups 46/77/4/78/79/170/47), with a separate retained filename,
   defaults, presence, and matrix-completeness state. Generated ASCII/Binary
   tests cover enum/flag domains, 15-/17-value matrices, copy/reset, bounded
   filename replacement at exact and one-byte-under retained-owner caps,
   exact raw ordering and replay, cross-encoding output, typed-writer field
   order, transactional invalid-data refusal, and a following LINE sentinel.
   Do not infer any DWG MATERIAL body support from this DXF model.
5. **RPP-4g reflection map (implemented below; DXF only).** Type blend/source/
   filename/projection/tiling/auto-transform and the 16-real row-major mapper
   transform (groups 48/171/6/172/173/174/49), using its own retained filename
   lease and matrix-completeness state. The generated ASCII/Binary vector must
   assert reflection values remain distinct from diffuse/specular fields,
   enforce the 464/465 Normal Map delimiter, preserve raw order and both
   encoding projections, and reject source/projection/tiling/flag domains,
   non-finite values, and short/long matrices before callback. Cover typed
   writer order and transactional refusal/retry, copy/reset defaults, exact/
   one-byte-under filename ownership, and a following LINE sentinel. No DWG
   body or rendering claim follows from this DXF slice.
6. **RPP-4h opacity fields/map (implemented below; DXF only).** Type opacity
   percent and opacity-map blend (groups 140/141), source/file/projection/
   tiling/auto-transform (175/7/176/177/178), and the 16-real row-major mapper
   transform (142). Autodesk documents defaults and the map enum domains but
   does not state numeric bounds for the two opacity reals; validate finiteness
   and do not infer a unit interval from the field names. Generated ASCII/
   Binary tests must assert exact order, normal-map delimiter isolation, raw
   replay, cross-encoding projection, callback refusal for invalid enums,
   non-finite values and short/long matrices, copy/reset defaults, bounded
   filename replacement at exact/one-byte-under caps, typed writer order and
   transactional retry, plus the following LINE sentinel.
7. **RPP-4i bump map (implemented below; DXF only).** Type blend/source/file/
   projection/tiling/auto-transform and the 16-real row-major mapper transform
   (groups 143/179/8/270/271/272/144). Since 270/271/272 are reused later for
   luminance mode, Normal Map method, and global-illumination mode, process
   them as bump fields only before the 464/465 delimiter and preserve later
   occurrences in raw order. Generated ASCII/Binary tests must assert the
   context split and following LINE alignment, reject invalid enum/flag
   domains, non-finite blend/matrix values and short/long matrix cardinality,
   cover source zero, exact/raw/cross-encoding replay, copy/reset defaults,
   bounded group-8 filename replacement at exact/one-byte-under caps, typed
   writer order, and transactional refusal/retry.
8. **RPP-4j refraction index/map (implemented below; DXF only).** Type refraction
   index and map blend/source/file/projection/tiling/auto-transform plus the
   16-real row-major mapper matrix (groups 145/146/273/9/274/275/276/147).
   Keep group 273 typed only before the 464/465 boundary because it is reused
   later as Final Gather Mode. Generated ASCII/Binary tests assert the full
   order, raw group-273 context split, same-/cross-encoding replay, following
   LINE alignment, copy/reset/defaults, invalid domains, non-finite ASCII
   values, short/long matrices, source-zero writer output, transactional
   refusal/retry, and exact/one-byte-under group-9 filename budgeting. This
   adds DXF field coverage only; it does not qualify rendering or DWG bodies.
9. **RPP-4k later MATERIAL physical controls and Normal Map (implemented below; DXF only).** Use the current
   [Autodesk MATERIAL table](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-E540C5BB-E166-44FA-B36D-5C739878B272.htm)
   and [LibreDWG MATERIAL object schema](https://www.gnu.org/software/libredwg/manual/html_node/OBJECTS.html)
   groups 460–463, 290, 464/270/271/465, and the Normal Map groups 42/72/3/
   73/74/75/43 by context, data type, and actual local handling. These
   unambiguous DXF fields now have explicit presence/defaults, finite or
   documented-domain validation, tests across the 464/465 boundary, raw
   ordering, copy/reset, retained-text budgets, and writer preflight. Group
   300 marks entry into the generic procedural table; later reused group 271
   and group 90 are not routed back into Normal Map method or ambient color.
   No DWG MATERIAL body changed.
10. **RPP-4l remaining MATERIAL tail audit (implemented below; DXF only).** Resolve and test
   groups 293, 272/273, 300/291/271/469/301/292/62/420/430, and
   270/148/468/93/94 by context and value type. Keep the generic procedural
   by context and value type. The parser preserves the generic procedural
   sequence in its ordered raw net; its complete typed writer remains out of
   scope until the full name/type/value sequence can be retained and replayed
   losslessly. Autodesk and LibreDWG disagree on the self-illumination DXF
   group (90 vs 149); keep both mappings untyped until an authoritative,
   version-specific witness resolves the conflict. Generated ASCII/Binary
   controls cover the procedural start/end, reused-code boundaries, raw order,
   malformed bool/real domains, and following-record alignment; typed writer
   checks cover only uniquely mapped fields. No DWG mapping without the ODA
   object schema and a version-matched trace.
11. **RPP-5 TABLESTYLE (bounded row projection and raw/typed loss-avoidance verified; cell-style authoring remains open).**
   The generated legacy DWG round-trip distinguishes
   data/title/header row fields and verifies separate true-color/CMC text and
   fill plus text-style handles. Existing R24 vectors cover cell-style type
   domains, border overrides, and invalid flags. A generated AC1032 object-map
   control declares one repeated cell style but emits none; it proves no
   `addTableStyle` callback for the malformed record, one object-level failure,
   successful publication of the valid next-byte-range sentinel, and a
   successful OBJECTS pass. The documented supported DXF row-style fields now
   have a bounded typed projection while the full ordered raw carrier remains
   preserved; unsupported nested cell-style fields remain raw. Generated
   ASCII/Binary tests check the raw-net fields and following style sentinel;
   malformed nested handle references or divergent typed row values refuse
   export without replacing the destination. Typed-edit merging, a complete
   cell-style model/writer, and DWG version-upconvert evidence remain open.
   Keep DWG version-upconvert claims separate from DXF nested-field coverage.
12. **Peer artifact admission.** Before any optional peer run, record immutable
   commit/package identity, direction, format version, route, command, output
   hash, and whether its parser/writer shares lineage with the producer. Run
   only the narrow comparative probe needed for an open question; do not add a
   peer executable or sample to routine CI or commit external/customer
   drawings. Use generated-from-scratch controls for committed regression
   coverage.
13. **Validation cadence and unblocking.** Keep ordinary implementation slices
   on focused fast tests plus the changed-target `-Werror` build and
   `lc3_compat_check`. Use full suites/sanitizers only at composed checkpoints
   or when a changed risk surface warrants them. After each slice, update this
   plan and its receipt, identify the next unblocked local slice, and report
   the committed-slice progress when a commit is actually made. Research in
   this pass changes no execution order and resolves none of the external
   gates.

vector in both ASCII and Binary DXF. It exercises AC1014 and AC1015 on the
legacy side of the group-91 boundary, then AC1018 and AC1024 on the R2004+
side. The values cover every documented CLASSES group emitted by this writer:
record name, C++ class name, application name, proxy capabilities, optional

The DXF-origin TABLESTYLE raw-carrier merge now overlays typed edits to
existing documented repeated row fields: group 170 alignment, groups 62/63
text/fill colors, group 283 background-enabled state, groups 274–279 border
lineweights, groups 284–289 border visibility, and groups 64–69 border colors.
The earlier group-140 text-height edit remains supported. Each field uses the
existing typed writer's domain: alignment 0–65535, colors 0–255, lineweight
signed 16-bit, Boolean fields 0/1, and text height finite/nonnegative.

unmodeled values must continue to match the retained raw projection.

The parser's row contract requires the core text-style/height/alignment/color/
background fields, but border families are optional. The merge therefore
updates only present raw slots, retains omitted border slots without
synthesizing them, and refuses a typed change to an omitted slot rather than
silently dropping the edit. A generated sparse-row control removes row 0's
group 279, edits its present text-height slot, checks the exact resulting group

<a id="implementation-progress-rpp5l-tablestyle-group-90-91-enum-projection-and-bounded-edit-2026-10-22-generated-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>

## Implementation progress — RPP-5l TABLESTYLE group-90/91 enum projection and bounded edit (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

Research resolved the DXF-facing enum domain more fully while exposing a
versioned DWG serialization gap. Autodesk's DXF reference identifies TABLESTYLE
groups 90 and 91 as cell data type and cell unit type, respectively. Its
`TableStyle.SetDataType` API explicitly takes `DataType` and `UnitType` for
selected row types; the published enums list data types 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32,
64, 128, 256, and 512, and unit types 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 (Currency), 32
(Percentage), and 65536 (AngleNotTransformed). ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.99 (PDF pp.
232–233) describes the value payload and lists only the five common unit types;
§20.4.101.1 maps TABLESTYLE's R2007+ group 90/91 fields to ACAD_TABLE's data
and unit types. Autodesk's API contract is direct evidence for the semantic
enum names, but does not alone prove that every API enum value is accepted in
every DWG serialization version. That discrepancy remains explicit rather
than being hidden behind a support claim.

The typed DXF parser and bounded raw-carrier edit path now recognize the
documented enum values for R2007+ records. Only an existing paired group-90 /
group-91 slot can be edited; group order and untouched ASCII source spellings
remain intact, sparse pairs do not get synthesized, and invalid values remain
raw-only instead of producing a typed TABLESTYLE projection. The typed DXF
writer emits the same scalar codes. DWG reading can retain documented API
enum codes as opaque integers, but DWG writing continues to restrict units to
ODA's explicit 0/1/2/4/8 set until an independent AutoCAD/ODA-produced drawing
demonstrates the additional values in the relevant DWG versions. `m_valueFormatString`
has row-format semantics in the AutoCAD API and an ODA DWG group-1 mapping, but
Autodesk's public TABLESTYLE DXF reference does not document group 1; its TABLE
entity instead documents a separate group-4 standard/title/header row format
string. No TABLESTYLE DXF group-1 mapping is inferred from that nearby field,
so a nonempty typed format string remains fail-closed on the typed writer and
unrecognized source text stays on the raw-carrier path. Cell-value
interpretation/conversion and complete custom cell-style authoring are not
added by this slice.

Generated ASCII/Binary controls cover valid common data types and API-only
unit codes, typed readback, exact raw order, unchanged lexemes, paired-slot
editing, invalid data/unit values, sparse absent-pair preservation and
destination-preserving refusal, plus a following TABLESTYLE sentinel. The
generated DWG local roundtrip exercises only ODA-listed unit values. No
persistent fixture or external DWG/DXF sample was added.

Evidence references:

- [Autodesk TABLESTYLE DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-0DBCA057-9F6C-4DEB-A66F-8A9B3C62FB1A.htm) identifies the group-90/91 meanings and row repetition.
- [Autodesk TableStyle.SetDataType (2018)](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2018/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OREFNET-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_TableStyle_SetDataType_Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_DataType_Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_UnitType_Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_R.html) binds the row-style API to `DataType` and `UnitType`.
- [Autodesk DataType enum](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_DataType.html) and [UnitType enum](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_UnitType.html) list the API numeric codes.
- [Autodesk TableStyle.Format](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/OARX-ManagedRefGuide/files/OARX-ManagedRefGuide-Autodesk_AutoCAD_DatabaseServices_TableStyle_Format_RowType.html) confirms row-format semantics; [Autodesk TABLE DXF](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D8CCD2F0-18A3-42BB-A64D-539114A07DA0.htm) separately documents group 4 for standard/title/header row format. This does not establish group 1 as a TABLESTYLE DXF field.
- [ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf), §§20.4.99 and 20.4.101.1, pp. 232–233, is the DWG layout authority and lists the narrower serialized unit set.

## Implementation progress — RPP-5m CELLSTYLEMAP typed adapter retention and graph refusal (2026-10-22; generated fast slice, uncommitted)

The DWG object reader already parsed `AcDbCellStyleMap` and invoked the
non-pure `DRW_Interface::addCellStyleMap` callback, but the `dwg2dxf` adapter
did not override that callback. As a result, typed custom cell-style metadata
was discarded by the concrete conversion adapter. This slice adds a bounded
adapter-owned `DRW_CellStyleMap` store and a sticky capture-failure state.
Accounting includes the table-entry metadata, cell-style vector, each cell's
borders and associated CMC/value-format strings, subrecord ranges and their
names, plus list-node overhead. Limits are 100,000 records, 4,000,000 nested
items, and `DRW::kMaxDxfBinaryPayloadBytes` aggregate retained bytes.

The exported DXF currently has no qualified serializer for the separate
CELLSTYLEMAP object graph. Export preflight now explicitly refuses both a
failed/incomplete capture and any successfully captured map, before output
publication. This is a no-loss guard and typed retention step; it does not
claim that custom cell styles are converted or semantically supported. It
does not change the DWG parser, object dispatch, public DRW model, or the
existing raw unsupported-object report.

Generated coverage builds a map with nested cell, border, CMC, format-string,
and subrecord-name payloads; checks exact retained record/item/byte counts;
admits the exact aggregate-byte boundary; rejects byte, record, and item
overages without partial retention; and asserts the explicit export refusal
diagnostic plus absence of a published DXF for both populated and failed
captures. The test creates no persistent DWG/DXF fixture.

<a id="implementation-progress-rpp-5n-cellstylemap-versioned-identity-domains-2026-10-22-generated-dwg-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>

## Implementation progress — RPP-5n CELLSTYLEMAP versioned identity domains (2026-10-22; generated DWG fast slice, uncommitted)

ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.102 identifies the built-in CELLSTYLEMAP style IDs as 1
(title), 2 (header), and 3 (data), with ID 4 introduced in R24; custom style
IDs start at 101. The parser previously accepted any signed ID and class and
published them as typed cell-style identity. It now rejects ID 0, the reserved
gap 5–100, and all negative IDs; IDs 1–3 remain valid from AC1021, ID 4 is
accepted only from AC1024, and IDs 101+ remain available for custom styles.
ODA defines class 1=data and 2=label. Class 0 remains an opaque compatibility
value, following the existing R24 TABLESTYLE repeated-style read path; values
below 0 or above 2 are refused without assigning class-0 semantics.

On any invalid identity, the existing parser failure path invalidates the
bounded object buffer and resets the entire `DRW_CellStyleMap`, including
previously-held cell styles and subrecord ranges. No unsupported class number
was added to object dispatch; generated vectors invoke the typed object parser
directly and separately identify their synthetic common-object envelope.

Generated frames exercise AC1021/AC1024/AC1027/AC1032, built-in and custom
IDs, the AC1021-to-AC1024 ID-4 boundary, the reserved gap, negative IDs,
classes 0/1/2 and invalid class values, style names, and atomic failure/reset.
The vectors create no persistent DWG/DXF fixture.

Evidence:

- ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.102, PDF p. 246, specifies the built-in IDs, R24 addition,
  custom-ID starting range, and class values. The local copy used is
  `/Users/dli/dev/ACadSharp/reference/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf`.

<a id="deeperbroader-research-update--lineage-aware-peer-matrix-and-fast-evidence-admission-2026-10-22"></a>

## Deeper/broader research update — lineage-aware peer matrix and fast evidence admission (2026-10-22)

This research pass expands the comparison beyond the previously tracked
LibreDWG, ACadSharp, ezdxf, GDAL/OGR, FreeCAD, and LibreCAD routes. It adds
recent Rust implementations and checks their disclosed source lineage,
capability ceilings, and the actual path used by downstream applications.
This is an evidence-admission refinement, not a new local defect report.

### Expanded peer and consumer crosswalk

| Project / route | Primary-source finding | Permitted use in this plan |
|---|---|---|
| [dwg-rs](https://github.com/DrunkOnJava/dwg-rs) | A spec-led Rust DWG reader based on ODA DWG Specification v5.4.1. Its README labels the project pre-alpha: the container/page-map/object walker is the more mature layer, entity decoding is alpha/partial, the DXF parser is not implemented, and the DWG writer has no automated external-CAD acceptance. The project discloses consulting ACadSharp algorithm comments for one LZ77 ambiguity, but says no executable LibreDWG code was used. | New candidate for a narrow, pinned cross-check of DWG container sections, page maps, object boundaries, and selected raw object metadata. Do not use it as a complete entity/graph oracle or as proof of writer acceptance. Its declared coverage and its own corpus result must be retained alongside each observation. |
| [acadrust](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust) | The crate advertises DXF/DWG R12–R2018+ read/write and SAT/SAB/B-rep features, but explicitly says entity support varies and AC1009 DWG fidelity is incomplete. Its [third-party notice](https://github.com/hakanaktt/acadrust/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) says its DWG reader/writer includes code ported and adapted from ACadSharp. Docs.rs and GitHub main also showed different package/source versions during this pass (0.6.5 published vs 0.6.6 on main), so a test must pin one exact artifact. Its round-trip tests normalize handles and discard the reader-only `raw_record` cache before comparison. | Useful as a candidate executable DXF and DWG comparator, but not an independent DWG implementation relative to ACadSharp. Treat ACIS capabilities as claimed until their parser/writer/kernel boundaries and external acceptance are independently established. A self-round-trip proves internal consistency only; report raw-record/count loss separately from normalized field equality. |
| [Open CAD Studio](https://github.com/HakanSeven12/OpenCADStudio) | The application describes itself as actively developed and uses acadrust for native DWG/DXF work. Its own discussion says a DWG constraint graph was checked through acadrust's own read/write and had not yet been opened in AutoCAD or BricsCAD; it also notes that the DXF writer omits some dependency-chain objects. | A downstream workflow target, not a separate codec oracle. Any native acceptance run must record application build, file version, and the exact import/save path; app marketing claims and same-engine round-trips do not promote format support. |
| [CADCraft DWG bridge](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/main/crates/dwg/src/lib.rs) | Its DWG module uses acadrust to convert DWG to DXF bytes before CADCraft's own DXF reader builds its model. A recent issue documents one 47.8 MB AC1032 file whose 276 MB intermediate and process peak exceeded 4.5 GB; this is one reported workload, not a general benchmark. | A route example, not an independent DWG parser. Preserve the plan's no-unbounded-intermediate / bounded-memory requirement; do not copy the materialized whole-DXF bridge for speed. Large-file performance measurement remains a composed checkpoint, not a per-slice test. |
| [uncad](https://github.com/iyulab/uncad) / [undxf](https://docs.rs/undxf/latest/undxf/) | `uncad` says DWG is read through LibreDWG FFI, DXF is read by a separate Rust `undxf` parser, and DWG/DXF writing is not offered. | `uncad` is not an independent DWG codec. `undxf` may be a narrow ASCII-DXF parse observer if a specific compatible field is in question; it does not qualify DXF writing, Binary DXF, or ACIS semantics. |
| [ixmilia/dxf-rs](https://github.com/ixmilia/dxf-rs) | A Rust DXF/DXB reader/writer with integration/interop tests that run only on Windows when ODA File Converter is installed. It is not a DWG implementation. | Optional independent DXF parser/writer for specifically covered ASCII/Binary records. Record when ODA is part of the test path; do not count it as a standalone open-source DWG witness or ACIS kernel. |
| [ezdxf 1.4.5](https://ezdxf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) | DXF-native reader/writer with third-party DXF content retention; its ACIS API supports a limited known subset and explicitly cannot load/re-export arbitrary ACIS. `odafc` delegates DWG conversion to an installed ODA File Converter and documents external-process security concerns. | Strong candidate for selected DXF record/raw-carrier comparisons. Separate the pure ezdxf route from the ODA converter route in results. Do not use it as an arbitrary ACIS semantic oracle or claim that the optional converter is open-source. |
| [GDAL/OGR DXF](https://gdal.org/en/stable/drivers/vector/dxf.html) | A GIS projection, not a drawing-model round-trip: it tessellates some curves, may inline blocks, and supports an optional raw ASM carrier plus transform for AC1027+ while not producing OGR solid geometry. Binary DXF support (GDAL 3.12+) is explicitly distinct from DWG. | Use only for supported projected geometries or exact raw-carrier observations. Count skipped entities, tessellation, inlining, and style losses; do not infer object graph or solid semantics. |

The key correction is to qualify *lineage* as well as product name. `acadrust`
and ACadSharp are not independent DWG implementations for differential
validation. Open CAD Studio and CADCraft are consumers of that route, not
additional parsers. `uncad` delegates DWG decoding to LibreDWG. Conversely,
`dwg-rs` is a distinct code lineage suitable for narrow container evidence,
but its own declared maturity precludes treating it as a semantic or writer
acceptance oracle. A matrix that only lists repository names would overcount
independent evidence.

### Additive evidence protocol for the existing PAR-07/S8 route ledger

Before a peer result can affect a local support or regression decision, record:

1. **Immutable identity:** repository URL, commit SHA or release artifact and
   checksum, package version, build options, OS/architecture, and invocation.
2. **Lineage class:** independent implementation, code-derived peer, wrapper,
   projection/exporter, or downstream consumer. Record inherited codec and
   kernel components explicitly; do not count related routes as separate votes.
3. **Exact route:** source format/version → parser → intermediate model or
   converter → writer → destination format/version → observer. State whether
   the observation is raw bytes, typed fields, graph links, projected geometry,
   visual output, or native CAD acceptance.
4. **Loss accounting:** compare object/entity counts by type, stable source
   handles where available, unresolved references, unknown/raw payload sizes,
   unsupported-record diagnostics, and geometry/topology metrics. If a peer
   test normalizes handles or drops raw caches, list those normalizations and
   retain unnormalized count/raw evidence separately.
5. **Independent acceptance:** peer self-round-trip is internal consistency.
   For DWG writer acceptance, require a disjoint parser and, before promoting a
   broad claim, a qualified native/producer route. For ACIS/ACDS semantics,
   require a kernel-backed independent geometry observer with expected
   geometry derived independently of the producer; a SAT/SAB token match,
   raw-carrier preservation, or triangle mesh from the same parser is not a
   semantic oracle.
6. **Fast implementation loop:** local generated-from-scratch adversarial
   controls and changed-target `-Werror` build remain the per-slice gate. Run a
   peer only for the open question it can resolve; use full suites, sanitizers,
   large-corpus performance checks, and native applications at composed or
   release checkpoints. No downloaded/customer DWG/DXF is committed; reuse
   only repository-admitted fixtures or locally generated controls.

### Plan disposition and next work

- Record the new peer rows and lineage/evidence fields in the existing
  PAR-07/S8 route ledger and its hash-bound receipt/support ledger. Keep source
  branches and release claims timestamped; resolve exact immutable revisions
  immediately before any comparator run.
- For current ACIS/ACDS work, no newly found repository has yet supplied
  independently authored positive DWG evidence plus an independent kernel
  result that closes the gate. Keep the ACIS/ACDS semantic qualification
  separate and `NOT_RUN`; FreeCAD's documented standard DXF path does not read
  ACIS solid blobs.
- For local DWG reader fixes, `dwg-rs` may be consulted for container-level
  cross-checks only. Continue to use the repository-mandated ODA spec as byte
  authority and real/sample-traced data for entity bodies and type dispatch.
- For local DXF preservation work, use ezdxf, GDAL, or dxf-rs only against the
  exact entity/object field families and transformations each implements.
  Retain raw-vs-semantic and projected-vs-model evidence as distinct results.
- This research adds no confirmed local defect and changes no implementation
  order. Continue the already-open local queue, including its one-slice-at-a-
  time fast validation and plan/receipt update. Native FreeCAD Linux/Windows
  qualification remains separate. J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295
  remain `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL`; none of these sources promotes them.

`processTables()` intentionally retains at most eight unknown nested-TABLE name
prefixes of at most 64 bytes, but those strings and the final
`unsupported-table-skipped` diagnostic were outside the shared DXF
retained-byte budget. The parser now reserves each name prefix before copying
it, then reserves the peak needed to join the bounded diagnostic while the
source prefixes are still live. Once the diagnostic is published, its message
charge transfers to the operation budget; if a prior failure prevents

<a id="implementation-progress-par134-tracked-ac1027-redundant-aci-reserved-index-vport-dxf-projection-2026-10-22"></a>

## Implementation progress — PAR-134 tracked AC1027 redundant ACI reserved-index VPORT DXF projection (2026-10-22; focused fast slice, uncommitted)

The repository's tracked LibreCAD `ordinary_enc_AC1027.dwg` fixture reaches
the DXF TABLES writer with a VPORT ambient CMC whose method is ACI (`0xC3`),
whose packed CMC word resolves to ACI 250, and whose leading R2004+ BS is also
250. ODA v5.4.1 §2.11 says that this CMC BS index is always zero, so the source
form is noncanonical and is not accepted for DWG re-encoding. However, the
same section defines the method/color packed BL and the current LibreDWG reader
derives the effective index from that packed word; LibreDWG's investigation
also describes the R2004+ CMC BS as vestigial. For DXF projection only, a
nonzero reserved index is therefore accepted when it exactly duplicates the
packed ACI value. A nonzero mismatch, other methods with nonzero index, unknown
flags, and invalid optional-name state remain refused. DWG encoders continue
to use the stricter zero-index metadata validator.

This is a deliberately narrow compatibility inference from the tracked
fixture plus packed CMC semantics, not a change to the DWG layout contract or
a general claim that arbitrary nonzero reserved values are valid. The relevant
sources are the [ODA specification §2.11](https://www.opendesign.com/files/guestdownloads/OpenDesign_Specification_for_.dwg_files.pdf),
[LibreDWG's current CMC reader](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/master/src/bits.c),
and [LibreDWG issue #1415's corrective analysis](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/issues/1415).

Generated ASCII/Binary DXF controls prove that matching ACI 250 metadata emits
VPORT group 63 only, a mismatched reserved index refuses atomically, and the
same nonzero index remains rejected by the DWG encoder before body/string/
handle output. The repository's existing tracked AC1027 input then passes the
exact FreeCAD-shaped `input -o output` conversion. Two tracked special-record
inputs have an earlier class/header CRC completeness discrepancy; strict CLI
tests now assert that exact first refusal diagnostic and atomic no-output
behavior. The separate `dwg2dxf_cli_contract` test still exercises the
typed-proxy refusal route directly. Pre-investigation unconditional stderr
traces were removed. Strict CLI preflight errors are now surfaced when the
caller requests resolved-owner/complete conversion, even without `-d`.

<a id="implementation-progress-rpp5-tablestyle-typed-per-edge-border-dxf-projection-2026-10-22-generated-fast-slice-uncommitted"></a>

## Implementation progress — RPP-5 TABLESTYLE typed per-edge border DXF projection (2026-10-22; generated ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

The typed `TABLESTYLE` DXF writer previously rejected a row when its six
border edges differed in lineweight, visibility, or scalar color, even though
the model retains six independently identified edge slots and the DXF schema
provides separate groups for each slot. This mapping follows Autodesk's
[TABLESTYLE group-code reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-0DBCA057-9F6C-4DEB-A66F-8A9B3C62FB1A.htm).
Its output loops also sourced every
group from `row.m_borders.front()`, so distinct values could not be emitted.
Validation now applies the existing range/representability checks to each
edge independently, and the writer serializes that edge's own values for
groups 274–279, 284–289, and 64–69.

The existing generated three-row typed TABLESTYLE export/readback now assigns
different values to every edge and row. ASCII and Binary DXF assertions check
all six values in each of the 18 edge/property group-code streams by group
code and typed readback, while retaining the
existing graph, suppression, unsupported-color atomic-refusal, and following

## Implementation progress — RPP-5aa DXF TABLE base-style-ID loss-prevention gate (2026-10-22; generated ASCII/Binary fast slice, uncommitted)

Autodesk's [TABLE (DXF) group-code reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D8CCD2F0-18A3-42BB-A64D-539114A07DA0.htm)
documents row heights, column widths, per-cell type/flags/content, and
overrides, but no numeric column/row/cell base-style-ID field. Group 91 is
documented as the row count and repeated per-cell override flag; group 92 is
the column count and, for R2007+, repeated extended cell flags. Mapping the
DWG IDs into either code would collide with published DXF meanings. Therefore
this slice does not invent a DXF encoding: `dxfRW::writeTable` now explicitly
refuses nonzero column and row IDs as it already refused nonzero cell IDs.
This closes a silent-loss path for column/row IDs while preserving atomic
destination behavior.

Generated in-memory AC1021 controls run through both ASCII and Binary export.
Each uses a valid rooted TABLESTYLE graph, sets exactly one nonzero built-in
ID at the column, row, or cell level, confirms export refusal, and verifies an
existing destination sentinel remains byte-for-byte unchanged. No DWG/DXF
fixture was added.

## Implementation progress — RPP-5ac AC1021 TABLECONTENT DWG payload and ODA TU correction (2026-10-22; uncommitted)

`DRW_TableContentObject` now has a validated, transactional AC1021 DWG
payload encoder. ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.97 defines the standalone R21 object;
AC1024+ requires the inline TABLE entity profile. The encoder preserves
column/row/cell base-style IDs directly in DWG, named columns, row heights,
cell state/tooltip, typed CadValues, FIELD/block hard pointers, per-content

reactor, and extension-dictionary links retain their handle roles and writer
occurrence tracking. Caller data/string/handle streams are replaced only
after successful staging, including when a late UTF-16 length check fails.
Publication uses a non-allocating `dwgBufferW::swap` for all stream state;
the writer buffer's defaulted destructor otherwise suppresses implicit move
operations, so assigning `std::move(buffer)` would still copy its vectors.

The initial inverse-codec test exposed a reader defect: TABLE's modern text
helper interpreted a TU character count as a byte count, and earlier
generated vectors followed that assumption. ODA §2 explicitly defines TV as
TU from R2007 and TU's BS count as UTF-16 code units. The helper now uses the
shared bounded variable-text reader; the TABLE/TABLECONTENT byte-length
overrides were removed. Modern direct-codec callers without a file codec
decode the specified UTF-16LE representation. AC1021 vectors now emit TU;
the independent AC1024 literal helper counts code units. Earlier receipts
describing byte-counted generated TABLE strings are historical and do not
establish that byte layout as valid. The earlier generated self-tests are
superseded on this specific string-length assumption by this correction.

The reader also withholds `m_semanticContentComplete` when it skips a
nonzero scalar custom-data value, any custom-data collection, a nonzero
unretained no-data style type, or an optional geometry cache whose marker
and handle role are not retained. Bounded reading continues; the typed
encoder refuses such incomplete snapshots. Authored linked-data/attribute
payloads are tested for transport, while their existing adapter graph
completeness gate remains incomplete on readback.

Generated tests cover eight CadValue kinds, trailing point bytes, general
bytes, Unicode including a supplementary character, native style IDs,
reference order/roles, field ownership, merged ranges, authored links and
attributes, and eleven skipped-data cases. Refusal controls cover version,
incomplete snapshots, reserved style IDs, missing style/field targets,
ragged grids, overlap/range errors, geometry, conflicting object-ID aliases,
undocumented units, non-finite dimensions, invalid UTF-8/NUL text, oversized
UTF-16 text, and missing/aliased streams. No persistent drawing fixture was
added.

## Implementation progress — RPP-5ai GROUP description, dictionary identity and repeat export (2026-10-22; uncommitted)

The GROUP refusal was a model/identity conflation, not a need to accept an
unresolved owner. ODA §20.4.72's full GROUP layout and example were reviewed
visually on pages 191–192. Its TV is labelled a name, but the existing
producer-paired `2007/Leader.dwg` and DXF distinguish the values: dictionary
D maps key `*A1` to GROUP 829, while its body TV and DXF group 300 contain
`Superhatch`. The group is unnamed and has five member handles. Autodesk's
published DXF schema calls 300 the description; pinned ACadSharp reader/
writer source and LibreDWG's 300 mapping corroborate the distinction. The
same paired ACadSharp AC1021 source has named dictionary entries `*A1`/`*A2`
for groups 69E/6A5 with empty descriptions and six members each. No byte
layout, type dispatch, handle role, or field order was changed from ODA.

`DRW_Group::parseDwg` now places the bounded TV in `m_description`, leaving
`name` unresolved at the low-level callback as in DXF. Native encoding writes
that description, including the empty case, rather than silently dropping it
and serializing the dictionary key in its place. Embedded NUL and malformed
UTF-8 descriptions refuse before payload bytes. The facade still requires
valid named registration and reciprocal owner/member identity. Consumers
that used the mislabelled body text as a name must instead use the owning
dictionary; the converter does so after its complete import.

`resolveGroupNames` now applies the same complete unique NOD/ACAD_GROUP
dictionary-key resolution for DWG and DXF. It retains duplicate/alias/target/
owner checks and rejects a conflicting prepopulated name. It neither infers
identity from description nor changes flags or ordered member edges. The
source drawings now get past GROUP preflight and reach the unchanged strict
DWG completeness refusal.

The new cross-encoding test exposed a second, independently actionable bug:
after the first ASCII export, borrowed LINE handles changed from 1280/1281
while GROUP member IDs still referenced the source namespace; the subsequent
encoding failed during OBJECTS emission. The adapter's existing callback-local
identity guard is now latched for GROUP graphs before their list is adopted
by the codec. Its private flag is renamed `m_preserveGraphSourceIdentities`;
the same child lifetime/budget/restoration rules and HATCH behavior remain.
No library-wide direct-writer mutation contract is changed and no pointer
journal survives the callback. Both successful and failed writes preserve
the source GROUP/member/LINE identity graph for reuse.

Coverage includes six literal TV assertions, four modern BMP/surrogate-pair
descriptions, 18 malformed-text refusals, 32 generated native dictionary/
GROUP writer scenarios across AC1015/1018/1021/1024/1027/1032, and 128-group
dictionary/callback/facade checks per version. Twelve named/empty-description
source drawings project through both ASCII and Binary DXF with exact key,
description, flags, reciprocal dictionary owner and ordered member identity.
Five deliberately corrupted public callback graphs (name, owner, duplicate
root, target and folded key) produce ten diagnosed reads, 20 atomic export
refusals across both completeness modes, and ten corrected fresh-data retries
using the same importer/exporter objects.

Those 24 positive projections explicitly use the existing bounded
`AllowPartial` read policy while retaining strict owner/reference checks.
They are **not** complete-drawing evidence. The minimal generated drawing

they never clear the read receipt, fake retention counters or waive a guard.
This precise standard-object handoff remains locally implementable.

The source-identity probe passes for the generated control and both existing

their names, and referenced same-import aliases refuse. Saved per-frame
version/codepage metadata selects the decoder, independent of the latest
mutable HEADER/read envelope. Adjacent identical profiles reuse one decoder
instead of rebuilding a multibyte converter for every object. The source

instead of the actual generated record ID. GROUP destinations are now planned
after writeHeader() returns and before dependent emission. Explicit qualified
destinations are honored; otherwise the allocator mints them. Both typed and
translated raw-group references use the same final object/GROUP namespace.

transport policy; this change does not reinterpret opaque section references.

source-object emission map or satisfy finalized identity queries. The actual

cannot also be entity/table identities; fixed/shared destinations and alias

for GROUP-bearing attempts so later callbacks cannot invalidate earlier

The generated-dictionary metadata prerequisite is locally implemented for the

common fields and numeric policies. The converter makes independent bounded
copies, leaving source records available to callbacks/finalization. The public
API consumes transferred owners even on refusal, retains previous accepted
setup on failure, and stores accepted records as const owners. Its aggregate

edge-role state cannot be laundered into accepted metadata. These are extra

exact allocator-heap accounting. Temporary output-index names/counts are also
bounded. No borrowed source-record pointer survives synchronous emission.

selection still controls the output graph. An unselected valid DWG null child

policy; this does not qualify source-image alias preservation. The GROUP
dictionary independently retains its entry order and roles while requiring
exact source-key/name membership against the emitted GROUPs. This does not
authorize arbitrary GROUP deletion/renaming under an unchanged source snapshot.

mappings. Direct/named writers keep their existing target rules; generated
source C/D metadata emits its captured numeric fields in the exercised R14+

generated path. Metadata aliases cannot relabel accepted records; metadata
and root selection freeze after the header callback. Source metadata cannot
