## Implementation progress — RPP-5aq staged OBJECTS modeled-field proof and rooted native XRECORD (2026-10-23)

Actual output inspection is implemented, not another input/handle-only check.
`dxfRW::setDxfObjectsWriteInspector` accepts an optional callback outside an
active write. The existing OBJECTS record transaction supplies a borrowed view
of its exact materialized bytes before append, together with actual version,
encoding, encoder codepage and classifier profile. The view excludes section
framing and expires on callback return. The empty default performs no decoding
or second retained section copy. Veto/throw and guarded write/setup mutations
refuse the attempt. Write APIs are now closed during finalization as well as
inspection. Future-operation policy setters retain their usual semantics.
Callback success is tentative through append, finalization and publication.

The converter's new internal helper scans physical record scopes/presence and
then reuses the production typed DXF parsers on selected borrowed record spans.
This avoids tolerant default values or ignored extra fields becoming proof.
Checks include one self/owner/subclass, dictionary flag/entry pairing, GROUP
flag domains/presence, versioned XRECORD header/application-data distinction,
application nesting, exact XDATA coordinate tuples and forbidden embedded
section framing. One secondary decoder is reused across records, not rebuilt
per GROUP. No decoded section/span inventory or borrowed source pointer escapes
the synchronous callback.

Working limits are explicit: 4,194,304 group/value pairs per pass, 1,000,000
OBJECTS records, 256 MiB input and decode work per reader, bounded token/text
leases and typed-node ceilings, plus a candidate ledger bounded by 100,000
source frames, 64 MiB visible facts and one million references. These are
distinct logical/work limits, not a process-heap promise. Source/target lookup
indexes also remain bounded by those source/fact cardinalities. The generic
public callback itself is caller code and owns its own resource policy.

Candidates compare the complete modeled dictionary entry order/spelling/roles/
targets, GROUP description/flags/member order, XRECORD ordered values and
admitted common metadata against the private import-matched models. An edge
must resolve through an actual written object/table/entity source binding,
never just a reservation, plan or equal numeric fallback. Finalization verifies
physical identities/owners and unique reference targets. Dictionary-derived
GROUP names join only after all candidate owner dictionaries pass; membership
is indexed once, avoiding dictionary-size times GROUP-count work. Source keys
omitted by the existing root projection, extra defaults and mismatched values
remain unqualified, not silently discounted. The original orphan XRECORD
control still produces only three modeled matches from four source frames.

A native checkpoint exposed that typed records can leave their legacy

## Implementation progress — RPP-5ar frozen source-text decode issues and framed TU boundaries (2026-10-23)

Raw/typed equality alone can match the same damaged text twice. The codec now
accumulates a fixed-size issue mask across primary, exact-named, recovery and
CP8 decode returns. Clean later calls do not erase earlier events. Explicit
reset starts a new frame envelope; swap/move preserves the accumulator with
the codec. Existing last-value snapshots, decoded strings and tolerant policy
remain separate. Unprofiled CP8 high-byte pass-through contributes an unsupported
profile issue to the aggregate without rewriting its historical return or
last-value snapshot. This adds no source-text owner or per-call allocation.

Standard-object raw reparsing resets that mask for each bounded frame even
when its saved version/codepage decoder is reused. Successful correlation freezes
the mask with the private canonical model. Revalidation must reproduce both;
export never refreshes the evidence from edited values. The staged-output
candidate selector excludes any frame with observed text issues. This neither
turns known malformed text into a fatal ordinary import nor admits strict
conversion: those are distinct contracts. A clean mask means no issues observed
by these decoding calls, not a complete source-schema/text certificate.

The first native controls correctly exposed a framing distinction: ordinary
nonempty TU fields emitted by the existing writer include a final NUL, and the
generic Unicode converter records that dropped code point as discarded source.
It would be incorrect to ignore every DiscardedSource bit, weaken the native
expected count, or exempt an entire record family. PDF-skill text and visual
review of ODA v5.4.1 §2/page7 confirmed the T/TU/TV length and code-unit boundary;
the established reader/writer terminator behavior was inspected separately.
At the ordinary getUCSText boundary, exactly one complete final NUL code unit is
now excluded from the borrowed conversion view. The cursor still consumes the
same declared/optional terminator bytes, the public tolerant text is unchanged,
and embedded or repeated NULs still register discarded content. No per-version
DWG layout, DWG dispatch type or parseDwg body changes. XRECORD application's
separate counted text body is not silently given this framing exemption.

Generated controls:

  keep earlier issues across a clean call, and isolate explicit resets. Four
  UTF16 controls distinguish actual malformed units from a valid U+FFFD scalar.
  Mixed primary/CP8, unprofiled-byte, exact-named and swap/move controls cover
  independent return paths without inferring loss from result characters.
- Eleven framed TU cells cover empty/un-terminated/terminated text, embedded and

- The earlier GROUP name-byte controls now also check corrected retry and
  cleared diagnostics. NOD normalization is bounded before copying, and every

The existing writer appended common XDATA to XRECORD, but its typed reader folded
those tags into both application vectors. This was a real preservation defect,
not merely an absent qualification receipt. The first group1001 after the
subclass/header now starts the common trailing channel; production base parsing
retains its APPID/string/control/integer/handle/binary/point values in extData,
under that channel's existing node and string leases. Ordinary application
payload cannot reopen after XDATA. Ordered body102/280/330 fields, first-header
280 handling, repeated body subclass-marker strings, copy/assignment and ordinary
non-XDATA compatibility views keep their separate contracts.

and [common object codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-6939D69E-04CB-4F4C-87B2-67BC540FCF58.htm).

metadata is not discounted. Null binary owners now fail comparison safely.

Sixty domain refusal/same-adapter retry cells cover three payload carriers,

The source-schema audit found a concrete reader defect: legacy XRECORD
application text consumed its per-value codepage byte but discarded it, then
decoded all values using the enclosing file codec. A scratch-authored CP936
string under a CP1252 file profile and the reverse CP1252/CP936 control expose
wrong text. Unknown and aliased pages could also disappear behind matching
ASCII/empty results, while trailing counted NUL bytes were stripped without an
observation. Both focused test selectors failed before the production change;
that failure log remains separate from the passing final receipts.

reviewed before changing the application-body reader. Legacy XRECORD has a
one-byte per-value codepage field, unlike the separate common EED framing.
No code or fixture was copied from a peer repository. The specification's
legacy RC count conflicts with the library's established RS count: this slice
does not silently choose another layout, add speculative heuristics or claim
producer qualification. Resolve that discrepancy separately against the ODA
layout/example and a traceable producer-created legacy XRECORD source.

Nonzero legacy pages now use the existing internal named-DWG-page conversion
and issue transfer. Named profiles decode independently of the file profile;
unknown pages retain file/raw fallback and mark UnknownCodePage, and existing
many-to-one aliases mark CompatibilityCodePage even for empty or ASCII values.
The file codec and byte-channel selection remain unchanged. Zero keeps its
existing file-default convention; modern counted Unicode strings have no page
byte and retain their existing route. Known profiles also decode without an
observation sink; unknown/default null-sink values keep raw fallback.

The existing trailing-NUL normalization is retained, but any bytes it removes
from decoded counted application text merge DiscardedSource into the enclosing
frame mask. No ordinary TV/TU single-terminator exemption applies to this path.
Modern Unicode losses are already observed by the converter. A later clean
field cannot erase earlier issues; explicit frame reset prevents contamination
of the next object. Existing source capture freezes and rechecks the mask and
keeps issue-bearing frames out of modeled-output correspondence. No adapter
state, public callback or stricter ordinary import policy was added. The stale
writer comment about uncombined UTF16 surrogate pairs was also corrected.

The next output-side gate now has an actual-byte observation route rather than
trusting mutable table rows or preallocated handles. `setDxfTablesWriteInspector`
is an opt-in nonvirtual dxfRW API over the existing whole-TABLES record scope.
It receives the exact staged/backpatched body and actual revision, encoding,
codepage and compatibility profile before append and before BLOCKS/ENTITIES/
OBJECTS. It shares the OBJECTS callback's expiring view and mutation guard.
Default empty inspectors add no copying/decoding pass; no DRW_Interface virtual
was added. Consumer rebuild is required, without a binary ABI promise.

Primary sources verified this round are Autodesk's
[TABLES example](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2023/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-A66D0ACA-3F43-4B2E-A0C2-2B490C1E5268.htm),
[LAYER fields](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-D94802B0-8BE8-4AC9-8054-17197688AFDB.htm)
and [APPID fields](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-6E3140E9-E560-4C77-904E-480382F0553E.htm).
No DWG parseDwg body, byte layout, dispatch type or fixture changed.

The internal dx_symbol_output scanner uses the production ASCII/Binary value
reader and one lexical name owner at a time. TABLE/row/ENDTAB scope is explicit;
selected tables cannot repeat. A name/identity candidate requires its complete
selected table header, one nonzero primary handle, a version-appropriate owner
matching that table, one name/flags field and exact ordered subclass markers.
Names, owners and handles inside balanced102 metadata groups cannot substitute
for primary fields. Missing/duplicate/defaulted/wrong-subclass/owner/wide values
remain unqualified, and malformed/unclosed framing invalidates the whole call,
including earlier callback rows. The visitor owns/charges anything it retains;
the scanner makes no section-sized row, span or model inventory.

Each semantic name decode compares the reader's event count, not a bit-mask
delta. Repeated identical damage stays unqualified while a later clean row can
qualify. Literal U+FFFD is not presumed damaged. Unknown legacy codepage metadata
does not qualify even ASCII values; modern UTF8 remains independent of that
legacy declaration. Default limits cover1,000,000 group-0 records,4,194,304
group/value pairs,1 MiB wire name and512 KiB decoded name. Exact/one-below tests
cover name owners/wire and record limits; these are logical recipe/scanner
bounds, not a process allocator or heap/RSS guarantee.

Adversarial API controls exposed an actual contract gap: a byte inspector could
ignore a rejected nested whole-operation write and still allow publication.
The WholeOperationScope rejection now marks the outer write failed only during
byte inspection, including attempted nested read/readAscii. It still admits no
nested scope and does not reset outer diagnostics/maps/cursors. Existing source
tests explicitly require harmless whole-operation rejection in ordinary
callbacks AND the consumer finalizer; those contracts remain unchanged. Record
writes/setup mutations in finalization continue to refuse as before. A veto,
throw, forbidden inspection action or later emission/finalization failure
retracts aliases and tentative bytes, preserves the old destination and permits
a corrected same-codec retry.

The writer adds two nonvirtual scoped queries. A forward table allocation does
not satisfy dxfWriteEmittedSourceTableHandle; successful LAYER/APPID/STYLE/VPORT

plan. Contradictory fixed remaps and duplicate/cross-family identities refuse;
all derived aliases/receipts roll back on failed encoding, append or publication.
Source rows/caller registrations are not rewritten. No inventory means no final
identity receipt; scoped queries expire outside an active/finalizing operation.
Consumers must rebuild dxfRW, with no binary ABI promise or new public virtual.

The source review also found that existing ASCII-only symbol folding was not
sufficient for Unicode ambiguity. Peer research confirms a Unicode-aware name
key in [ezdxf's validator](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/lldxf/validator.py),
but no peer code was copied or peer execution claimed. The new ambiguity-only
policy is generated from pinned official Unicode17
[full-fold data](https://www.unicode.org/Public/17.0.0/ucd/CaseFolding.txt) and
[simple-uppercase data](https://www.unicode.org/Public/17.0.0/ucd/UnicodeData.txt).
Its locale-independent fixed-point closure covers all1585 default full-fold
and1505 simple-uppercase relations in1586 stored mappings. The generator checks
source hashes, closure/idempotence, valid scalar sequences and maximum3x UTF8
expansion. Runtime keys strictly validate UTF8 and bound512 KiB input/1.5 MiB
expanded output. Exact output/source spelling still compares byte-for-byte;
keys never rewrite names or invent Unicode normalization. This conservative
collision policy is not a particular native consumer's collation certificate.
The existing Unicode License V3 is retained; README and CMake/Automake distribution
lists include the new generated data/helper/generator. Builds require no download,
generator execution or new runtime Unicode dependency.

The frame-scoped verifier is used only for common-EED1003. It requires the frozen
full-width dependency, resolved layer-name marker, actual qualified table tuple
and exact source/output names; null/wide/unbound/synthetic references remain
unqualified. APPID dependencies must also close their actual output tuples.

to reject DWG layer-ID metadata. Finalization rechecks source aliases, unique
TABLES record/header identities and row/table owners, in addition to unchanged
imported name owners, before retaining a modeled OBJECTS fact. Failed export
attempts retract tentative facts/names; import provenance is never refreshed.

## Research refresh — RPP-5be raster source integrity and consumer boundaries (2026-10-23)

This deeper/broader pass checks current primary sources as well as the local
implementation. It does not reopen the completed native compound IMAGE fix or
turn a peer's feature list into this library's support certificate.

Primary-source findings and implementation decisions:

1. ODA v5.4.1 §§20.4.81–82, complete rendered pages206–208, specify the
   IMAGEDEF body as BL class version,2RD pixel dimensions, versioned text path,
   B loaded flag, RC resolution units and2RD pixel size. IMAGEDEF's parent is
   hard ownership; IMAGEDEF_REACTOR's parent is a soft pointer. Common state
   includes reactors and optional extension ownership, with version-specific
   header/stream organization. The local compound writer now closes these
   links, but source callbacks alone do not establish field spans or handle
   roles from the input bytes.
2. Current [ACadSharp reader](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/IO/DWG/DwgStreamReaders/DwgObjectReader.cs)
   and [LibreDWG record grammar](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/dwg.spec)
   independently describe that body order and a separate reactor class-version
   body. However, LibreDWG's [shared object-handle grammar](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/common_object_handle_data.spec)
   uses a generic soft-pointer owner. Do not flatten the ODA-specified
   IMAGEDEF/reactor distinction to match a shared peer helper. Use the ODA
   layout plus literal bytes and separately record independent producer results.
   Source class ordinals remain file-local: bind actual published class identity,
   never assume the writer's default class number is a universal reader code.
3. [Autodesk IMAGEDEF DXF](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-EFE5319F-A71A-4612-9431-42B6C7C3941F.htm)
   documents pixel V group12 and resolution units0/2/5. [ezdxf's model](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/image.py)
   uses a conventional point2d field at group11 and validates the same unit
   set. Preserve the local documented group12 output and tolerant group21
   input; do not make a peer's code21 convention a silent wire-format change.
   Keep compatible byte-domain retention distinct from qualified enum profiles.
4. Current [FreeCAD importDWG](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/main/src/Mod/Draft/importDWG.py)
   invokes `dwg2dxf input -o output`, checks whether the file exists, then passes
   it to `importDXF.open/insert`; its ODA route asks for ACAD2000 DXF. Therefore
   CLI syntax/existence success alone is insufficient: maintain atomic output,
   failure exit/output behavior, paths with spaces and non-ASCII text, and real
   document geometry/placement checks. Keep actual converter selection and both
   open/insert gates separate from the direct DXF importer. This source review
   is not native Linux/Windows or a new FreeCAD qualification run.
5. [ezdxf's ACIS layer](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/acis/entities.py)
   separates SAT/SAB version targets and refuses export of unsupported entity
   structures rather than silently dropping them. Its [export traversal](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/acis/abstract.py)
   registers identities before writing graph references. Keep the equivalent
   local separation among opaque retention, rooted graph projection, supported
   serializer grammar and independent kernel acceptance. Peer parsing, a body
   count or container hashes do not unblock ACIS/ACDS semantic claims.

Implementation-ready ordering refined for speed:

- RPP-5be now implements a separate bounded raster source lane using existing
  raw frame/publication carriers and the existing bounded production grammars.
  No new callback/reader dispatch is needed. Save generation, bytes, physical
  frame location/ordinal, actual custom-class identity and decoder profile;
  correlate typed bodies/common links, then freeze separately owned models.
  Add source-edit and final-publication guards without feeding any new records
  into the standard-object output/completeness lane.
- Exercise exact and one-byte-short budgets at raw, publication and baseline
  ownership stages, identity/size/class mismatches, failed/closed generations,
  single-field edits, corrected retries and late mutations. Reuse the existing
  fast generated-image selector and its six native revision sources. Build one
  decoder per import, not per object, and keep unchanged-source queries
  allocation-free. Run affected owning suites only at the composed checkpoint.
- A local build-cost audit also found the same large `dx_iface.cpp` compiled
  separately by the CLI and twelve test targets. Queue a narrowly scoped build
  slice: inventory per-target compile definitions, C++ flags, sanitizers,
  platform frameworks and include/link interfaces; extract an uninstalled
  converter support object/static target only for identical configurations;
  switch consumers without changing installed library metadata or core ABI.
  Keep any flag-specific target separate. Verify normal/ASan links, lc3 and the
  affected converter/CLI suites once at that checkpoint. This is source-audited
  duplicate work, not a claimed speedup or permission to skip validation.
- Next add reader-independent field spans/width/presence and literal handle-role
  observations, a complete class/source-profile matrix and independently bound
  EED APPID/LAYER dependencies. Reparse equality must not become that oracle.
- Then implement nondefault reactor metadata conversion policy and actual
  output field/identity/edge/publication proof. Only a fully composed attempt
  may approach strict admission; remain closed until then. Preserve the fast
  2D compatibility route and opt-in qualified 3D routes, with no new pure
  virtuals or binary ABI promise.
- Preserve all broader APPID/LAYER, legacy XRECORD, AC1024/container/SUN,
  TABLE/extension, MATERIAL and warning-debt queues. The six J items stay
  DEFERRED_EXTERNAL; native Linux/Windows FreeCAD and independent ACIS/ACDS
  semantic/kernel qualification stay NOT_RUN. None blocks local improvements.

  Reject missing/overflowing field spans, unreasonable counts and unexpected

  do not assume the native writer's default class number532.

  families' reactors require soft-pointer role4. Canonical NULL remains role0;
  explicit typed zero and checked soft-pointer offsets6/8/A/C are distinct
  literal observations, not relabeled ownership. Offset arithmetic cannot wrap.
  The observer preserves the library's32-bit handle domain; oversized handle
  encodings refuse instead of truncating, not a claim of wider-handle support.
- Pre-2007 byte paths and 2007+ detached TU spans are separate. No independent
  text/codepage decoding is claimed. Nonzero EED, DataStorage, unknown revisions
  and unrecognized reactor-string profiles stay Unsupported/unqualified and
  retain the existing bounded production-correlation route. A partial observer
  receipt is never a complete-profile or support certificate.

  units. This observer uses16-bit RS words, anchored by literal/scratch vectors

  observed24-zero empty-string trailer is named separately; only that exact
  trailer plus bounded scalar padding is admitted. Producer discrepancies and
  the complete profile matrix remain qualification work. OT tag3 is retained

Authoritative and peer review:

- Read ODA v5.4.1 chapter28 in full (rendered page269), CLASSES chapter10
  (pages86–88), and the IMAGEDEF/reactor layouts (pages207–208), alongside the
  already-reviewed common-object and bit-code rules. No peer code is copied.
- Chapter28 fixes BS chunk lengths excluding APPID H, a role5 APPID reference,
  terminating BS0 and raw item widths. It distinguishes legacy byte strings
  plus a two-byte codepage from R2007+ length/UTF16 strings, eight-byte LAYER
  and entity references, binary chunks, control bytes, points/reals and ints.
  The observer now follows those widths independently, not by reparsing with
  the production grammar or comparing it with its own encoder.
- A real disagreement stays visible: the ODA prose describes eight-byte LAYER
  handles without explicitly spelling out a distinct byte order;
  [LibreDWG's decoder](https://github.com/LibreDWG/libredwg/blob/master/src/decode.c)
  uses RLL/LE for LAYER but RLL_BE for entity references, while
  [ACadSharp's reader](https://github.com/DomCR/ACadSharp/blob/master/src/ACadSharp/IO/DWG/DwgStreamReaders/DwgObjectReader.cs)
  uses BE for both. Preserve both LAYER interpretations. The local/LibreDWG LE
  binding is explicitly labeled; differing alternatives set a disagreement
  issue. Successful target lookup cannot decide byte order or qualify the
  other interpretation. Legacy EED codepage bytes also retain both numeric
  interpretations; no independent decoder is claimed here.
- CLASSES defines object itemclassid0x1F3 and separate proxy/version/unknown
  trailer fields. Capture those existing metadata fields without guessing
  source ordinals from writer defaults. Mark proxy/unknown metadata, missing
  envelopes and unbound codepages explicitly; raw CLASSES-section byte evidence
  remains production-supplied, not newly independent.

The defect was an admission mismatch in `prepareMTextBackgroundCmc`: DXF
retains background ACI (63) and active RGB (421) together, but the helper
accepted RGB only when the scalar ACI was 256. The authored AC1032 ATTDEF and
ATTRIB input uses ACI 3/4 with RGB `0x123456`/`0x654321`. The existing native
oracle already expected scalar 256 on readback, plus exact active RGB, names,
defined height, scale, transparency, text, owners and following geometry.

reserved zero BS index and method-tagged BL payload. The attribute/embedded
MTEXT and standalone MTEXT chapters (PDF pages 112–114 and 153–155) were
reviewed/rendered before selecting the fix. The [Autodesk MTEXT DXF reference](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2020/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-5E5DB93B-F8D3-4433-ADF7-E92E250D2BAB.htm)

permits body-102 control strings. Profile-aware role interpretation must retain
such distinctions rather than guessing one global post-subclass rule. No DWG
byte layout, native encoding or external ACIS/ACDS kernel claim changes here.

## Implementation progress RPP-5dz: original common identities and compound structural roles (2026-10-25)

Parent is `3edcba12`. This advances the original common-identity and logical
compound-membership dependencies, not the complete model/body, target, live-state,
output or external semantic/platform requirements.

Source rules: Autodesk distinguishes common outer identity/ownership from
application groups and warns that common field order can vary
([common entity codes](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3610039E-27D1-4E23-B6D3-7E60B22BB5BD.htm)).
INSERT's declared attribute-follow flag defaults to zero and a declared sequence
terminates with SEQEND
([INSERT](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-28FA4CFB-9D5E-4880-9F11-36C97578252F.htm));
POLYLINE's obsolete group 66 is ignored, not treated as that INSERT flag
([POLYLINE](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-ABF6B778-BE20-4B49-9B58-A94E64CEFFF3.htm)).
The [ezdxf linked-entity implementation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/subentity.py)
assigns child entities to the compound parent, but its SEQEND linking and later
ownership-taking paths differ. Accordingly, retain a terminator's observed
BLOCK_RECORD/compound-parent owner separately from its logical sequence parent.
Do not normalize that distinction or treat these sources as independent kernel
qualification. No external drawing is copied into the repository.

1. [x] Add a converter-private, bounded immutable structural audit over the
   existing original physical inventory and validated dispatch partition.
   Record exact original outer self/owner group indices, dispatch and logical
   parent indices, member roles and observed owner roles. Allow base/common
   field interleaving; ignore application-scoped and entity-body/embedded 5/330
   fields as outer aliases. Original body handles that overwrite a delivered
   child's convenience identity cannot borrow its original membership.
2. [x] Distinguish primary records, POLYLINE/VERTEX/SEQEND and
   INSERT-or-MINSERT/ATTRIB/SEQEND chains. Check parser routes/known aliases,
   expected sequence names/order/termination, declared/default INSERT follow
   state, owner roles and duplicate self IDs, including collisions with BLOCK,
   BLOCK_RECORD and ENDBLK. Preserve supported physical footer-owner forms,
   not a rewritten owner. Unflagged attribute chains remain compatibility
   reads, not a qualified declared sequence. Raw orphan VERTEX/ATTRIB/SEQEND and
   zero-callback dispositions remain explicit gaps.
3. [x] Compare actual delivered compound child counts/order/self/owner and
   retained SEQEND identities against original physical members, including null,
   dropped, reordered or identity-mutated children. Pin exact immutable physical,
   delivery and endpoint owners, generation and actual data-container identity.
   Require successful whole import and complete observed replay when querying.
   Stale or copied successful evidence cannot qualify a new container.
4. [x] Pin the structural audit in each selected ATTDEF origin. Require its
   exact original primary/self/owner role and successful enclosing structural
   membership before returning the existing advisory origin fact. A structural
   gap or later quota/callback/context failure cannot borrow an earlier ATTDEF
   pair. Keep resource-family count, `rawTypedMatched` and output gates unchanged.
5. [x] Precharge aggregate records/logical bytes/work before vector/control
   allocation and inspection; include transient sorted identity indices and
   observed-child visits. Defaults are 100,000 physical members and 64 MiB each
   for logical byte/work allowances. Sorting indices avoids per-record map
   allocation and quadratic duplicate checks. Own quota/allocation failure

selected-definition worklist. It does not substitute for ENTITIES space,
remaining primary member families, common/opaque targets, live/output or the
original native-consumer/independent semantic objective.

Implemented:

1. [x] Resolve each original admitted INSERT/MINSERT body name in the
   BLOCK_RECORD namespace, preserving its distinct role from a handle or local
   style ID. Require the target row's existing source proof and its uniquely
   reconciled complete admitted definition, then expand each selected target
   only once. Shared and repeated references retain their separate edge counts
   without repeatedly qualifying the same definition. A raw/unqualified leaf
   cannot borrow the root's positive compound proof.
2. [x] Reuse the existing invariant Unicode key for ambiguity detection and
   candidate lookup only. Admit exact UTF-8 spelling and ASCII-case variants
   with unchanged non-ASCII bytes. A wider fold-only alias is explicitly
   `BlockNameCollationUnqualified`, not an assumed native collation match.
   Preserve semantic spelling and never rewrite output names or interpret a
   handle-looking name numerically. Empty/invalid/unresolved/ambiguous names
   cannot set the completed graph fact. Native Unicode collation remains open.
3. [x] Append edges in deduplicated source-node order, build bounded adjacency
   offsets and run iterative color/stack DFS. Self, two-node, three-node and
   deep tail back edges refuse the graph with an actual source member diagnostic.
   No recursive traversal or all-definition scan per edge is introduced. The
   [Autodesk complex-entity/block guidance](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/FRA/AutoCAD-AutoLISP/files/GUID-7DA0E2BA-963F-4E41-AF33-C6B9D89D4688.htm)
   describes block references and the self-reference boundary; these local
   graph controls are not a native CAD acceptance or geometry-kernel witness.
4. [x] Charge normalization attempts before key allocation, map/vector node
   workspace, edges, offsets, colors and iterative stack under the existing
   shared binding-work and 64 MiB query allowances. Index/visit work is bounded
   separately from retained source budgets. Allocation/limit failures refuse
   the report, leave immutable input unchanged and allow an unmodified retry.
   Accounting remains logical attempt/workspace allowance, not RSS, a strict
   CPU bound, every allocator or leak-detector certification.
5. [x] Fix a newly exercised source-profile prerequisite instead of excluding
   the valid array shape. The previous local profile rejects the original
   `INSERT`/`AcDbMInsertBlock` record even though the existing writer emits it.
   Admit this subclass with positive grid dimensions and at least one dimension
   greater than one; omitted dimensions retain their default one. Preserve the
   already admitted base-class/grid and legacy MINSERT reader compatibility
   shapes. A multi-insert marker without the admitted grid, zero dimensions,
   unknown derived markers and other incomplete profiles still refuse source
   qualification without tightening ordinary import. This changes the private
   field profile, not the geometry decoder or writer. The
   [Autodesk INSERT fields](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2024/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-28FA4CFB-9D5E-4880-9F11-36C97578252F.htm),
   local writer/existing authored fixture and
   [ezdxf's INSERT export implementation](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/src/ezdxf/entities/insert.py)
   corroborate name/grid/default/subclass distinctions. No peer fixture or code
   payload is copied, and source inspection is not independently executed CAD
   semantic evidence. The stored red run is the local pre-profile-fix working
   binary, not a separately rebuilt pristine parent.

Owning evidence per configuration:

## Implementation progress — RPP-5ee original ENTITIES intervals and selected TABLE origins (2026-10-26)

This implements the original physical-interval prerequisite of RPP-5ed's
ENTITIES item, including an integrated selected TABLE origin gate. It does not
claim complete ENTITIES dispatch/body/space or whole-drawing semantics. A raw
interval can contain unresolved references and no-callback records while still
being a complete physical observation. Such records do not acquire model,
graph, output or support qualification from that transport fact.

Implemented:

1. [x] Add a separate optional `DRW_DxfEntitiesSourceHandler` and source/limits
   types, not a BLOCK manifest with owner zero. Selection is latched per section.
   Capture begins at the actual pending first code-0 marker after
   `readEntityBoundary` and terminates at real ENDSEC, including an empty
   interval whose begin/end marker is the same ENDSEC. Section headers and
   comments before the first marker are explicitly outside this interval.
   Preserve original record names, scalar kinds/values, ASCII spellings,
   ordinals, byte intervals, compound subrecords and observer-identified ignored
   comments, not reconstructed callback values. The
   [Autodesk ENTITIES structure](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-995ABB55-571A-4D0F-882E-8A74A738643E.htm)
   supplies the section/record boundary distinction. New public transport types
   are additive; existing drawing-model layouts, DRW_Interface and existing
   facet vtables are unchanged, not formally ABI-certified.
2. [x] Factor neutral physical scalar capture from the existing BLOCK collector
   and retain separate ENDBLK/ENDSEC wrappers. Preserve shared-reader observer
   chaining, the already-observed pending marker, logical byte/node/work leases
   and exception-safe detach. Publish ENTITIES source only after accepted ENDSEC
   and ordinary callbacks; do not stage an entire ENTITIES section or change
   legacy callback ordering. Aborted/truncated/throwing sections publish no
   completed report; a later whole-file failure cannot qualify an earlier
   completed interval. Own collection quotas/allocation failures report failed
   evidence without rejecting otherwise compatible import. Shared reader limits
   remain authoritative and can still fail the read.
3. [x] Bound per-section collection at 65,536 physical records, 262,144 groups,
   32 MiB logical bytes and 67,108,864 logical work units by default. The CLI
   additionally bounds aggregate immutable copies at 1,024 retained scopes,
   100,000 charged records (including one scope sentinel each), 4,000,000 groups,
   64 MiB logical bytes and 67,108,864 work units. Share physical-carrier copy
   validation/accounting with BLOCKs, including dormant variant payloads and
   rejection of forged native/assembled carriers before copying. No unbounded
   per-record map is added for every entity; only actual ACAD_TABLE origins
   receive a bounded identity index. Accounting is logical allowance, not RSS,
   every allocator, strict CPU or leak-detector evidence.
4. [x] Freeze source owners with actual container/generation/version/scope
   context. A transport report requires successful actual first-generation
   import and retained owner/context matches. It describes retained opted-in
   scopes only, not proof that every section opted in or is semantically valid.
   Duplicate/stale/out-of-phase, copied/appended or failed-import contexts cannot
   borrow completion. Reader-source mutations after capture cannot edit the
   immutable snapshot, and its owners tear down without an owning context cycle.
5. [x] Integrate selected TABLE physical origins into the existing binding
   report after direct roles. Join actual scoped outer identities, exact pinned
   interval owners and literal raw scalar/type/spelling equality, ignoring only
   original observer-identified comments. Missing observations or replaced/
   mismatched owners, identities, raw values and equivalent-but-different handle
   spellings refuse the gate while `directRolesBound` stays distinct. This proves
   original TABLE presence/body transport, NOT all TABLE field semantics,
   observed primary callbacks or model/paper/BLOCK_RECORD associations. In
   particular, [common owner/space fields](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2015/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-3610039E-27D1-4E23-B6D3-7E60B22BB5BD.htm)
   and [model/paper block distinctions](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-66D32572-005A-4E23-8B8B-8726E8C14302.htm)
   require separate role/target qualification, not one owner for the whole
   section or a TABLE owner's metadata row alone.
6. [x] List the new private headers in CMake and Autotools. Use locally authored
   runtime inputs only; do not commit external drawings. Register the existing
   focused proxy graphic/loss-policy selector as its own fast CTest rather than
   repeatedly running the entire DXF fixture suite.
7. [x] Fix a reproduced generic raw-entity reader scope defect, not an invalid
   vendor fixture. An original vendor-subclass group 160 with value 4 GiB was
   incorrectly interpreted as a common proxy-byte count. Autodesk's
   [subclass rules](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/AutoCAD-DXF/files/GUID-CC5ACB1B-BBA3-463B-84A5-6CCD320C66E7.htm)
   segregate class fields, and its
   [custom group ranges](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2021/ENU/OARX-DevGuide/files/GUID-A0E46BAC-ECE3-4E31-854A-3616A532C826.htm)
   allow groups 160..169 as class-specific 64-bit integers and 310..319 as
   binary. Stop feeding proxy-only 92/160/310 fields to the common proxy host
   after the first foreign subclass or embedded boundary. Repeated AcDbEntity
   cannot reopen that scope; fake subclass markers inside application groups
   cannot close it. Preserve legacy no-subclass caches, actual common count
   limits and raw fields verbatim. The positive vendor input retains group 160;
   the oversized-proxy negative now uses the actual common scope. This changes
   DXF proxy field routing, not DWG bytes, proxy decoder math/opcodes or complete
   specialized/application/XDATA grammar qualification.

This implements the bounded original identity-index prerequisite identified by
RPP-5ej. It is an index of observable original DXF identity envelopes, not body
support, actual typed target/owner/layout resolution, hidden application/kernel
identities, editable/live/output parity, native collation or external support.
There is no DWG byte-layout/parser/encoder change and no new drawing fixture.

Implemented:

   before the first scalar. A reader-owned observer sees the actual whole-read
   stream, including ignored comments, unknown/raw/no-callback records, compound
   subrecords, repeated sections, TABLE controls and skipped nested tables. It
   coexists with existing per-scope observers; their callback timing and spans
   are unchanged. No established DRW_Interface/source-facet vtable or public
   dxfRW/drawing-model object layout changes; internal observer/reader and private

   lexemes, ASCII spellings and exact physical ordinal/byte spans. Application,

   metadata are not database-object identities. Do not parse arbitrary bodies
   with another payload decoder. Unknown sections/unframed candidates, opaque
   identity-like fields outside a known application scope and malformed framing
   remain explicit, rather than disappearing from coverage.

   accepted/null/duplicate/invalid and repeated admission of the same scalar are

   DIMSTYLE group 105 and skipped unknown-table entries bypass this registry;
   typed entities can tolerate duplicate IDs. None means unobserved, not absent
   or accepted. The independent source index detects collisions even when the

   equal replacement owners, different shared control blocks and copied
   containers cannot reuse the real source certificate.
5. [x] Build the converter's separate 64-bit original source identity map.
   TABLE controls use group 5; only actual DIMSTYLE table entries use 105 and

   spellings with ASCII case folding, not a helper requiring an uppercase second
   argument. Unknown/raw/no-callback bodies do not acquire body support from

define visible identity/application envelopes. They are field references, not
independent execution, target-type, hidden-payload or native collation evidence.
